mula_pali:
1. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati devadahaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘santi, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evaṃvādino, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā.

‘‘Evaṃvādāhaṃ , bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhe upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti? Te ca me, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā evaṃ puṭṭhā ‘āmā’ti paṭijānanti.

‘‘Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, jānātha – ahuvamheva mayaṃ pubbe, na nāhuvamhā’ti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’.

‘‘‘Kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, jānātha – akaramheva mayaṃ pubbe pāpakammaṃ, na nākaramhā’ti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’.

‘‘‘Kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, jānātha – evarūpaṃ vā evarūpaṃ vā pāpakammaṃ akaramhā’ti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’.

‘‘‘Kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, jānātha – ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ, ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjīretabbaṃ, ettakamhi vā dukkhe nijjiṇṇe sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’.

‘‘‘Kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, jānātha – diṭṭheva dhamme akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampada’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’.
mula_english:
1. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans where there was a town of the Sakyans named Devadaha. There the Fortunate One addressed the monks (saying): "Monks." "Venerable sir," those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: "Bhikkhus, there are some recluses and *brāhmaṇas* who hold such a doctrine and view as this: 'Whatever this person (*purisapuggalo*) feels, whether pleasure (*sukhaṃ*) or pain (*dukkhaṃ*) or neither-pain-nor-pleasure (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*), all that is caused by what was done in the past (*pubbekatahetu*). So by annihilating with asceticism past actions (*purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā*) and by doing no fresh actions (*navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā*), there will be no consequence in the future (*āyatiṃ anavassavo*); with no consequence in the future, there is the destruction of action (*kammakkhayo*); with the destruction of action, there is the destruction of suffering (*dukkhakkhayo*); with the destruction of suffering, there is the destruction of feeling (*vedanākkhayo*); with the destruction of feeling, all suffering will be exhausted (*sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī*)’ti. So speak the Niganthas (*nigaṇṭhā*), bhikkhus."

"Bhikkhus, I go to the Niganthas who speak thus and I say: ‘Friend Niganthas, is it true that you hold such a doctrine and view as this: “Whatever this person feels...all suffering will be exhausted”’ti? And when the Niganthas are questioned by me in this way, they acknowledge ‘Yes’."

"Then I say this: ‘But, friends, do you Niganthas, know that we existed in the past, and that it is not the case that we did not exist (*ahuvamheva mayaṃ pubbe, na nāhuvamhā*)?’ ‘No, friend.’"

"‘But, friends, do you Niganthas, know that we did evil actions in the past, and did not abstain from them (*akaramheva mayaṃ pubbe pāpakammaṃ, na nākaramhā*)?’ ‘No, friend.’"

"‘But, friends, do you Niganthas, know that we did such and such kind of evil action (*evarūpaṃ vā evarūpaṃ vā pāpakammaṃ akaramhā*)?’ ‘No, friend.’"

"‘But, friends, do you Niganthas, know that so much suffering has already been exhausted (*ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ*), or that so much suffering has still to be exhausted (*ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjīretabbaṃ*), or that when so much suffering has been exhausted all suffering will have been exhausted (*ettakamhi vā dukkhe nijjiṇṇe sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī*)?’ ‘No, friend.’"

"‘But, friends, do you Niganthas, know that in this very life there is abandonment of unwholesome states and the attainment of wholesome states (*diṭṭheva dhamme akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampada*)?’ ‘No, friend.’"
commentary_pali:
1.Evaṃme sutanti devadahasuttaṃ. Tattha devadahaṃ nāmāti devā vuccanti rājāno, tattha ca sakyarājūnaṃ maṅgalapokkharaṇī ahosi pāsādikā ārakkhasampannā, sā devānaṃ dahattā ‘‘devadaha’’nti paññāyittha. Tadupādāya sopi nigamo devadahantveva saṅkhaṃ gato. Bhagavā taṃ nigamaṃ nissāya lumbinivane viharati. Sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetūti pubbe katakammapaccayā. Iminā kammavedanañca kiriyavedanañca paṭikkhipitvā ekaṃ vipākavedanameva sampaṭicchantīti dasseti. Evaṃ vādino, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhāti iminā pubbe aniyametvā vuttaṃ niyametvā dasseti.

Ahuvamhevamayanti idaṃ bhagavā tesaṃ ajānanabhāvaṃ jānantova kevalaṃ kalisāsanaṃ āropetukāmo pucchati. Ye hi ‘‘mayaṃ ahuvamhā’’tipi na jānanti, te kathaṃ kammassa katabhāvaṃ vā akatabhāvaṃ vā jānissanti. Uttaripucchāyapi eseva nayo.

Ahuvamheva maya
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard.
This is the Devadaha Sutta.
There, *devadahaṃ nāma* means, *devā* are called kings, and there was a beautiful and well-protected auspicious lotus pond of the Sakya kings there, and because it belonged to the gods, it was known as "Devadaha."
Because of this, that town also came to be known as Devadaha.
The Blessed One, relying on that town, dwells in the Lumbini Grove.
*Sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetū* means because of past actions.
By this, he shows that they accept only one result of action, rejecting both karmic feeling and action feeling.
*Evaṃ vādino, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā* by this, having previously spoken without restriction, he shows with restriction.

*Ahuvamheva maya* this the Blessed One, knowing their state of not knowing, asks only wishing to impose the stain teaching.
For those who do not even know "we were," how will they know whether an action has been done or not done?
The same rule applies to further questions.

*Ahuvamheva maya*

mula_pali:
2. ‘‘Iti kira tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, na jānātha – ahuvamheva mayaṃ pubbe, na nāhuvamhāti , na jānātha – akaramheva mayaṃ pubbe pāpakammaṃ, na nākaramhāti, na jānātha – evarūpaṃ vā evarūpaṃ vā pāpakammaṃ akaramhāti, na jānātha – ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ, ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjīretabbaṃ, ettakamhi vā dukkhe nijjiṇṇe sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatīti, na jānātha – diṭṭheva dhamme akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadaṃ; evaṃ sante āyasmantānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ na kallamassa veyyākaraṇāya – yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’’ti.

‘‘Sace pana tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, jāneyyātha – ahuvamheva mayaṃ pubbe, na nāhuvamhāti, jāneyyātha – akaramheva mayaṃ pubbe pāpakammaṃ, na nākaramhāti, jāneyyātha – evarūpaṃ vā evarūpaṃ vā pāpakammaṃ akaramhāti, jāneyyātha – ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ, ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjīretabbaṃ, ettakamhi vā dukkhe nijjiṇṇe sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatīti, jāneyyātha – diṭṭheva dhamme akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadaṃ; evaṃ sante āyasmantānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ kallamassa veyyākaraṇāya – yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’’ti.
mula_english:
2. “So, friends, it seems that you do not know that you existed in the past and that it is not the case that you did not exist; or that you did evil actions (pāpakammaṃ) in the past and did not abstain from them; or that you did such and such evil actions; or that so much suffering (dukkhaṃ) has already been exhausted, or that so much suffering (dukkhaṃ) has still to be exhausted, or that when so much suffering (dukkhaṃ) has been exhausted all suffering (dukkhaṃ) will have been exhausted; or what the abandoning of unwholesome states (akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ) is and what the cultivation of wholesome states (kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ) is; that being so, it is not fitting for the venerable Niganthas to declare: “Whatever this person feels, whether pleasure (sukhaṃ) or pain (dukkhaṃ) or neither-pain-nor-pleasure (adukkhamasukhaṃ), all that is caused by what was done in the past (pūrbekatahetu).” So by annihilating with asceticism past actions (kammānaṃ) and by doing no fresh actions, there will be no consequence in the future. With no consequence in the future, there is the destruction of action (kammakkhayo). With the destruction of action (kammakkhayo), there is the destruction of suffering (dukkhakkhayo). With the destruction of suffering (dukkhakkhayo), there is the destruction of feeling (vedanākkhayo). With the destruction of feeling (vedanākkhayo), all suffering (dukkhaṃ) will be exhausted.”

“If, friend Niganthas, you knew that you existed in the past and that it is not the case that you did not exist; or that you did evil actions (pāpakammaṃ) in the past and did not abstain from them; or that you did such and such evil actions; or that so much suffering (dukkhaṃ) has already been exhausted, or that so much suffering (dukkhaṃ) has still to be exhausted, or that when so much suffering (dukkhaṃ) has been exhausted all suffering (dukkhaṃ) will have been exhausted; or what the abandoning of unwholesome states (akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ) is and what the cultivation of wholesome states (kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ) is; that being so, it is not fitting for the venerable Niganthas to declare: “Whatever this person feels, whether pleasure (sukhaṃ) or pain (dukkhaṃ) or neither-pain-nor-pleasure (adukkhamasukhaṃ), all that is caused by what was done in the past (pūrbekatahetu).” So by annihilating with asceticism past actions (kammānaṃ) and by doing no fresh actions, there will be no consequence in the future. With no consequence in the future, there is the destruction of action (kammakkhayo). With the destruction of action (kammakkhayo), there is the destruction of suffering (dukkhakkhayo). With the destruction of suffering (dukkhakkhayo), there is the destruction of feeling (vedanākkhayo). With the destruction of feeling (vedanākkhayo), all suffering (dukkhaṃ) will be exhausted.”
commentary_pali: 2.Evaṃ santeti cūḷadukkhakkhandhe (ma. ni. 1.179-180) mahānigaṇṭhassa vacane sacce santeti attho, idha pana ettakassa ṭhānassa tumhākaṃ ajānanabhāve santeti attho. Na kallanti na yuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
"evaṃ sante" means in the Cūḷadukkhakkhandha (in the Great Collection of Discourses, 1. 179-180), "in the words of the great Nigaṇṭha, there is truth," this is the meaning. Here, however, the meaning is, "In your state of not knowing this much, there is..."
"na kalla" means it is not fitting.

mula_pali:
3. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, puriso sallena viddho assa savisena gāḷhūpalepanena gāḷhapalepanena (ka.); so sallassapi vedhanahetu vedanāhetu (sī. pī. ka.) dukkhā tibbā tippā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kaṭukā vedanā vediyeyya. Tassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ. Tassa so bhisakko sallakatto satthena vaṇamukhaṃ parikanteyya; so satthenapi vaṇamukhassa parikantanahetu dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyeyya. Tassa so bhisakko sallakatto esaniyā sallaṃ eseyya; so esaniyāpi sallassa esanāhetu dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyeyya . Tassa so bhisakko sallakatto sallaṃ abbuheyya abbuyheyya (sī.), abbhūṇheyya (syā. kaṃ.); so sallassapi abbuhanahetu abbuyhanahetu (sī.), abbhūṇhanahetu (syā. kaṃ.) dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyeyya. Tassa so bhisakko sallakatto agadaṅgāraṃ vaṇamukhe odaheyya; so agadaṅgārassapi vaṇamukhe odahanahetu dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyeyya. So aparena samayena rūḷhena vaṇena sañchavinā arogo assa sukhī serī sayaṃvasī yena kāmaṅgamo. Tassa evamassa – ahaṃ kho pubbe sallena viddho ahosiṃ savisena gāḷhūpalepanena. Sohaṃ sallassapi vedhanahetu dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyiṃ. Tassa me mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhapesuṃ. Tassa me so bhisakko sallakatto satthena vaṇamukhaṃ parikanti; sohaṃ satthenapi vaṇamukhassa parikantanahetu dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyiṃ. Tassa me so bhisakko sallakatto esaniyā sallaṃ esi; so ahaṃ esaniyāpi sallassa esanāhetu dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyiṃ. Tassa me so bhisakko sallakatto sallaṃ abbuhi abbuyhi (sī.), abbhūṇhi (syā. kaṃ.); sohaṃ sallassapi abbuhanahetu dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyiṃ. Tassa me so bhisakko sallakatto agadaṅgāraṃ vaṇamukhe odahi; sohaṃ agadaṅgārassapi vaṇamukhe odahanahetu dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyiṃ. Somhi etarahi rūḷhena vaṇena sañchavinā arogo sukhī serī sayaṃvasī yena kāmaṅgamo’’ti.

‘‘Evameva kho, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, sace tumhe jāneyyātha – ahuvamheva mayaṃ pubbe, na nāhuvamhāti, jāneyyātha – akaramheva mayaṃ pubbe pāpakammaṃ, na nākaramhāti, jāneyyātha – evarūpaṃ vā evarūpaṃ vā pāpakammaṃ akaramhāti, jāneyyātha – ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ, ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjīretabbaṃ, ettakamhi vā dukkhe nijjiṇṇe sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatīti, jāneyyātha – diṭṭheva dhamme akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadaṃ; evaṃ sante āyasmantānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ kallamassa veyyākaraṇāya – yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’’ti.

‘‘Yasmā ca kho tumhe, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, na jānātha – ahuvamheva mayaṃ pubbe, na nāhuvamhāti, na jānātha – akaramheva mayaṃ pubbe pāpakammaṃ, na nākaramhāti, na jānātha – evarūpaṃ vā evarūpaṃ vā pāpakammaṃ akaramhāti, na jānātha – ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ, ettakaṃ vā dukkhaṃ nijjīretabbaṃ, ettakamhi vā dukkhe nijjiṇṇe sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatīti, na jānātha – diṭṭheva dhamme akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadaṃ; tasmā āyasmantānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ na kallamassa veyyākaraṇāya – yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’’ti.
mula_english:
3. “Just as, friend Nigaṇṭhas, suppose a man were wounded by an arrow thickly smeared with poison; and because of this arrow he would feel painful, racking, piercing feelings. His friends and companions, his kinsmen and relatives, would bring a physician (*bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ*) to treat him. The physician, the surgeon (*sallakatto*), would cut around the opening of the wound with a knife; and because of cutting around the opening of the wound with a knife he would feel painful, racking, piercing feelings. The physician, the surgeon, would probe for the arrow with a probe; and because of probing for the arrow with a probe he would feel painful, racking, piercing feelings. The physician, the surgeon, would pull out the arrow; and because of pulling out the arrow he would feel painful, racking, piercing feelings. The physician, the surgeon, would apply a medicinal cauteriser (*agadaṅgāraṃ*) to the opening of the wound; and because of applying a medicinal cauteriser to the opening of the wound he would feel painful, racking, piercing feelings. Then on a later occasion, when the wound was healed and covered with skin, the man would be well and happy, independent, master of himself, able to go where he likes. He might think: “Formerly I was pierced by an arrow thickly smeared with poison, and because of this arrow I felt painful, racking, piercing feelings. Then my friends and companions, my kinsmen and relatives, brought a physician, a surgeon, to treat me. The physician, the surgeon, cut around the opening of the wound with a knife; and because of cutting around the opening of the wound with a knife I felt painful, racking, piercing feelings. The physician, the surgeon, probed for the arrow with a probe; and because of probing for the arrow with a probe I felt painful, racking, piercing feelings. The physician, the surgeon, pulled out the arrow; and because of pulling out the arrow I felt painful, racking, piercing feelings. The physician, the surgeon, applied a medicinal cauteriser to the opening of the wound; and because of applying a medicinal cauteriser to the opening of the wound I felt painful, racking, piercing feelings. But now that the wound is healed and covered with skin, I am well and happy, independent, my own master, able to go where I like.”

“So too, friend Nigaṇṭhas, if you knew that you existed in the past and that it is not the case that you did not exist; or that you did evil actions in the past and did not abstain from them; or that you did such and such evil actions; or that so much suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) has already been exhausted, or that so much suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) has still to be exhausted, or that when so much suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) has been exhausted all suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) will have been exhausted; or what the abandoning of unwholesome states is and what the cultivation of wholesome states is here and now; that being so, it would be fitting for the venerable Nigaṇṭhas to declare: “Whatever this person feels, whether pleasure (*sukhaṃ*) or pain (*dukkhaṃ*) or neither-pain-nor-pleasure (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*), all that is caused by what was done in the past. So by annihilating with asceticism past actions and by doing no fresh actions, there will be no consequence in the future. With no consequence in the future, there is the destruction of action. With the destruction of action, there is the destruction of suffering (*dukkhaṃ*). With the destruction of suffering (*dukkhaṃ*), there is the destruction of feeling (*vedanā*). With the destruction of feeling (*vedanā*), all suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) will be exhausted.”
“But since you, friends, the Nigaṇṭhas, do not know that we existed in the past and that it is not the case that we did not exist; you do not know that we did evil actions ( pāpakamma) in the past and did not abstain from them; you do not know that we did such and such evil actions; you do not know that so much suffering (dukkhaṃ ) has already been exhausted, or that so much suffering has still to be exhausted, or that when so much suffering has been exhausted all suffering will be exhausted; you do not know what the abandoning of unwholesome states (akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ), is and what the attainment (upasampadaṃ) of wholesome states (kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ) is here and now; therefore, it is not fitting for the venerable Nigaṇṭhas to declare: “Whatever this person feels, whether it is pleasure (sukhaṃ), pain (dukkhaṃ), or neither-pleasure-nor-pain (adukkhamasukhaṃ), all of that is due to past actions.”

Thus, by the destruction through asceticism (tapasā) of old actions (purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ), by the non-doing of new actions (navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā), there is no consequence in the future (āyatiṃ anavassavo); with no consequence in the future (āyatiṃ anavassavā), there is the destruction of action (kammakkhayo); with the destruction of action (kammakkhayā), there is the destruction of suffering ( dukkhakkhayo); with the destruction of suffering ( dukkhakkhayā), there is the destruction of feeling (vedanākkhayo); with the destruction of feeling (vedanākkhayā), all suffering (sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ) will be exhausted."
commentary_pali:
3.Gāḷhūpalepanenāti bahalūpalepanena, punappunaṃ visarañjitena, na pana khaliyā littena viya. Esaniyāti esanisalākāya antamaso nantakavaṭṭiyāpi. Eseyyāti gambhīraṃ vā uttānaṃ vāti vīmaṃseyya. Agadaṅgāranti jhāmaharītakassa vā āmalakassa vā cuṇṇaṃ. Odaheyyāti pakkhipeyya. Arogotiādi māgaṇḍiyasutte (ma. ni. 2.213) vuttameva.

Evameva khoti ettha idaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ, sallena viddhassa hi viddhakāle vedanāya pākaṭakālo viya imesaṃ ‘‘mayaṃ pubbe ahuvamhā vā no vā, pāpakammaṃ akaramhā vā no vā, evarūpaṃ vā pāpaṃ karamhā’’ti jānanakālo siyā. Vaṇamukhassa parikantanādīsu catūsu kālesu vedanāya pākaṭakālo viya ‘‘ettakaṃ vā no dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ, ettake vā nijjiṇṇe sabbameva dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissati, suddhante patiṭṭhitā nāma bhavissāmā’’ti jānanakālo siyā. Aparabhāge phāsubhāvajānanakālo viya diṭṭheva dhamme akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya jānanakālo siyā. Evamettha ekāya upamāya tayo atthā, catūhi upamāhi eko attho paridīpito.

Evameva kho
commentary_english:
3. *Gāḷhūpalepanenā* means with a thick plastering, that is, with a dense plastering, repeatedly made distinct, not like something smeared with mere oil-cake.
*Esaniyā* means even with an *esani* probe, or at least with a straining cloth (*nantakavaṭṭi*).
*Eseyyā* means he should investigate whether it is deep (*gambhīraṃ*) or shallow (*uttānaṃ*).
*Agadaṅgāra* means powder (*cuṇṇaṃ*) of scorched *harītakī* or *āmalaka*.
*Odaheyyā* means he should throw it in (*pakkhipeyya*).
*Arogo* and the rest was already stated in the Māgaṇḍiya Sutta (M.
N.
2, 213).

*Evameva kho* here is a connection of similes. Just as the time of obvious pain (*vedanāya pākaṭakālo*) for one pierced by a dart (*sallena viddhassa*) is at the time of being pierced (*viddhakāle*), so the time of their knowing (*jānanakālo siyā*) is "Did we exist in the past or not? Did we commit an evil deed (*pāpakammaṃ akaramhā*) or not? Did we do such an evil deed (*pāpaṃ karamhā*)?"
Just as the time of obvious pain at the four times of cutting the opening of a wound (*vaṇamukhassa parikantanādīsu catūsu kālesu vedanāya pākaṭakālo*) is, "So much suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) has been destroyed in us, when so much has been destroyed all suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) will be destroyed, we will be established in purity (*suddhante patiṭṭhitā nāma bhavissāmā*)," so the time of their knowing (*jānanakālo siyā*) is:
Just as the time of knowing the easeful state (*phāsubhāvajānanakālo*) in the latter part is like the time of knowing in this very life (*diṭṭheva dhamme*) for the abandoning of unwholesome qualities (*akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya*) and for the attainment of wholesome qualities (*kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya*), so the time of their knowing (*jānanakālo siyā*) is.
Thus here, by one simile, three meanings, by four similes, one meaning is fully illuminated (*paridīpito*).

*Evameva kho*

mula_pali: 4. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, te nigaṇṭhā maṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘nigaṇṭho , āvuso, nāṭaputto nāthaputto (sī.) sabbaññū sabbadassāvī, aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti . Carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti. So evamāha – ‘atthi kho vo, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, pubbeva pāpakammaṃ kataṃ, taṃ imāya kaṭukāya dukkarakārikāya nijjīretha, yaṃ panettha etarahi kāyena saṃvutā vācāya saṃvutā manasā saṃvutā taṃ āyatiṃ pāpakammassa akaraṇaṃ. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca, tena camhā attamanā’’ti.
mula_english:
4. Thus, bhikkhus, said, the Nigaṇṭhas told me: "The Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, claims to be omniscient, all-seeing, to have complete knowledge and vision, ‘Whether I am walking or standing or sleeping or awake, knowledge and vision are continuously and uninterruptedly present to me.’"

He says thus: “Niganthas, you have done evil actions in the past; exhaust them with the performance of piercing austerities. And when you are here and now restrained in body (kāya), speech (vāc), and mind (manas), that is doing no evil actions for the future.

So by annihilating with asceticism past actions and by doing no fresh actions, there will be no consequence in the future. With no consequence in the future, there is the destruction of action (kammakkhayo). With the destruction of action, there is the destruction of suffering (dukkakkhayo). With the destruction of suffering, there is the destruction of feeling (vedanākkhayo). With the destruction of feeling, all suffering (dukkhaṃ) will be exhausted.’

We approve of and accept this, and so we are satisfied."
commentary_pali: 4. Ime pana tato ekampi na jānanti, virajjhitvā gate salle aviddhova ‘‘viddhosi mayā’’ti paccatthikassa vacanappamāṇeneva ‘‘viddhosmī’’ti saññaṃ uppādetvā dukkhappattapuriso viya kevalaṃ mahānigaṇṭhassa vacanappamāṇena sabbametaṃ saddahantā evaṃ sallopamāya bhagavatā niggahitā paccāharituṃ asakkontā yathā nāma dubbalo sunakho migaṃ uṭṭhāpetvā sāmikassa abhimukhaṃ karitvā attanā osakkati, evaṃ mahānigaṇṭhassa matthake vādaṃ pakkhipantā nigaṇṭho, āvusotiādīmāhaṃsu.
commentary_english: And yet, they do not know even one of those things. When the dart has gone, having been cleansed, even though not struck, thinking "I have been struck by you" merely by the word of the opponent, and generating the perception "I am struck," like a man afflicted with suffering, believing all of this merely by the word of the great naked ascetic (mahānigaṇṭha), thus, being unable to refute the simile of the dart rejected by the Blessed One (bhagavatā), just as a weak dog, having roused a deer, makes it face its master and retreats himself, so, casting the argument on the head of the great naked ascetic, they said, "The naked ascetic, friend (āvuso)," and so on.

mula_pali:
5. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhikkhave, te nigaṇṭhe etadavocaṃ – ‘pañca kho ime, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, dhammā diṭṭheva dhamme dvidhāvipākā. Katame pañca? Saddhā, ruci, anussavo, ākāraparivitakko, diṭṭhinijjhānakkhanti – ime kho, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, pañca dhammā diṭṭheva dhamme dvidhāvipākā. Tatrāyasmantānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ kā atītaṃse satthari saddhā, kā ruci, ko anussavo, ko ākāraparivitakko, kā diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantī’ti. Evaṃvādī evaṃvādīsu (ka.) kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhesu na kañci kiñci (sī. pī. ka.) sahadhammikaṃ vādapaṭihāraṃ samanupassāmi.

‘‘Puna caparāhaṃ puna ca panāhaṃ (sī. pī. ka.), bhikkhave, te nigaṇṭhe evaṃ vadāmi – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññatha, āvuso nigaṇṭhā. Yasmiṃ vo samaye tibbo tippo (pī.) upakkamo hoti tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyetha; yasmiṃ pana vo samaye na tibbo upakkamo hoti na tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, na tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyethā’ti? ‘Yasmiṃ no, āvuso gotama, samaye tibbo upakkamo hoti tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyāma; yasmiṃ pana no samaye na tibbo upakkamo hoti na tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, na tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyāmā’’’ti.

puna ca panāhaṃ (sī. pī. ka.) tippo (pī.)
mula_english:
5. “When this was said, I, mendicants, told the Nigaṇṭhas: ‘There are five things, friend Nigaṇṭhas, that may turn out in two different ways here and now.

What are the five? They are: faith (*saddhā*), approval (*ruci*), oral tradition (*anussava*), reasoned cogitation (*ākāraparivitakka*), and reflective acceptance of a view (*diṭṭhinijjhānakkhanti*)—these five things, friend Nigaṇṭhas, may turn out in two different ways here and now.

Herein, what kind of faith do the venerable Nigaṇṭhas have in a teacher who speaks about the past? What kind of approval, what kind of oral tradition, what kind of reasoned cogitation, what kind of reflective acceptance of a view?”

Speaking thus, mendicants, I do not see any coherent refutation based on the *Dharma* among the Nigaṇṭhas.

“Again, in the afternoon, mendicants, I said to the Nigaṇṭhas: ‘What do you think, friend Nigaṇṭhas?

When there is intense exertion (*upakkama*), do you feel painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion; but when there is no intense exertion, do you then not feel any painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion?’” ‘When there is intense exertion, friend Gotama, intense striving, then we feel painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion; but when there is no intense exertion, no intense striving, then we do not feel any painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion.’
commentary_pali: 5. Atha ne bhagavā sācariyake niggaṇhanto pañca kho imetiādimāha. Tatrāyasmantānanti tesu pañcasu dhammesu āyasmantānaṃ. Kā atītaṃse satthari saddhāti atītaṃsavādimhi satthari kā saddhā. Yā atītavādaṃ saddahantānaṃ tumhākaṃ mahānigaṇṭhassa saddhā, sā katamā? Kiṃ bhūtatthā abhūtatthā, bhūtavipākā abhūtavipākāti pucchati. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Sahadhammikanti sahetukaṃ sakāraṇaṃ. Vādapaṭihāranti paccāgamanakavādaṃ. Ettāvatā tesaṃ ‘‘apanetha saddhaṃ, sabbadubbalā esā’’ti saddhāchedakavādaṃ nāma dasseti.
commentary_english:
5. Then, the Blessed One, while rebuking the one with a teacher (sācariyake), said, "These are the five..." etc.

"There, for the venerable ones" (tatrāyasmantānaṃ)—for the venerable ones among those five characteristics (pañcasu dhammesu).

"What faith (saddhā) is in the teacher (satthari) of the past?" (kā atītaṃse satthari saddhā) means: What faith is in the teacher who speaks of the past?

What is that faith (saddhā) of you, the great Nigaṇṭhas, who believe in the doctrine of the past (atītavādaṃ)? What is it? Is it truth (bhūtatthā) or untruth (abhūtatthā), having real results (bhūtavipākā) or unreal results (abhūtavipākā)?—he asks.

The same method (nayo) applies to the remaining clauses (sesapadesupi).

"With a fellow practitioner" (sahadhammika)—means: with a cause (sahetukaṃ), with a reason (sakāraṇaṃ).

"Reply to an argument" (vādapaṭihāra)—means: an argument that involves returning (paccāgamanakavādaṃ).

In so much, he shows their doctrine (vādaṃ) of cutting off faith (saddhāchedaka), [saying]: "Remove faith, it is all weakness!" (apanetha saddhaṃ, sabbadubbalā esā).

mula_pali:
6. ‘‘Iti kira, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, yasmiṃ vo samaye tibbo upakkamo hoti tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyetha; yasmiṃ pana vo samaye na tibbo upakkamo hoti na tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, na tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyetha. Evaṃ sante āyasmantānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ na kallamassa veyyākaraṇāya – yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo ; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatīti. Sace, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, yasmiṃ vo samaye tibbo upakkamo hoti tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, na tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyetha; yasmiṃ pana vo samaye na tibbo upakkamo hoti na tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyetha padhānaṃ, tiṭṭheyyeva tasmiṃ samaye… vedanā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.); evaṃ sante āyasmantānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ kallamassa veyyākaraṇāya – yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’’ti.

‘‘‘Yasmā ca kho, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, yasmiṃ vo samaye tibbo upakkamo hoti tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyetha; yasmiṃ pana vo samaye na tibbo upakkamo hoti na tibbaṃ padhānaṃ, na tibbā tasmiṃ samaye opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyetha; te tumhe sāmaṃyeva opakkamikā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vedayamānā avijjā aññāṇā sammohā vipaccetha – yaṃ kiñcāyaṃ purisapuggalo paṭisaṃvedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ pubbekatahetu. Iti purāṇānaṃ kammānaṃ tapasā byantībhāvā, navānaṃ kammānaṃ akaraṇā, āyatiṃ anavassavo; āyatiṃ anavassavā kammakkhayo; kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo; dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo ; vedanākkhayā sabbaṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evaṃvādīpi evaṃvādīsupi (ka.) kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhesu na kañci sahadhammikaṃ vādapaṭihāraṃ samanupassāmi.

evaṃvādīsupi (ka.)
mula_english:
‘“So it seems, friend Niganthas, that when there is intense exertion, intense striving, you feel painful, racking, piercing feelings (*vedanā*) due to intense exertion; but when there is no intense exertion, no intense striving, you do not feel any painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion. That being so, it is not fitting for the venerable Niganthas to declare: “Whatever this person feels, whether pleasure (*sukha*) or pain (*duḥkha*) or neither-pain-nor-pleasure (*adukkhamasukha*), all that is caused by what was done in the past. So by annihilating with asceticism past actions (*karma*) and by doing no fresh actions, there will be no consequence in the future. With no consequence in the future, there is the destruction of action. With the destruction of action, there is the destruction of suffering. With the destruction of suffering, there is the destruction of feeling; with the destruction of feeling, all suffering will be exhausted.”

‘“If, friend Niganthas, when there was intense exertion, intense striving, then painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion were *not* present, and when there was no intense exertion, no intense striving, then painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion *were* present; that being so, it *would* be fitting for the venerable Niganthas to declare: “Whatever this person feels, whether pleasure or pain or neither-pain-nor-pleasure, all that is caused by what was done in the past. So by annihilating with asceticism past actions and by doing no fresh actions, there will be no consequence in the future. With no consequence in the future, there is the destruction of action. With the destruction of action, there is the destruction of suffering. With the destruction of suffering, there is the destruction of feeling; with the destruction of feeling, all suffering will be exhausted.”’

‘“But since, friend Niganthas, when there is intense exertion, intense striving, then you feel painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion; but when there is no intense exertion, no intense striving, then you do not feel any painful, racking, piercing feelings due to intense exertion, you are therefore feeling only the painful, racking, piercing feelings of your self-imposed exertion, and it is through ignorance (*avidyā*), unknowing (*aññāṇa*), and delusion (*sammoha*) that you mistakenly hold: “Whatever this person feels, whether pleasure or pain or neither-pain-nor-pleasure, all that is caused by what was done in the past. So by annihilating with asceticism past actions (*karma*) and by doing no fresh actions, there will be no consequence in the future. With no consequence in the future, there is the destruction of action. With the destruction of action, there is the destruction of suffering. With the destruction of suffering, there is the destruction of feeling; with the destruction of feeling, all suffering will be exhausted.”’

Speaking thus, bhikkhus, I did not see any legitimate defence of their position by the Niganthas.
commentary_pali: 6.Avijjā aññāṇāti avijjāya aññāṇena. Sammohāti sammohena. Vipaccethāti viparītato saddahatha, vipallāsaggāhaṃ vā gaṇhathāti attho.
commentary_english:
6. *Avijjā aññāṇā* means by ignorance (*avijjāya*) and by lack of knowledge (*aññāṇena*).

*Sammohā* means by delusion (*sammohena*).

*Vipaccethā* means believe perversely (*viparītato saddahatha*), or grasp the perverted (*vipallāsaggāhaṃ gaṇhatha*), is the meaning.

mula_pali: 7. ‘‘Puna caparāhaṃ, bhikkhave, te nigaṇṭhe evaṃ vadāmi – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññathāvuso nigaṇṭhā, yamidaṃ kammaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā samparāyavedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Yaṃ panidaṃ kammaṃ samparāyavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Taṃ kiṃ maññathāvuso nigaṇṭhā, yamidaṃ kammaṃ sukhavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā dukkhavedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Yaṃ panidaṃ kammaṃ dukkhavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā sukhavedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Taṃ kiṃ maññathāvuso nigaṇṭhā, yamidaṃ kammaṃ paripakkavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā aparipakkavedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Yaṃ panidaṃ kammaṃ aparipakkavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā paripakkavedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Taṃ kiṃ maññathāvuso nigaṇṭhā, yamidaṃ kammaṃ bahuvedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā appavedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Yaṃ panidaṃ kammaṃ appavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā bahuvedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Taṃ kiṃ maññathāvuso nigaṇṭhā, yamidaṃ kammaṃ savedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā avedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’. ‘Yaṃ panidaṃ kammaṃ avedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā savedanīyaṃ hotūti labbhameta’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, āvuso’.
mula_english:
7. Again, bhikkhus, I say this to the Nigaṇṭhas: 'What do you think, friends Nigaṇṭhas? Is it possible that an action (karma) whose result is to be experienced here and now (dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ), can, through exertion (upakkama) and striving (pradhānena), become one whose result is to be experienced in the next life (saṃparāyavedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'But is it possible that an action (karma) whose result is to be experienced in the next life (saṃparāyavedanīyaṃ) can, through exertion (upakkama) and striving (pradhānena), become one whose result is to be experienced here and now (dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'What do you think, friends Nigaṇṭhas? Is it possible that an action (karma) whose result is to be experienced as pleasant (sukhavedanīyaṃ) can, through exertion (upakkama) and striving (pradhānena), become one whose result is to be experienced as painful (duḥkhavedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'But is it possible that an action (karma) whose result is to be experienced as painful (duḥkhavedanīyaṃ) can, through exertion (upakkama) and striving (pradhānena), become one whose result is to be experienced as pleasant (sukhavedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'What do you think, friends Nigaṇṭhas? Is it possible that an action (karma) whose result is to be experienced in a matured personality (paripakkavedanīyaṃ) can, by exertion (upakkama) and striving (pradhānena), become one whose result is to be experienced in an unmatured personality (aparipakkavedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'But is it possible that an action (karma) whose result is to be experienced in an unmatured personality (aparipakkavedanīyaṃ) can, by exertion (upakkama) and striving (pradhānena), become one whose result is to be experienced in a matured personality (paripakkavedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'What do you think, friends Nigaṇṭhas? Is it possible that an action (karma) which is much experienced (bahuvedanīyaṃ) can through exertion (upakkama) or effort (pradhānena) become little experienced (appavedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'But is it possible that an action (karma) which is little experienced (appavedanīyaṃ) can through exertion (upakkama) or effort (pradhānena) become much experienced (bahuvedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'What do you think, friends Nigaṇṭhas? Is it possible that an action (karma) whose result is to be experienced (savedanīyaṃ) can, through exertion (upakkama) and striving (pradhānena), become one whose result is not to be experienced (avedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'

'But is it possible that an action (karma) whose result is not to be experienced (avedanīyaṃ) can, through exertion (upakkama) and striving (pradhānena), become one whose result is to be experienced (savedanīyaṃ)?' 'No, friend.'
commentary_pali:
7.Diṭṭhadhammavedanīyanti imasmiṃyeva attabhāve vipākadāyakaṃ. Upakkamenāti payogena. Padhānenāti vīriyena. Samparāyavedanīyanti dutiye vā tatiye vā attabhāve vipākadāyakaṃ. Sukhavedanīyanti iṭṭhārammaṇavipākadāyakaṃ kusalakammaṃ. Viparītaṃ dukkhavedanīyaṃ. Paripakkavedanīyanti paripakke nipphanne attabhāve vedanīyaṃ, diṭṭhadhammavedanīyassevetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Aparipakkavedanīyanti aparipakke attabhāve vedanīyaṃ, samparāyavedanīyassevetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Evaṃ santepi ayamettha viseso – yaṃ paṭhamavaye kataṃ paṭhamavaye vā majjhimavaye vā pacchimavaye vā vipākaṃ deti, majjhimavaye kataṃ majjhimavaye vā pacchimavaye vā vipākaṃ deti, pacchimavaye kataṃ tattheva vipākaṃ deti, taṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ nāma. Yaṃ pana sattadivasabbhantare vipākaṃ deti, taṃ paripakkavedanīyaṃ nāma. Taṃ kusalampi hoti akusalampi.

Tatrimāni vatthūni – puṇṇo nāma kira duggatamanusso rājagahe sumanaseṭṭhiṃ nissāya vasati. Tamenaṃ ekadivasaṃ nagaramhi nakkhatte saṅghuṭṭhe seṭṭhi āha – ‘‘sace ajja kasissasi, dve ca goṇe naṅgalañca labhissasi. Kiṃ nakkhattaṃ kīḷissasi, kasissasī’’ti. Kiṃ me nakkhattena, kasissāmīti? Tena hi ye goṇe icchasi, te gahetvā kasāhīti. So kasituṃ gato. Taṃ divasaṃ sāriputtatthero nirodhā vuṭṭhāya ‘‘kassa saṅgahaṃ karomī’’ti? Āvajjanto puṇṇaṃ disvā pattacīvaraṃ ādāya tassa kasanaṭṭhānaṃ gato. Puṇṇo kasiṃ ṭhapetvā therassa dantakaṭṭhaṃ datvā mukhodakaṃ adāsi. Thero sarīraṃ paṭijaggitvā kammantassa avidūre nisīdi bhattābhihāraṃ olokento. Athassa bhariyaṃ bhattaṃ āharantiṃ disvā antarāmaggeyeva attānaṃ dassesi.

puṇṇo

Sā sāmikassa āhaṭabhattaṃ therassa patte pakkhipitvā puna gantvā aññaṃ bhattaṃ sampādetvā divā agamāsi. Puṇṇo ekavāraṃ kasitvā nisīdi. Sāpi bhattaṃ gahetvā āgacchantī āha – ‘‘sāmi pātova te bhattaṃ āhariyittha, antarāmagge pana sāriputtattheraṃ disvā taṃ tassa datvā aññaṃ pacitvā āharantiyā me ussūro jāto, mā kujjhi sāmī’’ti. Bhaddakaṃ te bhadde kataṃ, mayā therassa pātova dantakaṭṭhañca mukhodakañca dinnaṃ, amhākaṃyevānena piṇḍapātopi paribhutto, ajja therena katasamaṇadhammassa mayaṃ bhāgino jātāti cittaṃ pasādesi. Ekavāraṃ kasitaṭṭhānaṃ suvaṇṇameva ahosi. So bhuñjitvā kasitaṭṭhānaṃ olokento vijjotamānaṃ disvā uṭṭhāya yaṭṭhiyā paharitvā rattasuvaṇṇabhāvaṃ jānitvā ‘‘rañño akathetvā paribhuñjituṃ na sakkā’’ti gantvā rañño ārocesi. Rājā taṃ sabbaṃ sakaṭehi āharāpetvā rājaṅgaṇe rāsiṃ kāretvā ‘‘kassimasmiṃ nagare ettakaṃ suvaṇṇaṃ atthī’’ti pucchi. Kassaci natthīti ca vutte seṭṭhiṭṭhānamassa adāsi. So puṇṇaseṭṭhi nāma jāto.

puṇṇaseṭṭhi

Aparampi vatthu – tasmiṃyeva rājagahe kāḷaveḷiyo nāma duggato atthi. Tassa bhariyā paṇṇambilayāguṃ paci. Mahākassapatthero nirodhā vuṭṭhāya ‘‘kassa saṅgahaṃ karomī’’ti āvajjanto taṃ disvā gantvā gehadvāre aṭṭhāsi. Sā pattaṃ gahetvā sabbaṃ tattha pakkhipitvā therassa adāsi, thero vihāraṃ gantvā satthu upanāmesi. Satthā attano yāpanamattaṃ gaṇhi, sesaṃ pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ pahosi. Kāḷavaḷiyopi taṃ ṭhānaṃ patto cūḷakaṃ labhi. Mahākassapo satthāraṃ kāḷavaḷiyassa vipākaṃ pucchi. Satthā ‘‘ito sattame divase seṭṭhicchattaṃ labhissatī’’ti āha. Kāḷavaḷiyo taṃ kathaṃ sutvā gantvā bhariyāya ārocesi.

kāḷaveḷiyo

Tadā ca rājā nagaraṃ anusañcaranto bahinagare jīvasūle nisinnaṃ purisaṃ addasa. Puriso rājānaṃ disvā uccāsaddaṃ akāsi ‘‘tumhākaṃ me bhuñjanabhattaṃ pahiṇatha devā’’ti. Rājā ‘‘pesessāmī’’ti vatvā sāyamāsabhatte upanīte saritvā ‘‘imaṃ harituṃ samatthaṃ jānāthā’’ti āha, nagare sahassabhaṇḍikaṃ cāresuṃ. Tatiyavāre kāḷavaḷiyassa bhariyā aggahesi . Atha naṃ rañño dassesuṃ, sā purisavesaṃ gahetvā pañcāvudhasannaddhā bhattapātiṃ gahetvā nagarā nikkhami. Bahinagare tāle adhivattho dīghatālo nāma yakkho taṃ rukkhamūlena gacchantiṃ disvā ‘‘tiṭṭha tiṭṭha bhakkhosi me’’ti āha. Nāhaṃ tava bhakkho, rājadūto ahanti. Kattha gacchasīti. Jīvasūle nisinnassa purisassa santikanti. Mamapi ekaṃ sāsanaṃ harituṃ sakkhissasīti. Āma sakkhissāmīti. ‘‘Dīghatālassa bhariyā sumanadevarājadhītā kāḷī puttaṃ vijātā’’ti āroceyyāsi. Imasmiṃ tālamūle satta nidhikumbhiyo atthi, tā tvaṃ gaṇheyyāsīti. Sā ‘‘dīghatālassa bhariyā sumanadevarājadhītā kāḷī puttaṃ vijātā’’ti ugghosentī agamāsi.

dīghatālo

Sumanadevo yakkhasamāgame nisinno sutvā ‘‘eko manusso amhākaṃ piyapavattiṃ āharati, pakkosatha na’’nti sāsanaṃ sutvā pasanno ‘‘imassa rukkhassa parimaṇḍalacchāyāya pharaṇaṭṭhāne nidhikumbhiyo tuyhaṃ dammī’’ti āha. Jīvasūle nisinnapuriso bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā mukhapuñchanakāle itthiphassoti ñatvā cūḷāya ḍaṃsi, sā asinā attano cūḷaṃ chinditvā rañño santikaṃyeva gatā. Rājā bhattabhojitabhāvo kathaṃ jānitabboti? Cūḷasaññāyāti vatvā rañño ācikkhitvā taṃ dhanaṃ āharāpesi. Rājā aññassa ettakaṃ dhanaṃ nāma atthīti. Natthi devāti. Rājā tassā patiṃ tasmiṃ nagare dhanaseṭṭhiṃ akāsi. Mallikāyapi deviyā vatthu kathetabbaṃ. Imāni tāva kusalakamme vatthūni.

Mallikāyapi kusalakamme vatthūni

Nandamāṇavako pana uppalavaṇṇāya theriyā vippaṭipajji, tassa mañcato uṭṭhāya nikkhamitvā gacchantassa mahāpathavī bhijjitvā okāsamadāsi, tattheva mahānarakaṃ paviṭṭho. Nandopi goghātako paṇṇāsa vassāni goghātakakammaṃ katvā ekadivasaṃ bhojanakāle maṃsaṃ alabhanto ekassa jīvamānakagoṇassa jivhaṃ chinditvā aṅgāresu pacāpetvā khādituṃ āraddho. Athassa jivhā mūle chijjitvā bhattapātiyaṃyeva patitā, so viravanto kālaṃ katvā niraye nibbatti. Nandopi yakkho aññena yakkhena saddhiṃ ākāsena gacchanto sāriputtattheraṃ navoropitehi kesehi rattibhāge abbhokāse nisinnaṃ disvā sīse paharitukāmo itarassa yakkhassa ārocetvā tena vāriyamānopi pahāraṃ datvā ḍayhāmi ḍayhāmīti viravanto tasmiṃyeva ṭhāne bhūmiṃ pavisitvā mahāniraye nibbattoti imāni akusalakamme vatthūni.

Nandamāṇavako Nando Nandopi yakkho akusalakamme vatthūni

Yaṃ pana antamaso maraṇasantikepi kataṃ kammaṃ bhavantare vipākaṃ deti, taṃ sabbaṃ samparāyavedanīyaṃ nāma. Tattha yo aparihīnassa jhānassa vipāko nibbattissati, so idha nibbattitavipākoti vutto. Tassa mūlabhūtaṃ kammaṃ neva diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ na samparāyavedanīyanti, na vicāritaṃ, kiñcāpi na vicāritaṃ, samparāyavedanīyameva panetanti veditabbaṃ. Yo paṭhamamaggādīnaṃ bhavantare phalasamāpattivipāko, so idha nibbattitaguṇotveva vutto. Kiñcāpi evaṃ vutto, maggakammaṃ pana paripakkavedanīyanti veditabbaṃ. Maggacetanāyeva hi sabbalahuṃ phaladāyikā anantaraphalattāti.

samparāyavedanīyaṃ paripakkavedanīya
commentary_english:
7. *Diṭṭhadhammavedanīya* means yielding its result in this very existence. *Upakkamenā* means by effort. *Padhānenā* means by energy (vīriyena). *Samparāyavedanīya* means yielding its result in the second or third existence. *Sukhavedanīya* means wholesome karma (kusalakammaṃ) that yields a desirable object. The opposite is *dukkhavedanīya*. *Paripakkavedanīya* means experienceable in a fully ripened, accomplished existence; this is another term for *diṭṭhadhammavedanīya*. *Aparipakkavedanīya* means experienceable in an unripened existence; this is another term for *samparāyavedanīya*. Even so, this is the distinction here: that which is done in the first stage of life yields its result in the first, middle, or last stage of life; that which is done in the middle stage of life yields its result in the middle or last stage of life; that which is done in the last stage of life yields its result right there; this is called *diṭṭhadhammavedanīya*. Moreover, that which yields its result within seven days is called *paripakkavedanīya*. That can be either wholesome or unwholesome. The following are stories about this: They say that in Rājagaha there lived a poor man named *Puṇṇa*, dependent on the treasurer Sumana. One day, when the festival was proclaimed in the city, the treasurer said to him, "If you plough today, you will get two oxen and a plough. Why celebrate the festival; will you plough?" What is the festival to me, I will plough? Then take whichever oxen you want and plough! So he went to plough. That day, the Elder Sāriputta, having risen from cessation, considered, "Whom shall I help?" Seeing Puṇṇa, he took his bowl and robe and went to his ploughing place. Puṇṇa stopped ploughing, gave the Elder a toothbrush and provided water for washing his face . The Elder refreshed himself and sat down not far from the work site looking for an offering of food. Then, seeing his wife bringing food, he showed himself right there on the road. *Puṇṇa* She placed the food brought for her husband into the Elder's bowl, went back again, prepared other food and came during the day. Puṇṇa ploughed once and sat down. She too, arriving with the food, said, "Husband, I brought food for you early in the morning, but on the road seeing the Elder Sāriputta, I gave it to him and, cooking other food, I feel remorseful; don't be angry, husband." Good, good was done by you, my dear, I gave the Elder a toothbrush and water for washing his face early in the morning; the almsfood was also enjoyed by him for our sake; today we have become partakers in the ascetic practice done by the Elder, thus he gladdened his heart. The place that was ploughed once became gold. Having eaten and looking at the ploughed place, seeing it shining, he got up, struck it with a stick, recognised its state of being red gold, [thinking] "It is not possible to enjoy [this] without telling the king," he went and announced it to the king. The king had all of that brought in carts, piled it up in the royal courtyard, and asked, "Is there this much gold in this city for anyone?" When it was said that there was none for anyone, he gave him the place of a treasurer. So *Puṇṇaseṭṭhi* (Puṇṇa the Treasurer) was born. *Puṇṇaseṭṭhi* Another story: In that same Rājagaha there was a poor man named *Kāḷaveḷiyo*. His wife was cooking gruel made with decayed leaves. The Elder Mahākassapa, having risen from cessation, considering "Whom shall I help?" seeing him, went and stood at the door of his house. She took the bowl, put everything into it, and gave it to the elder. The elder went to the monastery and presented it to the Teacher (Buddha). The Teacher took only what was necessary for his sustenance, and the rest was enough for five hundred monks. Kāḷavaḷiya also obtained that place and received the tonsure. Mahākassapa asked the Teacher about the result of Kāḷavaḷiya's actions. The Teacher said, "From this day, on the seventh day, he will receive the umbrella of a wealthy man." Kāḷavaḷiya, having heard that speech, went and announced it to his wife.

Kāḷaveḷiyo Then, the king, while wandering in the city, saw a man sitting impaled outside the city. The man, having seen the king, made a loud noise, "Send food for me, O gods!" The king, saying "I will send it," and when the evening meal was brought, remembering, said, "Do you know anyone capable of taking this away?" They sent out a herald in the city, offering a thousand. On the third try, Kāḷavaḷiya's wife took it. Then they showed her to the king. She, having taken the guise of a man, fully armed with the five weapons, and having taken a bowl of food, went out of the city. Outside the city, in a palm tree, lived a Yaksha named Dīghatālo, having seen her going by the base of the tree, said, "Stop! Stop! You are food for me!" "I am not your food; I am a royal messenger," she said. "Where are you going?" "To the presence of the man sitting impaled." "Are you able to take even one message for me?" "Yes, I am able." "Announce, 'Dīghatāla's wife, Sumanadevarāja's daughter, Kāḷī, has given birth to a son.'" "In this palm tree's base, there are seven treasure pots. You may take them." She, shouting, "Dīghatāla's wife, Sumanadevarāja's daughter, Kāḷī, has given birth to a son!" went on.

Dīghatālo Sumanadeva, sitting in the Yaksha assembly, having heard, "A certain man is bringing a dear message to us, call him!" Having heard the message, pleased, said, "In the place of protection in the perfectly round shade of this tree, I will give the treasure pots to you." The man sitting on the stake, having enjoyed the food, knowing it was a woman's touch at the time of wiping his mouth, bit her hair. She, having cut off her hair with a sword, went to the king's presence. The king asked, "How is the state of having eaten the food to be known?" "By the sign of the hair," she said. Having told the king, he had that wealth brought. The king said, "Does another have so much wealth?" "No, O god!" The king made her husband a wealthy merchant in that city. Mallikāyapi's story should be told. These are instances of meritorious deeds.

Mallikāyapi's instances of meritorious deeds Nandamāṇavako, however, acted improperly toward the elder Uppalavaṇṇā. As he was getting up from the bed and going out, the great earth split open, giving him an opening, and he entered the great hell right there. Nando also, a butcher of cows, having done the work of butchering cows for fifty years, one day, not getting meat at mealtime, having cut off the tongue of a living cow, and having had it cooked in embers, began to eat it. Then his tongue, having been cut off at the root, fell right into the food bowl. He, crying out, having done his time, was reborn in hell. Nando, the Yaksha, by another Yaksha These are instances of unwholesome actions (*akuśalakamme vatthūni*). ...going with the sky, having seen venerable Śāriputta seated in the open air in the night, with freshly shaved hair, wanting to strike (him) on the head, having announced (this) to another *yakṣa*, even while being prevented by him, having delivered a blow, crying out "I burn, I burn!", having entered the earth in that very place, was reborn in the great hell. Nanda the young man, Nanda, Nanda also the *yakṣa*. These are instances of unwholesome actions (*akuśalakamme vatthūni*). Moreover, even the least deed done at the moment of death gives its result (*vipāka*) in another existence; all that is to be experienced in a future existence (*samparāyavedanīyaṃ*). ...by name. There, whatever result (*vipāka*) of the undiminished *jhāna* will arise, that is called a result that has arisen here. The deed that is its root is neither to be experienced in this very life (*diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ*) nor to be experienced in a future existence (*samparāyavedanīyaṃ*); it is not considered. Although it is not considered, it should be understood that it is precisely what is to be experienced in a future existence (*samparāyavedanīyameva panetanti veditabbaṃ*). Whatever is the result (*phalasamāpattivipāko*) of the fruition attainment of the first path and so on, in another existence, that is called a quality that has arisen here. Although it was said thus, it should be understood that the deed of the path (*maggakammaṃ*) is to be experienced when it is ripe (*paripakkavedanīya*). For the consciousness of the path (*maggacetanā*) alone is the giver of all that is swift, because it has immediate fruit. To be experienced in a future existence (*samparāyavedanīyaṃ*). To be experienced when ripe (*paripakkavedanīya*).

mula_pali:
8. ‘‘Iti kira, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, yamidaṃ kammaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā samparāyavedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yaṃ panidaṃ kammaṃ samparāyavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yamidaṃ kammaṃ sukhavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā dukkhavedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yamidaṃ kammaṃ dukkhavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā sukhavedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yamidaṃ kammaṃ paripakkavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā aparipakkavedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yamidaṃ kammaṃ aparipakkavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā paripakkavedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yamidaṃ kammaṃ bahuvedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā appavedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yamidaṃ kammaṃ appavedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā bahuvedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yamidaṃ kammaṃ savedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā avedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ, yamidaṃ kammaṃ avedanīyaṃ taṃ upakkamena vā padhānena vā savedanīyaṃ hotūti alabbhametaṃ; evaṃ sante āyasmantānaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ aphalo upakkamo hoti, aphalaṃ padhānaṃ’’.

‘‘Evaṃvādī, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā. Evaṃvādīnaṃ, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhānaṃ dasa sahadhammikā vādānuvādā gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchanti.
mula_english:
“So it seems, friend Niganthas, that it is impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced here and now (*dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced in the next life (*samparāyavedanīyaṃ*), and impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced in the next life (*samparāyavedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced here and now (*dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ*); impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced as pleasant (*sukhavedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced as painful (*duḥkhavedanīyaṃ*); impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced as painful (*duḥkhavedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced as pleasant (*sukhavedanīyaṃ*); impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced as ripe (*paripakkavedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced as unripe (*aparipakkavedanīyaṃ*); impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced as unripe (*aparipakkavedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced as ripe (*paripakkavedanīyaṃ*); impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced as much (*bahuvedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced as little (*appavedanīyaṃ*); impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced as little (*appavedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced as much (*bahuvedanīyaṃ*); impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is to be experienced (*savedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is not to be experienced (*avedanīyaṃ*); impossible that an action (*karma*) whose result is not to be experienced (*avedanīyaṃ*) can, through exertion (*upakkama*) and striving (*padhāna*), become one whose result is to be experienced (*savedanīyaṃ*). Thus being the case, the exertion (*upakkama*) of you venerable Niganthas is fruitless (*aphalaṃ*), your striving (*padhānaṃ*) is fruitless.”

“Monks, the Niganthas speak thus. Because the Niganthas speak thus, there are ten legitimate deductions (*sahadhammikā vādānuvādā*) from their assertions that provide ground for censuring (*gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchanti*) them."
commentary_pali: 8.Bahuvedanīyanti saññābhavūpagaṃ. Appavedanīyanti asaññābhavūpagaṃ. Savedanīyanti savipākaṃ kammaṃ. Avedanīyanti avipākaṃ kammaṃ. Evaṃ santeti imesaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyādīnaṃ kammānaṃ upakkamena samparāyavedanīyādi bhāvakāraṇassa alābhe sati. Aphaloti nipphalo niratthakoti. Ettāvatā aniyyānikasāsane payogassa aphalataṃ dassetvā padhānacchedakavādo nāma dassitoti veditabbo. Sahadhammikā vādānuvādāti parehi vuttakāraṇena sakāraṇā hutvā nigaṇṭhānaṃ vādā ca anuvādā ca. Gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchantīti viññūhi garahitabbaṃ kāraṇaṃ āgacchanti. ‘‘Vādānuppattā gārayhaṭṭhānā’’tipi pāṭho. Tassattho – parehi vuttena kāraṇena sakāraṇā nigaṇṭhānaṃ vādaṃ anuppattā taṃ vādaṃ sosentā milāpentā dukkaṭakammakārinotiādayo dasa gārayhaṭṭhānā āgacchanti.
commentary_english:
8. *bahuvedanīya* means associated with the realm of perception.

*appavedanīya* means associated with the realm of non-perception.

*savedanīya* means karma with results.

*avedanīya* means karma without results.

*evaṃ sante* means when, due to the lack of a cause for future becoming, such as the arising of karma that matures in this very life, and so on.

*aphala* means fruitless, pointless.

Thus, by showing the fruitlessness of effort in a teaching that does not lead out [of saṃsāra], it should be understood that what is called the doctrine of severing effort has been taught.

*sahadhammikā vādānuvādā* means arguments and counter-arguments that are reasoned, having a cause because of a cause spoken by others, are the arguments and counter-arguments of the *nigaṇṭhas*.

*gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchantī* means causes that are blameworthy by the wise come about.

There is also the reading “*vādānuppattā gārayhaṭṭhānā*”.

Its meaning is: causes that are reasoned, having a cause because of what is spoken by others, approaching the arguments of the *nigaṇṭhas*, drying up that argument, making it wither, the ten blameworthy causes, beginning with those who do bad deeds, come about.

mula_pali:
9. ‘‘Sace, bhikkhave, sattā pubbekatahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti; addhā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā pubbe dukkaṭakammakārino yaṃ etarahi evarūpā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyanti. Sace, bhikkhave, sattā issaranimmānahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti; addhā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā pāpakena issarena nimmitā yaṃ etarahi evarūpā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyanti. Sace, bhikkhave, sattā saṅgatibhāvahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti; addhā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā pāpasaṅgatikā yaṃ etarahi evarūpā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyanti. Sace, bhikkhave, sattā abhijātihetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti; addhā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā pāpābhijātikā yaṃ etarahi evarūpā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyanti. Sace, bhikkhave, sattā diṭṭhadhammūpakkamahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti; addhā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā evarūpā diṭṭhadhammūpakkamā yaṃ etarahi evarūpā dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vediyanti.

‘‘Sace, bhikkhave, sattā pubbekatahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā; no ce sattā pubbekatahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā. Sace, bhikkhave, sattā issaranimmānahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā; no ce sattā issaranimmānahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā. Sace, bhikkhave, sattā saṅgatibhāvahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā; no ce sattā saṅgatibhāvahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā. Sace, bhikkhave, sattā abhijātihetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā; no ce sattā abhijātihetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā. Sace, bhikkhave, sattā diṭṭhadhammūpakkamahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā; no ce sattā diṭṭhadhammūpakkamahetu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedenti, gārayhā nigaṇṭhā. Evaṃvādī, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā. Evaṃvādīnaṃ, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhānaṃ ime dasa sahadhammikā vādānuvādā gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchanti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, aphalo upakkamo hoti, aphalaṃ padhānaṃ.
mula_english:
“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by what was done in the past, then the Niganthas surely must have done bad deeds in the past, since they now feel such painful, racking, piercing feelings.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by the creative act of a Supreme God, then the Niganthas surely must have been created by an evil Supreme God, since they now feel such painful, racking, piercing feelings.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by circumstance and nature, then the Niganthas surely must have bad luck, since they now feel such painful, racking, piercing feelings.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by class among the six classes of birth, then the Niganthas surely must belong to a bad class, since they now feel such painful, racking, piercing feelings.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by exertion here and now, then the Niganthas surely must strive badly here and now, since they now feel such painful, racking, piercing feelings.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by what was done in the past, then the Niganthas are to be censured; if not, then the Niganthas are still to be censured.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by the creative act of a Supreme God, then the Niganthas are to be censured; if not, they are still to be censured.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by chance, then the Niganthas are to be censured; if not, they are still to be censured.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by class, then the Niganthas are to be censured; if not, they are still to be censured.

“If the pleasure and pain that beings feel are caused by exertion here and now, then the Niganthas are to be censured; if not, they are still to be censured.

“So speak the Niganthas, bhikkhus.

And because the Niganthas speak thus, these ten legitimate deductions from their assertions provide grounds for censuring them.

Thus their exertion is fruitless, their striving is fruitless.
commentary_pali: 9.Saṅgatibhāvahetūti niyatibhāvakāraṇā. Pāpasaṅgatikāti pāpaniyatino. Abhijātihetūti chaḷabhijātihetu.
commentary_english: 9. saṅgatibhāvahetūti means the causes of the nature of association, and niyatibhāvakāraṇā means the causes of the nature of restriction. pāpasaṅgatikāti means those associated with evil, and pāpaniyatino means those restricted by evil. abhijātihetūti means the causes of noble birth, and chaḷabhijātihetu means the six causes of noble birth.

mula_pali: 10. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, saphalo upakkamo hoti, saphalaṃ padhānaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na heva anaddhabhūtaṃ attānaṃ dukkhena addhabhāveti, dhammikañca sukhaṃ na pariccajati, tasmiñca sukhe anadhimucchito hoti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘imassa kho me dukkhanidānassa saṅkhāraṃ padahato saṅkhārappadhānā virāgo hoti, imassa pana me dukkhanidānassa ajjhupekkhato upekkhaṃ bhāvayato virāgo hotī’ti. So yassa hi khvāssa yassa kho panassa (sī.), yassa khvāssa (pī.) dukkhanidānassa saṅkhāraṃ padahato saṅkhārappadhānā virāgo hoti, saṅkhāraṃ tattha padahati. Yassa panassa dukkhanidānassa ajjhupekkhato upekkhaṃ bhāvayato virāgo hoti, upekkhaṃ tattha bhāveti. Tassa tassa dukkhanidānassa saṅkhāraṃ padahato saṅkhārappadhānā virāgo hoti – evampissa taṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ hoti. Tassa tassa dukkhanidānassa ajjhupekkhato upekkhaṃ bhāvayato virāgo hoti – evampissa taṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ hoti.
mula_english:
10. Bhikkhus, how is striving fruitful, and effort successful? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not overwhelmed by suffering and does not overwhelm himself with suffering; and he does not give up the pleasure that accords with the Dhamma, yet he is not infatuated with that pleasure.

He knows thus: ‘When I strive with determination (*saṅkhāra*) this particular source of suffering (*dukkhanidāna*) fades away in me because of that determined striving (*saṅkhārappadhānā*); and when I look on with equanimity (*upekkhā*), this particular source of suffering (*dukkhanidāna*) fades away in me while I develop equanimity (*upekkhā*)’

He strives with determination (*saṅkhāra*) in regard to that particular source of suffering (*dukkhanidāna*) which fades away in him because of that determined striving (*saṅkhārappadhānā*); he strives with determination (*saṅkhāra*) in that regard.

And he develops equanimity (*upekkhā*) in regard to that particular source of suffering (*dukkhanidāna*) which fades away in him while he is developing equanimity (*upekkhā*); he develops equanimity (*upekkhā*) in that regard.

When he strives with determination (*saṅkhāra*), such and such a source of suffering (*dukkhanidāna*) fades away in him because of that determined striving (*saṅkhārappadhānā*); thus that suffering (*dukkha*) is exhausted in him.

When he looks on with equanimity (*upekkhā*), such and such a source of suffering (*dukkhanidāna*) fades away in him while he develops equanimity (*upekkhā*); thus that suffering (*dukkha*) is exhausted in him.
commentary_pali:
10. Evaṃ nigaṇṭhānaṃ upakkamassa aphalataṃ dassetvā idāni niyyānikasāsane upakkamassa vīriyassa ca saphalataṃ dassetuṃ kathañca, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha anaddhabhūtanti anadhibhūtaṃ. Dukkhena anadhibhūto nāma manussattabhāvo vuccati, na taṃ addhabhāveti nābhibhavatīti attho. Tampi nānappakārāya dukkarakārikāya payojento dukkhena addhabhāveti nāma. Ye pana sāsane pabbajitvā āraññakā vā honti rukkhamūlikādayo vā, te dukkhena na addhabhāventi nāma. Niyyānikasāsanasmiñhi vīriyaṃ sammāvāyāmo nāma hoti.

Thero panāha – yo issarakule nibbatto sattavassiko hutvā alaṅkatappaṭiyatto pituaṅke nisinno ghare bhattakiccaṃ katvā nisinnena bhikkhusaṅghena anumodanāya kariyamānāya tisso sampattiyo dassetvā saccesu pakāsitesu arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, mātāpitūhi vā ‘‘pabbajissasi tātā’’ti vutto ‘‘āma pabbajissāmī’’ti vatvā nhāpetvā alaṅkaritvā vihāraṃ nīto tacapañcakaṃ uggaṇhitvā nisinno kesesu ohāriyamānesu khuraggeyeva arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, navapabbajito vā pana manosilātelamakkhitena sīsena punadivase mātāpitūhi pesitaṃ kājabhattaṃ bhuñjitvā vihāre nisinnova arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayaṃ na dukkhena attānaṃ addhabhāveti nāma. Ayaṃ pana ukkaṭṭhasakkāro. Yo dāsikucchiyaṃ nibbatto antamaso rajatamuddikampi piḷandhitvā gorakapiyaṅgumattenāpi sarīraṃ vilimpetvā ‘‘pabbājetha na’’nti nīto khuragge vā punadivase vā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, ayampi na anaddhabhūtaṃ attānaṃ dukkhena addhabhāveti nāma.

Dhammikaṃ sukhaṃ nāma saṅghato vā gaṇato vā uppannaṃ catupaccayasukhaṃ. Anadhimucchitoti taṇhāmucchanāya amucchito. Dhammikañhi sukhaṃ na pariccajāmīti na tattha gedho kātabbo. Saṅghato hi uppannaṃ salākabhattaṃ vā vassāvāsikaṃ vā ‘‘idamatthaṃ eta’’nti paricchinditvā saṅghamajjhe bhikkhūnaṃ antare paribhuñjanto pattantare padumaṃ viya sīlasamādhivipassanāmaggaphalehi vaḍḍhati. Imassāti paccuppannānaṃ pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ mūlabhūtassa. Dukkhanidānassāti taṇhāya. Sā hi pañcakkhandhadukkhassa nidānaṃ. Saṅkhāraṃ padahatoti sampayogavīriyaṃ karontassa. Virāgohotīti maggena virāgo hoti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘saṅkhārapadhānena me imassa dukkhanidānassa virāgo hotī’’ti evaṃ pajānātīti iminā sukhāpaṭipadā khippābhiññā kathitā. Dutiyavārena tassa sampayogavīriyassa majjhattatākāro kathito. So yassa hi khvāssāti ettha ayaṃ saṅkhepattho – so puggalo yassa dukkhanidānassa saṅkhārapadhānena virāgo hoti, saṅkhāraṃ tattha padahati, maggapadhānena padahati. Yassa pana dukkhanidānassa ajjhupekkhato upekkhaṃ bhāventassa virāgo hoti, upekkhaṃ tattha bhāveti, maggabhāvanāya bhāveti. Tassāti tassa puggalassa.

Dhammikaṃ sukhaṃ Anadhimucchito Imassā Dukkhanidānassā Saṅkhāraṃ padahato Virāgo hotī evaṃ pajānātī So yassa hi khvāssā Tassā
commentary_english:
10. Having shown the fruitlessness of the efforts of the Nigaṇṭhas, now, in order to show the fruitfulness of effort and energy in the teaching that leads out [of suffering], he says, "And how, monks," etc.

There, "anaddhabhūta" means anadhibhūtaṃ. The state of being a human being is said to be "anadhibhūta" by suffering; that is, he does not overcome or dominate it by suffering. But while employing even that in various kinds of difficult practices, he overcomes it by suffering. Those, however, who have gone forth in the Dispensation, whether they are forest-dwellers or those who live at the foot of a tree, do not overcome it by suffering. For in the teaching that leads out [of suffering], energy is called right effort (sammāvāyāmo).

The Elder, however, said: "A person born in a wealthy family, becoming seven years old, being adorned and prepared, sitting on his father's lap, attaining arahantship when the truth is revealed after the meal is finished in the house and the Saṅgha of monks is performing the anumodana; or, when his parents say, 'Go forth, dear one,' and he says, 'Yes, I will go forth,' being bathed and adorned, being taken to the monastery, having learned the five skins, sitting down and attaining arahantship at the very tip of the razor when his hairs are being removed; or again, a newly ordained monk, having eaten the kājabhattaṃ sent by his parents on the following day with his head anointed with manosilā oil, attaining arahantship while sitting in the monastery: this one does not overcome himself with suffering."

This is an excessive honor.

But the one born in a slave's womb, even wearing a silver ring, anointing his body with gorakapiyaṅgu-sized pieces, being brought and [told] "Let him go forth," attaining arahantship at the tip of the razor or on the following day, this one also does not overcome himself, who is not already overcome, with suffering.

"Dhammikaṃ sukhaṃ" means the four-necessity happiness that arises from the Saṅgha or a group. "Anadhimucchito" means not infatuated by craving-infatuation. For one should not be greedy there, [thinking,] "I will not abandon justifiable happiness." For a salākabhattaṃ or vassāvāsikaṃ that arises from the Saṅgha, after determining, "This is for that purpose," while partaking of it among the monks in the midst of the Saṅgha, he grows with sīla, samādhi, vipassanā, magga, and phala, like a lotus in a bowl. "Imassā" [means] of this, the root of the five aggregates of the present. "Dukkhanidānassā" [means] of craving (taṇhā). For that is the cause of the suffering of the five aggregates. "Saṅkhāraṃ padahato" [means] of one who is making effort of application. "Virāgo hotī" means virāga arises through the path. This has been said: "Through the exertion of effort, virāga arises for me from this cause of suffering." "Evaṃ pajānātīti" [means] in this way, the sukha-paṭipadā khippābhiññā has been spoken of. In the second statement, the middleness of that effort of application has been spoken of. "So yassa hi khvāssā" Here, this is the condensed meaning: That person for whom virāga arises from the cause of suffering through the exertion of effort, he exerts effort there, he exerts effort through the path-exertion. But for whomever virāga arises from the cause of suffering through overlooking while developing equanimity, he develops equanimity there, he develops it through the development of the path. "Tassā" [means] of that person.

"Dhammikaṃ sukhaṃ anadhimucchito imassā dukkhanidānassā saṅkhāraṃ padahato virāgo hotī evaṃ pajānātī so yassa hi khvāssā tassā"

mula_pali:
11. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso itthiyā sāratto paṭibaddhacitto tibbacchando tibbāpekkho. So taṃ itthiṃ passeyya aññena purisena saddhiṃ santiṭṭhantiṃ sallapantiṃ sañjagghantiṃ saṃhasantiṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu tassa purisassa amuṃ itthiṃ disvā aññena purisena saddhiṃ santiṭṭhantiṃ sallapantiṃ sañjagghantiṃ saṃhasantiṃ uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassūpāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Amu hi, bhante, puriso amussā itthiyā sāratto paṭibaddhacitto tibbacchando tibbāpekkho . Tasmā taṃ itthiṃ disvā aññena purisena saddhiṃ santiṭṭhantiṃ sallapantiṃ sañjagghantiṃ saṃhasantiṃ uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassūpāyāsā’’ti. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, tassa purisassa evamassa – ‘ahaṃ kho amussā itthiyā sāratto paṭibaddhacitto tibbacchando tibbāpekkho. Tassa me amuṃ itthiṃ disvā aññena purisena saddhiṃ santiṭṭhantiṃ sallapantiṃ sañjagghantiṃ saṃhasantiṃ uppajjanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassūpāyāsā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yo me amussā itthiyā chandarāgo taṃ pajaheyya’nti. So yo amussā itthiyā chandarāgo taṃ pajaheyya. So taṃ itthiṃ passeyya aparena samayena aññena purisena saddhiṃ santiṭṭhantiṃ sallapantiṃ sañjagghantiṃ saṃhasantiṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu tassa purisassa amuṃ itthiṃ disvā aññena purisena saddhiṃ santiṭṭhantiṃ sallapantiṃ sañjagghantiṃ saṃhasantiṃ uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassūpāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Amu hi, bhante, puriso amussā itthiyā virāgo. Tasmā taṃ itthiṃ disvā aññena purisena saddhiṃ santiṭṭhantiṃ sallapantiṃ sañjagghantiṃ saṃhasantiṃ na uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassūpāyāsā’’ti.

‘‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na heva anaddhabhūtaṃ attānaṃ dukkhena addhabhāveti, dhammikañca sukhaṃ na pariccajati, tasmiñca sukhe anadhimucchito hoti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘imassa kho me dukkhanidānassa saṅkhāraṃ padahato saṅkhārappadhānā virāgo hoti, imassa pana me dukkhanidānassa ajjhupekkhato upekkhaṃ bhāvayato virāgo hotī’ti. So yassa hi khvāssa dukkhanidānassa saṅkhāraṃ padahato saṅkhārappadhānā virāgo hoti, saṅkhāraṃ tattha padahati; yassa panassa dukkhanidānassa ajjhupekkhato upekkhaṃ bhāvayato virāgo hoti, upekkhaṃ tattha bhāveti. Tassa tassa dukkhanidānassa saṅkhāraṃ padahato saṅkhārappadhānā virāgo hoti – evampissa taṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ hoti . Tassa tassa dukkhanidānassa ajjhupekkhato upekkhaṃ bhāvayato virāgo hoti – evampissa taṃ dukkhaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ hoti. Evampi, bhikkhave, saphalo upakkamo hoti, saphalaṃ padhānaṃ.
mula_english:
11. “Suppose, *bhikkhus*, a man loved a woman with his mind bound to her by intense desire and passion. He might see that woman standing with another man, chatting, joking, and laughing. What do you think, *bhikkhus*? Would not sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise in that man when he sees that woman standing with another man, chatting, joking, and laughing?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Why is that?” “Because that man loves that woman with his mind bound to her by intense desire and passion. Therefore, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair would arise in him when he sees that woman standing with another man, chatting, joking, and laughing.” “Then, *bhikkhus*, the man might think: ‘I love this woman with my mind bound to her by intense desire and passion. Thus sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise in me when I see her standing with another man, chatting, joking, and laughing. What if I were to abandon my desire and lust for that woman?’ He would abandon his desire and lust for that woman. On a later occasion he might see that woman standing with another man, chatting, joking, and laughing. What do you think, *bhikkhus*? Would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise in that man when he sees that woman standing with another man, chatting, joking, and laughing?” “No, venerable sir.” “Why is that?” “Because that man no longer loves that woman. that is why sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair do not arise in him when he sees that woman standing with another man…”

“So too, *bhikkhus*, when a *bhikkhu* is not overwhelmed by suffering *duḥkha* and does not overwhelm himself with suffering; and he does not give up the pleasure that accords with Dhamma, yet he is not infatuated with that pleasure. He knows thus: ‘When I strive with determination, this particular source of suffering *duḥkha-nidānassa* fades away in me because of that determined striving; and when I look on with equanimity, this particular source of suffering fades away in me while I develop equanimity (*upekkhā*)’ He strives with determination in regard to that particular source of suffering which fades away in him because of that determined striving; When he looks oh with equanimity, such and such a source of suffering fades away in him while he develops equanimity; thus that suffering is exhausted in him. Thus, *bhikkhus*, the exertion is fruitful, the striving is fruitful.
commentary_pali:
11.Paṭibaddhacittoti chandarāgena baddhacitto. Tibbacchandoti bahalacchando. Tibbāpekkhoti bahalapatthano. Santiṭṭhantinti ekato tiṭṭhantiṃ. Sañjagghantinti mahāhasitaṃ hasamānaṃ. Saṃhasantinti sitaṃ kurumānaṃ.

Evameva kho, bhikkhaveti ettha idaṃ opammavibhāvanaṃ – eko hi puriso ekissā itthiyā sāratto ghāsacchādanamālālaṅkārādīni datvā ghare vāseti. Sā taṃ aticaritvā aññaṃ sevati. So ‘‘nūna ahaṃ assā anurūpaṃ sakkāraṃ na karomī’’ti sakkāraṃ vaḍḍhesi. Sā bhiyyosomattāya aticaratiyeva. So – ‘‘ayaṃ sakkariyamānāpi aticarateva, ghare me vasamānā anatthampi kareyya, nīharāmi na’’nti parisamajjhe alaṃvacanīyaṃ katvā ‘‘mā puna gehaṃ pāvisī’’ti vissajjesi.
