commentary_pali: 25.Tatrāti sattasu ucchedavādesu bhummaṃ. Uddhaṃ saranti uddhaṃ vuccati anāgatasaṃsāravādo, anāgataṃ saṃsāravādaṃ sarantīti attho. Āsattiṃyeva abhivadanti lagganakaṃyeva vadanti. ‘‘Āsatta’’ntipi pāṭho, taṇhaṃyeva vadantīti attho. Iti pecca bhavissāmāti evaṃ pecca bhavissāma. Khattiyā bhavissāma, brāhmaṇā bhavissāmāti evamettha nayo netabbo. Vāṇijūpamāmaññeti vāṇijūpamā viya vāṇijapaṭibhāgā vāṇijasadisā mayhaṃ upaṭṭhahanti. Sakkāyabhayāti sakkāyassa bhayā. Te hi yatheva ‘‘cattāro kho, mahārāja, abhayassa bhāyanti. Katame cattāro? Gaṇḍuppādo kho, mahārāja, bhayā pathaviṃ na khādati ‘mā pathavī khiyī’ti, konto kho, mahārāja, ekapādena tiṭṭhati ‘mā pathavī osīdī’ti, kikī kho, mahārāja, uttānā seti ‘mā ambhā undriyī’ti, brāhmaṇadhammiko kho, mahārāja, brahmacariyaṃ na carati ‘mā loko ucchijjī’ti ime cattāro abhayassa bhāyanti, evaṃ sakkāyassa bhāyanti’’. Sakkāyaparijegucchāti tameva tebhūmakasaṅkhātaṃ sakkāyaṃ parijigucchamānā. Sā gaddulabaddhoti daṇḍake rajjuṃ pavesetvā baddhasunakho. Evamevimeti ettha daḷhatthambho viya khīlo viya ca tebhūmakadhammasaṅkhāto sakkāyo daṭṭhabbo, sā viya diṭṭhigatiko, daṇḍako viya diṭṭhi, rajju viya taṇhā, gaddulena bandhitvā thambhe vā khīle vā upanibaddhasunakhassa attano dhammatāya chinditvā gantuṃ asamatthassa anuparidhāvanaṃ viya diṭṭhigatikassa diṭṭhidaṇḍake pavesitāya taṇhārajjuyā bandhitvā sakkāye upanibaddhassa anuparidhāvanaṃ veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
25. *tatrā* means in those (sattasu) annihilationist theories (ucchedavādesu), the ground (bhummaṃ).

*uddhaṃ sara* means *uddhaṃ* is said to be the doctrine of the future round of rebirth (anāgatasaṃsāravādo), the meaning is those who remember the doctrine of the future round of rebirth (anāgataṃ saṃsāravādaṃ sarantīti attho).

*āsattiṃyeva abhivadanti* means they only speak of clinging (āsattiṃyeva), they only speak of attachment (lagganakaṃyeva vadanti).

"āsatta"ntipi pāṭho, taṇhaṃyeva vadantīti attho." The reading is also "clinging", the meaning is they speak of craving (taṇhaṃyeva vadantīti attho).

*iti pecca bhavissāmā* means thus, we will be after death (iti pecca bhavissāma).

We will be Kṣatriyas (khattiyā bhavissāma), we will be *brāhmaṇas* (brāhmaṇā bhavissāmāti), in this way, the method should be understood (evamettha nayo netabbo).

*vāṇijūpamā* *maññe* means like the simile of a merchant (vāṇijūpamā viya), the merchant's share (vāṇijapaṭibhāgā), similar to a merchant (vāṇijasadisā) occurs to me (mayhaṃ upaṭṭhahanti).

*sakkāyabhayā* means fear of the existing body (sakkāyassa bhayā).

They fear danger (abhayassa bhāyanti), just as (yatheva), “O Great King (mahārāja), there are these four (cattāro kho)."

Which four (katame cattāro)? O Great King (mahārāja), because of fear, the earthworm (gaṇḍuppādo) does not eat the earth (pathaviṃ na khādati), thinking, 'lest the earth be consumed (mā pathavī khiyī’ti)', O Great King (mahārāja), the heron (konto) stands on one foot (ekapādena tiṭṭhati), thinking, 'lest the earth sink (mā pathavī osīdī’ti)', O Great King (mahārāja), the *kikī* (kikī) lies on its back (uttānā seti), thinking, 'lest the waters overflow (mā ambhā undriyī’ti)', O Great King (mahārāja), the *brāhmaṇa* (brāhmaṇadhammiko) does not practice *brahmacarya* (brahmacariyaṃ na carati), thinking, 'lest the world be destroyed (mā loko ucchijjī’ti)', these four (ime cattāro) fear danger (abhayassa bhāyanti), in the same way (evaṃ) they fear the existing body (sakkāyassa bhāyanti’”.

*sakkāyaparijegucchā* means disgusted with that very existing body reckoned as the three realms (tameva tebhūmakasaṅkhātaṃ sakkāyaṃ parijigucchamānā).

*sā gaddulabaddho* means a dog tied to a cart stake (daṇḍake rajjuṃ pavesetvā baddhasunakho).

*evamevime* means here (ettha), the existing body (sakkāyo) reckoned as the three realms of existence (tebhūmakadhammasaṅkhāto) should be seen (daṭṭhabbo) as like a firm post (daḷhatthambho viya) or like a peg (khīlo viya ca), that (sā) is like the adherent to views (diṭṭhigatiko), the cart stake (daṇḍako) is like views (diṭṭhi), the rope (rajju) is like craving (taṇhā), just as (viya) the dog tied by a cart stake (gaddulena bandhitvā) to a post or peg (thambhe vā khīle vā upanibaddhasunakhassa) is unable to go away having severed it according to its own nature (attano dhammatāya chinditvā gantuṃ asamatthassa anuparidhāvanaṃ), so too (viya) it should be understood (veditabbaṃ) that the adherent to views (diṭṭhigatikassa) tied by the rope of craving (taṇhārajjuyā bandhitvā) inserted into the cart stake of views (diṭṭhidaṇḍake pavesitāya) runs around clinging to the existing body (sakkāye upanibaddhassa anuparidhāvanaṃ).

mula_pali: 26. ‘‘Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā aparantakappikā aparantānudiṭṭhino aparantaṃ ārabbha anekavihitāni adhivuttipadāni abhivadanti, sabbe te imāneva pañcāyatanāni abhivadanti etesaṃ vā aññataraṃ.
mula_english: “Bhikkhus, any recluses or *brāhmaṇas* who speculate about the future (*aparantakappikā*) and hold views about the future, who assert various doctrinal propositions (*anekavihitāni adhivuttipadāni*) concerning the future, all assert these five sense bases (*pañcāyatanāni*) or a certain one among them.
commentary_pali: 26.Imāneva pañcāyatanānīti imāneva pañca kāraṇāni. Iti mātikaṃ ṭhapentenapi pañceva ṭhapitāni, nigamentenapi pañceva nigamitāni, bhājentena pana cattāri bhājitāni. Diṭṭhadhammanibbānaṃ kuhiṃ paviṭṭhanti. Ekattanānattavasena dvīsu padesu paviṭṭhanti veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
"<hi rend="bold">imāneva pañcāyatanānī</hi>ti" means these very five causes.

Thus, even when establishing the table of contents (mātikā), five were established; even when concluding (nigamana), only five were concluded; but when dividing (bhājana), four were divided.

Where does direct-vision nirvāṇa enter?

It should be understood that it enters into two locations, in terms of oneness and difference.

mula_pali: 27. ‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā pubbantakappikā pubbantānudiṭṭhino pubbantaṃ ārabbha anekavihitāni adhivuttipadāni abhivadanti. ‘Sassato attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘asassato attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘sassato ca asassato ca attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘nevasassato nāsassato attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘antavā attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘anantavā attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘antavā ca anantavā ca attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘nevantavā nānantavā attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘ekattasaññī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘nānattasaññī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘parittasaññī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘appamāṇasaññī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘ekantasukhī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘ekantadukkhī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘sukhadukkhī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti, ‘adukkhamasukhī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – ittheke abhivadanti.
mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, there are some recluses and brahmins who speculate about the past, who hold views about the past, who, concerning the past, assert various doctrinal propositions.

Some assert thus: ‘The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are eternal: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are not eternal: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: ‘The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are both eternal and not eternal: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are neither eternal nor not eternal: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are finite: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are infinite: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are both finite and infinite: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are neither finite nor infinite: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are percipient of unity: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are percipient of diversity: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are percipient of the limited: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) are percipient of the immeasurable: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) experience exclusively pleasure: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) experience exclusively pain: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) experience both pleasure and pain: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ Some assert thus: “The *ātman* (self) and the *loka* (world) experience neither pleasure nor pain: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’
commentary_pali:
27. Evañca catucattālīsa aparantakappike dassetvā idāni aṭṭhārasa pubbantakappike dassetuṃ santi, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha atītakoṭṭhāsasaṅkhātaṃ pubbantaṃ kappetvā vikappetvā gaṇhantīti pubbantakappikā. Pubbantakappo vā etesaṃ atthīti pubbantakappikā. Evaṃ sesampi pubbe vuttappakāraṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Sassato attā ca loko cāti rūpādīsu aññataraṃ attāti ca lokoti ca gahetvā sassato amaro nicco dhuvoti abhivadanti. Yathāha ‘‘rūpaṃ attā ceva loko ca sassato cāti attānañca lokañca paññapentī’’ti vitthāro. Asassatādīsupi eseva nayo. Ettha ca paṭhamavādena cattāro sassatavādā vuttā, dutiyavādena satta ucchedavādā.

Nanu cete heṭṭhā āgatā, idha kasmā puna gahitāti. Heṭṭhā tattha tattha mato tattha tattheva ucchijjatīti dassanatthaṃ āgatā. Idha pana pubbenivāsalābhī diṭṭhigatiko atītaṃ passati, na anāgataṃ, tassa evaṃ hoti ‘‘pubbantato āgato attā idheva ucchijjati, ito paraṃ na gacchatī’’ti imassatthassa dassanatthaṃ gahitā. Tatiyavādena cattāro ekaccasassatavādā vuttā, catutthavādena cattāro amarāvikkhepikā vuttā. Antavāti sapariyanto paricchinno parivaṭumo. Avaḍḍhitakasiṇassa taṃ kasiṇaṃ attāti ca lokoti ca gahetvā evaṃ hoti. Dutiyavādo vaḍḍhitakasiṇassa vasena vutto, tatiyavādo tiriyaṃ vaḍḍhetvā uddhamadho avaḍḍhitakasiṇassa, catutthavādo takkivasena vutto. Anantaracatukkaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva.

Antavā

Ekantasukhīti nirantarasukhī. Ayaṃ diṭṭhi lābhījātissaratakkīnaṃ vasena uppajjati. Lābhino hi pubbenivāsañāṇena khattiyādikule ekantasukhameva attano jātiṃ anussarantassa evaṃ diṭṭhi uppajjati. Tathā jātissarassa paccuppannaṃ sukhamanubhavato atītāsu sattasu jātīsu tādisameva attabhāvaṃ anussarantassa. Takkissa pana idha sukhasamaṅgino ‘‘atītepāhaṃ evameva ahosi’’nti takkeneva uppajjati.

Ekantasukhī

Ekantadukkhīti ayaṃ diṭṭhi lābhino nuppajjati. So hi ekanteneva idha jhānasukhena sukhī hoti. Idha dukkhena phuṭṭhassa pana jātissarassa takkisseva ca sā uppajjati. Tatiyā idha vokiṇṇasukhadukkhānaṃ sabbesampi tesaṃ uppajjati, tathā catutthā diṭṭhi. Lābhino hi idāni catutthajjhānavasena adukkhamasukhassa, pubbe catutthajjhānikameva brahmalokaṃ anussarantassa . Jātissarassāpi paccuppanne majjhattassa, anussarantassāpi majjhattabhūtaṭṭhānameva anussarantassa, takkinopi paccuppanne majjhattassa, atītepi evaṃ bhavissatīti takkeneva gaṇhantassa esā diṭṭhi uppajjati. Ettāvatā cattāro sassatavādā, cattāro ekaccasassatikā, cattāro antānantikā, cattāro amarāvikkhepikā , dve adhicca-samuppannikāti aṭṭhārasapi pubbantakappikā kathitā honti.

Ekantadukkhī
commentary_english:
27. Thus, having shown the forty-four views relating to the future ( *aparantakappike* ), now, in order to show the eighteen views relating to the past ( *pubbantakappike* ), he says, “There are, monks…” and so forth. Therein, those who conceive and discriminate the past, which is reckoned in terms of past divisions, are called those who relate to the past ( *pubbantakappikā* ). Or, “they have the past,” thus they are those who relate to the past. In this way, the remainder should also be understood according to the method that has been stated previously. “The self is eternal, and the world is eternal”: having taken one or another among forms etc., as "the self" and "the world," they declare, “It is eternal, immortal, constant, permanent.” As it is said: "‘Form is the self and the world; it is eternal,’ thus they designate the self and the world," this is the detailed explanation. The same method applies in the case of non-eternal etc. Here, by the first assertion, four eternalist views are stated, and by the second assertion, seven annihilationist views.

“But surely these have come below; why are they taken up again here?” They have come to show that there, in that very place, he dies and is annihilated. Here, however, one who gains the ability to recall past lives, a theorist, sees the past but not the future; it occurs to him thus: “The self, having come from the past, is annihilated right here; it does not go beyond this.” They are taken up in order to show the meaning of this. By the third assertion, four partly eternalist views are stated, and by the fourth assertion, four equivocating views are stated. “Having an end” ( *antavā* ) means having a limit, bounded, circumscribed. With regard to one whose *kasiṇa* has not been developed, having taken that *kasiṇa* as "the self" and "the world," it occurs to him thus. The second assertion is stated in dependence on the developed *kasiṇa*; the third assertion is regarding one whose *kasiṇa* is developed horizontally but not developed upwards or downwards; the fourth assertion is stated in dependence on reasoning. The immediately following tetrad is just according to the method stated below.

“Wholly happy" means continuously happy. This view arises in dependence on those who have gained the ability to recall past lives and on reasoning. For this view arises in one who has gained the ability to recall past lives, and who, by means of the knowledge of past lives, recollects his birth in a *kṣatriya* family etc. as being wholly happy. Similarly, [it arises in] one who has the ability to recall past lives, and who, experiencing present happiness, recollects a similar state of self in seven past lives. However, in the case of one who reasons, it arises simply through reasoning, in one who is presently endowed with happiness, [thinking], “In the past, I was just like this.”

“Wholly happy” [and] “wholly miserable”: this view does not arise in one who has gained [the ability to recall past lives]. For he is happy only through the bliss of absorption here. However, in one who is touched by suffering here, and who has the ability to recall past lives, it arises simply through reasoning. The third view arises in all those whose happiness and suffering are mixed here, and so does the fourth view. For now, in one who has gained [the ability to recall past lives] and is without suffering or happiness by means of the fourth *dhyāna*, [and] who recollects only the *brahmaloka* in which he previously existed as one possessing the fourth *dhyāna*. Even in one who has the ability to recall past lives, it is this view which arises in one who is presently in a state of equanimity, in one who recollects the state of equanimity itself, in one who reasons, it is this view which arises in one who is presently in a state of equanimity, [thinking], “In the past, it will be like this.” To this extent, the four eternalist views, the four partly eternalist views, the four views about the world being finite and infinite, the four equivocating views, and the two views that arise without a cause—these eighteen views relating to the past have been stated.

mula_pali: 28. ‘‘Tatra , bhikkhave, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sassato attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti , tesaṃ vata aññatreva saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā paccattaṃyeva ñāṇaṃ bhavissati parisuddhaṃ pariyodātanti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Paccattaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, ñāṇe asati parisuddhe pariyodāte yadapi yadipi (ka.) te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā tattha ñāṇabhāgamattameva pariyodapenti tadapi tesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ upādānamakkhāyati. ‘Tayidaṃ saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ atthi kho pana saṅkhārānaṃ nirodho attheta’nti – iti viditvā tassa nissaraṇadassāvī tathāgato tadupātivatto.
mula_english:
"Here, O bhikkhus, those ascetics and Brahmins who maintain such a doctrine and view, saying, 'The self and the world are eternal; only this is true, anything else is wrong,' that, apart from faith ( *saddhā*), apart from approval (*ruci*), apart from oral tradition (*anussava*), apart from reasoned cogitation (*ākāraparivitakka*), apart from reflective acceptance of a view (*diṭṭhinijjhānakkhanti*), they will have any pure and clear personal knowledge (*paccattaṃ ñāṇaṃ*) of this – that is impossible.

Since they have no pure and clear personal knowledge (*paccattaṃ ñāṇaṃ*), even the mere fragmentary knowledge that those good ascetics and Brahmins clarify about their view is declared to be clinging (*upādāna*).

'That is conditioned (*saṅkhataṃ*) and gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), but there is cessation (*nirodha*) of formations (*saṅkhārānaṃ*.' Having known ‘There is this’ seeing the escape (*nissaraṇa*) from that, the *Tathāgata* has gone beyond that (*tadupātivatto*)."
commentary_pali: 28. Idāni diṭṭhuddhāraṃ uddharanto tatra, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha paccattaṃyeva ñāṇanti paccakkhañāṇaṃ. Parisuddhanti nirupakkilesaṃ. Pariyodātanti pabhassaraṃ. Sabbapadehi vipassanāñāṇaṃyeva kathitaṃ. Saddhādayo hi pañca dhammā bāhirasamayasmimpi honti, vipassanāñāṇaṃ sāsanasmiṃyeva. Tattha ñāṇabhāgamattameva pariyodapentīti mayamidaṃ jānāmāti evaṃ tattha ñāṇakoṭṭhāsaṃ otārentiyeva. Upādānamakkhāyatīti na taṃ ñāṇaṃ, micchādassanaṃ nāmetaṃ, tasmā tadapi tesaṃ bhavantānaṃ diṭṭhupādānaṃ akkhāyatīti attho. Athāpi taṃ jānanamattalakkhaṇattā ñāṇabhāgamattameva, tathāpi tassa dassanassa anupātivattanato upādānapaccayato ca upādānameva. Tadupātivattoti taṃ diṭṭhiṃ atikkanto. Ettāvatā cattāro sassatavādā, cattāro ekaccasassatikā, cattāro antānantikā, cattāro amarāvikkhepikā, dve adhiccasamuppannikā, soḷasa saññīvādā, aṭṭha asaññīvādā, aṭṭha nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā, satta ucchedavādā, pañca diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādāti brahmajāle āgatā dvāsaṭṭhipi diṭṭhiyo kathitā honti. Brahmajāle pana kathite idaṃ suttaṃ akathitameva hoti. Kasmā? Idha tato atirekāya sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā āgatattā. Imasmiṃ pana kathite brahmajālaṃ kathitameva hoti.
commentary_english:
28. Now, singling out the view, he said, “Here, *bhikkhus*,” etc.

There, “*personally known knowledge*” means direct knowledge (paccakkhañāṇaṃ).

“*Perfectly pure*” means without defilements (nirupakkilesaṃ).

“*Spotless*” means radiant (pabhassaraṃ).

Vipassanā-knowledge (vipassanāñāṇaṃ) is spoken of by all the terms.

For the five qualities, beginning with faith (saddhā), exist even in outside (bāhirasamaya) systems, but vipassanā-knowledge exists only in the Teaching (*sāsana*).

“*Merely clarifying the knowledge-portion therein*” means just introducing the knowledge section there with "we know this".

"*It is called grasping*" means that is not knowledge; this is called wrong view (*micchādassanaṃ*). Therefore, that too is called grasping of views for those venerable ones; this is the meaning.

Even though that which has the mere characteristic of knowing is only a knowledge-portion, even so, because of the continued tendency of that view and because of the condition of grasping, it is indeed grasping (*upādāna*).

“*Having transcended that*” means having overcome that view (*diṭṭhiṃ atikkanto*).

Thus far, the four eternalist views (*sassatavādā*), the four partial-eternalist views (*ekaccasassatikā*), the four views concerning the finite and infinite (*antānantikā*), the four evasive wrigglers (*amarāvikkhepikā*), the two causally adventitious views (*adhiccasamuppannikā*), the sixteen perception-theories (*saññīvādā*), the eight non-perception theories (*asaññīvādā*), the eight neither-perception-nor-non-perception theories (*nevasaññīnāsaññīvādā*), the seven annihilationist views (*ucchedavādā*), the five here-and-now-Nibbāna views (*diṭṭhadhammanibbānavādā*)—these sixty-two views that appear in the Brahma-net (*brahmajāla*) Sūtra have been discussed.

However, when the Brahma-net (*brahmajāla*) Sūtra has been spoken of, this sutta is as good as unspoken.

Why? Because here, self-view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) comes in excess of that.

However, when this has been spoken of, the Brahma-net (*brahmajāla*) has been spoken of.

mula_pali: 29. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘asassato attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti…pe… yathā sassatavāre, tathā vitthāretabbaṃ sassato ca asassato ca attā ca loko ca… nevasassato nāsassato attā ca loko ca… antavā attā ca loko ca… anantavā attā ca loko ca… antavā ca anantavā ca attā ca loko ca… nevantavā nānantavā attā ca loko ca… ekattasaññī attā ca loko ca… nānattasaññī attā ca loko ca… parittasaññī attā ca loko ca… appamāṇasaññī attā ca loko ca… ekantasukhī attā ca loko ca… ekantadukkhī attā ca loko ca… sukhadukkhī attā ca loko ca… adukkhamasukhī attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti, tesaṃ vata aññatreva saddhāya aññatra ruciyā aññatra anussavā aññatra ākāraparivitakkā aññatra diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā paccattaṃyeva ñāṇaṃ bhavissati parisuddhaṃ pariyodātanti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Paccattaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, ñāṇe asati parisuddhe pariyodāte yadapi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā tattha ñāṇabhāgamattameva pariyodapenti tadapi tesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ upādānamakkhāyati. ‘Tayidaṃ saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ atthi kho pana saṅkhārānaṃ nirodho attheta’nti – iti viditvā tassa nissaraṇadassāvī tathāgato tadupātivatto.
mula_english:
“Therein, *bhikkhus*, as to those *samaṇa* and *brāhmaṇa* recluses who hold such a doctrine and view as this: ‘The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are not eternal (*asassato*)... only this is true (*saccaṃ*), anything else is wrong (*mogha*)’...etc... <note>as in the case of the eternalist view, so it should be expanded</note> The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are both eternal (*sassato*) and not eternal (*asassato*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are neither eternal (*nevasassato*) nor not eternal (*nāsassato*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are finite (*antavā*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are infinite (*anantavā*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are both finite (*antavā*) and infinite (*anantavā*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are neither finite (*nevantavā*) nor infinite (*nānantavā*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are percipient of unity (*ekattasaññī*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are percipient of diversity (*nānattasaññī*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are percipient of the limited (*parittasaññī*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) are percipient of the immeasurable (*appamāṇasaññī*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) experience exclusively pleasure (*ekantasukhī*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) experience exclusively pain (*ekantadukkhī*)… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) experience both pleasure (*sukhadukkhī*) and pain… The self (*ātta*) and the world (*loka*) experience neither pleasure nor pain (*adukkhamasukhī*) only this is true (*saccaṃ*), anything else is wrong (*mogha*)’ as to those, apart from faith (*saddhā*), apart from approval (*ruciyā*), apart from oral tradition (*anussavā*), apart from reasoned cogitation (*ākāraparivitakkā*), apart from reflective acceptance of a view (*diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā*) , they will have any pure (*parisuddhaṃ*) and clear (*pariyodātaṃ*) personal knowledge (*paccattaṃyeva ñāṇaṃ*) of this - that is impossible (*netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati*).

Since they have no pure (*parisuddhe*) and clear (*pariyodāte*) personal knowledge (*paccattaṃ*), even the mere fragmentary knowledge (*ñāṇabhāgamattameva*) that those good recluses *samaṇa* and *brāhmaṇa* clarify about their view is declared to be clinging (*upādānamakkhāyati*) on their part.

‘That is conditioned (*saṅkhataṃ*) and gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), but there is cessation (*nirodho*) of formations (*saṅkhārānaṃ*)’ Having known ‘There is this’ seeing the escape (*nissaraṇadassāvī*) from that, the *Tathāgata* has gone beyond that (*tadupātivatto*).

mula_pali: 30. ‘‘Idha , bhikkhave, ekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, aparantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, sabbaso kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā, pavivekaṃ pītiṃ upasampajja viharati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ pavivekaṃ pītiṃ upasampajja viharāmī’ti. Tassa sā pavivekā pīti nirujjhati. Pavivekāya pītiyā nirodhā uppajjati domanassaṃ, domanassassa nirodhā uppajjati pavivekā pīti. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yaṃ chāyā jahati taṃ ātapo pharati, yaṃ ātapo jahati taṃ chāyā pharati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, pavivekāya pītiyā nirodhā uppajjati domanassaṃ, domanassassa nirodhā uppajjati pavivekā pīti. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato abhijānāti. Ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā , aparantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, sabbaso kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā, pavivekaṃ pītiṃ upasampajja viharati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ pavivekaṃ pītiṃ upasampajja viharāmī’ti. Tassa sā pavivekā pīti nirujjhati. Pavivekāya pītiyā nirodhā uppajjati domanassaṃ, domanassassa nirodhā uppajjati pavivekā pīti. ‘Tayidaṃ saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ atthi kho pana saṅkhārānaṃ nirodho attheta’nti – iti viditvā tassa nissaraṇadassāvī tathāgato tadupātivatto.
mula_english:
“Here, *bhikkhus*, some recluse or *brāhmin*, with the relinquishing of views about the past (*pubbanta*) and the future (*aparanta*) and through complete lack of resolve upon the fetters of sensual pleasure (*kāmasaṃyojana*), enters upon and abides in the rapture (*pīti*) of seclusion (*paviveka*). He thinks: ‘This is the peaceful, this is the sublime, that I enter upon and abide in the rapture of seclusion.’

That rapture of seclusion ceases in him.

With the cessation (*nirodha*) of the rapture of seclusion, grief (*domanassa*) arises, and with the cessation of grief, the rapture of seclusion arises.

Just as the sunlight pervades the area that the shadow leaves, and the shadow pervades the area that the sunlight leaves, so too, with the cessation of the rapture of seclusion, grief arises, and with the cessation of grief, the rapture of seclusion arises.

The *Tathāgata*, *bhikkhus*, understands this.

This good recluse or *brāhmin*, with the relinquishing of views about the past and the future, through complete lack of resolve upon the fetters of sensual pleasure, enters upon and abides in the rapture of seclusion. He thinks: ‘This is the peaceful, this is the sublime, that I enter upon and abide in the rapture of seclusion.’

That rapture of seclusion ceases in him.

With the cessation of the rapture of seclusion, grief arises, and with the cessation of grief, the rapture of seclusion arises.

‘That is conditioned (*saṅkhata*) and gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), but there is cessation of formations (*saṅkhārānaṃ*). Having known ‘There is this’ seeing the escape from that, the *Tathāgata* has gone beyond that.
commentary_pali:
30. Idāni imā dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhiyo uppajjamānā sakkāyadiṭṭhipamukheneva uppajjantīti dassetuṃ idha, bhikkhave, ekaccotiādimāha. Tattha paṭinissaggāti pariccāgena. Kāmasaṃyojanānaṃanadhiṭṭhānāti pañcakāmaguṇataṇhānaṃ nissaṭṭhattā. Pavivekaṃ pītinti sappītikajjhānadvayapītiṃ. Nirujjhatīti jhānanirodhena nirujjhati. Samāpattito pana vuṭṭhitassa niruddhā nāma hoti. Yatheva hi ‘‘adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya nirodhā uppajjati nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ, nirāmisasukhassa nirodhā uppajjati adukkhamasukhā vedanā’’ti ettha na ayamattho hoti – catutthajjhānanirodhā tatiyajjhānaṃ upasampajja viharatīti. Ayaṃ panettha attho – catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhāya tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjati, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhāya catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjatīti, evaṃsampadamidaṃ veditabbaṃ. Uppajjati domanassanti hīnajjhānapariyādānakadomanassaṃ. Samāpattito vuṭṭhitacittassa pana kammanīyabhāvo kathito.

Pavivekā pītīti sā eva jhānadvayapīti. Yaṃ chāyā jahatīti yaṃ ṭhānaṃ chāyā jahati. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Yasmiṃ ṭhāne chāyā atthi, tasmiṃ ātapo natthi. Yasmiṃ ātapo atthi, tasmiṃ chāyā natthīti.

Pavivekā pītī Yaṃ chāyā jahatī
commentary_english:
30. Now, in order to show that these sixty-two views arise with the *satkāyadṛṣṭi* (view of self-identity) as their chief cause, he says, "<hi rend="bold">Here, *bhikṣus*, some</hi>" etc.

There, *paṭinissaggā* means by abandonment (*pariccāgena*).

*kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā* means because of the rejection of the craving (*tṛṣṇā*) for the five sense objects (*pañcakāmaguṇa*).

*pavivekaṃ pīti* means joy (*prīti*) in the two *dhyānas* associated with joy (*sappītikajjhāna*).

*nirujjhatī* means it is obstructed by the obstruction of *dhyāna* (*jhānanirodhena nirujjhati*).

But for one who has arisen from *samāpatti*, it is called obstructed (*niruddhā nāma hoti*).

Just as, indeed, it is said, "Through the obstruction of the feeling (*vedanā*) that is neither painful nor pleasant (*adukkhamasukhāya*), painless happiness (*nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ*) arises; through the obstruction of painless happiness, a feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant arises," here, this is not the meaning: through the obstruction of the fourth *dhyāna* (*catutthajjhāna*), one attains to and dwells in the third *dhyāna* (*tatiyajjhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*).

But here, this is the meaning: having arisen from the fourth *dhyāna*, one attains to the third *dhyāna*; having arisen from the third *dhyāna*, one attains to the fourth *dhyāna*; this is how this attainment should be understood.

*uppajjati domanassa* means sadness (*daumanasya*) due to the failure to obtain inferior *dhyānas* (*hīnajjhāna-pariyādānaka-daumanasyaṃ*).

But for one whose mind (*citta*) has arisen from *samāpatti*, suitability (*kammanīyabhāvo*) is spoken of.

*pavivekā pītī* means that very joy (*pīti*) in the two *dhyānas*.

*yaṃ chāyā jahatī* means that place (*ṭhāna*) which shadow (*chāyā*) abandons (*jahati*).

What does it mean? In whatever place there is shadow, there is no heat (*ātapa*).

In whatever place there is heat, there is no shadow.

*pavivekā pītī yaṃ chāyā jahatī*

mula_pali: 31. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, aparantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, sabbaso kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā, pavivekāya pītiyā samatikkamā nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ upasampajja viharati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ upasampajja viharāmī’ti. Tassa taṃ nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ nirujjhati. Nirāmisassa sukhassa nirodhā uppajjati pavivekā pīti, pavivekāya pītiyā nirodhā uppajjati nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ . Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yaṃ chāyā jahati taṃ ātapo pharati, yaṃ ātapo jahati taṃ chāyā pharati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, nirāmisassa sukhassa nirodhā uppajjati pavivekā pīti, pavivekāya pītiyā nirodhā uppajjati nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato abhijānāti. Ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, aparantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, sabbaso kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā , pavivekāya pītiyā samatikkamā, nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ upasampajja viharati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ upasampajja viharāmī’ti. Tassa taṃ nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ nirujjhati. Nirāmisassa sukhassa nirodhā uppajjati pavivekā pīti, pavivekāya pītiyā nirodhā uppajjati nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ. ‘Tayidaṃ saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ atthi kho pana saṅkhārānaṃ nirodho attheta’nti – iti viditvā tassa nissaraṇadassāvī tathāgato tadupātivatto.
mula_english:
31. “Here, *bhikkhus*, some recluse or *brāhmaṇa*, through relinquishing views about the past (*pūrvānta*) and relinquishing views about the future (*aparānta*), through complete lack of resolve upon the fetters of sensual pleasure (*kāmasaṃyojana*), and through surpassing the rapture (*prīti*) of seclusion (*praviveka*), enters upon and abides in unworldly pleasure (*nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ*), thinking: ‘This is the peaceful, this is the sublime, that I enter upon and abide in unworldly pleasure.’

That unworldly pleasure ceases in him.

With the cessation (*nirodha*) of unworldly pleasure, the rapture of seclusion arises; and with the cessation of the rapture of seclusion, unworldly pleasure arises.

Just as, *bhikkhus*, the shadow leaves and the sunlight pervades, and the sunlight leaves and the shadow pervades; so too, *bhikkhus*, with the cessation of unworldly pleasure, the rapture of seclusion arises, and with the cessation of the rapture of seclusion, unworldly pleasure arises.

The *Tathāgata*, *bhikkhus*, understands this.

This good recluse or *brāhmaṇa*, through relinquishing views about the past and relinquishing views about the future, through complete lack of resolve upon the fetters of sensual pleasure, and through surpassing the rapture of seclusion, enters upon and abides in unworldly pleasure, thinking: ‘This is the peaceful, this is the sublime, that I enter upon and abide in unworldly pleasure.’

That unworldly pleasure ceases in him.

With the cessation of unworldly pleasure, the rapture of seclusion arises; and with the cessation of the rapture of seclusion, unworldly pleasure arises.

‘This is conditioned (*saṅkhataṃ*) and gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), but there is the cessation of formations (*saṅkhārānaṃ nirodhaḥ*)’— thus, having understood, the *Tathāgata*, seeing the escape from that, has gone beyond that.
commentary_pali: 31.Nirāmisaṃ sukhanti tatiyajjhānasukhaṃ.
commentary_english: *Nirāmisaṃ sukha* means the bliss of the third *dhyāna* (*tatiyajjhānasukhaṃ*).

mula_pali: 32. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, aparantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, sabbaso kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā, pavivekāya pītiyā samatikkamā, nirāmisassa sukhassa samatikkamā, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharāmī’ti. Tassa sā adukkhamasukhā vedanā nirujjhati. Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya nirodhā uppajjati nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ, nirāmisassa sukhassa nirodhā uppajjati adukkhamasukhā vedanā. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yaṃ chāyā jahati taṃ ātapo pharati, yaṃ ātapo jahati taṃ chāyā pharati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya nirodhā uppajjati nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ, nirāmisassa sukhassa nirodhā uppajjati adukkhamasukhā vedanā. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato abhijānāti. Ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā , aparantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, sabbaso kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā, pavivekāya pītiyā samatikkamā, nirāmisassa sukhassa samatikkamā, adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ upasampajja viharāmī’ti. Tassa sā adukkhamasukhā vedanā nirujjhati. Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya nirodhā uppajjati nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ, nirāmisassa sukhassa nirodhā uppajjati adukkhamasukhā vedanā. ‘Tayidaṃ saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ atthi kho pana saṅkhārānaṃ nirodho attheta’nti – iti viditvā tassa nissaraṇadassāvī tathāgato tadupātivatto.
mula_english:
32. Here, bhikkhus, some recluse or *brāhmaṇa*, with the relinquishing of views about the past and the future, through complete lack of resolve upon the fetters of sensual pleasure ( *kāmasaṃyojana*), and with the surmounting of the rapture of seclusion and unworldly pleasure (*nirāmisa sukha*), enters upon and abides in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ*). He thinks: ‘This is the peaceful, this is the sublime, that I enter upon and abide in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’

That neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling ceases in him.

With the cessation of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya nirodhā*), unworldly pleasure (*nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ*) arises, and with the cessation of unworldly pleasure, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises.

Just as, bhikkhus, the shadow leaves an area and the sunlight pervades it, and the sunlight leaves an area and the shadow pervades it; so too, bhikkhus, with the cessation of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, unworldly pleasure arises, and with the cessation of unworldly pleasure, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises.

The *Tathāgata*, bhikkhus, understands this.

This, bhikkhus, some recluse or *brāhmaṇa*, with the relinquishing of views about the past and the future, through complete lack of resolve upon the fetters of sensual pleasure, and with the surmounting of the rapture of seclusion and unworldly pleasure, enters upon and abides in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. He thinks: ‘This is the peaceful, this is the sublime, that I enter upon and abide in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.’

That neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling ceases in him.

With the cessation of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, unworldly pleasure arises, and with the cessation of unworldly pleasure, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises.

‘This is conditioned (*saṅkhataṃ*) and gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), but there is cessation (*nirodho*) of formations (*saṅkhārānaṃ*). There is this.’ Thus knowing, the *Tathāgata*, seeing the escape from that (*nissaraṇadassāvī*), has gone beyond that (*tadupātivatto*).
commentary_pali: 32.Adukkhamasukhanti catutthajjhānavedanaṃ.
commentary_english: *adukkhamasukha* means the sensation of the fourth *jhāna*. ( *caturthajjhānavedanaṃ*)

mula_pali:
33. ‘‘Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, aparantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, sabbaso kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā, pavivekāya pītiyā samatikkamā, nirāmisassa sukhassa samatikkamā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya samatikkamā – ‘santohamasmi, nibbutohamasmi, anupādānohamasmī’ti samanupassati. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato abhijānāti. Ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, aparantānudiṭṭhīnañca paṭinissaggā, sabbaso kāmasaṃyojanānaṃ anadhiṭṭhānā, pavivekāya pītiyā samatikkamā, nirāmisassa sukhassa samatikkamā, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya samatikkamā – ‘santohamasmi, nibbutohamasmi, anupādānohamasmī’ti samanupassati; addhā ayamāyasmā nibbānasappāyaṃyeva paṭipadaṃ abhivadati. Atha ca panāyaṃ bhavaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā pubbantānudiṭṭhiṃ vā upādiyamāno upādiyati, aparantānudiṭṭhiṃ vā upādiyamāno upādiyati, kāmasaṃyojanaṃ vā upādiyamāno upādiyati, pavivekaṃ vā pītiṃ upādiyamāno upādiyati, nirāmisaṃ vā sukhaṃ upādiyamāno upādiyati, adukkhamasukhaṃ vā vedanaṃ upādiyamāno upādiyati. Yañca kho ayamāyasmā – ‘santohamasmi, nibbutohamasmi, anupādānohamasmī’ti samanupassati tadapi imassa bhoto samaṇassa brāhmaṇassa upādānamakkhāyati. ‘Tayidaṃ saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ atthi kho pana saṅkhārānaṃ nirodho attheta’nti – iti viditvā tassa nissaraṇadassāvī tathāgato tadupātivatto.

‘‘Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, tathāgatena anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ yadidaṃ – channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimokkho. tayidaṃ bhikkhave tathāgatena anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ, yadidaṃ channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimokkhoti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) anupādāvimokkho’’ti anupādāvimokkho. tayidaṃ bhikkhave tathāgatena anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ, yadidaṃ channaṃ phassāyatanaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca adīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimokkhoti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

anupādāvimokkho. tayidaṃ bhikkhave tathāgatena anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ, yadidaṃ channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimokkhoti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) anupādāvimokkho. tayidaṃ bhikkhave tathāgatena anuttaraṃ santivarapadaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ, yadidaṃ channaṃ phassāyatanaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca adīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimokkhoti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Pañcattayasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
“Here, *bhikkhus*, some recluse or *brāhmin*, with the relinquishing of views about the past (*pūrvānta*) and the future (*aparantā*), through complete lack of resolve upon the fetters of sensual pleasure (*kāmasaṃyojana*), and with the surmounting of the rapture (*prīti*) of seclusion (*praviveka*), unworldly pleasure, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhā vedanā*), regards himself thus: ‘I am at peace (*śānto’hamasmi*), I have attained *Nirvāṇa* (*nirvṛto’hamasmi*), I am without clinging (*anupādāno’hamasmi*)’".

“The *Tathāgata*, *bhikkhus*, understands this.”

“This good recluse or *brāhmin*, with the relinquishing of views about the past and the future… regards himself thus: “I am at peace, I have attained *Nirvāṇa*, I am without clinging.” Certainly this venerable one asserts the way directed to *Nirvāṇa*.

Yet this good recluse or *brāhmin* still clings, clinging either to a view about the past or to a view about the future or to a fetter of sensual pleasure or to the rapture of seclusion or to unworldly pleasure or to neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.

And when this venerable one regards himself thus: “I am at peace, I have attained *Nirvāṇa*, I am without clinging,” that too is declared to be clinging on the part of this good recluse or *brāhmin*.

That is conditioned (*saṃkhata*) and gross (*oḷārika*), but there is cessation (*nirodha*) of formations (*saṅkhārāna*). Having known ‘There is this’ seeing the escape (*nissaraṇa*) from that, the *Tathāgata* has gone beyond that.

“*Bhikkhus*, this unsurpassed state of sublime peace (*śāntivarapada*) has been fully awakened (*abhisambuddha*) by the *Tathāgata*, that is, liberation (*vimokkha*) through not clinging (*anupādā*), by understanding as they actually are (*yathābhūtaṃ*) the origination (*samudaya*), the disappearance (*atthaṅgama*), the gratification (*assāda*), the danger (*ādīnava*), and the escape (*nissaraṇa*) in the case of the six bases of contact (*ṣaṇṇāṃ sparśāyatanānāṃ*).

The Blessed One said this. Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Pañcattaya Sutta, the second, is finished.
commentary_pali:
33.Anupādānohamasmīti niggahaṇo ahamasmi. Nibbānasappāyanti nibbānassa sappāyaṃ upakārabhūtaṃ . Nanu ca maggadassanaṃ nāma sabbattha nikantiyā sukkhāpitāya uppajjati, kathametaṃ nibbānassa upakārapaṭipadā nāma jātanti, sabbattha anupādiyanavasena aggaṇhanavasena upakārapaṭipadā nāma jātaṃ. Abhivadatīti abhimānena upavadati. Pubbantānudiṭṭhinti aṭṭhārasavidhampi pubbantānudiṭṭhiṃ. Aparantānudiṭṭhinti catucattārīsavidhampi aparantānudiṭṭhiṃ. Upādānamakkhāyatīti ahamasmīti gahaṇassa sakkāyadiṭṭhipariyāpannattā diṭṭhupādānaṃ akkhāyati.

Santivarapadanti vūpasantakilesattā santaṃ uttamapadaṃ. Channaṃ phassāyatanānanti bhagavatā ‘‘yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati so āyatano veditabbo’’ti ettha dvinnaṃ āyatanānaṃ paṭikkhepena nibbānaṃ dassitaṃ.

Santivarapada Channaṃ phassāyatanāna

‘‘Yattha āpo ca pathavī, tejo vāyo na gādhati;

Ato sarā nivattanti, ettha vaṭṭaṃ na vattati;

Ettha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhatī’’ti. (saṃ. ni. 1.27) –

Ettha pana saṅkhārapaṭikkhepena nibbānaṃ dassitaṃ.

‘‘Kattha āpo ca pathavī, tejo vāyo na gādhati;

Kattha dīghañca rassañca, aṇuṃ thūlaṃ subhāsubhaṃ;

Kattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhatī’’ti. (dī. ni. 1.498);

Tatra veyyākaraṇaṃ bhavati –

‘‘Viññāṇaṃ anidassanaṃ, anantaṃ sabbato pabha’’nti –

Ettha saṅkhārapaṭikkhepena nibbānaṃ dassitaṃ. Imasmiṃ pana sutte chaāyatanapaṭikkhepena dassitaṃ. Aññattha ca anupādāvimokkhoti nibbānameva dassitaṃ, idha pana arahattaphalasamāpatti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

anupādāvimokkho

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Pañcattayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
33. "`I am without grasping (anupādānohamasmī)`" means that I am the one being disciplined (niggahaṇo ahamasmi).

"`Conducive to nirvāṇa (nibbānasappāyaṃ)`" means helpful (upakārabhūtaṃ) and suitable (sappāyaṃ) for nirvāṇa.

Now, the vision of the path (maggadassanaṃ) arises everywhere upon the drying up of craving (nikantiyā sukkhāpitāya), so how can this be called a practice conducive to nirvāṇa (nibbānassa upakārapaṭipadā)? It is called a practice conducive to help because it arises everywhere by way of non-grasping (anupādiyanavasena), by way of non-seizing (aggaṇhanavasena).

"`Disparages (abhivadatī)`" means to disparage (upavadati) with pride (abhimānena).

"`Views about the past (pubbantānudiṭṭhiṃ)`" means the eighteen kinds of views about the past (aṭṭhārasavidhampi pubbantānudiṭṭhiṃ).

"`Views about the future (aparantānudiṭṭhiṃ)`" means the forty-four kinds of views about the future (catucattārīsavidhampi aparantānudiṭṭhiṃ).

"`Signifies clinging (upādānamakkhāyati)`" means it signifies clinging to views (diṭṭhupādānaṃ akkhāyati), since the grasping of "`I am (ahamasmīti)`" is included in the category of self-view (sakkāyadiṭṭhipariyāpannattā).

"`The unsurpassed state of peace (santivarapadaṃ)`" means the peaceful (santaṃ) unsurpassed state (uttamapadaṃ), because of the subsiding of defilements (vūpasantakilesattā).

"`The six sense-bases (channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ)`" means that the Blessed One (bhagavatā) showed nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ dassitaṃ) by rejecting (paṭikkhepena) two bases (dvinnāṃ āyatanānaṃ) in this statement (ettha): "`Where (yattha) the eye (cakkhu) ceases (nirujjhati) and the perception of forms (rūpasaññā) ceases (nirujjhati), that is the base to be known (so āyatano veditabbo).`"

The unsurpassed state of peace (santivarapadaṃ), the six sense-bases (channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ).

"`Where water (āpo) and earth (pathavī), fire (tejo) and wind (vāyo) do not find a footing (na gādhati);

from there the streams turn back (ato sarā nivattanti), here the cycle (vaṭṭaṃ) does not turn (na vattati);

here name (nāma) and form (rūpa), cease without remainder (asesaṃ uparujjhati).`"

(Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.27)

Here (ettha), nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ dassitaṃ) is shown by rejecting (paṭikkhepena) formations (saṅkhāra).

"`Where (kattha) water (āpo) and earth (pathavī), fire (tejo) and wind (vāyo) do not find a footing (na gādhati);

where (kattha) long and short (dīghañca rassañca), subtle and gross (aṇuṃ thūlaṃ), beautiful and ugly (subhāsubhaṃ);

where (kattha) name (nāma) and form (rūpa), cease without remainder (asesaṃ uparujjhati).`"

(Dīgha Nikāya 1.498)

There (tatra) is the explanation (veyyākaraṇaṃ bhavati):

"`Consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) is invisible (anidassanaṃ), endless (anantaṃ), radiant in every way (sabbato pabha).`"

Here (ettha), nirvāṇa (nibbānaṃ dassitaṃ) is shown by rejecting (paṭikkhepena) formations (saṅkhāra). In this sutta (imasmiṃ pana sutte), it is shown by rejecting the six bases (chaāyatanapaṭikkhepena dassitaṃ). And elsewhere (aññattha ca), only nirvāṇa (nibbānameva dassitaṃ) is shown as "`release through non-grasping (anupādāvimokkho),"` but here (idha pana) it is the attainment of the fruit of arahantship (arahattaphalasamāpatti). The rest (sesaṃ) is clear (uttānameva) throughout (sabbattha).

Release through non-grasping (anupādāvimokkho).

The commentary on the Pañcattaya Sutta is finished (niṭṭhitā) in the Papañcasūdanī, the commentary on the Middle Length Discourses (Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya).

mula_pali:
34. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā pisinārāyaṃ kusinārāyaṃ (sī.) viharati baliharaṇe vanasaṇḍe. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘kinti vo , bhikkhave, mayi hoti – ‘cīvarahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti, piṇḍapātahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti, senāsanahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti, itibhavābhavahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ desetī’’’ti? ‘‘Na kho no, bhante, bhagavati evaṃ hoti – ‘cīvarahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti, piṇḍapātahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti, senāsanahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti, itibhavābhavahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ desetī’’’ti.

‘‘Na ca kira vo, bhikkhave, mayi evaṃ hoti – ‘cīvarahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ deseti…pe… itibhavābhavahetu vā samaṇo gotamo dhammaṃ desetī’ti; atha kinti carahi vo atha kinti vo (sī. pī.), atha kiñcarahi vo (ka.), bhikkhave, mayi hotī’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ kho no, bhante, bhagavati hoti – ‘anukampako bhagavā hitesī; anukampaṃ upādāya dhammaṃ desetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evañca evaṃ (sī. pī.) kira vo, bhikkhave, mayi hoti – ‘anukampako bhagavā hitesī; anukampaṃ upādāya dhammaṃ desetī’’’ti.

atha kinti vo (sī. pī.), atha kiñcarahi vo (ka.) evaṃ (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
34. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was living at Pisinārā in the Baliharaṇa grove, in the forest thicket. There the Blessed One addressed the monks (bhikkhus), saying: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir (bhadante),” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “What do you think about me, bhikkhus? [Do you think] that the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma (dharma) for the sake of robes (cīvarahetu), or that the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma for the sake of almsfood (piṇḍapātahetu), or that the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma for the sake of a resting place (senāsanahetu), or that the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma for the sake of some better state of being (itibhavābhavahetu)?” “No, venerable sir (bhante), we do not think thus about the Blessed One: ‘The ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma for the sake of robes, or for the sake of almsfood, or for the sake of a resting place, or for the sake of some better state of being.’”

“So, bhikkhus, you do not think thus about me: ‘The ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma for the sake of robes…or for the sake of some better state of being.’ Then what do you think about me?” “Thus, venerable sir (bhante), we think about the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is compassionate (anukampako) and seeks our welfare (hitesī); he teaches the Dhamma out of compassion (anukampaṃ upādāya dhammaṃ desetī).’” “So, bhikkhus, you think thus about me: ‘The Blessed One is compassionate (anukampako) and seeks our welfare (hitesī); he teaches the Dhamma out of compassion (anukampaṃ upādāya dhammaṃ desetī).’”
commentary_pali: 34.Evaṃme sutanti kintisuttaṃ. Tattha pisinārāyanti evaṃnāmake maṇḍalapadese. Baliharaṇeti tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe bhūtānaṃ baliṃ āharanti, tasmā so baliharaṇanti vutto. Cīvarahetūti cīvarakāraṇā, cīvaraṃ paccāsīsamānoti attho. Itibhavābhavahetūti evaṃ imaṃ desanāmayaṃ puññakiriyavatthuṃ nissāya tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhave sukhaṃ vedissāmīti dhammaṃ desetīti kiṃ tumhākaṃ evaṃ hotīti attho.
commentary_english:
34.
Evaṃ me sutaṃti kintisuttaṃ.
Tattha pisinārāyanti evaṃnāmake maṇḍalapadese.
Baliharaṇeti tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe bhūtānaṃ baliṃ āharanti, tasmā so baliharaṇanti vutto.
Cīvarahetūti cīvarakāraṇā, cīvaraṃ paccāsīsamānoti attho.
Itibhavābhavahetūti evaṃ imaṃ desanāmayaṃ puññakiriyavatthuṃ nissāya tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhave sukhaṃ vedissāmīti dhammaṃ desetīti kiṃ tumhākaṃ evaṃ hotīti attho.

mula_pali: 35. ‘‘Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ye vo ye te (ka.) mayā dhammā abhiññā desitā, seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā cattāro sammappadhānā cattāro iddhipādā pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅgā ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, tattha sabbeheva samaggehi sammodamānehi avivadamānehi sikkhitabbaṃ. Tesañca vo, bhikkhave, samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ sikkhataṃ siyaṃsu siyuṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.) saddanīti oloketabbā dve bhikkhū abhidhamme nānāvādā. Tatra ce tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘imesaṃ kho āyasmantānaṃ atthato ceva nānaṃ byañjanato ca nāna’nti, tattha yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ subbacataraṃ (ka.) maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmantānaṃ kho atthato ceva nānaṃ, byañjanato ca nānaṃ. Tadamināpetaṃ tadimināpetaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) āyasmanto jānātha – yathā atthato ceva nānaṃ, byañjanato ca nānaṃ. Māyasmanto vivādaṃ āpajjitthā’ti. Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmantānaṃ kho atthato ceva nānaṃ, byañjanato ca nānaṃ. Tadamināpetaṃ āyasmanto jānātha – yathā atthato ceva nānaṃ, byañjanato ca nānaṃ. Māyasmanto vivādaṃ āpajjitthā’ti. Iti duggahitaṃ duggahitato dhāretabbaṃ, suggahitaṃ suggahitato dhāretabbaṃ. Duggahitaṃ duggahitato dhāretvā suggahitaṃ suggahitato dhāretvā iti duggahitaṃ duggahitato dhāretabbaṃ, duggahitaṃ duggahitato dhāretvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) anantaravārattaye pana idaṃ pāṭhanānattaṃ natthi yo dhammo yo vinayo so bhāsitabbo.
mula_english:
“Therefore, bhikkhus, those things which I have taught, having directly known them – that is, the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*), the four right exertions (*cattāro sammappadhānā*), the four bases of spiritual power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), the five faculties (*pañcindriyāṇi*), the five powers (*pañca balāni*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*satta bojjhaṅgā*), the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo*) – in these things you should all train in concord, with mutual appreciation, without disputing.

“While you are training in concord, with mutual appreciation, without disputing, two bhikkhus might differ about the higher Dhamma.

“Now if you should think thus: ‘These venerable ones differ about both the meaning (*attha*) and the phrasing (*byañjana*)’, then whichever bhikkhu you think is the more reasonable should be approached and addressed thus: ‘The venerable ones differ about both the meaning (*attha*) and the phrasing (*byañjana*).

“The venerable ones should know that it is for this reason that there is difference about the meaning (*attha*) and difference about the phrasing (*byañjana*); let the venerable ones not fall into a dispute.’

“Then whichever bhikkhu you think is the most reasonable of those who side together on the opposite part should be approached and addressed thus: ‘The venerable ones differ about the meaning (*attha*) and the phrasing (*byañjana*).

"The venerable ones should know that it is for this reason that there is difference about the meaning (*attha*) and difference about the phrasing (*byañjana*); let the venerable ones not fall into a dispute.’

So what has been wrongly grasped should be borne in mind as wrongly grasped, what has been rightly grasped should be borne in mind as rightly grasped. Bearing in mind what has been wrongly grasped as wrongly grasped, and bearing in mind what has been rightly grasped as rightly grasped, what is Dhamma (*dharma*) and what is Discipline (*vinaya*) should be expounded."
commentary_pali: 35.Cattāro satipaṭṭhānātiādayo sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiyadhammā lokiyalokuttarāva kathitā. Tatthāti tesu sattatiṃsāya dhammesu. Siyaṃsūti bhaveyyuṃ. Abhidhammeti visiṭṭhe dhamme, imesu sattatiṃsabodhipakkhiyadhammesūti attho. Tatra ceti idampi bodhipakkhiyadhammesveva bhummaṃ. Atthato ceva nānaṃ byañjanato cāti ettha ‘‘kāyova satipaṭṭhānaṃ vedanāva satipaṭṭhāna’’nti vutte atthato nānaṃ hoti , ‘‘satipaṭṭhānā’’ti vutte pana byañjanato nānaṃ nāma hoti. Tadamināpīti taṃ tumhe imināpi kāraṇena jānāthāti atthañca byañjanañca samānetvā athassa ca aññathā gahitabhāvo byañjanassa ca micchā ropitabhāvo dassetabbo. Yo dhammo yo vinayoti ettha atthañca byañjanañca viññāpanakāraṇameva dhammo ca vinayo ca.
commentary_english:
The thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, beginning with the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*), are spoken of as mundane (*lokiya*) and supramundane (*lokuttara*).

*Tattha* means: among those thirty-seven factors.

*Siyaṃsū* means: may there be.

*Abhidhamme* means: in the distinguished Dharma; the meaning is, in these thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening.

*Tatra ce* means: this too is abundant only in the factors conducive to awakening.

*Atthato ceva nānaṃ byañjanato cā* means: Here, when it is said, "The body itself is the foundation of mindfulness, the feeling itself is the foundation of mindfulness," there is difference in meaning (*attha*). But when it is said, "foundations of mindfulness" (*satipaṭṭhānā*), there is a difference in the expression (*byañjana*).

*Tadamināpī* means: you should know that by this reason too, meaning (*attha*) and expression (*byañjana*) having been brought together, the state of the meaning being grasped otherwise and the state of the expression being wrongly applied should be shown.

*Yo dhammo yo vinayo* means: here, meaning (*attha*) and expression (*byañjana*) are simply the cause of making known, the Dharma (*dhammo*) and the Discipline (*vinayo*).

mula_pali: 36. ‘‘Tatra ce tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘imesaṃ kho āyasmantānaṃ atthato hi kho nānaṃ, byañjanato sametī’ti, tattha yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmantānaṃ kho atthato hi nānaṃ, byañjanato sameti. Tadamināpetaṃ āyasmanto jānātha – yathā atthato hi kho nānaṃ, byañjanato sameti. Māyasmanto vivādaṃ āpajjitthā’ti. Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmantānaṃ kho atthato hi kho nānaṃ, byañjanato sameti. Tadamināpetaṃ āyasmanto jānātha – yathā atthato hi kho nānaṃ, byañjanato sameti. Māyasmanto vivādaṃ āpajjitthā’ti . Iti duggahitaṃ duggahitato dhāretabbaṃ, suggahitaṃ suggahitato dhāretabbaṃ. Duggahitaṃ duggahitato dhāretvā suggahitaṃ suggahitato dhāretvā yo dhammo yo vinayo so bhāsitabbo.
mula_english:
36. It is said, "Now if you should think thus: ‘These venerable ones differ about the meaning (attha) but agree about the phrasing (byañjana),' then whichever *bhikkhu* you think is the more reasonable should be approached and addressed thus: ‘The venerable ones differ about the meaning but agree about the phrasing.’ The venerable ones should know that it is for this reason that there is agreement about the meaning but difference about the phrasing. Let the venerable ones not fall into a dispute (vivāda).’

Then whichever *bhikkhu* you think is the most reasonable of those who side together on the opposite part should be approached and addressed thus: ‘The venerable ones differ about the meaning but agree about the phrasing.’ The venerable ones should know that it is for this reason that there is agreement about the meaning but difference about the phrasing. Let the venerable ones not fall into a dispute.

So what has been wrongly grasped (*duggahita*) should be borne in mind as wrongly grasped, and what has been rightly grasped (*suggahita*) should be borne in mind as rightly grasped. Bearing in mind what has been wrongly grasped as wrongly grasped, and bearing in mind what has been rightly grasped as rightly grasped, what is *dharma* and what is *vinaya* should be expounded.

mula_pali: 37. ‘‘Tatra ce tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘imesaṃ kho āyasmantānaṃ atthato hi kho sameti, byañjanato nāna’nti, tattha yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmantānaṃ kho atthato hi sameti, byañjanato nānaṃ. Tadamināpetaṃ āyasmanto jānātha – yathā atthato hi kho sameti, byañjanato nānaṃ. Appamattakaṃ kho panetaṃ yadidaṃ – byañjanaṃ. Māyasmanto appamattake vivādaṃ āpajjitthā’ti. Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmantānaṃ kho atthato hi sameti, byañjanato nānaṃ. Tadamināpetaṃ āyasmanto jānātha – yathā atthato hi kho sameti, byañjanato nānaṃ. Appamattakaṃ kho panetaṃ yadidaṃ – byañjanaṃ. Māyasmanto appamattake appamattakehi (sī. pī.) vivādaṃ āpajjitthā’ti. Iti suggahitaṃ suggahitato dhāretabbaṃ, duggahitaṃ duggahitato dhāretabbaṃ. Suggahitaṃ suggahitato dhāretvā duggahitaṃ duggahitato dhāretvā yo dhammo yo vinayo so bhāsitabbo.
mula_english:
37. “Now if you should think thus: ‘These venerable ones agree about the meaning (*artha*) but differ about the phrasing (*byañjana*),’ then whichever *bhikkhu* you think is the more reasonable should be approached and addressed thus: ‘The venerable ones agree about the meaning (*artha*) but differ about the phrasing (*byañjana*).’

The venerable ones should know that it is for this reason that there is agreement about the meaning (*artha*) but difference about the phrasing (*byañjana*).

But the phrasing (*byañjana*) is a mere trifle.

Let the venerable ones not fall into a dispute over a mere trifle.’

Then whichever *bhikkhu* you think is the most reasonable of those who side together on the opposite part should be approached and addressed thus: ‘The venerable ones agree about the meaning (*artha*) but differ about the phrasing (*byañjana*).’

The venerable ones should know that it is for this reason that there is agreement about the meaning (*artha*) but difference about the phrasing (*byañjana*).

But the phrasing (*byañjana*) is a mere trifle.

Let the venerable ones not fall into a dispute over a mere trifle.’

So what has been rightly grasped should be borne in mind as rightly grasped, and what has been wrongly grasped should be borne in mind as wrongly grasped.

Bearing in mind what has been rightly grasped as rightly grasped, and bearing in mind what has been wrongly grasped as wrongly grasped, what is *dharma* and what is *vinaya* should be expounded.
commentary_pali:
37.Atthato hi kho sametīti satiyeva satipaṭṭhānanti gahitā. Byañjanato nānanti kevalaṃ byañjanameva satipaṭṭhānoti vā satipaṭṭhānāti vā micchā ropetha. Appamattakaṃ khoti suttantaṃ patvā byañjanaṃ appamattakaṃ nāma hoti. Parittamattaṃ dhanitaṃ katvā ropitepi hi nibbutiṃ pattuṃ sakkā hoti.

Tatridaṃ vatthu – vijayārāmavihāravāsī kireko khīṇāsavatthero dvinnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ suttaṃ āharitvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathento – ‘‘samuddho samuddhoti, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano bhāsatī’’ti dhanitaṃ katvā āha. Eko bhikkhu ‘‘samuddho nāma, bhante’’ti āha. Āvuso, samuddhoti vuttepi samuddoti vuttepi mayaṃ loṇasāgarameva jānāma, tumhe pana no atthagavesakā, byañjanagavesakā, gacchatha mahāvihāre paguṇabyañjanānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ santike byañjanaṃ sodhāpethāti kammaṭṭhānaṃ akathetvāva uṭṭhāpesi. So aparabhāge mahāvihāre bheriṃ paharāpetvā bhikkhusaṅghassa catūsu maggesu pañhaṃ kathetvāva parinibbuto. Evaṃ suttantaṃ patvā byañjanaṃ appamattakaṃ nāma hoti.

Vinayaṃ pana patvā no appamattakaṃ. Sāmaṇerapabbajjāpi hi ubhatosuddhito vaṭṭati, upasampadādikammānipi sithilādīnaṃ dhanitādikaraṇamatteneva kuppanti. Idha pana suttantabyañjanaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
37. *Atthato hi kho sametī* means that it comes together with mindfulness itself, and is thus grasped as mindfulness.

*Byañjanato nāna* means: do not falsely impose merely the literal expression, thinking that the literal expression alone is mindfulness.

*Appamattakaṃ kho* means that having attained the Sūtra, the literal expression is only a small matter.

Even having made a mere limited sound, it is possible to attain *nirvāṇa*.

Therein, this is the story: A certain elder, whose *āsavas* were destroyed, dwelling in the Vijayārāma monastery, having brought forth a *sūtra* for two *bhikkhus*, while telling them about the meditation subject, making a sound, said: "The uninstructed ordinary person speaks of 'ocean, ocean,' O *bhikkhus*."

One *bhikkhu* said, "It is called 'ocean,' Venerable Sir."

"Friend, even when 'ocean' is said, even when 'ocean' is said, we know only the salt ocean. But you are not seekers of the meaning, but seekers of the literal expression. Go to the Mahāvihāra, to the *bhikkhus* who are skilled in the literal expression, purify the literal expression," he said, and without telling them the meditation subject, he dismissed them.

That one, in the latter part [of his life], having had a drum beaten in the Mahāvihāra, having asked a question of the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* in the four paths, was completely extinguished.

Thus, having attained the Sūtra, the literal expression is only a small matter.

Having attained the Vinaya, however, it is not a small matter.

Even the *sāmaṇera* ordination is valid only if it is pure on both sides; the *upasampadā* etc. actions are ruined by merely making a sound like the loose ones, etc.

Here, however, this was said with reference to the literal expression of the Sūtra.

mula_pali: 38. ‘‘Tatra ce tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘imesaṃ kho āyasmantānaṃ atthato ceva sameti byañjanato ca sametī’ti, tattha yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmantānaṃ kho atthato ceva sameti, byañjanato ca sameti. Tadamināpetaṃ āyasmanto jānātha – yathā atthato ceva sameti byañjanato ca sameti. Māyasmanto vivādaṃ āpajjitthā’ti. Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmantānaṃ kho atthato ceva sameti byañjanato ca sameti. Tadamināpetaṃ āyasmanto jānātha – yathā atthato ceva sameti byañjanato ca sameti. Māyasmanto vivādaṃ āpajjitthā’ti. Iti suggahitaṃ suggahitato dhāretabbaṃ. Suggahitaṃ suggahitato dhāretvā yo dhammo yo vinayo so bhāsitabbo.
mula_english: 38. It is said, "Now if you should think thus: 'These venerable ones agree about both the meaning (*attha*) and the phrasing (*byañjana*),' then whichever *bhikkhu* you think is the more reasonable should be approached and addressed thus: 'The venerable ones agree about both the meaning and the phrasing. The venerable ones should know that it is for this reason that there is agreement about both the meaning and the phrasing; let the venerable ones not fall into a dispute." Then whichever *bhikkhu* you think is the most reasonable of those who side together on the opposite part should be approached and addressed thus: ‘The venerable ones agree about both the meaning and the phrasing. The venerable ones should know that it is for this reason that there is agreement about both the meaning and the phrasing; let them not fall into a dispute.’ So what has been rightly grasped (*suggahita*) should be borne in mind as rightly grasped. Bearing in mind what has been rightly grasped as rightly grasped, what is *dharma* and what is *vinaya* should be expounded.
commentary_pali: 38. Atha catutthavāre vivādo kasmā? Saññāya vivādo. ‘‘Ahaṃ satimeva satipaṭṭhānaṃ vadāmi, ayaṃ ‘kāyo satipaṭṭhāna’nti vadatī’’ti hi nesaṃ saññā hoti. Byañjanepi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
Now, why is there a dispute at the fourth turn? The dispute is about perception (saṃjñā).

"I speak only of mindfulness (smṛti), of the foundations of mindfulness (smṛti-pratiṣṭhāna)," while this one says, "The body (kāya) is a foundation of mindfulness (smṛti-pratiṣṭhāna)." Thus, they have a perception (saṃjñā).

And the same method applies to the consonants as well.

mula_pali:
39. ‘‘Tesañca vo, bhikkhave, samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ sikkhataṃ siyā aññatarassa bhikkhuno āpatti siyā vītikkamo, tatra, bhikkhave, na codanāya taritabbaṃ coditabbaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) turitabbaṃ (?). Puggalo upaparikkhitabbo – ‘iti mayhañca avihesā bhavissati parassa ca puggalassa anupaghāto, paro hi puggalo akkodhano anupanāhī adaḷhadiṭṭhī suppaṭinissaggī, sakkomi cāhaṃ etaṃ puggalaṃ akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpetu’nti. Sace, bhikkhave, evamassa, kallaṃ vacanāya.

‘‘Sace pana, bhikkhave, evamassa – ‘mayhaṃ kho avihesā bhavissati parassa ca puggalassa upaghāto, paro hi puggalo kodhano upanāhī adaḷhadiṭṭhī suppaṭinissaggī, sakkomi cāhaṃ etaṃ puggalaṃ akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpetuṃ. Appamattakaṃ kho panetaṃ yadidaṃ – parassa yadidaṃ mayhañca vihesā bhavissati parassa ca (ka.) puggalassa upaghāto. Atha kho etadeva bahutaraṃ – svāhaṃ sakkomi etaṃ puggalaṃ akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpetu’nti . Sace, bhikkhave, evamassa, kallaṃ vacanāya.

yadidaṃ mayhañca vihesā bhavissati parassa ca (ka.)

‘‘Sace pana, bhikkhave, evamassa – ‘mayhaṃ kho vihesā bhavissati parassa ca puggalassa anupaghāto. Paro hi puggalo akkodhano anupanāhī daḷhadiṭṭhī duppaṭinissaggī, sakkomi cāhaṃ etaṃ puggalaṃ akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpetuṃ. Appamattakaṃ kho panetaṃ yadidaṃ – mayhaṃ vihesā mayhañca vihesā bhavissati parassa ca puggalassa upaghāto (ka.). Atha kho etadeva bahutaraṃ – svāhaṃ sakkomi etaṃ puggalaṃ akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpetu’nti. Sace, bhikkhave, evamassa, kallaṃ vacanāya.

mayhañca vihesā bhavissati parassa ca puggalassa upaghāto (ka.)

‘‘Sace pana, bhikkhave, evamassa – ‘mayhañca kho vihesā bhavissati parassa ca puggalassa upaghāto. Paro hi puggalo kodhano upanāhī daḷhadiṭṭhī duppaṭinissaggī, sakkomi cāhaṃ etaṃ puggalaṃ akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpetuṃ. Appamattakaṃ kho panetaṃ yadidaṃ – mayhañca vihesā bhavissati parassa ca puggalassa upaghāto. Atha kho etadeva bahutaraṃ – svāhaṃ sakkomi etaṃ puggalaṃ akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpetu’nti. Sace, bhikkhave, evamassa, kallaṃ vacanāya.

‘‘Sace pana, bhikkhave, evamassa – ‘mayhañca kho vihesā bhavissati parassa ca puggalassa upaghāto. Paro hi puggalo kodhano upanāhī daḷhadiṭṭhī duppaṭinissaggī, na cāhaṃ sakkomi etaṃ puggalaṃ akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpetu’nti. Evarūpe, bhikkhave, puggale upekkhā nātimaññitabbā.
mula_english:
39. “While you, the monks, are training in concord, with mutual appreciation, without disputing, if some monk should commit an offense or a transgression, then, monks, you should not rush to reprove him.

The person should be examined thus: ‘By this, I shall not be troubled, and the other person will not be hurt; for the other person is not given to anger and revenge, is not firmly attached to his view, and relinquishes easily, and I can make that person emerge from the unwholesome and establish him in the wholesome.’ If such occurs to you, monks, it is proper to speak.

“But if it occurs to you, monks: ‘I shall be troubled, but the other person will be hurt, for the other person is given to anger and revenge, is not firmly attached to his view, and relinquishes easily, and I can make that person emerge from the unwholesome and establish him in the wholesome.’ It is a mere trifle that the other person will be hurt. But it is a much greater thing that I can make that person emerge from the unwholesome and establish him in the wholesome.’ If such occurs to you, monks, it is proper to speak.

“If it occurs to you, monks: ‘I shall be troubled, but the other person will not be hurt. For the other person is not given to anger and revenge, is not firmly attached to his view, and relinquishes with difficulty, and I can make that person emerge from the unwholesome and establish him in the wholesome.’ It is a mere trifle that I shall be troubled. But it is a much greater thing that I can make that person emerge from the unwholesome and establish him in the wholesome.’ If such occurs to you, monks, it is proper to speak.

“If it occurs to you, monks: ‘I shall be troubled, and the other person will be hurt. For the other person is given to anger and revenge, is firmly attached to his view, and relinquishes with difficulty, and I cannot make that person emerge from the unwholesome and establish him in the wholesome.’ One should not underrate equanimity towards such a person.
commentary_pali:
39.Nacodanāya taritabbanti na codanatthāya vegāyitabbaṃ. Ekacco hi puggalo ‘‘nalāṭe te sāsapamattā piḷakā’’ti vutto ‘‘mayhaṃ nalāṭe sāsapamattaṃ piḷakaṃ passasi, attano nalāṭe tālapakkamattaṃ mahāgaṇḍaṃ na passasī’’ti vadati. Tasmā puggalo upaparikkhitabbo. Adaḷhadiṭṭhīti anādānadiṭṭhī suṃsumāraṃ hadaye pakkhipanto viya daḷhaṃ na gaṇhāti.

Upaghātoti caṇḍabhāvena vaṇaghaṭṭitassa viya dukkhuppatti. Suppaṭinissaggīti ‘‘kiṃ nāma ahaṃ āpanno, kadā āpanno’’ti vā ‘‘tvaṃ āpanno, tava upajjhāyo āpanno’’ti vā ekaṃ dve vāre vatvāpi ‘‘asukaṃ nāma asukadivase nāma, bhante, āpannattha, saṇikaṃ anussarathā’’ti saritvā tāvadeva vissajjeti. Vihesāti bahuṃ atthañca kāraṇañca āharantassa kāyacittakilamatho. Sakkomīti evarūpo hi puggalo okāsaṃ kāretvā ‘‘āpattiṃ āpannattha, bhante’’ti vutto ‘‘kadā kismiṃ vatthusmi’’nti vatvā ‘‘asukadivase asukasmiṃ vatthusmi’’nti vutte ‘‘na sarāmi, āvuso’’ti vadati, tato ‘‘saṇikaṃ, bhante, sarathā’’ti bahuṃ vatvā sārito saritvā vissajjeti. Tenāha ‘‘sakkomī’’ti. Iminā nayena sabbattha attho veditabbo.

Upaghāto Suppaṭinissaggī Vihesā Sakkomī

Upekkhā nātimaññitabbāti upekkhā na atikkamitabbā, kattabbā janetabbāti attho. Yo hi evarūpaṃ puggalaṃ ṭhitakaṃyeva passāvaṃ karontaṃ disvāpi ‘‘nanu, āvuso, nisīditabba’’nti vadati, so upekkhaṃ atimaññati nāma.

Upekkhā nātimaññitabbā

mula_pali:
40. ‘‘Tesañca vo, bhikkhave, samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ sikkhataṃ aññamaññassa vacīsaṃhāro vacīsaṅkhāro (sī. pī.) uppajjeyya diṭṭhipaḷāso diṭṭhipalāso (sī. ka.) cetaso āghāto appaccayo anabhiraddhi. Tattha ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘yaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ sikkhataṃ aññamaññassa vacīsaṃhāro uppanno diṭṭhipaḷāso cetaso āghāto appaccayo anabhiraddhi, taṃ jānamāno samaṇo garaheyyā’ti samāno (sī. ka.). Sammā byākaramāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ byākareyya – ‘yaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ sikkhataṃ aññamaññassa vacīsaṃhāro uppanno diṭṭhipaḷāso cetaso āghāto appaccayo anabhiraddhi, taṃ jānamāno samaṇo garaheyyāti. Etaṃ panāvuso, dhammaṃ appahāya nibbānaṃ sacchikareyyā’ti. Sammā byākaramāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ byākareyya – ‘etaṃ, āvuso, dhammaṃ appahāya na nibbānaṃ sacchikareyyā’ti.

‘‘Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yaṃ bhikkhuṃ suvacataraṃ maññeyyātha, so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘yaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ sikkhataṃ aññamaññassa vacīsaṃhāro uppanno diṭṭhipaḷāso cetaso āghāto appaccayo anabhiraddhi, taṃ jānamāno samaṇo garaheyyā’ti. Sammā byākaramāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ byākareyya – ‘yaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ sikkhataṃ aññamaññassa vacīsaṃhāro uppanno diṭṭhipaḷāso cetaso āghāto appaccayo anabhiraddhi taṃ jānamāno samaṇo garaheyyāti. Etaṃ panāvuso, dhammaṃ appahāya nibbānaṃ sacchikareyyā’ti. Sammā byākaramāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ byākareyya – ‘etaṃ kho, āvuso, dhammaṃ appahāya na nibbānaṃ sacchikareyyā’’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ pare evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘āyasmatā no ete bhikkhū akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhāpitā’ti? Sammā byākaramāno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ byākareyya – ‘idhāhaṃ, āvuso, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃ, tassa me bhagavā dhammaṃ desesi, tāhaṃ dhammaṃ sutvā tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhāsiṃ. Taṃ te bhikkhū dhammaṃ sutvā akusalā vuṭṭhahiṃsu, kusale patiṭṭhahiṃsū’ti. Evaṃ byākaramāno kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na ceva attānaṃ ukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaroti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Kintisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
40. “While you are training in concord, with mutual appreciation, without disputing, there might arise mutual verbal friction (*vacīsaṃhāro*), domineering views (*diṭṭhipaḷāso*), mental annoyance (*cetaso āghāto*), bitterness (*appaccayo*), and dejection (*anabhiraddhi*). Then whichever *bhikkhu* you think is the most reasonable of those who side together on the one part should be approached and addressed thus: ‘While we were training in concord, friend (*āvuso*), with mutual appreciation, without disputing, there arose mutual verbal friction, domineering views, mental annoyance, bitterness, and dejection. If the Recluse (*samaṇo*) knew, would he censure that?’ Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhu* would answer thus: ‘While we were training in concord, friend (*āvuso*), with mutual appreciation, without disputing, there arose mutual verbal friction, domineering views, mental annoyance, bitterness, and dejection. If the Recluse knew, he would censure that. But, friend (*āvuso*), without abandoning that thing (*dhammaṃ*), can one realise *Nibbāna*?’ Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhu* would answer thus: ‘Friend, without abandoning that thing (*dhammaṃ*), one cannot realise *Nibbāna*.’

“Then whichever *bhikkhu* you think is the most reasonable of those who side together on the opposite part should be approached and addressed thus: ‘While we were training in concord, friend (*āvuso*), with mutual appreciation, without disputing, there arose mutual verbal friction, domineering views, mental annoyance, bitterness, and dejection. If the Recluse knew, would he censure that?’ Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhu* would answer thus: ‘While we were training in concord, friend (*āvuso*), with mutual appreciation, without disputing, there arose mutual verbal friction, domineering views, mental annoyance, bitterness, and dejection. If the Recluse knew, he would censure that. But, friend (*āvuso*), without abandoning that thing (*dhammaṃ*), can one realise *Nibbāna*?’ Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhu* would answer thus: ‘Friend (*āvuso*), without abandoning that thing, one cannot realise *Nibbāna*.’

“If others should ask that *bhikkhu* thus: ‘Was it the venerable one (*āyasmatā*) who made those *bhikkhus* emerge from the unwholesome (*akusalā*) and established them in the wholesome (*kusale*)?’ Answering rightly, *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhu* would answer thus: ‘Here, friend (*āvuso*), I went to the Blessed One (*Bhagavā*). The Blessed One taught me the Dhamma. Having heard that Dhamma, I spoke to those *bhikkhus*. The *bhikkhus* heard that Dhamma, and they emerged from the unwholesome and became established in the wholesome.’ Answering thus, *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhu* neither exalts himself nor disparages others; he answers in accordance with the *Dhamma* in such a way that nothing which provides a ground for censure can be legitimately deduced from his assertion.”

Thus spoke the Lord (*Bhagavā*). Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Kinti-sutta, the third, is finished.
commentary_pali:
40.Vacīsaṃhāroti vacanasañcāro. Imehi kathitaṃ amūsaṃ antaraṃ paveseyya, tumhe imehi idañcidañca vuttāti amūhi kathitaṃ imesaṃ antaraṃ paveseyyāti attho. Diṭṭhipaḷāsotiādīhi cittassa anārādhaniyabhāvo kathito. Taṃ jānamāno samāno garaheyyāti taṃ satthā jānamāno samāno nindeyya amheti. Etaṃpanāvuso, dhammanti etaṃ kalahabhaṇḍanadhammaṃ.

Tañceti taṃ saññattikārakaṃ bhikkhuṃ. Evaṃ byākareyyāti mayā ete suddhante patiṭṭhāpitāti avatvā yena kāraṇena saññatti katā, tadeva dassento evaṃ byākareyya. Tāhaṃ dhammaṃ sutvāti ettha dhammoti sāraṇīyadhammo adhippeto. Na ceva attānantiādīsu ‘‘brahmalokappamāṇo hesa aggi uṭṭhāsi, ko etamaññatra mayā nibbāpetuṃ samattho’’ti hi vadanto attānaṃ ukkaṃseti nāma. ‘‘Ettakā janā vicaranti, okāso laddhuṃ na sakkā, ekopi ettakamattaṃ nibbāpetuṃ samattho nāma natthī’’ti vadamāno paraṃ vambheti nāma. Tadubhayampesa na karoti. Dhammo panettha sammāsambuddhassa byākaraṇaṃ, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ saññattikaraṇaṃ anudhammo, tadeva byākaroti nāma. Na ca koci sahadhammikoti añño cassa koci sahetuko parehi vutto vādo vā anuvādo vā garahitabbabhāvaṃ āgacchanto nāma natthi. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Tañce Evaṃ byākareyyā Tāhaṃ dhammaṃ sutvā dhammo Na ceva attāna Dhammo anudhammo, byākaroti nāma. Na ca koci sahadhammiko

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Kintisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
40. *Vacīsaṃhāro* means vacanasañcāro (speech intercourse).

imehi kathitaṃ amūsaṃ antaraṃ paveseyya, tumhe imehi idañcidañca vuttāti amūhi kathitaṃ imesaṃ antaraṃ paveseyyāti attho.
