(If) they should introduce what was spoken by these into those, (saying) "You have been told such and such by these," and (then) introduce what was spoken by those into these, that is the meaning.

*Diṭṭhipaḷāso* and so on, the state of mind that is not easily pleased is described.

*Taṃ jānamāno samāno garaheyyā* means that the teacher, knowing, being the same, would censure us.

*Etaṃ* *panāvuso, dhamma* means this is a strife-and-contention teaching.

*Tañce* that Saññattikārakaṃ Bhikkhuṃ, that monk who makes known.

*Evaṃ Byākareyyā* means not having said, "I have established these in the pure doctrine," but showing that by which reason the Saññatti was made, thus should he explain.

*Tāhaṃ Dhammaṃ Sutvā* here, *dhammo* means the *sāraṇīyadhammo* is intended.

*Na Ceva Attāna* and so on, "This fire arose measuring the Brahmaloka, who is able to extinguish it other than me?", he praises himself, it is said.

"So many people are wandering about, an opportunity cannot be obtained, even one is not able to extinguish this much," he flatters others, it is said.

He does not do both.

*Dhammo* here is the Sammāsambuddha's explanation, the Saññattikaraṇa of those monks is *Anudhammo,* thus he explains, it is said.

*Na Ca Koci Sahadhammiko* means another who is a Sahatuko, a Vādo or Anuvādo spoken by others, approaching a state of being censured, there is not, it is said.

The rest is clear throughout.

*Tañce* *Evaṃ Byākareyyā* *Tāhaṃ Dhammaṃ Sutvā* *Dhammo* *Na Ceva Attāna* *Dhammo* *Anudhammo,* *Byākaroti Nāma.*
*Na Ca Koci Sahadhammiko* Papañcasūdaniyā Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya Kintisuttavaṇṇanā Niṭṭhitā.

mula_pali: 41. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati sāmagāme. Tena kho pana samayena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto nāthaputto (sī. pī.) pāvāyaṃ adhunākālaṅkato kālakato (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) hoti. Tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā dveḷhakajātā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti – ‘‘na tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāsi, ahaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāmi. Kiṃ tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānissasi! Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi, ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Sahitaṃ me, asahitaṃ te. Purevacanīyaṃ pacchā avaca , pacchāvacanīyaṃ pure avaca. Adhiciṇṇaṃ aviciṇṇaṃ (sī. pī.) te viparāvattaṃ. Āropito te vādo. Niggahitosi, cara vādappamokkhāya; nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī’’ti. Vadhoyeva kho vadhoyeveko (syā. kaṃ. ka.) maññe nigaṇṭhesu nāṭaputtiyesu vattati. Yepi nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā tepi nigaṇṭhesu nāṭaputtiyesu nibbinnarūpā nibbindarūpā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) virattarūpā paṭivānarūpā yathā taṃ durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe.
mula_english:
41.
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the Sakyan country at Sāmagāma.

Now on that occasion, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta had just died in Pāvā.

On his death the Nigaṇṭhas split into two factions. They kept arguing, quarreling, & disputing, stabbing one another with weapons of the mouth: “You don’t understand this *Dhamma*-*Vinaya*. I understand this *Dhamma*-*Vinaya*.

How can you understand this *Dhamma*-*Vinaya*? You’re practising the wrong way. I’m practicing the right way.

I’m being consistent. You’re inconsistent.

What should have been said first you said last, what should have been said last you said first.

What you cogitated so long has been turned inside out.

Your position has been overthrown.

You’re trapped, so go try to release your position or disentangle yourself if you can!”

Nothing but slaughter, as it were, was being committed among the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭa-sons.

And his white-clothed lay disciples were disgusted, dismayed, and disappointed with the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta’s pupils, as they were with his badly proclaimed and badly expounded *Dhamma* and Discipline, which was unemancipating, unconducive to peace, expounded by one not fully enlightened, and was now with its shrine broken, left without a refuge.
commentary_pali:
41.Evaṃme sutanti sāmagāmasuttaṃ. Tattha sāmagāmeti sāmākānaṃ ussannattā evaṃladdhanāme gāme. Adhunā kālaṅkatoti sampati kālaṃ kato. Dvedhikajātāti dvejjhajātā dvebhāgajātā. Bhaṇḍanādīsu bhaṇḍanaṃ pubbabhāgakalaho, taṃ daṇḍādānādivasena paṇṇattivītikkamavasena ca vaddhitaṃ kalaho, ‘‘na tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāsī’’tiādikaṃ viruddhavacanaṃ vivādo. Vitudantāti vitujjantā. Sahitaṃ meti mama vacanaṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ. Adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvattanti yaṃ tava adhiciṇṇaṃ cirakālasevanavasena paguṇaṃ, taṃ mama vādaṃ āgamma nivattaṃ. Āropito te vādoti tuyhaṃ upari mayā doso āropito. Cara vādappamokkhāyāti bhattapuṭaṃ ādāya taṃ taṃ upasaṅkamitvā vādappamokkhatthāya uttari pariyesamāno cara. Nibbeṭhehi vāti atha mayā āropitavādato attānaṃ mocehi. Sace pahosīti sace sakkosi. Vadhoyevāti maraṇameva.

Nāṭaputtiyesūti nāṭaputtassa antevāsikesu. Nibbinnarūpāti ukkaṇṭhitasabhāvā, abhivādanādīni na karonti. Virattarūpāti vigatapemā. Paṭivānarūpāti tesaṃ nipaccakiriyato nivattasabhāvā. Yathā tanti yathā ca durakkhātādisabhāve dhammavinaye nibbinnavirattapaṭivānarūpehi bhavitabbaṃ, tatheva jātāti attho. Durakkhāteti dukkathite. Duppavediteti duviññāpite. Anupasamasaṃvattaniketi rāgādīnaṃ upasamaṃ kātuṃ asamattho. Bhinnathūpeti bhinnapatiṭṭhe. Ettha hi nāṭaputtova nesaṃ patiṭṭhena thūpo, so pana bhinno mato. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘bhinnathūpe’’ti. Appaṭisaraṇeti tasseva abhāvena paṭisaraṇavirahite.

Nāṭaputtiyesū Nibbinnarūpā Virattarūpā Paṭivānarūpā Yathā ta Durakkhāte Duppavedite Anupasamasaṃvattanike Bhinnathūpe Appaṭisaraṇe

Nanu cāyaṃ nāṭaputto nāḷandavāsiko, so kasmā pāvāyaṃ kālaṃkatoti. So kira upālinā gahapatinā paṭividdhasaccena dasahi gāthāhi bhāsite buddhaguṇe sutvā uṇhaṃ lohitaṃ chaḍḍesi. Atha naṃ aphāsukaṃ gahetvā pāvaṃ agamaṃsu, so tattha kālamakāsi. Kālaṃ kurumāno ca ‘‘mama laddhi aniyyānikā sārarahitā, mayaṃ tāva naṭṭhā, avasesajano mā apāyapūrako ahosi . Sace panāhaṃ ‘mama sāsanaṃ aniyyānika’nti vakkhāmi, na saddahissanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ dvepi jane na ekanīhārena uggaṇhāpeyyaṃ, te mamaccayena aññamaññaṃ vivadissanti. Satthā taṃ vivādaṃ paṭicca ekaṃ dhammakathaṃ kathessati, tato te sāsanassa mahantabhāvaṃ jātissantī’’ti.

Atha naṃ eko antevāsiko upasaṅkamitvā āha ‘‘bhante, tumhe dubbalā, mayhaṃ imasmiṃ dhamme sāraṃ ācikkhatha ācariyappamāṇa’’nti. Āvuso, tvaṃ mamaccayena sassatanti gaṇheyyāsīti. Aparopi taṃ upasaṅkami, taṃ ucchedaṃ gaṇhāpesi. Evaṃ dvepi jane ekaladdhike akatvā bahū nānānīhārena uggaṇhāpetvā kālamakāsi. Te tassa sarīrakiccaṃ katvā sannipatitvā aññamaññaṃ pucchiṃsu ‘‘kassāvuso, ācariyo sāramācikkhī’’ti? Eko uṭṭhahitvā mayhanti āha. Kiṃ ācikkhīti? Sassatanti. Aparo taṃ paṭibāhitvā mayhaṃ sāraṃ ācikkhīti āha. Evaṃ sabbe ‘‘mayhaṃ sāraṃ ācikkhi, ahaṃ jeṭṭhako’’ti aññamaññaṃ vivādaṃ vaḍḍhetvā akkose ceva paribhāse ca hatthapādapahārādīni ca pavattetvā ekamaggena dve agacchantā nānādisāsu pakkamiṃsu, ekacce gihī ahesuṃ.

Bhagavato pana dharamānakālepi bhikkhusaṅghe vivādo na uppajji. Satthā hi tesaṃ vivādakāraṇe uppannamatteyeva sayaṃ vā gantvā te vā bhikkhū pakkosāpetvā khanti mettā paṭisaṅkhā avihiṃsā sāraṇīyadhammesu ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ kathetvā vivādaṃ vūpasameti. Evaṃ dharamānopi saṅghassa patiṭṭhāva ahosi. Parinibbāyamānopi avivādakāraṇaṃ katvāva parinibbāyi. Bhagavatā hi sutte desitā cattāro mahāpadesā (a. ni. 4.180; dī. ni. 2.187) yāvajjadivasā bhikkhūnaṃ patiṭṭhā ca avassayo ca. Tathā khandhake desitā cattāro mahāpadesā (mahāva. 305) sutte vuttāni cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni (a. ni. 4.42) ca. Tenevāha – ‘‘yo vo mayā, ānanda, dhammo ca vinayo ca desito paññatto, so vo mamaccayena satthā’’ti (dī. ni. 2.216).
commentary_english:
41. It is like this, the *Sāmagāmasutta*.

There, *sāmagāme* means in a village named thus, because of the abundance of *sāmāka* grass.

*Adhunā kālaṅkato* means now he has died.

*Dvedhikajātā* is *dvejjhajātā dvebhāgajātā*.

Among strife, etc., *bhaṇḍanaṃ* is a preliminary quarrel; that which is increased by means of punishment, giving, etc., and by means of transgression of the precepts is *kalaho*; the contradictory speech "you do not know this *dharmavinaya*" is *vivādo*.

*Vitudantā* means *vitujjantā*.

*Sahitaṃ me* means my speech is connected with the meaning *atthasaṃhitaṃ*.

*Adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvatta* means that which is habitual to you, strengthened by long practice, that has turned back, having come to my argument *vādaṃ*.

*Āropito te vādo* means a fault *doso* has been imputed by me upon you.

*Cara vādappamokkhāyā* means, having taken a food packet, wander around approaching them to seek release from argument, *vādappamokkha*.

*Nibbeṭhehi vā* means then free yourself from the imputed argument *āropitavādato*.

*Sace pahosī* means if you are able *sakkosi*.

*Vadhoyevā* means it is death itself *maraṇameva*.

*Nāṭaputtiyesū* means among the disciples *antevāsikesu* of *Nāṭaputta*.

*Nibbinnarūpā* means having an agitated nature *ukkaṇṭhitasabhāvā*, they do not perform salutations *abhivādanādīni*.

*Virattarūpā* means with departed love *vigatapemā*.

*Paṭivānarūpā* means having a nature turned away from their prostrations *nipaccakiriyato nivattasabhāvā*.

*Yathā ta* means just as, in a doctrine and discipline *dhammavinaye* of bad exposition etc. *durakkhātādi*, one should be with a nature disgusted, detached and turned away *nibbinnavirattapaṭivānarūpehi*, so is the meaning *attho* of being born *jātāti*.

*Durakkhāte* means badly spoken *dukkathite*.

*Duppavedite* means badly explained *duviññāpite*.

*Anupasamasaṃvattanike* means incapable *asamattho* of calming passions *rāgādīnaṃ* .

*Bhinnathūpe* means with a broken support *bhinnapatiṭṭhe*.

Here, the support *thūpo* is like *Nāṭaputta* for them, but that is considered broken *bhinno mato*.

Therefore it was said, "with a broken support *bhinnathūpe*."

*Appaṭisaraṇe* means without refuge *paṭisaraṇavirahite* due to the absence *abhāvena* of that itself *tasseva*.

Among the *Nāṭaputtiyas*, disgusted in appearance *nibbinnarūpā*, detached in appearance *virattarūpā*, turned away in appearance *paṭivānarūpā*, just as *yathā ta*, badly proclaimed *durakkhāte*, badly taught *duppavedite*, not conducive to calm *anupasamasaṃvattanike*, with a broken stupa *bhinnathūpe*, without refuge *appaṭisaraṇe*.

Why did this *Nāṭaputta*, a resident of *Nāḷanda*, die at *Pāvā*?

It is said that having heard the qualities of the Buddha *buddhaguṇe* spoken *bhāsite* in ten verses *gāthāhi* with penetrating truth *paṭividdhasaccena* by the householder *gahapatinā* *Upāli*, he vomited hot blood *uṇhaṃ lohitaṃ chaḍḍesi*.

Then, having taken him unwell *aphāsukaṃ gahetvā*, they went to *Pāvaṃ*, and there he died *kālamakāsi*.

And while dying *kālaṃ kurumāno*, he said, "My doctrine *laddhi* is not a means of escape *aniyyānikā*, it is without essence *sārarahitā*, we are ruined *naṭṭhā*, may the remaining people *avasesajano* not be filled with misery *apāyapūrako*.

If I were to say, "My teaching *sāsanaṃ* is not a means of escape *aniyyānikā*," they will not believe *saddahissanti*.

Why should I not have two people *dvepi jane* learn *uggaṇhāpeyyaṃ* without one method *ekanīhārena*; they will dispute *vivadissanti* with each other *aññamaññaṃ* at my death *mamaccayena*.

The teacher *satthā*, having regarded that dispute *vivādaṃ paṭicca*, will tell one *dhamma* talk *kathaṃ*, then they will realize *jātissantī* the greatness *mahantabhāvaṃ* of the teaching *sāsanassa*."
Then, a certain resident approached him and said:
“Venerable sir, you are weak. Please explain to me the essence of this *dharma*, according to your teacher's authority.”
“Friend, you should take it that after my passing, the *dharma* is eternal.”
Another approached him and led him to grasp annihilation.
Thus, without making even two people of like mind, he passed away after causing many to learn in various ways.
Having performed his funeral rites, they gathered together and asked each other, "Friend, to whom did the teacher explain the essence?" One stood up and said, "To me."
"What did he explain?" "Eternality."
Another refuted him and said, "He explained the essence to me."
Thus, all of them, "He explained the essence to me, I am the elder," having stirred up a dispute with each other, and having set in motion abuse, insults, and beatings with hands and feet, not going together on one path, they departed in various directions, some becoming householders.

Even while the Blessed One was living, there was no dispute in the community of monks (*bhikkhusaṃgha*).
Indeed, the teacher himself, as soon as a cause of dispute arose among them, either by going himself or by having those monks summoned, would explain one reason in the teachings leading to mindfulness, gentleness, loving-kindness, reflection, non-violence, and conciliation, and would pacify the dispute.
Thus, even while living, he was the support of the community (*saṃgha*).
Even while passing into complete extinction (*parinirvāyamāṇopi*), he passed away after making a cause of non-dispute.
For the Blessed One taught in the *sūtras* the four great references (*cattāro mahāpadesā*) (A.
N. 4.180; D.
N. 2.187) that are until this day the support and refuge of the monks.
Similarly, in the *khandhakas* are taught the four great references (Mahāva.
305) and in the *sūtras* are stated the four ways of answering questions (*cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni*) (A.
N. 4.42).
Therefore, he said: "Ānanda, the *dharma* (teaching) and the discipline (*vinaya*) that I have taught and established will be your teacher after my passing away" (D.
N. 2.216).

mula_pali:
42. Atha kho cundo samaṇuddeso pāvāyaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭho vassaṃvuttho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) yena sāmagāmo yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho cundo samaṇuddeso āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘nigaṇṭho, bhante, nāṭaputto pāvāyaṃ adhunākālaṅkato. Tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā…pe… bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando cundaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘atthi kho idaṃ, āvuso cunda, kathāpābhataṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Āyāma, āvuso cunda, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ bhagavato ārocessāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho cundo samaṇuddeso āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi.

Atha kho āyasmā ca ānando cundo ca samaṇuddeso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ayaṃ, bhante, cundo samaṇuddeso evamāha – ‘nigaṇṭho , bhante, nāṭaputto pāvāyaṃ adhunākālaṅkato. Tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā…pe… bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘māheva bhagavato accayena saṅghe vivādo uppajji; svāssa so (sī. pī.), svāyaṃ (ka.) vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussāna’’’nti.

so (sī. pī.), svāyaṃ (ka.)
mula_english:
42. Then the novice Cuṇḍa, who had spent the Rains at Pāvā, went to the venerable Ānanda at Sāmagāma; having approached, he bowed down to the venerable Ānanda and sat down at a respectful distance.

Sitting at a respectful distance, the novice Cuṇḍa said to the venerable Ānanda: "Venerable sir, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta has just died in Pāvā. With his passing away, the Nigaṇṭhas have split, divided into two...and now [their] stūpas are broken, left without a refuge."

When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the novice Cuṇḍa: "Friend Cuṇḍa, this is a matter worth reporting to the Blessed One. Let's go to the Blessed One; having approached, we will inform him of this matter."

"As you say, venerable sir," the novice Cuṇḍa responded to the venerable Ānanda.

Then the venerable Ānanda and the novice Cuṇḍa went to the Blessed One; having approached, they bowed down to the Blessed One and sat down at a respectful distance.

Sitting at a respectful distance, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, this novice Cuṇḍa said: 'Venerable sir, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta has just died in Pāvā. With his passing away, the Nigaṇṭhas have split, divided into two...and now [their] stūpas are broken, left without a refuge.'

Venerable sir, it occurred to me: 'Let no dispute arise in the *saṃgha* after the Blessed One's passing; such a dispute would be for the harm of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the detriment, harm, and suffering of gods and humans.'"
commentary_pali:
42.Athakho cundo samaṇuddesoti ayaṃ thero dhammasenāpatissa kaniṭṭhabhātiko. Taṃ bhikkhū anupasampannakāle cundo samaṇuddesoti samudācaritvā therakālepi tatheva samudācariṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘cundo samaṇuddeso’’ti. Upasaṅkamīti kasmā upasaṅkami? Nāṭaputte kira kālaṃkate jambudīpe manussā tattha tattha kathaṃ pavattayiṃsu – ‘‘nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto eko satthāti paññāyittha, tassa kālakiriyāya sāvakānaṃ evarūpo vivādo jāto, samaṇo pana gotamo jambudīpe cando viya sūriyo viya ca pākaṭoyeva, kīdiso nu kho samaṇe gotame parinibbute sāvakānaṃ vivādo bhavissatī’’ti. Thero taṃ kathaṃ sutvā cintesi – ‘‘imaṃ kathaṃ gahetvā dasabalassa ārocessāmi, satthā ca etaṃ atthuppattiṃ katvā ekaṃ desanaṃ kathessatī’’ti. So nikkhamitvā yena sāmagāmo, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami. Ujumeva bhagavato santikaṃ agantvā yenassa upajjhāyo āyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamīti attho. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘upajjhāyo me mahāpañño, so imaṃ sāsanaṃ satthu ārocessati, atha satthā tadanurūpaṃ dhammaṃ desessatī’’ti. Kathāpābhatanti kathāmūlaṃ, mūlañhi pābhatanti vuccati. Yathāha –

‘‘Appakenapi medhāvī, pābhatena vicakkhaṇo;

Samuṭṭhāpeti attānaṃ, aṇuṃ aggiṃva sandhama’’nti. (jā. 2.1.4);

Dassanāyāti dassanatthāya. Kiṃ paniminā bhagavā na diṭṭhapubboti? No na diṭṭhapubbo, ayañhi āyasmā divā nava vāre rattiṃ nava vāreti ekāhaṃ aṭṭhārasa vāre upaṭṭhānameva gacchati. Divasassa pana satakkhattuṃ vā sahassakkhattuṃ vā gantukāmo samānopi na akāraṇā gacchati, ekaṃ pañhuddhāraṃ gahetvāva gacchati. So taṃdivasaṃ tena gantukāmo evamāha.

Dassanāyā

Ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānanti ekasmiṃ vihāre saṅghamajjhe uppanno vivādo kathaṃ devamanussānaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvattati? Kosambakakkhandhake (mahāva. 451) viya hi dvīsu bhikkhūsu vivādaṃ āpannesu tasmiṃ vihāre tesaṃ antevāsikā vivadanti, tesaṃ ovādaṃ gaṇhanto bhikkhunisaṅgho vivadati, tato tesaṃ upaṭṭhākā vivadanti, atha manussānaṃ ārakkhadevatā dve koṭṭhāsā honti. Tattha dhammavādīnaṃ ārakkhadevatā dhammavādiniyo honti, adhammavādīnaṃ adhammavādiniyo honti. Tato tāsaṃ ārakkhadevatānaṃ mittā bhummadevatā bhijjanti. Evaṃ paramparāya yāva brahmalokā ṭhapetvā ariyasāvake sabbe devamanussā dve koṭṭhāsā honti. Dhammavādīhi pana adhammavādinova bahutarā honti, tato yaṃ bahūhi gahitaṃ, taṃ gaṇhanti. Dhammaṃ vissajjetvā bahutarāva adhammaṃ gaṇhanti. Te adhammaṃ pūretvā viharantā apāye nibbattanti. Evaṃ ekasmiṃ vihāre saṅghamajjhe uppanno vivādo bahūnaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya hoti.

Ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussāna
commentary_english:
42.
Now, Cunda the novice, was the younger brother of the Dharma-commander.

The monks addressed him as Cunda the novice both when he had not yet received the higher ordination and continued to do so even after he became a senior monk.

Therefore it was said, “Cunda the novice.”

Why did he approach? It seems that when Nāṭaputta died in Jambudīpa, people were discussing it in various places, saying, "Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta was considered to be the one teacher, but after his death, such a dispute arose among his disciples. But the renunciate Gotama is well-known in Jambudīpa, like the moon and the sun. What kind of dispute will arise among the disciples when the renunciate Gotama has attained final *nirvāṇa*?”

Having heard this discussion, the senior monk thought, "I will take this matter and report it to the one with ten powers (i.e. the Buddha), and the Teacher, having considered this event, will deliver a discourse."

He left and went to Sāmagāma, where the venerable Ānanda was.

The meaning is that instead of going directly to the Blessed One, he went to the venerable Ānanda, who was his preceptor.

It was thus in his mind, "My preceptor is very wise, he will report this teaching to the Teacher, and then the Teacher will teach the *dharma* accordingly."

The meaning of "**kathāpābhata**" is the basis of the story, for the basis is indeed called *pābhata*.

As it was said:

"Even with a small gift, the wise,
skilled in giving,
can build themselves up,
like a small fire fanned by the wind."

(Jā. 2.1.4);

The meaning of "**dassanāyā**" is for the sake of seeing.

Did the Blessed One not see [Ānanda] before? No, it is not that he had not seen him before, for this venerable one would attend him eighteen times a day, nine times during the day and nine times during the night.

But although he was willing to go a hundred or a thousand times a day, he would not go without a reason, he would go only after taking up a question.

Thus, being willing to go to him that day, he said this:

The meaning of "**ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussāna**" is: How does a dispute that has arisen in a monastery, in the midst of the *saṃgha*, lead to harm and suffering for gods and humans? Just as in the Kosambaka Khandhaka (Mahāva. 451), when a dispute arose between two monks, their disciples argued in that monastery, and the community of nuns, taking their advice, argued, then their supporters argued, and then the guardian deities of the people were divided into two factions.

There, the guardian deities of those who speak the Dharma are those who speak the Dharma, and the guardian deities of those who do not speak the Dharma are those who do not speak the Dharma.

Then the friendly earth deities of those guardian deities are divided.

Thus, in succession, up to the Brahmā world, all the gods and humans, except for the noble disciples, are divided into two factions.

But those who do not speak the Dharma are more numerous than those who speak the Dharma, and therefore they take what is seized by the many.

Having abandoned the Dharma, most take what is not the Dharma.

Having filled themselves with *adharma*, they live in suffering and are reborn in the lower realms.

Thus, a dispute that has arisen in a monastery, in the midst of the *saṃgha*, leads to harm and suffering for many.

The meaning of "**ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussāna**" is...

mula_pali: 43. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, ānanda, ye vo mayā dhammā abhiññā desitā, seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā cattāro sammappadhānā cattāro iddhipādā pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅgā ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, passasi no tvaṃ, ānanda, imesu dhammesu dvepi bhikkhū nānāvāde’’ti? ‘‘Ye me, bhante, dhammā bhagavatā abhiññā desitā, seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā cattāro sammappadhānā cattāro iddhipādā pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅgā ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, nāhaṃ passāmi imesu dhammesu dvepi bhikkhū nānāvāde. Ye ca kho santi ca kho (syā. kaṃ.), santi ca (ka.), bhante, puggalā bhagavantaṃ patissayamānarūpā viharanti tepi bhagavato accayena saṅghe vivādaṃ janeyyuṃ ajjhājīve vā adhipātimokkhe vā. Svāssa sossa (sī. pī.), svāyaṃ (ka.) vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussāna’’nti. Appamattako so, ānanda, vivādo yadidaṃ – ajjhājīve vā adhipātimokkhe vā. Magge vā hi, ānanda, paṭipadāya vā saṅghe vivādo uppajjamāno uppajjeyya; svāssa vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ.
mula_english:
43. “What do you think, Ānanda? Those doctrines that have been taught by me, having directly known them, that is to say, the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*), the four right exertions (*cattāro sammappadhānā*), the four bases of spiritual power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), the five faculties (*pañcindriyāṇi*), the five powers (*pañca balāni*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*satta bojjhaṅgā*), and the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo*), do you see, Ānanda, even two *bhikkhus* who have differing views about these doctrines?”

“Venerable sir, those doctrines that have been taught by the Blessed One, having directly known them, that is to say, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right exertions, the four bases of spiritual power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the Noble Eightfold Path, I do not see even two *bhikkhus* who have differing views about these doctrines.

But, venerable sir, there are persons who live deferential towards the Blessed One who might, when the Blessed One has passed away, create a dispute in the *saṃgha* about livelihood (*ajjhājīve*) or about the *Pāṭimokkha* (*adhipātimokkhe*). Such a dispute would be for the harm and unhappiness of many people, for the loss, harm, and suffering of gods and humans.”

“A dispute about livelihood (*ajjhājīve*) or about the *Pāṭimokkha* (*adhipātimokkhe*) would be trifling, Ānanda.

But should a dispute arise in the *saṃgha* about the path (*magge*) or the practice (*paṭipadāya*), such a dispute would be for the harm and unhappiness of many people, for the loss, harm, and suffering of gods and humans.”
commentary_pali:
43.Abhiññā desitāti mahābodhimūle nisinnena paccakkhaṃ katvā paveditā. Patissayamānarūpā viharantīti upanissāya viharanti. Bhagavatoaccayenāti etarahi bhagavantaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā sagāravā viharanti, tumhākaṃ, bhante, uggatejatāya durāsadatāya vivādaṃ janetuṃ na sakkonti, bhagavato pana accayena vivādaṃ janeyyunti vadati. Yattha pana taṃ vivādaṃ janeyyuṃ, taṃ dassento ajjhājīve vā adhipātimokkhe vāti āha. Tattha ajjhājīveti ājīvahetu ājīvakāraṇā – ‘‘bhikkhu uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapati āpatti pārājikassā’’tiādinā (pari. 287) nayena parivāre paññattāni cha sikkhāpadāni, tāni ṭhapetvā sesāni sabbasikkhāpadāni adhipātimokkhaṃ nāma. Appamattako so ānandāti ajjhājīvaṃ adhipātimokkhañca ārabbha uppannavivādo nāma yasmā parassa kathāyapi attano dhammatāyapi sallakkhetvā suppajaho hoti, tasmā ‘‘appamattako’’ti vutto.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – idhekacco ‘‘na sakkā uttarimanussadhammaṃ anullapantena kiñci laddhu’’ntiādīni cintetvā ājīvahetu uttarimanussadhammaṃ vā ullapati sañcarittaṃ vā āpajjati, yo te vihāre vasati, so bhikkhu arahātiādinā nayena sāmantajappanaṃ vā karoti, agilāno vā attano atthāya paṇītabhojanāni viññāpetvā bhuñjati, bhikkhunī vā pana tāni viññāpetvā pāṭidesanīyaṃ āpajjati, yo koci dukkaṭavatthukaṃ yaṃkiñci sūpodanaviññattimeva vā karoti, aññataraṃ vā pana paṇṇattivītikkamaṃ karonto viharati, tamenaṃ sabrahmacārī evaṃ sañjānanti – ‘‘kiṃ imassa iminā lābhena laddhena, yo sāsane pabbajitvā micchājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti, paṇṇattivītikkamaṃ karotī’’ti. Attano dhammatāyapissa evaṃ hoti – ‘‘kissa mayhaṃ iminā lābhena, yvāhaṃ evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitvā micchājīvena jīvikaṃ kappemi, paṇṇattivītikkamaṃ karomī’’ti sallakkhetvā tato oramati. Evaṃ parassa kathāyapi attano dhammatāyapi sallakkhetvā suppajaho hoti. Tena bhagavā ‘‘appamattako’’ti āha.

Magge vā hi, ānanda, paṭipadāya vāti lokuttaramaggaṃ patvā vivādo nāma sabbaso vūpasammati, natthi adhigatamaggānaṃ vivādo. Pubbabhāgamaggaṃ pana pubbabhāgapaṭipadañca sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Magge vā hi, ānanda, paṭipadāya vā

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – evaṃ bhikkhuṃ manussā lokuttaradhamme sambhāventi. So saddhivihārikādayo āgantvā vanditvā ṭhite pucchati ‘‘kiṃ āgatatthā’’ti. Manasikātabbakammaṭṭhānaṃ pucchituṃ, bhanteti. Nisīdatha, khaṇeneva arahattaṃ pāpetuṃ samatthakammaṭṭhānakathaṃ ācikkhissāmīti vatvā vadati – ‘‘idha bhikkhu attano vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pavisitvā nisinno mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ manasi karoti, tassa taṃ manasikaroto obhāso uppajjati. Ayaṃ paṭhamamaggo nāma. So dutiyaṃ obhāsañāṇaṃ nibbatteti, dutiyamaggo adhigato hoti, evaṃ tatiyañca catutthañca. Ettāvatā maggappatto ceva phalappatto ca hotī’’ti. Atha te bhikkhū ‘‘akhīṇāsavo nāma evaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathetuṃ na sakkoti, addhāyaṃ khīṇāsavo’’ti niṭṭhaṃ gacchanti.

So aparena samayena kālaṃ karoti. Samantā bhikkhācāragāmehi manussā āgantvā pucchanti ‘‘kenaci, bhante, thero pañhaṃ pucchito’’ti. Upāsakā pubbeva therena pañho kathito amhākanti. Te pupphamaṇḍapaṃ pupphakūṭāgāraṃ sajjetvā suvaṇṇena akkhipidhānamukhapidhānādiṃ karitvā gandhamālādīhi pūjetvā sattāhaṃ sādhukīḷikaṃ kīḷetvā jhāpetvā aṭṭhīni ādāya cetiyaṃ karonti. Aññe āgantukā vihāraṃ āgantvā pāde dhovitvā ‘‘mahātheraṃ passissāma, kahaṃ, āvuso, mahāthero’’ti pucchanti. Parinibbuto, bhanteti. Dukkaraṃ, āvuso, therena kataṃ maggaphalāni nibbattentena, pañhaṃ pucchittha, āvusoti. Bhikkhūnaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathento iminā niyāmena kathesi, bhanteti. Na eso, āvuso, maggo, vipassanupakkileso nāmesa, na tumhe jānittha, puthujjano, āvuso, theroti. Te kalahaṃ karontā uṭṭhahitvā ‘‘sakalavihāre bhikkhū ca bhikkhācāragāmesu manussā ca na jānanti, tumheyeva jānātha. Kataramaggena tumhe āgatā, kiṃ vo vihāradvāre cetiyaṃ na diṭṭha’’nti. Evaṃvādīnaṃ pana bhikkhūnaṃ sataṃ vā, hotu sahassaṃ vā, yāva taṃ laddhiṃ nappajahanti, saggopi maggopi vāritoyeva.

Aparopi tādisova kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathento evaṃ katheti – citteneva tīsu uddhanesu tīṇi kapallāni āropetvā heṭṭhā aggiṃ katvā citteneva attano dvattiṃsākāraṃ uppāṭetvā kapallesu pakkhipitvā citteneva daṇḍakena parivattetvā parivattetvā bhajjitabbaṃ, yā jhāyamāne chārikā hoti, sā mukhavātena palāsetabbā. Ettakena dhūtapāpo nāmesa samaṇo hoti. Sesaṃ purimanayeneva vitthāretabbaṃ.

Aparo evaṃ katheti – citteneva mahācāṭiṃ ṭhapetvā matthuṃ yojetvā citteneva attano dvattiṃsākāraṃ uppāṭetvā tattha pakkhipitvā matthuṃ otāretvā manthitabbaṃ. Mathiyamānaṃ vilīyati, vilīne upari pheṇo uggacchati. So pheṇo paribhuñjitabbo. Ettāvatā vo amataṃ paribhuttaṃ nāma bhavissati . Ito paraṃ ‘‘atha te bhikkhū’’tiādi sabbaṃ purimanayeneva vitthāretabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
43. “*Abhiññā desitā*” means it was directly realized and proclaimed by [the Buddha] seated at the foot of the great *bodhi* tree.

"*Patissayamānarūpā viharantī*" means they dwell in dependence.

"*Bhagavato accayenā*" means now, with the Blessed One as the elder, they dwell respectfully. "It is not possible, venerable sir, to create discord due to the Blessed One's intense energy and unapproachability. But they say that discord might arise after the Blessed One's passing away.

When he shows where they might create that discord, he says, "*ajjhājīve vā adhipātimokkhe vā*."

There, "*ajjhājīve*" means on account of livelihood, for the sake of livelihood – "Monk, if you boast about superhuman qualities, you incur an offense entailing expulsion" – and with the six training rules prescribed in the *parivāra* by the method beginning with (Par. 287), setting those aside, all the remaining training rules are called *adhipātimokkha*.

"*Appamattako so ānandā*" means, Ānanda, because the arising discord concerning livelihood and concerning the *adhipātimokkha*, since he is very skilled in considering another's speech as well as his own nature, is easily abandoned; therefore, he is called "diligent."

Here is the method: A certain person here thinks, "It is not possible to gain anything without boasting of superhuman qualities," and so on, and on account of livelihood, he boasts of superhuman qualities or incurs impure conduct. The monk who dwells in their monastery knows him as an *arhat*, and so on, and he makes a jingle of praise or he, being ill, requests delicious foods for his own benefit and consumes them, or a nun, having requested those things, incurs an offense requiring confession. Whatever inferior object he may be, whatever soup, rice, or invitation he makes, while transgressing another prescribed rule, he dwells [in the monastery]. His fellow practitioners understand him thus: "What is the use of this gain that he has obtained, since, having gone forth into the dispensation, he makes a living by wrong livelihood and transgresses the prescribed rule?"

Also, it occurs to him according to his own nature, "What is the use to me of this gain, since I, having gone forth into the well-expounded *dharma* and *vinaya*, make a living by wrong livelihood and transgress the prescribed rule?" Considering this, he then abstains.

Thus, skilled in considering another's speech as well as his own nature, he is easily abandoned.

Therefore, the Blessed One said, "diligent."

"*Magge vā hi, ānanda, paṭipadāya vā*" means having attained the supramundane path, discord is completely calmed; there is no discord for those who have attained the path.

But this was said intending the preliminary path and the preliminary practice.

"*Magge vā hi, ānanda, paṭipadāya vā*" There is the method here: In this way, people esteem a monk in the supramundane *dharmas*.

Having come, his fellow students and others, having venerated and stood to one side, ask, "What is the purpose of your coming?"

[He replies,] "To ask about the object of mindfulness, venerable sir."

"Sit down. I will explain to you in a moment a teaching on the object of mindfulness that is capable of bringing about *arhatship*." Having said this, he says, "Here, a monk, having entered his own dwelling place and sat down, applies his mind to the fundamental object of mindfulness. For him, as he applies his mind to it, light arises.

This is called the first path.

He produces a second light of knowledge, the second path is attained, and so forth for the third and fourth.

To this extent, he is both a path-attainer and a fruit-attainer."

Then those monks conclude, "A non-stream-enterer is not able to expound the object of mindfulness in this way. Indeed, he is a stream-enterer."

After that, at another time, he passes away.

People from all the alms-villages come and ask, "Venerable sir, was the elder questioned about a certain matter?"

The lay followers [reply,] "The elder had already spoken to us about the question."

Having decorated a flower-pavilion and a flower-peak-chamber, having made a golden eye-covering, mouth-covering, and so forth, having worshiped with incense, garlands, and so forth, having played and burned [the body] for a week, they take the bones and make a *caitya*.

Other newcomers, having come to the monastery, having washed their feet, ask, "We will see the great elder. Where, friend, is the great elder?"

"He is completely extinguished, venerable sirs."

"It was difficult, friend, what the elder did, producing the fruits of the path! He asked the question, friend.

When he was teaching the object of mindfulness to the monks, he taught with this method, venerable sirs."

"That is not the path, friend. It is called an impurity of *vipaśyanā*. You did not know [him]. The elder, friend, was an ordinary person."
They, quarreling, having risen up, (said): "The monks in the entire monastery and the people in the alms-collecting villages do not know; you alone know."

"By which path did you come? What, was the *cetiya* not seen at the gate of your monastery?"

To monks who speak thus, be they a hundred or a thousand, as long as they do not abandon that view, heaven and the path are obstructed.

Another, while describing the *kammaṭṭhāna*, says thus: "Having, with the mind, placed three skull-bowls on three hearths, and having made a fire beneath, and having, with the mind, torn apart one's own thirty-two aspects, and having thrown (them) into the skull-bowls, and having, with the mind, turned (them) around and around with a stick, it should be burned. Whatever ashes arise while burning, that should be blown away by the wind of the mouth."

By so much, one is named a purified ascetic.

The remainder should be elaborated according to the previous method.

Another says thus: "Having, with the mind, placed a large pot and having added whey, and having, with the mind, torn apart one's own thirty-two aspects, and having thrown (them) therein, and having poured in the whey, it should be churned."

While being churned, it dissolves; when dissolved, foam rises to the top.

That foam should be consumed.

By so much, it will be that the immortal has been consumed by you.

From here on, everything beginning with "Then those monks..." should be elaborated according to the previous method.

mula_pali: 44. ‘‘Chayimāni, ānanda, vivādamūlāni. Katamāni cha? Idhānanda, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī. Yo so, ānanda, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti. Yo so, ānanda, bhikkhu satthari agāravo viharati appatisso, dhamme… saṅghe agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāya na paripūrakārī hoti, so saṅghe vivādaṃ janeti; yo hoti vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evarūpañce tumhe, ānanda, vivādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, ānanda, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha. Evarūpañce tumhe, ānanda, vivādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, ānanda, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānaṃ hoti, evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavo hoti.
mula_english:
44. “There are, Ānanda, these six roots of disputes ( *vivādamūlāni*).

What are the six? Here, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* is angry (*kodhano*) and revengeful (*upanāhī*).

Such a *bhikkhu* dwells disrespectful (*agāravo*) and undeferential (*appatisso*) towards the Teacher ( *satthari*), towards the *Dhamma*, and

disrespectful and undeferential towards the *Saṃgha*, and

disrespectful and undeferential towards the training (*sikkhāya*), and he does not fulfill the training (*na paripūrakārī hoti*).

Such a *bhikkhu* dwells disrespectful and undeferential towards the Teacher (*satthari*), towards the *Dhamma*... towards the *Saṃgha*.

...undeferential, he does not fulfill the training, he creates a dispute (*vivādaṃ janeti*) in the *Saṃgha*; a dispute which would be for the harm (*ahitāya*) and unhappiness (*asukha*) of many people (*bahujana*), for the loss (*anatthāya*), harm, and suffering (*dukkhāya*) of gods (*deva*) and humans (*manussānaṃ*).

Now if you see any such root of dispute (*vivādamūlaṃ*) either in yourselves (*ajjhattaṃ vā*) or externally (*bahiddhā vā*), you should strive to abandon (*pahānāya vāyameyyātha*) that same evil (*pāpakassa*) root of dispute.

And if you do not see any such root of dispute either in yourselves or externally,

you should practice so that in the future it doesn’t arise (*āyatiṃ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha*).

Thus there is the abandoning (*pahānaṃ hoti*) of that evil (*pāpakassa*) root of dispute; thus there is the non-eruption of that evil root of dispute in the future (*āyatiṃ anavassavo hoti*).
commentary_pali:
44. Idāni yo evaṃ vivādo uppajjeyya, tassa mūlaṃ dassento chayimānītiādimāha. Tattha agāravoti gāravavirahito. Appatissoti appatissayo anīcavutti. Ettha pana yo bhikkhu satthari dharamāne tīsu kālesu upaṭṭhānaṃ na yāti, satthari anupāhane caṅkamante saupāhano caṅkamati, nīce caṅkame caṅkamante ucce caṅkame caṅkamati, heṭṭhā vasante upari vasati, satthu dassanaṭṭhāne ubho aṃse pārupati, chattaṃ dhāreti, upāhanaṃ dhāreti, nhānatitthe uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā karoti, parinibbute vā pana cetiyaṃ vandituṃ na gacchati, cetiyassa paññāyanaṭṭhāne satthudassanaṭṭhāne vuttaṃ sabbaṃ karoti, aññehi ca bhikkhūhi ‘‘kasmā evaṃ karosi, na idaṃ vaṭṭati, sammāsabuddhassa nāma lajjituṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti vutte ‘‘tūṇhī hoti, kiṃ buddho buddhoti vadasī’’ti bhaṇati, ayaṃ satthari agāravo nāma.

Yo pana dhammassavane saṅghuṭṭhe sakkaccaṃ na gacchati, sakkaccaṃ dhammaṃ na suṇāti, niddāyati vā sallapento vā nisīdati, sakkaccaṃ na gaṇhāti na dhāreti, ‘‘kiṃ dhamme agāravaṃ karosī’’ti vutte ‘‘tuṇhī hoti, dhammo dhammoti vadasi, kiṃ dhammo nāmā’’ti vadati, ayaṃ dhamme agāravo nāma.

dhamme agāravo

Yo pana therena bhikkhunā anajjhiṭṭho dhammaṃ deseti, nisīdati pañhaṃ katheti, vuḍḍhe bhikkhū ghaṭṭento gacchati, tiṭṭhati nisīdati, dussapallatthikaṃ vā hatthapallatthikaṃ vā karoti, saṅghamajjhe ubho aṃse pārupati, chattupāhanaṃ dhāreti, ‘‘bhikkhusaṅghassa lajjituṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti vuttepi ‘‘tuṇhī hoti, saṅgho saṅghoti vadasi, kiṃ saṅgho, migasaṅgho ajasaṅgho’’tiādīni vadati, ayaṃ saṅghe agāravo nāma. Ekabhikkhusmimpi hi agārave kate saṅghe katoyeva hoti. Tisso sikkhā pana aparipūrayamānova sikkhāya na paripūrakārī nāma.

saṅghe agāravo sikkhāya na paripūrakārī

Ajjhattaṃ vāti attani vā attano parisāya vā. Bāhiddhāti parasmiṃ vā parassa parisāya vā.

Ajjhattaṃ vā Bāhiddhā
commentary_english:
44. Now, if a dispute should arise in this way, [the author] shows the origin of it, beginning with "<hi rend="bold">chayimānī</hi>."

Therein, *agāravo* means without respect (*gārava*).

*appatisso* means without reverence (*appatissaya*), of ignoble conduct (*anīcavutti*).

Here, further, if a *bhikkhu* (*bhikṣu*) when the Teacher is living does not go to [offer] attendance at the three times, when the Teacher is walking without shoes, he walks with shoes, when [the Teacher] is walking on a low promenade (*caṅkama*), he walks on a high promenade, when [the Teacher] is dwelling below, he dwells above, in the place for seeing the Teacher he covers both shoulders, he holds an umbrella, he holds shoes, at the bathing place he makes excrement or urine, when [the Teacher] is fully passed away (*parinibbute*), he does not go to venerate a *cetiya* (*caitya*), in the place for venerating the *cetiya*, in the place for seeing the Teacher, he does all that has been said, and if other *bhikkhus* (*bhikṣus*) [say], "Why do you do this? This is not fitting, it is indeed fitting to be ashamed in the name of the truly awakened Buddha (*sammāsabuddha*)!" if [he] is told thus, [he] says, "Be silent! Why do you say 'Buddha, Buddha'?" This is called disrespect (*agāravo*) for the Teacher (*satthari*).

Furthermore, if one does not go respectfully (*sakkaccaṃ*) when the Dharma is proclaimed for the hearing of the Dharma (*dhammassavane*), does not listen respectfully to the Dharma, dozes or sits conversing, does not respectfully grasp [the Dharma], does not bear [it] in mind, [and others say], "Why do you show disrespect (*agāravaṃ*) for the Dharma?" if [he] is told, "Be silent! You speak of the Dharma, the Dharma! What is Dharma, indeed?" he says. This is called disrespect (*agāravo*) for the Dharma (*dhamme*).

Disrespect (*agāravo*) for the Dharma (*dhamme*): If, further, a *bhikkhu* (*bhikṣu*), unasked by an elder *bhikkhu* (*bhikṣu*), teaches the Dharma, sits down, relates a question, goes pushing elderly *bhikkhus* (*bhikṣus*), stands, sits down, makes a garment support or a hand support, in the midst of the *saṅgha* (*saṃgha*) he covers both shoulders, holds an umbrella and shoes, [and others say], "It is fitting for the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* (*bhikṣu-saṃgha*) to be ashamed!" even if told thus, [he] says, "Be silent! You speak of the *saṅgha* (*saṃgha*), the *saṅgha*! What is the *saṅgha*? A herd of deer? A herd of goats?" etc., he says. This is called disrespect (*agāravo*) for the *saṅgha* (*saṃghe*).

Even in the case of disrespect (*agārave*) toward a single *bhikkhu* (*bhikṣu*), [it] is just the same as disrespect (*agāravo*) done to the *saṅgha* (*saṃghe*).

Moreover, not fulfilling the three trainings (*sikkhā*), he is called "not a fulfiller of the training (*sikkhāya na paripūrakārī*)."

Disrespect (*agāravo*) for the *saṅgha* (*saṃghe*):

Not a fulfiller of the training (*sikkhāya na paripūrakārī*): Internal (*ajjhattaṃ vā*) means in oneself (*attani*) or in one's own assembly (*attano parisāya vā*).

External (*bāhiddhā*) means in another (*parasmiṃ*) or in another's assembly (*parassa parisāya vā*).

Internal or external.

mula_pali: 45. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu makkhī hoti paḷāsī…pe… issukī hoti maccharī…pe… saṭho hoti māyāvī…pe… pāpiccho hoti micchādiṭṭhi micchādiṭṭhī (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) …pe… sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī. Yo so, ānanda, bhikkhu sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti. Yo so, ānanda, bhikkhu satthari agāravo viharati appatisso, dhamme… saṅghe… sikkhāya na paripūrakārī hoti so saṅghe vivādaṃ janeti; yo hoti vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evarūpañce tumhe, ānanda, vivādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, ānanda, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha. Evarūpañce tumhe, ānanda, vivādamūlaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha, tatra tumhe, ānanda, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānaṃ hoti , evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṃ anavassavo hoti. Imāni kho, ānanda, cha vivādamūlāni.
mula_english:
“Again, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* is contemptuous and domineering… envious and avaricious… deceitful and fraudulent… has evil wishes and wrong view… adheres to his own views (*sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī*), holds on to them tenaciously (*ādhānaggāhī*), and relinquishes them with difficulty (*duppaṭinissaggī*).

“Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* who adheres to his own views, holds on to them tenaciously, and relinquishes them with difficulty, dwells without respect and without deference for the Teacher, for the *Dharma*, and for the *Saṃgha*, and he does not fulfill the training.

“Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* who dwells disrespectful and undeferential towards the Teacher, towards the *Dharma*, and towards the *Saṃgha*, and who does not fulfil the training, creates a dispute (*vivādaṃ janeti*) in the *Saṃgha*, which would be for the harm and unhappiness of many, for the loss, harm, and suffering of gods (*deva*) and humans (*manussānaṃ*).

“Ānanda, if you see any such root of dispute (*vivādamūlaṃ*) either in yourselves (*ajjhattaṃ*) or externally (*bahiddhā*),

then, Ānanda, you should strive to abandon that same evil root of dispute (*pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha*).

“Ānanda, if you do not see any such root of dispute either in yourselves or externally, then, Ānanda, you should practice in such a way that that same evil root of dispute does not erupt in the future (*āyatiṃ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha*).

Thus there is the abandoning (*pahānaṃ hoti*) of that evil root of dispute, thus there is the non-eruption (*anavassavo hoti*) of that evil root of dispute in the future.

These, Ānanda, are the six roots of dispute (*cha vivādamūlāni*).

mula_pali: 46. ‘‘Cattārimāni , ānanda, adhikaraṇāni. Katamāni cattāri? Vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ – imāni kho, ānanda, cattāri adhikaraṇāni. Satta kho panime, ānanda, adhikaraṇasamathā – uppannuppannānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ samathāya vūpasamāya sammukhāvinayo dātabbo, sativinayo dātabbo, amūḷhavinayo dātabbo, paṭiññāya kāretabbaṃ, yebhuyyasikā, tassapāpiyasikā, tiṇavatthārako.
mula_english:
“Ānanda, there are these four kinds of litigation (*adhikaraṇāni*). What are the four? Litigation because of a dispute (*vivādādhikaraṇaṃ*), litigation because of an accusation (*anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ*), litigation because of an offense (*āpattādhikaraṇaṃ*), and litigation concerning proceedings (*kiccādhikaraṇaṃ*) – These are the four kinds of litigation, Ānanda.

“Ānanda, there are these seven kinds of settlement of litigation (*adhikaraṇasamathā*). For the settlement (*samathāya*) and pacification (*vūpasamāya*) of litigations whenever they arise: removal of litigation by confrontation (*sammukhāvinayo*) may be provided (*dātabbo*), removal of litigation on account of memory (*sativinayo*) may be provided (*dātabbo*), removal of litigation on account of past insanity (*amūḷhavinayo*) may be provided (*dātabbo*), the effecting of acknowledgement of an offense (*paṭiññāya kāretabbaṃ*), the opinion of the majority (*yebhuyyasikā*), the pronouncement of bad character against someone (*tassapāpiyasikā*), and covering over with grass (*tiṇavatthārako*).
commentary_pali:
46. Idāni ayaṃ cha ṭhānāni nissāya uppannavivādo vaḍḍhanto yāni adhikaraṇāni pāpuṇāti, tāni dassetuṃ cattārimānītiādimāha. Tattha vūpasamanatthāya pavattamānehi samathehi adhikātabbānīti adhikaraṇāni. Vivādova adhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Itaresupi eseva nayo.

Idāni imānipi cattāri adhikaraṇāni patvā upari vaḍḍhento so vivādo yehi samathehi vūpasammati, tesaṃ dassanatthaṃ satta kho panimetiādimāha. Tattha adhikaraṇāni samenti vūpasamentīti adhikaraṇasamathā. Uppannuppannānanti uppannānaṃ uppannānaṃ. Adhikaraṇānanti etesaṃ vivādādhikaraṇādīnaṃ catunnaṃ. Samathāya vūpasamāyāti samanatthañceva vūpasamanatthañca. Sammukhāvinayo dātabbo…pe… tiṇavatthārakoti ime satta samathā dātabbā.

satta kho panime adhikaraṇasamathā. Uppannuppannāna Adhikaraṇāna Samathāya vūpasamāyā Sammukhāvinayo dātabbo…pe… tiṇavatthārako

Tatrāyaṃ vinicchayakathā – adhikaraṇesu tāva dhammoti vā adhammoti vāti aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi vivadantānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yo vivādo, idaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ nāma. Sīlavipattiyā vā ācāradiṭṭhiājīvavipattiyā vā anuvadantānaṃ yo anuvādo upavadanā ceva codanā ca, idaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ nāma. Mātikāyaṃ āgatā pañca vibhaṅge dveti satta āpattikkhandhā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ nāma. Yaṃ saṅghassa apalokanādīnaṃ catunnaṃ kammānaṃ karaṇaṃ, idaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ nāma.

anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kiccādhikaraṇaṃ

Tattha vivādādhikaraṇaṃ dvīhi samathehi sammati sammukhāvinayena ca yebhuyyasikāya ca. Sammukhāvinayeneva sammamānaṃ yasmiṃ vihāre uppannaṃ, tasmiṃyeva vā, aññattha vūpasametuṃ gacchantānaṃ antarāmagge vā, yattha gantvā saṅghassa niyyātitaṃ, tattha saṅghena vā gaṇena vā vūpasametuṃ asakkonte tattheva ubbāhikāya sammatapuggalehi vā vinicchitaṃ sammati. Evaṃ sammamāne pana tasmiṃ yā saṅghasammukhatā dhammasammukhatā, vinayasammukhatā, puggalasammukhatā, ayaṃ sammukhāvinayo nāma.

sammukhāvinayo

Tattha ca kārakasaṅghassa sāmaggivasena sammukhībhāvo saṅghasammukhatā. Sametabbassa vatthuno bhūtatā dhammasammukhatā. Yathā taṃ sametabbaṃ, tatheva samanaṃ vinayasammukhatā. Yo ca vivadati, yena ca vivadati, tesaṃ ubhinnaṃ attapaccatthikānaṃ sammukhībhāvo puggalasammukhatā. Ubbāhikāya vūpasame panettha saṅghasammukhatā parihāyati. Evaṃ tāva sammukhāvinayeneva sammati.

Sace panevampi na sammati, atha naṃ ubbāhikāya sammatā bhikkhū ‘‘na mayaṃ sakkoma vūpasametu’’nti saṅghasseva niyyātenti. Tato saṅgho pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ salākaggāhakaṃ sammannitvā tena guḷhakavivaṭakasakaṇṇajappakesu tīsu salākaggāhesu aññataravasena salākaṃ gāhetvā sannipatitaparisāya dhammavādīnaṃ yebhuyyatāya yathā te dhammavādino vadanti, evaṃ vūpasantaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ sammukhāvinayena ca yebhuyyasikāya ca vūpasantaṃ hoti. Tattha sammukhāvinayo vuttanayo eva. Yaṃ pana yebhuyyasikāya kammassa karaṇaṃ, ayaṃ yebhuyyasikā nāma. Evaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ dvīhi samathehi sammati.

yebhuyyasikā

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ catūhi samathehi sammati sammukhāvinayena ca sativinayena ca amūḷhavinayena ca tassapāpiyasikāya ca. Sammukhāvinayeneva sammamānaṃ yo ca anuvadati, yañca anuvadati, tesaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā, sace kāci āpatti natthi, ubho khamāpetvā, sace atthi, ayaṃ nāmettha āpattīti evaṃ vinicchitaṃ vūpasammati. Tattha sammukhāvinayalakkhaṇaṃ vuttanayameva.

Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ

Yadā pana khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno amūlikāya sīlavipattiyā anuddhaṃsitassa sativinayaṃ yācamānassa saṅgho ñatticatutthena kammena sativinayaṃ deti, tadā sammukhāvinayena ca sativinayena ca vūpasantaṃ hoti. Dinne pana sativinaye puna tasmiṃ puggale kassaci anuvādo na ruhati.

Yadā ummattako bhikkhu ummādavasena kate assāmaṇake ajjhācāre ‘‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ āpatti’’nti bhikkhūhi vuccamāno – ‘‘ummattakena me, āvuso, etaṃ kataṃ, nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmī’’ti bhaṇantopi bhikkhūhi codiyamānova puna acodanatthāya amūḷhavinayaṃ yācati, saṅgho cassa ñatticatutthena kammena amūḷhavinayaṃ deti, tadā sammukhāvinayena ca amūḷhavinayena ca vūpasantaṃ hoti. Dinne pana amūḷhavinaye puna tasmiṃ puggale kassaci tappaccayā anuvādo na ruhati.

Yadā pana pārājikena vā pārājikasāmantena vā codiyamānassa aññenāññaṃ paṭicarato pāpussannatāya pāpiyassa puggalassa – ‘‘sacāyaṃ acchinnamūlo bhavissati, sammā vattitvā osāraṇaṃ labhissati, sace chinnamūlo, ayamevassa nāsanā bhavissatī’’ti maññamāno saṅgho ñatticatutthena kammena tassapāpiyasikaṃ karoti, tadā sammukhāvinayena ca tassa pāpiyasikāya ca vūpasantaṃ hoti. Evaṃ anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ catūhi samathehi sammati.

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ tīhi samathehi sammati sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca. Tassa sammukhāvinayeneva vūpasamo natthi. Yadā pana ekassa vā bhikkhuno santike saṅghagaṇamajjhesu vā bhikkhu lahukaṃ āpattiṃ deseti, tadā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena ca vūpasammati. Tattha sammukhāvinayo tāva yo ca deseti, yassa ca deseti, tesaṃ sammukhatā. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Puggalassa ca gaṇassa ca desanākāle saṅghasammukhatā parihāyati. Yaṃ panettha ‘‘ahaṃ, bhante, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ apanno’’ti ca, āma ‘‘passāmī’’ti ca paṭiññātāya ‘‘āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī’’ti karaṇaṃ, taṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ nāma. Saṅghādisese parivāsādiyācanā paṭiññā, parivāsādīnaṃ dānaṃ paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ nāma.

Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ

Dvepakkhajātā pana bhaṇḍanakārakā bhikkhū bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhācāraṃ caritvā puna lajjidhamme uppanne ‘‘sace mayaṃ imāhi āpattīhi aññamaññaṃ kāressāma, siyāpi taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ kakkhaḷattāya saṃvatteyyā’’ti aññamaññaṃ āpattiyā kārāpane dosaṃ disvā yadā tiṇavatthārakakammaṃ karonti, tadā āpattādhikaraṇaṃ sammukhāvinayena ca tiṇavatthārakena ca sammati. Tatra hi yattakā hatthapāsupagatā ‘‘na me taṃ khamatī’’ti evaṃ diṭṭhāvikammaṃ akatvā ‘‘dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma’’nti na ukkoṭenti, niddampi okkantā honti, sabbesampi ṭhapetvā thullavajjañca gihipaṭisaṃyuttañca sabbāpattiyo vuṭṭhahanti. Evaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ tīhi samathehi sammati. Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ ekena samathena sammati sammukhāvinayeneva.

Kiccādhikaraṇaṃ

Imāni cattāri adhikaraṇāni yathānurūpaṃ imehi sattahi samathehi sammanti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘uppannuppannānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ samathāya vūpasamāya sammukhāvinayo dātabbo…pe… tiṇavatthārako’’ti. Ayamettha vinicchayanayo, vitthāro pana samathakkhandhake (cūḷava. 185) āgatoyeva. Vinicchayopissa samantapāsādikāya vutto.

samantapāsādikāya
commentary_english:
46. Now, to show which *adhikaraṇas* (cases, disputes) this dispute arises relying on six bases and grows, he says "these four" etc.

There, *adhikaraṇas* are to be settled by *samathas* (settlements) which are proceeding for the sake of pacification.

A dispute is an *adhikaraṇa*; a dispute-adhikaraṇa (*vivādādhikaraṇaṃ*).

The same method applies in the other cases as well.

Now, that dispute, having reached these four *adhikaraṇas*, grows further; to show those settlements by which it is pacified, he says, "but these seven" etc.

There, *adhikaraṇas* are settled and pacified; therefore, [they are called] *adhikaraṇasamathā* (settlements of cases).

"Of those that have arisen, that have arisen" means of those that have arisen, that have arisen.

"*Adhikaraṇānaṃ*" means of these four, beginning with dispute-*adhikaraṇa*.

"*Samathāya vūpasamāyā*" means for the sake of settlement and for the sake of pacification.

"*Sammukhāvinayo dātabbo…pe… tiṇavatthārako*" These seven settlements should be given.

These seven are the *adhikaraṇasamathā*.

"*Uppannuppannāna adhikaraṇāna samathāya vūpasamāyā sammukhāvinayo dātabbo…pe… tiṇavatthārako*"

There, this is the discussion of judgment: Among the *adhikaraṇas*, what is *dhamma* (right, law) or what is *adhamma* (wrong, unlawful)—that dispute of monks who are disputing with eighteen grounds, that is called *vivādādhikaraṇaṃ* (dispute-adhikaraṇa).

Or, the recrimination of those who are blaming with respect to failure in morality (*sīlavipatti*), or failure in conduct, views, or livelihood (*ācāradiṭṭhiājīvavipatti*)—that recrimination, both reproach and accusation, is called *anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ* (recrimination-adhikaraṇa).

The seven groups of offenses (*āpattikkhandhā*) that are included in the *mātikā* (matrix) and the five in the *vibhaṅga* (analysis) and the two [others]—that is called *āpattādhikaraṇaṃ* (offense-adhikaraṇa).

The performance of those four kinds of actions beginning with proclamation (*apalokana*) by the *saṃgha* (community)—that is called *kiccādhikaraṇaṃ* (business-adhikaraṇa).

*Anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, kiccādhikaraṇaṃ*

There, a dispute-*adhikaraṇa* is settled by two *samathas*, by presence-*vinaya* (*sammukhāvinaya*) and by majority (*yebhuyyasikāya*).

When [the case] is being settled by presence-*vinaya*, the [case] having arisen in whichever monastery, either in that very one, or on the road for those who are going elsewhere to pacify [the dispute], or after going to where it has been handed over to the *saṃgha*, there, when it is impossible to pacify [the dispute] by the *saṃgha* or by a group, it is settled right there by persons authorized by the *ubbāhikā*.

Thus, while [the case] is being settled, then, in that [instance], that the *saṃgha* is present, that the *dhamma* is present, that the *vinaya* is present, that the person is present—this is called *sammukhāvinayo* (presence-*vinaya*).

*Sammukhāvinayo*

And there, the presence of the active *saṃgha* by way of harmony is *saṅghasammukhatā* (presence of the *saṃgha*).

The realness of the matter to be settled is *dhammasammukhatā* (presence of the *dhamma*).

Just as that is to be settled, so likewise the propriety is *vinayasammukhatā* (presence of the *vinaya*).

And that one disputes, and by whom one disputes, the facing of those two opponents is *puggalasammukhatā* (presence of the person).

But here, in the pacification by the *ubbāhikā*, the presence of the *saṃgha* declines.

Thus, so far it is settled just by presence-*vinaya*.

If, however, it is not settled even in this way, then the monks authorized by the *ubbāhikā* hand over [the case] to the *saṃgha* itself, [saying] "we are not able to settle [this]".

Then the *saṃgha*, having authorized a monk endowed with five qualities as a taker of lots (*salākaggāhaka*), and having had a lot taken by him in one of three ways—secretly, openly, or whispering in the ear—according to the majority of those speaking the *dhamma* in the assembled assembly, just as those speakers of the *dhamma* say, thus the *adhikaraṇa* is pacified; and the *adhikaraṇa* is settled by presence-*vinaya* and by majority (*yebhuyyasikāya*).

There, presence-*vinaya* is just as has been said.

But that which is the performance of an action by majority, this is called *yebhuyyasikā* (majority).

Thus, a dispute-*adhikaraṇa* is settled by two *samathas*.

*Yebhuyyasikā*

A recrimination-*adhikaraṇa* is settled by four *samathas*, by presence-*vinaya*, by mindfulness-*vinaya* (*sativinaya*), by non-delusion-*vinaya* (*amūḷhavinaya*), and by confession of wrong-doing (*tassapāpiyasikāya*).

When [the case] is being settled by presence-*vinaya*, and that one recriminates, and thatHerein, he repeats the words, having heard their statement, if there is no offense, he asks both for forgiveness, if there is, he decides thus: "This is the offense," and it is settled.
Herein, the characteristic of the presence of the *vinaya* is as already stated.

A legal issue arising from an accusation:

When, however, a monk who is without outflows, who has not been reproached for an unfounded breach of morality, requests the *sati-vinaya*, the Order gives the *sati-vinaya* by means of a *jñatti-caturtha* action, then it is settled through the presence of the *vinaya* and the *sati-vinaya*.
When, however, the *sati-vinaya* has been given, no accusation against that person arises again.

When a mad monk, due to his madness, commits an improper act that is unmonastic, and the monks say to him, "The venerable one has committed such an offense," and he says, "Friends, this was done by me in my madness, I do not remember it," even though he says this, the monks...

When, being interrogated, he again requests the *amūḷha-vinaya* in order to be free from interrogation, and the Order gives him the *amūḷha-vinaya* by means of a *jñatti-caturtha* action, then it is settled through the presence of the *vinaya* and the *amūḷha-vinaya*.
When, however, the *amūḷha-vinaya* has been given, no accusation based on that reason arises again against that person.

When, however, being interrogated by someone who has committed a *pārājika* offense or is close to committing a *pārājika* offense, a blameworthy person, who is evading the question by answering something else, thinking, "If this one is not cut off at the root, having behaved well, he will obtain release, but if he is cut off at the root, this will be his destruction," the Order performs the *tassapāpiyasikā* action by means of a *jñatti-caturtha* action, then it is settled through the presence of the *vinaya* and the *tassapāpiyasikā*.
Thus, a legal issue arising from an accusation is settled through four principles.

A legal issue arising from an offense is settled through three principles: the presence of the *vinaya*, the act of acknowledgement, and the covering over with grass.
For him, there is no settling only through the presence of the *vinaya*.
When, however, a monk confesses a minor offense in the presence of one monk or in the midst of the Order, then the legal issue arising from an offense is settled through the presence of the *vinaya* and the act of acknowledgement.
There, the presence of the *vinaya* is the presence of those who confess and those to whom he confesses.
The rest is as already stated.
The presence of the Order is lost at the time of confession by a person or a group.
Here, the statement "I, venerable sir, have committed such and such an offense," and the act of acknowledging "Yes, I see it," and the act of saying, "In the future, you should restrain yourself," that is called the act of acknowledgement (*paṭiññātakaraṇa*).
In the case of the *saṃghādisesa*, the request for *parivāsa* etc. is the acknowledgement, the giving of *parivāsa* etc. is called the act of acknowledgement.

When, however, monks who are quarrelsome and argumentative, having engaged in much unmonastic behavior and improper conduct, and when remorse arises in them, thinking, "If we were to cause each other to be punished for these offenses, that legal issue would likely lead to harshness," seeing the fault in causing each other to be punished for the offenses, when they perform the covering over with grass action, then the legal issue arising from an offense is settled through the presence of the *vinaya* and the covering over with grass.
There, those who are within arm's reach, without making a show of disobedience by saying, "That is not pleasing to me," they do not cry out, "A bad deed, a deed must be done again," and they are intent even on sleep, having set aside all the offenses, both the serious offenses and those connected with laypeople, they are freed from all offenses.
Thus, a legal issue arising from an offense is settled through three principles.
A legal issue arising from a duty is settled through one principle: only through the presence of the *vinaya*.

These four legal issues are settled appropriately by these seven principles for settling.
Therefore, it was said, "For the settling and appeasing of legal issues that have arisen, the presence of the *vinaya* should be given…pe… the covering over with grass."
This is the method of deciding here, but the full explanation is already given in the *Samatha-kkhandhaka* (*Cūḷava*.
185).
The method of deciding is also explained in the *Samantapāsādikā*.

mula_pali: 47. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, sammukhāvinayo hoti? Idhānanda, bhikkhū vivadanti dhammoti vā adhammoti vā vinayoti vā avinayoti vā. Tehānanda, bhikkhūhi sabbeheva samaggehi sannipatitabbaṃ. Sannipatitvā dhammanetti samanumajjitabbā . Dhammanettiṃ samanumajjitvā yathā tattha sameti tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametabbaṃ. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, sammukhāvinayo hoti; evañca panidhekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vūpasamo hoti yadidaṃ – sammukhāvinayena.
mula_english:
47. Now, Ānanda, how does the *sammukhāvinaya* come about? Here, Ānanda, the *bhikkhus* dispute, saying, “It is *dhamma* (the teaching),” or “It is *adhamma* (not the teaching),” or “It is *vinaya* (the discipline),” or “It is *avinaya* (not the discipline)."

Then, Ānanda, those *bhikkhus* should all meet together in concord (*samaggehi sannipatitabbaṃ*).

Having met together, the guideline of the *dhamma* should be examined.

Having examined the guideline of the *dhamma*, that legal issue (*adhikaraṇaṃ*) should be resolved in this way.

And so, Ānanda, there comes to be the *sammukhāvinaya*; and so there comes to be the settlement (*vūpasamo hoti*) of some litigations (*adhikaraṇānaṃ*) here by the *sammukhāvinaya*.
commentary_pali:
47. Yo panāyaṃ imasmiṃ sutte ‘‘idhānanda, bhikkhū vivadantī’’tiādiko vitthāro vutto, so etena nayena saṅkhepatova vuttoti veditabbo. Tattha dhammotiādīsu suttantapariyāyena tāva dasa kusalakammapathā dhammo, akusalakammapathā adhammo. Tathā ‘‘cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’’ti heṭṭhā āgatā sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiyadhammā, tayo satipaṭṭhānā tayo sammappadhānā tayo iddhipādā cha indriyāni cha balāni aṭṭha bojjhaṅgā navaṅgiko maggo cāti, cattāro upādānā pañca nīvaraṇānītiādayo saṅkaliṭṭhadhammā cāti ayaṃ adhammo.

Tattha yaṃkiñci ekaṃ adhammakoṭṭhāsaṃ gahetvā ‘‘imaṃ adhammaṃ dhammoti karissāma, evaṃ amhākaṃ ācariyakulaṃ niyyānikaṃ bhavissati, mayañca loke pākaṭā bhavissāmā’’ti taṃ adhammaṃ ‘‘dhammo aya’’nti kathentā dhammoti vivadanti. Tattheva dhammakoṭṭhāsesu ekaṃ gahetvā ‘‘adhammo aya’’nti kathentā adhammoti vivadanti.

Vinayapariyāyena pana bhūtena vatthunā codetvā sāretvā yathāpaṭiññāya kātabbakammaṃ dhammo nāma, abhūtena pana vatthunā acodetvā asāretvā apaṭiññāya katabbakammaṃ adhammo nāma. Tesupi adhammaṃ ‘‘dhammo aya’’nti kathentā dhammoti vivadanti, ‘‘adhammo aya’’nti kathentā adhammoti vivadanti.

Suttantapariyāyena pana rāgavinayo dosavinayo mohavinayo saṃvaro pahānaṃ paṭisaṅkhāti ayaṃ vinayo nāma, rāgādīnaṃ avinayo asaṃvaro appahānaṃ appaṭisaṅkhāti ayaṃ avinayo nāma. Vinayapariyāyena vatthusampatti ñattisampatti anusāvanasampatti sīmasampati parisasampattīti ayaṃ vinayo nāma, vatthuvipatti…pe… parisavipattīti ayaṃ avinayo nāma. Tesupi yaṃkiñci avinayaṃ ‘‘vinayo aya’’nti kathentā vinayoti vivadanti, vinayaṃ avinayoti kathentā avinayoti vivadanti.

vinayo avinayo vinayo avinayo

Dhammanetti samanumajjitabbāti dhammarajju anumajjitabbā ñāṇena ghaṃsitabbā upaparikkhitabbā. Sā panesā dhammanetti ‘‘iti kho vaccha ime dasa dhammā akusalā dasa dhammā kusalā’’ti evaṃ mahāvacchagottasutte (ma. ni. 2.194) āgatāti vuttā. Sā eva vā hotu, yo vā idha dhammoti ca vinayo ca vutto. Yathā tattha sametīti yathā tāya dhammanettiyā sameti, ‘‘dhammo dhammova hoti, adhammo adhammova, vinayo vinayova hoti, avinayo avinayova’’. Tathā tanti evaṃ taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametabbaṃ. Ekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānanti idha vivādādhikaraṇameva dassitaṃ, sammukhāvinayo pana na kismiñci adhikaraṇe na labbhati.

Dhammanetti samanumajjitabbā Yathā tattha sametī Tathā ta Ekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇāna
commentary_english:
47. Now, in this *sutta*, the expansion beginning with "Here, Ānanda, monks dispute," that has been spoken of, that should be understood as spoken of succinctly by this method.

There, in regard to "*dharma*," etc., first, by the method of the *sūtrānta*, the ten skillful paths of action are *dharma*; the unskillful paths of action are *adharma*. Similarly, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment that come below, "The four close placements of mindfulness" (*cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*), the three close placements of mindfulness, the three right abandonments (*sammappadhānā*), the three bases of spiritual power (*iddhipādā*), the six faculties (*indriyāṇi*), the six powers (*balāni*), the eight factors of enlightenment (*bojjhaṅgā*), the path with nine factors (*navaṅgiko maggo*), the four grasping aggregates (*upādānā*), the five hindrances (*nīvaraṇānī*) and so on, and the defiled phenomena (*saṅkaliṭṭhadhammā*) are *adharma*.

There, taking just any portion of *adharma*, saying "We will make this *adharma* into *dharma*. Thus, our teacher's lineage will be liberating, and we will become known in the world," those who say that that *adharma* is "*dharma*," dispute about *dharma*.

There itself, taking just one portion of *dharma*, saying "This is *adharma*," those who say "*adharma*," dispute about *adharma*.

Now, by the method of the *vinaya*, that which is right action (*kātabbakammaṃ*) in accordance with the promise (*yathāpaṭiññāya*), having urged and reminded them with a factual basis (*bhūtena vatthunā*) is called *dharma*; now, that which is right action without urging and reminding them with an unfactual basis (*abhūtena vatthunā*) and without a promise (*apaṭiññāya*) is called *adharma*.

Even among those, those who say that *adharma* is "*dharma*," dispute about *dharma*; those who say "*adharma*," dispute about *adharma*.

Now, by the method of the *sūtrānta*, the removal of passion (*rāgavinayo*), the removal of hatred (*dosavinayo*), the removal of delusion (*mohavinayo*), restraint (*saṃvaro*), abandonment (*pahānaṃ*), reflection (*paṭisaṅkhāti*) this is called *vinaya*; the lack of removal of passion, etc. (*rāgādīnaṃ avinayo*), lack of restraint (*asaṃvaro*), lack of abandonment (*appahānaṃ*), lack of reflection (*appaṭisaṅkhāti*) this is called *avinaya*.

By the method of the *vinaya*, the accomplishment of the basis (*vatthusampatti*), the accomplishment of the motion (*ñattisampatti*), the accomplishment of the announcement (*anusāvanasampatti*), the accomplishment of the boundary (*sīmasampati*), the accomplishment of the assembly (*parisasampattīti*) this is called *vinaya*; the failure of the basis (*vatthuvipatti*) ...pe... the failure of the assembly (*parisavipattīti*) this is called *avinaya*.

Even among those, those who, saying that just any *avinaya* is "*vinaya*," dispute about *vinaya*; those who, saying that *vinaya* is *avinaya*, dispute about *avinaya*.

*Vinaya*. *Avinaya*. *Vinaya*. *Avinaya*. The *dharmanetti* should be thoroughly pondered, the rope of *dharma* (*dhammarajju*) should be pondered, it should be rubbed with knowledge (*ñāṇena ghaṃsitabbā*), it should be examined (*upaparikkhitabbā*).

Now, that *dharmanetti*, it is said, has come in this way in the Mahāvacchagotta Sutta (*mahāvacchagottasutte*) (M. Ni. 2.194): "Thus, Vaccha, these ten phenomena (*dhammā*) are unskillful, these ten phenomena are skillful."

Or let it be that itself, or that which has been spoken of here as *dharma* and *vinaya*.

"Just as it coincides there" (*yathā tattha sametī*) means just as it coincides with that *dharmanetti*: "*Dharma* is just *dharma*, *adharma* is just *adharma*, *vinaya* is just *vinaya*, *avinaya* is just *avinaya*."

"Thus that" (*tathā ta*) means thus, that issue (*adhikaraṇaṃ*) should be thoroughly pacified (*vūpasametabbaṃ*).

"Of some issues" (*ekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇāna*) means here, just the issue of dispute (*vivādādhikaraṇameva*) has been shown, but the *sammukhāvinaya* is not obtained in any issue.

The *dharmanetti* should be thoroughly pondered, just as it coincides there, thus that, of some issues.

mula_pali: 48. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, yebhuyyasikā hoti? Te ce, ānanda, bhikkhū na sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ tasmiṃ āvāse vūpasametuṃ. Tehānanda, bhikkhūhi yasmiṃ āvāse bahutarā bhikkhū so āvāso gantabbo. Tattha sabbeheva samaggehi sannipatitabbaṃ. Sannipatitvā dhammanetti samanumajjitabbā. Dhammanettiṃ samanumajjitvā yathā tattha sameti tathā taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametabbaṃ. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, yebhuyyasikā hoti, evañca panidhekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vūpasamo hoti yadidaṃ – yebhuyyasikāya.
mula_english: How, Ānanda, does settling a matter by majority occur? If those *bhikkhus* (monks) cannot settle that *adhikaraṇaṃ* (legal issue, litigation) in that dwelling place, then, Ānanda, those *bhikkhus* should go to a dwelling place where there are a greater number of *bhikkhus*. There, they should all meet together in concord. Having met together, the guideline of the *Dhamma* (Doctrine, Law) should be drawn out. Having drawn out the guideline of the *Dhamma*, that *adhikaraṇaṃ* (legal issue, litigation) should be settled in a way that accords with it. And so, Ānanda, there comes to be the settling of a matter by majority opinion (*yebhuyyasikāya*). And so there comes to be the settlement of some litigations here by the opinion of a majority.
commentary_pali: 48. Taṃ panetaṃ yasmā dvīhi samathehi sammati sammukhāvinayena ca yebhuyyasikāya ca, tasmā heṭṭhā mātikāya ṭhapitānukkamena idāni sativinayassa vāre pattepi taṃ avatvā vivādādhikaraṇayeva tāva dutiyasamathaṃ dassento kathañcānanda, yebhuyyasikātiādimāha. Tattha bahutarāti antamaso dvīhi tīhipi atirekatarā. Sesamettha heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
Because of that, examine that, since with two, with *samatha*s, with agreement (*sammati*), with face-to-face discipline (*sammukhāvinayena*), and with the majority (*yebhuyyasikāya*), therefore, having placed [it] in the lower matrix (*heṭṭhā mātikāya*) in established order (*ṭhapitānukkamena*), now, even when the turn (*vāre*) of mindfulness-discipline (*sativinayassa*) has arrived (*pattepi*), not having spoken (*avatvā*) about that (*tam*), but showing (*dassento*) the second appeasement (*dutiyasamathaṃ*) just as (*iva*) a dispute (*vivāda*) court (*adhikaraṇayeva*), he says (*āha*) "How then, Ānanda, [about the way of proceeding by] the majority (*yebhuyyasikā*)," and so forth (*itiādim*).

There (*tattha*), "more numerous" (*bahutarā*) means (*iti*) at the very least (*antamaso*) exceeding (*atirekatarā*) by two or three (*dvīhi tīhipi*).

The remainder (*sesam*) here (*ettha*) should be understood (*veditabbaṃ*) in accordance with the method (*vuttanayeneva*) stated (*vutta*) below (*heṭṭhā*).

mula_pali: 49. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, sativinayo hoti? Idhānanda, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ evarūpāya garukāya āpattiyā codenti pārājikena vā pārājikasāmantena vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ evarūpaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) evarūpāya-iti vuccamānavacanena sameti. vinayenapi saṃsandetabbaṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti? So evamāha – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sarāmi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. Tassa kho tassa kho evaṃ (sabbattha), ānanda, bhikkhuno sativinayo dātabbo. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, sativinayo hoti, evañca panidhekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vūpasamo hoti yadidaṃ – sativinayena.
mula_english: 49. Now, Ānanda, how does removal of litigation on account of memory (*smṛti-vinaya*) occur? Here, Ānanda, one *bhikṣu* reproves another for such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat (*pārājika*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmanta*): ‘Does the venerable one remember having committed such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat (*pārājika*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmanta*)?’ And he says thus: ‘No, friend (*āvuso*), I do not remember having committed such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat (*pārājika*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmanta*)’. To that *bhikṣu*, Ānanda, removal of litigation on account of memory (*smṛti-vinaya*) should be granted. Such is the removal of litigation on account of memory (*smṛti-vinaya*), Ānanda. And so there comes to be the settlement of some litigations here by removal of litigation on account of memory (*smṛti-vinaya*).
commentary_pali: 49. Idāni heṭṭhā avitthāritaṃ sativinayaṃ ādiṃ katvā vitthāritāvasesasamathe paṭipāṭiyā vitthāretuṃ kathañcānanda, sativinayotiādimāha. Tattha pārājikasāmantena vāti dve sāmantāni khandhasāmantañca āpattisāmantañca. Tattha pārājikāpattikkhandho saṅghādisesāpattikkhandho thullaccaya-pācittiya-pāṭidesanīya-dukkaṭa-dubbhāsitāpattikkhandhoti evaṃ purimassa pacchimakhandhaṃ khandhasāmantaṃ nāma hoti. Paṭhamapārājikassa pana pubbabhāge dukkaṭaṃ, sesānaṃ thullaccayanti idaṃ āpattisāmantaṃ nāma. Tattha khandhasāmante pārājikasāmantaṃ garukāpatti nāma hoti. Saratāyasmāti saratu āyasmā. Ekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānanti idha anuvādādhikaraṇameva dassitaṃ.
commentary_english:
Now, having made *sati-vinaya* (mindfulness and discipline) the beginning, which was not explained below, in order to explain in detail the remaining *samatha* (tranquility) according to the arrangement, [he] said, "How then, Ānanda, *sati-vinaya*?" and so forth.

There, "**by means of *pārājika-sāmanta***" means there are two *sāmanta*: *khandha-sāmanta* and *āpatti-sāmanta*.

There, *pārājika-āpatti-khandha*, *saṅghādisesa-āpatti-khandha*, *thullaccaya-pācittiya-pāṭidesanīya-dukkaṭa-dubbhāsita-āpatti-khandha*: thus, the latter *khandha* of the former is called *khandha-sāmanta*.

Furthermore, in the initial part of the first *pārājika*, there is *dukkaṭa*; for the remaining ones, there is *thullaccaya*: this is called *āpatti-sāmanta*.

There, in *khandha-sāmanta*, *pārājika-sāmanta* is called *garukāpatti*.

"*Saratāyasmā*" means remember, venerable one.

"*Ekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇāna*" means here only *anuvāda-adhikaraṇa* is shown.

mula_pali: 50. ‘‘Kathañcānanda , amūḷhavinayo hoti? Idhānanda, bhikkhū bhikkhuṃ evarūpāya garukāya āpattiyā codenti pārājikena vā pārājikasāmantena vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti? (So evamāha – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sarāmi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. Tamenaṃ so nibbeṭhentaṃ ativeṭheti – ‘iṅghāyasmā sādhukameva jānāhi yadi sarasi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti.) ( ) etthantare pāṭho cūḷava. 237 natthi tassapāpiyasikāvāreevetena bhavitabbaṃ So evamāha – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, ummādaṃ pāpuṇiṃ cetaso vipariyāsaṃ. Tena me ummattakena bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ bhāsitaparikantaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi. Mūḷhena me etaṃ kata’nti. Tassa kho tassa kho evaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.), ānanda, bhikkhuno amūḷhavinayo dātabbo. Evaṃ kho, ānanda , amūḷhavinayo hoti, evañca panidhekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vūpasamo hoti yadidaṃ – amūḷhavinayena.
mula_english:
50. How, Ānanda, does resolution of insanity (*amūḷhavinaya*) come about? Here, Ānanda, one *bhikkhu* reproves another *bhikkhu* for such and such a grave offense (*garuka āpatti*), one involving defeat (*pārājika*) or bordering on defeat: ‘Does the venerable one remember having committed such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat or bordering on defeat?’ He says: ‘I do not, friends (*āvuso*), remember having committed such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat or bordering on defeat.’

Despite the denial, the former presses the latter further: ‘Surely the venerable one must know quite well if he remembers having committed such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat or bordering on defeat?’

() In this connection, the reading is “*cūḷava*.
237 *natthi tassapāpiyasikāvāreevetena bhavitabbaṃ*”

He says: ‘I, friends, experienced insanity (*ummādaṃ pāpuṇiṃ*), derangement of mind (*cetaso vipariyāsaṃ*).
Because of that insanity (*ummattakena*), I did and said many things unworthy of a *śrāmaṇa* (*assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ*).

I don’t remember it.
I did it because I was insane (*mūḷhena me etaṃ kataṃ*.’).
If he’s no longer insane, Ānanda, that *bhikkhu* should be granted resolution of insanity (*amūḷhavinayo dātabbo*).
And so, Ānanda, there comes to be resolution of insanity (*amūḷhavinayo hoti*), and so there comes to be the settlement of some litigations here by resolution of insanity (*amūḷhavinayena*).
commentary_pali: 50.Bhāsitaparikkantanti vācāya bhāsitaṃ kāyena ca parikkantaṃ, parakkamitvā katanti attho. Ekaccānanti idhāpi anuvādādhikaraṇameva adhippetaṃ. Paṭiññātakaraṇe ‘‘ekaccāna’’nti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ dassitaṃ.
commentary_english:
bhāsitaparikkanta means that which is spoken by speech and encompassed by the body; having approached, it is done, such is the meaning.

ekaccāna means here also, the topic is understood to be a restatement.

In the case of acknowledgement, "ekaccāna" indicates the topic of offense.

mula_pali: 51. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ hoti? Idhānanda, bhikkhu codito vā acodito vā āpattiṃ sarati, vivarati uttānīkaroti uttāniṃ karoti (ka.).
