Tena, ānanda, bhikkhunā vuḍḍhataraṃ bhikkhuṃ vuḍḍhataro bhikkhu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ahaṃ, bhante, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, taṃ paṭidesemī’ti. So evamāha – ‘passasī’ti? ‘Āma passāmī’ti. ‘Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī’ti. (‘Saṃvarissāmī’ti.) ( ) vinaye natthi Evaṃ kho, ānanda, paṭiññātakaraṇaṃ hoti, evañca panidhekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vūpasamo hoti yadidaṃ – paṭiññātakaraṇena.
mula_english:
"And how, Ānanda, does acknowledgment-and-doing come to be? Here, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu*, whether accused or not accused, remembers an offense (*āpatti*), reveals it, and makes it known.

Then, Ānanda, the *bhikkhu* should approach a more senior *bhikkhu*, and after arranging his robe on one shoulder, pay homage at his feet, and sit on his heels, raise his joined palms, and say this to him: ‘Venerable sir (*bhante*), I have committed such and such an offense (*āpatti*); I confess it.’

He says: ‘Do you see it?’ ‘Yes, I see it.’

‘You should restrain yourself in the future (*āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī’ti*).’

(‘I will restrain myself.’) Thus, Ānanda, acknowledgment-and-doing comes to be, and in this way there is a settling of some legal questions by means of acknowledgment-and-doing."

mula_pali: 52. ‘‘Kathañcānanda , tassapāpiyasikā hoti? Idhānanda, bhikkhu bhikkhuṃ evarūpāya garukāya āpattiyā codeti pārājikena vā pārājikasāmantena vā – ‘saratāyasmā evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti? So evamāha – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sarāmi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. Tamenaṃ so nibbeṭhentaṃ ativeṭheti – ‘iṅghāyasmā sādhukameva jānāhi yadi sarasi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. So evamāha – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sarāmi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā; sarāmi ca kho ahaṃ, āvuso, evarūpiṃ appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā’ti. Tamenaṃ so nibbeṭhentaṃ ativeṭheti – ‘iṅghāyasmā sādhukameva jānāhi yadi sarasi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti? So evamāha – ‘imañhi nāmāhaṃ, āvuso, appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā apuṭṭho paṭijānissāmi. Kiṃ panāhaṃ evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā puṭṭho napaṭijānissāmī’ti? So evamāha – ‘imañhi nāma tvaṃ, āvuso , appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā apuṭṭho napaṭijānissasi, kiṃ pana tvaṃ evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā puṭṭho apuṭṭho (syā. kaṃ. ka.) paṭijānissasi? Iṅghāyasmā sādhukameva jānāhi yadi sarasi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. So evamāha – ‘sarāmi kho ahaṃ, āvuso, evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā. Davā me etaṃ vuttaṃ, ravā me etaṃ vuttaṃ – nāhaṃ taṃ sarāmi evarūpiṃ garukaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitā pārājikaṃ vā pārājikasāmantaṃ vā’ti. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, tassapāpiyasikā hoti, evañca panidhekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vūpasamo hoti yadidaṃ – tassapāpiyasikāya.
mula_english:
52. Now, Ānanda, how does the pronouncement of bad character against someone take place? Here, Ānanda, one *bhikkhu* reproves another *bhikkhu* for such and such a grave offence, one involving defeat (*pārājika*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmantena*): ‘Does the venerable one remember having committed such and such a grave offence, one involving defeat or bordering on defeat?’ He says: ‘I do not, friends (*āvuso*), remember having committed such and such a grave offence, one involving defeat or bordering on defeat.’

Despite the denial, the former presses the latter further: ‘Come on, Venerable (*āyasmā*), try harder to remember whether you’ve committed such and such a heavy offense, one involving defeat (*pārājikaṃ*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmantam*)?’

He says: ‘I do not, friends (*āvuso*), remember having committed such and such a grave offence, one involving defeat or bordering on defeat. But, friends (*āvuso*), I remember having committed such and such a minor offence (*appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ*)’

Despite the denial, the former presses the latter further: ‘Come on, Venerable (*āyasmā*), try harder to remember whether you’ve committed such and such a heavy offense, one involving defeat (*pārājikaṃ*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmantam*)?’

He says: ‘Indeed, friend (*āvuso*), having committed a minor offense (*appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ*), I would acknowledge it even if not asked.

But why would I, having committed such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat (*pārājikaṃ*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmantam*), not acknowledge it when asked?’

He says: ‘Indeed, friend (*āvuso*), if you had committed a minor offense (*appamattikaṃ āpattiṃ*) you would not acknowledge it if not asked, so why would you, having committed such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat (*pārājikaṃ*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmantam*), acknowledge it when asked?’ Come on, Venerable (*āyasmā*), try harder to remember whether you’ve committed such and such a heavy offense, one involving defeat (*pārājikaṃ*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmantam*)?’

He says: ‘I remember, friends (*āvuso*), having committed such and such a grave offense, one involving defeat (*pārājikaṃ*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmantam*).

That was said to me in a moment of panic; that was said to me in a moment of confusion – I do not remember committing such and such a grave offence, one involving defeat (*pārājikaṃ*) or bordering on defeat (*pārājikasāmantam*)’

Thus, Ānanda, does the pronouncement of bad character against someone take place. And so there comes to be the settlement of some litigations here by the pronouncement of bad character against someone.
commentary_pali: 52.Davāti sahasā. Ravāti aññaṃ bhaṇitukāmena aññaṃ vuttaṃ. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, tassapāpiyasikā hotīti tassapuggalassa pāpussannatā pāpiyasikā hoti. Iminā kammassa vatthu dassitaṃ. Evarūpassa hi puggalassa kammaṃ kāttabbaṃ. Kammena hi adhikaraṇassa vūpasamo hoti, na puggalassa pāpussannatāya. Idhāpi ca anuvādādhikaraṇameva adhikaraṇanti veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
52. *davāti sahasā.*
*ravāti aññaṃ bhaṇitukāmena aññaṃ vuttaṃ.*
*evaṃ kho, Ānanda, tassapāpiyasikā hotī*ti tassapuggalassa pāpussannatā pāpiyasikā hoti.
iminā kammassa vatthu dassitaṃ.
evarūpassa hi puggalassa kammaṃ kāttabbaṃ.
kammena hi adhikaraṇassa vūpasamo hoti, na puggalassa pāpussannatāya.
idhāpi ca anuvādādhikaraṇameva adhikaraṇanti veditabbaṃ.

mula_pali:
53. ‘‘Kathañcānanda , tiṇavatthārako hoti? Idhānanda, bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ hoti bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Tehānanda, bhikkhūhi sabbeheva samaggehi sannipatitabbaṃ. Sannipatitvā ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ byattena byattatarena (sī. pī. ka.) bhikkhunā uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

‘Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ . Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva imesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ āpatti yā ca attano āpatti, imesañceva āyasmantānaṃ atthāya attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ ṭhapetvā gihipaṭisaṃyutta’’’nti.

‘‘Athāparesaṃ ekatopakkhikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ byattena bhikkhunā uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

‘Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ amhākaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ kalahajātānaṃ vivādāpannānaṃ viharataṃ bahuṃ assāmaṇakaṃ ajjhāciṇṇaṃ bhāsitaparikkantaṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ yā ceva imesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ āpatti yā ca attano āpatti, imesañceva āyasmantānaṃ atthāya attano ca atthāya, saṅghamajjhe tiṇavatthārakena deseyyaṃ, ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ ṭhapetvā gihipaṭisaṃyutta’’’nti.

‘‘Evaṃ kho, ānanda, tiṇavatthārako hoti, evañca panidhekaccānaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ vūpasamo hoti yadidaṃ – tiṇavatthārakena.
mula_english:
53. How, Ānanda, does the covering over with grass ( *tiṇavatthāraka*) occur? Here, Ānanda, when monks have taken to quarreling and brawling and are deep in disputes, they may have said and done many things improper for a recluse. Those bhikkhus should all meet together in concord. Then, having met together, a capable ( *byatta*) monk among the monks on one side (or holding one view) should rise from his seat, put his upper robe over one shoulder, pay respect with joined palms, and inform the *saṃgha*:

‘Bhante, may the *saṃgha* hear me. When we took to quarreling and brawling and were deep in disputes, we said and did many things improper for a recluse. If it seems appropriate to the *saṃgha*, then for the benefit of these venerables and myself, I’ll confess in the midst of the *saṃgha* by the method of covering over with grass ( *tiṇavatthāraka*), except for heavy offenses (*thullavajja*) and offenses connected with householders (*gihipaṭisaṃyutta*)’’.

Then a capable monk among the monks on one side should rise from his seat, put his upper robe over one shoulder, pay respect with joined palms, and inform the *saṃgha*:

‘Bhante, may the *saṃgha* hear me. When we took to quarreling and brawling and were deep in disputes, we said and did many things improper for a recluse. If it seems appropriate to the *saṃgha*, then for the benefit of these venerables and myself, I’ll confess in the midst of the *saṃgha* by the method of covering over with grass, except for heavy offenses and offenses connected with householders.’

Thus, Ānanda, is the covering over with grass ( *tiṇavatthāraka*) . And so there comes to be the settlement (*vūpasama*) of some litigations (*adhikaraṇānaṃ*) here by the covering over with grass ( *tiṇavatthāraka*).
commentary_pali: 53.Kathañcānanda, tiṇavatthārakoti ettha idaṃ kammaṃ tiṇavatthārakasadisattā tiṇavatthārakoti vuttaṃ. Yathā hi gūthaṃ vā muttaṃ vā ghaṭṭiyamānaṃ duggandhatāya bādhati, tiṇehi avattharitvā suppaṭicchāditassa panassa so gandho na bādhati, evameva yaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ mūlānumūlaṃ gantvā vūpasamiyamānaṃ kakkhaḷattāya vāḷattāya bhedāya saṃvattati, taṃ iminā kammena vūpasantaṃ gūthaṃ viya tiṇavatthārakena paṭicchannaṃ vūpasantaṃ hotīti idaṃ kammaṃ tiṇavatthārakasadisattā tiṇavatthārakoti vuttaṃ. Tassa idhānanda, bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātānantiādivacanena ākāramattameva dassitaṃ, khandhake āgatāyeva panettha kammavācā pamāṇaṃ. Ṭhapetvā thullavajjaṃ ṭhapetvā gihipaṭisaṃyuttanti. Ettha pana thullavajjanti thūllavajjaṃ pārājikañceva saṅghādisesañca. Gihipaṭisaṃyuttanti gihīnaṃ hīnena khuṃsanavambhanadhammikapaṭissavesu āpannā āpatti. Adhikaraṇānanti idha āpattādhikaraṇameva veditabbaṃ. Kiccādhikaraṇassa pana vasena idha na kiñci vuttaṃ. Kiñcāpi na vuttaṃ, sammukhāvinayeneva panassa vūpasamo hotīti veditabbo.
commentary_english:
53. How, Ānanda, is it a 'covering-over like grass' ( *tiṇavatthārako*)? Here, this action is called "covering-over like grass" because of its similarity to covering-over like grass ( *tiṇavatthāraka-sadisattā* ).

Just as, if excrement ( *gūthaṃ* ) or urine ( *muttaṃ* ) is being stirred, it stinks and is offensive, but if it is covered over with grass ( *tiṇehi avattharitvā* ) and well-concealed, that smell is not offensive, so too, any legal question ( *adhikaraṇaṃ* ) that, after going from root to root ( *mūlānumūlaṃ gantvā* ) and being appeased ( *vūpasamiyamānaṃ* ), tends towards harshness ( *kakkhaḷattāya* ), violence ( *vāḷattāya* ), and division ( *bhedāya saṃvattati* ), is calmed by this action, covered over like excrement is covered by grass, and is appeased—therefore, this action is called "covering-over like grass" because of its similarity to covering-over like grass.

Regarding this, by the statement "Here, Ānanda, among the monks who are quarrelsome (*bhikkhūnaṃ bhaṇḍanajātāna*)," etc., only a general idea (*ākāramattameva*) has been shown; in the *khandhaka*, the formal act (*kammavācā*) itself, which has come down [to us], is the standard (*pramāṇaṃ*).

"[Excepting] a grave offense (*thullavajjaṃ*), [excepting matters] connected with laypeople (*gihipaṭisaṃyuttaṃ*)."

Here, *thullavajjaṃ* means a grave offense, a defeat ( *pārājikañceva* ), and a formal suspension ( *saṃghādisesañca* ).

"*Gihipaṭisaṃyuttaṃ*" means an offense ( *āpatti* ) incurred by laypeople in connection with base flattery, boasting, and making deceptive promises related to the Dharma.

"*Adhikaraṇāna*" here should be understood as offenses regarding legal questions ( *āpattādhikaraṇameva veditabbaṃ* ).

However, nothing has been said here concerning the procedural questions ( *kiccādhikaraṇassa pana vasena* ).

Even though nothing has been said, it should be understood that its appeasement ( *vūpasamo hoti* ) comes about only through the *sammukhāvinaya*.

mula_pali:
54. ‘‘Chayime , ānanda, dhammā sāraṇīyā piyakaraṇā garukaraṇā saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattanti. Katame cha? Idhānanda, bhikkhuno mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu – ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi tathārūpehi lābhehi – apaṭivibhattabhogī hoti, sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu – yāni tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṃvattanikāni tathārūpesu sīlesu – sīlasāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu – yāyaṃ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayā tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā – diṭṭhisāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca. Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, ānanda, cha sāraṇīyā dhammā piyakaraṇā garukaraṇā saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattanti.

‘‘Ime ce tumhe, ānanda, cha sāraṇīye dhamme samādāya vatteyyātha, passatha no tumhe, ānanda, taṃ vacanapathaṃ aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vā yaṃ tumhe nādhivāseyyāthā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Tasmātihānanda , ime cha sāraṇīye dhamme samādāya vattatha. Taṃ vo bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Sāmagāmasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.
mula_english:
54. Ananda, there are these six memorable qualities that create love and respect, and conduce to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

What are the six? Here, Ananda, a *bhikkhu* maintains bodily acts of loving-kindness (*mettā*) both in public and in private towards his companions in the holy life. This too is a condition (*dhamma*) that is conducive to amiability, that engenders feelings of endearment, engenders feelings of respect, leading to a sense of fellowship, a lack of disputes, harmony, & a state of unity.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* maintains verbal acts of loving-kindness (*mettā*) both in public and in private towards his companions in the holy life. This too is a condition (*dhamma*) that is conducive to amiability, that engenders feelings of endearment, engenders feelings of respect, leading to a sense of fellowship, a lack of disputes, harmony, & a state of unity.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* maintains mental acts of loving-kindness (*mettā*) both in public and in private towards his companions in the holy life. This too is a condition (*dhamma*) that is conducive to amiability, that engenders feelings of endearment, engenders feelings of respect, leading to a sense of fellowship, a lack of disputes, harmony, & a state of unity.

Furthermore, Ānanda, whatever gains a *bhikkhu* obtains that are in accordance with the Dharma (*dhamma*) and have been righteously gained, even the mere contents of his alms bowl, he shares without reservation with his virtuous companions in the holy life. This too is a condition (*dhamma*) that is conducive to amiability, that engenders feelings of endearment, engenders feelings of respect, leading to a sense of fellowship, a lack of disputes, harmony, & a state of unity.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* dwells both in public and in private possessing in common with his companions in the holy life those virtues (*śīla*) that are unbroken, untorn, unblotched, unmottled, liberating, commended by the wise, not misapprehended, and conducive to concentration (*samādhi*). This too is a condition (*dhamma*) that is conducive to amiability, that engenders feelings of endearment, engenders feelings of respect, leading to a sense of fellowship, a lack of disputes, harmony, & a state of unity.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* dwells both in public and in private possessing in common with his companions in the holy life that view (*dṛṣṭi*) that is noble and emancipating, and leads the one who practises in accordance with it to the complete destruction of suffering (*duḥkha*). This too is a condition (*dhamma*) that is conducive to amiability, that engenders feelings of endearment, engenders feelings of respect, leading to a sense of fellowship, a lack of disputes, harmony, & a state of unity.

These are the six memorable qualities that create love and respect, and conduce to helpfulness, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.

Ānanda, if you undertake and maintain these six memorable qualities, do you see any course of speech, trivial or gross, that you could not endure?

"No, venerable sir."

Therefore, Ānanda, undertake and maintain these six memorable qualities. That will lead to your welfare and happiness for a long time.

Thus spoke the Lord.

The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Sāmagāma Sutta, the fourth [discourse], is finished.
commentary_pali:
54.Chayime, ānanda, dhammā sāraṇīyāti heṭṭhā kalahavasena suttaṃ āraddhaṃ, upari sāraṇīyadhammā āgatā. Iti yathānusandhināva desanā gatā hoti. Heṭṭhā kosambiyasutte (ma. ni. 1.498-500) pana sotāpattimaggasammādiṭṭhi kathitā, imasmiṃ sutte sotāpattiphalasammādiṭṭhi vuttāti veditabbā. Aṇunti appasāvajjaṃ. Thūlanti mahāsāvajjaṃ. Sesamettha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Sāmagāmasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
54. "These six things, Ānanda, are conducive to cordiality," thus the *sutta* was begun below in terms of strife, and above the things conducive to cordiality have come. Thus, the teaching proceeds according to connection. Below, in the Kosambiya Sutta (Majjhima Nikāya 1.498-500), the right view of the path of stream-entry (*sotāpattimagga-sammādiṭṭhi*) is spoken of, in this *sutta* the right view of the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala-sammādiṭṭhi*) is said; this should be understood. *Aṇu* means a small fault. *Thūla* means a great fault. The rest is evident.

The Samagāma Sutta Commentary, from the Papañcasūdanī, commentary on the Majjhima Nikāya, is finished.

mula_pali: 55. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulehi bhikkhūhi bhagavato santike aññā byākatā hoti – ‘‘‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā’’ti. Assosi kho sunakkhatto licchaviputto – ‘‘sambahulehi kira bhikkhūhi bhagavato santike aññā byākatā hoti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā’’ti. Atha kho sunakkhatto licchaviputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho sunakkhatto licchaviputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘sambahulehi kira bhikkhūhi bhagavato santike aññā byākatā – khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ye te, bhante, bhikkhū bhagavato santike aññaṃ byākaṃsu – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā’’ti, kacci te, bhante, bhikkhū sammadeva aññaṃ byākaṃsu udāhu santetthekacce bhikkhū adhimānena aññaṃ byākaṃsūti?
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Vesali in the Great Wood in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.

Now on that occasion a number of *bhikkhus* had declared final knowledge in the presence of the Blessed One thus: “We understand: Birth is destroyed (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā*).”

Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, heard: “A number of *bhikkhus*, it seems, have declared final knowledge in the presence of the Blessed One thus: ‘We understand: Birth is destroyed (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā*).”

Then Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, said to the Blessed One: “I have heard, venerable sir, that a number of *bhikkhus* have declared final knowledge in the presence of the Blessed One, saying: ‘We understand: Birth is destroyed (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā*).”

“Those *bhikkhus*, venerable sir, who in the presence of the Blessed One declared final knowledge, saying: ‘Birth is destroyed (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā*)’—did those *bhikkhus* rightly declare final knowledge, venerable sir, or are there some *bhikkhus* here who declared final knowledge out of conceit (*adhimānena*)?”
commentary_pali: 55.Evaṃme sutanti sunakkhattasuttaṃ. Tattha aññāti arahattaṃ. Byākatāti khīṇā jātītiādīhi catūhi padehi kathitā. Adhimānenāti appatte pattasaññino, anadhigate adhigatasaññino hutvā adhigataṃ amhehīti mānena byākariṃsu.
commentary_english: 55. *Evaṃ me suta* is the Sunakkhatta Sutta. There, *aññā* means *arhattva* (arahatship). *Byākatā* means spoken with four terms beginning with "destroyed is birth." *Adhimānenā* means, thinking what is unobtained to be obtained, and what is unachieved to be achieved, they declared out of pride, "We have achieved [it]."

mula_pali: 56. ‘‘Ye te, sunakkhatta, bhikkhū mama santike aññaṃ byākaṃsu – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmā’’ti . ‘‘Santetthekacce bhikkhū sammadeva aññaṃ byākaṃsu, santi panidhekacce bhikkhū adhimānenapi adhimānena (?) aññaṃ byākaṃsu. Tatra, sunakkhatta, ye te bhikkhū sammadeva aññaṃ byākaṃsu tesaṃ taṃ tatheva hoti; ye pana te bhikkhū adhimānena aññaṃ byākaṃsu tatra, sunakkhatta, tathāgatassa evaṃ hoti – ‘dhammaṃ nesaṃ desessa’nti deseyyanti (pī. ka.). Evañcettha, sunakkhatta, tathāgatassa hoti – ‘dhammaṃ nesaṃ desessa’nti. Atha ca panidhekacce moghapurisā pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharitvā abhisaṅkharitvā tathāgataṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchanti. Tatra, sunakkhatta, yampi tathāgatassa evaṃ hoti – ‘dhammaṃ nesaṃ desessa’nti tassapi hoti aññathatta’’nti. ‘‘Etassa bhagavā kālo, etassa sugata kālo, yaṃ bhagavā dhammaṃ deseyya. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, sunakkhatta suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi ; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho sunakkhatto licchaviputto bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
56. “When those *bhikkhus*, Sunakkhatta, declared final knowledge in my presence, saying, ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being,’
There were some *bhikkhus* who declared final knowledge rightly, and there were some *bhikkhus* who declared final knowledge because they overestimated themselves.
Therein, Sunakkhatta, when *bhikkhus* declare final knowledge rightly, their declaration is true. But when *bhikkhus* declare final knowledge because they overestimate themselves, the *Tathāgata* thinks: ‘Let me teach them the *Dhamma*.’
Thus it is in this case, Sunakkhatta, that the *Tathāgata* thinks: ‘Let me teach them the *Dhamma*.’
But some misguided men here formulate a question, come to the *Tathāgata*, and ask it.
In that case, Sunakkhatta, though the *Tathāgata* has thought: ‘Let me teach them the *Dhamma*,’ he changes his mind.”
“This is the time, Blessed One (*Bhagavā*), this is the time, Sublime One (*Sugata*), for the Blessed One to teach the *Dhamma*.
Having heard it from the Blessed One, the *bhikkhus* will remember it.”
“Then listen, Sunakkhatta, and attend closely to what I shall say; I will speak.”
“Yes, venerable sir (*bhante*),” Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
commentary_pali: 56.Evañcettha sunakkhatta tathāgatassa hotīti sunakkhatta ettha etesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañhabyākaraṇe – ‘‘idaṃ ṭhānaṃ etesaṃ avibhūtaṃ andhakāraṃ, tenime anadhigate adhigatasaññino, handa nesaṃ visodhetvā pākaṭaṃ katvā dhammaṃ desemī’’ti, evañca tathāgatassa hoti. Atha ca panidhekacce…pe… tassapi hoti aññathattanti bhagavā paṭipannakānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti. Yattha pana icchācāre ṭhitā ekacce moghapurisā honti, tatra bhagavā passati – ‘‘ime imaṃ pañhaṃ uggahetvā ajānitvāva jānantā viya appatte pattasaññino hutvā gāmanigamādīsu visevamānā vicarissanti, taṃ nesaṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’’ti evamassāyaṃ icchācāre ṭhitānaṃ kāraṇā paṭipannakānampi atthāya ‘‘dhammaṃ desissāmī’’ti uppannassa cittassa aññathābhāvo hoti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
56. Moreover, in this case, Sunakkhatta, the *Tathāgata* has this thought: Sunakkhatta, in this questioning of the monks, "This place is unmanifest, dark for them, so these are those who perceive themselves as having attained what they have not attained. Come, having purified and made manifest for them, I will teach the *Dharma*." Thus, the *Tathāgata* has this thought.

Furthermore, the Blessed One teaches the *Dharma* to those who are practicing, [saying] "But some here...pe... he also has a different state."

Wherever, moreover, some foolish men abide in arbitrary conduct, there the Blessed One sees: "Having taken up this question, without knowing, they wander about behaving as if they know in the villages and towns, experiencing as attained what is unattained. That will be for their harm and suffering for a long time." Thus, this alteration of mind occurs to him because of those abiding in arbitrary conduct, also for the sake of those who are practicing, thinking, "I will teach the *Dharma*."

This was said with reference to this.

mula_pali: 57. ‘‘Pañca kho ime, sunakkhatta, kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, sunakkhatta, pañca kāmaguṇā.
mula_english:
Verse 57.
"Sunakkhatta, there are these five cords of sensual pleasure (pañca kāmaguṇā). Which five? Forms cognizable by the eye (cakṣurvijñeyyā rūpā) that are wished for (iṣṭhā), desired (kāntā), agreeable (manāpā), and likeable (priyarūpā), connected with sensual desire (kāmūpasaṃhitā) and provocative of lust (rajanīyā); sounds cognizable by the ear (śotravijñeyyā śabdā)...odours cognizable by the nose (ghānavijñeyyā gandhā)...flavours cognizable by the tongue (jihvāvijñeyyā rasā)...tangibles cognizable by the body (kāyavijñeyyā spraṣṭavyā) that are wished for (iṣṭhā), desired (kāntā), agreeable (manāpā), and likeable (priyarūpā), connected with sensual desire (kāmūpasaṃhitā) and provocative of lust (rajanīyā). These, Sunakkhatta, are the five cords of sensual pleasure (pañca kāmaguṇā)."

mula_pali: 58. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco purisapuggalo lokāmisādhimutto assa. Lokāmisādhimuttassa kho, sunakkhatta, purisapuggalassa tappatirūpī ceva kathā saṇṭhāti, tadanudhammañca anuvitakketi, anuvicāreti, tañca purisaṃ bhajati, tena ca vittiṃ āpajjati; āneñjapaṭisaṃyuttāya ca pana kathāya kacchamānāya na sussūsati, na sotaṃ odahati, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti upaṭṭhapeti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), na ca taṃ purisaṃ bhajati, na ca tena vittiṃ āpajjati. Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, puriso sakamhā gāmā vā nigamā vā ciravippavuttho assa. So aññataraṃ purisaṃ passeyya tamhā gāmā vā nigamā vā acirapakkantaṃ. So taṃ purisaṃ tassa gāmassa vā nigamassa vā khematañca subhikkhatañca appābādhatañca puccheyya; tassa so puriso tassa gāmassa vā nigamassa vā khematañca subhikkhatañca appābādhatañca saṃseyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, api nu so puriso tassa purisassa sussūseyya, sotaṃ odaheyya, aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyya, tañca purisaṃ bhajeyya, tena ca vittiṃ āpajjeyyā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Evameva kho, sunakkhatta, ṭhānametaṃ vijjati yaṃ idhekacco purisapuggalo lokāmisādhimutto assa. Lokāmisādhimuttassa kho, sunakkhatta, purisapuggalassa tappatirūpī ceva kathā saṇṭhāti, tadanudhammañca anuvitakketi, anuvicāreti, tañca purisaṃ bhajati, tena ca vittiṃ āpajjati; āneñjapaṭisaṃyuttāya ca pana kathāya kacchamānāya na sussūsati, na sotaṃ odahati, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na ca taṃ purisaṃ bhajati, na ca tena vittiṃ āpajjati. So evamassa veditabbo – ‘āneñjasaṃyojanena hi kho visaṃyutto āneñjasaṃyojanena hi kho visaṃyutto-iti pāṭho sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi, aṭṭhakathāsu pana tabbaṇṇanā dissatiyeva lokāmisādhimutto purisapuggalo’’’ti.
mula_english:
58. “It is possible, Sunakkhatta, that some person here may be intent on worldly material things ( *lokāmisādhimutto*).

When a person is intent on worldly material things ( *lokāmisādhimuttassa*), only talk concerning that interests him, and his thinking and pondering are in line with that, and he associates with that kind of person, and he finds satisfaction through him; when talk about the imperturbable is going on, he will not listen to it or give it ear or exert his mind to understand it, and he does not associate with that kind of person, and he does not find satisfaction through him.

“Suppose, Sunakkhatta, a man had left his own village or town a long time ago, and he were to see another man who had only recently left that village or town. He would ask that man whether the people of that village or town were safe, prosperous, and healthy, and that man would tell him whether the people of that village or town were safe, prosperous, and healthy.

What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Would that first man listen to him, give him ear, and exert his mind to understand, and associate with that man, and find satisfaction through him?” “Yes, sir.”

“So too, Sunakkhatta, it is possible that some person here may be intent on worldly material things ( *lokāmisādhimutto*).

When a person is intent on worldly material things ( *lokāmisādhimuttassa*), only talk concerning that interests him, and his thinking and pondering are in line with that, and he associates with that kind of person, and he finds satisfaction through him; when talk about the imperturbable is going on, he will not listen to it or give it ear or exert his mind to understand it, and he does not associate with that kind of person, and he does not find satisfaction through him.

He should be understood thus: ‘The person intent on worldly material things ( *lokāmisādhimutto purisapuggalo*) is detached from the bond of the imperturbable.’
commentary_pali: 58.Lokāmisādhimuttoti vaṭṭāmisa-kāmāmisa-lokāmisabhūtesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu adhimutto tanninno taggaruko tappabbhāro. Tappatirūpīti kāmaguṇasabhāgā. Āneñjapaṭisaṃyuttāyāti āneñjasamāpattipaṭisaṃyuttāya. Saṃseyyāti katheyya. Āneñjasaṃyojanena hi kho visaṃyuttoti āneñjasamāpattisaṃyojanena visaṃsaṭṭho. Lokāmisādhimuttoti evarūpo hi lūkhacīvaradharo mattikāpattaṃ ādāya attano sadisehi katipayehi saddhiṃ paccantajanapadaṃ gacchati, gāmaṃ piṇḍāya paviṭṭhakāle manussā disvā ‘‘mahāpaṃsukulikā āgatā’’ti yāgubhattādīni sampādetvā sakkaccaṃ dānaṃ denti, bhattakicce niṭṭhite anumodanaṃ sutvā – ‘‘svepi, bhante, idheva piṇḍāya pavisathā’’ti vadanti. Alaṃ upāsakā, ajjāpi vo bahūnaṃ dinnanti. Tena hi, bhante, antovassaṃ idha vaseyyāthāti adhivāsetvā vihāramaggaṃ pucchitvā vihāraṃ gacchanti. Tattha senāsanaṃ gahetvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭisāmenti. Sāyaṃ eko āvāsiko te bhikkhū pucchati ‘‘kattha piṇḍāya caritthā’’ti? Asukagāmeti. Bhikkhāsampannāti? Āma evarūpā nāma manussānaṃ saddhā hoti. ‘‘Ajjeva nu kho ete edisā, niccampi edisā’’ti? Saddhā te manussā niccampi edisā, te nissāyeva ayaṃ vihāro vaḍḍhatīti. Tato te paṃsukulikā punappunaṃ tesaṃ vaṇṇaṃ kathenti , divasāvasesaṃ kathetvā rattimpi kathenti. Ettāvatā icchācāre ṭhitassa sīsaṃ nikkhantaṃ hoti udaraṃ phālitaṃ. Evaṃ lokāmisādhimutto veditabbo.
commentary_english:
58. *Lokāmisādhimutto* means one who is intent on worldly material things, attached to the five sense pleasures ( *kāmaguṇa*), immersed in them, delighting in them, and given over to them.

*Tappatirūpī* means sharing the same nature as the sense pleasures (*kāmaguṇa*).

*Āneñjapaṭisaṃyuttāyā* means associated with the attainment of imperturbability (*āneñjasamāpatti*).

*Saṃseyyā* means he should say.

*Āneñjasaṃyojanena hi kho visaṃyutto* means detached from the fetter of the attainment of imperturbability (*āneñjasamāpatti*).

*Lokāmisādhimutto* means someone who is of this kind: clothed in rough robes (*lūkhacīvaradhara*), carrying a clay bowl (*mattikāpattaṃ*), and going with some others like himself to a border area (*paccantajanapadaṃ*). When they enter a village for alms (*piṇḍāya*), people see them and, thinking, "The great *paṃsukulikas* have arrived," they prepare rice gruel and other things (*yāgubhattādīni*) and respectfully give alms (*dānaṃ denti*). When the meal is finished, after hearing the thanksgiving (*anumodanaṃ*), they say, "Venerable sirs (*bhante*), may you enter here for alms again tomorrow (*svepi*)."

Enough, lay followers (*upāsaka*), even today alms have been given to many of you.

Then, having invited them with the words, "Venerable sirs (*bhante*), may you spend the rainy season (*antovassaṃ*) here," they ask the way to the monastery (*vihāramaggaṃ*) and go to the monastery (*vihāraṃ*).

There, having taken lodging (*senāsanaṃ*), they put away their bowl and robe (*pattacīvaraṃ*).

In the evening, one resident monk (*āvāsiko*) asks those monks (*bhikkhū*), "Where did you go for alms (*piṇḍāya* )?" "To such and such a village."

"Are you accomplished in alms-begging (*bhikkhāsampannā*)?" "Yes, such faith (*saddhā*) arises in people (*manussānaṃ*)."

"Are they like this only today, or are they always like this (*niccampi*)?" "The faith (*saddhā*) of those people (*manussā*) is always (*niccampi*) like this; it is because of them that this monastery (*vihāro*) thrives (*vaḍḍhati*)."

Then those *paṃsukulikas* repeatedly tell their praise (*vaṇṇaṃ kathenti*), having told it during the remainder of the day (*divasāvasesaṃ kathetvā*), they tell it even at night (*rattimpi kathenti*).

To such an extent, the head of one abiding in arbitrary conduct (*icchācāre ṭhita*) bursts off, and the belly is split open (*udaraṃ phālitaṃ*).

In this way, one should understand *lokāmisādhimutto*.

mula_pali: 59. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco purisapuggalo āneñjādhimutto assa. Āneñjādhimuttassa kho, sunakkhatta, purisapuggalassa tappatirūpī ceva kathā saṇṭhāti, tadanudhammañca anuvitakketi, anuvicāreti, tañca purisaṃ bhajati, tena ca vittiṃ āpajjati; lokāmisapaṭisaṃyuttāya ca pana kathāya kacchamānāya na sussūsati, na sotaṃ odahati, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na ca taṃ purisaṃ bhajati, na ca tena vittiṃ āpajjati. Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, paṇḍupalāso bandhanā pavutto abhabbo haritattāya; evameva kho, sunakkhatta, āneñjādhimuttassa purisapuggalassa ye lokāmisasaṃyojane se pavutte. So evamassa veditabbo – ‘lokāmisasaṃyojanena hi kho visaṃyutto āneñjādhimutto purisapuggalo’’’ti.
mula_english:
59. Moreover, Sunakkhatta, it is possible that a certain person here is intent on the imperturbable.

When a person is intent on the imperturbable, only talk concerning that interests him, and his thinking and pondering are in line with that, and he associates with that kind of person, and he finds satisfaction through him. But when talk about worldly material things is going on, he will not listen to it or give it ear or exert his mind to understand it. He does not associate with that kind of person, and he does not find satisfaction through him.

“Just as a yellow leaf that has fallen from its stalk is incapable of becoming green again, so too, Sunakkhatta, when a person is intent on the imperturbable he has shed the fetter of worldly material things.

He should be understood as a person not bound by the fetter of worldly material things who is intent on the imperturbable.
commentary_pali: 59. Idāni āneñjasamāpattilābhiṃ adhimānikaṃ dassento ṭhānaṃ kho panetantiādimāha. Āneñjādhimuttassāti kilesasiñcanavirahitāsu heṭṭhimāsu chasu samāpattīsu adhimuttassa tanninnassa taggaruno tappabbhārassa. Se pavutteti taṃ pavuttaṃ. Cha samāpattilābhino hi adhimānikassa pañcakāmaguṇāmisabandhanā patitapaṇḍupalāso viya upaṭṭhāti. Tenetaṃ vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
Now, showing the conceited person who has gained access to the attainment of immovability, he says, "Indeed, this is the place," and so forth.

"'For one resolved on immovability' means for one resolved on the lower six attainments, which are free from the sprinkling of defilements, for one who inclines toward that, who holds that dear, who is devoted to that.

"'Because it is spoken' means it is spoken.

Indeed, for the conceited person who has obtained the six attainments, the bond of the allurement of the five sense pleasures stands like a fallen yellow leaf.

Therefore, it was said:

mula_pali: 60. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco purisapuggalo ākiñcaññāyatanādhimutto assa. Ākiñcaññāyatanādhimuttassa kho, sunakkhatta, purisapuggalassa tappatirūpī ceva kathā saṇṭhāti, tadanudhammañca anuvitakketi, anuvicāreti, tañca purisaṃ bhajati, tena ca vittiṃ āpajjati ; āneñjapaṭisaṃyuttāya ca pana kathāya kacchamānāya na sussūsati, na sotaṃ odahati, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti , na ca taṃ purisaṃ bhajati, na ca tena vittiṃ āpajjati. Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, puthusilā dvedhābhinnā appaṭisandhikā hoti; evameva kho, sunakkhatta, ākiñcaññāyatanādhimuttassa purisapuggalassa ye āneñjasaṃyojane se bhinne. So evamassa veditabbo – ‘āneñjasaṃyojanena hi kho visaṃyutto ākiñcaññāyatanādhimutto purisapuggalo’’’ti.
mula_english:
“It is possible, Sunakkhatta, that some person here may be intent on the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatanādhimutto).

When a person is intent on the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatanādhimuttassa), only talk concerning that interests him, and his thinking and pondering are in line with that, and he associates with that kind of person, and he finds satisfaction through him. But when talk about the imperturbable is going on, he will not listen to it or give it ear or exert his mind to understand it. He does not associate with that kind of person, and he does not find satisfaction through him.

“Just as a thick stone that has split in two cannot be joined together again, so too, Sunakkhatta, when a person is intent on the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatanādhimuttassa) his fetter of the imperturbable (āneñjasaṃyojane) has been split.

He should be understood as a person not bound by the fetter of the imperturbable (āneñjasaṃyojanena) who is intent on the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatanādhimutto).
commentary_pali: 60. Idāni ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpatti lābhino adhimānikassa nighaṃsaṃ dassetuṃ ṭhānaṃ kho panātiādimāha. Tattha dvedhā bhinnāti majjhe bhinnā. Appaṭisandhikāti khuddakā muṭṭhipāsāṇamattā jatunā vā silesena vā allīyāpetvā paṭisandhātuṃ sakkā. Mahantaṃ pana kuṭāgārappamāṇaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Se bhinneti taṃ bhinnaṃ. Upari samāpattilābhino hi heṭṭhāsamāpatti dvedhābhinnā selā viya hoti, taṃ samāpajjissāmīti cittaṃ na uppajjati. Tenetaṃ vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
Now, to show the disparagement of the conceited one who has attained the attainment of the sphere of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpatti*), he said, "But where is the place?" and so forth.

There, "*dvedhā bhinnā*" means broken in the middle.

"*appaṭisandhikā*" means small, the size of a fist-stone (*muṭṭhipāsāṇa*), and it is possible to rejoin [them] by sticking [them] together with lac (*jatu*) or glue (*silesa*).

But this was said referring to the size of a large hall (*kuṭāgārappamāṇa*).

"*se bhinne*" means that is broken.

Furthermore, for one who has attained the attainment (*samāpatti*), the lower attainment (*heṭṭhāsamāpatti*), being split in two (*dvedhābhinnā*), is like a rock (*selā viya*), [and] the thought does not occur, "I will attain that (*samāpajjissāmi*)."

That is why it was said.

mula_pali: 61. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco purisapuggalo nevasaññānāsaññāyatanādhimutto assa. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanādhimuttassa kho, sunakkhatta, purisapuggalassa tappatirūpī ceva kathā saṇṭhāti, tadanudhammañca anuvitakketi, anuvicāreti, tañca purisaṃ bhajati, tena ca vittiṃ āpajjati; ākiñcaññāyatanapaṭisaṃyuttāya ca pana kathāya kacchamānāya na sussūsati, na sotaṃ odahati, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na ca taṃ purisaṃ bhajati, na ca tena vittiṃ āpajjati. Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, puriso manuññabhojanaṃ bhuttāvī chaḍḍeyya chaddeyya (?). Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, api nu tassa purisassa tasmiṃ bhatte vante (ka. sī.), bhutte (ka. sī. ka.) puna bhottukamyatā assā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Aduñhi, bhante, bhattaṃ vantaṃ (sī.) paṭikūlasammata’’nti. ‘‘Evameva kho, sunakkhatta, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanādhimuttassa purisapuggalassa ye ākiñcaññāyatanasaṃyojane se vante. So evamassa veditabbo – ‘ākiñcaññāyatanasaṃyojanena hi kho visaṃyutto nevasaññānāsaññāyatanādhimutto purisapuggalo’ti.
mula_english:
61. “It is possible, Sunakkhatta, that some person here may be intent on the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception ( *nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*).

When a person is intent on the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*), only talk concerning that interests him, and his thinking and pondering are in line with that, and he associates with that kind of person, and he finds satisfaction through him. But when talk about the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*) is going on, he will not listen to it or give it ear or exert his mind to understand it. He does not associate with that kind of person, and he does not find satisfaction through him.

“Suppose a person has eaten some delicious food and thrown it up.

What do you think, Sunakkhatta, would that person still have any desire for that food he vomited?” “No, venerable sir.”

“What is the reason for that?” “Because, venerable sir, that food is regarded as repulsive.”

“In the same way, Sunakkhatta, for a person intent on the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*), the attachments to the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*) are like vomit.

He should be understood thus: ‘This person is detached from attachment to the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*) and is intent on the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*)’."
commentary_pali: 61. Idāni nevasaññānāsaññāyatanalābhino adhimānikassa ca nighaṃsaṃ dassento ṭhānaṃ kho panātiādimāha. Tattha se vanteti taṃ vantaṃ. Aṭṭhasamāpattilābhino hi heṭṭhāsamāpattiyo vantasadisā hutvā upaṭṭhahanti, puna samāpajjissāmīti cittaṃ na uppajjati. Tenetaṃ vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
Now, showing the rejection of the over-conceited one who has attained the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception, he says, "But where is the place?" and so on.

There, "he vomits" means that which is vomited.

Because for one who has attained the eight attainments, the lower attainments, having become like vomit, are present, the thought, "I will attain [them] again" does not arise.

That is why it was said.

mula_pali: 62. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco purisapuggalo sammā nibbānādhimutto assa. Sammā nibbānādhimuttassa kho, sunakkhatta, purisapuggalassa tappatirūpī ceva kathā saṇṭhāti, tadanudhammañca anuvitakketi, anuvicāreti, tañca purisaṃ bhajati, tena ca vittiṃ āpajjati; nevasaññānāsaññāyatanapaṭisaṃyuttāya ca pana kathāya kacchamānāya na sussūsati, na sotaṃ odahati, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, na ca taṃ purisaṃ bhajati, na ca tena vittiṃ āpajjati. Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo puna viruḷhiyā; evameva kho, sunakkhatta, sammā nibbānādhimuttassa purisapuggalassa ye nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaṃyojane se ucchinnamūle tālāvatthukate anabhāvaṃkate anabhāvakate (sī. pī.), anabhāvaṅgate (syā. kaṃ.) āyatiṃ anuppādadhamme. So evamassa veditabbo – ‘nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaṃyojanena hi kho visaṃyutto sammā nibbānādhimutto purisapuggalo’’’ti.
mula_english:
“It is possible, Sunakkhatta, that some person here may be completely intent on *Nibbana* (nirvāṇa).

When a person is completely intent on *Nibbana* (nirvāṇa), only talk concerning that interests him, and his thinking and pondering are in line with that, and he associates with that kind of person, and he finds satisfaction through him. But when talk about the base of neither-perception-nor- non-perception is going on, he will not listen to it or give it ear or exert his mind to understand it. He does not associate with that kind of person, and he does not find satisfaction through him.

“Just as a palm tree with its top cut off is incapable of growing again, so too, Sunakkhatta, when a person is completely intent on *Nibbana* (nirvāṇa), his fetter of the base of neither-perception-nor-non- perception has been cut off - cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with so that it is no longer subject to future arising.

He should be understood as a person not bound by the fetter of the base of neither-perception-nor-non- perception who is completely intent on *Nibbana* (nirvāṇa).
commentary_pali: 62. Idāni khīṇāsavassa nighaṃsaṃ dassento ṭhānaṃ kho panātiādimāha. Tattha se ucchinnamūleti so ucchinnamūlo. Upari samāpattilābhino hi heṭṭhāsamāpatti mūlacchinnatālo viya upaṭṭhāti, taṃ samāpajjissāmīti cittaṃ na uppajjati. Tenetaṃ vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
Now, showing the destruction of the *khīṇāsava*, he says, "But where is the place?" etc.

There, "He, with the roots cut off," means he whose root is cut off.

Indeed, for one who has gained higher attainments (*samāpatti*), the lower attainment arises like a palm tree with its roots cut off; the thought, "I will attain that," does not arise.

That is why it was said.

mula_pali:
63. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ idhekaccassa bhikkhuno evamassa – ‘taṇhā kho sallaṃ samaṇena vuttaṃ, avijjāvisadoso, chandarāgabyāpādena ruppati. Taṃ me taṇhāsallaṃ pahīnaṃ, apanīto avijjāvisadoso, sammā nibbānādhimuttohamasmī’ti. Evaṃmāni evaṃmānī (sī. pī. ka.), evamādi (syā. kaṃ.) assa atathaṃ samānaṃ atthaṃ samānaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.), atthasamānaṃ (sī.). So yāni sammā nibbānādhimuttassa asappāyāni tāni anuyuñjeyya; asappāyaṃ cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ sotena saddaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ ghānena gandhaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ jivhāya rasaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ anuyuñjeyya , asappāyaṃ manasā dhammaṃ anuyuñjeyya. Tassa asappāyaṃ cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ sotena saddaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ ghānena gandhaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ jivhāya rasaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ manasā dhammaṃ anuyuttassa rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseyya. So rāgānuddhaṃsitena cittena maraṇaṃ vā nigaccheyya maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, puriso sallena viddho assa savisena gāḷhūpalepanena. Tassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ. Tassa so bhisakko sallakatto satthena vaṇamukhaṃ parikanteyya. Satthena vaṇamukhaṃ parikantitvā esaniyā sallaṃ eseyya. Esaniyā sallaṃ esitvā sallaṃ abbuheyya, apaneyya visadosaṃ saupādisesaṃ. Saupādisesoti anupādisesoti (sabbattha) ayaṃ hi tathāgatassa visayo jānamāno so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ambho purisa, ubbhataṃ kho te sallaṃ, apanīto visadoso saupādiseso anupādiseso (sabbattha) ayampi tathāgatassa visayo. Analañca te antarāyāya. Sappāyāni ceva bhojanāni bhuñjeyyāsi, mā te asappāyāni bhojanāni bhuñjato vaṇo assāvī assa. Kālena kālañca vaṇaṃ dhoveyyāsi, kālena kālaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpeyyāsi, mā te na kālena kālaṃ vaṇaṃ dhovato na kālena kālaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpato pubbalohitaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ pariyonandhi. Mā ca vātātape cārittaṃ anuyuñji, mā te vātātape cārittaṃ anuyuttassa rajosūkaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ anuddhaṃsesi. Vaṇānurakkhī ca, ambho purisa, vihareyyāsi vaṇasāropī’ti vaṇassāropīti (ka.) vaṇa + saṃ + ropī = vaṇasāropī-iti padavibhāgo. Tassa evamassa – ‘ubbhataṃ kho me sallaṃ, apanīto visadoso anupādiseso. Analañca me antarāyāyā’ti. So asappāyāni ceva bhojanāni bhuñjeyya. Tassa asappāyāni bhojanāni bhuñjato vaṇo assāvī assa. Na ca kālena kālaṃ vaṇaṃ dhoveyya, na ca kālena kālaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpeyya. Tassa na kālena kālaṃ vaṇaṃ dhovato, na kālena kālaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpato pubbalohitaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ pariyonandheyya. Vātātape ca cārittaṃ anuyuñjeyya. Tassa vātātape cārittaṃ anuyuttassa rajosūkaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ anuddhaṃseyya. Na ca vaṇānurakkhī vihareyya na vaṇasāropī. Tassa imissā ca asappāyakiriyāya, asuci visadoso apanīto saupādiseso tadubhayena vaṇo puthuttaṃ gaccheyya. So puthuttaṃ gatena vaṇena maraṇaṃ vā nigaccheyya maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ.

anupādisesoti (sabbattha) ayaṃ hi tathāgatassa visayo anupādiseso (sabbattha) ayampi tathāgatassa visayo vaṇassāropīti (ka.) vaṇa + saṃ + ropī = vaṇasāropī-iti padavibhāgo

‘‘Evameva kho, sunakkhatta, ṭhānametaṃ vijjati yaṃ idhekaccassa bhikkhuno evamassa – ‘taṇhā kho sallaṃ samaṇena vuttaṃ, avijjāvisadoso chandarāgabyāpādena ruppati. Taṃ me taṇhāsallaṃ pahīnaṃ, apanīto avijjāvisadoso, sammā nibbānādhimuttohamasmī’ti. Evaṃmāni assa atathaṃ samānaṃ. So yāni sammā nibbānādhimuttassa asappāyāni tāni anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ sotena saddaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ ghānena gandhaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ jivhāya rasaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ anuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ manasā dhammaṃ anuyuñjeyya. Tassa asappāyaṃ cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ sotena saddaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ ghānena gandhaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ jivhāya rasaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ anuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ manasā dhammaṃ anuyuttassa rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseyya. So rāgānuddhaṃsitena cittena maraṇaṃ vā nigaccheyya maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ. Maraṇañhetaṃ, sunakkhatta, ariyassa vinaye yo sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati; maraṇamattañhetaṃ, sunakkhatta, dukkhaṃ yaṃ aññataraṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati.
mula_english:
63. It is possible, Sunakkhatta, that some *bhikkhu* here might think thus: ‘Craving (*taṇhā*) has been called an arrow (*salla*) by the Recluse (*samaṇa*); the poisonous humor of ignorance (*avijjā*) is spread about by desire (*chanda*), lust (*rāga*), and ill will (*byāpāda*). That arrow of craving (*taṇhāsalla*) has been pulled out from me; the poisonous humor of ignorance (*avijjā*) has been expelled. I am one who is completely intent on *Nibbana* (*nibbānādhimutto*).’

Thinking thus, he might be in a state that is not true. He might pursue those things that are unsuitable (*asappāya*) for one completely intent on *Nibbana* (*nibbānādhimuttassa*). He might pursue the sight of unsuitable (*asappāya*) forms (*rūpadassanaṃ*) with the eye (*cakkhunā*), he might pursue unsuitable (*asappāyaṃ*) sounds (*saddaṃ*) with the ear (*sotena*), he might pursue unsuitable (*asappāyaṃ*) odors (*gandhaṃ*) with the nose (*ghānena*), he might pursue unsuitable (*asappāyaṃ*) flavors (*rasaṃ*) with the tongue (*jivhāya*), he might pursue unsuitable (*asappāyaṃ*) tangibles (*phoṭṭhabbaṃ*) with the body (*kāyena*), or unsuitable (*asappāyaṃ*) mind-objects (*dhammaṃ*) with the mind (*manasā*). When he pursues the sight of unsuitable (*asappāyaṃ*) forms (*rūpadassanaṃ*) with the eye (*cakkhunā*)…unsuitable (*asappāyaṃ*) mind-objects (*dhammaṃ*) with the mind (*manasā*), lust (*rāgo*) invades his mind (*cittaṃ anuddhaṃseyya*). With his mind (*cittena*) invaded by lust (*rāgānuddhaṃsitena*), he would incur death (*maraṇaṃ*) or deadly suffering (*maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ*).

Suppose, Sunakkhatta, a man were wounded by an arrow (*sallena*) thickly smeared with poison (*savisena gāḷhūpalepanena*). Then his friends and companions, his kinsmen and relatives (*ñātisālohitā*), would bring a physician (*bhisakkaṃ*) to treat him. The surgeon (*sallakatto*) would cut around the opening of the wound (*vaṇamukhaṃ*) with a knife (*satthena*), then he would probe for the arrow (*sallaṃ*) with a probe (*esaniyā*). Having probed for the arrow (*sallaṃ*) with a probe (*esaniyā*), he would pull out the arrow (*sallaṃ abbuheyya*) and would expel the poisonous humor (*visadosaṃ*) with a trace (*saupādisesaṃ*) left behind.

Knowing that a trace was left behind (*saupādisesoti*), he would say: ‘Good man (*ambho purisa*), the arrow (*sallaṃ*) has been pulled out from you; the poisonous humor (*visadoso*) has been expelled with a trace (*saupādiseso*) left behind. And it is incapable of harming you.’ Eat only suitable (*sappāyāni*) food (*bhojanāni*); do not eat unsuitable (*asappāyāni*) food (*bhojanāni*) or else the wound (*vaṇo*) may suppurate (*assāvī assa*). From time to time wash the wound (*vaṇaṃ dhoveyyāsi*) and from time to time anoint its opening (*vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpeyyāsi*), so that pus and blood (*pubbalohitaṃ*) do not cover the opening of the wound (*vaṇamukhaṃ pariyonandhi*). Do not walk around in the wind and sun (*vātātape cārittaṃ anuyuñji*) or else dust and dirt (*rajosūkaṃ*) may infect the opening of the wound (*vaṇamukhaṃ anuddhaṃsesi*). Take care of your wound (*vaṇānurakkhī*), good man (*ambho purisa*), and see to it that the wound heals (*vaṇasāropī*).’

He might think thus: ‘The arrow (*sallaṃ*) has been pulled out from me; the poisonous humor (*visadoso*) has been expelled with no trace left behind (*anupādiseso*). And it is incapable of harming me.’ He would eat unsuitable (*asappāyāni*) food (*bhojanāni*). Because he eats unsuitable (*asappāyāni*) food (*bhojanāni*), the wound (*vaṇo*) would suppurate (*assāvī assa*). He would not wash the wound (*vaṇaṃ dhoveyya*) from time to time (*kālena kālaṃ*), nor would he anoint its opening (*vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpeyya*) from time to time (*kālena kālaṃ*). Because he does not wash the wound (*vaṇaṃ dhovato*) from time to time (*kālena kālaṃ*), nor does he anoint its opening (*vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpato*) from time to time (*kālena kālaṃ*), pus and blood (*pubbalohitaṃ*) would cover the opening of the wound (*vaṇamukhaṃ pariyonandheyya*). He would walk around in the wind and sun (*vātātape ca cārittaṃ anuyuñjeyya*).
When his character is engaged in wind and heat, the opening of the wound [is like] dust.

He would not take care of his wound, nor would he promote the wound's healing.

Then, both because of this unsuitable action, and because the impure, poisonous humour had been expelled with a trace left behind, the wound would swell.

The wound would swell, and with its swelling he would incur death or deadly suffering.

<note> *anupādisesoti* (everywhere), this is the domain of the *Tathāgata*.</note> <note>*anupādiseso* (everywhere), this too is the domain of the *Tathāgata*.</note>
<note>*vaṇassāropīti* (ka.) *vaṇa* + *saṃ* + *ropī* = *vaṇasāropī*-iti *padavibhāgo*</note>

‘‘So too, Sunakkhatta, it is possible that some bhikkhus here might think thus: ‘Craving has been called an arrow by the Recluse; the poisonous humour of ignorance is spread about by desire, lust, and ill will.

That arrow of craving has been pulled out from me; the poisonous humour of ignorance has been expelled. I am one who is completely intent on *Nibbāna*.’

Such thoughts might be untrue for him.

he might pursue those things that are unsuitable for one completely intent on *Nibbāna*. He might pursue the sight of unsuitable forms with the eye, he might pursue unsuitable sounds with the ear, unsuitable odors with the nose, unsuitable flavors with the tongue, unsuitable tangibles with the body, or unsuitable mind-objects with the mind.

When he pursues the sight of unsuitable forms with the eye…unsuitable mind-objects with the mind, lust invades his mind.

With his mind invaded by lust, he would incur death or deadly suffering.

“For it is death in the Discipline of the Noble One, Sunakkhatta, when one abandons the training and reverts to the low life; and it is deadly suffering when one commits some defiled offence.
commentary_pali:
63.Ṭhānaṃkho panāti pāṭiyekko anusandhi. Heṭṭhā hi samāpattilābhino adhimānikassapi khīṇāsavassapi nighaṃso kathito, sukkhavipassakassa pana adhimānikassapi khīṇāsavassapi na kathito. Tesaṃ dvinnampi nighaṃsaṃ dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Taṃ pana paṭikkhittaṃ. Samāpattilābhino hi adhimānikassa nighaṃse kathite sukkhavipassakassapi adhimānikassa kathitova hoti, samāpattilābhino ca khīṇāsavassa kathite sukkhavipassakakhīṇāsavassa kathitova hoti. Etesaṃ pana dvinnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sappāyāsappāyaṃ kathetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Tattha siyā – puthujjanassa tāva ārammaṇaṃ asappāyaṃ hotu, khīṇāsavassa kathaṃ asappāyanti. Yadaggena puthujjanassa asappāyaṃ, tadaggena khīṇāsavassāpi asappāyameva. Visaṃ nāma jānitvā khāditampi ajānitvā khāditampi visameva. Na hi khīṇāsavenapi ‘‘ahaṃ khīṇāsavo’’ti asaṃvutena bhavitabbaṃ. Khīṇāsavenapi yuttapayutteneva bhavituṃ vaṭṭati.
commentary_english:
Section 63.

"But indeed, why is this stated?" This is a connection based on distinction.

Below, the downfall *nighaṃsa* has been spoken of for both the one who has attained meditative accomplishments *samāpatti* and the conceited one *adhimānika*, as well as for the one whose influxes are destroyed *khīṇāsava*, but it has not been spoken of for the dry-insight practitioner *sukkhavipassaka* whether conceited or with destroyed influxes.

This discourse was begun in order to show the downfall of both of those.

But that was rejected.

For when the downfall of the conceited one who has attained meditative accomplishments is spoken of, it is as good as spoken of for the conceited dry-insight practitioner; and when it is spoken of for the one with destroyed influxes who has attained meditative accomplishments, it is as good as spoken of for the dry-insight practitioner with destroyed influxes.

This discourse was begun in order to speak of the suitable and unsuitable for these two monks.

There, one might ask: "Even if the object is unsuitable for the ordinary person *puthujjana*, how is it unsuitable for the one whose influxes are destroyed?"

That by which it is unsuitable for the ordinary person, by that very thing it is also unsuitable for the one whose influxes are destroyed.

Poison, whether knowingly eaten or unknowingly eaten, is still poison.

Indeed, even the one whose influxes are destroyed should not be uncomposed, thinking "I am one whose influxes are destroyed."

Even the one whose influxes are destroyed should behave fittingly and appropriately.

mula_pali:
64. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ idhekaccassa bhikkhuno evamassa – ‘taṇhā kho sallaṃ samaṇena vuttaṃ, avijjāvisadoso chandarāgabyāpādena ruppati. Taṃ me taṇhāsallaṃ pahīnaṃ, apanīto avijjāvisadoso, sammā nibbānādhimuttohamasmī’ti. Sammā nibbānādhimuttasseva sato so yāni sammā nibbānādhimuttassa asappāyāni tāni nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ sotena saddaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ ghānena gandhaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ jivhāya rasaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ manasā dhammaṃ nānuyuñjeyya. Tassa asappāyaṃ cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ sotena saddaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ ghānena gandhaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ jivhāya rasaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ manasā dhammaṃ nānuyuttassa rāgo cittaṃ nānuddhaṃseyya. So na rāgānuddhaṃsitena cittena neva maraṇaṃ vā nigaccheyya na maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, puriso sallena viddho assa savisena gāḷhūpalepanena. Tassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ. Tassa so bhisakko sallakatto satthena vaṇamukhaṃ parikanteyya. Satthena vaṇamukhaṃ parikantitvā esaniyā sallaṃ eseyya. Esaniyā sallaṃ esitvā sallaṃ abbuheyya, apaneyya visadosaṃ anupādisesaṃ. Anupādisesoti jānamāno so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ambho purisa, ubbhataṃ kho te sallaṃ, apanīto visadoso anupādiseso. Analañca te antarāyāya. Sappāyāni ceva bhojanāni bhuñjeyyāsi, mā te asappāyāni bhojanāni bhuñjato vaṇo assāvī assa. Kālena kālañca vaṇaṃ dhoveyyāsi, kālena kālaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpeyyāsi. Mā te na kālena kālaṃ vaṇaṃ dhovato na kālena kālaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpato pubbalohitaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ pariyonandhi. Mā ca vātātape cārittaṃ anuyuñji, mā te vātātape cārittaṃ anuyuttassa rajosūkaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ anuddhaṃsesi . Vaṇānurakkhī ca, ambho purisa, vihareyyāsi vaṇasāropī’ti. Tassa evamassa – ‘ubbhataṃ kho me sallaṃ, apanīto visadoso anupādiseso. Analañca me antarāyāyā’ti. So sappāyāni ceva bhojanāni bhuñjeyya. Tassa sappāyāni bhojanāni bhuñjato vaṇo na assāvī assa. Kālena kālañca vaṇaṃ dhoveyya, kālena kālaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpeyya. Tassa kālena kālaṃ vaṇaṃ dhovato kālena kālaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ ālimpato na pubbalohitaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ pariyonandheyya. Na ca vātātape cārittaṃ anuyuñjeyya. Tassa vātātape cārittaṃ ananuyuttassa rajosūkaṃ vaṇamukhaṃ nānuddhaṃseyya. Vaṇānurakkhī ca vihareyya vaṇasāropī. Tassa imissā ca sappāyakiriyāya asu ca asuci (sabbattha) socāti tabbaṇṇanā manasikātabbā visadoso apanīto anupādiseso tadubhayena vaṇo viruheyya. So ruḷhena vaṇena sañchavinā neva maraṇaṃ vā nigaccheyya na maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ.

asuci (sabbattha) socāti tabbaṇṇanā manasikātabbā

‘‘Evameva kho, sunakkhatta, ṭhānametaṃ vijjati yaṃ idhekaccassa bhikkhuno evamassa – ‘taṇhā kho sallaṃ samaṇena vuttaṃ, avijjāvisadoso chandarāgabyāpādena ruppati. Taṃ me taṇhāsallaṃ pahīnaṃ, apanīto avijjāvisadoso, sammā nibbānādhimuttohamasmī’ti. Sammā nibbānādhimuttasseva sato so yāni sammā nibbānādhimuttassa asappāyāni tāni nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ sotena saddaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ ghānena gandhaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ jivhāya rasaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ nānuyuñjeyya, asappāyaṃ manasā dhammaṃ nānuyuñjeyya. Tassa asappāyaṃ cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ sotena saddaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ ghānena gandhaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ jivhāya rasaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ nānuyuttassa, asappāyaṃ manasā dhammaṃ nānuyuttassa, rāgo cittaṃ nānuddhaṃseyya. So na rāgānuddhaṃsitena cittena neva maraṇaṃ vā nigaccheyya na maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkhaṃ.
mula_english:
64. It is possible, Sunakkhatta, that some *bhikkhu* here might think thus: ‘Craving (*taṇhā*) has been called an arrow (*salla*) by the Recluse; the poisonous humour of ignorance (*avijjā*) is spread about by desire (*chanda*), lust (*rāga*), and ill will (*byāpāda*). That arrow of craving has been pulled out from me; the poisonous humour of ignorance has been expelled. I am one who is completely intent on *Nibbāna*.’ Being one who really is completely intent on *Nibbāna*, he would not pursue those things that are unsuitable (*asappāya*) for one completely intent on *Nibbāna*. He would not pursue the sight of unsuitable forms with the eye (*cakkhunā rūpadassanaṃ*), he would not pursue unsuitable sounds with the ear (*sotena saddaṃ*), unsuitable odours with the nose (*ghānena gandhaṃ*), unsuitable flavours with the tongue (*jivhāya rasaṃ*), unsuitable tangibles with the body (*kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ*), or unsuitable mind-objects with the mind (*manasā dhammaṃ*). Because he does not pursue the sight of unsuitable forms with the eye, unsuitable sounds with the ear, unsuitable odours with the nose, unsuitable flavours with the tongue, unsuitable tangibles with the body, or unsuitable mind-objects with the mind, lust (*rāga*) does not invade his mind (*cittaṃ*). Because his mind is not invaded by lust, he would not incur death or deadly suffering (*maraṇamattaṃ dukkhaṃ*).

Suppose, Sunakkhatta, a man were wounded by an arrow thickly smeared with poison. Then his friends and companions, his kinsmen and relatives, would bring a surgeon (*sallakattaṃ*). The surgeon would cut around the opening of the wound with a knife. After cutting around the opening of the wound with a knife, he would probe for the arrow with a probe (*esanī*). After probing for the arrow with a probe, he would pull out the arrow and would expel the poisonous humour without leaving a trace of it behind (*anupādisesaṃ*). Knowing that no trace was left behind, he would say: ‘Good man, the arrow has been pulled out from you; the poisonous humour has been expelled with no trace left behind. And it is incapable of harming you (*analañca te antarāyāya*). Eat only suitable food (*sappāyāni bhojanāni*); do not eat unsuitable food or else the wound (*vaṇo*) may suppurate. From time to time wash the wound and from time to time anoint its opening. so that pus and blood do not cover the opening of the wound. Do not walk around in the wind and sun or else dust and dirt may infect the opening of the wound. Take care of your wound, good man, and see to it that the wound heals.’ The man would think: ‘The arrow has been pulled out from me; the poisonous humour has been expelled with no trace left behind. And it is incapable of harming me.’ He would eat only suitable food. The wound would not suppurate if he eats only suitable food. From time to time he would wash the wound and from time to time he would anoint its opening. Pus and blood would not cover the opening of the wound because he washes the wound and anoints its opening from time to time. He would not walk around in the wind and sun. Dust and dirt would not infect the opening of the wound because he does not walk around in the wind and sun. He would take care of his wound and would see to it that the wound heals. Because of his care and proper treatment, and because the poisonous humour has been expelled without a trace, the wound would heal. Because it had healed and was covered with skin, he would not incur death or deadly suffering.

Just so, Sunakkhatta, it is possible that some *bhikkhu* here might think thus: ‘Craving has been called an arrow by the Recluse; the poisonous humour of ignorance is spread about by desire, lust, and ill will. That arrow of craving has been pulled out from me; the poisonous humour of ignorance has been expelled. I am one who is completely intent on *Nibbāna*.’
Being truly intent on *Nirvāṇa* (Nibbana), he would not pursue those things that are unsuitable (*asappāya*) for one truly intent on *Nirvāṇa*. He would not pursue the sight of unsuitable forms (*rūpadassana*) with the eye (*cakkhunā*), he would not pursue unsuitable sounds (*sadda*) with the ear (*sotena*), unsuitable odors (*gandha*) with the nose (*ghānena*), unsuitable flavors (*rasa*) with the tongue (*jivhāya*), unsuitable tangibles (*phoṭṭhabba*) with the body (*kāyena*), or unsuitable mind-objects (*dhamma*) with the mind (*manasā*).

Because he does not pursue the sight of unsuitable forms with the eye, unsuitable sounds with the ear, unsuitable odors with the nose, unsuitable flavors with the tongue, unsuitable tangibles with the body, or unsuitable mind-objects with the mind, lust (*rāga*) does not invade his mind (*cittaṃ*).

With his mind not invaded by lust, he would not incur death (*maraṇaṃ*) or deadly suffering (*dukkhaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
64. Tattha samaṇenāti buddhasamaṇena. Chandarāgabyāpādenāti so avijjāsaṅkhāto visadoso chandarāgena ca byāpādena ca ruppati kuppati. Asappāyānīti avaḍḍhikarāni ārammaṇāni. Anuddhaṃseyyāti soseyya milāpeyya. Saupādisesanti sagahaṇasesaṃ, upāditabbaṃ gaṇhitabbaṃ idha upādīti vuttaṃ. Analañca te antarāyāyāti jīvitantarāyaṃ te kātuṃ asamatthaṃ. Rajosūkanti rajo ca vīhisukādi ca sūkaṃ. Asu ca visadosoti so ca visadoso. Tadubhayenāti yā sā asappāyakiriyā ca yo visadoso ca, tena ubhayena. Puthuttanti mahantabhāvaṃ.

Evameva khoti ettha saupādānasalluddhāro viya appahīno avijjāvisadoso daṭṭhabbo, asappāyakiriyāya ṭhitabhāvo viya chasu dvāresu asaṃvutakālo, tadubhayena vaṇe puthuttaṃ gate maraṇaṃ viya sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattanaṃ, maraṇamattaṃ dukkhaṃ viya aññatarāya garukāya saṃkiliṭṭhāya āpattiyā āpajjanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sukkapakkhepi imināva nayena opammasaṃsandanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Evameva kho
commentary_english:
64.
"samaṇenā" means by a Buddha-ascetic.
"chandarāgabyāpādenā" means that the ignorance-aggregate, the taintedness, is ruined and agitated by desire-passion and malevolence.
"asappāyānī" means unconducive sense objects.
"anuddhaṃseyyā" means would cast down.
"saupādisesa" means with the residue of grasping; what should be grasped, what should be taken up, this is said to be *upādi*.
"analañca te antarāyāyā" means incapable of causing an obstruction to your life.
"rajosūka" means dust and the awn of rice, etc., and awn.
"asu ca visadoso" means that defiled one.
"tadubhayenā" means by that both, that is, by that unconducive activity and that taintedness.
"puthutta" means the state of being great.

evameva kho" means here, just like extracting a dart with its accessories, the unabandoned ignorance-taintedness should be seen; just like the established state of unconducive activity is the time of unguardedness at the six doors; having gone to distinctiveness in the wound by that both, like turning back to inferiority after rejecting the training; like suffering just as much as death is incurring an offense of another serious defilement should be seen.
Even in the bright fortnight, the connection of similes should be understood in this way, by this method.

evameva kho

mula_pali:
65. ‘‘Upamā kho me ayaṃ, sunakkhatta, katā atthassa viññāpanāya. Ayaṃyevettha attho – vaṇoti kho, sunakkhatta, channetaṃ ajjhattikānaṃ āyatanānaṃ adhivacanaṃ; visadosoti kho, sunakkhatta, avijjāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ; sallanti kho, sunakkhatta, taṇhāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ; esanīti kho, sunakkhatta, satiyāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ; satthanti kho, sunakkhatta, ariyāyetaṃ paññāya adhivacanaṃ; bhisakko sallakattoti kho, sunakkhatta, tathāgatassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa.

‘‘So vata, sunakkhatta, bhikkhu chasu phassāyatanesu saṃvutakārī ‘upadhi dukkhassa mūla’nti – iti viditvā nirupadhi upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto upadhismiṃ vā kāyaṃ upasaṃharissati cittaṃ vā uppādessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, āpānīyakaṃso vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno; so ca kho visena saṃsaṭṭho. Atha puriso āgaccheyya jīvitukāmo amaritukāmo sukhakāmo dukkhapaṭikūlo. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, api nu so puriso amuṃ āpānīyakaṃsaṃ piveyya yaṃ jaññā – ‘imāhaṃ pivitvā maraṇaṃ vā nigacchāmi maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkha’’’nti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Evameva kho, sunakkhatta, so vata bhikkhu chasu phassāyatanesu saṃvutakārī ‘upadhi dukkhassa mūla’nti – iti viditvā nirupadhi upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto upadhismiṃ vā kāyaṃ upasaṃharissati cittaṃ vā uppādessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Seyyathāpi, sunakkhatta, āsīviso āsiviso (ka.) ghoraviso. Atha puriso āgaccheyya jīvitukāmo amaritukāmo sukhakāmo dukkhapaṭikūlo. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, api nu so puriso amussa āsīvisassa ghoravisassa hatthaṃ vā aṅguṭṭhaṃ vā dajjā yuñjeyya (ka.) yaṃ jaññā – ‘imināhaṃ daṭṭho maraṇaṃ vā nigacchāmi maraṇamattaṃ vā dukkha’’’nti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Evameva kho, sunakkhatta, so vata bhikkhu chasu phassāyatanesu saṃvutakārī ‘upadhi dukkhassa mūla’nti – iti viditvā nirupadhi upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto upadhismiṃ vā kāyaṃ upasaṃharissati cittaṃ vā uppādessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’ti.

āsiviso (ka.) yuñjeyya (ka.)

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano sunakkhatto licchaviputto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Sunakkhattasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
65. “Sunakkhatta, I have given this simile in order to convey a meaning.

This is the meaning here: ‘Wound’ *vaṇo* is a term for the six internal bases (*ajjhattikānaṃ āyatanānaṃ*). ‘Poisonous humour’ *visadoso* is a term for ignorance (*avijjāya*). ‘Arrow’ *salla* is a term for craving (*taṇhā*). ‘Probe’ *esanī* is a term for mindfulness (*satiyā*). ‘Knife’ *satthanti* is a term for noble wisdom (*ariyā paññāya*). Surgeon *bhisakko sallakatto* is a term for the *Tathāgata*, the Accomplished One (*arahato*), the Fully Enlightened One (*sammāsambuddhassa*).

“When, Sunakkhatta, a *bhikkhu* practises restraint (*saṃvutakārī*) in the six bases of contact (*phassāyatanesu*), and having understood that attachment (*upadhi*) is the root (*mūla*) of suffering (*dukkha*), is without attachment (*nirupadhi*), liberated (*vimutto*) by the destruction of attachment (*upadhisaṅkhaye*), it is not possible that he would direct (*upasaṃharissati*) his body (*kāyaṃ*) or arouse (*uppādessati*) his mind (*cittaṃ*) towards any object of attachment.

“Suppose, Sunakkhatta, there were a bronze cup of beverage (*āpānīyakaṃso*) possessing a good colour (*vaṇṇasampanno*), smell (*gandhasampanno*), and taste (*rasasampanno*), but it was mixed with poison (*visena saṃsaṭṭho*),

and a man came who wanted to live (*jīvitukāmo*), not to die (*amaritukāmo*), who wanted pleasure (*sukhakāmo*) and recoiled from pain (*dukkhapaṭikūlo*).

What do you think, Sunakkhatta, would that man drink (*piveyya*) from that bronze cup of beverage (*āpānīyakaṃsaṃ*) knowing: ‘If I drink (*pivitvā*) this, I will incur (*nigacchāmi*) death (*maraṇaṃ*) or deadly suffering (*maraṇamattaṃ dukkha*)’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“So too, Sunakkhatta, when a *bhikkhu* practises restraint (*saṃvutakārī*) in the six bases of contact (*phassāyatanesu*), and having understood that attachment (*upadhi*) is the root (*mūla*) of suffering (*dukkha*), is without attachment (*nirupadhi*), liberated (*vimutto*) by the destruction of attachment (*upadhisaṅkhaye*), it is not possible that he would direct (*upasaṃharissati*) his body (*kāyaṃ*) or arouse (*uppādessati*) his mind (*cittaṃ*) towards any object of attachment.

“Suppose, Sunakkhatta, there were a deadly poisonous snake (*āsīviso ghoraviso*),

and a man came who wanted to live (*jīvitukāmo*), not to die (*amaritukāmo*), who wanted pleasure (*sukhakāmo*) and recoiled from pain (*dukkhapaṭikūlo*).

What do you think, Sunakkhatta, would that man give that deadly poisonous snake (*āsīvisassa ghoravisassa*) his hand (*hatthaṃ*) or his thumb (*aṅguṭṭhaṃ*), knowing: ‘If I am bitten (*daṭṭho*) by him, I will incur (*nigacchāmi*) death (*maraṇaṃ*) or deadly suffering (*maraṇamattaṃ dukkha*)’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“So too, Sunakkhatta, when a *bhikkhu* practises restraint (*saṃvutakārī*) in the six bases of contact (*phassāyatanesu*), and having understood that attachment (*upadhi*) is the root (*mūla*) of suffering (*dukkha*), is without attachment (*nirupadhi*), liberated (*vimutto*) by the destruction of attachment (*upadhisaṅkhaye*), it is not possible that he would direct (*upasaṃharissati*) his body (*kāyaṃ*) or arouse (*uppādessati*) his mind (*cittaṃ*) towards any object of attachment.”

This is what the Blessed One said. Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words (*bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti*).

The Sunakkhatta Sutta is finished, the fifth.
commentary_pali:
65.Satiyāyetaṃadhivacananti ettha sati paññāgatikā. Lokikāya paññāya lokikā hoti, lokuttarāya lokuttarā. Ariyāyetaṃ paññāyāti parisuddhāya vipassanāpaññāya.

Idāni khīṇāsavassa balaṃ dassento so vatātiādimāha. Tattha saṃvutakārīti pihitakārī. Itividitvā nirupadhīti evaṃ jānitvā kilesupadhipahānā nirupadhi hoti, nirupādānoti attho. Upadhisaṅkhaye vimuttoti upadhīnaṃ saṅkhayabhūte nibbāne ārammaṇato vimutto. Upadhisminti kāmupadhismiṃ. Kāyaṃ upasaṃharissatīti kāyaṃ allīyāpessati. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – taṇhakkhaye nibbāne ārammaṇato vimutto khīṇāsavo pañca kāmaguṇe sevituṃ, kāyaṃ vā upasaṃharissati cittaṃ vā uppādessatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

so vatā saṃvutakārī Iti viditvā nirupadhī Upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto Upadhismi Kāyaṃ upasaṃharissatī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Sunakkhattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
65. "It is a designation of mindfulness (satiyāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ)," here, mindfulness is connected with wisdom (paññā). With mundane wisdom (lokikāya paññāya), it is mundane; with supramundane (lokuttarāya), it is supramundane. "It is a designation of noble wisdom (ariyāyetaṃ paññāya)," [meaning] with pure insight wisdom (parisuddhāya vipassanāpaññāya).

Now, showing the power of one with destroyed influxes (khīṇāsavassa), he said, "So vatā," etc. There, "saṃvutakārī" means one who does what is concealed (pihitakārī). "Having understood thus, without basis (iti viditvā nirupadhī)," having known thus, due to the abandonment of the defilement-basis (kilesupadhi), he is without basis (nirupadhi), meaning without grasping (nirupādānoti attho). "Freed in the destruction of the basis (upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto)," freed in nibbāna, which is the destruction of the basis (upadhīnaṃ saṅkhayabhūte nibbāne), from the perspective of an object (ārammaṇato). "In the basis (upadhismiṃ)," [meaning] in the basis of sense desire (kāmupadhismiṃ). "He will draw the body near (kāyaṃ upasaṃharissatī)," he will cause the body to adhere (kāyaṃ allīyāpessati).

This is what was said: the one with destroyed influxes (khīṇāsavo), freed from the perspective of an object (ārammaṇato) in nibbāna, which is the destruction of craving (taṇhakkhaye nibbāne), [whether] to enjoy the five sense pleasures (pañca kāmaguṇe sevituṃ), or he will draw the body near (kāyaṃ upasaṃharissati), or he will generate the mind (cittaṃ vā uppādessatīti), this is not a possibility (netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati). The rest is clear throughout (sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti).

So vatā saṃvutakārī iti viditvā nirupadhī upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto upadhismiṃ kāyaṃ upasaṃharissatī

The Sunakkhatta Sutta Commentary in the Papañcasūdanī, the Majjhima Nikāya Commentary, is finished.

mula_pali: 66. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kurūsu viharati kammāsadhammaṃ nāma kurūnaṃ nigamo. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘aniccā, bhikkhave, kāmā tucchā musā mosadhammā. Māyākatame taṃ, bhikkhave, bālalāpanaṃ. Ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā; yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā – ubhayametaṃ māradheyyaṃ, mārassesa mārasseva (ka.) visayo, mārassesa nivāpo, mārassesa gocaro. Etthete pāpakā akusalā mānasā abhijjhāpi byāpādāpi sārambhāpi saṃvattanti. Teva ariyasāvakassa idhamanusikkhato antarāyāya sambhavanti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ye ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmā, ye ca samparāyikā kāmā; yā ca diṭṭhadhammikā kāmasaññā, yā ca samparāyikā kāmasaññā – ubhayametaṃ māradheyyaṃ, mārassesa visayo, mārassesa nivāpo, mārassesa gocaro. Etthete pāpakā akusalā mānasā abhijjhāpi byāpādāpi sārambhāpi saṃvattanti, teva ariyasāvakassa idhamanusikkhato antarāyāya sambhavanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ vipulena mahaggatena cetasā vihareyyaṃ abhibhuyya lokaṃ adhiṭṭhāya manasā.
