“Here, *bhikkhu*, an untaught ordinary person ( *puthujjana*), who has no regard for noble ones (*ariyānaṃ adassāvī*) and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma (*ariyadhamme avinīto*), who has no regard for true men (*sappurisānaṃ adassāvī*) and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, regards form (*rūpa*) as self (*āttato*), or self as possessed of form (*rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ*), or form as in self (*attani vā rūpaṃ*), or self as in form (*rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ*). He regards feeling (*vedanā*) as self, or self as possessed of feeling (*vedanāvantaṃ vā attānaṃ*), or feeling as in self (*attani vā vedanaṃ*), or self as in feeling (*vedanāya vā attānaṃ*). He regards perception (*saññaṃ*) as self, or self as possessed of perception (*saññāvantaṃ vā attānaṃ*), or perception as in self (*attani vā saññaṃ*), or self as in perception (*saññāya vā attānaṃ*). He regards formations (*saṅkhāre*) as self, or self as possessed of formations (*saṅkhāravantaṃ vā attānaṃ*), or formations as in self (*attani vā saṅkhāre*), or self as in formations (*saṅkhāresu vā attānaṃ*). He regards consciousness (*viññāṇaṃ*) as self, or self as possessed of consciousness (*viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ*), or consciousness as in self (*attani vā viññāṇaṃ*), or self as in consciousness (*viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ*). That is how, *bhikkhu*, identity view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) comes to be.”

“How, venerable sir, does identity view not come to be?”

“Here, *bhikkhu*, a well-taught noble disciple (*ariyasāvako*), who has regard for noble ones (*ariyānaṃ dassāvī*) and is skilled in their Dhamma (*ariyadhammassa kovido*) and well-disciplined in their Dhamma (*ariyadhamme suvinīto*), who has regard for true men (*sappurisānaṃ dassāvī*) and is skilled in their Dhamma and well-disciplined in their Dhamma, does not regard form (*rūpaṃ*) as self (*attato*), or self as possessed of form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He does not regard feeling as self, or self as possessed of feeling, or feeling as in self, or self as in feeling. He does not regard perception as self, or self as possessed of perception, or perception as in self, or self as in perception. He does not regard formations as self, or self as possessed of formations, or formations as in self, or self as in formations. He does not regard consciousness as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. That is how, *bhikkhu*, identity view does not come to be.”
commentary_pali: 87.Kathaṃ pana, bhanteti idaṃ kittakena nu khoti vaṭṭaṃ pucchanto evamāha. Sakkāyadiṭṭhi na hotīti idaṃ vivaṭṭaṃ pucchanto evamāha.
commentary_english:
How, then, *bhante*—asking in what way, indeed, Venerable One, Vatta said thus.

"There is no view of self"—asking clearly, he said thus.

mula_pali: 88. ‘‘Ko nu kho, bhante, rūpe assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko vedanāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko saññāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko saṅkhāresu assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko viññāṇe assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇa’’nti? ‘‘Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, rūpaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ rūpe assādo. Yaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, ayaṃ rūpe ādīnavo. Yo rūpe chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ rūpe nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ kho yañca (syā. kaṃ.), bhikkhu, vedanaṃ paṭicca… saññaṃ paṭicca… saṅkhāre paṭicca… viññāṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ viññāṇe assādo. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, ayaṃ viññāṇe ādīnavo. Yo viññāṇe chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ viññāṇe nissaraṇa’’nti.
mula_english:
88. "But what, venerable sir, is the gratification (assāda), what is the danger (ādīnava), and what is the escape (nissaraṇaṃ) in the case of form (rūpa)? What is the gratification, what is the danger, and what is the escape in the case of feeling (vedanā)? What is the gratification, what is the danger, and what is the escape in the case of perception (saṃjñā)? What is the gratification, what is the danger, and what is the escape in the case of volitional formations (saṅkhāresu)? What is the gratification, what is the danger, and what is the escape in the case of consciousness (vijñāṇa)?"

"The pleasure (sukhaṃ) and joy (somanassaṃ) that arise in dependence on form, this is the gratification in the case of form. Form is impermanent (aniccaṃ), suffering (dukkhaṃ), and subject to change (vipariṇāmadhammaṃ) - this is the danger in the case of form. The removal of desire and lust (chandarāgavinayo), the abandonment of desire and lust (chandarāgappahānaṃ) for form - this is the escape in the case of form.

The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on feeling…in dependence on perception…in dependence on volitional formations…in dependence on consciousness - this is the gratification in the case of consciousness. Consciousness is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change - this is the danger in the case of consciousness. The removal and abandonment of desire and lust for consciousness - this is the escape in the case of consciousness."
commentary_pali: 88.Ayaṃrūpe assādoti iminā pariññāpaṭivedho ceva dukkhasaccañca kathitaṃ. Ayaṃ rūpe ādīnavoti iminā pahānapaṭivedho ceva samudayasaccañca. Idaṃ rūpe nissaraṇanti iminā sacchikiriyāpaṭivedho ceva nirodhasaccañca. Ye imesu tīsu ṭhānesu sammādiṭṭhiādayo dhammā, ayaṃ bhāvanāpaṭivedho maggasaccaṃ. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
This [is] "enjoyment in form (rūpe assādo)"; by this, the penetration of full understanding (pariññāpaṭivedho) and the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) are spoken of.

This [is] "danger in form (rūpe ādīnavo)"; by this, the penetration of abandoning (pahānapaṭivedho) and the truth of origin (samudayasacca) [are spoken of].

This [is] "escape from form (rūpe nissaraṇa)"; by this, the penetration of realization (sacchikiriyāpaṭivedho) and the truth of cessation (nirodhasacca) [are spoken of].

Those things, such as right view (sammādiṭṭhi), in these three places, this [is] the penetration of development (bhāvanāpaṭivedho), the truth of the path (maggasaccaṃ).

And so with the other clauses (sesapadesupi eseva nayo).

mula_pali: 89. ‘‘Kathaṃ pana, bhante, jānato kathaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṃkāramamaṃkāramānānusayā na hontī’’ti? ‘‘Yaṃ kiñci, bhikkhu, rūpaṃ – atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā – sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ – atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā – sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passati. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, jānato evaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṃkāramamaṃkāramānānusayā na hontī’’ti.
mula_english:
89. “But how, venerable sir, when one knows, how when one sees, do I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit not occur in regard to this body with its consciousness and in regard to all external signs?”

“Any kind of form (rūpa) whatsoever, bhikkhu, whether past (atītā), future (anāgata), or present (paccuppanna); internal (ajjhattaṃ) or external (bahiddhā); gross (oḷārikaṃ) or subtle (sukhumaṃ); inferior (hīnaṃ) or superior (paṇītaṃ); far (dūre) or near (santike): all form (rūpa)—‘This is not mine (netaṃ mama), this I am not (nesohamasmi), this is not my self (na meso attā)’—one sees all form as it actually is (yathābhūtaṃ) with proper wisdom (sammappaññāya).

Any kind of feeling (vedanā) whatsoever… Any kind of perception (saññā) whatsoever… Any kind of volitional formations (saṅkhārā) whatsoever… Any kind of consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) whatsoever, whether past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’—one sees all consciousness as it actually is with proper wisdom.

“When one knows thus, bhikkhu, when one sees thus, then in regard to this body with consciousness and in regard to all external signs, I-making (ahaṃkāra), mine-making (mamaṃkāra), and the underlying tendency to conceit (mānānusayā) no longer occur within.”
commentary_pali: 89.Bahiddhāti parassa saviññāṇake kāye. Sabbanimittesūti iminā pana anindriyabaddhampi saṅgaṇhāti. ‘‘Saviññāṇake kāye’’ti vacanena vā attano ca parassa ca kāyo gahitova, bahiddhā ca sabbanimittaggahaṇena anindriyabaddhaṃ gaṇhāti.
commentary_english: 89. bahiddhā: in the body of another that possesses consciousness ( *saviññāṇake kāye*). sabbanimittesū: by this, it also includes that which is not bound by the senses ( *anindriyabaddhampi*). ‘‘Because of the expression, *saviññāṇake kāye*, the body of oneself and of another is taken, and *bahiddhā*, through the taking of all signs (*sabbanimittaggahaṇena*), it takes that which is not bound by the senses (*anindriyabaddhaṃ*).

mula_pali:
90. Atha kho aññatarassa bhikkhuno evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘‘iti kira, bho, rūpaṃ anattā, vedanā anattā, saññā anattā, saṅkhārā anattā, viññāṇaṃ anattā; anattakatāni kammāni kamattānaṃ kathamattānaṃ (saṃ. ni. 3.82) phusissantī’’ti? Atha kho bhagavā tassa bhikkhuno cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco moghapuriso avidvā avijjāgato taṇhādhipateyyena cetasā satthu sāsanaṃ atidhāvitabbaṃ maññeyya – ‘iti kira, bho, rūpaṃ anattā, vedanā anattā, saññā anattā, saṅkhārā anattā, viññāṇaṃ anattā; anattakatāni kammāni kamattānaṃ phusissantī’ti. Paṭivinītā paṭicca vinītā (sī. pī.), paṭipucchāmi vinītā (syā. kaṃ.) kho me tumhe, bhikkhave , tatra tatra dhammesu’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Aniccaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Dukkhaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ , bhante’’. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Aniccaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Dukkhaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ – ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati; nibbindaṃ virajjati , virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti. Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne saṭṭhimattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsūti.

Mahāpuṇṇamasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.
mula_english:
90. Then, in the mind of a certain *bhikkhu* (monk) this thought arose: “So, it seems, material form (*rūpa*) is not self (*anattā*), feeling (*vedanā*) is not self, perception (*saññā*) is not self, formations (*saṅkhārā*) are not self, consciousness (*viññāṇa*) is not self. What self, then, will actions (*kamma*) done by the not-self affect?”

Then the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), knowing in his mind the thought in the mind of that *bhikkhu*, addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: “It is possible, *bhikkhus*, that some misguided man here, obtuse and ignorant, with his mind dominated by craving, might think that he can outstrip the Teacher’s Dispensation thus: ‘So, it seems, material form (*rūpa*) is not self (*anattā*)…consciousness (*viññāṇa*) is not self. What self, then, will actions (*kamma*) done by the not-self affect?’”

“Am I one whose doubts have been dispelled, O *bhikkhus*, concerning those things in that very place?”

“What do you think, *bhikkhus*, is material form (*rūpa*) permanent (*nicca*) or impermanent (*anicca*)?” “Impermanent (*anicca*), Lord (*bhante*)”.

“But that which is impermanent (*anicca*), is that unpleasant (*dukkha*) or pleasant (*sukha*)?” “Unpleasant (*dukkha*), Lord (*bhante*)”.

“That impermanent (*anicca*), unpleasant (*dukkha*), changing thing, is it suitable to be considered, that is mine (*mama*), that I am (*asmi*), that is my self (*attā*)?” “No, Lord (*bhante*)”.

“What do you think, *bhikkhus*, is feeling (*vedanā*)… perception (*saññā*)… volitional formations (*saṅkhārā*)… consciousness (*viññāṇa*) permanent (*nicca*) or impermanent (*anicca*)?” “Impermanent (*anicca*), Lord (*bhante*)”.

“That which is impermanent (*anicca*), is that unpleasant (*dukkha*) or pleasant (*sukha*)?” “Unpleasant (*dukkha*), Lord (*bhante*)”.

“That which is impermanent (*anicca*), unpleasant (*dukkha*), subject to change, is it fitting to regard thus: ‘This is mine (*mama*), this I am (*asmi*), this is my self (*attā*)’?” “No, Lord (*bhante*)”.

“Therefore, *bhikkhus*, any kind of material form (*rūpa*) whatever, whether past (*atīta*), future (*anāgata*), or present (*paccuppanna*), internal (*ajjhatta*) or external (*bahiddhā*), gross (*oḷārika*) or subtle (*sukhuma*), inferior (*hīna*) or superior (*paṇīta*), far (*dūre*) or near (*santike*), all material form (*rūpa*) should be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom (*sammappaññā*) thus: “This is not mine (*mama*), this I am not (*asmi*), this is not my self (*attā*)’.”

Any kind of feeling (*vedanā*) whatsoever… Any kind of perception (*saññā*) whatsoever…Any kind of volitional formations (*saṅkhārā*) whatsoever…Any kind of consciousness (*viññāṇa*) whatsoever, whether past (*atīta*), future (*anāgata*), or present (*paccuppanna*), internal (*ajjhatta*) or external (*bahiddhā*), gross (*oḷārika*) or subtle (*sukhuma*), inferior (*hīna*) or superior (*paṇīta*), far (*dūre*) or near (*santike*) - one sees all consciousness (*viññāṇa*) as it really is with correct wisdom (*sammappaññā*) thus: ‘This is not mine (*mama*), this I am not (*asmi*), this is not my self (*attā*)’."

Seeing thus, *bhikkhus*, the instructed noble disciple (*ariyasāvako*) experiences revulsion (*nibbindati*) towards form (*rūpa*), revulsion (*nibbindati*) towards feeling (*vedanā*), revulsion (*nibbindati*) towards perception (*saññā*), revulsion (*nibbindati*) towards volitional formations (*saṅkhārā*), revulsion (*nibbindati*) towards consciousness (*viññāṇa*). Experiencing revulsion (*nibbindaṃ*), he becomes dispassionate (*virajjati*). Through dispassion (*virāgā*) his mind is liberated (*vimuccati*).

When it is liberated (*vimuttasmiṃ*) there comes the knowledge (*ñāṇaṃ*): ‘It is liberated (*vimuttamiti*)’ He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth (*jāti*), the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) has been lived, what had to be done (*karaṇīyaṃ*) has been done, there is no more coming back to any state of being (*itthattāyā*)’.”

Thus spoke the Blessed One (*bhagavā*). Those *bhikkhus* were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s (*bhagavato*) words (*bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti*).

And while this explanation (*veyyākaraṇasmiṃ*) was being given, the hearts (*cittāni*) of 60 *bhikkhus*, through no clinging (*anupādāya*), were fully released (*vimucciṃsūti*) from fermentation/effluents (*āsavehi*).

The Great Full Moon Discourse (*mahāpuṇṇamasuttaṃ*) is finished, the ninth.
commentary_pali:
90.Anattakatānīti anattani ṭhatvā katāni. Kamattānaṃ phusissantīti katarasmiṃ attani ṭhatvā vipākaṃ dassentīti sassatadassanaṃ okkamanto evamāha. Taṇhādhipateyyenāti taṇhājeṭṭhakena. Tatra tatrāti tesu tesu dhammesu. Saṭṭhimattānanti ime bhikkhū pakatikammaṭṭhānaṃ jahitvā aññaṃ navakammaṭṭhānaṃ sammasantā pallaṅkaṃ abhinditvā tasmiṃyeva āsane arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāpuṇṇamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
90. **anattakatānī**ti p. 4.0079 anattani ṭhatvā katāni.
**kamattānaṃ phusissantī**ti katarasmiṃ attani ṭhatvā vipākaṃ dassentīti sassatadassanaṃ okkamanto evamāha.
**taṇhādhipateyyenā**ti taṇhājeṭṭhakena.
**tatra tatrā**ti tesu tesu dhammesu.
**saṭṭhimattāna**nti ime bhikkhū pakatikammaṭṭhānaṃ jahitvā aññaṃ navakammaṭṭhānaṃ sammasantā pallaṅkaṃ abhinditvā tasmiṃyeva āsane arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu.
sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

mahāpuṇṇamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

mula_pali:
91. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe pannarase puṇṇāya puṇṇamāya rattiyā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto abbhokāse nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anuviloketvā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘jāneyya nu kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisaṃ – ‘asappuriso ayaṃ bhava’’’nti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Sādhu, bhikkhave; aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṃ asappuriso asappurisaṃ jāneyya – ‘asappuriso ayaṃ bhava’nti. Jāneyya pana, bhikkhave, asappuriso sappurisaṃ – ‘sappuriso ayaṃ bhava’’’nti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Sādhu, bhikkhave; etampi kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhānaṃ anavakāso yaṃ asappuriso sappurisaṃ jāneyya – ‘sappuriso ayaṃ bhava’nti. Asappuriso, bhikkhave, assaddhammasamannāgato hoti, asappurisabhatti asappurisabhattī (sabbattha) hoti, asappurisacintī hoti, asappurisamantī hoti, asappurisavāco hoti, asappurisakammanto hoti, asappurisadiṭṭhi asappurisadiṭṭhī (sabbattha) hoti; asappurisadānaṃ deti’’.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, asappuriso assaddhammasamannāgato hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, appassuto hoti , kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti, duppañño hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso assaddhammasamannāgato hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisabhatti hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, asappurisassa ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā assaddhā ahirikā anottappino appassutā kusītā muṭṭhassatino duppaññā tyāssa mittā honti te sahāyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisabhatti hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisacintī hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisacintī hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisamantī hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso attabyābādhāyapi manteti, parabyābādhāyapi manteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi manteti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisamantī hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisavāco hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti , samphappalāpī hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisavāco hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisakammanto hoti? Idha , bhikkhave, asappuriso pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisakammanto hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisadiṭṭhi hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso evaṃdiṭṭhi evaṃdiṭṭhī (sī. pī.), evaṃdiṭṭhiko (syā. kaṃ.) hoti – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ sukkaṭadukkaṭānaṃ (sī. pī.) kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā samaggatā (ka.) sammāpaṭipannā, ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisadiṭṭhi hoti.

evaṃdiṭṭhī (sī. pī.), evaṃdiṭṭhiko (syā. kaṃ.) sukkaṭadukkaṭānaṃ (sī. pī.) samaggatā (ka.)

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisadānaṃ deti? Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso asakkaccaṃ dānaṃ deti, asahatthā dānaṃ deti, acittīkatvā dānaṃ deti, apaviṭṭhaṃ dānaṃ deti anāgamanadiṭṭhiko dānaṃ deti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisadānaṃ deti.

‘‘So, bhikkhave, asappuriso evaṃ assaddhammasamannāgato, evaṃ asappurisabhatti, evaṃ asappurisacintī, evaṃ asappurisamantī, evaṃ asappurisavāco, evaṃ asappurisakammanto, evaṃ asappurisadiṭṭhi; evaṃ asappurisadānaṃ datvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā yā asappurisānaṃ gati tattha upapajjati. Kā ca, bhikkhave, asappurisānaṃ gati? Nirayo vā tiracchānayoni vā.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park in Migāramātā’s mansion.

Then, on that day of the uposatha, on the fifteenth, on the full-moon night, the Blessed One was seated in the open air surrounded by the Community of monks.

Then, surveying the silent Sangha of bhikkhus, the Blessed One addressed them thus: “Bhikkhus, would an untrue man know of an untrue man: ‘This person is an untrue man’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Good, bhikkhus. It is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot be, that an untrue man should know of an untrue man: ‘This person is an untrue man.’

But would an untrue man know of a true man: ‘This person is a true man’?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Good, bhikkhus. It is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot be, that an untrue man should know of a true man: ‘This person is a true man.’

Bhikkhus, an untrue man is possessed of bad qualities (*asaddhamma-samannāgato*); he associates as an untrue man (*asappurisa-bhatti*), he wills as an untrue man, he counsels as an untrue man, he speaks as an untrue man, he acts as an untrue man, he holds views as an untrue man; and he gives gifts as an untrue man.”

“And how, bhikkhus, is an untrue man possessed of bad qualities? Here, bhikkhus, an untrue man has no faith (*assaddho*), no shame (*ahiriko*), no fear of wrongdoing (*anottappī*); he is unlearned (*appassuto*), lazy (*kusīto*), forgetful (*muṭṭhassati*), and unwise (*duppañño*).

That is how an untrue man is possessed of bad qualities.

“And how, bhikkhus, does an untrue man associate as an untrue man? Here, bhikkhus, those recluses and Brahmins who are without faith, without shame, without fear of wrong-doing, unlearned, lazy, forgetful, and unwise are the friends and companions of an untrue man.

That is how an untrue man associates as an untrue man.

“And how, bhikkhus, does an untrue man will as an untrue man? Here, bhikkhus, an untrue man wills for his own affliction, for the affliction of others, and for the affliction of both.

That is how an untrue man wills as an untrue man.

“And how, bhikkhus, does an untrue man counsel as an untrue man? Here, bhikkhus, an untrue man counsels for his own affliction, for the affliction of others, and for the affliction of both.

That is how an untrue man counsels as an untrue man.

“And how, bhikkhus, does an untrue man speak as an untrue man? Here, bhikkhus, an untrue man is a liar, a slanderer, one who speaks harshly, and a gossip.

That is how an untrue man speaks as an untrue man.

“And how, bhikkhus, does an untrue man act as an untrue man? Here, bhikkhus, an untrue man kills living beings (*prāṇātipātī*), takes what is not given (*adinnādāyī*), and misconducts himself in sensual pleasures (*kāmesu-micchācārī*).

That is how an untrue man acts as an untrue man.

“And how, bhikkhus, does an untrue man hold views as an untrue man? Here, bhikkhus, an untrue man holds such a view as this: ‘There is nothing given (*natthi dinnaṃ*), nothing offered (*natthi yiṭṭhaṃ*), nothing sacrificed (*natthi hutaṃ*); there is no fruit or result of good and bad actions; no this world, no other world; no mother, no father; no beings who are reborn spontaneously; no good and virtuous recluses and Brahmins in the world who have realised for themselves by direct knowledge and declare this world and the other world.’
) The result of actions (*kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko*) is that there is nothing given, there is no this world (*natthi ayaṃ loko*), there is no other world (*natthi paro loko*), there is no mother (*natthi mātā*), there is no father (*natthi pitā*), there are no beings who are reborn spontaneously (*natthi sattā opapātikā*), there are no ascetics and Brahmins in the world (*natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā*) who have reached the state of being rightly attained, who have themselves realised this world and the next world by direct knowledge (*abhiññā*) and declare it.

That is how, mendicants, an untrue man holds untrue views.

Furthermore, mendicants, how does an untrue man give a gift as an untrue man? Here, mendicants, an untrue man gives a gift carelessly, gives it not with his own hand, gives it without showing respect, gives what is to be discarded, gives it with the view that nothing will come of it.

That is how, mendicants, an untrue man gives gifts as an untrue man.

That untrue man, mendicants, is thus endowed with disbelief in the Dhamma, with untrue devotion, with untrue thoughts, with untrue counsel, with untrue speech, with untrue actions, and with untrue views; having given gifts in such a way, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he is reborn in such a destination of untrue men.

And what is the destination of untrue men? Either hell (*nirayo*) or the animal realm (*tiracchānayoni*).
commentary_pali:
91.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷapuṇṇamasuttaṃ. Tattha tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtanti yaṃ yaṃ disaṃ anuviloketi, tattha tattha tuṇhībhūtameva. Anuviloketvāti pañcapasādapaṭimaṇḍitāni akkhīni ummīletvā tato tato viloketvā antamaso hatthakukkuccapādakukkuccānampi abhāvaṃ disvā. Asappurisoti pāpapuriso. No hetaṃ, bhanteti yasmā andho andhaṃ viya so taṃ jānituṃ na sakkoti, tasmā evamāhaṃsu. Eteneva nayena ito paresupi vāresu attho veditabbo. Assaddhasamannāgatoti pāpadhammasamannāgato. Asappurisabhattīti asappurisasevano. Asappurisacintīti asappurisacintāya cintako. Asappurisamantīti asappurisamantanaṃ mantetā. Asappurisavācoti asappurisavācaṃ bhāsitā. Asappurisakammantoti asappurisakammānaṃ kattā. Asappurisadiṭṭhīti asappurisadiṭṭhiyā samannāgato. Asappurisadānanti asappurisehi dātabbaṃ dānaṃ. Tyāssa mittāti te assa mittā. Attabyābādhāyapi cetetīti pāṇaṃ hanissāmi, adinnaṃ ādiyissāmi, micchā carissāmi, dasa akusalakammapathe samādāya vattissāmīti evaṃ attano dukkhatthāya cinteti. Parabyābādhāyāti yathā asuko asukaṃ pāṇaṃ hanti, asukassa santakaṃ adinnaṃ ādiyati, dasa akusalakammapathe samādāya vattati, evaṃ naṃ āṇāpessāmīti evaṃ parassa dukkhatthāya cinteti. Ubhayabyābādhāyāti ahaṃ asukañca asukañca gahetvā dasa akusalakammapathe samādāya vattissāmīti evaṃ ubhayadukkhatthāya cintetīti.

Attabyābādhāyapi mantetītiādīsu ahaṃ dasa akusalakammapathe samādāya vattissāmīti mantento attabyābādhāya manteti nāma. Asukaṃ dasa akusalakammapathe samādapessāmīti mantento parabyābādhāya manteti nāma. Aññena saddhiṃ – ‘‘mayaṃ ubhopi ekato hutvā dasa akusalakammapathe samādāya vattissāmā’’ti mantento ubhayabyābādhāya manteti nāma.

Attabyābādhāyapi mantetī

Asakkaccaṃ dānaṃ detīti deyyadhammampi puggalampi na sakkaroti. Deyyadhammaṃ na sakkaroti nāma uttaṇḍulādidosasamannāgataṃ āhāraṃ deti, na pasannaṃ karoti. Puggalaṃ na sakkaroti nāma nisīdanaṭṭhānaṃ asammajjitvā yattha vā tattha vā nisīdāpetvā yaṃ vā taṃ vā ādhārakaṃ ṭhapetvā dānaṃ deti. Asahatthāti attano hatthena, na deti, dāsakammakārādīhi dāpeti. Acittikatvāti heṭṭhā vuttanayena deyyadhammepi puggalepi na cittīkāraṃ katvā deti. Apaviddhanti chaḍḍetukāmo hutvā vammike uragaṃ pakkhipanto viya deti. Anāgamanadiṭṭhikoti no phalapāṭikaṅkhī hutvā deti.

Asakkaccaṃ dānaṃ detī Asahatthā Acittikatvā Apaviddha Anāgamanadiṭṭhiko

Tatthaupapajjatīti na dānaṃ datvā niraye upapajjati. Yaṃ pana tena pāpaladdhikāya micchādassanaṃ gahitaṃ, tāya micchādiṭṭhiyā niraye upapajjati. Sukkapakkho vuttapaṭipakkhanayena veditabbo. Devamahattatāti chakāmāvacaradevā. Manussamahattatāti tiṇṇaṃ kulānaṃ sampatti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Idaṃ pana suttaṃ suddhavaṭṭavaseneva kathitanti.

Tattha upapajjatī Devamahattatā Manussamahattatā

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷapuṇṇamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
91. Thus have I heard: the Cūḷapuṇṇama Sutta.

There, "silent, silent," wherever he looks around, it is only silence. "Having looked around" means having opened the eyes adorned with the five sense-organs, having looked here and there, and having seen the absence of even hand-worrying and foot-worrying. "An unrighteous man" means a sinful man. "Certainly not, venerable sir," because just as a blind man cannot know a blind man, so they said thus. In this way, the meaning should be understood in the subsequent instances as well. "Endowed with lack of faith" means endowed with sinful qualities. "Devoted to unrighteous men" means associating with unrighteous men. "Thinking unrighteous thoughts" means thinking with unrighteous thoughts. "Counseling unrighteous counsel" means counseling unrighteous counsel. "Speaking unrighteous speech" means speaking unrighteous speech. "Doing unrighteous deeds" means doing unrighteous deeds. "Having unrighteous views" means endowed with unrighteous views. "Unrighteous giving" means giving what should be given to unrighteous men. "Those are his friends" means those are his friends. "He intends for his own harm" means he thinks for his own suffering, "I will kill a living being, I will take what is not given, I will behave wrongly, I will undertake and engage in the ten unwholesome courses of action." "For the harm of others" means he thinks for the suffering of others, "Just as so-and-so kills such-and-such a living being, takes what is not given belonging to so-and-so, undertakes and engages in the ten unwholesome courses of action, so I will command him." "For the harm of both" means he thinks for the suffering of both, "I will take such-and-such and undertake and engage in the ten unwholesome courses of action."

In "he intends for his own harm," etc., intending, "I will undertake and engage in the ten unwholesome courses of action," is called intending for his own harm. Intending, "I will induce so-and-so to undertake the ten unwholesome courses of action," is called intending for the harm of others. With another, intending, "We both, having become one, will undertake and engage in the ten unwholesome courses of action," is called intending for the harm of both.

"He gives a gift disrespectfully" means he does not respect either the gift-worthy object or the recipient. He does not respect the gift-worthy object, meaning he gives food with impurities such as coarse rice, and does not make it pleasing. He does not respect the recipient, meaning he does not sweep the seat, or having seated [the recipient] just anywhere, or having placed just any kind of support, he gives the gift. "Without his own hand" means not with his own hand, he has it given by slaves, servants, etc. "Without paying attention" means he gives without paying attention to either the gift-worthy object or the recipient, in the manner stated below. "Apaviddha" means wanting to throw it away, he gives as if throwing a snake into an anthill. "Having no expectation of return" means he gives without expecting any fruit.

"There, he is reborn" means he is not reborn in hell by giving a gift. But by that wrong view taken by him due to sinful acquisition, he is reborn in hell. The bright side should be understood in the manner opposite to what has been said.
*devamahattatā* means the gods of the six desire realms.

*manussamahattatā* means the prosperity of three families.

The rest is clear throughout.

This sutra, however, is said to be spoken purely in terms of the cycle.

There, *upapajjati* *devamahattatā* *manussamahattatā*.

The Commentary on the Cūḷapuṇṇama Sutta in the Papañcasūdanī, Commentary to the Middle Length Discourses, is finished.

The Commentary on the First Chapter is finished.

mula_pali:
92. ‘‘Jāneyya nu kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisaṃ – ‘sappuriso ayaṃ bhava’’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ , bhante’’. ‘‘Sādhu, bhikkhave; ṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, vijjati yaṃ sappuriso sappurisaṃ jāneyya – ‘sappuriso ayaṃ bhava’nti. Jāneyya pana, bhikkhave, sappuriso asappurisaṃ – ‘asappuriso ayaṃ bhava’’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Sādhu, bhikkhave; etampi kho, bhikkhave, ṭhānaṃ vijjati yaṃ sappuriso asappurisaṃ jāneyya – ‘asappuriso ayaṃ bhava’nti. Sappuriso, bhikkhave, saddhammasamannāgato hoti, sappurisabhatti hoti, sappurisacintī hoti, sappurisamantī hoti, sappurisavāco hoti, sappurisakammanto hoti, sappurisadiṭṭhi hoti; sappurisadānaṃ deti’’.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, sappuriso saddhammasamannāgato hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, bahussuto hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti, paññavā hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso saddhammasamannāgato hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisabhatti hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, sappurisassa ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā saddhā hirimanto ottappino bahussutā āraddhavīriyā upaṭṭhitassatino paññavanto tyāssa mittā honti, te sahāyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisabhatti hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisacintī hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso nevattabyābādhāya ceteti, na parabyābādhāya ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisacintī hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisamantī hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso nevattabyābādhāya manteti, na parabyābādhāya manteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya manteti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisamantī hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisavāco hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisavāco hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisakammanto hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisakammanto hoti.

‘‘Kathañca , bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisadiṭṭhi hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso evaṃdiṭṭhi hoti – ‘atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ, atthi hutaṃ, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, atthi ayaṃ loko , atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisadiṭṭhi hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisadānaṃ deti? Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso sakkaccaṃ dānaṃ deti, sahatthā dānaṃ deti, cittīkatvā dānaṃ deti, anapaviṭṭhaṃ dānaṃ deti, āgamanadiṭṭhiko dānaṃ deti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappuriso sappurisadānaṃ deti.

‘‘So, bhikkhave, sappuriso evaṃ saddhammasamannāgato, evaṃ sappurisabhatti, evaṃ sappurisacintī, evaṃ sappurisamantī, evaṃ sappurisavāco, evaṃ sappurisakammanto, evaṃ sappurisadiṭṭhi; evaṃ sappurisadānaṃ datvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā yā sappurisānaṃ gati tattha upapajjati. Kā ca, bhikkhave, sappurisānaṃ gati? Devamahattatā vā manussamahattatā vā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Cūḷapuṇṇamasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

Devadahavaggo niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Devadahaṃ pañcattayaṃ, kinti-sāma-sunakkhattaṃ;

Sappāya-gaṇa-gopaka-mahāpuṇṇacūḷapuṇṇañcāti.
mula_english:
"Bhikkhus, would a true man know a true man, thinking, ‘This person is a true man’?" "Yes, venerable sir." "Good, bhikkhus. It is possible, bhikkhus, that a true man would know a true man, thinking, ‘This person is a true man.’ But, bhikkhus, would a true man know an untrue man, thinking, ‘This person is an untrue man’?" "Yes, venerable sir." "Good, bhikkhus. It is possible, bhikkhus, that a true man would know an untrue man, thinking, ‘This person is an untrue man.’ A true man, bhikkhus, is possessed of good qualities; he associates as a true man, he wills as a true man, he counsels as a true man, he speaks as a true man, he acts as a true man, he holds views as a true man, and he gives gifts as a true man."

"And how, bhikkhus, is a true man possessed of good qualities? Here, bhikkhus, a true man has faith (saddhā), shame (hirī), and fear of wrongdoing (ottappa); he is learned (bahussuta), energetic (āraddhavīriya), mindful (upaṭṭhitasati), and wise (paññavā). That is how a true man is possessed of good qualities."

"And how, bhikkhus, does a true man associate as a true man? Here, bhikkhus, those ascetics and Brahmins who are faithful, have shame and fear of wrongdoing, are learned, energetic, mindful, and wise—these are his friends and companions. That is how a true man associates as a true man."

"And how, bhikkhus, does a true man will as a true man? Here, bhikkhus, a true man does not will for his own affliction, for the affliction of others, or for the affliction of both. That is how a true man wills as a true man."

"And how, bhikkhus, does a true man counsel as a true man? Here, bhikkhus, a true man does not counsel for his own affliction, for the affliction of others, or for the affliction of both. That is how a true man counsels as a true man."

"And how, bhikkhus, does a true man speak as a true man? Here, bhikkhus, a true man abstains from false speech (musāvāda), from malicious speech (pisuṇā vācā), from harsh speech (pharusā vācā), and from gossip (samphappalāpa). That is how a true man speaks as a true man."

"And how, bhikkhus, does a true man act as a true man? Here, bhikkhus, a true man abstains from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā), abstains from taking what is not given (adinnādānā), abstains from misconduct in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācāra). That is how a true man acts as a true man."

"And how, bhikkhus, does a true man hold views as a true man? Here, bhikkhus, a true man holds such a view as this: ‘There is what is given (dinna), what is offered (yiṭṭha), and what is sacrificed (huta); there is fruit and result of good and bad actions (sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko); there is this world (ayaṃ loko) and the other world (paro loko); there is mother (mātā) and father (pitā); there are beings who are reborn spontaneously (sattā opapātikā); there are good and virtuous recluses and brahmins in the world who have realised for themselves by direct knowledge (abhiññā) and declare this world and the other world.’ That is how a true man holds views as a true man."

"And how, bhikkhus, does a true man give gifts as a true man? Here, bhikkhus, a true man gives a gift carefully (sakkaccaṃ dānaṃ deti), gives it with his own hand (sahatthā dānaṃ deti), gives it showing respect (cittīkatvā dānaṃ deti), gives a valuable gift (anapaviṭṭhaṃ dānaṃ deti), gives it with the view that something will come of it (āgamanadiṭṭhiko dānaṃ deti). That is how a true man gives gifts as a true man."

"That true man - thus possessed of good qualities, who thus associates as a true man, wills as a true man, counsels as a true man, speaks as a true man, acts as a true man, holds views as a true man, and gives gifts as a true man - on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in the destination of true men. And what, bhikkhus, is the destination of true men? Greatness among the gods or greatness among human beings."

The Blessed One said this. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.
The *Cūḷapuṇṇama Sutta*, the tenth, is finished.

The Devadaha Section, the first, is finished.

Its summary:

Devadaha, five triads, *kinti*, *sāma*, *sunakkhatta*;

*sappāya*, *gaṇa*, *gopaka*, *mahāpuṇṇa*, and *cūḷapuṇṇa*.

mula_pali:
93. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, sāriputto; mahāpañño, bhikkhave, sāriputto; puthupañño, bhikkhave, sāriputto; hāsapañño hāsupañño (sī. pī.), bhikkhave, sāriputto; javanapañño, bhikkhave, sāriputto; tikkhapañño, bhikkhave, sāriputto; nibbedhikapañño, bhikkhave, sāriputto; sāriputto, bhikkhave, aḍḍhamāsaṃ anupadadhammavipassanaṃ vipassati. Tatridaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputtassa anupadadhammavipassanāya hoti.

hāsupañño (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāavatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks!”

“Venerable sir,” those monks replied.

The Blessed One said this:

“Monks, Sāriputta is wise (paṇḍito); monks, Sāriputta has great wisdom (mahāpañño); monks, Sāriputta has wide wisdom (puthupañño); monks, Sāriputta has joyous wisdom (hāsa pañño); monks, Sāriputta has quick wisdom (javanapañño); monks, Sāriputta has keen wisdom (tikkhapañño); monks, Sāriputta has penetrative wisdom (nibbedhikapañño); monks, Sāriputta for half a month had insight into states one by one as they occurred (anupadadhammavipassanāṃ vipassati).

Now, monks, Sāriputta’s insight into states one by one as they occurred was this:
commentary_pali:
93.Evaṃme sutanti anupadasuttaṃ. Tattha etadavocāti etaṃ (paṭi. ma. 3.4) ‘‘paṇḍito’’tiādinā nayena dhammasenāpatisāriputtattherassa guṇakathaṃ avoca. Kasmā? Avasesattheresu hi mahāmoggallānattherassa iddhimāti guṇo pākaṭo, mahākassapassa dhutavādoti, anuruddhattherassa dibbacakkhukoti, upālittherassa vinayadharoti, revatattherassa jhāyī jhānābhiratoti, ānandattherassa bahussutoti. Evaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ therānaṃ te te guṇā pākaṭā, sāriputtattherassa pana apākaṭā. Kasmā? Paññavato hi guṇā na sakkā akathitā jānituṃ. Iti bhagavā ‘‘sāriputtassa guṇe kathessāmī’’ti sabhāgaparisāya sannipātaṃ āgamesi. Visabhāgapuggalānañhi santike vaṇṇaṃ kathetuṃ na vaṭṭati, te vaṇṇe kathiyamāne avaṇṇameva kathenti. Imasmiṃ pana divase therassa sabhāgaparisā sannipati, tassā sannipatitabhāvaṃ disvā satthā vaṇṇaṃ kathento imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Tattha paṇḍitoti dhātukusalatā āyatanakusalatā paṭiccasamuppādakusalatā ṭhānāṭṭhānakusalatāti imehi catūhi kāraṇehi paṇḍito. Mahāpaññotiādīsu mahāpaññādīhi samannāgatoti attho.

paṇḍito Mahāpañño

Tatridaṃ mahāpaññādīnaṃ nānattaṃ – tattha katamā mahāpaññā? Mahante sīlakkhandhe pariggaṇhātīti mahāpaññā, mahante samādhikkhandhe, paññākkhandhe, vimuttikkhandhe, vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhe pariggaṇhātīti mahāpaññā, mahantāni ṭhānāṭṭhānāni, mahantā vihārasamāpattiyo , mahantāni ariyasaccāni, mahante satipaṭṭhāne, sammappadhāne, iddhipāde, mahantāni indriyāni, balāni, bojjhaṅgāni, mahante ariyamagge, mahantāni sāmaññaphalāni, mahantā abhiññāyo, mahantaṃ paramatthaṃ nibbānaṃ pariggaṇhātīti mahāpaññā.

mahāpaññā

Katamā puthupaññā, puthu nānākhandhesu ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti puthupaññā. Puthu nānādhātūsu, puthu nānāāyatanesu, puthu nānāatthesu, puthu nānāpaṭiccasamuppādesu, puthu nānāsuññatamanupalabbhesu, puthu nānāatthesu, dhammesu, niruttīsu, paṭibhānesu, puthu nānāsīlakkhandhesu, puthu nānāsamādhi-paññā-vimutti-vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhesu, puthu nānāṭhānāṭṭhānesu, puthu nānāvihārasamāpattīsu, puthu nānāariyasaccesu, puthu nānāsatipaṭṭhānesu, sammappadhānesu, iddhipādesu, indriyesu, balesu, bojjhaṅgesu, puthu nānāariyamaggesu, sāmaññaphalesu, abhiññāsu, puthu nānājanasādhāraṇe dhamme samatikkamma paramatthe nibbāne ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti puthupaññā.

puthupaññā,

Katamā hāsapaññā, idhekacco hāsabahulo vedabahulo tuṭṭhibahulo pāmojjabahulo sīlaṃ paripūreti, indriyasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti, bhojane mattaññutaṃ, jāgariyānuyogaṃ, sīlakkhandhaṃ, samādhikkhandhaṃ, paññākkhandhaṃ, vimuttikkhandhaṃ, vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhaṃ paripūretīti hāsapaññā. Hāsabahulo pāmojjabahulo ṭhānāṭṭhānaṃ paṭivijjhati, hāsabahulo vihārasamāpattiyo paripūretīti hāsapaññā, hāsabahulo ariyasaccāni paṭivijjhati. Satipaṭṭhāne, sammappadhāne, iddhipāde, indriyāni, balāni, bojjhaṅgāni, ariyamaggaṃ bhāvetīti hāsapaññā, hāsabahulo sāmaññaphalāni sacchikaroti, abhiññāyo paṭivijjhatīti hāsapaññā, hāsabahulo vedatuṭṭhipāmojjabahulo paramatthaṃ nibbānaṃ sacchikarotīti hāsapaññā.

hāsapaññā,

Katamā javanapaññā, yaṃkiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ aniccato khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Dukkhato khippaṃ… anattato khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Yā kāci vedanā…pe… yaṃkiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Cakkhu…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhena, dukkhaṃ bhayaṭṭhena, anattā asārakaṭṭhenāti tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā rūpanirodhe nibbāne khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Vedanā, saññā, saṅkhārā, viññāṇaṃ , cakkhu…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhena…pe… vibhūtaṃ katvā jarāmaraṇanirodhe nibbāne khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… viññāṇaṃ. Cakkhu…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā jarāmaraṇanirodhe nibbāne khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā.

javanapaññā,

Katamā tikkhapaññā, khippaṃ kilese chindatīti tikkhapaññā. Uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti, uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ, uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ, uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme, uppannaṃ rāgaṃ, dosaṃ, mohaṃ, kodhaṃ, upanāhaṃ, makkhaṃ, paḷāsaṃ, issaṃ, macchariyaṃ, māyaṃ, sāṭheyyaṃ, thambhaṃ, sārambhaṃ, mānaṃ, atimānaṃ, madaṃ, pamādaṃ, sabbe kilese, sabbe duccarite, sabbe abhisaṅkhāre, sabbe bhavagāmikamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṃ gametīti tikkhapaññā. Ekasmiṃ āsane cattāro ariyamaggā, cattāri sāmaññaphalāni, catasso paṭisambhidāyo, cha ca abhiññāyo adhigatā honti sacchikatā passitā paññāyāti tikkhapaññā.

tikkhapaññā,

Katamā nibbedhikapaññā, idhekacco sabbasaṅkhāresu ubbegabahulo hoti uttāsabahulo ukkaṇṭhanabahulo aratibahulo anabhiratibahulo bahimukho na ramati sabbasaṅkhāresu, anibbiddhapubbaṃ appadālitapubbaṃ lobhakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāletīti nibbedhikapaññā. Anibbiddhapubbaṃ appadālitapubbaṃ dosakkhandhaṃ, mohakkhandhaṃ, kodhaṃ, upanāhaṃ…pe… sabbe bhavagāmikamme nibbijjhati padāletīti nibbedhikapaññā.

nibbedhikapaññā,

Anupadadhammavipassananti samāpattivasena vā jhānaṅgavasena vā anupaṭipāṭiyā dhammavipassanaṃ vipassati, evaṃ vipassanto addhamāsena arahattaṃ patto. Mahāmoggallānatthero pana sattahi divasehi. Evaṃ santepi sāriputtatthero mahāpaññavantataro. Mahāmoggallānatthero hi sāvakānaṃ sammasanacāraṃ yaṭṭhikoṭiyā uppīḷento viya ekadesameva sammasanto satta divase vāyamitvā arahattaṃ patto. Sāriputtatthero ṭhapetvā buddhānaṃ paccekabuddhānañca sammasanacāraṃ sāvakānaṃ sammasanacāraṃ nippadesaṃ sammasi. Evaṃ sammasanto addhamāsaṃ vāyami. Arahattañca kira patvā aññāsi – ‘‘ṭhapetvā buddhe ca paccekabuddhe ca añño sāvako nāma paññāya mayā pattabbaṃ pattuṃ samattho nāma na bhavissatī’’ti. Yathā hi puriso veḷuyaṭṭhiṃ gaṇhissāmīti mahājaṭaṃ veḷuṃ disvā jaṭaṃ chindantassa papañco bhavissatīti antarena hatthaṃ pavesetvā sampattameva yaṭṭhiṃ mūle ca agge ca chinditvā ādāya pakkameyya, so kiñcāpi paṭhamataraṃ gacchati, yaṭṭhiṃ pana sāraṃ vā ujuṃ vā na labhati. Aparo ca tathārūpameva veṇuṃ disvā ‘‘sace sampattaṃ yaṭṭhiṃ gaṇhissāmi, sāraṃ vā ujuṃ vā na labhissāmī’’ti kacchaṃ bandhitvā mahantena satthena veṇujaṭaṃ chinditvā sārā ceva ujū ca yaṭṭhiyo uccinitvā ādāya pakkameyya. Ayaṃ kiñcāpi pacchā gacchati, yaṭṭhiyo pana sārā ceva ujū ca labhati. Evaṃsampadamidaṃ veditabbaṃ imesaṃ dvinnaṃ therānaṃ padhānaṃ.

Anupadadhammavipassana

Evaṃ pana addhamāsaṃ vāyamitvā dhammasenāpati sāriputtatthero sūkarakhataleṇadvāre bhāgineyyassa dīghanakhaparibbājakassa vedanāpariggahasuttante desiyamāne dasabalaṃ bījayamāno ṭhito desanānusārena ñāṇaṃ pesetvā pabbajitadivasato pannarasame divase sāvakapāramiñāṇassa matthakaṃ patvā sattasaṭṭhi ñāṇāni paṭivijjhitvā soḷasavidhaṃ paññaṃ anuppatto.

Tatridaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputtassa anupadadhammavipassanāyāti yā anupadadhammavipassanaṃ vipassatīti anupadadhammavipassanā vuttā, tatra anupadadhammavipassanāya sāriputtassa idaṃ hoti. Idāni vattabbaṃ taṃ taṃ vipassanākoṭṭhāsaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Tatridaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputtassa anupadadhammavipassanāyā

93. Thus.

I have heard that the *anupadasuttaṃ* (the connected or sequential discourse).

There, "thus he spoke," means that he spoke about the qualities (*guṇa*) of the Dharma-army-chief, the venerable Śāriputta, in the manner beginning with "wise."

Why? Because among the remaining elders, the venerable Mahāmoggallāna was known for his quality of having magical power (*iddhi*), Mahākassapa for his asceticism, Anuruddha for his divine eye, Upāli for his mastery of the Vinaya, Revata for his delight in meditative absorption (*jhāna*), and Ānanda for his great learning.

Thus, those qualities were evident in those respective elders, but not in Śāriputta.

Why? Because the qualities of the wise are not easily known if they are not spoken of.

Thus, the Blessed One, thinking, "I will speak of the qualities of Śāriputta," approached the assembly of those who shared similar virtues.

It is not fitting to speak of virtues in the presence of those who do not share them, for when virtues are spoken of, they speak only of faults.

On this day, however, the assembly of the elder's virtuous companions had gathered, and seeing their gathering, the Teacher began this discourse, speaking of virtues.

There, "wise" means wise due to skill in the elements (dhātu), skill in the sense-fields (āyatana), skill in dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*), and skill in what is possible and impossible; thus, he is wise due to these four causes.

In "[he is] greatly wise" and so forth, the meaning is that he is endowed with great wisdom and so forth.

Wise, greatly wise.

Here, there is a distinction among the types of great wisdom and so forth—what is "great wisdom" (*mahāpaññā*)? *Mahāpaññā* is because he comprehends great aggregates of moral conduct (śīlakkhandha), great aggregates of concentration (*samādhi*), great aggregates of wisdom (*paññā*), great aggregates of liberation (*vimutti*), and great aggregates of the vision of the knowledge of liberation (*vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandha*); thus, it is *mahāpaññā*. [It is also *mahāpaññā* because he comprehends] great possibilities and impossibilities, great meditative attainments (*vihārasamāpatti*), great noble truths (*ariyasacca*), great mindfulness practices (*satipaṭṭhāna*), right efforts (*sammappadhāna*), bases of power (*iddhipāda*), faculties (*indriya*), strengths (*bala*), factors of enlightenment (*bojjhaṅga*), the great noble path (*ariyamagga*), great fruits of asceticism (*sāmaññaphala*), great superknowledges (*abhiññā*), and comprehends the ultimate meaning, *nirvāṇa*; thus, it is *mahāpaññā*.

*Mahāpaññā*.

What is "extensive wisdom" (*puthupaññā*)? *Puthupaññā* is because knowledge functions extensively in various aggregates; thus, it is *puthupaññā*. [It is also *puthupaññā* because knowledge functions extensively] in various elements, in various sense-fields, in various meanings, in various instances of dependent origination, in various apprehended voids, in various meanings, in the *dharmas*, in etymologies (*nirutti*), in eloquence (*paṭibhāna*), in various aggregates of moral conduct (*sīlakkhandha*), in various aggregates of concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the vision of the knowledge of liberation, in various possibilities and impossibilities, in various meditative attainments, in various noble truths, in various mindfulness practices, right efforts, bases of power, faculties, strengths, factors of enlightenment, in various noble paths, fruits of asceticism, superknowledges, and having transcended what is common to various ordinary people, knowledge functions in the ultimate meaning, *nirvāṇa*; thus, it is *puthupaññā*.

*Puthupaññā*.

What is "joyful wisdom" (*hāsapaññā*)? Here, a certain person, abounding in joy (*hāsa*), abounding in *vedas*, abounding in satisfaction (*tuṭṭhi*), abounding in delight (*pāmojja*), perfects moral conduct, perfects restraint of the senses, [knows] moderation in eating, devotion to wakefulness, perfects the aggregate of moral conduct, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the vision of the knowledge of liberation; thus, it is *hāsapaññā*.

Abounding in joy, abounding in delight, he penetrates what is possible and impossible; abounding in joy, he perfects the meditative attainments; thus, it is *hāsapaññā*; abounding in joy, he penetrates the noble truths.

[He cultivates] mindfulness practices, right efforts, bases of power, faculties, strengths, factors of enlightenment, and cultivates the noble path; thus, it is *hāsapaññā*; abounding in joy, he realizes the fruits of asceticism, penetrates the superknowledges; thus, it is *hāsapaññā*; abounding in joy, abounding in the *vedas*, satisfaction, and delight, he realizes the ultimate meaning, *nirvāṇa*; thus, it is *hāsapaññā*.

*Hāsapaññā*.

What is "swift wisdom" (*javanapaññā*)? Whatever form there is—past, future, or present… whatever is far or near—all form swiftly passes away due to impermanence; thus, it is *javanapaññā*.

Swiftly due to suffering… swiftly due to non-self; thus, it is *javanapaññā*.

Whatever feeling there is… whatever consciousness there is—past, future, or present… all consciousness swiftly passes away due to impermanence, suffering, and non-self; thus, it is *javanapaññā*.

Eye… old age and death—past, future, or present—swiftly pass away due to impermanence and suffering; thus, it is *javanapaññā*.

Having weighed, having examined, having analyzed, having made manifest, form—past, future, or present—is impermanent in the sense of destruction, suffering in the sense of terror, and non-self in the sense of lacking essence, and having made it disappear, he swiftly proceeds to *nirvāṇa* where form ceases; thus, it is *javanapaññā*.

Feeling, perception, volitions, consciousness, eye… old age and death—past, future, or present—are impermanent in the sense of destruction… and having made it disappear, he swiftly proceeds to *nirvāṇa* where old age and death cease; thus, it is *javanapaññā*.
Materiality, whether past, future or present… and so on… consciousness.

Eye… and so on… aging and death, whether past, future or present, are impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to decay, subject to fading away, subject to cessation.’ Having weighed, considered, analyzed, and made distinct, quick insight swiftly inclines towards the cessation of aging and death, towards *nirvāṇa*; thus, it is swift insight (*javanapaññā*).

94. ‘‘Idha, bhikkhave, sāriputto vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ye ca paṭhame jhāne paṭhamajjhāne (ka. sī. pī. ka.) dhammā vitakko ca vicāro ca pīti ca sukhañca cittekaggatā ca, phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ chando adhimokkho vīriyaṃ sati upekkhā manasikāro – tyāssa dhammā anupadavavatthitā honti. Tyāssa dhammā viditā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho appaṭibandho (ka.) vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘atthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā atthitvevassa atthitevassa (sī. pī.) hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputto vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ye ca dutiye jhāne dhammā – ajjhattaṃ sampasādo ca pīti ca sukhañca cittekaggatā ca, phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ chando adhimokkho vīriyaṃ sati upekkhā manasikāro – tyāssa dhammā anupadavavatthitā honti. Tyāssa dhammā viditā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘atthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā atthitvevassa hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputto pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti. Yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ye ca tatiye jhāne dhammā – sukhañca sati ca sampajaññañca cittekaggatā ca, phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ chando adhimokkho vīriyaṃ sati upekkhā manasikāro – tyāssa dhammā anupadavavatthitā honti, tyāssa dhammā viditā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘atthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā atthitvevassa hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputto sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ye ca catutthe jhāne dhammā – upekkhā adukkhamasukhā vedanā passaddhattā cetaso anābhogo satipārisuddhi cittekaggatā ca, phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ chando adhimokkho vīriyaṃ sati upekkhā manasikāro – tyāssa dhammā anupadavavatthitā honti. Tyāssa dhammā viditā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘atthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā atthitvevassa hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputto sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ye ca ākāsānañcāyatane dhammā – ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā ca cittekaggatā ca phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ chando adhimokkho vīriyaṃ sati upekkhā manasikāro – tyāssa dhammā anupadavavatthitā honti. Tyāssa dhammā viditā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘atthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā atthitvevassa hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputto sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ye ca viññāṇañcāyatane dhammā – viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā ca cittekaggatā ca, phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ chando adhimokkho vīriyaṃ sati upekkhā manasikāro – tyāssa dhammā anupadavavatthitā honti. Tyāssa dhammā viditā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘atthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā atthitvevassa hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputto sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ye ca ākiñcaññāyatane dhammā – ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā ca cittekaggatā ca, phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ chando adhimokkho vīriyaṃ sati upekkhā manasikāro – tyāssa dhammā anupadavavatthitā honti. Tyāssa dhammā viditā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘atthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā atthitvevassa hoti.

“Here, bhikkhus, Sāriputta, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.

And the states in the first *jhāna*—the applied thought, the sustained thought, the rapture, the pleasure, and the unification of mind; the contact, feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saññā*), volition, and mind; the zeal, decision, energy, mindfulness (*sati*), equanimity (*upekkhā*), and attention—these states were defined by him one by one as they occurred.

Known to him those states arose, known they were present, known they disappeared.

He understands thus: ‘So indeed, these states, not having been, come into being; having been, they vanish.’

Regarding those states, he abides unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

He understood: ‘There is an escape beyond.’

and with the cultivation of that attainment, he confirmed that there is.

“Again, bhikkhus, Sāriputta, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, by gaining inner tranquility and oneness of mind, he enters and remains in the second *jhāna*, which is without thinking and pondering, born of concentration, filled with delight and joy.

And the states in the second *jhāna*—the self-confidence, the rapture, the pleasure, and the unification of mind; the contact, feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saññā*), volition, and mind; the zeal, decision, energy, mindfulness (*sati*), equanimity (*upekkhā*), and attention—these states were defined by him one by one as they occurred.

Known to him those states arose, known they were present, known they disappeared.

He understands thus: ‘So indeed, these states, not having been, come into being; having been, they vanish.’

Regarding those states, he abides unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

He understood: ‘There is an escape beyond.’

and with the cultivation of that attainment, he confirmed that there is.

“Again, bhikkhus, Sāriputta, with the fading away as well of rapture, abides in equanimity (*upekkhā*), and mindful (*sati*) and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body. He enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*, on account of which noble ones announce: ‘He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.’

And the states in the third *jhāna*—the equanimity (*upekkhā*), the pleasure, the mindfulness (*sati*), the full awareness, and the unification of mind; the contact, feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saññā*), volition, and mind; the zeal, decision, energy, mindfulness (*sati*), equanimity (*upekkhā*), and attention—these states were defined by him one by one as they occurred; known to him those states arose, known they were present, known they disappeared.

He understands thus: ‘So indeed, these states, not having been, come into being; having been, they vanish.’

Regarding those states, he abides unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

He understood: ‘There is an escape beyond.’

and with the cultivation of that attainment, he confirmed that there is.

“Again, bhikkhus, Sāriputta, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, entered upon and abided in the fourth *jhāna*, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity (*upekkhā*).

And the states in the fourth *jhāna*—the equanimity (*upekkhā*), the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*vedanā*), the mental unconcern due to tranquillity, the purity of mindfulness (*sati*), and the unification of mind; the contact, feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saññā*), volition, and mind; the zeal, decision, energy, mindfulness (*sati*), equanimity (*upekkhā*), and attention—these states were defined by him one by one as they occurred.
Those states are known to him as they arise, known as they persist, known as they vanish.

He understands thus: 'So indeed, these states, not having been, come into being; having been, they vanish.'

Regarding those states, he abides unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

He understands: 'There is an escape beyond.'

And with the cultivation of that attainment, he confirmed that there is.

And the states in the base of infinite space – the perception of the base of infinite space and the unification of mind; the contact, feeling, perception, volition, and mind; the zeal, decision, energy, mindfulness, equanimity, and attention - these states were defined by him one by one as they occurred;

Those states are known to him as they arise, known as they persist, known as they vanish.

He understands thus: 'So indeed, these states, not having been, come into being; having been, they vanish.'

Regarding those states, he abides unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

He understands: 'There is an escape beyond.'

And with the cultivation of that attainment, he confirmed that there is.

Again, monks, Sāriputta, with the complete surmounting of the base of infinite space (ākāśānantyāyatana), aware that 'consciousness is infinite,' enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness (vijñāṇānantyāyatana).

And the states in the base of infinite consciousness - the perception of the base of infinite consciousness and the unification of mind; the contact, feeling, perception, volition, and mind; the zeal, decision, energy, mindfulness, equanimity, and attention - these states were defined by him one by one as they occurred;

Those states are known to him as they arise, known as they persist, known as they vanish.

Regarding those states, he abides unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

He understands: 'There is an escape beyond.'

And with the cultivation of that attainment, he confirmed that there is.

Again, monks, Sāriputta, with the complete surmounting of the base of infinite consciousness (vijñāṇānantyāyatana), aware that 'there is nothing,' enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness (ākiñcanyāyatana).

And the states in the base of nothingness - the perception of the base of nothingness and the unification of mind; the contact, feeling, perception, volition, and mind; the zeal, decision, energy, mindfulness, equanimity, and attention - these states were defined by him one by one as they occurred;

Those states are known to him as they arise, known as they persist, known as they vanish.

He understands thus: 'So indeed, these states, not having been, come into being; having been, they vanish.'

Regarding those states, he abides unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

He understands: 'There is an escape beyond.'

And with the cultivation of that attainment, he confirmed that there is.

commentary_pali:
94.Paṭhame jhāneti ye paṭhame jhāne antosamāpattiyaṃ dhammā. Tyāssāti te assa. Anupadavavatthitā hontīti anupaṭipāṭiyā vavatthitā paricchinnā ñātā viditā honti. Kathaṃ? Thero hi te dhamme olokento abhiniropanalakkhaṇo vitakko vattatīti jānāti. Tathā anumajjanalakkhaṇo vicāro, pharaṇalakkhaṇā pīti, sātalakkhaṇaṃ sukhaṃ, avikkhepalakkhaṇā cittekaggatā, phusanalakkhaṇo phasso vedayitalakkhaṇā vedanā, sañjānanalakkhaṇā saññā, cetayitalakkhaṇā cetanā, vijānanalakkhaṇaṃ viññāṇaṃ, kattukamyatālakkhaṇo chando, adhimokkhalakkhaṇo adhimokkho, paggāhalakkhaṇaṃ vīriyaṃ upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇā sati, majjhattalakkhaṇā upekkhā, anunayamanasikāralakkhaṇo manasikāro vattatīti jānāti. Evaṃ jānaṃ abhiniropanaṭṭhena vitakkaṃ sabhāvato vavatthapeti…pe… anunayamanasikāraṇaṭṭhena manasikāraṃ sabhāvabhāvato vavatthapeti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘tyāssa dhammā anupadavavatthitā hontī’’ti.

Viditā uppajjantīti uppajjamānā viditā pākaṭāva hutvā uppajjanti. Viditā upaṭṭhahantīti tiṭṭhamānāpi viditā pākaṭāva hutvā tiṭṭhanti. Viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchantīti nirujjhamānāpi viditā pākaṭāva hutvā nirujjhanti. Ettha pana taṃñāṇatā ceva ñāṇabahutā ca mocetabbā. Yathā hi teneva aṅgulaggena taṃ aṅgulaggaṃ na sakkā phusituṃ, evameva teneva cittena tassa cittassa uppādo vā ṭhiti vā bhaṅgo vā na sakkā jānitunti. Evaṃ tāva taṃñāṇatā mocetabbā. Yadi pana dve cittāni ekato uppajjeyyuṃ, ekena cittena ekassa uppādo vā ṭhiti vā bhaṅgo vā sakkā bhaveyya jānituṃ. Dve pana phassā vā vedanā vā saññā vā cetanā vā cittāni vā ekato uppajjanakāni nāma natthi, ekekameva uppajjati. Evaṃ ñāṇabahutā mocetabbā. Evaṃ sante kathaṃ? Mahātherassa antosamāpattiyaṃ soḷasa dhammā viditā pākaṭā hontīti. Vatthārammaṇānaṃ pariggahitatāya. Therena hi vatthu ceva ārammaṇañca pariggahitaṃ, tenassa tesaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādaṃ āvajjantassa uppādo pākaṭo hoti, ṭhānaṃ āvajjantassa ṭhānaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti, bhedaṃ āvajjantassa bhedo pākaṭo hoti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘viditā uppajjanti viditā upaṭṭhahanti viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchantī’’ti. Ahutvā sambhontīti iminā udayaṃ passati. Hutvā paṭiventīti iminā vayaṃ passati.

Viditā uppajjantī Viditā upaṭṭhahantī Viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchantī Ahutvā sambhontī Hutvā paṭiventī

Anupāyoti rāgavasena anupagamano hutvā. Anapāyoti paṭighavasena anapagato. Anissitoti taṇhādiṭṭhinissayehi anissito. Appaṭibaddhoti chandarāgena abaddho. Vippamuttoti kāmarāgato vippamutto. Visaṃyuttoti catūhi yogehi sabbakilesehi vā visaṃyutto. Vimariyādīkatenāti nimmariyādīkatena. Cetasāti evaṃvidhena cittena viharati.

Anupāyo Anapāyo Anissito Appaṭibaddho Vippamutto Visaṃyutto Vimariyādīkatenā Cetasā

Tattha dve mariyādā kilesamariyādā ca ārammaṇamariyādā ca. Sace hissa antosamāpattiyaṃ pavatte soḷasa dhamme ārabbha rāgādayo uppajjeyyuṃ, kilesamariyādā tena katā bhaveyya, tesu panassa ekopi na uppannoti kilesamariyādā natthi. Sace panassa antosamāpattiyaṃ pavatte soḷasa dhamme āvajjantassa ekacce āpāthaṃ nāgaccheyyuṃ. Evamassa ārammaṇamariyādā bhaveyyuṃ. Te panassa soḷasa dhamme āvajjantassa āpāthaṃ anāgatadhammo nāma natthīti ārammaṇamariyādāpi natthi.

Aparāpi dve mariyādā vikkhambhanamariyādā ca samucchedamariyādā ca. Tāsu samucchedamariyādā upari āgamissati, imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne vikkhambhanamariyādā adhippetā. Tassa vikkhambhitapaccanīkattā natthīti vimariyādikatena cetasā viharati.

Uttarinissaraṇanti ito uttari nissaraṇaṃ. Aññesu ca suttesu ‘‘uttari nissaraṇa’’nti nibbānaṃ vuttaṃ, idha pana anantaro viseso adhippetoti veditabbo. Tabbahulīkārāti tassa pajānanassa bahulīkaraṇena. Atthitvevassa hotīti tassa therassa atthītiyeva daḷhataraṃ hoti. Iminā nayena sesavāresupi attho veditabbo.

Uttari nissaraṇa Tabbahulīkārā Atthitvevassa hotī

Dutiyavāre pana sampasādanaṭṭhena sampasādo. Sabhāvato vavatthapeti.

sampasādo

Catutthavāre upekkhāti sukhaṭṭhāne vedanupekkhāva. Passaddhattā cetaso anābhogoti yo so ‘‘yadeva tattha sukha’’nti cetaso ābhogo, etenetaṃ oḷārikamakkhāyatīti evaṃ passaddhattā cetaso anābhogo vutto, tassa abhāvāti attho. Satipārisuddhīti parisuddhāsatiyeva. Upekkhāpi pārisuddhiupekkhā.

upekkhā Passaddhattā cetaso anābhogo Satipārisuddhī Upekkhāpi
commentary_english:
94. *Paṭhame jhāne* means the *dharmas* in the first *jhāna* that are internal to meditative attainment (*antosamāpatti*).

*Tyāssā* means "they are his."

*Anupadavavatthitā hontī* means they are arranged successively (*anupaṭipāṭiyā*), determined (*vavatthitā*), distinct (*paricchinnā*), known (*ñātā*), and recognized (*viditā*).

How so? A *thera*, while contemplating these *dharmas*, knows that initial application of mind (*vitakka*) is characterized by directing the mind (*abhiniropanalakkhaṇa*).

Similarly, sustained application of mind (*vicāra*) is characterized by repeated engagement (*anumajjanalakkhaṇa*), joy (*pīti*) is characterized by suffusion (*pharaṇalakkhaṇā*), happiness (*sukhaṃ*) is characterized by satisfaction (*sātalakkhaṇaṃ*), one-pointedness of mind (*cittekaggatā*) is characterized by non-distraction (*avikkhepalakkhaṇā*), contact (*phasso*) is characterized by touching (*phusanalakkhaṇa*), feeling (*vedanā*) is characterized by experiencing (*vedayitalakkhaṇā*), perception (*saññā*) is characterized by cognizing (*sañjānanalakkhaṇā*), volition (*cetanā*) is characterized by intending (*cetayitalakkhaṇā*), consciousness (*viññāṇaṃ*) is characterized by discerning (*vijānanalakkhaṇaṃ*), intention (*chando*) is characterized by wanting to do (*kattukamyatālakkhaṇo*), resolve (*adhimokkho*) is characterized by decision (*adhimokkhalakkhaṇo*), effort (*vīriyaṃ*) is characterized by exertion (*paggāhalakkhaṇaṃ*), mindfulness (*sati*) is characterized by establishing (*upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇā*), equanimity (*upekkhā*) is characterized by balance (*majjhattalakkhaṇā*), and attention (*manasikāro*) is characterized by directing towards conformity (*anunayamanasikāralakkhaṇo*).

Knowing thus, he determines (*vavatthapeti*) initial application of mind (*vitakkaṃ*) in terms of its nature (*sabhāvato*) through the meaning of directing the mind (*abhiniropanaṭṭhena*)… and he determines (*vavatthapeti*) attention (*manasikāraṃ*) in terms of the nature of its being (*sabhāvabhāvato*) through the meaning of directing towards conformity (*anunayamanasikāraṇaṭṭhena*).

Therefore, it was said, "their *dharmas* are arranged successively (*anupadavavatthitā hontī*)."

*Viditā uppajjantī* means, while arising, they arise as recognized and manifest (*pākaṭāva hutvā uppajjanti*).

*Viditā upaṭṭhahantī* means, while persisting, they persist as recognized and manifest (*pākaṭāva hutvā tiṭṭhanti*).

*Viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchantī* means, while ceasing, they cease as recognized and manifest (*pākaṭāva hutvā nirujjhanti*).

Here, however, both that knowledge-ness (*taṃñāṇatā*) and knowledge-abundance (*ñāṇabahutā*) must be removed (*mocetabbā*).

Just as it is not possible to touch that fingertip with that very fingertip (*aṅgulaggena taṃ aṅgulaggaṃ na sakkā phusituṃ*), just so it is not possible to know (*jānitunti*) the arising (*uppādo*), persistence (*ṭhiti*), or dissolution (*bhaṅgo*) of that mind with that very mind (*teneva cittena tassa cittassa*).

Thus, first knowledge-ness (*taṃñāṇatā*) must be removed (*mocetabbā*).

If, however, two minds should arise at once (*dve cittāni ekato uppajjeyyuṃ*), it would be possible to know the arising (*uppādo*), persistence (*ṭhiti*), or dissolution (*bhaṅgo*) of one with one mind (*ekena cittena ekassa*).

But indeed (*pana*) there are no *dharmas* that arise at once (*ekato uppajjanakāni nāma natthi*), be they two contacts (*dve phassā*), or feelings (*vedanā*), or perceptions (*saññā*), or volitions (*cetanā*), or minds (*cittāni*); only one at a time arises (*ekekameva uppajjati*).

Thus, knowledge-abundance (*ñāṇabahutā*) must be removed (*mocetabbā*).

Thus being the case (*evaṃ sante*), how so? For the great *thera*, sixteen *dharmas* in internal meditative attainment (*antosamāpattiyaṃ*) are recognized and manifest (*viditā pākaṭā hontīti*).

Because of being apprehended in terms of the object-basis (*vatthārammaṇānaṃ pariggahitatāya*).

For the *thera* has indeed apprehended both the basis and the object (*vatthu ceva ārammaṇañca pariggahitaṃ*); therefore, for him, while considering the arising (*uppādaṃ āvajjantassa*) of those *dharmas*, the arising is manifest (*uppādo pākaṭo hoti*), while considering the persistence (*ṭhānaṃ āvajjantassa*), the persistence is manifest (*ṭhānaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti*), and while considering the dissolution (*bhedaṃ āvajjantassa*), the dissolution is manifest (*bhedo pākaṭo hoti*).

Therefore, it was said, "They arise recognized (*viditā uppajjanti*), they persist recognized (*viditā upaṭṭhahanti*), they cease recognized (*viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchantī*)."

*Ahutvā sambhontī* means, with this, he sees arising (*udayaṃ passati*).

*Hutvā paṭiventī* means, with this, he sees passing away (*vayaṃ passati*).

Recognized they arise, recognized they persist, recognized they cease, not having been, they come to be, having been, they pass away.

*Anupāyo* means, having been a non-approach (*anupagamano*), due to the force of desire (*rāgavasena*).

*Anapāyo* means, not having departed (*anapagato*), due to the force of aversion (*paṭighavasena*).

*Anissito* means, not being dependent (*anissito*) on the bases of craving, views, etc. (*taṇhādiṭṭhinissayehi*).

*Appaṭibaddho* means, not being bound (*abaddho*) by the desire and passion (*chandarāgena*).

*Vippamutto* means, being liberated (*vippamutto*) from sensual passion (*kāmarāgato*).

*Visaṃyutto* means, being disjoined (*visaṃyutto*) from the four yokes (*catūhi yogehi*) or from all defilements (*sabbakilesehi vā*).

*Vimariyādīkatenā* means, with that which has transcended limits (*nimmariyādīkatena*).

*Cetasā* means, he dwells (*viharati*) with a mind (*cittena*) of such a kind (*evaṃvidhena*).

Without skillful means, without misfortune, without dependence, without attachment, without liberation, without being disjoined, with that which has transcended limits, with the mind.

There, however, are two limits: the limit of defilements (*kilesamariyādā*) and the limit of objects (*ārammaṇamariyādā ca*).

If, indeed, having aroused the sixteen *dharmas* occurring in internal meditative attainment (*antosamāpattiyaṃ pavatte soḷasa dhamme ārambha*), craving and so forth (*rāgādayo*) should arise (*uppajjeyyuṃ*), the limit of defilements (*kilesamariyādā*) would have been made by him (*tena katā bhaveyya*); but since even one of them has not arisen in them (*tesu panassa ekopi na uppanno*), there is no limit of defilements (*kilesamariyādā natthi*).
If, when engaging in internal attainment, some of the sixteen things that one considers do not come into the field of awareness, then that would be a limit of the object [of meditation]. But if, when considering those sixteen things, the future dhamma named *āpātha* does not come into the field of awareness, then there is no limit to the object either.

Furthermore, there are two other limits: the limit of overcoming ( *vikkhambhanamariyādā*) and the limit of eradication (*samucchedamariyādā*). Among these, the limit of eradication will come up later; however, in this context, the limit of overcoming is intended. Because of the overcoming of the opposing factors, he dwells with a mind that has no limit, thinking "there is nothing."

*uttari nissaraṇa* means a further escape from this. And in other discourses (*sutta*), " *uttari nissaraṇa* " is said to be nirvāṇa, but here an immediate distinction is intended, it should be understood. *tabbahulīkārā* means by making that understanding abundant. *atthitvevassa hotī* means for that elder monk, it is indeed more firmly the case that it exists. The meaning should be understood in this way in the remaining instances as well.

*uttari nissaraṇa* *tabbahulīkārā* *atthitvevassa hotī* In the second instance, *sampasādo* [means] through the state of inducing confidence. He determines according to its own nature.

*sampasādo* In the fourth instance, *upekkhā* means equanimity of feeling in the place of happiness. *passaddhattā cetaso anābhogo* means that the mind's focus is "whatever happiness is there." Thus, this is called coarse. Thus, because of the tranquility, there is no focus of the mind; that is, there is an absence of it is the meaning. *satipārisuddhī* means purely mindfulness itself. *upekkhāpi* is also equanimity of purity.

*upekkhā* *passaddhattā cetaso anābhogo* *satipārisuddhī* *upekkhāpi*

mula_pali: 95. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputto sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. So tāya samāpattiyā sato vuṭṭhahati. So tāya samāpattiyā sato vuṭṭhahitvā ye dhammā ye te dhammā (sī.) atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā te dhamme samanupassati – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘atthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā atthitvevassa hoti.
mula_english:
