Again, O monks, Sāriputta, by completely transcending the base of nothingness (ākiñcanyāyatana), enters and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ).
He emerges mindful from that attainment (samāpatti).
Having emerged mindfully from that attainment, he reviews those past states (dhamma) which have ceased, been suppressed, and changed, thinking, ‘So indeed, these states, not having been, come into being; having been, they vanish.’
Regarding those states (dhamma), he abides unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, liberated, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers (vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati).
He understands: ‘There is an escape beyond (uttari nissaraṇa).’
And with the cultivation of that attainment, he confirms that there is (atthitvevassa hoti).
commentary_pali:
95.Sato vuṭṭhahatīti satiyā samannāgato ñāṇena sampajāno hutvā vuṭṭhāti. Te dhamme samanupassatīti yasmā nevasaññānāsaññāyatane buddhānaṃyeva anupadadhammavipassanā hoti, na sāvakānaṃ, tasmā ettha kalāpavipassanaṃ dassento evamāha.

Paññāyacassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā hontīti maggapaññāya cattāri saccāni disvā cattāro āsavā khīṇā honti. Sāriputtattherassa samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ āharitvā arahattaṃ pattavāropi atthi, nirodhasamāpattisamāpannavāropi. Arahattaṃ pattavāro idha gahito, nirodhaṃ pana ciṇṇavasitāya aparāparaṃ samāpajjissatīti vadanti.

Paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā hontī

Tatthassa yasmiṃ kāle nirodhasamāpatti sīsaṃ hoti, nirodhassa vāro āgacchati, phalasamāpatti gūḷhā hoti. Yasmiṃ kāle phalasamāpatti sīsaṃ hoti, phalasamāpattiyā vāro āgacchati, nirodhasamāpatti gūḷhā hoti. Jambudīpavāsino therā pana vadanti ‘‘sāriputtatthero samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ āharitvā anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikatvā nirodhaṃ samāpajji, nirodhā vuṭṭhāya arahattaṃ patto’’ti. Te dhammeti antosamāpattiyaṃ pavatte tisamuṭṭhānikarūpadhamme, heṭṭhā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyaṃ pavattadhamme vā. Tepi hi imasmiṃ vāre vipassitabbadhammāva, tasmā te vā vipassatīti dassetuṃ idaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

Te dhamme
commentary_english:
95. "One who rises mindfully (sato vuṭṭhahatī)" means one rises possessing mindfulness (smṛti), fully knowing with wisdom (jñāna), having become conscious.

"He contemplates those phenomena (te dhamme samanupassatī)" Since in the realm of neither perception nor non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatana), the uninterrupted contemplation of phenomena (anupadadhammavipassanā) is only for Buddhas, not for disciples (śrāvakas), therefore, here, showing the contemplation of aggregates (kalāpavipassanā), he speaks thus.

By wisdom (prajñā).

Having seen, his outflows are eliminated (cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā hontī)" means by the wisdom of the path (maggapaññā), having seen the four truths (catvāri satyāni), the four outflows (catvāro āsavā) are eliminated (khīṇā).

Sāriputta, having brought together serenity and insight (śamathavipassanā) in a paired manner, there is also the attainment of arhatship (arahattaṃ pattavāropi), and the attainment of cessation (nirodhasamāpattisamāpannavāropi).

Here, the attainment of arhatship (arahattaṃ pattavāro) is taken, but they say that one will attain cessation (nirodhaṃ) again and again by the power of habituation (ciṇṇavasitāya).

By wisdom (prajñā).

Having seen, his outflows are eliminated (cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā hontī).

There, at what time the cessation attainment (nirodhasamāpatti) is at its peak, the moment of cessation (nirodhassa vāro) arrives, the fruition attainment (phalasamāpatti) is hidden (gūḷhā).

At what time the fruition attainment (phalasamāpatti) is at its peak, the moment of fruition attainment (phalasamāpattiyā vāro) arrives, the cessation attainment (nirodhasamāpatti) is hidden (gūḷhā).

The elders (therā) dwelling in Jambudvīpa (jambudīpavāsino) say, "Sāriputta, having brought together serenity and insight (śamathavipassanā) in a paired manner, having realized the fruit of non-returning (anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikatvā), attained cessation (nirodhaṃ samāpajji), having arisen from cessation (nirodhā vuṭṭhāya), attained arhatship (arahattaṃ patto)."

"Those phenomena (te dhamme)" means the compounded form-phenomena (tisamuṭṭhānikarūpadhamme) that occur in the inner attainment (antosamāpattiyaṃ pavatte), or the phenomena that occur in the lower realm of neither perception nor non-perception attainment (nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyaṃ pavattadhamme).

Indeed, even those phenomena are to be contemplated (vipassitabbadhammāva) at this time, therefore, to show that he contemplates them (te vā vipassatīti), this was said (idaṃ vuttanti), it should be understood (veditabbaṃ).

Those phenomena (te dhamme).

mula_pali: 96. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sāriputto sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati. Paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. So tāya samāpattiyā sato vuṭṭhahati. So tāya samāpattiyā sato vuṭṭhahitvā ye dhammā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā te dhamme samanupassati – ‘evaṃ kirame dhammā ahutvā sambhonti, hutvā paṭiventī’ti. So tesu dhammesu anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. So ‘natthi uttari nissaraṇa’nti pajānāti. Tabbahulīkārā natthitvevassa hoti.
mula_english:
“Again, monks, Sāriputta, by entirely transcending the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling (saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ *upasampajja viharati*).

And his taints (*āsavā*) are destroyed by seeing with wisdom (paññāya *cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti*).

He emerges mindful from that attainment (*samāpattiyā*) (so *tāya samāpattiyā sato vuṭṭhahati*).

Having done so, he contemplates the past states (*dhammā*), which have ceased (*niruddhā*) and changed (*vipariṇatā*), thus: ‘So indeed, these states (*dhammā*), not having been, come into being; having been, they vanish.’

Regarding those states (*dhammesu*), he abides unattracted (*anupāyo*), unrepelled (*anapāyo*), independent (*anissito*), detached (*appaṭibaddho*), free (*vippamutto*), dissociated (*visaṃyutto*), with a mind (cetasā) rid of barriers.

He understands: ‘There is an escape (nissaraṇa) beyond.’

Through repeated practice, it is simply non-existent for him.

mula_pali:
97. ‘‘Yaṃ kho taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘vasippatto pāramippatto ariyasmiṃ sīlasmiṃ, vasippatto pāramippatto ariyasmiṃ samādhismiṃ, vasippatto pāramippatto ariyāya paññāya , vasippatto pāramippatto ariyāya vimuttiyā’ti, sāriputtameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘vasippatto pāramippatto ariyasmiṃ sīlasmiṃ, vasippatto pāramippatto ariyasmiṃ samādhismiṃ, vasippatto pāramippatto ariyāya paññāya, vasippatto pāramippatto ariyāya vimuttiyā’ti. Yaṃ kho taṃ, bhikkhave , sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘bhagavato putto oraso mukhato jāto dhammajo dhammanimmito dhammadāyādo no āmisadāyādo’ti, sāriputtameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘bhagavato putto oraso mukhato jāto dhammajo dhammanimmito dhammadāyādo no āmisadāyādo’ti. Sāriputto, bhikkhave, tathāgatena anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ sammadeva anuppavattetī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Anupadasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, rightly speaking, were it to be said of anyone: ‘He has attained mastery and perfection in noble virtue, attained mastery and perfection in noble concentration, attained mastery and perfection in noble wisdom, attained mastery and perfection in noble deliverance,’ it is of Śāriputra indeed that rightly speaking this should be said: ‘He has attained mastery and perfection in noble virtue, attained mastery and perfection in noble concentration, attained mastery and perfection in noble wisdom, attained mastery and perfection in noble deliverance.’

“Bhikkhus, rightly speaking, were it to be said of anyone: ‘He is the son of the Blessed One, born of his breast, born of his mouth, born of the Dharma, created by the Dharma, an heir in the Dharma, not an heir in material things,’ it is of Śāriputra indeed that rightly speaking this should be said: ‘He is the son of the Blessed One, born of his breast, born of his mouth, born of the Dharma, created by the Dharma, an heir in the Dharma, not an heir in material things.’ Śāriputra properly continues to keep in motion the unsurpassed Wheel of the Dharma (anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ) set in motion by the Tathāgata.”

This the Blessed One said. Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Anupada Sutta, the first, is finished.
commentary_pali:
97.Vasippatoti ciṇṇavasitaṃ patto. Pāramippattoti nipphattiṃ patto. Orasotiādīsu thero bhagavato ure nibbattasaddaṃ sutvā jātoti oraso, mukhena pabhāvitaṃ saddaṃ sutvā jātoti mukhato jāto, dhammena pana jātattā nimmitattā dhammajo dhammanimmito, dhammadāyassa ādiyanato dhammadāyādo, āmisadāyassa anādiyanato no āmisadāyādoti veditabbo. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Anupadasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
97. "Having mastery (vasippatto)" means having attained mastery in conduct.

"Having attained the perfection (pāramippatto)" means having attained completion.

Among "the own son (oraso)" etc., the Elder, having heard the sound arising from the breast (ure) of the Blessed One, was born, therefore (he is called) "the own son (oraso)"; having heard the sound brought forth from the mouth, he was born, therefore (he is called) "born from the mouth (mukhato jāto)"; but because of being born or created by the Dharma, (he is called) "born of the Dharma (dhammajo)," "created by the Dharma (dhammanimmito)"; because of taking the inheritance of the Dharma, (he is called) "heir to the Dharma (dhammadāyādo)"; because of not taking the inheritance of material things, (he is called) "not heir to material things (no āmisadāyādo)"—this should be understood.

The rest is clear throughout.

The Commentary on the Anupada Sutta, from the Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary to the Middle Length Discourses, is finished.

mula_pali:
98. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā pañho pucchitabbo – ‘cattārome, āvuso, vohārā tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātā. Katame cattāro? Diṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, sute sutavāditā, mute mutavāditā, viññāte viññātavāditā – ime kho, āvuso, cattāro vohārā tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātā. Kathaṃ jānato panāyasmato, kathaṃ passato imesu catūsu vohāresu anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta’nti? Khīṇāsavassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vusitavato katakaraṇīyassa ohitabhārassa anuppattasadatthassa parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanassa sammadaññāvimuttassa ayamanudhammo hoti veyyākaraṇāya – ‘diṭṭhe kho ahaṃ , āvuso, anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharāmi. Sute kho ahaṃ, āvuso…pe… mute kho ahaṃ, āvuso… viññāte kho ahaṃ, āvuso, anupāyo anapāyo anissito appaṭibaddho vippamutto visaṃyutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharāmi. Evaṃ kho me, āvuso, jānato evaṃ passato imesu catūsu vohāresu anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditabbaṃ anumoditabbaṃ. ‘Sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uttariṃ pañho pucchitabbo.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Anathapindika’s monastery, in the Jeta Grove, near Savatthi.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks (saying): “Monks.”

“Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied.

The Blessed One said this:

“Here, monks, a monk declares: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’

Monks, the declaration of such a bhikkhu is neither to be received with approval nor with scorn.

Without approving or disapproving, a question should be put thus: ‘Friend, there are four kinds of expression rightly proclaimed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened.

What are these four? Telling the seen as it is seen; telling the heard as it is heard; telling the sensed as it is sensed; telling the cognized as it is cognized – These, friend, are the four kinds of expression rightly proclaimed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened.

How, in knowing, friend, how, in seeing, regarding these four kinds of expression, is the mind liberated from the taints through non-clinging?’ Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is one with taints destroyed’, who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached the true goal, destroyed the fetters of being, and is completely liberated through final knowledge, this is the nature of his answer: ‘Friends, regarding the seen I abide unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

Regarding the heard…Regarding the sensed…Regarding the cognized I abide unattracted, unrepelled, independent, detached, free, dissociated, with a mind rid of barriers.

It is by knowing thus, seeing thus, regarding these four kinds of expression, that through not clinging my mind is liberated from the taints.’

“Saying ‘good,’ monks, one may delight and rejoice in that bhikkhu’s words.

Saying ‘good,’ delighting and rejoicing in that statement, a further question should be asked.
commentary_pali: 98.Evaṃme sutanti chabbisodhanasuttaṃ. Tattha khīṇā jātītiādīsu ekenāpi padena aññā byākatāva hoti, dvīhipi. Idha pana catūhi padehi aññabyākaraṇaṃ āgataṃ. Diṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditātiādīsu yāya cetanāya diṭṭhe diṭṭhaṃ meti vadati, sā diṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā nāma. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Ayamanudhammoti ayaṃ sabhāvo. Abhinanditabbanti na kevalaṃ abhinanditabbaṃ, parinibbutassa panassa sabbopi khīṇāsavassa sakkāro kātabbo. Uttariṃ pañhoti sace panassa veyyākaraṇena asantuṭṭhā hotha, uttarimpi ayaṃ pañho pucchitabboti dasseti. Ito paresupi tīsu vāresu ayameva nayo.
commentary_english:
98. Thus, "me sutaṃ" is the Chabbisodhana Sutta.

There, in "khīṇā jātī" etc., even with one word, the meaning is explained; [and] with two.

Here, however, the explanation comes with four words.

In "diṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā" etc., when one says, "With consciousness, in what is seen, I say 'it is seen'," that is called *diṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā*.

The same method [of explanation] applies to the remaining terms as well.

"*Ayamanudhammo*" means this is its nature ( *svabhāva*).

"*Abhinanditabbaṃ*" means not only is it to be rejoiced at, but for one who has attained *parinirvāṇa*, all honor (*satkāra*) is to be done for such an *arhat* whose *āsravas* are destroyed (*kṣīṇāsrava*).

"*Uttariṃ pañho*" means if you are not satisfied with this explanation, he shows that this question can be asked again.

The same method applies in the three remaining instances.

mula_pali: 99. ‘‘‘Pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātā. Katame pañca? Seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho – ime kho, āvuso, pañcupādānakkhandhā tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātā. Kathaṃ jānato panāyasmato, kathaṃ passato imesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta’nti? Khīṇāsavassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vusitavato katakaraṇīyassa ohitabhārassa anuppattasadatthassa parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanassa sammadaññāvimuttassa ayamanudhammo hoti veyyākaraṇāya – ‘rūpaṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso, abalaṃ virāgunaṃ virāgaṃ (sī. pī.), virāgutaṃ (ṭīkā) anassāsikanti viditvā ye rūpe upāyūpādānā upayūpādānā (ka.) cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā tesaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā vimuttaṃ me cittanti pajānāmi. Vedanaṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso…pe… saññaṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso… saṅkhāre kho ahaṃ, āvuso… viññāṇaṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso, abalaṃ virāgunaṃ anassāsikanti viditvā ye viññāṇe upāyūpādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā tesaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā vimuttaṃ me cittanti pajānāmi. Evaṃ kho me, āvuso, jānato evaṃ passato imesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditabbaṃ, anumoditabbaṃ. ‘Sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uttariṃ pañho pucchitabbo.
mula_english:
99. “‘These five aggregates affected by clinging (pañcupādānakkhandhā), friends (*āvuso*), are rightly expounded by the Blessed One (bhagavatā)—the one who knows (jānatā), the one who sees (passatā), the Worthy One (arhatā), rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddhena).

Which five? They are: the material form aggregate affected by clinging (rūpupādānakkhandho), the feeling aggregate affected by clinging (vedanupādānakkhandho), the perception aggregate affected by clinging (saññupādānakkhandho), the formations aggregate affected by clinging (saṅkhārupādānakkhandho), and the consciousness aggregate affected by clinging (viññāṇupādānakkhandho). These, friends, are the five aggregates affected by clinging, rightly proclaimed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened.

How does the venerable one (panāyasmato) know, how does he see, regarding these five aggregates affected by clinging, so that through not clinging his mind (cittaṃ) is liberated (vimuttaṃ) from the taints (āsavehi)?’

“Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is one with taints destroyed (khīṇāsavassa)… and is completely liberated through final knowledge, this is the nature of his answer: ‘“Friends, having known material form (rūpaṃ) to be feeble (abalaṃ), fading away (virāgunaṃ), and comfortless (anassāsikanti), with the destruction (khayā), fading away (virāgā), cessation (nirodhā), giving up (cāgā), and relinquishing (paṭinissaggā) of attraction and clinging regarding material form, of mental standpoints (cetaso), adherences (adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā), and underlying tendencies regarding material form, I have understood that my mind is liberated (vimuttaṃ me cittanti pajānāmi).

‘Friends, having known feeling (vedanaṃ)…perception (saññaṃ)…formations (saṅkhāre)…consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) to be feeble (abalaṃ), fading away (virāgunaṃ), and comfortless (anassāsikanti), with the destruction, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishing of attraction and clinging regarding consciousness, of mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies regarding consciousness, I have understood that my mind is liberated (vimuttaṃ me cittanti pajānāmi).

‘“It is by knowing thus, seeing thus, regarding these five aggregates affected by clinging, that through not clinging my mind is liberated (vimuttaṃ) from the taints.’

“Saying ‘good (sādhū),’ bhikkhus, one may delight (abhinanditabbaṃ) and rejoice (anumoditabbaṃ) in that bhikkhu’s words.

Having delighted and rejoiced in that bhikkhu’s words saying ‘good (sādhū),’ a further question should be asked (pucchitabbo)."
commentary_pali: 99.Abalanti dubbalaṃ. Virāgunanti vigacchanasabhāvaṃ. Anassāsikanti assāsavirahitaṃ. Upāyūpādānāti taṇhādiṭṭhīnametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Taṇhādiṭṭhiyo hi tebhūmakadhamme upentīti upāyā, upādiyantīti upādānā. Cetaso adiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayātipi tāsaṃyeva nāmaṃ. Cittañhi taṇhādiṭṭhīhi sakkāyadhammesu tiṭṭhati adhitiṭṭhatīti taṇhādiṭṭhiyo cetaso adhiṭṭhānā, tāhi taṃ abhinivisatīti abhinivesā, tāhiyeva taṃ anusetīti anusayāti vuccanti. Khayāvirāgātiādīsu khayena virāgenāti attho. Sabbāni cetāni aññamaññavevacanāneva.
commentary_english:
99. *Abala* means weak.
*Virāguna* means the nature of vanishing.
*Anassāsika* means without exhalation.
*Upāyūpādānā* is another word for craving and views (*taṇhādiṭṭhi*).
Because craving and views approach the three planes of existence, they are *upāyā*; because they are clung to, they are *upādānā*.
*Cetaso adiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā* is also a name for them.
Because the mind abides and strongly abides in the *sakkāyadhamma* (things related to the existing body) through craving and views, craving and views are the *cetaso adhiṭṭhānā*; because the mind is intent on that, they are *abhinivesā*; because the mind habitually inclines towards that, they are called *anusayā*.
*Khayā*, *virāgā*, etc., means by destruction, by dispassion, this is the meaning.
All these are just synonyms for each other.

mula_pali: 100. ‘‘‘Chayimā , āvuso, dhātuyo tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātā. Katamā cha? Pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, ākāsadhātu, viññāṇadhātu – imā kho, āvuso, cha dhātuyo tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātā. Kathaṃ jānato panāyasmato, kathaṃ passato imāsu chasu dhātūsu anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta’nti? Khīṇāsavassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vusitavato katakaraṇīyassa ohitabhārassa anuppattasadatthassa parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanassa sammadaññāvimuttassa ayamanudhammo hoti veyyākaraṇāya – ‘pathavīdhātuṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso, na attato upagacchiṃ, na ca pathavīdhātunissitaṃ attānaṃ. Ye ca pathavīdhātunissitā upāyūpādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā tesaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā vimuttaṃ me cittanti pajānāmi. Āpodhātuṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso…pe… tejodhātuṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso… vāyodhātuṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso… ākāsadhātuṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso… viññāṇadhātuṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso, na attato upagacchiṃ, na ca viññāṇadhātunissitaṃ attānaṃ. Ye ca viññāṇadhātunissitā upāyūpādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā tesaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā vimuttaṃ me cittanti pajānāmi. Evaṃ kho me, āvuso, jānato, evaṃ passato imāsu chasu dhātūsu anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditabbaṃ, anumoditabbaṃ. ‘Sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uttariṃ pañho pucchitabbo.
mula_english:
100. “Friend, there are these six *dhātus* (elements) rightly proclaimed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened.

What are the six? They are the earth element (*pathavīdhātu*), the water element (*āpodhātu*), the fire element (*tejodhātu*), the air element (*vāyodhātu*), the space element (*ākāsadhātu*), and the consciousness element (*viññāṇadhātu*). These, friend, are the six elements rightly proclaimed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened.

How, in knowing, how, in seeing, is the mind liberated from the taints through not clinging to these six elements?” “Bhikkhus, when a *bhikkhu* (monk) is one with taints destroyed, one who has lived the life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own benefit, with the fetters of being destroyed, and is completely liberated through final knowledge, this is the nature of his answer: ‘Friend, I have treated the earth element as not self, with no self based on the earth element.

And with the destruction, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishing of attraction and clinging, of mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies based on the earth element, I have understood that my mind is liberated.

‘Friend, I have treated the water element…the fire element…the air element…the space element…the consciousness element as not self, with no self based on the consciousness element.

And with the destruction, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishing of attraction and clinging based on the consciousness element, of mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies based on the consciousness element, I have understood that my mind is liberated.

It is by knowing thus, seeing thus, regarding these six elements, that through not clinging my mind is liberated from the taints.’

Bhikkhus, the speech of that monk should be rejoiced over and approved. Having rejoiced over and approved his speech, a further question should be asked.
commentary_pali: 100.Pathavīdhātūti patiṭṭhānadhātu. Āpodhātūti ābandhanadhātu. Tejodhātūti paripācanadhātu. Vāyodhātūti vitthambhanadhātu. Ākāsadhātūti asamphuṭṭhadhātu. Viññāṇadhātūti vijānanadhātu. Na anattato upagacchinti ahaṃ attāti attakoṭṭhāsena na upagamiṃ. Na ca pathavīdhātunissitanti pathavīdhātunissitā sesadhātuyo ca upādārūpañca arūpakkhandhā ca. Tepi hi nissitavatthurūpānaṃ pathavīdhātunissitattā ekena pariyāyena pathavīdhātunissitāva. Tasmā ‘‘na ca pathavīdhātunissita’’nti vadanto sesarūpārūpadhammepi attato na upagacchinti vadati. Ākāsadhātunissitapade pana avinibbhogavasena sabbampi bhūtupādārūpaṃ ākāsadhātunissitaṃ nāma , tathā taṃnissitarūpavatthukā arūpakkhandhā. Evaṃ idhāpi rūpārūpaṃ gahitameva hoti. Viññāṇadhātunissitapade pana sahajātā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānarūpañca viññāṇadhātunissitanti rūpārūpaṃ gahitameva hoti.
commentary_english:
100. *pathavīdhātu* means *patiṭṭhānadhātu*.
*āpodhātu* means *ābandhanadhātu*.
*tejodhātu* means *paripācanadhātu*.
*vāyodhātu* means *vitthambhanadhātu*.
*ākāsadhātu* means *asamphuṭṭhadhātu*.
*viññāṇadhātu* means *vijānanadhātu*.
"*na anattato upagacchi*" means I did not approach with the idea of self, thinking "I am self" with a self-made idea.
"*na ca pathavīdhātunissita*" means earth element-dependent. The remaining elements, appropriated form, and formless aggregates are earth element-dependent.
Because they are dependent on the form of the object that is dependent, they are, in one sense, dependent only on the earth element.
Therefore, those who say "not dependent on the earth element" are saying that they do not approach the remaining form and formless phenomena as self.
However, in the phrase *ākāsadhātunissita* (dependent on the space element), all appropriated form that has not been separated is called *ākāsadhātunissita*, as well as the formless aggregates that have the form of an object dependent on it.
Thus, here also, form and formless are taken as grasped.
However, in the phrase *viññāṇadhātunissita* (dependent on the consciousness element), the three co-arisen aggregates and the form arising from the mind are *viññāṇadhātunissita*, thus form and formless are taken as grasped.

mula_pali: 101. ‘‘‘Cha kho panimāni, āvuso, ajjhattikabāhirāni ajjhattikāni bāhirāni (syā. kaṃ. pī.) āyatanāni tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātāni. Katamāni cha? Cakkhu ceva rūpā ca, sotañca saddā ca, ghānañca gandhā ca, jivhā ca rasā ca, kāyo ca phoṭṭhabbā ca, mano ca dhammā ca – imāni kho, āvuso, cha ajjhattikabāhirāni āyatanāni tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātāni. Kathaṃ jānato panāyasmato, kathaṃ passato imesu chasu ajjhattikabāhiresu āyatanesu anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta’nti? Khīṇāsavassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vusitavato katakaraṇīyassa ohitabhārassa anuppattasadatthassa parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanassa sammadaññāvimuttassa ayamanudhammo hoti veyyākaraṇāya – ‘cakkhusmiṃ, āvuso, rūpe cakkhuviññāṇe cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī nandi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) yā taṇhā ye ca upāyūpādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā tesaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā vimuttaṃ me cittanti pajānāmi. Sotasmiṃ, āvuso, sadde sotaviññāṇe…pe… ghānasmiṃ, āvuso, gandhe ghānaviññāṇe… jivhāya, āvuso, rase jivhāviññāṇe… kāyasmiṃ, āvuso, phoṭṭhabbe kāyaviññāṇe… manasmiṃ, āvuso, dhamme manoviññāṇe manoviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu yo chando yo rāgo yā nandī yā taṇhā ye ca upāyūpādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā tesaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā vimuttaṃ me cittanti pajānāmi. Evaṃ kho me, āvuso, jānato evaṃ passato imesu chasu ajjhattikabāhiresu āyatanesu anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimutta’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditabbaṃ anumoditabbaṃ. ‘Sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uttariṃ pañho pucchitabbo.
mula_english:
101. “But, friend, there are these six internal and external bases (*ajjhattikabāhirāni āyatanāni*) rightly proclaimed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened.

What are the six? They are the eye (cakṣu) and forms (*rūpā*), the ear (*sotañca*) and sounds (*saddā ca*), the nose (*ghānañca*) and odours (*gandhā ca*), the tongue (*jivhā*) and flavours (*rasā ca*), the body (*kāyo*) and tangibles (*phoṭṭhabbā ca*), the mind (*mano*) and mind-objects (*dhammā ca*)—these, friend, are the six internal and external bases rightly proclaimed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened.

How, friend, by knowing, how, by seeing, regarding these six internal and external bases, is the mind liberated through non-clinging from the taints? Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is one with taints destroyed, has lived the life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own welfare, completely destroyed the fetters of being, and is completely liberated through final knowledge, this is the nature of his reply: ‘“Friend, regarding the eye (*cakkhusmiṃ*), form (*rūpe*), eye-consciousness (*cakkhuviññāṇe*), things cognizable by the mind through eye-consciousness (*cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu*), whatever desire (*chando*), lust (*rāgo*), delight (*nandī*), craving (*taṇhā*), attraction and clinging (*upāyūpādānā*), mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies (*adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā*) based on the consciousness element, with their destruction, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishing, I have understood that my mind is liberated.

Regarding the ear (*sotasmiṃ*), sound (*sadde*), ear-consciousness (*sotaviññāṇe*)…pe… regarding the nose (*ghānasmiṃ*), odour (*gandhe*), nose-consciousness (*ghānaviññāṇe*)… regarding the tongue (*jivhāya*), flavour (*rase*), tongue-consciousness (*jivhāviññāṇe*)… regarding the body (*kāyasmiṃ*), tangible (*phoṭṭhabbe*), body-consciousness (*kāyaviññāṇe*)… regarding the mind (*manasmiṃ*), mind-object (*dhamme*), mind-consciousness (*manoviññāṇe*) things cognizable by the mind through mind-consciousness (*manoviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu*), whatever desire (*chando*), lust (*rāgo*), delight (*nandī*), craving (*taṇhā*), attraction and clinging (*upāyūpādānā*), mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies (*adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā*) based on the consciousness element, with their destruction, fading away, cessation, giving up, and relinquishing, I have understood that my mind is liberated.

It is by knowing thus, friend, seeing thus, regarding these six internal and external bases, that through not clinging my mind is liberated from the taints.’

Saying ‘good,’ bhikkhus, one may delight and rejoice in that bhikkhu’s words. After delighting and rejoicing in his words, a further question should be asked.
commentary_pali: 101.Rūpe cakkhuviññāṇe cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesūti ettha yaṃ atīte cakkhudvārassa āpāthaṃ āgantvā niruddhaṃ, yañca anāgate āpāthaṃ āgantvā nirujjhissati, yampi etarahi āgantvā niruddhaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ rūpaṃ nāma. Yaṃ pana atītepi āpāthaṃ anāgantvā niruddhaṃ, anāgatepi anāgantvā nirujjhissati, etarahipi anāgantvā niruddhaṃ, taṃ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbadhammesu saṅgahitanti vutte tipiṭakacūḷābhayatthero āha – ‘‘imasmiṃ ṭhāne dvidhā karotha, upari chandovāre kinti karissatha, nayidaṃ labbhatī’’ti. Tasmā tīsu kālesu āpāthaṃ āgataṃ vā anāgataṃ vā sabbampi taṃ rūpameva, cakkhuviññāṇasampayuttā pana tayo khandhā cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbadhammāti veditabbā. Ayañhettha attho ‘‘cakkhuviññāṇena saddhiṃ viññātabbesu dhammesū’’ti. Chandoti taṇhāchando. Rāgoti sveva rajjanavasena rāgo. Nandīti sveva abhinandanavasena nandī. Taṇhāti sveva taṇhāyanavasena taṇhā. Sesadvāresupi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
101. "When there is *rūpa* (form), eye-consciousness (*cakṣurvijñāna*), in phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness (*cakṣurvijñāṇavijñātabbesu dhammesū*)," that which in the past, having come to the range of the eye-door (*cakṣudvārassa āpāthaṃ*), has ceased (*niruddhaṃ*), and that which in the future will come to the range of the eye and will cease, and that which now having come has ceased, all that is called *rūpa* (form).

But that which even in the past, without coming to the range, has ceased, and even in the future, without coming, will cease, and even now without coming has ceased, that is included in phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness. So said Tipiṭaka Cūḷābhaya Thera: "In this place, divide into two; above, in the *chandovāra*, what will you do? This cannot be obtained."

Therefore, in the three times, whether having come to the range or not having come, all that is *rūpa* (form) itself. But the three aggregates (*khandhā*) associated with eye-consciousness are to be understood as phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness.

Here is the meaning: "In phenomena cognizable together with eye-consciousness."

*Chanda* (desire) is craving-desire (*taṇhāchando*).

*Rāga* (passion) is passion due to its own coloring (*rajjanavasena rāgo*).

*Nandī* (delight) is delight due to its own rejoicing (*abhinandanavasena nandī*).

*Taṇhā* (craving) is craving due to its own craving (*taṇhāyanavasena taṇhā*).

The same rule applies to the remaining doors.

mula_pali:
102. ‘‘‘Kathaṃ jānato panāyasmato, kathaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṃkāramamaṃkāramānānusayā samūhatā’ti susamūhatāti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)? Khīṇāsavassa , bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vusitavato katakaraṇīyassa ohitabhārassa anuppattasadatthassa parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanassa sammadaññāvimuttassa ayamanudhammo hoti veyyākaraṇāya – ‘pubbe kho ahaṃ, āvuso, agāriyabhūto samāno aviddasu ahosiṃ. Tassa me tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā dhammaṃ desesi. Tāhaṃ dhammaṃ sutvā tathāgate saddhaṃ paṭilabhiṃ. So tena saddhāpaṭilābhena samannāgato iti paṭisañcikkhiṃ – sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā. Nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’’’nti.

‘‘So kho ahaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena appaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya, appaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajiṃ. So evaṃ pabbajito samāno bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato ahosiṃ nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho, lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī vihāsiṃ. Adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato ahosiṃ dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī, athenena sucibhūtena attanā vihāsiṃ. Abrahmacariyaṃ pahāya brahmacārī ahosiṃ ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā. Musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato ahosiṃ saccavādī saccasandho theto paccayiko avisaṃvādako lokassa. Pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato ahosiṃ, ito sutvā na amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā na imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya; iti bhinnānaṃ vā sandhātā sahitānaṃ vā anuppadātā samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā ahosiṃ. Pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato ahosiṃ; yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā ahosiṃ. Samphappalāpaṃ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato ahosiṃ; kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī nidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā ahosiṃ kālena sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ.

‘‘So bījagāmabhūtagāmasamārambhā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, ekabhattiko ahosiṃ rattūparato virato vikālabhojanā. Naccagītavāditavisūkadassanā paṭivirato ahosiṃ. Mālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānā paṭivirato ahosiṃ. Uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭivirato ahosiṃ. Jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, āmakadhaññapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, āmakamaṃsapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ; itthikumārikapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, dāsidāsapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, ajeḷakapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, kukkuṭasūkarapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ , hatthigavassavaḷavapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, khettavatthupaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato ahosiṃ. Dūteyyapahiṇagamanānuyogā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, kayavikkayā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, tulākūṭakaṃsakūṭamānakūṭā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, ukkoṭanavañcananikatisāciyogā paṭivirato ahosiṃ, chedanavadhabandhanaviparāmosaālopasahasākārā paṭivirato ahosiṃ.

‘‘So santuṭṭho ahosiṃ kāyaparihārikena cīvarena, kucchiparihārikena piṇḍapātena. So yena yeneva yena yena ca (ka.) pakkamiṃ samādāyeva pakkamiṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma pakkhī sakuṇo yena yeneva ḍeti sapattabhārova ḍeti; evameva kho ahaṃ, āvuso; santuṭṭho ahosiṃ kāyaparihārikena cīvarena, kucchiparihārikena piṇḍapātena. So yena yeneva pakkamiṃ samādāyeva pakkamiṃ. So iminā ariyena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato ajjhattaṃ anavajjasukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedesiṃ.

yena yena ca (ka.)
mula_english:
102. “But, friend, how does the venerable one know, how does he see, so that in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external signs, I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit have been eradicated?”

“Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is one with taints destroyed, who has lived [the spiritual life], done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached his own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and is completely liberated through final knowledge, this is the nature of his answer: ‘Formerly when I lived the home life, I was ignorant. Then the *Tathāgata* or his disciple taught me the *Dharma*. On hearing the *Dharma* I acquired faith (*saddhā*) in the *Tathāgata*. Possessing that faith, I considered thus: “Household life is crowded and dusty; life gone forth is wide open. It is not easy while living in a home to lead the holy life (*brahmacariya*) utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell. I will shave off my hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and go forth from the home life into homelessness.”’

“So, friend, on a later occasion, abandoning a small or a large fortune, abandoning a small or a large circle of relations, I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and went forth from the home life into homelessness. Having thus gone forth and possessing the bhikkhus’ training and way of life, abandoning the killing of living beings, I abstained from killing living beings; with rod and weapon laid aside, gentle and kindly, I abided compassionate to all living beings. Abandoning taking what is not given, I abstained from taking what is not given; I took only what was given, and expected only what was given. I abided with a self that was pure. Having abandoned incelibacy, I led the holy life (*brahmacārī*) of celibacy. I dwelt aloof and abstained from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. Having abandoned untrue speech, I indeed turned away from speaking untruth: I was a truth-speaker, one who is truthful, reliable, trustworthy, and not deceitful to the world. Having abandoned malicious speech, I abstained from malicious speech; I did not repeat elsewhere what I had heard here in order to divide those people from these, nor did I repeat to these people what I had heard elsewhere in order to divide these people from those; thus I was one who reunites those who are divided, a promoter of friendships, who enjoys concord, rejoices in concord, delights in concord, a speaker of words that promote concord. Having abandoned harsh speech, I abstained from harsh speech; I spoke such words as are gentle, pleasing to the ear, and loveable, as go to the heart, are courteous, desired by many and agreeable to many. Having abandoned idle chatter, I abstained from idle chatter. I spoke at the right time, spoke what is factual and beneficial, spoke on the *Dharma* and the *Vinaya*; my words were worth treasuring; they were timely, backed by reasons, measured, and connected with the good.

“I abstained from damaging seeds and plants. I took only one meal a day, abstaining from food at night and from untimely meals. I abstained from dancing, singing, instrumental music, and from witnessing unsuitable shows. I abstained from wearing garlands, embellishing myself with scents, and beautifying myself with unguents. I abstained from high and luxurious beds and seats. I abstained from receiving gold and silver. I abstained from receiving raw grain. I abstained from receiving raw meat. I abstained from receiving women and girls. I abstained from receiving male and female slaves. I abstained from receiving goats and sheep. I abstained from receiving fowl and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares. I abstained from receiving fields and lands. I abstained from going on errands and messages. I abstained from buying and selling. I abstained from false weights, counterfeit metal, and false measures. I abstained from cheating, deception, trickery, and crooked ways. I abstained from cutting, killing, binding, robbery, plunder, and violence.

I was content with robes to protect my body and with alms food to sustain my belly. Wherever I went, I went with only these.”
Just as a bird, wherever it flies, flies with only its wings as a burden, so too, I, friend, was content with robes to protect my body and with alms-food to sustain my stomach.

And wherever he went, he set out, taking only these with him.

Endowed with this noble aggregate of moral discipline (*ārya śīlaskandha*), he experienced within himself a blameless happiness (*anavajjasukhaṃ*).

Note: wherever and (ka.
)
commentary_pali:
102.Ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayāti ettha ahaṅkāro māno, mamaṅkāro taṇhā, sveva mānānusayo. Āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāyāti idaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ dibbacakkhuñca avatvā kasmā vuttaṃ? Bhikkhū lokiyadhammaṃ na pucchanti, lokuttarameva pucchanti, tasmā pucchitapañhaṃyeva kathento evamāha. Ekavissajjitasuttaṃ nāmetaṃ, chabbisodhanantipissa nāmaṃ. Ettha hi cattāro vohārā pañca khandhā cha dhātuyo cha ajjhattikabāhirāni āyatanāni attano saviññāṇakakāyo paresaṃ saviññāṇakakāyoti ime cha koṭṭhāsā visuddhā, tasmā ‘‘chabbisodhaniya’’nti vuttaṃ. Parasamuddavāsittherā pana attano ca parassa ca viññāṇakakāyaṃ ekameva katvā catūhi āhārehi saddhinti cha koṭṭhāse vadanti.

Ime pana cha koṭṭhāsā ‘‘kiṃ te adhigataṃ, kinti te adhigataṃ, kadā te adhigataṃ, kattha te adhigataṃ, katame te kilesā pahīnā, katamesaṃ tvaṃ dhammānaṃ lābhī’’ti (pārā. 198) evaṃ vinayaniddesapariyāyena sodhetabbā.

Ettha hi kiṃ te adhigatanti adhigamapucchā, jhānavimokkhādīsu sotāpattimaggādīsu vā kiṃ tayā adhigataṃ. Kinti te adhigatanti upāyapucchā. Ayañhi etthādhippāyo – kiṃ tayā aniccalakkhaṇaṃ dhuraṃ katvā adhigataṃ, dukkhānattalakkhaṇesu aññataraṃ vā, kiṃ vā samādhivasena abhinivisitvā , udāhu vipassanāvasena, tathā kiṃ rūpe abhinivisitvā, udāhu arūpe, kiṃ vā ajjhattaṃ abhinivisitvā, udāhu bahiddhāti. Kadā te adhigatanti kālapucchā, pubbaṇhamajjhanhikādīsu katarasmiṃ kāleti vuttaṃ hoti.

kiṃ te adhigata Kinti te adhigata Kadā te adhigata

Kattha te adhigatanti okāsapucchā, kismiṃ okāse, kiṃ rattiṭṭhāne divāṭṭhāne rukkhamūle maṇḍape katarasmiṃ vā vihāreti vuttaṃ hoti. Katame te kilesā pahīnāti pahīnakilese pucchati, kataramaggavajjhā tava kilesā pahīnāti vuttaṃ hoti.

Kattha te adhigata Katame te kilesā pahīnā

Katamesaṃ tvaṃ dhammānaṃ lābhīti paṭiladdhadhammapucchā, paṭhamamaggādīsu katamesaṃ tvaṃ dhammānaṃ lābhīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Katamesaṃ tvaṃ dhammānaṃ lābhī

Tasmā idāni cepi koci bhikkhu uttarimanussadhammādhigamaṃ byākareyya, na so ettāvatāva sakkātabbo. Imesu pana chasu ṭhānesu sodhanatthaṃ vattabbo ‘‘kiṃ te adhigataṃ, kiṃ jhānaṃ udāhu vimokkhādīsu aññatara’’nti? Yo hi yena adhigato dhammo, so tassa pākaṭo hoti. Sace ‘‘idaṃ nāma me adhigata’’nti vadati, tato ‘‘kinti te adhigata’’nti pucchitabbo. Aniccalakkhaṇādīsu kiṃ dhuraṃ katvā, aṭṭhatiṃsāya vā ārammaṇesu rūpārūpaajjhattabahiddhādibhedesu vā dhammesu kena mukhena abhinivisitvāti? Yo hi yassābhiniveso, so tassa pākaṭo hoti.

Sace pana ‘‘ayaṃ nāma me abhiniveso, evaṃ mayā adhigata’’nti vadati, tato ‘‘kadā te adhigata’’nti pucchitabbo, ‘‘kiṃ pubbaṇhe, udāhu majjhanhikādīsu aññatarasmiṃ kāle’’ti ? Sabbesañhi attanā adhigatakālo pākaṭo hoti. Sace ‘‘amukasmiṃ nāma me kāle adhigata’’nti vadati, tato ‘‘kattha te adhigata’’nti pucchitabbo, ‘‘kiṃ divāṭṭhāne, udāhu rattiṭṭhānādīsu aññatarasmiṃ okāse’’ti? Sabbesañhi attanā adhigatokāso pākaṭo hoti. Sace ‘‘amukasmiṃ nāma me okāse adhigata’’nti vadati, tato ‘‘katame te kilesā pahīnā’’ti pucchitabbo, ‘‘kiṃ paṭhamamaggavajjhā, udāhu dutiyādimaggavajjhā’’ti? Sabbesañhi attanā adhigatamaggena pahīnakilesā pākaṭā honti.

Sace ‘‘ime nāma me kilesā pahīnā’’ti vadati, tato ‘‘katamesaṃ tvaṃ dhammānaṃ lābhī’’ti pucchitabbo, ‘‘kiṃ sotāpattimaggassa, udāhu sakadāgāmimaggādīsu aññatarassā’’ti? Sabbesañhi attanā adhigatadhammo pākaṭo hoti. Sace ‘‘imesaṃ nāmāhaṃ dhammānaṃ lābhī’’ti vadati, ettāvatāpissa vacanaṃ na saddhātabbaṃ. Bahussutā hi uggahaparipucchākusalā bhikkhū imāni cha ṭhānāni sodhetuṃ sakkonti. Imassa bhikkhuno āgamanapaṭipadā sodhetabbā, yadi āgamanapaṭipadā na sujjhati, ‘‘imāya paṭipadāya lokuttaradhammā nāma na labbhantī’’ti apanetabbo.

Yadi panassa āgamanapaṭipadā sujjhati, ‘‘dīgharattaṃ tīsu sikkhāsu appamatto jāgariyamanuyutto catūsu paccayesu alaggo ākāse pāṇisamena cetasā viharatī’’ti paññāyati, tassa bhikkhuno byākaraṇaṃ paṭipadāya saddhiṃ saṃsandati sameti. ‘‘Seyyathāpi nāma gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakena saddhiṃ saṃsandati sameti, evameva supaññattā tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā saṃsandati sameti nibbānañca paṭipadā cā’’ti (dī. ni. 2.296) vuttasadisaṃ hoti.

Apica kho ettakenāpi sakkāro na kātabbo. Kasmā? Ekaccassa hi puthujjanassāpi sato khīṇāsavapaṭipattisadisā paṭipadā hoti. Tasmā so bhikkhu tehi tehi upāyehi uttāsetabbo. Khīṇāsavassa nāma asaniyāpi matthake patamānāya bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā na hoti, puthujjanassa appamattakenāpi hoti.

Tatrimāni vatthūni – dīghabhāṇakaabhayatthero kira ekaṃ piṇḍapātikaṃ pariggahetuṃ asakkonto daharassa saññaṃ adāsi. So taṃ nhāyamānaṃ kalyāṇīnadīmukhadvāre nimujjitvā pāde aggahesi. Piṇḍapātiko kumbhīloti saññāya mahāsaddamakāsi, tadā naṃ puthujjanoti sañjāniṃsu. Candamukhatissarājakāle pana mahāvihāre saṅghatthero khīṇāsavo dubbalacakkhuko vihāreyeva acchi. Rājā theraṃ pariggaṇhissāmīti bhikkhūsu bhikkhācāraṃ gatesu appasaddo upasaṅkamitvā sappo viya pāde aggahesi. Thero silāthambho viya niccalo hutvā ko etthāti āha ? Ahaṃ, bhante, tissoti. Sugandhaṃ vāyasi no tissāti? Evaṃ khīṇāsavassa bhayaṃ nāma natthīti.

Ekacco pana puthujjanopi atisūro hoti nibbhayo. So rañjanīyena ārammaṇena pariggaṇhitabbo. Vasabharājāpi hi ekaṃ theraṃ pariggaṇhamāno ghare nisīdāpetvā tassa santike badarasāḷavaṃ maddamāno nisīdi. Mahātherassa kheḷo cali, tato therassa puthujjanabhāvo āvibhūto. Khīṇāsavassa hi rasataṇhā nāma suppahīnā, dibbesupi rasesu nikanti nāma na hoti. Tasmā imehi upāyehi pariggahetvā sacassa bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā rasataṇhā vā uppajjati, na tvaṃ arahāti apanetabbo. Sace pana abhīrū acchambhī anutrāsī hutvā sīho viya nisīdati, dibbārammaṇepi nikantiṃ na janeti. Ayaṃ bhikkhu sampannaveyyākaraṇo samantā rājarājamahāmattādīhi pesitaṃ sakkāraṃ arahatīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Chabbisodhanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
102. *Ahaṅkāramamaṅkāramānānusayā* means here *ahaṅkāra* is pride (*māna*), *mamaṅkāra* is craving (*taṇhā*), and it is pride (*mānānusaya*) itself.

Why is this said, *āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāyā*, without mentioning the former dwelling and the divine eye? Monks do not ask about mundane things, they only ask about supramundane things, therefore he speaks thus, relating only to the question that was asked.

This is named the “sutra of one explanation” (*ekavissajjitasuttaṃ*), and it is also named the “sixfold purification” (*chabbisodhanantipissa*).

Here, indeed, the six sections are purified: the four expressions, the five aggregates (*pañca khandhā*), the six elements (*cha dhātuyo*), the six internal and external sense bases (*cha ajjhattikabāhirāni āyatanāni*), one's own body together with consciousness (*attano saviññāṇakakāyo*), and the body of others together with consciousness (*paresāṃ saviññāṇakakāyo*), therefore it is said "sixfold purification" (*chabbisodhanīyanti*).

However, the Elders dwelling beyond the sea (*parasamuddavāsittherā*) say that the six sections are the four kinds of nutriment (*āhārehi*) together with one's own body together with consciousness and the body of others together with consciousness made as one.

But these six sections should be examined by way of the exposition of the discipline, "What have you attained? How have you attained it? When have you attained it? Where have you attained it? What defilements have been abandoned? Of what qualities have you gained?"

Here, *kiṃ te adhigataṃ* is a question about attainment. What have you attained in the absorptions (*jhāna*), liberations (*vimokkha*), etc., or in the path of stream-entry (*sotāpattimaggādīsu*), etc.?

*Kinti te adhigataṃ* is a question about the means.

For here is the meaning in this: What have you attained by taking impermanence as your burden, or one of the characteristics of suffering and non-self, or what by clinging to absorption, or by way of insight (*vipassanā*), likewise, by clinging to form, or to the formless, or by clinging to what is internal, or to what is external?

*Kadā te adhigataṃ* is a question about time, it is said, “In which time, in the forenoon, at midday, etc.?”

*Kattha te adhigataṃ* is a question about place, it is said, “In which place, in the night dwelling, in the day dwelling, at the foot of a tree, in a pavilion, or in which monastery?”

*Katame te kilesā pahīnā* asks about abandoned defilements, it is said, “Which defilements are abandoned by you by way of which path?”

*Katamesaṃ tvaṃ dhammānaṃ lābhī* is a question about qualities attained, it is said, “Of which qualities have you gained, of the first path, etc.?”

Therefore, even now, if any monk should declare the attainment of a superhuman quality (*uttarimanussadhammādhigamaṃ*), he should not be respected merely by that much.

But to these six places should be spoken for the sake of examination, "What have you attained, what absorption or one of the liberations, etc.?" For the quality that has been attained by someone, that is evident to him.

If he says, "This is what I have attained," then he should be asked, "How have you attained it?"

By taking what as your burden among the characteristics of impermanence, etc., or in the thirty-eight objects, or in the qualities that are divided into form, formless, internal, external, etc., by which means have you clung? For the thing to which someone clings, that is evident to him.

But if he says, "This is my clinging, thus I have attained it," then he should be asked, "When have you attained it?", "In the forenoon, or in which time among midday, etc.?" For the time that has been attained by oneself is evident to all.

If he says, "I attained it at such and such a time," then he should be asked, "Where have you attained it?", "In the day dwelling, or in which place among the night dwelling, etc.?" For the place that has been attained by oneself is evident to all.

If he says, "I attained it in such and such a place," then he should be asked, "What defilements have been abandoned?", "What is to be abandoned by the first path, or what is to be abandoned by the second path, etc.?" For the defilements abandoned by the path that has been attained by oneself are evident to all.

If he says, "These defilements have been abandoned by me," then he should be asked, "Of what qualities have you gained?", "Of the path of stream-entry, or of which among the path of once-returning, etc.?" For the quality that has been attained by oneself is evident to all.

If he says, "I have gained these qualities," even by that much his statement should not be trusted.

For monks who are very learned, skilled in learning and questioning, are able to examine these six places.

The conduct of this monk's coming should be examined, if the conduct of his coming is not pure, he should be expelled, "By this conduct, supramundane qualities are not attained."

But if the conduct of his coming is pure, it is known, "For a long time he dwells, unattached to the four requisites, intent on wakefulness, devoted to the three trainings, with a mind like the palm of the hand in the sky," the statement of that monk accords and agrees with the practice.

"Just as the water of the Ganges accords and agrees with the water of the Yamunā, even so, the path leading to *Nibbāna*, well-proclaimed by the Blessed One to his disciples, accords and agrees, both *Nibbāna* and the path."
ni.
2.
296) It is similar to what has been said.

Moreover, respect should not be done even to this extent.
Why? For even a worldling sometimes has a practice similar to the practice of one with destroyed influxes (*khīṇāsava*).
Therefore, that *bhikkhu* should be frightened by those means.
For one with destroyed influxes, there is no fear, terror, or hair-raising even when a thunderbolt falls on his head, but for a worldling, it is even with a small matter.

These are the instances: Elder Dīghabhāṇaka Abhaya, unable to accept a single alms-bowl portion, gave a sign to a young boy.
He dived into the Kalyāṇī River at the river mouth while [the boy] was bathing and grabbed his feet.
The alms-food receiver made a loud noise with the thought "a crocodile!", then they recognized him as a worldling.
In the time of King Candamukhatissa, Elder Saṅgha, a *khīṇāsava* with weak eyes, dwelt in the Mahāvihāra.
The king, thinking, "I will favor the Elder," approached quietly when the *bhikkhus* had gone for alms, and grabbed his feet like a snake.
The Elder, being as motionless as a stone pillar, said, "Who is here?" I am Tissa, *bhante*.
"Do you smell a good fragrance, Tissa?" Thus, there is no fear for a *khīṇāsava*.

But even a worldling is very brave and fearless.
He should be favored with an attractive object.
King Vasabha, while favoring an Elder, had him sit in his house and sat near him, crushing *badara* fruits.
The Elder's saliva dripped, then the worldling-state of the Elder became apparent.
For a *khīṇāsava*, craving for flavors is completely abandoned; there is no craving even for divine flavors.
Therefore, having favored [him] by these means, if fear, terror, or hair-raising, or craving for flavors arises in one who is attached, he should be removed [saying], "You are not worthy."
But if he sits like a lion, fearless, unperturbed, and undismayed, he does not generate craving even for divine objects.
"This *bhikkhu* is accomplished in grammar, he deserves the honor sent from all sides by kings, great ministers, and so forth."

The commentary on the Chabbisodhana Sutta is finished.

mula_pali:
103. ‘‘So cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī ahosiṃ nānubyañjanaggāhī; yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjiṃ ; rakkhiṃ cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjiṃ. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya na nimittaggāhī ahosiṃ nānubyañjanaggāhī; yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjiṃ; rakkhiṃ manindriyaṃ, manindriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjiṃ. So iminā ariyena indriyasaṃvarena samannāgato ajjhattaṃ abyāsekasukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedesiṃ.

‘‘So abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī ahosiṃ, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī ahosiṃ, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī ahosiṃ, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī ahosiṃ, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī ahosiṃ, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī ahosiṃ, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī ahosiṃ.

‘‘So iminā ca ariyena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato, (imāya ca ariyāya santuṭṭhiyā samannāgato,) passa ma. ni. 1.296 cūḷahatthipadopame iminā ca ariyena indriyasaṃvarena samannāgato, iminā ca ariyena satisampajaññena samannāgato vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajiṃ araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. So pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto nisīdiṃ pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā.

passa ma. ni. 1.296 cūḷahatthipadopame

‘‘So abhijjhaṃ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā vihāsiṃ, abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodhesiṃ. Byāpādapadosaṃ pahāya abyāpannacitto vihāsiṃ sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādapadosā cittaṃ parisodhesiṃ. Thinamiddhaṃ pahāya vigatathinamiddho vihāsiṃ ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodhesiṃ. Uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāya anuddhato vihāsiṃ ajjhattaṃ, vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodhesiṃ. Vicikicchaṃ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho vihāsiṃ akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodhesiṃ.
mula_english:
103. "Having seen a form with the eye, I was not one who grasped at its features, nor at its secondary characteristics. Because, if I were to dwell unrestrained in the eye faculty, evil, unwholesome states, namely covetousness and displeasure, would flow into me. For their restraint, I practiced; I guarded the eye faculty, I undertook the restraint of the eye faculty.

Having heard a sound with the ear… Having smelled an odor with the nose… Having tasted a taste with the tongue… Having felt a tactile object with the body… Having cognized a mental phenomenon with the mind, I was not one who grasped at its features, nor at its secondary characteristics. Because, if I were to dwell unrestrained in the mind faculty, evil, unwholesome states, namely covetousness and displeasure, would flow into me. For their restraint, I practiced; I guarded the mind faculty, I undertook the restraint of the mind faculty.

Possessing this noble restraint of the faculties, I experienced within myself a bliss that is unsullied.

"In going forward and in going back, I was one who acted with full awareness; in looking ahead and in looking around, I was one who acted with full awareness; in drawing in and in stretching out, I was one who acted with full awareness; in wearing the double robe, the bowl, and the single robe, I was one who acted with full awareness; in eating, drinking, chewing, and savoring, I was one who acted with full awareness; in evacuating excrement and urine, I was one who acted with full awareness; in going, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and being silent, I was one who acted with full awareness.

"Possessing this noble aggregate of moral discipline, (possessing this noble contentment,) possessing this noble restraint over the sense faculties, and possessing this noble mindfulness and clear comprehension, I frequented a secluded dwelling—a forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a glen, a hillside cave, a cremation ground, a jungle grove, the open air, a heap of straw. After returning from my almsround, after my meal, I sat down, folding my legs crosswise, setting my body erect, and establishing mindfulness before me.

"Having abandoned longing for the world, I dwelled with a mind free from longing; I purified my mind from longing. Having abandoned ill will and hatred, I dwelled with a mind free from ill will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings; I purified my mind from ill will and hatred. Having abandoned dullness and drowsiness, I dwelled free from dullness and drowsiness, percipient of light, mindful and fully aware; I purified my mind from dullness and drowsiness. Having abandoned restlessness and remorse, I dwelled unagitated, with a mind inwardly peaceful; I purified my mind from restlessness and remorse. Having abandoned doubt, I dwelled as one who has passed beyond doubt, unperplexed about wholesome states; I purified my mind from doubt.

mula_pali:
104. ‘‘So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ.

‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ. So idaṃ dukkhanti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ayaṃ dukkhasamudayoti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ayaṃ dukkhanirodhoti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ; ime āsavāti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ayaṃ āsavasamudayoti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ayaṃ āsavanirodhoti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ. Tassa me evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccittha, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccittha, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccitthaः vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ ahosi. Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti abbhaññāsiṃ. Evaṃ kho me, āvuso, jānato evaṃ passato imasmiñca saviññāṇake kāye bahiddhā ca sabbanimittesu ahaṃkāramamaṃkāramānānusayā samūhatā’’ti . ‘‘Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditabbaṃ anumoditabbaṃ. ‘Sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘lābhā no, āvuso, suladdhaṃ no, āvuso, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ tādisaṃ sabrahmacāriṃ samanupassāmā’’’ti passāmāti (sī.).

passāmāti (sī.)

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Chabbisodhanasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
104. So, having abandoned the five hindrances, the defilements of the mind, the weakening of wisdom, quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I attained and dwelled in the first *jhāna*, which is with thought and examination, with joy and pleasure born of seclusion (*vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ*).

With the subsiding of thought and examination, with inner tranquility and unification of mind, without thought, without examination, I attained and dwelled in the second *jhāna*, which is with joy and pleasure born of concentration (*samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ*)...pe... the third *jhāna*... the fourth *jhāna*.

So, when the mind was thus concentrated, purified, clarified, stainless, rid of defilements, pliable, workable, firm, and attained to imperturbability, I directed my mind to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints (*āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmesiṃ*).

I accurately understood: ‘This is suffering (*idaṃ dukkha*),’ as it actually is; ‘This is the origin of suffering (*ayaṃ dukkhasamudaya*),’ as it actually is; ‘This is the cessation of suffering (*ayaṃ dukkhanirodha*),’ as it actually is; ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering (*ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā*),’ as it actually is; ‘These are the taints (*ime āsavā*),’ as they actually are; ‘This is the origin of the taints (*ayaṃ āsavasamudaya*),’ as it actually is; ‘This is the cessation of the taints (*ayaṃ āsavanirodha*),’ as it actually is; ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of the taints (*ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā*),’ as it actually is.

Knowing thus, seeing thus, my mind was liberated from the taint of sensual pleasures (*kāmāsava*), liberated from the taint of becoming (*bhavāsava*), liberated from the taint of ignorance (*avijjāsava*). In the liberated state, there was knowledge that it is liberated.

I directly knew: ‘Destroyed is birth (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’

Thus, friend, knowing thus, seeing thus, in this very body with consciousness and externally in all signs, the tendencies to I-making, mine-making, and conceit have been eradicated.

"Bhikkhus, the words of that bhikkhu should be applauded and approved.

Having applauded and approved his words, you should say this to him: ‘It is a gain for us, friend, a great gain for us, that we see such a spiritual companion as you.’"

The Blessed One said this.

The bhikkhus were delighted and rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

The Chabbisodhana Sutta, the second, is finished.

mula_pali:
105. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘sappurisadhammañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi asappurisadhammañca. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo? Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso uccākulā pabbajito hoti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khomhi uccākulā pabbajito, ime panaññe bhikkhū na uccākulā pabbajitā’ti. So tāya uccākulīnatāya attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Ayaṃ ayampi (sī. pī.), bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo. Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘na kho uccākulīnatāya lobhadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, dosadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti , mohadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. No cepi uccākulā pabbajito hoti; so ca hoti dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī , so tattha pujjo, so tattha pāsaṃso’ti. So paṭipadaṃyeva antaraṃ karitvā tāya uccākulīnatāya nevattānukkaṃseti na paraṃ vambheti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo.

ayampi (sī. pī.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, asappuriso mahākulā pabbajito hoti…pe… yathā uccākulavāre tathā vitthāretabbaṃ mahābhogakulā pabbajito hoti…pe… uḷārabhogakulā pabbajito hoti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khomhi uḷārabhogakulā pabbajito, ime panaññe bhikkhū na uḷārabhogakulā pabbajitā’ti. So tāya uḷārabhogatāya attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo. Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘na kho uḷārabhogatāya lobhadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, dosadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, mohadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. No cepi uḷārabhogakulā pabbajito hoti; so ca hoti dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tattha pujjo, so tattha pāsaṃso’ti. So paṭipadaṃyeva antaraṃ karitvā tāya uḷārabhogatāya nevattānukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo.

yathā uccākulavāre tathā vitthāretabbaṃ
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jetavana at Anāthapiṇḍika’s park.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks.”

“Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the character of a true man (*satpuruṣadharma*) and the character of an untrue man (*asatpuruṣadharma*).

Listen, pay close attention. I will speak.”

“As you say, lord,” the monks responded to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“Bhikkhus, what is the character of an untrue man (*asatpuruṣadharma*)? Here, bhikkhus, an untrue man (*asatpuruṣa*) has gone forth from an aristocratic family (*uccākula*).

He considers thus: ‘I have gone forth from an aristocratic family (*uccākula*); but these other bhikkhus have not gone forth from aristocratic families (*uccākula*).’

So he lauds himself and disparages others because of his aristocratic family (*uccākulīnatā*).

This, monks, is the character of an untrue man (*asatpuruṣadharma*).

But a true man (*satpuruṣa*) considers thus: ‘It is not because of one’s aristocratic family (*uccākulīnatā*) that states of greed ( *lobhadharma*), hatred (*doṣadharma*), or delusion (*mohadharma*) are destroyed.

Even though someone has not gone forth from an aristocratic family (*uccākula*); yet if he has entered upon the way that accords with the *dharma*, entered upon the proper way (*sāmīcippaṭipanna*), and conducts himself according to the *dharma* (*anudhammacārī*), he should be honored for that, he should be praised for that.’

So, putting the practice of the way first, he neither lauds himself nor disparages others because of his aristocratic family (*uccākulīnatā*).

This, monks, is the character of a true man (*satpuruṣadharma*).”

“Again, bhikkhus, an untrue man (*asatpuruṣa*) has gone forth from a wealthy family (*mahākula*)…pe… As with the aristocratic family (*uccākulavāra*), so it should be explained in detail. He has gone forth from a family of great wealth (*mahābhogakula*)…pe… He has gone forth from an influential family (*uḷārabhogakula*).

He considers thus: ‘I have gone forth from an influential family (*uḷārabhogakula*); but these other bhikkhus have not gone forth from influential families (*uḷārabhogakula*).’

So he lauds himself and disparages others because of his influential family (*uḷārabhogatā*).

This too, monks, is the character of an untrue man (*asatpuruṣadharma*).

But a true man (*satpuruṣa*) considers thus: ‘It is not because of one’s influential family (*uḷārabhogatā*) that states of greed (*lobhadharma*) hatred (*doṣadharma*), or delusion (*mohadharma*) are destroyed.

Even though someone has not gone forth from an influential family (*uḷārabhogakula*); yet if he has entered upon the way that accords with the *dharma*, entered upon the proper way (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), and conducts himself according to the *dharma* (*anudhammacārī*), he should be honored for that, he should be praised for that.’

So, putting the practice of the way first, he neither lauds himself nor disparages others because of his influential family (*uḷārabhogatā*).

This too, monks, is the character of a true man (*satpuruṣadharma*).
commentary_pali:
105.Evaṃme sutanti sappurisadhammasuttaṃ. Tattha sappurisadhammanti sappurisānaṃ dhammaṃ. Asappurisadhammanti pāpapurisānaṃ dhammaṃ. Evaṃ mātikaṃ ṭhapetvāpi puna yathā nāma maggakusalo puriso vāmaṃ muñcitvā dakkhiṇaṃ gaṇhāti. Paṭhamaṃ muñcitabbaṃ katheti, evaṃ pahātabbaṃ dhammaṃ paṭhamaṃ desento katamo ca, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammotiādimāha. Tattha uccākulāti khattiyakulā vā brāhmaṇakulā vā. Etadeva hi kuladvayaṃ ‘‘uccākula’’nti vuccati. So tattha pujjoti so bhikkhu tesu bhikkhūsu pūjāraho. Antaraṃ karitvāti abbhantaraṃ katvā.

Mahākulāti khattiyakulā vā brāhmaṇakulā vā vessakulā vā. Idameva hi kulattayaṃ ‘‘mahākula’’nti vuccati. Mahābhogakulāti mahantehi bhogehi samannāgatā kulā. Uḷārabhogakulāti uḷārehi paṇītehi bhogehi sampannakulā. Imasmiṃ padadvaye cattāripi kulāni labbhanti. Yattha katthaci kule jāto hi puññabalehi mahābhogopi uḷārabhogopi hotiyeva.

Mahākulā Mahābhogakulā Uḷārabhogakulā
commentary_english:
105. It is like this: *sappurisadhammasuttaṃ*.

There, *sappurisadhamma* means the dharma of the *sappurisas*.

*asappurisadhamma* means the dharma of the *pāpapurisas*.

Thus, having established the matrix, again, just as a person skilled in the path relinquishes the left and grasps the right.

First he tells what should be relinquished, thus, teaching first the dharma that should be abandoned, [saying]: "Which, O monks, is the *asappurisadhamma*?" and so forth.

There, *uccākulā* means *khattiyakulā* or *brāhmaṇakulā*.

Indeed, this pair of families is called "*uccākula*."

*so tattha pujjo* means that *bhikkhu* is worthy of honor among those *bhikkhus*.

*antaraṃ karitvā* means having made an interior.

*mahākulā* means *khattiyakulā* or *brāhmaṇakulā* or *vessakulā*.

Indeed, this triad of families is called "*mahākula*."

*mahābhogakulā* means families endowed with great *bhogas*.

*uḷārabhogakulā* means families endowed with excellent and refined *bhogas*.

In these two lines, even four families are obtained.

Wherever one is born, through the power of merit, one becomes *mahābhogopi* and *uḷārabhogopi*.

*mahākulā*
*mahābhogakulā*
*uḷārabhogakulā*

mula_pali:
106. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, asappuriso ñāto hoti yasassī. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khomhi ñāto yasassī, ime panaññe bhikkhū appaññātā appesakkhā’ti. So tena ñattena ñātena (sī. ka.), ñātattena (syā. kaṃ. pī.) attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo. Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘na kho ñattena lobhadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, dosadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, mohadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. No cepi ñāto hoti yasassī; so ca hoti dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tattha pujjo , so tattha pāsaṃso’ti. So paṭipadaṃyeva antaraṃ karitvā tena ñattena nevattānukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, asappuriso lābhī hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khomhi lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ, ime panaññe bhikkhū na lābhino cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna’nti. So tena lābhena attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo. Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘na kho lābhena lobhadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, dosadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, mohadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. No cepi lābhī hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ; so ca hoti dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tattha pujjo, so tattha pāsaṃso’ti. So paṭipadaṃyeva antaraṃ karitvā tena lābhena nevattānukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, asappuriso bahussuto hoti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khomhi bahussuto, ime panaññe bhikkhū na bahussutā’ti. So tena bāhusaccena attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo. Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave , iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘na kho bāhusaccena lobhadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti , dosadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, mohadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. No cepi bahussuto hoti; so ca hoti dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tattha pujjo, so tattha pāsaṃso’ti. So paṭipadaṃyeva antaraṃ karitvā tena bāhusaccena nevattānukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, asappuriso vinayadharo hoti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khomhi vinayadharo, ime panaññe bhikkhū na vinayadharā’ti. So tena vinayadharattena attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo. Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘na kho vinayadharattena lobhadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, dosadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, mohadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. No cepi vinayadharo hoti; so ca hoti dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tattha pujjo, so tattha pāsaṃso’ti. So paṭipadaṃyeva antaraṃ karitvā tena vinayadharattena nevattānukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, asappuriso dhammakathiko hoti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khomhi dhammakathiko, ime panaññe bhikkhū na dhammakathikā’ti. So tena dhammakathikattena attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo. Sappuriso ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘na kho dhammakathikattena lobhadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, dosadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, mohadhammā vā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. No cepi dhammakathiko hoti; so ca hoti dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tattha pujjo, so tattha pāsaṃso’ti. So paṭipadaṃyeva antaraṃ karitvā tena dhammakathikattena nevattānukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo.
mula_english:
106. “Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, an untrue man is known and famous (ñāto yasassī).

He considers thus: ‘I am known and famous (ñāto yasassī); but these other *bhikkhus* are unknown and insignificant.’

On account of that recognition, he lauds himself and disparages others.

This, too, *bhikkhus*, is the characteristic of an untrue man (*asappurisadhamma*).

But a true man (*sappurisa*), *bhikkhus*, considers thus: ‘It is not because of being known that states of greed (*lobhadhamma*), hatred (*dosadhamma*), or delusion (*mohadhamma*) are destroyed.

Even though someone may not be known and famous (ñāto yasassī); yet if he has entered upon the way that accords with the *dharma* (dhammānudhammappaṭipanno), entered upon the proper way (sāmīcippaṭipanno), and conducts himself according to the *dharma* (anudhammacārī), he should be honored for that, he should be praised for that.’

So, putting the practice of the way first, he neither lauds himself nor disparages others because of his recognition.

This, too, *bhikkhus*, is the characteristic of a true man (*sappurisadhamma*).

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, an untrue man gains robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting places (*senāsana*), and requisites of medicine (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāra*).

He considers thus: ‘I gain robes (*cīvara*), almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*), resting places (*senāsana*), and requisites of medicine (*gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāra*); but these other *bhikkhus* do not gain these things.’

So he lauds himself and disparages others because of gain (*lābha*).

This, too, *bhikkhus*, is the characteristic of an untrue man (*asappurisadhamma*).

But a true man (*sappurisa*), *bhikkhus*, considers thus: ‘It is not because of gain (*lābha*) that states of greed (*lobhadhamma*), hatred (*dosadhamma*), or delusion (*mohadhamma*) are destroyed.

Even though someone has no gain (*lābha*), yet if he has entered upon the way that accords with the *dharma* (dhammānudhammappaṭipanno), entered upon the proper way (sāmīcippaṭipanno), and conducts himself according to the *dharma* (anudhammacārī), he should be honored for that, he should be praised for that.’

So, putting the practice of the way first, he neither lauds himself nor disparages others because of gain (*lābha*).

This, too, *bhikkhus*, is the characteristic of a true man (*sappurisadhamma*).

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, an untrue man is learned (*bahussuto*).

He considers thus: ‘I am learned (*bahussuto*); but these other *bhikkhus* are not learned (*bahussutā*).’

So, on account of that great learning (*bāhusacca*), he lauds himself and disparages others.

This, too, *bhikkhus*, is the characteristic of an untrue man (*asappurisadhamma*).

But a true man (*sappurisa*), *bhikkhus*, considers thus: ‘It is not because of great learning (*bāhusacca*) that states of greed (*lobhadhamma*), hatred (*dosadhamma*), or delusion (*mohadhamma*) are destroyed.

Even though someone may not be learned (*bahussuto*); yet if he has entered upon the way that accords with the *dharma* (dhammānudhammappaṭipanno), entered upon the proper way (sāmīcippaṭipanno), and conducts himself according to the *dharma* (anudhammacārī), he should be honored for that, he should be praised for that.’

So, putting the practice of the way first, he neither lauds himself nor disparages others because of that great learning (*bāhusacca*).

This, too, *bhikkhus*, is the characteristic of a true man (*sappurisadhamma*).

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, an untrue man is a master of the *Vinaya* (*vinayadhara*).
He considers thus: ‘I am an expert in the Discipline (vinayadhara); but these other monks are not experts in the Discipline.’
So he lauds himself and disparages others because of his being an expert in the Discipline.
This too, monks, is the characteristic of an untrue man.
But a true man, monks, considers thus: ‘It is not because of being an expert in the Discipline that greed (lobha), hatred (dosa), or delusion (moha) diminish.’
Even though someone may not be an expert in the Discipline, if he has entered upon the way that accords with the Dhamma, entered upon the proper way, and conducts himself according to the Dhamma, he should be honored for that, he should be praised for that.
So, putting the practice of the way first, he neither lauds himself nor disparages others because of being an expert in the Discipline.
This too, monks, is the characteristic of a true man.

Moreover, monks, an untrue man is a preacher of the Dhamma (dhammakathika).
He considers thus: ‘I am a preacher of the Dhamma; but these other monks are not preachers of the Dhamma.’
So he lauds himself and disparages others because of his being a preacher of the Dhamma.
This too, monks, is the characteristic of an untrue man.
