129. ‘He understands: ‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that two Accomplished Ones (arahaṃ), Fully Enlightened Ones (sammāsambuddhā), could arise contemporaneously in one world-system (lokadhātuyā)—there is no such possibility (ṭhānaṃ vijjatī).’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that one Accomplished One (arahaṃ), a Fully Enlightened One (sammāsambuddho), might arise in one world-system (lokadhātuyā)—there is such a possibility (ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī).’

He understands: ‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that two Wheel-turning Monarchs (rājāno cakkavattino) could arise contemporaneously in one world-system (lokadhātuyā)… It is possible that one Wheel-turning Monarch (rājā cakkavattī) might arise in one world-system (lokadhātuyā)—there is such a possibility (ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī).’
commentary_pali:
129.Ekissā lokadhātuyāti dasasahassilokadhātuyā. Tīṇi hi khettāni jātikhettaṃ āṇākhettaṃ visayakhettaṃ. Tattha jātikhettaṃ nāma dasasahassī lokadhātu. Sā hi tathāgatassa mātukucchiokkamanakāle nikkhamanakāle sambodhikāle dhammacakkappavattane āyusaṅkhārossajjane parinibbāne ca kampati. Koṭisatasahassacakkavāḷaṃ pana āṇākhettaṃ nāma. Āṭānāṭiyamoraparittadhajaggaparittaratanaparittādīnañhi ettha āṇā vattati. Visayakhettassa pana parimāṇaṃ natthi. Buddhānañhi ‘‘yāvatakaṃ ñāṇaṃ tāvatakaṃ neyyaṃ, yāvatakaṃ neyyaṃ tāvatakaṃ ñāṇaṃ, ñāṇapariyantikaṃ neyyaṃ neyyapariyantikaṃ ñāṇa’’nti (paṭi. ma. 3.5) vacanato avisayo nāma natthi.

Imesu pana tīsu khettesu ṭhapetvā imaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ aññasmiṃ cakkavāḷe buddhā uppajjantīti suttaṃ natthi, na uppajjantīti pana atthi. Tīṇi piṭakāni vinayapiṭakaṃ suttantapiṭakaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ, tisso saṅgītiyo mahākassapattherassa saṅgīti, yasattherassa saṅgīti, moggaliputtatissattherassa saṅgītīti. Imā tisso saṅgītiyo āruḷhe tepiṭake buddhavacane imaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ muñcitvā aññattha buddhā uppajjantīti suttaṃ natthi, na uppajjantīti pana atthi.

Tīṇi piṭakāni tisso saṅgītiyo

Apubbaṃ acarimanti apure apacchā. Ekato na uppajjanti, pure vā pacchā vā uppajjantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha hi bodhipallaṅke bodhiṃ appatvā na uṭṭhahissāmīti nisinnakālato paṭṭhāya yāva mātukucchismiṃ paṭisandhiggahaṇaṃ, tāva pubbeti na veditabbaṃ. Bodhisattassa hi paṭisandhiggahaṇena dasasahassacakkavāḷakampaneneva khettapariggaho kato, aññassa buddhassa uppatti nivāritāva hoti. Parinibbānakālato paṭṭhāya yāva sāsapamattā dhātu tiṭṭhati, tāva pacchāti na veditabbaṃ. Dhātūsu hi ṭhitāsu buddhā ṭhitāva honti. Tasmā etthantare aññassa buddhassa uppatti nivāritāva hoti. Dhātuparinibbāne pana jāte aññassa buddhassa uppatti na nivāritā.

Apubbaṃ acarima

Tīṇi hi antaradhānāni nāma pariyattiantaradhānaṃ, paṭivedhaantaradhānaṃ, paṭipattiantaradhānanti. Tattha pariyattīti tīṇi piṭakāni. Paṭivedhoti saccapaṭivedho. Paṭipattīti paṭipadā. Tattha paṭivedho ca paṭipatti ca hotipi na hotipi. Ekasmiñhi kāle paṭivedhadharā bhikkhū bahū honti, eso bhikkhu puthujjanoti aṅguliṃ pasāretvā dassetabbo hoti. Imasmiṃyeva dīpe ekavāre puthujjanabhikkhu nāma nāhosi. Paṭipattipūrikāpi kadāci bahū honti kadāci appā. Iti paṭivedho ca paṭipatti ca hotipi na hotipi, sāsanaṭṭhitiyā pana pariyatti pamāṇaṃ.

Tīṇi hi antaradhānāni pariyattī Paṭivedho Paṭipattī pariyatti pamāṇaṃ

Paṇḍito hi tepiṭakaṃ sutvā dvepi pūreti. Yathā amhākaṃ bodhisatto āḷārassa santike pañcābhiññā satta ca samāpattiyo nibbattetvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā parikammaṃ pucchi, so na jānāmīti āha. Tato udakassa santikaṃ gantvā adhigataṃ visesaṃ saṃsandetvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa parikammaṃ pucchi, so ācikkhi, tassa vacanasamanantarameva mahāsatto taṃ sampādesi, evameva paññavā bhikkhu pariyattiṃ sutvā dvepi pūreti. Tasmā pariyattiyā ṭhitāya sāsanaṃ ṭhitaṃ hoti.

Yadā pana sā antaradhāyati, tadā paṭhamaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ nassati. Tattha paṭṭhānaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ antaradhāyati, anukkamena pacchā dhammasaṅgaho, tasmiṃ antarahite itaresu dvīsu piṭakesu ṭhitesu sāsanaṃ ṭhitameva hoti. Tattha suttantapiṭake antaradhāyamāne paṭhamaṃ aṅguttaranikāyo ekādasakato paṭṭhāya yāva ekakā antaradhāyati, tadanantaraṃ saṃyuttanikāyo cakkapeyyālato paṭṭhāya yāva oghataraṇā antaradhāyati, tadanantaraṃ majjhimanikāyo indriyabhāvanato paṭṭhāya yāva mūlapariyāyā antaradhāyati, tadanantaraṃ dīghanikāyo dasuttarato paṭṭhāya yāva brahmajālā antaradhāyati. Ekissāpi dvinnampi gāthānaṃ pucchā addhānaṃ gacchati, sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ na sakkoti sabhiyapucchā (su. ni. sabhiyasuttaṃ) viya āḷavakapucchā (su. ni. āḷavakasuttaṃ; saṃ. ni. 1.246) viya ca. Etā kira kassapabuddhakālikā antarā sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu.

abhidhammapiṭakaṃ

Dvīsu pana piṭakesu antarahitesupi vinayapiṭake ṭhite sāsanaṃ tiṭṭhati, parivārakhandhakesu antarahitesu ubhatovibhaṅge ṭhite ṭhitameva hoti. Ubhatovibhaṅge antarahite mātikāya ṭhitāyapi ṭhitameva hoti. Mātikāya antarahitāya pātimokkhapabbajjaupasampadāsu ṭhitāsu sāsanaṃ tiṭṭhati. Liṅgamaddhānaṃ gacchati, setavatthasamaṇavaṃso pana kassapabuddhakālato paṭṭhāya sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ nāsakkhi. Pacchimakassa pana saccapaṭivedhato pacchimakassa sīlabhedato ca paṭṭhāya sāsanaṃ osakkitaṃ nāma hoti. Tato paṭṭhāya aññassa buddhassa uppatti na vāritāti.

Tīṇi parinibbānāni nāma kilesaparinibbānaṃ khandhaparinibbānaṃ dhātuparinibbānanti. Tattha kilesaparinibbānaṃ bodhipallaṅke ahosi, khandhaparinibbānaṃ kusinārāyaṃ, dhātuparinibbānaṃ anāgate bhavissati. Sāsanassa kira osakkanakāle imasmiṃ tambapaṇṇidīpe dhātuyo sannipatitvā mahācetiyaṃ gamissanti, mahācetiyato nāgadīpe rājāyatanacetiyaṃ, tato mahābodhipallaṅkaṃ gamissanti, nāgabhavanatopi devalokatopi brahmalokatopi dhātuyo mahābodhipallaṅkameva gamissanti. Sāsapamattāpi dhātu antarā na nassissati. Sabbā dhātuyo mahābodhipallaṅke rāsibhūtā suvaṇṇakkhandho viya ekagghanā hutvā chabbaṇṇarasmiyo vissajjessanti, tā dasasahassilokadhātuṃ pharissanti.

Tīṇi parinibbānāni

Tato dasasahassacakkavāḷe devatā yo sannipatitvā ‘‘ajja satthā parinibbāyati, ajja sāsanaṃ osakkati, pacchimadassanaṃ dāni idaṃ amhāka’’nti dasabalassa parinibbutadivasato mahantataraṃ kāruññaṃ karissanti. Ṭhapetvā anāgāmikhīṇāsave avasesā sakabhāvena saṇṭhātuṃ na sakkhissanti. Dhātūsu tejodhātu uṭṭhahitvā yāva brahmalokā uggacchissati, sāsapamattāyapi dhātuyā sati ekajālāva bhavissati, dhātūsu pariyādānaṃ gatāsu pacchijjissati. Evaṃ mahantaṃ ānubhāvaṃ dassetvā dhātūsu antarahitāsu sāsanaṃ antarahitaṃ nāma hoti. Yāva evaṃ na anantaradhāyati, tāva acarimaṃ nāma hoti. Evaṃ apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyunti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

Kasmā pana apubbaṃ acarimaṃ na uppajjantīti. Anacchariyattā. Buddhā hi acchariyamanussā. Yathāha – ‘‘ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati acchariyamanusso, katamo ekapuggalo, tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’’ti (a. ni. 1.171-174).

Yadi ca dve vā cattāro vā aṭṭha vā soḷasa vā ekato uppajjeyyuṃ, na acchariyā bhaveyyuṃ. Ekasmiñhi vihāre dvinnaṃ cetiyānampi lābhasakkāro uḷāro na hoti bhikkhūpi bahutāya na acchariyā jātā, evaṃ buddhāpi bhaveyyuṃ. Tasmā na uppajjanti.

Desanāya ca visesābhāvato. Yañhi satipaṭṭhānādibhedaṃ dhammaṃ eko deseti, aññena uppajjitvāpi sova desetabbo siyā. Tato na acchariyo siyā, ekasmiṃ pana dhammaṃ desente desanāpi acchariyā hoti.

Vivādābhāvato ca. Bahūsu ca buddhesu uppajjantesu bahūnaṃ ācariyānaṃ antevāsikā viya ‘‘amhākaṃ buddho pāsādiko, amhākaṃ buddho madhurassaro lābhī puññavā’’ti vivadeyyuṃ, tasmāpi evaṃ na uppajjanti. Apicetaṃ kāraṇaṃ milindaraññā puṭṭhena nāgasenattherena vitthāritameva. Vuttañhi (mi. pa. 5.1.1) –

‘‘Tattha, bhante nāgasena, bhāsitampetaṃ bhagavatā ‘aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso, yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti. Desentā ca, bhante nāgasena, sabbepi tathāgatā sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiyadhamme desenti, kathayamānā ca cattāri ariyasaccāni kathenti, sikkhāpentā ca tīsu sikkhāsu sikkhāpenti, anusāsamānā ca appamādapaṭipattiyaṃ anusāsanti. Yadi, bhante nāgasena, sabbesampi tathāgatānaṃ ekā desanā ekā kathā ekā sikkhā ekā anusiṭṭhi, kena kāraṇena dve tathāgatā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti? Ekenapi tāva buddhuppādena ayaṃ loko obhāsajāto. Yadi dutiyo buddho bhaveyya, dvinnaṃ pabhāya ayaṃ loko bhiyyosomattāya obhāsajāto bhaveyya. Ovadamānā ca dve tathāgatā sukhaṃ ovadeyyuṃ, anusāsamānā ca sukhaṃ anusāseyyuṃ, tattha me kāraṇaṃ brūhi, yathāhaṃ nissaṃsayo bhaveyyanti.

Ayaṃ mahārāja dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī, ekasseva tathāgatassa guṇaṃ dhāreti, yadi dutiyo buddho uppajjeyya, nāyaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu dhāreyya, caleyya kampeyya nameyya onameyya vinameyya vikireyya vidhameyya viddhaṃseyya, na ṭhānamupagaccheyya.

Yathā, mahārāja, nāvā ekapurisasandhāraṇī bhaveyya. Ekasmiṃ purise abhirūḷhe sā nāvā samupādikā bhaveyya. Atha dutiyo puriso āgaccheyya tādiso āyunā vaṇṇena vayena pamāṇena kisathūlena sabbaṅgapaccaṅgena, so taṃ nāvaṃ abhirūheyya. Apinu sā mahārāja, nāvā dvinnampi dhāreyyāti? Na hi, bhante, caleyya kampeyya nameyya onameyya vinameyya vikireyya vidhameyya viddhaṃseyya, na ṭhānamupagaccheyya, osīdeyya udaketi. Evameva kho, mahārāja, ayaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī, ekasseva tathāgatassa guṇaṃ dhāreti, yadi dutiyo buddho uppajjeyya, nāyaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu dhāreyya, caleyya…pe… na ṭhānamupagaccheyya.

Yathā vā pana mahārāja puriso yāvadatthaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjeyya chādentaṃ yāvakaṇṭhamabhipūrayitvā, so dhāto pīṇito paripuṇṇo nirantaro tandikato anonamitadaṇḍajāto punadeva tattakaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjeyya, apinu kho, mahārāja, puriso sukhito bhaveyyāti? Na hi, bhante, sakiṃ bhuttova mareyyāti. Evameva kho, mahārāja, ayaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī …pe… na ṭhānamupagaccheyyāti.

Kiṃ nu kho, bhante nāgasena, atidhammabhārena pathavī calatīti? Idha, mahārāja, dve sakaṭā ratanaparipūritā bhaveyyuṃ yāva mukhasamā. Ekasmā sakaṭato ratanaṃ gahetvā ekasmiṃ sakaṭe ākireyyuṃ, apinu kho taṃ, mahārāja, sakaṭaṃ dvinnampi sakaṭānaṃ ratanaṃ dhāreyyāti? Na hi, bhante, nābhipi tassa phaleyya, arāpi tassa bhijjeyyuṃ, nemipi tassa opateyya, akkhopi tassa bhijjeyyāti. Kiṃ nu kho, mahārāja, atiratanabhārena sakaṭaṃ bhijjatīti? Āma, bhanteti. Evameva kho, mahārāja, atidhammabhārena pathavī calatīti.

Apica mahārāja imaṃ kāraṇaṃ buddhabalaparidīpanāya osāritaṃ, aññampi tattha abhirūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ suṇohi, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti. Yadi, mahārāja, dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, tesaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya – ‘‘tumhākaṃ buddho amhākaṃ buddho’’ti ubhatopakkhajātā bhaveyyuṃ. Yathā, mahārāja, dvinnaṃ balavāmaccānaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya ‘tumhākaṃ amacco amhākaṃ amacco’ti ubhatopakkhajātā honti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yadi, dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, tesaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya ‘tumhākaṃ buddho amhākaṃ buddho’ti ubhatopakkhajātā bhaveyyuṃ. Idaṃ tāva, mahārāja, ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti.

Aparampi, mahārāja, uttariṃ kāraṇaṃ suṇohi, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti. Yadi, mahārāja, dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, aggo buddhoti yaṃ vacanaṃ, taṃ micchā bhaveyya. Jeṭṭho buddhoti yaṃ vacanaṃ, taṃ micchā bhaveyya. Seṭṭho buddhoti, visiṭṭho buddhoti, uttamo buddhoti, pavaro buddhoti, asamo buddhoti, asamasamo buddhoti, appaṭisamo buddhoti, appaṭibhāgo buddhoti, appaṭipuggalo buddhoti yaṃ vacanaṃ , taṃ micchā bhaveyya. Idampi kho tvaṃ, mahārāja , kāraṇaṃ atthato sampaṭiccha, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti.

Apica kho mahārāja buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ sabhāvapakati esā, yaṃ ekoyeva buddho loke uppajjati. Kasmā kāraṇā? Mahantatāya sabbaññubuddhaguṇānaṃ. Aññampi mahārāja yaṃ loke mahantaṃ, taṃ ekaṃyeva hoti. Pathavī, mahārāja, mahantī, sā ekāyeva. Sāgaro mahanto, so ekoyeva. Sineru girirājā mahanto, so ekoyeva. Ākāso mahanto, so ekoyeva. Sakko mahanto, so ekoyeva. Māro mahanto, so ekoyeva. Brahmā mahanto, so ekoyeva. Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho mahanto, so ekoyeva lokasmiṃ. Yattha te uppajjanti, tattha aññassa okāso na hoti. Tasmā, mahārāja, tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho ekoyeva lokasmiṃ uppajjatīti. Sukathito, bhante nāgasena, pañho opammehi kāraṇehī’’ti.

Ekissā lokadhātuyāti ekasmiṃ cakkavāḷe. Heṭṭhā imināva padena dasacakkavāḷasahassāni gahitāni tānipi, ekacakkavāḷeneva paricchindituṃ vaṭṭanti. Buddhā hi uppajjamānā imasmiṃyeva cakkavāḷe uppajjanti, uppajjanaṭṭhāne pana vārite ito aññesu cakkavāḷesu nuppajjantīti vāritameva hoti.

Apubbaṃ acarimanti ettha cakkaratanapātubhāvato pubbe pubbaṃ, tasseva antaradhānato pacchā carimaṃ. Tattha dvidhā cakkaratanassa antaradhānaṃ hoti, cakkavattino kālaṃkiriyato vā pabbajjāya vā. Antaradhāyamānañca pana taṃ kālaṃkiriyato vā pabbajjato vā sattame divase antaradhāyati, tato paraṃ cakkavattino pātubhāvo avārito.

Apubbaṃ acarima

Kasmā pana ekacakkavāḷe dve cakkavattino nuppajjantīti . Vivādupacchedato acchariyabhāvato cakkaratanassa mahānubhāvato ca. Dvīsu hi uppajjantesu ‘‘amhākaṃ rājā mahanto amhākaṃ rājā mahanto’’ti vivādo uppajjeyya. Ekasmiṃ dīpe cakkavattīti ca ekasmiṃ dīpe cakkavattīti ca anacchariyā bhaveyyuṃ . Yo cāyaṃ cakkaratanassa dvisahassadīpaparivāresu catūsu mahādīpesu issariyānuppadānasamattho mahānubhāvo, so parihāyetha. Iti vivādupacchedato acchariyabhāvato cakkaratanassa mahānubhāvato ca na ekacakkavāḷe dve uppajjanti.
commentary_english:
129. *Ekissā lokadhātuyā* means *dasasahassilokadhātuyā*.

There are three fields (*khettāni*): the field by birth (*jātikhettaṃ*), the field of authority (*āṇākhettaṃ*), and the field of range (*visayakhettaṃ*).

Therein, *jātikhettaṃ* means the ten-thousandfold world-system (*dasasahassī lokadhātu*).

For it shakes when the Tathāgata descends into his mother's womb, at his departure, at the time of his awakening, at the turning of the wheel of the Dharma, at the relinquishing of the life-sustaining aggregates, and at his final passing away.

Moreover, *āṇākhettaṃ* means a hundred thousand million world-spheres (*koṭisatasahassacakkavāḷaṃ*).

For here the authority (*āṇā*) of the Āṭānāṭiya, the Peacock Protection, the Banner-top Protection, the Jewel Protection, and so on, extends.

But there is no measure to the *visayakhettassa*.

For regarding the Buddhas, there is no such thing as a non-object, since it is said, "As far as the knowledge extends, so far extends the object; as far as the object extends, so far extends the knowledge; knowledge is the limit of the object, and the object is the limit of knowledge" (Paṭi. Ma. 3.5).

However, among these three fields, there is no sutra saying that Buddhas arise in another world-sphere, setting aside this world-sphere; but there is [a sutra saying] that they do not arise.

The three baskets (*tīṇi piṭakāni*) are the Basket of Discipline (*vinayapiṭakaṃ*), the Basket of Discourses (*suttantapiṭakaṃ*), and the Basket of Higher Doctrine (*abhidhammapiṭakaṃ*); the three recitations (*tisso saṅgītiyo*) are the recitation of the Elder Mahākassapa, the recitation of the Elder Yasa, and the recitation of the Elder Moggaliputtatissa.

These three recitations, when one has mastered the three baskets, in the Buddha's word, setting aside this world-sphere, there is no sutra saying that Buddhas arise elsewhere; but there is [a sutra saying] that they do not arise.

*Tīṇi piṭakāni*, *tisso saṅgītiyo*.

*Apubbaṃ acarimaṃti* means not before, not after (*apure apacchā*).

They do not arise at the same time; it is said that they arise before or after.

Therein, from the time he sat down at the Bodhi-seat, [thinking,] "I will not rise up from this seat until I attain awakening," until the seizing of rebirth in his mother's womb, it is not to be understood as "before."

For, with the seizing of rebirth by the Bodhisattva, with the shaking of the ten-thousandfold world-system itself, the delimitation of the field is done, and the arising of another Buddha is warded off.

From the time of his final passing away until a mustard-seed sized relic remains, it is not to be understood as "after."

For while the relics remain, the Buddhas remain.

Therefore, in this interval, the arising of another Buddha is warded off.

But when the final passing away of the relics has occurred, the arising of another Buddha is not warded off.

*Apubbaṃ acarima*.

The three disappearances (*tīṇi hi antaradhānāni*) are the disappearance of learning (*pariyattiantaradhānaṃ*), the disappearance of realization (*paṭivedhaantaradhānaṃ*), and the disappearance of practice (*paṭipattiantaradhānaṃ*).

Therein, *pariyattī* means the three baskets.

*Paṭivedho* means the realization of the truths.

*Paṭipattī* means the course of practice.

Therein, realization and practice both exist and do not exist.

For at one time, there are many monks who maintain realization; that monk must be pointed out by extending a finger, [saying,] "This is an ordinary person."

On this island itself, at one time, there was no monk called an ordinary person.

Those who fulfill the practice are also sometimes many and sometimes few.

Thus, realization and practice both exist and do not exist, but for the continuation of the teaching, learning is the measure (*pariyatti pamāṇaṃ*).

*Tīṇi hi antaradhānāni*, *pariyattī*, *paṭivedho*, *paṭipattī*, *pariyatti pamāṇaṃ*.

For the wise man, having heard the three baskets, fulfills both.
Just as our bodhisattva, having developed the five superknowledges and seven attainments in the presence of Āḷāra, asked about the preliminary practice for the attainment of the realm of neither perception nor non-perception, he said, "I do not know."

Then, having gone to Udaka, having compared the special qualities he had attained, he asked about the preliminary practice for the attainment of the realm of neither perception nor non-perception, and he explained it. Immediately after his words, the great being accomplished it. Just so, a wise *bhikkhu*, having heard the *pariyatti*, fulfills both.

Therefore, when the *sāsana* is established, the *pariyatti* is established.

But when that disappears, then first the *Abhidhamma Piṭaka* vanishes.

There, the *Paṭṭhāna* disappears first of all, and gradually afterwards the *Dhamma Saṅgaṇi*. When that has disappeared, even if the other two *Piṭakas* remain, the *sāsana* is still established.

There, when the *Suttanta Piṭaka* is disappearing, first the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, from the *Ekādasaka*, disappears up to the *Ekaka*; after that the *Saṃyutta Nikāya*, from the *Cakkapeyyāla*, disappears up to the *Oghataraṇa*; after that the *Majjhima Nikāya*, from the *Indriyabhāvanā*, disappears up to the *Mūlapariyāya*; after that the *Dīgha Nikāya*, from the *Dasuttara*, disappears up to the *Brahmajāla*.

The question of even one or two verses goes astray, [and one] is not able to maintain the *sāsana*, like the question of Sabhiya (Sn. Sabhiyasutta) and like the question of Āḷavaka (Sn. Āḷavakasutta; Saṃ. Ni. 1.246).

It is said that those [questions] from the time of the Buddha Kassapa were not able to maintain the *sāsana* in the intervening period.

Even when two *Piṭakas* have disappeared, the *sāsana* remains if the *Vinaya Piṭaka* remains. When the *Parivāra Khandhakas* have disappeared, it still remains if the *Ubhatovibhaṅga* remains.

When the *Ubhatovibhaṅga* has disappeared, it still remains even if the *Mātikā* remains.

When the *Mātikā* has disappeared, the *sāsana* remains if the *Pātimokkha*, *Pabbajjā*, and *Upasampadā* remain.

The sign goes astray, but the lineage of white-clothed ascetics has not been able to maintain the *sāsana* since the time of the Buddha Kassapa.

But from the decline of the last realization of truth and from the last breach of morality, the *sāsana* is said to be declining.

From then on, the arising of another Buddha is not prevented.

The three *parinibbānas* are: the *kilesaparinibbāna* (extinguishment of defilements), the *khandhaparinibbāna* (extinguishment of aggregates), and the *dhātuparinibbāna* (extinguishment of elements).

There, the *kilesaparinibbāna* was at the Bodhi tree, the *khandhaparinibbāna* was at Kusinārā, and the *dhātuparinibbāna* will be in the future.

It is said that at the time of the decline of the *sāsana*, in this Tambapaṇṇi island, the elements will gather together and go to the Mahācetiya, from the Mahācetiya to the Rājāyatanacetiya in Nāgadīpa, from there they will go to the Mahābodhi tree; from the Nāga-bhavana, from the Deva-loka, and from the Brahma-loka, the elements will go to the Mahābodhi tree itself.

Not even an element the size of a mustard seed will be destroyed in between.

All the elements, having gathered together at the Mahābodhi tree, having become a single mass like a golden trunk, will emit six-colored rays, and they will pervade the ten-thousand world-systems.

The three *parinibbānas*.

Then, in the ten-thousand *cakkavāḷas*, the deities, having gathered together, will show greater compassion than on the day of the *parinibbāna* of the Ten-Powered One, saying, "Today the Teacher attains *parinibbāna*, today the *sāsana* declines, now this is our last sight."

Except for the non-returners and those with extinguished *āsavas*, the rest will not be able to remain in their own state.

A fire element will arise among the elements and will ascend up to the Brahma-world; even with an element the size of a mustard seed, there will be a single flame; when the elements have reached their end, it will be cut off.

Having shown such great power, when the elements have disappeared, the *sāsana* is said to have disappeared.
As long as it does not continuously flow on, so long is it called "last."

Thus, it is not possible for the unprecedented and last to arise.

Why then do the unprecedented and last not arise?

Because of not being wonderful.

For Buddhas are wonderful humans.

As he said: "When one individual arises in the world, monks, he arises as a wonderful human. Which one individual? The *tathāgata*, the *arhat*, the perfectly awakened one" (A. Ni. 1. 171-174).

If two, four, eight, or sixteen were to arise at once, they would not be wonderful.

For in one *vihāra*, the gain and honor, even of two *cetiya*s, is not abundant. Monks, too, would not be wonderful in abundance. Thus, even Buddhas would come to be.

Therefore, they do not arise.

And because there is no difference in the teaching.

For the *dharma* that one teaches with the distinctions of the *smṛtyupasthāna*s (foundations of mindfulness) etc., even if another were to arise, he himself would be the one to be taught.

Therefore, he would not be wonderful. But when one teaches the *dharma*, the teaching itself is wonderful.

And because of the absence of disputes.

And if many Buddhas were arising, the pupils of many teachers would dispute, saying, "Our Buddha is pleasing, our Buddha has a sweet voice, is a gainer, is meritorious." Therefore, they do not arise in this way.

Moreover, this reason has been extensively explained by the Elder Nāgasena when questioned by King Milinda.

For it was said (Mi. Pa. 5.1.1):

"There, Venerable Nāgasena, this was spoken by the Blessed One: 'This is impossible, monks, it cannot happen that two *arhat*s, perfectly awakened Buddhas, should arise as unprecedented and last in one world-system.'

And when they are teaching, Venerable Nāgasena, all *tathāgata*s teach the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment; and when they are talking, they talk the Four Noble Truths; and when they are training, they train in the three trainings; and when they are instructing, they instruct in the practice of diligence.

If, Venerable Nāgasena, the teaching is one, the talk is one, the training is one, and the instruction is one of all *tathāgata*s, for what reason do two *tathāgata*s not arise at one moment? Even by the arising of one Buddha, this world is made radiant.

If there were a second Buddha, this world would be made even more radiant by the light of both. And when exhorting, two *tathāgata*s could exhort easily, and when instructing, they could instruct easily. Tell me the reason for this, so that I may be without doubt."

This ten-thousandfold world-system, great king, is a single Buddha-sustaining element; it sustains the quality of only one *tathāgata*. If a second Buddha were to arise, this ten-thousandfold world-system could not sustain it; it would shake, tremble, bend, incline, turn away, scatter, dissolve, be destroyed, and would not reach a [stable] state.

Just as, great king, a boat might be a single-person-sustaining one. When one person has boarded, that boat is fit [for only that one].
Then, suppose a second man were to come along, similar to the first in age, appearance, stage of life, size, and lean and strong in all his limbs, and he were to embark in the boat.

“Sire, could that boat sustain both of them?”

“No, venerable sir, it would shake and tremble, it would bend this way and that, it would disperse, scatter into pieces, dissolve, be utterly destroyed. It could not reach a standing place; it would sink in the water.”

“Besides that, sire, this ten-thousandfold world-system ( *dasasahassī lokadhātu*) is the sustainer of one Buddha; it sustains the special qualities (*guṇa*) of one *Tathāgata* only. If a second *Buddha* were to arise, this ten-thousandfold world-system ( *dasasahassī lokadhātu*) could not bear him, it would shake…pe… it could not reach a standing place.”

Suppose, great king, that a man were to eat food according to his need, filling himself right up to the throat; if he were then nourished, replete, fully satisfied, with no break, refreshed, upright, and with strength unimpaired, were he to eat just that much food again, could that man be comfortable?”

“No, venerable sir, he would die after eating only once.”

“Just so, great king, this ten-thousandfold world-system ( *dasasahassī lokadhātu*) is the sustainer of one *Buddha*, the holder of one Buddha…pe… it could not reach a standing place.”

“Venerable Nāgasena, is it because of an overload of *dharma* that the earth trembles? Here, great king, suppose there were two carts filled to the brim with jewels ( *ratana*).

If, taking the jewels ( *ratana*) from one cart, they were to pile them into the one cart, could that cart sustain the jewels ( *ratana*) of both carts?”

“No, venerable sir, its axle would break, its spokes would be shattered, its felly would collapse, and the yoke pin would break.”

“Is it then, great king, because of an overload of jewels ( *ratana*) that the cart breaks?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”

“Just so, great king, it is because of an overload of *dharma* that the earth trembles.”

“Furthermore, great king, this reason has been set forth for the purpose of illuminating the power of a *Buddha*. Now listen to another fitting reason why two Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā*) do not arise at the same time.

If, great king, two Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā*) were to arise at the same moment, a dispute would arise in their assemblies—‘This is your *Buddha*, this is our Buddha’—and they would become divided into two factions.

Just as, great king, a dispute might arise in the assemblies of two powerful ministers, ‘This is your minister, this is our minister,’ and they would become divided into two factions, so too, great king, if two Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā*) were to arise at the same moment, a dispute would arise in their assemblies—‘This is your *Buddha*, this is our Buddha’—and they would become divided into two factions.

This, great king, is one reason why two Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā*) do not arise at the same moment.

Again, great king, listen to a further reason why two Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā*) do not arise at the same moment.

If, great king, two Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā*) were to arise at the same moment, the statement ‘The *Buddha* is foremost’ would be false.

The statement ‘The *Buddha* is the eldest’ would be false.

The statement ‘The *Buddha* is the best ( *seṭṭho*), the most distinguished ( *visiṭṭho*), the highest ( *uttamo*), the most excellent ( *pavaro*), the unequalled ( *asamo*), the one unequalled in the world ( *asamasamo*), the one without compare ( *appaṭisamo*), the one without peer ( *appaṭibhāgo*), the one without rival ( *appaṭipuggalo*)’ would be false.

Do you then, great king, rightly grasp the meaning of this reason why two Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā*) do not arise at the same moment?

Furthermore, great king, this is the intrinsic nature ( *sabhāvapakati*) of the Buddhas, the Fortunate Ones ( *bhagavantānaṃ*), that one *Buddha* only arises in the world.

What is the reason for this? Because of the greatness of the qualities (*guṇa*) of an all-knowing *Buddha* ( *sabbaññubuddhaguṇānaṃ*).

Of other things also, great king, whatever is mighty in the world is singular.

The earth, great king, is mighty, and it is only one.

The ocean is mighty, and it is only one.

Sineru, the king of mountains, is mighty, and it is only one.

Space is mighty, and it is only one.

Sakka is mighty, and he is only one.

Māra is mighty, and he is only one.

Brahmā is mighty, and he is only one.

The *Tathāgata*, the *Arhat*, the Fully Awakened One ( *sammāsambuddho*), is mighty, and he is alone in the world.

Wherever they arise, there also to another"...there is no occasion. Therefore, great king, only one *Tathāgata*, worthy one, perfectly enlightened *Buddha* arises in the world."

"Well spoken, venerable Nāgasena, is this question with similes and reasons."

*ekissā lokadhātuyā*: in one world-element, in one *cakkavāḷa*.

Below, by this same word, ten thousand *cakkavāḷas* are included. These too, it is fitting to limit to one *cakkavāḷa*.

For *Buddhas*, when arising, arise in this very *cakkavāḷa*; but at the place of arising, it is prohibited that they do not arise in other *cakkavāḷas*.

*apubbaṃ acarima*: here, before the appearance of the wheel-jewel (*cakkaratana*), it is *pubbaṃ*; after its disappearance, it is *carimaṃ*.

Therein, there are two kinds of disappearance of the wheel-jewel: from the death of a wheel-turning monarch (*cakkavattin*) or from his renunciation.

And that which is disappearing vanishes on the seventh day from death or renunciation; after that, the appearance of a wheel-turning monarch is not prevented.

Why do two wheel-turning monarchs not arise in one *cakkavāḷa*?

Because of the cessation of dispute, because of being wonderful, and because of the great power of the wheel-jewel.

For if two were to arise, a dispute would arise: "Our king is great, our king is great."

And the fact that there is a wheel-turning monarch in one continent would not be wonderful.

And that great power of the wheel-jewel, which is capable of not giving dominion in the two thousand surrounding islands and in the four great continents, would diminish.

Thus, because of the cessation of dispute, because of being wonderful, and because of the great power of the wheel-jewel, two do not arise in one *cakkavāḷa*.

mula_pali: 130. ‘‘‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī arahaṃ assa sammāsambuddho , netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso arahaṃ assa sammāsambuddho, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti. ‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī rājā assa cakkavattī, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso rājā assa cakkavattī, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti. ‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī sakkattaṃ kareyya … mārattaṃ kareyya… brahmattaṃ kareyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ puriso sakkattaṃ kareyya… mārattaṃ kareyya… brahmattaṃ kareyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti.
mula_english:
“He understands: ‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a woman could be an *arhat* (arahaṃ), a *sammāsambuddha* (sammāsambuddho)—there is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that a man might be an *arhat*, a *sammāsambuddha*—there is such a possibility.’

‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a woman could be a *cakravartin* (cakkavattī), a Wheel-turning Monarch—there is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that a man might be a *cakravartin*, a Wheel-turning Monarch—there is such a possibility.’

‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a woman could occupy the position of Śakra (sakkattaṃ)… that a woman could occupy the position of Māra (mārattaṃ)… that a woman could occupy the position of Brahmā (brahmmattaṃ)—there is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that a man might occupy the position of Śakra… that a man might occupy the position of Māra… that a man might occupy the position of Brahmā—there is such a possibility.’
commentary_pali:
130.Yaṃ itthī assa arahaṃ sammāsambuddhoti ettha tiṭṭhatu tāva sabbaññuguṇe nibbattetvā lokuttāraṇasamattho buddhabhāvo, paṇidhānamattampi itthiyā na sampajjati.

Manussattaṃ liṅgasampatti, hetu satthāradassanaṃ;

Pabbajjā guṇasampatti, adhikāro ca chandatā;

Aṭṭhadhammasamodhānā, abhinīhāro samijjhatīti. (bu. vaṃ. 2.59) –

Imāni hi paṇidhānasampattikāraṇāni. Iti paṇidhānampi sampādetuṃ asamatthāya itthiyā kuto buddhabhāvoti ‘‘aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī assa arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’’ti vuttaṃ. Sabbākāraparipūro ca puññussayo sabbākāraparipūrameva attabhāvaṃ nibbattetīti purisova arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho.

Yaṃ itthī rājā assa cakkavattītiādīsupi yasmā itthiyā kosohitavatthaguyhatādīnaṃ abhāvena lakkhaṇāni na paripūrenti, itthiratanābhāvena sattaratanasamaṅgitā na sampajjati, sabbamanussehi ca adhiko attabhāvo na hoti, tasmā ‘‘aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī rājā assa cakkavattī’’ti vuttaṃ. Yasmā ca sakkattādīni tīṇi ṭhānāni uttamāni, itthiliṅgañca hīnaṃ, tasmā tassā sakkattādīnipi paṭisiddhāni.

Yaṃ itthī rājā assa cakkavattī

Nanu ca yathā itthiliṅgaṃ, evaṃ purisaliṅgampi brahmaloke natthi? Tasmā ‘‘yaṃ puriso brahmattaṃ kareyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’’tipi na vattabbaṃ siyāti. No na vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? Idha purisassa tattha nibbattanato. Brahmattanti hi mahābrahmattaṃ adhippetaṃ. Itthī ca idha jhānaṃ bhāvetvā kālaṃ katvā brahmapārisajjānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati, na mahābrahmānaṃ, puriso pana tattha na uppajjatīti na vattabbo. Samānepi cettha ubhayaliṅgābhāve purisasaṇṭhānāva brahmāno, na itthisaṇṭhānā, tasmā suvuttamevetaṃ.
commentary_english:
130.
Concerning the statement, "If a woman were to be an *arhat*, a perfectly awakened Buddha," let the buddha-nature competent to liberate the world, having produced all-knowing qualities, remain for now; even the mere vow is not accomplished by a woman.

Human existence, possession of gender, the cause of seeing a teacher;
Renunciation, possession of qualities, authority, and desire;
With the combination of these eight qualities, the aspiration is fulfilled.
(bu.
vaṃ.
2.
59) –

These are the causes for the accomplishment of the vow.
Thus, since a woman is incapable of even accomplishing the vow, how could she [achieve] buddha-nature? Therefore, it is said, "It is impossible; there is no opportunity for a woman to be an *arhat*, a perfectly awakened Buddha."
And because a collection of merit that is fully complete in all aspects produces a fully complete self-nature, only a man can be an *arhat*, a perfectly awakened Buddha.

Concerning the statements beginning with, "If a woman were to be a king, a *cakravartin*," because the characteristics are not fully complete due to the absence of the hidden nature of the *kośa*, the covered object, and the secret parts, and because the complete assembly of seven jewels does not occur due to the absence of a woman-jewel, and because a superior self-nature does not exist among all humans, therefore, it is said, "It is impossible; there is no opportunity for a woman to be a king, a *cakravartin*."
And because the three positions beginning with Lordship are supreme, and the female gender is inferior, therefore those Lordship and so forth are also prohibited for her.

If a woman were to be a king, a *cakravartin*

Now, isn't it the case that just as there is no female gender, so too there is no male gender in the Brahmā realm? Therefore, it should not be said, "If a man were to make the Brahmā state, this position exists."
No, it should not be said.
Why? Because of the arising of a male in that [realm].
"Brahmā-state" here is understood to mean Great Brahmā-state.
And a woman, having cultivated *dhyāna* here, and having made time [i.e., died], attains companionship among the retinue of Brahmā, not Great Brahmā. But a man does not arise there.
Even if there is similarity here in the absence of both genders, the Brahmās are only of male form, not female form; therefore, this is well said.

mula_pali:
131. ‘‘‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyaduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyaduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti. ‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīduccaritassa…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ vacīduccaritassa…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatīti pajānāti. ‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyasucaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyasucaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti. ‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīsucaritassa…pe… yaṃ manosucaritassa aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ vacīsucaritassa…pe… yaṃ manosucaritassa iṭṭho kanto manāpo vipāko nibbatteyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti.

‘‘‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī taṃnidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī taṃnidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti. ‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīduccaritasamaṅgī…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritasamaṅgī taṃnidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ vacīduccaritasamaṅgī…pe… yaṃ manoduccaritasamaṅgī taṃnidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti. ‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyasucaritasamaṅgī taṃnidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ kāyasucaritasamaṅgī taṃnidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti. ‘Aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ vacīsucaritasamaṅgī…pe… yaṃ manosucaritasamaṅgī taṃnidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti; ‘ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ vacīsucaritasamaṅgī…pe… yaṃ manosucaritasamaṅgī taṃnidānā tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī’ti pajānāti. Ettāvatā kho, ānanda, ‘ṭhānāṭhānakusalo bhikkhū’ti alaṃ vacanāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
131. “He understands: ‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that an unwished for, undesired, disagreeable result could be produced from bad bodily conduct. There is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that an unwished for, undesired, disagreeable result might be produced from bad bodily conduct. There is such a possibility.’

‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that an unwished for, undesired, disagreeable result could be produced from bad verbal conduct…from bad mental conduct. There is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that an unwished for, undesired, disagreeable result might be produced from bad verbal conduct…from bad mental conduct. There is such a possibility.’

“He understands: ‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a wished for, desired, agreeable result could be produced from good bodily conduct. There is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that a wished for, desired, agreeable result might be produced from good bodily conduct. There is such a possibility.’

‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a wished for, desired, agreeable result could be produced from good verbal conduct…from good mental conduct. There is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that a wished for, desired, agreeable result might be produced from good verbal conduct…from good mental conduct. There is such a possibility.’

“He understands: ‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a person engaging in bad bodily conduct, for that reason, on the dissolution of the body, after death, could reappear in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world. There is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that a person engaging in bad bodily conduct, for that reason, on the dissolution of the body, after death, could reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell. There is such a possibility.’

‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a person engaging in bad verbal conduct…engaging in bad mental conduct might on that account, for that reason, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world. There is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that a person engaging in bad verbal conduct…engaging in bad mental conduct might on that account, for that reason, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell. There is such a possibility.’

‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a person engaging in good bodily conduct, for that reason, on the dissolution of the body, after death, could reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell. There is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘It is possible that a person engaging in good bodily conduct, for that reason, on the dissolution of the body, after death, could reappear in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world. There is such a possibility.’

‘It is impossible, it cannot happen that a person engaging in good verbal conduct… engaging in good mental conduct might on that account, for that reason, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell. There is no such possibility.’ And he understands: ‘engaging in good verbal conduct… engaging in good mental conduct might on that account, for that reason, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappear in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world.’

In this way, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* can be called skilled in what is possible and what is impossible.”
commentary_pali:
131.Kāyaduccaritassātiādīsu yathā nimbabījakosātakībījādīni madhuraphalaṃ na nibbattenti, asātaṃ amadhurameva nibbattenti, evaṃ kāyaduccaritādīni madhuravipākaṃ na nibbattenti, amadhurameva vipākaṃ nibbattenti. Yathā ca ucchubījasālibījādīni madhuraṃ sādurasameva phalaṃ nibbattenti, na asātaṃ kaṭukaṃ, evaṃ kāyasucaritādīni madhurameva vipākaṃ nibbattenti, na amadhuraṃ. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘‘Yādisaṃ vapate bījaṃ, tādisaṃ harate phalaṃ;

Kalyāṇakārī kalyāṇaṃ, pāpakārī ca pāpaka’’nti. (saṃ. ni. 1.256);

Tasmā ‘‘aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyaduccaritassā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

Kāyaduccaritasamaṅgītiādīsu samaṅgīti pañcavidhā samaṅgitā āyūhanasamaṅgitā cetanāsamaṅgitā kammasamaṅgitā vipākasamaṅgitā, upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitāti. Tattha kusalākusalakammāyūhanakkhaṇe āyūhanasamaṅgitāti vuccati. Tathā cetanāsamaṅgitā. Yāva pana arahattaṃ na pāpuṇanti, tāva sabbepi sattā pubbe upacitaṃ vipākārahaṃ kammaṃ sandhāya ‘‘kammasamaṅgino’’ti vuccanti, esā kammasamaṅgitā. Vipākasamaṅgitā vipākakkhaṇeyeva veditabbā. Yāva pana sattā arahattaṃ na pāpuṇanti, tāva nesaṃ tato tato cavitvā niraye tāva uppajjamānānaṃ aggijālalohakumbhiādīhi upaṭṭhānākārehi nirayo, gabbhaseyyakattaṃ āpajjamānānaṃ mātukucchi, devesu uppajjamānānaṃ kapparukkhavimānādīhi upaṭṭhānākārehi devalokoti evaṃ uppattinimittaṃ upaṭṭhāti, iti nesaṃ iminā uppattinimittaupaṭṭhānena aparimuttatā upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā nāma. Sā calati sesā niccalā. Niraye hi upaṭṭhitepi devaloko upaṭṭhāti, devaloke upaṭṭhitepi nirayo upaṭṭhāti, manussaloke upaṭṭhitepi tiracchānayoni upaṭṭhāti, tiracchānayoniyā ca upaṭṭhitāyapi manussaloko upaṭṭhātiyeva.

Kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī samaṅgī āyūhanasamaṅgitā cetanāsamaṅgitā kammasamaṅgitā. Vipākasamaṅgitā upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā

Tatridaṃ vatthu – soṇagiripāde kira acelavihāre soṇatthero nāma eko dhammakathiko, tassa pitā sunakhajīviko ahosi. Thero taṃ paṭibāhantopi saṃvare ṭhapetuṃ asakkonto ‘‘mā nassi jarako’’ti mahallakakāle akāmakaṃ pabbājesi. Tassa gilānaseyyāya nipannassa nirayo upaṭṭhāti, soṇagiripādato mahantā mahantā sunakhā āgantvā khāditukāmā viya samparivāresuṃ. So mahābhayabhīto – ‘‘vārehi, tāta soṇa, vārehi, tāta soṇā’’ti āha. Kiṃ mahātherāti. Na passasi tātāti taṃ pavattiṃ ācikkhi. Soṇatthero – ‘‘kathañhi nāma mādisassa pitā niraye nibbattissati, patiṭṭhā’ssa bhavissāmī’’ti sāmaṇerehi nānāpupphāni āharāpetvā cetiyaṅgaṇabodhiyaṅgaṇesu talasantharaṇapūjaṃ āsanapūjañca kāretvā pitaraṃ mañcena cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ āharitvā mañce nisīdāpetvā – ‘‘ayaṃ mahāthera-pūjā tumhākaṃ atthāya katā ‘ayaṃ me bhagavā duggatapaṇṇākāro’ti vatvā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā cittaṃ pasādehī’’ti āha. So mahāthero pūjaṃ disvā tathā karonto cittaṃ pasādesi, tāvadevassa devaloko upaṭṭhāsi, nandanavana-cittalatāvana-missakavana-phārusakavanavimānāni ceva nāṭakāni ca parivāretvā ṭhitāni viya ahesuṃ. So ‘‘apetha apetha soṇā’’ti āha. Kimidaṃ therāti? Etā te, tāta, mātaro āgacchantīti . Thero ‘‘saggo upaṭṭhito mahātherassā’’ti cintesi. Evaṃ upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā calatīti veditabbā. Etāsu samaṅgitāsu idha āyūhanacetanākammasamaṅgitāvasena kāyaduccaritasamaṅgītiādi vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
131.
In the *kāyaduccaritassā* and so on: Just as nimb seeds, kosātakī seeds and so forth do not produce sweet fruit, but produce only unsavory, non-sweet [fruit], so also bodily misconduct, and so forth, do not produce a sweet result, but produce only a non-sweet result.

Just as sugarcane seeds, rice seeds, and so forth, produce sweet, flavorful fruit, not unsavory, bitter [fruit], so also bodily good conduct and so forth produce only a sweet result, not a non-sweet one.

Thus it was said:

“Whatever seed one sows,
That kind of fruit one reaps;
The one who does good [reaps] good,
And the one who does evil, evil.”

(Saṃ.
Ni.
1.
256);

Therefore, “This is not a possibility, there is no opportunity for bodily misconduct,” and so forth was said.

In the *kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī* and so on: *samaṅgī* means five kinds of completeness: completeness of effort (āyūhana), completeness of intention (cetanā), completeness of karma, completeness of result (vipāka), and completeness of presentation (upaṭṭhāna).

There, at the moment of effort regarding wholesome and unwholesome karma, it is called *āyūhanasamaṅgitā*, completeness of effort.

Likewise, *cetanāsamaṅgitā*, completeness of intention.

As long as beings do not attain *arhatship*, all beings are called “complete in karma” in relation to the karma previously accumulated that is fit for ripening. This is *kammasamaṅgitā*, completeness of karma.

*vipākasamaṅgitā*, completeness of result, should be understood as [occurring] only at the moment of result.

As long as beings do not attain *arhatship*, then for those who pass away from here and there and are being born in hell, hell arises through the presentation of fire flames, iron pots, and so forth. For those who are attaining the state of lying in the womb, [there arises] the mother's womb. For those who are being born among the gods, the heaven world arises through the presentation of wish-fulfilling trees, celestial mansions, and so forth. Thus, the sign of rebirth arises. Thus, their non-liberation through this sign of rebirth is called *upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā*, completeness of presentation.

That moves, the rest are unmoving.

When hell arises, the heaven world also arises. When the heaven world arises, hell also arises. When the human world arises, the animal realm also arises, and when the animal realm arises, the human world also arises.

*kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī* *samaṅgī* *āyūhanasamaṅgitā* *cetanāsamaṅgitā* *kammasamaṅgitā*.
*vipākasamaṅgitā* *upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā*

Here is this story: At Soṇagiri's foot, it is said that in the Acela monastery, there was a Dharma-speaker named Soṇatthera, his father was a dog-butcher.

The elder, while preventing him and being unable to establish him in restraint, ordained him against his will in old age, [saying], "Do not perish, old man!"

For him, lying on his sickbed, hell arose. Huge, huge dogs came from Soṇagiri's foot and surrounded him as if wanting to devour him.

He, greatly frightened, said, "Ward them off, father Soṇa! Ward them off, father Soṇa!"

What is it, great elder?

You do not see, father?

He described that situation.

Soṇatthero [thought]: “How could my father be born in hell? I will be a support for him.” Having novices bring various flowers, and having a ground-covering offering and a seat offering made in the stūpa precinct and the Bodhi tree precinct, and having his father brought on a palanquin to the stūpa precinct, and having him seated on the palanquin, [he said]: “This great elder offering has been done for your benefit, [thinking], ‘This is my Blessed One, the maker of the refuge of the wretched,’ and having venerated the Blessed One, gladden your mind.”

That great elder, seeing the offering and doing likewise, gladdened his mind. Immediately, the heaven world arose for him. The Nandana forest, the Cittalatā forest, the Mixed forest, the Phārusaka forest, celestial mansions, and dramas surrounded him and stood ready.

He said: "Go away, go away, Soṇa!"

What is this, elder? These, father, are your mothers coming.

The elder thought, "Heaven has arisen for the great elder!"

Thus, it should be understood that completeness of presentation moves.

Among these completenesses, here, by way of completeness of effort, intention, and karma, the *kāyaduccaritasamaṅgī* and so on was said.

132. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Konāmo ayaṃ, bhante, dhammapariyāyo’’ti? ‘‘Tasmātiha tvaṃ, ānanda, imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ ‘bahudhātuko’tipi naṃ dhārehi, ‘catuparivaṭṭo’tipi naṃ dhārehi, ‘dhammādāso’tipi naṃ dhārehi, ‘amatadundubhī’tipi dudrabhītipi (ka.) naṃ dhārehi, ‘anuttaro saṅgāmavijayo’tipi naṃ dhārehī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Bahudhātukasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
Thus spoken, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, venerable sir, it is marvelous, venerable sir! What, venerable sir, is the name of this discourse on the Dharma (dhammapariyāya)?"

"Therefore then, Ānanda, you should remember this discourse on the Dharma as 'The Many Elements' (bahudhātuko); you should remember it as 'The Fourfold Round' (catuparivaṭṭo); you should remember it as 'The Mirror of the Dharma' (dhammādāso); you should remember it as 'The Drum of the Deathless' (amatadundubhī); you should remember it as 'The Unexcelled Victory in Battle' (anuttaro saṅgāmavijayo)."

This is what the Blessed One said. The venerable Ānanda, being pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One's words (bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti).

The Many Elements Discourse (bahudhātukasuttaṃ) is finished, the fifth.
commentary_pali:
132.Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānandoti ‘‘evaṃ bhagavatā imasmiṃ sutte vutte thero ādito paṭṭhāya sabbasuttaṃ samannāharitvā evaṃ sassirikaṃ katvā desitasuttassa nāma bhagavatā nāmaṃ na gahitaṃ. Handassa nāmaṃ gaṇhāpessāmī’’ti cintetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca.

Tasmā tiha tvantiādīsu ayaṃ atthayojanā –

Tasmā tiha tva

Ānanda, yasmā imasmiṃ dhammapariyāye ‘‘aṭṭhārasa kho imā, ānanda, dhātuyo, cha imā, ānanda, dhātuyo’’ti evaṃ bahudhātuyo vibhattā, tasmā tiha tvaṃ imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ bahudhātukotipi naṃ dhārehi. Yasmā panettha dhātuāyatanapaṭiccasamuppādaṭṭhānāṭṭhānavasena cattāro parivaṭṭā kathitā , tasmā catuparivaṭṭotipi naṃ dhārehi. Yasmā ca ādāsaṃ olokentassa mukhanimittaṃ viya imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ olokentassa ete dhātuādayo atthā pākaṭā honti, tasmā dhammādāsotipi naṃ dhārehi. Yasmā ca yathā nāma parasenamaddanā yodhā saṅgāmatūriyaṃ paggahetvā parasenaṃ pavisitvā sapatte madditvā attano jayaṃ gaṇhanti, evameva kilesasenamaddanā yogino idha vuttavasena vipassanaṃ paggahetvā kilese madditvā attano arahattajayaṃ gaṇhanti, tasmā amatadundubhītipi naṃ dhārehi. Yasmā ca yathā saṅgāmayodhā pañcāvudhaṃ gahetvā parasenaṃ viddhaṃsetvā jayaṃ gaṇhanti, evaṃ yoginopi idha vuttaṃ vipassanāvudhaṃ gahetvā kilesasenaṃ viddhaṃsetvā arahattajayaṃ gaṇhanti. Tasmā anuttaro saṅgāmavijayotipi naṃ dhārehīti.

bahudhātuko catuparivaṭṭo dhammādāso amatadundubhī anuttaro saṅgāmavijayo

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Bahudhātukasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
132. . evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando: "When this was said, the venerable Ānanda" means, "When this was said by the Blessed One in this *sutta*, the Elder, having from the beginning gathered together the entire *sutta*, and having made it so auspicious, the Blessed One did not take the name of the *desitasutta*. Thinking, "I will have [him] take the name of the text," he said this to the Blessed One.

tasmā tiha tvantiādīsu ayaṃ atthayojanā –

tasmā tiha tva

Ānanda, because in this *dhammapariyāya* "There are these eighteen *dhātus*, Ānanda; there are these six *dhātus*," thus the many *dhātus* are distinguished, therefore, Ānanda, you should remember this *dhammapariyāya* as bahudhātuko. And because here four *parivaṭṭas* have been spoken of by way of *dhātu*, *āyatana*, *paṭiccasamuppāda*, *ṭhāna*, and *aṭṭhāna*, therefore you should remember it as catuparivaṭṭo. And because, just as when looking in a mirror, the facial image is clear, so when looking at this *dhammapariyāya*, these *dhātu*, etc., meanings are clear, therefore you should remember it as dhammādāso. And because, just as warriors who destroy the army of the enemy, having taken up the musical instruments of battle, enter the army of the enemy, crush the foes, and gain their own victory, just so, those *yogins* who destroy the army of defilements, having taken up insight (*vipassanā*) in the way that has been said here, crush the defilements and gain their own victory of *arahatta*, therefore you should remember it as amatadundubhī. And because, just as warriors in battle, having taken up the five weapons, destroy the army of the enemy and gain victory, so also, the *yogins*, having taken up the weapon of insight (*vipassanā*) that has been spoken of here, destroy the army of defilements and gain the victory of *arahatta*. Therefore, you should remember it as anuttaro saṅgāmavijayo."

bahudhātuko catuparivaṭṭo dhammādāso amatadundubhī anuttaro saṅgāmavijayo

‘‘Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṃ vebhāraṃ pabbata’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Etassapi kho, bhikkhave, vebhārassa pabbatassa aññāva samaññā ahosi aññā paññatti’’.

‘‘Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṃ vepullaṃ pabbata’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Etassapi kho, bhikkhave, vepullassa pabbatassa aññāva samaññā ahosi aññā paññatti’’.

‘‘Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṃ gijjhakūṭaṃ pabbata’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Etassapi kho, bhikkhave, gijjhakūṭassa pabbatassa aññāva samaññā ahosi aññā paññatti’’.

‘‘Passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, imaṃ isigiliṃ pabbata’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Imassa kho pana, bhikkhave, isigilissa pabbatassa esāva samaññā ahosi esā paññatti’’.

Tamenaṃ manussā disvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ayaṃ pabbato ime isī isayo (ka.) gilatī’ti; ‘isigili isigili’ tveva samaññā udapādi. Ācikkhissāmi acikkhissāmi vo (ka.), bhikkhave, paccekabuddhānaṃ nāmāni; kittayissāmi, bhikkhave, paccekabuddhānaṃ nāmāni; desessāmi, bhikkhave , paccekabuddhānaṃ nāmāni . Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

mula_english:
133. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha, at Isigili mountain. There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks.” “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Fortunate One. The Fortunate One said this:

“Do you see that mountain, Vebhāra, monks?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “There used to be another name, another designation, for that mountain Vebhāra, monks.”

“Do you see that mountain, Paṇḍava, monks?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “There used to be another name, another designation, for that mountain Paṇḍava, monks.”

“Do you see that mountain, Vepulla, monks?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “There used to be another name, another designation, for that mountain Vepulla, monks.”

“Do you see that mountain, Gijjhakūṭa, monks?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “There used to be another name, another designation, for that mountain Gijjhakūṭa, monks.”

“Do you see this mountain, Isigili, monks?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “There used to be this same name, this same designation, for this mountain Isigili, monks.”

“In the past, monks, five hundred *pratyekabuddhas* lived for a long time on this mountain, Isigili. They were seen entering into this mountain, but after entering were not seen again. When people saw this, they said, ‘This mountain swallows these seers.’ Thus the designation ‘Isigili, Isigili’ arose. I will declare to you the names of the *pratyekabuddhas*; I will recount the names of the *pratyekabuddhas*; I will teach the names of the *pratyekabuddhas*. Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.” “As you say, lord,” the monks responded to the Fortunate One. The Fortunate One said this:
commentary_pali:
133.Evaṃme sutanti isigilisuttaṃ. Tattha aññāva samaññā ahosīti isigilissa isigilīti samaññāya uppannakāle vebhāro na vebhāroti paññāyittha, aññāyevassa samaññā ahosi. Aññā paññattīti idaṃ purimapadasseva vevacanaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

Tadā kira bhagavā sāyanhasamaye samāpattito vuṭṭhāya gandhakuṭito nikkhamitvā yasmiṃ ṭhāne nisinnānaṃ pañca pabbatā paññāyanti, tattha bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisīditvā ime pañca pabbate paṭipāṭiyā ācikkhi. Tattha na bhagavato pabbatehi attho atthi, iti imesu pana pabbatesu paṭipāṭiyā kathiyamānesu isigilissa isigilibhāvo kathetabbo hoti. Tasmiṃ kathiyamāne padumavatiyā puttānaṃ pañcasatānaṃ paccekabuddhānaṃ nāmāni ceva padumavatiyā ca patthanā kathetabbā bhavissatīti bhagavā imaṃ pañca pabbatapaṭipāṭiṃ ācikkhi.

Pavisantādissanti paviṭṭhā na dissantīti yathāphāsukaṭṭhāne piṇḍāya caritvā katabhattakiccā āgantvā cetiyagabbhe yamakamahādvāraṃ vivarantā viya taṃ pabbataṃ dvedhā katvā anto pavisitvā rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānāni māpetvā tattha vasiṃsu, tasmā evamāha. Ime isīti ime paccekabuddhaisī.

Pavisantā dissanti paviṭṭhā na dissantī Ime isī

Kadā pana te tattha vasiṃsu? Atīte kira anuppanne tathāgate bārāṇasiṃ upanissāya ekasmiṃ gāmake ekā kuladhītā khettaṃ rakkhamānā ekassa paccekabuddhassa pañcahi lājāsatehi saddhiṃ ekaṃ padumapupphaṃ datvā pañca puttasatāni patthesi. Tasmiṃyeva ca khaṇe pañcasatā migaluddakā madhuramaṃsaṃ datvā ‘‘etissā puttā bhaveyyāmā’’ti patthayiṃsu. Sā yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā devaloke nibbattā, tato cutā jātassare padumagabbhe nibbatti. Tameko tāpaso disvā paṭijaggi, tassā vicarantiyāva pāduddhāre pāduddhāre bhūmito padumāni uṭṭhahanti. Eko vanacarako disvā bārāṇasirañño ārocesi. Rājā naṃ āharāpetvā aggamahesiṃ akāsi, tassā gabbho saṇṭhāsi. Mahāpadumakumāro mātukucchiyaṃ vasi, sesā gabbhamalaṃ nissā nibbattā. Vayappattā uyyāne padumassare kīḷantā ekekasmiṃ padume nisīditvā khayavayaṃ paṭṭhapetvā paccekabodhiñāṇaṃ nibbattayiṃsu. Ayaṃ tesaṃ byākaraṇagāthā ahosi –

‘‘Saroruhaṃ padumapalāsapattajaṃ, supupphitaṃ bhamaragaṇānuciṇṇaṃ;

Aniccatāyupagataṃ viditvā, eko care khaggavisāṇakappo’’ti.

Tasmiṃ kāle te tattha vasiṃsu, tadā cassa pabbatassa isigilīti samaññā udapādi.
commentary_english:
133. It was thus that I heard. This is the *Iṣigilisutta*.

Herein, "there was a different designation" means that when the designation *Iṣigili* arose for *Iṣigili*, it was known [to be] *vebhāra*, not *vebhāra*; there was a different designation for it.

"*A different explanation*" means this is a synonym of the first word.

The same rule applies to the rest.

At that time, the Blessed One, in the late afternoon, arose from meditation, went out from the Perfume Chamber, and sat down surrounded by the community of monks in a place where five mountains were visible, and systematically described these five mountains.

Herein, the Blessed One does not need the mountains, but when these mountains are systematically spoken of, the *Iṣigilibhāva* of *Iṣigili* must be spoken of.

While that was being spoken of, the names of the five hundred sons of Padumavatī, and the aspirations of Padumavatī, must be spoken of. Therefore, the Blessed One systematically described these five mountains.

"Entering, they are seen; having entered, they are not seen" means, having wandered for alms in a comfortable place, and having done their meal duties, they come and, as if opening the twin great doors in a *cetiyagabbha*, split that mountain in two and, having entered within, built places for staying at night and places for staying during the day, and lived there. Therefore he said this:

"These are sages" means these are individual Buddha sages.

Entering, they are seen; having entered, they are not seen.

These are sages. When did they live there? In the past, when a *Tathāgata* had not arisen, near Vārāṇasī, in a certain village, a certain daughter of a good family, while guarding a field, gave a lotus flower, together with five hundred handfuls of parched grain, to an individual Buddha, and wished for five hundred sons.

At that very moment, five hundred hunters, having given sweet meat, wished, "May we be her sons."

She, having remained as long as her life lasted, was reborn in the world of the gods, and having passed away from there, she was miraculously reborn in a lotus womb.

A certain ascetic, having seen her, tended to her. As she wandered about, lotuses arose from the earth at every step.

A certain forester, having seen [this], announced [it] to the king of Vārāṇasī.

The king had her brought [to him] and made [her] his chief queen, and she conceived.

Mahāpaduma-kumāra lived in his mother's womb; the rest were born dependent on the filth of the womb.

Having reached adulthood, while playing in the pleasure garden at Padumassara, sitting on each lotus, establishing decay and death, they brought forth the knowledge of individual enlightenment (*paccekabodhiñāṇa*).

This was their declaration verse:

"A lotus born from the leaves and petals of a lotus, beautifully flowered, frequented by swarms of bees, having known [it] to be subject to impermanence, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn."

At that time, they lived there; then the designation *Iṣigili* arose for that mountain.

mula_pali:
136. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘ariyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhiṃ desessāmi saupanisaṃ saparikkhāraṃ. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo sammāsamādhi saupaniso saparikkhāro? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati; yā kho, bhikkhave, imehi sattahaṅgehi cittassa ekaggatā parikkhatā – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyo sammāsamādhi saupaniso itipi, saparikkhāro itipi. Tatra, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti? Micchādiṭṭhiṃ ‘micchādiṭṭhī’ti pajānāti, sammādiṭṭhiṃ ‘sammādiṭṭhī’ti pajānāti – sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi.

‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi? ‘Natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi.

‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi? Sammādiṭṭhiṃpahaṃ sammādiṭṭhimahaṃ (ka.) evaṃ sammāsaṅkappaṃpahaṃkyādīsupi, bhikkhave, dvāyaṃ dvayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ṭīkā oloketabbā vadāmi – atthi, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi sāsavā puññabhāgiyā upadhivepakkā; atthi, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi ariyā anāsavā lokuttarā maggaṅgā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi sāsavā puññabhāgiyā upadhivepakkā ? ‘Atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ, atthi hutaṃ, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, atthi ayaṃ loko, atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi sāsavā puññabhāgiyā upadhivepakkā.

sammādiṭṭhimahaṃ (ka.) evaṃ sammāsaṅkappaṃpahaṃkyādīsupi dvayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ṭīkā oloketabbā

‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi ariyā anāsavā lokuttarā maggaṅgā? Yā kho, bhikkhave, ariyacittassa anāsavacittassa ariyamaggasamaṅgino ariyamaggaṃ bhāvayato paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo sammādiṭṭhi maggaṅgaṃ maggaṅgā (sī. pī.) – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi ariyā anāsavā lokuttarā maggaṅgā. So micchādiṭṭhiyā pahānāya vāyamati, sammādiṭṭhiyā, upasampadāya, svāssa svāyaṃ (ka.) hoti sammāvāyāmo. So sato micchādiṭṭhiṃ pajahati, sato sammādiṭṭhiṃ upasampajja viharati, sāssa sāyaṃ (ka.) hoti sammāsati. Itiyime itime (sī.), itissime (syā. kaṃ. pī.) tayo dhammā sammādiṭṭhiṃ anuparidhāvanti anuparivattanti, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati.

maggaṅgā (sī. pī.) svāyaṃ (ka.) sāyaṃ (ka.) itime (sī.), itissime (syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Bhikkhus!”

“Venerable sir,” those monks replied.

The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you noble right concentration with its supports and its requisites.

Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.”

“As you say, lord,” the monks responded to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“And what, bhikkhus, is noble right concentration with its supports and its requisites? That is, right view (sammādiṭṭhi), right intention (sammāsaṅkappo), right speech (sammāvācā), right action (sammākammanto), right livelihood (sammāājīvo), right effort (sammāvāyāmo), and right mindfulness (sammāsati); that unification of mind equipped with these seven factors, bhikkhus, is called noble right concentration with its supports and its requisites.”

Therein, bhikkhus, right view comes first.

And how, bhikkhus, does right view come first? One understands wrong view as wrong view, and right view as right view: that is one's right view.

“And what, bhikkhus, is wrong view? ‘There is nothing given, nothing offered, nothing sacrificed; there is no fruit or result of good and bad actions; there is no this world, no other world; there is no mother, no father; there are no beings who are reborn spontaneously; there are in the world no recluses or brahmins who are truly advanced & practice rightly, who proclaim this world & the next after having directly known & realized it for themselves.’ This, bhikkhus, is wrong view.

“And what, bhikkhus, is right view? Right view, I say, is twofold: there is right view that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment; and there is right view that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path.

And what, bhikkhus, is right view that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment? ‘There is what is given, what is offered, what is sacrificed. There are fruits & results of good & bad actions. There is this world & the next world. There is mother & father. There are spontaneously reborn beings; there are brahmans & contemplatives who, faring rightly & practicing rightly, proclaim this world & the next after having directly known & realized it for themselves.’ This, bhikkhus, is right view that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment.

“And what, bhikkhus, is right view that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path? The wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, the path factor of right view in one whose mind is noble, whose mind is taintless, who possesses the noble path and is developing the noble path: this is right view that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path.

For the abandoning of wrong view one makes an effort, for the entering upon right view, that is one’s right effort.

Mindfully one abandons wrong view, mindfully one enters upon and abides in right view: that is one’s right mindfulness.
There is right mindfulness.

Thus, these three states run and circle around right view, that is, right view (sammā-diṭṭhi), right effort (sammā-vāyāmo), and right mindfulness (sammā-sati).
commentary_pali:
136.Evaṃme sutanti mahācattārīsakasuttaṃ. Tattha ariyanti niddosaṃ lokuttaraṃ, niddosañhi ‘‘ariya’’nti vuccati. Sammāsamādhinti maggasamādhiṃ. Saupanisanti sapaccayaṃ. Saparikkhāranti saparivāraṃ.

Parikkhatāti parivāritā. Sammādiṭṭhipubbaṅgamā hotīti dvidhā sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti purecārikā vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi ca maggasammādiṭṭhi ca. Vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi tebhūmakasaṅkhāre aniccādivasena parivīmaṃsati; maggasammādiṭṭhi pana parivīmaṃsanapariyosāne bhūmiladdhaṃ vaṭṭaṃ samugghāṭayamānā vūpasamayamānā sītudakaghaṭasahassaṃ matthake āsiñcamānā viya uppajjati. Yathā hi khettaṃ kurumāno kassako paṭhamaṃ araññe rukkhe chindati, pacchā aggiṃ deti, so aggi paṭhamaṃ chinne rukkhe anavasese jhāpeti, evameva vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi paṭhamaṃ aniccādivasena saṅkhāre vīmaṃsati, maggasammādiṭṭhi tāya vīmaṃsanatthaṃ saṅkhāre puna appavattivasena samugghāṭayamānā uppajjati, sā duvidhāpi idha adhippetā.

Parikkhatā Sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hotī

Micchādiṭṭhīti pajānātīti micchādiṭṭhiṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti lakkhaṇapaṭivedhena ārammaṇato pajānāti, sammādiṭṭhiṃ kiccato asammohato pajānāti. Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhīti sā evaṃ pajānanā assa sammādiṭṭhi nāma hoti.

Micchādiṭṭhīti pajānātī Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhī

Dvāyaṃ vadāmīti dvayaṃ vadāmi, duvidhakoṭṭhāsaṃ vadāmīti attho. Puññabhāgiyāti puññakoṭṭhāsabhūtā. Upadhivepakkāti upadhisaṅkhātassa vipākassa dāyikā.

Dvāyaṃ vadāmī Puññabhāgiyā Upadhivepakkā

Paññā paññindriyantiādīsu vibhajitvā vibhajitvā amatadvāraṃ paññapeti dassetīti paññā. Tasmiṃ atthe indattaṃ karotīti paññindriyaṃ. Avijjāya na kampatīti paññābalaṃ. Bojjhaṅgappattā hutvā catusaccadhamme vicinātīti dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo. Maggasampattiyā pasaṭṭhā sobhanā diṭṭhīti sammādiṭṭhi. Ariyamaggassa aṅganti maggaṅgaṃ. Soti so bhikkhu. Pahānāyāti pajahanatthāya. Upasampadāyāti paṭilābhatthāya. Sammāvāyāmoti niyyāniko kusalavāyāmo. Satoti satiyā samannāgato hutvā. Anuparidhāvanti anuparivattantīti sahajātā ca purejātā ca hutvā parivārenti. Ettha hi sammāvāyāmo ca sammāsati ca lokuttarasammādiṭṭhiṃ sahajātā parivārenti rājānaṃ viya ekarathe ṭhitā asiggāhachattaggāhā. Vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi pana purejātā hutvā parivāreti rathassa purato pattikādayo viya. Dutiyapabbato paṭṭhāya pana sammāsaṅkappādīnaṃ tayopi sahajātaparivārāva hontīti veditabbā.

Paññā paññindriya paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo sammādiṭṭhi maggaṅgaṃ. So Pahānāyā Upasampadāyā Sammāvāyāmo Sato Anuparidhāvanti anuparivattantī
commentary_english:
136. "Thus I have heard" is [the title of] the Mahācattārīsaka Sutta.

There, *ariya* means faultless, transcendent; for "ariya" is said to be faultless.

*Sammāsamādhi* means the samādhi of the path.

*Saupanisa* means with conditions (*sapaccayaṃ*).

*Saparikkhāra* means with retinue (*saparivāraṃ*).

*Parikkhatā* means surrounded (*parivāritā*).

*"Sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti"* means right view is foremost in two ways: as the preliminary and as the leader, namely insight right view (*vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi*) and path right view (*maggasammādiṭṭhi*).

Insight right view examines conditioned things of the triple world as impermanent, etc.; path right view, however, at the end of the examination, as the fruition of the [noble] level, eradicates the round [of rebirth], pacifying [suffering], arising like [someone] pouring a thousand pots of cool water on the head.

Just as a farmer preparing a field first cuts down trees in the forest and afterwards sets fire [to them], so the fire first completely burns the cut-down trees, just so insight right view first examines conditioned things as impermanent, etc. Path right view arises eradicating conditioned things for the sake of that examination, as non-occurring again; both of these are intended here.

*Parikkhatā sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti*

*"Micchādiṭṭhīti pajānāti"* means he understands wrong view in terms of its characteristic penetration as impermanent, suffering, not-self in its object; he understands right view as non-delusion in its function.

*"Sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhī"* means that this understanding of his is called right view.

*Micchādiṭṭhīti pajānāti sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhī*

*"Dvāyaṃ vadāmī"* means I speak of two, I speak of a twofold division, is the meaning.

*"Puññabhāgiyā"* means belonging to the division of merit.

*"Upadhivepakkā"* means productive of the result consisting of renewed existence (*upadhi*).

*Dvāyaṃ vadāmī puññabhāgiyā upadhivepakkā*

*"Paññā paññindriya"* and so forth, *paññā* means that having divided and divided, it makes known and shows the door to the Deathless.

*Paññindriyaṃ* means that it performs the function of sovereignty in that connection.

*Paññābalaṃ* means it does not tremble at ignorance.

*Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo* means having attained the enlightenment factor, it investigates the four noble truths.

*Sammādiṭṭhi* means the good view that is excellent through attainment of the path.

*Maggaṅgaṃ* means a factor of the noble path.

*So* means that bhikkhu.

*Pahānāyā* means for the sake of abandoning.

*Upasampadāyā* means for the sake of obtaining.

*Sammāvāyāmo* means effort that is the cause of emergence, wholesome effort.

*Sato* means having come possessed of mindfulness.

*Anuparidhāvanti anuparivattantī* means having arisen together and previously, they surround.

Here, right effort and right mindfulness surround the transcendent right view, having arisen together, like axe-bearers and umbrella-bearers standing in the same chariot as the king.

Insight right view, however, surrounds, having arisen previously, like foot soldiers and so forth in front of the chariot.

From the second section onwards, it should be understood that the three, beginning with right thought, are those that have arisen together as a retinue.

*Paññā paññindriya paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo sammādiṭṭhi maggaṅgaṃ.*
That is, for abandoning and fully attaining, right effort and mindfulness run around and circulate.

mula_pali:
137. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti? Micchāsaṅkappaṃ ‘micchāsaṅkappo’ti pajānāti, sammāsaṅkappaṃ ‘sammāsaṅkappo’ti pajānāti, sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi .

‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo? Kāmasaṅkappo, byāpādasaṅkappo, vihiṃsāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo.

‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo? Sammāsaṅkappaṃpahaṃ, bhikkhave, dvāyaṃ vadāmi – atthi, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko; atthi, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko? Nekkhammasaṅkappo, abyāpādasaṅkappo, avihiṃsāsaṅkappo – ‘ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko’’’.

‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo? Yo kho, bhikkhave, ariyacittassa anāsavacittassa ariyamaggasamaṅgino ariyamaggaṃ bhāvayato takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā cetaso abhiniropanā vacīsaṅkhāro – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo. So micchāsaṅkappassa pahānāya vāyamati, sammāsaṅkappassa upasampadāya, svāssa hoti sammāvāyāmo. So sato micchāsaṅkappaṃ pajahati, sato sammāsaṅkappaṃ upasampajja viharati; sāssa hoti sammāsati. Itiyime tayo dhammā sammāsaṅkappaṃ anuparidhāvanti anuparivattanti, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati.
mula_english:
137. "Therein, *bhikkhus*, right view (*sammāditthi*) comes first.

And how, *bhikkhus*, does right view come first? One understands wrong intention (*micchāsaṅkappa*) as 'wrong intention,' and right intention (*sammāsaṅkappa*) as 'right intention.' This is one's right view.

"And what, *bhikkhus*, is wrong intention? It is the intention of sensual pleasure (*kāmasaṅkappa*), the intention of ill-will (*byāpādasaṅkappa*), and the intention of cruelty (*vihiṃsāsaṅkappa*) - this, *bhikkhus*, is wrong intention.

"And what, *bhikkhus*, is right intention? Right intention, I say, *bhikkhus*, is twofold: there is right intention that is affected by taints (*sāsava*), partaking of merit (*puññabhāgiya*), ripening on the side of attachment (*upadhivepakka*); and there is right intention that is noble (*ariya*), taintless (*anāsava*), supramundane (*lokuttara*), a factor of the path (*maggaṅga*).

"And what, *bhikkhus*, is right intention that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment? It is the intention of renunciation (*nekkhammasaṅkappa*), the intention of non-ill-will (*abyāpādasaṅkappa*), and the intention of non-cruelty (*avihiṃsāsaṅkappa*) - this, *bhikkhus*, is right intention that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment."

"And what, *bhikkhus*, is right intention that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path? The thinking (*takka*), thought (*vitakka*), intention (*saṅkappa*), mental absorption (*appanā*), mental fixity (*byappanā*), directing of mind (*cetaso abhiniropanā*), verbal formation (*vacīsaṅkhāra*) in one whose mind is noble, whose mind is taintless, who possesses the noble path and is developing the noble path: this, *bhikkhus*, is right intention that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path.

One makes an effort (*vāyamati*) to abandon wrong intention and to enter upon right intention: this is one’s right effort (*sammāvāyāma*).

Mindfully (*sato*) one abandons wrong intention, mindfully one enters upon and abides in right intention: this is one’s right mindfulness (*sammāsati*).

Thus these three states run and circle around right intention, that is, right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), right effort (*sammāvāyāma*), and right mindfulness (*sammāsati*).
commentary_pali:
137.Micchāsaṅkappoti pajānātīti micchāsaṅkappaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti lakkhaṇapaṭivedhena ārammaṇato pajānāti sammāsaṅkappaṃ kiccato asammohato pajānāti. Ito aparesu sammāvācādīsupi evameva yojanā veditabbā. Kāmasaṅkappādayo dvedhāvitakkasutte (ma. ni. 1.206) vuttāyeva.

Takkotiādīsu takkanavasena takko. Sveva ca upasaggena padaṃ vaḍḍhetvā vitakkoti vutto, sveva saṅkappanavasena saṅkappo. Ekaggo hutvā ārammaṇe appetīti appanā. Upasaggena pana padaṃ vaḍḍhetvā byappanāti vuttaṃ. Cetaso abhiniropanāti cittassa abhiniropanā. Vitakkasmiñhi sati vitakko ārammaṇe cittaṃ abhiniropeti vitakke pana asati attanoyeva dhammatāya cittaṃ ārammaṇaṃ abhiruhati jātisampanno abhiññātapuriso viya rājagehaṃ. Anabhiññātassa hi paṭihārena vā dovārikena vā attho hoti, abhiññātaṃ jātisampannaṃ sabbe rājarājamahāmattā jānantīti attanova dhammatāya nikkhamati ceva pavisati ca, evaṃsampadamidaṃ veditabbaṃ. Vācaṃ saṅkharotīti vacīsaṅkhāro. Ettha ca lokiyavitakko vācaṃ saṅkharoti, na lokuttaro. Kiñcāpi na saṅkharoti, vacīsaṅkhārotveva ca panassa nāmaṃ hoti. Sammāsaṅkappaṃ anuparidhāvantīti lokuttarasammāsaṅkappaṃ parivārenti.
