Ettha ca tayopi nekkhammasaṅkappādayo pubbabhāge nānācittesu labbhanti, maggakkhaṇe pana tiṇṇampi kāmasaṅkappādīnañca padacchedaṃ samugghātaṃ karonto maggaṅgaṃ pūrayamāno ekova sammāsaṅkappo uppajjitvā nekkhammasaṅkappādivasena tīṇi nāmāni labhati. Parato sammāvācādīsupi eseva nayo.

Takko takko vitakko saṅkappo appanā byappanā Cetaso abhiniropanā vacīsaṅkhāro Sammāsaṅkappaṃ anuparidhāvantī
commentary_english:
137. “He understands ‘wrong intention ( *micchāsaṅkappa*)’": he understands wrong intention as impermanent (*anicca*), suffering (*dukkha*), and not-self (*anatta*) by way of the penetration of characteristics, from the perspective of the object. He understands right intention (*sammāsaṅkappa*) from the perspective of its function, as non-delusion.

The same method should be understood as applying to the other [factors of the path] beginning with right speech (*sammāvācā*).

Volitional thought regarding sense pleasures (*kāmasaṅkappa*) and so forth have already been explained in the Two Kinds of Thinking Discourse (Majjhima Nikāya 1.206).

In "thinking (*takko*)" and so forth, *takko* [is named] due to the nature of thinking. That same [word] is called *vitakko* by increasing the word with a prefix. That same is *saṅkappo* due to the nature of intention. *Appanā*: [the mind] becomes one-pointed and applies [itself] to the object. By increasing the word with a prefix, it is called *byappanā*. *Cetaso abhiniropanā*: the application of the mind. When there is volitional thought (*vitakka*), that volitional thought applies the mind to the object. But when there is no volitional thought, the mind rises to the object by its very nature, like a well-born man known [to the palace guards] going to the royal palace. For a man who is not known, there is need of either a pass or a doorkeeper. But all the kings, royal ministers, and great ministers know a well-born man, and he goes out and enters by his very nature. This analogy should be understood. *Vacīsaṅkhāro*: that which fabricates speech. Here, mundane volitional thought (*lokiyavitakka*) fabricates speech, not supramundane [volitional thought] (*lokuttara*). Although it does not fabricate, it is still named verbal fabrication (*vacīsaṅkhāro*). “They attend to right intention (*sammāsaṅkappa*)": they attend upon supramundane right intention (*lokuttarasammāsaṅkappa*). Here, these three, namely, volitional thought regarding renunciation (*nekkhammasaṅkappa*) and so forth, are obtained in various minds in the preliminary stage. But at the moment of the path, while making a word-break and extirpation of the three, namely, volitional thought regarding sense pleasures (*kāmasaṅkappa*) and so forth, and while fulfilling the path factor, only one right intention (*sammāsaṅkappa*) arises and obtains three names by way of being volitional thought regarding renunciation (*nekkhammasaṅkappa*) and so forth. Hereafter, the same method applies to right speech (*sammāvācā*) and so forth.

*Takko*, *takko*, *vitakko*, *saṅkappo*, *appanā*, *byappanā*, *cetaso abhiniropanā*, *vacīsaṅkhāro*, *sammāsaṅkappaṃ anuparidhāvantī*.

mula_pali: 138. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti? Micchāvācaṃ ‘micchāvācā’ti pajānāti, sammāvācaṃ ‘sammāvācā’ti pajānāti; sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, micchāvācā? Musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, micchāvācā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāvācā? Sammāvācaṃpahaṃ, bhikkhave, dvāyaṃ vadāmi – atthi, bhikkhave, sammāvācā sāsavā puññabhāgiyā upadhivepakkā; atthi, bhikkhave , sammāvācā ariyā anāsavā lokuttarā maggaṅgā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāvācā sāsavā puññabhāgiyā upadhivepakkā? Musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammāvācā sāsavā puññabhāgiyā upadhivepakkā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāvācā ariyā anāsavā lokuttarā maggaṅgā? Yā kho, bhikkhave, ariyacittassa anāsavacittassa ariyamaggasamaṅgino ariyamaggaṃ bhāvayato catūhi vacīduccaritehi ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammāvācā ariyā anāsavā lokuttarā maggaṅgā. So micchāvācāya pahānāya vāyamati, sammāvācāya upasampadāya; svāssa hoti sammāvāyāmo. So sato micchāvācaṃ pajahati, sato sammāvācaṃ upasampajja viharati; sāssa hoti sammāsati. Itiyime tayo dhammā sammāvācaṃ anuparidhāvanti anuparivattanti, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati.
mula_english:
138. “Therein, bhikkhus, right view comes first.

And how, bhikkhus, does right view come first? One understands wrong speech as ‘wrong speech,’ and right speech as ‘right speech’; that is one’s right view.

And what, bhikkhus, is wrong speech? False speech (musāvāda), malicious speech (pisuṇā vācā), harsh speech (pharusā vācā), and gossip (samphappalāpo): this, bhikkhus, is wrong speech.

And what, bhikkhus, is right speech? Right speech, bhikkhus, I say is twofold: There is right speech that is affected by taints, on the side of merit, ripening in attachment; and there is right speech that is noble (ariya), taintless (anāsava), supramundane (lokuttara), a factor of the path (maggaṅga).

And what, bhikkhus, is right speech that is affected by taints, on the side of merit, ripening in attachment? Abstinence (veramaṇī) from false speech (musāvādā), abstinence from malicious speech (pisuṇāya vācāya), abstinence from harsh speech (pharusāya vācāya), abstinence from gossip (samphappalāpa): this, bhikkhus, is right speech that is affected by taints, on the side of merit, ripening in attachment.

And what, bhikkhus, is right speech that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path? The desisting (ārati), abstaining (virati), refraining (paṭivirati), abstinence (veramaṇī) from the four kinds of verbal misconduct (vacīduccaritehi) in one whose mind is noble (ariyacittassa), whose mind is taintless (anāsavacittassa), who possesses the noble path (ariyamaggasamaṅgino) and is developing the noble path (ariyamaggaṃ bhāvayato): this, bhikkhus, is right speech that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path.

One makes an effort (vāyamati) to abandon wrong speech (micchāvācāya pahānāya) and to enter upon right speech (sammāvācāya upasampadāya): this is one’s right effort (sammāvāyāmo).

Mindful (sato), one abandons wrong speech (micchāvācaṃ pajahati); mindful, one enters upon and dwells in right speech (sato sammāvācaṃ upasampajja viharati): this is one’s right mindfulness (sammāsati).

Thus, these three states run and circle around right speech, that is, right view (sammādiṭṭhi), right effort (sammāvāyāmo), and right mindfulness (sammāsati).
commentary_pali: 138.Musāvādāveramaṇītiādīsu viratipi cetanāpi vaṭṭati. Āratītiādīsu vacīduccaritehi ārakā ramatīti ārati. Vinā tehi ramatīti virati. Tato tato paṭinivattāva hutvā tehi vinā ramatīti paṭivirati. Upasaggavasena vā padaṃ vaḍḍhitaṃ, sabbamidaṃ oramanabhāvasseva adhivacanaṃ. Veraṃ maṇati vināsetīti veramaṇi. Idampi oramanasseva vevacanaṃ.
commentary_english:
138.
*Musāvādā*, *veramaṇī* etc., *virati* consciousness is fitting.
*Āratī* etc., because of speech being uttered, those who are far away rejoice, thus *ārati*.
Without them, there is rejoicing, thus *virati*.
Having turned back from that, because one rejoices without them, thus *paṭivirati*.
Or, a word is increased by means of a prefix; all of this is an appellation of abstaining.
One thinks of hostility, one destroys, thus *veramaṇi*.
This too is a synonym of abstaining.

mula_pali: 139. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti? Micchākammantaṃ ‘micchākammanto’ti pajānāti, sammākammantaṃ ‘sammākammanto’ti pajānāti ; sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, micchākammanto? Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, micchākammanto. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammākammanto? Sammākammantaṃpahaṃ, bhikkhave , dvāyaṃ vadāmi – atthi, bhikkhave, sammākammanto sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko; atthi, bhikkhave, sammākammanto ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammākammanto sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammākammanto sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammākammanto ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo? Yā kho, bhikkhave, ariyacittassa anāsavacittassa ariyamaggasamaṅgino ariyamaggaṃ bhāvayato tīhi kāyaduccaritehi ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammākammanto ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo. So micchākammantassa pahānāya vāyamati, sammākammantassa upasampadāya; svāssa hoti sammāvāyāmo. So sato micchākammantaṃ pajahati, sato sammākammantaṃ upasampajja viharati; sāssa hoti sammāsati. Itiyime tayo dhammā sammākammantaṃ anuparidhāvanti anuparivattanti, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati.
mula_english:
“Therein, monks, right view comes first.

And how, monks, does right view come first? One understands wrong action as ‘wrong action,’ and right action as ‘right action’; this is one's right view (sammādiṭṭhi).

And what, monks, is wrong action (micchākammanto)? Killing living beings (pāṇātipāto), taking what is not given (adinnādānaṃ), and misconduct in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācāro): this, monks, is wrong action.

And what, monks, is right action (sammākammanto)? Right action, I say, monks, is twofold: there is right action that is affected by taints (sāsavo), partaking of merit (puññabhāgiyo), ripening on the side of attachment (upadhivepakko); and there is right action that is noble (ariyo), taintless (anāsavo), supramundane (lokuttaro), a factor of the path (maggaṅgo).

And what, monks, is right action that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment? Abstinence (veramaṇī) from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā), abstinence from taking what is not given (adinnādānā), abstinence from misconduct in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārā): this, monks, is right action that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment.

And what, monks, is right action that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path? The desisting (ārati), abstaining (virati), refraining (paṭivirati), abstinence (veramaṇī) from the three kinds of bodily misconduct (kāyaduccaritehi) in one whose mind is noble (ariyacittassa), whose mind is taintless (anāsavacittassa), who possesses the noble path (ariyamaggasamaṅgino) and is developing the noble path (ariyamaggaṃ bhāvayato): this, monks, is right action that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path.

One makes an effort (vāyamati) to abandon wrong action (micchākammantassa pahānāya) and to enter upon right action (sammākammantassa upasampadāya); this is one's right effort (sammāvāyāmo).

Mindfully (sato) one abandons wrong action (micchākammantaṃ pajahati), mindfully one enters upon and abides in right action (sato sammākammantaṃ upasampajja viharati); this is one's right mindfulness (sammāsati).

Thus these three states (dhammā) run and circle around right action, that is, right view (sammādiṭṭhi), right effort (sammāvāyāmo), and right mindfulness (sammāsati).
commentary_pali: 139.Pāṇātipātā veramaṇītiādīsupi cetanā viratīti ubhayampi vaṭṭatiyeva.
commentary_english: Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī etc., both intention (cetanā) and abstinence (virati) are applicable.

mula_pali: 140. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti? Micchāājīvaṃ ‘micchāājīvo’ti pajānāti, sammāājīvaṃ ‘sammāājīvo’ti pajānāti; sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, micchāājīvo? Kuhanā, lapanā, nemittikatā, nippesikatā, lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatā nijigiṃ sanatā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, micchāājīvo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo? Sammāājīvaṃpahaṃ, bhikkhave , dvāyaṃ vadāmi – atthi, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko; atthi, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako micchāājīvaṃ pahāya sammāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo? Yā kho, bhikkhave, ariyacittassa anāsavacittassa ariyamaggasamaṅgino ariyamaggaṃ bhāvayato micchāājīvā ārati virati paṭivirati veramaṇī – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo. So micchāājīvassa pahānāya vāyamati, sammāājīvassa upasampadāya ; svāssa hoti sammāvāyāmo. So sato micchāājīvaṃ pajahati, sato sammāājīvaṃ upasampajja viharati; sāssa hoti sammāsati. Itiyime tayo dhammā sammāājīvaṃ anuparidhāvanti anuparivattanti, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati.
mula_english:
“Therein, *bhikkhus*, right view comes first.

And how, *bhikkhus*, does right view come first? One understands wrong livelihood as ‘wrong livelihood,’ and one understands right livelihood as ‘right livelihood’; that is one's right view.

And what, *bhikkhus*, is wrong livelihood? Deceitfulness, flattery, prognosticating, disparaging, and gaining a profit by means of a profit – this, *bhikkhus*, is wrong livelihood.

And what, *bhikkhus*, is right livelihood? Right livelihood, I say, is twofold: there is right livelihood that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment (*sāsavo puññabhāgiyo upadhivepakko*); and there is right livelihood that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path (*ariyo anāsavo lokuttaro maggaṅgo*).

And what, *bhikkhus*, is right livelihood that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment? Here, *bhikkhus*, a noble disciple abandons wrong livelihood and gains his living by right livelihood: this, *bhikkhus*, is right livelihood that is affected by taints, partaking of merit, ripening on the side of attachment.

And what, *bhikkhus*, is right livelihood that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path? The desisting from wrong livelihood, the abstaining, refraining, abstinence from it in one whose mind is noble, whose mind is taintless, who possesses the noble path and is developing the noble path: this, *bhikkhus*, is right livelihood that is noble, taintless, supramundane, a factor of the path.

One makes an effort to abandon wrong livelihood, to attain right livelihood; this is one's right effort (*sammāvāyāmo*).

Mindfully one abandons wrong livelihood, mindfully one enters upon and abides in right livelihood; this is one’s right mindfulness (*sammāsati*).

Thus these three states run and circle around right livelihood, that is, right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), right effort (*sammāvāyāmo*), and right mindfulness (*sammāsati*).
commentary_pali: 140.Kuhanātiādīsu tividhena kuhanavatthunā lokaṃ etāya kuhayanti vimhāpayantīti kuhanā. Lābhasakkāratthikā hutvā etāya lapantīti lapanā. Nimittaṃ sīlametesanti nemittikā, tesaṃ bhāvo nemittikatā. Nippeso sīlametesanti nippesikā, tesaṃ bhāvo nippesikatā. Lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanti magganti pariyesantīti lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanā, tesaṃ bhāvo lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatā. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthārena panetā kuhanādikā visuddhimagge sīlaniddeseyeva pāḷiñca aṭṭhakathañca āharitvā pakāsitā. Micchāājīvassa pahānāyāti ettha na kevalaṃ pāḷiyaṃ āgatova micchāājīvo, ājīvahetu pana pavattitā pāṇātipātādayo sattakammapathacetanāpi micchāājīvova. Tāsaṃyeva sattannaṃ cetanānaṃ padapacchedaṃ samugghātaṃ kurumānaṃ maggaṅgaṃ pūrayamānā uppannā virati sammāājīvo nāma.
commentary_english:
140. In "kuhanā," etc., people deceive and amaze the world with a threefold deceitful object; therefore, it is called *kuhanā* (hypocrisy).

Because they are desirous of gain and respect, they prattle about this, therefore it is called *lapanā* (prattling).

"A sign is their virtue" thus are the *naimittikas* (those who rely on omens), their state is *naimittikatā* (reliance on omens).

"Pressure is their virtue" thus are the *naippeśikas* (those who practice oppression), their state is *naippeśikatā* (practice of oppression).

"They seek to overcome gain with gain, they search and strive," therefore it is "striving to overcome gain with gain," their state is *lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatā* (striving to overcome gain with gain).

This is a summary here; however, these [qualities] beginning with hypocrisy, etc., have been extensively explained in the chapter on virtue in the *Visuddhimagga*, drawing from both the Pāli and the Aṭṭhakathā.

Regarding "*micchājīvassa pahānāyā* (for the abandonment of wrong livelihood)," here, not only is wrong livelihood mentioned in the Pāli, but even the sevenfold path of unwholesome actions such as killing, etc., which are engaged in for the sake of livelihood, are also wrong livelihood.

The abandonment (*virati*) that arises when those seven intentionalities are severed at the root, completely eradicated, and the path factor is fulfilled, is called right livelihood (*sammā-ājīva*).

mula_pali: 141. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti? Sammādiṭṭhissa , bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo pahoti, sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācā pahoti, sammāvācassa sammākammanto pahoti, sammākammantassa sammāājīvo pahoti, sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmo pahoti, sammāvāyāmassa sammāsati pahoti, sammāsatissa sammāsamādhi pahoti, sammāsamādhissa sammāñāṇaṃ pahoti, sammāñāṇassa sammāvimutti pahoti. Iti kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato sekkho aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatā sekhā paṭipadā (sī.), aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato sekho pāṭipado (pī. ka.) ( ) natthi sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu, dasaṅgasamannāgato arahā hoti. (Tatrapi sammāñāṇena aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā vigatā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti).
mula_english:
"Therein, monks, right view comes first.

And how, monks, does right view come first? In one of right view, monks, right intention arises; in one of right intention, right speech arises; in one of right speech, right action arises; in one of right action, right livelihood arises; in one of right livelihood, right effort arises; in one of right effort, right mindfulness arises; in one of right mindfulness, right concentration arises; in one of right concentration, right knowledge arises; in one of right knowledge, right liberation arises.

Thus, monks, the path of the disciple in higher training possesses eight factors (*aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato sekkho*), the *arhat* possesses ten factors. (Even there, with right knowledge, many evil unwholesome states are dispelled, [and] one goes to the fulfillment of development)."
commentary_pali: 141.Sammādiṭṭhissāti maggasammādiṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitassa puggalassa. Sammāsaṅkappo pahotīti maggasammāsaṅkappo pahoti, phalasammādiṭṭhissapi phalasammāsaṅkappo pahotīti evaṃ sabbapadesu attho veditabbo. Sammāñāṇassasammāvimuttīti ettha pana maggasammāsamādhimhi ṭhitassa maggapaccavekkhaṇaṃ sammāñāṇaṃ pahoti, phalasammāsamādhimhi ṭhitassa phalapaccavekkhaṇaṃ sammāñāṇaṃ pahoti. Maggapaccavekkhaṇasammāñāṇe ca ṭhitassa maggasammāvimutti pahoti, phalapaccavekkhaṇasammāñāṇe ṭhitassa phalasammāvimutti pahotīti attho. Ettha ca ṭhapetvā aṭṭha phalaṅgāni sammāñāṇaṃ paccavekkhaṇaṃ katvā sammāvimuttiṃ phalaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
"When one possesses right view" means for an individual established in the right view of the path.

"Right intention arises" means the right intention of the path arises. Similarly, the right intention of the fruit also arises from the right view of the fruit. The meaning should be understood in this way in all instances.

"Right knowledge, right liberation": Here, right knowledge, in the sense of reflection on the path, arises for one established in right concentration of the path. Right knowledge, in the sense of reflection on the fruit, arises for one established in right concentration of the fruit.

And right liberation of the path arises for one established in right knowledge of reflection on the path, and right liberation of the fruit arises for one established in right knowledge of reflection on the fruit—this is the meaning.

Here, it is said that having established the eight factors of the fruit, it is fitting to make right liberation the fruit by making right knowledge reflection.

mula_pali:
142. ‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi pubbaṅgamā hoti? Sammādiṭṭhissa, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi nijjiṇṇā hoti. Ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti. Sammādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Sammāsaṅkappassa, bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo nijjiṇṇo hoti…pe… sammāvācassa, bhikkhave, micchāvācā nijjiṇṇā hoti… sammākammantassa, bhikkhave, micchākammanto nijjiṇṇo hoti… sammāājīvassa, bhikkhave, micchāājīvo nijjiṇṇo hoti… sammāvāyāmassa , bhikkhave , micchāvāyāmo nijjiṇṇo hoti… sammāsatissa, bhikkhave, micchāsati nijjiṇṇā hoti… sammāsamādhissa, bhikkhave, micchāsamādhi nijjiṇṇo hoti… sammāñāṇassa, bhikkhave, micchāñāṇaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ hoti… sammāvimuttassa, bhikkhave, micchāvimutti nijjiṇṇā hoti. Ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti. Sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

‘‘Iti kho, bhikkhave, vīsati kusalapakkhā, vīsati akusalapakkhā – mahācattārīsako dhammapariyāyo pavattito appaṭivattiyo samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ.
mula_english:
“Therein, *bhikkhus*, right view comes first. And how does right view come first? In one of right view, *bhikkhus*, wrong view is abolished. And the many evil unwholesome states that originate with wrong view as condition are also abolished, and the many wholesome states that originate with right view as condition come to fulfilment by development.

“In one of right intention, *bhikkhus*, wrong intention is abolished… In one of right speech, *bhikkhus*, wrong speech is abolished… In one of right action, *bhikkhus*, wrong action is abolished… In one of right livelihood, *bhikkhus*, wrong livelihood is abolished… In one of right effort, *bhikkhus*, wrong effort is abolished… In one of right mindfulness, *bhikkhus*, wrong mindfulness is abolished… In one of right concentration, *bhikkhus*, wrong concentration is abolished… In one of right knowledge, *bhikkhus*, wrong knowledge is abolished… In one of right deliverance, *bhikkhus*, wrong deliverance is abolished. The many evil, unskillful qualities that come into play with wrong release as their condition are also abolished, while the many skillful qualities that have right release as their condition go to the culmination of their development.

“Thus, *bhikkhus*, there are twenty factors on the side of the wholesome (*kuśala-pakṣa*), and twenty factors on the side of the unwholesome (*akuśala-pakṣa*). This Dhamma discourse on the Great Forty has been set rolling and cannot be stopped by any recluse (*śramaṇa*) or *brāhmin* or god (*deva*) or *Māra* or *Brahmā* or anyone in the world.
commentary_pali:
142.Sammādiṭṭhissa, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi nijjiṇṇā hotītiādīsu avasesanikāyabhāṇakā phalaṃ kathitanti vadanti, majjhimabhāṇakā pana dasannaṃ nijjaravatthūnaṃ āgataṭṭhāne maggo kathitoti vadanti. Tattha dassanaṭṭhena sammādiṭṭhi veditabbā, viditakaraṇaṭṭhena sammāñāṇaṃ, tadadhimuttaṭṭhena sammāvimutti.

Vīsati kusalapakkhāti sammādiṭṭhiādayo dasa, ‘‘sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā’’tiādinā nayena vuttā dasāti evaṃ vīsati kusalapakkhā honti. Vīsati akusalapakkhāti ‘‘micchādiṭṭhi nijjiṇṇā hotī’’tiādinā nayena vuttā micchādiṭṭhiādayo dasa, ‘‘ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā’’tiādinā vuttā dasa cāti evaṃ vīsati akusalapakkhā veditabbā. Mahācattārīsakoti mahāvipākadānena mahantānaṃ kusalapakkhikānañceva akusalapakkhikānañca cattārīsāya dhammānaṃ pakāsitattā mahācattārīsakoti.

Vīsati kusalapakkhā Vīsati akusalapakkhā Mahācattārīsako

Imasmiñca pana sutte pañca sammādiṭṭhiyo kathitā vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi kammassakatāsammādiṭṭhi maggasammādiṭṭhi phalasammādiṭṭhi paccavekkhaṇāsammādiṭṭhīti. Tattha ‘‘micchādiṭṭhiṃ micchādiṭṭhīti pajānātī’’tiādinā nayena vuttā vipassanāsammādiṭṭhi nāma. ‘‘Atthi dinna’’ntiādinā nayena vuttā kammassakatāsammādiṭṭhi nāma. ‘‘Sammādiṭṭhissa, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo pahotī’’ti ettha pana maggasammādiṭṭhi phalasammādiṭṭhīti dvepi kathitā. ‘‘Sammāñāṇaṃ pahotī’’ti. Ettha pana paccavekkhaṇāsammādiṭṭhi kathitāti veditabbā.
commentary_english:
142. sammādiṭṭhissa, Monks, micchādiṭṭhi nijjiṇṇā hotīti, those who recite the remainder of the Nikāyas say that the fruit is spoken of, but the Middle reciters say that the path is spoken of in the place where the ten objects of annihilation have come. Therein, right view ( *samyagdṛṣṭi*) should be understood in the sense of seeing, right knowledge ( *samyagjñāna*) in the sense of the cause of knowing, and right liberation ( *samyagvimukti*) in the sense of being devoted to that.

vīsati kusalapakkhāti, the ten beginning with right view (*samyagdṛṣṭi*), "because of right view, many wholesome qualities ( *kuśalā dhammā*) are spoken of in this way, thus there are twenty wholesome factors. vīsati akusalapakkhāti, "wrong view ( *mithyādṛṣṭi*) is annihilated", the ten beginning with wrong view ( *mithyādṛṣṭi*) are spoken of in this way, "and because of wrong view, many evil things ( *pāpakā*) are spoken of, thus twenty unwholesome factors should be understood. mahācattārīsakoti, because of the great result (*mahāvipāka*), the forty qualities ( *dhammānaṃ*) of the great wholesome and unwholesome factors are manifested, thus it is called great forty.

vīsati kusalapakkhā vīsati akusalapakkhā mahācattārīsako

And in this Sūtra, five right views ( *samyagdṛṣṭi*) are spoken of: insight right view ( *vipaśyanāsamyagdṛṣṭi*), the right view of the ownership of karma, the right view of the path, the right view of the fruit, and the right view of retrospection. Therein, "one understands wrong view as wrong view," the insight right view ( *vipaśyanāsamyagdṛṣṭi*) is spoken of in this way. "There is giving," the right view of the ownership of karma is spoken of in this way. "For one with right view (*samyagdṛṣṭi*), monks, right intention arises," here the right view of the path and the right view of the fruit are both spoken of. "Right knowledge arises." Here, the right view of retrospection is spoken of.

mula_pali:
143. ‘‘Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā imaṃ mahācattārīsakaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ garahitabbaṃ paṭikkositabbaṃ maññeyya tassa diṭṭheva dhamme dasasahadhammikā vādānuvādā gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchanti – sammādiṭṭhiṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati, ye ca micchādiṭṭhī samaṇabrāhmaṇā te bhoto pujjā, te bhoto pāsaṃsā; sammāsaṅkappaṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati , ye ca micchāsaṅkappā samaṇabrāhmaṇā te bhoto pujjā, te bhoto pāsaṃsā; sammāvācaṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati…pe… sammākammantaṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati… sammāājīvaṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati… sammāvāyāmaṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati… sammāsatiṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati… sammāsamādhiṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati… sammāñāṇaṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati … sammāvimuttiṃ ce bhavaṃ garahati, ye ca micchāvimuttī samaṇabrāhmaṇā te bhoto pujjā, te bhoto pāsaṃsā. Yo koci, bhikkhave, samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā imaṃ mahācattārīsakaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ garahitabbaṃ paṭikkositabbaṃ maññeyya tassa diṭṭheva dhamme ime dasasahadhammikā vādānuvādā gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchanti. Yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ okkalā vassabhaññā vayabhiññā (ka.) saṃ. ni. 3.62; a. ni. 4.30 passitabbaṃ ahetuvādā akiriyavādā natthikavādā tepi mahācattārīsakaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ na garahitabbaṃ napaṭikkositabbaṃ amaññiṃsu maññeyyuṃ (ka.). Taṃ kissa hetu? Nindābyārosaupārambhabhayā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Mahācattārīsakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, if any recluse or *brāhmaṇa* thinks that this *Dhamma* discourse on the Great Forty should be censured and rejected, then there are ten legitimate deductions from his assertions that would provide grounds for censuring him here and now. If that worthy one censures right view (*sammādiṭṭhiṃ*), then he would honour and praise those recluses and *brāhmaṇas* who are of wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhī*). If that worthy one censures right intention (*sammāsaṅkappaṃ*), then he would honour and praise those recluses and *brāhmaṇas* who are of wrong intention. If that worthy one censures right speech (*sammāvācaṃ*)… If that worthy one censures right action (*sammākammantaṃ*)… If that worthy one censures right livelihood (*sammāājīvaṃ*)… If that worthy one censures right effort (*sammāvāyāmaṃ*)… If that worthy one censures right mindfulness (*sammāsatiṃ*)… If that worthy one censures right concentration (*sammāsamādhiṃ*)… If that worthy one censures right knowledge (*sammāñāṇaṃ*)… If that worthy one censures right liberation (*sammāvimuttiṃ*), then he would honour and praise those recluses and *brāhmaṇas* who are of wrong liberation.

"Bhikkhus, if any recluse or *brāhmaṇa* thinks that this *Dhamma* discourse on the Great Forty should be censured and rejected, then these are ten legitimate deductions from his assertions that would provide grounds for censuring him here and now.

Those recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of Okkala and Vassabhañña, who held to the doctrine of no-cause (*ahetuvādā*), the doctrine of no-action (*akiriyavādā*), and the annihilationist doctrine (*natthikavādā*), did not think that this *Dhamma* discourse on the Great Forty should be censured or rejected. What is the reason for that? [They feared] the danger of blame, reproach, and disparagement."

This is what the Buddha said. Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Great Forty Discourse, the seventh [sutta], is finished.
commentary_pali:
143.Sammādiṭṭhiṃce bhavaṃ garahatīti micchādiṭṭhi nāmāyaṃ sobhanāti vadantopi sammādiṭṭhi nāmāyaṃ na sobhanāti vadantopi sammādiṭṭhiṃ garahati nāma. Okkalāti okkalajanapadavāsino. Vassabhaññāti vasso ca bhañño cāti dve janā. Ahetuvādāti natthi hetu natthi paccayo sattānaṃ visuddhiyāti evamādivādino. Akiriyavādāti karoto na karīyati pāpanti evaṃ kiriyapaṭikkhepavādino. Natthikavādāti natthi dinnantiādivādino. Te imesu tīsupi dassanesu okkantaniyāmā ahesuṃ. Kathaṃ panetesu niyāmo hotīti. Yo hi evarūpaṃ laddhiṃ gahetvā rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhāne nisinno sajjhāyati vīmaṃsati, tassa ‘‘natthi hetu natthi paccayo karoto na karīyati pāpaṃ, natthi dinnaṃ, kāyassa bhedā ucchijjatī’’ti tasmiṃ ārammaṇe micchāsati santiṭṭhati, cittaṃ ekaggaṃ hoti, javanāni javanti. Paṭhamajavane satekiccho hoti, tathā dutiyādīsu. Sattame buddhānampi atekiccho anivattī ariṭṭhakaṇḍakasadiso hoti.

Tattha koci ekaṃ dassanaṃ okkamati, koci dve, koci tīṇipi, niyatamicchādiṭṭhikova hoti, patto saggamaggāvaraṇañceva mokkhamaggāvaraṇañca. Abhabbo tassa attabhāvassa anantaraṃ saggampi gantuṃ, pageva mokkhaṃ, vaṭṭakhāṇu nāmesa satto pathavīgopako, yebhuyyena evarūpassa bhavato vuṭṭhānaṃ natthi. Vassabhaññāpi edisā ahesuṃ. Nindābyārosaupārambhabhayāti attano nindābhayena ghaṭṭanabhayena upavādabhayena cāti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Nindābyārosaupārambhabhayā

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahācattārīsakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
143.
If one reviles *sammādiṭṭhi*, it is called wrong view. Even if one says, "This is beautiful," it is called wrong view. Even if one says, "This is not beautiful," one is reviling *sammādiṭṭhi*.

*okkalā* means inhabitants of the Okkala region.

*vassabhaññā* means Vassa and Bhañña, these two people.

*ahetuvādā* means those who claim "There is no cause, there is no condition for the purification of beings," and so on.

*akiriyavādā* means those who deny action by saying, "By doing so there is no evil," and so on.

*natthikavādā* means those who claim, "There is no giving," and so on.

They were fixed on these three views.

How is there a fixed consequence in these?

Someone who, having taken up such a view, sits contemplating and pondering day and night, for him, "There is no cause, there is no condition. By doing so there is no evil, there is no giving. At the breakup of the body, one is annihilated," in that object wrong mindfulness is established, the mind becomes one-pointed, impulsive moments occur.

In the first impulsive moment there is effort, likewise in the second and so on.

In the seventh, even for Buddhas, there is effortlessness, irreversibility, similar to an *ariṭṭhakaṇḍaka*.

There, someone might espouse one view, another two, another three. But whether one espouses one, two, or three views, one adopts a wrong view with fixed consequences. One has met an obstruction to the path to heaven and an obstruction to the path to liberation.

It is impossible for him to reach heaven immediately following this present existence, much less to reach liberation. This being has become a stump in the round of existence, a watchman of the earth. Generally, one like this does not emerge from existence.

The *vassabhaññās* were also like this.

*nindābyārosaupārambhabhayā* means fear of blame, fear of abuse, fear of censure, this is the meaning.

The rest is clear throughout.

*nindābyārosaupārambhabhayā*

Explanation of the *Mahācattārīsakasutta* in the *Papañcasūdanī*, commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*, is finished.

mula_pali:
144. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde sambahulehi abhiññātehi abhiññātehi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ – āyasmatā ca sāriputtena āyasmatā ca mahāmoggallānena mahāmoggalānena (ka.) āyasmatā ca mahākassapena āyasmatā ca mahākaccāyanena āyasmatā ca mahākoṭṭhikena āyasmatā ca mahākappinena āyasmatā ca mahācundena āyasmatā ca anuruddhena āyasmatā ca revatena āyasmatā ca ānandena, aññehi ca abhiññātehi abhiññātehi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ.

Tena kho pana samayena therā bhikkhū nave bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti. Appekacce therā bhikkhū dasapi bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti, appekacce therā bhikkhū vīsampi bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti, appekacce therā bhikkhū tiṃsampi bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti, appekacce therā bhikkhū cattārīsampi bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti. Te ca navā bhikkhū therehi bhikkhūhi ovadiyamānā anusāsiyamānā uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānanti pajānanti (syā. kaṃ.), sañjānanti (ka.).

pajānanti (syā. kaṃ.), sañjānanti (ka.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvattha in the Eastern Park, in the Palace of Migāra’s Mother, together with many very well-known elder disciples - the venerable Sāriputta, the venerable Mahā Moggallāna, the venerable Mahā Kassapa, the venerable Mahā Kaccāyana, the venerable Mahā Kotthita, the venerable Mahā Kappina, the venerable Mahā Cunda, the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Revata, and the venerable Ānanda, and other very well-known elder disciples.

Now on that occasion elder *bhikkhus* had been teaching and instructing new *bhikkhus*; some elder *bhikkhus* had been teaching and instructing ten new *bhikkhus*, some elder *bhikkhus* had been teaching and instructing twenty new *bhikkhus*, some elder *bhikkhus* had been teaching and instructing thirty new *bhikkhus*, some elder *bhikkhus* had been teaching and instructing forty new *bhikkhus*. And the new *bhikkhus*, taught and instructed by the elder *bhikkhus*, achieved successive stages of high distinction.
commentary_pali:
144.Evaṃme sutanti ānāpānassatisuttaṃ. Tattha aññehi cāti ṭhapetvā pāḷiyaṃ āgate dasa there aññehipi abhiññātehi bahūhi sāvakehi saddhiṃ. Tadā kira mahā bhikkhusaṅgho ahosi aparicchinnagaṇano.

Ovadanti anusāsantīti āmisasaṅgahena dhammasaṅgahena cāti dvīhi saṅgahehi saṅgaṇhitvā kammaṭṭhānovādānusāsanīhi ovadanti ca anusāsanti ca. Te cāti cakāro āgamasandhimattaṃ. Uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānantīti sīlaparipūraṇādito pubbavisesato uḷārataraṃ aparaṃ kasiṇaparikammādivisesaṃ jānantīti attho.

Ovadanti anusāsantī Te cā Uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānantī
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard: the Ānāpānassatisutta.

There, excluding "aññehi ca," the ten elders mentioned in the Pāli [text] were together with many other well-known disciples. At that time, it seems there was a great Saṅgha of monks, whose number was incalculable.

"Ovadanti anusāsantī": by means of two kinds of generosity, generosity with material things and generosity with the Dharma, having gathered them with instructions on the bases of action, they both advised and instructed. "Te cā": the "ca" is merely a euphonic addition. "Uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānantī": they know a superior, further distinction than the previous distinction, beginning with the complete fulfillment of morality, a superior further distinction, such as the preliminary activities for the kasiṇa, etc.; this is the meaning.

Ovadanti anusāsantī, te cā, uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānantī.

mula_pali: 145. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe pannarase pavāraṇāya puṇṇāya puṇṇamāya rattiyā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto abbhokāse nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anuviloketvā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘āraddhosmi, bhikkhave, imāya paṭipadāya; āraddhacittosmi, bhikkhave, imāya paṭipadāya. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, bhiyyosomattāya vīriyaṃ ārabhatha appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya , asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idhevāhaṃ sāvatthiyaṃ komudiṃ cātumāsiniṃ āgamessāmī’’ti. Assosuṃ kho jānapadā bhikkhū – ‘‘bhagavā kira tattheva sāvatthiyaṃ komudiṃ cātumāsiniṃ āgamessatī’’ti. Te jānapadā bhikkhū sāvatthiṃ sāvatthiyaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) osaranti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Te ca kho therā bhikkhū bhiyyosomattāya nave bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti. Appekacce therā bhikkhū dasapi bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti, appekacce therā bhikkhū vīsampi bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti , appekacce therā bhikkhū tiṃsampi bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti, appekacce therā bhikkhū cattārīsampi bhikkhū ovadanti anusāsanti. Te ca navā bhikkhū therehi bhikkhūhi ovadiyamānā anusāsiyamānā uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānanti.
mula_english:
At that time, the Blessed One was seated in the open, surrounded by the Saṃgha of *bhikkhus*, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, the full moon night of the *Pavarana* ceremony.

Then, surveying the silent Saṃgha of *bhikkhus*, the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: "Oh *bhikkhus*, I am content with this progress; my mind is content with this progress. Therefore, oh *bhikkhus*, here exert yourselves all the more for the attainment of the unattained (*appattassa pattiyā*), for the accomplishment of the unaccomplished (*anadhigatassa adhigamāya*), for the realization of the unrealized (*asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya*). I will remain right here in Sāvatthī until the fourth month of Komudī."

The *bhikkhus* of the countryside heard: "The Blessed One will remain there in Sāvatthī until the Komudī full moon of the fourth month."

Those *bhikkhus* of the countryside went to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One. And those elder *bhikkhus* still more intensively taught and instructed new *bhikkhus*. Some elder *bhikkhus* taught and instructed ten new *bhikkhus*, some elder *bhikkhus* taught and instructed twenty, some elder *bhikkhus* taught and instructed thirty, some elder *bhikkhus* taught and instructed forty new *bhikkhus*. And those new *bhikkhus*, being advised and instructed by the elder *bhikkhus*, came to know a superior and distinct (state) beyond the previous one.
commentary_pali:
145.Āraddhoti tuṭṭho. Appattassa pattiyāti appattassa arahattassa pāpuṇanatthaṃ. Sesapadadvayepi ayameva attho. Komudiṃ cātumāsininti pacchimakattikacātumāsapuṇṇamaṃ. Sā hi kumudānaṃ atthitāya komudī, catunnaṃ vassikānaṃ māsānaṃ pariyosānattā cātumāsinīti vuccati. Āgamessāmīti udikkhissāmi, ajja apavāretvā yāva sā āgacchati, tāva katthaci agantvā idheva vasissāmīti attho. Iti bhikkhūnaṃ pavāraṇasaṅgahaṃ anujānanto evamāha.

Pavāraṇasaṅgaho nāma ñattidutiyena kammena diyyati kassa panesa diyyati, kassa na diyyatīti. Akārakassa tāva bālaputhujjanassa na diyyati, tathā āraddhavipassakassa ceva ariyasāvakassa ca. Yassa pana samatho vā taruṇo hoti vipassanā vā, tassa diyyati. Bhagavāpi tadā bhikkhūnaṃ cittācāraṃ parivīmaṃsanto samathavipassanānaṃ taruṇabhāvaṃ ñatvā – ‘‘mayi ajja pavārente disāsu vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhū idha osarissanti. Tato ime bhikkhū vuḍḍhatarehi bhikkhūhi senāsane gahite visesaṃ nibbattetuṃ na sakkhissanti. Sacepi cārikaṃ pakkamissāmi, imesaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ dullabhameva bhavissati. Mayi pana apavārente bhikkhūpi imaṃ sāvatthiṃ na osarissanti, ahampi cārikaṃ na pakkamissāmi, evaṃ imesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ apalibuddhaṃ bhavissati. Te attano attano vasanaṭṭhāne phāsu viharantā samathavipassanā thāmajātā katvā visesaṃ nibbattetuṃ sakkhissantī’’ti so taṃdivasaṃ apavāretvā kattikapuṇṇamāyaṃ pavāressāmīti bhikkhūnaṃ pavāraṇasaṅgahaṃ anujāni. Pavāraṇasaṅgahasmiñhi laddhe yassa nissayapaṭipannassa ācariyupajjhāyā pakkamanti, sopi ‘‘sace patirūpo nissayadāyako āgamissati, tassa santike nissayaṃ gaṇhissāmī’’ti yāva gimhānaṃ pacchimamāsā vasituṃ labhati. Sacepi saṭṭhivassā bhikkhū āgacchanti, tassa senāsanaṃ gahetuṃ na labhanti. Ayañca pana pavāraṇasaṅgaho ekassa dinnopi sabbesaṃ dinnoyeva hoti.

Pavāraṇasaṅgaho

Sāvatthiṃ osarantīti bhagavatā pavāraṇasaṅgaho dinnoti sutasutaṭṭhāneyeva yathāsabhāvena ekaṃ māsaṃ vasitvā kattikapuṇṇamāya uposathaṃ katvā osarante sandhāya idaṃ vuttaṃ. Pubbenāparanti idha taruṇasamathavipassanāsu kammaṃ katvā samathavipassanā thāmajātā akaṃsu, ayaṃ pubbe viseso nāma. Tato samāhitena cittena saṅkhāre sammasitvā keci sotāpattiphalaṃ…pe… keci arahattaṃ sacchikariṃsu. Ayaṃ aparo uḷāro viseso nāma.

Sāvatthiṃ osarantī Pubbenāpara
commentary_english:
145. *Āraddho* means delighted. *Appattassa pattiyā* means for the purpose of attaining the unattained arahantship. The same is the meaning in the remaining two words as well. *Komudiṃ cātumāsini* means the last Kārttika full moon of the four months. That [night] is called *komudī* because of the existence of white lotuses (*kumuda*), and *cātumāsinī* because it is the end of the four rainy season months. *Āgamessāmī* means I will wait, having dismissed [them] today, I will stay right here without going anywhere else until that [day] comes. Thus, while approving the acceptance of the *pavāraṇā-saṅgaha*, he said this.

The *pavāraṇā-saṅgaha* is given through a formal motion and a second motion. To whom is it given, and to whom is it not given? It is not given to the inactive childish ordinary person, nor to one who has initiated insight meditation, nor to a noble disciple. But it is given to one whose serenity (*samatha*) or insight (*vipassanā*) is still young. The Blessed One, examining the conduct of the minds of the monks, knowing the young state of serenity and insight, [thought:] "Today, while I am holding *pavāraṇā*, the monks who have spent the rainy season in various directions will gather here. Then, if the senior monks take the lodgings, these monks will not be able to produce distinction. Even if I leave for a tour, it will be difficult for them to find a place to stay. But if I hold *apavāraṇā*, the monks will not come down to this Śrāvastī, and I too will not leave for a tour. Thus, the dwelling place of these monks will be unencumbered. They, living comfortably in their own dwelling places, having made their serenity and insight strong, will be able to produce distinction." So, having dismissed [them] that day, he approved the acceptance of the *pavāraṇā-saṅgaha* for the monks, [saying:] “I will hold the *pavāraṇā* on the Kārttika full moon." Indeed, when the *pavāraṇā-saṅgaha* is received, the teachers and preceptors of the one who has undertaken dependence may leave, and he may live until the last month of the hot season, [thinking:] "If a suitable giver of support comes, I will take dependence from him." Even if monks of sixty years come, they are not allowed to take his lodging. And this *pavāraṇā-saṅgaha*, even if given to one, is indeed given to all.

Coming down to Śrāvastī: This was said with reference to [those monks] who, having heard that the Blessed One had given the *pavāraṇā-saṅgaha*, lived for a month in the very place where they had heard it, according to their own nature, and then, having performed the *uposatha* on the Kārttika full moon, came down. Earlier and later: Here, having done work on young serenity and insight, they made serenity and insight strong. This is what is called the earlier distinction. Then, having properly contemplated the conditioned things with a concentrated mind, some realized the fruit of stream-entry... some realized arahantship. This is what is called the later, magnificent distinction.

mula_pali: 146. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe pannarase komudiyā cātumāsiniyā puṇṇāya puṇṇamāya rattiyā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto abbhokāse nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anuviloketvā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘apalāpāyaṃ, bhikkhave, parisā; nippalāpāyaṃ, bhikkhave, parisā; suddhā sāre suddhasāre patiṭṭhitā (syā. kaṃ. pī.) patiṭṭhitā. Tathārūpo ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho; tathārūpā ayaṃ, bhikkhave, parisā yathārūpā parisā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa. Tathārūpo ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho; tathārūpā ayaṃ, bhikkhave, parisā yathārūpāya parisāya appaṃ dinnaṃ bahu hoti, bahu dinnaṃ bahutaraṃ. Tathārūpo ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho; tathārūpā ayaṃ, bhikkhave, parisā yathārūpā parisā dullabhā dassanāya lokassa. Tathārūpo ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho; tathārūpā ayaṃ, bhikkhave, parisā yathārūpaṃ parisaṃ alaṃ yojanagaṇanāni dassanāya gantuṃ puṭosenāpi’’ puṭosenāpi, tathārūpo ayaṃ bhikkhave bhikkhusaṃgho, tathārūpā ayaṃ parisā (sī. pī. ka.).
mula_english:
146. On that occasion, the Blessed One was seated in the open, surrounded by the *saṃgha* of *bhikṣus*, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, the full-moon night of the Komudi full moon of the fourth month.

Then, surveying the silent *saṃgha* of *bhikṣus*, the Blessed One addressed the *bhikṣus* thus: "This assembly, *bhikṣus*, is free from prattle; this assembly, *bhikṣus*, is free from prattle; it is pure, established in the core."

Such, *bhikṣus*, is this *saṃgha* of *bhikṣus*; such, *bhikṣus*, is this assembly. Such an assembly as is worthy of gifts (*āhuneyyā*), worthy of hospitality (*pāhuneyyā*), worthy of offerings (*dakkhiṇeyyā*), worthy of reverential salutation (*añjalikaraṇīyā*), an unsurpassed field of merit (*anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ*) for the world (*lokassa*).

Such, *bhikṣus*, is this *saṃgha* of *bhikṣus*; such, *bhikṣus*, is this assembly. Such an assembly that a small gift given to it becomes great and a great gift greater.

Such, *bhikṣus*, is this *saṃgha* of *bhikṣus*; such, *bhikṣus*, is this assembly. Such an assembly as is rare for the world to see.

Such, *bhikṣus*, is this *saṃgha* of *bhikṣus*; such, *bhikṣus*, is this assembly. Such an assembly as would be worth journeying many leagues with a travel-bag to see.
commentary_pali: 146.Alanti yuttaṃ. Yojanagaṇanānīti ekaṃ yojanaṃ yojanameva, dasapi yojanāni yojanāneva, tato uddhaṃ yojanagaṇanānīti vuccanti. Idha pana yojanasatampi yojanasahassampi adhippetaṃ. Puṭosenāpīti puṭosaṃ vuccati pātheyyaṃ. taṃ pātheyyaṃ gahetvāpi upasaṅkamituṃ yuttamevāti attho. ‘‘Puṭaṃsenā’’tipi pāṭho, tassattho – puṭo aṃse assāti puṭaṃso, tena puṭaṃsena, aṃse pātheyyapuṭaṃ vahantenāpīti vuttaṃ hoti.
commentary_english:
ala nti yuttaṃ.

yojanagaṇanānīti ekaṃ yojanaṃ yojanameva, dasapi yojanāni yojanāneva, tato uddhaṃ yojanagaṇanānīti vuccanti.

Here, however, a hundred *yojana*s (*yojanaśatam api*) or a thousand *yojana*s (*yojanasahasram api*) are intended.

puṭosenāpīti puṭosaṃ vuccati pātheyyaṃ.

That *pātheyyaṃ*, having taken, it is fitting to approach.

"puṭaṃsenā"tipi pāṭho, tassattho – puṭo aṃse assāti puṭaṃso, tena puṭaṃsena, aṃse pātheyyapuṭaṃ vahantenāpīti vuttaṃ hoti.

mula_pali:
147. ‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññāvimuttā – evarūpāpi, bhikkhave, santi bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe . Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā – evarūpāpi, bhikkhave, santi bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe. Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino sakideva sakiṃ deva (ka.) imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti – evarūpāpi, bhikkhave, santi bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe . Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyanā – evarūpāpi, bhikkhave, santi bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe.

‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti – evarūpāpi, bhikkhave, santi bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe. Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe catunnaṃ sammappadhānānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti…pe… catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ… pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ… pañcannaṃ balānaṃ… sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ… ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa bhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti – evarūpāpi, bhikkhave, santi bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe. Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe mettābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti… karuṇābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti… muditābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti… upekkhābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti… asubhabhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti… aniccasaññābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti – evarūpāpi, bhikkhave, santi bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe. Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe ānāpānassatibhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti. Ānāpānassati, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Ānāpānassati, bhikkhave, bhāvitā bahulīkatā cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti. Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti. Satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti.
mula_english:
“In this Sangha of *bhikkhus* there are *arahants* with taints destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached the true goal, destroyed the fetters of being, and are completely liberated through final knowledge - such *bhikkhus* are there in this Sangha of *bhikkhus*.

“In this Sangha of *bhikkhus* there are *bhikkhus* who, with the destruction of the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ*), are due to reappear spontaneously (*opapātikā*) in the Pure Abodes and there attain final *Nibbana*, without ever returning from that world - such *bhikkhus* are there in this Sangha of *bhikkhus*.

“In this Sangha of *bhikkhus* there are *bhikkhus* who, with the destruction of three fetters and with the attenuation of lust (*rāga*), hate (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*), are once-returners (*sakadāgāmino*), returning once to this world to make an end of suffering - such *bhikkhus* are there in this Sangha of *bhikkhus*.

“In this Sangha of *bhikkhus* there are *bhikkhus* who, with the destruction of the three fetters (*saṃyojanānaṃ*), are stream-enterers (*sotāpannā*), no longer subject to perdition, bound for deliverance, headed for enlightenment - such *bhikkhus* are there in this Sangha of *bhikkhus*.

“In this Sangha of *bhikkhus* there are *bhikkhus* who abide devoted to the development of the four foundations of mindfulness (*catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) - such *bhikkhus* are there in this Sangha of *bhikkhus*.

In this Sangha of *bhikkhus* there are *bhikkhus* who abide devoted to the development of the four right kinds of striving (*catunnaṃ sammappadhānānaṃ bhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) . . . of the four bases for spiritual power (*catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ*) . . . of the five faculties (*pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ*) . . . of the five powers (*pañcannaṃ balānaṃ*) . . . of the seven enlightenment factors (*sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ*) . . . of the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa bhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) - such *bhikkhus* are there in this Sangha of *bhikkhus*.

“In this Sangha of *bhikkhus* there are *bhikkhus* who abide devoted to the development of loving-kindness (*mettābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) . . . of compassion (*karuṇābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) . . . of appreciative joy (*muditābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) . . . of equanimity (*upekkhābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) . . . of the meditation on foulness (*asubhabhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) . . . of the perception of impermanence (*aniccasaññābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*) - such *bhikkhus* are there in this Sangha of *bhikkhus*.

In this Sangha of *bhikkhus* there are *bhikkhus* who abide devoted to the development of mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpānassatibhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*).

Bhikkhus, when mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpānassati*) is developed and cultivated, it is of great fruit and great benefit.

When mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpānassati*) is developed and cultivated, it fulfils the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti*).

When the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*) are developed and cultivated, they fulfil the seven enlightenment factors (*satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti*).

When the seven enlightenment factors (*satta bojjhaṅgā*) are developed and cultivated, they fulfil true knowledge and deliverance (*vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti*).
commentary_pali: 147. Idāni evarūpehi caraṇehi samannāgatā ettha bhikkhū atthīti dassetuṃ santi, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānantiādīni tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ abhiniviṭṭhakammaṭṭhānadassanatthaṃ vuttāni. Tattha sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiyadhammā lokiyalokuttarā kathitā. Tatra hi ye bhikkhū tasmiṃ khaṇe maggaṃ bhāventi, tesaṃ lokuttarā honti. Āraddhavipassakānaṃ lokiyā. Aniccasaññābhāvanānuyoganti ettha saññāsīsena vipassanā kathitā . Yasmā panettha ānāpānakammaṭṭhānavasena abhiniviṭṭhāva bahū bhikkhū, tasmā sesakammaṭṭhānāni saṅkhepena kathetvā ānāpānakammaṭṭhānaṃ vitthārena kathento ānāpānassati, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Idaṃ pana ānāpānakammaṭṭhānaṃ sabbākārena visuddhimagge vitthāritaṃ, tasmā tattha vuttanayenevassa pāḷittho ca bhāvanānayo ca veditabbo.
commentary_english:
Now, to show that bhikkhus endowed with such conduct exist, he said, “There are, bhikkhus,” etc.

There, "of the four foundations of mindfulness," etc., is said to show the fixed meditation subject of those bhikkhus.

There, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, both mundane (lokiya) and supramundane (lokuttara), are described.

There, those bhikkhus who cultivate the path at that moment have the supramundane ones. The mundane ones belong to those who have started insight (vipassanā).

"Application to the cultivation of the perception of impermanence" here speaks of insight with perception as the head.

And because here many bhikkhus are fixed on the basis of the mindfulness of breathing meditation subject, therefore, having spoken of the remaining meditation subjects in brief, he said, "Mindfulness of breathing, bhikkhus," etc., speaking of the mindfulness of breathing meditation subject in detail.

However, this mindfulness of breathing meditation subject is described in detail in all ways in the *Visuddhimagga*, therefore, its Pali text and method of cultivation should be understood according to the method stated there.

mula_pali:
148. ‘‘Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, ānāpānassati kathaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati satova sato (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) passasati.

‘‘Dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; ‘sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

‘‘‘Pītipaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘pītipaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sukhapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sukhapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittasaṅkhārapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittasaṅkhārapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

‘‘‘Cittapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati ; ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

‘‘‘Aniccānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘aniccānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘virāgānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘virāgānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘nirodhānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘nirodhānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, ānāpānassati evaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā.
mula_english:
“And how, bhikkhus, is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated, so that it is of great fruit and great benefit? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, gone to the wilderness, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty place, sits down, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness in front of him.

Simply mindful, he breathes in; mindful, he breathes out.

“Breathing in long, he understands: ‘I breathe in long’; or breathing out long, he understands: ‘I breathe out long.’ Breathing in short, he understands: ‘I breathe in short’; or breathing out short, he understands: ‘I breathe out short.’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body of breath’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body of breath.’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in tranquillising the bodily formation ( *kāyasaṅkhāra* )’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out tranquillising the bodily formation ( *kāyasaṅkhāra* ).’

“He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing rapture ( *pīti* )’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing rapture ( *pīti* ).’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing pleasure ( *sukha*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing pleasure ( *sukha*) .’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the mental formation ( *cittasaṅkhāra*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the mental formation ( *cittasaṅkhāra*) .’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in tranquillising the mental formation ( *cittasaṅkhāra*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out tranquillising the mental formation ( *cittasaṅkhāra*) .’

“He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the mind (*citta*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the mind (*citta*) .’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in gladdening the mind (*citta*)’; life trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out gladdening the mind (*citta*) .’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in concentrating the mind (*citta*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out concentrating the mind (*citta*) .’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in liberating the mind (*citta*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out liberating the mind (*citta*) .’

“He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating impermanence (*anitya*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating impermanence (*anitya*) .’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating detachment (*virāga*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating detachment (*virāga*) .’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating cessation (*nirodha*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating cessation (*nirodha*) .’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating relinquishment (*patinissagga*)’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating relinquishment (*patinissagga*) .’

“Bhikkhus, that is how mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpānassati*) is developed and cultivated, so that it is of great fruit and great benefit.

mula_pali:
149. ‘‘Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, ānāpānassati kathaṃ bahulīkatā cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti? Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; ‘sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; kāye kāyānupassī, bhikkhave, tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Kāyesu kāyaññatarāhaṃ, bhikkhave, evaṃ vadāmi yadidaṃ – assāsapassāsā. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, kāye kāyānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

‘‘Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘pītipaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘pītipaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sukhapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sukhapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittasaṅkhārapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittasaṅkhārapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; vedanāsu vedanānupassī, bhikkhave, tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanāññatarāhaṃ, bhikkhave, evaṃ vadāmi yadidaṃ – assāsapassāsānaṃ sādhukaṃ manasikāraṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, vedanāsu vedanānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

‘‘Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘cittapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; citte cittānupassī, bhikkhave, tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa ānāpānassatiṃ vadāmi. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, citte cittānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

‘‘Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘aniccānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘aniccānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘virāgānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘virāgānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘nirodhānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘nirodhānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; dhammesu dhammānupassī, bhikkhave, tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. So yaṃ taṃ abhijjhādomanassānaṃ pahānaṃ taṃ paññāya disvā sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, dhammesu dhammānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

‘‘Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, ānāpānassati evaṃ bahulīkatā cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti.
mula_english:
“149. Now, how, bhikkhus, is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so that it fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness? On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu breathing in long, understands, ‘I am breathing in long’; or breathing out long, understands, ‘I am breathing out long’; breathing in short, understands, ‘I am breathing in short’; or breathing out short, understands, ‘I am breathing out short’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in tranquillising the bodily formation’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out tranquillising the bodily formation’; on that occasion, bhikkhus, the bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having eliminated covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

I say that this is a certain body among the bodies, namely, in-breathing and out-breathing.

That is why on that occasion a bhikkhu abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

“On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in experiencing rapture’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out experiencing rapture’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in experiencing pleasure’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out experiencing pleasure’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the mental formation’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the mental formation’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in tranquillising the mental formation’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out tranquillising the mental formation’; on that occasion, bhikkhus, the bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having eliminated covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

I say that this is a certain feeling among the feelings, namely, giving close attention to in-breathing and out-breathing.

That is why on that occasion a bhikkhu abides contemplating feelings as feelings, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

“On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the mind’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the mind’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in gladdening the mind’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out gladdening the mind’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in concentrating the mind’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out concentrating the mind’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in liberating the mind’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out liberating the mind’; on that occasion, bhikkhus, the bhikkhu dwells contemplating mind in mind, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having eliminated covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

I do not say that there is mindfulness of breathing for one who is forgetful, who is not fully aware.

That is why on that occasion a bhikkhu abides contemplating mind as mind, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

“On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in contemplating impermanence’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out contemplating impermanence’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in contemplating fading away’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out contemplating fading away’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in contemplating cessation’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out contemplating cessation’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe in contemplating relinquishment’; trains himself, ‘I shall breathe out contemplating relinquishment’; on that occasion, bhikkhus, the bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having eliminated covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

Having seen with wisdom the abandoning of covetousness and grief, he closely looks on with equanimity.

That is why on that occasion a bhikkhu abides contemplating mind-objects as mind-objects, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.

“Bhikkhus, that is how mindfulness of breathing, developed and cultivated, fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness.
commentary_pali:
149.Kāyaññataranti pathavīkāyādīsu catūsu kāyesu aññataraṃ vadāmi, vāyo kāyaṃ vadāmīti attho. Atha vā rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāroti pañcavīsati rūpakoṭṭhāsā rūpakāyo nāma. Tesu ānāpānaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatane saṅgahitattā kāyaññataraṃ hoti, tasmāpi evamāha. Tasmātihāti yasmā catūsu kāyesu aññataraṃ vāyokāyaṃ, pañcavīsatirūpakoṭṭhāse vā rūpakāye aññataraṃ ānāpānaṃ anupassati, tasmā kāye kāyānupassīti attho. Evaṃ sabbattha attho veditabbo. Vedanāññataranti tīsu vedanāsu aññataraṃ, sukhavedanaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Sādhukaṃ manasikāranti pītipaṭisaṃveditādivasena uppannaṃ sundaramanasikāraṃ. Kiṃ pana manasikāro sukhavedanā hotīti. Na hoti, desanāsīsaṃ panetaṃ. Yatheva hi ‘‘aniccasaññābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā’’ti ettha saññānāmena paññā vuttā, evamidhāpi manasikāranāmena vedanā vuttāti veditabbā. Etasmiṃ catukke paṭhamapade pītisīsena vedanā vuttā, dutiyapade sukhanti sarūpeneva vuttā. Cittasaṅkhārapadadvaye ‘‘saññā ca vedanā ca cetasikā, ete dhammā cittapaṭibaddhā cittasaṅkhārā’’ti (paṭi. ma. 1.174) vacanato ‘‘vitakkavicāre ṭhapetvā sabbepi cittasampayuttakā dhammā cittasaṅkhāre saṅgahitā’’ti vacanato cittasaṅkhāranāmena vedanā vuttā. Taṃ sabbaṃ manasikāranāmena saṅgahetvā idha ‘‘sādhukaṃ manasikāra’’nti āha.

Evaṃ santepi yasmā esā vedanā ārammaṇaṃ na hoti, tasmā vedanānupassanā na yujjatīti. No na yujjati, satipaṭṭhānavaṇṇanāyampi hi ‘‘taṃtaṃsukhādīnaṃ vatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā vedanāva vedayati, taṃ pana vedanāpavattiṃ upādāya ‘ahaṃ vedayāmī’ti vohāramattaṃ hotī’’ti vuttaṃ . Apica pītipaṭisaṃvedītiādīnaṃ atthavaṇṇanāyametassa parihāro vuttoyeva. Vuttañhetaṃ visuddhimagge –

‘‘Dvīhākārehi pīti paṭisaṃviditā hoti ārammaṇato ca asammohato ca. Kathaṃ ārammaṇato pīti paṭisaṃviditā hoti? Sappītike dve jhāne samāpajjati, tassa samāpattikkhaṇe jhānapaṭilābhena ārammaṇato pīti paṭisaṃviditā hoti ārammaṇassa paṭisaṃviditattā. Kathaṃ asammohato (pīti paṭisaṃviditā hoti)? Sappītike dve jhāne samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya jhānasampayuttaṃ pītiṃ khayato vayato sammasati, tassa vipassanākkhaṇe lakkhaṇapaṭivedhā asammohato pīti paṭisaṃviditā hoti. Vuttampi cetaṃ paṭisambhidāyaṃ ‘dīghaṃ assāsavasena cittassa ekaggataṃ avikkhepaṃ pajānato sati upaṭṭhitā hoti, tāya satiyā, tena ñāṇena sā pīti paṭisaṃviditā hotī’ti. Eteneva nayena avasesapadānipi atthato veditabbānī’’ti.

Iti yatheva jhānapaṭilābhena ārammaṇato pītisukhacittasaṅkhārā paṭisaṃviditā honti, evaṃ imināpi jhānasampayuttena vedanāsaṅkhātamanasikārapaṭilābhena ārammaṇato vedanā paṭisaṃviditā hoti. Tasmā suvuttametaṃ hoti ‘‘vedanāsu vedanānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharatī’’ti.

Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassāti ettha ayamadhippāyo – yasmā cittapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmītiādinā nayena pavatto bhikkhu kiñcāpi assāsapassāsanimittaṃ ārammaṇaṃ karoti, tassa pana cittassa ārammaṇe satiñca sampajaññañca upaṭṭhapetvā pavattanato citte cittānupassīyeva nāmesa hoti. Na hi muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa ānāpānassatibhāvanā atthi. Tasmā ārammaṇato cittapaṭisaṃviditādivasena citte cittānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharatīti. So yaṃ taṃ abhijjhādomanassānaṃ pahānaṃ, taṃ paññāya disvā sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hotīti ettha abhijjhāya kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ, domanassavasena byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ dassitaṃ. Idañhi catukkaṃ vipassanāvaseneva vuttaṃ, dhammānupassanā ca nīvaraṇapabbādivasena chabbidhā hoti, tassā nīvaraṇapabbaṃ ādi, tassapi idaṃ nīvaraṇadvayaṃ ādi, iti dhammānupassanāya ādiṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘abhijjhādomanassāna’’nti āha. Pahānanti aniccānupassanāya niccasaññaṃ pajahatīti evaṃ pahānakarañāṇaṃ adhippetaṃ. Taṃ paññāya disvāti taṃ aniccavirāganirodhapaṭinissaggāñāṇasaṅkhātaṃ pahānañāṇaṃ aparāya vipassanāpaññāya, tampi aparāyāti evaṃ vipassanāparamparaṃ dasseti. Ajjhupekkhitā hotīti yañca samathapaṭipannaṃ ajjhupekkhati, yañca ekato upaṭṭhānaṃ ajjhupekkhatīti dvidhā ajjhupekkhati nāma. Tattha sahajātānampi ajjhupekkhanā hoti ārammaṇassapi ajjhupekkhanā, idha ārammaṇaajjhupekkhanā adhippetā. Tasmātiha, bhikkhaveti yasmā aniccānupassī assasissāmītiādinā nayena pavatto na kevalaṃ nīvaraṇādidhamme, abhijjhādomanassasīsena pana vuttānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānañāṇampi paññāya disvā ajjhupekkhitā hoti, tasmā ‘‘dhammesu dhammānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharatī’’ti veditabbo.

Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassā So yaṃ taṃ abhijjhādomanassānaṃ pahānaṃ, taṃ paññāya disvā sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hotī Pahāna Taṃ paññāya disvā Ajjhupekkhitā hotī Tasmātiha, bhikkhave
commentary_english:
149. *Kāyaññatara*nti: I say one among the four bodies, beginning with the earth body; that is, I say the air body.

Alternatively, *rūpāyatanaṃ*...pe... *kabaḷīkāro āhāroti*: the twenty-five rūpa constituents are called the *rūpakāya*.

Among these, because the in-breath and out-breath are included in the touch sense-base (*phoṭṭhabbāyatana*), it is one of the bodies (*kāyaññataraṃ*); therefore, he said this.

*Tasmātihā*ti: Because one observes one of the four bodies, the air body, or among the twenty-five rūpa constituents, one observes the in-breath and out-breath, therefore, the meaning is, one is an observer of the body in the body (*kāye kāyānupassīti*).

The meaning should be understood in this way everywhere.

*Vedanāññatara*nti: One among the three feelings; this was said intending the pleasant feeling (*sukhavedanaṃ*).

*Sādhukaṃ manasikāra*nti: A beautiful attention (*manasikāraṃ*) that has arisen in the manner of experiencing joy (*pītipaṭisaṃveditādivasena*).

But is attention (*manasikāro*) a pleasant feeling (*sukhavedanā*)?

It is not; but this is the main point of the teaching (*desanāsīsaṃ*).

Just as here in "one who is devoted to the practice of the perception of impermanence (*aniccasaññābhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā*)," wisdom (*paññā*) is stated by means of perception (*saññānāmena*), so also here it should be understood that feeling (*vedanā*) is stated by means of attention (*manasikāranāmena*).

In this quatrain, in the first phrase, feeling (*vedanā*) is stated with joy (*pītisīsena*); in the second phrase, it is stated by its own nature as pleasure (*sukha*).

In the two phrases of mental formation (*cittasaṅkhāra*), because of the statement "perception and feeling are mental factors; these things, being bound up with cognizance, are cognizance formations (*saññā ca vedanā ca cetasikā, ete dhammā cittapaṭibaddhā cittasaṅkhārā*)," and because of the statement "having set aside thought and examination, all things associated with consciousness are included in the mental formations (*vitakkavicāre ṭhapetvā sabbepi cittasampayuttakā dhammā cittasaṅkhāre saṅgahitā*)," feeling (*vedanā*) is stated by means of mental formation (*cittasaṅkhāranāmena*).

Having included all that by means of attention (*manasikāranāmena*), here he said "rightful attention (*sādhukaṃ manasikāra*)."

Even so, because this feeling is not an object (*ārammaṇaṃ*), therefore, the contemplation of feeling is not fitting.

No, it is fitting; for even in the Satipaṭṭhāna commentary it was said, "having made the basis of such and such pleasure etc. the object, feeling feels; but depending on that occurrence of feeling, there is only the expression ‘I feel’ (*taṃtaṃsukhādīnaṃ vatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā vedanāva vedayati, taṃ pana vedanāpavattiṃ upādāya ahaṃ vedayāmīti vohāramattaṃ hotī*)."

Moreover, this problem has already been addressed in the explanation of the meaning of *pītipaṭisaṃvedītiādīnaṃ*.

For it was said in the Visuddhimagga –

"Joy is experienced in two ways: with the object and with non-confusion.

How is joy experienced with the object? One enters into the two jhānas with joy; for him, at the moment of attaining that attainment, joy is experienced with the object because of the object being experienced.

How is joy experienced with non-confusion? Having entered into the two jhānas with joy and having arisen, one contemplates the joy associated with the jhāna as decaying and vanishing; for him, at the moment of insight, joy is experienced with non-confusion by means of the penetration of the characteristics.

And this was said in the Paṭisambhidā: ‘For one who knows that the mind’s one-pointedness and non-distraction are due to long in-breaths, mindfulness is established; by that mindfulness, by that knowledge, that joy is experienced.’

The remaining terms should also be understood in meaning in this way."

Thus, just as joy, pleasure, and mental formations are experienced with the object by means of the attainment of jhāna, so also by this attainment of attention designated as feeling (*vedanāsaṅkhātamanasikāra*) associated with jhāna, feeling is experienced with the object.

Therefore, it is well said, "At that time, the monk dwells as an observer of feeling in feelings (*vedanāsu vedanānupassī tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu viharatī*)."

*Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassā*ti: Here, this is the intention – Because a monk who proceeds in the manner of ‘I will breathe in experiencing the mind (*cittapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmīti*),’ etc., although he makes the sign of the in-breath and out-breath the object, nevertheless, because of proceeding by establishing mindfulness and full awareness in the object of that mind, he is indeed called an observer of the mind in the mind (*citte cittānupassīyeva nāmesa hoti*).

For mindfulness of breathing is not possible for one who is unmindful and without full awareness (*muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa ānāpānassatibhāvanā atthi*).

Therefore, at that time, the monk dwells as an observer of the mind in the mind by means of experiencing the mind etc. with the object.

*So yaṃ taṃ abhijjhādomanassānaṃ pahānaṃ, taṃ paññāya disvā sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hotī*ti: Here, with *abhijjhā* is shown the desire for sensual pleasure hindrance (*kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ*), and by means of *domanassa* is shown the ill-will hindrance (*byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ*).
Here, this tetrad is spoken of only in terms of insight (*vipassanā*). And mindfulness of phenomena (*dhammānupassanā*) is sixfold in terms of the section on the hindrances (*nīvaraṇapabbādivasena*), etc. Of that, the section on the hindrances is the beginning. Even of that, this pair of hindrances is the beginning. Thus, to show the beginning of mindfulness of phenomena, he said, "Greed and displeasure."

*Pahāna* means it is intended as the knowledge that causes abandonment, such as abandoning the perception of permanence through contemplating impermanence (*anicānupassanāya niccasaññaṃ pajahatīti evaṃ pahānakarañāṇaṃ adhippetaṃ*).

"Having seen that with wisdom" (*taṃ paññāya disvā*) means having seen that abandoning knowledge (*pahānañāṇaṃ*), which is designated as knowledge of impermanence, detachment, cessation, and relinquishment, with another insight wisdom (*aparāya vipassanāpaññāya*), and that also with another. Thus he shows the succession of insight (*vipassanāparamparaṃ*).

"Remains equanimous" (*ajjhupekkhitā hoti*) means what he regards with equanimity is twofold: one who has undertaken serenity and one who regards attendance with equanimity.

There, there is equanimity towards co-arisen things and there is equanimity towards an object. Here, equanimity towards an object is intended.

"Therefore, here, monks" (*tasmātiha, bhikkhave*) means since one who contemplates impermanence is active in the way of "I will breathe in contemplating impermanence," not only towards phenomena such as the hindrances, but also towards the abandonment knowledge of phenomena spoken of with greed and displeasure as the head, he remains seeing with wisdom, therefore, "a monk dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena at that time" is to be understood.

"Monks, I do not (say there is) mindfulness for one who is forgetful or uncomprehending."

"So, having seen with wisdom that abandonment of greed and displeasure, he remains properly equanimous."

mula_pali:
150. ‘‘Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā kathaṃ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti? Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, upaṭṭhitāssa tasmiṃ samaye sati hoti asammuṭṭhā appammuṭṭhā (syā. kaṃ.). Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno upaṭṭhitā sati hoti asammuṭṭhā, satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti. Satisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

‘‘So tathāsato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicayati pavicarati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) parivīmaṃsaṃ āpajjati.
