166. Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* possesses faith (*saddhā*), possesses virtue (*sīla*), possesses learning (*suta*)… generosity (*cāga*)… and understanding (*paññā*).

He hears that the Two Thousand Brahma…pe… the Three Thousand Brahma… the Four Thousand Brahma… the Five Thousand Brahma is long-lived, beautiful, and enjoys great happiness (*sukhabahuloti*).

Now the Five Thousand Brahma, *bhikkhus*, abides intent on pervading a world-system of five thousand worlds (*pañcasahassilokadhātuṃ pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati*).

And he abides intent on pervading the beings that have reappeared there (*yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati*).

Just as, *bhikkhus*, a man with good sight might take five gallnuts (*āmaṇḍāni*) in his hand and review them; so the Five Thousand Brahma, *bhikkhus*, abides intent on pervading a world-system of five thousand worlds (*pañcasahassilokadhātuṃ pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati*).

And he abides intent on pervading the beings that have reappeared there (*yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati*).

It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), I might reappear in the company of the Five Thousand Brahma (*pañcasahassassa brahmuno sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya*)!’

He fixes his mind on that thought (*cittaṃ dahati*), establishes that thought (*cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti*), develops that thought (*cittaṃ bhāveti*).

These dispositions (*saṅkhārā*) and abidings (*vihārā*) of his, thus developed (*bhāvitā*) and cultivated (*bahulīkatā*), lead to his reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti*).

This, *bhikkhus*, is the path (*maggo*), this is the way (*paṭipadā*) that leads to reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati*).

mula_pali: 167. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena samannāgato hoti, sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘dasasahasso brahmā dīghāyuko vaṇṇavā sukhabahulo’ti. Dasasahasso, bhikkhave, brahmā dasasahassilokadhātuṃ pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati. Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato paṇḍukambale nikkhitto bhāsate ca tapate ca bhāsati ca tapati ca (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) virocati ca; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dasasahasso brahmā dasasahassilokadhātuṃ pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati. Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā dasasahassassa brahmuno sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati.
mula_english:
“Again, O monks, a monk possesses faith (saddhā), possesses virtue (*śīla*), possesses learning (*śruta*), generosity (*cāga*), and wisdom (*prajñā*).

He hears that the Brahma of Ten Thousand (*daśasahasra*) is long-lived (*dīghāyuka*), beautiful (*varṇavān*), and enjoys great happiness (*sukhabahula*).

Now, the Brahma of Ten Thousand (*daśasahasra*), O monks, abides intent on pervading a world-system of ten thousand worlds (*daśasāhassalokadhātu*).

And he abides intent on pervading the beings (*sattva*) that have reappeared there.

Just as a fine beryl gem (*maṇi veḷuriya*) of purest water, eight-faceted (*aṭṭhaṃsa*), well cut (*suparikammakato*), lying on red brocade (*paṇḍukambala*), glows (*bhāsate*) radiates (*tapate*), and shines (*virocati*), so the Brahma of Ten Thousand (*daśasahasra*), O monks, abides intent on pervading a world-system of ten thousand worlds (*daśasāhassalokadhātu*).

And he abides intent on pervading the beings (*sattva*) that have reappeared there.

The bhikkhu thinks: ‘Oh, that on the dissolution of the body (*kāya*), after death (*maraṇa*), I might reappear in the company of the Brahma of Ten Thousand (*daśasahasra*)!’

He fixes his mind on that thought (*citta*), establishes it (*adhiṭṭhāti*), develops it (*bhāveti*).

These aspirations (*saṅkhāra*) and this abiding (*vihāra*) of his, thus developed (*bhāvitā*) and cultivated (*bahulīkatā*), lead to his reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti*).

This, O monks, is the path (*magga*), the way (*pratipadā*) that leads to reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati*)."
commentary_pali: 167.Subhoti sundaro. Jātimāti ākarasampanno. Suparikammakatoti dhovanādīhi suṭṭhukataparikammo. Paṇḍukambale nikkhittoti rattakambale ṭhapito.
commentary_english:
167. *Subho* means beautiful (*sundaraḥ*).

*Jātimā* means endowed with a mine of qualities (*ākarasampannaḥ*).

*Suparikammakato* means well prepared by washing and so on (*dhovanādīhi suṭṭhukataparikammo*).

*Paṇḍukambale nikkhitto* means placed on a red blanket (*rattakambale ṭhapito*).

mula_pali: 168. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena… sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘satasahasso brahmā dīghāyuko vaṇṇavā sukhabahulo’ti. Satasahasso, bhikkhave, brahmā satasahassilokadhātuṃ pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati. Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, nikkhaṃ jambonadaṃ nekkhaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) dakkhakammāraputtaukkāmukhasukusalasampahaṭṭhaṃ paṇḍukambale nikkhittaṃ bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evameva kho, bhikkhave, satasahasso brahmā satasahassilokadhātuṃ pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati. Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā satasahassassa brahmuno sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti . So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati.
mula_english:
Again, bhikkhus, a *bhikkhu* possesses faith (*saddhā*), possesses virtue (*sīla*)… learning (*sutena*)… generosity (*cāga*)… understanding (*prajñā*).

He hears that the Brahma of a Hundred Thousand is long-lived, beautiful, and enjoys great happiness.

Now the Brahma of a Hundred Thousand, *bhikkhus*, abides intent on pervading a world-system of a hundred thousand worlds (*satasahassilokadhātuṃ pharitvā adhimuccitvā viharati*).

And he abides intent on pervading the beings that have reappeared there.

Just as an ornament of finest gold, very skilfully wrought in the furnace by a clever goldsmith, lying on red brocade, glows, radiates, and shines, so the Brahma of a Hundred Thousand abides intent on pervading a world-system of a hundred thousand worlds.

And he abides intent on pervading the beings that have reappeared there.

The *bhikkhu* thinks: ‘Oh, that on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), I might reappear in the company of the Brahma of a Hundred Thousand (*satasahassassa brahmuno sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya*)!’

He fixes his mind on this (*so taṃ cittaṃ dahati*), establishes it (*taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti*), develops it (*taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti*).

These aspirations (*saṅkhārā*) and this abiding (*vihārā*) of his, thus developed and cultivated (*evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā*), lead to his reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti*).

This, *bhikkhus*, is the path (*maggo*), the way (*paṭipadā*) that leads to reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati*).
commentary_pali:
168.Satasahassoti lokadhātusatasahassamhi ālokapharaṇabrahmā. Nikkhanti nikkhena kataṃ piḷandhanaṃ, nikkhaṃ nāma pañcasuvaṇṇaṃ, ūnakanikkhena kataṃ pasādhanañhi ghaṭṭanamajjanakkhamaṃ na hoti, atirekena kataṃ ghaṭṭanamajjanaṃ khamati, vaṇṇavantaṃ pana na hoti, pharusadhātukaṃ khāyati. Nikkhena kataṃ ghaṭṭanamajjanañceva khamati, vaṇṇavantañca hoti. Jambonadanti jambunadiyaṃ nibbattaṃ. Mahājamburukkhassa hi ekekā sākhā paṇṇāsa paṇṇāsa yojanāni vaḍḍhitā, tāsu mahantā nadiyo sandanti, tāsaṃ nadīnaṃ ubhayatīresu jambupakkānaṃ patitaṭṭhāne suvaṇṇaṅkurā uṭṭhahanti, te nadījalena vuyhamānā anupubbena mahāsamuddaṃ pavisanti. Taṃ sandhāya jambonadanti vuttaṃ. Dakkhakammāraputtaukkāmukhasukusalasampahaṭṭhanti dakkhena sukusalena kammāraputtena ukkāmukhe pacitvā sampahaṭṭhaṃ. Ukkāmukheti uddhane. Sampahaṭṭhanti dhotaghaṭṭitamajjitaṃ. Vatthopame (ma. ni. 1.75-76) ca dhātuvibhaṅge (ma. ni. 3.357-360) ca piṇḍasodhanaṃ vuttaṃ. Imasmiṃ sutte katabhaṇḍasodhanaṃ vuttaṃ.

Yaṃ pana sabbavāresu pharitvā adhimuccitvāti vuttaṃ, tattha pañcavidhaṃ pharaṇaṃ cetopharaṇaṃ kasiṇapharaṇaṃ dibbacakkhupharaṇaṃ ālokapharaṇaṃ sarīrapharaṇanti. Tattha cetopharaṇaṃ nāma lokadhātusahasse sattānaṃ cittajānanaṃ. Kasiṇapharaṇaṃ nāma lokadhātusahasse kasiṇapattharaṇaṃ. Dibbacakkhupharaṇaṃ nāma ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā dibbena cakkhunā sahassalokadhātudassanaṃ. Ālokapharaṇampi etadeva. Sarīrapharaṇaṃ nāma lokadhātusahasse sarīrapabhāya pattharaṇaṃ. Sabbattha imāni pañca pharaṇāni avināsentena kathetabbanti.

pharitvā adhimuccitvā

Tipiṭakacūḷābhayatthero panāha – ‘‘maṇiopamme kasiṇapharaṇaṃ viya nikkhopamme sarīrapharaṇaṃ viya dissatī’’ti. Tassa vādaṃ viya aṭṭhakathā nāma natthīti paṭikkhitvā sarīrapharaṇaṃ na sabbakālikaṃ, cattārimāni pharaṇāni avināsetvāva kathetabbanti vuttaṃ. Adhimuccatīti padaṃ pharaṇapadasseva vevacanaṃ, atha vā pharatīti pattharati. Adhimuccatīti jānāti.

Adhimuccatī pharatī Adhimuccatī
commentary_english:
168. "Ten-thousandfold" means a thousandfold world system with light-pervading Brahmā.

"Nikkha" means an ornament made of nikkha. Nikkha is called five *suvaṇṇa*s. An adornment made of an insufficient nikkha is not capable of rubbing and cleaning. An adornment made of an excess [of nikkha] is capable of rubbing and cleaning, but is not attractive and appears to be of coarse material.
An adornment made of nikkha is capable of rubbing and cleaning and is attractive.

"*Jambonada*" means produced in the Jambu River.

Indeed, each branch of the great Jambu tree is fifty by fifty *yojana*s, it has grown. In them, great rivers flow. On both banks of those rivers, golden shoots arise in the place where ripe jambu fruits have fallen. Carried away by the water of the rivers, they gradually enter the great ocean.

Referring to that, it is said "*jambonada*."

"*Dakkhakammāraputtaukkāmukhasukusalasampahaṭṭha*" means well-hammered by a skilled blacksmith's son, having cooked [it] in the *ukkāmukha*.

"*Ukkāmukha*" means in the oven.

"*Sampahaṭṭha*" means washed, rubbed, and polished.

In the *Vatthopama* (Majjhima Nikāya 1.75-76) and in the *Dhātuvibhaṅga* (Majjhima Nikāya 3.357-360), the purification of alms-food is mentioned.
In this *Sutta*, the purification of *katabhaṇḍa* is mentioned.

That which is said, "having pervaded and resolved" in all respects, there are five kinds of pervasion: mind-pervasion (*cetopharaṇa*), *kasiṇa*-pervasion, divine-eye-pervasion (*dibbacakkhupharaṇa*), light-pervasion (*ālokapharaṇa*), and body-pervasion (*sarīrapharaṇa*).

There, mind-pervasion (*cetopharaṇa*) is the knowing of the minds of beings in a thousand world-systems (*lokadhātu*).

*Kasiṇa*-pervasion is the spreading of the *kasiṇa* in a thousand world-systems (*lokadhātu*).

Divine-eye-pervasion (*dibbacakkhupharaṇa*) is, having increased the light, seeing a thousand world-systems (*sahassalokadhātu*) with the divine eye (*dibba cakkhu*).

Light-pervasion (*ālokapharaṇa*) is just that.

Body-pervasion (*sarīrapharaṇa*) is the spreading of the light of the body in a thousand world-systems (*lokadhātu*).

Everywhere, these five pervasions should be spoken without destroying [their meaning].

Having pervaded and resolved, the Elder Cūḷābhaya of the Three Baskets said: "The *kasiṇa*-pervasion is seen like a jewel, the body-pervasion (*sarīrapharaṇa*) is seen like a *nikkha*."

Having rejected his statement that there is no commentary like that saying, body-pervasion (*sarīrapharaṇa*) is not perpetual. These four pervasions should be spoken without destroying [their meaning].

"*Adhimuccatī*" is a synonym for the word "pervasion" (*pharaṇa*), or "*pharatī*" means spreads.

"*Adhimuccatī*" means knows.

*Adhimuccatī*, *pharatī*, *adhimuccatī*.

mula_pali: 169. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena… sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ābhā devā…pe… parittābhā devā… appamāṇābhā devā… ābhassarā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulāti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā ābhassarānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati.
mula_english:
“Again, monks, a *bhikkhu* possesses faith (*śraddhā*), possesses virtue (*śīla*)… learning (*śruta*)… generosity (*tyāga*)… wisdom (*prajñā*).

He hears that the gods of Radiance (*ābhā devā*)… the gods of Limited Radiance (*parittābhā devā*)… the gods of Immeasurable Radiance (*appamāṇābhā devā*)… the gods of Streaming Radiance (*ābhassarā devā*) are long-lived, beautiful, and enjoy great happiness.

The thought occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*maraṇā*), I may be reborn in companionship with the gods of Streaming Radiance (*ābhassarānaṃ devānaṃ*)!’

He fixes his mind on that (*cittaṃ dahati*), establishes it (*cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti*), develops it (*cittaṃ bhāveti*).

Those determinations (*saṅkhārā*) and those abidings (*vihārā*) of his, thus maintained in being (*bhāvitā*) and developed (*bahulīkatā*), lead to his reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti*).

This, monks, is the path (*maggo*), this is the way (*paṭipadā*) that leads to reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati*).
commentary_pali:
169.Ābhātiādīsu ābhādayo nāma pāṭiyekkā devā natthi, tayo parittābhādayo devā ābhā nāma, parittāsubhādayo ca. Subhakiṇhādayo ca subhā nāma. Vehapphalādivārā pākaṭāyeva.

Ime tāva pañca dhamme bhāvetvā kāmāvacaresu nibbattatu. Brahmaloke nibbattaṃ pana āsavakkhayañca kathaṃ pāpuṇātīti? Ime pañca dhammā sīlaṃ, so imasmiṃ sīle patiṭṭhāya kasiṇaparikammaṃ katvā tā tā samāpattiyo bhāvetvā rūpībrahmaloke nibbattati, arūpajjhānāni nibbattetvā arūpībrahmaloke, samāpattipadaṭṭhānaṃ vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikatvā pañcasu suddhāvāsesu nibbattati. Uparimaggaṃ bhāvetvā āsavakkhayaṃ pāpuṇātīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Saṅkhārupapattisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
169. The *ābhā*-deities, etc., namely the *ābhā* deities, are not a single group, [but] three: the *parittābhā* deities are called *ābhā*, as are the *parittāsubhā* deities.

The *subhakiṇhā* deities, etc., are called *subhā*.

The *vehapphalā* deities, etc., are clearly [defined] by their turns.

These five qualities, having cultivated them, may they be reborn in the realms of desire (*kāmāvacara*).

Having been reborn in the Brahma-world (*brahmaloka*), how does one attain the destruction of the influxes (*āsavakkhaya*)? These five qualities are morality (*śīla*). He, having established himself in this morality, having performed the preliminary act of the *kasiṇa*, having cultivated those attainments (*samāpatti*), is reborn in the Brahma-world with form (*rūpībrahmaloka*); having brought about the formless absorptions (*arūpajjhāna*) and having developed insight (*vipaśyanā*) at the base of attainment (*samāpattipadaṭṭhāna*), having realized the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*), he is reborn in the five pure abodes (*pañcasu śuddhāvāsesu*).

Having cultivated the higher path (*uparimagga*), he attains the destruction of the influxes (*āsavakkhaya*).

The commentary on the *Papañcasūdanī Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā*

The exposition of the *Saṅkhārupapattisutta* is finished.

The exposition of the second section is finished.

mula_pali: 170. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena … sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – parittasubhā devā…pe… appamāṇasubhā devā… subhakiṇhā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulāti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā subhakiṇhānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati.
mula_english:
“Again, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possesses faith (saddhā), virtue (sīla)… learning (suta)… generosity (cāga)… and wisdom (paññā).
He hears that the gods of Limited Glory (parittasubhā devā)… the gods of Immeasurable Glory (appamāṇasubhā devā)… the gods of Refulgent Glory (subhakiṇhā devā) are long-lived (dīghāyukā), beautiful (vaṇṇavanto), and abound in happiness (sukhabahulāti).
It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that with the breakup of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), may I be reborn in companionship with the gods of Refulgent Glory (subhakiṇhānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya)!’
He fixes his mind on that (taṃ cittaṃ dahati), establishes it (taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti), develops it (taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti).
These aspirations (saṅkhārā) and this abiding (vihārā) of his, thus developed (bhāvitā) and cultivated (bahulīkatā), lead to his reappearance there (tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti).
This, bhikkhus, is the path (maggo), the way (paṭipadā) that leads to reappearance there (tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati).

mula_pali: 171. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena… sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – vehapphalā devā…pe… avihā devā… atappā devā… sudassā devā… sudassī devā… akaniṭṭhā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulāti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā akaniṭṭhānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati.
mula_english:
“Again, bhikkhus, a *bhikkhu* possesses faith (*śraddhā*), possesses virtue (*śīla*)… learning (*śruta*)… generosity (*tyāga*)… wisdom (*prajñā*).

He has heard: ‘The gods of Great Fruit (*vehapphalā devā*)…the Aviha gods (*avihā devā*)…the Atappa gods (*atappā devā*)…the Sudassa gods (*sudassā devā*)…the Sudassi gods (*sudassī devā*)…the Akanittha gods (*akaniṭṭhā devā*) are long-lived, beautiful, and enjoy great happiness.’

It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*maraṇā*), I might reappear in the company of the Akanittha gods (*akaniṭṭhānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya*)!’

He fixes his mind on that (*cittaṃ dahati*), establishes it (*cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti*), develops it (*cittaṃ bhāveti*).

These aspirations (*saṅkhārā*) and this abiding (*vihārā*) of his, thus developed (*bhāvitā*) and cultivated (*bahulīkatā*), lead to his reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti*).

This, *bhikkhus*, is the path (*maggo*), the way (*paṭipadā*) that leads to reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati*).

mula_pali: 172. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena… sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā devā dīghāyukā ciraṭṭhitikā sukhabahulā’ti . Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati.
mula_english:
“Again, *bhikkhus*, a *bhikkhu* possesses faith (*śraddhā*), possesses virtue (*śīla*)… learning (*śruta*)… generosity (*tyāga*)… wisdom (*prajñā*).

He hears that the gods of the base of infinite space (*ākāśānañcāyatana*)... are long-lived, long-enduring, and enjoy great happiness.

It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that on the dissolution of the body (*kāya*), after death (*maraṇa*), I might reappear in the company of the gods of the base of infinite space (*ākāśānañcāyatana*)!’

He fixes his mind on this thought (*citta*), establishes his mind on this thought, develops his mind on this thought.

These mental formations (*saṃskāra*) and abidings (*vihāra*) of his, thus developed and cultivated, lead to his reappearance there.

This, *bhikkhus*, is the path (*mārga*), this is the way (*pratipadā*) that leads to reappearance there.

mula_pali: 173. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena… sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā devā dīghāyukā ciraṭṭhitikā sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā viññāṇañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati.
mula_english:
173. Again, monks, a monk possesses faith ( *saddhā*), possesses virtue (*sīla*)… learning (*suta*)… generosity (*cāga*)… wisdom (*paññā*).

He has heard: ‘The gods (*devā*) of the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*) are long-lived (*dīghāyukā*), of enduring duration (*ciraṭṭhitikā*), and abound in happiness (*sukhabahulā*)’

It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), I might reappear in the company (*sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya*) of the gods (*devānaṃ*) of the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*)!’

He fixes his mind on that (*cittaṃ dahati*), establishes his mind on that (*cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti*), develops that mind (*cittaṃ bhāveti*).

These volitional formations (*saṅkhārā*) and abidings (*vihārā*) of his, thus developed (*bhāvitā*) and cultivated (*bahulīkatā*), lead to his reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti*).

This, monks, is the path (*maggo*), this is the way (*paṭipadā*) that leads to reappearance there (*tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati*).

mula_pali: 174. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena… sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā devā…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagā devā dīghāyukā ciraṭṭhitikā sukhabahulāti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti. So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Tassa te saṅkhārā ca vihārā ca evaṃ bhāvitā evaṃ bahulīkatā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattanti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā tatrupapattiyā saṃvattati.
mula_english:
“Again, monks, a *bhikṣu* is endowed with faith (*śraddhā*), is endowed with virtue (*śīla*)… learning (*śruta*)… generosity (*tyāga*)… wisdom (*prajñā*).
He hears that the gods of the sphere of nothingness (*ākiṃcanyāyatana*)…and the gods of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana*) are long-lived, long-enduring, and abound in happiness (*sukhabahula*).
It occurs to him: ‘Oh, that on the dissolution of the body (*kāya*), after death (*maraṇa*), I might reappear in the company of the gods of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana*)!’
He fixes his mind (*citta*) on this, establishes his mind on this, develops this mind.
Those volitional formations (*saṃskāra*) and those dwellings (*vihāra*) of his, thus developed and cultivated, conduce to reappearance there.
This, monks, is the path (*mārga*), this is the practice (*pratipadā*) that leads to reappearance there.

mula_pali:
175. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhāya samannāgato hoti, sīlena… sutena… cāgena… paññāya samannāgato hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti. So āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na katthaci upapajjatī’’ti na katthaci upapajjati, na kuhiñci upapajjatīti (sī. pī.), na katthaci upapajjati, na kuhiñci upasampajja viharatīti. (ka.).

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Saṅkhārupapattisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

Anupadavaggo niṭṭhito dutiyo.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Anupāda-sodhana-porisadhammo, sevitabba-bahudhātu-vibhatti;

Buddhassa kittināma-cattārīsena, ānāpāno kāyagato upapatti ito paraṃ syā. kaṃ. ka. potthakesu evampi dissati –-§candake vimale parisuddhe, puṇṇasammodinirodhaattano;§dandhā bahujanasevitaṃ dhammavaraṃ, yaṃ anupadaṃ vaggavaraṃ dutiyāti.

ito paraṃ syā. kaṃ. ka. potthakesu evampi dissati –-§candake vimale parisuddhe, puṇṇasammodinirodhaattano;§dandhā bahujanasevitaṃ dhammavaraṃ, yaṃ anupadaṃ vaggavaraṃ dutiyāti
mula_english:
175. Furthermore, monks, a *bhikṣu* possesses faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

He thinks: ‘Oh, that by realising for myself with direct knowledge, I might here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the destruction of the taints!’

By the destruction of the taints, in very life he enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, realizing it for himself with direct knowledge.

“This *bhikṣu*, monks, does not come into being anywhere.”

This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those *bhikṣus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Saṅkhārupapattisutta, the tenth, is finished.

The Anupadavagga, the second, is finished.

Its summary:

Anupāda-sodhana-porisadhammo, sevitabba-bahudhātu-vibhatti;

buddhassa kittināma-cattārīsena, ānāpāno kāyagato upapatti.

mula_pali: 176. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde. Atha kho āyasmā ānando sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ekamidaṃ, bhante, samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati nagarakaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo. Tattha me, bhante, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘suññatāvihārenāhaṃ, ānanda, etarahi bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti. Kacci metaṃ, bhante, sussutaṃ suggahitaṃ sumanasikataṃ sūpadhārita’’nti? ‘‘Taggha te etaṃ, ānanda, sussutaṃ suggahitaṃ sumanasikataṃ sūpadhāritaṃ. Pubbepāhaṃ pubbecāhaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), ānanda, etarahipi etarahi ca (sabbattha) suññatāvihārena bahulaṃ viharāmi. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, ayaṃ migāramātupāsādo suñño hatthigavassavaḷavena, suñño jātarūparajatena, suñño itthipurisasannipātena atthi cevidaṃ asuññataṃ yadidaṃ – bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭicca ekattaṃ; evameva kho, ānanda, bhikkhu amanasikaritvā gāmasaññaṃ, amanasikaritvā manussasaññaṃ, araññasaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattaṃ . Tassa araññasaññāya cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘ye assu darathā gāmasaññaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, ye assu darathā manussasaññaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, atthi cevāyaṃ darathamattā yadidaṃ – araññasaññaṃ paṭicca ekatta’nti. So ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ gāmasaññāyā’ti pajānāti, ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ manussasaññāyā’ti pajānāti, ‘atthi cevidaṃ asuññataṃ yadidaṃ – araññasaññaṃ paṭicca ekatta’nti. Iti yañhi kho tattha na hoti tena taṃ suññaṃ samanupassati, yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti taṃ ‘santamidaṃ atthī’’’ti pajānāti. Evampissa esā, ānanda, yathābhuccā avipallatthā parisuddhā suññatāvakkanti bhavati.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park, in Migāramātā’s mansion.

Then Venerable Ānanda, arising from seclusion in the late afternoon, went to the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, on one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at a town of the Sakyans named Nagaraka.

There, venerable sir, I heard and learned this from the Blessed One's own lips: 'Now, Ānanda, I often abide in voidness ( *śūnyatāvihāra* ).'

Bhante, did I hear that correctly from the Blessed One, grasp it correctly, attend to it correctly, remember it correctly?"

"Indeed, Ānanda, you heard that correctly, grasped it correctly, attended to it correctly, remembered it correctly.

Before, Ānanda, and now, I often abide in voidness ( *śūnyatāvihāra* ).

Ānanda, just as this Migāramātā’s mansion is void of elephants, cattle, horses, and mares, void of gold and silver, void of the assembly of men and women, and there is present only this non-voidness, namely, the singleness dependent on the Saṅgha of *bhikkhus*; so too, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu*—not attending to the perception of village (*grāmasaṃjñā*), not attending to the perception of people (*manuṣyasaṃjñā*)—attends to the singleness dependent on the perception of forest (*araṇyasaṃjñā*).

His mind enters into that perception of forest (*araṇyasaṃjñā*) and acquires confidence, steadiness, and resolution.

He understands thus: ‘Whatever disturbances there might be dependent on the perception of village (*grāmasaṃjñā*), those are not present here; whatever disturbances there might be dependent on the perception of people (*manuṣyasaṃjñā*), those are not present here. There is present only this amount of disturbance, namely, the singleness dependent on the perception of forest (*araṇyasaṃjñā*).’

He understands: ‘This field of perception (*saṃjñāgata*) is void of the perception of village (*grāmasaṃjñā*); this field of perception is void of the perception of people (*manuṣyasaṃjñā*). There is present only this non-voidness, namely, the singleness dependent on the perception of forest (*araṇyasaṃjñā*).’

Thus he regards it as void of what is not there, but as to what remains there he understands that which is present thus: ‘This is present.’

Thus, Ānanda, this is his genuine, undistorted, pure descent into voidness (*śūnyatāvakkanti*).
commentary_pali:
176.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷasuññatasuttaṃ. Tattha ekamidanti thero kira bhagavato vattaṃ katvā attano divāṭṭhānaṃ gantvā kālaparicchedaṃ katvā nibbānārammaṇaṃ suññatāphalasamāpattiṃ appetvā nisinno yathāparicchedena vuṭṭhāsi. Athassa saṅkhārā suññato upaṭṭhahiṃsu. So suññatākathaṃ sotukāmo jāto. Athassa etadahosi – ‘‘na kho pana sakkā dhurena dhuraṃ paharantena viya gantvā ‘suññatākathaṃ me, bhante, kathethā’ti bhagavantaṃ vattuṃ, handāhaṃ yaṃ me bhagavā nagarakaṃ upanissāya viharanto ekaṃ kathaṃ kathesi, taṃ sāremi, evaṃ me bhagavā suññatākathaṃ kathessatī’’ti dasabalaṃ sārento ekamidantiādimāha.

Tattha idanti nipātamattameva. Kaccimetaṃ, bhanteti thero ekapade ṭhatvā saṭṭhipadasahassāni uggahetvā dhāretuṃ samattho, kiṃ so ‘‘suññatāvihārenā’’ti ekaṃ padaṃ dhāretuṃ na sakkhissati, sotukāmena pana jānantena viya pucchituṃ na vaṭṭati, pākaṭaṃ katvā vitthāriyamānaṃ suññatākathaṃ sotukāmo ajānanto viya evamāha. Eko ajānantopi jānanto viya hoti, thero evarūpaṃ kohaññaṃ kiṃ karissati, attano jānanaṭṭhānepi bhagavato apacitiṃ dassetvā ‘‘kaccimeta’’ntiādimāha.

ida Kaccimetaṃ, bhante

Pubbepīti paṭhamabodhiyaṃ nagarakaṃ upanissāya viharaṇakālepi. Etarahipīti idānipi. Evaṃ pana vatvā cintesi – ‘‘ānando suññatākathaṃ sotukāmo, eko pana sotuṃ sakkoti, na uggahetuṃ, eko sotumpi uggahetumpi sakkoti, na kathetuṃ, ānando pana sotumpi sakkoti uggahetumpi kathetumpi, (kathemissa) suññatākatha’’nti. Iti taṃ kathento seyyathāpītiādimāha. Tattha suñño hatthigavāssavaḷavenāti tattha kaṭṭharūpapotthakarūpacittarūpavasena katā hatthiādayo atthi, vessavaṇamandhātādīnaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhāne cittakammavasena katampi, ratanaparikkhatānaṃ vātapānadvārabandhamañcapīṭhādīnaṃ vasena saṇṭhitampi, jiṇṇapaṭisaṅkharaṇatthaṃ ṭhapitampi jātarūparajataṃ atthi, kaṭṭharūpādivasena katā dhammasavanapañhapucchanādivasena āgacchantā ca itthipurisāpi atthi, tasmā na so tehi suñño. Indriyabaddhānaṃ saviññāṇakānaṃ hatthiādīnaṃ, icchiticchitakkhaṇe paribhuñjitabbassa jātarūparajatassa, nibaddhavāsaṃ vasantānaṃ itthipurisānañca abhāvaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Pubbepī Etarahipī seyyathāpī suñño hatthigavāssavaḷavenā

Bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭiccāti bhikkhūsu hi piṇḍāya paviṭṭhesupi vihārabhattaṃ sādiyantehi bhikkhūhi ceva gilānagilānupaṭṭhākauddesacīvarakammapasutādīhi ca bhikkhūhi so asuññova hoti, iti niccampi bhikkhūnaṃ atthitāya evamāha. Ekattanti ekabhāvaṃ, ekaṃ asuññataṃ atthīti attho. Eko asuññabhāvo atthīti vuttaṃ hoti. Amanasikaritvāti citte akatvā anāvajjitvā apaccavekkhitvā. Gāmasaññanti gāmoti pavattavasena vā kilesavasena vā uppannaṃ gāmasaññaṃ. Manussasaññāyapi eseva nayo. Araññasaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattanti idaṃ araññaṃ, ayaṃ rukkho, ayaṃ pabbato, ayaṃ nīlobhāso vanasaṇḍoti evaṃ ekaṃ araññaṃyeva paṭicca araññasaññaṃ manasi karoti. Pakkhandatīti otarati. Adhimuccatīti evanti adhimuccati. Ye assu darathāti ye ca pavattadarathā vā kilesadarathā vā gāmasaññaṃ paṭicca bhaveyyuṃ, te idha araññasaññāya na santi. Dutiyapadepi eseva nayo. Atthi cevāyanti ayaṃ pana ekaṃ araññasaññaṃ paṭicca uppajjamānā pavattadarathamattā atthi.

Bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭiccā Ekatta Amanasikaritvā Gāmasañña Araññasaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekatta Pakkhandatī Adhimuccatī Ye assu darathā Atthi cevāya

Yañhikho tattha na hotīti yaṃ migāramātupāsāde hatthiādayo viya imissā araññasaññāya gāmasaññāmanussasaññāvasena uppajjamānaṃ pavattadarathakilesadarathajātaṃ, taṃ na hoti. Yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭhanti yaṃ migāramātupāsāde bhikkhusaṅgho viya tattha araññasaññāya pavattadarathamattaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti. Taṃ santamidaṃ atthīti pajānātīti taṃ vijjamānameva ‘‘atthi ida’’nti pajānāti, suññatāvakkantīti suññatānibbatti.

Yañhi kho tattha na hotī Yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭha Taṃ santamidaṃ atthīti pajānātī suññatāvakkantī
commentary_english:
176. *Evaṃ me suta* is the Cūḷasuññatasutta.

There, *ekam idaṃ* means: it seems that the Elder, having performed his duties to the Blessed One, went to his daytime dwelling, set a time limit, relinquished the emptiness-fruit attainment that had nibbāna as its object, and sat down. As the time limit expired, he arose. Then, emptiness presented itself to his mental formations (saṅkhārā). He became desirous of hearing a talk on emptiness. Then, this occurred to him: "It is not possible to go to the Blessed One and say, 'Venerable sir, please give me a talk on emptiness,' as if striking one burden against another. Suppose I recall that talk which the Blessed One gave when he was staying near Nagaraka. In this way, the Blessed One will give me a talk on emptiness." Recalling the Ten-Powered One, he said *ekam idaṃ*, and so on.

There, *idaṃ* is merely a particle.

*Kaccimetaṃ, bhante*: the Elder was capable of learning and retaining sixty thousand verses while standing in one place. Would he not be capable of retaining one word, "*suññatāvihārena*"? However, it is not proper to ask as if knowing, when one is desirous of hearing. He spoke thus as if not knowing, being desirous of hearing a talk on emptiness that was made manifest and expanded upon. One who does not know is like one who knows. What will the Elder do with such pretending? Showing respect to the Blessed One even in his place of knowing, he said *kaccimetaṃ*, and so on.

*idaṃ kaccimetaṃ, bhante*

*Pubbe pi* means: even at the time of the first enlightenment, while dwelling near Nagaraka.

*Etarahi pi* means: even now.

Having spoken thus, he thought: "Ānanda is desirous of hearing a talk on emptiness. One is capable of hearing, but not of learning. One is capable of both hearing and learning, but not of speaking. But Ānanda is capable of hearing, learning, and speaking; [therefore I will give] a talk on emptiness."

Thus, while speaking about him, he said *seyyathāpi*, and so on.

There, *suñño hatthigavāssavaḷavena*: there, elephants and so on made of wood, book covers, and paintings exist. And in the places of Vessavaṇa, Mandhātā, and others, things made by means of painting exist. And things arranged by means of jeweled windows, doorframes, couches, and chairs exist. And gold and silver placed for the purpose of renovating what is old exists. And men and women coming for the sake of hearing the Dhamma, asking questions, and so on, who are made of wood and so on, also exist. Therefore, it is not empty of these things. This was said having in mind the absence of elephants and so on that are bound by the senses and have consciousness, the absence of gold and silver that is to be used at any desired moment, and the absence of men and women who dwell in constant residence.

*pubbe pi etarahi pi seyyathāpi suñño hatthigavāssavaḷavena*

*Bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭicca*: even when the monks have entered for alms, it is not empty because of the monks who partake of monastery meals, and because of the monks who are diligent in tending to the sick, attending to the sick, giving instructions, doing robe work, and so on. Thus, he spoke thus because of the constant existence of monks.

*Ekattaṃ* means: a single state, meaning there is one non-emptiness. It has been said that there is one non-empty state.

*Amanasikaritvā*: not making it in the mind, not considering, not reflecting.

*Gāmasaññaṃ*: the perception of a village that has arisen by way of continuity or by way of defilements. The same method applies to the perception of human beings.

*Araññasaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattaṃ*: regarding the perception of the forest, he focuses his mind on one thing, thinking, "This is the forest, this is the tree, this is the mountain, this is the blue-hued forest thicket." Thus, regarding only one forest, he focuses his mind on the perception of the forest.

*Pakkhandati*: he descends.

*Adhimuccati*: he is resolved that it is so.

*Ye assu darathā*: those disturbances, whether disturbances of continuity or disturbances of defilements, that would occur regarding the perception of the village, do not exist here in the perception of the forest. The same method applies in the second phrase as well.

*Atthi cevāyaṃ*: but this mere disturbance of continuity that arises regarding one perception of the forest exists.

*bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭicca ekattaṃ amanasikaritvā gāmasaññaṃ araññasaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattaṃ pakkhandati adhimuccati ye assu darathā atthi cevāyaṃ*

*Yañhi kho tattha na hoti*: whatever sort of continuity-disturbance or defilement-disturbance arises by way of the perception of the village or the perception of human beings in this perception of the forest, just as the elephants and so on [were absent] in the Migāramātupāsāda, that does not exist.

*Yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭhaṃ*: just as the community of monks [was present] in the Migāramātupāsāda, whatever mere continuity-disturbance is left there in the perception of the forest remains.

*Taṃ santam idaṃ atthīti pajānāti*: he understands that, just as it exists, "this exists." *Suññatāvakkanti*: the arising of emptiness.
yañhi kho tattha na hotī yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭhaṃ taṃ santamidaṃ atthīti pajānāti suññatāvakkantī

mula_pali: 177. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu amanasikaritvā manussasaññaṃ, amanasikaritvā araññasaññaṃ, pathavīsaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattaṃ. Tassa pathavīsaññāya cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, āsabhacammaṃ saṅkusatena suvihataṃ vigatavalikaṃ; evameva kho, ānanda, bhikkhu yaṃ imissā pathaviyā ukkūlavikkūlaṃ nadīviduggaṃ khāṇukaṇṭakaṭṭhānaṃ pabbatavisamaṃ taṃ sabbaṃ sabbaṃ (ka.) amanasikaritvā pathavīsaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattaṃ. Tassa pathavīsaññāya cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘ye assu darathā manussasaññaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, ye assu darathā araññasaññaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, atthi cevāyaṃ darathamattā yadidaṃ – pathavīsaññaṃ paṭicca ekatta’nti. So ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ manussasaññāyā’ti pajānāti, ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ araññasaññāyā’ti pajānāti, ‘atthi cevidaṃ asuññataṃ yadidaṃ – pathavīsaññaṃ paṭicca ekatta’nti. Iti yañhi kho tattha na hoti tena taṃ suññaṃ samanupassati, yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti taṃ ‘santamidaṃ atthī’ti pajānāti. Evampissa esā, ānanda, yathābhuccā avipallatthā parisuddhā suññatāvakkanti bhavati.
mula_english:
“Again, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* - not attending to the perception of people (*manussasaññaṃ*), not attending to the perception of forest (*araññasaññaṃ*) - attends to the singleness dependent on the perception of earth (*pathavīsaññaṃ*).

His mind enters into that perception of earth (*pathavīsaññāya*) and acquires confidence, steadiness, and decision.

Just as a bull’s hide becomes free from folds when fully stretched with a hundred pegs; so too, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* - not attending to any of the ridges and hollows of this earth, to the rivers and ravines, the tracts of stumps and thorns, the mountains and uneven places - attends to the singleness dependent on the perception of earth (*pathavīsaññaṃ*).

His mind enters into that perception of earth (*pathavīsaññāya*) and acquires confidence, steadiness, and decision.

He understands thus: ‘Whatever disturbances there might be dependent on the perception of people (*manussasaññaṃ*), those are not present here; whatever disturbances there might be dependent on the perception of forest (*araññasaññaṃ*), those are not present here. There is present only this amount of disturbance, namely, the singleness dependent on the perception of earth (*pathavīsaññaṃ*).’

He understands: ‘This field of perception is void of the perception of people (*manussasaññāya*); this field of perception is void of the perception of forest (*araññasaññāya*). There is present only this non-voidness, namely, the singleness dependent on the perception of earth (*pathavīsaññaṃ*).’

Thus he regards it as void of what is not there, but as to what remains there he understands that which is present thus: ‘This is present.’

Thus, Ānanda, this is his genuine, undistorted, pure descent into voidness (*suññatāvakkanti*).
commentary_pali:
177.Amanasikaritvāmanussasaññanti idha gāmasaññaṃ na gaṇhāti. Kasmā? Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘manussasaññāya gāmasaññaṃ nivattetvā, araññasaññāya manussasaññaṃ, pathavīsaññāya araññasaññaṃ, ākāsānañcāyatanasaññāya pathavīsaññaṃ…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāya ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṃ , vipassanāya nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññaṃ, maggena vipassanaṃ nivattetvā anupubbena accantasuññataṃ nāma dassessāmī’’ti. Tasmā evaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha pathavīsaññanti kasmā araññasaññaṃ pahāya pathavīsaññaṃ manasi karoti? Araññasaññāya visesānadhigamanato. Yathā hi purisassa ramaṇīyaṃ khettaṭṭhānaṃ disvā – ‘‘idha vuttā sāliādayo suṭṭhu sampajjissanti, mahālābhaṃ labhissāmī’’ti sattakkhattumpi khettaṭṭhānaṃ olokentassa sāliādayo na sampajjanteva, sace pana taṃ ṭhānaṃ vihatakhāṇukakaṇṭakaṃ katvā kasitvā vapati, evaṃ sante sampajjanti, evameva – ‘‘idaṃ araññaṃ, ayaṃ rukkho, ayaṃ pabbato, ayaṃ nīlobhāso vanasaṇḍo’’ti sacepi sattakkhattuṃ araññasaññaṃ manasi karoti, nevūpacāraṃ na samādhiṃ pāpuṇāti, pathavīsaññāya panassa dhuvasevanaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ pathavīkasiṇaṃ parikammaṃ katvā jhānāni nibbattetvā jhānapadaṭṭhānampi vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā sakkā arahattaṃ pāpuṇituṃ. Tasmā araññasaññaṃ pahāya pathavīsaññaṃ manasi karoti. Paṭiccāti paṭicca sambhūtaṃ.

Idāni yasmiṃ pathavīkasiṇe so pathavīsaññī hoti, tassa opammadassanatthaṃ seyyathāpītiādimāha. Tattha usabhassa etanti āsabhaṃ. Aññesaṃ pana gunnaṃ gaṇḍāpi honti pahārāpi. Tesañhi cammaṃ pasāriyamānaṃ nibbalikaṃ na hoti, usabhassa lakkhaṇasampannatāya te dosā natthi. Tasmā tassa cammaṃ gahitaṃ. Saṅkusatenāti khilasatena. Suvihatanti pasāretvā suṭṭhu vihataṃ. Ūnakasatasaṅkuvihatañhi nibbalikaṃ na hoti, saṅkusatena vihataṃ bheritalaṃ viya nibbalikaṃ hoti. Tasmā evamāha. Ukkūlavikkūlanti uccanīcaṃ thalaṭṭhānaṃ ninnaṭṭhānaṃ. Nadīvidugganti nadiyo ceva duggamaṭṭhānañca. Pathavīsaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattanti kasiṇapathaviyaṃyeva paṭicca sambhūtaṃ ekaṃ saññaṃ manasi karoti. Darathamattāti ito paṭṭhāya sabbavāresu pavattadarathavasena darathamattā veditabbā.

seyyathāpī āsabhaṃ Saṅkusatenā Suvihata Ukkūlavikkūla Nadīvidugga Pathavīsaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekatta Darathamattā
commentary_english:
177. *Amanasikaritvā manussasañña* means here that the perception of a village is not taken into consideration. Why? It seems that the following occurred to him: "Having dismissed the perception of a village by means of the perception of a human being, the perception of a human being by means of the perception of a forest, the perception of a forest by means of the perception of earth, the perception of earth by means of the perception of the sphere of infinite space… and the perception of the sphere of nothingness by means of the perception of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, having dismissed the perception of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by means of insight, and insight by means of the path, I will show complete emptiness gradually." Therefore, he began the teaching in this way.

Here, with regard to *pathavīsaññaṃ*, why, having abandoned the perception of a forest, does he attend to the perception of earth? Because of not attaining a distinction in the perception of a forest. Just as for a man, having seen a delightful field-site, even if he looks at the field-site seven times, thinking, "Here the rice and other crops will thrive well, I will gain great profit," the rice and other crops do not thrive at all; but if, having made that place free from stumps and thorns, he cultivates it and sows [seeds], thus being the case, they thrive. In the same way, even if one attends to the perception of a forest seven times, thinking, "This is a forest, this is a tree, this is a mountain, this is a grove with a blue gleam," one does not attain even proximity or concentration. However, by means of the perception of earth, constant cultivation is possible, and by making the earth *kasiṇa* the basis for work, having produced the *jhānas* and having developed insight even in the place where the *jhānas* are established, it is possible to attain arhatship. Therefore, having abandoned the perception of a forest, he attends to the perception of earth. *Paṭicca* means having originated dependently.

Now, in which earth *kasiṇa* is he one who has the perception of earth? For the purpose of showing a comparison of that, he said, beginning with *seyyathāpī*. There, *āsabhaṃ* means belonging to a bull (*usabha*). For other cattle, there are both swellings and blows. For when their hide is stretched out, it does not become free from folds; because of the bull's perfection of characteristics, those defects do not exist. Therefore, his hide is taken. *Saṅkusatenā* means with a hundred pegs (*khila*). *Suvihataṃ* means well-stretched, well-beaten. For [a hide] stretched with less than a hundred pegs does not become free from folds; [a hide] stretched with a hundred pegs becomes free from folds, like the surface of a drum. Therefore, he spoke thus. *Ukkūlavikkūla* means high and low places, elevated places, and low-lying places. *Nadīvidugga* means both rivers and difficult places. *Pathavīsaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekatta* means he attends to a single perception, originated dependently, only in the *kasiṇa* earth. *Darathamattā* means "to the extent of being agitated"; from here onward, "to the extent of being agitated" should be understood in terms of agitation occurring in all instances.

Just as a bull's hide, well-stretched with a hundred pegs, free from folds; uneven places; rivers and difficult passages; he attends to singleness dependent on the earth-perception; to the extent of being agitated.

mula_pali: 178. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu amanasikaritvā araññasaññaṃ, amanasikaritvā pathavīsaññaṃ, ākāsānañcāyatanasaññaṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattaṃ. He understands thus: ‘Whatever disturbances (*darathā*) there might be dependent on the perception of the forest (*araññasaññaṃ*), those are not present here; whatever disturbances (*darathā*) there might be dependent on the perception of earth (*pathavīsaññaṃ*) are not present here. He understands: ‘This field of perception is void (*suññamidaṃ*) of the perception of the forest (*araññasaññāyā*); this field of perception is void (*suññamidaṃ*) of the perception of earth (*pathavīsaññāyā*). Thus he regards it as void of what is not there, but as to what remains there he understands that which is present thus: ‘This is present.’

Thus, Ānanda, this is his genuine, undistorted, pure descent into voidness (*śūnyatāvakkanti*).

mula_pali: 182. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu amanasikaritvā ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṃ, amanasikaritvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññaṃ, animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattaṃ. Tassa animitte cetosamādhimhi cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘ye assu darathā ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, ye assu darathā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, atthi cevāyaṃ darathamattā yadidaṃ – imameva kāyaṃ paṭicca saḷāyatanikaṃ jīvitapaccayā’ti . So ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ ākiñcaññāyatanasaññāyā’ti pajānāti, ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāyā’ti pajānāti, ‘atthi cevidaṃ asuññataṃ yadidaṃ – imameva kāyaṃ paṭicca saḷāyatanikaṃ jīvitapaccayā’ti. Iti yañhi kho tattha na hoti tena taṃ suññaṃ samanupassati, yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti taṃ ‘santamidaṃ atthī’ti pajānāti. Evampissa esā, ānanda, yathābhuccā avipallatthā parisuddhā suññatāvakkanti bhavati.
mula_english:
“Again, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu*, not attending to the perception of the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā*), not attending to the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññā*), attends to singleness (*ekattaṃ*) dependent on the signless concentration of mind (*animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ*).

His mind (*cittaṃ*) enters into that signless concentration of mind (*animitte cetosamādhimhi*) and acquires confidence, steadiness, and resolution (*pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati*).

He understands thus (*so evaṃ pajānāti*) : ‘Whatever disturbances (*darathā*) there might be dependent on the perception of the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṃ paṭicca*), those are not present here (*tedha na santi*); whatever disturbances (*darathā*) there might be dependent on the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññaṃ paṭicca*), those are not present here (*tedha na santi*). There is present only this amount of disturbance (*darathamattā*), namely, that connected with the six bases (*saḷāyatanikaṃ*) that are dependent on this body (*imameva kāyaṃ paṭicca*) and conditioned by life (*jīvitapaccayā*) .’

He understands (*so pajānāti*): ‘This field of perception (*saññāgataṃ*) is void (*suññamidaṃ*) of the perception of the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanasaññāyā*)’; ‘This field of perception (*saññāgataṃ*) is void (*suññamidaṃ*) of the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāyā*)’. ‘There is present only this non-voidness (*asuññataṃ*), namely, that connected with the six bases (*saḷāyatanikaṃ*) that are dependent on this body (*imameva kāyaṃ paṭicca*) and conditioned by life (*jīvitapaccayā*)’.

Thus he regards it as void (*suññaṃ samanupassati*) of what is not there (*yañhi kho tattha na hoti*), but as to what remains there (*yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti*) he understands (*pajānāti*) that which is present thus: ‘This is present (*santamidaṃ atthi*) .’

Thus, Ānanda, this is his genuine (*yathābhuccā*), undistorted (*avipallatthā*), pure (*parisuddhā*) descent into voidness (*suññatāvakkanti*) (*evampissa esā … bhavati*).
commentary_pali: 182.Animittaṃ cetosamādhinti vipassanācittasamādhiṃ. So hi niccanimittādivirahito animittoti vuccati. Imameva kāyanti vipassanāya vatthuṃ dasseti. Tattha imamevāti imaṃ eva catumahābhūtikaṃ. Saḷāyatanikanti saḷāyatanapaṭisaṃyuttaṃ. Jīvitapaccayāti yāva jīvitindriyānaṃ pavatti, tāva jīvitapaccayā pavattadarathamattā atthīti vuttaṃ hoti.
commentary_english:
182. *Animittaṃ cetosamādhi* means mindfulness (*vipassanā*) and concentration (*samādhi*) of the mind (*citta*).

That is to say, since it is devoid of the signs of permanence (*nicca*), etc., it is called signless (*animitta*).

*Imameva kāya* shows the basis (*vatthuṃ*) of mindfulness (*vipassanā*).

There, *imamevā* means just this aggregate of the four great elements (*catumahābhūtikaṃ*).

*Saḷāyatanika* means connected with the six sense spheres (*saḷāyatanapaṭisaṃyuttaṃ*).

*Jīvitapaccayā* means that as long as the life faculty (*jīvitindriyānaṃ*) continues, so long does there exist the mere moment of the duration (*pavattadarathamattā*) of life-related conditions (*jīvitapaccayā*), so it is said.

mula_pali: 183. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu amanasikaritvā ākiñcaññāyatanasaññaṃ, amanasikaritvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññaṃ, animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ paṭicca manasi karoti ekattaṃ. Tassa animitte cetosamādhimhi cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘ayampi kho animitto cetosamādhi abhisaṅkhato abhisañcetayito’. ‘Yaṃ kho pana kiñci abhisaṅkhataṃ abhisañcetayitaṃ tadaniccaṃ nirodhadhamma’nti pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘ye assu darathā kāmāsavaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, ye assu darathā bhavāsavaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, ye assu darathā avijjāsavaṃ paṭicca tedha na santi, atthi cevāyaṃ darathamattā yadidaṃ – imameva kāyaṃ paṭicca saḷāyatanikaṃ jīvitapaccayā’ti. So ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ kāmāsavenā’ti pajānāti, ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ bhavāsavenā’ti pajānāti, ‘suññamidaṃ saññāgataṃ avijjāsavenā’ti pajānāti, ‘atthi cevidaṃ asuññataṃ yadidaṃ – imameva kāyaṃ paṭicca saḷāyatanikaṃ jīvitapaccayā’ti. Iti yañhi kho tattha na hoti tena taṃ suññaṃ samanupassati, yaṃ pana tattha avasiṭṭhaṃ hoti taṃ ‘santamidaṃ atthī’ti pajānāti. Evampissa esā, ānanda, yathābhuccā avipallatthā parisuddhā paramānuttarā suññatāvakkanti bhavati.
mula_english:
183.
"Again, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* (monk) not attending to the perception of the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā*), not attending to the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññā*) attends to the singleness dependent on the signless concentration of mind (*animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ*).

His mind enters into that signless concentration of mind and acquires confidence, steadiness, and decision.

He understands thus: ‘This signless concentration of mind is conditioned and volitionally produced (*abhisaṅkhataṃ abhisañcetayitaṃ*)’.

‘But whatever is conditioned and volitionally produced is impermanent (*aniccaṃ*), subject to cessation (*nirodhadhammaṃ*)’ he understands.

When he knows and sees thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*), from the taint of being (*bhavāsava*), and from taint of ignorance (*avijjāsava*).

When it is liberated, there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated (*vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti*)’.

‘Destroyed is birth (*khīṇā jāti*), the spiritual life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming back to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāya*)’ he understands.

He understands thus: ‘Whatever disturbances there might be dependent on the taint of sensual desire, those are not present here; whatever disturbances there might be dependent on the taint of being, those are not present here; whatever disturbances there might be dependent on the taint of ignorance, those are not present here. There is present only this amount of disturbance, namely, that connected with the six bases (*saḷāyatanikaṃ*) that are dependent on this body (*kāyaṃ*) and conditioned by life (*jīvitapaccayā*)’.

He understands: ‘This field of perception is void of the taint of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*); this field of perception is void of the taint of being (*bhavāsava*); this field of perception is void of the taint of ignorance (*avijjāsava*). There is present only this non-voidness, namely, that connected with the six bases that are dependent on this body and conditioned by life’.

Thus he regards it as void of what is not there, but as to what remains there he understands that which is present thus: ‘This is present (*santamidaṃ atthī*)’.

Thus, Ānanda, this is a perfectly pure, unsurpassed, undeceiving, genuine breakthrough to emptiness (*suññatāvakkanti*).
commentary_pali: 183. Puna animittanti vipassanāya paṭivipassanaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Kāmāsavaṃ paṭiccāti kāmāsavaṃ paṭicca uppajjanapavattadarathā idha na santi, ariyamagge ceva ariyaphale ca natthīti vuttaṃ hoti. Imameva kāyanti imaṃ upādisesadarathadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Iti manussasaññāya gāmasaññaṃ nivattetvā…pe… maggena vipassanaṃ nivattetvā anupubbena accantasuññatā nāma dassitā hoti.
commentary_english:
183. Further, "<hi rend="bold">animitta</hi>" is stated to show the counter-vipassanā to vipassanā.

"<hi rend="bold">kāmāsavaṃ paṭicca</hi>" means here there is no arising or occurrence of suffering dependent on the canker of sensual desire; it is stated that it does not exist in the Noble Path and the fruit of the Noble Path.

"<hi rend="bold">imameva kāya</hi>" is stated to show the suffering remaining with the residue of clinging.

Thus, having averted the human perception and the village perception…pe… having averted vipassanā by the path, gradually emptiness beyond measure, namely, is shown.

mula_pali:
184. ‘‘Yepi hi keci, ānanda, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā parisuddhaṃ paramānuttaraṃ suññataṃ upasampajja vihariṃsu, sabbe te imaṃyeva parisuddhaṃ paramānuttaraṃ suññataṃ upasampajja vihariṃsu. Yepi ye (sī. pī.) hi keci, ānanda, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā parisuddhaṃ paramānuttaraṃ suññataṃ upasampajja viharissanti, sabbe te imaṃyeva parisuddhaṃ paramānuttaraṃ suññataṃ upasampajja viharissanti. Yepi ye (sī. pī.) hi keci, ānanda, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā parisuddhaṃ paramānuttaraṃ suññataṃ upasampajja viharanti, sabbe te imaṃyeva parisuddhaṃ paramānuttaraṃ suññataṃ upasampajja viharanti. Tasmātiha, ānanda, ‘parisuddhaṃ paramānuttaraṃ suññataṃ upasampajja viharissāmā’ti viharissāmīti (pī. ka.) – evañhi vo te (ka.), ānanda, sikkhitabba’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Cūḷasuññatasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
184. “Ānanda, whatever ascetics (*śramaṇa*) and priests (*brāhmaṇa*) in the past entered upon and abided in pure, supreme, unsurpassed emptiness (*śūnyatā*), all entered upon and abided in this same pure, supreme, unsurpassed emptiness.

Ānanda, whatever ascetics and priests in the future will enter upon and abide in pure, supreme, unsurpassed emptiness, all will enter upon and abide in this same pure, supreme, unsurpassed emptiness.

Ānanda, whatever ascetics and priests in the present enter upon and abide in pure, supreme, unsurpassed emptiness, all enter upon and abide in this same pure, supreme, unsurpassed emptiness.

Therefore, Ānanda, ‘We shall enter upon and abide in pure, supreme, unsurpassed emptiness’ – thus, Ānanda, should you train yourselves.”

This the Blessed One (*bhagavān*) said. The venerable Ānanda, being pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

The Cūḷasuññatasuttaṃ, the first, is finished.
commentary_pali:
184.Parisuddhanti nirupakkilesaṃ. Anuttaranti uttaravirahitaṃ sabbaseṭṭhaṃ. Suññatanti suññataphalasamāpattiṃ. Tasmāti yasmā atītepi, buddhapaccekabuddhabuddhasāvakasaṅkhātā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Anāgatepi, etarahipi buddhabuddhasāvakasaṅkhātā samaṇabrāhmaṇā imaṃyeva parisuddhaṃ paramaṃ anuttaraṃ suññataṃ upasampajja vihariṃsu viharissanti viharanti ca, tasmā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷasuññatasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
184. *Parisuddha* means without defilement (*nirupakkilesaṃ*).
*Anuttara* means without superior (*uttaravirahitaṃ*), the best of all (*sabbaseṭṭhaṃ*).
*Suññata* means fruition attainment through Voidness (*suññataphalasamāpattiṃ*).
*Tasmā* means because in the past (*atītepi*) there were ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇā*) who were designated as Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and Buddha's disciples (*buddhapaccekabuddhabuddhasāvakasaṅkhātā*).
Also in the future (*anāgatepi*), even now (*etarahipi*), ascetics and Brahmins (*samaṇabrāhmaṇā*)—designated as Buddhas and Buddha's disciples (*buddhabuddhasāvakasaṅkhātā*)—having attained this very purified (*parisuddhaṃ*), supreme (*paramaṃ*), unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*), voidness (*suññataṃ*), lived (*vihariṃsu*), will live (*viharissanti*), and are living (*viharanti ca*); therefore (*tasmā*).
The rest is clear throughout (*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti*).

The *Cūḷasuññatasuttavaṇṇanā* is finished in the *Papañcasūdanī*, a commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

mula_pali: 185. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kapilavatthuṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Kapilavatthusmiṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena kāḷakhemakassa sakkassa vihāro tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Tena kho pana samayena kāḷakhemakassa sakkassa vihāre sambahulāni senāsanāni paññattāni honti. Addasā kho bhagavā kāḷakhemakassa sakkassa vihāre sambahulāni senāsanāni paññattāni. Disvāna bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘sambahulāni kho kāḷakhemakassa sakkassa vihāre senāsanāni paññattāni. Sambahulā nu kho idha bhikkhū viharantī’’ti.
mula_english:
185. Thus have I heard:

On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was living in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in Nigrodha’s Park (nigrodhārāme).

Then, when it was morning, the Blessed One (bhagavā) dressed, and taking his bowl (patta) and outer robe (cīvara), went into Kapilavatthu for alms (piṇḍāya pāvisi).

When he had wandered for alms in Kapilavatthu and had returned from his almsround, after his meal he went to the dwelling of Kalakhemaka the Sakyan (kāḷakhemakassa sakkassa vihāro) for the day’s abiding (divāvihārāya).

Now on that occasion there were many resting places (sambahulāni senāsanāni) prepared in Kalakhemaka the Sakyan’s dwelling.

When the Blessed One (bhagavā) saw this, there were many resting places prepared in Kalakhemaka the Sakyan’s dwelling.

He thought: “There are many resting places prepared in Kalakhemaka the Sakyan’s dwelling.

Do many *bhikkhus* live here?"
commentary_pali:
185.Evaṃme sutanti mahāsuññatasuttaṃ. Tattha kāḷakhemakassāti chavivaṇṇena so kāḷo, khemakoti panassa nāmaṃ. Vihāroti tasmiṃyeva nigrodhārāme ekasmiṃ padese pākārena parikkhipitvā dvārakoṭṭhakaṃ māpetvā haṃsavaṭṭakādisenāsanāni ceva maṇḍalamāḷabhojanasālādīni ca patiṭṭhapetvā kato vihāro. Sambahulāni senāsanānīti mañco pīṭhaṃ bhisibimbohanaṃ taṭṭikā cammakhaṇḍo tiṇasanthāro paṇṇasanthāro palālasanthārotiādīni paññattāni honti, mañcena mañcaṃ…pe… palālasanthāreneva palālasanthāraṃ āhacca ṭhapitāni, gaṇabhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānasadisaṃ ahosi.

Sambahulānu khoti bhagavato bodhipallaṅkeyeva sabbakilesānaṃ samugghāṭitattā saṃsayo nāma natthi, vitakkapubbabhāgā pucchā, vitakkapubbabhāge cāyaṃ nukāro nipātamatto. Pāṭimatthakaṃ gacchante avinicchito nāma na hoti. Ito kira pubbe bhagavatā dasa dvādasa bhikkhū ekaṭṭhāne vasantā na diṭṭhapubbā.

Sambahulā nu kho

Athassa etadahosi – gaṇavāso nāmāyaṃ vaṭṭe āciṇṇasamāciṇṇo nadīotiṇṇaudakasadiso, nirayatiracchānayonipettivisayāsurakāyesupi, manussaloka-devalokabrahmalokesupi gaṇavāsova āciṇṇo. Dasayojanasahasso hi nirayo tipucuṇṇabharitā nāḷi viya sattehi nirantaro, pañcavidhabandhanakammakāraṇakaraṇaṭṭhāne sattānaṃ pamāṇaṃ vā paricchedo vā natthi, tathā vāsīhi tacchanādiṭhānesu, iti gaṇabhūtāva paccanti. Tiracchānayoniyaṃ ekasmiṃ vammike upasikānaṃ pamāṇaṃ vā paricchedo vā natthi, tathā ekekabilādīsupi kipillikādīnaṃ. Tiracchānayoniyampi gaṇavāsova. Petanagarāni ca gāvutikāni aḍḍhayojanikānipi petabharitāni honti. Evaṃ pettivisayepi gaṇavāsova. Asurabhavanaṃ dasayojanasahassaṃ kaṇṇe pakkhittasūciyā kaṇṇabilaṃ viya hoti. Iti asurakāyepi gaṇavāsova. Manussaloke sāvatthiyaṃ sattapaṇṇāsa kulasatasahassāni, rājagahe anto ca bahi ca aṭṭhārasa manussakoṭiyo vasiṃsu. Evaṃ aññesupi ṭhānesūti manussalokepi gaṇavāsova. Bhummadevatā ādiṃ katvā devalokabrahmalokesupi gaṇavāsova. Ekekassa hi devaputtassa aḍḍhatiyā nāṭakakoṭiyo honti, navapi koṭiyo honti, ekaṭṭhāne dasasahassāpi brahmāno vasanti.

nirayo Tiracchānayoniyaṃ Petanagarāni Asurabhavanaṃ Manussaloke Bhummadevatā

Tato cintesi – ‘‘mayā satasahassakappādhikāni cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni gaṇavāsaviddhaṃsanatthaṃ dasa pāramiyo pūritā, ime ca bhikkhū ito paṭṭhāyeva gaṇaṃ bandhitvā gaṇābhiratā jātā ananucchavikaṃ karontī’’ti. So dhammasaṃvegaṃ uppādetvā puna cintesi – ‘‘sace ‘ekaṭṭhāne dvīhi bhikkhūhi na vasitabba’nti sakkā bhaveyya sikkhāpadaṃ paññapetuṃ, sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpeyyaṃ, na kho panetaṃ sakkā. Handāhaṃ mahāsuññatāpaṭipattiṃ nāma suttantaṃ desemi, yaṃ sikkhākāmānaṃ kulaputtānaṃ sikkhāpadapaññatti viya nagaradvāre nikkhittasabbakāyikaādāso viya ca bhavissati. Tato yathā nāmekasmiṃ ādāse khattiyādayo attano vajjaṃ disvā taṃ pahāya anavajjā honti, evamevaṃ mayi parinibbutepi pañcavassasahassāni imaṃ suttaṃ āvajjitvā gaṇaṃ vinodetvā ekībhāvābhiratā kulaputtā vaṭṭadukkhassa antaṃ karissantī’’ti. Bhagavato ca manorathaṃ pūrentā viya imaṃ suttaṃ āvajjitvā gaṇaṃ vinodetvā vaṭṭadukkhaṃ khepetvā parinibbutā kulaputtā gaṇanapathaṃ vītivattā. Vālikapiṭṭhivihārepi hi ābhidhammikaabhayatthero nāma vassūpanāyikasamaye sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ imaṃ suttaṃ sañjhāyitvā ‘‘sammāsambuddho evaṃ kāreti, mayaṃ kiṃ karomā’’ti āha. Te sabbepi antovasse gaṇaṃ vinodetvā ekībhāvābhiratā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Gaṇabhedanaṃ nāma idaṃ suttanti.
commentary_english:
185. It is like this.

This is what I have heard: the *Mahāsuññatasutta*.

There, *kāḷakhemakassā* means he is black in color like the color of a corpse; but Khema is his name.

*Vihāra* means a dwelling made in that same Nigrodha's park, in one part, by erecting a surrounding wall, building a gate house, constructing dwellings like those called haṃsa-vaṭṭaka?, such as a meeting hall, a refectory, and so forth.

*Sambahulāni senāsanāni* means many resting places: bed, chair, mattress, pillow, straw mat, leather mat, spread grass, spread leaves, spread straw and so forth were prepared. They were placed bed touching bed … spread straw touching spread straw, so that it resembled the dwelling place of *bhikkhus* who have formed themselves into a society.

Sambahulā nu kho...

Then it occurred to him: “This social life is developed to the utmost in the round of becoming. As water collects into rivers, so social life is developed by beings in hell, in the animal world, in the realm of ghosts, and in the Asura group; and also in the human world, the divine world, and the Brahma world.

For hell (*nirayo*) is ten-thousand leagues across and is crammed with beings like a tube packed with bath powder. There is no counting or reckoning the beings in the place of torture by the fivefold binding; likewise in the places of paring with adzes and so forth. Such is the way they roast in society.

As to the animal world (*tiracchānayoniyaṃ*) there is no counting or reckoning the termites in a single termite hill; and likewise ants in each ants’ nest.

Such is social life in the animal world too.

*Petanagarāni* cities of departed spirits were full of spirits, and were a gāvuta in extent or half a *yojana*.

Such is social life in the ghost realm, too.

The ten-thousand league sphere of the Asura abode (*asurabhavanaṃ*) is like an earring or hole when the needle is put into the ear .

Such is social life in the Asura Group too.

As regards the human world (*manussaloke*), there were 5,700,000 in the large clans living at Sāvatthī, and inside and outside Rājagaha 1,800,000 people 18 *koṭis*.

Such is social life in certain places of the human world too.

Beginning with the earth deities (*bhummadevatā*), there is social life in the divine world and the Brahma world also.

Each deity has two and a half *koṭis* of dancers, even up to nine *koṭis*. Also there are ten thousand *Brahmās* living in one place.”

*Nirayo*, *tiracchānayoniyaṃ*, *petanagarāni*, *asurabhavanaṃ*, *manussaloke*, *bhummadevatā*

Thereupon he thought: “For four incalculable ages and a hundred thousand aeons the Perfections have been fulfilled by me for the purpose of undoing living in societies. And as soon as these *bhikkhus* have formed themselves into a society and get to delight in society, they will act contrary to that.”

Then feeling concern for the *dhamma*, he thought again: “If it were possible to announce a training precept that two *bhikkhus* should not live in one place I would do so; but that is not possible.

Come now, I will explain the discourse called the *Mahāsuññatāpaṭipatti*, which will be like a looking-glass for those clansmen who desire training, and like the announcement of training precepts at the city gate.

After that, just as *Khattiyas* nobles and so on, seeing their blemishes in that looking glass get rid of them and become unblemished, so indeed, even for 5,000 years after I have attained complete extinction, clansmen delighting in solitude will make an end of the suffering due to the round of becoming by harkening to this discourse and avoiding society.”

And the number of clansmen who, by harkening to this discourse and avoiding society have, as though fulfilling the Blessed One’s wish, made an end of suffering and attained complete extinction is past reckoning.

For in the Vālikapiṭṭhi Monastery in Ceylon the Abhidhamma scholar called the Elder Abhaya, after reciting this discourse together with a number of *bhikkhus* on the occasion of taking up residence for the rainy season, exclaimed: “The Fully Enlightened One enjoins us to act thus; and what are we doing?”

And by avoiding society and delighting in solitude all of them attained *arahatship* within that same rainy season.

This discourse is called the “breaker-up of societies.”

186. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ ghaṭāya sakkassa vihāre cīvarakammaṃ karoti. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena ghaṭāya sakkassa vihāro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘sambahulāni kho, ānanda, kāḷakhemakassa sakkassa vihāre senāsanāni paññattāni. Sambahulā nu kho ettha bhikkhū viharantī’’ti? ‘‘Sambahulāni, bhante, kāḷakhemakassa sakkassa vihāre senāsanāni paññattāni. Sambahulā bhikkhū ettha viharanti. Cīvarakārasamayo no, bhante, vattatī’’ti.

‘‘Na kho, ānanda, bhikkhu sobhati saṅgaṇikārāmo saṅgaṇikarato saṅgaṇikārāmataṃ anuyutto gaṇārāmo gaṇarato gaṇasammudito. So vatānanda, bhikkhu saṅgaṇikārāmo saṅgaṇikarato saṅgaṇikārāmataṃ anuyutto gaṇārāmo gaṇarato gaṇasammudito yaṃ taṃ nekkhammasukhaṃ pavivekasukhaṃ upasamasukhaṃ sambodhisukhaṃ sambodhasukhaṃ (sī. pī.), sambodhasukhaṃ cittekaggatāsukhaṃ (ka.) upari araṇavibhaṅgasutte pana sambodhisukhantveva dissati tassa sukhassa nikāmalābhī bhavissati akicchalābhī akasiralābhīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Yo ca kho so, ānanda, bhikkhu eko gaṇasmā vūpakaṭṭho viharati tassetaṃ bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ taṃ nekkhammasukhaṃ pavivekasukhaṃ upasamasukhaṃ sambodhisukhaṃ tassa sukhassa nikāmalābhī bhavissati akicchalābhī akasiralābhīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

‘‘So vatānanda, bhikkhu saṅgaṇikārāmo saṅgaṇikarato saṅgaṇikārāmataṃ anuyutto gaṇārāmo gaṇarato gaṇasammudito sāmāyikaṃ vā kantaṃ cetovimuttiṃ upasampajja viharissati asāmāyikaṃ vā akuppanti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Yo ca kho so, ānanda, bhikkhu eko gaṇasmā vūpakaṭṭho viharati tassetaṃ bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ sāmāyikaṃ vā kantaṃ cetovimuttiṃ upasampajja viharissati asāmāyikaṃ vā akuppanti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

‘‘Nāhaṃ, ānanda, ekaṃ rūpampi ekarūpampi (sī.) samanupassāmi yattha rattassa yathābhiratassa rūpassa vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā na uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassūpāyāsā.

186. Now on that occasion, the venerable Ānanda, along with many *bhikkhus*, was busy making robes at Ghata the Sakyan’s dwelling.

Then, when it was evening, the Blessed One rose from retreat and went to Ghata the Sakyan’s dwelling. There he sat down on a seat made ready.

Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, many resting places have been prepared in Kāḷakhemaka’s dwelling.

Are many *bhikkhus* living here?”

“Venerable Sir, many resting places have been prepared in Kāḷakhemaka the Sakyan’s dwelling.

Many *bhikkhus* are living here.

Is this our time for making robes, venerable sir?”

“Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* does not shine by delighting in company, by taking delight in company, by devoting himself to delight in company; by delighting in society, by taking delight in society, by rejoicing in society.

Indeed, Ānanda, it is not possible that a *bhikkhu* who delights in company, takes delight in company, and devotes himself to delight in company, who delights in society, takes delight in society, and rejoices in society, will ever obtain at will, without trouble or difficulty, the bliss of renunciation (*naikkhamma-sukhaṃ*), the bliss of seclusion (*paviveka-sukhaṃ*), the bliss of peace (*upasama-sukhaṃ*), the bliss of enlightenment (*sambodhi-sukhaṃ*) [note: *sambodhi-sukhaṃ* (Sī., Pī.), *sambodhi-sukhaṃ cittekaggatā-sukhaṃ* (Ka.) above, in the Araṇavibhaṅgasutta, only *sambodhi-sukhaṃ* is seen] .

But it can be expected that when a *bhikkhu* lives alone, withdrawn from society, he will obtain at will, without trouble or difficulty, the bliss of renunciation (*naikkhamma-sukhaṃ*), the bliss of seclusion (*paviveka-sukhaṃ*), the bliss of peace (*upasama-sukhaṃ*), the bliss of enlightenment (*sambodhi-sukhaṃ*).

[note: *sambodhi-sukhaṃ* (Sī., Pī.), *sambodhi-sukhaṃ cittekaggatā-sukhaṃ* (Ka.) above, in the Araṇavibhaṅgasutta, only *sambodhi-sukhaṃ* is seen]

“Indeed, Ānanda, it is not possible that a *bhikkhu* who delights in company, takes delight in company, and devotes himself to delight in company, who delights in society, takes delight in society, and rejoices in society, will ever enter upon and abide in either the deliverance of mind that is temporary and delectable or in the deliverance of mind that is perpetual and unshakeable.

But it can be expected that when a *bhikkhu* lives alone, withdrawn from society, he will enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind that is temporary and delectable or in the deliverance of mind that is perpetual and unshakeable.

“I do not see even a single kind of form, Ānanda, from the change and alteration of which there would not arise sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair in one who lusts for it and takes delight in it.
commentary_pali:
186.Ghaṭāyāti evaṃnāmakassa sakkassa. Vihāreti ayampi vihāro nigrodhārāmasseva ekadese kāḷakhemakassa vihāro viya katoti veditabbo. Cīvarakammanti jiṇṇamalinānaṃ aggaḷaṭṭhānuppādanadhovanādīhi kataparibhaṇḍampi, cīvaratthāya uppannavatthānaṃ vicāraṇasibbanādīhi akataṃ saṃvidhānampi vaṭṭati, idha pana akataṃ saṃvidhānaṃ adhippetaṃ. Manussā hi ānandattherassa cīvarasāṭake adaṃsu. Tasmā thero sambahule bhikkhū gahetvā tattha cīvarakammaṃ akāsi. Tepi bhikkhū pātova sūcipāsakassa paññāyanakālato paṭṭhāya nisinnā apaññāyanakāle uṭṭhahanti. Sūcikamme niṭṭhiteyeva senāsanāni saṃvidahissāmāti na saṃvidahiṃsu. Cīvarakārasamayo noti thero kira cintesi – ‘‘addhā etehi bhikkhūhi na paṭisāmitāni senāsanāni, bhagavatā ca diṭṭhāni bhavissanti. Iti anattamano satthā suṭṭhu niggahetukāmo, imesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ upatthambho bhavissāmī’’ti; tasmā evamāha. Ayaṃ panettha adhippāyo – ‘‘na, bhante, ime bhikkhū kammārāmā eva, cīvarakiccavasena pana evaṃ vasantī’’ti.

Na kho, ānandāti, ānanda, kammasamayo vā hotu akammasamayo vā, cīvarakārasamayo vā hotu acīvarakārasamayo vā, atha kho saṅgaṇikārāmo bhikkhu na sobhatiyeva. Mā tvaṃ anupatthambhaṭṭhāne upatthambho ahosīti. Tattha saṅgaṇikāti sakaparisasamodhānaṃ. Gaṇoti nānājanasamodhānaṃ. Iti saṅgaṇikārāmo vā hotu gaṇārāmo vā, sabbathāpi gaṇabāhullābhirato gaṇabandhanabaddho bhikkhu na sobhati. Pacchābhatte pana divāṭṭhānaṃ sammajjitvā sudhotahatthapādo mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā ekārāmatamanuyutto bhikkhu buddhasāsane sobhati. Nekkhammasukhanti kāmato nikkhantassa sukhaṃ. Pavivekasukhampi kāmapavivekasukhameva. Rāgādīnaṃ pana vūpasamatthāya saṃvattatīti upasamasukhaṃ. Maggasambodhatthāya saṃvattatīti sambodhisukhaṃ. Nikāmalābhīti kāmalābhī icchitalābhī. Akicchalābhīti adukkhalābhī. Akasiralābhīti vipulalābhī.

Na kho, ānandā saṅgaṇikā Gaṇo Nekkhammasukha Pavivekasukhampi upasamasukhaṃ sambodhisukhaṃ. Nikāmalābhī Akicchalābhī Akasiralābhī

Sāmāyikanti appitappitasamaye kilesehi vimuttaṃ. Kantanti manāpaṃ. Cetovimuttinti rūpārūpāvacaracittavimuttiṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ – ‘‘cattāri ca jhānāni catasso ca arūpasamāpattiyo, ayaṃ sāmāyiko vimokkho’’ti (paṭi. ma. 1.213). Asāmāyikanti na samayavasena kilesehi vimuttaṃ, atha kho accantavimuttaṃ lokuttaraṃ vuttaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ – ‘‘cattāro ca ariyamaggā cattāri ca sāmaññaphalāni, ayaṃ asāmāyiko vimokkho’’ti. Akuppanti kilesehi akopetabbaṃ.

Sāmāyika Kanta Cetovimutti Asāmāyika Akuppa

Ettāvatā kiṃ kathitaṃ hoti? Saṅgaṇikārāmo bhikkhu gaṇabandhanabaddho neva lokiyaguṇaṃ, na ca lokuttaraguṇaṃ nibbattetuṃ sakkoti, gaṇaṃ vinodetvā pana ekābhirato sakkoti. Tathā hi vipassī bodhisatto caturāsītiyā pabbajitasahassehi parivuto satta vassāni vicaranto sabbaññuguṇaṃ nibbattetuṃ nāsakkhi, gaṇaṃ vinodetvā sattadivase ekībhāvābhirato bodhimaṇḍaṃ āruyha sabbaññuguṇaṃ nibbattesi. Amhākaṃ bodhisatto pañcavaggiyehi saddhiṃ chabbassāni vicaranto sabbaññuguṇaṃ nibbattetuṃ nāsakkhi, tesu pakkantesu ekībhāvābhirato bodhimaṇḍaṃ āruyha sabbaññuguṇaṃ nibbattesi.

Evaṃ saṅgaṇikārāmassa guṇādhigamābhāvaṃ dassetvā idāni dosuppattiṃ dassento nāhaṃ ānandātiādimāha. Tattha rūpanti sarīraṃ. Yattha rattassāti yasmiṃ rūpe rāgavasena rattassa. Na uppajjeyyunti yasmiṃ rūpe rattassa na uppajjeyyuṃ, taṃ rūpaṃ na samanupassāmi, atha kho sāriputtamoggallānānaṃ dasabalasāvakattupagamanasaṅkhātena aññathābhāvena sañcayassa viya, upāligahapatino aññathābhāvena nāṭaputtassa viya, piyajātikasutte seṭṭhiādīnaṃ viya ca uppajjantiyeva.
