commentary_english:
186. "Ghaṭāyā" means of Sakka named thus.

"Vihāre" means this monastery is like the monastery of Kāḷakhemaka in one part of Nigrodhārāma, so it should be understood.

"Cīvarakamma" means the accessories that have been prepared with cleaning, dyeing and so on, of old dirty robes; it also applies to the arrangement that has not been prepared with consideration, sewing and so on, of cloths that have arisen for robes; but here, the arrangement that has not been prepared is intended.

People had given the Elder Ānanda material for robes (cīvarasāṭake).

Therefore, the Elder, having taken a number of monks, did work on robes (cīvarakammaṃ) there.

And those bhikkhus, sitting from the time announced for the needle work in the morning, get up from it some time unannounced.

When the sewing is finished we shall set our resting places in order,” they had not set them in order.

"Cīvarakārasamayo no" the Elder thought: "Indeed, the resting places have not been put in order by these bhikkhus, and the Blessed One will see them."

Consequently the Master is displeased and desires to give a severe reproof. I will be a support for those bhikkhus.” That is why he spoke as he did.

The intention here is this: "Venerable Sir, these bhikkhus are living in this way not just because they delight in being busy, but on account of robe-making."

"Na kho, Ānandā" means, Ānanda, whether it is an instance of being busy or whether it is an instance of robe-making or not, still a bhikkhu who delights in company does not shine forth.

Do not be a support where there is no occasion for support.”

"Saṅgaṇikā" means gathering with one’s own community.

"Gaṇo" means gathering with various people.

So whether he delights in company or in society, in either case a bhikkhu who likes the fullness of society, who is bound by the ties of society, does not shine forth.

But it is when a bhikkhu sweeps out his daytime quarters after his meal and, after washing his feet well, takes up his basic meditation subject and devotes himself to delight in solitude, he shines forth in the Buddha’s Dispensation.

"Nekkhammasukha" means the bliss in him who has renounced sense-desires.

"Pavivekasukhampi" is just the bliss of isolation from desires.

That which leads to the subsiding of lust etc., is the bliss of pacification ( *upaśamasukhaṃ* ).

What leads to the enlightenment due to the path is the bliss of enlightenment ( *saṃbodhisukhaṃ* ). *Nikāmalābhī* means obtaining desires, obtaining what is wished for.

*Akicchalābhī* means obtaining without difficulty.

*Akasiralābhī* means obtaining abundantly.

Na kho, Ānandā, Saṅgaṇikā, Gaṇo, Nekkhammasukha, Pavivekasukhampi, Upasamasukhaṃ, Sambodhisukhaṃ. Nikāmalābhī, Akicchalābhī, Akasiralābhī. *Sāmāyika* means freed from defilements at the time of appitappita.

*Kanta* means charming.

*Cetovimutti* means deliverance of the mind in the realms of form and the formless.

For it is said: “The four absorptions (jhāna) and the four immaterial attainments, these are the temporary liberation” (paṭi. ma. 1. 213).

*Asāmāyika* means not deliverance from defilements occasionally but rather deliverance which is perpetual and supramundane (lokuttaraṃ).

For it is said: “The four noble paths and the four fruitions of recluseship, these are the permanent liberation.”

*Akuppa* means not to be shaken by defilements (kilesehi).

What is said by this? A monk who delights in company, who is bound by the bonds of a group, is not able to produce mundane qualities, nor supramundane qualities. But one who delights in solitude is able to do so, having removed the group.

Just as the Bodhisattva Vipassī, while wandering for seven years surrounded by eighty-four thousand homeless ones, was not able to produce the quality of omniscience; but having removed the group, delighting in solitude for seven days, he ascended the seat of enlightenment and produced the quality of omniscience.

Also, as long as our Bodhisattva wandered with the Group of Five for six years, he was unable to produce the quality of omniscience; but when they had left, delighting in solitude, he ascended the seat of enlightenment and produced the quality of omniscience.

Thus, having shown the absence of acquiring qualities of one delighting in company, now, showing the arising of faults, he says, "I, Ānanda..."

There, *rūpa* means body.

*Yattha rattassā* means in whatever form one is colored by passion.

*Na uppajjeyyu* means in whatever form passions would not arise, that form I do not perceive. But rather, through the difference denoted by the statement of Sāriputta and Moggallāna having attained the state of disciples of the Ten Powers, like the difference of Upāligahapati, like Nātaputta, like the merchants and others in the Piyajātika Sutta, they arise.

mula_pali: 187. ‘‘Ayaṃ kho panānanda, vihāro tathāgatena abhisambuddho yadidaṃ – sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ upasampajja viharituṃ viharataṃ (ka. sī.), viharati (syā. kaṃ. ka.). Tatra ce, ānanda, tathāgataṃ iminā vihārena viharantaṃ bhavanti bhagavantaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.) upasaṅkamitāro bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo rājāno rājamahāmattā titthiyā titthiyasāvakā. Tatrānanda, tathāgato vivekaninneneva cittena vivekapoṇena vivekapabbhārena vūpakaṭṭhena nekkhammābhiratena byantībhūtena sabbaso āsavaṭṭhānīyehi dhammehi aññadatthu uyyojanikapaṭisaṃyuttaṃyeva kathaṃ kattā hoti. Tasmātihānanda, bhikkhu cepi ākaṅkheyya – ‘ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ upasampajja vihareyya’nti, tenānanda, bhikkhunā ajjhattameva cittaṃ saṇṭhapetabbaṃ sannisādetabbaṃ ekodi kātabbaṃ samādahātabbaṃ.
mula_english:
187.
“However, Ānanda, there is this abiding discovered by the *Tathāgata* (Tathāgatena abhisambuddho): to enter and abide in voidness internally (*ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ upasampajja viharituṃ*) by giving no attention to all signs (*sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā*).

If, while the *Tathāgata* (tathāgataṃ) is abiding thus in this dwelling (*iminā vihārena viharantaṃ*), he is visited by *bhikkhus* or *bhikkhunīs*, by men or women lay followers (*upāsaka upāsikā*), by kings (*rājāno*) or kings’ ministers (*rājamahāmattā*), by other sectarians (*titthiyā*) or their disciples (*titthiyasāvakā*).

Then, Ānanda, with a mind leaning to seclusion (*vivekaninneneva cittena*), tending and inclining to seclusion (*vivekapoṇena vivekapabbhārena*), withdrawn (*vūpakaṭṭhena*), delighting in renunciation (*nekkhammābhiratena*), and altogether done with (*byantībhūtena sabbaso*) things that are the basis for taints (*āsavaṭṭhānīyehi dhammehi*), the *Tathāgata* invariably talks to them in a way concerned with dismissing them (*aññadatthu uyyojanikapaṭisaṃyuttaṃyeva kathaṃ kattā hoti*).

“Therefore, Ānanda, if a *bhikkhu* should wish: ‘May I enter upon and abide in voidness internally (*ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ upasampajja vihareyya*)’ he should steady his mind internally (*ajjhattameva cittaṃ saṇṭhapetabbaṃ*), quiet it (*sannisādetabbaṃ*), bring it to singleness (*ekodi kātabbaṃ*), and concentrate it (*samādahātabbaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
187.Ayaṃkho panānandāti ko anusandhi? Sace hi koci dubbuddhī navapabbajito vadeyya – ‘‘sammāsambuddho khettaṃ paviṭṭhā gāviyo viya amheyeva gaṇato nīharati, ekībhāve niyojeti, sayaṃ pana rājarājamahāmattādīhi parivuto viharatī’’ti, tassa vacanokāsupacchedanatthaṃ – ‘‘cakkavāḷapariyantāya parisāya majjhe nisinnopi tathāgato ekakovā’’ti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha sabbanimittānanti rūpādīnaṃ saṅkhanimittānaṃ. Ajjhattanti visayajjhattaṃ. Suññatanti suññataphalasamāpattiṃ. Tatra ceti upayogatthe bhummaṃ, taṃ ceti vuttaṃ hoti. Puna tatrāti tasmiṃ parisamajjhe ṭhito. Vivekaninnenāti nibbānaninnena. Byantībhūtenāti āsavaṭṭhānīyadhammehi vigatantena nissaṭena visaṃyuttena. Uyyojanikapaṭisaṃyuttanti gacchatha tumheti evaṃ uyyojanikena vacanena paṭisaṃyuttaṃ.

Kāya pana velāya bhagavā evaṃ katheti? Pacchābhattakiccavelāya, vā purimayāmakiccavelāya vā. Bhagavā hi pacchābhatte gandhakuṭiyaṃ sīhaseyyaṃ kappetvā vuṭṭhāya phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā nisīdati. Tasmiṃ samaye dhammassavanatthāya parisā sannipatanti. Atha bhagavā kālaṃ viditvā gandhakuṭito nikkhamitvā buddhāsanavaragato dhammaṃ desetvā bhesajjatelapākaṃ gaṇhanto viya kālaṃ anatikkamitvā vivekaninnena cittena parisaṃ uyyojeti . Purimayāmepi ‘‘abhikkantā kho vāseṭṭhā ratti, yassa dāni kālaṃ maññathā’’ti (dī. ni. 3.299) evaṃ uyyojeti . Buddhānañhi bodhipattito paṭṭhāya dve pañcaviññāṇānipi nibbānaninnāneva. Tasmātihānandāti yasmā suññatāvihāro santo paṇīto, tasmā.

Tasmātihānandā
commentary_english:
187.

Now then, Ānanda, what is the connection here? If any unintelligent bhikkhu, newly gone forth, should say: “The Fully Enlightened One leads us away from society like cattle sent into a field, and he exhorts us to solitude, but he himself lives surrounded by kings, kings’ ministers, and so on,” for the purpose of removing the occasion for that statement he began this teaching to show that the *Tathāgata* is alone, even when sitting in the midst of a community extending over a world sphere.

There, "all signs" means signs of mental proliferation such as form and so forth.

"Inwardly" means inwardly in relation to the object.

"Voidness" (*śūnyatā*) means the fruition attainment through voidness (*śūnyatāphalasamāpattiṃ*).

There, "in that case" means a locative meaning "use," that is what is said.

Furthermore, "there" means standing in the midst of that assembly.

"Inclining to seclusion" means inclining to *nirvāṇa*.

"Having become devoid" means separated, expelled, and disconnected from the *dharmas* that are the basis of the outflows (*āsava*), having come to an end.

"*Uyyojanikapaṭisaṃyutta*" means "go forth," thus it is connected to dismissal (*uyyojanika*) by way of speech.

At what time does the Blessed One say this? At the time of the after-meal duty, or at the time of the first watch of the night.

For after the meal the Blessed One adopts the lion’s pose in the Perfumed Cell, and then he rises and sits absorbed in fruition attainment.

At that time the community gathers for the purpose of hearing the Dharma.

Then the Blessed One, knowing the time, comes forth from the Perfumed Cell and goes to the excellent seat of the Buddha and teaches the *dharma*. Then, not exceeding the time, like one judging the cooking of a medicinal oil, he dismisses the community with his mind inclining to seclusion.

Also in the first watch of the night, he dismisses the community thus: “The night is well advanced; now it is time to do as you think fit.”

For since reaching enlightenment even the Buddhas’ twofold five-door-consciousness incline to *Nirvāṇa*.

Therefore, Ānanda, because dwelling in voidness is peaceful and sublime, therefore.

mula_pali:
188. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, bhikkhu ajjhattameva cittaṃ saṇṭhapeti sannisādeti ekodiṃ karoti ekodikaroti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) samādahati? Idhānanda, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, bhikkhu ajjhattameva cittaṃ saṇṭhapeti sannisādeti ekodiṃ karoti samādahati. So ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasi karoti. Tassa ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasikaroto suññatāya cittaṃ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati . Evaṃ santametaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu evaṃ pajānāti – ‘ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ kho me manasikaroto ajjhattaṃ suññatāya cittaṃ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccatī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. So bahiddhā suññataṃ manasi karoti…pe… so ajjhattabahiddhā suññataṃ manasi karoti …pe… so āneñjaṃ manasi karoti. Tassa āneñjaṃ manasikaroto āneñjāya cittaṃ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati. Evaṃ santametaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu evaṃ pajānāti – ‘āneñjaṃ kho me manasikaroto āneñjāya cittaṃ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccatī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti.

‘‘Tenānanda, bhikkhunā tasmiṃyeva purimasmiṃ samādhinimitte ajjhattameva cittaṃ saṇṭhapetabbaṃ sannisādetabbaṃ ekodi kātabbaṃ samādahātabbaṃ. So ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasi karoti. Tassa ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasikaroto ajjhattaṃ suññatāya cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati. Evaṃ santametaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu evaṃ pajānāti – ‘ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ kho me manasikaroto ajjhattaṃ suññatāya cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccatī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. So bahiddhā suññataṃ manasi karoti…pe… so ajjhattabahiddhā suññataṃ manasi karoti…pe… so āneñjaṃ manasi karoti. Tassa āneñjaṃ manasikaroto āneñjāya cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati. Evaṃ santametaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu evaṃ pajānāti – ‘āneñjaṃ kho me manasikaroto āneñjāya cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccatī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti.
mula_english:
“And how, Ānanda, does a bhikkhu steady his mind internally, quiet it, bring it to singleness, and concentrate it (samādahati)? Here, Ānanda, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states…he enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*…the second *jhāna*…the third *jhāna*…the fourth *jhāna*. That is how, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* steadies his mind internally, quiets it, brings it to singleness, and concentrates it.

Then he gives attention to voidness internally (ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasi karoti). While he is giving attention to voidness internally (ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasikaroto), his mind does not enter into voidness or acquire confidence, steadiness, and decision. When that is so, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* understands thus: ‘While I am giving attention to voidness internally, my mind does not enter into voidness internally or acquire confidence, steadiness, and decision.’ In this way he has full awareness of that.

He gives attention to voidness externally…He gives attention to voidness internally and externally…He gives attention to imperturbability (*āneñjaṃ*). While he is giving attention to imperturbability (*āneñjaṃ*), his mind does not enter into imperturbability or acquire confidence, steadiness, and decision. When that is so, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* understands thus: ‘While I am giving attention to imperturbability, my mind does not enter into imperturbability or acquire confidence, steadiness, and decision.’ In this way he has full awareness of that.

“Then, Ānanda, that *bhikkhu* should steady his mind internally, quiet it, bring it to singleness, and concentrate it on that same sign of concentration (*samādhi*) as before.

He gives attention to voidness internally (ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasi karoti). While he is giving attention to voidness internally (ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasikaroto), his mind enters into voidness and acquires confidence, steadiness, and decision. When that is so, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* understands thus: ‘While I am giving attention to voidness internally, my mind enters into voidness and acquires confidence, steadiness, and decision.’ In this way he has full awareness of that.

He gives attention to voidness externally…He gives attention to voidness internally and externally…He gives attention to imperturbability (*āneñjaṃ*). While he is giving attention to imperturbability (*āneñjaṃ*), his mind enters into imperturbability and acquires confidence, steadiness, and decision. When that is so, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu* understands thus: ‘While I am giving attention to imperturbability, my mind enters into imperturbability and acquires confidence, steadiness, and decision.’ In this way he has full awareness of that.
commentary_pali:
188.Ajjhattamevāti gocarajjhattameva. Ajjhattaṃ suññatanti idha niyakajjhattaṃ, attano pañcasu khandhesu nissitanti attho. Sampajāno hotīti kammaṭṭhānassa asampajjanabhāvajānanena sampajāno. Bahiddhāti parassa pañcasu khandhesu. Ajjhattabahiddhāti kālena ajjhattaṃ kālena bahiddhā . Āneñjanti ubhatobhāgavimutto bhavissāmāti āneñjaṃ arūpasamāpattiṃ manasi karoti.

Tasmiṃyeva purimasminti pādakajjhānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Apaguṇapādakajjhānato vuṭṭhitassa hi ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasikaroto tattha cittaṃ na pakkhandati. Tato ‘‘parassa santāne nu kho katha’’nti bahiddhā manasi karoti, tatthapi na pakkhandati. Tato – ‘‘kālena attano santāne, kālena parassa santāne nu kho katha’’nti ajjhattabahiddhā manasi karoti, tatthapi na pakkhandati. Tato ubhatobhāgavimutto hotukāmo ‘‘arūpasamāpattiyaṃ nu kho katha’’nti āneñjaṃ manasi karoti, tatthapi na pakkhandati. Idāni – ‘‘na me cittaṃ pakkhandatīti vissaṭṭhavīriyena upaṭṭhākādīnaṃ pacchato na caritabbaṃ, pādakajjhānameva pana sādhukaṃ punappunaṃ manasikātabbaṃ. Evamassa rukkhe chindato pharasumhi avahante puna nisitaṃ kāretvā chindantassa chijjesu pharasu viya kammaṭṭhāne manasikāro vahatī’’ti dassetuṃ tasmiṃyevātiādimāha. Idānissa evaṃ paṭipannassa yaṃ yaṃ manasi karoti, tattha tattha manasikāro sampajjatīti dassento pakkhandatīti āha.

Tasmiṃyeva purimasmi tasmiṃyevā pakkhandatī
commentary_english:
188. *Ajjhattamevā* means just internal range.

*Ajjhattaṃ suññata* means here, "internally in himself," the meaning is: produced in regard to his own five aggregates ( *attano pañcasu khandhesu nissitanti attho*).

*Sampajāno hotī* means he is fully aware through the knowledge of the non-occurrence of non-mentation on the object of meditation.

*Bahiddhā* means in regard to another’s five aggregates.

*Ajjhattabahiddhā* means at one time internally, at one time externally.

*Āneñja* means desiring to become one who is both ways released, he brings to mind the imperturbable, the immaterial attainment (*arūpasamāpattiṃ manasi karoti*).

*Tasmiṃyeva purimasmi* means having in mind the basic jhāna, it was said.

For when one who has emerged from a basic jhāna which is still unfamiliar (*apaguṇapādakajjhānato vuṭṭhitassa*), and brings to mind voidness internally (*ajjhattaṃ suññataṃ manasikaroto*), his mind (*cittaṃ*) does not enter into voidness (*na pakkhandati*).

Thereupon, thinking: “How about another’s continuity of aggregates (*parassa santāne*)?” he brings it to mind externally (*bahiddhā manasi karoti*). There also it does not enter into it (*tatthapi na pakkhandati*).

Thereupon thinking: “How about at one time in my own continuity (*attano santāne*), and another time in another’s continuity (*parassa santāne*)?” he brings to mind internally and externally (*ajjhattabahiddhā manasi karoti*). There also it does not enter into it (*tatthapi na pakkhandati*).

Thereupon, desiring to become one who is Both Ways Released (*ubhatobhāgavimutto hotukāmo*), thinking: “How about the immaterial attainment (*arūpasamāpattiyaṃ*)?” he brings to mind the imperturbable (*āneñjaṃ manasi karoti*). There also it does not enter into voidness (*tatthapi na pakkhandati*).

Now in that case he should not give up his effort and go following after supporters and so on (*upaṭṭhākādīnaṃ pacchato na caritabbaṃ*), but the same basic jhāna (*pādakajjhānameva*) should be thoroughly brought to mind again and again (*sādhukaṃ punappunaṃ manasikātabbaṃ*).

Just as when someone is cutting a tree and after wielding his axe, sharpens it again, likewise, mindfulness on the object of meditation occurs. To show this, he said "*tasmiṃyevā*," and so on.

Now, for one who is so practicing, whatever he brings to mind, mindfulness occurs there and there. Showing this, he said, "*pakkhandati*".

*Tasmiṃyeva purimasmi*
*Tasmiṃyevā*
*Pakkhandati*

mula_pali:
189. ‘‘Tassa ce, ānanda, bhikkhuno iminā vihārena viharato caṅkamāya cittaṃ namati, so caṅkamati – ‘evaṃ maṃ caṅkamantaṃ nābhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssavissantī’ti . Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. Tassa ce, ānanda, bhikkhuno iminā vihārena viharato ṭhānāya cittaṃ namati, so tiṭṭhati – ‘evaṃ maṃ ṭhitaṃ nābhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssavissantī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. Tassa ce, ānanda, bhikkhuno iminā vihārena viharato nisajjāya cittaṃ namati, so nisīdati – ‘evaṃ maṃ nisinnaṃ nābhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssavissantī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. Tassa ce, ānanda, bhikkhuno iminā vihārena viharato sayanāya cittaṃ namati , so sayati – ‘evaṃ maṃ sayantaṃ nābhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssavissantī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti.

‘‘Tassa ce, ānanda, bhikkhuno iminā vihārena viharato kathāya bhassāya (sī.), bhāsāya (syā. kaṃ. pī.) cittaṃ namati, so – ‘yāyaṃ kathā hīnā gammā pothujjanikā anariyā anatthasaṃhitā na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathā corakathā mahāmattakathā senākathā bhayakathā yuddhakathā annakathā pānakathā vatthakathā sayanakathā mālākathā gandhakathā ñātikathā yānakathā gāmakathā nigamakathā nagarakathā janapadakathā itthikathā surākathā visikhākathā kumbhaṭṭhānakathā pubbapetakathā nānattakathā lokakkhāyikā samuddakkhāyikā itibhavābhavakathā iti vā iti – evarūpiṃ kathaṃ na kathessāmī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. Yā ca kho ayaṃ, ānanda, kathā abhisallekhikā cetovinīvaraṇasappāyā cetovicāraṇasappāyā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), cetovivaraṇasappāyā (pī.) ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati, seyyathidaṃ – appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā pavivekakathā asaṃsaggakathā vīriyārambhakathā sīlakathā samādhikathā paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā iti – ‘evarūpiṃ kathaṃ kathessāmī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti.

bhassāya (sī.), bhāsāya (syā. kaṃ. pī.) cetovicāraṇasappāyā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), cetovivaraṇasappāyā (pī.)

‘‘Tassa ce, ānanda, bhikkhuno iminā vihārena viharato vitakkāya cittaṃ namati, so – ‘ye te vitakkā hīnā gammā pothujjanikā anariyā anatthasaṃhitā na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattanti, seyyathidaṃ – kāmavitakko byāpādavitakko vihiṃsāvitakko iti evarūpe vitakke evarūpena vitakkena (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.) na vitakkessāmī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. Ye ca kho ime, ānanda, vitakkā ariyā niyyānikā niyyanti takkarassa sammādukkhakkhayāya, seyyathidaṃ – nekkhammavitakko abyāpādavitakko avihiṃsāvitakko iti – ‘evarūpe vitakke evarūpena vitakkena (ka.) vitakkessāmī’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti.

evarūpena vitakkena (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.) evarūpena vitakkena (ka.)
mula_english:
“Furthermore, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* is dwelling in this dwelling, if his mind inclines to walking (*caṅkama*), he walks, thinking, ‘While I am walking in this way, no evil, unwholesome states of covetousness (*abhijjhā*) and grief (*domanassā*) will beset me.’ Thus he has full awareness of that.

And furthermore, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* is dwelling in this dwelling, if his mind inclines to standing (*ṭhāna*), he stands, thinking, ‘While I am standing in this way, no evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and grief will beset me.’ Thus he has full awareness of that.

And furthermore, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* is dwelling in this dwelling, if his mind inclines to sitting (*nisajjā*), he sits, thinking, ‘While I am sitting in this way, no evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and grief will beset me.’ Thus he has full awareness of that.

And furthermore, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* is dwelling in this dwelling, if his mind inclines to lying down (*sayana*), he lies down, thinking, ‘While I am lying down in this way, no evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and grief will beset me.’ Thus he has full awareness of that.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* is dwelling in this dwelling, if his mind inclines to talking (*kathā*), he resolves: ‘Such talk as is low, vulgar, coarse, ignoble, unbeneficial, and which does not lead to disenchantment (*nibbidā*), dispassion (*virāga*), cessation (*nirodha*), peace (*upasama*), direct knowledge (*abhijñā*), enlightenment (*sambodha*), and *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbāna*), that is, talk of kings (*rājakathā*), robbers (*corakathā*), ministers (*mahāmattakathā*), armies (*senākathā*), dangers (*bhayakathā*), battles (*yuddhakathā*), food (*annakathā*), drink (*pānakathā*), clothing (*vatthakathā*), beds (*sayanakathā*), garlands (*mālākathā*), perfumes (*gandhakathā*), relatives (*ñātikathā*), vehicles (*yānakathā*), villages (*gāmakathā*), towns (*nigamakathā*), cities (*nagarakathā*), countries (*janapadakathā*), women (*itthikathā*), heroes (*surākathā*), streets (*visikhākathā*), wells (*kumbhaṭṭhānakathā*), the dead (*pubbapetakathā*), trivialities (*nānattakathā*), the origin of the world (*lokakkhāyikā*), the ocean (*samuddakkhāyikā*), thus it was, thus it will be (*itibhavābhavakathā*): such talk I shall not utter.’ Thus he has full awareness of that.

But such talk as deals with effacement (*abhisallekhikā*), as favours the mind’s release (*cetovinīvaraṇasappāyā*), and which leads to complete disenchantment (*ekantanibbidāya*), dispassion (*virāga*), cessation (*nirodha*), peace (*upasama*), direct knowledge (*abhiññāya*), enlightenment (*sambodhāya*), and *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānāya*), that is, talk on wanting little (*appicchakathā*), on contentment (*santuṭṭhikathā*), seclusion (*pavivekakathā*), aloofness from society (*asaṃsaggakathā*), arousing energy (*vīriyārambhakathā*), virtue (*sīlakathā*), concentration (*samādhikathā*), wisdom (*paññākathā*), deliverance (*vimuttikathā*), knowledge and vision of deliverance (*vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā*): such talk I shall utter.’ Thus he has full awareness of that.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* is dwelling in this dwelling, if his mind inclines to thinking (*vitakka*), he resolves: ‘Such thoughts as are low, vulgar, coarse, ignoble, unbeneficial, and which do not lead to disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, and *Nirvāṇa*, that is, thoughts of sensual desire (*kāmavitakko*), thoughts of ill will (*byāpādavitakko*), and thoughts of cruelty (*vihiṃsāvitakko*): such thoughts I shall not think.’
“But he resolves: ‘Such thoughts as are noble and emancipating, and lead the one who practises in accordance with them to the complete destruction of suffering, that is, thoughts of renunciation (*nekkhammavitakko*), thoughts of non-ill will (*abyāpādavitakko*), and thoughts of non-cruelty (*avihiṃsāvitakko*): such thoughts I shall think.’

Thus he clearly comprehends this.
commentary_pali:
189.Iminā vihārenāti iminā samathavipassanāvihārena. Itiha tattha sampajānoti iti caṅkamantopi tasmiṃ kammaṭṭhāne sampajjamāne ‘‘sampajjati me kammaṭṭhāna’’nti jānanena sampajāno hoti. Sayatīti nipajjati. Ettha kañci kālaṃ caṅkamitvā – ‘‘idāni ettakaṃ kālaṃ caṅkamituṃ sakkhissāmī’’ti ñatvā iriyāpathaṃ ahāpetvā ṭhātabbaṃ. Esa nayo sabbavāresu . Na kathessāmīti, itiha tatthāti evaṃ na kathessāmīti jānanena tattha sampajānakārī hoti.

Puna dutiyavāre evarūpiṃ kathaṃ kathessāmīti jānanena sampajānakārī hoti, imassa bhikkhuno samathavipassanā taruṇāva, tāsaṃ anurakkhaṇatthaṃ –

evarūpiṃ kathaṃ kathessāmī

‘‘Āvāso gocaro bhassaṃ, puggalo atha bhojanaṃ;

Utu iriyāpatho ceva, sappāyo sevitabbako’’ti.

Satta sappāyāni icchitabbāni. Tesaṃ dassanatthamidaṃ vuttaṃ. Vitakkavāresu avitakkanassa ca vitakkanassa ca jānanena sampajānatā veditabbā.
commentary_english:
189. *Iminā vihārenā* means: in this way, consisting of serenity concentration and insight (*samatha-vipassanā*).

*Itiha tattha sampajāno* means: so, when the meditation subject succeeds while he is walking, he is possessed of full awareness through knowing that his meditation subject has succeeded.

*Sayati* means: he lies down.

Here, after walking for any given length of time, now knowing, “I am able to walk for so long,” he should stand, without breaking the sequence of postures.

This is the method in all instances.

*Na kathessāmīti, itiha tatthā* means: through knowing that I will not speak in this way, he is one who practices with full awareness.

Furthermore, in the second instance, through knowing *evarūpiṃ kathaṃ kathessāmī*, he is one who practices with full awareness. For the sake of protecting the freshness of this *bhikkhu*'s serenity and insight—

*Evarūpiṃ kathaṃ kathessāmī*:

“Dwelling place, pasture, speech, individual, and also food;
Season, posture, and what is agreeable should be cultivated.”

Seven things that are agreeable should be desired.

This is said for the purpose of pointing these out.

As regards the paragraphs dealing with thoughts, full awareness should be understood as knowing respectively the not thinking and the thinking of the thoughts.

mula_pali: 190. ‘‘Pañca kho ime, ānanda, kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, ānanda, pañca kāmaguṇā yattha bhikkhunā abhikkhaṇaṃ sakaṃ cittaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘atthi nu kho me imesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu aññatarasmiṃ vā aññatarasmiṃ vā āyatane uppajjati cetaso samudācāro’ti? Sace, ānanda, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ pajānāti – ‘atthi kho me imesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu aññatarasmiṃ vā aññatarasmiṃ vā āyatane uppajjati cetaso samudācāro’ti, evaṃ santametaṃ evaṃ santaṃ (aṭṭha.), ānanda, bhikkhu evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yo kho imesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu chandarāgo so me nappahīno’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. Sace panānanda, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ pajānāti – ‘natthi kho me imesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu aññatarasmiṃ vā aññatarasmiṃ vā āyatane uppajjati cetaso samudācāro’ti, evaṃ santametaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yo kho imesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu chandarāgo so me pahīno’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti.
mula_english:
“Ānanda, there are these five cords of sensual pleasure (*pañca kāmaguṇā*).

What are the five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust; sounds heard by the ear; smells smelt by the nose; tastes savoured by the tongue; tangibles felt by the body which are agreeable, . . .arousing desire. These are the five cords of sensual pleasure. Herein a *bhikkhu* should constantly review his own mind thus: ‘Does any mental excitement (*cetaso samudācāro*) concerning these five cords of sensual pleasure arise in me on any occasion?’ If, on reviewing his mind, the *bhikkhu* understands: ‘Mental excitement concerning these five cords of sensual pleasure does arise in me on certain occasions,’ then he understands: ‘Desire and lust (*chanda-rāgo*) for the five cords of sensual pleasure are unabandoned in me.’ Thus he clearly comprehends this.

But if, on reviewing his mind, the *bhikkhu* understands: ‘No mental excitement concerning these five cords of sensual pleasure arises in me on any occasion,’ then he understands: ‘Desire and lust for the five cords of sensual pleasure are abandoned in me.’ Thus he clearly comprehends this.
commentary_pali: 190. Iti vitakkapahānena dve magge kathetvā idāni tatiyamaggassa vipassanaṃ ācikkhanto pañca kho ime, ānanda, kāmaguṇātiādimāha. Āyataneti tesuyeva kāmaguṇesu kismiñcideva kilesuppattikāraṇe. Samudācāroti samudācaraṇato appahīnakileso. Evaṃsantanti evaṃ vijjamānameva. Sampajānoti kammaṭṭhānassa asampattijānanena sampajāno. Dutiyavāre evaṃ santametanti evaṃ sante etaṃ. Sampajānoti kammaṭṭhānasampattijānanena sampajāno. Ayañhi ‘‘pahīno nu kho me pañcasu kāmaguṇesu chandarāgo no’’ti paccavekkhamāno apahīnabhāvaṃ ñatvā vīriyaṃ paggahetvā taṃ anāgāmimaggena samugghāṭeti, tato maggānantaraṃ phalaṃ, phalato vuṭṭhāya paccavekkhamāno pahīnabhāvaṃ jānāti, tassa jānanena ‘‘sampajāno hotī’’ti vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
190.
Having spoken of the two paths by means of the abandonment of thought (*vitakka-pahāna*), now, while indicating the transcendent insight (*vipassanā*) of the third path, he says, “These five, Ānanda, are the cords of sensual desire (*kāmaguṇā*),” and so forth.

"*Āyatane*” means in each of those very cords of sensual desire (*kāmaguṇesu*) as a cause of the arising of defilements (*kilesuppatti-kāraṇe*).

"*Samudācāro*" means attachment (*samudācaraṇato appahīnakileso*).

"*Evaṃ santa*" means thus, just as it exists (*evaṃ vijjamānameva*).

"*Sampajāno*" means fully aware (*kammaṭṭhānassa asampattijānanena sampajāno*), through the knowledge of the non-attainment of the meditation subject.

In the second instance, "*evaṃ santameta*" means thus, as it exists (*evaṃ sante etaṃ*).

"*Sampajāno*" means fully aware (*kammaṭṭhānasampattijānanena sampajāno*), through the knowledge of the attainment of the meditation subject.

For when he reviews thus: “Is desire and greed in regard to these five cords of sense-desire (*pañcasu kāmaguṇesu chandarāgo*) abandoned in me or not?” and knows that it is not abandoned, this *bhikkhu* exerts energy and abolishes it by means of the path of Non-Return (*anāgāmimaggena*). Thereupon, when he reviews after emerging from the fruition (*phalaṃ*) which follows next upon the path, he knows that it is abandoned. He is possessed of full awareness (*sampajāno hotī*) through knowing that, is what is meant.

mula_pali: 191. ‘‘Pañca kho ime, ānanda, upādānakkhandhā yattha bhikkhunā udayabbayānupassinā vihātabbaṃ – ‘iti rūpaṃ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo, iti vedanā… iti saññā… iti saṅkhārā… iti viññāṇaṃ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti. Tassa imesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassino viharato yo pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu asmimāno so pahīyati. Evaṃ santametaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yo kho imesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu asmimāno so me pahīno’ti. Itiha tattha sampajāno hoti. Ime kho te, ānanda, dhammā ekantakusalā kusalāyātikā dhammā ekantakusalāyatikā (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathāṭīkā oloketabbā ariyā lokuttarā anavakkantā pāpimatā. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, ānanda, kaṃ atthavasaṃ sampassamāno arahati sāvako satthāraṃ anubandhituṃ api paṇujjamāno’’ti api panujjamānopīti (ka. sī.), api payujjamānoti (syā. kaṃ. pī.)? ‘‘Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā . Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti.
mula_english:
“Ānanda, there are these five aggregates subject to clinging, in regard to which a *bhikkhu* should abide contemplating rise and fall thus: ‘Such is material form (*rūpaṃ*), such its arising (*rūpassa samudayo*), such its passing away (*rūpassa atthaṅgamo*); such is feeling (*vedanā*) … such is perception (*saññā*) … such are volitional formations (*saṅkhārā*) … such is consciousness (*viññāṇaṃ*), such its origin (*viññāṇassa samudayo*), such its passing away (*viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo*).’

“When he abides contemplating rise and fall in these five aggregates subject to clinging, the conceit ‘I am’ (*asmimāno*) based on these five aggregates subject to clinging is abandoned (*pahīyati*) in him.

“When that is so, that *bhikkhu* understands: ‘The conceit “I am” (*asmimāno*) based on these five aggregates affected by clinging is abandoned (*pahīno*) in me.’

Thus he clearly comprehends this (*sampajāno hoti*).

“These, Ānanda, are altogether wholesome *dharmas*, which lead to wholesome results, are noble, supramundane, unconquerable, and untainted.

“What do you think, Ānanda? What good (*atthavasaṃ*) does a disciple see that he should seek the Teacher’s (*satthāraṃ*) company even if he is told to go away (*paṇujjamāno*)?”

“Venerable sir (*bhante*), our teachings (*dhammā*) are rooted in the Blessed One (*bhagavaṃmūlakā*), guided by the Blessed One (*bhagavaṃnettikā*), have the Blessed One as their resort (*bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā*). It would be good if the Blessed One would explain (*paṭibhātu*) the meaning (*attho*) of these words (*bhāsitassa*). Having heard (*sutvā*) it from the Blessed One (*bhagavato*), the *bhikkhus* will remember (*dhāressantī*) it.”

Now, explaining the insight of the path of Arhatship, he says, "These, Ānanda, are the five aggregates subject to grasping," and so on.

Therein, "it is abandoned" means that conceit 'I am form,' craving 'I am,' and latent tendency 'I am' are abandoned.

Likewise, that based on feeling and so on. Full awareness should be understood as previously stated.

These, Ānanda, are those things are with reference to the concentrations, the path, and the fruit that were spoken of earlier due to the stilling and the insight.

*Kusalāyatikā* means that [they] come from the profitable (*kusala*).

For profitable states can be both profitable and derived from the profitable (*kusalāyatikā*), that is to say, the first *jhāna* is profitable, the second *jhāna* is both profitable and derived from the profitable; the sphere of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*) is profitable, the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) is both profitable and derived from the profitable; the path of Stream-entry (*sotāpattimagga*) is both profitable and derived from the profitable; the path of Non-returning (*anāgāmimagga*) is profitable, the path of Arahatship (*arahattamagga*) is both profitable and derived from the profitable.

Likewise the first *jhāna* is profitable and states associated therewith are both profitable and derived from the profitable; the path of Arahatship (*arahattamagga*) is profitable and the states associated therewith are both profitable and derived from the profitable.

mula_pali:
192. ‘‘Na kho, ānanda, arahati sāvako satthāraṃ anubandhituṃ, yadidaṃ suttaṃ geyyaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ tassa hetu veyyākaraṇassa hetu (ka.). Taṃ kissa hetu? Dīgharattassa dīgharattaṃ + assāti padacchedo hi te, ānanda, dhammā sutā dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. Yā ca kho ayaṃ, ānanda, kathā abhisallekhikā cetovinīvaraṇasappāyā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati, seyyathidaṃ – appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā pavivekakathā asaṃsaggakathā vīriyārambhakathā sīlakathā samādhikathā paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā – evarūpiyā kho, ānanda, kathāya hetu arahati sāvako satthāraṃ anubandhituṃ api paṇujjamāno.

‘‘Evaṃ sante kho, ānanda, ācariyūpaddavo hoti, evaṃ sante antevāsūpaddavo hoti, evaṃ sante brahmacārūpaddavo hoti.
mula_english:
“Ānanda, a disciple should not seek the Teacher’s company for the sake of discourses (sūtra), stanzas (geyya), and expositions (veyyākaraṇa). Why is this so? Because, Ānanda, these teachings (dharma) have long been heard, borne in mind, recited, examined in the mind, and thoroughly penetrated by understanding (dṛṣṭi).

But such talk as deals with effacement (abhisallekhika), as favors the mind’s release (cetovinīvaraṇasappāya), and which leads to complete disenchantment (ekantanibbidā), dispassion (virāga), cessation (nirodha), peace (upasama), direct knowledge (abhijñā), enlightenment (saṃbodha), and Nirvāṇa (nibbāna), that is, talk on wanting little (appicchakathā), on contentment (santuṭṭhikathā), seclusion (pavivekathā), aloofness from society (asaṃsaggakathā), arousing energy (vīriyārambhakathā), virtue (sīlakathā), concentration (samādhikathā), wisdom (paññākathā), deliverance (vimuttikathā), knowledge and vision of deliverance (vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā): for the sake of such talk a disciple should seek the Teacher’s company even if he is told to go away.

Since this is so, Ānanda, a teacher’s undoing (ācariyūpaddavo) may come about, a pupil’s undoing (antevāsūpaddavo) may come about, and the undoing of one who lives the holy life (brahmacārūpaddavo) may come about.

mula_pali: 193. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, ācariyūpaddavo hoti? Idhānanda, ekacco satthā vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. Tassa tathāvūpakaṭṭhassa viharato anvāvattanti anvāvaṭṭanti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamā ceva jānapadā ca. So anvāvattantesu brāhmaṇagahapatikesu negamesu ceva jānapadesu ca mucchaṃ nikāmayati mucchati kāmayati (sī. pī.) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana na tathā dissati, gedhaṃ āpajjati, āvattati bāhullāya. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, upaddavo upadduto (sī. pī.) ācariyo. Ācariyūpaddavena avadhiṃsu naṃ pāpakā akusalā dhammā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā ponobhavikā (sī. pī.) sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, ācariyūpaddavo hoti.
mula_english:
193. How, Ānanda, does a teacher's undoing come about? Here, Ānanda, a certain teacher frequents a secluded dwelling place, a forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a glen, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest thicket, an open space, or a heap of straw. As he dwells thus withdrawn, Brahmins, householders, townsfolk, and country people gather around him. He then longs for honor (mucchaṃ nikāmayati) from those who gather around him—Brahmins, householders, townsfolk, and country people—he falls into greed (gedhaṃ āpajjati), and reverts to luxury (āvattati bāhullāya).

This, Ānanda, is called the undoing of a teacher (upaddavo ācariyo). He is struck down by the evil, unwholesome *dharmas* (pāpakā akusalā dhammā), which are defiling (*saṃkilesikā*), lead to renewed existence (*ponobbhavikā*), give trouble (*sadarā*), ripen in suffering (*dukkhavipākā*), and conduce to future birth, aging, and death (*āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā*).

That is how, Ānanda, a teacher’s undoing comes about (ācariyūpaddavo hoti).
commentary_pali:
193.Satthāti bāhirako titthakarasatthā. Anvāvattantīti anuāvattanti upasaṅkamanti. Mucchaṃ kāmayatīti mucchanataṇhaṃ pattheti, pavattetīti attho. Ācariyūpaddavenāti abbhantare uppannena kilesūpaddavena ācariyassupaddavo. Sesupaddavesupi eseva nayo. Avadhiṃsu nanti mārayiṃsu naṃ. Etena hi guṇamaraṇaṃ kathitaṃ.

Vinipātāyāti suṭṭhu nipatanāya. Kasmā pana brahmacārupaddavova – ‘‘dukkhavipākataro ca kaṭukavipākataro ca vinipātāya ca saṃvattatī’’ti vuttoti. Bāhirapabbajjā hi appalābhā, tattha mahanto nibbattetabbaguṇo natthi, aṭṭhasamāpattipañcābhiññāmattakameva hoti. Iti yathā gadrabhapiṭṭhito patitassa mahantaṃ dukkhaṃ na hoti, sarīrassa paṃsumakkhanamattameva hoti, evaṃ bāhirasamaye lokiyaguṇamattatova parihāyati, tena purimaṃ upaddavadvayaṃ na evaṃ vuttaṃ. Sāsane pana pabbajjā mahālābhā, tattha cattāro maggā cattāri phalāni nibbānanti mahantā adhigantabbaguṇā. Iti yathā ubhato sujāto khattiyakumāro hatthikkhandhavaragato nagaraṃ anusañcaranto hatthikkhandhato patito mahādukkhaṃ nigacchati, evaṃ sāsanato parihāyamāno navahi lokuttaraguṇehi parihāyati. Tenāyaṃ brahmacārupaddavo evaṃ vutto.

Vinipātāyā
commentary_english:
193. *Satthā* means a teacher who is external, a teacher of other schools.

*Anvāvattantī* means they return, they approach.

*Mucchaṃ kāmayatī* means he desires the thirst for delusion, he longs for it, this is the meaning.

*Ācariyūpaddavenā* means the undoing of the teacher is the undoing of the teacher by the afflictions (*kilesa*) arising internally.

So with the other kinds of undoing, the same method applies.

*Avadhiṃsu na* means they killed him.

By this, the death of his special qualities and virtues (*guṇa*) is stated.

*Vinipātāyā* means for well falling down.

But why is it said that the undoing of the dweller in the life of purity has a more painful result (*duḥkhavipākataro*), a more bitter result (*kaṭukavipākataro*) and it even leads to rebirth in states of woe (*vinipātāya ca saṃvattatī*)?

Going into homelessness outside the Dispensation brings small gain; there, there is no outstandingly great special quality (*nibbattetabbaguṇo*) to be developed, but only the eight meditative attainments (*aṭṭhasamāpatti*) and the five supernormal powers (*pañcābhiññā*) are achieved.

Accordingly, just as there is no great suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) for one who falls from the back of a donkey, so, since in a sect outside the Dispensation he falls only from worldly special qualities (*lokiya-guṇa*), it is not said in this way of the first two kinds of undoing.

But going into homelessness in the Dispensation brings great gain. Here, the four paths (*cattāro maggā*), the four fruitions (*cattāri phalāni*), and *nirvāṇa* are outstandingly special qualities (*adhigantabbaguṇā*) to be attained.

Accordingly, just as when a noble youth, wellborn on both parental sides, traversing a city and seated in the place of honor on the back of an elephant, falls from the elephant’s back, he comes to great suffering; so, since in falling away from the Dispensation he falls away from the nine supramundane special qualities (*lokuttaraguṇa*).

it is said in this way of the undoing of the dweller in the life of purity (*brahmacārupaddavo*).

*Vinipātāyā*

mula_pali: 194. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, antevāsūpaddavo hoti? Tasseva kho panānanda, satthu sāvako tassa satthu vivekamanubrūhayamāno vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. Tassa tathāvūpakaṭṭhassa viharato anvāvattanti brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamā ceva jānapadā ca. So anvāvattantesu brāhmaṇagahapatikesu negamesu ceva jānapadesu ca mucchaṃ nikāmayati, gedhaṃ āpajjati, āvattati bāhullāya. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, upaddavo antevāsī. Antevāsūpaddavena avadhiṃsu naṃ pāpakā akusalā dhammā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, antevāsūpaddavo hoti.
mula_english: 194. How, Ānanda, does the undoing of a pupil (*antevāsūpaddavo*) come about? Here, Ānanda, a disciple (*sāvako*) of that teacher, emulating the solitude of that teacher, resorts to a secluded lodging (*vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ*): the forest (*araññaṃ*), the foot of a tree (*rukkhamūlaṃ*), a mountain (*pabbataṃ*), a ravine (*kandaraṃ*), a hillside cave (*giriguhaṃ*), a charnel ground (*susānaṃ*), a jungle highland (*vanapatthaṃ*), the open air (*abbhokāsaṃ*), a heap of straw (*palālapuñjaṃ*). While he lives thus withdrawn (*tathāvūpakaṭṭhassa viharato*), brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*) and householders (*gahapatika*) from town (*negama*) and country (*jānapadā*) visit him. And as a result, he, surrounded by those brahmins and householders from town and country, goes astray (*mucchaṃ nikāmayati*), becomes filled with desire (*gedhaṃ āpajjati*), succumbs to craving (*āvattati*) and reverts to luxury (*bāhullāya*). This pupil (*antevāsī*) is said to be undone (*upaddavo*). He has been struck down (*avadhiṃsu*) by evil (*pāpakā*) unwholesome (*akusalā*) states (*dhamma*) that defile (*saṃkilesikā*), bring renewal of being (*ponobbhavikā*), give trouble (*sadarā*), ripen in suffering (*dukkhavipākā*), and lead to future birth (*jāti*), ageing (*jarā*), and death (*maraṇiyā*) . Thus, Ānanda, comes about the undoing of a pupil (*antevāsūpaddavo hoti*).

mula_pali:
195. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, brahmacārūpaddavo hoti? Idhānanda, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. Tassa tathāvūpakaṭṭhassa viharato anvāvattanti brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamā ceva jānapadā ca. So anvāvattantesu brāhmaṇagahapatikesu negamesu ceva jānapadesu ca na mucchaṃ nikāmayati, na gedhaṃ āpajjati, na āvattati bāhullāya. Tasseva kho panānanda, satthu sāvako tassa satthu vivekamanubrūhayamāno vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. Tassa tathāvūpakaṭṭhassa viharato anvāvattanti brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamā ceva jānapadā ca. So anvāvattantesu brāhmaṇagahapatikesu negamesu ceva jānapadesu ca mucchaṃ nikāmayati, gedhaṃ āpajjati, āvattati bāhullāya. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, upaddavo brahmacārī. Brahmacārūpaddavena avadhiṃsu naṃ pāpakā akusalā dhammā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, brahmacārūpaddavo hoti.

‘‘Tatrānanda, yo cevāyaṃ ācariyūpaddavo, yo ca antevāsūpaddavo ayaṃ tehi brahmacārūpaddavo dukkhavipākataro ceva kaṭukavipākataro ca, api ca vinipātāya saṃvattati.
mula_english:
‘‘And how, Ānanda, does the undoing of one who lives the holy life come about? Here, Ānanda, the *tathāgata* arises in the world, an *arhat*, a fully enlightened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and good conduct, a *sugata*, a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a guide for those who can be trained, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a *bhagavā*.

He resorts to a secluded resting place: the forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a hillside cave, a charnel ground, a jungle highland, the open air, a heap of straw.

While he lives thus withdrawn, *brāhmaṇas* and householders from town and country visit him.

Yet he does not long for the intoxication, does not incur the greed, and does not revert to luxury in those visiting *brāhmaṇas* and householders from town and country.

But a disciple of this teacher, emulating his teacher’s seclusion, resorts to a secluded resting place: the forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a hillside cave, a charnel ground, a jungle highland, the open air, a heap of straw.

While he lives thus withdrawn, *brāhmaṇas* and householders from town and country visit him.

And he longs for the intoxication, incurs the greed, and reverts to luxury in those visiting *brāhmaṇas* and householders from town and country.

This one who lives the holy life is said to be undone.

He has been struck down by evil unwholesome *dharmas* that defile, bring renewal of being, give trouble, ripen in suffering, and lead to future birth, ageing, and death.

Thus there comes to be the undoing of one who leads the holy life, Ānanda.

Moreover, Ānanda, the undoing of one who leads the holy life has a more painful result, a more bitter result, than the teacher’s undoing or the pupil’s undoing, and it even leads to perdition.

mula_pali:
196. ‘‘Tasmātiha maṃ, ānanda, mittavatāya samudācaratha, mā sapattavatāya. Taṃ vo bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya.

‘‘Kathañcānanda , satthāraṃ sāvakā sapattavatāya samudācaranti, no mittavatāya? Idhānanda, satthā sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti anukampako hitesī anukampaṃ upādāya – ‘idaṃ vo hitāya, idaṃ vo sukhāyā’ti. Tassa sāvakā na sussūsanti, na sotaṃ odahanti, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhapenti, vokkamma ca satthusāsanā vattanti. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, satthāraṃ sāvakā sapattavatāya samudācaranti, no mittavatāya.

‘‘Kathañcānanda, satthāraṃ sāvakā mittavatāya samudācaranti, no sapattavatāya? Idhānanda, satthā sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti anukampako hitesī anukampaṃ upādāya – ‘idaṃ vo hitāya, idaṃ vo sukhāyā’ti. Tassa sāvakā sussūsanti, sotaṃ odahanti, aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhapenti, na ca vokkama satthusāsanā vattanti. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, satthāraṃ sāvakā mittavatāya samudācaranti, no sapattavatāya.

‘‘Tasmātiha maṃ, ānanda, mittavatāya samudācaratha, mā sapattavatāya. Taṃ vo bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Na vo ahaṃ, ānanda, tathā parakkamissāmi yathā kumbhakāro āmake āmakamatte. Niggayha niggayhāhaṃ, ānanda, vakkhāmi; pavayha pavayha, ānanda, vakkhāmi pavayha pavayha (sī. pī.), paggayha paggayha ānanda vakkhāmi (ka.). Yo sāro so ṭhassatī’’ti.

pavayha pavayha (sī. pī.), paggayha paggayha ānanda vakkhāmi (ka.)

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Mahāsuññatasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
196. Therefore, Ānanda, behave towards me with friendliness (*mittavatāya*), not with hostility (*sapattavatāya*).

That will lead to your welfare (*hitāya*) and happiness (*sukhāya*) for a long time (*dīgharattaṃ*).

How then, Ānanda, do disciples behave towards the Teacher with hostility (*sapattavatāya*), not with friendliness (*mittavatāya*)? Here, Ānanda, the Teacher teaches his disciples the Dharma, being compassionate, seeking their welfare, taking compassion as his basis, [saying]: 'This is for your welfare (*hitāya*), this is for your happiness (*sukhāya*)'.

His disciples do not want to hear (*sussūsanti*), do not give ear (*sotaṃ odahanti*), do not exert their minds to understand (*aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhapenti*), and they err and turn aside from the Teacher's Dispensation (*satthusāsanā vattanti*).

Thus, Ānanda, do disciples behave towards the Teacher with hostility (*sapattavatāya*), not with friendliness (*mittavatāya*).

How then, Ānanda, do disciples behave towards the Teacher with friendliness (*mittavatāya*), not with hostility (*sapattavatāya*)? Here, Ānanda, the Teacher teaches his disciples the Dharma, being compassionate, seeking their welfare, taking compassion as his basis, [saying]: 'This is for your welfare (*hitāya*), this is for your happiness (*sukhāya*)'.

His disciples want to hear (*sussūsanti*), they give ear (*sotaṃ odahanti*), they exert their minds to understand (*aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhapenti*), and they do not err and turn aside from the Teacher’s Dispensation (*satthusāsanā vattanti*).

Thus, Ānanda, do disciples behave towards the Teacher with friendliness (*mittavatāya*), not with hostility (*sapattavatāya*).

Therefore, Ānanda, behave towards me with friendliness (*mittavatāya*), not with hostility (*sapattavatāya*).

That will lead to your welfare (*hitāya*) and happiness (*sukhāya*) for a long time (*dīgharattaṃ*).

I shall not treat you as the potter treats the raw damp clay (*āmake āmakamatte*), Ānanda.

Repeatedly restraining you, I shall speak to you, Ānanda; repeatedly admonishing you, Ānanda, I shall speak to you.

The sound core will stand the test (*yo sāro so ṭhassatī’*).

This was stated by the Blessed One (*bhagavā*).

The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words (*bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti*).

The Greater Discourse on Emptiness (*mahāsuññatasuttaṃ*) is finished, the second.
commentary_pali:
196.Tasmāti yasmā sesupaddavehi brahmacārupaddavo dukkhavipākataro, yasmā vā sapattapaṭipattiṃ vītikkamanto dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvattati, mittapaṭipatti hitāya, tasmā. Evaṃ uparimenapi heṭṭhimenapi atthena yojetabbaṃ. Mittavatāyāti mittapaṭipattiyā. Sapattavatāyāti verapaṭipattiyā.

Vokkammaca satthusāsanāti dukkaṭadubbhāsitamattampi hi sañcicca vītikkamanto vokkamma vattati nāma. Tadeva avītikkamanto na vokkamma vattati nāma.

Vokkamma ca satthusāsanā

Na vo ahaṃ, ānanda, tathā parakkamissāmīti ahaṃ tumhesu tathā na paṭipajjissāmi. Āmaketi apakke. Āmakamatteti āmake nātisukkhe bhājane. Kumbhakāro hi āmakaṃ nātisukkhaṃ apakkaṃ ubhohi hatthehi saṇhikaṃ gaṇhāti ‘‘mā bhijjatū’’ti. Iti yathā kumbhakāro tattha paṭipajjati, nāhaṃ tumhesu tathā paṭipajjissāmi. Niggayha niggayhāti sakiṃ ovaditvā tuṇhī na bhavissāmi, niggaṇhitvā niggaṇhitvā punappunaṃ ovadissāmi anusāsissāmi. Pavayha pavayhāti dose pavāhetvā pavāhetvā. Yathā pakkabhājanesu kumbhakāro bhinnachinnajajjarāni pavāhetvā ekato katvā supakkāneva ākoṭetvā ākoṭetvā gaṇhāti, evameva ahampi pavāhetvā pavāhetvā punappunaṃ ovadissāmi anusāsissāmi. Yosāro so ṭhassatīti evaṃ vo mayā ovadiyamānānaṃ yo maggaphalasāro, so ṭhassati. Apica lokiyaguṇāpi idha sārotveva adhippetā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Na vo ahaṃ, ānanda, tathā parakkamissāmī Āmake Āmakamatte Niggayha niggayhā Pavayha pavayhā Yo sāro so ṭhassatī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāsuññatasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
196. Therefore (tasmā): Because the brahmacārupaddava [state of existence] is more prone to suffering (duḥkhavipākataro) due to the remaining disturbances (sesupaddavehi), and because one who transgresses (vītikkamanto) the proper conduct towards a co-celibate (sapattapaṭipattiṃ) tends toward (saṃvattati) prolonged (dīgharattaṃ) suffering (duḥkhāya) and harm (ahitāya), therefore (tasmā) proper conduct towards a friend (mittapaṭipatti) leads to welfare (hitāya). Thus, this should be connected with both the preceding and the following meaning. By "friendliness" (*mittavatāyā*) is meant friendly conduct (*mittapaṭipattiyā*). By "conduct befitting a co-celibate" (*sapattavatāyā*) is meant hostile conduct (*verapaṭipattiyā*).

Transgressing (*vokkamma*) the Teacher's instruction (*satthusāsanā*): Even something as small as an improper or wrongly spoken word (*dukkaṭadubbhāsitamattampi*) is considered a transgression (*vītikkamanto vokkamma vattati nāma*) if done intentionally (sañcicca). Not transgressing (*avītikkamanto*) means not deviating (*na vokkamma vattati nāma*).

Transgressing, and The Teacher's instruction, O Ānanda, I will not behave towards you as [the potter behaves]. Meaning, I will not treat you like that (*ahaṃ tumhesu tathā na paṭipajjissāmi*).

"Raw" (*āmake*) means "unripe" (*apakke*).

"Being raw" (*āmakamatte*) means in a raw (*āmake*), not-too-dry (*nātisukkhe*) vessel (*bhājane*).

For a potter (kumbhakāro), indeed, takes the raw (āmakaṃ), not too dry (nātisukkhaṃ), unripe (apakkaṃ) [clay pot] gently (saṇhikaṃ) with both hands (ubhohi hatthehi), [thinking,] "May it not break!" (‘‘mā bhijjatū’’ti). Thus (iti), just as (yathā) a potter (kumbhakāro) behaves (paṭipajjati) in that way (tattha), I (ahaṃ) will not behave (na paṭipajjissāmi) towards you (tumhesu) in that way (tathā).

"Reproving, reproving" (*niggayha niggayhā*) means I will not be silent (tuṇhī na bhavissāmi) after advising (ovaditvā) once (sakiṃ). Rather, having reproved (niggaṇhitvā niggaṇhitvā) again and again (punappunaṃ), I will advise (ovadissāmi) and instruct (anusāsissāmi).

"Rejecting, rejecting" (*pavayha pavayhā*) means having washed away (pavāhetvā pavāhetvā) the faults (dose).

Just as (yathā) among cooked pots (pakkabhājanesu) a potter (kumbhakāro), having discarded (pavāhetvā) the cracked (bhinna), broken (chinna), and fragile (jajjarāni) ones, and having gathered (ekato katvā) only the well-cooked ones (supakkāneva), tapping (ākoṭetvā ākoṭetvā), he takes [them], just so (evameva) I also (ahampi), having washed away (pavāhetvā pavāhetvā) again and again (punappunaṃ), will advise (ovadissāmi) and instruct (anusāsissāmi).

"He who is sound, he will endure" (*yo sāro so ṭhassatī*) means: thus (evaṃ), of you (vo) who are being advised (ovadiyamānānaṃ) by me (mayā), he who (yo) is of the essence of the path and its fruit (maggaphalasāro), he (so) will endure (ṭhassati).

Furthermore (apica), even worldly qualities (lokiyaguṇāpi) are intended (adhippetā) here (idha) by "sound" (sāro).

The rest (sesaṃ) is clear (uttānamevāti) throughout (sabbattha).

O Ānanda, I will not behave towards you as [the potter behaves]. Raw, Being raw, Reproving, reproving, Rejecting, rejecting, He who is sound, he will endure.

The *Papañcasūdanī*, Commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya*.

The *Mahāsuññatasuttavaṇṇanā* is finished.

mula_pali: 197. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho sambahulānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṃ upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, āvuso, abbhutaṃ, āvuso, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā, yatra hi nāma tathāgato atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivatte jānissati anussarissati jānissati (ka.) – ‘evaṃjaccā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ itipi, ‘evaṃnāmā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ itipi, ‘evaṃgottā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ itipi, ‘evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ itipi, ‘evaṃdhammā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ itipi, ‘evaṃpaññā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ itipi, ‘evaṃvihārī te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ itipi, ‘evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ itipī’’ti! Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando te bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyā ceva, āvuso, tathāgatā acchariyadhammasamannāgatā ca; abbhutā ceva, āvuso, tathāgatā abbhutadhammasamannāgatā cā’’ti. Ayañca hidaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ antarākathā vippakatā hoti.
mula_english:
197. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavān) was staying at Sāavatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park (Jetavane Anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

Then, after their meal, when the monks had returned from their alms round, a large number of monks (sambahulānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ) were sitting together, gathered in the service hall (upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ). This discussion arose among them: “It is wonderful (acchariyaṃ), friends (āvuso), it is marvellous (abbhutaṃ), friends (āvuso), how mighty (mahiddhikatā) and powerful (mahānubhāvatā) is the *Tathāgata*! For if the *Tathāgata* knows about the past Buddhas (atīte buddhe), who have attained final *Nirvāṇa* (parinibbute), cut off proliferation (chinnapapañce), broken the cycle (pariyādinnavaṭṭe), brought suffering to an end (sabbadukkhavītivatte), [namely:] ‘Such was the birth of those Blessed Ones (evaṃjaccā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ)’; ‘Such were the names of those Blessed Ones (evaṃnāmā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ)’; ‘Such was the lineage of those Blessed Ones (evaṃgottā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ)’; ‘Such was the virtue of those Blessed Ones (evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ)’; ‘Such was the teaching of those Blessed Ones (evaṃdhammā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ)’; ‘Such was the wisdom of those Blessed Ones (evaṃpaññā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ)’; ‘Such was the conduct of those Blessed Ones (evaṃvihārī te bhagavanto ahesuṃ)’; ‘Such was the liberation of those Blessed Ones (evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ).’”

When this was said, venerable Ānanda (āyasmā ānando) said this to those monks: “The *Tathāgatas* are wonderful (acchariyā), friends (āvuso), and endowed with wonderful qualities (acchariyadhammasamannāgatā ca); the *Tathāgatas* are marvelous (abhutā), friends (āvuso), and endowed with marvelous qualities (abbhutadhammasamannāgatā ca).”

And this conversation of those monks was interrupted (ayañca hidaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ antarākathā vippakatā hoti).
commentary_pali:
197.Evaṃme sutanti acchariyaabbhutasuttaṃ. Tattha yatra hi nāmāti acchariyatthe nipāto. Yo nāma tathāgatoti attho. Chinnapapañceti ettha papañcā nāma taṇhā māno diṭṭhīti ime tayo kilesā. Chinnavaṭumeti ettha vaṭumanti kusalākusalakammavaṭṭaṃ vuccati. Pariyādinnavaṭṭeti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Sabbadukkhavītivatteti sabbaṃ vipākavaṭṭasaṅkhātaṃ dukkhaṃ vītivatte. Anussarissatīti idaṃ yatrāti nipātavasena anāgatavacanaṃ, attho panettha atītavasena veditabbo. Bhagavā hi te buddhe anussari, na idāni anussarissati. Evaṃjaccāti vipassīādayo khattiyajaccā, kakusandhādayo brāhmaṇajaccāti. Evaṃgottāti vipassīādayo koṇḍaññagottā, kakusandhādayo kassapagottāti. Evaṃsīlāti lokiyalokuttarasīlena evaṃsīlā. Evaṃdhammāti ettha samādhipakkhā dhammā adhippetā . Lokiyalokuttarena samādhinā evaṃsamādhinoti attho. Evaṃpaññāti lokiyalokuttarapaññāya evaṃpaññā. Evaṃvihārīti ettha pana heṭṭhā samādhipakkhānaṃ dhammānaṃ gahitattā vihāro gahitova, puna kasmā gahitameva gaṇhātīti ce, na idaṃ gahitameva. Idañhi nirodhasamāpattidīpanatthaṃ, tasmā evaṃnirodhasamāpattivihārīti ayamettha attho.

Evaṃvimuttāti ettha vikkhambhanavimutti tadaṅgavimutti samucchedavimutti paṭippassaddhivimutti nissaraṇavimuttīti pañcavidhā vimuttiyo. Tattha aṭṭha samāpattiyo sayaṃ vikkhambhitehi nīvaraṇādīhi vimuttattā vikkhambhanavimuttīti saṅkhaṃ gacchanti. Aniccānupassanādikā satta anupassanā sayaṃ tassa tassa paccanīkaṅgavasena paricattāhi niccasaññādīhi vimuttattā tadaṅgavimuttīti saṅkhaṃ gacchanti. Cattāro ariyamaggā sayaṃ samucchinnehi kilesehi vimuttattā samucchedavimuttīti saṅkhaṃ gacchanti. Cattāri sāmaññaphalāni maggānubhāvena kilesānaṃ paṭippassaddhante uppannattā paṭippassaddhivimuttīti saṅkhaṃ gacchanti. Nibbānaṃ sabbakilesehi nissaṭattā apagatattā dūre ṭhitattā nissaraṇavimuttīti saṅkhaṃ gataṃ. Iti imāsaṃ pañcannaṃ vimuttīnaṃ vasena evaṃvimuttāti evamettha attho veditabbo.

Evaṃvimuttā vikkhambhanavimuttī tadaṅgavimuttī samucchedavimuttī paṭippassaddhivimuttī nissaraṇavimuttī
commentary_english:
197. "Thus have I heard"—the Achariyabbhutasutta.

There, " *yatra hi nāmā* " is a particle indicating astonishment.

*yo nāma tathāgato* means "who is called the Tathāgata."

In " *chinnapapañce* ," *papañcā* means these three defilements: craving, conceit, and views.

In " *chinnavaṭume* ," *vaṭuma* means the cycle of wholesome and unwholesome actions.

*pariyādinnavaṭṭe* is a synonym for that.

*sabbadukkhavītivatte* means one who has transcended all suffering, which is known as the cycle of ripening.

*anussarissatī* here, due to the particle *yatrāti*, is a future tense, but its meaning should be understood as past tense here.

The Blessed One recollected those Buddhas; he will not recollect them now.

*evaṃjaccā* means Vipassī and others were born into the khattiya caste, Kakusandha and others were born into the brāhmaṇa caste.

*evaṃgottā* means Vipassī and others were of the Koṇḍañña clan, Kakusandha and others were of the Kassapa clan.

*evaṃsīlā* means having such morality through mundane and supramundane morality.

*evaṃdhammā* here implies the qualities pertaining to concentration.

*evaṃsamādhinoti* means having such concentration through mundane and supramundane concentration.

*evaṃpaññā* means having such wisdom through mundane and supramundane wisdom.

As for *evaṃvihārī*, since qualities pertaining to concentration have already been mentioned below, the dwelling has already been mentioned. If one asks why it is mentioned again, it is not just a mere repetition.

This is in order to illuminate the cessation-attainment (*nirodhasamāpatti*). Therefore, *evaṃnirodhasamāpattivihārīti* is the meaning here.

*evaṃvimuttā* here refers to the five kinds of liberation: liberation by suppression (*vikkhambhanavimutti*), liberation by temporary suspension (*tadaṅgavimutti*), liberation by eradication (*samucchedavimutti*), liberation by tranquilization (*paṭippassaddhivimutti*), and liberation by escape (*nissaraṇavimutti*).

Therein, the eight attainments (*samāpattis*) are called *vikkhambhanavimutti* because they are liberated from hindrances and so on by suppression.

The seven contemplations beginning with the contemplation of impermanence are called *tadaṅgavimutti* because they are liberated from the perception of permanence and so on by temporarily abandoning them according to their respective opposing factors.

The four noble paths (*ariyamagga*) are called *samucchedavimutti* because they are liberated from defilements by eradication.

The four fruits of recluseship (*sāmaññaphalāni*) are called *paṭippassaddhivimutti* because they arise at the end of the tranquilization of defilements by the power of the paths.

Nibbāna is called *nissaraṇavimutti* because it has escaped, departed, and stands far away from all defilements.

Thus, based on these five kinds of liberation, *evaṃvimuttāti* should be understood to mean thus here.

*evaṃvimuttā vikkhambhanavimutti tadaṅgavimutti samucchedavimutti paṭippassaddhivimutti nissaraṇavimutti*

mula_pali: 198. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi . Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘kāya nuttha, bhikkhave, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā’’ti? ‘‘Idha, bhante, amhākaṃ pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṃ upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – ‘acchariyaṃ, āvuso, abbhutaṃ, āvuso, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā, yatra hi nāma tathāgato atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivatte jānissati – evaṃjaccā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipi, evaṃnāmā… evaṃgottā… evaṃsīlā… evaṃdhammā.. evaṃpaññā… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipī’ti! Evaṃ vutte, bhante, āyasmā ānando amhe etadavoca – ‘acchariyā ceva, āvuso, tathāgatā acchariyadhammasamannāgatā ca, abbhutā ceva, āvuso, tathāgatā abbhutadhammasamannāgatā cā’ti. Ayaṃ kho no, bhante, antarākathā vippakatā; atha bhagavā anuppatto’’ti.
mula_english: Then the Blessed One, arising from retreat in the evening, approached the service hall; having approached, he sat down on the appointed seat. Seated, the Blessed One addressed the monks, "With what discussion are you assembled here, monks? And what was the interrupted discussion?" "Here, venerable sir, after our meal, returning from alms-gathering, assembled and gathered in the service hall, this discussion arose: 'Amazing, friends, astonishing, friends, is the great power and might of the *Tathāgata*, in that the *Tathāgata* knows past *Buddhas* who are fully liberated, their proliferation cut off, their cycle ended, their round completed, all suffering overcome—that those Blessed Ones were of such a birth, of such a name, of such a clan, of such virtue, of such a *dharma*, of such wisdom, of such a dwelling, of such liberation!' When this was said, venerable sir, the venerable Ānanda said this to us: 'Amazing, friends, are the *Tathāgatas*, endowed with amazing qualities; astonishing, friends, are the *Tathāgatas*, endowed with astonishing qualities.' This, venerable sir, was the discussion that was interrupted when the Blessed One arrived."

mula_pali:
199. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘tasmātiha taṃ, ānanda, bhiyyosomattāya paṭibhantu tathāgatassa acchariyā abbhutadhammā’’ti abbhutā dhammāti (?).

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘sato sampajāno, ānanda, bodhisatto tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapajjī’ti. Yampi, bhante, sato sampajāno bodhisatto tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapajji idaṃpāhaṃ , bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘sato sampajāno, ānanda, bodhisatto tusite kāye aṭṭhāsī’ti. Yampi, bhante, sato sampajāno bodhisatto tusite kāye aṭṭhāsi idaṃpāhaṃ idaṃpahaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

idaṃpahaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
199. Then, indeed, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda, saying: "Therefore, Ānanda, may the wonderful and marvelous qualities of the Tathāgata shine forth all the more!"

"Venerable sir, I have heard and learned this from the Blessed One's own lips, face to face: 'Mindful and fully aware, Ānanda, the Bodhisattva appeared in the Tusita heaven.'
And that mindful and fully aware the Bodhisattva appeared in the Tusita heaven, this I, venerable sir, remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One."

"Venerable sir, I have heard and learned this from the Blessed One's own lips, face to face: 'Mindful and fully aware, Ānanda, the Bodhisattva remained in the Tusita heaven.'
And that mindful and fully aware the Bodhisattva remained in the Tusita heaven, this I, venerable sir, remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One."
commentary_pali:
199.Tasmātihāti yasmā tvaṃ ‘‘tathāgatā acchariyā’’ti vadasi, tasmā taṃ bhiyyoso mattāya paṭibhantu tathāgatassa acchariyā abbhutadhammāti. Sato sampajānoti ettha dvesampajaññāni manussaloke devaloke ca. Tattha vessantarajātake brāhmaṇassa dve putte datvā punadivase sakkassa deviṃ datvā sakkena pasīditvā dinne aṭṭha vare gaṇhanto –

‘‘Ito vimuccamānāhaṃ, saggagāmī visesagū;

Anivattī tato assaṃ, aṭṭhametaṃ varaṃ vare’’ti. (jā. 2.22.2300) –

Evaṃ tusitabhavane me paṭisandhi hotūti varaṃ aggahesi, tato paṭṭhāya tusitabhavane uppajjissāmīti jānāti, idaṃ manussaloke sampajaññaṃ. Vessantarattabhāvato pana cuto puna tusitabhavane nibbattitvā nibbattosmīti aññāsi, idaṃ devaloke sampajaññaṃ.

Kiṃ pana sesadevatā na jānantīti? No na jānanti. Tā pana uyyānavimānakapparukkhe oloketvā devanāṭakehi tūriyasaddena pabodhitā ‘‘mārisa ayaṃ devaloko tumhe idha nibbattā’’ti sāritā jānanti. Bodhisatto paṭhamajavanavāre na jānāti, dutiyajavanato paṭṭhāya jānāti. Iccassa aññehi asādhāraṇajānanaṃ hoti.

Aṭṭhāsīti ettha kiñcāpi aññepi devā tattha ṭhitā ṭhitamhāti jānanti, te pana chasu dvāresu balavatā iṭṭhārammaṇena abhibhuyyamānā satiṃ vissajjetvā attano bhuttapītabhāvampi ajānantā āhārūpacchedena kālaṃ karonti. Bodhisattassa kiṃ tathārūpaṃ ārammaṇaṃ natthīti? No natthi. So hi sesadeve dasahi ṭhānehi adhiggaṇhāti, ārammaṇena pana attānaṃ maddituṃ na deti, taṃ ārammaṇaṃ abhibhavitvā tiṭṭhati. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘sato sampajāno, ānanda, bodhisatto tusite kāye aṭṭhāsī’’ti.

Aṭṭhāsī
commentary_english:
199. Therefore, because you say, "The *tathāgatas* are amazing," therefore, may the amazing and wonderful qualities of the *tathāgata* be revealed even more greatly!

Here, "mindful and fully aware" refers to the two kinds of full awareness in the human world and the world of the gods.

In the *Vessantara Jātaka*, after giving two sons, and on the following day, after giving the queen to Śakra, Śakra was pleased and gave eight boons, which he accepted, saying:

"When I am released from here, I will go to heaven, skilled in special knowledge; may I not return from there; this is the eighth excellent boon."

(Jā. 2.22.2300)

Thus, he grasped the boon, "May my rebirth be in the Tuṣita heaven," and from then on, he knows, "I will be reborn in the Tuṣita heaven"; this is full awareness in the human world.

Furthermore, having passed away from the state of being Vessantara and being reborn in the Tuṣita heaven, he knew, "I am reborn"; this is full awareness in the world of the gods.

But do the remaining deities not know? No, they do not know.

However, those who, having looked at the garden-palace wish-fulfilling trees, are awakened by the sounds of divine music from the divine dramas, are made to remember, "O venerable one, this is the world of the gods; you are reborn here," they know.

The *bodhisattva* does not know in the first moment of impulsion, but knows from the second moment of impulsion onward.

For this one, there is knowledge that is uncommon to others.

Here, "He stood firm" means that even though other gods are there, they know "we are standing here," but being overwhelmed in the six sense spheres by a powerful, desirable object, having abandoned mindfulness, and not even knowing their state of having eaten and drunk, they pass away due to the interruption of food.

Does the *bodhisattva* not have such an object? No, he does not.

Indeed, he grasps the remaining deities with ten qualities, but he does not allow the object to crush himself; having overcome that object, he stands firm.

Therefore it was said: "Mindful and fully aware, Ānanda, the *bodhisattva* stood in the Tuṣita heaven."

He stood firm.

mula_pali:
200. ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yāvatāyukaṃ, ānanda, bodhisatto tusite kāye aṭṭhāsī’ti. Yampi, bhante, yāvatāyukaṃ bodhisatto tusite kāye aṭṭhāsi idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘sato sampajāno, ānanda, bodhisatto tusitā, kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamī’ti. Yampi, bhante , sato sampajāno bodhisatto tusitā kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkami idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.
mula_english:
“Venerable sir, I have heard and learned this from the Blessed One's own lips, I have received it directly: ‘For the whole of his life-span, Ānanda, the *bodhisattva* remained in the Tuṣita heaven ( *tuṣite kāye aṭṭhāsī* ).’ And that, venerable sir, for the whole of his life-span the *bodhisattva* remained in the Tuṣita heaven – this I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality ( *acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi* ) of the Blessed One.

“Venerable sir, I have heard and learned this from the Blessed One's own lips, I have received it directly: ‘Mindful and fully aware ( *sato sampajāno* ), Ānanda, the *bodhisattva* passed away from the Tuṣita heaven ( *tusitā kāyā cavitvā* ) and descended into his mother’s womb ( *mātukucchiṃ okkamī* ).’ And that, venerable sir, mindful and fully aware the *bodhisattva* passed away from the Tuṣita heaven and descended into his mother’s womb – this I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality ( *acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi* ) of the Blessed One.
commentary_pali:
200.Yāvatāyukanti sesattabhāvesu kiṃ yāvatāyukaṃ na tiṭṭhattīti? Āma na tiṭṭhati. Aññadā hi dīghāyukadevaloke nibbatto tattha pāramiyo na sakkā pūretunti akkhīni nimīletvā adhimuttikālaṃkiriyaṃ nāma katvā manussaloke nibbattati . Ayaṃ kālaṅkiriyā aññesaṃ na hoti. Tadā pana adinnadānaṃ nāma natthi, arakkhitasīlaṃ nāma natthi, sabbapāramīnaṃ pūritattā yāvatāyukaṃ aṭṭhāsi.

Sato sampajāno tusitā kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamatīti evaṃ tāva sabbapāramiyo pūretvā tadā bodhisatto yāvatāyukaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Devatānaṃ pana – ‘‘manussagaṇanāvasena idāni sattahi divasehi cuti bhavissatī’’ti pañca pubbanimittāni uppajjanti – mālā milāyanti, vatthāni kilissanti, kacchehi sedā muccanti, kāye dubbaṇṇiyaṃ okkamati, devo devāsane na saṇṭhāti.

Sato sampajāno tusitā kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamatī

Tattha mālāti paṭisandhiggahaṇadivase piḷandhanamālā. Tā kira saṭṭhisatasahassādhikā sattapaṇṇāsa-vassakoṭiyo amilāyitvā tadā milāyanti. Vatthesupi eseva nayo. Ettakaṃ pana kālaṃ devānaṃ neva sītaṃ na uṇhaṃ hoti, tasmiṃ kāle sarīrato bindubinduvasena sedā muccanti. Ettakañca kālaṃ tesaṃ sarīre khaṇḍiccapāliccādivasena vivaṇṇatā na paññāyati, devadhītā soḷasavassuddesikā viya, devaputtā vīsativassuddesikā viya khāyanti. Maraṇakāle pana nesaṃ kilantarūpo attabhāvo hoti. Ettakañca nesaṃ kālaṃ devaloke ukkaṇṭhitā nāma natthi, maraṇakāle pana nissasanti vijambhanti, sake āsane nābhiramanti.

mālā Vatthesu sedā vivaṇṇatā ukkaṇṭhitā

Imāni pana pubbanimittāni, yathā loke mahāpuññānaṃ rājarājamahāmattādīnaṃyeva ukkāpātabhūmicālacandaggāhādīni nimittāni paññāyanti, na sabbesaṃ, evameva mahesakkhānaṃ devatānaṃyeva paññāyanti, na sabbesaṃ. Yathā ca manussesu pubbanimittāni nakkhattapāṭhakādayova jānanti, na sabbe, evameva tānipi sabbe devā na jānanti, paṇḍitā eva pana jānanti. Tattha ye ca mandena kusalakammena nibbattā devaputtā, te tesu uppannesu – ‘‘idāni ko jānāti, kuhiṃ nibbattissāmā’’ti bhāyanti. Ye mahāpuññā, te – ‘‘amhehi dinnaṃ dānaṃ rakkhitaṃ sīlaṃ bhāvitaṃ bhāvanaṃ āgamma uparidevalokesu sampattiṃ anubhavissāmā’’ti na bhāyanti. Bodhisattopi tāni pubbanimittāni disvā ‘‘idāni anantare attabhāve buddho bhavissāmī’’ti na bhāyi. Athassa tesu nimittesu pātubhūtesu dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatā sannipatitvā – ‘‘mārisa tumhehi dasa pāramiyo pūrentehi na sakkasampattiṃ na mārabrahmacakkavattisampattiṃ patthentehi pūritā, lokanittharaṇatthāya pana buddhattaṃ patthayamānehi pūritā. So vo idāni kālo mārisa buddhattāya, samayo mārisa buddhattāyā’’ti yācanti.

Atha mahāsatto devatānaṃ paṭiññaṃ adatvāva kāladīpadesakulajanettiāyuparicchedavasena pañcamahāvilokanaṃ nāma vilokesi. Tattha ‘‘kālo nu kho, na kālo’’ti paṭhamaṃ kālaṃ vilokesi. Tattha vassasatasahassato uddhaṃ vaḍḍhitaāyukālo kālo nāma na hoti. Kasmā? Tadā hi sattānaṃ jātijarāmaraṇāni na paññāyanti, buddhānañca dhammadesanā nāma tilakkhaṇamuttā natthi, tesaṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti kathentānaṃ ‘‘kiṃ nāmetaṃ kathentī’’ti neva sotuṃ na saddhātuṃ maññanti, tato abhisamayo na hoti, tasmiṃ asati aniyyānikaṃ sāsanaṃ hoti. Tasmā so akālo. Vassasatato ūnaāyukālopi kālo nāma na hoti. Kasmā? Tadā hi sattā ussannakilesā honti, ussannakilesānañca dinnovādo ovādaṭṭhāne na tiṭṭhati. Udake daṇḍarāji viya khippaṃ vigacchati. Tasmā sopi akālo. Satasahassato pana paṭṭhāya heṭṭhā vassasatato paṭṭhāya uddhaṃ āyukālo kālo nāma. Tadā ca vassasatakālo hoti. Atha mahāsatto ‘‘nibbattitabbakālo’’ti kālaṃ passi.

pañcamahāvilokanaṃ kālaṃ

Tato dīpaṃ vilokento saparivāre cattāro dīpe oloketvā – ‘‘tīsu dīpesu buddhā na nibbattanti, jambudīpeyeva nibbattantī’’ti dīpaṃ passi.

dīpaṃ

Tato – ‘‘jambudīpo nāma mahā, dasayojanasahassaparimāṇo, katarasmiṃ nu kho padese buddhā nibbattantī’’ti desaṃ vilokento majjhimadesaṃ passi. Majjhimadeso nāma ‘‘puratthimāya disāya gajaṅgalaṃ nāma nigamo’’tiādinā nayena vinaye (mahāva. 259) vuttova. So pana āyāmato tīṇi yojanasatāni. Vitthārato aḍḍhatiyāni, parikkhepato navayojanasatānīti. Etasmiñhi padese cattāri aṭṭha soḷasa vā asaṅkhyeyyāni, kappasatasahassañca pāramiyo pūretvā sammāsambuddhā uppajjanti. Dve asaṅkhyeyyāni, kappasatasahassañca pāramiyo pūretvā paccekabuddhā uppajjanti, ekaṃ asaṅkhyeyyaṃ, kappasatasahassañca pāramiyo pūretvā sāriputtamoggallānādayo mahāsāvakā uppajjanti, catunnaṃ mahādīpānaṃ dvisahassānaṃ parittadīpānañca issariyādhipaccakārakacakkavattirājāno uppajjanti, aññe ca mahesakkhā khattiyabrāhmaṇagahapatimahāsālā uppajjanti. Idañcettha kapilavatthu nāma nagaraṃ, tattha mayā nibbattitabbanti niṭṭhamagamāsi.

desaṃ

Tato kulaṃ vilokento – ‘‘buddhā nāma lokasammate kule nibbattanti, idāni ca khattiyakulaṃ lokasammataṃ, tattha nibbattissāmi, suddhodano nāma rājā me pitā bhavissatī’’ti kulaṃ passi.

kulaṃ

Tato mātaraṃ vilokento – ‘‘buddhamātā nāma lolā surādhuttā na hoti, kappasatasahassaṃ pūritapāramī jātito paṭṭhāya akhaṇḍapañcasīlā hoti, ayañca mahāmāyā nāma devī edisā. Ayaṃ me mātā bhavissati. Kittakaṃ panassā āyū’’ti āvajjanto – ‘‘dasannaṃ māsānaṃ upari satta divasānī’’ti passi.
