mātaraṃ

Iti imaṃ pañcamahāvilokanaṃ viloketvā – ‘‘kālo me mārisā buddhabhāvāyā’’ti devatānaṃ saṅgahaṃ karonto paṭiññaṃ datvā ‘‘gacchatha tumhe’’ti tā devatā uyyojetvā tusitadevatāhi parivuto tusitapure nandanavanaṃ pāvisi. Sabbadevalokesu hi nandanavanaṃ atthiyeva. Tattha naṃ devatā – ‘‘ito cuto sugatiṃ gaccha, ito cuto sugatiṃ gacchā’’ti pubbekatakusalakammokāsaṃ sārayamānā vicaranti. So evaṃ devatāhi kusalaṃ sārayamānāhi parivuto tattha vicarantova cavi.

pañcamahāvilokanaṃ

Evaṃ cuto cavāmīti pajānāti, cuticittaṃ na jānāti. Paṭisandhiṃ gahetvāpi paṭisandhicittaṃ na jānāti, imasmiṃ me ṭhāne paṭisandhi gahitāti evaṃ pana jānāti. Keci pana therā ‘‘āvajjanapariyāyo nāma laddhuṃ vaṭṭati, dutiyatatiyacittavāreyeva jānissatī’’ti vadanti. Tipiṭakamahāsīvatthero panāha – ‘‘mahāsattānaṃ paṭisandhi na aññesaṃ paṭisandhisadisā, koṭippattaṃ tesaṃ satisampajaññaṃ. Yasmā pana teneva cittena taṃ cittaṃ ñātuṃ na sakkā, tasmā cuticittaṃ na jānāti. Cutikkhaṇepi cavāmīti pajānāti, paṭisandhiṃ gahetvāpi paṭisandhicittaṃ na jānāti, asukasmiṃ ṭhāne paṭisandhi gahitāti pajānāti, tasmiṃ kāle dasasahassī kampatī’’ti. Evaṃ sato sampajāno mātukucchiṃ okkamanto pana ekūnavīsatiyā paṭisandhicittesu mettāpubbabhāgassa somanassa-sahagata-ñāṇasampayutta-asaṅkhārika-kusalacittassa sadisamahāvipākacittena paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhi. Mahāsīvatthero pana ‘‘upekkhāsahagatenā’’ti āha.

Paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhanto pana āsāḷhīpuṇṇamāyaṃ uttarāsāḷhanakkhattena aggahesi. Tadā kira mahāmāyā pure puṇṇamāya sattamadivasato paṭṭhāya vigatasurāpānaṃ mālāgandhavibhūsanasampannaṃ nakkhattakīḷaṃ anubhavamānā sattame divase pāto vuṭṭhāya gandhodakena nhāyitvā sabbālaṅkāravibhūsitā varabhojanaṃ bhuñjitvā uposathaṅgāni adhiṭṭhāya sirīgabbhaṃ pavisitvā sirīsayane nipannā niddaṃ okkamamānā idaṃ supinaṃ addasa – ‘‘cattāro kira naṃ mahārājāno sayaneneva saddhiṃ ukkhipitvā anotattadahaṃ netvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha nesaṃ deviyo āgantvā manussamalaharaṇatthaṃ nhāpetvā dibbavatthaṃ nivāsetvā gandhehi vilimpetvā dibbapupphāni piḷandhitvā tato avidūre rajatapabbato, tassa anto kanakavimānaṃ atthi, tasmiṃ pācīnato sīsaṃ katvā nipajjāpesuṃ. Atha bodhisatto setavaravāraṇo hutvā tato avidūre eko suvaṇṇapabbato, tattha caritvā tato oruyha rajatapabbataṃ abhiruhitvā uttaradisato āgamma kanakavimānaṃ pavisitvā mātaraṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā dakkhiṇapassaṃ phāletvā kucchiṃ paviṭṭhasadiso ahosi.

Atha pabuddhā devī taṃ supinaṃ rañño ārocesi. Rājā pabhātāya rattiyā catusaṭṭhimatte brāhmaṇapāmokkhe pakkosāpetvā haritūpalittāya lājādīhi katamaṅgalasakkārāya bhūmiyā mahārahāni āsanāni paññāpetvā tattha nisinnānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ sappimadhusakkarābhisaṅkhārassa varapāyāsassa suvaṇṇarajatapātiyo pūretvā suvaṇṇarajatapātītiheva paṭikujjitvā adāsi, aññehi ca ahatavatthakapilagāvīdānādīhi te santappesi. Atha nesaṃ sabbakāmasantappitānaṃ supinaṃ ārocāpetvā – ‘‘kiṃ bhavissatī’’ti pucchi. Brāhmaṇā āhaṃsu – ‘‘mā cintayi mahārāja, deviyā te kucchimhi gabbho patiṭṭhito, so ca kho purisagabbho, na itthigabbho, putto te bhavissati. So sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasissati, rājā bhavissati cakkavattī. Sace agārā nikkhamma pabbajissati, buddho bhavissati loke vivaṭṭacchado’’ti. Evaṃ sato sampajāno bodhisatto tusitakāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamati.

Tattha sato sampajānoti iminā catutthāya gabbhāvakkantiyā okkamatīti dasseti. Catasso hi gabbhāvakkantiyo.

sato sampajāno

‘‘Catasso imā, bhante, gabbhāvakkantiyo. Idha, bhante, ekacco asampajāno mātukucchiṃ okkamati, asampajāno mātukucchismiṃ ṭhāti, asampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, ayaṃ paṭhamā gabbhāvakkanti.

Puna caparaṃ, bhante, idhekacco sampajāno mātukucchiṃ okkamati, asampajāno mātukucchismiṃ ṭhāti, asampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, ayaṃ dutiyā gabbhāvakkanti.

Puna caparaṃ, bhante, idhekacco sampajāno mātukucchiṃ okkamati, sampajāno mātukucchismiṃ ṭhāti, asampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, ayaṃ tatiyā gabbhāvakkanti.

Puna caparaṃ, bhante, idhekacco sampajāno mātukucchiṃ okkamati, sampajāno mātukucchismiṃ ṭhāti, sampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, ayaṃ catutthā gabbhāvakkantī’’ti (dī. ni. 3.147).

Etāsu paṭhamā lokiyamanussānaṃ hoti, dutiyā asītimahāsāvakānaṃ, tatiyā dvinnaṃ aggasāvakānaṃ paccekabodhisattānañca. Te kira kammajavātehi uddhaṃpādā adhosirā anekasataporise papāte viya yonimukhe tāḷacchiggalena hatthī viya ativiya sambādhena yonimukhena nikkhamamānā anantaṃ dukkhaṃ pāpuṇanti. Tena nesaṃ ‘‘mayaṃ nikkhamāmā’’ti sampajānatā na hoti. Catutthā sabbaññubodhisattānaṃ. Te hi mātukucchismiṃ paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhantāpi jānanti, tattha vasantāpi jānanti. Nikkhamanakālepi nesaṃ kammajavātā uddhaṃpāde adhosire katvā khipituṃ na sakkonti, dve hatthe pasāretvā akkhīni ummīletvā ṭhitakāva nikkhamanti.
commentary_english:
200. What does *yāvatāyuka* mean—in the remaining states of existence, does *yāvatāyuka* not endure? Yes, it does not endure.

Moreover, someone reborn in a long-lived *devaloka*, unable to perfect the *pāramīs* there, closes their eyes, makes something called an *adhimuttikālaṃkiriya*, and is reborn in the human world.

This *kālaṅkiriya* does not happen to others. But then, there is no such thing as un-given alms, there is no such thing as unprotected morality; due to the perfection of all the *pāramīs*, *yāvatāyuka* endures.

*sato sampajāno tusitā kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamatī*—thus, first, having perfected all the *pāramīs*, then the *bodhisattva* remains *yāvatāyuka*.

Moreover, for the gods—"Due to the calculation of humans, after seven days there will now be death"—five preliminary signs arise: garlands wither, clothes become soiled, sweat flows from the armpits, ugliness overtakes the body, and a god does not stand firm on the divine seat.

*sato sampajāno tusitā kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamatī*. There, *mālā* means garlands worn on the day of conception. Those sixty-seven million and fifty-seven hundred thousand *vassakoṭis*, un-withered, then wither. This is the same with clothes. Moreover, for this long, there is neither cold nor heat for the gods; at that time, sweat flows from the body in a drop-by-drop fashion. And for this long, ugliness is not apparent in their bodies in the manner of breakage and decay; the daughters of the gods appear like sixteen-year-olds, the sons of the gods appear like twenty-year-olds. But at the time of death, their existence becomes exhausted. Moreover, for this long, there is no such thing as *ukkaṇṭhitā* in the *devaloka*; but at the time of death, they sigh, they yawn, they do not delight in their own seats.

garlands, clothes, sweat, ugliness, *ukkaṇṭhitā*. Moreover, these preliminary signs, just as in the world, signs such as meteors, earthquakes, and lunar eclipses appear only to the greatly meritorious kings and great ministers, not to everyone; in the same way, they appear only to deities of great power, not to everyone.

And just as among humans, astrologers alone know the preliminary signs, not everyone, in the same way, all the gods do not know those signs, only the wise know. Moreover, those sons of gods who are born of meager meritorious deeds, when those signs arise in them, they are afraid—"Now, who knows, where will we be reborn?"

Those who are greatly meritorious, they are not afraid—"Having performed almsgiving, protected morality, and cultivated meditation, we will experience prosperity in the upper *devalokas*."

Even the *bodhisattva*, having seen those preliminary signs, is not afraid—"Now, in the next existence, I will become a Buddha."

Then, when those signs have appeared in him, ten thousand *cakkavāḷa* deities, having gathered together, implore—"O honorable one, by your performing the ten *pāramīs*, *sakkasampatti* was not fulfilled by those desiring it, but *buddhatva* was fulfilled by those desiring to liberate the world. Now is the time for you to become a Buddha, O honorable one, now is the opportunity to become a Buddha!"

Then the *mahāsattva*, without giving a pledge to the deities, contemplated what is called the Five Great Contemplations—time, continent, country, family, and mother—by means of determining lifespan. There, first he contemplated time, thinking, "Is it the time, or is it not the time?" There, a lifespan increased to more than a hundred thousand years, that is not called the time. Why? Because at that time, birth, old age, and death are not apparent in beings, and there is no such thing as the *dhammadesanā* of the Buddhas devoid of the three characteristics; when they preach, "Impermanent, suffering, without self," they do not think, "What are they preaching?", and they neither listen nor trust, therefore there is no attainment, and when that is not present, the teaching is one that does not lead out. Therefore, that is not the time. A lifespan less than a hundred years is also not called the time. Why? Because at that time, beings are overcome by defilements, and for those overcome by defilements, a sermon given does not stand in the place of instruction. Like a line drawn on water, it quickly vanishes. Therefore, that also is not the time. More than a hundred thousandWhen, however, the span of life is under a hundred thousand and over a hundred years, that is called the proper time.
Now at that time the span of life was one hundred years.
Then the great being saw the time to be reborn (nibbattitabbakālo).

The five great investigations (pañcamahāvilokanaṃ)

Then, investigating the continent (dīpaṃ), and considering the four continents with their retinues, [he] saw the continent (dīpaṃ), [thinking,] "Buddhas are not born in three continents; they are born only in Jambudvīpa."

Then, considering THE DISTRICT (desaṃ), and thinking : “Jambudvipa indeed is large, ten thousand *yojanas* in extent; now in which district of it do the Buddhas appear?" he fixed upon the Middle Country (majjhimadesaṃ)

The Middle Country (majjhimadeso), namely, in the *Vinaya*, it has been said in this manner: "In the eastern direction, there is a market-town called Gajaṅgala."
That, however, is three hundred *yojanas* in length, two and a half in width, and nine hundred *yojanas* in circumference.
In this district (padese), four, eight, or sixteen incalculable (asaṅkhyeyyāni) Buddhas, having fulfilled the perfections (pāramiyo) during a hundred thousand aeons (kappasatasahassañca), arise.
Two incalculable (asaṅkhyeyyāni) *Pratyekabuddhas*, having fulfilled the perfections (pāramiyo) during a hundred thousand aeons (kappasatasahassañca), arise; one incalculable (asaṅkhyeyyaṃ) Great Disciples such as Sāriputta and Moggallāna arise, having fulfilled the perfections (pāramiyo) during a hundred thousand aeons (kappasatasahassañca); Wheel-turning Kings, exercising sovereignty and dominance over the four great continents (mahādīpānaṃ), the two thousand minor islands (parittadīpānañca), and other powerful *Kṣatriyas*, *Brāhmaṇas*, householders (*gahapati*), and great *Sālas* arise.
And here in Kapilavatthu (kapilavatthu) by name, he made the firm resolution to be reborn.

Then, investigating the family (kulaṃ), he saw the family, [thinking,] "Buddhas are born in a family held in high esteem by the world, and now the *Kṣatriya* family is held in high esteem by the world; there I will be born; the king named Śuddhodana will be my father."

Then, investigating THE MOTHER (mātaraṃ), he thought: “The mother of a Buddha is not lustful, or corrupt as to drink, but has fulfilled the perfections (pāramī) for a hundred thousand ages, and from her birth upwards has kept the five Precepts unbroken, and this lady Mahā Māyā is such a one.
She will be my mother.
“ And further considering how long her life should last, he foresaw that it would still last ten months and seven days.

Thus, having investigated these five great investigations (pañcamahāvilokanaṃ) - "The time has arrived, sirs, for me to become a Buddha" - consenting to the deities, giving the promise, dismissing those deities, saying, "Go!", surrounded by the deities of the Tusita heaven, he entered the Nandana grove in the Tusita heaven.
Indeed, in all the worlds of the deities, there is assuredly a Nandana grove.
There, the deities, reminding him of the opportunity he had gained by good deeds done in a former birth, saying to him, "When hence deceased, go to a good destiny! When hence deceased, go to a good destiny!", are wont to roam about.
And thus he also, surrounded by deities reminding him of his acquired merit, departing thence while walking about there.

Thus, knowing "having deceased thus, I will decease," he does not know the consciousness of deceasing (cuticittaṃ).
Even having taken rebirth (paṭisandhiṃ), he does not know the consciousness of rebirth (paṭisandhicittaṃ); but thus he knows, "In this place, I have taken rebirth."
Some elders, however, say, "The turn of mind, namely, is fit to be obtained; he will know it even at the second or third moment of consciousness."
The *Tipiṭaka* *Mahāsīva Thera*, however, said: “The rebirth (paṭisandhi) of great beings is not like the rebirth (paṭisandhi) of others; their mindfulness and comprehension have reached the highest point.
Since, however, it is not possible to know that consciousness (cittaṃ) with that very consciousness (cittena), therefore he does not know the consciousness of deceasing (cuticittaṃ).
Even at the moment of deceasing, he knows "I am deceasing"; even having taken rebirth (paṭisandhiṃ), he does not know the consciousness of rebirth (paṭisandhicittaṃ); he knows "In such and such a place, rebirth has been taken"; at that time, the ten-thousandfold world quakes."
Thus, mindful and fully aware, entering the womb of his mother, however, in the consciousnesses of rebirth on the nineteenth, he took rebirth (paṭisandhiṃ) with the *kusala* consciousness of a kind with the impartial great resultant consciousness (sadisamahāvipākacittena), associated with joy, connected with knowledge (*ñāṇa*), and unprompted, with goodwill as a preliminary part.
The *Mahāsīva Thera*, however, said: “With what is associated with equanimity (upekkhāsahagatenā)."
However, when [the Bodhisattva] was conceived, he took rebirth on the full moon day of Āsāḷha, under the lunar asterism of Uttarāsāḷha.

At that time, it is said that Mahāmāyā, starting from the seventh day before the full moon, was enjoying the asterism festival, replete with merriment, free from drinking alcohol, and adorned with garlands and fragrances. On the seventh day, having risen early in the morning, bathed with scented water, adorned herself with all ornaments, eaten excellent food, undertaken the observance of the Uposatha vows, she entered the royal chamber and lay down on the royal bed, and as she was falling asleep, she saw this dream: "Four great kings lifted her up, along with her bed, took her to Lake Anotatta and stood her on one side. Then their goddesses came, bathed her to remove human impurities, dressed her in divine garments, anointed her with perfumes, and adorned her with divine flowers. Not far from there was a silver mountain, and inside it was a golden mansion. There, facing east, they laid her down. Then the Bodhisattva, having become a superb white elephant, wandered on the Golden Mountain not far from there, descended from there, ascended the Silver Mountain, came from the north, entered the golden mansion, circumambulated his mother, split her right side, and seemed to enter her womb."

Then, awakened, the queen told the dream to the king. In the morning, the king summoned sixty-four eminent *brāhmaṇas*, had costly seats spread on a ground prepared for the auspicious ceremony with green leaves and parched rice, and filling gold and silver bowls with excellent milk-rice mixed with ghee, honey, and sugar, he gave it to the *brāhmaṇas*, overturning the gold and silver bowls themselves. He satisfied them with gifts of new clothes and tawny cows, etc. Then, having satisfied all their desires, he related the dream and asked, "What will become of it?"

The *brāhmaṇas* said, "Do not worry, great king, a *garbha* is established in your queen's womb, and it is a male *garbha*, not a female *garbha*. You will have a son. If he lives the household life, he will become a *cakravartin* (universal monarch). If, leaving the household, he goes forth into homelessness, he will become a Buddha, who will remove the veils [of ignorance] in the world." Thus, mindful and clearly comprehending, the *bodhisattva* descended from the Tuṣita heaven into his mother's womb.

There, "mindful and clearly comprehending" indicates that he descends with the fourth type of entering a womb. For there are four ways of entering a womb.

"There are these four ways, venerable sir, of entering a womb. Here, venerable sir, a certain person descends into the mother’s womb unmindful, stays in the mother’s womb unmindful, and leaves the mother’s womb unmindful. This is the first way of entering a womb.

"Again, venerable sir, a certain person descends into the mother’s womb mindful, stays in the mother’s womb unmindful, and leaves the mother’s womb unmindful. This is the second way of entering a womb.

"Again, venerable sir, a certain person descends into the mother’s womb mindful, stays in the mother’s womb mindful, and leaves the mother’s womb unmindful. This is the third way of entering a womb.

"Again, venerable sir, a certain person descends into the mother’s womb mindful, stays in the mother’s womb mindful, and leaves the mother’s womb mindful. This is the fourth way of entering a womb" (Dīgha Nikāya 3.147).

Among these, the first is for ordinary people, the second for the eighty great disciples, and the third for the two chief disciples and the *pratyekabuddhas*. It is said that they, driven by karmic winds, emerge from the womb's opening headfirst and feet up, like an elephant through a hole in a door, experiencing infinite suffering from the extremely tight vaginal opening, like someone falling into a chasm inhabited by hundreds of people. Therefore, they are not mindful that "we are emerging." The fourth is for all-knowing Buddhas. For they are aware even when taking rebirth in their mother's womb, and they are aware while dwelling there. At the time of birth also, the karmic winds cannot throw them headfirst and feet up. They emerge standing upright, with their two hands outstretched and their eyes open.

mula_pali: 201. ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto tusitā kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamati, atha sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso loke pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Yāpi tā lokantarikā aghā asaṃvutā andhakārā andhakāratimisā, yatthapime candimasūriyā evaṃmahiddhikā evaṃmahānubhāvā ābhāya nānubhonti tatthapi appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso loke pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi tenobhāsena aññamaññaṃ sañjānanti – aññepi kira, bho, santi sattā idhūpapannāti. Ayañca dasasahassī lokadhātu saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati appamāṇo ca uḷāro obhāso loke pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāva’nti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.
mula_english:
201. “Venerable sir, I have heard and learned this directly from the Blessed One, directly received: ‘When, Ānanda, the Bodhisattva passed away from the Tuṣita heaven and descended into his mother’s womb, then in this world with its gods (devas), its Māras, and its Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics (śramaṇa) and Brahmins (brāhmaṇī), with its princes and its people, an immeasurable, splendid light ( *uḷāro obhāso*) appeared in the world, surpassing the glory of the gods.

And even those dark, obscured, unfathomable, unknown, interstitial worlds where even the sun and moon, so mighty and splendid, do not shine with their light,

there too, an immeasurable, splendid light (*appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso*) appeared in the world, surpassing the glory of the gods (devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ).

And those beings (sattā) that have been reborn there recognise each other by this light and know: “Other beings, too, have been born here!”

And this ten-thousandfold world-system (*dasasahassī lokadhātu*) shakes and quakes and trembles, and there too an immeasurable, splendid light (*appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso*) appeared in the world, surpassing the glory of the gods.’

And that, venerable sir… …this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.”
commentary_pali:
201.Mātukucchiṃ okkamatīti ettha mātukucchiṃ okkanto hotīti attho. Okkante hi tasmiṃ evaṃ hoti, na okkamamāne. Appamāṇoti buddhappamāṇo, vipuloti attho. Uḷāroti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Devānubhāvanti ettha devānaṃ ayamānubhāvo – nivatthavatthassa pabhā dvādasa yojanāni pharati, tathā sarīrassa, tathā alaṅkārassa, tathā vimānassa, taṃ atikkamitvāti attho.

Lokantarikāti tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ cakkavāḷānaṃ antarā ekeko lokantarikā hoti, tiṇṇaṃ sakaṭacakkānaṃ pattānaṃ vā aññamaññaṃ āhacca ṭhapitānaṃ majjhe okāso viya. So pana lokantarikanirayo parimāṇato aṭṭhayojanasahasso hoti. Aghāti niccavivaṭā. Asaṃvutāti heṭṭhāpi appatiṭṭhā. Andhakārāti tamabhūtā. Andhakāratimisāti cakkhuviññāṇuppattinivāraṇato andhabhāvakaraṇatimisena samannāgatā. Tattha kira cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na jāyati. Evaṃmahiddhikāti candimasūriyā kira ekappahāreneva tīsu dīpesu paññāyanti, evaṃmahiddhikā. Ekekāya disāya navanavayojanasatasahassāni andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ālokaṃ dassenti, evaṃ mahānubhāvā. Ābhāyanānubhontīti attano pabhāya nappahonti. Te kira cakkavāḷapabbatassa vemajjhena caranti, cakkavāḷapabbatañca atikkamma lokantarikanirayo, tasmā te tattha ābhāya nappahonti.

Lokantarikā Aghā Asaṃvutā Andhakārā Andhakāratimisā Evaṃmahiddhikā Ābhāya nānubhontī

Yepi tattha sattāti yepi tasmiṃ lokantaramahāniraye sattā upapannā. Kiṃ pana kammaṃ katvā te tattha uppajjantīti? Bhāriyaṃ dāruṇaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ dhammikasamaṇabrāhmaṇānañca upari aparādhaṃ aññañca divase divase pāṇavadhādisāhasikakammaṃ katvā uppajjanti tambapaṇṇidīpe abhayacoranāgacorādayo viya. Tesaṃ attabhāvo tigāvutiko hoti, vaggulīnaṃ viya dīghanakhā honti. Te rukkhe vagguliyo viya nakhehi cakkavāḷapāde lagganti. Yadā pana saṃsappantā aññamaññassa hatthapāsaṃ gatā honti, atha ‘‘bhakkho no laddho’’ti maññamānā tattha vāvaṭā viparivattitvā lokasandhārakaudake patanti. Vāte paharante madhukaphalāni viya chijjitvā udake patanti. Patitamattā ca accantakhāre udake piṭṭhapiṇḍi viya vilīyanti.

Yepi tattha sattā

Aññepi kira bho santi sattāti – ‘‘yathā mayaṃ mahādukkhaṃ anubhavāma, evaṃ aññepi kira sattā idaṃ dukkhaṃ anubhavantā idhūpapannā’’ti taṃ divasaṃ passanti. Ayaṃ pana obhāso ekayāgupānamattampi na tiṭṭhati, yāvatā niddāyitvā pabuddho ārammaṇaṃ vibhāveti, tattakaṃ kālaṃ hoti. Dīghabhāṇakā pana ‘‘accharāsaṅghāṭamattameva vijjubhāso viya niccharitvā kiṃ idanti bhaṇantānaṃyeva antaradhāyatī’’ti vadanti. Saṅkampatīti samantato kampati. Itaradvayaṃ purimapasseva vevacanaṃ. Puna appamāṇo cātiādi nigamanatthaṃ vuttaṃ.

Aññepi kira bho santi sattā Saṅkampatī appamāṇo cā
commentary_english:
201. "Having entered the mother's womb": here, the meaning is that he has entered the mother's womb. For it is thus when he has entered, not while he is entering. "Immeasurable": immeasurable like the Buddha, meaning vast. "Magnificent": a synonym for that. "Divine power": here, this is the divine power of the devas: the light of the garment worn pervades twelve yojanas, likewise of the body, likewise of the ornaments, likewise of the palace; the meaning is that it transcends that.

"Worlds-in-between": between every three sets of three world-spheres there is one world-in-between, like the space in the middle of the bowls of three cartwheels struck and placed against each other. But that hell of the worlds-in-between is eight thousand yojanas in extent. "Aghā": always open. "Asaṃvutā": without support even below. "Andhakārā": of the nature of darkness. "Andhakāratimisā": endowed with darkness that causes blindness, because it prevents the arising of eye-consciousness. It is said that eye-consciousness does not arise there. "Of such great power": it is said that the moon and sun appear in the three continents with just one strike, of such great power. In each direction they dispel the darkness for nine hundred and ninety thousand yojanas and show the light, of such great power. "Do not experience with light": they are not able to with their own light. It is said that they travel in the middle of the world-sphere-mountain, and the hell of the worlds-in-between is beyond the world-sphere-mountain, therefore they are not able to with light there.

Worlds-in-between, aghā, asaṃvutā, andhakārā, andhakāratimisā, of such great power, do not experience with light.

"Those beings who are there": those beings who have arisen in that great hell of the worlds-in-between. What kind of karma do they do to arise there? They commit heavy, cruel offenses against their parents, righteous ascetics and brahmins, and other daring deeds such as killing living beings day after day, like Abhayacora, Nāgacora, and others in Tambapaṇṇidīpa. Their bodies are three gavutas tall, and they have long nails like bats. Like bats, they cling to the foot of the world-sphere-mountain with their nails. When, as they creep along, they come within reach of each other's hands, then, thinking "we have not gotten food," they turn around there and fall into the world-sustaining water. When the wind strikes, they break off and fall into the water like madhuka fruits. As soon as they fall, they dissolve in the extremely salty water like lumps of flour.

Those beings who are there.

"Are there other beings, sir?": "Just as we experience great suffering, so other beings who are experiencing this suffering have arisen here," they see that day. But this light does not last even for the time it takes to drink one portion of gruel, only as long as it takes to fall asleep and awaken and discern an object. But the long reciters say, "It just shoots out like a flash of lightning for the space of a letter cluster and disappears as soon as they say, 'What is this?'" "Saṅkampatī": it trembles all around. The other two are synonyms for the previous passage. Again, "immeasurable" etc. was said for the purpose of conclusion.

Are there other beings, sir?, saṅkampatī, immeasurable.

mula_pali: 202. ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti, cattāro devaputtā catuddisaṃ ārakkhāya upagacchanti – mā naṃ bodhisattaṃ vā bodhisattamātaraṃ vā manusso vā amanusso vā koci vā viheṭhesī’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.
mula_english:
“Venerable sir, I have heard and learned this from the Blessed One's own lips: 'When, Ānanda, the *bodhisattva* has descended into his mother's womb (mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti), four young deities (devaputtā) approach to guard him in the four directions, so that no human (manusso) or non-human (amanusso), or anyone at all might harm (viheṭhesī) the *bodhisattva* (bodhisattaṃ) or the *bodhisattva's* mother (bodhisattamātaraṃ).'

And also, venerable sir... and so on... this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality (acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ) of the Blessed One (bhagavato)."
commentary_pali:
202.Cattāro devaputtā catuddisaṃ ārakkhāya upagacchantīti ettha cattāroti catunnaṃ mahārājūnaṃ vasena vuttaṃ, dasasahassacakkavāḷe pana cattāro cattāro katvā cattālīsadasasahassā honti. Tattha imasmiṃ cakkavāḷe mahārājāno khaggahatthā āgantvā bodhisattassa ārakkhaṇatthāya upagantvā sirīgabbhaṃ paviṭṭhā, itare gabbhadvārato paṭṭhāya avaruddhapaṃsupisācakādiyakkhagaṇe paṭikkamāpetvā yāva cakkavāḷā ārakkhaṃ gaṇhiṃsu.

Kimatthaṃ panāyaṃ rakkhā āgatā? Nanu paṭisandhikkhaṇe kalalakālato paṭṭhāya sacepi koṭisatasahassā mārā koṭisatasahassaṃ sineruṃ ukkhipitvā bodhisattassa vā bodhisattamātuyā vā antarāyakaraṇatthaṃ āgaccheyyuṃ, sabbe antarāva antaradhāyeyyuṃ. Vuttampi cetaṃ bhagavatā ruhiruppādavatthusmiṃ – ‘‘aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso, yaṃ parūpakkamena tathāgataṃ jīvitā voropeyya. Anupakkamena, bhikkhave, tathāgatā parinibbāyanti. Gacchatha tumhe, bhikkhave, yathāvihāraṃ, arakkhiyā, bhikkhave, tathāgatā’’ti (cūḷava. 341). Evametaṃ, na parūpakkamena tesaṃ jīvitantarāyo atthi. Santi kho pana amanussā virūpā duddasikā, bheravarupā pakkhino, yesaṃ rūpaṃ disvā saddaṃ vā sutvā bodhisattamātu bhayaṃ vā santāso vā uppajjeyya, tesaṃ nivāraṇatthāya rakkhaṃ aggahesuṃ. Apica kho bodhisattassa puññatejena sañjātagāravā attano gāravacoditāpi te evamakaṃsu.

Kiṃ pana te antogabbhaṃ pavisitvā ṭhitā cattāro mahārājāno bodhisattamātuyā attānaṃ dassenti na dassentīti? Nahānamaṇḍanabhojanādisarīrakiccakāle na dassenti, sirīgabbhaṃ pavisitvā varasayane nipannakāle pana dassenti. Tattha kiñcāpi amanussadassanaṃ nāma manussānaṃ sappaṭibhayaṃ hoti, bodhisattamātā pana attano ceva puttassa ca puññānubhāvena te disvā na bhāyati, pakatiantepurapālakesu viya assā tesu cittaṃ uppajjati.
commentary_english:
202. "The four sons of the gods approach in the four directions for protection" – here, "four" is said with reference to the four Great Kings. In ten thousand world-systems, having made four groups of four, there are forty thousand.

There, in this world-system, the Great Kings, sword in hand, having come and approached for the protection of the Bodhisattva, entered the auspicious womb. Others, from the door of the womb onwards, having driven back the groups of *yakṣas*, including the obstructed ash-colored *piśācas*, took up protection as far as the world-circle.

Why then, has this protection come? Surely, from the moment of rebirth, from the time of the *kalala*, even if hundreds of thousands of *Māras*, having lifted up a hundred thousand Sumerus, should come for the purpose of causing an obstruction to the Bodhisattva or the Bodhisattva's mother, all would disappear in the space in between.

This was also said by the Blessed One in the context of the production of blood: "This is impossible, monks, there is no opportunity, that one should deprive a *tathāgata* of life by an attack by others. Monks, *tathāgatas* attain *parinirvāṇa* without attack. Go forth, monks, according to your dwelling, the *tathāgatas* are without protection," (Cūḷava. 341). Thus it is, there is no obstruction to their life by an attack by others.

Indeed, there are non-human beings, deformed, difficult to see, birds of terrible form, whose form having been seen, or whose sound having been heard, fear or terror would arise for the Bodhisattva's mother; for the prevention of them, they took up protection.

Moreover, through the power of the merit of the Bodhisattva, having become respectful, even urged on by their own respect, they did thus.

Do those four Great Kings, having entered and stood inside the womb, show themselves to the Bodhisattva's mother or do they not show themselves? At the time of bodily activities such as bathing, adornment, eating, and so on, they do not show themselves. Having entered the auspicious womb, they show themselves at the time of lying down on an excellent bed.

There, although the sight of non-humans is frightening to humans, the Bodhisattva's mother, however, having seen them, does not fear through the power of the merit of herself and her son, but rather, confidence arises in them, like in the regular palace guards.

mula_pali:
203. ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti, pakatiyā sīlavatī bodhisattamātā hoti viratā pāṇātipātā viratā adinnādānā viratā kāmesumicchācārā viratā musāvādā viratā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā , ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti, na bodhisattamātu purisesu mānasaṃ uppajjati kāmaguṇūpasaṃhitaṃ, anatikkamanīyā ca bodhisattamātā hoti kenaci purisena rattacittenā’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti, lābhinī bodhisattamātā hoti pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ. Sā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricāretī’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.
mula_english:
203. “I heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: ‘When the *Bodhisattva* had descended into his mother’s womb, she became intrinsically virtuous, refraining from killing living beings (*prāṇātipātā*), from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā*), from misconduct in sensual pleasures (*kāmesumicchācārā*), from false speech (*musāvādā*), and from wines, liquors, and intoxicants, which are the basis of negligence (*surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā*).’
That too, venerable sir…pe… this I, venerable sir, remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.

“I heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: ‘When the *Bodhisattva* had descended into his mother’s womb, no sensual thought (*mānasaṃ*) arose in her concerning men, and she was inaccessible to any man having a lustful mind (*rattacittenā*).’
That too, venerable sir…pe… this I, venerable sir, remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.

“I heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: ‘When the *Bodhisattva* had descended into his mother’s womb, she obtained the five cords of sensual pleasure (*kāmaguṇānaṃ*).
and furnished and endowed with them, she enjoyed herself with them.’
That too, venerable sir…pe… this I, venerable sir, remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.
commentary_pali:
203.Pakatiyāsīlavatīti sabhāveneva sīlasampannā. Anuppanne kira buddhe manussā tāpasaparibbājakānaṃ santike vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā sīlaṃ gaṇhanti, bodhisattamātāpi kāladevilassa isino santike gaṇhāti. Bodhisatte pana kucchigate aññassa pādamūle nisīdituṃ nāma na sakkā, samāsane nisīditvā gahitasīlampi avaññā kāraṇamattaṃ hoti. Tasmā sayameva sīlaṃ aggahesīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Purisesūti bodhisattassa pitaraṃ ādiṃ katvā kesuci manussesu purisādhippāyacittaṃ nuppajjati. Tañca kho bodhisatte gāravena, na pahīnakilesatāya. Bodhisattamātu rūpaṃ pana sukusalāpi sippikā potthakammādīsupi kātuṃ na sakkonti, taṃ disvā purisassa rāgo nuppajjatīti na sakkā vattuṃ. Sace pana taṃ rattacitto upasaṅkamitukāmo hoti, pādā na vahanti, dibbasaṅkhalikā viya bajjhanti. Tasmā ‘‘anatikkamanīyā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

Purisesū

Pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānanti pubbe ‘‘kāmaguṇūpasaṃhita’’nti purisādhippāyavasena vatthupaṭikkhepo kathito, idha ārammaṇappaṭilābho dassito. Tadā kira ‘‘deviyā evarūpo putto kucchismiṃ uppanno’’ti, sutvā samantato rājāno mahagghaābharaṇatūriyādivasena pañcadvārārammaṇavatthubhūtaṃ paṇṇākāraṃ pesenti, bodhisattassa ca bodhisattamātuyā ca katakammassa ussannattā lābhasakkārassa pamāṇaparicchedo nāma natthi.

Pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇāna
commentary_english:
203. *pakatiyā sīlavatī* means those who are virtuous are naturally endowed with virtue.

When Buddhas have not yet arisen, people go to ascetics and wanderers, pay homage, squat on their heels, and take vows. The Bodhisattva's mother also takes vows in the presence of the sage Kāḷadevila.

When the Bodhisattva is in the womb, it is not possible to sit at the feet of another. Even the vows taken while sitting on an equal seat are merely a cause for disrespect.

Therefore, it is said that she herself took the vows.

*purisesū* means that the father of the Bodhisattva, having made a beginning, does not generate a mind with a man's intention in some men.

And that is with reverence for the Bodhisattva, not because of the abandonment of defilements (kilesa).

Even the most skilled artisans cannot make an image of the Bodhisattva's mother, even in paintings and so on. It is not possible to say that lust does not arise in a man who sees her.

If he is lustful and wants to approach her, his feet do not carry him; they are bound as if by divine chains.

Therefore, it is said, "She is unapproachable," and so on.

*pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇāna* means previously, "associated with the objects of desire."

Rejection of the object is spoken of in terms of the intention towards a man; here, attainment of the object (ārammaṇa) is shown.

Then, having heard, "A son of this form has been born to the queen!" from all around, kings send gifts of valuable ornaments, musical instruments, and so on, in the manner of tribute, which are the basis of the five sense objects. Because of the eminence of the meritorious deeds done by the Bodhisattva and the Bodhisattva's mother, there is no limit or measure to the gain and honor.

mula_pali: 204. ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti, na bodhisattamātu kocideva ābādho uppajjati; sukhinī bodhisattamātā hoti akilantakāyā; bodhisattañca bodhisattamātā tirokucchigataṃ passati sabbaṅgapaccaṅgaṃ ahīnindriyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato. Tatrāssa suttaṃ āvutaṃ nīlaṃ vā pītaṃ vā lohitaṃ vā odātaṃ vā paṇḍusuttaṃ vā. Tamenaṃ cakkhumā puriso hatthe karitvā paccavekkheyya – ayaṃ kho maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato, tatridaṃ suttaṃ āvutaṃ nīlaṃ vā pītaṃ vā lohitaṃ vā odātaṃ vā paṇḍusuttaṃ vāti. Evameva kho, ānanda, yadā bodhisatto mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti , na bodhisattamātu kocideva ābādho uppajjati; sukhinī bodhisattamātā hoti akilantakāyā; bodhisattañca bodhisattamātā tirokucchigataṃ passati sabbaṅgapaccaṅgaṃ ahīnindriya’nti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.
mula_english:
204. “Venerable sir, I have heard and learned this directly from the Blessed One: ‘When, Ānanda, a *bodhisattva* has descended into his mother's womb (mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti), his mother experiences no ailment (ābādho). The *bodhisattva*'s mother is happy and her body is without fatigue (*akilantakāyā*). The *bodhisattva*'s mother sees the *bodhisattva* inside her womb with all limbs and faculties unimpaired (*ahīnindriyaṃ*).

Suppose, Ānanda, there were a beautiful *beryl* gem (*maṇi veḷuriyo*), pure, of excellent quality (*subho jātimā*), eight-faceted (*aṭṭhaṃso*), well-cut (*suparikammakato*). And a thread – blue, yellow, red, white, or brownish – were strung through it (*suttaṃ āvutaṃ nīlaṃ vā pītaṃ vā lohitaṃ vā odātaṃ vā paṇḍusuttaṃ vā*). A person with good eyesight, taking it in hand, might reflect: ‘This is a *beryl* gem, beautiful, genuine, eight-faceted, well-cut; and through it a thread – blue, yellow, red, white, or brownish – is strung.’

In the same way (*evameva kho*), Ānanda, when a *bodhisattva* has descended into his mother’s womb (mātukucchiṃ okkanto hoti), his mother experiences no ailment (*ābādho*). The *bodhisattva*'s mother is happy and her body is without fatigue (*akilantakāyā*). The *bodhisattva*'s mother sees the *bodhisattva* inside her womb with all limbs and faculties unimpaired (*ahīnindriyaṃ*)’.

And that, venerable sir... …this too, venerable sir, I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One (*bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi*).”
commentary_pali: 204.Akilantakāyāti yathā aññā itthiyo gabbhabhārena kilamanti, hatthapādā uddhumātakādīni pāpuṇanti, na evaṃ tassā koci kilamatho ahosi. Tirokucchigatanti antokucchigataṃ. Kalalādikālaṃ atikkamitvā sañjātaaṅgapaccaṅgaṃ ahīnindriyabhāvaṃ upagataṃyeva passati. Kimatthaṃ passati? Sukhavāsatthaṃ. Yatheva hi mātā puttena saddhiṃ nisinnā vā nipannā vā ‘‘hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā olambantaṃ ukkhipitvā saṇṭhapessāmī’’ti sukhavāsatthaṃ puttaṃ oloketi, evaṃ bodhisattamātāpi yaṃ taṃ mātu uṭṭhānagamanaparivattananisajjādīsu uṇhasītaloṇikatittakakaṭukāhāraajjhoharaṇakālesu ca gabbhassa dukkhaṃ uppajjati, atthi nu kho me taṃ puttassāti sukhavāsatthaṃ bodhisattaṃ olokayamānā pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā nisinnaṃ bodhisattaṃ passati. Yathā hi aññe antokucchigatā pakkāsayaṃ ajjhottharitvā āmāsayaṃ ukkhipitvā udarapaṭalaṃ piṭṭhito katvā piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃ nissāya ukkuṭikā dvīsu muṭṭhīsu hanukaṃ ṭhapetvā deve vassante rukkhasusire makkaṭā viya nisīdanti, na evaṃ bodhisatto. Bodhisatto pana piṭṭhikaṇṭakaṃ piṭṭhito katvā dhammāsane dhammakathiko viya pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā puratthābhimukho nisīdati. Pubbe katakammaṃ panassā vatthuṃ sodheti, suddhe vatthumhi sukhumacchavilakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati . Atha naṃ kucchigataṃ taco paṭicchādetuṃ na sakkoti, olokentiyā bahi ṭhito viya paññāyati. Tamatthaṃ upamāya vibhāvento seyyathāpītiādimāha. Bodhisatto pana antokucchigato mātaraṃ na passati. Na hi antokucchiyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppajjati.
commentary_english:
204. *Akilantakāyā:* Just as other women are exhausted by the burden of pregnancy and their hands and feet experience bloating, etc., she did not have any such exhaustion.

*Tirokucchigata:* *Antokucchigataṃ* means inside the womb.

Having passed the *kalala*, etc. stages, she sees [him] with all limbs and organs developed, having attained unimpaired faculties.

Why does she see? For the sake of comfortable dwelling.

Just as a mother, sitting or lying down with her son, watches her son for the sake of comfortable dwelling, thinking, "I will lift up and arrange his hand or foot if it is dangling down," so too, the Bodhisattva's mother, contemplating the Bodhisattva for the sake of comfortable dwelling, wonders, "Does my son experience suffering in the womb during the mother's getting up, going, turning over, sitting, etc., and during the times of ingesting hot, cold, salty, bitter, and pungent foods?" She sees the Bodhisattva sitting cross-legged.

Just as other [beings] inside the womb, covering the cecum, lifting up the stomach, placing the abdominal membrane behind, relying on the spine, squatting, placing the chin on two fists, sit like monkeys in a tree hollow when the gods are raining, the Bodhisattva is not like that.

But the Bodhisattva, placing the spine behind, sits cross-legged facing east, like a preacher of the Dharma on a Dharma seat.

His previous good *kamma* purifies the substance (womb), and in the purified substance, a subtle, beautiful complexion arises. Then, the skin is not able to cover him inside the womb; while she is looking, he appears as if standing outside.

Revealing that meaning by way of simile, he said, beginning with *seyyathāpi*.

But the Bodhisattva, while inside the womb, does not see the mother. For eye-consciousness does not arise inside the womb.

mula_pali:
205. ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘sattāhajāte, ānanda, bodhisatte bodhisattamātā kālaṃ karoti, tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapajjatī’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yathā kho panānanda, aññā itthikā nava vā dasa vā māse gabbhaṃ kucchinā pariharitvā vijāyanti, na hevaṃ bodhisattaṃ bodhisattamātā vijāyati. Daseva māsāni bodhisattaṃ bodhisattamātā kucchinā pariharitvā vijāyatī’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yathā kho panānanda, aññā itthikā nisinnā vā nipannā vā vijāyanti, na hevaṃ bodhisattaṃ bodhisattamātā vijāyati. Ṭhitāva bodhisattaṃ bodhisattamātā vijāyatī’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā , ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, devā naṃ paṭhamaṃ paṭiggaṇhanti pacchā manussā’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.
mula_english:
“I heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: ‘Seven days after the birth of the *Bodhisattva*, his mother died and reappeared in the Tusita heaven.’ This too I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.

“I heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: ‘Other women give birth after carrying the child in the womb for nine or ten months, but not so the *Bodhisattva*'s mother. The *Bodhisattva*'s mother gave birth after carrying him in her womb for exactly ten months.’ This too I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.

“I heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: ‘Other women give birth seated or lying down, but not so the *Bodhisattva*'s mother. The *Bodhisattva*'s mother gave birth to him standing up.’ This too I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.

“I heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: ‘When the *Bodhisattva* came forth from his mother’s womb, first gods received him, then human beings.’ This too I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.
commentary_pali:
205.Kālaṃkarotīti na vijātabhāvapaccayā, āyuparikkhayeneva. Bodhisattena vasitaṭṭhānañhi cetiyakuṭisadisaṃ hoti aññesaṃ aparibhogaṃ, na ca sakkā bodhisattamātaraṃ apanetvā aññaṃ aggamahesiṭṭhāne ṭhapetunti tattakaṃyeva bodhisattamātu āyuppamāṇaṃ hoti, tasmā tadā kālaṃ karoti. Katarasmiṃ pana vaye kālaṃ karotīti? Majjhimavaye. Paṭhamavayasmiñhi sattānaṃ attabhāve chandarāgo balavā hoti, tena tadā sañjātagabbhā itthī taṃ gabbhaṃ anurakkhituṃ na sakkonti, gabbho bahvābādho hoti. Majjhimavayassa pana dve koṭṭhāse atikkamma tatiyakoṭṭhāse vatthuṃ visadaṃ hoti, visade vatthumhi nibbattā dārakā arogā honti. Tasmā bodhisattamātāpi paṭhamavaye sampattiṃ anubhavitvā majjhimavayassa tatiyakoṭṭhāse vijāyitvā kālaṃ karoti.

Nava vā dasa vāti ettha vā-saddena vikappanavasena satta vā aṭṭha vā ekādasa vā dvādasa vāti evamādīnampi saṅgaho veditabbo. Tattha sattamāsajāto jīvati, sītuṇhakkhamo pana na hoti. Aṭṭhamāsajāto na jīvati, sesā jīvanti.

Nava vā dasa vā

Ṭhitāvāti ṭhitāva hutvā. Mahāmāyāpi devī upavijaññā ñātikulagharaṃ gamissāmīti rañño ārocesi. Rājā kapilavatthuto devadahanagaragāmimaggaṃ alaṅkārāpetvā deviṃ suvaṇṇasivikāya nisīdāpesi. Sakalanagaravāsino sakyā parivāretvā gandhamālādīhi pūjayamānā deviṃ gahetvā pāyiṃsu. Sā devadahanagarassa avidūre lumbinisālavanuyyānaṃ disvā uyyānavicaraṇatthāya cittaṃ uppādetvā rañño saññaṃ adāsi. Rājā uyyānaṃ paṭijaggāpetvā ārakkhaṃ saṃvidahāpesi. Deviyā uyyānaṃ paviṭṭhamattāya kāyadubbalyaṃ ahosi, athassā maṅgalasālamūle sirīsayanaṃ paññāpetvā sāṇiyā parikkhipiṃsu. Sā antosāṇiṃ pavisitvā sālasākhaṃ hatthena gahetvā aṭṭhāsi. Athassā tāvadeva gabbhavuṭṭhānaṃ ahosi.

Ṭhitāvā

Devā naṃ paṭhamaṃ paṭiggaṇhantīti khīṇāsavā suddhāvāsabrahmāno paṭiggaṇhanti. Kathaṃ? Sūtivesaṃ gaṇhitvāti eke. Taṃ pana paṭikkhipitvā idaṃ vuttaṃ – tadā bodhisattamātā suvaṇṇakhacitaṃ vatthaṃ nivāsetvā macchakkhisadisaṃ dukūlapaṭaṃ yāva pādantāva pārupitvā aṭṭhāsi. Athassā sallahukaṃ gabbhavuṭṭhānaṃ ahosi dhammakaraṇato udakanikkhamanasadisaṃ. Atha te pakatibrahmaveseneva upasaṅkamitvā paṭhamaṃ suvaṇṇajālena paṭiggahesuṃ. Tesaṃ hatthato manussā dukūlacumbaṭakena paṭiggahesuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘devā naṃ paṭhamaṃ paṭiggaṇhanti pacchā manussā’’ti.

Devā naṃ paṭhamaṃ paṭiggaṇhantī
commentary_english:
205. *kālaṃ karotīti na vijātabhāvapaccayā, āyuparikkhayeneva.* [It] dies not because of the condition of having given birth, but only from the exhaustion of [its] life-span. *bodhisattena vasitaṭṭhānañhi cetiyakuṭisadisaṃ hoti aññesaṃ* unfit for others, is like a shrine-hut; and it is not possible to remove the Bodhisattva's mother and install another in the place of chief consort. Thus, the Bodhisattva's mother's life-span is only that long, therefore she dies then.

But at what age does she die? At middle age. For in early age, the desire and lust in the beings' own existence is strong; therefore then, a woman who has conceived cannot protect that embryo, [and] the embryo has many diseases. But having passed two parts of middle age, in the third part, the physical basis is clear; children born in a clear physical basis are healthy. Therefore, the Bodhisattva's mother also, having experienced prosperity in early age, gives birth in the third part of middle age, and dies.

*nava vā dasa vā*ti here, with the word *vā* ("or"), it should be understood that there is a collection of possibilities, such as seven or eight or eleven or twelve, etc. There, one born after seven months lives, but is not resistant to cold and heat. One born after eight months does not live, the rest live.

*nava vā dasa vā*

*ṭhitāvā*ti having been standing. Devī Mahāmāyā also announced to the king, "I will go to my relatives' home, being aware [of my pregnancy]." The king had the road from Kapilavatthu to Devadaha-nagaragāma decorated, [and] had the queen seated in a golden palanquin. All the Sakyas dwelling in the city, surrounding [her], honoring [her] with perfumes, garlands, etc., escorted the queen. She, seeing the Lumbini Sāla-grove park not far from Devadaha-nagara, having produced the thought of walking about in the park, gave a signal to the king. The king had the park prepared and had protection arranged. As soon as the queen had entered the park, weakness of body arose in her; then they had a magnificent bed prepared at the foot of the auspicious Sāla tree and surrounded it with cloth. She, entering inside the cloth, grasped a Sāla branch with her hand and stood. Then, just then, the birth occurred.

*ṭhitāvā*

*devā naṃ paṭhamaṃ paṭiggaṇhantī*ti the *khīṇāsava*s, pure Brahmās of the Pure Abodes, receive [him]. How? Some say, "Taking the form of midwives." But rejecting that, this was said: Then the Bodhisattva's mother, having put on a gold-embroidered cloth, stood having covered [herself] with a fine cloth resembling a fish's eye, down to the end of her feet. Then the birth occurred to her very easily, like the flowing out of water from a water-pot. Then those [Brahmās], just in their natural Brahma form, approached and first received [him] with a golden net. From their hands, humans received [him] with a fine cotton cloth. Therefore it was said, "First the gods receive him, afterwards the humans."

*devā naṃ paṭhamaṃ paṭiggaṇhantī*

mula_pali:
206. ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, appattova bodhisatto pathaviṃ hoti, cattāro naṃ devaputtā paṭiggahetvā mātu purato ṭhapenti – attamanā, devi, hohi; mahesakkho te putto uppanno’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, visadova nikkhamati amakkhito udena uddena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) amakkhito semhena amakkhito ruhirena amakkhito kenaci asucinā suddho visado visuddho (syā.). Seyyathāpi, ānanda, maṇiratanaṃ kāsike vatthe nikkhittaṃ neva maṇiratanaṃ kāsikaṃ vatthaṃ makkheti nāpi kāsikaṃ vatthaṃ maṇiratanaṃ makkheti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ubhinnaṃ suddhattā. Evameva kho, ānanda, yadā bodhisatto mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, visadova nikkhamati amakkhito udena amakkhito semhena amakkhito ruhirena amakkhito kenaci asucinā suddho visado’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

uddena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) visuddho (syā.)

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, dve udakassa dhārā antalikkhā pātubhavanti – ekā sītassa, ekā uṇhassa; yena bodhisattassa udakakiccaṃ karonti mātu cā’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.
mula_english:
206.
"Bhante, I heard and received this directly from the Blessed One: 'Ānanda, when the Bodhisattva comes forth from his mother's womb, before the Bodhisattva touches the earth, four young gods receive him and place him before his mother, saying, "Rejoice, O queen, a son of great power has been born to you."'
Bhante, I remember this as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.

"Bhante, I heard and received this directly from the Blessed One: 'Ānanda, when the Bodhisattva comes forth from his mother's womb, he comes forth unsullied, not defiled by water, not defiled by mucus, not defiled by blood, not defiled by any impurity, pure and spotless.'
Just as if a jewel were placed on Kāśi cloth, the jewel would not stain the Kāśi cloth, nor would the Kāśi cloth stain the jewel.
What is the reason for that? Because both are pure.
Even so, Ānanda, when the Bodhisattva comes forth from his mother's womb, he comes forth unsullied, not defiled by water, not defiled by mucus, not defiled by blood, not defiled by any impurity, pure and spotless."
Bhante, I remember this as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.

"Bhante, I heard and received this directly from the Blessed One: 'Ānanda, when the Bodhisattva comes forth from his mother's womb, two streams of water appear from the sky, one cool and one warm, with which they bathe the Bodhisattva and his mother.'"
Bhante, I remember this as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One.
commentary_pali:
206.Cattāro naṃ devaputtāti cattāro mahārājāno. Paṭiggahetvāti ajinappaveṇiyā paṭiggahetvā. Mahesakkhoti mahātejo mahāyaso lakkhaṇasampannoti attho.

Visadova nikkhamatīti yathā aññe sattā yonimagge laggantā bhaggavibhaggā nikkhamanti, na evaṃ nikkhamati, alaggo hutvā nikkhamatīti attho. Udenāti udakena. Kenaci asucināti yathā aññe sattā kammajavātehi uddhaṃpādā adhosirā yonimagge pakkhittā sataporisanarakapapātaṃ patantā viya tāḷacchiddena nikkaḍḍhiyamānā hatthī viya mahādukkhaṃ anubhavantā nānāasucimakkhitāva nikkhamanti, na evaṃ bodhisatto. Bodhisattañhi kammajavātā uddhaṃpādaṃ adhosiraṃ kātuṃ na sakkonti. So dhammāsanato otaranto dhammakathiko viya nisseṇito otaranto puriso viya ca dve hatthe ca pāde ca pasāretvā ṭhitakova mātukucchisambhavena kenaci asucinā amakkhitova nikkhamati.

Visadova nikkhamatī Udenā Kenaci asucinā

Udakassa dhārāti udakavaṭṭiyo. Tāsu sītā suvaṇṇakaṭāhe patati, uṇhā rajatakaṭāhe. Idañca pathavītale kenaci asucinā asammissaṃ tesaṃ pānīyaparibhojanīyaudakañceva aññehi asādhāraṇaṃ kīḷanaudakañca dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Aññassa pana suvaṇṇarajataghaṭehi āhariyamānaudakassa ceva haṃsavaṭṭakādipokkharaṇigatassa ca udakassa paricchedo natthi.

Udakassa dhārā
commentary_english:
206.
" *Cattāro naṃ devaputtā* " means the Four Great Kings.
" *Paṭiggahetvā* " means having accepted with an antelope hide garment.
" *Mahesakkho* " means great power, great glory, possessing auspicious marks; this is the meaning.

" *Visadova nikkhamatī* " means just as other beings emerge from the womb stained and broken, he does not emerge in that way; he emerges unstained; this is the meaning.
" *Udenā* " means with water ( *udakena* ).
" *Kenaci asucinā* " means just as other beings, driven by karmic winds, head downwards, feet upwards, are thrown into the womb, falling into the hell of the hundred-spiked iron stake, like an elephant being dragged out of a palm-tree hole, experiencing great suffering, covered with various impurities, emerge; the *bodhisattva* does not emerge in this way.
Because karmic winds cannot make the *bodhisattva* head downwards and feet upwards.
He emerges from the Dharma seat like a preacher descending, or like a man descending from a ladder, erect, stretching out both hands and feet, unstained by any impurity arising from his mother’s womb.

" *Visadova nikkhamatī* " " *udenā* " " *kenaci asucinā* "

" *Udakassa dhārā* " means water containers ( *udakavaṭṭiyo* ).
In them, cool water falls into a golden bowl, and hot water into a silver bowl.
And this water, on the surface of the earth, unmixed with any impurity, is their water for drinking and eating, and it is uncommon to others.
It is said that even the play water ( *kīḷanaudakañca* ) was shown.
But for others, there is no limit ( *paricchedo natthi* ) to the water that is brought in golden and silver pots, and to the water in ponds and so forth, which is home to swans and ducks.

" *Udakassa dhārā* "

mula_pali:
207. ‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘sampatijāto, ānanda, bodhisatto samehi pādehi pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhahitvā uttarābhimukho sattapadavītihārena gacchati, setamhi chatte anudhāriyamāne, sabbā ca disā viloketi, āsabhiñca vācaṃ bhāsati – aggohamasmi lokassa, jeṭṭhohamasmi lokassa, seṭṭhohamasmi lokassa. Ayamantimā jāti , natthi dāni punabbhavo’ti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi.

‘‘Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā, ānanda, bodhisatto mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, atha sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso loke pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Yāpi tā lokantarikā aghā asaṃvutā andhakārā andhakāratimisā yatthapime candimasūriyā evaṃmahiddhikā evaṃmahānubhāvā ābhāya nānubhonti tatthapi appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso loke pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi tenobhāsena aññamaññaṃ sañjānanti – aññepi kira, bho, santi sattā idhūpapannāti. Ayañca dasasahassī lokadhātu saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati, appamāṇo ca uḷāro obhāso loke pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāva’nti. Yampi, bhante…pe… idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremī’’ti.
mula_english:
207. “I heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s own lips: ‘As soon as the *Bodhisattva* was born, Ānanda, he stood firmly with his feet on the earth (*pathavī*), then he took seven steps north, and with a white parasol held over him, he surveyed each quarter and uttered the words of the Leader of the Herd: “I am the highest in the world (*lokassa*); I am the best in the world (*lokassa*); I am the foremost in the world (*lokassa*). This is my last birth (*jāti*); now there is no renewal of being for me”’.
That when the *Bodhisattva* came forth from his mother’s womb, then a great immeasurable light surpassing the splendor of the gods (*devānām*), appeared in the world with its gods (*sadevake loke*), its *Maras*, and its *Brahmas*, in this generation with its recluses and *brahmins*, with its princes and its people, an immeasurable and glorious radiance (*appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso*) appeared in the world (*loke*) surpassing the divine majesty of the gods (*devānubhāvaṃ*).

And whatever dark spaces (*lokantarikā aghā*) lie beyond the world’s end, chaotic, blind and black (*andhakārā andhakāratimisā*), such that they are not even reached by the mighty rays of sun and moon (*candimasūriyā*), are yet illumined by this immeasurable splendid light (*appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso*) surpassing the glory of the most powerful *devas* (*devānubhāvaṃ*).

And those beings (*sattā*) that have been reborn there recognize each other by this light and know: “Other beings (*sattā*), too, have been born here!”

And this ten-thousandfold world system (*lokadhātu*) shook and quaked and trembled, and an immeasurable and glorious radiance (*appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso*) appeared in the world (*loke*) surpassing the divine majesty of the gods (*devānubhāvaṃ*)’.

That…I remember as a wonderful and marvelous quality of the Blessed One (*bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremi*).”
commentary_pali:
207.Sampatijātoti muhuttajāto. Pāḷiyaṃ pana mātukucchito nikkhantamatto viya dassito, na pana evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Nikkhantamattañhi taṃ paṭhamaṃ brahmāno suvaṇṇajālena paṭiggaṇhiṃsu, tesaṃ hatthato cattāro mahārājāno maṅgalasammatāya sukhasamphassāya ajinappaveṇiyā, tesaṃ hatthato manussā dukūlacumbaṭakena, manussānaṃ hatthato muccitvā pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhito.

Setamhi chatte anudhāriyamāneti dibbasetacchatte anudhāriyamāne. Ettha ca chattassa parivārāni khaggādīni pañca rājakakudhabhaṇḍānipi āgatāneva. Pāḷiyaṃ pana rājagamane rājā viya chattameva vuttaṃ. Tesu chattameva paññāyati, na chattaggāhakā. Tathā khagga-tālavaṇṭa-morahatthaka-vāḷabījani-uṇhīsamattāyeva paññāyanti, na tesaṃ gāhakā. Sabbāni kira tāni adissamānarūpā devatā gaṇhiṃsu. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

Setamhi chatte anudhāriyamāne

‘‘Anekasākhañca sahassamaṇḍalaṃ,

Chattaṃ marū dhārayumantalikkhe;

Suvaṇṇadaṇḍā vipatanti cāmarā,

Na dissare cāmarachattagāhakā’’ti. (su. ni. 693);

Sabbā ca disāti idaṃ sattapadavītihārūpari ṭhitassa viya sabbadisānuvilokanaṃ vuttaṃ, na kho panevaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Mahāsatto hi manussānaṃ hatthato muccitvā puratthimadisaṃ olokesi, anekacakkavāḷasahassāni ekaṅgaṇāni ahesuṃ. Tattha devamanussā gandhamālādīhi pūjayamānā – ‘‘mahāpurisa idha tumhehi sadisopi natthi, kuto uttaritaro’’ti āhaṃsu. Evaṃ catasso disā, catasso anudisā, heṭṭhā, uparīti dasapi disā anuviloketvā attanā sadisaṃ adisvā ayaṃ uttarā disāti sattapadavītihārena agamāsīti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Āsabhinti uttamaṃ. Aggoti guṇehi sabbapaṭhamo. Itarāni dve padāni etasseva vevacanāni. Ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavoti padadvayena imasmiṃ attabhāve pattabbaṃ arahattaṃ byākāsi.

Sabbā ca disā Āsabhi Aggo Ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo

Ettha ca samehi pādehi pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhānaṃ catuiddhipādapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, uttarābhimukhabhāvo mahājanaṃ ajjhottharitvā abhibhavitvā gamanassa pubbanimittaṃ , sattapadagamanaṃ sattabojjhaṅgaratanapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, dibbasetacchattadhāraṇaṃ vimutticchattapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, pañcarājakakudhabhaṇḍāni pañcahi vimuttīhi vimuccanassa pubbanimittaṃ, disānuvilokanaṃ anāvaraṇañāṇapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, āsabhīvācābhāsanaṃ appaṭivattiyadhammacakkappavattanassa pubbanimittaṃ. ‘‘Ayamantimā jātī’’ti sīhanādo anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbānassa pubbanimittanti veditabbaṃ. Ime vārā pāḷiyaṃ āgatā, sambahulavāro pana āgato, āharitvā dīpetabbo.

Mahāpurisassa hi jātadivase dasasahassilokadhātu kampi. Dasasahassilokadhātumhi devatā ekacakkavāḷe sannipatiṃsu. Paṭhamaṃ devā paṭiggahiṃsu, pacchā manussā. Tantibaddhā vīṇā cammabaddhā bheriyo ca kenaci avāditā sayameva vajjiṃsu, manussānaṃ andubandhanādīni khaṇḍākhaṇḍaṃ bhijjiṃsu. Sabbarogā ambilena dhotatambamalaṃ viya vigacchiṃsu, jaccandhā rūpāni passiṃsu. Jaccabadhirā saddaṃ suṇiṃsu, pīṭhasappī javanasampannā ahesuṃ, jātijaḷānampi eḷamūgānaṃ sati patiṭṭhāsi, videse pakkhandanāvā supaṭṭanaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu, ākāsaṭṭhakabhūmaṭṭhakaratanāni sakatejobhāsitāni ahesuṃ, verino mettacittaṃ paṭilabhiṃsu, avīcimhi aggi nibbāyi. Lokantare āloko udapādi, nadīsu jalaṃ na pavatti, mahāsamuddesu madhurasadisaṃ udakaṃ ahosi, vāto na vāyi, ākāsapabbatarukkhagatā sakuṇā bhassitvā pathavīgatā ahesuṃ, cando atiroci, sūriyo na uṇho na sītalo nimmalo utusampanno ahosi, devatā attano attano vimānadvāre ṭhatvā apphoṭanaseḷanacelukkhepādīhi mahākīḷaṃ kīḷiṃsu, cātuddīpikamahāmegho vassi, mahājanaṃ neva khudā na pipāsā pīḷesi, dvārakavāṭāni sayameva vivariṃsu, pupphūpagaphalūpagā rukkhā pupphaphalāni gaṇhiṃsu, dasasahassilokadhātu ekaddhajamālā ahosīti.

Tatrāpissa dasasahassilokadhātukampo sabbaññutañāṇapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, devatānaṃ ekacakkavāḷe sannipāto dhammacakkappavattanakāle ekappahārena sannipatitvā dhammapaṭiggaṇhanassa pubbanimittaṃ, paṭhamaṃ devatānaṃ paṭiggahaṇaṃ catunnaṃ rūpāvacarajjhānānaṃ paṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ. Pacchā manussānaṃ paṭiggahaṇaṃ catunnaṃ arūpajjhānānaṃ paṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, tantibaddhavīṇānaṃ sayaṃ vajjanaṃ anupubbavihārapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, cammabaddhabherīnaṃ vajjanaṃ mahatiyā dhammabheriyā anussāvanassa pubbanimittaṃ, andubandhanādīnaṃ chedo asmimānasamucchedassa pubbanimittaṃ, sabbarogavigamo sabbakilesavigamassa pubbanimittaṃ, jaccandhānaṃ rūpadassanaṃ dibbacakkhupaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, jaccabadhirānaṃ saddassavanaṃ dibbasotadhātupaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ , pīṭhasappīnaṃ javanasampadā catuiddhipādādhigamassa pubbanimittaṃ, jaḷānaṃ satipatiṭṭhānaṃ catusatipaṭṭhānapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, videsapakkhandanāvānaṃ supaṭṭanasampāpuṇanaṃ catupaṭisambhidādhigamassa pubbanimittaṃ, ratanānaṃ sakatejobhāsitattaṃ yaṃ lokassa dhammobhāsaṃ dassessati tassa pubbanimittaṃ.

Verīnaṃ mettacittapaṭilābho catubrahmavihārapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, avīcimhi agginibbānaṃ ekādasaagginibbānassa pubbanimittaṃ, lokantarāloko avijjandhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ñāṇālokadassanassa pubbanimittaṃ, mahāsamuddassa madhuratā nibbānarasena ekarasabhāvassa pubbanimittaṃ, vātassa avāyanaṃ dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhigatabhindanassa pubbanimittaṃ, sakuṇānaṃ pathavīgamanaṃ mahājanassa ovādaṃ sutvā pāṇehi saraṇagamanassa pubbanimittaṃ, candassa ativirocanaṃ bahujanakantatāya pubbanimittaṃ, sūriyassa uṇhasītavivajjanautusukhatā kāyikacetasikasukhuppattiyā pubbanimittaṃ, devatānaṃ vimānadvāresu apphoṭanādīhi kīḷanaṃ buddhabhāvaṃ patvā udānaṃ udānassa pubbanimittaṃ, cātuddīpikamahāmeghavassanaṃ mahato dhammameghavassanassa pubbanimittaṃ, khudāpīḷanassa abhāvo kāyagatāsatiamatapaṭilābhassa pubbanimittaṃ, pipāsāpīḷanassa abhāvo vimuttisukhena sukhitabhāvassa pubbanimittaṃ, dvārakavāṭānaṃ sayameva vivaraṇaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikamaggadvāravivaraṇassa pubbanimittaṃ, rukkhānaṃ pupphaphalagahaṇaṃ vimuttipupphehi pupphitassa ca sāmaññaphalabhārabharitabhāvassa ca pubbanimittaṃ, dasasahassilokadhātuyā ekaddhajamālatā ariyaddhajamālāmālitāya pubbanimittanti veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ sambahulavāro nāma.

Ettha pañhe pucchanti – ‘‘yadā mahāpuriso pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhahitvā uttarābhimukho gantvā āsabhiṃ vācaṃ bhāsati, tadā kiṃ pathaviyā gato , udāhu ākāsena? Dissamāno gato, udāhu adissamāno? Acelako gato, udāhu alaṅkatappaṭiyatto? Daharo hutvā gato, udāhu mahallako? Pacchāpi kiṃ tādisova ahosi, udāhu puna bāladārako’’ti? Ayaṃ pana pañho heṭṭhā lohapāsāde saṅghasannipāte tipiṭakacūḷābhayattherena vissajjitova. Thero kirettha niyati pubbekatakamma-issaranimmānavādavasena taṃ taṃ bahuṃ vatvā avasāne evaṃ byākāsi – ‘‘mahāpuriso pathaviyaṃ gato, mahājanassa pana ākāse gacchanto viya ahosi. Dissamāno gato, mahājanassa pana adissamāno viya ahosi. Acelako gato, mahājanassa pana alaṅkatappaṭiyattova upaṭṭhāsi. Daharova gato, mahājanassa pana soḷasavassuddesiko viya ahosi. Pacchā pana bāladārakova ahosi, na tādiso’’ti. Evaṃ vutte parisā cassa ‘‘buddhena viya hutvā bho therena pañho kathito’’ti attamanā ahosi. Lokantarikavāro vuttanayo eva.

Viditāti pākaṭā hutvā. Yathā hi sāvakā nahānamukhadhovanakhādanapivanādikāle anokāsagate atītasaṅkhāre nippadese sammasituṃ na sakkonti, okāsapattayeva sammasanti, na evaṃ buddhā. Buddhā hi sattadivasabbhantare vavatthitasaṅkhāre ādito paṭṭhāya sammasitvā tilakkhaṇaṃ āropetvāva vissajjenti, tesaṃ avipassitadhammo nāma natthi, tasmā ‘‘viditā’’ti āha. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Viditā

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Acchariyaabbhutasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
207. *Sampratijāto* means born at the moment. In the Pāli [text], it is shown as just having emerged from the mother's womb, but it should not be seen like that. For when he had just emerged, first the Brahmās received him in a golden net, from whose hands the Four Great Kings received him on antelope skins agreeable for auspicious occasions and soft to the touch; from their hands men received him on a roll of fine cloth; [and] having been released from the hands of men, he stood on the ground. *Setamhi chatte anudhāriyamāne* means while a white umbrella was being held, namely, a divine white umbrella was being held. And here, the retinue of the umbrella, swords, etc., and the five royal emblems of royalty also arrived. But in the Pāli [text], in the king's procession, only the umbrella is mentioned, like a king. Among those, only the umbrella is evident, not the umbrella-bearers. Likewise, the sword, palm-leaf fan, peacock-feather fan, yak-tail whisk, and turban are evident by themselves, not their bearers. It is said that all those deities of invisible form took [them]. It was also said: While the white umbrella was being held in the sky, the Maruts bore an umbrella with many branches and a thousand circles; yak-tail whisks with golden handles fall down, but the yak-tail whisk and umbrella bearers are not seen. (Su. Ni. 693); *Sabbā ca disā* means this statement that he looked in all directions is like [saying that] he stood on the seven-pace path, but it should not be seen like that. For the great being, having been released from the hands of men, looked toward the east. Thousands of world systems became a single open space. There, gods and humans, making offerings with fragrant garlands, etc., said, "Great man, there is no one equal to you here, how could there be one greater?" Thus, having looked in the four directions, the four intermediate directions, below, and above—ten directions in all—and not seeing anyone equal to himself, he went seven paces, [saying,] "This is the north direction." Thus, the meaning should be understood here. *Āsabhi* means excellent. *Aggo* means first in qualities. The other two words are synonyms of this. *Ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo* means he declared arhatship, which is to be attained in this very existence, with [these] two lines. *Sabbā ca disā*, *āsabhi*, *aggo*, *ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo* Here, standing on the earth with even feet was a preliminary sign of obtaining the four bases of miraculous power; having his face turned toward the north was a preliminary sign of going, overwhelming and surpassing the great multitude; going seven paces was a preliminary sign of obtaining the seven jewels of enlightenment factors; holding a divine white umbrella was a preliminary sign of obtaining the umbrella of liberation; the five royal emblems of royalty were a preliminary sign of being released by the five liberations; looking in all directions was a preliminary sign of obtaining unobstructed knowledge; and speaking a fearless speech was a preliminary sign of turning the irreversible wheel of Dharma. "This is the last birth" – this lion's roar should be understood as a preliminary sign of parinirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder. These passages have come in the Pāli [text], and many passages have come; they should be brought and explained. On the day of the great being's birth, the ten-thousandfold world system shook. In the ten-thousandfold world system, the deities gathered in one *cakravāḍa*. First the gods received [him], then the humans. Stringed *vīṇās* and leather-covered drums played by themselves without being played by anyone, and the chains, bonds, etc., of the humans shattered into pieces. All diseases disappeared like dirt on copper washed with acid, and those born blind saw forms. Those born deaf heard sounds, the lame became swift, mindfulness arose even in the congenitally dull and mute, ships sailing to foreign lands reached safe harbors, celestial and terrestrial jewels shone with their own radiance, enemies obtained minds of loving-kindness, and the fire in Avīci went out. Light arose in the intermediate world, water did not flow in the rivers, the water in the great oceans became like honey, the wind did not blow, and birds dwelling in the sky, mountains, and trees cried out and went to the earth. 0187"/> There were [omens of the Buddha's birth]: the moon shone brightly, the sun was neither hot nor cold, [but] pure and seasonable; the deities, standing at the doors of their respective celestial mansions, engaged in great sport with clapping, cheering, and waving cloths, etc.; a great rain cloud covering the four continents rained; hunger nor thirst distressed the multitude; the doors and gates opened of themselves; trees bearing flowers and fruits brought forth flowers and fruits; the ten-thousand world-element became a single garland-offering.

Moreover, there, the earthquake of the ten-thousand world-element [is] a former sign of the attainment of the omniscient knowledge, the assembly of deities in a single world-circle [is] a former sign of receiving the Dharma by assembling with a single blow at the time of the turning of the wheel of the Dharma. Firstly, the deities' receiving [is] a former sign of the attainment of the four *rūpāvacara-jhānas*. Afterwards, the humans' receiving [is] a former sign of the attainment of the four *arūpajjhānas*, the self-sounding of stringed *vīṇās* [is] a former sign of the attainment of successive abodes, the sounding of leather-bound drums [is] a former sign of the proclamation of the great Dharma-drum, the cutting of ball-bonds, etc., [is] a former sign of the destruction of the conceit "I am", the disappearance of all diseases [is] a former sign of the disappearance of all defilements, the sight of forms by those born blind [is] a former sign of the attainment of the divine eye, the hearing of sounds by those born deaf [is] a former sign of the attainment of the divine ear-element , the quick success of the seats for the butter [or ghee?] [is] a former sign of the attainment of the four bases of magical power (*catuiddhipāda*), the mindfulness of the dull [is] a former sign of the attainment of the four establishments of mindfulness (*catusatipaṭṭhāna*), the good attainment and accomplishment of ships setting forth to foreign lands [is] a former sign of the attainment of the four analytical knowledges (*catupaṭisambhidādhigama*), the self-illuminating nature of the jewels [is] a former sign of that which will show the Dharma-light to the world.

The attainment of loving-kindness of the enemies [is] a former sign of the attainment of the four *brahmavihāras*, the extinguishing of fire in *avīci* [is] a former sign of the extinguishing of the eleven fires, the light in the *lokantarika* [is] a former sign of destroying the darkness of ignorance and seeing the light of knowledge, the sweetness of the great ocean [is] a former sign of the state of one taste with the taste of *nirvāṇa*, the non-blowing of the wind [is] a former sign of the breaking of the sixty-two kinds of views, the going of birds to the earth [is] a former sign of the multitude hearing the advice and going for refuge with their lives, the excessive shining of the moon [is] a former sign of the loveliness of the multitude, the happiness of the season in which the sun avoids heat and cold [is] a former sign of the arising of physical and mental happiness, the deities' playing with clapping, etc., at the doors of their celestial mansions [is] a former sign of attaining the state of Buddha and uttering the utterance of joy (*udāna*), the raining of the great rain cloud covering the four continents [is] a former sign of the raining of the great Dharma-cloud, the absence of hunger-torment [is] a former sign of the attainment of the unsurpassed mindfulness regarding the body, the absence of thirst-torment [is] a former sign of the state of being happy with the happiness of liberation, the self-opening of the doors and gates [is] a former sign of the opening of the door of the eightfold path (*aṭṭhaṅgikamagga*), the trees' taking flowers and fruits [is] a former sign of being adorned with the flowers of liberation and of the state of being filled with the burden of the fruit of asceticism, and the garland-offering of the ten-thousand world-element [is] a former sign of being adorned with a garland-offering of noble banners. This should be known as a very great opportunity.

Here they ask a question: "When the great man (*mahāpurisa*) having stood on the earth, goes facing north, and speaks an authoritative speech, then does he go from the earth , or through the sky? Does he go seen, or does he go unseen? Does he go naked (*acelaka*), or does he go adorned and prepared? Does he go [as] a youth (*dahara*), or does he go [as] an old man (*mahallaka*)? Afterwards, will he be just like that, or will he again be a foolish boy?" This question, however, was answered below in the Iron Palace, in the assembly of the *saṃgha*, by the *Tripitaka* Cūḷābhaya Thera. The Thera, indeed, there, having spoken much according to the school of fate, former action, lord (*īśvara*), [and] creation (*nirmāṇa*), at the end declared thus: "The great man went on the earth, but to the multitude, it was as if he were going in the sky. He went seen, but to the multitude, it was as if he were going unseen. He went naked, but to the multitude, he appeared adorned and prepared. He went [as] a youth, but to the multitude, it was as if he were about sixteen years old. Afterwards, however, he was just a foolish boy, not like that." Having been said thus, the assembly, saying, "Having become like a Buddha, the question has been spoken by the venerable Thera," was delighted. The *lokantarika-vāra* [is] just as said.

Known means having become manifest. Just as, indeed, the disciples, at the time of bathing, face-washing, eating, drinking, etc., are not able to reflect upon the past aggregates in a place where there is no opportunity (*anokāsa*), but they reflect only when they have obtained an opportunity, not so the Buddhas. For the Buddhas, indeed, having reflected upon the aggregates established within seven days, having imposed the three characteristics from the beginning, dismiss [them], there is no Dharma un-discerned by them, therefore he said "known". The remainder is clear everywhere.

Known

The Abridgement (*papañcasūdanī*) [of the] *Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā*

The Commentary on the Wonderful and Amazing Sūtra (*acchariyaabbhutasutta-vaṇṇanā*) is finished.

mula_pali:
208. ‘‘Tasmātiha tvaṃ, ānanda, idampi tathāgatassa acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhārehi. Idhānanda, tathāgatassa viditā vedanā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti; viditā saññā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti; viditā vitakkā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Idampi kho, tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatassa acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhārehī’’ti. ‘‘Yampi, bhante, bhagavato viditā vedanā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti; viditā saññā… viditā vitakkā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṃ gacchanti. Idaṃpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ dhāremī’’ti.

Idamavoca āyasmā ānando. Samanuñño satthā ahosi; attamanā ca te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Acchariyaabbhutasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
“That being so, Ānanda, remember this too as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the *Tathāgata*:

Here, Ānanda, for the *Tathāgata* feelings (*vedanā*) are known as they arise (*uppajjanti*), known as they are present (*upaṭṭhahanti*), known as they disappear (*abbatthaṃ gacchanti*); perceptions (*saṃjñā*) are known as they arise, known as they are present, known as they disappear; thoughts (*vitarkā*) are known as they arise, known as they are present, known as they disappear.

Remember this too, Ānanda, as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the *Tathāgata*.”

“Venerable sir, since for the Blessed One feelings are known as they arise, as they are present, as they disappear; perceptions are known… thoughts are known as they arise, known as they are present, as they disappear.

- this too I remember as a wonderful and marvellous quality of the Blessed One.”

This said the venerable Ānanda.

The Teacher approved; and those monks, glad at heart, rejoiced at the words of the venerable Ānanda.

The Wonderful and Marvellous Discourse is concluded, the third.

mula_pali:
209. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā bākulo bakkulo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho acelakassapo āyasmato bākulassa purāṇagihisahāyo yenāyasmā bākulo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā bākulena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho acelakassapo āyasmantaṃ bākulaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Kīvaciraṃ pabbajitosi, āvuso bākulā’’ti? ‘‘Asīti me, āvuso, vassāni pabbajitassā’’ti. ‘‘Imehi pana te, āvuso bākula, asītiyā vassehi katikkhattuṃ methuno dhammo paṭisevito’’ti? ‘‘Na kho maṃ, āvuso kassapa, evaṃ pucchitabbaṃ – ‘imehi pana te, āvuso bākula, asītiyā vassehi katikkhattuṃ methuno dhammo paṭisevito’ti. Evañca kho maṃ, āvuso kassapa, pucchitabbaṃ – ‘imehi pana te, āvuso bākula, asītiyā vassehi katikkhattuṃ kāmasaññā uppannapubbā’’’ti? ( ) (imehi pana te āvuso bakkula asītiyo vassehi katikkhattuṃ kāmasaññā uppannapubbāti.) (sī. pī.)

(imehi pana te āvuso bakkula asītiyo vassehi katikkhattuṃ kāmasaññā uppannapubbāti.) (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard:
