217. ‘‘Seyyathāpi , aggivessana, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto nāgavanikaṃ āmanteti – ‘ehi tvaṃ, samma nāgavanika, rañño nāgaṃ abhiruhitvā nāgavanaṃ pavisitvā āraññakaṃ nāgaṃ atipassitvā rañño nāgassa gīvāyaṃ upanibandhāhī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, aggivessana, nāgavaniko rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa paṭissutvā rañño nāgaṃ abhiruhitvā nāgavanaṃ pavisitvā āraññakaṃ nāgaṃ atipassitvā rañño nāgassa gīvāyaṃ upanibandhati. Tamenaṃ rañño nāgo abbhokāsaṃ nīharati. Ettāvatā kho, aggivessana, āraññako nāgo abbhokāsaṃ gato hoti. Etthagedhā etagedhā (sī. pī.) hi, aggivessana, āraññakā nāgā yadidaṃ – nāgavanaṃ. Tamenaṃ nāgavaniko rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa ārocesi – ‘abbhokāsagato kho kho te (syā. kaṃ. ka.), deva, āraññako nāgo’ti. Atha kho aggivessana, tamenaṃ rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto hatthidamakaṃ āmantesi – ‘ehi tvaṃ, samma hatthidamaka, āraññakaṃ nāgaṃ damayāhi āraññakānañceva sīlānaṃ abhinimmadanāya āraññakānañceva sarasaṅkappānaṃ abhinimmadanāya āraññakānañceva darathakilamathapariḷāhānaṃ abhinimmadanāya gāmante abhiramāpanāya manussakantesu sīlesu samādapanāyā’’’ti samādāpanāyāti (?).

‘‘‘Evaṃ , devā’ti kho, aggivessana, hatthidamako rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa paṭissutvā mahantaṃ thambhaṃ pathaviyaṃ nikhaṇitvā āraññakassa nāgassa gīvāyaṃ upanibandhati āraññakānañceva sīlānaṃ abhinimmadanāya āraññakānañceva sarasaṅkappānaṃ abhinimmadanāya āraññakānañceva darathakilamathapariḷāhānaṃ abhinimmadanāya gāmante abhiramāpanāya manussakantesu sīlesu samādapanāya. Tamenaṃ hatthidamako yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā tathārūpāhi vācāhi samudācarati. Yato kho, aggivessana, āraññako nāgo hatthidamakassa yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā tathārūpāhi vācāhi samudācariyamāno sussūsati, sotaṃ odahati, aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti; tamenaṃ hatthidamako uttari tiṇaghāsodakaṃ anuppavecchati.

‘‘Yato kho, aggivessana, āraññako nāgo hatthidamakassa tiṇaghāsodakaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, tatra hatthidamakassa evaṃ hoti – ‘jīvissati kho nu kho (sī. ka.) dāni āraññako rañño (sī. pī.) nāgo’ti. Tamenaṃ hatthidamako uttari kāraṇaṃ kāreti – ‘ādiya, bho, nikkhipa, bho’ti. Yato kho, aggivessana, āraññako nāgo hatthidamakassa ādānanikkhepe vacanakaro hoti ovādappaṭikaro, tamenaṃ hatthidamako uttari kāraṇaṃ kāreti – ‘abhikkama, bho, paṭikkama, bho’ti. Yato kho, aggivessana, āraññako nāgo hatthidamakassa abhikkamapaṭikkamavacanakaro hoti ovādappaṭikaro, tamenaṃ hatthidamako uttari kāraṇaṃ kāreti – ‘uṭṭhaha, bho, nisīda, bho’ti. Yato kho, aggivessana, āraññako nāgo hatthidamakassa uṭṭhānanisajjāya vacanakaro hoti ovādappaṭikaro, tamenaṃ hatthidamako uttari āneñjaṃ nāma kāraṇaṃ kāreti, mahantassa phalakaṃ soṇḍāya upanibandhati, tomarahattho ca puriso uparigīvāya nisinno hoti, samantato ca tomarahatthā purisā parivāretvā ṭhitā honti, hatthidamako ca dīghatomarayaṭṭhiṃ gahetvā purato ṭhito hoti. So āneñjaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāriyamāno neva purime pāde copeti na pacchime pāde copeti, na purimakāyaṃ copeti na pacchimakāyaṃ copeti, na sīsaṃ copeti, na kaṇṇe copeti, na dante copeti , na naṅguṭṭhaṃ copeti, na soṇḍaṃ copeti. So hoti āraññako nāgo khamo sattippahārānaṃ asippahārānaṃ usuppahārānaṃ sarapattappahārānaṃ parasatthappahārānaṃ (sī.), parasattuppahārānaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.) bheripaṇavavaṃsasaṅkhaḍiṇḍimaninnādasaddānaṃ bheripaṇavasaṅkhatiṇavaninnādasaddānaṃ (pī.) sabbavaṅkadosanihitaninnītakasāvo rājāraho rājabhoggo rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṃ gacchati.

nu kho (sī. ka.) rañño (sī. pī.) parasatthappahārānaṃ (sī.), parasattuppahārānaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.) bheripaṇavasaṅkhatiṇavaninnādasaddānaṃ (pī.)
mula_english:
217. Just as, Aggivessana, a head-anointed noble king addresses his elephant woodsman thus: ‘Come, good elephant woodsman, mount the king’s elephant, enter the elephant wood, and when you see a forest elephant, bind him by the neck to the king’s elephant.’

‘Even so, sire,’ Aggivessana, the elephant woodsman, having replied to the noble head-anointed king, mounts the king’s elephant, enters the elephant wood, and when he sees a forest elephant, binds him by the neck to the king’s elephant.

The king's elephant leads him out into the open.

It is in this way that a forest elephant comes out into the open.

Here, Aggivessana, 'forest elephants' means the elephant wood.

Then the elephant woodsman informs the noble head-anointed king: ‘The forest elephant has come out into the open, sire.’

Then, Aggivessana, the noble head-anointed king addresses his elephant tamer thus: ‘Come, good elephant tamer, tame the forest elephant. Subdue his forest habits, subdue his forest memories and intentions, subdue his distress, fatigue, and fever over leaving the forest. Get him to take delight in the town, inculcate in him habits congenial to human beings.’

‘Even so, sire,’ Aggivessana, the elephant tamer, having replied to the noble head-anointed king, plants a large post in the earth and binds the forest elephant to it by the neck in order to subdue his forest habits...and to inculcate in him habits congenial to human beings.

Then the elephant tamer addresses the elephant with words that are gentle, pleasing to the ear, and loveable, as go to the heart, are courteous, desired by many, and agreeable to many.

When the forest elephant is addressed by such words, he listens, gives ear, and exerts his mind to understand. The elephant tamer next rewards him with grass-fodder and water.

When the forest elephant accepts the grass-fodder and water from him, the elephant tamer knows: ‘Now the king’s elephant will live!’

Then the elephant tamer trains him further thus: ‘Take up, put down!’

When the forest elephant obeys his tamer’s orders to take up and put down and carries out his instructions, the elephant tamer trains him further thus: ‘Go forward, go back!’

When the forest elephant obeys his tamer’s orders to go forward and go back and carries out his instructions, the elephant tamer trains him further thus: ‘Get up, sit down!’

When the forest elephant obeys his tamer’s orders to get up and sit down and carries out his instructions, the elephant tamer trains him further in the task called imperturbability. He ties a giant plank to his trunk; a man with a lance in his hand sits on his neck; men with lances in their hands surround him on all sides; and the elephant tamer himself stands in front of him holding a long lance pole.

When the elephant is being trained in the task of imperturbability, he does not move his forelegs or his hindlegs; he does not move his forequarters or his hindquarters; he does not move his head, ears, tusks, tail, or trunk.

Thus the forest elephant becomes capable of enduring the blows of a sword, the blows of a spear, the blows of a club, and the blows of a sharp-pointed arrow.
The thundering sounds of drums (bheri), kettledrums (paṇava), trumpets (vaṃsa), conches (saṅkha), and tomtoms (ḍiṇḍima). Being rid of all faults and defects, purged of flaws, he is worthy of the king, in the king’s service, considered one of the factors of a king.
commentary_pali:
217.Nāgavanikanti hatthipadopame (ma. ni. 1.288 ādayo) nāgavanacarako puriso ‘‘nāgavaniko’’ti vutto, idha hatthisikkhāya kusalo hatthiṃ gahetuṃ samattho. Atipassitvāti disvā. Etthagedhāti etasmiṃ pavattagedhā. Sarasaṅkappānanti dhāvanasaṅkappānaṃ. Manussakantesu sīlesu samādapanāyāti ettha yadā nāgo itthipurisehi kumārakumārikāhi soṇḍādīsu gahetvā upakeḷayamāno vikāraṃ na karoti sukhāyati, tadānena manussakantāni sīlāni samādinnāni nāma honti.

Pemanīyāti tāta rājā te pasanno maṅgalahatthiṭṭhāneva ṭhapessati, rājārahāni bhojanādīni labhissasīti evarūpī nāgehi piyāpitabbā kathā. Sussūsatīti taṃ pemanīyakathaṃ sotukāmo hoti. Tiṇaghāsodakanti tiṇaghāsañceva udakañca, tiṇaghāsanti ghāsitabbaṃ tiṇaṃ, khāditabbanti attho.

Pemanīyā Sussūsatī Tiṇaghāsodaka tiṇaghāsa

Paṇavoti ḍiṇḍimo. Sabbavaṅkadosanihitaninnītakasāvoti nihitasabbavaṅkadoso ceva apanītakasāvo ca. Aṅganteva saṅkhaṃ gacchatīti aṅgasamo hoti.

Paṇavo Sabbavaṅkadosanihitaninnītakasāvo Aṅganteva saṅkhaṃ gacchatī
commentary_english:
217. " *Nāgavanika* " means one who is similar to an elephant's foot. (M.
N.
1.
288 ff.) *Nāgavanacarako puriso* means a man who dwells in a Nāga forest. " *Nāgavaniko* " means one who is skilled in elephant lore and is capable of handling elephants.
" *Atipassitvā* " means having seen.
" *Etthagedhā* " means greed in this matter.
" *Sarasaṅkappāna* " means thoughts of running.
" *Manussakantesu sīlesu samādapanāyā* " means here, when a Nāga, with women and men, boys and girls, is playing around with trunks, etc., and does not cause any alteration or find happiness, then these are called conduct pleasing to humans.

" *Pemanīyā* " means, dear one, the king, being pleased with you, will establish you in the place of the auspicious elephant. You will obtain food and so on that are worthy of a king; such is the talk dear and pleasing to the Nāgas.
" *Sussūsatī* " means he wishes to hear that endearing talk.
" *Tiṇaghāsodaka* " means grass, fodder, and water. " *Tiṇaghāsa* " means grass that is to be eaten, that is the meaning.

*Pemanīyā*, *sussūsatī*, *tiṇaghāsodaka*, *tiṇaghāsa*
" *Paṇavo* " means a small drum.
" *Sabbavaṅkadosanihitaninnītakasāvo* " means one who has deposited all crooked faults and removed astringency.
" *Aṅganteva saṅkhaṃ gacchati* " means it is similar to a limb.

*Paṇavo*, *sabbavaṅkadosanihitaninnītakasāvo*, *aṅganteva saṅkhaṃ gacchati*

mula_pali:
218. ‘‘Evameva kho, aggivessana, idha tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Taṃ dhammaṃ suṇāti gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aññatarasmiṃ vā kule paccājāto. So taṃ dhammaṃ sutvā tathāgate saddhaṃ paṭilabhati. So tena saddhāpaṭilābhena samannāgato iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā. Nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti.

‘‘So aparena samayena appaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya appaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Ettāvatā kho, aggivessana, ariyasāvako abbhokāsagato hoti. Etthagedhā hi, aggivessana, devamanussā yadidaṃ – pañca kāmaguṇā. Tamenaṃ tathāgato uttariṃ vineti – ‘ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, sīlavā hohi, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharāhi ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhassu sikkhāpadesū’’’ti.

‘‘Yato kho, aggivessana, ariyasāvako sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu, tamenaṃ tathāgato uttariṃ vineti – ‘ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, indriyesu guttadvāro hohi, cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā mā nimittaggāhī…pe… (yathā gaṇakamoggallānasuttante, evaṃ vitthāretabbāni.)
mula_english:
“So too, Aggivessana, a *Tathāgata* appears in the world, worthy and perfectly awakened, consummate in clear knowing and conduct, well-gone, an expert with regard to the cosmos, unsurpassed trainer of tamable people, teacher of beings human and divine, awakened, blessed. He proclaims this world with its gods (*devas*), *Māras*, and *Brahmās*, this generation with its recluses and *brāhmaṇas*, its rulers and commonfolk, having come to know it by his own knowledge. He teaches the *Dhamma* that is good at the beginning, good in the middle, and good at the end; he reveals the spiritual life (*brahmacariya*) that is utterly perfect and pure. A householder or a householder’s son or one born in some other clan hears that *Dhamma*. On hearing the *Dhamma* he acquires faith (*saddhā*) in the *Tathāgata*. Possessing that faith (*saddhā*), he reflects: “Household life is crowded, a path of dust. Going forth is like the open air. It is not easy for one dwelling at home to lead the perfectly complete, perfectly purified holy life (*brahmacariya*), bright as a polished conch. Suppose I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on saffron robes, and go forth from home to homelessness.”

“After some time he abandons his accumulation of wealth, be it large or small; he abandons his circle of relatives, be it large or small; he shaves off his hair and beard, puts on saffron robes, and goes forth from home to homelessness. It is in this way that a noble disciple (*ariyasāvako*) comes out into the open. For gods (*devas*) and humans cling to the five enjoyments of the senses (*pañca kāmaguṇā*). Then the *Tathāgata* disciplines him further: ‘Come, *bhikkhu*, be virtuous (*sīlavā*), restrained with the restraint of the *Pātimokkha*, be perfect in conduct and resort, and seeing fear in the slightest fault, train by undertaking the training precepts.’”

“When, Aggivessana, the noble disciple (*ariyasāvako*) is virtuous (*sīlavā*), restrained with the restraint of the *Pātimokkha*, perfect in conduct and resort, and seeing fear in the slightest fault, trains by undertaking the training precepts, then the *Tathāgata* disciplines him further: ‘Come, *bhikkhu*, guard the doors of your sense faculties (*indriyesu guttadvāro*). On seeing a form (*rūpaṃ*) with the eye (*cakkhunā*), do not grasp at its signs and features…pe… (As in the Gaṇakamoggallānasutta, so it should be expanded.)”

mula_pali: 219. ‘‘So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Seyyathāpi, aggivessana, hatthidamako mahantaṃ thambhaṃ pathaviyaṃ nikhaṇitvā āraññakassa nāgassa gīvāyaṃ upanibandhati āraññakānañceva sīlānaṃ abhinimmadanāya āraññakānañceva sarasaṅkappānaṃ abhinimmadanāya āraññakānañceva darathakilamathapariḷāhānaṃ abhinimmadanāya gāmante abhiramāpanāya manussakantesu sīlesu samādapanāya; evameva kho, aggivessana, ariyasāvakassa ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā cetaso upanibandhanā honti gehasitānañceva sīlānaṃ abhinimmadanāya gehasitānañceva sarasaṅkappānaṃ abhinimmadanāya gehasitānañceva darathakilamathapariḷāhānaṃ abhinimmadanāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya.
mula_english:
219. Having abandoned these five hindrances (pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya), the defilements of the mind (cetaso upakkilese) that weaken wisdom (paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe), he dwells contemplating the body in the body (kāye kāyānupassī viharati), ardent (ātāpī), clearly comprehending (sampajāno), mindful (satimā), having overcome avarice and displeasure for the world (vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ).

He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings (vedanāsu…pe…), mind in mind (citte…pe…), mental objects in mental objects (dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati), ardent (ātāpī), clearly comprehending (sampajāno), mindful (satimā), having overcome avarice and displeasure for the world (vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ).

"Just as, Aggivessana, the elephant tamer plants a large post in the earth (mahantaṃ thambhaṃ pathaviyaṃ nikhaṇitvā) and binds the forest elephant to it by the neck (āraññakassa nāgassa gīvāyaṃ upanibandhati) in order to subdue his forest habits (āraññakānañceva sīlānaṃ abhinimmadanāya), to subdue his forest memories and intentions (āraññakānañceva sarasaṅkappānaṃ abhinimmadanāya), to subdue his forest distress, fatigue, and fever (āraññakānañceva darathakilamathapariḷāhānaṃ abhinimmadanāya), to make him enjoy the village (gāmante abhiramāpanāya), and to train him in habits congenial to human beings (manussakantesu sīlesu samādapanāya); even so, Aggivessana, these four foundations of mindfulness (ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā) are the bindings for the mind (cetaso upanibandhanā) of the noble disciple (ariyasāvakassa) in order to subdue his habits based on the household life (gehasitānañceva sīlānaṃ abhinimmadanāya), to subdue his memories and intentions based on the household life (gehasitānañceva sarasaṅkappānaṃ abhinimmadanāya), to subdue his distress, fatigue, and fever based on the household life (gehasitānañceva darathakilamathapariḷāhānaṃ abhinimmadanāya), for the attainment of right knowledge (ñāyassa adhigamāya), for the realization of nirvāṇa (nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya)."
commentary_pali: 219.Gehasitasīlānanti pañcakāmaguṇanissitasīlānaṃ. Ñāyassāti aṭṭhaṅgikamaggassa.
commentary_english: 219. gehasitasīlānanti: *pañcakāmaguṇa-nissitasīlānaṃ*. ñāyassāti: *aṭṭhaṅgika-maggassa*.

mula_pali:
220. ‘‘Tamenaṃ tathāgato uttariṃ vineti – ‘ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, kāye kāyānupassī viharāhi , mā ca kāmūpasaṃhitaṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkesi. Vedanāsu… citte… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharāhi, mā ca kāmūpasaṃhitaṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkesī’’’ti.

‘‘So vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati.
mula_english:
“Then the *Tathāgata* further trains him, ‘Come, *bhikkhu*, abide contemplating the body (*kāye*) as a body (*kāyānupassī*), but do not think thoughts connected with sensual desire (*kāmūpasaṃhitaṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkesi*).

abide contemplating feelings (*vedanāsu*)… mind (*citte*)… phenomena (*dhammesu*) as phenomena (*dhammānupassī*), but do not think thoughts connected with sensual desire (*kāmūpasaṃhitaṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkesī*)’”.

“Having attained the stilling of thought and examination (*vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā*), inner tranquility (*ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ*), the unification of the mind (*cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ*), the *dvitīyaṃ dhyānam* second *jhāna*, which is without thought and examination (*avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ*), born of *samādhi* (*samādhijaṃ*), joyful and happy (*pītisukhaṃ*)... the third *jhāna* (*tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ*)… the fourth *jhāna* (*catutthaṃ jhānaṃ*)… he abides, having attained it (*upasampajja viharati*).

With his mind thus stilled (*evaṃ samāhite citte*), purified (*parisuddhe*), cleansed (*pariyodāte*), flawless (*anaṅgaṇe*), free from defilements (*vigatūpakkilese*), supple (*mudubhūte*), wieldy (*kammaniye*), steady (*ṭhite*), and unshakable (*āneñjappatte*), he directs his mind (*cittaṃ abhininnāmeti*) to the knowledge of the recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya*).

He recollects his manifold past lives (*anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati*), that is, one birth (*ekampi jātiṃ*), two births (*dvepi jātiyo*)… Thus with their aspects and particulars he recollects his manifold past lives (*sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati*).

mula_pali:
221. ‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.

‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti; ‘ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.

‘‘So hoti bhikkhu khamo sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ, uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātiko hoti sabbarāgadosamohanihitaninnītakasāvo āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa.
mula_english:
221. "When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, free from defects, pliant, malleable, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings.

He sees—by means of the divine eye ( *dibba-cakkhunā*), which is purified and surpasses the human—beings passing away and re-appearing, and he discerns how they are inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate in accordance with their *karma*: he understands beings passing on according to their actions (*yathākammūpage satte pajānāti*).

"When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, free from defects, pliant, malleable, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints ( *āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya*).

He understands as it actually is: ‘This is suffering (*idaṃ dukkha*)’; ‘This is the origin of suffering (*dukkhasamudayo*)’; ‘This is the cessation of suffering (*dukkhanirodho*)’; ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering (*dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā*)’; ‘These are the taints (*ime āsavā*)’; ‘This is the origin of the taints (*āsavasamudayo*)’; ‘This is the cessation of the taints (*āsavanirodho*)’; ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of the taints (*āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā*)’.

When he knows and sees thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*), from the taint of becoming (*bhavāsava*), and from the taint of ignorance (*avijjāsava*).

With release, there is the knowledge, ‘Released (*vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti*)’.

He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā*)’."

"That *bhikkhu* is able to endure cold and heat, hunger and thirst, and contact with gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, the sun, and creeping things; he is able to endure ill-spoken, unwelcome words and arisen bodily feelings that are painful, racking, sharp, piercing, disagreeable, distressing, and menacing to life. Being rid of all lust (*rāga*), hate (*dosa*), and delusion (*moha*), purged of flaws, he is worthy of gifts (*āhuneyya*), worthy of hospitality (*pāhuneyya*), worthy of offerings (*dakkhiṇeyya*), worthy of reverential salutations (*añjalikaraṇīyo*), an unsurpassed field of merit (*puññakkhettaṃ*) for the world (*lokassa*)."

mula_pali:
222. ‘‘Mahallako cepi, aggivessana, rañño nāgo adanto avinīto kālaṅkaroti, ‘adantamaraṇaṃ adantaṃ maraṇaṃ (ka.) mahallako rañño nāgo kālaṅkato’tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati; majjhimo cepi, aggivessana, rañño nāgo. Daharo cepi, aggivessana, rañño nāgo adanto avinīto kālaṅkaroti , ‘adantamaraṇaṃ daharo rañño nāgo kālaṅkato’tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati; evameva kho, aggivessana, thero cepi bhikkhu akhīṇāsavo kālaṅkaroti, ‘adantamaraṇaṃ thero bhikkhu kālaṅkato’tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati; majjhimo cepi, aggivessana, bhikkhu. Navo cepi, aggivessana, bhikkhu akhīṇāsavo kālaṅkaroti, ‘adantamaraṇaṃ navo bhikkhu kālaṅkato’tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati.

‘‘Mahallako cepi, aggivessana, rañño nāgo sudanto suvinīto kālaṅkaroti, ‘dantamaraṇaṃ mahallako rañño nāgo kālaṅkato’tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati; majjhimo cepi, aggivessana, rañño nāgo… daharo cepi, aggivessana, rañño nāgo sudanto suvinīto kālaṅkaroti, ‘dantamaraṇaṃ daharo rañño nāgo kālaṅkato’tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati; evameva kho, aggivessana, thero cepi bhikkhu khīṇāsavo kālaṅkaroti, ‘dantamaraṇaṃ thero bhikkhu kālaṅkato’tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati; majjhimo cepi, aggivessana, bhikkhu. Navo cepi, aggivessana, bhikkhu khīṇāsavo kālaṅkaroti, ‘dantamaraṇaṃ navo bhikkhu kālaṅkato’tveva saṅkhaṃ gacchatī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano aciravato samaṇuddeso bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Dantabhūmisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
222. “If, Aggivessana, the king’s *nāga* elephant dies in old age untamed and undisciplined, then he is considered an old elephant that has died an untamed death ( *adantamaraṇaṃ*). If the king’s *nāga* elephant dies when middle-aged untamed and undisciplined, then he is considered a middle-aged elephant that has died an untamed death.

If the king’s *nāga* elephant dies when young untamed and undisciplined, then he is considered a young elephant that has died an untamed death. So too, Aggivessana, if an elder *bhikkhu* dies with his taints undestroyed (*akhīṇāsavo*), then he is considered an elder *bhikkhu* who has died an untamed death. If a *bhikkhu* of middle status dies with his taints undestroyed, then he is considered a *bhikkhu* of middle status who has died an untamed death.

If a newly ordained *bhikkhu* dies with his taints undestroyed (*akhīṇāsavo*), then he is considered a newly ordained *bhikkhu* who has died an untamed death.

“If, Aggivessana, the king’s *nāga* elephant dies in old age well tamed and well disciplined, then he is considered an old elephant that has died a tamed death (*dantamaraṇaṃ*). If the king’s *nāga* elephant dies when middle-aged well tamed and well disciplined, then he is considered a middle-aged elephant that has died a tamed death. If the king’s *nāga* elephant dies when young well tamed and well disciplined, then he is considered a young elephant that has died a tamed death. So too, Aggivessana, if an elder *bhikkhu* dies with his taints destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*), then he is considered an elder *bhikkhu* who has died a tamed death. If a *bhikkhu* of middle status dies with his taints destroyed, then he is considered a *bhikkhu* of middle status who has died a tamed death.

If a newly ordained *bhikkhu* dies with his taints destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*), then he is considered a newly ordained *bhikkhu* who has died a tamed death.”

Thus spoke the Blessed One (*bhagavā*).

The novice Aciravata was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words (*bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti*).

The Dantabhūmi Sutta, the fifth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
222.Adantamaraṇaṃ mahallako rañño nāgo kālaṅkatoti rañño mahallako nāgo adantamaraṇaṃ mato kālaṃ kato hoti, adantamaraṇaṃ kālaṃkiriyaṃ nāma kariyatīti ayamettha attho. Esa nayo sabbattha. Sesaṃ uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Dantabhūmisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
"Adantamaraṇaṃ, the great elephant of the king, has died untimely," that is, the great elephant of the king died an untimely death. It is said that an untimely death is called *kālaṃkiriya*. This is the meaning here.

This method applies to all the other cases.

The rest is clear throughout.

The commentary of the Papañcasūdanī to the *Majjhimanikāya*

The *Dantabhūmisutta* commentary is finished.

mula_pali: 223. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho āyasmā bhūmijo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena jayasenassa rājakumārassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho jayaseno rājakumāro yenāyasmā bhūmijo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā bhūmijena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jayaseno rājakumāro āyasmantaṃ bhūmijaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘santi, bho bhūmija, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘āsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā carati, abhabbo (sī. pī.) evamuparipi ekavacaneneva dissati phalassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi āsañca anāsañca cepi (aṭṭha.) karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāyā’ti. Idha bhoto bhūmijassa satthā kiṃvādī kiṃvādī kiṃdiṭṭhī (syā. kaṃ. ka.) kimakkhāyī’’ti? ‘‘Na kho metaṃ, rājakumāra, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ bhagavā evaṃ byākareyya – ‘āsañcepi karitvā ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya ; anāsañcepi karitvā ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya. Āsañcepi karitvā yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, bhabbā phalassa adhigamāya ; anāsañcepi karitvā yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, bhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, bhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, bhabbā phalassa adhigamāyā’ti. Na kho me taṃ, rājakumāra, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ bhagavā evaṃ byākareyyā’’ti. ‘‘Sace kho bhoto bhūmijassa satthā evaṃvādī evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhī (syā. kaṃ. ka.) evamakkhāyī, addhā bhoto bhūmijassa satthā sabbesaṃyeva puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ muddhānaṃ buddhānaṃ (ka.) muddhānantimuddhaṃ, matthakanti attho maññe āhacca tiṭṭhatī’’ti . Atha kho jayaseno rājakumāro āyasmantaṃ bhūmijaṃ sakeneva thālipākena parivisi.
mula_english:
223. Thus I have heard.

On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary ( *veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe* ).

Then, the venerable Bhumija ( *āyasmā bhūmijo* ), when it was morning, dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went to the house of Prince Jayasena ( *jayasenassa rājakumārassa nivesanaṃ* ) and sat down on a seat made ready.

Then Prince Jayasena ( *jayaseno rājakumāro* ) went to the venerable Bhumija ( *āyasmā bhūmijo* ) and exchanged greetings with him.

When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.

Having sat down to one side, Prince Jayasena ( *jayaseno rājakumāro* ) said to the venerable Bhumija ( *āyasmantaṃ bhūmijaṃ* ): “Master Bhumija ( *bho bhūmija* ), there are some recluses and *brāhmaṇas* who make such assertions and hold such views as this: ‘If one makes an aspiration and one leads the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is unable to procure any fruit ( *phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still unable to procure any fruit ( *phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one both makes an aspiration and makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still unable to procure any fruit ( *phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one neither makes an aspiration nor makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still unable to procure any fruit."

"Here, what does the teacher (*satthā*) of Master Bhumija ( *bhoto bhūmijassa* ) proclaim, what does he make known?"

"I have not heard and learned that from the Blessed One’s ( *bhagavato* ) own lips, prince (*rājakumāra* ).

But it is possible that the Blessed One might say this: ‘If one makes an aspiration and one leads the holy life unwisely (*ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is unable to procure any fruit ( *phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life unwisely (*ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still unable to procure any fruit ( *phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one both makes an aspiration and makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life unwisely (*ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still unable to procure any fruit ( *phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one neither makes an aspiration nor makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life unwisely (*ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still unable to procure any fruit.

However, if one makes an aspiration and one leads the holy life wisely (*yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is able to procure fruit ( *phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life wisely (*yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still able to procure fruit (*phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one both makes an aspiration and makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life wisely (*yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still able to procure fruit (*phalassa adhigamāya* ); if one neither makes an aspiration nor makes no aspiration and one leads the holy life wisely (*yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti*), one is still able to procure fruit.’

I have not heard and learned this from the Blessed One’s ( *bhagavato* ) own lips, prince (*rājakumāra* ).

But it is possible that the Blessed One would answer as I have stated.”

“If the teacher (*satthā*) of Master Bhumija ( *bhoto bhūmijassa* ) proclaimed that, then indeed the teacher (*satthā*) of Master Bhumija ( *bhoto bhūmijassa* ), I think, stands striking the heads of all the various recluses and *brāhmaṇas*.”

Then Prince Jayasena ( *jayaseno rājakumāro* ) served the venerable Bhumija ( *āyasmantaṃ bhūmijaṃ* ) from his own dish of milk rice (*thālipākena parivisi*).
commentary_pali:
223.Evaṃme sutanti bhūmijasuttaṃ. Tattha bhūmijoti ayaṃ thero jayasenarājakumārassa mātulo. Āsañca anāsañcāti kālena āsaṃ kālena anāsaṃ. Sakenathālipākenāti pakatipavattāya bhikkhāya attano niṭṭhitabhattatopi bhattena parivisi. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Bhūmijasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
223. Thus, *me suta* is the Bhūmijasutta.

There, *bhūmijo* is the maternal uncle of Jayasenarājakumāra.

*Āsañca anāsañcā* means I approached at the right time, I did not approach at the wrong time.

*Sakena thālipākenā* means he served the alms-food to the *bhikkhu* according to custom, even from his own finished meal.

The rest is clear throughout.

This is the commentary to the Majjhimanikāya by Papañcasūdanī.

The Bhūmijasuttavaṇṇanā is finished.

mula_pali:
224. Atha kho āyasmā bhūmijo pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā bhūmijo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idhāhaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena jayasenassa rājakumārassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃ. Atha kho, bhante, jayaseno rājakumāro yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mayā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, bhante, jayaseno rājakumāro maṃ etadavoca – ‘santi, bho bhūmija, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – āsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāyā’ti. ‘Idha bhoto bhūmijassa satthā kiṃvādī kimakkhāyī’ti? Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhante, jayasenaṃ rājakumāraṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘na kho me taṃ, rājakumāra, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ bhagavā evaṃ byākareyya – āsañcepi karitvā ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya. Āsañcepi karitvā yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, bhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā yoniso brahmacariyaṃ caranti, bhabbā phalassa adhigamāyāti. Na kho me taṃ, rājakumāra, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati yaṃ bhagavā evaṃ byākareyyā’ti. ‘Sace bhoto bhūmijassa satthā evaṃvādī evamakkhāyī, addhā bhoto bhūmijassa satthā sabbesaṃyeva puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ muddhānaṃ maññe āhacca tiṭṭhatī’ti. ‘Kaccāhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva bhagavato homi, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhāmi, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaromi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī’’’ti?

‘‘Taggha tvaṃ, bhūmija, evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me hosi, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhasi, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākarosi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati. Ye hi keci, bhūmija, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā micchādiṭṭhino micchāsaṅkappā micchāvācā micchākammantā micchāājīvā micchāvāyāmā micchāsatī micchāsamādhino te āsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ayoni hesā, bhūmija, phalassa adhigamāya.
mula_english:
Then, the venerable Bhumija, having returned from his alms round after his meal, went to the Blessed One. Having approached, paid homage to the Blessed One, and sat down at one side.

Seated at one side, the venerable Bhumija said this to the Blessed One: "Here, venerable sir, in the forenoon, having dressed, taking my bowl and robe, I went to the residence of Prince Jayasena; having approached, I sat down on the seat that was prepared.

Then, venerable sir, Prince Jayasena came to me; having approached, he exchanged greetings with me.

Having concluded the courteous and amiable talk, he sat down at one side.

Seated at one side, venerable sir, Prince Jayasena said this to me: 'Master Bhumija, there are some ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* who assert such views as this: "Even if one makes an aspiration and practices the holy life (*brahmacariya*), one is incapable of attaining the fruit; even if one makes no aspiration… and so on … even if one both makes an aspiration and makes no aspiration and practices the holy life, one is incapable of attaining the fruit; even if one neither makes an aspiration nor makes no aspiration, and practices the holy life, one is incapable of attaining the fruit."

'Here, what does Master Bhumija's teacher say, what does he declare?' When this was said, I said this to Prince Jayasena: 'Prince, I have not heard and learned this from the Blessed One's own lips.

But it is possible that the Blessed One might say this: "Even if one makes an aspiration and practices the holy life unwisely (*ayoniso brahmacariyaṃ*), one is incapable of attaining the fruit; even if one makes no aspiration and practices the holy life unwisely, one is incapable of attaining the fruit; even if one both makes an aspiration and makes no aspiration and practices the holy life unwisely, one is incapable of attaining the fruit; even if one neither makes an aspiration nor makes no aspiration and practices the holy life unwisely, one is incapable of attaining the fruit.

Even if one makes an aspiration and practices the holy life wisely (*yoniso brahmacariyaṃ*), one is capable of attaining the fruit; even if one makes no aspiration… and so on … even if one both makes an aspiration and makes no aspiration… and so on … even if one neither makes an aspiration nor makes no aspiration and practices the holy life wisely, one is capable of attaining the fruit."

Prince, I have not heard and learned this from the Blessed One's own lips.

But it is possible that the Blessed One would answer as I have stated.'

'If Master Bhumija's teacher speaks thus, if he declares thus, then it certainly seems that the venerable Bhumija's teacher stands ahead of all the ordinary ascetics and *brāhmaṇas*.'

'Venerable sir, if I, having been asked thus, answer thus, am I one who speaks what has been said by the Blessed One, and do I not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is contrary to fact, and do I explain in accordance with the *Dhamma*, and does nothing which provides a ground for censure legitimately deduced from my assertion arise?'

'Surely, Bhumija, when you were asked such a question and answered thus, you said what has been said by me and did not misrepresent me with what is contrary to fact. You explained in accordance with the *Dhamma* in such a way that nothing which provides a ground for censure can be legitimately deduced from your assertion.

Whatever ascetics or *brāhmaṇas* have wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong concentration, if they make an aspiration and practice the holy life, they are incapable of attaining the fruit; if they make no aspiration and practice the holy life, they are incapable of attaining the fruit; if they both make an aspiration and make no aspiration and practice the holy life, they are incapable of attaining the fruit; if they neither make an aspiration nor make no aspiration and practice the holy life, they are incapable of attaining the fruit.

What is the reason for that? Because that wrong path is not a proper method for procuring fruit.

225. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhūmija, puriso telatthiko telagavesī telapariyesanaṃ caramāno vālikaṃ doṇiyā ākiritvā udakena paripphosakaṃ paripphosakaṃ pīḷeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ayoni hesā, bhūmija, telassa adhigamāya. Evameva kho, bhūmija, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā micchādiṭṭhino micchāsaṅkappā micchāvācā micchākammantā micchāājīvā micchāvāyāmā micchāsatī micchāsamādhino te āsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya. ‘‘Seyyathāpi , bhūmija, puriso khīratthiko khīragavesī khīrapariyesanaṃ caramāno gāviṃ taruṇavacchaṃ visāṇato āviñcheyya āviñjeyya (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Āsañcepi karitvā gāviṃ taruṇavacchaṃ visāṇato āviñcheyya, abhabbo khīrassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā gāviṃ taruṇavacchaṃ visāṇato āviñcheyya, abhabbo khīrassa adhigamāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ayoni hesā, bhūmija, khīrassa adhigamāya. Evameva kho, bhūmija, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā micchādiṭṭhino…pe… micchāsamādhino te āsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, abhabbā phalassa adhigamāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ayoni hesā, bhūmija, phalassa adhigamāya.

āviñjeyya (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
225. “Suppose, Bhūmija, a man needing oil, seeking oil, wandering in search of oil, were to heap up gravel in a tub, sprinkle it all over with water, and press it.

Then, if he made an aspiration and acted thus, he would be unable to procure any oil; if he made no aspiration and acted thus, he would still be unable to procure any oil; if he both made an aspiration and made no aspiration and acted thus, he would still be unable to procure any oil; if he neither made an aspiration nor made no aspiration and acted thus, he would still be unable to procure any oil.

What is the reason? It is not the proper means, Bhūmija, for the attainment of oil.

So too, Bhūmija, whatever recluses (*śramaṇa*) and *brāhmaṇas* have wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong concentration, if they make an aspiration and they lead the holy life (*brahmacarya*), they are unable to procure any fruit; if they make no aspiration and they lead the holy life, they are still unable to procure any fruit; if they both make an aspiration and make no aspiration and they lead the holy life, they are still unable to procure any fruit; if they neither make an aspiration nor make no aspiration and they lead the holy life, they are still unable to procure any fruit.

What is the reason? It is not the proper means, Bhūmija, for the attainment of fruit.

“Suppose, Bhūmija, a man needing milk, seeking milk, wandering in search of milk, were to pull a recently-calved cow by her horn.

Then, if he made an aspiration and acted thus, he would be unable to procure any milk; if he made no aspiration and acted thus…if he both made an aspiration and made no aspiration and acted thus…if he neither made an aspiration nor made no aspiration and acted thus, he would still be unable to procure any milk.

What is the reason? It is not the proper means, Bhūmija, for the attainment of milk.

So too, Bhūmija, whatever recluses (*śramaṇa*) and *brāhmaṇas* have wrong view…wrong concentration, if they make an aspiration and they lead the holy life (*brahmacarya*), they are unable to procure any fruit; if they make no aspiration and acted thus…if they both made an aspiration and made no aspiration and acted thus…if they neither made an aspiration nor made no aspiration and acted thus, they are still unable to procure any fruit.

What is the reason? It is not the proper means, Bhūmija, for the attainment of fruit.

Āsañcepi karitvā udakaṃ kalase āsiñcitvā matthena āviñcheyya, abhabbo navanītassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā udakaṃ kalase āsiñcitvā matthena āviñcheyya, abhabbo navanītassa adhigamāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yoni hesā, bhūmija, phalassa adhigamāya.

aggatthiko (sī.) abhimattheyya (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.)
mula_english:
226. “Suppose, Bhūmija, a man needing butter, seeking butter, wandering in search of butter, were to pour water into a churn and churn it with a churning-stick.

Then, if he made an aspiration and poured water into a churn and churned it with a churning stick, he would still be unable to procure any butter. If he made no aspiration…and so on… if he both made an aspiration and made no aspiration…and so on…if he neither made an aspiration nor made no aspiration and acted thus, he would still be unable to procure any butter.

What is the cause of that? It is because it is unwise, Bhūmija, to seek to acquire butter in that way.

So too, Bhūmija, whatever recluses and *brāhmaṇas* have wrong view…and so on… wrong concentration, if they make an aspiration and lead the holy life (*brahmacariya*), they are unable to procure any fruit (*phala*); if they make no aspiration…and so on…if they both make an aspiration and make no aspiration…and so on… if they neither make an aspiration nor make no aspiration and lead the holy life, they are still unable to procure any fruit.

What is the cause of that? It is because it is unwise, Bhūmija, to seek to acquire fruit (*phala*) in that way.”

“Suppose, Bhūmija, a man needing fire, seeking fire, wandering in search of fire, were to take an upper fire-stick and rub a damp, sappy piece of wood with it.

Then, if he made an aspiration and took a damp, sappy piece of wood with an upper fire-stick and rubbed it, he would still be unable to procure any fire. If he made no aspiration…and so on… if he both made an aspiration and made no aspiration…and so on…if he neither made an aspiration nor made no aspiration and acted thus, he would still be unable to procure any fire.

What is the cause of that? It is because it is unwise, Bhūmija, to seek to acquire fire in that way.”

So too, Bhūmija, whatever recluses and *brāhmaṇas* have wrong view…and so on… wrong concentration, if they make an aspiration and lead the holy life (*brahmacariya*), they are unable to procure any fruit (*phala*); if they make no aspiration…and so on… if they both make an aspiration and make no aspiration…and so on… if they neither make an aspiration nor make no aspiration and lead the holy life, they are still unable to procure any fruit (*phala*).

What is the cause of that? It is because it is unwise, Bhūmija, to seek to acquire fruit (*phala*) in that way.

Whatever recluses and *brāhmaṇas* have right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration, if they make an aspiration and lead the holy life (*brahmacariya*), they are able to procure fruit (*phala*); if they make no aspiration and lead the holy life (*brahmacariya*), they are still able to procure fruit (*phala*); if they both make an aspiration and make no aspiration and lead the holy life (*brahmacariya*), they are still able to procure fruit (*phala*); if they neither make an aspiration nor make no aspiration and lead the holy life (*brahmacariya*), they are still able to procure fruit (*phala*).

What is the cause of that? It is because it is wise, Bhūmija, to seek to acquire fruit (*phala*) in that way.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhūmija, puriso khīratthiko khīragavesī khīrapariyesanaṃ caramāno gāviṃ taruṇavacchaṃ thanato āviñcheyya. Āsañcepi karitvā gāviṃ taruṇavacchaṃ thanato āviñcheyya, bhabbo khīrassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā…pe… nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā gāviṃ taruṇavacchaṃ thanato āviñcheyya, bhabbo khīrassa adhigamāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yoni hesā, bhūmija, phalassa adhigamāya.
mula_english:
“Suppose, Bhūmija, a man needing oil, seeking oil, wandering in search of oil, were to heap up sesamum flour in a tub, sprinkle it all over with water, and press it.

Then, if he made an aspiration and acted thus, he would be able to procure oil; if he made no aspiration and acted thus...if he both made an aspiration and made no aspiration and acted thus...if he neither made an aspiration nor made no aspiration and acted thus, he would still be able to procure oil.

What is the reason for that? Because it is a means, Bhūmija, for the attainment of oil.

So too, Bhūmija, whatever recluses or *brāhmaṇas* have right view...right concentration, if they make an aspiration and practice the holy life (*brahmacariya*), they are able to procure fruit (*phala*); if they make no aspiration...if they both make an aspiration and make no aspiration...if they neither make an aspiration nor make no aspiration and practice the *brahmacariya*, they are able to procure *phala*.

What is the reason for that? Because it is a means, Bhūmija, for the attainment of *phala*.

Suppose, Bhūmija, a man needing milk, seeking milk, wandering in search of milk, were to pull a recently-calved cow by her udder.

Then, if he made an aspiration and acted thus, he would be able to procure milk; if he made no aspiration and acted thus...if he both made an aspiration and made no aspiration and acted thus...if he neither made an aspiration nor made no aspiration and acted thus, he would still be able to procure milk.

What is the reason for that? Because it is a means, Bhūmija, for the attainment of milk.

So too, Bhūmija, whatever recluses or *brāhmaṇas* have right view…right concentration, if they make an aspiration…if they make no aspiration…if they both make an aspiration and make no aspiration…if they neither make an aspiration nor make no aspiration and practice the *brahmacariya*, they are able to procure *phala*.

What is the reason for that? Because it is a means, Bhūmija, for the attainment of *phala*.

228. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhūmija, puriso navanītatthiko navanītagavesī navanītapariyesanaṃ caramāno dadhiṃ kalase āsiñcitvā matthena āviñcheyya. Āsañcepi karitvā dadhiṃ kalase āsiñcitvā matthena āviñcheyya, bhabbo navanītassa adhigamāya; anāsañcepi karitvā… āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā… nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā dadhiṃ kalase āsiñcitvā matthena āviñcheyya, bhabbo navanītassa adhigamāya. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhūmija, puriso aggitthiko aggigavesī aggipariyesanaṃ caramāno sukkhaṃ kaṭṭhaṃ koḷāpaṃ uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya abhimantheyya; ( ) (bhabbo aggissa adhigamāya) (sabbattha) āsañcepi karitvā… anāsañcepi karitvā.. āsañca anāsañcepi karitvā… nevāsaṃ nānāsañcepi karitvā sukkha kaṭṭhaṃ koḷāpaṃ uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya abhimantheyya, bhabbo aggissa adhigamāya.
