‘‘So kho ahaṃ, anuruddhā…pe… tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘atilīnavīriyaṃ kho me udapādi , atilīnavīriyādhikaraṇañca pana me samādhi cavi. Samādhimhi cute obhāso antaradhāyati dassanañca rūpānaṃ. Seyyathāpi, anuruddhā, puriso vaṭṭakaṃ sithilaṃ gaṇheyya, so tassa hatthato uppateyya; evameva kho me, anuruddhā, atilīnavīriyaṃ udapādi, atilīnavīriyādhikaraṇañca pana me samādhi cavi. Samādhimhi cute obhāso antaradhāyati dassanañca rūpānaṃ. Sohaṃ tathā karissāmi yathā me puna na vicikicchā uppajjissati, na amanasikāro, na thinamiddhaṃ, na chambhitattaṃ, na uppilaṃ, na duṭṭhullaṃ, na accāraddhavīriyaṃ, na atilīnavīriya’’’nti.

‘‘So kho ahaṃ, anuruddhā…pe… tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘abhijappā kho me udapādi, abhijappādhikaraṇañca pana me samādhi cavi. Samādhimhi cute obhāso antaradhāyati dassanañca rūpānaṃ. Sohaṃ tathā karissāmi yathā me puna na vicikicchā uppajjissati, na amanasikāro, na thinamiddhaṃ, na chambhitattaṃ, na uppilaṃ, na duṭṭhullaṃ, na accāraddhavīriyaṃ, na atilīnavīriyaṃ, na abhijappā’’’ti.

‘‘So kho ahaṃ, anuruddhā…pe… tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘nānattasaññā kho me udapādi, nānattasaññādhikaraṇañca pana me samādhi cavi. Samādhimhi cute obhāso antaradhāyati dassanañca rūpānaṃ. Sohaṃ tathā karissāmi yathā me puna na vicikicchā uppajjissati, na amanasikāro, na thinamiddhaṃ, na chambhitattaṃ, na uppilaṃ, na duṭṭhullaṃ, na accāraddhavīriyaṃ, na atilīnavīriyaṃ, na abhijappā, na nānattasaññā’’’ti.

‘‘So kho ahaṃ, anuruddhā, appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto obhāsañceva sañjānāmi dassanañca rūpānaṃ. So kho pana me obhāso nacirasseva antaradhāyati dassanañca rūpānaṃ. Tassa mayhaṃ anuruddhā etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo yena me obhāso antaradhāyati dassanañca rūpāna’nti. Tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘atinijjhāyitattaṃ kho me rūpānaṃ udapādi, atinijjhāyitattādhikaraṇañca pana me rūpānaṃ samādhi cavi. Samādhimhi cute obhāso antaradhāyati dassanañca rūpānaṃ. Sohaṃ tathā karissāmi yathā me puna na vicikicchā uppajjissati, na amanasikāro, na thinamiddhaṃ, na chambhitattaṃ, na uppilaṃ, na duṭṭhullaṃ, na accāraddhavīriyaṃ, na atilīnavīriyaṃ, na abhijappā, na nānattasaññā, na atinijjhāyitattaṃ rūpāna’’’nti.
mula_english:
241. “Excellent, excellent, Anuruddha! As you abide here diligent, ardent, and resolute, is there a superior human state, a distinction of knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding attained?” “Here, venerable sir, as we abide diligent, ardent, and resolute, we perceive both light (*obhāsa*) and a vision of forms (*rūpa*). Soon afterward the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) disappear, but we have not discovered the cause for that.” “You should discover the cause for that, Anuruddha. Before my enlightenment, while I was still only an unenlightened *Bodhisattva*, I too perceived both light (*obhāsa*) and a vision of forms (*rūpa*). Soon afterwards the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) disappeared. I thought: ‘What is the cause and condition why the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) have disappeared?’ I thought: ‘Doubt (*vicikicchā*) arose in me, and because of doubt (*vicikicchā*) my *samādhi* fell away. When my *samādhi* fell away, the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) disappeared. I shall so act that doubt (*vicikicchā*) will not arise in me again.’” “As, Anuruddha, I was abiding diligent, ardent, and resolute, I perceived both light (*obhāsa*) and a vision of forms (*rūpa*). Soon afterward the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) disappeared. I thought: ‘What is the cause and condition why the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) have disappeared?’ I thought: ‘Inattention (*amanasikāra*) arose in me, and because of inattention (*amanasikāra*) my *samādhi* fell away. When my *samādhi* fell away, the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) disappeared. I shall so act that neither doubt (*vicikicchā*) nor inattention (*amanasikāra*) will arise in me again.’” “As, Anuruddha, … I considered thus: ‘Sloth and torpor (*thinamiddha*) arose in me, and because of sloth and torpor (*thinamiddha*) my *samādhi* fell away. When my *samādhi* fell away, the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) disappeared. I shall so act that neither doubt (*vicikicchā*) nor inattention (*amanasikāra*) nor sloth and torpor (*thinamiddha*) will arise in me again.’” “As, Anuruddha, … I considered thus: ‘Fear (*chambhitatta*) arose in me, and because of fear (*chambhitatta*) my *samādhi* fell away. When my *samādhi* fell away, the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) disappeared. Suppose a man set out on a journey and murderers leaped out on both sides of him; then fear (*chambhitatta*) would arise in him because of that. So too, fear (*chambhitatta*) arose in me… When my *samādhi* fell away, the light (*obhāsa*) and the vision of forms (*rūpa*) disappeared. I shall so act that neither doubt (*vicikicchā*) nor inattention (*amanasikāra*) nor sloth and torpor (*thinamiddha*) nor fear (*chambhitatta*) will arise in me again.’” kaṃ. pī. ) [Note:] [omitted] Then I considered thus: ‘Elation arose in me, and because of elation my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away. When my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away, the light and the vision of forms disappeared. Suppose a man seeking one entrance to a hidden treasure came all at once upon five entrances to a hidden treasure; then elation would arise in him because of that. So too, elation arose in me, and because of elation my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away. When my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away, the light and the vision of forms disappeared. I considered thus: ‘I shall so act that neither doubt nor inattention, nor sloth and torpor, nor fear, nor elation will arise in me again.’ [Note:] ‘‘As, Anuruddha, I was abiding diligent…I considered thus: ‘Inertia arose in me, and because of inertia my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away. When my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away, the light and the vision of forms disappeared. I considered thus: ‘I shall so act that neither doubt nor inattention…nor elation nor inertia will arise in me again.’ “As, Anuruddha, I was abiding diligent…I considered thus: ‘Excess of energy arose in me, and because of excess of energy my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away. When my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away, the light and the vision of forms disappeared. Suppose a man were to grip a quail tightly with both hands; it would die then and there. So too, an excess of energy arose in me, and because of excess of energy my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away. When my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away, the light and the vision of forms disappeared. I considered thus: ‘I shall so act that neither doubt nor inattention…nor inertia nor excess of energy will arise in me again.’ [Note:] “As, Anuruddha, I was abiding diligent…I considered thus: ‘Deficiency of energy arose in me, and because of deficiency of energy my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away. When my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away, the light and the vision of forms disappeared. Suppose a man were to grip a quail loosely; it would fly out of his hands. So too, a deficiency of energy arose in me, and because of deficiency of energy my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away. When my concentration (*samādhi*) fell away, the light and the vision of forms disappeared. I considered thus: ‘I shall so act that neither doubt nor inattention…nor excess of energy nor deficiency of energy will arise in me again.’ 0198"/>

“As, Anuruddha…pe… I considered thus: ‘Longing (abhijappā) arose in me, and because of that longing my concentration (samādhi) fell away. when my concentration (samādhi) fell away, the light (obhāsa) and the vision (dassana) of forms (rūpānaṃ) disappeared. I shall so act that neither doubt (vicikicchā) nor inattention (amanasikāro)…nor deficiency of energy (atilīnavīriyaṃ) nor longing (abhijappā) will arise in me again.’

“As, Anuruddha…pe… I considered thus: ‘Perception of diversity (nānattasaññā) arose in me, and because of perception of diversity (nānattasaññā) my concentration (samādhi) fell away. when my concentration (samādhi) fell away, the light (obhāsa) and the vision (dassana) of forms (rūpānaṃ) disappeared. I shall so act that neither doubt (vicikicchā) nor inattention (amanasikāro)…nor longing (abhijappā) nor perception of diversity (nānattasaññā) will arise in me again.’

“As, Anuruddha, I was abiding diligent (appamatto), ardent (ātāpī), and resolute (pahitatto), I perceived both light (obhāsa) and a vision (dassana) of forms (rūpānaṃ). Soon afterward the light (obhāsa) and the vision (dassana) of forms (rūpānaṃ) disappeared. I thought: ‘What is the cause (hetu) and condition (paccayo) why the light (obhāsa) and the vision (dassana) of forms (rūpānaṃ) have disappeared?” I considered thus: ‘Excessive meditation upon forms (rūpānaṃ) arose in me, and because of excessive meditation upon forms (rūpānaṃ) my concentration (samādhi) fell away. when my concentration (samādhi) fell away, the light (obhāsa) and the vision (dassana) of forms (rūpānaṃ) disappeared. I shall so act that neither doubt (vicikicchā) nor inattention (amanasikāro)…nor perception of diversity (nānattasaññā) nor excessive meditation upon forms (rūpānaṃ) will arise in me again.’
commentary_pali:
241.Atthi pana voti pacchimapucchāya lokuttaradhammaṃ puccheyya. So pana therānaṃ natthi, tasmā taṃ pucchituṃ na yuttanti parikammobhāsaṃ pucchati. Obhāsañceva sañjānāmāti parikammobhāsaṃ sañjānāma. Dassanañca rūpānanti dibbacakkhunā rūpadassanañca sañjānāma. Tañca nimittaṃ nappaṭivijjhāmāti tañca kāraṇaṃ na jānāma, yena no obhāso ca rūpadassanañca antaradhāyati.

Taṃ kho pana vo anuruddhā nimittaṃ paṭivijjhitabbanti taṃ vo kāraṇaṃ jānitabbaṃ. Ahampi sudanti anuruddhā tumhe kiṃ na āḷulessanti, ahampi imehi ekādasahi upakkilesehi āḷulitapubboti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Vicikicchā kho metiādīsu mahāsattassa ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā dibbacakkhunā nānāvidhāni rūpāni disvā ‘‘idaṃ kho ki’’nti vicikicchā udapādi. Samādhi cavīti parikammasamādhi cavi. Obhāsoti parikammobhāsopi antaradhāyi, dibbacakkhunāpi rūpaṃ na passi. Amanasikāroti rūpāni passato vicikicchā uppajjati, idāni kiñci na manasikarissāmīti amanasikāro udapādi.

Taṃ kho pana vo anuruddhā nimittaṃ paṭivijjhitabba Ahampi suda Vicikicchā kho me Samādhi cavī Obhāso Amanasikāro

Thinamiddhanti kiñci amanasikarontassa thinamiddhaṃ udapādi.

Thinamiddha

Chambhitattanti himavantābhimukhaṃ ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā dānavarakkhasaajagarādayo addasa, athassa chambhitattaṃ udapādi.

Chambhitatta

Uppilanti ‘‘mayā diṭṭhabhayaṃ pakatiyā olokiyamānaṃ natthi. Adiṭṭhe kiṃ nāma bhaya’’nti cintayato uppilāvitattaṃ udapādi. Sakidevāti ekapayogeneva pañca nidhikumbhiyopi passeyya.

Uppila Sakidevā

Duṭṭhullanti mayā vīriyaṃ gāḷhaṃ paggahitaṃ, tena me uppilaṃ uppannanti vīriyaṃ sithilamakāsi, tato kāyadaratho kāyaduṭṭhullaṃ kāyālasiyaṃ udapādi.

Duṭṭhulla

Accāraddhavīriyanti mama vīriyaṃ sithilaṃ karoto duṭṭhullaṃ uppannanti puna vīriyaṃ paggaṇhato accāraddhavīriyaṃ udapādi. Patameyyāti mareyya.

Accāraddhavīriya Patameyyā

Atilīnavīriyanti mama vīriyaṃ paggaṇhato evaṃ jātanti puna vīriyaṃ sithilaṃ karoto atilīnavīriyaṃ udapādi.

Atilīnavīriya

Abhijappāti devalokābhimukhaṃ ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā devasaṅghaṃ passato taṇhā udapādi.

Abhijappā

Nānattasaññāti mayhaṃ ekajātikaṃ rūpaṃ manasikarontassa abhijappā uppannā, nānāvidharūpaṃ manasi karissāmīti kālena devalokābhimukhaṃ kālena manussalokābhimukhaṃ vaḍḍhetvā nānāvidhāni rūpāni manasikaroto nānattasaññā udapādi.

Nānattasaññā

Atinijjhāyitattanti mayhaṃ nānāvidhāni rūpāni manasikarontassa nānattasaññā udapādi, iṭṭhaṃ vā aniṭṭhaṃ vā ekajātikameva manasi karissāmīti tathā manasikaroto atinijjhāyitattaṃ rūpānaṃ udapādi.

Atinijjhāyitatta
commentary_english:
241. "Is there?" he should ask concerning the supramundane Dharma in the final question.

But he does not have [that] from the elders. Therefore, thinking that it is not appropriate to ask about that, he asks about preliminary illumination.

"We are conscious of illumination," means, we are conscious of preliminary illumination.

"And the sight of forms," means, with the divine eye, we are conscious of the sight of forms.

"And we do not penetrate that condition," means, we do not know that cause, by which the illumination and the sight of forms disappear for us.

"And that condition, Anuruddha, should be penetrated by you," means, that cause should be known by you.

"I too, indeed," means, Anuruddha, why do you not harass [yourselves]? I, too, with these eleven defilements, having harassed in the past, to show this teaching, he began.

"Doubt, indeed, to me," etc., to the great being, having increased the light, having seen various forms with the divine eye, "What is this?" doubt arose.

"Cessation of concentration," means, cessation of preliminary concentration.

"Illumination," means, preliminary illumination also disappeared, with the divine eye also, he did not see form.

"Non-attention," means, while seeing forms, doubt arises, now I will not attend to anything, thus non-attention arose.

That condition, Anuruddha, should be penetrated by you. I too, indeed.

Doubt, indeed, to me. Cessation of concentration. Illumination. Non-attention.

"Sloth and torpor," means, to one not attending to anything, sloth and torpor arose.

Sloth and torpor.

"Terrified state," means, having increased the light towards the Himalayas, he saw demons, ogres, pythons, etc., then to him, a terrified state arose.

Terrified state.

"Excitement," means, "Fear seen by me does not exist by nature when looking around. What is fear in the unseen?" to one thinking, a state of excitedness arose.

"At once," means, with a single application, he could see even five treasure pots.

Excitement. At once.

"Disgust," means, by me, energy was strongly exerted, therefore, excitement arose to me, thus he made energy weak, then bodily agitation, bodily disgust, bodily sloth arose.

Disgust.

"Excessive energy," means, while making my energy weak, disgust arose, thus again, while taking up energy, excessive energy arose.

"He might die," means, he might decease.

Excessive energy. He might die.

"Excessively sluggish energy," means, while taking up my energy, thus it happened, thus again, while making energy weak, excessively sluggish energy arose.

Excessively sluggish energy.

"Longing," means, having increased the light towards the world of the gods, while seeing the assembly of gods, craving arose.

Longing.

"Various perceptions," means, to me, while attending to a single kind of form, longing arose, a various kind of form, "I will attend in mind," thus, at one time, towards the world of the gods, at one time, towards the world of humans, having increased, while attending in mind to various forms, various perceptions arose.

Various perceptions.

"Excessive absorption," means, to me, while attending in mind to various kinds of forms, various perceptions arose, desirable or undesirable, or I will attend in mind only to a single kind, thus, while attending in mind, excessive absorption of forms arose.

Excessive absorption.

mula_pali: 242. ‘‘So kho ahaṃ, anuruddhā, ‘vicikicchā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā vicikicchaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘amanasikāro cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā amanasikāraṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘thinamiddhaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā thinamiddhaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘chambhitattaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā chambhitattaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘uppilaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā uppilaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘duṭṭhullaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā duṭṭhullaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘accāraddhavīriyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā accāraddhavīriyaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘atilīnavīriyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā atilīnavīriyaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘abhijappā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā abhijappaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘nānattasaññā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā nānattasaññaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ, ‘atinijjhāyitattaṃ rūpānaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā atinijjhāyitattaṃ rūpānaṃ cittassa upakkilesaṃ pajahiṃ.
mula_english: 242. “When, Anuruddha, I understood that doubt (*vicikicchā*) is an imperfection (*upakkilesa*) of the mind (*citta*), I abandoned doubt, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that inattention (*amanasikāro*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned inattention, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that sloth and torpor (*thinamiddhaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned sloth and torpor, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that fear (*chambhitattaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned fear, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that elation (*uppilaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned elation, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that inertia (*duṭṭhullaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned inertia, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that excess of energy (*accāraddhavīriyaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned excess of energy, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that deficiency of energy (*atilīnavīriyaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned deficiency of energy, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that longing (*abhijappā*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned longing, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that perception of diversity (*nānattasaññā*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned perception of diversity, an imperfection of the mind. When I understood that excessive meditation upon forms (*atinijjhāyitattaṃ rūpānaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind, I abandoned excessive meditation upon forms, an imperfection of the mind.

mula_pali:
243. ‘‘So kho ahaṃ, anuruddhā, appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto obhāsañhi kho sañjānāmi, na ca rūpāni passāmi; rūpāni hi kho passāmi, na ca obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi – ‘kevalampi rattiṃ, kevalampi divaṃ divasaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), kevalampi rattindivaṃ’ rattidivaṃ (ka.). Tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo yvāhaṃ obhāsañhi kho sañjānāmi na ca rūpāni passāmi; rūpāni hi kho kho tasmiṃ samaye (sī. ka.) passāmi na ca obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi – kevalampi rattiṃ, kevalampi divaṃ, kevalampi rattindiva’nti. Tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘yasmiñhi kho ahaṃ samaye rūpanimittaṃ amanasikaritvā obhāsanimittaṃ manasi karomi, obhāsañhi kho tasmiṃ samaye sañjānāmi, na ca rūpāni passāmi. Yasmiṃ panāhaṃ samaye obhāsanimittaṃ amanasikaritvā rūpanimittaṃ manasi karomi, rūpāni hi kho tasmiṃ samaye passāmi na ca obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi – kevalampi rattiṃ, kevalampi divaṃ, kevalampi rattindiva’’’nti.

‘‘So kho ahaṃ, anuruddhā, appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto parittañceva obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi, parittāni ca rūpāni passāmi; appamāṇañceva obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi, appamāṇāni ca rūpāni passāmi – kevalampi rattiṃ, kevalampi divaṃ, kevalampi rattindivaṃ. Tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo yvāhaṃ parittañceva obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi, parittāni ca rūpāni passāmi ; appamāṇañceva obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi, appamāṇāni ca rūpāni passāmi – kevalampi rattiṃ, kevalampi divaṃ, kevalampi rattindiva’nti. Tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘yasmiṃ kho me samaye paritto samādhi hoti, parittaṃ me tasmiṃ samaye cakkhu hoti. Sohaṃ parittena cakkhunā parittañceva obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi, parittāni ca rūpāni passāmi. Yasmiṃ pana me samaye appamāṇo samādhi hoti, appamāṇaṃ me tasmiṃ samaye cakkhu hoti. Sohaṃ appamāṇena cakkhunā appamāṇañceva obhāsaṃ sañjānāmi, appamāṇāni ca rūpāni passāmi – kevalampi rattiṃ, kevalampi divaṃ, kevalampi rattindiva’’’nti.
mula_english:
“As, Anuruddha, I was abiding diligent, ardent, and resolute, I perceived light but I did not see forms; I saw forms but I did not perceive light, even for a whole night or a whole day, or a whole day and night.

I thought: ‘What is the cause and condition for this? ‘

Then I considered thus: ‘On the occasion when I do not attend to the sign of form but attend to the sign of light, I then perceive light but do not see forms.

On the occasion when I do not attend to the sign of light but attend to the sign of forms, I then see forms but do not perceive light, even for a whole night or a whole day or a whole day and night.’

“As, Anuruddha, I was abiding diligent, ardent, and resolute, I perceived limited light and saw limited forms; I perceived immeasurable light and saw immeasurable forms, even for a whole night or a whole day or a whole day and night.

I thought: ‘What is the cause and condition for this?

Then I considered thus: ‘On the occasion when concentration is limited, my vision (cakṣu) is limited, and with limited vision (cakṣunā) I perceive limited light and limited forms.

But on the occasion when concentration (samādhi) is immeasurable, my vision (cakṣu) is immeasurable, and with immeasurable vision (cakṣunā) I perceive immeasurable light and see immeasurable forms, even for a whole night or a whole day or a whole day and night.’
commentary_pali:
243.Obhāsanimittaṃmanasi karomīti parikammobhāsameva manasi karomi. Na ca rūpāni passāmīti dibbacakkhunā rūpāni na passāmi. Rūpanimittaṃ manasi karomīti dibbacakkhunā visayarūpameva manasi karomi.

Parittañceva obhāsanti parittakaṭṭhāne obhāsaṃ. Parittāni ca rūpānīti parittakaṭṭhāne rūpāni. Vipariyāyena dutiyavāro veditabbo. Paritto samādhīti parittako parikammobhāso, obhāsaparittatañhi sandhāya idha parikammasamādhi ‘‘paritto’’ti vutto. Parittaṃ me tasmiṃ samayeti tasmiṃ samaye dibbacakkhupi parittakaṃ hoti. Appamāṇavārepi eseva nayo.

Parittañceva obhāsa Parittāni ca rūpānī Paritto samādhī Parittaṃ me tasmiṃ samaye
commentary_english:
243.
"I attend to the light-sign (obhāsanimittaṃ manasi karomī)," thus, I attend to the preliminary light alone.
"And I do not see forms (na ca rūpāṇi passāmī)," thus, with the divine eye, I do not see forms.
"I attend to the form-sign (rūpanimittaṃ manasi karomī)," thus, with the divine eye, I attend to the objective form alone.

"Limited light (parittañceva obhāsa)," [means] light in a limited place (parittakaṭṭhāne obhāsaṃ).
"Limited forms (parittāni ca rūpānī)," [means] forms in a limited place (parittakaṭṭhāne rūpāni).
The second turn should be understood in the opposite way (vipariyāyena dutiyavāro veditabbo).
"Limited concentration (paritto samādhī)," [means] limited preliminary light, for, referring to the limitedness of light, here, preliminary concentration is called "limited" (paritto’ti vutto).
"Limited to me at that time (parittaṃ me tasmiṃ samaye)," [means] at that time, even the divine eye is limited (tasmim samaye dibbacakkhupi parittakaṃ hoti).
The same method (eseva nayo) applies in the case of the immeasurable turn as well (appamāṇavārepi).

Limited light (parittañceva obhāsa), limited forms (parittāni ca rūpānī), limited concentration (paritto samādhī), limited to me at that time (parittaṃ me tasmiṃ samaye).

mula_pali: 244. Yato kho me , anuruddhā, ‘vicikicchā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā vicikicchā cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘amanasikāro cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā amanasikāro cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘thinamiddhaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā thinamiddhaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘chambhitattaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā chambhitattaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘uppilaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā uppilaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘duṭṭhullaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā duṭṭhullaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘accāraddhavīriyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā accāraddhavīriyaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘atilīnavīriyaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā atilīnavīriyaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘abhijappā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā abhijappā cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘nānattasaññā cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā nānattasaññā cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi, ‘atinijjhāyitattaṃ rūpānaṃ cittassa upakkileso’ti – iti viditvā atinijjhāyitattaṃ rūpānaṃ cittassa upakkileso pahīno ahosi.
mula_english: 244. When, Anuruddha, I knew that doubt (*vicikicchā*) is an imperfection of the mind (*cittassa upakkileso*)—thus knowing, doubt, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned (*pahīno ahosi*); when I knew that inattention (*amanasikāro*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, inattention, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that sloth and torpor (*thinamiddhaṃ*) are imperfections of the mind—thus knowing, sloth and torpor, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that fear (*chambhitattaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, fear, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that elation (*uppilaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, elation, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that inertia (*duṭṭhullaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, inertia, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that excess of energy (*accāraddhavīriyaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, excess of energy, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that deficiency of energy (*atilīnavīriyaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, deficiency of energy, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that longing (*abhijappā*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, longing, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that perception of diversity (*nānattasaññā*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, perception of diversity, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned; when I knew that excessive meditation (*atinijjhāyitattaṃ*) upon forms (*rūpānaṃ*) is an imperfection of the mind—thus knowing, excessive meditation upon forms, an imperfection of the mind, was abandoned.

mula_pali:
245. ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, anuruddhā, etadahosi – ‘ye kho me cittassa upakkilesā te me pahīnā. Handa, dānāhaṃ tividhena samādhiṃ bhāvemī’ti bhāvesinti (sī. syā. kaṃ.). So kho ahaṃ, anuruddhā, savitakkampi savicāraṃ samādhiṃ bhāvesiṃ bhāvemi (ka.), avitakkampi vicāramattaṃ samādhiṃ bhāvesiṃ, avitakkampi avicāraṃ samādhiṃ bhāvesiṃ, sappītikampi samādhiṃ bhāvesiṃ, nippītikampi samādhiṃ bhāvesiṃ, sātasahagatampi samādhiṃ bhāvesiṃ, upekkhāsahagatampi samādhiṃ bhāvesiṃ. Yato kho me, anuruddhā, savitakkopi savicāro samādhi bhāvito ahosi, avitakkopi vicāramatto samādhi bhāvito ahosi, avitakkopi avicāro samādhi bhāvito ahosi, sappītikopi samādhi bhāvito ahosi, nippītikopi samādhi bhāvito ahosi, sātasahagatopi samādhi bhāvito ahosi, upekkhāsahagatopi samādhi bhāvito ahosi. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi, akuppā me cetovimutti. Ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā anuruddho bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Upakkilesasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
245. “Then I thought: ‘I have abandoned those imperfections ( *upakkilesa*) of the mind.

So I developed concentration (*samādhi*) with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ samādhiṃ*); I developed concentration without applied thought but with sustained thought only (*avitakkaṃ vicāramattaṃ samādhiṃ*); I developed concentration without applied thought and without sustained thought (*avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhiṃ*); I developed concentration with rapture (*sappītikampi samādhiṃ*); I developed concentration without rapture (*nippītikampi samādhiṃ*); I developed concentration accompanied by enjoyment (*sātasahagatampi samādhiṃ*); I developed concentration accompanied by equanimity (*upekkhāsahagatampi samādhiṃ*).

When, Anuruddha, I had developed concentration with applied thought and sustained thought; when I had developed concentration without applied thought but with sustained thought only; when I had developed concentration without applied thought and without sustained thought; when I had developed concentration with rapture; when I had developed concentration without rapture; when I had developed concentration accompanied by enjoyment; when I had developed concentration accompanied by equanimity.

And knowledge and vision (*ñāṇañca dassanaṃ*) arose in me: ‘My deliverance is unshakeable (*akuppā me cetovimutti*). This is my last birth; now there is no renewal of being for me.’” (*ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’*).

The Buddha spoke thus. The venerable Anuruddha was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Discourse on the Imperfections is finished, the eighth.
commentary_pali:
245.Avitakkampi vicāramattanti pañcakanaye dutiyajjhānasamādhiṃ. Avitakkampi avicāranti catukkanayepi pañcakanayepi jhānattayasamādhiṃ. Sappītikanti dukatikajjhānasamādhiṃ. Nippītikanti dukajjhānasamādhiṃ. Sātasahagatanti tikacatukkajjhānasamādhiṃ. Upekkhāsahagatanti catukkanaye catutthajjhānasamādhiṃ pañcakanaye pañcamajjhānasamādhiṃ.

Kadā pana bhagavā imaṃ tividhaṃ samādhiṃ bhāveti? Mahābodhimūle nisinno pacchimayāme. Bhagavato hi paṭhamamaggo paṭhamajjhāniko ahosi, dutiyādayo dutiyatatiyacatutthajjhānikā . Pañcakanaye pañcamajjhānassa maggo natthīti so lokiyo ahosīti lokiyalokuttaramissakaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Upakkilesasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
245. *Avitakkampi vicāramatta* means the second *jhāna-samādhi* in the fivefold method.

*Avitakkampi avicāra* means the *samādhi* of the three *jhānas* in both the fourfold and fivefold methods.

*Sappītika* means the *jhāna-samādhi* of the dual triad.

*Nippītika* means the *jhāna-samādhi* of the dual.

*Sātasahagata* means the *jhāna-samādhi* of the triad-tetrad.

*Upekkhāsahagata* means the fourth *jhāna-samādhi* in the fourfold method and the fifth *jhāna-samādhi* in the fivefold method.

When does the Blessed One cultivate this threefold *samādhi*? In the last watch of the night, seated at the foot of the Great Bodhi tree.

For the Blessed One, the first path was associated with the first *jhāna*, and the second and subsequent paths were associated with the second, third, and fourth *jhānas*.

It is said that in the fivefold method, there is no path of the fifth *jhāna*, so it was mundane; this was said with reference to the mixture of mundane and supramundane.

The rest is clear throughout.

The Commentary on the *Upakkilesa Sutta* in Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary to the Middle Length Discourses, is finished.

mula_pali:
246. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, bālassa bālalakkhaṇāni bālanimittāni bālāpadānāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Idha, bhikkhave, bālo duccintitacintī ca hoti dubbhāsitabhāsī ca dukkaṭakammakārī ca. No cetaṃ no cedaṃ (saṃ. ni. 3.27-28), bhikkhave, bālo duccintitacintī ca abhavissa dubbhāsitabhāsī ca dukkaṭakammakārī ca kena naṃ na tena naṃ (ka.), na naṃ (?) paṇḍitā jāneyyuṃ – ‘bālo ayaṃ bhavaṃ asappuriso’ti? Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, bālo duccintitacintī ca hoti dubbhāsitabhāsī ca dukkaṭakammakārī ca tasmā naṃ paṇḍitā jānanti – ‘bālo ayaṃ bhavaṃ asappuriso’ti. Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bālo tividhaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Sace, bhikkhave, bālo sabhāyaṃ vā nisinno hoti, rathikāya rathiyāya (bahūsu) vā nisinno hoti, siṅghāṭake vā nisinno hoti; tatra ce jano tajjaṃ tassāruppaṃ kathaṃ manteti. Sace, bhikkhave, bālo pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī hoti, tatra, bhikkhave, bālassa evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃ kho jano tajjaṃ tassāruppaṃ kathaṃ manteti, saṃvijjanteva te saṃvijjante te ca (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmī’ti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, bālo paṭhamaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.

no cedaṃ (saṃ. ni. 3.27-28) na tena naṃ (ka.), na naṃ (?) rathiyāya (bahūsu) saṃvijjante te ca (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard:

On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was staying at Sāvatthi in the Jetavana, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying, "Monks!" "Venerable sir," they replied. The Blessed One said this:

"These three are the characteristics, signs and distinguishing features of a fool (bāla). What three? Here, a fool thinks bad thoughts ( *duccintitacintī*), speaks bad words (*dubbhāsitabhāsī*), and does bad deeds (*dukkaṭakammakārī*). If, monks, a fool did not think bad thoughts, speak bad words, and do bad deeds, then why would the wise recognize him as: ‘This person is a fool, an untrue man’? But because, monks, a fool thinks bad thoughts, speaks bad words and does bad deeds, therefore the wise know him as: ‘This person is a fool, an untrue man.’

"That fool, monks, experiences pain (*dukkha*) and grief (*domanassa*) in three ways, here and now.

If, monks, a fool is sitting in an assembly (*sabhāyaṃ*) or along a street (*rathikāya*) or in a square (*siṅghāṭake*), and people there are discussing certain pertinent and relevant matters, he thinks:

If, monks, a fool is one who kills living beings (*pāṇātipātī*), takes what is not given (*adinnādāyī*), misconducts himself in sensual pleasures (*kāmesumicchācārī*), speaks falsehood (*musāvādī*), and indulges in wine (*surā*), liquor (*meraya*), and intoxicants (*majja*), which are the basis of negligence (*pamādaṭṭhāyī*), he thinks: ‘These people are discussing certain pertinent and relevant matters; these things are found in me, and I am seen engaging in those things.’

This, monks, is the first kind of pain and grief that a fool experiences here and now."
commentary_pali: 246.Evaṃme sutanti bālapaṇḍitasuttaṃ. Tattha bālalakkhaṇānīti bālo ayanti etehi lakkhiyati ñāyatīti bālalakkhaṇāni. Tāneva tassa sañjānanakāraṇānīti bālanimittāni. Bālassa apadānānīti bālāpadānāni. Duccintitacintīti cintayanto abhijjhābyāpādamicchādassanavasena duccintitameva cinteti. Dubbhāsitabhāsīti bhāsamānopi musāvādādibhedaṃ dubbhāsitameva bhāsati. Dukkaṭakammakārīti karontopi pāṇātipātādivasena dukkaṭakammameva karoti. Tatra ceti yattha nisinno, tassaṃ parisati. Tajjaṃ tassāruppanti tajjātikaṃ tadanucchavikaṃ, pañcannaṃ verānaṃ diṭṭhadhammakasamparāyikaādīnavappaṭisaṃyuttanti adhippāyo. Tatrāti tāya kathāya kacchamānāya. Bālantiādīni sāmiatthe upayogavacanaṃ.
commentary_english:
246. "Thus have I heard," concerning the Bālapaṇḍitasutta.

There, *bālalakkhaṇāni* means the characteristics of a fool, by which a fool is known or understood.

*Bālanimittāni* means the signs of a fool, those very things that are the cause of his understanding.

*Bālāpadānāni* means the deeds of a fool.

*Duccintitacintī* means thinking only evil thoughts in terms of covetousness, ill-will, and wrong views.

*Dubbhāsitabhāsī* means speaking only evil speech, such as lies and so forth.

*Dukkaṭakammakārī* means doing only evil deeds in terms of killing living beings and so forth.

*Tatra ce* means in that assembly where he is sitting.

*Tajjaṃ tassāruppa* means befitting him, suitable for him, connected with the dangers of the five kinds of hatred, visible here and now, and related to future lives; this is the meaning.

*Tatrā* means in that story that is being discussed.

*Bāla* etc., are words used in the sense of ownership.

mula_pali: 247. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bālo passati rājāno coraṃ āgucāriṃ gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kārente – kasāhipi tāḷente vettehipi tāḷente addhadaṇḍakehipi tāḷente hatthampi chindante pādampi chindante hatthapādampi chindante kaṇṇampi chindante nāsampi chindante kaṇṇanāsampi chindante bilaṅgathālikampi karonte saṅkhamuṇḍikampi karonte rāhumukhampi karonte jotimālikampi karonte hatthapajjotikampi karonte erakavattikampi karonte cīrakavāsikampi karonte eṇeyyakampi karonte baḷisamaṃsikampi karonte kahāpaṇikampi karonte khārāpatacchikampi khārāpaṭicchakampi (ka.) karonte palighaparivattikampi karonte palālapīṭhakampi palālapiṭṭhakampi (pī.) karonte tattenapi telena osiñcante sunakhehipi khādāpente jīvantampi sūle uttāsente asināpi sīsaṃ chindante. Tatra, bhikkhave, bālassa evaṃ hoti – ‘yathārūpānaṃ kho pāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ hetu rājāno coraṃ āgucāriṃ gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kārenti – kasāhipi tāḷenti…pe… asināpi sīsaṃ chindanti; saṃvijjanteva te dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmi. Maṃ cepi rājāno sace mampi (ka.) jāneyyuṃ, mampi rājāno gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kāreyyuṃ – kasāhipi tāḷeyyuṃ…pe… jīvantampi sūle uttāseyyuṃ, asināpi sīsaṃ chindeyyu’nti. Idampi, bhikkhave, bālo dutiyaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.
mula_english: 247. Again, when a fool, O monks, sees kings arresting a robber who is a culprit and inflicting various kinds of punishments on him—flogging him with whips (*kasāhipi tāḷente*), beating him with canes (*vettehipi tāḷente*), beating him with half-clubs (*addhadaṇḍakehipi tāḷente*), cutting off his hands (*hatthampi chindante*), cutting off his feet (*pādampi chindante*), cutting off his hands and feet (*hatthapādampi chindante*), cutting off his ears (*kaṇṇampi chindante*), cutting off his nose (*nāsampi chindante*), cutting off his ears and nose (*kaṇṇanāsampi chindante*), inflicting the "porridge pot" punishment (*bilaṅgathālikampi karonte*), inflicting the "polished-shell shave" punishment (*saṅkhamuṇḍikampi karonte*), inflicting the "Rāhu's mouth" punishment (*rāhumukhampi karonte*), inflicting the "fiery wreath" punishment (*jotimālikampi karonte*), inflicting the "flaming hand" punishment (*hatthapajjotikampi karonte*), inflicting the "blades of grass" punishment (*erakavattikampi karonte*), inflicting the "bark dress" punishment (*cīrakavāsikampi karonte*), inflicting the "antelope" punishment (*eṇeyyakampi karonte*), inflicting the "hooked-flesh" punishment (*baḷisamaṃsikampi karonte*), inflicting the "penny" punishment (*kahāpaṇikampi karonte*), inflicting the *khārāpatacchika* punishment, inflicting the *palighaparivattika* punishment, inflicting the *palālapīṭhaka* punishment, drenching him with hot oil, setting dogs on him to eat him, impaling him alive, and cutting off his head with a sword (*asināpi sīsaṃ chindante*)—then, O monks, the fool thinks thus: ‘Because of such evil actions (*pāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ hetu*) as these, kings arrest a robber who is a culprit and inflict various kinds of punishments on him—flogging him with whips…cutting off his head with a sword (*asināpi sīsaṃ chindanti*); such things exist in me, and I am to be found among such things. If the kings should recognize me (*maṃ cepi rājāno jāneyyuṃ*), the kings would arrest me and inflict various kinds of punishments on me—they would flog me with whips…impale me alive, and cut off my head with a sword (*asināpi sīsaṃ chindeyyu’nti*).’ This, O monks, is the second kind of pain and grief that a fool experiences here and now (*dutiyaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti*).

mula_pali:
248. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bālaṃ pīṭhasamārūḷhaṃ vā mañcasamārūḷhaṃ vā chamāyaṃ chamāya (sī. pī.) vā semānaṃ, yānissa pubbe pāpakāni kammāni katāni kāyena duccaritāni vācāya duccaritāni manasā duccaritāni tānissa tamhi samaye olambanti ajjholambanti abhippalambanti. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahataṃ pabbatakūṭānaṃ chāyā sāyanhasamayaṃ pathaviyā olambanti ajjholambanti abhippalambanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bālaṃ pīṭhasamārūḷhaṃ vā mañcasamārūḷhaṃ vā chamāyaṃ vā semānaṃ, yānissa pubbe pāpakāni kammāni katāni kāyena duccaritāni vācāya duccaritāni manasā duccaritāni tānissa tamhi samaye olambanti ajjholambanti abhippalambanti. Tatra, bhikkhave, bālassa evaṃ hoti – ‘akataṃ vata me kalyāṇaṃ, akataṃ kusalaṃ, akataṃ bhīruttāṇaṃ; kataṃ pāpaṃ, kataṃ luddaṃ, kataṃ kibbisaṃ. Yāvatā, bho, akatakalyāṇānaṃ akatakusalānaṃ akatabhīruttāṇānaṃ katapāpānaṃ kataluddānaṃ katakibbisānaṃ gati taṃ gatiṃ pecca gacchāmī’ti. So socati kilamati paridevati urattāḷiṃ kandati sammohaṃ āpajjati. Idampi, bhikkhave, bālo tatiyaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.

‘‘Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bālo kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Yaṃ kho taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘ekantaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ ekantaṃ akantaṃ ekantaṃ amanāpa’nti, nirayameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘ekantaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ ekantaṃ akantaṃ ekantaṃ amanāpa’nti. Yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, upamāpi upamāhipi (sī.) na sukarā yāva dukkhā nirayā’’ti.

upamāhipi (sī.)
mula_english:
“Again, monks, when a fool is sitting on a chair ( *pīṭhasamārūḷhaṃ* ) or lying on a couch ( *mañcasamārūḷhaṃ* ) or resting on the ground, the evil actions ( *pāpakāni kammāni* ) done by him in the past, the misconduct ( *duccaritāni* ) of body ( *kāyena* ), speech ( *vācāya* ), and mind ( *manasā* ), cover him, overspread him, and envelop him.

Just as the shadow of a great mountain peak in the evening covers, overspreads, and envelops the earth, so too, monks, when a fool is sitting on a chair or lying on a couch or resting on the ground, the evil actions done by him in the past, the misconduct of body, speech, and mind, cover him, overspread him, and envelop him.

There, monks, the fool thinks, ‘Indeed, I have not done good ( *kalyāṇaṃ* ), I have not done wholesome deeds ( *kusalaṃ* ), I have not made myself a shelter from anguish ( *bhīruttāṇaṃ* ); I have done evil ( *pāpaṃ* ), I have done what is cruel ( *luddaṃ* ), I have done what is wicked ( *kibbisaṃ* ).’

‘When I pass away, I shall go to the destination ( *gatiṃ* ) of those who have not done what is good, have not done what is wholesome, have not made themselves a shelter from anguish, have done evil, have done what is cruel, have done what is wicked.’

He sorrows, grieves, and laments, he weeps beating his breast and becomes distraught.

This too, monks, is the third kind of pain ( *dukkhaṃ* ) and grief ( *domanassaṃ* ) that a fool feels here and now.

“Furthermore, monks, that fool, having practiced misconduct of body ( *kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā* ), having practiced misconduct of speech ( *vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā* ), having practiced misconduct of mind ( *manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā* ), upon the dissolution of the body ( *kāyassa bhedā* ), after death ( *maraṇā* ), is reborn in a state of deprivation ( *apāyaṃ* ), in an unhappy destination ( *duggatiṃ* ), in perdition ( *vinipātaṃ* ), even in hell ( *nirayaṃ upapajjati* ).

“Monks, were one rightly speaking to say of anything: ‘That is utterly unwished for ( *aniṭṭhaṃ* ), utterly undesired ( *akantaṃ* ), utterly disagreeable ( *amanāpaṃ* ),’ one would be rightly speaking of hell ( *nirayameva* ) when one says: ‘That is utterly unwished for, utterly undesired, utterly disagreeable.’

“Monks, it is so hard to find a simile ( *upamāpi na sukarā* ) for the suffering ( *dukkhā* ) in hell ( *nirayā* ).”
commentary_pali: 248.Olambantīti upaṭṭhahanti. Sesapadadvayaṃ tasseva vevacanaṃ, olambanādiākārena hi tāni upaṭṭhahanti, tasmā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Pathaviyā olambantīti pathavitale pattharanti. Sesapadadvayaṃ tasseva vevacanaṃ. Pattharaṇākāroyeva hesa. Tatra, bhikkhave, bālassāti tasmiṃ upaṭṭhānākāre āpāthagate bālassa evaṃ hoti.
commentary_english:
248.
"Olambantī," they attend.
"Sesapadadvayaṃ" is a synonym of that itself; they attend with the form of olambana, etc.; therefore, it is said thus.
"Pathaviyā olambantī," they spread on the surface of the earth.
"Sesapadadvayaṃ" is a synonym of that itself.
It is just the form of spreading.
"Tatra, bhikkhave, bālassā," thus it is for the fool in that attending form that has come into view.

mula_pali: 249. Evaṃ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sakkā pana, bhante, upamaṃ kātu’’nti? ‘‘Sakkā bhikkhū’’ti bhagavā avoca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, coraṃ āgucāriṃ gahetvā rañño dasseyyuṃ – ‘ayaṃ kho, deva, coro āgucārī, imassa yaṃ icchasi taṃ daṇḍaṃ paṇehī’ti. Tamenaṃ rājā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘gacchatha, bho, imaṃ purisaṃ pubbaṇhasamayaṃ sattisatena hanathā’ti . Tamenaṃ pubbaṇhasamayaṃ sattisatena haneyyuṃ. Atha rājā majjhanhikasamayaṃ majjhantikasamayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.), majjhantikaṃ samayaṃ (pī.) evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ambho, kathaṃ so puriso’ti? ‘‘‘Tatheva, deva, jīvatī’ti. Tamenaṃ rājā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘gacchatha, bho, taṃ purisaṃ majjhanhikasamayaṃ sattisatena hanathā’ti. Tamenaṃ majjhanhikasamayaṃ sattisatena haneyyuṃ. Atha rājā sāyanhasamayaṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ambho, kathaṃ so puriso’ti? ‘Tatheva, deva, jīvatī’ti. Tamenaṃ rājā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘gacchatha, bho, taṃ purisaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ sattisatena hanathā’ti. Tamenaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ sattisatena haneyyuṃ. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha , bhikkhave, api nu so puriso tīhi sattisatehi haññamāno tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvediyethā’’ti? ‘‘Ekissāpi, bhante, sattiyā haññamāno so puriso tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvediyetha, ko pana vādo tīhi sattisatehī’’ti?
mula_english:
249. Having spoken thus, a certain *bhikkhu* said this to the Blessed One: “Is it possible, venerable sir, to make a simile?” “It is possible, *bhikkhu*,” the Blessed One said.

“Suppose, *bhikkhu*, men were to arrest a robber culprit and present him to the king, saying: ‘Sire, here is a robber culprit. Order what punishment you wish for him.’

Then the king would say: ‘Go, men, strike this man in the morning with a hundred spears.’

And they would strike him in the morning with a hundred spears.

Then the king would say at noon: ‘Sirs, how is that man?’ “ ‘Sire, he is still alive.’

Then the king would say: ‘Go, men, strike that man at noon with a hundred spears.’

And they would strike him at noon with a hundred spears.

Then the king would say in the evening: ‘Sirs, how is that man?’ ‘Sire, he is still alive.’

Then the king would say: ‘Go, men, strike that man in the evening with a hundred spears.’

And they would strike him in the evening with a hundred spears.

What do you think, *bhikkhus*: if that man were struck with three hundred spears, would he experience pain and grief because of that?” “Venerable sir, that man would experience pain and grief because of being struck with even one spear, let alone three hundred.”
commentary_pali: 249.Etadavocāti anusandhikusalo bhikkhu ‘‘nirayassa upamā kātuṃ na sakkā’’ti na bhagavā vadati, ‘‘na sukarā’’ti pana vadati, na sukaraṃ pana sakkā hoti kātuṃ, handāhaṃ dasabalaṃ upamaṃ kārāpemīti cintetvā etaṃ ‘‘sakkā, bhante’’ti vacanaṃ avoca. Haneyyunti vinivijjhitvā gamanavasena yathā ekasmiṃ ṭhāne dve pahārā nipatanti, evaṃ haneyyuṃ. Tenassa dve vaṇamukhasatāni honti. Ito uttaripi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
249. The monk skilled in connecting (anusandhi), thinking, “The Blessed One does not say, ‘It is not possible (sakkā) to make a comparison (upamā) of hell (nirayassa),’ but he does say, ‘It is not easy (sukarā).’ However, it is not easy, but it is possible (sakkā) to do it. Come now, let me make a comparison of the Ten Powers (dasabalaṃ),” and contemplating this, he said (avoca) this word (vacanaṃ), “It is possible (sakkā), venerable sir (bhante).”

"They should strike (haneyyuṃ)," having pierced through (vinivijjhitvā), according to the manner of going (gamanavasena), just as two (dve) blows (pahārā) fall (nipatanti) in one (ekasmiṃ) place (ṭhāne), so (evaṃ) they should strike (haneyyuṃ).

Then (tenassa) there are (honti) two hundred (dve vaṇamukhasatāni).

Hereafter (ito uttaripi), this same (eseva) is the method (nayo).

mula_pali:
250. Atha kho bhagavā parittaṃ pāṇimattaṃ pāsāṇaṃ gahetvā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamo nu kho mahantataro – yo cāyaṃ mayā paritto pāṇimatto pāsāṇo gahito, yo ca himavā pabbatarājā’’ti? ‘‘Appamattako ayaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā paritto pāṇimatto pāsāṇo gahito, himavantaṃ pabbatarājānaṃ upanidhāya saṅkhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti, upanidhampi upanidhimpi (sī. pī.) na upeti’’. ‘‘Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ so puriso tīhi sattisatehi haññamāno tatonidānaṃ dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti taṃ nirayakassa dukkhassa upanidhāya saṅkhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti’’.

‘‘Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā pañcavidhabandhanaṃ nāma kammakāraṇaṃ karonti – tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ ayokhīlaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) hatthe gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ dutiye hatthe gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ pāde gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ dutiye pāde gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ majjhe urasmiṃ gamenti. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṃ karoti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti byantihoti (pī. ka.). Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā saṃvesetvā kuṭhārīhi kudhārīhi (ka.) tacchanti. So tattha dukkhā tibbā…pe… byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā uddhaṃpādaṃ adhosiraṃ gahetvā vāsīhi tacchanti. So tattha dukkhā tibbā…pe… byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā rathe yojetvā ādittāya pathaviyā sampajjalitāya sajotibhūtāya sañjotibhūtāya (syā. kaṃ. pī.) sārentipi paccāsārentipi . So tattha dukkhā tibbā…pe… byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā mahantaṃ aṅgārapabbataṃ ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ āropentipi oropentipi. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṃ karoti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā uddhaṃpādaṃ adhosiraṃ gahetvā tattāya lohakumbhiyā pakkhipanti ādittāya sampajjalitāya sajotibhūtāya. So tattha pheṇuddehakaṃ paccati. So tattha pheṇuddehakaṃ paccamāno sakimpi uddhaṃ gacchati, sakimpi adho gacchati, sakimpi tiriyaṃ gacchati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā nirayapālā punappunaṃ (ka.) mahāniraye pakkhipanti. So kho pana, bhikkhave, mahānirayo –

ayokhīlaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) byantihoti (pī. ka.) kudhārīhi (ka.) sañjotibhūtāya (syā. kaṃ. pī.) nirayapālā punappunaṃ (ka.)

‘‘Catukkaṇṇo catudvāro, vibhatto bhāgaso mito;

Ayopākārapariyanto, ayasā paṭikujjito.

‘‘Tassa ayomayā bhūmi, jalitā tejasā yutā;

Samantā yojanasataṃ, pharitvā tiṭṭhati sabbadā’’.

‘‘Anekapariyāyenapi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayakathaṃ katheyyaṃ; yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, na sukarā akkhānena pāpuṇituṃ yāva dukkhā nirayā.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One, having taken up a small, hand-sized stone, addressed the monks, saying: “What do you think, monks, which is greater: this small, hand-sized stone that I have taken up, or the Himavant, the king of mountains?”

“This small, hand-sized stone taken up by the Blessed One is insignificant, O venerable one. Compared to the Himavant, the king of mountains, it does not reach a count, does not reach a fraction, does not reach a comparison.”

“In the same way, monks, the pain and displeasure that a person experiences when being struck by three hundred spears, does not reach a count, does not reach a fraction, does not reach a comparison with the suffering of hell."

“Then, monks, the wardens of hell inflict on him what is called the fivefold binding of karmic causation: they drive a hot iron stake into his hand, they drive a hot iron stake into his second hand, they drive a hot iron stake into his foot, they drive a hot iron stake into his second foot, they drive a hot iron stake into the middle of his chest. There he experiences painful, intense, harsh, and bitter sensations, and he does not die until that evil action is exhausted.

Then, monks, the wardens of hell bind him and chop him with axes. There he experiences painful, intense sensations… and he does not die until that evil action is exhausted.

Then, monks, the wardens of hell, having seized him with his feet up and his head down, pare him with adzes. There he experiences painful, intense sensations… and he does not die until that evil action is exhausted.

Then, monks, the wardens of hell harness him to a chariot and drive him back and forth across burning ground, blazing, and glowing. There he experiences painful, intense sensations… and he does not die until that evil action is exhausted.

Then, monks, the wardens of hell make him climb up and down a great mountain of burning coals, blazing and glowing. There he experiences painful, intense, harsh, and bitter sensations, and he does not die until that evil action is exhausted.

Then, monks, the wardens of hell, having seized him with his feet up and his head down, plunge him into a red-hot metal cauldron, burning, blazing, and glowing. There he is cooked in a swirl of froth. As he is cooked there in a swirl of froth, he is swept now up, now down, and now across. There he experiences painful, intense, harsh, and bitter sensations, and he does not die until that evil action is exhausted.

Then, monks, the wardens of hell repeatedly throw him into the Great Hell. Now, monks, that Great Hell…
