Verse: "Four-eared, four-doored, divided into portions, measured;

Verse: surrounded by an iron wall, overturned with iron.

Verse: "His iron ground, ablaze, endowed with energy;

Verse: on all sides, a hundred *yojana*, having pervaded, it stands always."

"In many ways, *bhikkhus*, I could tell about hell; so much so that it is not easy to attain through description how much suffering there is in hell.
commentary_pali:
250.Pāṇimattanti antomuṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhapanamattaṃ. Saṅkhampi na upetīti gaṇanamattampi na gacchati. Kalabhāgampīti satimaṃ kalaṃ sahassimaṃ kalaṃ satasahassimaṃ vā kalaṃ upagacchatītipi vattabbataṃ na upeti. Upanidhampīti upanikkhepanamattampi na upeti, olokentassa olokitamattampi natthi. Tattaṃayokhilanti tigāvutaṃ attabhāvaṃ sampajjalitāya lohapathaviyā uttānakaṃ nipajjāpetvā tassa dakkhiṇahatthe tālappamāṇaṃ ayasūlaṃ pavesenti, tathā vāmahatthādīsu. Yathā ca uttānakaṃ nipajjāpetvā, evaṃ urenapi dakkhiṇapassenapi vāmapassenapi nipajjāpetvā taṃ kammakāraṇaṃ karontiyeva. Saṃvesetvāti sampajjalitāya lohapathaviyā tigāvutaṃ attabhāvaṃ nipajjāpetvā. Kuṭhārīhīti mahatīhi gehassa ekapakkhachadanamattāhi kuṭhārīhi tacchanti. Lohitaṃ nadī hutvā sandati, lohapathavito jālā uṭṭhahitvā tacchitaṭṭhānaṃ gaṇhanti. Mahādukkhaṃ uppajjati, tacchantā pana suttāhataṃ karitvā dārū viya aṭṭhaṃsampi chaḷaṃsampi karonti. Vāsīhīti mahāsuppapamāṇāhi vāsīhi. Tāhi tacchantā tacato yāva aṭṭhīni saṇikaṃ tacchanti, tacchitaṃ tacchitaṃ paṭipākatikaṃ hoti. Rathe yojetvāti saddhiṃ yugayottapañcaracakkakubbarapācanehi sabbato sampajjalite rathe yojetvā. Mahantanti mahākūṭāgārappamāṇaṃ. Āropentīti sampajjalitehi ayamuggarehi pothentā āropenti. Sakimpiuddhanti supakkuthitāya ukkhaliyā pakkhittataṇḍulā viya uddhaṃ adho tiriyañca gacchati.

Bhāgaso mitoti bhāge ṭhapetvā ṭhapetvā vibhatto. Pariyantoti parikkhitto. Ayasāti upari ayapaṭṭena chādito.

Bhāgaso mito Pariyanto Ayasā

Samantā yojanasataṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhatīti evaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhati, yathā samantā yojanasate ṭhāne ṭhatvā olokentassa akkhīni yamakagoḷakā viya nikkhamanti.

Samantā yojanasataṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhatī

Na sukarā akkhānena pāpuṇitunti nirayo nāma evampi dukkho evampi dukkhoti vassasataṃ vassasahassaṃ kathentenāpi matthakaṃ pāpetvā kathetuṃ na sukarāti attho.

Na sukarā akkhānena pāpuṇitu
commentary_english:
250. *Pāṇimatta* means the measure of the palm, or the amount that can be held in a closed fist.

*Saṅkhampi na upetī* means it does not reach even the measure of counting.

*Kalabhāgampī* means it does not reach the state of being spoken of as a sixteenth part, a thousandth part, or a hundred-thousandth part.

*Upanidhampī* means it does not reach even the state of being something set aside; when one is looking, there is nothing there to be seen.

*Tattaṃ ayokhila* means having laid [them] face up on the iron ground that is blazing with heat, having measured three *gāvuta*s in extent, they insert an iron stake the size of a palm fruit into their right hand, and similarly in the left hand, etc.

And just as they lay [them] face up, so too, having laid them on their chest, or on their right side, or on their left side, they perform that act of torture.

*Saṃvesetvā* means having laid [them] down on the iron ground blazing with heat, measuring three *gāvuta*s in extent.

*Kuṭhārīhī* means they carve with large axes, with axes the size of a single roof covering of a house.

Blood flows like a river, and flames rise up from the iron ground and seize the carved spot.

Great suffering arises; while carving, they make eight pieces or six pieces, like wood that has been marked with a string and struck.

*Vāsīhī* means with large knives the size of winnowing baskets.

While they are carving with those, they carve bit by bit right down to the bones, and what has been carved becomes repulsive.

*Rathe yojetvā* means having harnessed [them] to a chariot that is blazing with heat on all sides, together with its yoke, straps, five poles, wheels, *kubbara,* and goads.

*Mahanta* means the size of a large peaked house.

*Āropentī* means while striking with blazing iron hammers, they impale [them].

*Sakimpi uddha* means just as when grains of rice are tossed into a pot that is very well-cooked, they go upwards, downwards, and sideways.

*Bhāgaso mito* means divided up after placing [them] in portions.

*Pariyanto* means surrounded.

*Ayasā* means covered on top with a plate of iron.

*Bhāgaso mito pariyanto ayasā samantā yojanasataṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhatī* means in this way, it stands pervading a hundred *yojana*s all around, just as when one stands in a place a hundred *yojana*s all around and looks, one’s eyes come out like jujube fruits.

*Samantā yojanasataṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhatī*

*Na sukarā akkhānena pāpuṇitu* means the hell called Niraya is just so painful, just so painful, that even if one were to speak for a hundred years or a thousand years, one could not easily bring [the description] to its peak.

*Na sukarā akkhānena pāpuṇitu*

mula_pali:
251. ‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā tiṇabhakkhā. Te allānipi tiṇāni sukkhānipi tiṇāni dantullehakaṃ khādanti. Katame ca, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā tiṇabhakkhā? Hatthī assā goṇā gadrabhā ajā migā, ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānagatā pāṇā tiṇabhakkhā. Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bālo idha pubbe rasādo idha pāpāni kammāni karitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā tesaṃ sattānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati ye te sattā tiṇabhakkhā.

‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā gūthabhakkhā. Te dūratova gūthagandhaṃ ghāyitvā dhāvanti – ‘ettha bhuñjissāma, ettha bhuñjissāmā’ti. Seyyathāpi nāma brāhmaṇā āhutigandhena dhāvanti – ‘ettha bhuñjissāma, ettha bhuñjissāmā’ti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, santi tiracchānagatā pāṇā gūthabhakkhā, te dūratova gūthagandhaṃ ghāyitvā dhāvanti – ‘ettha bhuñjissāma, ettha bhuñjissāmā’ti. Katame ca, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā gūthabhakkhā? Kukkuṭā sūkarā soṇā siṅgālā, ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānagatā pāṇā gūthabhakkhā. Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bālo idha pubbe rasādo idha pāpāni kammāni karitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā tesaṃ sattānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati ye te sattā gūthabhakkhā.

‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā andhakāre jāyanti andhakāre jīyanti jiyyanti (ka.) andhakāre mīyanti miyyanti (ka.). Katame ca, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā andhakāre jāyanti andhakāre jīyanti andhakāre mīyanti? Kīṭā puḷavā paṭaṅgā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) gaṇḍuppādā, ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānagatā pāṇā andhakāre jāyanti andhakāre jīyanti andhakāre mīyanti. Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bālo idha pubbe rasādo, idha pāpāni kammāni karitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā tesaṃ sattānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati ye te sattā andhakāre jāyanti andhakāre jīyanti andhakāre mīyanti.

jiyyanti (ka.) miyyanti (ka.) paṭaṅgā (syā. kaṃ. ka.)

‘‘Santi, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā udakasmiṃ jāyanti udakasmiṃ jīyanti udakasmiṃ mīyanti. Katame ca, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā udakasmiṃ jāyanti udakasmiṃ jīyanti udakasmiṃ mīyanti? Macchā kacchapā susumārā, ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānagatā pāṇā udakasmiṃ jāyanti udakasmiṃ jīyanti udakasmiṃ mīyanti. Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bālo idha pubbe rasādo idha pāpāni kammāni karitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā tesaṃ sattānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati ye te sattā udakasmiṃ jāyanti udakasmiṃ jīyanti udakasmiṃ mīyanti.

‘‘Santi , bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā asucismiṃ jāyanti asucismiṃ jīyanti asucismiṃ mīyanti. Katame ca, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatā pāṇā asucismiṃ jāyanti asucismiṃ jīyanti asucismiṃ mīyanti? Ye te, bhikkhave, sattā pūtimacche vā jāyanti pūtimacche vā jīyanti pūtimacche vā mīyanti pūtikuṇape vā…pe… pūtikummāse vā… candanikāya vā… oligalle vā jāyanti, (ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānagatā pāṇā asucismiṃ jāyanti asucismiṃ jīyanti asucismiṃ mīyanti.) ( ) natthi sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bālo idha pubbe rasādo idha pāpāni kammāni karitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā tesaṃ sattānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati ye te sattā asucismiṃ jāyanti asucismiṃ jīyanti asucismiṃ mīyanti.

( ) natthi sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu

‘‘Anekapariyāyenapi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, tiracchānayonikathaṃ katheyyaṃ; yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, na sukaraṃ akkhānena pāpuṇituṃ yāva dukkhā tiracchānayoni.
mula_english:
251. Bhikkhus, there are animals that feed on grass.

They eat by cropping fresh or dried grass with their teeth.

And what animals feed on grass? Elephants, horses, cattle, donkeys, goats, and deer, and any other such animals feed on grass.

A fool who formerly delighted in tastes here and did evil actions here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in the company of animals that feed on grass.

There are animals that feed on dung.

They smell dung from a distance and run to it, thinking: ‘We can eat, we can eat!”

Just as *brāhmaṇas* run to the smell of a sacrifice, thinking: ‘We can eat, we can eat!’ so too these animals that feed on dung smell dung from a distance and run to it, thinking: ‘We can eat, we can eat!’

And what animals feed on dung? Fowls, pigs, dogs, and jackals, and any other such animals feed on dung.

A fool who formerly delighted in tastes here and did evil actions here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in the company of animals that feed on dung.

There are animals that are born, age, and die in darkness.

And what animals are born, age, and die in darkness? Moths, maggots, and earthworms, and any other such animals are born, age, and die in darkness.

A fool who formerly delighted in tastes here and did evil actions here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in the company of animals that are born, age, and die in darkness.

“There are animals that are born, age, and die in water.

And what animals are born, age, and die in water? Fish, turtles, and crocodiles, and any other such animals are born, age, and die in water.

A fool who formerly delighted in tastes here and did evil actions here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in the company of animals that are born, age, and die in water.

“There are animals that are born, age, and die in filth.

And what animals are born, age, and die in filth? Those animals that are born, age, and die in a rotten fish or in a rotten corpse or in rotten dough or in a cesspit or in a sewer, and any other such animals are born, age, and die in filth.
kaṃ.
pī.
In books, monks, the fool, having formerly delighted in tastes here and done evil actions here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in the company of those beings that are born, age, and die in filth.
natthi sī.
syā.
kaṃ.
pī.
Monks, I could tell you in many ways about the animal realm, so much so that it is hard to find a simile for the suffering in the animal realm.
commentary_pali: 251.Dantullehakanti dantehi ullehitvā, luñcitvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Rasādoti rasagedhena paribhuttaraso.
commentary_english:
251. *dantullehaka* means having scraped with the teeth, having plucked out.

*rasāda* means one who enjoys flavors due to craving for taste.

mula_pali:
252. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso ekacchiggalaṃ yugaṃ mahāsamudde pakkhipeyya. Tamenaṃ puratthimo vāto pacchimena saṃhareyya, pacchimo vāto puratthimena saṃhareyya, uttaro vāto dakkhiṇena saṃhareyya, dakkhiṇo vāto uttarena saṃhareyya. Tatrāssa kāṇo kacchapo, so vassasatassa vassasatassa vassasatassa vassasahassassa vassasatasahassassa (sī.), vassasatassa (syā. kaṃ. pī.) accayena sakiṃ ummujjeyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu so kāṇo kacchapo amusmiṃ ekacchiggale yuge gīvaṃ paveseyyā’’ti? (‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.) ( ) natthi sī. pī. potthakesu ‘‘Yadi pana yadi nūna (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), bhante, kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayenā’’ti. ‘‘Khippataraṃ kho so, bhikkhave, kāṇo kacchapo amusmiṃ ekacchiggale yuge gīvaṃ paveseyya, ato dullabhatarāhaṃ, bhikkhave, manussattaṃ vadāmi sakiṃ vinipātagatena bālena. Taṃ kissa hetu? Na hettha, bhikkhave, atthi dhammacariyā samacariyā kusalakiriyā puññakiriyā. Aññamaññakhādikā ettha, bhikkhave, vattati dubbalakhādikā’’.

‘‘Sa kho so, bhikkhave, bālo sace kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena manussattaṃ āgacchati, yāni tāni nīcakulāni – caṇḍālakulaṃ vā nesādakulaṃ vā venakulaṃ veṇakulaṃ (sī. pī.) vā rathakārakulaṃ vā pukkusakulaṃ vā. Tathārūpe kule paccājāyati dalidde appannapānabhojane kasiravuttike, yattha kasirena ghāsacchādo labbhati. So ca hoti dubbaṇṇo duddasiko okoṭimako bavhābādho bahvābādho (ka.) kāṇo vā kuṇī vā khujjo vā pakkhahato vā na lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa. So kāyena duccaritaṃ carati vācāya duccaritaṃ carati manasā duccaritaṃ carati. So kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati.

veṇakulaṃ (sī. pī.) bahvābādho (ka.)

‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, akkhadhutto paṭhameneva kaliggahena puttampi jīyetha, dārampi jīyetha, sabbaṃ sāpateyyampi jīyetha, uttaripi adhibandhaṃ anubandhaṃ (sī. pī.), addhubandhaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) nigaccheyya. Appamattako so, bhikkhave, kaliggaho yaṃ so akkhadhutto paṭhameneva kaliggahena puttampi jīyetha, dārampi jīyetha, sabbaṃ sāpateyyampi jīyetha, uttaripi adhibandhaṃ nigaccheyya. Atha kho ayameva tato mahantataro kaliggaho yaṃ so bālo kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, kevalā paripūrā kevalaparipūrā (sī. pī.) ma. ni. 1.244 pāḷiyā saṃsandetabbā bālabhūmī’’ti.

anubandhaṃ (sī. pī.), addhubandhaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) kevalaparipūrā (sī. pī.) ma. ni. 1.244 pāḷiyā saṃsandetabbā
mula_english:
252. Suppose, bhikkhus, a man threw into the sea a yoke with one hole in it. and the east wind carried it to the west, and the west wind carried it to the east, and the north wind carried it to the south, and the south wind carried it to the north. Suppose there were a blind turtle that came up once at the end of each century. What do you think, bhikkhus? Would that blind turtle put his neck into that yoke with one hole in it? “ “He might, venerable sir, sometime or other at the end of a long period.” “Bhikkhus, the blind turtle would take less time to put his neck into that yoke with a single hole in it than a fool, once gone to perdition, would take to regain the human state, I say. Why is that? Because there is no practising of the *dharma* there, no practising of what is righteous, no doing of what is wholesome, no performance of merit. Bhikkhus, there it is a matter of eating each other, devouring the weak.” If, sometime or other, at the end of a long period, that fool comes back to the human state, it is into a low family that he is reborn - into a family of *caṇḍālas* or hunters or bamboo-workers or cartwrights or *pukkusas*. one that is poor with little to eat and drink, surviving with difficulty, where he scarcely finds food and clothing; robes, conveyances, garlands, perfumes, ointments, bedding, He misconducts himself in body, speech, and mind. on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell. Suppose, *bhikkhus*, a gambler lost, with the first unlucky throw of the dice, even his son, his wife, and all his possessions, right up to his shirtfront. ), *addhubandhaṃ* (syā. kaṃ. ) *nigaccheyya*. Bhikkhus, a small unlucky throw ( *kaliggaho*) is that whereby a gambler ( *akkhadhutto*) loses his son ( *puttampi*), his wife ( *dārampi*), and all his property ( *sabbaṃ sāpateyyampi*) at the very first unlucky throw ( *paṭhameneva kaliggahena*), and furthermore incurs additional bondage ( *uttaripi adhibandhaṃ nigaccheyya*). Moreover, it is a far greater unlucky throw ( *mahantataro kaliggaho*) when a fool ( *bālo*) who, having conducted himself poorly ( *duccaritaṃ caritvā*) in body ( *kāyena*), having conducted himself poorly in speech ( *vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā*), and having conducted himself poorly in mind ( *manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā*), upon the dissolution of the body ( *kāyassa bhedā*), after death ( *paraṃ maraṇā*), is reborn in a state of loss (*apāyaṃ*), in an unhappy destination (*duggatiṃ*), in ruin (*vinipātaṃ*), even in hell ( *nirayaṃ upapajjati*). Bhikkhus, this is utter and complete *kevalaparipūrā* (sī. pī. ) ma. ni. 1. 244 *pāḷiyā saṃsandetabbā* the ground of a fool ( *bālabhūmīti*).

*anubandhaṃ* (sī. pī. ), *addhubandhaṃ* (syā. kaṃ. ) *kevalaparipūrā* (sī. pī. ) ma. ni. 1. 244 *pāḷiyā saṃsandetabbā*
commentary_pali:
252.Aññamaññakhādikāti aññamaññakhādanaṃ.

Dubbaṇṇoti durūpo. Duddasikoti dārakānaṃ bhayāpanatthaṃ katayakkho viya duddaso. Okoṭimakoti lakuṇḍako paviṭṭhagīvo mahodaro. Kāṇoti ekakkhikāṇo vā ubhayakkhikāṇo vā. Kuṇīti ekahatthakuṇī vā ubhayahatthakuṇī vā. Pakkhahatoti pīṭhasappī. Sokāyenāti idamassa dukkhānupabandhadassanatthaṃ āraddhaṃ.

Dubbaṇṇo Duddasiko Okoṭimako Kāṇo Kuṇī Pakkhahato So kāyenā

Kaliggahenāti parājayena. Adhibandhaṃ nigaccheyyāti yasmā bahuṃ jito sabbasāpateyyampissa nappahoti, tasmā attanāpi bandhaṃ nigaccheyya. Kevalā paripūrā bālabhūmīti bālo tīṇi duccaritāni pūretvā niraye nibbattati, tattha pakkāvasesena manussattaṃ āgato pañcasu nīcakulesu nibbattitvā puna tīṇi duccaritāni pūretvā niraye nibbattatīti ayaṃ sakalā paripuṇṇā bālabhūmi.

Kaliggahenā Adhibandhaṃ nigaccheyyā Kevalā paripūrā bālabhūmī
commentary_english:
252. *Aññamaññakhādikā* means aññamaññakhādanaṃ (mutually devouring).

*Dubbaṇṇo* means *durūpo* (ugly).
*Duddasiko* means *duddaso* (hard to see), like a demon created to frighten children.
*Okoṭimako* means *lakuṇḍako* (dwarf), with a sunken neck and a large belly.
*Kāṇo* means *ekakkhikāṇo* or *ubhayakkhikāṇo* (one-eyed or both-eyed blind).
*Kuṇī* means *ekahatthakuṇī* or *ubhayahatthakuṇī* (one-handed or two-handed maimed).
*Pakkhahato* means *pīṭhasappī* (paralyzed).
*So kāyenā* means this is begun to show the connection to suffering.

*Kaliggahenā* means by defeat.
*Adhibandhaṃ nigaccheyya* means since much is won, even all his property is not enough, therefore he would incur a debt by himself.
*Kevalā paripūrā bālabhūmī* means a fool, having filled the three evil deeds, is reborn in hell; having come to human existence there with the remainder of his deeds, being reborn in the five low families, again having filled the three evil deeds, is reborn in hell; this is the complete and perfect ground of the fool.

mula_pali: 253. ‘‘Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, paṇḍitassa paṇḍitalakkhaṇāni paṇḍitanimittāni paṇḍitāpadānāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Idha, bhikkhave, paṇḍito sucintitacintī ca hoti subhāsitabhāsī ca sukatakammakārī ca. No cetaṃ, bhikkhave, paṇḍito sucintitacintī ca abhavissa subhāsitabhāsī ca sukatakammakārī ca, kena naṃ na tena naṃ (ka.), na naṃ (?) paṇḍitā jāneyyuṃ – ‘paṇḍito ayaṃ bhavaṃ sappuriso’ti? Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, paṇḍito sucintitacintī ca hoti subhāsitabhāsī ca sukatakammakārī ca tasmā naṃ paṇḍitā jānanti – ‘paṇḍito ayaṃ bhavaṃ sappuriso’ti. Sa kho so, bhikkhave, paṇḍito tividhaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Sace, bhikkhave, paṇḍito sabhāyaṃ vā nisinno hoti, rathikāya vā nisinno hoti, siṅghāṭake vā nisinno hoti; tatra ce jano tajjaṃ tassāruppaṃ kathaṃ manteti . Sace, bhikkhave, paṇḍito pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti; tatra, bhikkhave, paṇḍitassa evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃ kho jano tajjaṃ tassāruppaṃ kathaṃ manteti; saṃvijjanteva te dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmī’ti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, paṇḍito paṭhamaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.
mula_english:
“Monks, there are these three characteristics of a wise man (paṇḍita), these are the signs of a wise man (paṇḍita), the indications of a wise man (paṇḍita), and the qualities of a wise man (paṇḍita).

What are the three? Here, monks, a wise man (paṇḍita) is one who thinks good thoughts (*sucintitacintī*), speaks good words (*subhāṣitabhāṣī*), and does good deeds (*sukatakarmakārī*).

If a wise man (paṇḍita) did not think good thoughts (*sucintitacintī*), speak good words (*subhāṣitabhāṣī*), and do good deeds (*sukatakarmakārī*), how would wise men know him as ‘This person is a wise man (paṇḍita), a true man (satpuruṣa)’? But because a wise man (paṇḍita) thinks good thoughts (*sucintitacintī*), speaks good words (*subhāṣitabhāṣī*), and does good deeds (*sukatakarmakārī*), therefore wise men know him as ‘This person is a wise man (paṇḍita), a true man (satpuruṣa).’

That wise man (paṇḍita), monks, experiences threefold pleasure (*sukha*) and joy (*saumanasya*) in this very life.

If, monks, a wise man (paṇḍita) is seated in an assembly (sabhā) or along a street (rathikā) or at a crossroads (siṅghāṭaka), and people there are discussing certain pertinent and relevant matters,

If, monks, a wise man (paṇḍita) abstains from killing living beings (*prāṇātipātā*), from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā*), from misconduct in sensual pleasures (*kāmesumicchācārā*), from false speech (*mṛṣāvādā*), and from liquor (*surā*), wine (*meraya*), and intoxicants (*madyapramādaṭṭhānā*), which are the basis of negligence, the wise man (paṇḍita) thinks thus: ‘These people are discussing certain pertinent and relevant matters; those things are not found in me, and I am not seen engaging in them.’

This, monks, is the first kind of pleasure (*sukha*) and joy (*saumanasya*) that a wise man (paṇḍita) experiences in this very life.
commentary_pali:
253.Paṇḍitalakkhaṇānītiādi vuttānusāreneva veditabbaṃ. Sucintitacintītiādīni cettha manosucaritādīnaṃ vasena yojetabbāni.

Cakkaratanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
The characteristics of a *paṇḍita* (paṇḍitalakkhaṇānī), and so on, are to be understood in accordance with what has been said.

*Sucintitacintī* ("well-thought thinker"), and so forth, should be connected here in terms of good mental conduct (*manas-sucarita*), and so forth.

Explanation of the Jewel Wheel (*cakkaratanavaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali: 254. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, paṇḍito passati rājāno coraṃ āgucāriṃ gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kārente – kasāhipi tāḷente vettehipi tāḷente addhadaṇḍakehipi tāḷente hatthampi chindante pādampi chindante hatthapādampi chindante kaṇṇampi chindante nāsampi chindante kaṇṇanāsampi chindante bilaṅgathālikampi karonte saṅkhamuṇḍikampi karonte rāhumukhampi karonte jotimālikampi karonte hatthapajjotikampi karonte erakavattikampi karonte cīrakavāsikampi karonte eṇeyyakampi karonte balisamaṃsikampi karonte kahāpaṇikampi karonte khārāpatacchikampi karonte palighaparivattikampi karonte palālapīṭhakampi karonte tattenapi telena osiñcante sunakhehipi khādāpente jīvantampi sūle uttāsente asināpi sīsaṃ chindante. Tatra, bhikkhave, paṇḍitassa evaṃ hoti – ‘yathārūpānaṃ kho pāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ hetu rājāno coraṃ āgucāriṃ gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kārenti kasāhipi tāḷenti, vettehipi tāḷenti, addhadaṇḍakehipi tāḷenti, hatthampi chindanti , pādampi chindanti, hatthapādampi chindanti, kaṇṇampi chindanti, nāsampi chindanti, kaṇṇanāsampi chindanti, bilaṅgathālikampi karonti, saṅkhamuṇḍikampi karonti, rāhumukhampi karonti, jotimālikampi karonti, hatthapajjotikampi karonti, erakavattikampi karonti, cīrakavāsikampi karonti, eṇeyyakampi karonti, balisamaṃsikampi karonti, kahāpaṇikampi karonti, khārāpatacchikampi karonti, palighaparivattikampi karonti, palālapīṭhakampi karonti, tattenapi telena osiñcanti, sunakhehipi khādāpenti, jīvantampi sūle uttāsenti, asināpi sīsaṃ chindanti, na te dhammā mayi saṃvijjanti, ahañca na tesu dhammesu sandissāmī’ti. Idampi, bhikkhave, paṇḍito dutiyaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.
mula_english:
“Again, when a wise man, *bhikkhus*, sees kings arresting a robber who is a wrongdoer and having various kinds of tortures inflicted on him: flogging him with whips, beating him with canes, beating him with clubs; having his hands cut off, his feet cut off, his hands and feet cut off; his ears cut off, his nose cut off, his ears and nose cut off; having him subjected to the ‘porridge pot,’ to the ‘polished-shell shave,’ to the ‘Rāhu’s mouth,’ to the ‘fiery wreath,’ to the ‘flaming hand,’ to the ‘blades of grass,’ to the ‘bark dress,’ to the ‘antelope,’ to the ‘fish-hook flesh,’ to the *kahāpaṇa*, to the ‘rough rasp,’ to the ‘gate-pivot,’ to the ‘straw seat’; drenching him with hot oil, having him devoured by dogs, impaling him alive, and cutting off his head with a sword.

Then the wise man thinks thus: ‘Because of such evil actions as those, when kings arrest a robber who is a wrongdoer, they have many kinds of tortures inflicted on him: flogging him with whips, beating him with canes, beating him with clubs; having his hands cut off, his feet cut off, his hands and feet cut off; his ears cut off, his nose cut off, his ears and nose cut off; having him subjected to the ‘porridge pot,’ to the ‘polished-shell shave,’ to the ‘Rāhu’s mouth,’ to the ‘fiery wreath,’ to the ‘flaming hand,’ to the ‘blades of grass,’ to the ‘bark dress,’ to the ‘antelope,’ to the ‘fish-hook flesh,’ to the *kahāpaṇa*, to the ‘rough rasp,’ to the ‘gate-pivot,’ to the ‘straw seat’; drenching him with hot oil, having him devoured by dogs, impaling him alive, and cutting off his head with a sword. Those things are not found in me, and I am not seen engaging in those things.’

This is the second land of pleasure and joy that a wise man feels here and now.

mula_pali:
255. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, paṇḍitaṃ pīṭhasamārūḷhaṃ vā mañcasamārūḷhaṃ vā chamāyaṃ vā semānaṃ, yānissa pubbe kalyāṇāni kammāni katāni kāyena sucaritāni vācāya sucaritāni manasā sucaritāni tānissa tamhi samaye olambanti…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahataṃ pabbatakūṭānaṃ chāyā sāyanhasamayaṃ pathaviyā olambanti ajjholambanti abhippalambanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, paṇḍitaṃ pīṭhasamārūḷhaṃ vā mañcasamārūḷhaṃ vā chamāyaṃ vā semānaṃ yānissa pubbe kalyāṇāni kammāni katāni kāyena sucaritāni vācāya sucaritāni manasā sucaritāni tānissa tamhi samaye olambanti ajjholambanti abhippalambanti. Tatra, bhikkhave, paṇḍitassa evaṃ hoti – ‘akataṃ vata me pāpaṃ, akataṃ luddaṃ, akataṃ kibbisaṃ; kataṃ kalyāṇaṃ, kataṃ kusalaṃ, kataṃ bhīruttāṇaṃ. Yāvatā, bho, akatapāpānaṃ akataluddānaṃ akatakibbisānaṃ katakalyāṇānaṃ katakusalānaṃ katabhīruttāṇānaṃ gati taṃ gatiṃ pecca gacchāmī’ti. So na socati, na kilamati, na paridevati, na urattāḷiṃ kandati, na sammohaṃ āpajjati. Idampi, bhikkhave, paṇḍito tatiyaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.

‘‘Sa kho so, bhikkhave, paṇḍito kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā vācāya sucaritaṃ caritvā manasā sucaritaṃ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Yaṃ kho taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘ekantaṃ iṭṭhaṃ ekantaṃ kantaṃ ekantaṃ manāpa’nti, saggameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘ekantaṃ iṭṭhaṃ ekantaṃ kantaṃ ekantaṃ manāpa’nti. Yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, upamāpi na sukarā yāva sukhā saggā’’ti.
mula_english:
255.
Again, *bhikkhus*, when a wise man is seated on a chair (*pīṭha-samārūḷhaṃ*) or a couch (*mañca-samārūḷhaṃ*) or resting on the ground (*chamāyaṃ semānaṃ*), then the good deeds (*kalyāṇāni kammāni*) that he has done in the past—his good conduct (*sucaritāni*) in body (*kāyena*), speech (*vācāya*), and mind (*manasā*)—cover him… Just as, *bhikkhus*, the shadow of a great mountain peak covers, overspreads, and envelops the earth in the evening, so too, *bhikkhus*, when a wise man is seated on a chair or a couch or resting on the ground, then the good deeds that he has done in the past—his good conduct in body, speech, and mind—cover him, overspread him, and envelop him.

Then, *bhikkhus*, the wise man thinks thus: ‘I have not done what is evil (*pāpaṃ*), I have not done what is cruel (*luddaṃ*), I have not done what is wicked (*kibbisaṃ*); I have done what is good (*kalyāṇaṃ*), I have done what is wholesome (*kusalaṃ*), I have made myself a shelter from anguish (*bhīruttāṇaṃ*).’

When I pass away, *bho*, I shall go to the destination of those who have not done evil, who have not done cruel deeds, who have not done wicked deeds, who have done good, who have done wholesome deeds, who have made themselves a shelter from anguish.’

He does not sorrow, grieve, or lament, he does not weep beating his breast, and he does not become distraught.

This is the third kind of pleasure (*sukhaṃ*) and joy (*somanassaṃ*) that a wise man feels here and now.

“Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, that wise man, having practiced good conduct in body (*kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā*), having practiced good conduct in speech (*vācāya sucaritaṃ caritvā*), having practiced good conduct in mind (*manasā sucaritaṃ caritvā*), at the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*) after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*) goes to a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), a heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati*).

“Whatever, *bhikkhus*, one speaking rightly might say, ‘That is utterly wished for (*ekaṃtaṃ iṭṭhaṃ*), utterly desired (*ekaṃtaṃ kantaṃ*), utterly agreeable (*ekaṃtaṃ manāpaṃ*)’—of heaven itself, one speaking rightly might say, ‘That is utterly wished for, utterly desired, utterly agreeable.’

So much so, *bhikkhus*, that a comparison is not easily made for the happiness (*sukhā*) of heaven (*saggā*)".

mula_pali:
256. Evaṃ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sakkā pana, bhante, upamaṃ kātu’’nti? ‘‘Sakkā bhikkhū’’ti bhagavā avoca. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī sattahi ratanehi samannāgato catūhi ca iddhīhi tatonidānaṃ sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Katamehi sattahi? Idha, bhikkhave, rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa tadahuposathe pannarase sīsaṃnhātassa uposathikassa uparipāsādavaragatassa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pātubhavati sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ. Taṃ disvāna rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa evaṃ hoti etadahosi (syā. kaṃ. ka.) – ‘sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ yassa rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa tadahuposathe pannarase sīsaṃnhātassa uposathikassa uparipāsādavaragatassa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pātubhavati sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ, so hoti rājā cakkavattīti. Assaṃ nu kho ahaṃ rājā cakkavattī’’’ti?

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto vāmena hatthena bhiṅkāraṃ gahetvā dakkhiṇena hatthena cakkaratanaṃ abbhukkirati – ‘pavattatu bhavaṃ cakkaratanaṃ, abhivijinātu bhavaṃ cakkaratana’nti. Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ puratthimaṃ disaṃ pavattati. Anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Yasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, padese cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāti tattha rājā cakkavattī vāsaṃ upeti saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave , puratthimāya disāya paṭirājāno te rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ehi kho, mahārāja! Svāgataṃ te, mahārāja svāgataṃ mahārāja (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)! Sakaṃ te, mahārāja! Anusāsa, mahārājā’ti . Rājā cakkavattī evamāha – ‘pāṇo na hantabbo, adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ, kāmesumicchā na caritabbā, musā na bhāsitabbā, majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ, yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, puratthimāya disāya paṭirājāno te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā anuyuttā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhavanti ahesuṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.).

svāgataṃ mahārāja (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) anuyuttā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ahesuṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.)
mula_english:
256. Having been said thus, a certain *bhikkhu* said this to the Blessed One: "Is it possible, venerable sir, to make a comparison?" "It is possible, *bhikkhus*," said the Blessed One.

"Suppose, *bhikkhus*, that a Wheel-turning Monarch (*rājā cakkavattī*) possesses the seven treasures (*sattahi ratanehi*) and the four kinds of success (*catūhi ca iddhīhi*), and because of that experiences pleasure (*sukhaṃ*) and joy (*somanassaṃ*)."

"Which are the seven? Here, *bhikkhus*, when a head-anointed noble king (*rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa*) on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth (*tadahuposathe pannarase*), having bathed his head (*sīsaṃnhātassa*), has ascended to the upper palace chamber (*uparipāsādavaragatassa*) for the Uposatha, there appears to him the divine wheel-treasure (*dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ*) with its thousand spokes (*sahassāraṃ*), its tire (*sanemikaṃ*), and its nave (*sanābhikaṃ*), complete in every aspect (*sabbākāraparipūraṃ*)."

On seeing it, the head-anointed noble king (*rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa*) thinks thus: ‘Now it has been heard by me that when a head-anointed noble king (*yassa rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa*) on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth (*tadahuposathe pannarase*), having bathed his head (*sīsaṃnhātassa*), has ascended to the upper palace chamber (*uparipāsādavaragatassa*) for the Uposatha, there appears to him the divine wheel-treasure (*dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ*) with its thousand spokes (*sahassāraṃ*), its tire (*sanemikaṃ*), and its nave (*sanābhikaṃ*), complete in every aspect (*sabbākāraparipūraṃ*), then that king becomes a Wheel-turning Monarch (*rājā cakkavattī*). Am I then a Wheel-turning Monarch (*rājā cakkavattī*)?’"

"Then, *bhikkhus*, the head-anointed noble king (*rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto*) takes a water-sprinkler (*bhiṅkāraṃ*) with his left hand (*vāmena hatthena*) and sprinkles the wheel-treasure (*cakkaratanaṃ*) with his right hand (*dakkhiṇena hatthena*), saying: ‘May the wheel-treasure turn forward (*pavattatu bhavaṃ cakkaratanaṃ*), may the wheel-treasure conquer (*abhivijinātu bhavaṃ cakkaratanaṃ*)!’"

"Then, *bhikkhus*, the wheel-treasure (*cakkaratanaṃ*) turns forward rolling in the eastern direction (*puratthimaṃ disaṃ pavattati*). The Wheel-turning Monarch (*rājā cakkavattī*) follows it with his fourfold army (*saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya*). And in whatever region (*yasmiṃ padese*) the wheel-treasure (*cakkaratanaṃ*) pauses (*patiṭṭhāti*), there the Wheel-turning Monarch (*rājā cakkavattī*) takes up his abode (*vāsaṃ upeti*) with his four-constituent army (*saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya*)."

"And those who opposed him (*paṭirājāno*) in the eastern direction (*puratthimāya disāya*) came to the king, the Wheel-turner (*rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ*) and said: 'Come, great king (*mahārāja*)! Welcome to you, great king (*svāgataṃ te, mahārāja*)! We are yours, great king (*sakaṃ te, mahārāja*)! Rule us, great king (*anusāsa, mahārājā*)!'"

The Wheel-turning Monarch (*rājā cakkavattī*) speaks thus: ‘You should not kill living beings (*pāṇo na hantabbo*); you should not take what has not been given (*adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ*); you should not misconduct yourselves in sensual pleasures (*kāmesumicchā na caritabbā*); you should not speak falsehood (*musā na bhāsitabbā*); you should not drink intoxicants (*majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ*); you should eat what you are accustomed to eat (*yathābhuttañca bhuñjatha*)’."

"And the opposing kings (*paṭirājāno*) in the eastern direction (*puratthimāya disāya*) submit to the Wheel-turning Monarch (*te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā*)."
)
commentary_pali:
256.Sīsaṃ nhātassāti sīsena saddhiṃ gandhodakena nhātassa. Uposathikassāti samādinnauposathaṅgassa. Uparipāsādavaragatassāti pāsādavarassa upari gatassa subhojanaṃ bhuñjitvā pāsādavarassa upari mahātale sirīgabbhaṃ pavisitvā sīlāni āvajjantassa. Tadā kira rājā pātova satasahassaṃ vissajjetvā mahādānaṃ datvā punapi soḷasahi gandhodakaghaṭehi sīsaṃ nhāyitvā katapātarāso suddhaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ ekaṃsaṃ katvā uparipāsādassa sirīsayane pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā nisinno attano dānamayapuññasamudayaṃ āvajjetvā nisīdati, ayaṃ sabbacakkavattīnaṃ dhammatā .

Tesaṃ taṃ āvajjantānaṃyeva vuttappakārapuññakammapaccayaṃ utusamuṭṭhānaṃ nīlamaṇisaṅghāṭasadisaṃ pācīnasamuddajalatalaṃ chindamānaṃ viya ākāsaṃ alaṅkurumānaṃ viya dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pātubhavati. Tayidaṃ dibbānubhāvayuttattā dibbanti vuttaṃ. Sahassaṃ assa arānanti sahassāraṃ. Saha nemiyā saha nābhiyā cāti sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ. Sabbehi ākārehi paripūranti sabbākāraparipūraṃ.

dibba sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ

Tattha cakkañca taṃ ratijananaṭṭhena ratanañcāti cakkaratanaṃ. Yāya pana taṃ nābhiyā ‘‘sanābhika’’nti vuttaṃ, sā indanīlamaṇimayā hoti. Majjhe panassā rajatamayā panāḷi, yāya suddhasiniddhadantapantiyā hasamānaṃ viya virocati. Majjhe chiddena viya candamaṇḍalena ubhosupi bāhirantesu rajatapaṭṭena kataparikkhepo hoti. Tesu panassā nābhipanāḷi parikkhepapaṭṭesu yuttaṭṭhāne paricchedalekhā suvibhattāva hutvā paññāyanti. Ayaṃ tāvassa nābhiyā sabbākāraparipūratā.

cakkaratanaṃ

Yehi pana taṃ arehi ‘‘sahassāra’’nti vuttaṃ, te sattaratanamayā sūriyarasmiyo viya pabhāsampannā honti. Tesampi ghaṭamaṇikaparicchedalekhādīni suvibhattāneva paññāyanti. Ayamassa arānaṃ sabbākāraparipūratā.

Yāya pana taṃ nemiyā saha ‘‘sanemika’’nti vuttaṃ, sā bālasūriyarasmikalāpasiriṃ avahasamānā viya surattasuddhasiniddhapavāḷamayā hoti. Sandhīsu panassā sañjhārāgasassirikarattajambonadapaṭṭā vaṭṭaparicchedalekhā ca suvibhattā paññāyanti. Ayamassa nemiyā sabbākāraparipūratā.

Nemimaṇḍalapiṭṭhiyaṃ panassa dasannaṃ dasannaṃ arānamantare dhamanavaṃso viya antosusiro chiddamaṇḍalacitto vātagāhī pavāḷadaṇḍo hoti, yassa vātena paharitassa sukusalasamannāhatassa pañcaṅgikatūriyassa viya saddo vaggu ca rajanīyo ca kamanīyo ca hoti. Tassa kho pana pavāḷadaṇḍassa upari setacchattaṃ, ubhosu passesu samosaritakusumadāmapantiyoti evaṃ samosaritakusumadāmapantisatadvayaparivārena setacchattasatadhārinā pavāḷadaṇḍasatena samupasobhitanemiparikkhepassa dvinnampi nābhipanāḷīnaṃ anto dve sīhamukhāni honti, yehi tālakkhandhappamāṇā puṇṇacandakiraṇakalāpasassirikā taruṇaravisamānarattakambalageṇḍukapariyantā ākāsagaṅgāgatisobhaṃ abhibhavamānā viya dve muttakalāpā olambanti, yehi cakkaratanena saddhiṃ ākāse samparivattamānehi tīṇi cakkāni ekato parivattantāni viya khāyanti. Ayamassa sabbaso sabbākāraparipūratā.

Taṃ panetaṃ evaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ pakatiyā sāyamāsabhattaṃ bhuñjitvā attano attano gharadvāre paññattāsanesu nisīditvā pavattakathāsallāpesu manussesu vīthicatukkādīsu kīḷamāne dārakajane nātiuccena nātinīcena vanasaṇḍamatthakāsannena ākāsappadesena upasobhayamānaṃ viya rukkhasākhaggāni, dvādasayojanato paṭṭhāya suyyamānena madhurassarena sattānaṃ sotāni odhāpayamānaṃ yojanato paṭṭhāya nānappabhāsamudayasamujjalena vaṇṇena nayanāni samākaḍḍhantaṃ rañño cakkavattissa puññānubhāvaṃ ugghosayantaṃ viya rājadhāniabhimukhaṃ āgacchati.

Atha tassa cakkaratanassa saddassavaneneva ‘‘kuto nu kho, kassa nu kho ayaṃ saddo’’ti āvajjitahadayānaṃ puratthimadisaṃ olokayamānānaṃ tesaṃ manussānaṃ aññataro aññataraṃ evamāha – ‘‘passa bho acchariyaṃ, ayaṃ puṇṇacando pubbe eko uggacchati, ajja pana attadutiyo uggato, etañhi rājahaṃsamithunaṃ viya puṇṇacandamithunaṃ pubbāpariyena gaganatalaṃ abhilaṅghatī’’ti. Tamañño āha – ‘‘kiṃ kathesi samma kahaṃ nāma tayā dve puṇṇacandā ekato uggacchantā diṭṭhapubbā, nanu esa tapanīyaraṃsidhāro piñcharakiraṇo divākaro uggato’’ti. Tamañño sitaṃ katvā evamāha – ‘‘kiṃ ummattosi, nanu kho idānimeva divākaro atthaṅgato, so kathaṃ imaṃ puṇṇacandaṃ anubandhamāno uggacchissati, addhā panetaṃ anekaratanappabhāsamujjalaṃ ekassa puññavato vimānaṃ bhavissatī’’ti. Te sabbepi apasādayantā aññe evamāhaṃsu – ‘‘kiṃ bahuṃ vippalapatha, nevesa puṇṇacando, na sūriyo na devavimānaṃ. Na hetesaṃ evarūpā sirisampatti atthi, cakkaratanena panetena bhavitabba’’nti.

Evaṃ pavattasallāpasseva tassa janassa candamaṇḍalaṃ ohāya taṃ cakkaratanaṃ abhimukhaṃ hoti. Tato tehi ‘‘kassa nu kho idaṃ nibbatta’’nti vutte bhavanti vattāro – ‘‘na kassaci aññassa, nanu amhākaṃ rājā pūritacakkavattivatto, tassetaṃ nibbatta’’nti. Atha so ca mahājano, yo ca añño passati, sabbo cakkaratanameva anugacchati. Tampi cakkaratanaṃ raññoyeva atthāya attano āgatabhāvaṃ ñāpetukāmaṃ viya sattakkhattuṃ pākāramatthakeneva nagaraṃ anusaṃyāyitvā rañño antepuraṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā antepurassa uttarasīhapañjaraāsanne ṭhāne yathā gandhapupphādīhi sukhena sakkā hoti pūjetuṃ, evaṃ akkhāhataṃ viya tiṭṭhati.

Evaṃ ṭhitassa panassa vātapānacchiddādīhi pavisitvā nānāvirāgaratanappabhāsamujjalaṃ anto pāsādaṃ alaṅkurumānaṃ pabhāsamūhaṃ disvā dassanatthāya sañjātābhilāso rājā hoti. Parijanopissa piyavacanapābhatena āgantvā tamatthaṃ nivedeti. Atha rājā balavapītipāmojjaphuṭasarīro pallaṅkaṃ mocetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā sīhapañjarasamīpaṃ gantvā taṃ cakkaratanaṃ disvā ‘‘sutaṃ kho pana meta’’ntiādikaṃ cintanaṃ cintesi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘disvāna rañño khattiyassa…pe… assaṃ nu kho ahaṃ rājā cakkavattī’’ti. Tattha so hoti rājā cakkavattīti kittāvatā cakkavattī hoti? Ekaṅguladvaṅgulamattampi cakkaratane ākāsaṃ abbhuggantvā pavatte.

so hoti rājā cakkavattī

Idāni tassa pavattāpanatthaṃ yaṃ kātabbaṃ taṃ dassento atha kho, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha uṭṭhāyāsanāti nisinnāsanato uṭṭhahitvā cakkaratanasamīpaṃ āgantvā. Bhiṅkāraṃ gahetvāti hatthisoṇḍasadisapanāḷiṃ suvaṇṇabhiṅkāraṃ ukkhipitvā vāmahatthena udakaṃ gahetvā. Pavattatu bhavaṃ cakkaratanaṃ, abhivijinātu bhavaṃ cakkaratananti. Anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāyāti sabbacakkavattīnañhi udakena abhisiñcitvā ‘‘abhivijānātu bhavaṃ cakkaratana’’nti vacanasamanantarameva vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā cakkaratanaṃ pavattati, yassa pavattisamakālameva so rājā cakkavattī nāma hoti.

atha kho, bhikkhave uṭṭhāyāsanā Bhiṅkāraṃ gahetvā Anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāyā

Pavatte pana cakkaratane taṃ anubandhamānova rājā cakkavattī yānavaraṃ āruyha vehāsaṃ abbhuggacchati, athassa chattacāmarādihattho parijano ceva antepurajano ca. Tato nānappakārakañcukakavacādisannāhavibhūsitena vividhāharaṇappabhāsamujjalitena samussitaddhajapaṭākapaṭimaṇḍitena attano attano balakāyena saddhiṃ uparājasenāpati pabhūtayopi vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā rājānameva parivārenti. Rājayuttā pana janasaṅgahatthaṃ nagaravīthīsu bheriyo carāpenti ‘‘tātā amhākaṃ rañño cakkaratanaṃ nibbattaṃ, attano attano vibhavānurūpena maṇḍitappasādhitā sannipatathā’’ti. Mahājano pana pakatiyā cakkaratanasaddeneva sabbakiccāni pahāya gandhapupphādīni ādāya sannipatitova, sopi sabbo vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā rājānameva parivāreti. Yassa yassa hi raññā saddhiṃ gantukāmatā uppajjati, so so ākāsagatova hoti. Evaṃ dvādasayojanāyāmavitthārā parisā hoti. Tattha ekapurisopi chinnabhinnasarīro vā kiliṭṭhavattho vā natthi. Suciparivāro hi rājā cakkavattī. Cakkavattiparisā nāma vijjādharaparisā viya ākāse gacchamānā indanīlamaṇitale vippakiṇṇaratanasadisā hoti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāyā’’ti.

Tampi cakkaratanaṃ rukkhaggānaṃ uparūpari nātiuccena gaganapadesena pavattati, yathā rukkhānaṃ pupphaphalapallavehi atthikā tāni sukhena gahetuṃ sakkonti, bhūmiyaṃ ṭhitā ‘‘esa rājā, esa uparājā, esa senāpatī’’ti sallakkhetuṃ sakkonti. Ṭhānādīsupi iriyāpathesu yo yena icchati, so teneva gacchati. Cittakammādisippapasutā cettha attano attano kiccaṃ karontāyeva gacchanti. Yatheva hi bhūmiyaṃ, tathā nesaṃ sabbakiccāni ākāse ijjhanti. Evaṃ cakkavattiparisaṃ gahetvā taṃ cakkaratanaṃ vāmapassena sineruṃ pahāya samuddassa uparibhāgena aṭṭhayojanasahassappamāṇaṃ pubbavidehaṃ gacchati.

Tattha yo vinibbedhena dvādasayojanāya parikkhepato chattiṃsayojanaparisāya sannivesakkhamo sulabhāhārūpakaraṇo chāyūdakasampanno sucisamatalo ramaṇīyo bhūmibhāgo, tassa uparibhāge taṃ cakkaratanaṃ ākāse akkhāhataṃ viya tiṭṭhati. Atha tena saññāṇena so mahājano otaritvā yathāruci nhānabhojanādīni sabbakiccāni karonto vāsaṃ kappeti, tena vuttaṃ ‘‘yasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, padese taṃ cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāti, tattha rājā cakkavattī vāsaṃ upeti saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāyā’’ti.

Evaṃ vāsaṃ upagate cakkavattimhi ye tattha rājāno, te ‘‘paracakkaṃ āgata’’nti sutvāpi na balakāyaṃ sannipātetvā yuddhasajjā honti. Cakkaratanassa uppattisamanantarameva natthi so satto nāma, yo paccatthikasaññāya rājānaṃ ārabbha āvudhaṃ ukkhipituṃ visaheyya. Ayamanubhāvo cakkaratanassa.

Cakkānubhāvena hi tassa rañño,

Arī asesā damathaṃ upenti;

Arindamaṃ nāma narādhipassa,

Teneva taṃ vuccati tassa cakkaṃ.

Tasmā sabbepi te rājāno attano attano rajjasirivibhavānurūpaṃ pābhataṃ gahetvā taṃ rājānaṃ upagamma onatasirā attano moḷiyamaṇippabhābhisekenassa pādapūjaṃ karonto ‘‘ehi kho mahārājā’’tiādīhi vacanehi tassa kiṅkārappaṭissāvitaṃ āpajjanti. Tena vuttaṃ ye kho pana, bhikkhave, puratthimāya…pe… anusāsa mahārājāti.

ye kho pana, bhikkhave, puratthimāya…pe… anusāsa mahārājā

Tattha svāgatanti suāgamanaṃ. Ekasmiñhi āgate socanti, gate nandanti. Ekasmiṃ āgate nandanti, gate socanti. Tādiso tvaṃ āgatanandano gamanasocano, tasmā tava āgamanaṃ suāgamananti vuttaṃ hoti. Evaṃ vutte pana cakkavattī nāpi ‘‘ettakaṃ nāma me anuvassaṃ baliṃ upakappethā’’ti vadati, nāpi aññassa bhogaṃ acchinditvā aññassa deti. Attano pana dhammarājabhāvassa anurūpāya paññāya pāṇātipātādīni upaparikkhitvā pemanīyena mañjunā sarena ‘‘passatha tātā, pāṇātipāto nāmesa āsevito bhāvito bahulīkato nirayasaṃvattaniko hotī’’tiādinā nayena dhammaṃ desetvā ‘‘pāṇo na hantabbo’’tiādikaṃ ovādaṃ deti. Tena vuttaṃ rājā cakkavattī evamāha pāṇo na hantabbo…pe… yathābhuttañca bhuñjathāti.

svāgata rājā cakkavattī evamāha pāṇo na hantabbo…pe… yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā

Kiṃ pana sabbepi rañño imaṃ ovādaṃ gaṇhantīti. Buddhassapi tāva sabbe na gaṇhanti, rañño kiṃ gaṇhissanti. Tasmā ye paṇḍitā vibhāvino, te gaṇhanti. Sabbe pana anuyantā bhavanti. Tasmā ‘‘ye kho pana, bhikkhave’’tiādimāha.

Atha taṃ cakkaratanaṃ evaṃ pubbavidehavāsīnaṃ ovāde dinne katapātarāse cakkavattībalena vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā puratthimaṃ samuddaṃ ajjhogāhati. Yathā yathā ca taṃ ajjhogāhati, tathā tathā agadagandhaṃ ghāyitvā saṃkhittaphaṇo nāgarājā viya saṃkhittaūmivipphāraṃ hutvā ogacchamānaṃ mahāsamuddasalilaṃ yojanamattaṃ ogantvā antosamudde veḷuriyabhitti viya tiṭṭhati. Taṅkhaṇaññeva ca tassa rañño puññasiriṃ daṭṭhukāmāni viya mahāsamuddatale vippakiṇṇāni nānāratanāni tato tato āgantvā taṃ padesaṃ pūrayanti. Atha sā rājaparisā taṃ nānāratanaparipūraṃ mahāsamuddatalaṃ disvā yathāruci ucchaṅgādīhi ādiyati, yathāruci ādinnaratanāya pana parisāya taṃ cakkaratanaṃ paṭinivattati. Paṭinivattamāne ca tasmiṃ parisā aggato hoti, majjhe rājā, ante cakkaratanaṃ. Tampi jalanidhijalaṃ palobhiyamānamiva cakkaratanasiriyā, asahamānamiva ca tena viyogaṃ, nemimaṇḍalapariyantaṃ abhihanantaṃ nirantarameva upagacchati.
commentary_english:
256. "sīsaṃ nhātassā" means of one who has bathed his head with fragrant water.
"uposathikassā" means of one who has undertaken the *uposatha* vows.
"uparipāsādavaragatassā" means of one who, having gone to the upper terrace of the palace, having eaten a fine meal, having entered the auspicious chamber on the great terrace above the palace, reflects on moral conduct.

Then, it is said that in the morning the king, having disbursed a hundred thousand, having given a great gift, and again having bathed his head with sixteen water-jars filled with scented water, having completed the morning meal, having arranged the pure upper robe over one shoulder, having ascended to the auspicious bedchamber of the upper palace, sits having crossed his legs, reflecting on the accumulation of merit arising from his generosity. This is the custom of all wheel-turning monarchs.

Then, because of the aforementioned accumulation of merit from good deeds, for those reflecting on this, the divine wheel-jewel (cakkaratana) appears, as if cleaving the surface of the eastern ocean, resembling a sapphire *saṅghāṭa*, as if adorning the sky.
Because it is endowed with divine power, it is called "divine".
"sahassāraṃ" [means] it has a thousand spokes.
"sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ" means with the felly (nemi) and with the nave (nābhi).
"sabbākāraparipūraṃ" means complete in all aspects.

The divine thousand-spoked, with felly and nave, complete in every way:
There, because the wheel (cakka) is a jewel (ratana) by its nature of producing delight (ratijanana), it is called the "wheel-jewel" (*cakkaratana*).
That nave (nābhi) which is called "with nave" (*sanābhika*) is made of *indanīla* jewel.
In its center is a channel (*panāḷi*) made of silver (*rajatamayā*), which shines as if smiling with a row of pure, smooth teeth.
In the middle, with a circle like a moon disc, on both the inner and outer sides, there is a pattern (*parikkhepo*) made with a silver band (*rajatapaṭṭena*).
In those channels of the nave, the demarcation lines (*paricchedalekhā*) at the joined places of the surrounding bands are very clearly visible.
This is the completeness of the nave in every aspect.

That wheel-jewel (*cakkaratana*):
Those spokes (ara) which are called "thousand-spoked" (*sahassāra*) are made of seven jewels (sattaratanamayā), and are radiant with splendor like rays of the sun.
The *ghaṭamaṇika* demarcation lines etc. on them are also very clearly visible.
This is the completeness of the spokes in every aspect.

That rim (nemi) which is called "with a rim" (*sanemika*) is made of very red, pure, smooth coral (*pavāḷamaya*), as if mocking the splendor of a cluster of young sun rays (*bālasūriyarasmikalāpasiriṃ*).
In its joints (*sandhīsu*), there are very clearly visible bands (*paṭṭā*) of twilight hue (sañjhārāga), possessing splendor (sassirika), and round delineation lines (vaṭṭaparicchedalekhā).
This is the completeness of the rim in every aspect.

On the surface of the wheel-band (*nemimaṇḍalapiṭṭhiyaṃ*), between each group of ten spokes (*arānaṃ antare*), there is a coral rod (*pavāḷadaṇḍo*) with a hollow interior (*antosusiro*), marked with perforated circles (chiddamaṇḍalacitto), like a windpipe (*dhamanavaṃso*), which is receptive to the wind (*vātagāhī*), and when struck by the wind (*vātena paharitassa*), the sound (*saddo*) is melodious (vaggu), delightful (rajanīyo), and pleasing (kamanīyo), like a well-tuned five-piece orchestra (*pañcaṅgikatūriyassa viya*).
Moreover, above that coral rod (*pavāḷadaṇḍassa upari*), there is a white umbrella (*setacchattaṃ*), and on both sides (*ubhosu passesu*) are rows of gathered flower garlands (*samosaritakusumadāmapantiyo*). Thus, that circumference of the rim (nemiparikkhepassa), adorned with hundreds of coral rods (*pavāḷadaṇḍasatena*) bearing hundreds of white umbrellas (*setacchattasatadhārinā*), surrounded by pairs of rows of gathered flower garlands (*samosaritakusumadāmapantisatadvayaparivārena*), has within the two channels of the nave (*dvinnampi nābhipanāḷīnaṃ anto*) two lion faces (*dve sīhamukhāni*), from which hang two pearl clusters (*muttakalāpā olambanti*), equal in measure to a palm tree trunk (*tālakkhandhappamāṇā*), possessing the splendor (sassirikā) of a collection of full-moon rays (*puṇṇacandakiraṇakalāpasassirikā*), with ends like red woolen balls equal to a young sun (*taruṇaravisamānarattakambalageṇḍukapariyantā*), as if surpassing the beauty of the course of the *ākāśa gaṅgā* (sky river), and when the three wheels are turned together in the sky, they appear as if turning together (*samparivattamānehi tīṇi cakkāni ekato parivattantāni viya khāyanti*).
This is its completeness in every way (*sabbaso sabbākāraparipūratā*).

Then, this being complete in all aspects (*evaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ*), in accordance with its nature (*pakatiyā*), having eaten the evening meal (*sāyamāsabhattaṃ bhuñjitvā*), having sat down on the appointed seats (*paññattāsanesu*) at their own house doors (*attano attano gharadvāre nisīditvā*), while people were engaged in continuous conversation (pravattakathāsallāpesu manussesu), and children were playing in the crossroads of the streets (*vīthicatukkādīsu kīḷamāne dārakajane*), it comes toward the capital (*rājadhāniabhimukhaṃ āgacchati*), as if adorning the sky region (*ākāsappadesena upasobhayamānaṃ viya*) with the tops of the tree branches (*rukkhasākhaggāni*) not too high and not too low (*nātiuccena nātinīcena*), close to the tops of the forest groves (*vanasaṇḍamatthakāsannena*), making the ears of beings to be filled with a sweet sound (*madhurassarena sattānaṃ sotāni odhāpayamānaṃ*) that is heard from twelve leagues away (*dvādasayojanato paṭṭhāya suyyamānena*), attracting the eyes with a color (*vaṇṇena nayanāni samākaḍḍhantaṃ*) that is brilliant with the rising of various splendors (*nānappabhāsamudayasamujjalena*) from a league away (*yojanato paṭṭhāya*), proclaiming the power of merit (*puññānubhāvaṃ ugghosayantaṃ viya*) of the wheel-turning king (*rañño cakkavattissa*).

Then, merely at the sound of that wheel-jewel (*atha tassa cakkaratanassa saddassavaneneva*), those people (*tesaṃ manussānaṃ*) whose hearts were turned (*āvajjitahadayānaṃ*), looking in the eastern direction (*puratthimadisaṃ olokayamānānaṃ*), thinking, "From where now, whose now, is this sound?" (*kuto nu kho, kassa nu kho ayaṃ saddo'ti*) one of them said this to another (*aññataro aññataraṃ evamāha*) – "Look, sir, a marvel! (*passa bho acchariyaṃ*) This full moon (*ayaṃ puṇṇacando*) formerly rose alone (*pubbe eko uggacchati*), but today (*ajja pana*) another one has risen with it (*attadutiyo uggato*). Indeed, this pair of full moons (*etañhi puṇṇacandamithunaṃ*), like a pair of royal swans (*rājahaṃsamithunaṃ viya*), flies through the surface of the sky in sequence (*pubbāpariyena gaganatalaṃ abhilaṅghatī*)."
Another one said, "What are you talking about, friend? Where have you ever seen two full moons rising together? Surely this is the sun, with its stream of golden rays and variegated colors!"

Another one, smiling, said thus: "Are you crazy? Just now the sun has set. How can it rise again, following this full moon? Surely this is a celestial mansion (vimāna) of a meritorious being, shining with the light of many jewels."

All of them, rejecting [the previous opinions], said thus: "Why do you babble so much? This is neither the full moon, nor the sun, nor a divine celestial mansion.

[Since] they do not have such splendor and wealth, it must be the wheel treasure (cakraratana)!"

Thus, while that crowd was engaged in conversation, the moon-like circle disappeared, and that wheel treasure (cakraratana) appeared before that group of people.

Then, when they said, "To whom does this belong?", [some] speakers said, "It belongs to no one else. Surely, our king is fulfilling the duties of a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin); it belongs to him!"

Then, that great crowd, and whoever else saw [it], all followed the wheel treasure (cakkaratana).

That wheel treasure (cakraratana) too, as if wishing to make known its arrival for the sake of the king, having circled the city seven times on the ramparts themselves, having circumambulated the king's inner palace (antepura) clockwise, stood in a place near the northern lion-window (uttarasīhapañjara) of the inner palace (antepura), where it was easy to honor it with fragrant flowers and other offerings. It stood as if fixed [there].

Thus, having seen the mass of light entering the inner palace through the window openings and other [apertures] and adorning the palace interior with various colors, detachment, jewel-like splendor, the king developed a desire for seeing [it].

His attendant (parijano), having come with pleasing words of homage, reported that matter.

Then, the king, with a body invigorated by joy and delight, having descended from the couch, having risen from his seat, went to the vicinity of the lion-window (sīhapañjara), and having seen that wheel treasure (cakraratana), reflected on thoughts such as, "It has been heard by me..." and so on.

Therefore, it was said: "Having seen the king, a Kṣatriya…pe… would I be a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin)?"

There [it is said], "He becomes a wheel-turning monarch (rājā cakkavattī)"; by what extent does he become a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin)? Even [if] by the measure of one or two inches, the wheel treasure (cakkaratana) rises up into the sky and proceeds.

There [it is said], "He becomes a wheel-turning monarch (rājā cakkavattī)." Now, showing what should be done for causing that to proceed, [the text] says, "Then, monks (bhikkhave)," and so on.

There [it says], "Having risen from his seat (uṭṭhāyāsanā)"; having risen up from the seat on which he was sitting, having come near to the wheel treasure (cakkaratanasamīpaṃ āgantvā).

"[Having taken the water vessel (bhiṅkāraṃ gahetvā)]"; having lifted up the golden water vessel (suvaṇṇabhiṅkāraṃ), which had a spout resembling an elephant’s trunk (hatthisoṇḍasadisa-panāḷiṃ), having taken water with his left hand.

"May the wheel treasure (cakkaratanaṃ) proceed, may you conquer (abhivijinātu), venerable wheel treasure (cakkaratana)!".

"[Immediately after that, the wheel-turning monarch (rājā cakkavattī) with the four-part army (caturaṅginiyā senāyā)]"; indeed, having sprinkled water on all the wheel-turning monarchs (sabbacakkavattīnañhi) and immediately after the utterance of the words, "May you be victorious, venerable wheel treasure (cakkaratana)," the wheel treasure (cakkaratanaṃ), having risen up into the sky (vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā), proceeds (pavattati), at the same time as whose proceeding, that king is called a wheel-turning monarch (rājā cakkavattī).

Then, monks (bhikkhave), "[Having risen from his seat (uṭṭhāyāsanā)], [having taken the water vessel (bhiṅkāraṃ gahetvā)], [immediately after that, the wheel-turning monarch (rājā cakkavattī) with the four-part army (caturaṅginiyā senāyā)]," when the wheel treasure (cakkaratana) has proceeded, the wheel-turning monarch (rājā cakkavattī), following after it, mounts an excellent vehicle (yānavaraṃ āruyha) and rises up into the sky (vehāsaṃ abbhuggacchati), and then his retinue (parijano), holding the umbrella, chowrie, and other [items], and also the people of the inner palace (antepurajano ca).

Then, together with their respective forces, adorned with various kinds of armor, mail, and other [equipment], shining with the splendor of various ornaments, decorated with raised banners and flags, the viceroy (uparājasenāpati) and other [officials] also, having risen up into the sky (vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā), surround the king himself.

However, those entrusted by the king announce with drums in the city streets for the purpose of gathering the people, "Fathers (tātā), the wheel treasure (cakkaratanaṃ) of our king has arisen; gather together, adorned and prepared in accordance with your respective wealth!".

However, the great crowd (mahājano), by nature, having abandoned all their duties at just the sound of the wheel treasure (cakkaratana), having taken fragrant flowers and other [offerings], gather together; that entire crowd also, having risen up into the sky (vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā), surrounds the king himself.

Indeed, whomever the desire to go together with the king arises in, that one becomes a sky-goer.

Thus, the assembly is twelve yojanas in length and breadth.

There, even one person is not to be found with a body that is cut and broken, or with soiled clothes.

Indeed, the wheel-turning monarch (rājā cakkavattī) has a very pure retinue (suciparivāro).

The wheel-turning monarch (cakkavattī) assembly (parisā) is like a Vidyādhara assembly (vijjādharaparisā), wandering in the sky (ākāse gacchamānā), [and] on the surface of sapphire gems (indanīlamaṇitale) it is like scattered jewels (vippakiṇṇaratanasadisā).

Therefore, it was said, "Immediately after that, the wheel-turning monarch (rājā cakkavattī) with the four-part army (caturaṅginiyā senāyā)."
