That evil action, however, was not done by your mother, nor done by your father, nor done by your brother, nor done by your sister, nor done by your friends and companions, nor done by your relatives, nor done by ascetics or *brāhmaṇas*, <pb ed="v" n="3.
0221"/> nor done by the gods; this evil action was done by you alone, and you alone will experience its result.’”
commentary_pali: 265.Catutthaṃ devadūtanti ettha pana kammakāraṇā vā devadūtāti kātabbā kammakāraṇikā vā. Tattha pana kammakāraṇapakkhe bāttiṃsa tāva kammakāraṇā atthato evaṃ vadanti nāma – ‘‘mayaṃ nibbattamānā na rukkhe vā pāsāṇe vā nibbattāma, tumhādisānaṃ sarīre nibbattāma, iti amhākaṃ pure nibbattitova kalyāṇaṃ karothā’’ti. Tenete devadūtā nāma jātā. Kammakāraṇikāpi atthato evaṃ vadanti nāma – ‘‘mayaṃ dvattiṃsa kammakāraṇā karontā na rukkhādīsu karoma, tumhādisesu sattesuyeva karoma, iti amhākaṃ tumhesu pure kammakāraṇākaraṇatova kalyāṇaṃ karothā’’ti. Tenetepi devadūtā nāma jātā.
commentary_english:
265. "The fourth *devadūta*" Here, it is said that the *devadūta* is to be regarded as either a cause of karma (*kammakāraṇā*) or an agent of karma (*kammakāraṇikā*).

In that case, on the side of the cause of karma, the thirty-two causes of karma speak thus in meaning: "We, being reborn, are not reborn in trees or stones, but we are reborn in the bodies of those like you. Thus, do good for us, as we have been reborn previously."

By that, these are called *devadūtas*.

Even the agents of karma speak thus in meaning: "We, performing the thirty-two causes of karma, do not do [them] on trees, etc., but we do [them] on beings like you. Thus, do good for us, as we were previously the non-performance of the causes of karma in you."

By that, these are also called *devadūtas*.

mula_pali:
266. ‘‘Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, yamo rājā catutthaṃ devadūtaṃ samanuyuñjitvā samanugāhitvā samanubhāsitvā pañcamaṃ devadūtaṃ samanuyuñjati samanugāhati samanubhāsati – ‘ambho purisa, na tvaṃ addasa manussesu pañcamaṃ devadūtaṃ pātubhūta’nti? So evamāha – ‘nāddasaṃ, bhante’’’ti.

‘‘Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, yamo rājā evamāha – ‘ambho purisa, na tvaṃ addasa manussesu itthiṃ vā purisaṃ vā ekāhamataṃ vā dvīhamataṃ vā tīhamataṃ vā uddhumātakaṃ vinīlakaṃ vipubbakajāta’nti? So evamāha – ‘addasaṃ, bhante’’’ti.

‘‘Tamenaṃ , bhikkhave, yamo rājā evamāha – ‘ambho purisa, tassa te viññussa sato mahallakassa na etadahosi – ahampi khomhi maraṇadhammo, maraṇaṃ anatīto. Handāhaṃ kalyāṇaṃ karomi kāyena vācāya manasā’ti? So evamāha – ‘nāsakkhissaṃ, bhante, pamādassaṃ, bhante’’’ti.

‘‘Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, yamo rājā evamāha – ‘ambho purisa, pamādavatāya na kalyāṇamakāsi kāyena vācāya manasā. Taggha tvaṃ, ambho purisa, tathā karissanti yathā taṃ pamattaṃ. Taṃ kho pana te etaṃ pāpakammaṃ neva mātarā kataṃ na pitarā kataṃ na bhātarā kataṃ na bhaginiyā kataṃ na mittāmaccehi kataṃ na ñātisālohitehi kataṃ na samaṇabrāhmaṇehi kataṃ na devatāhi kataṃ, tayāvetaṃ pāpakammaṃ kataṃ, tvaññevetassa vipākaṃ paṭisaṃvedissasī’’’ti.
mula_english:
266.
“Then, monks, King Yama, after pressing and questioning and cross-questioning him about the fourth divine messenger, presses and questions and cross-questions him about the fifth divine messenger: ‘Good man, did you not see the fifth divine messenger appear in the world?’ He says: ‘No, venerable sir.’”

“Then, monks, King Yama says to him: ‘Good man, have you never seen in the world a woman or a man one day dead, two days dead, three days dead, bloated, livid, and festering?’ He says: ‘Yes, venerable sir.’”

“Then, monks, King Yama says to him: ‘Good man, did it never occur to you—an intelligent and mature person—"I too am subject to death, I am not exempt from death. Let me now do good deeds through body, speech, and mind (kāyena vācāya manasā)"?’ He says: ‘I was not able, venerable sir, I was negligent, venerable sir.’”

“Then, monks, King Yama says to him: ‘Good man, through negligence you did not do good deeds through body, speech, and mind (kāyena vācāya manasā). Indeed, good man, they will do to you as befits your negligence. That evil deed was not done by your mother, nor by your father, nor by your brother, nor by your sister, nor by your friends and companions, nor by your relatives and kinsmen, nor by ascetics and Brahmins, nor by the gods; that evil deed was done by you alone, and you alone will experience its result.’”
commentary_pali:
266.Pañcamaṃ devadūtanti ettha matakasatto atthato evaṃ vadati nāma – ‘‘passatha bho maṃ āmakasusāne chaḍḍitaṃ uddhumātakādibhāvaṃ pattaṃ, maraṇatomhi aparimuttatāya ediso jāto. Na kho panāhameva, tumhepi maraṇato aparimuttāva. Yatheva hi mayhaṃ, evaṃ tumhākampi maraṇaṃ āgamissati, iti tassa pure āgamanāva kalyāṇaṃ karothā’’ti. Tenesa devadūto nāma jāto.

Imaṃ pana devadūtānuyogaṃ ko labhati, ko na labhatīti? Yena tāva bahuṃ pāpaṃ kataṃ, so gantvā niraye nibbattatiyeva. Yena pana parittaṃ pāpakammaṃ kataṃ, so labhati. Yathā hi sabhaṇḍaṃ coraṃ gahetvā kattabbameva karonti, na vinicchinanti. Anuvijjitvā gahitaṃ pana vinicchayaṭṭhānaṃ nayanti, so vinicchayaṃ labhati. Evaṃsampadametaṃ. Parittapāpakammā hi attano dhammatāyapi saranti, sāriyamānāpi saranti.

Tattha dīghajayantadamiḷo nāma attano dhammatāya sari. So kira damiḷo sumanagirivihāre ākāsacetiyaṃ rattapaṭena pūjesi. Atha niraye ussadasāmante nibbatto aggijālasaddaṃ sutvāva attano pūjitapaṭaṃ anussari, so gantvā sagge nibbatto. Aparopi puttassa daharabhikkhuno khalisāṭakaṃ dento pādamūle ṭhapesi, maraṇakālamhi paṭapaṭāti sadde nimittaṃ gaṇhi, sopi ussadasāmante nibbatto jālasaddena taṃ sāṭakaṃ anussaritvā sagge nibbatto. Evaṃ tāva attano dhammatāya kusalaṃ kammaṃ saritvā sagge nibbattatīti.

Attano dhammatāya asarante pana pañca devadūte pucchati. Tattha koci paṭhamena devadūtena sarati, koci dutiyādīhi. Yo pana pañcahipi na sarati, taṃ yamo rājā sayaṃ sāreti. Eko kira amacco sumanapupphakumbhena mahācetiyaṃ pūjetvā yamassa pattiṃ adāsi, taṃ akusalakammena niraye nibbattaṃ yamassa santikaṃ nayiṃsu. Tasmiṃ pañcahipi devadūtehi kusale asarante yamo sayaṃ olokento disvā – ‘‘nanu tvaṃ mahācetiyaṃ sumanapupphakumbhena pūjetvā mayhaṃ pattiṃ adāsī’’ti sāresi, so tasmiṃ kāle saritvā devalokaṃ gato. Yamo pana sayaṃ oloketvāpi apassanto – ‘‘mahādukkhaṃ nāma anubhavissati ayaṃ satto’’ti tuṇhī hoti.
commentary_english:
266. "The fifth divine messenger" (pañcamaṃ devadūta) - here, a deceased being speaks thus, in meaning, by name: “Behold (passatha), good sirs (bho), I (maṃ) was cast (chaḍḍitaṃ) into a charnel ground (āmakasusāne), having attained (pattaṃ) the state (bhāvaṃ) of being bloated (uddhumātaka), and being not freed (aparimuttatāya) from death (maraṇato), I have become (jāto) like this (ediso).

It is not only I (na kho panāhameva), but you also (tumhepi) are not freed (aparimuttāva) from death (maraṇato). Just as (yatheva) death (maraṇaṃ) will come (āgamissati) to me (mayhaṃ), so too (evaṃ) it will come (āgamissati) to you (tumhākampi); therefore (iti), before (pure) its arrival (āgamanāva), do (karotha) what is good (kalyāṇaṃ).” Thus (tena), he is known (nāma) as a divine messenger (devadūto jāto).

But who (ko) obtains (labhati) this (imaṃ) divine messenger's (devadūta) instruction (anuyogaṃ), and who (ko) does not (na labhatīti)? Whoever (yena) has done (kataṃ) much (bahuṃ) evil (pāpaṃ), he (so) goes (gantvā) and is reborn (nibbattatiyeva) in hell (niraye). But whoever (yena pana) has done (kataṃ) a little (parittaṃ) evil action (pāpakammaṃ), he (so) obtains (labhati) it. Just as (yathā hi) having seized (gahetvā) a thief (coraṃ) with all the stolen goods (sabhaṇḍaṃ), they do (karonti) only what needs to be done (kattabbameva), and they do not investigate (na vinicchinanti). But (pana) having thoroughly investigated (anuvijjitvā) and seized (gahitaṃ), they take (nayanti) him to the place of judgement (vinicchayaṭṭhānaṃ), and he (so) obtains (labhati) judgement (vinicchayaṃ). Thus (evaṃ) is this (etaṃ) accomplishment (sampadaṃ). For those with little (parittapāpakammā) evil karma (dhammatāyapi), even they (hi) remember (saranti) their own (attano) nature (dhammatāyapi), and being reminded (sāriyamānāpi), they remember (saranti).

There (tattha), a certain (nāma) Dīghajayantadamiḷa remembered (sari) his own (attano) nature (dhammatāya). It seems (kira) that Damiḷa (so damiḷo) worshipped (pūjesi) the ākāśa-cetiya (ākaśacetiyaṃ) at Sumanagirivihāra with a red cloth (rattapaṭena). Then (atha), having been reborn (nibbatto) in hell (niraye), at the edge of a charnel ground (ussadasāmante), having heard (sutvāva) the sound (saddaṃ) of blazing fire (aggijāla), he remembered (anussari) his own (attano) worshipped cloth (pūjitapaṭaṃ), and he (so) went (gantvā) and was reborn (nibbatto) in heaven (sagge). Also (aparopi), someone (dento) giving (dento) a coarse cloth (khalisāṭakaṃ) to his son (puttassa), a young monk (daharabhikkhuno), placed (ṭhapesi) it at the base of a tree (pādamūle), at the time of death (maraṇakālamhi), he took (gaṇhi) the sound (sadde) paṭapaṭāti as a sign (nimittaṃ), and he also (sopi), having been reborn (nibbatto) at the edge of a charnel ground (ussadasāmante), having remembered (anussaritvā) that (taṃ) cloth (sāṭakaṃ) by the sound (jālasaddena), was reborn (nibbatto) in heaven (sagge). Thus (evaṃ tāva), by one's own (attano) nature (dhammatāya), remembering (saritvā) good karma (kusalaṃ kammaṃ), one is reborn (nibbattatīti) in heaven (sagge).

But (pana), if those who do not remember (asarante) their own (attano) nature (dhammatāya), he asks (pucchati) the five (pañca) divine messengers (devadūte). There (tattha), some (koci) remember (sarati) the first (paṭhamena) divine messenger (devadūtena), and some (koci) the second (dutiyādīhi) and so on. But (yo pana) if someone (pañcahipi) does not (na sarati), Yama (yamo), the king (rājā), himself (sayaṃ) reminds (sāreti) him (taṃ). It seems (eko kira) that a minister (amacco), having worshipped (pūjetvā) the great cetiya (mahācetiyaṃ) with a vase of sumana flowers (sumanapupphakumbhena), gave (adāsi) a share (pattiṃ) to Yama (yamassa), and due to his bad karma (akusalakammena), they led (nayiṃsu) him (taṃ), reborn (nibbattaṃ) in hell (niraye), into the presence (santikaṃ) of Yama (yamassa). In that (tasmiṃ), if, among the five (pañcahipi) divine messengers (devadūtehi), they do not remember (asarante) good (kusale), Yama (yamo) himself (sayaṃ), looking around (olokento), having seen (disvā), reminds (sāresi): "Surely (nanu), you (tvaṃ) worshipped (pūjetvā) the great cetiya (mahācetiyaṃ) with a vase of sumana flowers (sumanapupphakumbhena) and gave (adāsi) a share (pattiṃ) to me (mayhaṃ)?" So (so), at that (tasmiṃ) time (kāle), having remembered (saritvā), he went (gato) to the world of the gods (devalokaṃ). But (pana) Yama (yamo) himself (sayaṃ), even looking around (oloketvāpi), if he does not see (apassanto), he becomes (hoti) silent (tuṇhī), saying: "This (ayaṃ) being (satto) will experience (anubhavissati) great suffering (mahādukkhaṃ nāma)."

mula_pali:
267. ‘‘Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, yamo rājā pañcamaṃ devadūtaṃ samanuyuñjitvā samanugāhitvā samanubhāsitvā tuṇhī hoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā pañcavidhabandhanaṃ nāma kammakāraṇaṃ karonti – tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ hatthe gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ dutiye hatthe gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ pāde gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ dutiye pāde gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhilaṃ majjheurasmiṃ gamenti. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṃ karoti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā saṃvesetvā kuṭhārīhi tacchanti…pe… tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā uddhaṃpādaṃ adhosiraṃ gahetvā vāsīhi tacchanti…pe… tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā rathe yojetvā ādittāya pathaviyā sampajjalitāya sajotibhūtāya sārentipi, paccāsārentipi…pe… tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā mahantaṃ aṅgārapabbataṃ ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ āropentipi oropentipi…pe… tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā uddhaṃpādaṃ adhosiraṃ gahetvā tattāya lohakumbhiyā pakkhipanti ādittāya sampajjalitāya sajotibhūtāya. So tattha pheṇuddehakaṃ paccati. So tattha pheṇuddehakaṃ paccamāno sakimpi uddhaṃ gacchati, sakimpi adho gacchati, sakimpi tiriyaṃ gacchati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā mahāniraye pakkhipanti. So kho pana, bhikkhave, mahānirayo –

‘‘Catukkaṇṇo catudvāro, vibhatto bhāgaso mito;

Ayopākārapariyanto, ayasā paṭikujjito.

‘‘Tassa ayomayā bhūmi, jalitā tejasāyutā;

Samantā yojanasataṃ, pharitvā tiṭṭhati sabbadā’’ .
mula_english:
267. “Then, after pressing and questioning and cross-questioning him about the fifth divine messenger, King Yama is silent.

Then, *bhikkhus*, the wardens of hell inflict a fivefold punishment, namely, they drive a hot iron stake into his hand, they drive a hot iron stake into his other hand, they drive a hot iron stake into his foot, they drive a hot iron stake into his other foot, they drive a hot iron stake into the middle of his chest.

There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

Then, *bhikkhus*, the wardens of hell throw him down and pare him with axes…pe… Then, *bhikkhus*, the wardens of hell set him with his feet up and his head down and pare him with adzes…pe… Then, *bhikkhus*, the wardens of hell harness him to a chariot and drive him back and forth across ground that is burning, blazing, and glowing…pe… Next the wardens of hell make him climb up and down a great mound of coals that are burning, blazing,and glowing…pe… Next the wardens of hell turn him upside down and plunge him into a red-hot copper cauldron that is burning, blazing, and glowing.

He is cooked there in a swirl of froth.

And as he is being cooked there in a swirl of froth, he is swept now up, now down, and now across.

There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

“Next the wardens of hell throw him into the Great Hell (*mahāniraya*).

Now, *bhikkhus*, the Great Hell (*mahāniraya*)—

"It has four corners and four gates,
It is divided and properly measured.

It is surrounded by an iron wall,
With an iron roof above.

Its ground is made of iron,
And is always ablaze with heat.

On every side for a hundred *yojanas*,
It stands always enveloping all."
commentary_pali: 267.Mahānirayeti avīcimahānirayamhi. Kiṃ panassa pamāṇaṃ? Abbhantaraṃ āyāmena ca vitthārena ca yojanasataṃ hoti. Lohapathavī lohachadanaṃ ekekā ca bhitti navanavayojanikā hoti. Puratthimāya bhittiyā acci uṭṭhitā pacchimaṃ bhittiṃ gahetvā taṃ vinivijjhitvā parato yojanasataṃ gacchati. Sesadisāsupi eseva nayo. Iti jālapariyantavasena āyāmavitthārato aṭṭhārasayojanādhikāni tīṇi yojanasatāni, parikkhepato pana navayojanasatāni catupaṇṇāsayojanāni, samantā pana ussadehi saddhiṃ dasayojanasahassaṃ hoti.
commentary_english: 267. "Mahāniraye": in the Avīci great hell. What is its extent? Internally, it is one hundred *yojana*s in length and breadth. The iron ground, the iron covering, and each wall is nine by nine *yojana*s. From the eastern wall, a flame arises, seizes the western wall, pierces it, and goes beyond for one hundred *yojana*s. The same rule applies in the remaining directions. Thus, by way of the circumference of the net, from its length and breadth, it is three hundred *yojana*s with eighteen *yojana*s additional; but in circumference, it is nine hundred *yojana*s [with] fifty-four *yojana*s; but all around, together with the projections, it is ten thousand *yojana*s.

mula_pali:
268. ‘‘Tassa kho pana, bhikkhave, mahānirayassa puratthimāya bhittiyā acci uṭṭhahitvā pacchimāya bhittiyā paṭihaññati, pacchimāya bhittiyā acci uṭṭhahitvā puratthimāya bhittiyā paṭihaññati, uttarāya bhittiyā acci uṭṭhahitvā dakkhiṇāya bhittiyā paṭihaññati, dakkhiṇāya bhittiyā acci uṭṭhahitvā uttarāya bhittiyā paṭihaññati, heṭṭhā acci uṭṭhahitvā upari paṭihaññati, uparito acci uṭṭhahitvā heṭṭhā paṭihaññati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

‘‘Hoti kho so, bhikkhave, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena tassa mahānirayassa puratthimaṃ dvāraṃ apāpurīyati avāpurīyati (sī.). So tattha sīghena javena dhāvati. Tassa sīghena javena dhāvato chavimpi ḍayhati, cammampi ḍayhati, maṃsampi ḍayhati, nhārumpi ḍayhati, aṭṭhīnipi sampadhūpāyanti, ubbhataṃ tādisameva hoti. Yato ca kho so, bhikkhave, bahusampatto hoti, atha taṃ dvāraṃ pidhīyati pithīyati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

avāpurīyati (sī.) pithīyati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘Hoti kho so, bhikkhave, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena tassa mahānirayassa pacchimaṃ dvāraṃ apāpurīyati…pe… uttaraṃ dvāraṃ apāpurīyati…pe… dakkhiṇaṃ dvāraṃ apāpurīyati . So tattha sīghena javena dhāvati. Tassa sīghena javena dhāvato chavimpi ḍayhati, cammampi ḍayhati, maṃsampi ḍayhati, nhārumpi ḍayhati, aṭṭhīnipi sampadhūpāyanti, ubbhataṃ tādisameva hoti. Yato ca kho so, bhikkhave, bahusampatto hoti, atha taṃ dvāraṃ pidhīyati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

‘‘Hoti kho so, bhikkhave, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena tassa mahānirayassa puratthimaṃ dvāraṃ apāpurīyati. So tattha sīghena javena dhāvati. Tassa sīghena javena dhāvato chavimpi ḍayhati, cammampi ḍayhati, maṃsampi ḍayhati, nhārumpi ḍayhati, aṭṭhīnipi sampadhūpāyanti, ubbhataṃ tādisameva hoti. So tena dvārena nikkhamati.
mula_english:
“Now, monks, the flames that rise from the eastern wall of the Great Hell (mahāniraya) strike the western wall, the flames that rise from the western wall strike the eastern wall, the flames that rise from the northern wall strike the southern wall, the flames that rise from the southern wall strike the northern wall, the flames that rise from below strike above, and the flames that rise from above strike below. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings, yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

“Some time or other, monks, at the end of a long period, there comes an occasion when the Great Hell's eastern door is opened. He runs towards it with speed and swiftness. As he runs swiftly, his outer skin burns, his inner skin burns, his flesh burns, his sinews burn, and his bones turn to smoke; and it is the same when his foot is uplifted. When at long last he reaches the door, then it is shut. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings, yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

“Some time or other, monks, at the end of a long period, there comes an occasion when the Great Hell’s western door is opened…and so on…when its northern door is opened…and so on…when its southern door is opened. He runs towards it with speed and swiftness. As he runs swiftly, his outer skin burns, his inner skin burns, his flesh burns, his sinews burn, and his bones turn to smoke; and it is the same when his foot is uplifted. When at long last he reaches the door, then it is shut. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings, yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

“Some time or other, monks, at the end of a long period, there comes an occasion when the Great Hell's eastern door is opened. He runs towards it with speed and swiftness. As he runs swiftly, his outer skin burns, his inner skin burns, his flesh burns, his sinews burn, and his bones turn to smoke; and it is the same when his foot is uplifted. He exits through that door.
commentary_pali:
268.Ubbhataṃ tādisameva hotīti ettha akkantapadaṃ yāva aṭṭhito daḷhaṃ uddharitumeva na sakkā. Ayaṃ panettha attho – heṭṭhato paṭṭhāya ḍayhati, uparito paṭṭhāya jhāyati, iti akkamanakāle ḍayhamānaṃ paññāyati, uddharaṇakāle tādisameva, tasmā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Bahusampattoti bahūni vassasatavassasahassāni sampatto.

Kasmā panesa narako avīcīti saṅkhaṃ gatoti. Vīci nāma antaraṃ vuccati, tattha ca aggijālānaṃ vā sattānaṃ vā dukkhassa vā antaraṃ natthi. Tasmā so avīcīti saṅkhaṃ gatoti. Tassa hi puratthimabhittito jālā uṭṭhitā saṃsibbamānā yojanasataṃ gantvā pacchimabhittiṃ vinivijjhitvā parato yojanasataṃ gacchati. Sesadisāsupi eseva nayo.

Imesaṃ channaṃ jālānaṃ majjhe nibbatto devadatto, tassa yojanasatappamāṇo attabhāvo, dve pādā yāva gopphakā lohapathaviṃ paviṭṭhā, dve hatthā yāva maṇibandhā lohabhittiyo paviṭṭhā, sīsaṃ yāva bhamukaṭṭhito lohachadane paviṭṭhaṃ, adhobhāgena ekaṃ lohasūlaṃ pavisitvā kāyaṃ vinivijjhantaṃ chadane paviṭṭhaṃ, pācīnabhittito nikkhantasūlaṃ hadayaṃ vinivijjhitvā pacchimabhittiṃ paviṭṭhaṃ , uttarabhittito nikkhantasūlaṃ phāsukā vinivijjhitvā dakkhiṇabhittiṃ paviṭṭhaṃ. Niccale tathāgatamhi aparaddhattā niccalova hutvā paccatīti kammasarikkhatāya ediso jāto. Evaṃ jālānaṃ nirantaratāya avīci nāma.

Abbhantare panassa yojanasatike ṭhāne nāḷiyaṃ koṭṭetvā pūritapiṭṭhaṃ viya sattā nirantarā, ‘‘imasmiṃ ṭhāne satto atthi, imasmiṃ natthī’’ti na vattabbaṃ, gacchantānaṃ ṭhitānaṃ nisinnānaṃ nipannānaṃ anto natthi, gacchante vā ṭhite vā nisinne vā nipanne vā aññamaññaṃ na bādhanti. Evaṃ sattānaṃ nirantaratāya avīci.

Kāyadvāre pana cha upekkhāsahagatāni cittāni uppajjanti, ekaṃ dukkhasahagataṃ. Evaṃ santepi yathā jivhagge cha madhubindūni ṭhapetvā ekasmiṃ tambalohabindumhi ṭhapite anudahanabalavatāya tadeva paññāyati, itarāni abbohārikāni honti, evaṃ anudahanabalavatāya dukkhamevettha nirantaraṃ, itarāni abbohārikānīti. Evaṃ dukkhassa nirantaratāya avīci.
commentary_english:
268. “*ubbhataṃ tādisameva hotī*”ti: Here, it is not possible to remove the deeply embedded *akkantapadaṃ* unless it is firmly established.

Here, the meaning is this: it burns from below (*heṭṭhato paṭṭhāya ḍayhati*), it scorches from above (*uparito paṭṭhāya jhāyati*). Thus, during the process of burning, it is known as *akkamanakāle ḍayhamānaṃ*; during the process of removal, it is just the same (*tādisameva*). Therefore, it is said thus (*evaṃ vuttaṃ*).

“*bahusampatto*”ti: Having attained many hundreds of thousands of years (*bahūni vassasatavassasahassāni sampatto*).

Why is this hell called Avīci (Avici hell)?

The name *vīci* means interval (*antaraṃ*), and there is no interval there, whether of fire flames (*aggijālānaṃ*), or of beings (*sattānaṃ*), or of suffering (*dukkha*).

Therefore, it is called Avīci (Avici hell).

Indeed, flames arise from its eastern wall (*puratthimabhittito jālā uṭṭhitā*), continuously spreading (*saṃsibbamānā*) and, after going a hundred yojanas (*yojanasataṃ gantvā*), piercing the western wall (*pacchimabhittiṃ vinivijjhitvā*), they go a hundred yojanas beyond (*parato yojanasataṃ gacchati*).

The same method (*nayo*) applies to the other directions as well (*sesadisāsupi eseva nayo*).

In the middle of these six flame-masses (*imesaṃ channaṃ jālānaṃ majjhe*) Devadatta is reborn (*nibbatto devadatto*), and his individual existence measures a hundred yojanas (*tassa yojanasatappamāṇo attabhāvo*). His two feet, up to the ankles (*dve pādā yāva gopphakā*), are immersed in the iron ground (*lohapathaviṃ paviṭṭhā*), his two hands, up to the wrists (*dve hatthā yāva maṇibandhā*), are immersed in the iron walls (*lohabhittiyo paviṭṭhā*), his head, up to the eyebrows (*sīsaṃ yāva bhamukaṭṭhito*), is immersed in the iron roof (*lohachadane paviṭṭhaṃ*), and an iron stake going downwards (*adhobhāgena ekaṃ lohasūlaṃ*) having entered, pierces through his body (*kāyaṃ vinivijjhantaṃ*), is immersed in the roof (*chadane paviṭṭhaṃ*). A stake emerging from the eastern wall (*pācīnabhittito nikkhantasūlaṃ*) pierces through his heart (*hadayaṃ vinivijjhitvā*) and is immersed in the western wall (*pacchimabhittiṃ paviṭṭhaṃ*), a stake emerging from the northern wall (*uttarabhittito nikkhantasūlaṃ*) pierces through his ribs (*phāsukā vinivijjhitvā*) and is immersed in the southern wall (*dakkhiṇabhittiṃ paviṭṭhaṃ*).

Because of offending the unmoving Tathāgata (*niccale tathāgatamhi aparaddhattā*), having become unmoving, he suffers (*niccalova hutvā paccatīti*). Due to the similarity of the karma (*kammasarikkhatāya*), he is born thus (*ediso jāto*).

Thus, because of the continuous nature of the flames (*evaṃ jālānaṃ nirantaratāya*), it is called Avīci (Avici hell).

Within, in that place measuring a hundred yojanas (*abbhantare panassa yojanasatike ṭhāne*), beings are continuous, like being pressed in a bamboo tube filled with flour (*nāḷiyaṃ koṭṭetvā pūritapiṭṭhaṃ viya sattā nirantarā*). It should not be said, "In this place there is a being (*imasmiṃ ṭhāne satto atthi*), in this place there is not (*imasmiṃ natthī*)." There is no end to those going, standing, sitting, or lying down (*gacchantānaṃ ṭhitānaṃ nisinnānaṃ nipannānaṃ anto natthi*); whether going, standing, sitting, or lying down (*gacchante vā ṭhite vā nisinne vā nipanne vā*), they do not obstruct each other (*aññamaññaṃ na bādhanti*).

Thus, because of the continuous nature of the beings (*evaṃ sattānaṃ nirantaratāya*), it is Avīci (Avici hell).

At the body door (*kāyadvāre*) six minds accompanied by equanimity arise (*cha upekkhāsahagatāni cittāni uppajjanti*), and one accompanied by suffering (*ekaṃ dukkhasahagataṃ*).

Even so, just as, having placed six drops of honey on the tip of the tongue (*yathā jivhagge cha madhubindūni ṭhapetvā*), if an iron drop is placed on one of them (*ekasmiṃ tambalohabindumhi ṭhapite*), due to the power of intense burning (*anudahanabalavatāya*), only that one is known (*tadeva paññāyati*), the others are nominal (*itarāni abbohārikāni honti*), so too, due to the power of intense burning (*evaṃ anudahanabalavatāya*), only suffering is continuous there (*dukkham evettha nirantaraṃ*), the others are nominal (*itarāni abbohārikānīti*).

Thus, because of the continuous nature of suffering (*evaṃ dukkhassa nirantaratāya*), it is Avīci (Avici hell).

mula_pali:
269. ‘‘Tassa kho pana, bhikkhave, mahānirayassa samanantarā sahitameva mahanto gūthanirayo. So tattha patati. Tasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, gūthaniraye sūcimukhā pāṇā chaviṃ chindanti, chaviṃ chetvā cammaṃ chindanti, cammaṃ chetvā maṃsaṃ chindanti, maṃsaṃ chetvā nhāruṃ chindanti, nhāruṃ chetvā aṭṭhiṃ chindanti, aṭṭhiṃ chetvā aṭṭhimiñjaṃ khādanti. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

‘‘Tassa kho pana, bhikkhave, gūthanirayassa samanantarā sahitameva mahanto kukkulanirayo. So tattha patati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

‘‘Tassa kho pana, bhikkhave, kukkulanirayassa samanantarā sahitameva mahantaṃ simbalivanaṃ uddhaṃ uccaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), ubbhato (ka.) yojanamuggataṃ soḷasaṅgulakaṇṭakaṃ soḷasaṅgulakaṇḍakaṃ (sī.) ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ. Tattha āropentipi oropentipi. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

uccaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), ubbhato (ka.) soḷasaṅgulakaṇḍakaṃ (sī.)

‘‘Tassa kho pana, bhikkhave, simbalivanassa samanantarā sahitameva mahantaṃ asipattavanaṃ. So tattha pavisati. Tassa vāteritāni pattāni patitāni hatthampi chindanti, pādampi chindanti, hatthapādampi chindanti, kaṇṇampi chindanti, nāsampi chindanti, kaṇṇanāsampi chindanti. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

‘‘Tassa kho pana, bhikkhave, asipattavanassa samanantarā sahitameva mahatī khārodakā nadī khārodikā nadī (sī.). So tattha patati. So tattha anusotampi vuyhati , paṭisotampi vuyhati, anusotapaṭisotampi vuyhati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

khārodikā nadī (sī.)
mula_english:
269.
“Immediately next to the Great Hell, is the vast Hell of Excrement (gūthanirayo). He falls into that. In that Hell of Excrement, needle-mouthed creatures bore through his outer skin and bore through his inner skin and bore through his flesh and bore through his sinews and bore through his bones and devour his marrow. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that bad karma is not exhausted.

“Immediately next to the Hell of Excrement, is the vast Hell of Embers (kukkulanirayo). He falls into that. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that bad karma is not exhausted.

“Immediately next to the Hell of Embers, is a vast Wood of Silk-cotton Trees (śimbalivana) that rises high – a league high – with sixteen-finger-length thorns, burning, flaming and blazing. They make him climb up and down those trees. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that bad karma is not exhausted.

“Immediately next to the Wood of Silk-cotton Trees is a vast Wood of Sword-leaf Trees (asipattavanaṃ). He goes into that. The leaves, stirred by the wind, cut off his hands and cut off his feet and cut off his hands and feet; they cut off his ears and cut off his nose and cut off his ears and nose. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that bad karma is not exhausted.

“Immediately next to the Wood of Sword-leaf Trees is a great river of caustic water (khārodakā nadī). He falls into that. There he is swept upstream and he is swept downstream and he is swept upstream and downstream. There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings. Yet he does not die so long as that bad karma is not exhausted.
commentary_pali:
269.Mahantoti yojanasatiko. So tattha patatīti eko pādo mahāniraye hoti, eko gūthaniraye nipatati. Sūcimukhāti sūcisadisamukhā, te hatthigīvappamāṇā ekadoṇikanāvāppamāṇā vā honti.

Kukkulanirayoti yojanasatappamāṇova anto kūṭāgāramattavitaccitaaṅgārapuṇṇo ādittachārikanirayo, yattha patitapatitā kudrūsakarāsimhi khittaphālavāsisilādīni viya heṭṭhimatalameva gaṇhanti.

Kukkulanirayo

Āropentīti ayadaṇḍehi pothentā āropenti. Tesaṃ ārohanakāle te kaṇṭakā adhomukhā honti, orohanakāle uddhaṃmukhā.

Āropentī

Vāteritānīti kammamayena vātena calitāni. Hatthampi chindantīti phalake maṃsaṃ viya koṭṭayamānāni chindanti. Sace uṭṭhāya palāyati, ayopākāro samuṭṭhahitvā parikkhipati, heṭṭhā khuradhārā samuṭṭhāti.

Vāteritānī Hatthampi chindantī

Khārodakā nadīti vetaraṇī nāma tambalohanadī. Tattha ayomayāni kharavālika-pokkharapattāni, heṭṭhā khuradhārā ubhosu tīresu vettalatā ca kusatiṇāni ca. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharāti so tattha uddhañca adho ca vuyhamāno pokkharapattesu chijjati. Siṅghāṭakasaṇṭhānāya kharavālikāya kaṇṭakehi vijjhiyati, khuradhārāhi phāliyati, ubhosu tīresu kusatiṇehi vilekhati, vettalatāhi ākaḍḍhiyati, tikkhasattīhi phāliyati.

Khārodakā nadī So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā
commentary_english:
269.
“Great” means one hundred *yojana*s.
“He falls there” means one foot is in the great hell (mahāniraya), one falls into the excrement hell.
“Needle-mouthed” means having faces like needles; they are the size of an elephant’s neck, or the size of a small boat.

“Coal-pit hell” means the interior is full of embers, the size of one hundred *yojana*s, like a hut; it is a hell of burning ashes, where those who have fallen fall, like *kudrūsaka* heaps, they grasp only the lower level with thrown winnowing fans, stones, and so on.

Coal-pit hell.
“They hoist up” means they hoist them up, striking them with iron clubs.
For them, at the time of ascending, those thorns are face-down; at the time of descending, they are face-up.

They hoist up.
“Wind-driven” means they are moved by wind made of karma (karma).
“Even cutting off hands” means they cut, pounding them like meat on a chopping board.
If one rises and flees, an iron wall rises up and surrounds him; below, a razor-sharp edge rises up.

Wind-driven.
Even cutting off hands.
“Salt-water river” means the river named Vaitaraṇī, a river of red iron.
There, there are iron, sharp-sanded lotus leaves; below, there is a razor-sharp edge; on both shores there are rattan vines and *kuśa* grass.
“He is there with intense, sharp suffering” means being carried upward and downward there, he is cut in the lotus leaves.
He is pierced by thorns in the shape of a crossroads with sharp sands, he is split by razor edges, he scratches himself with *kuśa* grass on both shores, he is pulled by rattan vines, he is split by sharp spears.

Salt-water river.
He is there with intense, sharp suffering.

mula_pali:
270. ‘‘Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā balisena uddharitvā thale patiṭṭhāpetvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ambho purisa, kiṃ icchasī’ti? So evamāha – ‘jighacchitosmi, bhante’ti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā tattena ayosaṅkunā mukhaṃ vivaritvā ādittena sampajjalitena sajotibhūtena tattaṃ lohaguḷaṃ mukhe pakkhipanti ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ. So tassa taṃ tassa (ka.), tassa (sī. pī.) oṭṭhampi dahati ḍayhati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), mukhampi dahati, kaṇṭhampi dahati, urampi udarampi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) dahati, antampi antaguṇampi ādāya adhobhāgā nikkhamati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti.

‘‘Tamenaṃ , bhikkhave, nirayapālā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ambho purisa, kiṃ icchasī’ti? So evamāha – ‘pipāsitosmi, bhante’ti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā tattena ayosaṅkunā mukhaṃ vivaritvā ādittena sampajjalitena sajotibhūtena tattaṃ tambalohaṃ mukhe āsiñcanti ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ. Taṃ tassa ettha pana pāṭhabhedo natthi oṭṭhampi dahati, mukhampi dahati, kaṇṭhampi dahati, urampi dahati, antampi antaguṇampi ādāya adhobhāgā nikkhamati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti, na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti, yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā puna mahāniraye pakkhipanti.

ettha pana pāṭhabhedo natthi

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, yamassa rañño etadahosi – ‘ye kira , bho, loke pāpakāni akusalāni kammāni karonti te evarūpā vividhā kammakāraṇā karīyanti. Aho vatāhaṃ manussattaṃ labheyyaṃ. Tathāgato ca loke uppajjeyya arahaṃ sammāsambuddho. Tañcāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāseyyaṃ. So ca me bhagavā dhammaṃ deseyya. Tassa cāhaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ ājāneyya’nti. Taṃ kho panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nāññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā sutvā vadāmi, api ca yadeva sāmaṃ ñātaṃ sāmaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sāmaṃ viditaṃ tadevāhaṃ vadāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
270. Monks, then the wardens of hell, having lifted him up with a hook and placed him on the ground, ask him, ‘Good man, what do you desire?’ He replies, ‘I am hungry, venerable sirs.’

Then the wardens of hell prise open his mouth with red-hot iron tongs, burning, blazing, and glowing, and they throw into his mouth a red-hot metal ball, burning, blazing, and glowing.

It burns his lips, it burns his mouth, it burns his throat, it burns his chest, and it passes out below carrying with it his large and small intestines.

There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings, yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

Monks, then the wardens of hell ask him, ‘Good man, what do you desire?’ He replies, ‘I am thirsty, venerable sirs.’

Then the wardens of hell prise open his mouth with red-hot iron tongs, burning, blazing, and glowing, and they pour into his mouth molten copper, burning, blazing, and glowing.

It burns his lips, it burns his mouth, it burns his throat, it burns his chest, and it passes out below carrying with it his large and small intestines.

There he feels painful, racking, piercing feelings, yet he does not die so long as that evil action has not exhausted its result.

Then the wardens of hell throw him back again into the Great Hell.

Once, monks, King Yama thought: ‘Those in the world who do evil unwholesome actions indeed have all these many kinds of tortures inflicted on them.

Oh, that I might attain the human state! That a *Tathāgata*, *Arhat*, Perfectly Enlightened One might arise in the world! That I might attend upon that Blessed One! That the Blessed One might teach me the *Dharma*! And that I might come to understand that Blessed One’s *Dharma*!’

Bhikkhus, I tell you this not as something I heard from another recluse or *brahmin*. I tell you this as something that I have actually known, seen, and discovered by myself.
commentary_pali:
270.Tattenaayosaṅkunāti tena jigacchitomhīti vutte mahantaṃ lohapacchiṃ lohaguḷānaṃ pūretvā taṃ upagacchanti, so lohaguḷabhāvaṃ ñatvā dante samphuseti, athassa te tattena ayosaṅkunā mukhaṃ vivaranti, tambalohadhārehi mahantena lohakaṭāhena tambalohaṃ upanetvā evamevaṃ karonti. Puna mahānirayeti evaṃ pañcavidhabandhanato paṭṭhāya yāva tambalohapānā tambalohapānato paṭṭhāya puna pañcavidhabandhanādīni kāretvā mahāniraye pakkhipanti. Tattha koci pañcavidhabandhaneneva muccati, koci dutiyena, koci tatiyena, koci tambalohapānena muccati, kamme pana aparikkhīṇe puna mahāniraye pakkhipanti.

Idaṃ pana suttaṃ gaṇhanto eko daharabhikkhu, – ‘‘bhante, ettakaṃ dukkhamanubhavitasattaṃ punapi mahāniraye pakkhipantī’’ti āha. Āma, āvuso, kamme aparikkhīṇe punappunaṃ evaṃ karontīti. Tiṭṭhatu, bhante, uddeso, kammaṭṭhānameva kathethāti kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathāpetvā sotāpanno hutvā āgamma uddesaṃ aggahesi. Aññesampi imasmiṃ padese uddesaṃ ṭhapetvā arahattaṃ pattānaṃ gaṇanā natthi. Sabbabuddhānañcetaṃ suttaṃ avijahitameva hoti.
commentary_english:
270. "With heated iron stakes (tatta-ayena-śaṅkunā)," thus, because he was hungry. When this was said, they fill a large iron cauldron (mahantaṃ lohapacchiṃ) with iron balls (lohaguḷānaṃ pūretvā) and approach him. He, knowing the nature of the iron balls, touches his teeth. Then, with a heated iron stake (tattena ayosaṅkunā), they open his mouth, and bringing molten copper (tambalohaṃ) in a large iron cauldron (mahantena lohakaṭāhena tambalohaṃ upanetvā), they do exactly this (evamevaṃ karonti).

Again, in the great hell (mahāniraye), thus, starting from the fivefold binding (pañcavidhabandhanato paṭṭhāya), up to drinking molten copper (yāva tambalohapānā), and starting from drinking molten copper (tambalohapānato paṭṭhāya), again, having caused the fivefold binding, etc. (pañcavidhabandhanādīni kāretvā), they throw him into the great hell (mahāniraye pakkhipanti).

There, someone is freed by the fivefold binding itself (pañcavidhabandhaneneva muccati), someone by the second (dutiyena), someone by the third (tatiyena), someone is freed by drinking molten copper (tambalohapānena muccati). But when the karma is not exhausted (kamme pana aparikkhīṇe), they throw [him] again into the great hell (puna mahāniraye pakkhipanti).

Now, a certain young monk, taking hold of this sūtra (idaṃ pana suttaṃ gaṇhanto eko daharabhikkhu), said, "Venerable sir (bhante), even a being who has experienced so much suffering, do they throw again into the great hell (mahāniraye pakkhipanti)?"

"Yes (āma), friend (āvuso), when the karma is not exhausted (kamme aparikkhīṇe), they do thus again and again (punappunaṃ evaṃ karontīti)."

"Let the exposition (uddeso) stand, venerable sir (bhante); rather, speak of the practice (kammaṭṭhānameva kathetha)," having caused [him] to speak of the practice (kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathāpetvā), having become a stream-enterer (sotāpanno hutvā), having come (āgamma), he grasped the exposition (uddesaṃ aggahesi).

Even for others in this place (aññesampi imasmiṃ padese), having established the exposition (uddesaṃ ṭhapetvā), there is no counting of those who have attained arhatship (arahattaṃ pattānaṃ gaṇanā natthi).

And this sūtra (sabbabuddhānañcetaṃ suttaṃ) is never abandoned by all the Buddhas (avijahitameva hoti).

mula_pali:
271. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna idaṃ vatvā (sī. pī.) evamīdisesu ṭhānesu sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Coditā devadūtehi, ye pamajjanti māṇavā;

Te dīgharattaṃ socanti, hīnakāyūpagā narā.

‘‘Ye ca kho devadūtehi, santo sappurisā idha;

Coditā nappamajjanti, ariyadhamme kudācanaṃ.

‘‘Upādāne bhayaṃ disvā, jātimaraṇasambhave;

Anupādā vimuccanti, jātimaraṇasaṅkhaye.

‘‘Te khemappattā sukhino, diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā;

Sabbaverabhayātītā, sabbadukkhaṃ sabbadukkhā (ka.) upaccagu’’nti.

sabbadukkhā (ka.)

Devadūtasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

Suññatavaggo niṭṭhito tatiyo.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Dvidhāva suññatā hoti, abbhutadhammabākulaṃ;

Aciravatabhūmijanāmo, anuruddhupakkilesaṃ;

Bālapaṇḍito devadūtañca te dasāti.
mula_english:
271. Thus spoke the Blessed One (bhagavā). Having said this, O Well-Gone (sugato), then the Teacher (satthā) said something further:

“Admonished by divine messengers (devadūtehi), those youths (māṇavā) who are negligent,
Those men (narā) go to a miserable state (hīnakāyūpagā), they grieve for a long time (dīgharattaṃ socanti).

“And those noble persons (sappurisā) here, who are mindful (santo) because of the divine messengers (devadūtehi),
Admonished, they are never negligent (nappamajjanti) in the noble Dharma (ariyadhamme).

“Having seen fear (bhayaṃ disvā) in clinging (upādāne), which is the origin (sambhave) of birth and death (jātimaraṇa),
Without clinging (anupādā), they are liberated (vimuccanti) in the cessation (saṅkhaye) of birth and death (jātimaraṇa).

“They have attained security (khemappattā), they are happy (sukhino), they have directly experienced the Dharma (diṭṭhadhamma) and are fully extinguished (abhinibbutā);
Having gone beyond (atītā) all hatred and fear (sabbaverabhaya), they have overcome (upaccagu) all suffering (sabbadukkha).”

The tenth discourse, the *Devadūta Sutta*, is finished.

The third section, the Emptiness Division (*Suññatavaggo*), is finished.

Summary:

Emptiness (suññatā) is twofold (dvidhāva hoti), filled with wondrous teachings (abbhutadhammabākulaṃ);
Aciravata, Bhūmijana, Anuruddha, Pakkilesa;
The fool, the wise man, and the divine messengers (devadūta)—these are the ten.
commentary_pali:
271.Hīnakāyūpagāti hīnakāyaṃ upagatā hutvā. Upādāneti taṇhādiṭṭhigahaṇe. Jātimaraṇasambhaveti jātiyā ca maraṇassa ca kāraṇabhūte. Anupādāti catūhi upādānehi anupādiyitvā. Jātimaraṇasaṅkhayeti jātimaraṇasaṅkhayasaṅkhāte nibbāne vimuccanti.

Diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutāti diṭṭhadhamme imasmiṃyeva attabhāve sabbakilesanibbānena nibbutā. Sabbadukkhaṃ upaccagunti sabbadukkhātikkantā nāma honti.

Diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā Sabbadukkhaṃ upaccagu

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Devadūtasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Tatiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
271. *hīnakāyūpagā* means having approached a base body, *hīnakāyaṃ upagatā hutvā*.

*upādāne* means in grasping, *taṇhādiṭṭhigahaṇe*.

*jātimaraṇasambhave* means in the arising of birth and death, *jātiyā ca maraṇassa ca kāraṇabhūte*.

*anupādā* means without grasping, *catūhi upādānehi anupādiyitvā*.

*jātimaraṇasaṅkhaye* means in the cessation of birth and death, *jātimaraṇasaṅkhayasaṅkhāte nibbāne vimuccanti*.

*diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā* at *pb ed="v" n="4. 0175"* and *pb ed="p" n="4. 0239"* means extinguished through the directly seen Dhamma, *diṭṭhadhamme imasmiṃyeva attabhāve sabbakilesanibbānena nibbutā*.

*sabbadukkhaṃ upaccagu* means having overcome all suffering, *sabbadukkhātikkantā nāma honti*.

*diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā* at *pb ed="v" n="4. 0175"* and *pb ed="p" n="4. 0239"*

*sabbadukkhaṃ upaccagu*

The Devadūta Sutta Commentary of the Papañcasūdanī, Majjhimanikāya Aṭṭhakathā is completed.

The commentary on the third section is completed.

mula_pali:
272. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘bhaddekarattassa vo, bhikkhave, uddesañca vibhaṅgañca desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo yaṃ (nettipāḷi) dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

yaṃ (nettipāḷi)

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃhiraṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

asaṃhiraṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.)

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ kiccaṃ ātappaṃ (sī. ka.), ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

kiccaṃ ātappaṃ (sī. ka.)

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate muni’’ munīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

munīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī) in the Jetavana (Jetavana) in Anāthapindika’s Park.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: "Monks!"

"Venerable sir," those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this: "Monks, I will teach you the summary and exposition of one who has had an auspicious day (bhaddekaratta)."

Listen, pay close attention. I will speak.”

“As you say, lord,” the monks responded to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said:

“One should not yearn for the past,
nor be expectant about the future;

For the past is left behind,
and the future has not been reached.

But whoever sees insightfully the present phenomenon (paccuppannaṃ dhammaṃ)
again and again in each case,

Unmoved (asaṃhīraṃ), unshaken (asaṃkuppaṃ),
knowing that, one should cultivate it.

Today the effort must be made;
Tomorrow Death may come, who knows?

There is no bargaining with Mortality (maccunā) and his mighty horde (mahāsenena).

One who abides thus, ardent (ātāpiṃ),
untiring (atanditaṃ) day and night,

That one truly is auspicious (bhaddekarattoti),
so the sage (muni) declares, serene (santo)."
commentary_pali:
272.Evaṃme sutanti bhaddekarattasuttaṃ. Tattha bhaddekarattassāti vipassanānuyogasamannāgatattā bhaddakassa ekarattassa. Uddesanti mātikaṃ. Vibhaṅganti vitthārabhājanīyaṃ.

Atītanti atīte pañcakkhandhe. Nānvāgameyyāti taṇhādiṭṭhīhi nānugaccheyya. Nappaṭikaṅkheti taṇhādiṭṭhīhi na pattheyya. Yadatītanti idamettha kāraṇavacanaṃ. Yasmā yaṃ atītaṃ, taṃ pahīnaṃ niruddhaṃ atthaṅgataṃ, tasmā taṃ puna nānugaccheyya. Yasmā ca yaṃ anāgataṃ, taṃ appattaṃ ajātaṃ anibbattaṃ, tasmā tampi na pattheyya.

Atīta Nānvāgameyyā Nappaṭikaṅkhe Yadatīta

Tattha tatthāti paccuppannampi dhammaṃ yattha yattheva uppanno, tattha tattheva ca naṃ aniccānupassanādīhi sattahi anupassanāhi yo vipassati araññādīsu vā tattha tattheva vipassati. Asaṃhīraṃasaṃkuppanti idaṃ vipassanāpaṭivipassanādassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Vipassanā hi rāgādīhi na saṃhīrati na saṃkuppatīti asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ anubrūhaye vaḍḍheyya, paṭivipasseyyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Atha vā nibbānaṃ rāgādīhi na saṃhīrati na saṃkuppatīti asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ. Taṃ vidvā paṇḍito bhikkhu anubrūhaye, punappunaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ taṃ taṃ phalasamāpattiṃ appento vaḍḍheyyāti attho.

Tattha tatthā Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppa vidvā

Tassa pana anubrūhantassa atthāya – ajjeva kiccamātappanti kilesānaṃ ātāpanaparitāpanena ātappanti laddhanāmaṃ vīriyaṃ ajjeva kātabbaṃ. Ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suveti sve jīvitaṃ vā maraṇaṃ vā ko jānāti. Ajjeva dānaṃ vā dassāmi, sīlaṃ vā rakkhissāmi, aññataraṃ vā pana kusalaṃ karissāmīti hi ‘‘ajja tāva papañco atthi, sve vā punadivase vā karissāmī’’ti cittaṃ anuppādetvā ajjeva karissāmīti evaṃ vīriyaṃ kātabbanti dasseti. Mahāsenenāti aggivisasatthādīni anekāni maraṇakāraṇāni tassa senā, tāya mahatiyā senāya vasena mahāsenena evarūpena maccunā saddhiṃ ‘‘katipāhaṃ tāva āgamehi yāvāhaṃ buddhapūjādiṃ attano avassayakammaṃ karomī’’ti . Evaṃ mittasanthavākārasaṅkhāto vā, ‘‘idaṃ sataṃ vā sahassaṃ vā gahetvā katipāhaṃ āgamehī’’ti evaṃ lañjānuppadānasaṅkhāto vā, ‘‘imināhaṃ balarāsinā paṭibāhissāmī’’ti evaṃ balarāsisaṅkhāto vā saṅgaro natthi. Saṅgaroti hi mittasanthavākāralañjānuppadānabalarāsīnaṃ nāmaṃ, tasmā ayamattho vutto.

ajjeva kiccamātappa Ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve Mahāsenenā Saṅgaro

Atanditanti analasaṃ uṭṭhāhakaṃ. Evaṃ paṭipannattā bhaddo ekaratto assāti bhaddekaratto. Iti taṃ evaṃ paṭipannapuggalaṃ ‘‘bhaddekaratto aya’’nti. Rāgādīnaṃ santatāya santo buddhamuni ācikkhati.

Atandita bhaddekaratto santo buddhamuni
commentary_english:
272. "Thus I have heard" [is the beginning of] the *bhaddekarattasutta*.

There, *bhaddekarattassa* means, due to being endowed with the application of insight (*vipassanā*), [it refers to] the auspicious single night (*bhaddakassa ekarattassa*).

*Uddesa* means outline (*mātikaṃ*).

*Vibhaṅga* means [a text that is] fit for detailed exposition (*vitthārabhājanīyaṃ*).

*Atīta* means the past five aggregates (*pañcakkhandhe*).

*Nānvāgameyyā* means one should not go along with it through craving and wrong views (*taṇhādiṭṭhīhi nānugaccheyya*).

*Nappaṭikaṅkhe* means one should not long for it through craving and wrong views (*taṇhādiṭṭhīhi na pattheyya*).

*Yadatīta* this is a statement of reason here.

Since what is past is abandoned, ceased, and has passed away, therefore one should not go along with it again.

And since what is future is unobtained, unborn, and unproduced, therefore one should not long for that either.

*Atīta nānvāgameyyā nappaṭikaṅkhe yadatīta*

*Tattha tatthā* means even with regard to a present object of consciousness (*dhammaṃ*) wherever it arises, there itself one sees it with the seven contemplations beginning with the contemplation of impermanence (*anicānupassanādīhi sattahi anupassanāhi*), or in a forest etc., there itself he sees.

*Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ* this is said in order to show insight and counter-insight.

For insight is not disturbed or shaken by lust etc., thus [it is] *asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ*, that one should develop and increase, one should practice counter-insight, this is what is meant.

Or alternatively, nirvāṇa is not disturbed or shaken by lust etc., thus [it is] *asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ*.

That, having known (*vidvā*) the wise *bhikkhu* should develop, repeatedly making that its object, increasing it by attaining that and that fruition attainment (*phalasamāpattiṃ*), this is the meaning.

*Tattha tatthā asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppa vidvā*

Now, for the sake of one who is developing it: *ajjeva kiccamātappa* means the energy (*vīriyaṃ*) that has obtained the name *ātappa* through the burning and tormenting of the defilements (*kilesānaṃ ātāpanaparitāpanena*) should be done today itself.

*Ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve* means who knows whether tomorrow there will be life or death.

For one should generate energy thinking, "Today itself I will give a gift, or observe morality, or do some other wholesome deed." Thus, [he] shows that one should not produce the thought, "There is still time today, tomorrow or the day after tomorrow I will do it," but rather, "I will do it today itself."

*Mahāsenena* means the many causes of death such as fire, poison, weapons etc. are his army (*senā*), through that great army, together with such a great army (*mahāsenena*) of death (*maccunā*), there is no agreement saying, "Wait a few days until I perform the necessary acts such as the Buddha-puja".

Thus, there is no agreement consisting of friendly conversation, or consisting of giving bribes saying, "Take this hundred or thousand and wait a few days," or consisting of a mass of strength saying, "I will ward it off with this mass of strength."

*Saṅgaro* is a name for friendly conversation, giving bribes, and a mass of strength; therefore, this meaning is stated.

*Ajjeva kiccamātappa ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve mahāsenenā saṅgaro*

*Atandita* means unwearied, energetic.

Because of being one who has undertaken thus, he is an auspicious single night (*bhaddekaratto*).

Thus, *santo buddhamuni* indicates that person who has undertaken thus is "an auspicious single night."

*Atandita bhaddekaratto santo buddhamuni*

mula_pali:
273. ‘‘Kathañca , bhikkhave, atītaṃ anvāgameti? ‘Evaṃrūpo ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, ‘evaṃvedano ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, ‘evaṃsañño ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, ‘evaṃsaṅkhāro ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, ‘evaṃviññāṇo ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, atītaṃ anvāgameti.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, atītaṃ nānvāgameti? ‘Evaṃrūpo ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, ‘evaṃvedano ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, ‘evaṃsañño ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, ‘evaṃsaṅkhāro ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, ‘evaṃviññāṇo ahosiṃ atītamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, atītaṃ nānvāgameti.
mula_english:
273.
How, monks, does one revive the past? Thinking, ‘I had such material form (*rūpa*) in the past (*atītamaddhāna*)’ one finds delight (*nandi*) in that. Thinking, ‘I had such feeling (*vedanā*) in the past’…‘I had such perception (*saññā*) in the past,’…‘I had such formations (*saṅkhāra*) in the past,’…‘I had such consciousness (*viññāṇa*) in the past’ one finds delight in that. That is how, monks, one revives the past (*atītaṃ anvāgameti*).

How, monks, does one not revive the past? Thinking, ‘I had such material form in the past’ one does not find delight in that. Thinking, ‘I had such feeling in the past’…‘I had such perception in the past,’…‘I had such formations in the past,’…‘I had such consciousness in the past’ one does not find delight in that. That is how, monks, one does not revive the past (*atītaṃ nānvāgameti*).
commentary_pali:
273.Evaṃrūpotiādīsu kāḷopi samāno indanīlamaṇivaṇṇo ahosinti evaṃ manuññarūpavaseneva evaṃrūpo ahosiṃ. Kusalasukhasomanassavedanāvaseneva evaṃvedano. Taṃsampayuttānaṃyeva saññādīnaṃ vasena evaṃsañño evaṃsaṅkhāro evaṃviññāṇo ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti.

Tattha nandiṃ samanvānetīti tesu rūpādīsu taṇhaṃ samanvāneti anupavatteti. Hīnarūpādivasena pana evaṃrūpo ahosiṃ…pe… evaṃviññāṇo ahosinti na maññati.

Tattha nandiṃ samanvānetī

Nandiṃ na samanvānetīti taṇhaṃ vā taṇhāsampayuttadiṭṭhiṃ vā nānupavattayati.

Nandiṃ na samanvānetī
commentary_english:
273.
‘Having such a form’ etc., although being dark, he was similar to the color of an indigo-blue jewel; thus, due to the power of having such a pleasing form, I had such a form.
Due to the power of wholesome, pleasant, joyful feeling, I had such feeling (evaṃvedano).
Due to the power of the perceptions etc. associated with that, I had such perception (evaṃsañño), such formations (evaṃsaṅkhāro), such consciousness (evaṃviññāṇo) in the past.

'One finds delight in that' means one finds delight in craving (taṇhaṃ) in those forms etc., one continues [craving].
However, he does not think, "Due to the power of inferior forms etc., I had such a form...pe...I had such consciousness."

'One finds delight in that.' 'One does not find delight in delight' means he does not continue craving (taṇhaṃ) or views associated with craving (taṇhāsampayuttadiṭṭhiṃ).

One does not find delight in delight.

mula_pali:
274. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati? ‘Evaṃrūpo siyaṃ anāgatamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, evaṃvedano siyaṃ…pe… evaṃsañño siyaṃ… evaṃsaṅkhāro siyaṃ… evaṃviññāṇo siyaṃ anāgatamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati? ‘Evaṃrūpo siyaṃ anāgatamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, evaṃvedano siyaṃ … evaṃsañño siyaṃ… evaṃsaṅkhāro siyaṃ… ‘evaṃviññāṇo siyaṃ anāgatamaddhāna’nti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati.
mula_english:
274. Monks, how does one build up hope upon the future? Thinking, ‘I may have such *rūpa* (material form) in the future’ one finds delight in that. Thinking, ‘I may have such *vedanā* (feeling) in the future,’…‘I may have such *saṃjñā* (perception) in the future,’…‘I may have such *saṃskāra* (formations) in the future,’…‘I may have such *vijñāna* (consciousness) in the future,’ one finds delight in that. That is how, monks, one builds up hope upon the future.

Monks, how does one *not* build up hope upon the future? Thinking, ‘I may have such *rūpa* (material form) in the future’ one does *not* find delight in that. Thinking, ‘I may have such *vedanā* (feeling) in the future,’…‘I may have such *saṃjñā* (perception) in the future,’…‘I may have such *saṃskāra* (formations) in the future,’…‘I may have such *vijñāna* (consciousness) in the future,’ one does *not* find delight in that. That is how, monks, one does *not* build up hope upon the future.
commentary_pali: 274.Evaṃrūpo siyantiādīsupi taṃmanuññarūpādivaseneva taṇhādiṭṭhipavattasaṅkhātā nandisamanvānayanāva veditabbā.
commentary_english:
`

274. evaṃrūpo siyantiādīsupi taṃmanuññarūpādivaseneva taṇhādiṭṭhipavattasaṅkhātā nandisamanvānayanāva veditabbā.

` means: Also in passages beginning with "May I be of such a form" (*evaṃrūpo siya*), the bringing about of joy (*nandisamanvānayanāva*), which is reckoned as the occurrence of craving and views, should be understood specifically through the attraction to forms, etc.

mula_pali:
275. ‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhave, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati? Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ; vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati.

‘‘Kathañca , bhikkhave, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati? Idha, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā rūpaṃ, na rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ; na vedanaṃ… na saññaṃ… na saṅkhāre… na viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā viññāṇaṃ, na viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati.

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘‘Bhaddekarattassa vo, bhikkhave, uddesañca vibhaṅgañca desessāmī’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vutta’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Bhaddekarattasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
275. And how, bhikkhus, is one entangled in present phenomena? Here, bhikkhus, an uninstructed ordinary person, who has no regard for the noble ones, is unskilled and undisciplined in the Dhamma of the noble ones, who has no regard for true men, and is unskilled and undisciplined in the Dhamma of true men, regards material form (rūpa) as self (ātman), or self as possessed of material form, or material form as in self, or self as in material form. He regards feeling (vedanā)…perception (saṃjñā)…volitional formations (saṃskāra)…consciousness (vijñāna) as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness – in this way, bhikkhus, one is entangled in present phenomena.

And how, bhikkhus, is one not entangled in present phenomena? Here, bhikkhus, a well-taught noble disciple, who has regard for the noble ones, is skilled and disciplined in their Dhamma, who has regard for true men, and is skilled and disciplined in their Dhamma, does not regard material form as self, or self as possessed of material form, or material form as in self, or self as in material form. He does not regard feeling…nor perception…nor volitional formations…nor consciousness as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness – in this way, bhikkhus, one is not entangled in present phenomena.

"One should not revive the past, nor should one yearn for the future;

What is past is left behind, and the future has not yet been reached.

But whoever sees insightfully here and now each phenomenon,

Unwavering, unshaken— knowing it, let him develop it.

Today is the time to act intently; who knows, tomorrow death may come?

There is no bargain to be struck with Death and his mighty hosts."

"The one who dwells thus earnestly, tirelessly, day and night—

That one, truly, is called 'one of auspicious destiny' by the peaceful sage."

"I will teach you, bhikkhus, both the summary and the detailed explanation of the 'Auspicious Destiny'” – it was with reference to this that this was said."

This is what the Blessed One said.
Gratified, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Bhaddekaratta Sutta, the first, is finished.
commentary_pali:
275.Kathañca, bhikkhave, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīratīti idaṃ ‘‘paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati. Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppa’’nti uddesassa niddesatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Kāmañcettha ‘‘kathañca, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ dhammaṃ na vipassatī’’tiādi vattabbaṃ siyā, yasmā pana asaṃhīrāti ca asaṃkuppāti ca vipassanā vuttā, tasmā tassā eva abhāvañca bhāvañca dassetuṃ saṃhīratīti mātikaṃ uddharitvā vitthāro vutto. Tattha saṃhīratīti vipassanāya abhāvato taṇhādiṭṭhīhi ākaḍḍhiyati. Na saṃhīratīti vipassanāya bhāvena taṇhādiṭṭhīhi nākaḍḍhiyati. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Bhaddekarattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
275. How, monks, does one shrink in present circumstances? That is, “whoever sees the present thing, here and there.” *asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppa* is said to be the meaning of the designation of the subject matter.

If it should be said, “How, monks, does one not see the present thing?”, because *asaṃhīrāti ca asaṃkuppāti ca vipassanā vuttā*, therefore, to show the presence and absence of that very thing, having lifted up the *saṃhīratīti mātikaṃ*, the expansion is stated.

There, *saṃhīratī* means, due to the absence of insight, one is drawn by craving and views.

*na saṃhīratī* means, with the presence of insight, one is not drawn by craving and views.

The rest is clear throughout.

The commentary on the *Papañcasūdanī* *Majjhimanikāya*

The commentary on the *Bhaddekarattasutta* is finished.

mula_pali:
276. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca bhāsati.

Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘ko nu kho, bhikkhave, upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsī’’ti? ‘‘Āyasmā, bhante, ānando upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsī’’ti.

Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi , bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsī’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesiṃ samādapesiṃ samuttejesiṃ sampahaṃsesiṃ, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsiṃ –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate muni’’.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard:

Once the Blessed One (bhagavā) was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jetavana (jetavane) at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery (anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

Now on that occasion, the venerable Ānanda was instructing, urging, rousing, and encouraging the monks (bhikkhūnaṃ) with talk on the Dhamma (dhammiyā kathāya) in the assembly hall (upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ). He was reciting the summary (uddesaṃ ca) and exposition (vibhaṅgaṃ ca) of "One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment" (bhaddekarattassa).

Then, in the evening (sāyanhasamayaṃ), the Blessed One (bhagavā) rose from meditation (paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito) and went to the assembly hall (upaṭṭhānasālā). On arrival, he sat down on a seat (āsane) made ready (paññatte).

Having sat down (nisajja), the Blessed One (bhagavā) addressed the monks (bhikkhū) : "Monks (bhikkhave), who has been instructing, urging, rousing, and encouraging the monks (bhikkhūnaṃ) with talk on the Dhamma (dhammiyā kathāya) in the assembly hall (upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ)? Who has been reciting the summary (uddesaṃ ca) and exposition (vibhaṅgaṃ ca) of 'One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment' (bhaddekarattassa)?"

"[Venerable] Ānanda (ānando), venerable sir (bhante), has been instructing, urging, rousing, and encouraging the monks (bhikkhūnaṃ) with talk on the Dhamma (dhammiyā kathāya) in the assembly hall (upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ). He has been reciting the summary (uddesaṃ ca) and exposition (vibhaṅgaṃ ca) of 'One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment' (bhaddekarattassa)."

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā) addressed the venerable Ānanda (ānandaṃ): "Ānanda (ānanda), how were you instructing, urging, rousing, and encouraging the monks (bhikkhūnaṃ) with talk on the Dhamma (dhammiyā kathāya), and reciting the summary (uddesaṃ ca) and exposition (vibhaṅgaṃ ca) of 'One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment' (bhaddekarattassa)?"

"In this way (evaṃ kho), venerable sir (bhante), I have been instructing, urging, rousing, and encouraging the monks (bhikkhūnaṃ) with talk on the Dhamma (dhammiyā kathāya), and reciting the summary (uddesaṃ ca) and exposition (vibhaṅgaṃ ca) of 'One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment' (bhaddekarattassa):

One should not yearn for the past (atītaṃ nānvāgameyya), nor should one long for the future (nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ);

For the past is gone (yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ), and the future is yet unreached (appattañca anāgataṃ).

But whoever sees the present (paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ) in each and every condition (tattha tattha vipassati),

Unmoved (asaṃhīraṃ) and unshaken (asaṃkuppaṃ), let them cultivate that insight (taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye).

Earnestness (kiccamātappaṃ) should be done today (ajjeva), for who knows if death (maraṇaṃ) will come tomorrow (suve)?

There is no bargaining with Mortality (na hi no saṅgaraṃ), or his mighty horde (mahāsenena maccunā).

One who lives thus, zealous (evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ), unwearied day and night (ahorattamatanditaṃ),

That one truly is ‘one with a fortunate attachment’ (taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti), so the peaceful sage declares (santo ācikkhate muni)."
commentary_pali: 276.Evaṃme sutanti ānandabhaddekarattasuttaṃ. Tattha paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitoti phalasamāpattito vuṭṭhito. Ko nu kho, bhikkhaveti jānantova kathāsamuṭṭhāpanatthaṃ pucchi.
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard. Ānanda Bhaddekaratta Sūtra.

There, "risen from seclusion" means risen from the fruition attainment (phalasamāpatti).

"What now, monks?" he asked, even though he knew, in order to initiate the discussion.

mula_pali:
277. ‘‘Kathañca, āvuso, atītaṃ anvāgameti? Evaṃrūpo ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, evaṃvedano ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, evaṃsañño ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, evaṃsaṅkhāro ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, evaṃviññāṇo ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti – evaṃ kho, āvuso, atītaṃ anvāgameti.

‘‘Kathañca, āvuso, atītaṃ nānvāgameti? Evaṃrūpo ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, evaṃvedano ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, evaṃsañño ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, evaṃsaṅkhāro ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, evaṃviññāṇo ahosiṃ atītamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti – evaṃ kho, āvuso, atītaṃ nānvāgameti.

‘‘Kathañca, āvuso, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati? Evaṃrūpo siyaṃ anāgatamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti, evaṃvedano siyaṃ…pe… evaṃsañño siyaṃ… evaṃsaṅkhāro siyaṃ… evaṃviññāṇo siyaṃ anāgatamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ samanvāneti – evaṃ kho, āvuso, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati.

‘‘Kathañca, āvuso, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati? Evaṃrūpo siyaṃ anāgatamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti, evaṃvedano siyaṃ…pe… evaṃsañño siyaṃ… evaṃsaṅkhāro siyaṃ… evaṃviññāṇo siyaṃ anāgatamaddhānanti tattha nandiṃ na samanvāneti – evaṃ kho, āvuso, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati.

‘‘Kathañca, āvuso, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati? Idha, āvuso, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ; vedanaṃ… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ – evaṃ kho, āvuso, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati.

‘‘Kathañca , āvuso, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati? Idha, āvuso, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā rūpaṃ, na rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ; na vedanaṃ… na saññaṃ… na saṅkhāre… na viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā viññāṇaṃ, na viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ – evaṃ kho, āvuso, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati.

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesiṃ samādapesiṃ samuttejesiṃ sampahaṃsesiṃ, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsi’’nti.
mula_english:
277. “And how, friend, does one revive the past? Thinking, ‘I had such material form in the past,’ one finds delight in that. Thinking, ‘I had such feeling in the past’…! had such perception in the past’…! had such formations in the past,’…! had such consciousness in the past,’ one finds delight in that. That is how, friend, one revives the past.

“And how, friend, does one not revive the past? Thinking, ‘I had such material form in the past,’ one does not find delight in that. Thinking, ‘I had such feeling in the past’… one does not find delight in that. Thinking, ‘I had such perception in the past’… one does not find delight in that. Thinking, ‘I had such formations in the past’… one does not find delight in that. Thinking, ‘I had such consciousness in the past,’ one does not find delight in that. That is how, friend, one does not revive the past.

“And how, friend, does one build up hope upon the future? Thinking, ‘I may have such material form in the future,’ one finds delight in that. Thinking, ‘I may have such feeling in the future,’… ‘I may have such perception in the future’…! may have such formations in the future’… ‘I may have such consciousness in the future,’ one finds delight in that. That is how, friend, one builds up hope upon the future.

“And how, friend, does one not build up hope upon the future? Thinking, ‘I may have such material form in the future,’ one does not find delight in that. Thinking, ‘I may have such feeling in the future,’… ‘I may have such perception in the future’… ‘I may have such formations in the future’… ‘I may have such consciousness in the future,’ one does not find delight in that. That is how, friend, one does not build up hope upon the future.

“And how, friend, does one get caught up in present phenomena? Here, friend, an uninstructed ordinary person who has not seen the noble ones, is not versed in the teachings of the noble ones, is not trained in the teachings of the noble ones, has not seen the superior persons, is not versed in the teachings of the superior persons, is not trained in the teachings of the superior persons, regards form as self (ātman), or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He regards feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. That is how, friend, one gets caught up in present phenomena.

“And how, friend, does one not get caught up in present phenomena? Here, friend, an instructed noble disciple who has seen the noble ones, is versed in the teachings of the noble ones, is well-trained in the teachings of the noble ones, has seen the superior persons, is versed in the teachings of the superior persons, is well-trained in the teachings of the superior persons, does not regard form as self (ātman), or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He does not regard feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. That is how, friend, one does not get caught up in present phenomena.

“One should not revive the past, nor hope for the future;
What is past is relinquished, and the future is not yet attained.

“But whoever sees the present phenomenon in each and every place,
Unmoved, unangered, knowing it, let him cultivate it.

“Today, the effort must be made; who knows, death may come tomorrow?
For we have no bargain with Death and his great army.

“The silent sages declare that one who dwells thus, ardent, unwearied day and night, is truly ‘one who has one fortunate attachment.’”

“Thus, venerable sir, I was instructing, urging, rousing, and encouraging the bhikkhus with talk on the Dhamma, and reciting the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment.’”

mula_pali:
278. ‘‘Sādhu , sādhu, ānanda! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsi –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya…pe…

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘Kathañca, ānanda, atītaṃ anvāgameti…pe… evaṃ kho, ānanda, atītaṃ anvāgameti. Kathañca, ānanda, atītaṃ nānvāgameti…pe… evaṃ kho, ānanda, atītaṃ nānvāgameti. Kathañca, ānanda, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati…pe… evaṃ kho, ānanda, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati. Kathañca, ānanda, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati…pe… evaṃ kho, ānanda, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati. Kathañca, ānanda, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati…pe… evaṃ kho, ānanda, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati. Kathañca, ānanda, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati…pe… evaṃ kho, ānanda, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati.

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya…pe…

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Ānandabhaddekarattasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
278. "Well said, Ānanda! Well said, Ānanda. You have shown, encouraged, aroused, and delighted the monks with a discourse on the Dharma, and you have spoken of the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One Night (bhaddekaratta)."

"He should not pursue the past…pe…

That one is truly fortunate, the sage declares, who is at peace."

"And how, Ānanda, does one revive the past?...pe... Thus, Ānanda, does one revive the past.

And how, Ānanda, does one not revive the past?...pe... Thus, Ānanda, does one not revive the past.

And how, Ānanda, does one build up hope upon the future?...pe... Thus, Ānanda, does one build up hope upon the future.

And how, Ānanda, does one not build up hope upon the future?...pe... Thus, Ānanda, does one not build up hope upon the future.

And how, Ānanda, is one invincible in regard to presently arisen states?...pe... Thus, Ānanda, is one invincible in regard to presently arisen states.

And how, Ānanda, is one not invincible in regard to presently arisen states?...pe... Thus, Ānanda, is one not invincible in regard to presently arisen states."

"He should not pursue the past…pe…

That one is truly fortunate, the sage declares, who is at peace."

This is what the Blessed One (bhagavān) said.

The venerable Ānanda (āyasmā Ānanda), being pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words (bhāsitaṃ).

The Ānanda-bhaddekaratta-suttaṃ, the second, is finished.
commentary_pali:
278.Sādhu sādhūti therassa sādhukāramadāsi. Sādhu kho tvanti parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi parisuddhehi kathitattā desanaṃ pasaṃsanto āha. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Ānandabhaddekarattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
278. Saying "Well done, well done! *sādhu sādhū*", he gave the elder an expression of approval *sādhukāramadāsi*. Praising the teaching *desanaṃ*, he said, "Well done *sādhu*, indeed, you *tva*," because it was spoken with rounded, pure phrases and expressions *parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi parisuddhehi kathitattā*. The rest *sesaṃ* is clear *uttānam* throughout *sabbattha*.

The commentary on the Ānandabhaddekarattasutta is finished.

mula_pali: 279. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati tapodārāme. Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya yena tapodo tapodā (sī.) tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṃ. Tapode gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsi gattāni pubbāpayamāno sukkhāpayamāno (ka.). Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ tapodaṃ obhāsetvā yenāyasmā samiddhi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā āyasmantaṃ samiddhiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘dhāresi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañcā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dhāremi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Tvaṃ panāvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañcā’’ti? ‘‘Ahampi kho, bhikkhu, na dhāremi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Dhāresi pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthāti. Tvaṃ panāvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’’ti? ‘‘Ahampi kho, bhikkhu na dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthāti. Uggaṇhāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca; pariyāpuṇāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca; dhārehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Atthasaṃhito, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddeso ca vibhaṅgo ca ādibrahmacariyako’’ti. Idamavoca sā devatā; idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
mula_english:
THUS HAVE I HEARD. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rajagaha in the Park of the Hot Springs (tapodārāme).

Then, when it was near dawn, the venerable Samiddhi went to the hot springs (tapoda) to bathe his limbs (gattāni parisiñcituṃ).

Having bathed his limbs (gattāni) at the hot springs (tapode), having come out and being clad in a single robe, he stood drying his limbs.

Then, when the night was well advanced, a certain deity (devatā) of beautiful appearance who illuminated the whole of the Hot Springs (tapodaṃ), approached the venerable Samiddhi; having approached, she stood at one side.

Standing at one side, the deity (devatā) said to the venerable Samiddhi: “Bhikkhu, do you remember the summary (uddesa) and exposition (vibhaṅga) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattassa)?” “No, friend (āvuso), I do not remember the summary (uddesa) and exposition (vibhaṅga) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattassa)."

"Then, friend (āvuso), do you remember the summary (uddesa) and exposition (vibhaṅga) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattassa)?" "I, also, bhikkhu, do not remember the summary (uddesa) and exposition (vibhaṅga) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattassa)."

“Then, bhikkhu, do you remember the verses (gāthā) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattiyo)?" “No, friend (āvuso), I do not remember the verses (gāthāti) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattiyo)."
