“Then, friend (āvuso), do you remember the verses (gāthā) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattiyo)?” "I, also, bhikkhu, do not remember the verses (gāthāti) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattiyo)."

"Bhikkhu, learn the summary (uddesa) and exposition (vibhaṅga) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattassa). Bhikkhu, master the summary (uddesa) and exposition (vibhaṅga) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattassa). Bhikkhu, remember the summary (uddesa) and exposition (vibhaṅga) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattassa)."

"The summary (uddeso) and the exposition (vibhaṅgo) of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ (bhaddekarattassa) are connected with the meaning (atthasaṃhito), and it is the beginning of the holy life (ādibrahmacariyako)."

This is what the deity (devatā) said; having said this, she vanished right there (tatthevantaradhāyi).
commentary_pali: 279.Evaṃme sutanti mahākaccānabhaddekarattasuttaṃ. Tattha tapodārāmeti tattodakassa rahadassa vasena evaṃladdhanāme ārāme. Vebhārapabbatassa kira heṭṭhā bhūmaṭṭhakanāgānaṃ pañcayojanasatikaṃ nāgabhavanaṃ devalokasadisaṃ maṇimayena talena ārāmauyyānehi ca samannāgataṃ, tattha nāgānaṃ kīḷanaṭṭhāne mahāudakarahado, tato tapodā nāma nadī sandati kuthitā uṇhodakā. Kasmā panesā edisā jātā? Rājagahaṃ kira parivāretvā mahā petaloko, tattha dvinnaṃ mahālohakumbhinirayānaṃ antarena ayaṃ tapodā āgacchati, tasmā sā kuthitā sandati. Vuttampi cetaṃ – ‘‘yatāyaṃ, bhikkhave, tapodā sandati, so daho acchodako sītodako sātodako setodako suppatittho ramaṇīyo pahūtamacchakacchapo, cakkamattāni ca padumāni pupphanti . Apicāyaṃ, bhikkhave, tapodā dvinnaṃ mahānirayānaṃ antarikāya āgacchati, tenāyaṃ tapodā kuthitā sandatī’’ti (pārā. 231). Imassa pana ārāmassa abhisammukhaṭṭhāne tato mahāudakarahado jāto, tassa nāmavasenāyaṃ vihāro tapodārāmoti vuccati.
commentary_english:
279. Thus have I heard: the Mahākaccāna-bhaddekaratta Sūtra.

There, *Tapodārāma* means a garden (ārāma) named thus, on account of the lake of hot water (tattodakassa rahadassa vasena evaṃladdhanāme).

Below the VeBhāra Mountain, there is a Nāga-dwelling (nāgabhavanaṃ) five hundred yojanas in extent, similar to the world of the gods (devalokasadisaṃ), complete with jeweled surfaces (maṇimayena talena) and pleasure gardens (ārāmauyyānehi ca samannāgataṃ). There, in the playing place of the Nāgas, is a great water-lake (mahāudakarahado), from which flows the Tapodā river (tapodā nāma nadī), stinking with hot water (kuthitā uṇhodakā).

Why did this happen? The world of the great departed spirits (mahā petaloko) is said to surround Rājagaha. The Tapodā comes between two great iron-pot hells (dvinnam் mahālohakumbhinirayānam் antarena), therefore it flows stinking (kuthitā sandati).

Thus it was said: "Monks, this Tapodā flows, that lake has clear water (acchodako), cold water (sītodako), pleasant water (sātodako), white water (setodako), is a good bathing place (suppatittho), is delightful (ramaṇīyo), has abundant fish and turtles (pahūtamacchakacchapo), and lotus flowers (padumāni) bloom as large as chariot wheels (cakkamattāni)."

Moreover, monks, this Tapodā comes in the space between two great hells (dvinnam் mahānirayānam் antarikāya āgacchati), therefore this Tapodā flows stinking (kuthitā sandati)."

(Pārā. 231).

Furthermore, opposite this garden (ārāmassa abhisammukhaṭṭhāne), a great water-lake (mahāudakarahado) came into being, and because of its name, this monastery (vihāro) is called *Tapodārāma*.

mula_pali:
280. Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā samiddhi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Idhāhaṃ, bhante, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya yena tapodo tenupasaṅkamiṃ gattāni parisiñcituṃ. Tapode gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsiṃ gattāni pubbāpayamāno. Atha kho bhante, aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ tapodaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā maṃ etadavoca – ‘dhāresi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañcā’’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhante, taṃ devataṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dhāremi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Tvaṃ panāvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañcā’ti? ‘Ahampi kho, bhikkhu, na dhāremi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Dhāresi pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthāti. Tvaṃ panāvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’ti? ‘Ahampi kho, bhikkhu, na dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthāti. Uggaṇhāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca; pariyāpuṇāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca; dhārehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Atthasaṃhito, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddeso ca vibhaṅgo ca ādibrahmacariyako’ti. Idamavoca, bhante, sā devatā; idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi. Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca desetū’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, bhikkhu, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā samiddhi bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā; idaṃ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ , acirapakkantassa bhagavato, etadahosi – ‘‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’’ti?

Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ; pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’’ti.
mula_english:
280. Then, venerable Samiddhi, when the night was over, approached the Blessed One; having approached, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, venerable Samiddhi said this to the Blessed One:

"Here, venerable sir, rising in the early morning, I went to the Hot Springs to bathe my limbs. At the Hot Springs having bathed my limbs and come up out of the water, I stood dressed in one robe, drying my limbs. Then, venerable sir, a certain deity of beautiful appearance, illuminating the whole of the Hot Springs, approached me; having approached, she stood to one side. Standing to one side, that deity said this to me: ‘Do you, bhikkhu, remember the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One’?"

"When this was said, I said this to that deity: ‘No, friend, I do not remember the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One. Then do you, friend, remember the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One?’ ‘I too, bhikkhu, do not remember the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One.’ Then do you, bhikkhu, remember the verses of the Fortunate One?’ ‘No, friend, I do not remember the verses of the Fortunate One.’ Then do you, friend, remember the verses of the Fortunate One?’ ‘I too, bhikkhu, do not remember the verses of the Fortunate One.’ Learn, bhikkhu, the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One; master, bhikkhu, the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One; remember, bhikkhu, the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One. The summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One is connected with the goal, bhikkhu, and is the beginning of the holy life.’ That deity said this, venerable sir; having said this, she vanished right there. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would teach me the summary and the analysis of the Fortunate One." "Then, bhikkhu, listen and attend carefully to what I will say." "Yes, venerable sir," venerable Samiddhi replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

"One should not revive the past, nor long for the future; and as the past is left behind, the future is not attained.

"But whoever sees the present phenomenon in each and every place; unwavering and unmoving, let him develop it wisely.

"Today, in fact, one should do what must be done, who knows if death will come tomorrow? There is no bargaining with death and its mighty army.

"The silent sages declare that person who lives thus, ardent, unwearied day and night, is truly a Fortunate One."

The Blessed One said this; having said this, the Well-Gone One rose from his seat and entered the monastery. Then, after the Blessed One had left not long ago, this occurred to those *bhikkhus*: "The Blessed One, having briefly taught the summary, without explaining the meaning in detail, has risen from his seat and entered the monastery."

"One should not revive the past, nor long for the future; and as the past is left behind, the future is not attained.

"But whoever sees the present phenomenon in each and every place; unwavering and unmoving, let him develop it wisely.

"Today, in fact, one should do what must be done, who knows if death will come tomorrow? There is no bargaining with death and its mighty army.

"The silent sages declare that person who lives thus, ardent, unwearied day and night, is truly a Fortunate One."

"Who now can explain in detail the meaning of this summary that the Blessed One has taught, without explaining it in detail?"

Then this occurred to those *bhikkhus*: "The venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life; the venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this summary that the Blessed One has taught, without explaining it in detail." Suppose we went to the venerable Mahākaccāna; and having approached the venerable Mahākaccāna, asked him about the meaning of this.
commentary_pali: 280.Samiddhīti tassa kira therassa attabhāvo samiddho abhirūpo pāsādiko, tasmā samiddhitveva saṅkhaṃ gato. Ādibrahmacariyakoti maggabrahmacariyassa ādi pubbabhāgappaṭipattibhūto. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanāti madhupiṇḍikasutte (ma. ni. 1.199 ādayo) vuttanayeneva vitthāretabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
280. *Samiddhī*: It is said that the Elder's self ( *attabhāvo*) was radiant (*samiddho*), beautiful (*abhirūpo*), and pleasing (*pāsādiko*); therefore, he was reckoned as "radiant" (*samiddhitveva saṅkhaṃ gato*).

*Ādibrahmacariyako*: "[It] is the initial basis for practice which is the preliminary part (*pubbabhāgappaṭipattibhūto*) of the path of the holy life (*maggabrahmacariyassa ādi*)."

*Idaṃ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā*: As it says in the *Madhupiṇḍika Sutta* (Majjhima Nikāya 1.199 *ādayo*), [this] should be explained in detail in the manner that has been stated.

mula_pali:
281. Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākaccānena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso kaccāna, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya…pe…

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘Tesaṃ no, āvuso kaccāna, amhākaṃ, acirapakkantassa bhagavato, etadahosi – idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya…pe…

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyāti? Tesaṃ no , āvuso kaccāna, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti. Vibhajatāyasmā mahākaccāno’’ti.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṃ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva mūlaṃ atikkamma khandhaṃ sākhāpalāse sāraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ maññeyya; evaṃ sampadamidaṃ āyasmantānaṃ satthari sammukhībhūte taṃ bhagavantaṃ atisitvā amhe etamatthaṃ paṭipucchitabbaṃ maññatha maññetha (pī.). So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ passati, cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha, yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā’’ti.

maññetha (pī.)

‘‘Addhāvuso kaccāna, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ passati, cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma; yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāma. Api cāyasmā mahākaccāno satthuceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ; pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Vibhajatāyasmā mahākaccāno agaruṃ karitvā’’ti agarukaritvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

agarukaritvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘Tena hāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā mahākaccāno etadavoca –

‘‘Yaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya…pe…

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

Imassa kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi –
mula_english:
281. Then the bhikkhus went to the venerable Mahā Kaccāna and exchanged greetings with him. and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, sat down on one side. Sitting on one side, the bhikkhus said this to the venerable Mahā Kaccāna – “Reverend Kaccāna, the Blessed One, having briefly stated the teaching, without expounding the detailed meaning, rose from his seat and entered the monastery–

‘‘Not to pursue the past…pe…

That is truly the excellent one who lives by night, so the peaceful sage declares.’’

‘‘Reverend Kaccāna, this occurred to us after the Blessed One had recently departed – ‘The Blessed One, having briefly stated the teaching, without expounding the detailed meaning, rose from his seat and entered the monastery–

‘‘Not to pursue the past…pe…

That is truly the excellent one who lives by night, so the peaceful sage declares.’’

‘‘Who now might expound in detail the meaning of this summary stated in brief by the Blessed One, without expounding the detailed meaning?’ This occurred to us: ‘The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. He is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning. Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this.’” Let the venerable Mahā Kaccāna expound it to us.”

“Just as, friend, a man needing heartwood, seeking heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, passing by the root, passing by the trunk, branches and leaves of a great tree standing possessed of heartwood, might think that heartwood should be sought in the branches and leaves. So too, is this abundance available to the venerable ones, with the Teacher present before them. Do you think it proper to bypass that Blessed One and ask me about the meaning?

For knowing, the Blessed One knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision, he is knowledge, he is the Dhamma, he is the holy one; he is the sayer, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the giver of the Deathless, the lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata. That was the time when you should have asked the Blessed One the meaning. As he told you, so you should have remembered it.”

“Surely, friend Kaccāna, knowing, the Blessed One knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision…the Tathāgata. That was the time when we should have asked the Blessed One the meaning. As he told us, so we should have remembered it. Yet the venerable Mahā Kaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The venerable Mahā Kaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning. Let the venerable Mahā Kaccāna expound it without finding it troublesome.”

“Then listen, friends, and attend closely to what I shall say.” “As you say, friend,” the bhikkhus replied. The venerable Mahā Kaccāna said this:
‘‘That which, friends, the Blessed One, after giving a teaching in brief, without explaining the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery—

“One should not chase after the past…

…that one is truly called ‘blessed with a single night’ by the sage who is at peace.”

I understand the detailed meaning of this summary teaching given by the Blessed One, but not explained in detail, to be as follows:

mula_pali:
282. ‘‘Kathañca, āvuso, atītaṃ anvāgameti? Iti me cakkhu ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti rūpāti – tattha chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ chandarāgappaṭibandhaṃ (ka.) hoti viññāṇaṃ, chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā viññāṇassa tadabhinandati, tadabhinandanto atītaṃ anvāgameti. Iti me sotaṃ ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti saddāti…pe… iti me ghānaṃ ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti gandhāti… iti me jivhā ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti rasāti… iti me kāyo ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti phoṭṭhabbāti… iti me mano ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti dhammāti – tattha chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ hoti viññāṇaṃ, chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā viññāṇassa tadabhinandati, tadabhinandanto atītaṃ anvāgameti – evaṃ kho, āvuso, atītaṃ anvāgameti.

‘‘Kathañca , āvuso, atītaṃ nānvāgameti? Iti me cakkhu ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti rūpāti – tattha na chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ hoti viññāṇaṃ, na chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā viññāṇassa na tadabhinandati, na tadabhinandanto atītaṃ nānvāgameti. Iti me sotaṃ ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti saddāti…pe… iti me ghānaṃ ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti gandhāti… iti me jivhā ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti rasāti… iti me kāyo ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti phoṭṭhabbāti… iti me mano ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti dhammāti – tattha na chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ hoti viññāṇaṃ, na chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā viññāṇassa, na tadabhinandati, na tadabhinandanto atītaṃ nānvāgameti – evaṃ kho, āvuso, atītaṃ nānvāgameti.
mula_english:
282. How, friend, does one revive the past? Thinking, ‘My eye was thus in the past and forms were thus’—one’s consciousness becomes bound up with desire and lust (chandarāga) for that. Because one’s consciousness is bound up with desire and lust, one delights in that. When one delights in that, one revives the past.

Thinking, ‘My ear was thus in the past and sounds were thus…My nose and odours…My tongue and flavours…My body and tangibles…My mind was thus in the past and mind-objects were thus,’ one’s consciousness becomes bound up with desire and lust for that. Because one’s consciousness is bound up with desire and lust, one delights in that. When one delights in that, one revives the past. That is how one revives the past.

How, friend, does one *not* revive the past? Thinking, ‘My eye was thus in the past and forms were thus,’ one’s consciousness does not become bound up with desire and lust. Because one’s consciousness is not bound up with desire and lust, one does not delight in that. When one does not delight in that, one does not revive the past.

Thinking, ‘My ear was thus in the past and sounds were thus…My nose and odours…My tongue and flavours…My body and tangibles…My mind was thus in the past and mind-objects were thus,’ one’s consciousness does not become bound up with desire and lust. Because one’s consciousness is not bound up with desire and lust, one does not delight in that. When one does not delight in that, one does not revive the past. That is how one does not revive the past.
commentary_pali:
282.Iti me cakkhunti imasmiṃ kira sutte bhagavā dvādasāyatanavaseneva mātikaṃ ṭhapesi. Theropi ‘‘bhagavatā heṭṭhā dvīsu, upari catutthe cāti imesu tīsu suttesu pañcakkhandhavasena mātikā ca vibhaṅgo ca kato, idha pana dvādasāyatanavaseneva vibhajanatthaṃ mātikā ṭhapitā’’ti nayaṃ paṭilabhitvā evamāha. Imaṃ pana nayaṃ labhantena therena bhāriyaṃ kataṃ, apade padaṃ dassitaṃ, ākāse padaṃ kataṃ, tena naṃ bhagavā imameva suttaṃ sandhāya – ‘‘etadaggaṃ , bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajantānaṃ yadidaṃ mahākaccāno’’ti (a. ni. 1.197) etadagge ṭhapesi. Ettha pana cakkhūti cakkhupasādo. Rūpāti catusamuṭṭhānikarūpā. Iminā nayena sesāyatanānipi veditabbāni. Viññāṇanti nikantiviññāṇaṃ. Tadabhinandatīti taṃ cakkhuñceva rūpañca taṇhādiṭṭhivasena abhinandati. Anvāgametīti taṇhādiṭṭhīhi anugacchati.

Iti me mano ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti dhammāti ettha pana manoti bhavaṅgacittaṃ. Dhammāti tebhūmakadhammārammaṇaṃ.

Iti me mano ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti dhammā mano Dhammā
commentary_english:
"282. ‘*iti me cakkhu*’ means, in this very sūtra, the Blessed One established the matrix dependent on the twelve sense spheres alone.

The Elder also said, "In two sūtras below [page 5.0006] and in the fourth sūtra above, the matrix and the analysis were made dependent on the five aggregates. Here, however, the matrix is established for the purpose of analysis depending on the twelve sense spheres alone." Having obtained this method, he spoke thus:

"This method was well done by the Elder who obtained this method; a word was shown in the absence of a footing, a word was made in the sky." Therefore, the Blessed One, referring to this very sūtra, established Mahākaccāna as foremost among my disciples, the monks, who analyze in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief (A.Ni. 1.197).

Here, "*cakkhū*" means eye-sensitivity ( *cakkhupasāda*).

"*rūpā*" means the four-originated forms ( *catusamuṭṭhānikarūpā*).

By this method, the remaining sense spheres should be understood as well.

"*viññāṇa*" means clinging-consciousness ( *nikantiviññāṇaṃ*).

"*tadabhinandatī*" means he rejoices in that eye and form with craving and views.

"*anvāgametī*" means he follows craving and views.

"*iti me mano ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti dhammā*" means here, "*mano*" means the life-continuum mind ( *bhavaṅgacittaṃ*).

"*dhammā*" means the three-planes-dhamma object ( *tebhūmakadhammārammaṇaṃ*).

*iti me mano ahosi atītamaddhānaṃ iti dhammā mano dhammā*

mula_pali:
283. ‘‘Kathañca , āvuso, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati? Iti me cakkhu siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti rūpāti – appaṭiladdhassa paṭilābhāya cittaṃ paṇidahati, cetaso paṇidhānapaccayā tadabhinandati, tadabhinandanto anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati. Iti me sotaṃ siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti saddāti…pe… iti me ghānaṃ siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti gandhāti… iti me jivhā siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti rasāti… iti me kāyo siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti phoṭṭhabbāti… iti me mano siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti dhammāti – appaṭiladdhassa paṭilābhāya cittaṃ paṇidahati, cetaso paṇidhānapaccayā tadabhinandati, tadabhinandanto anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati – evaṃ kho, āvuso, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati.

‘‘Kathañca, āvuso, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati? Iti me cakkhu siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti rūpāti – appaṭiladdhassa paṭilābhāya cittaṃ nappaṇidahati , cetaso appaṇidhānapaccayā na tadabhinandati, na tadabhinandanto anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati. Iti me sotaṃ siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti saddāti…pe… iti me ghānaṃ siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti gandhāti… iti me jivhā siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti rasāti… iti me kāyo siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti phoṭṭhabbāti… iti me mano siyā anāgatamaddhānaṃ iti dhammāti – appaṭiladdhassa paṭilābhāya cittaṃ nappaṇidahati, cetaso appaṇidhānapaccayā na tadabhinandati, na tadabhinandanto anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati – evaṃ kho, āvuso, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati.
mula_english:
283. “And how, friend, does one build up hope upon the future (anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati)? Thinking, ‘My eye (cakkhu) may be thus in the future and forms (*rūpa*) may be thus,’ one sets one’s heart (cittaṃ paṇidahati) on obtaining what has not yet been obtained. Because one sets one’s heart (cetaso paṇidhānapaccayā) thus, one delights in that (tadabhinandati). When one delights in that (tadabhinandanto), one builds up hope upon the future.

Thinking, ‘My ear (sotaṃ) may be thus in the future and sounds (saddāti) may be thus…My nose (ghānaṃ) and odours (gandhāti)…My tongue (jivhā) and flavours (rasāti)…My body (kāyo) and tangibles (phoṭṭhabbāti)…My mind (mano) may be thus in the future and mind-objects (dhammāti) may be thus,’ one sets one’s heart (cittaṃ paṇidahati) on obtaining what has not yet been obtained. Because one sets one’s heart (cetaso paṇidhānapaccayā) thus, one delights in that (tadabhinandati). When one delights in that (tadabhinandanto), one builds up hope upon the future. That is how, friend, one builds up hope upon the future (anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati).

“And how, friend, does one not build up hope upon the future (anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati)? Thinking, ‘My eye (cakkhu) may be thus in the future and forms (*rūpa*) may be thus,’ one does not set one’s heart (cittaṃ nappaṇidahati) on obtaining what has not yet been obtained. Because one does not set one’s heart (cetaso appaṇidhānapaccayā) thus, one does not delight in that (na tadabhinandati). When one does not delight in that (na tadabhinandanto), one does not build up hope upon the future.

Thinking, ‘My ear (sotaṃ) may be thus in the future and sounds (saddāti) may be thus…My nose (ghānaṃ) and odours (gandhāti)…My tongue (jivhā) and flavours (rasāti)…My body (kāyo) and tangibles (phoṭṭhabbāti)…My mind (mano) may be thus in the future and mind-objects (dhammāti) may be thus,’ one does not set one’s heart (cittaṃ nappaṇidahati) on obtaining what has not yet been obtained. Because one does not set one’s heart (cetaso appaṇidhānapaccayā) thus, one does not delight in that (na tadabhinandati). When one does not delight in that (na tadabhinandanto), one does not build up hope upon the future. That is how, friend, one does not build up hope upon the future (anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati).”
commentary_pali:
283.Paṇidahatīti patthanāvasena ṭhapesi. Paṇidhānapaccayāti patthanāṭṭhapanakāraṇā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahākaccānabhaddekarattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
*Paṇidahatī* means he established it in terms of aspiration.

*Paṇidhānapaccayā* means the cause of the establishment of the aspiration.

The rest is clear throughout.

The commentary on the *Mahākaccānabhaddekarattasutta* in the *Papañcasūdanī*, the commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya*, is finished.

mula_pali:
284. ‘‘Kathañca, āvuso, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati? Yañcāvuso, cakkhu ye ca rūpā – ubhayametaṃ paccuppannaṃ. Tasmiṃ ce paccuppanne chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ hoti viññāṇaṃ, chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā viññāṇassa tadabhinandati, tadabhinandanto paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati. Yañcāvuso, sotaṃ ye ca saddā…pe… yañcāvuso, ghānaṃ ye ca gandhā… yā cāvuso, jivhā ye ca rasā… yo cāvuso, kāyo ye ca phoṭṭhabbā… yo cāvuso, mano ye ca dhammā – ubhayametaṃ paccuppannaṃ. Tasmiṃ ce paccuppanne chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ hoti viññāṇaṃ, chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā viññāṇassa tadabhinandati, tadabhinandanto paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati – evaṃ kho, āvuso, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati.

‘‘Kathañca , āvuso, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati? Yañcāvuso, cakkhu ye ca rūpā – ubhayametaṃ paccuppannaṃ. Tasmiṃ ce paccuppanne na chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ hoti viññāṇaṃ, na chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā viññāṇassa na tadabhinandati, na tadabhinandanto paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati. Yañcāvuso, sotaṃ ye ca saddā…pe… yañcāvuso, ghānaṃ ye ca gandhā… yā cāvuso, jivhā ye ca rasā… yo cāvuso, kāyo ye ca phoṭṭhabbā… yo cāvuso, mano ye ca dhammā – ubhayametaṃ paccuppannaṃ. Tasmiṃ ce paccuppanne na chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ hoti viññāṇaṃ, na chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā viññāṇassa na tadabhinandati, na tadabhinandanto paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati – evaṃ kho, āvuso, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati.
mula_english:
284. Now, how is one vanquished in regard to presently arisen states, friends? In regard to the eye (cakṣu) and forms (rūpa) – both of these are presently arisen (paccuppannaṃ).

When one’s consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) is bound up with desire and lust (chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ) for that which is presently arisen (paccuppanne), because one’s consciousness (viññāṇassa) is bound up with desire and lust (chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā), one delights in that (tadabhinandati). When one delights in that (tadabhinandanto), one is vanquished (saṃhīrati) in regard to presently arisen states (paccuppannesu dhammesu).

In regard to the ear (sotaṃ) and sounds (saddā)…the nose (ghānaṃ) and odours (gandhā)…the tongue (jivhā) and flavours (rasā)…the body (kāyo) and tangibles (phoṭṭhabbā)…the mind (mano) and mind-objects (dhammā) that are presently arisen (paccuppannaṃ).

When one’s consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) is bound up with desire and lust (chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ) for that which is presently arisen (paccuppanne), because one’s consciousness (viññāṇassa) is bound up with desire and lust (chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā), one delights in that (tadabhinandati). When one delights in that (tadabhinandanto), one is vanquished (saṃhīrati) in regard to presently arisen states (paccuppannesu dhammesu). That is how (evaṃ kho), friends (āvuso), one is vanquished (saṃhīrati) in regard to presently arisen states (paccuppannesu dhammesu).

Now, how is one not vanquished in regard to presently arisen states, friends? In regard to the eye (cakṣu) and forms (rūpa) – both of these are presently arisen (paccuppannaṃ).

When one’s consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) is not bound up with desire and lust (na chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ) for that which is presently arisen (paccuppanne), because one’s consciousness (viññāṇassa) is not bound up with desire and lust (na chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā), one does not delight in that (na tadabhinandati). When one does not delight in that (na tadabhinandanto), one is not vanquished (na saṃhīrati) in regard to presently arisen states (paccuppannesu dhammesu).

In regard to the ear (sotaṃ) and sounds (saddā)…the nose (ghānaṃ) and odours (gandhā)…the tongue (jivhā) and flavours (rasā)…the body (kāyo) and tangibles (phoṭṭhabbā)…the mind (mano) and mind-objects (dhammā) that are presently arisen (paccuppannaṃ).

When one’s consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) is not bound up with desire and lust (na chandarāgappaṭibaddhaṃ) for that which is presently arisen (paccuppanne), because one’s consciousness (viññāṇassa) is not bound up with desire and lust (na chandarāgappaṭibaddhattā), one does not delight in that (na tadabhinandati). When one does not delight in that (na tadabhinandanto), one is not vanquished (na saṃhīrati) in regard to presently arisen states (paccuppannesu dhammesu). That is how (evaṃ kho), friends (āvuso), one is not vanquished (na saṃhīrati) in regard to presently arisen states (paccuppannesu dhammesu).

mula_pali:
285. ‘‘Yaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya…pe…

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘Imassa kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe āyasmanto bhagavantaṃyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha, yathā vo bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā’’ti.

Atha kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘yaṃ kho no, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya…pe…

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ, acirapakkantassa bhagavato, etadahosi – ‘‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘‘Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’ti? Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipucchimha. Tesaṃ no, bhante, āyasmatā mahākaccānena imehi ākārehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi attho vibhatto’’ti.

‘‘Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, mahākaccāno; mahāpañño, bhikkhave mahākaccāno. Maṃ cepi tumhe, bhikkhave, etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi taṃ evamevaṃ byākareyyaṃ yathā taṃ mahākaccānena byākataṃ. Eso, cevetassa attho. Evañca naṃ dhārethā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Mahākaccānabhaddekarattasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
285. “Friends, the Blessed One having briefly stated the teaching, without explaining it in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery—

“One should not pursue the past…pe…

That person is truly blessed, so the sage declares.”

“Friends, I understand the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning, to be as follows. If you wish, friends, go to the Blessed One and ask him about the meaning of this. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so you should remember it.”

Then the monks, having delighted and rejoiced in the venerable Mahākaccāna’s words, rose from their seats and went to the Blessed One. After paying homage to him, they sat down at one side.

As they were sitting there, the monks said to the Blessed One, “Lord, the Blessed One having briefly stated the teaching, without explaining it in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery—

“One should not pursue the past…pe…”

That person is truly blessed, so the sage declares.”

“Then, venerable sir, we thought: ‘The Blessed One, having recently departed, gave a concise teaching, but did not explain the meaning in detail. He then rose from his seat and entered the monastery—

“One should not be attached to the past, nor long for the future;

But one should see the present phenomenon in each and every state.

Unwavering, unperturbed, knowing this, let him cultivate it.

Strenuous is the task today, who knows if death will come tomorrow?

There is no bargain with Death and his great army.

One who lives thus, ardent and unwearied, day and night,

That person is truly blessed, so the sage declares.”

“‘Who now can explain in detail the meaning of this brief teaching given by the Blessed One, without elaborating on it?’ Then, venerable sir, we thought: ‘The venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning. Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this.’

Then, venerable sir, we went to the venerable Mahākaccāna and asked him about the meaning.

The venerable Mahākaccāna explained the meaning to us with these terms, statements, and phrases.”

“Monks, Mahākaccāna is wise; monks, Mahākaccāna has great wisdom. If you were to ask me about the meaning of this, I would explain it to you in the same way that Mahākaccāna has explained it. Such is its meaning, and so you should remember it.”

The Blessed One spoke thus. Elated, those monks delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Mahākaccānabhaddekaratta Sutta is finished, the third.

mula_pali:
286. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā lomasakaṅgiyo lomasakakaṅgiyo (ṭīkā) sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho candano devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ nigrodhārāmaṃ obhāsetvā yenāyasmā lomasakaṅgiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho candano devaputto āyasmantaṃ lomasakaṅgiyaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘dhāresi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañcā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dhāremi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Tvaṃ panāvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañcā’’ti? ‘‘Ahampi kho, bhikkhu, na dhāremi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Dhāresi pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā. Tvaṃ panāvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’’ti? ‘‘Dhāremi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’’ti? ‘‘Ekamidaṃ, bhikkhu, samayaṃ bhagavā devesu tāvatiṃsesu viharati pāricchattakamūle paṇḍukambalasilāyaṃ. Tatra bhagavā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsi –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhu, dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā. Uggaṇhāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca; pariyāpuṇāhi tvaṃ , bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca; dhārehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Atthasaṃhito, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddeso ca vibhaṅgo ca ādibrahmacariyako’’ti. Idamavoca candano devaputto. Idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard:

Once the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī) in the Jeta Grove, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery (Anāthapiṇḍadasya ārāme).

Now at that time, the venerable Lomasakaṅgiya was living in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu (Kapilavastu) in Nigrodha’s Park.

Then Candana (Candano), a young deva (devaputto) of beautiful appearance, illuminating the entire Nigrodha’s Park as the night was far advanced, approached the venerable Lomasakaṅgiya; having approached, he stood to one side.

Standing to one side, Candana the young deva said this to the venerable Lomasakaṅgiya: “Bhikkhu (monk), do you remember the summary and the exposition of the *bhaddekaratta* (one who has one fortunate attachment)?”

“No, friend (āvuso), I do not remember the summary and the exposition of the *bhaddekaratta*.”

“Then, friend, do you remember the summary and the exposition of the *bhaddekaratta*?”

“I, too, bhikkhu, do not remember the summary and the exposition of the *bhaddekaratta*.”

“Then, bhikkhu, do you remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*?”

“No, friend, I do not remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*.”

“Then, friend, do you remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*?”

“Yes, bhikkhu, I do remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*.”

“In what way, friend, do you remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*?”

“Once, bhikkhu, the Blessed One was dwelling among the gods (devesu) in Tāvatiṃsa (Trāyastriṃśa), at the foot of the Pāricchattaka tree, on the Paṇḍukambala stone.

There, the Blessed One spoke this summary and exposition of the *bhaddekaratta* to the Tāvatiṃsa gods:

“One should not hark back to the past, nor long for the future;

For the past is left behind, and the future is not yet attained.

But one should contemplate the present moment, discerning the dharma (law) in each and every instance;

Unswayed, unperturbed, knowing this, may one cultivate it.

Today, the task must be done with zeal; who knows if death will come tomorrow?

For there is no bargaining with Death, nor with his mighty host.

Thus, one who dwells ardently, untiringly day and night;

That one, indeed, the sage declares to be ‘one with a fortunate attachment.’”

“Thus, bhikkhu, I remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*.

Learn, bhikkhu, the summary and the exposition of the *bhaddekaratta*; master, bhikkhu, the summary and the exposition of the *bhaddekaratta*; remember, bhikkhu, the summary and the exposition of the *bhaddekaratta*.

The summary and the exposition of the *bhaddekaratta* is beneficial, bhikkhu, it belongs to the fundamentals of the holy life.”

That is what was said by Candana the young deva.

Having said this, he vanished at once.
commentary_pali:
286.Evaṃme sutanti lomasakaṅgiyabhaddekarattasuttaṃ. Tattha lomasakaṅgiyoti aṅgathero kira nāmesa, kāyassa pana īsakalomasākāratāya lomasakaṅgiyoti pākaṭo jāto. Candanodevaputtoti kassapasammāsambuddhakāle kiresa candano nāma upāsako aḍḍho mahaddhano tīṇi ratanāni catūhi paccayehi pūjetvā devaloke nibbatto, purimanāmena candano devaputtotveva saṅkhaṃ gato. Paṇḍukambalasilāyanti rattakambalasilāyaṃ. Tassā kira rattakambalasseva jayasumanapuppharāsi viya vaṇṇo, tasmā ‘‘paṇḍukambalasilā’’ti vuccati.

Kadā pana tattha bhagavā vihāsīti? Bodhipattito sattame saṃvacchare sāvatthiyaṃ āsāḷhīmāsapuṇṇamāya dvādasayojanāya parisāya majjhe yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ katvā oruyha kaṇḍambamūle paññattavarabuddhāsane nisīditvā dhammadesanāya mahājanaṃ mahāviduggato uddharitvā buddhā nāma yasmā pāṭihāriyaṃ katvā manussapathe na vasanti, tasmā passamānasseva tassa janassa padavīkkamaṃ katvā tāvatiṃsabhavane pāricchattakamūle paṇḍukambalasilāyaṃ vassaṃ upagato, tasmiṃ samaye vihāsi.

Tatra bhagavāti tatra viharanto bhagavā yebhuyyena dasahi cakkavāḷasahassehi sannipatitāhi devatāhi parivuto mātaraṃ kāyasakkhiṃ katvā abhidhammapiṭakaṃ kathento gambhīraṃ nipuṇaṃ tilakkhaṇāhataṃ rūpārūpaparicchedakathaṃ paṭivijjhituṃ asakkontānaṃ devānaṃ saṃvegajananatthaṃ antarantarā bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsi. Tatrāyaṃ devaputto uggaṇhanto imā gāthā saddhiṃ vibhaṅgena uggaṇhi, devattassa pana pamādādhiṭṭhānattā dibbehi ārammaṇehi nippīḷiyamāno anupubbena suttaṃ sammuṭṭho gāthāmattameva dhāresi. Tenāha ‘‘evaṃ kho ahaṃ bhikkhu dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’’ti.

Tatra bhagavā abhidhammapiṭakaṃ

Uggaṇhāhitvantiādīsu tuṇhībhūto nisīditvā suṇanto uggaṇhāti nāma, vācāya sajjhāyaṃ karonto pariyāpuṇāti nāma, aññesaṃ vācento dhāreti nāma. Sesamettha uttānamevāti.

Uggaṇhāhi tva

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Lomasakaṅgiyabhaddekarattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
286. "Thus I have heard": this is from the Lomasakaṅgiyabhaddekarattasutta.

There, *Lomasakaṅgiyo* means: It seems that was the name of an elder (*thero*) from Aṅga. However, because his body was somewhat in the shape of hair (*lomasa*), he became known as Lomasakaṅgiya.

*Candano devaputto* means: It seems that in the time of the Buddha Kassapa, there was a lay follower (*upāsako*) named Candana, who was rich and wealthy. Having venerated the three jewels with the four requisites, he was reborn in the world of the gods. By his former name, he went by the designation Candana, a god.

*Paṇḍukambalasilāya* means: On a red cloth stone (*rattakambalasilāyaṃ*). It seems its color was like a heap of *jayasumana* flowers on a red cloth; therefore, it is called "Paṇḍukambalasilā."

When did the Blessed One dwell there? In the seventh year from his enlightenment, in Sāvatthi, on the full moon of Āsāḷhī month, having performed the twin miracle in the midst of a twelve *yojana* assembly, he descended and sat on the excellent Buddha-seat prepared at the foot of the Kaṇḍamba tree. Having rescued the great multitude from the great quagmire by means of a *dharma* talk, because Buddhas do not dwell on the path of humans after performing a miracle, while that crowd was still watching, having made an imperceptible stride, he went to the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, to the foot of the Pāricchatta tree, to the Paṇḍukambalasilā, and observed the rainy season retreat (*vassa*). At that time, he dwelt there.

"There, the Blessed One" means: There, dwelling, the Blessed One, mostly surrounded by deities who had assembled from ten thousand *cakkavāḷa*s, having made his mother a witness by [showing her] his body, while teaching the *Abhidhamma Piṭaka*, in order to generate a sense of urgency in the deities who were unable to penetrate the profound, subtle, and three characteristics-stricken, analysis of form and formless phenomena, in between, he spoke the summary and the analysis of the *bhaddekaratta*.

There, this *devaputta*, while learning, learned these verses together with the analysis. However, due to being based on negligence because of his divine nature, being oppressed by divine objects, gradually he forgot the *sutta* and retained only the verses. Therefore, he said, "Thus, I, *bhikkhu*, remember the verses of the *bhaddekarattiya*."

"There, the Blessed One [*taught*] the *Abhidhamma Piṭaka*"

"Learn you" and so on, means: remaining silent, sitting and listening, he is said to learn (*uggaṇhāti*); reciting with speech, he is said to master (*pariyāpuṇāti*); causing others to recite, he is said to retain (*dhāreti*).

The rest is evident here.

"Learn you"

The Lomasakaṅgiyabhaddekarattasuttavaṇṇanā is finished.

mula_pali:
287. Atha kho āyasmā lomasakaṅgiyo tassā rattiyā accayena senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā lomasakaṅgiyo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, bhante, samayaṃ sakkesu viharāmi kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho, bhante, aññataro devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ nigrodhārāmaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, bhante, so devaputto maṃ etadavoca – ‘dhāresi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañcā’ti? Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhante, taṃ devaputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dhāremi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Tvaṃ panāvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañcā’ti? ‘Ahampi kho, bhikkhu, na dhāremi bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Dhāresi pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā. Tvaṃ panāvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’ti? ‘Dhāremi kho ahaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’ti. ‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, dhāresi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā’ti? Ekamidaṃ, bhikkhu, samayaṃ bhagavā devesu tāvatiṃsesu viharati pāricchattakamūle paṇḍukambalasilāyaṃ . Tatra kho bhagavā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca abhāsi –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya…pe…

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhu, dhāremi bhaddekarattiyo gāthā. Uggaṇhāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca; pariyāpuṇāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca; dhārehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca. Atthasaṃhito, bhikkhu, bhaddekarattassa uddeso ca vibhaṅgo ca ādibrahmacariyako’ti. Idamavoca, bhante, so devaputto; idaṃ vatvā tatthevantaradhāyi. Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā bhaddekarattassa uddesañca vibhaṅgañca desetū’’ti.
mula_english:
Thereupon, the venerable Lomasakaṅgiya, at the end of that night, having arranged his bedding, taking his bowl and robe, left on a walking tour for Sāvatthī.

Wandering by stages, he arrived at Sāvatthī, Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. He went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side.

As he was sitting to one side, the venerable Lomasakaṅgiya said this to the Blessed One:

“Once, lord, I was staying in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in Nigrodha’s Park.

Then, lord, a certain young deity, in the far extreme of the night, his extreme radiance lighting up the entirety of Nigrodha’s Park, came to me and, on arrival, stood to one side.

Standing to one side, lord, that young deity said this to me: ‘Do you, bhikkhu, remember the summary and the analysis of the *bhaddekaratta* (one who has one fortunate attachment)?’ When this was said, I said this to that young deity: ‘No, friend, I do not remember the summary and the analysis of the *bhaddekaratta*.

Then, friend, do you remember the summary and the analysis of the *bhaddekaratta*?’ ‘I also, bhikkhu, do not remember the summary and the analysis of the *bhaddekaratta*.’

Then, do you, bhikkhu, remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*?’ ‘No, friend, I do not remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*.

Then, friend, do you remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*?’ ‘Yes, bhikkhu, I remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*.’

‘How then, friend, do you remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*?’ Once, bhikkhu, the Blessed One was staying among the gods of the Tāvatiṃsa heaven at the foot of the pāricchattaka tree on the paṇḍukambala stone slab.

There, the Blessed One recited the summary and the analysis of the *bhaddekaratta* to the Tāvatiṃsa gods –

“One should not pursue the past…pe…

That one is truly fortunate, so the peaceful ones declare.”

“In this way, bhikkhu, I remember the verses of the *bhaddekaratta*.

Bhikkhu, learn the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment.’ Bhikkhu, master the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment.’ Bhikkhu, remember the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment.’

Bhikkhu, the summary and exposition of ‘One Who Has One Fortunate Attachment’ is beneficial, it belongs to the fundamentals of the holy life.”

That is what the young deity said, lord; having said this, he vanished right there.

It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would teach me the summary and the analysis of the *bhaddekaratta*."

mula_pali:
288. ‘‘Jānāsi pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, taṃ devaputta’’nti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, bhante, jānāmi taṃ devaputta’’nti. ‘‘Candano nāma so, bhikkhu, devaputto. Candano, bhikkhu, devaputto aṭṭhiṃ katvā aṭṭhikatvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) manasikatvā sabbacetasā sabbaṃ cetaso (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sabbaṃ cetasā (ka.) samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti. Tena hi, bhikkhu, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā lomasakaṅgiyo bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā;

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate muni’’.

‘‘Kathañca, bhikkhu, atītaṃ anvāgameti…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, atītaṃ anvāgameti. Kathañca , bhikkhu, atītaṃ nānvāgameti…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, atītaṃ nānvāgameti. Kathañca, bhikkhu, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, anāgataṃ paṭikaṅkhati. Kathañca, bhikkhu, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, anāgataṃ nappaṭikaṅkhati. Kathañca, bhikkhu, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, paccuppannesu dhammesu saṃhīrati. Kathañca, bhikkhu, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, paccuppannesu dhammesu na saṃhīrati.

‘‘Atītaṃ nānvāgameyya, nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṃ;

Yadatītaṃ pahīnaṃ taṃ, appattañca anāgataṃ.

‘‘Paccuppannañca yo dhammaṃ, tattha tattha vipassati;

Asaṃhīraṃ asaṃkuppaṃ, taṃ vidvā manubrūhaye.

‘‘Ajjeva kiccamātappaṃ, ko jaññā maraṇaṃ suve;

Na hi no saṅgaraṃ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.

‘‘Evaṃ vihāriṃ ātāpiṃ, ahorattamatanditaṃ;

Taṃ ve bhaddekarattoti, santo ācikkhate munī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā lomasakaṅgiyo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Lomasakaṅgiyabhaddekarattasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.
mula_english:
288. “Monk, do you know that young deity?” “No, venerable sir, I do not know that young deity.”

“Bhikkhu, that young deity is named Candana. Candana, the young deity, gives it attention, engages it with all his mind, hears the Dhamma as with eager ears. Therefore, monk, listen and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Lomasakangiya replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“Let not a person revive the past
Or on the future build his hopes;

For the past is left behind,
And the future is not yet attained.

But whoever sees insightfully the present phenomenon
In each and every case,

Unshaken, unperturbed,
May he cultivate it, that sage."

“Ardently doing what should be done today, for — who knows? — tomorrow death.

There is no bargaining with Mortality & his mighty horde.

One who dwells thus ardently, relentlessly,
Is truly called blessed to live alone for a night by the peaceful sage.”

“And how, monk, does one revive the past? …So, monk, one revives the past. And how, monk, does one not revive the past? … So, monk, one does not revive the past. And how, monk, does one build hopes on the future? … So, monk, one builds hopes on the future. And how, monk, does one not build hopes on the future? … So, monk, one does not build hopes on the future. And how, monk, is one drawn together in present phenomena? … So, monk, one is drawn together in present phenomena. And how, monk, is one not drawn together in present phenomena? … So, monk, one is not drawn together in present phenomena.”

“Let not a person revive the past
Or on the future build his hopes;

For the past is left behind,
And the future is not yet attained.

But whoever sees insightfully the present phenomenon
In each and every case,

Unshaken, unperturbed,
May he cultivate it, that sage."

“Ardently doing what should be done today, for — who knows? — tomorrow death.
No bargaining with Death (maccu) and his mighty host (mahāsena) is possible for us.

"Thus, the sage (muni), at peace, describes one who lives diligently (ātāpi), ceaselessly (atanditaṃ) day and night as truly fortunate (bhaddekaratta)."

The Blessed One (bhagavā) spoke thus.

The venerable Āyasmā Lomasakangiya, being pleased (attamano), rejoiced (abhinandi) in the Blessed One's (bhagavato) words (bhāsitaṃ).

The Lomasakangiyabhaddekarattasuttaṃ, the fourth, is completed (niṭṭhitaṃ).

mula_pali:
289. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane, anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho subho māṇavo todeyyaputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yena manussānaṃyeva sataṃ manussabhūtānaṃ dissanti hīnappaṇītatā? Dissanti hi, bho gotama, manussā appāyukā, dissanti dīghāyukā; dissanti bavhābādhā bahvābādhā (syā. kaṃ. ka.), dissanti appābādhā; dissanti dubbaṇṇā, dissanti vaṇṇavanto; dissanti appesakkhā, dissanti mahesakkhā; dissanti appabhogā, dissanti mahābhogā; dissanti nīcakulīnā, dissanti uccākulīnā; dissanti duppaññā, dissanti paññavanto paññāvanto (sī. pī.). Ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yena manussānaṃyeva sataṃ manussabhūtānaṃ dissanti hīnappaṇītatā’’ti?

bahvābādhā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) paññāvanto (sī. pī.)

‘‘Kammassakā , māṇava, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammayoni kammabandhu (sī.) kammappaṭisaraṇā. Kammaṃ satte vibhajati yadidaṃ – hīnappaṇītatāyāti. Na kho ahaṃ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Sādhu me bhavaṃ gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetu yathā ahaṃ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājāneyya’’nti.

kammayoni kammabandhu (sī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.

Then the brahmin student Subha, Todeyya’s son, went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. Having exchanged greetings of friendliness and courtesy, he sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, the brahmin student Subha, Todeyya’s son, said this to the Blessed One:

“What is the cause and condition, Master Gotama, why human beings are seen to be inferior and superior? For humans are seen to be short-lived and long-lived; sickly, <note>bahvābādhā (syā.
kaṃ.
ka.)</note> and healthy; ugly and beautiful; uninfluential and influential; with little wealth and great wealth; born to low families and high families; stupid and wise. <note>paññāvanto (sī.
pī.)</note>

What is the cause and condition, Master Gotama, why human beings are seen to be inferior and superior?”

<note>bahvābādhā (syā.
kaṃ.
ka.)</note> <note>paññāvanto (sī.
pī.)</note>

“Beings are owners of their action (*kamma*), heir to their action, born of their action, related by their action, <note>kammayoni kammabandhu (sī.)</note> and have their action as their refuge. Action divides beings, that is, as inferior and superior.

I do not understand in detail the meaning of Master Gotama’s statement, which he spoke in brief without expounding the meaning in detail.

It would be good if Master Gotama would teach me the *dhamma* so that I might understand in detail the meaning of Master Gotama’s statement.”

<note>kammayoni kammabandhu (sī.)</note>
commentary_pali:
289.Evaṃme sutanti cūḷakammavibhaṅgasuttaṃ. Tattha subhoti so kira dassanīyo ahosi pāsādiko, tenassa aṅgasubhatāya subhotveva nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Māṇavoti pana taṃ taruṇakāle vohariṃsu, so mahallakakālepi teneva vohārena vohariyati. Todeyyaputtoti todeyyassa nāma pasenadirañño purohitabrāhmaṇassa putto. So kira sāvatthiyā avidūre tudigāmo nāma atthi, tassa adhipatittā todeyyoti saṅkhaṃ gato. Mahādhano pana hoti sattāsītikoṭivibhavo paramamaccharī, ‘‘dadato bhogānaṃ aparikkhayo nāma natthī’’ti cintetvā kassaci kiñci na deti. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘‘Añjanānaṃ khayaṃ disvā, vammikānañca sañcayaṃ;

Madhūnañca samāhāraṃ, paṇḍito gharamāvase’’ti.

Evaṃ adānameva sikkhāpesi. Dhuravihāre vasato sammāsambuddhassa yāguuḷuṅgamattaṃ vā bhattakaṭacchumattaṃ vā adatvā dhanalobhena kālaṃ katvā tasmiṃyeva ghare sunakho hutvā nibbatto. Subho taṃ sunakhaṃ ativiya piyāyati , attano bhuñjanakabhattaṃyeva bhojeti, ukkhipitvā varasayane sayāpeti. Atha bhagavā ekadivasaṃ paccūsasamaye lokaṃ volokento taṃ sunakhaṃ disvā – ‘‘todeyyabrāhmaṇo dhanalobhena attanova ghare sunakho hutvā nibbatto, ajja mayi subhassa gharaṃ gate maṃ disvā sunakho bhukkāraṃ karissati, athassāhaṃ ekaṃ vacanaṃ vakkhāmi, so ‘jānāti maṃ samaṇo gotamo’ti gantvā uddhanaṭṭhāne nipajjissati. Tatonidānaṃ subhassa mayā saddhiṃ eko kathāsallāpo bhavissati, so dhammaṃ sutvā saraṇesu patiṭṭhahissati, sunakho pana kālaṃ katvā niraye nibbattissatī’’ti imaṃ māṇavassa saraṇesu patiṭṭhānabhāvaṃ ñatvā bhagavā taṃ divasaṃ sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā ekakova gāmaṃ pavisitvā nikkhante māṇave taṃ gharaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi.

Sunakho bhagavantaṃ disvā bhukkāraṃ karonto bhagavato samīpaṃ gato. Tato naṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘todeyya tvaṃ pubbepi maṃ bho bhoti paribhavitvā sunakho jāto, idānipi bhukkāraṃ katvā avīciṃ gamissasī’’ti. Sunakho taṃ sutvā – ‘‘jānāti maṃ samaṇo gotamo’’ti vippaṭisārī hutvā gīvaṃ onāmetvā uddhanantare chārikāyaṃ nipanno. Manussā ukkhipitvā sayane sayāpetuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. Subho āgantvā – ‘‘kenāyaṃ sunakho sayanā oropito’’ti āha. Manussā na kenacīti vatvā taṃ pavattiṃ ārocesuṃ. Māṇavo sutvā – ‘‘mama pitā brahmaloke nibbatto, todeyyo nāma sunakho natthi. Samaṇo pana gotamo pitaraṃ sunakhaṃ karoti, yaṃkiñci esa mukhāruḷhaṃ bhāsatī’’ti kujjhitvā bhagavantaṃ musāvādena niggahetukāmo vihāraṃ gantvā taṃ pavattiṃ pucchi.

Bhagavāpi tassa tatheva vatvā avisaṃvādanatthaṃ āha – ‘‘atthi pana te māṇava pitarā anakkhātaṃ dhana’’nti . Atthi, bho gotama, satasahassagghanikā suvaṇṇamālā satasahassagghanikā suvaṇṇapādukā satasahassagghanikā suvaṇṇapāti satasahassañca kahāpaṇanti. Gaccha taṃ sunakhaṃ appodakapāyāsaṃ bhojāpetvā sayane āropetvā īsakaṃ niddaṃ okkantakāle puccha, sabbaṃ te ācikkhissati. Atha naṃ jāneyyāsi ‘‘pitā me eso’’ti. Māṇavo – ‘‘sace saccaṃ bhavissati, dhanaṃ lacchāmi, no ce, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ musāvādena niggaṇhissāmī’’ti dvīhipi kāraṇehi tuṭṭho gantvā tathā akāsi. Sunakho – ‘‘ñātomhi iminā’’ti roditvā huṃ hunti karonto dhananidhānaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā pādena pathaviṃ khaṇitvā saññaṃ adāsi, māṇavo dhanaṃ gahetvā – ‘‘bhavapaṭicchannaṃ nāma evaṃ sukhumaṃ paṭisandhiantaraṃ pākaṭaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa, addhā esa sabbaññū’’ti bhagavati pasannacitto cuddasa pañhe abhisaṅkhari. Aṅgavijjāpāṭhako kiresa, tenassa etadahosi – ‘‘idaṃ dhammapaṇṇākāraṃ gahetvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pañhe pucchissāmī’’ti dutiyagamanena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, tena puṭṭhapañhe pana bhagavā ekappahāreneva vissajjento kammassakātiādimāha.

kammassakā

Tattha kammaṃ etesaṃ sakaṃ attano bhaṇḍakanti kammassakā. Kammassa dāyādāti kammadāyādā, kammaṃ etesaṃ dāyajjaṃ bhaṇḍakanti attho. Kammaṃ etesaṃ yoni kāraṇanti kammayonī. Kammaṃ etesaṃ bandhūti kammabandhū, kammañātakāti attho. Kammaṃ etesaṃ paṭisaraṇaṃ patiṭṭhāti kammapaṭisaraṇā. Yadidaṃhīnappaṇītatāyāti yaṃ idaṃ ‘‘tvaṃ hīno bhava, tvaṃ paṇīto, tvaṃ appāyuko, tvaṃ dīghāyuko…pe… tvaṃ duppañño bhava, tvaṃ paññavā’’ti evaṃ hīnappaṇītatāya vibhajanaṃ, taṃ na añño koci karoti, kammameva evaṃ satte vibhajatīti attho. Na māṇavo kathitassa atthaṃ sañjānāsi, ghanadussapaṭṭenassa mukhaṃ bandhitvā madhuraṃ purato ṭhapitaṃ viya ahosi. Mānanissito kiresa paṇḍitamānī, attanā samaṃ na passati. Athassa ‘‘kiṃ samaṇo gotamo katheti, yamahaṃ jānāmi, tadeva kathetīti ayaṃ māno mā ahosī’’ti mānabhañjanatthaṃ bhagavā ‘‘āditova duppaṭivijjhaṃ katvā kathessāmi, tato ‘nāhaṃ bho gotama jānāmi, vitthārena me pākaṭaṃ katvā kathethā’ti maṃ yācissati, athassāhaṃ yācitakāle kathessāmi, evañcassa sātthakaṃ bhavissatī’’ti duppaṭivijjhaṃ katvā kathesi.

kammassakā kammadāyādā, kammayonī kammabandhū, kammapaṭisaraṇā. Yadidaṃ hīnappaṇītatāyā

Idāni so attano appaṭividdhabhāvaṃ pakāsento na kho ahantiādimāha.

na kho aha
commentary_english:
289. Thus have I heard: the Cūḷakammavibhaṅgasuttaṃ.

There, Subha was pleasing and delightful to see. Thus, because of his bodily beauty, they made the name Subha.

Māṇava is what they called him in his youth. So even in old age, he was called by that same term.

Todeyyaputta means the son of the brahmin Todeyya, who was the chaplain of King Pasenadi.

It is said that near Sāvatthi, there is a village named Tudigāma. Because he was the chief of that, he went by the designation Todeyya.

He was very rich, possessing eighty-seven koṭis of wealth. [But he was] extremely miserly, thinking, “There is no such thing as the exhaustion of possessions by giving,” he gave nothing to anyone.

It was also said:

“Having seen the destruction of ointment, and the accumulation of anthills;

And the collection of honey, the wise man should dwell at home.”

Thus, he only taught not giving.

While the Perfectly Awakened Buddha was dwelling at Dhuravihāra, [Todeyya], without giving even the amount of rice gruel in a small bowl or the amount of food in a ladle, because of greed for wealth, having made time, was reborn as a dog in that very house.

Subha was extremely fond of that dog, fed him only on the food that he himself ate, and lifting him up, had him lie on an excellent bed.

Then, one day, the Blessed One, surveying the world at dawn, saw that dog and [thought]: “Todeyya the brahmin, because of greed for wealth, having been reborn as a dog in his own house, today, when I have gone to Subha’s house, the dog will bark at me upon seeing me. Then I will speak one word to him, and he, thinking, ‘The renunciant Gotama knows me,’ will lie down in the charnel ground.

“From that cause, there will be a conversation between Subha and me, and having heard the Dharma, he will be established in the refuges. But the dog, having made time, will be reborn in hell.” Knowing this state of being established in the refuges for the youth, the Blessed One, having attended to his bodily needs that day, and having entered the village alone, when the youth had left, entered that house for alms.

The dog, seeing the Blessed One, barking, went near the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One said this to him: “Todeyya, you were born as a dog having insulted me in the past with ‘bho bhoti’. Now, even now, having barked, you will go to Avīci.”

The dog, hearing that, [thinking], “The renunciant Gotama knows me,” becoming remorseful, having bent his neck, lay down in the charnel ground.

The people were not able to lift him up and make him lie on the bed.

Subha, coming, said, “By whom was this dog taken down from the bed?”

The people, saying, “By no one,” announced that occurrence.

The youth, hearing [this], [said]: “My father was reborn in the Brahma-world. There is no dog named Todeyya.

The renunciant Gotama makes my father into a dog! Whatever this one speaks is just hot air!” Angered, desiring to refute the Blessed One with a lie, he went to the monastery and asked about that occurrence.

The Blessed One also said the same to him and, for the sake of non-deception, said, “Is there, youth, wealth not declared by your father?”

“There is, Gotama. A golden garland worth one hundred thousand, golden slippers worth one hundred thousand, a golden dish worth one hundred thousand, and one hundred thousand *kahāpaṇas*.”

“Go, feed that dog rice gruel with little water, and having lifted him up and placed him on the bed, ask him when he has fallen slightly asleep. He will tell you everything.

Then you will know, ‘This is my father.’”

The youth [thought], “If it will be true, I will get wealth, [but] if not, I will refute the renunciant Gotama with a lie.” Delighted by both causes, he went and did thus.

The dog, [thinking], “I am known by this one,” having cried and making *huṃ huṃ* sounds, having gone to the place where the wealth was hidden, dug the earth with his foot and gave a sign. The youth, having taken the wealth, [thought], “The Blessed One knows even such a subtle rebirth interval that is covered by existence. Truly, this one is all-knowing.” With his mind pleased with the Blessed One, he arranged fourteen questions.

It is said that he was a teacher of *aṅgavijjā*. Therefore, this occurred to him: “Having taken this Dharma-gift, I will ask the renunciant Gotama questions.” With a second coming, he approached the Blessed One, by whom the questions had been asked. Then the Blessed One, dismissing the questions with a single strike, spoke the *kammassakā*-sayings and so on.

*Kammassakā* There, *kammam* is their own possession, [their] own belonging; therefore, they are *kammassakā*.
*Kammadāyādā*: because they are the heirs of actions, meaning *karma* is their inheritance.
*Kammayonī*: because *karma* is the womb and cause for them.
*Kammabandhū*: because *karma* is their relative; meaning, *karma* is their kin.
*Kammapaṭisaraṇā*: because *karma* is their refuge and support.

*Hīnappaṇītatāyā*: That which is "you are inferior, you are superior, you are short-lived, you are long-lived…pe… you are unwise, you are wise," thus, the distinction due to inferiority and superiority is not made by anyone else; *karma* alone thus distinguishes beings—this is the meaning.

The youth does not understand the meaning of what was said; it was as if his face was bound with a thick cloth, and sweetness was placed before him.

That conceited one, relying on pride, thinking himself a wise man, does not consider himself equal to others.

Then, thinking, “What does the renunciate Gotama say? What I know, that alone he says—let this pride not arise!”, the Blessed One, in order to break his pride, said, “From the beginning, I will make it difficult to understand, then I will speak. Then he will ask me, ‘Venerable Gotama, I do not know. Please explain it to me in detail.’ Then I will speak at the time of his request, and thus it will be meaningful for him," making it difficult to understand, he spoke.

*Kammassakā, kammadāyādā, kammayonī, kammabandhū, kammapaṭisaraṇā.*

*Hīnappaṇītatāyā:* Now, revealing his incomprehension, he said, "*Na kho aha*," and so on.

*Na kho aha*.

mula_pali:
290. ‘‘Tena hi, māṇava, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Idha, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā pāṇātipātī hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu sabbapāṇabhūtesu (sī. ka.). So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena samādiṇṇena (pī. ka.) kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati appāyuko hoti. Appāyukasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – pāṇātipātī hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu.

sabbapāṇabhūtesu (sī. ka.) samādiṇṇena (pī. ka.)

‘‘Idha pana, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho, lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati dīghāyuko hoti. Dīghāyukasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho, lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.
mula_english:
“Then, student, listen and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“Yes, sir,” the brahmin student Subha, son of Todeyya, replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“Here, student, some woman or man is a killer of living beings, cruel, bloody-handed, devoted to violence and killing, and without compassion for living beings. Because of that action, performed and undertaken in such a way, at the break-up of the body ( *kāyassa bhedā*), after death, one is reborn in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in the nether world, in hell (*apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati*). But if at the break-up of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in the nether world, in hell, but instead comes back to the human state, then wherever he is reborn he is short-lived. This is the path, student, that leads to short life: being a killer of living beings, cruel, bloody-handed, devoted to violence and killing, and without compassion for living beings.

“But here, student, some woman or man, abandoning the killing of living beings, abstains from killing living beings; with rod and weapon laid aside ( *nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho*), conscientious, full of kindness, sympathetic for the welfare of all living beings ( *sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati*). Because of that action, performed and undertaken in such a way, at the break-up of the body, after death, one is reborn in a happy destination, in the heavenly world (*sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati*). But if at the break-up of the body, after death, one is not reborn in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, but instead comes back to the human state, then wherever he is reborn he is long-lived. This is the path, student, that leads to long life: abandoning the killing of living beings, abstaining from killing living beings, with rod and weapon laid aside, conscientious, full of kindness, sympathetic for the welfare of all living beings.
commentary_pali:
290.Samattenāti paripuṇṇena. Samādinnenāti gahitena parāmaṭṭhena. Appāyukasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ pāṇātipātīti yaṃ idaṃ pāṇātipātakammaṃ, esā appāyukasaṃvattanikā paṭipadāti.

Kathaṃ panesā appāyukataṃ karoti? Cattāri hi kammāni upapīḷakaṃ upacchedakaṃ janakaṃ upatthambhakanti. Balavakammena hi nibbattaṃ pavatte upapīḷakaṃ āgantvā atthato evaṃ vadati nāma – ‘‘sacāhaṃ paṭhamataraṃ jāneyyaṃ, na te idha nibbattituṃ dadeyyaṃ, catūsuyeva taṃ apāyesu nibbattāpeyyaṃ. Hotu, tvaṃ yattha katthaci nibbatta, ahaṃ upapīḷakakammaṃ nāma taṃ pīḷetvā nirojaṃ niyūsaṃ kasaṭaṃ karissāmī’’ti. Tato paṭṭhāya taṃ tādisaṃ karoti. Kiṃ karoti? Parissayaṃ upaneti, bhoge vināseti.

Tattha dārakassa mātukucchiyaṃ nibbattakālato paṭṭhāya mātu assādo vā sukhaṃ vā na hoti, mātāpitūnaṃ pīḷāva uppajjati. Evaṃ parissayaṃ upaneti. Dārakassa pana mātukucchimhi nibbattakālato paṭṭhāya gehe bhogā udakaṃ patvā loṇaṃ viya rājādīnaṃ vasena nassanti, kumbhadohanadhenuyo khīraṃ na denti, sūratā goṇā caṇḍā honti, kāṇā honti, khujjā honti, gomaṇḍale rogo patati, dāsādayo vacanaṃ na karonti, vāpitaṃ sassaṃ na jāyati, gehagataṃ gehe, araññagataṃ araññe nassati, anupubbena ghāsacchādanamattaṃ dullabhaṃ hoti, gabbhaparihāro na hoti, vijātakāle mātuthaññaṃ chijjati, dārako parihāraṃ alabhanto pīḷito nirojo niyūso kasaṭo hoti, idaṃ upapīḷakakammaṃ nāma.

upapīḷakakammaṃ

Dīghāyukakammena pana nibbattassa upacchedakakammaṃ āgantvā āyuṃ chindati. Yathā hi puriso aṭṭhusabhagamanaṃ katvā saraṃ khipeyya tamañño dhanuto vimuttamattaṃ muggarena paharitvā tattheva pāteyya, evaṃ dīghāyukakammena nibbattassa upacchedakakammaṃ āyuṃ chindati. Kiṃ karoti? Corānaṃ aṭaviṃ paveseti, vāḷamacchodakaṃ otāreti, aññataraṃ vā pana saparissayaṭṭhānaṃ upaneti, idaṃ upacchedakakammaṃ nāma, ‘‘upaghātaka’’ntipi etasseva nāmaṃ.

upacchedakakammaṃ

Paṭisandhinibbattakaṃ pana kammaṃ janakakammaṃ nāma. Appabhogakulādīsu nibbattassa bhogasampadādikaraṇena upatthambhakakammaṃ upatthambhakakammaṃ nāma.

janakakammaṃ upatthambhakakammaṃ

Imesu catūsu purimāni dve akusalāneva, janakaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, upatthambhakaṃ kusalameva. Tattha pāṇātipātakammaṃ upacchedakakammena appāyukasaṃvattanikaṃ hoti. Pāṇātipātinā vā kataṃ kusalakammaṃ uḷāraṃ na hoti, dīghāyukapaṭisandhiṃ janetuṃ na sakkoti. Evaṃ pāṇātipāto appāyukasaṃvattaniko hoti. Paṭisandhimeva vā niyāmetvā appāyukaṃ karoti, sanniṭṭhānacetanāya vā niraye nibbattati, pubbāparacetanāhi vuttanayena appāyuko hoti.

Dīghāyukasaṃvattanikā esā māṇava paṭipadāti ettha parittakammenapi nibbattaṃ pavatte etaṃ pāṇātipātā viratikammaṃ āgantvā atthato evaṃ vadati nāma – ‘‘sacāhaṃ paṭhamataraṃ jāneyyaṃ, na te idha nibbattituṃ dadeyyaṃ, devalokeyeva taṃ nibbattāpeyyaṃ. Hotu, tvaṃ yattha katthaci nibbatti, ahaṃ upatthambhakakammaṃ nāma thambhaṃ te karissāmī’’ti upatthambhaṃ karoti. Kiṃ karoti? Parissayaṃ nāseti, bhoge uppādeti.

Dīghāyukasaṃvattanikā esā māṇava paṭipadā

Tattha dārakassa mātukucchiyaṃ nibbattakālato paṭṭhāya mātāpitūnaṃ sukhameva sātameva hoti. Yepi pakatiyā manussāmanussaparissayā honti, te sabbe apagacchanti. Evaṃ parissayaṃ nāseti. Dārakassa pana mātukucchimhi nibbattakālato paṭṭhāya gehe bhogānaṃ pamāṇaṃ na hoti, nidhikumbhiyo puratopi pacchatopi gehaṃ pavaṭṭamānā pavisanti. Mātāpitaro parehi ṭhapitadhanassāpi sammukhībhāvaṃ gacchanti. Dhenuyo bahukhīrā honti, goṇā sukhasīlā honti, vappaṭṭhāne sassāni sampajjanti. Vaḍḍhiyā vā sampayuttaṃ, tāvakālikaṃ vā dinnaṃ dhanaṃ acoditā sayameva āharitvā denti, dāsādayo suvacā honti, kammantā na parihāyanti. Dārako gabbhato paṭṭhāya parihāraṃ labhati, komārikavejjā sannihitāva honti. Gahapatikule jāto seṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ, amaccakulādīsu jāto senāpatiṭṭhānādīni labhati. Evaṃ bhoge uppādeti. So aparissayo sabhogo ciraṃ jīvatīti. Evaṃ apāṇātipātakammaṃ dīghāyukasaṃvattanikaṃ hoti.

Apāṇātipātinā vā kataṃ aññampi kusalaṃ uḷāraṃ hoti, dīghāyukapaṭisandhiṃ janetuṃ sakkoti, evampi dīghāyukasaṃvattanikaṃ hoti. Paṭisandhimeva vā niyāmetvā dīghāyukaṃ karoti. Sanniṭṭhānacetanāya vā devaloke nibbattati, pubbāparacetanāhi vuttanayena dīghāyuko hoti. Iminā nayena sabbapañhavissajjanesu attho veditabbo.

Viheṭhanakammādīnipi hi pavatte āgantvā atthato tatheva vadamānāni viya upapīḷanena nibbhogataṃ āpādetvā paṭijagganaṃ alabhantassa roguppādanādīhi vā, viheṭhakādīhi katassa kusalassa anuḷāratāya vā, āditova paṭisandhiniyāmanena vā, vuttanayeneva pubbāparacetanāvasena vā bahvābādhatādīni karonti, apāṇātipāto viya ca aviheṭhanādīnipi appābādhatādīnīti.
commentary_english:
290. *Samattenā:* by that which is complete. *Samādinnena:* by that which is taken, touched. *Appāyukasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ pāṇātipātī:* that which is this act of killing living beings, this is the practice that leads to a short life.

How does this cause a short life? There are four kinds of karma: oppressive (*upapīḷakaṃ*), obstructive (*upacchedakaṃ*), generative (*janakaṃ*), and supportive (*upatthambhakaṃ*).

The oppressive karma, produced by strong karma, comes into being and speaks thus: "If I had known earlier, I would not have allowed you to be born here; I would have caused you to be born in one of the four woeful realms. Even if you are born somewhere, I, the oppressive karma, will torment you, making you weak, without essence, and wretched." From then on, it makes him such. What does it do? It brings about distress, it destroys possessions.

There, from the time of the child's birth in the mother's womb, there is no satisfaction or happiness for the mother; suffering arises for the parents. Thus, it brings about distress. But from the time of the child's birth in the mother's womb, possessions in the house are destroyed like salt in water due to kings and other causes, the milk cows that are milked in pots do not give milk, strong bulls become fierce, they are blind, they are hunchbacked, disease falls upon the cattle pen, servants and others do not do what is said, the sown crops do not grow, what is in the house is destroyed in the house, what is in the forest is destroyed in the forest, gradually only enough for food and clothing is difficult to obtain, there is no care for the embryo, at the time of birth the mother's breast milk is cut off, the child, not obtaining care, is tormented, weak, without essence, and wretched. This is called oppressive karma (*upapīḷakakammaṃ*).

The obstructive karma, for one born of long-life karma, comes and cuts off life. Just as a man, after having sexual intercourse, might shoot an arrow, and another might strike it with a club as soon as it is released from the bow, causing it to fall right there, so the obstructive karma cuts off the life of one born of long-life karma. What does it do? It causes [him] to enter a thieves' forest, it lowers [him] into a place of dangerous fish and water, or it brings [him] to some other place of danger. This is called obstructive karma (*upacchedakakammaṃ*); it is also called "destructive" (*upaghātakaṃ*).

The karma that produces rebirth is called generative karma (*janakakammaṃ*). The supportive karma, through bringing about the wealth of possessions, etc., for one born in a family with few possessions, etc., is called supportive karma (*upatthambhakakammaṃ*).
