Among these four, the first two are unwholesome only, the generative is wholesome and unwholesome, the supportive is wholesome only. There, the karma of killing living beings, by means of obstructive karma, leads to a short life. Or, a wholesome karma done by a killer of living beings is not great, it is not able to generate a long-life rebirth. Thus, killing living beings leads to a short life. Or, having determined the rebirth itself, it makes [him] short-lived, or by the intention of resolution [to kill], [he] is born in hell, [and] by the earlier and later intentions, he is short-lived in the manner stated.

*Dīghāyukasaṃvattanikā esā māṇava paṭipadā:* Here, even if one is born through small karma, this abstaining from killing living beings, when it comes into being, says thus: "If I had known earlier, I would not have allowed you to be born here; I would have caused you to be born in the heaven world. Even if you are born somewhere, I, the supportive karma, will make a pillar for you," and it makes support. What does it do? It destroys distress, it produces possessions.

There, from the time of the child's birth in the mother's womb, there is only happiness and satisfaction for the parents. And whatever natural dangers from humans and non-humans there are, all of them disappear. Thus, it destroys distress. But from the time of the child's birth in the mother's womb, there is no limit to the possessions in the house, treasure pots rush into the house from front and back.
Parents also face the consequences of wealth left behind by others.

Cows are full of milk, bulls are easy to train, and crops flourish in the fields.

Either wealth associated with growth, or wealth given temporarily, they bring back unasked, slaves and the like are obedient, and businesses do not decline.

The child, from the womb onwards, receives care, and female doctors are constantly present.

One born in a householder's family obtains the position of a treasurer, one born in a minister's family obtains the position of a general, and so on.

Thus, he produces enjoyment.

That one, without danger and with enjoyment, lives long.

Thus, the action of abstaining from killing leads to a long life.

Furthermore, good actions done by one who abstains from killing are excellent, he is able to generate rebirth leading to a long life, and thus it leads to a long life.

Or, having determined the rebirth itself, he makes [it] a long life.

Or, through the intention of determination, he is reborn in the world of gods; through former and later intentions, in the manner described, he has a long life.

In this way, the meaning should be understood in all answers to questions.

Furthermore, actions of harming and so on, coming into being, and speaking according to the meaning, as if oppressing, causing lack of enjoyment, and not obtaining maintenance, or through the arising of diseases and so on, or through the unexcelled nature of the good done by those who harm and so on, or from the beginning through the determination of rebirth, or in the manner described, through the force of former and later intentions, they create many sicknesses and so on; just as abstaining from killing, so also abstaining from harming and so on [leads to] few sicknesses and so on.

mula_pali:
291. ‘‘Idha , māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā sattānaṃ viheṭhakajātiko hoti, pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati bavhābādho hoti. Bavhābādhasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – sattānaṃ viheṭhakajātiko hoti pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā.

‘‘Idha pana, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā sattānaṃ aviheṭhakajātiko hoti pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati appābādho hoti. Appābādhasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – sattānaṃ aviheṭhakajātiko hoti pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā.
mula_english:
291. “Here, student (māṇava), some man or woman is given to injuring beings (sattānaṃ) with the hand (pāṇinā), with a clod (leḍḍunā), with a stick (daṇḍena), or with a knife (satthena). Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ). But if instead he does not reappear in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell, but instead comes back to the human state (manussattaṃ), then wherever he is reborn he is sickly (bavhābādho). This is the way, student, that leads to sickliness (bavhābādhasaṃvattanikā), namely, one is given to injuring beings with the hand, with a clod, with a stick, or with a knife.

“But here, student, some man or woman is not given to injuring beings with the hand, with a clod, with a stick, or with a knife. Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination (sugatiṃ), in the heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ). But if on the dissolution of the body, after death, he does not reappear in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, but instead comes back to the human state, then wherever he is reborn he is healthy (appābādho). This is the way, student, that leads to health (appābādhasaṃvattanikā), namely, one is not given to injuring beings with the hand, with a clod, with a stick, or with a knife.

mula_pali:
292. ‘‘Idha, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā kodhano hoti upāyāsabahulo. Appampi vutto samāno abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patiṭṭhīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati dubbaṇṇo hoti. Dubbaṇṇasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – kodhano hoti upāyāsabahulo; appampi vutto samāno abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patiṭṭhīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.

‘‘Idha pana, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā akkodhano hoti anupāyāsabahulo; bahumpi vutto samāno nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patiṭṭhīyati na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati pāsādiko hoti. Pāsādikasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – akkodhano hoti anupāyāsabahulo; bahumpi vutto samāno nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patiṭṭhīyati na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
mula_english:
292. “Here, student (māṇava), some man or woman is of an angry (kodhana) and irritable character;

even when criticised a little, he is offended (abhisajjati), becomes angry (kuppati), hostile (byāpajjati), and resentful (patiṭṭhīyati), and displays anger (kopañca), hate (dosañca), and bitterness (appaccayañca).
Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ).
But if instead he does not reappear, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ), but if instead he comes back to the human state (manussattaṃ), then wherever he is reborn (paccājāyati) he is ugly (dubbaṇṇo).
This is the way (paṭipadā), student (māṇava), that leads to ugliness (dubbaṇṇasaṃvattanikā), namely, one is of an angry (kodhana) and irritable character; even when criticised a little, he is offended (abhisajjati), becomes angry (kuppati), hostile (byāpajjati), and resentful (patiṭṭhīyati), and displays anger (kopañca), hate (dosañca), and bitterness (appaccayañca).

“But here, student (māṇava), some man or woman is not of an angry (akkodhana) and irritable character; even when criticised a lot, he is not offended (nābhisajjati), does not become angry (na kuppati), hostile (na byāpajjati), and resentful (na patiṭṭhīyati), and does not display anger (na kopañca), hate (na dosañca), and bitterness (na appaccayañca).
Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in a happy destination (sugatiṃ), in the heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ).
But if instead he does not reappear, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), in a happy destination (sugatiṃ), in the heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ), but if instead he comes back to the human state (manussattaṃ), then wherever he is reborn (paccājāyati) he is beautiful (pāsādiko).
This is the way (paṭipadā), student (māṇava), that leads to being beautiful (pāsādikasaṃvattanikā), namely, one is not of an angry (akkodhana) and irritable character; even when criticised a lot, he is not offended (nābhisajjati), does not become angry (na kuppati), hostile (na byāpajjati), and resentful (na patiṭṭhīyati), and does not display anger (na kopañca), hate (na dosañca), and bitterness (na appaccayañca).

mula_pali:
293. ‘‘Idha, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā issāmanako hoti; paralābhasakkāragarukāramānanavandanapūjanāsu issati upadussati issaṃ bandhati. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati appesakkho hoti. Appesakkhasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – issāmanako hoti; paralābhasakkāragarukāramānanavandanapūjanāsu issati upadussati issaṃ bandhati.

‘‘Idha pana, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā anissāmanako hoti; paralābhasakkāragarukāramānanavandanapūjanāsu na issati na upadussati na issaṃ bandhati. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati mahesakkho hoti. Mahesakkhasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava , paṭipadā yadidaṃ – anissāmanako hoti; paralābhasakkāragarukāramānanavandanapūjanāsu na issati na upadussati na issaṃ bandhati.
mula_english:
“Here, student, some man or woman is envious ( *īrṣyāmanaka*), one who envies, resents, and begrudges the gains ( *paralābha*), honour ( *satkāra*), respect ( *garukāra*), reverence ( *mānana*), salutations ( *vandana*), and veneration ( *pūjana*) received by others. Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body ( *kāyassa bhedā*), after death ( *paraṃ maraṇā*), he reappears in a state of deprivation ( *apāya*), in an unhappy destination ( *duggati*), in perdition ( *vinipāta*), even in hell ( *nirayaṃ upapajjati*). But if instead he comes back to the human state ( *manussattaṃ āgacchati*), then wherever he is reborn ( *yattha yattha paccājāyati*) he is uninfluential ( *appesakkho hoti*). This is the way, student, that leads to being uninfluential ( *appesakkhasaṃvattanikā*), namely, one is envious…towards the gains, honour, respect, reverence, salutations, and veneration received by others.

“But here, student, some man or woman is not envious (*anīrṣyāmanaka*), one who does not envy, resent, and begrudge the gains ( *paralābha*), honour ( *satkāra*), respect ( *garukāra*), reverence ( *mānana*), salutations ( *vandana*), and veneration ( *pūjana*) received by others. By his adopting such actions and putting them into effect, he reappears, on the dissolution of the body, after death, in a happy destination ( *sugati*), in the heavenly world ( *saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati*). But if on the dissolution of the body, after death, he does not reappear in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, but instead comes back to the human state ( *manussattaṃ āgacchati*), then wherever he is reborn he is influential ( *mahesakkho hoti*). This is the way, student, that leads to being influential, namely, one is not envious…towards the gains, honour, respect, reverence, salutations, and veneration received by others.
commentary_pali: 293. Ettha pana issāmanakoti issāsampayuttacitto. Upadussatīti issāvaseneva upakkosanto dussati. Issaṃ bandhatīti yavakalāpaṃ bandhanto viya yathā na nassati evaṃ bandhitvā viya ṭhapeti. Appesakkhoti appaparivāro, rattiṃ khitto viya saro na paññāyati, ucchiṭṭhahattho nisīditvā udakadāyakampi na labhati.
commentary_english:
Here, however, *issāmanako* means "one whose mind is associated with envy ( *īrsyā*)."

*Upadussati* means "he corrupts, scolding only through the power of envy ( *īrsyā*)."

*Issaṃ bandhati* means "he ties up envy ( *īrsyā*)"; just as one ties up a sheaf of barley so that it is not lost, so too he keeps it tied up, as it were.

*Appesakkho* means "with a small retinue"; like an arrow shot at night, he is not apparent; even sitting with a hand soiled with leftovers, he does not obtain a giver of water.

mula_pali:
294. ‘‘Idha, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā na dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati appabhogo hoti. Appabhogasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – na dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ.

‘‘Idha pana, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati mahābhogo hoti. Mahābhogasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ.
mula_english:
“Here, student, some man or woman does not give food, drink, clothing, carriages, garlands, scents, unguents, beds, dwelling, and lamps to recluses or *brāhmaṇas*. Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell. But if instead he comes back to the human state, then wherever he is reborn he is poor. This is the way, student, that leads to poverty, namely, one does not give food, drink, clothing, carriages, garlands, scents, unguents, beds, dwelling, and lamps to recluses or *brāhmaṇas*.

“But here, student, some man or woman gives food, drink, clothing, carriages, garlands, scents, unguents, beds, dwelling, and lamps to recluses or *brāhmaṇas*. Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world. But if instead he comes back to the human state, then wherever he is reborn he is wealthy. This is the way, student, that leads to wealth, namely, one gives food, drink, clothing, carriages, garlands, scents, unguents, beds, dwelling, and lamps to recluses or *brāhmaṇas*.
commentary_pali: 294.Nadātā hotīti macchariyavasena na dātā hoti. Tena kammenāti tena macchariyakammena.
commentary_english:
"""Not a giver,"" because of miserliness, he is not a giver.

""By that action,"" that is, by the action of miserliness."

mula_pali:
295. ‘‘Idha, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā thaddho hoti atimānī – abhivādetabbaṃ na abhivādeti, paccuṭṭhātabbaṃ na paccuṭṭheti, āsanārahassa na āsanaṃ deti, maggārahassa na maggaṃ deti, sakkātabbaṃ na sakkaroti, garukātabbaṃ na garukaroti, mānetabbaṃ na māneti, pūjetabbaṃ na pūjeti. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati nīcakulīno hoti. Nīcakulīnasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – thaddho hoti atimānī; abhivādetabbaṃ na abhivādeti, paccuṭṭhātabbaṃ na paccuṭṭheti, āsanārahassa na āsanaṃ deti, maggārahassa na maggaṃ deti, sakkātabbaṃ na sakkaroti, garukātabbaṃ na garukaroti, mānetabbaṃ na māneti, pūjetabbaṃ na pūjeti.

‘‘Idha pana, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā atthaddho hoti anatimānī; abhivādetabbaṃ abhivādeti, paccuṭṭhātabbaṃ paccuṭṭheti, āsanārahassa āsanaṃ deti, maggārahassa maggaṃ deti, sakkātabbaṃ sakkaroti, garukātabbaṃ garukaroti, mānetabbaṃ māneti, pūjetabbaṃ pūjeti. So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati uccākulīno hoti. Uccākulīnasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – atthaddho hoti anatimānī; abhivādetabbaṃ abhivādeti, paccuṭṭhātabbaṃ paccuṭṭheti, āsanārahassa āsanaṃ deti, maggārahassa maggaṃ deti, sakkātabbaṃ sakkaroti, garukātabbaṃ garukaroti, mānetabbaṃ māneti, pūjetabbaṃ pūjeti.
mula_english:
295. “Here, student, some man or woman is obstinate and arrogant; he does not pay homage to one who should receive homage, does not rise up for one in whose presence he should rise up, does not offer a seat to one who deserves a seat, does not make way for one for whom he should make way, and does not honour, respect, revere, and venerate one who should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated.

Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell.

But if instead he comes back to the human state, then wherever he is reborn he is low-born.

This is the way, student, that leads to low birth, namely, one is obstinate and arrogant… and does not honour, respect, revere, and venerate one who should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated.

“But here, student, some man or woman is not obstinate and arrogant; he pays homage to one who should receive homage, rises up for one in whose presence he should rise up, offers a seat to one who deserves a seat, makes way for one for whom he should make way, and honours, respects, reveres, and venerates one who should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated.

Because of performing and undertaking such action, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world.

But if instead he comes back to the human state, then wherever he is reborn he is high-born.

This is the way, student, that leads to high birth, namely, one is not obstinate and arrogant…and honours, respects, reveres, and venerates one who should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated.
commentary_pali: 295.Abhivādetabbanti abhivādanārahaṃ buddhaṃ vā paccekabuddhaṃ vā ariyasāvakaṃ vā. Paccuṭṭhātabbādīsupi eseva nayo. Imasmiṃ pana pañhavissajjane upapīḷakaupatthambhakakammāni na gahetabbāni. Na hi pavatte nīcakulinaṃ vā uccākulinaṃ vā sakkā kātuṃ, paṭisandhimeva pana niyāmetvā nīcakuliyaṃ kammaṃ nīcakule nibbatteti, uccākuliyaṃ kammaṃ uccākule.
commentary_english: " *Abhivādetabba* means one worthy of salutation, such as a Buddha, a Pratyekabuddha, or a noble disciple ( *ariyasāvaka*). The same method applies to *paccuṭṭhātabbā* and the like. In this question and answer, however, one should not take actions that are oppressive or supportive. For it is not possible to make someone of a low family or a high family once the process [of rebirth] has started; however, having determined rebirth, an action related to a low family produces [rebirth] in a low family, and an action related to a high family [produces rebirth] in a high family."

mula_pali:
296. ‘‘Idha, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā upasaṅkamitvā na paripucchitā hoti – ‘kiṃ, bhante, kusalaṃ, kiṃ akusalaṃ; kiṃ sāvajjaṃ, kiṃ anavajjaṃ; kiṃ sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ na sevitabbaṃ; kiṃ me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya hoti, kiṃ vā pana me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya hotī’ti? So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati duppañño hoti. Duppaññasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā upasaṅkamitvā na paripucchitā hoti – ‘kiṃ, bhante, kusalaṃ, kiṃ akusalaṃ; kiṃ sāvajjaṃ, kiṃ anavajjaṃ; kiṃ sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ na sevitabbaṃ ; kiṃ me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya hoti, kiṃ vā pana me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya hotī’’’ti?

‘‘Idha pana, māṇava, ekacco itthī vā puriso vā samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā upasaṅkamitvā paripucchitā hoti – ‘kiṃ, bhante, kusalaṃ, kiṃ akusalaṃ; kiṃ sāvajjaṃ, kiṃ anavajjaṃ; kiṃ sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ na sevitabbaṃ; kiṃ me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya hoti, kiṃ vā pana me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya hotī’ti? So tena kammena evaṃ samattena evaṃ samādinnena kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. No ce kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati, sace manussattaṃ āgacchati yattha yattha paccājāyati mahāpañño hoti. Mahāpaññasaṃvattanikā esā, māṇava, paṭipadā yadidaṃ – samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā upasaṅkamitvā paripucchitā hoti – ‘kiṃ, bhante, kusalaṃ, kiṃ akusalaṃ; kiṃ sāvajjaṃ, kiṃ anavajjaṃ; kiṃ sevitabbaṃ , kiṃ na sevitabbaṃ; kiṃ me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya hoti, kiṃ vā pana me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya hotī’’’ti?
mula_english:
“Here, young man, some woman or man does not approach a renunciate (*śramaṇa*) or a Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*) to ask: ‘Venerable sir (*bhante*), what is wholesome (*kuśala*)? What is unwholesome (*akuśala*)? What is blameworthy (*sāvajja*)? What is blameless (*anavajja*)? What should be cultivated (*sevitabba*)? What should not be cultivated (*na sevitabba*)? What action of mine will lead to harm and suffering for a long time? Or what action of mine will lead to welfare and happiness for a long time?’ So, by that action, thus completed, thus undertaken, on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*maraṇā*), he is reborn in a state of loss (*apāyaṃ*), a bad destination (*duggatiṃ*), a downfall (*vinipātaṃ*), and hell (*nirayaṃ*).

But if on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*maraṇā*), he is not reborn in a state of loss (*apāyaṃ*), a bad destination (*duggatiṃ*), a downfall (*vinipātaṃ*), and hell (*nirayaṃ*), but instead comes back to the human state (*manussattaṃ āgacchati*), then wherever he is reborn he is stupid (*duppañño*).

This is the way, young man, that leads to stupidity (*duppaññasaṃvattanikā*), namely, one does not approach a renunciate (*śramaṇa*) or Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*) to ask such questions: ‘Venerable sir (*bhante*), what is wholesome (*kuśala*)? What is unwholesome (*akuśala*)? What is blameworthy (*sāvajja*)? What is blameless (*anavajja*)? What should be cultivated (*sevitabba*)? What should not be cultivated (*na sevitabba*)? What action of mine will lead to harm and suffering for a long time? Or what action of mine will lead to welfare and happiness for a long time?’”

“But here, young man, some woman or man approaches a renunciate (*śramaṇa*) or a Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*) to ask: ‘Venerable sir (*bhante*), what is wholesome (*kuśala*)? What is unwholesome (*akuśala*)? What is blameworthy (*sāvajja*)? What is blameless (*anavajja*)? What should be cultivated (*sevitabba*)? What should not be cultivated (*na sevitabba*)? What action of mine will lead to harm and suffering for a long time? Or what action of mine will lead to welfare and happiness for a long time?’ So, by that action, thus completed, thus undertaken, on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*maraṇā*), he is reborn in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), a heavenly world (*saggaṃ*), a world (*lokaṃ*).

But if on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*maraṇā*), he is not reborn in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), a heavenly world (*saggaṃ*), a world (*lokaṃ*), but instead comes back to the human state (*manussattaṃ āgacchati*), then wherever he is reborn he is very wise (*mahāpañño*).

This is the way, young man, that leads to great wisdom (*mahāpaññasaṃvattanikā*), namely, one approaches a renunciate (*śramaṇa*) or Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*) to ask such questions: ‘Venerable sir (*bhante*), what is wholesome (*kuśala*)? What is unwholesome (*akuśala*)? What is blameworthy (*sāvajja*)? What is blameless (*anavajja*)? What should be cultivated (*sevitabba*)? What should not be cultivated (*na sevitabba*)? What action of mine will lead to harm and suffering for a long time? Or what action of mine will lead to welfare and happiness for a long time?’”
commentary_pali:
296.Na paripucchitā hotīti ettha pana aparipucchanena niraye na nibbattati. Aparipucchako pana ‘‘idaṃ kātabbaṃ, idaṃ na kātabba’’nti na jānāti, ajānanto kātabbaṃ na karoti, akātabbaṃ karoti. Tena niraye nibbattati, itaro sagge. Iti kho, māṇava…pe… yadidaṃ hīnappaṇītatāyāti satthā desanaṃ yathānusandhiṃ pāpesi. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷakammavibhaṅgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Subhasuttantipi vuccati.
commentary_english:
296. "One does not ask questions" - by not asking questions, one is not reborn in hell.

However, one who does not ask questions does not know what should be done and what should not be done; not knowing, one does not do what should be done, and does what should not be done.

By that, one is reborn in hell, the other in heaven.

"Thus, *māṇava*…pe… this is inferior and refined" - the teacher made the teaching reach in accordance with the connection.

The rest is clear throughout.

The *Papañcasūdanī*, commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya*.

The commentary on the *Cūḷakammavibhaṅgasutta* is finished.

It is also called the *Subhasuttanti*.

mula_pali:
297. ‘‘Iti kho, māṇava, appāyukasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā appāyukattaṃ upaneti, dīghāyukasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā dīghāyukattaṃ upaneti; bavhābādhasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā bavhābādhattaṃ upaneti, appābādhasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā appābādhattaṃ upaneti; dubbaṇṇasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā dubbaṇṇattaṃ upaneti, pāsādikasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā pāsādikattaṃ upaneti; appesakkhasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā appesakkhattaṃ upaneti, mahesakkhasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā mahesakkhattaṃ upaneti; appabhogasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā appabhogattaṃ upaneti, mahābhogasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā mahābhogattaṃ upaneti; nīcakulīnasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā nīcakulīnattaṃ upaneti, uccākulīnasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā uccākulīnattaṃ upaneti; duppaññasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā duppaññattaṃ upaneti, mahāpaññasaṃvattanikā paṭipadā mahāpaññattaṃ upaneti. Kammassakā, māṇava, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammappaṭisaraṇā. Kammaṃ satte vibhajati yadidaṃ – hīnappaṇītatāyā’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

Cūḷakammavibhaṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Thus, student, the practice that leads to short life brings about short life, the practice that leads to long life brings about long life; the practice that leads to much sickness brings about much sickness, the practice that leads to little sickness brings about little sickness; the practice that leads to ugliness brings about ugliness, the practice that leads to attractiveness brings about attractiveness; the practice that leads to little influence brings about little influence, the practice that leads to great influence brings about great influence; the practice that leads to little wealth brings about little wealth, the practice that leads to great wealth brings about great wealth; the practice that leads to low birth brings about low birth, the practice that leads to high birth brings about high birth; the practice that leads to little wisdom brings about little wisdom, the practice that leads to great wisdom brings about great wisdom.

"Beings are the owners of their karma (kammaṃ), student, the heirs of their karma (kamma), they originate from karma (kamma), are bound to karma (kamma), have karma (kamma) as their refuge.

It is karma (kammaṃ) that distinguishes beings as inferior (hīnappaṇītatā) and superior."

When this was said, Subha, the young man, Todeyya's son, said this to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ): “Excellent, Master Gotama, excellent, Master Gotama! Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or hold up a lamp in the dark, so that those with eyes might see forms—in the same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama.

I go to the revered Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma (dhammañca), and to the Sangha (bhikkhusaṅghañca)."

"May the revered Gotama accept me as a lay follower (upāsakaṃ) who has gone for refuge (saraṇaṃ gata) from this day forth, as long as life lasts."

The Cūḷakammavibhaṅgasuttaṃ is finished, the fifth.

mula_pali: 298. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā samiddhi araññakuṭikāyaṃ viharati. Atha kho potaliputto paribbājako jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yenāyasmā samiddhi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā samiddhinā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho potaliputto paribbājako āyasmantaṃ samiddhiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso samiddhi, samaṇassa gotamassa sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘moghaṃ kāyakammaṃ moghaṃ vacīkammaṃ, manokammameva sacca’nti. Atthi ca sā atthi cesā (sī. ka.) samāpatti yaṃ samāpattiṃ samāpanno na kiñci vediyatī’’ti? ‘‘Mā hevaṃ, āvuso potaliputta, avaca; (mā hevaṃ, āvuso potaliputta, avaca;) ( ) syā. kaṃ. potthakesu natthi mā bhagavantaṃ abbhācikkhi. Na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṃ. Na hi bhagavā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘moghaṃ kāyakammaṃ moghaṃ vacīkammaṃ, manokammameva sacca’nti. Atthi ca kho atthi ceva kho (sī. ka.) sā, āvuso, samāpatti yaṃ samāpattiṃ samāpanno na kiñci vediyatī’’ti. ‘‘Kīvaciraṃ pabbajitosi, āvuso samiddhī’’ti? ‘‘Na ciraṃ, āvuso! Tīṇi vassānī’’ti. ‘‘Ettha dāni mayaṃ there bhikkhū kiṃ vakkhāma, yatra hi nāma evaṃnavo bhikkhu navakena bhikkhunā (ka.) satthāraṃ parirakkhitabbaṃ maññissati. Sañcetanikaṃ, āvuso samiddhi, kammaṃ katvā kāyena vācāya manasā kiṃ so vediyatī’’ti? ‘‘Sañcetanikaṃ, āvuso potaliputta, kammaṃ katvā kāyena vācāya manasā dukkhaṃ so vediyatī’’ti. Atha kho potaliputto paribbājako āyasmato samiddhissa bhāsitaṃ neva abhinandi nappaṭikkosi; anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
mula_english:
298. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

At that time the venerable Samiddhi was staying in a forest hut.

Then the wanderer Potaliputta, while wandering and walking for exercise, went to the venerable Samiddhi and exchanged greetings with him.

Having concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, the wanderer Potaliputta said to the venerable Samiddhi: "Face to face with the *samaṇa* Gotama, friend Samiddhi, I have heard and learned, face to face it was accepted: 'Vain is bodily action, vain is verbal action, only mental action is real.'"

"But, friend, is there an attainment on entering which one does not feel anything at all?"

"No, friend Potaliputta, do not speak thus; do not misrepresent the Blessed One.

It is not right to misrepresent the Blessed One.

The Blessed One would not say: ‘Vain is bodily action, vain is verbal action, only mental action is real.’

But there is, friend, an attainment on entering which one does not feel anything at all."

"How long is it, friend Samiddhi, since you went forth?" "Not long, friend! Three years."

"What shall we say now to the elder *bhikkhus*, when a bhikkhu so new thinks the Teacher must be defended?

Having done an intentional action by way of body, speech, or mind, friend Samiddhi, what does one feel?" "Having done an intentional action by way of body, speech, or mind, friend Potaliputta, one feels suffering ( *duḥkha*)."

Then, neither approving nor disapproving of the venerable Samiddhi’s words, the wanderer Potaliputta rose from his seat and departed.
commentary_pali:
298.Evaṃme sutanti mahākammavibhaṅgasuttaṃ. Tattha moghanti tucchaṃ aphalaṃ. Saccanti tathaṃ bhūtaṃ. Idañca etena na sammukhā sutaṃ, upālisutte (ma. ni. 2.56) pana – ‘‘manokammaṃ mahāsāvajjataraṃ paññapemi pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā, no tathā kāyakammaṃ no tathā vacīkamma’’nti bhagavatā vuttaṃ atthi, sā kathā titthiyānaṃ antare pākaṭā jātā, taṃ gahetvā esa vadati. Atthi ca sā samāpattīti idaṃ – ‘‘kathaṃ nu kho, bho, abhisaññānirodho hotī’’ti poṭṭhapādasutte (dī. ni. 1.406 ādayo) uppannaṃ abhisaññānirodhakathaṃ sandhāya vadati. Na kiñci vediyatīti ekavedanampi na vediyati. Atthi ca khoti thero nirodhasamāpattiṃ sandhāya anujānāti. Parirakkhitabbanti garahato mocanena rakkhitabbaṃ. Sañcetanā assa atthīti sañcetanikaṃ, sābhisandhikaṃ sañcetanikakammaṃ katvāti attho. Dukkhaṃ soti thero ‘‘akusalameva sandhāya paribbājako pucchatī’’ti saññāya evaṃ vadati.

Dassanampi kho ahanti bhagavā caturaṅgepi andhakāre samantā yojanaṭṭhāne tilamattampi saṅkhāraṃ maṃsacakkhunāva passati, ayañca paribbājako na dūre gāvutamattabbhantare vasati, kasmā bhagavā evamāhāti? Samāgamadassanaṃ sandhāyevamāha.

Dassanampi kho aha
commentary_english:
298. Thus, I have heard: the Great Discourse on the Analysis of Action.

There, *mogha* means empty, fruitless.

*sacca* means truly, factually.

Moreover, this was not heard face to face by this person, [but is found] in the Upāli Discourse (Majjhima Nikāya 2.56): "I proclaim mental action (*manokamma*) to be more blameworthy than the performance or the arising of evil action; not so is bodily action (*kāyakamma*), not so is verbal action (*vacīkamma*)," so the Blessed One said. That talk became well-known among the sectarians, and taking it, this one speaks.

*atthi ca sā samāpattī*: This is with reference to the question, "How, indeed, does the cessation of perception (*abhisaññānirodha*) occur?" in the Poṭṭhapāda Sutta (Dīgha Nikāya 1.406 ff.), [which] speaks with reference to the arising of the discussion on the cessation of perception.

*na kiñci vediyatī* means he does not experience even a single feeling.

*atthi ca kho*: The elder approves with reference to the cessation attainment (*nirodhasamāpatti*).

*parirakkhitabba* means it should be protected by freeing [one] from blame.

*sañcetanikaṃ*: Because there is intention (*sañcetanā*) in him, [it is called] intentional. It means having done intentional action with purpose.

*dukkhaṃ so*: The elder speaks thus with perception (*saññāya*), thinking, "The wanderer is asking only with reference to unwholesome [action] (*akusala*)."

*dassanampi kho aha*: The Blessed One sees even a sesame seed-sized aggregate (*saṅkhāra*) in complete darkness all around a *yojana* distance with his physical eye (*maṃsacakkhu*). And this wanderer does not live far away, within a *gāvuta*. Why does the Blessed One say this? He speaks thus with reference to the vision of the assembly (*samāgamadassanaṃ*).

*dassanampi kho aha*

mula_pali:
299. Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi acirapakkante potaliputte paribbājake yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā samiddhi yāvatako ahosi potaliputtena paribbājakena saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo taṃ sabbaṃ āyasmato ānandassa ārocesi.

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ samiddhiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘atthi kho idaṃ, āvuso samiddhi, kathāpābhataṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Āyāmāvuso samiddhi, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ bhagavato ārocessāma. Yathā no bhagavā byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho āyasmā samiddhi āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi.

Atha kho āyasmā ca ānando āyasmā ca samiddhi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando yāvatako ahosi āyasmato samiddhissa potaliputtena paribbājakena saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavato ārocesi. Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘dassanampi kho ahaṃ, ānanda, potaliputtassa paribbājakassa nābhijānāmi, kuto panevarūpaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ? Iminā ca, ānanda, samiddhinā moghapurisena potaliputtassa paribbājakassa vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho ekaṃsena byākato’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sace pana kiṃ pana (ka.), bhante, āyasmatā samiddhinā idaṃ sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – yaṃ kiñci vedayitaṃ taṃ dukkhasmi’’nti.

kiṃ pana (ka.)
mula_english:
Then, after the wanderer Potaliputta had recently departed, the venerable Samiddhi approached the venerable Ānanda; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the venerable Ānanda. When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. Seated to one side, the venerable Samiddhi reported to the venerable Ānanda his entire conversation with the wanderer Potaliputta.

When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the venerable Samiddhi: “Friend Samiddhi, this conversation should be told to the Blessed One. Come, friend Samiddhi, let us approach the Blessed One; having approached, we shall report this matter to the Blessed One. As the Blessed One explains it to us, so should we retain it in mind.” “Yes, friend,” the venerable Samiddhi replied to the venerable Ānanda.

Then the venerable Ānanda and the venerable Samiddhi approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side. Seated to one side, the venerable Ānanda reported to the Blessed One his entire conversation—that which had occurred with the venerable Samiddhi and the wanderer Potaliputta.

When this was said, the Blessed One said to the venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, I don’t even recall having seen the wanderer Potaliputta, so how could there have been any conversation with him? And this question, Ānanda, which should have been answered with a qualified explanation, has been answered categorically by the fool Samiddhi to the wanderer Potaliputta.”

When this was said, the venerable Udāyī said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, perhaps the venerable Samiddhi spoke thus referring to the principle: ‘Whatever is felt is suffering.’”
commentary_pali: 299.Udāyīti lāludāyī. Taṃ dukkhasminti sabbaṃ taṃ dukkhameva. Iti imaṃ vaṭṭadukkhaṃ kilesadukkhaṃ saṅkhāradukkhaṃ sandhāya ‘‘sace bhāsitaṃ bhaveyya bhagavā’’ti pucchati.
commentary_english:
299. _udāyīti lāludāyī_.
_taṃ dukkhasmi_ means "all that is suffering."
Thus, referring to this suffering of the round (_vaṭṭadukkhaṃ_), the suffering of defilements (_kilesadukkhaṃ_), and the suffering of formations (_saṅkhāradukkhaṃ_), he asks, "If the Blessed One were to speak, what would he say?"

mula_pali:
300. Atha kho evaṃ vutte (syā. kaṃ.) bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘passasi no tvaṃ, ānanda, imassa udāyissa moghapurisassa ummaṅgaṃ ummaggaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), umaṅgaṃ (ka.)? Aññāsiṃ kho ahaṃ, ānanda – ‘idānevāyaṃ udāyī moghapuriso ummujjamāno ayoniso ummujjissatī’ti. Ādiṃyeva ādisova (sī. pī.), ādiyeva (ka.), ānanda, potaliputtena paribbājakena tisso vedanā pucchitā. Sacāyaṃ, ānanda, samiddhi moghapuriso potaliputtassa paribbājakassa evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākareyya – ‘sañcetanikaṃ, āvuso potaliputta, kammaṃ katvā kāyena vācāya manasā sukhavedanīyaṃ sukhaṃ so vedayati; sañcetanikaṃ, āvuso potaliputta, kammaṃ katvā kāyena vācāya manasā dukkhavedanīyaṃ dukkhaṃ so vedayati; sañcetanikaṃ, āvuso potaliputta, kammaṃ katvā kāyena vācāya manasā adukkhamasukhavedanīyaṃ adukkhamasukhaṃ so vedayatī’ti. Evaṃ byākaramāno kho, ānanda, samiddhi moghapuriso potaliputtassa paribbājakassa sammā (byākaramāno) ( ) natthi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) byākareyya. Api ca, ānanda, ke ca keci (ka.) aññatitthiyā paribbājakā bālā abyattā ke ca tathāgatassa mahākammavibhaṅgaṃ jānissanti? Sace tumhe, ānanda, suṇeyyātha tathāgatassa mahākammavibhaṅgaṃ vibhajantassā’’ti.

‘‘Etassa, bhagavā, kālo, etassa, sugata, kālo yaṃ bhagavā mahākammavibhaṅgaṃ vibhajeyya . Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hānanda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Cattārome, ānanda, puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame cattāro? Idhānanda, ekacco puggalo idha pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhi hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati.

‘‘Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo idha pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhi hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati.

‘‘Idhānanda, ekacco puggalo idha pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhi hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati.

‘‘Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo idha pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhi hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati.
mula_english:
300. Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda: “See, Ānanda, how this misguided man Udāyin interferes. I knew, Ānanda, that this misguided man Udāyin would unduly interfere right now.”

From the start the wanderer Potaliputta had asked Ānanda about the three kinds of feeling.

This misguided man Samiddhi would have answered the wanderer Potaliputta rightly if, when asked thus, he would have explained: ‘Friend Potaliputta, having done an intentional action by way of body, speech, or mind whose result is to be felt as pleasant, one feels pleasure. Having done an intentional action by way of body, speech, or mind whose result is to be felt as painful, one feels pain. Having done an intentional action by way of body, speech, or mind whose result is to be felt as neither painful nor pleasant, one feels what is neither painful nor pleasant.’

And again, Ānanda, who are these foolish, thoughtless wanderers of other sects, that they could understand the *Tathāgata’s* great exposition of action? If you, Ānanda, were to listen to the *Tathāgata* expounding the great exposition of action!”

“This is the time, Blessed One, this is the time, Sublime One, for the Blessed One to expound the great exposition of action. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the *bhikkhus* will remember it.”

“Then listen, Ānanda, and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“So be it, O Lord.” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“There are these four kinds of individuals existing in the world, Ānanda. Which four? Here, Ānanda, some person kills living beings, takes what is not given, misconducts himself in sensual pleasures, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, gossips; he is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and holds wrong view. On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, perdition, even in hell (apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati).

“But here some person kills living beings, takes what is not given, misconducts himself in sensual pleasures, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, gossips; he is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and holds wrong view. On the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world (sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati).

Here some person abstains from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, from misconduct in sensual pleasures, from false speech, from malicious speech, from harsh speech, from gossip; he is not covetous, his mind is without ill will, and he holds right view. At the dissolution of the body after death, a good rebirth occurs in a heavenly world (sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati).
Here:
"Here, Ānanda, some person abstains from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti), from taking what is not given (adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti), from misconduct in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti), from false speech (musāvādā paṭivirato hoti), from malicious speech (pisuṇāya vācāya) he abstains, from harsh speech (pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti), from gossip (samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti); he is without covetousness (anabhijjhālu hoti), his mind is without ill will (abyāpannacitto hoti), and he holds right view (sammādiṭṭhi hoti).

On the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in the fall (vinipātaṃ), in hell (nirayaṃ) .
commentary_pali:
300.Ummaṅganti pañhāummaṅgaṃ. Ummujjamānoti sīsaṃ nīharamāno. Ayoniso ummujjissatīti anupāyena sīsaṃ nīharissati. Idañca pana bhagavā jānanto neva dibbacakkhunā na cetopariyañāṇena na sabbaññutañāṇena jāni, adhippāyeneva pana aññāsi. Kathentassa hi adhippāyo nāma suvijāno hoti, kathetukāmo gīvaṃ paggaṇhāti, hanukaṃ cāleti, mukhamassa phandati, sannisīdituṃ na sakkoti. Bhagavā tassa taṃ ākāraṃ disvā ‘‘ayaṃ udāyī sannisīdituṃ na sakkoti, yaṃ abhūtaṃ, tadeva kathessatī’’ti oloketvāva aññāsi. Ādiṃ yevātiādimhiyeva. Tisso vedanāti ‘‘kiṃ so vediyatī’’ti? Pucchantena ‘‘tisso vedanā pucchāmī’’ti evaṃ vavatthapetvāva tisso vedanā pucchitā. Sukhavedaniyanti sukhavedanāya paccayabhūtaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

Ettha ca kāmāvacarakusalato somanassasahagatacittasampayuttā catasso cetanā, heṭṭhā tikajjhānacetanāti evaṃ paṭisandhipavattesu sukhavedanāya jananato sukhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ nāma. Kāmāvacarañcettha paṭisandhiyaṃyeva ekantena sukhaṃ janeti, pavatte iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe adukkhamasukhampi.

sukhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ

Akusalacetanā paṭisandhipavattesu dukkhasseva jananato dukkhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ nāma. Kāyadvāre pavatteyeva cetaṃ ekantena dukkhaṃ janeti, aññattha adukkhamasukhampi, sā pana vedanā aniṭṭhāniṭṭhamajjhattesuyeva ārammaṇesu uppajjanato dukkhātveva saṅkhaṃ gatā.

dukkhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ

Kāmāvacarakusalato pana upekkhāsahagatacittasampayuttā catasso cetanā, rūpāvacarakusalato catutthajjhānacetanāti evaṃ paṭisandhipavattesu tatiyavedanāya jananato adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ nāma. Ettha ca kāmāvacaraṃ paṭisandhiyaṃyeva ekantena adukkhamasukhaṃ janeti, pavatte iṭṭhārammaṇe sukhampi. Apica sukhavedaniyakammaṃ paṭisandhipavattivasena vaṭṭati, tathā adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ, dukkhavedaniyaṃ pavattivaseneva vaṭṭati. Etassa pana vasena sabbaṃ pavattivaseneva vaṭṭati.

adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ

Etassa bhagavāti thero tathāgatena mahākammavibhaṅgakathanatthaṃ ālayo dassito, tathāgataṃ yācitvā mahākammavibhaṅgañāṇaṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa pākaṭaṃ karissāmīti cintetvā anusandhikusalatāya evamāha. Tattha mahākammavibhaṅganti mahākammavibhajanaṃ. Katame cattāro…pe… idhānanda, ekacco puggalo…pe… nirayaṃ upapajjatīti idaṃ na mahākammavibhaṅgañāṇabhājanaṃ, mahākammavibhaṅgañāṇabhājanatthāya pana mātikāṭṭhapanaṃ.

Etassa bhagavā mahākammavibhaṅga Katame cattāro…pe… idhānanda, ekacco puggalo…pe… nirayaṃ upapajjatī
commentary_english:
300. *Ummaṅga* means "question-ummaṅga."
*Ummujjamāno* means "raising the head."
*Ayoniso ummujjissatī* means "he will raise his head unwisely," that is, "he will raise his head without a means."
Moreover, the Blessed One, knowing this, understood not by means of the divine eye, nor by means of knowing the minds of others, nor by means of all-knowing knowledge, but merely by intention.
Indeed, the intention of one who speaks is easily understood: One who desires to speak raises his neck, moves his jaw, his face throbs, he is unable to sit down.
The Blessed One, seeing that appearance of him, recognized, "This Udāyī is unable to sit down; whatever is unreal, that he will say," having looked [at him].
*Ādiṃ yevā* means *ādimhiyeva*.
*Tisso vedanā* means "What does he experience?" To one who asks, "I ask about three sensations," thus, having determined, three sensations are asked about.
*Sukhavedaniya* means "having pleasure as its cause."
The same rule applies to the rest.

Moreover, here, the four volitions associated with pleasure-tinged consciousness, wholesome in the desire realm, and the volitions of the three lower *jhānas*, thus, because of generating pleasant sensation in rebirth and in continued existence, it is called *sukhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ*, "karma ripening as pleasure."
Moreover, here, that which is of the desire realm generates only pleasure with certainty at the moment of rebirth, but in continued existence, it [may generate] what is neither painful nor pleasant in an agreeable or neutral object.

*Sukhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ*: Unwholesome volitions, because of generating only pain in rebirth and in continued existence, is called *dukkhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ*, "karma ripening as pain."
Indeed, in the case of the body-door, that consciousness generates only pain with certainty, but elsewhere, it [may generate] what is neither painful nor pleasant, but that sensation, because of arising in only disagreeable, disagreeable-neutral objects, has gone to reckoning as "pain."

*Dukkhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ*: Moreover, here, the four volitions associated with equanimity-tinged consciousness, wholesome in the desire realm, and the volitions of the fourth *jhāna*, wholesome in the form realm, thus, because of generating the third sensation in rebirth and in continued existence, it is called *adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ*, "karma ripening as neither pain nor pleasure."
Moreover, here, that which is of the desire realm generates only what is neither painful nor pleasant with certainty at the moment of rebirth, but in continued existence, it [may generate] even pleasure in an agreeable object.
Moreover, *sukhavedaniyakammaṃ* arises dependent on rebirth and continued existence, so does *adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ*, *dukkhavedaniyaṃ* arises only dependent on continued existence.
But by means of this, all arises only dependent on continued existence.

*Adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ kammaṃ* The Elder (thera), *Etassa bhagavā*, by the Tathāgata, the basis was shown for the purpose of speaking about the Great Analysis of Karma (*mahākammavibhaṅga*). Having requested the Tathāgata [to explain it], thinking, "I will make the knowledge of the Great Analysis of Karma (*mahākammavibhaṅga-ñāṇa*) manifest to the monastic community (*bhikkhusaṅgha*)," because of skill in connecting [the discourse], he said thus:
There, *mahākammavibhaṅga* means "great analysis of karma."
*Katame cattāro…pe… idhānanda, ekacco puggalo…pe… nirayaṃ upapajjatī* "Which are the four... to hell" This is not a vessel for knowledge of the Great Analysis of Karma (*mahākammavibhaṅga-ñāṇa*), but the laying down of a matrix for the sake of the vessel of knowledge of the Great Analysis of Karma (*mahākammavibhaṅga-ñāṇa*).

*Etassa bhagavā mahākammavibhaṅga katame cattāro…pe… idhānanda, ekacco puggalo…pe… nirayaṃ upapajjatī*

mula_english:
301. “Here, Ānanda, a certain *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa*, by means of ardour, endeavour, devotion, diligence, and right attention, attains such concentration of mind (*ceto-samādhi*) that, when his mind is concentrated, with the divine eye (*dibba-cakkhu*), which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees that person here who kills living beings, takes what is not given, engages in misconduct in sexual pleasures, speaks falsehood, speaks malicious speech, speaks harsh speech, speaks frivolous speech, is full of covetousness, is of corrupted mind, and holds wrong view, and he sees that on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), he has reappeared in a state of deprivation (*apāya*), in an unhappy destination (*duggati*), in perdition (*vinipāta*), even in hell (*nirayaṃ upapannaṃ*).

He says thus: ‘Indeed (*kira*), sir (*bho*), there are evil actions (*pāpakāni kammāni*), there is result (*vipāko*) of misconduct (*duccaritassa*).’
I saw a person here who kills living beings, takes what is not given… and holds wrong view, and I see that on the dissolution of the body, after death, he has reappeared in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell.’
He says thus: ‘On the dissolution of the body, after death, everyone who kills living beings, takes what is not given… and holds wrong view reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell.’
Those who know thus know rightly; those who think otherwise are mistaken.’
Thus he obstinately adheres to what he himself has known, seen, and discovered, insisting: ‘Only this is true (*saccaṃ*), anything else is wrong.’

commentary_pali: 301.Idhānanda, ekacco samaṇo vāti pāṭiyekko anusandhi. Idañhi bhagavā – ‘‘dibbacakkhukā samaṇabrāhmaṇā idaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā imaṃ paccayaṃ labhitvā idaṃ dassanaṃ gaṇhantī’’ti pakāsanatthaṃ ārabhi. Tattha ātappantiādīni pañcapi vīriyasseva nāmāni. Cetosamādhinti dibbacakkhusamādhiṃ. Passatīti ‘‘so satto kuhiṃ nibbatto’’ti olokento passati. Ye aññathāti ye ‘‘dasannaṃ kusalānaṃ kammapathānaṃ pūritattā nirayaṃ upapajjatī’’ti jānanti, micchā tesaṃ ñāṇanti vadati. Iminā nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo. Viditanti pākaṭaṃ. Thāmasāti diṭṭhithāmena. Parāmāsāti diṭṭhiparāmāsena. Abhinivissa voharatīti adhiṭṭhahitvā ādiyitvā voharati.
commentary_english:
301.
Here, Ānanda, *ekacco samaṇo vā* means *pāṭiyekko anusandhi*.
Because the Blessed One began to declare, "Monks and *brāhmaṇas* with the divine eye, having made this their object, having obtained this condition, grasp this vision."
There, *ātappa*, etc., are all names for energy (*vīriya*).
*cetosamādhi* means divine-eye concentration (*dibbacakkhusamādhiṃ*).
*passatī* means "He sees, looking around, 'Where was that being reborn?'"
*ye aññathā* means those who know that "due to the completion of the ten skillful courses of action, one is reborn in hell" speak falsely of their knowledge (*ñāṇa*).
In this way, the meaning is to be understood in all cases.
*vidita* means evident (*pākaṭaṃ*).
*thāmasā* means with fortitude of view (*diṭṭhithāmena*).
*parāmāsā* means with adherence to views (*diṭṭhiparāmāsena*).
*abhinivissa voharatī* means having resolved, having undertaken, he speaks (*adhiṭṭhahitvā ādiyitvā voharati*).

mula_english:
302. “Therein, Ānanda, when a *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* says thus: ‘Indeed, sir, there are evil actions (*pāpakāni kammaṇi*), there is result (*vipāka*) of misconduct (*duccarita*)’—this I grant him. And when he says thus: ‘I saw a person here who killed living beings (*prāṇātipātin*)…and held wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhin*), [and] on the dissolution (*bhedā*) of the body (*kāyassa*), after death (*maraṇā*), I see that he has reappeared in a state of deprivation (*apāya*), in an unhappy destination (*duggati*), in perdition (*vinipāta*), even in hell (*niraya*)’—this too I grant him. But when he says thus: ‘Everyone who kills living beings…and holds wrong view, on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, even in hell’—this I do not grant him. And when he says thus: ‘Those who know thus know rightly; those who know otherwise, their knowledge (*ñāṇa*) is wrong’—this too I do not grant him. And when he insists, adhering firmly to just what he himself has known (*ñātaṃ*), himself has seen (*diṭṭhaṃ*), himself has understood (*viditaṃ*) saying: ‘Only this is true, anything else is worthless’—this too I do not grant him.

Why is that? Because, Ānanda, the *Tathāgata*'s knowledge (*ñāṇaṃ*) of the great exposition of action (*mahākammavibhaṅge*) is otherwise.

commentary_pali: 302.Tatrānandāti idampi na mahākammavibhaṅgañāṇassa bhājanaṃ, atha khvāssa mātikāṭṭhapanameva. Ettha pana etesaṃ dibbacakkhukānaṃ vacane ettakā anuññātā, ettakā ananuññātāti idaṃ dassitaṃ. Tattha tatrāti tesu catūsu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu. Idamassāti idaṃ vacanaṃ assa. Aññathāti aññenākārena. Iti imesaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ vāde dvīsu ṭhānesu anuññātā, tīsu ananuññātāti evaṃ sabbattha anuññā nānuññā veditabbā.
commentary_english: 302. tatrānandāti Furthermore, this is not a receptacle of the great classification of knowledge of action (mahākammavibhaṅgañāṇassa), but rather merely the establishment of the matrix (mātikāṭṭhapana). Here, in the speech of those with divine eyes (dibbacakkhukānaṃ), so many are permitted (anuññātā), so many are unpermitted (ananuññātā)—this is shown. There, tatrāti, among those four ascetics and Brahmins (samaṇabrāhmaṇesu). idamassāti, this speech is his (vacanaṃ assa). aññathāti, in another way (aññenākārena). Thus, in the argument (vāde) of these ascetics and Brahmins (samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ), in two places (dvīsu ṭhānesu) they are permitted (anuññātā), in three (tīsu) they are unpermitted (ananuññātā). Thus, everywhere, permission (anuññā) and non-permission (nānuññā) should be understood (veditabbā).

‘‘Iti kho, ānanda, atthi kammaṃ abhabbaṃ abhabbābhāsaṃ, atthi kammaṃ abhabbaṃ bhabbābhāsaṃ, atthi kammaṃ bhabbañceva bhabbābhāsañca, atthi kammaṃ bhabbaṃ abhabbābhāsa’’nti.

“Therein, Ānanda, as to the person here who kills living beings, takes what is not given… and holds wrong view ( *mithyādṛṣṭi*), on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, perdition, even in hell (*apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati*): either earlier he did an evil action to be felt as painful, or later he did an evil action to be felt as painful, or at the time of death he acquired and undertook wrong view (*mithyādṛṣṭi samattā samādinnā*).

Because of that, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, perdition, even in hell (*apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati*).

But since he has here killed living beings, taken what is not given… and held wrong view, he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

“Therein, Ānanda, as to the person here who kills living beings, takes what is not given… and holds wrong view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*), on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world (*sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati*): either earlier he did a good action to be felt as pleasant, or later he did a good action to be felt as pleasant, or at the time of death he acquired and undertook right view (*sammādiṭṭhi samattā samādinnā*).

Because of that, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he has reappeared in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world (*sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati*).

But since he has here killed living beings, takes what is not given… and held wrong view, he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

“Therein, Ānanda, as to the person here who abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given… and holds right view ( *sammādiṭṭhi*), on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world (*sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati*): either earlier he did a good action to be felt as pleasant, or later he did a good action to be felt as pleasant, or at the time of death he acquired and undertook right view (*sammādiṭṭhi samattā samādinnā*).

Because of that, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he has reappeared in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world (*sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati*).

And since he has here abstained from killing living beings, abstained from taking what is not given… and held right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

“Therein, Ānanda, as to the person here who abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given… and holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), on the dissolution of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, perdition, even in hell (*apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati*): either earlier he did an evil action to be felt as painful, or later he did an evil action to be felt as painful, or at the time of death he acquired and undertook wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi samattā samādinnā*).

Because of that, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, perdition, even in hell (*apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati*).

And since he has here abstained from killing living beings, abstained from taking what is not given…and held right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), he will experience the result of that either here and now, or in his next rebirth, or in some subsequent existence.

“Thus, Ānanda, there is action that is incapable of good result and appears incapable; there is action that is incapable of good result and appears capable; there is action that is capable of good result and appears capable; and there is action that is capable of good result and appears incapable.”

Thus spoke the Lord. The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Great Analysis of Action *sūtra*, the sixth, is finished.

303. Evaṃ dibbacakkhukānaṃ vacane anuññā ca ananuññā ca dassetvā idāni mahākammavibhaṅgañāṇaṃ vibhajanto tatrānanda, yvāyaṃ puggalotiādimāha.

Pubbe vāssa taṃ kataṃ hotīti yaṃ iminā dibbacakkhukena kammaṃ karonto diṭṭho, tato pubbe kataṃ. Pubbe katenapi hi niraye nibbattati, pacchā katenapi nibbattati, maraṇakāle vā pana – ‘‘khando seṭṭho sivo seṭṭho, pitāmaho seṭṭho, issarādīhi vā loko visaṭṭho’’tiādinā micchādassanenapi nibbattateva. Diṭṭheva dhammeti yaṃ tattha diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ hoti, tassa diṭṭheva dhamme, yaṃ upapajjavedanīyaṃ, tassa upapajjitvā, yaṃ aparāpariyavedanīyaṃ, tassa aparasmiṃ pariyāye vipākaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.

commentary_english:
303. Thus, having shown the permission and non-permission in the words of those with divine eyes, now, while distinguishing the knowledge of the great division of karma, [he] says, "There, Ānanda, that person..." etc.

"Formerly, that was done by him," means that which was seen by this divine-eyed one doing the action; before that, it was done.

Having been done formerly, he is reborn in hell; having been done afterward, he is reborn; at the time of death, or even by wrong views such as, "Khandha is the best, Śiva is the best, the grandfather is the best, the world is scattered by Īśvara," he is reborn.

"In the seen Dharma" means that which is felt as immediately ripening, for him, it is in the seen Dharma; that which is to be experienced in rebirth, for him, having been reborn; that which is to be experienced in a subsequent life, for him, in a subsequent cycle, he experiences the result.

Formerly, that was done by him; in the seen Dharma. Thus, this renunciate or *brāhmaṇa* saw one mass of karma and one mass of result; the perfectly awakened one saw with this unseen [faculty] three masses of karma and two masses of result.

With this seen [faculty], and with the unseen, he saw four masses of karma and three masses of result.

These seven bases are called the knowledge of analysis of great *karma* of the *Tathāgata*.

In the second instance, nothing was seen by the divine-eyed one, but the *Tathāgata* saw three masses of *karma* and two masses of result.

These five individual bases are called the knowledge of analysis of great *karma* of the *Tathāgata*.

The same method applies in the remaining two instances.

"Incapable" means devoid of what has come to be, unwholesome.

"Seeming incapable" means it seems incapable; it overcomes, it rejects, this is the meaning.

Indeed, in much unwholesome action that has been accumulated, strong action, having repelled the result of weak action, creates an opportunity for its own result; this is both incapable and seeming incapable.

But having accumulated wholesome action, and near [death] unwholesome action has been done, that, having repelled the result of the wholesome, creates an opportunity for its own result; this is incapable, seeming capable.

Even in much wholesome action having been accumulated, strong action, having repelled the result of weak action, creates an opportunity for its own result; this is both capable and seeming capable.

But having accumulated unwholesome action, and near [death] wholesome action has been done, that, having repelled the result of the unwholesome, creates an opportunity for its own result; this is capable, seeming incapable.

Incapable, seeming incapable. Moreover, the meaning here should be understood in terms of the mode of presentation.

Indeed, it is said, "Because it seems incapable, it presents as incapable;" [this is] seeming incapable.

There, in the manner of "That person here is a killer of living beings," four persons are spoken of; among them, the action of the first is incapable and seeming incapable; because it is unwholesome, it is incapable, and because of his rebirth in hell, there, having become the cause of rebirth, the unwholesome arises.

The action of the second is incapable, seeming capable; because it is unwholesome, it is incapable.

But because of his rebirth in heaven, the wholesome, having become the cause of rebirth in heaven for those of other sects, arises.

The same method applies in the other two kinds of action.

The rest is clear everywhere.

Seeming incapable.

The commentary on the Great Discourse on the Division of Karma in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya*, is finished.

304. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘saḷāyatanavibhaṅgaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘‘Cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni veditabbāni, cha bāhirāni āyatanāni veditabbāni, cha viññāṇakāyā veditabbā, cha phassakāyā veditabbā, aṭṭhārasa manopavicārā veditabbā, chattiṃsa sattapadā veditabbā, tatra idaṃ nissāya idaṃ pajahatha, tayo satipaṭṭhānā yadariyo sevati yadariyo sevamāno satthā gaṇamanusāsitumarahati, so vuccati yoggācariyānaṃ yogācariyānaṃ (ka.) anuttaro purisadammasārathī’ti – ayamuddeso saḷāyatanavibhaṅgassa.

yogācariyānaṃ (ka.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Anāthapindika’s monastery, in the Jeta Grove, near Sāvatthi.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks (saying): “Monks!”

“Venerable sir,” they replied.

The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you an exposition of the sixfold base (*ṣaḷāyatanavibhaṅgaṃ*).

Listen & pay close attention. I will speak.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” the bhikkhus replied.

The Blessed One said this:

“The six internal bases (*ajjhattikāni āyatanāni*) should be understood. The six external bases (*bāhirāni āyatanāni*) should be understood. The six classes of consciousness (*viññāṇakāyā*) should be understood. The six classes of contact (*phassakāyā*) should be understood. The eighteen kinds of mental exploration (*manopavicārā*) should be understood. The thirty-six positions of beings (*sattapadā*) should be understood. Therein, by depending on this, abandon that. There are three foundations of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhānā*) that the Noble One cultivates, cultivating which the Noble One is a teacher (*satthā*) fit to instruct a group (*gaṇa*), and is called the unsurpassed guide (*anuttaro purisadammasārathī*) of those who practice yoga (*yoggācariyānaṃ*)” – this is a summary (*uddeso*) of the exposition of the sixfold base (*saḷāyatanavibhaṅgassa*).
commentary_pali: 304.Evaṃme sutanti saḷāyatanavibhaṅgasuttaṃ. Tattha veditabbānīti sahavipassanena maggena jānitabbāni. Manopavicārāti vitakkavicārā. Vitakkuppādakañhi mano idha manoti adhippetaṃ, manassa upavicārāti manopavicārā. Sattapadāti vaṭṭavivaṭṭanissitānaṃ sattānaṃ padā. Ettha hi aṭṭhārasa vaṭṭapadā nāma, aṭṭhārasa vivaṭṭapadā nāma, tepi sahavipassanena maggeneva veditabbā. Yoggācariyānanti hatthiyoggādiācārasikkhāpakānaṃ, dametabbadamakānanti attho. Sesaṃ vibhaṅgeyeva āvibhavissati. Ayamuddesoti idaṃ mātikāṭṭhapanaṃ.
commentary_english:
Thus it is said, "Thus I have heard," the *Saḷāyatanavibhaṅgasutta*.

There, *veditabbānī* means they should be known by the path together with insight.

*Manopavicārā* means *vitakkavicārā*.

For here, mind is intended as that which produces thought; *manassa upavicārāti manopavicārā*.

*Sattapadā* means the paths of beings dependent on the round and the reversal [of rebirth].

Here, there are eighteen paths of the round, and eighteen paths of the reversal; those, too, should be known by the path together with insight.

*Yoggācariyāna* means those who train in the practices of elephant training and so forth; the meaning is those who tame what should be tamed.

The rest will become clear in the analysis itself.

*Ayamuddeso* means this is the establishment of the matrix.

mula_pali:
305. ‘‘‘Cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni veditabbānī’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? ‘Cakkhāyatanaṃ sotāyatanaṃ ghānāyatanaṃ jivhāyatanaṃ kāyāyatanaṃ manāyatanaṃ – cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni veditabbānī’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘‘‘Cha bāhirāni āyatanāni veditabbānī’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ . Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? ‘Rūpāyatanaṃ saddāyatanaṃ gandhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ dhammāyatanaṃ – cha bāhirāni āyatanāni veditabbānī’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘‘‘Cha viññāṇakāyā veditabbā’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? ‘Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ ghānaviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ kāyaviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ – cha viññāṇakāyā veditabbā’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘‘‘Cha phassakāyā veditabbā’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? ‘Cakkhusamphasso sotasamphasso ghānasamphasso jivhāsamphasso kāyasamphasso manosamphasso – cha phassakāyā veditabbā’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘‘‘Aṭṭhārasa manopavicārā veditabbā’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? ‘Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā somanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati, domanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati, upekkhāṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya somanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati, domanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati, upekkhāṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati. Iti cha somanassūpavicārā, cha domanassūpavicārā, cha upekkhūpavicārā, aṭṭhārasa manopavicārā veditabbā’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
305. ‘“The six internal bases (*ajjhattikāni āyatanāni*) should be understood.”’ So it was said.

And in reference to what was it said? ‘The eye-base (*cakkhāyatana*), the ear-base (*sotāyatana*), the nose-base (*ghānāyatana*), the tongue-base (*jivhāyatana*), the body-base (*kāyāyatana*), and the mind-base (*manāyatana*) – the six internal bases (*ajjhattikāni āyatanāni*) should be understood.’ So it was with reference to this that it was said.

‘“The six external bases (*bāhirāni āyatanāni*) should be understood.”’ So it was said.

And in reference to what was it said? ‘The form-base (*rūpāyatana*), the sound-base (*saddāyatana*), the odour-base (*gandhāyatana*), the flavour-base (*rasāyatana*), the tangible-base (*phoṭṭhabbāyatana*), and the mind-object-base (*dhammāyatana*) – the six external bases (*bāhirāni āyatanāni*) should be understood.’ So it was with reference to this that it was said.

‘“The six classes of consciousness (*viññāṇakāyā*) should be understood.”’ So it was said.

And in reference to what was it said? ‘Eye-consciousness (*cakkhuviññāṇa*), ear-consciousness (*sotaviññāṇa*), nose-consciousness (*ghānaviññāṇa*), tongue-consciousness (*jivhāviññāṇa*), body-consciousness (*kāyaviññāṇa*), and mind-consciousness (*manoviññāṇa*) – the six classes of consciousness (*viññāṇakāyā*) should be understood.’ So it was with reference to this that it was said.

‘“The six classes of contact (*phassakāyā*) should be understood.”’ So it was said.

And in reference to what was it said? ‘Eye-contact (*cakkhusamphasso*), ear-contact (*sotasamphasso*), nose-contact (*ghānasamphasso*), tongue-contact (*jivhāsamphasso*), body-contact (*kāyasamphasso*), and mind-contact (*manosamphasso*) – the six classes of contact (*phassakāyā*) should be understood.’ So it was with reference to this that it was said.

‘“The eighteen kinds of mental exploration (*manopavicārā*) should be understood.”’ So it was said.

And in reference to what was it said? ‘On seeing a form (*rūpaṃ*) with the eye (*cakkhunā*), one explores a form productive of joy (*somanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati*), one explores a form productive of grief (*domanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati*), one explores a form productive of equanimity (*upekkhāṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati*).

On hearing a sound (*saddaṃ*) with the ear (*sotena*)… On smelling an odour (*gandhaṃ*) with the nose (*ghānena*)… On tasting a flavour (*rasaṃ*) with the tongue (*jivhāya*)… On touching a tangible (*phoṭṭhabbaṃ*) with the body (*kāyena*)… On cognizing a mind-object (*dhammaṃ*) with the mind (*manasā*), one explores a mind-object productive of joy (*somanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati*), one explores a mind-object productive of grief (*domanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati*), one explores a mind-object productive of equanimity (*upekkhāṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati*).

Thus there are six kinds of exploration with joy (*somanassūpavicārā*), six kinds of exploration with grief (*domanassūpavicārā*), and six kinds of exploration with equanimity (*upekkhūpavicārā*). The eighteen kinds of mental exploration (*manopavicārā*) should be understood.’ So it was with reference to this that it was said.
commentary_pali:
305.Cakkhāyatanādīni visuddhimagge vitthāritāni. Cakkhuviññāṇanti kusalākusalavipākato dve cakkhuviññāṇāni. Sesapasādaviññāṇesupi eseva nayo. Imāni pana dasa ṭhapetvā sesaṃ idha manoviññāṇaṃ nāma.

Cakkhusamphassoti cakkhumhi samphasso. Cakkhuviññāṇasampayuttasamphassassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

Cakkhusamphasso

Cakkhunārūpaṃ disvāti cakkhuviññāṇena rūpaṃ disvā. Eseva nayo sabbattha. Somanassaṭṭhāniyanti somanassassa ārammaṇavasena kāraṇabhūtaṃ. Upavicaratīti tattha vicārapavattanena upavicarati, vitakko taṃsampayutto cāti iminā nayena aṭṭhārasa vitakkavicārasaṅkhātā manopavicārā veditabbā. Cha somanassūpavicārāti ettha pana somanassena saddhiṃ upavicarantīti somanassūpavicārā. Sesapadadvayepi eseva nayo.

Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā Somanassaṭṭhāniya Upavicaratī Cha somanassūpavicārā
commentary_english:
305. *Cakkhāyatana*-*ādīni* are விரிthoroughly explained in the *Visuddhimagga*.

*Cakkhuviññāṇa* means two eye-consciousnesses (*cakṣur-vijñāna*) arising from wholesome and unwholesome results.

And the same rule applies to the remaining sense-sphere consciousnesses.

But setting aside these ten, what remains here is called mind-consciousness (*mano-vijñāṇa*).

*Cakkhusamphasso* means contact (*sparśa*) at the eye.

This is a designation for the contact (*sparśa*) associated with eye-consciousness (*cakṣur-vijñāna*).

And the same rule applies to the rest.

*Cakkhusamphasso*

*Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā* means having seen a form (*rūpa*) with eye-consciousness (*cakṣur-vijñāna*).

Similarly in each instance.

*Somanassaṭṭhāniya* means being the cause by way of being the object of joy (*somanassa*).

*Upavicarati* means one explores by the occurrence of consideration (*vicāra*) there; and by this method, eighteen mental explorations (*mano-pavicārā*) reckoned as thought (*vitakka*) and consideration (*vicāra*) associated with it, should be understood.

*Cha somanassūpavicārā* means here, *somanassūpavicārā* are those that explore along with joy (*somanassa*).

And the same rule applies in the case of the remaining two terms.

*Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā somanassaṭṭhāniya upavicarati cha somanassūpavicārā*

mula_pali:
306. ‘‘‘Chattiṃsa sattapadā veditabbā’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Cha gehasitāni gehassitāni (?) somanassāni, cha nekkhammasitāni nekkhammassitāni (ṭīkā) somanassāni, cha gehasitāni domanassāni, cha nekkhammasitāni domanassāni, cha gehasitā upekkhā, cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā. Tattha katamāni cha gehasitāni somanassāni? Cakkhuviññeyyānaṃ rūpānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ manoramānaṃ lokāmisapaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ paṭilābhaṃ vā paṭilābhato samanupassato pubbe vā paṭiladdhapubbaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vipariṇataṃ samanussarato uppajjati somanassaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ somanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati gehasitaṃ somanassaṃ. Sotaviññeyyānaṃ saddānaṃ… ghānaviññeyyānaṃ gandhānaṃ… jivhāviññeyyānaṃ rasānaṃ… kāyaviññeyyānaṃ phoṭṭhabbānaṃ… manoviññeyyānaṃ dhammānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ…pe… somanassaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ somanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati gehasitaṃ somanassaṃ. Imāni cha gehasitāni somanassāni.

‘‘Tattha katamāni cha nekkhammasitāni somanassāni? Rūpānaṃtveva aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmavirāganirodhaṃ vipariṇāmaṃ virāgaṃ nirodhaṃ (ka.), ‘pubbe ceva rūpā etarahi ca sabbe te rūpā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato uppajjati somanassaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ somanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati nekkhammasitaṃ somanassaṃ. Saddānaṃtveva… gandhānaṃtveva… rasānaṃtveva… phoṭṭhabbānaṃtveva… dhammānaṃtve aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmavirāganirodhaṃ, ‘pubbe ceva dhammā etarahi ca sabbe te dhammā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato uppajjati somanassaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ somanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati nekkhammasitaṃ somanassaṃ. Imāni cha nekkhammasitāni somanassāni.

vipariṇāmaṃ virāgaṃ nirodhaṃ (ka.)
mula_english:
306. “‘The thirty-six positions of beings should be understood.’ So it was said.

What was said with reference to what?
