Six kinds of joy based on the household life, six kinds of joy based on renunciation, six kinds of grief based on the household life, six kinds of grief based on renunciation, six kinds of equanimity based on the household life, six kinds of equanimity based on renunciation.

What are the six kinds of joy based on the household life? When one regards as an acquisition the acquisition of forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable, gratifying, and associated with worldliness—or when one recalls what was formerly acquired that has passed, ceased, and changed—joy (*somanassaṃ*) arises. Such joy (*somanassaṃ*) as this is called joy based on the household life (*gehasitaṃ somanassaṃ*).

When one regards as an acquisition the acquisition of sounds cognizable by the ear…the acquisition of odours cognizable by the nose…the acquisition of flavours cognizable by the tongue…the acquisition of tangibles cognizable by the body…the acquisition of mind-objects cognizable by the mind that are wished for, desired, agreeable, gratifying…joy (*somanassaṃ*) arises. Such joy (*somanassaṃ*) as this is called joy based on the household life (*gehasitaṃ somanassaṃ*). These are the six kinds of joy based on the household life (*gehasitāni somanassāni*).

What are the six kinds of joy based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitāni somanassāni*)? When, by knowing the impermanence (*aniccatā*), change, fading away (*virāga*), and cessation (*nirodha*) of forms, one sees as it actually is with proper wisdom (*sammappaññā*) that forms both formerly and now are all impermanent (*aniccā*), suffering (*dukkhā*), and subject to change, joy (*somanassaṃ*) arises. Such joy (*somanassaṃ*) as this is called joy based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitaṃ somanassaṃ*).

When, by knowing the impermanence (*aniccatā*), change, fading away (*virāga*), and cessation (*nirodha*) of sounds…of odours…of flavours…of tangibles…of mind-objects, one sees as it actually is with proper wisdom (*sammappaññā*) that mind-objects both formerly and now are all impermanent (*aniccā*), suffering (*dukkhā*), and subject to change, joy (*somanassaṃ*) arises. Such joy (*somanassaṃ*) as this is called joy based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitaṃ somanassaṃ*). These are the six kinds of joy based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitāni somanassāni*).
commentary_pali:
306.Gehasitānīti kāmaguṇanissitāni. Nekkhammasitānīti vipassanānissitāni. Iṭṭhānanti pariyesitānaṃ. Kantānanti kāmitānaṃ. Manoramānanti mano etesu ramatīti manoramāni, tesaṃ manoramānaṃ. Lokāmisapaṭisaṃyuttānanti taṇhāpaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ. Atītanti paṭiladdhaṃ . Paccuppannaṃ tāva ārabbha somanassaṃ uppajjatu, atīte kathaṃ uppajjatīti. Atītepi – ‘‘yathāhaṃ etarahi iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ anubhavāmi, evaṃ pubbepi anubhavi’’nti anussarantassa balavasomanassaṃ uppajjati.

Aniccatanti aniccākāraṃ. Vipariṇāmavirāganirodhanti pakativijahanena vipariṇāmaṃ, vigacchanena virāgaṃ, nirujjhanena nirodhaṃ. Sammapaññāyāti vipassanāpaññāya. Idaṃ vuccati nekkhammasitaṃ somanassanti idaṃ rañño viya attano sirisampattiṃ olokentassa vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā nisinnassa saṅkhārānaṃ bhedaṃ passato saṅkhāragatamhi tikkhe sūre vipassanāñāṇe vahante uppannasomanassaṃ ‘‘nekkhammasitaṃ somanassa’’nti vuccati. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

Aniccata Vipariṇāmavirāganirodha Sammapaññāyā Idaṃ vuccati nekkhammasitaṃ somanassa

‘‘Suññāgāraṃ paviṭṭhassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno;

Amānusī ratī hoti, sammā dhammaṃ vipassato.

Yato yato sammasati, khandhānaṃ udayabbayaṃ;

Labhatī pītipāmojjaṃ, amatantaṃ vijānata’’nti. (dha. pa. 373-374);

Imānīti imāni chasu dvāresu iṭṭhārammaṇe āpāthagate aniccādivasena vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā nisinnassa uppannāni cha nekkhammasitāni somanassāni.

Imānī
commentary_english:
306. *gehasitānī* means dependent on sensual qualities. *nekkhammasitānī* means dependent on insight (*vipassanā*). *iṭṭhāna*nti means desired. *kantāna*nti means longed for. *manoramāna*nti *mano etesu ramatīti manoramāni*, *tesaṃ manoramānaṃ* means the delightful, of those that are delightful, [as] the mind delights in them. *lokāmisapaṭisaṃyuttāna*nti means connected with craving (*taṇhā*). *atīta*nti means regained.

Even though pleasant feeling might arise having taken present objects as its basis, how could it arise regarding the past? Even regarding the past, strong pleasant feeling arises for one who recollects, "Just as I experience a desirable object now, so I have experienced it in the past."

*aniccata*nti means the characteristic of impermanence (*aniccākāraṃ*). *vipariṇāmavirāganirodha*nti means change (*vipariṇāmaṃ*) through abandoning its nature (*pakativijahanena*), detachment (*virāgaṃ*) through ceasing (*vigacchanena*), cessation (*nirodhaṃ*) through being stopped (*nirujjhanena*). *sammapaññāyā*ti means through the wisdom of insight (*vipassanāpaññāya*). *idaṃ vuccati nekkhammasitaṃ somanassa*nti means this is called pleasant feeling dependent on renunciation (*nekkhammasitaṃ somanassa*) - just as a king, looking at his own glorious prosperity, and having established insight (*vipassanā*) considers the breaking up of conditioned phenomena (*saṅkhārānaṃ*); the pleasant feeling that arises for him, seeing the sharp, heroic insight-knowledge (*vipassanāñāṇe*) in relation to conditioned phenomena (*saṅkhāragatamhi*), is called pleasant feeling dependent on renunciation (*nekkhammasitaṃ somanassa*).

And this was said:

Impermanence, change, detachment, cessation through right wisdom, this is called pleasant feeling dependent on renunciation.

"For a *bhikkhu* who has entered an empty dwelling, whose mind is peaceful, there is a superhuman joy, for one who rightly sees the *dhamma*. From whatever he ascertains the rise and fall of the aggregates, he obtains joy and delight, knowing that which is immortal." (Dhp. 373-374)

*imānī*ti means these six pleasant feelings dependent on renunciation (*nekkhammasitāni somanassāni*) arisen for one who, in these six sense-doors, having established insight (*vipassanā*) in relation to a desirable object (*iṭṭhārammaṇe*) that has come into the range [of perception] (*āpāthagate*), considers [it] in terms of impermanence etc. (*aniccādivasena*).

*imānī*

mula_pali:
307. ‘‘Tattha katamāni cha gehasitāni domanassāni? Cakkhuviññeyyānaṃ rūpānaṃ…pe… sotaviññeyyānaṃ saddānaṃ… ghānaviññeyyānaṃ gandhānaṃ… jivhāviññeyyānaṃ rasānaṃ… kāyaviññeyyānaṃ phoṭṭhabbānaṃ… manoviññeyyānaṃ dhammānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ manoramānaṃ lokāmisapaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ appaṭilābhaṃ vā appaṭilābhato samanupassato pubbe vā appaṭiladdhapubbaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vipariṇataṃ samanussarato uppajjati domanassaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ domanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati gehasitaṃ domanassaṃ. Imāni cha gehasitāni domanassāni.

‘‘Tattha katamāni cha nekkhammasitāni domanassāni? Rūpānaṃtveva aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmavirāganirodhaṃ, ‘pubbe ceva rūpā etarahi ca sabbe te rūpā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti – ‘kudāssu kadāssu (syā. kaṃ. pī.) nāmāhaṃ tadāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharissāmi yadariyā etarahi āyatanaṃ upasampajja viharantī’ti iti anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato uppajjati pihapaccayā domanassaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ domanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati nekkhammasitaṃ domanassaṃ. Saddānaṃtveva…pe… gandhānaṃtveva… rasānaṃtveva… phoṭṭhabbānaṃtveva… dhammānaṃtveva aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmavirāganirodhaṃ, ‘pubbe ceva dhammā etarahi ca sabbe te dhammā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti – ‘kudāssu nāmāhaṃ tadāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharissāmi yadariyā etarahi āyatanaṃ upasampajja viharantī’ti iti anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato uppajjati pihapaccayā domanassaṃ. Yaṃ evarūpaṃ domanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati nekkhammasitaṃ domanassaṃ. Imāni cha nekkhammasitāni domanassāni.

kadāssu (syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
307.
"Therein, what are the six kinds of grief based on the household life ( *gehasitaṃ domanassaṃ*)? When one regards as a non-acquisition the non-acquisition of forms cognizable by the eye (*cakkhuviññeyyānaṃ rūpānaṃ*) that are wished for...the non-acquisition of sounds cognizable by the ear (*sotaviññeyyānaṃ saddānaṃ*)...the non-acquisition of odours cognizable by the nose (*ghānaviññeyyānaṃ gandhānaṃ*)...the non-acquisition of flavours cognizable by the tongue (*jivhāviññeyyānaṃ rasānaṃ*)...the non-acquisition of tangibles cognizable by the body (*kāyaviññeyyānaṃ phoṭṭhabbānaṃ*)...the non-acquisition of mind-objects cognizable by the mind (*manoviññeyyānaṃ dhammānaṃ*) that are wished for, desired, agreeable, gratifying, and associated with worldliness ( *lokāmisapaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ* ) -or when one recalls what was formerly not acquired (*appaṭiladdhapubbaṃ*) that has passed, ceased, and changed - grief (*domanassaṃ*) arises.
Such grief as this is called grief based on the household life (*gehasitaṃ domanassaṃ*).
These are the six kinds of grief based on the household life (*gehasitāni domanassāni*)."

"Therein, what are the six kinds of grief based on renunciation ( *nekkhamma sitāni domanassāni*)? When, by knowing the impermanence (*aniccatāṃ*), change (*vipariṇāma*), fading away (*virāga*), and cessation (*nirodhaṃ*) of forms (*rūpānaṃtveva*), one sees as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom ( *sammappaññāya*) that forms (*rūpā*) both formerly (*pubbe ceva*) and now (*etarahi ca*) are all impermanent ( *aniccā*), suffering (* dukkhā*), and subject to change (*vipariṇāmadhammā*), one generates a longing ( *pihaṃ*) for the supreme liberations (*anuttaresu vimokkhesu*) thus: ‘When shall I enter upon and abide in that base (*tadāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharissāmi*) that the noble ones (*ariyā*) now enter upon and abide in (*āyatanaṃ upasampajja viharantī*)?' In one who generates thus a longing for the supreme liberations, grief (*domanassaṃ*) arises with that longing as condition ( *pihapaccayā*).
Such grief as this is called grief based on renunciation ( *nekkhamma sitaṃ domanassaṃ*).
When, by knowing the impermanence, change, fading away, and cessation of sounds (*saddānaṃtveva*)...of odours (*gandhānaṃtveva*)...of flavours (*rasānaṃtveva*)...of tangibles (*phoṭṭhabbānaṃtveva*)...of mind-objects (*dhammānaṃtveva*), one sees as it actually is with proper wisdom that mind-objects both formerly and now are all impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, one generates a longing for the supreme liberations thus: ‘When shall I enter upon and abide in that base that the noble ones now enter upon and abide in?’ In one who thus generates a longing for the supreme liberations, grief arises with that longing as condition.
Such grief as this is called grief based on renunciation.
These are the six kinds of grief based on renunciation."
commentary_pali:
307.Atītanti paccuppannaṃ tāva patthetvā alabhantassa domanassaṃ uppajjatu, atīte kathaṃ uppajjatīti. Atītepi ‘‘yathāhaṃ etarahi iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ patthetvā na labhāmi, evaṃ pubbepi patthetvā na labhi’’nti anussarantassa balavadomanassaṃ uppajjati.

Anuttaresu vimokkhesūti anuttaravimokkho nāma arahattaṃ, arahatte patthanaṃ paṭṭhapentassāti attho. Āyatananti arahattāyatanaṃ. Pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayatoti patthanaṃ paṭṭhapentassa. Taṃ panetaṃ patthanaṃ paṭṭhapentassa uppajjati, iti patthanāmūlakattā ‘‘pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato’’ti vuttaṃ. Imāni cha nekkhammasitāni domanassānīti imāni evaṃ chasu dvāresu iṭṭhārammaṇe āpāthagate arahatte pihaṃ paṭṭhapetvā tadadhigamāya aniccādivasena vipassanaṃ upaṭṭhapetvā ussukkāpetuṃ asakkontassa – ‘‘imampi pakkhaṃ imampi māsaṃ imampi saṃvaccharaṃ arahattaṃ pāpuṇituṃ nāsakkhi’’nti anusocato gāmantapabbhāravāsimahāsīvattherassa viya assudhārāpavattanavasena uppannadomanassāni cha nekkhammasitadomanassānīti veditabbāni. Vatthu pana sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya sakkapañhavaṇṇanāyaṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.361) vitthāritaṃ, icchantena tato gahetabbaṃ.

Anuttaresu vimokkhesū Āyatana Pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato Imāni cha nekkhammasitāni domanassānī sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya
commentary_english:
307. *Atīta* means, "let sadness arise in one who desires but does not obtain (something) in the present." How could it arise regarding the past? In the past, strong sadness arises in one who remembers, "Just as I do not obtain the desired object that I desire now, so too I did not obtain (it) when I desired (it) in the past."

*Anuttaresu vimokkhesu* means that *anuttaravimokkha* is the arahantship, the meaning is "in one who establishes a desire in arahantship." *Āyatana* means the attainment of arahantship. *Pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato* means in one who establishes a desire.

But that (sadness) arises in one who establishes that desire; thus, because of being rooted in desire, it is said "*pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato*." *Imāni cha nekkhammasitāni domanassānī* means: "These are the six kinds of sadness based on renunciation." Thus, in these six doors, sadness arises in one who, when a desired object has come into the range (of perception), establishes desire in arahantship and is unable to incite effort by establishing insight based on impermanence, etc., for the sake of attaining that. It should be understood that the sadnesses which arose in the manner of tears flowing from the Great Sīva Thera who lived in a village-forest-mountain when he lamented, "I was not able to attain arahantship even this fortnight, even this month, even this year," are the six sadnesses based on renunciation.

However, the story is related in detail in the Sakkapañha commentary of the *Sumangalavilāsinī Dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathā* (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 2.361); one who wishes should take it from there.

*Anuttaresu vimokkhesu āyatana pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato imāni cha nekkhammasitāni domanassānī Sumangalavilāsiniyā Dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya*

mula_pali:
308. ‘‘Tattha katamā cha gehasitā upekkhā? Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā uppajjati upekkhā bālassa mūḷhassa ( ) (mandassa) (ka.) puthujjanassa anodhijinassa avipākajinassa anādīnavadassāvino assutavato puthujjanassa. Yā evarūpā upekkhā, rūpaṃ sā nātivattati. Tasmā sā sāyaṃ (ka.) upekkhā ‘gehasitā’ti vuccati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya uppajjati upekkhā bālassa mūḷhassa puthujjanassa anodhijinassa avipākajinassa anādīnavadassāvino assutavato puthujjanassa. Yā evarūpā upekkhā, dhammaṃ sā nātivattati. Tasmā sā upekkhā ‘gehasitā’ti vuccati. Imā cha gehasitā upekkhā.

‘‘Tattha katamā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā? Rūpānaṃtveva aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmavirāganirodhaṃ, ‘pubbe ceva rūpā etarahi ca sabbe te rūpā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato uppajjati upekkhā. Yā evarūpā upekkhā, rūpaṃ sā ativattati. Tasmā sā upekkhā ‘nekkhammasitā’ti vuccati. Saddānaṃtveva… gandhānaṃtveva… rasānaṃtveva… phoṭṭhabbānaṃtveva… dhammānaṃtveva aniccataṃ viditvā vipariṇāmavirāganirodhaṃ, ‘pubbe ceva dhammā etarahi ca sabbe te dhammā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya passato uppajjati upekkhā. Yā evarūpā upekkhā, dhammaṃ sā ativattati. Tasmā sā upekkhā ‘nekkhammasitā’ti vuccati. Imā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā. ‘Chattiṃsa sattapadā veditabbā’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
308.
"Here, what is the sixfold equanimity based on the household life ( *gehasitā upekkhā*)? On seeing a form with the eye, equanimity arises in a foolish, infatuated ordinary person ( *puthujjana*), in an untaught ordinary person who has not conquered his limitations or conquered the results of action and who is blind to danger.
Such equanimity as this does not transcend the form ( *rūpaṃ* );
that is why it is called equanimity based on the household life ( *gehasitā*)."
On hearing a sound with the ear…On smelling an odour with the nose…On tasting a flavour with the tongue…On touching a tangible with the body…On cognizing a mind-object with the mind, equanimity arises in a foolish infatuated ordinary person, in an untaught ordinary person who has not conquered his limitations or conquered the results of action and who is blind to danger.
Such equanimity as this does not transcend the mind-object ( *dhammaṃ* );
that is why it is called equanimity based on the household life ( *gehasitā*).
These are the six kinds of equanimity based on the household life ( *gehasitā upekkhā*).

"Here, what is the sixfold equanimity based on renunciation ( *nekkhammasitā upekkhā*)? When, by knowing the impermanence (*aniccatāṃ*), change (*vipariṇāma*), fading away (*virāga*), and cessation (*nirodhaṃ*) of forms (*rūpānaṃ*), one sees as it actually is with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*) that forms (*rūpā*) both formerly (*pubbe*) and now are all impermanent (*aniccā*), suffering (*dukkhā*), and subject to change (*vipariṇāmadhammā*), equanimity (*upekkhā*) arises.
Such equanimity as this transcends the form (*rūpaṃ*);
that is why it is called equanimity based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitā*)."
…of odours…of flavours…of tangibles …of mind-objects, one sees as it actually is with proper wisdom that mind-objects both formerly and now are all impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, equanimity arises.
Such equanimity as this transcends the mind-object (*dhammaṃ*);
that is why it is called equanimity based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitā*).
These are the six kinds of equanimity based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitā upekkhā*).
“The thirty-six positions of beings should be understood.” So it was with reference to this that it was said.
commentary_pali:
308.Uppajjati upekkhāti ettha upekkhā nāma aññāṇupekhā. Anodhijinassāti kilesodhiṃ jinitvā ṭhitattā khīṇāsavo odhijino nāma, tasmā akhīṇāsavassāti attho. Avipākajinassāti etthapi āyatiṃ vipākaṃ jinitvā ṭhitattā khīṇāsavova vipākajino nāma, tasmā akhīṇāsavassevāti attho. Anādīnavadassāvinotiādīnavato upaddavato apassantassa. Imā cha gehasitā upekkhāti imā evaṃ chasu dvāresu iṭṭhārammaṇe āpāthagate guḷapiṇḍake nilīnamakkhikā viya rūpādīni anativattamānā tattha laggā laggitā hutvā uppannā upekkhā cha gehasitā upekkhāti veditabbā.

Rūpaṃ sā ativattatīti rūpaṃ sā anatikkamati, tattha nikantivasena na tiṭṭhati. Imā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhāti imā evaṃ chasu dvāresu iṭṭhādiārammaṇe āpāthagate iṭṭhe arajjantassa, aniṭṭhe adussantassa, asamapekkhane asammuyhantassa, uppannavipassanā-ñāṇasampayuttā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhāti veditabbā.

Rūpaṃ sā ativattatī Imā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā
commentary_english:
308. "Uppajjati upekkhā": Here, *upekkhā* means *aññāṇupekhā*.

"Anodhijinassā": Because one has conquered the flood of defilements (*kilesodhiṃ jinitvā ṭhitattā*), the one with depleted influxes (*khīṇāsavo*) is called *odhijino*; therefore, it means one who does not have depleted influxes (*akhīṇāsavassa*).

"Avipākajinassā": Here also, because one has conquered future ripening (*āyatiṃ vipākaṃ jinitvā ṭhitattā*), the one with depleted influxes (*khīṇāsavova*) is called *vipākajino*; therefore, it means one who does not have depleted influxes (*akhīṇāsavassa*).

"Anādīnavadassāvino": To one who does not see danger (*ādīnavato*) and oppression (*upaddavato apassantassa*).

"Imā cha gehasitā upekkhā": These are the six kinds of equanimity (*upekkhā*) that are attached to a house (*gehasitā*). Thus, in the six sense doors (*chasu dvāresu*), with regard to a pleasing object (*iṭṭhārammaṇe*), within range (*āpāthagate*), like flies clinging to a lump of sugar (*guḷapiṇḍake nilīnamakkhikā viya*), not transgressing forms etc. (*rūpādīni anativattamānā*), being attached and clinging there (*tattha laggā laggitā hutvā uppannā upekkhā*), these are known as the six kinds of equanimity attached to a house (*cha gehasitā upekkhāti veditabbā*).

"Rūpaṃ sā ativattatī": That form (*rūpaṃ sā*) does not transcend (*anatikkamati*); it does not stand there with longing (*tattha nikantivasena na tiṭṭhati*).

"Imā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā": These are the six kinds of equanimity connected with renunciation (*nekkhamma*). Thus, in the six sense doors (*chasu dvāresu*), with regard to a pleasing object etc. (*iṭṭhādiārammaṇe*), within range (*āpāthagate*), to one who is not attracted to what is pleasing (*iṭṭhe arajjantassa*), not averse to what is displeasing (*aniṭṭhe adussantassa*), not confused in what is equitable (*asamapekkhane asammuyhantassa*), connected with the wisdom of arisen insight (*uppannavipassanā-ñāṇasampayuttā*), these are known as the six kinds of equanimity connected with renunciation (*cha nekkhammasitā upekkhāti veditabbā*).

"Rūpaṃ sā ativattatī" "Imā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā"

mula_pali:
309. ‘‘Tatra idaṃ nissāya idaṃ pajahathā’’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ; kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tatra, bhikkhave, yāni cha nekkhammasitāni somanassāni tāni nissāya tāni āgamma yāni cha gehasitāni somanassāni tāni pajahatha, tāni samatikkamatha. Evametesaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametesaṃ samatikkamo hoti.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yāni cha nekkhammasitāni domanassāni tāni nissāya tāni āgamma yāni cha gehasitāni domanassāni tāni pajahatha, tāni samatikkamatha. Evametesaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametesaṃ samatikkamo hoti.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā tā nissāya tā āgamma yā cha gehasitā upekkhā tā pajahatha, tā samatikkamatha. Evametāsaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametāsaṃ samatikkamo hoti.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yāni cha nekkhammasitāni somanassāni tāni nissāya tāni āgamma yāni cha nekkhammasitāni domanassāni tāni pajahatha, tāni samatikkamatha. Evametesaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametesaṃ samatikkamo hoti.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā tā nissāya tā āgamma yāni cha nekkhammasitāni somanassāni tāni pajahatha, tāni samatikkamatha. Evametesaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametesaṃ samatikkamo hoti.
mula_english:
309. It is said, "Depending on this, abandon this" – but what is said in reliance on what? Here, monks, by depending and relying on the six kinds of joy based on renunciation ( *nekkhammasitāni somanassāni* ), abandon and surmount the six kinds of joy based on household life (*gehasitāni somanassāni*). It is thus they are abandoned; it is thus they are surmounted.

Here, monks, by depending and relying on the six kinds of grief based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitāni domanassāni*), abandon and surmount the six kinds of grief based on household life (*gehasitāni domanassāni*). It is thus they are abandoned; it is thus they are surmounted.

Here, monks, by depending and relying on the six kinds of equanimity based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitā upekkhā*), abandon and surmount the six kinds of equanimity based on household life (*gehasitā upekkhā*). It is thus these are abandoned; it is thus these are surmounted.

Here, monks, by depending and relying on the six kinds of joy based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitāni somanassāni*), abandon and surmount the six kinds of grief based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitāni domanassāni*). It is thus they are abandoned; it is thus they are surmounted.

Here, monks, by depending and relying on the six kinds of equanimity based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitā upekkhā*), abandon and surmount the six kinds of joy based on renunciation (*nekkhammasitāni somanassāni*). It is thus they are abandoned; it is thus they are surmounted.
commentary_pali:
309.Tatra idaṃ nissāya idaṃ pajahathāti tesu chattiṃsasattapadesu aṭṭhārasa nissāya aṭṭhārasa pajahathāti attho. Teneva – ‘‘tatra, bhikkhave, yāni cha nekkhammasitānī’’tiādimāha. Nissāya āgammāti pavattanavasena nissāya ceva āgamma ca. Evametesaṃ samatikkamohotīti evaṃ nekkhammasitānaṃ pavattanena gehasitāni atikkantāni nāma honti.

Evaṃ sarikkhakeneva sarikkhakaṃ jahāpetvā idāni balavatā dubbalaṃ jahāpento – ‘‘tatra, bhikkhave, yāni cha nekkhammasitāni somanassānī’’tiādimāha. Evaṃ nekkhammasitasomanassehi nekkhammasitadomanassāni , nekkhammasitaupekkhāhi ca nekkhammasitasomanassāni jahāpentena balavatā dubbalappahānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Ettha pana ṭhatvā upekkhākathā veditabbā – aṭṭhasu hi samāpattīsu paṭhamādīni ca tīṇi jhānāni, suddhasaṅkhāre ca pādake katvā vipassanaṃ āraddhānaṃ catunnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pubbabhāgavipassanā somanassasahagatā vā hoti upekkhāsahagatā vā, vuṭṭhānagāminī pana somanassasahagatāva. Catutthajjhānādīni pādakāni katvā vipassanaṃ āraddhānaṃ pañcannaṃ pubbabhāgavipassanā purimasadisāva. Vuṭṭhānagāminī pana upekkhāsahagatā hoti. Idaṃ sandhāya – ‘‘yā cha nekkhammasitā upekkhā, tā nissāya tā āgamma, yāni cha nekkhammasitāni somanassāni, tāni pajahathā’’ti vuttaṃ. Na kevalañca evaṃpaṭipannassa bhikkhuno ayaṃ vipassanāya vedanāvisesova hoti, ariyamaggepi pana jhānaṅgabojjhaṅgamaggaṅgānampi viseso hoti.

Ko panetaṃ visesaṃ niyameti? Keci tāva therā vipassanāpādakajjhānaṃ niyametīti vadanti, keci vipassanāya ārammaṇabhūtā khandhā niyamentīti vadanti, keci puggalajjhāsayo niyametīti vadanti. Tesampi vāde ayameva pubbabhāge vuṭṭhānagāminīvipassanā niyametīti veditabbā. Vinicchayakathā panettha visuddhimagge saṅkhārupekkhāniddese vuttāva.

visuddhimagge
commentary_english:
309. "There, by relying on this, abandon this" means that among those thirty-six based on attachment, by relying on eighteen, abandon eighteen.

Therefore, he said, "There, monks, those six based on renunciation," and so forth.

"Relying and approaching" means relying and approaching in terms of their arising.

"Thus, there is a surmounting of these" means that in this way, through the arising of those [factors] based on renunciation, those based on household life are said to have been overcome.

Having caused the similar to abandon the similar, now, causing the strong to abandon the weak, he said, "There, monks, those six kinds of joy based on renunciation," and so forth.

Thus, through joy based on renunciation, [one abandons] sorrow based on renunciation, and by causing joy based on renunciation to be abandoned by equanimity based on renunciation, the abandonment of the weak by the strong is described.

Here, however, standing, the talk of equanimity should be understood—indeed, in the eight attainments, the first three *jhānas*, and having made pure formations the basis, for those four monks who have begun insight, the preliminary insight is either accompanied by joy or accompanied by equanimity, but the insight that leads to arising is only accompanied by joy.

Having made the fourth *jhāna* and so forth the basis, for the five who have begun insight, the preliminary insight is just like the previous one.

But the insight that leads to arising is accompanied by equanimity.

With this in mind, it was said, "Those six equanimities based on renunciation, by relying on those, by approaching those, abandon those six joys based on renunciation."

And not only for a monk who has thus entered [the path] is this a distinction of feeling in insight, but also in the noble path, there is a distinction in the *jhāna* factors, awakening factors (*bojjhaṅga*), and path factors (*maggaṅga*).

What, then, determines this distinction? Some elders say that the *jhāna* that is the basis of insight determines it; some say that the aggregates (*khandha*) that are the object of insight determine it; some say that the inclination of the individual (*puggala*) determines it.

Even in their opinions, this very insight that leads to arising in the preliminary stage should be understood as determining it.

The discussion of the ascertainment is already stated in the *Visuddhimagga* in the section on equanimity regarding formations.

*Visuddhimagga*

mula_pali:
310. ‘‘Atthi , bhikkhave, upekkhā nānattā nānattasitā, atthi upekkhā ekattā ekattasitā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, upekkhā nānattā nānattasitā? Atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhā rūpesu, atthi saddesu , atthi gandhesu, atthi rasesu, atthi phoṭṭhabbesu – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, upekkhā nānattā nānattasitā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, upekkhā ekattā ekattasitā? Atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhā ākāsānañcāyatananissitā, atthi viññāṇañcāyatananissitā, atthi ākiñcaññāyatananissitā, atthi nevasaññānāsaññāyatananissitā – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, upekkhā ekattā ekattasitā.

‘‘Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṃ upekkhā ekattā ekattasitā taṃ nissāya taṃ āgamma yāyaṃ upekkhā nānattā nānattasitā taṃ pajahatha, taṃ samatikkamatha. Evametissā pahānaṃ hoti, evametissā samatikkamo hoti.

‘‘Atammayataṃ, bhikkhave, nissāya atammayataṃ āgamma yāyaṃ upekkhā ekattā ekattasitā taṃ pajahatha, taṃ samatikkamatha. Evametissā pahānaṃ hoti, evametissā samatikkamo hoti. ‘Tatra idaṃ nissāya idaṃ pajahathā’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
310. “There is, bhikkhus, equanimity that is diversified, based on diversity (nānattā nānattasitā); and there is equanimity that is unified, based on unity (ekattā ekattasitā).

“And what, bhikkhus, is equanimity that is diversified, based on diversity? There is, bhikkhus, equanimity regarding forms (rūpesu), there is equanimity regarding sounds (saddesu), there is equanimity regarding odors (gandhesu), there is equanimity regarding tastes (rasesu), and there is equanimity regarding tangibles (phoṭṭhabbesu). This, bhikkhus, is equanimity that is diversified, based on diversity.

“And what, bhikkhus, is equanimity that is unified, based on unity? There is, bhikkhus, equanimity regarding the base of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatananissitā), the base of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatananissitā), the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatananissitā), and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatananissitā). This, bhikkhus, is equanimity that is unified, based on unity.

“Here, bhikkhus, by depending and relying on equanimity that is unified, based on unity, abandon and surmount equanimity that is diversified, based on diversity. Thus this is abandoned; it is thus this is surmounted.

“Bhikkhus, by depending and relying on non-identification (atammayataṃ), abandon and surmount equanimity that is unified, based on unity. Thus this is abandoned; it is thus this is surmounted.

“So it was in reference to this that it was said: ‘Therein, by depending on this, abandon that.’
commentary_pali:
310.Nānattāti nānā bahū anekappakārā. Nānattasitāti nānārammaṇanissitā. Ekattāti ekā. Ekattasitāti ekārammaṇanissitā. Katamā panāyaṃ upekkhāti? Heṭṭhā tāva aññāṇupekkhā vuttā, upari chaḷaṅgupekkhā vakkhati, idha samathaupekkhā, vipassanupekkhāti dve upekkhā gahitā.

Tattha yasmā aññāva rūpesu upekkhā, aññāva saddādīsu, na hi yā rūpe upekkhā, sā saddādīsu hoti. Rūpe upekkhā ca rūpameva ārammaṇaṃ karoti , na saddādayo. Rūpe upekkhābhāvañca aññā samathaupekkhā pathavīkasiṇaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā uppajjati, aññā āpokasiṇādīni. Tasmā nānattaṃ nānattasitaṃ vibhajanto atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhā rūpesūtiādimāha . Yasmā pana dve vā tīṇi vā ākāsānañcāyatanāni vā viññāṇañcāyatanādīni vā natthi, tasmā ekattaṃ ekattasitaṃ vibhajanto atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhā ākāsānañcāyatananissitātiādimāha.

atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhā rūpesū atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhā ākāsānañcāyatananissitā

Tattha ākāsānañcāyatanaupekkhā sampayuttavasena ākāsānañcāyatananissitā, ākāsānañcāyatanakhandhe vipassantassa vipassanupekkhā ārammaṇavasena ākāsānañcāyatananissitā. Sesāsupi eseva nayo.

Taṃ pajahathāti ettha arūpāvacarasamāpattiupekkhāya rūpāvacarasamāpattiupekkhaṃ pajahāpeti, arūpāvacaravipassanupekkhāya rūpāvacaravipassanupekkhaṃ.

Taṃ pajahathā

Atammayatanti ettha tammayatā nāma taṇhā, tassā pariyādānato vuṭṭhānagāminīvipassanā atammayatāti vuccati. Taṃ pajahathāti idha vuṭṭhānagāminīvipassanāya arūpāvacarasamāpattiupekkhañca vipassanupekkhañca pajahāpeti.

Atammayata Taṃ pajahathā
commentary_english:
310. *Nānattā* means various, many, of diverse kinds.

*Nānattasitā* means based on diverse objects.

*Ekattā* means one.

*Ekattasitā* means based on a single object.

But what is this equanimity? A lower ignorance-equanimity was stated earlier; above, the six-membered equanimity will be stated; here, two kinds of equanimity are taken: serenity-equanimity and insight-equanimity.

There, since one equanimity is in forms, and another in sounds, etc., for the equanimity that is in form does not exist in sounds, etc.

And equanimity in form makes form itself the object, not sounds, etc.

And, other than equanimity in form, one is serenity-equanimity, having made the earth kasina the object, arises; another, the water kasina, etc.

Therefore, distinguishing diversity and what is based on diversity, he said, "There is, monks, equanimity in forms," etc.

Since, however, there are not two or three or the sphere of infinite space, or the sphere of infinite consciousness, etc., therefore, distinguishing oneness and what is based on oneness, he said, "There is, monks, equanimity based on the sphere of infinite space," etc.

There is, monks, equanimity in forms. There is, monks, equanimity based on the sphere of infinite space.

There, the equanimity of the sphere of infinite space is based on the sphere of infinite space in the sense of association; the insight-equanimity of one contemplating the aggregate of the sphere of infinite space is based on the sphere of infinite space in the sense of object.

The same rule applies to the others as well.

"Abandon that" here causes the abandonment of the fine-material-sphere equanimity by the immaterial-sphere-absorption equanimity, and the abandonment of the fine-material-sphere insight-equanimity by the immaterial-sphere insight-equanimity.

Abandon that.

*Atammayata*—here, *tammayata* means craving; *atammayatā* is said to be the insight leading to relinquishment because of its completion.

"Abandon that" here causes the abandonment of both immaterial-sphere-absorption equanimity and insight-equanimity by the insight leading to relinquishment.

Atammayata. Abandon that.

mula_pali:
311. ‘‘‘Tayo satipaṭṭhānā yadariyo sevati, yadariyo sevamāno satthā gaṇamanusāsitumarahatī’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ; kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, satthā sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti anukampako hitesī anukampaṃ upādāya – ‘idaṃ vo hitāya, idaṃ vo sukhāyā’ti. Tassa sāvakā na sussūsanti, na sotaṃ odahanti, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhapenti , vokkamma ca satthusāsanā vattanti. Tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgato na ceva anattamano hoti, na ca anattamanataṃ paṭisaṃvedeti, anavassuto ca viharati sato sampajāno. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ yadariyo sevati, yadariyo sevamāno satthā gaṇamanusāsitumarahati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, satthā sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti anukampako hitesī anukampaṃ upādāya – ‘idaṃ vo hitāya, idaṃ vo sukhāyā’ti. Tassa ekacce sāvakā na sussūsanti, na sotaṃ odahanti, na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhapenti, vokkamma ca satthusāsanā vattanti; ekacce sāvakā sussūsanti, sotaṃ odahanti, aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhapenti, na ca vokkamma satthusāsanā vattanti . Tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgato na ceva anattamano hoti, na ca anattamanataṃ paṭisaṃvedeti; na ca attamano hoti, na ca attamanataṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Anattamanatā ca attamanatā ca – tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dutiyaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ yadariyo sevati, yadariyo sevamāno satthā gaṇamanusāsitumarahati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, satthā sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti anukampako hitesī anukampaṃ upādāya – ‘idaṃ vo hitāya, idaṃ vo sukhāyā’ti. Tassa sāvakā sussūsanti, sotaṃ odahanti, aññācittaṃ upaṭṭhapenti, na ca vokkamma satthusāsanā vattanti. Tatra, bhikkhave, tathāgato attamano ceva hoti, attamanatañca paṭisaṃvedeti, anavassuto ca viharati sato sampajāno. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, tatiyaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ yadariyo sevati, yadariyo sevamāno satthā gaṇamanusāsitumarahati. ‘Tayo satipaṭṭhānā yadariyo sevati, yadariyo sevamāno satthā gaṇamanusāsitumarahatī’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
311.  ‘‘‘There are three *satipaṭṭhānas* (foundations of mindfulness) that the Noble One cultivates, cultivating which the Teacher is fit to instruct a group’—so it was said. And with reference to what was this said? Here, *bhikkhus*, the Teacher teaches the *dharma* to the disciples, compassionate, seeking their welfare, undertaking compassion, saying: ‘This is for your welfare; this is for your happiness.’

His disciples do not wish to hear, they do not lend an ear, they do not establish their minds with understanding, and they behave turning away from the Teacher's instruction.

With that, *bhikkhus*, the *Tathāgata* is neither unsatisfied, nor does he feel dissatisfaction; yet he dwells detached, mindful, and fully aware. This, *bhikkhus*, is the first *satipaṭṭhāna* that the Noble One cultivates, cultivating which the Teacher is fit to instruct a group.

‘‘Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, the Teacher teaches the *dharma* to the disciples, compassionate, seeking their welfare, undertaking compassion, saying: ‘This is for your welfare; this is for your happiness.’

Some of his disciples do not wish to hear, they do not lend an ear, they do not establish their minds with understanding, and they behave turning away from the Teacher's instruction; some of his disciples wish to hear, they lend an ear, they establish their minds with understanding, and they do not behave turning away from the Teacher's instruction.

With that, *bhikkhus*, the *Tathāgata* is neither unsatisfied, nor does he feel dissatisfaction; and he is neither satisfied, nor does he feel satisfaction. Remaining free from both dissatisfaction and satisfaction, he dwells in equanimity, mindful, and fully aware. This is called, *bhikkhus*, the second *satipaṭṭhāna* that the Noble One cultivates, cultivating which the Teacher is fit to instruct a group.

‘‘Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, the Teacher teaches the *dharma* to the disciples, compassionate, seeking their welfare, undertaking compassion, saying: ‘This is for your welfare; this is for your happiness.’

His disciples wish to hear, they lend an ear, they establish their minds with understanding, and they do not behave turning away from the Teacher's instruction.

With that, *bhikkhus*, the *Tathāgata* is satisfied and feels satisfaction; yet he dwells detached, mindful, and fully aware. This is called, *bhikkhus*, the third *satipaṭṭhāna* that the Noble One cultivates, cultivating which the Teacher is fit to instruct a group.

‘There are three *satipaṭṭhānas* that the Noble One cultivates, cultivating which the Teacher is fit to instruct a group’—so it was said; this was said with reference to this.
commentary_pali: 311.Yadariyoti ye satipaṭṭhāne ariyo sammāsambuddho sevati. Tattha tīsu ṭhānesu satiṃ paṭṭhapento satipaṭṭhāne sevatīti veditabbo. Na sussūsantīti saddahitvā sotuṃ na icchanti. Na aññāti jānanatthāya cittaṃ na upaṭṭhapenti. Vokkammāti atikkamitvā. Satthu sāsanāti satthu ovādaṃ gahetabbaṃ pūretabbaṃ na maññantīti attho. Na ca attamanoti na sakamano. Ettha ca gehasitadomanassavasena appatīto hotīti na evamattho daṭṭhabbo, appaṭipannakesu pana attamanatākāraṇassa abhāvenetaṃ vuttaṃ. Anavassutoti paṭighaavassavena anavassuto. Sato sampajānoti satiyā ca ñāṇena ca samannāgato . Upekkhakoti chaḷaṅgupekkhāya upekkhako. Attamanoti idhāpi gehasitasomanassavasena uppilāvitoti na evamattho daṭṭhabbo, paṭipannakesu pana anattamanatākāraṇassa abhāvenetaṃ vuttaṃ. Anavassutoti rāgāvassavena anavassuto.
commentary_english:
311. *Yadariyo* means the noble disciple, the truly enlightened Buddha, cultivates the mindfulness meditation. There, it should be understood that by establishing mindfulness in the three places, one cultivates mindfulness meditation.

*Na sussūsantī* means they do not wish to listen with faith.

*Na aññā* means they do not establish their mind for the sake of knowing.

*Vokkammā* means having transgressed.

*Satthu sāsanā* means the meaning is that they do not think that the teacher's advice should be taken and fulfilled.

*Na ca attamano* means not having one's own mind.

Here, this meaning should not be seen as being displeased due to the unhappiness associated with household life; rather, this is said because of the absence of a reason for having one's own mind in those who have not undertaken [the practice].

*Anavassuto* means not being affected by the influx of aversion.

*Sato sampajāno* means endowed with mindfulness and knowledge.

*Upekkhako* means equanimous with six-factored equanimity.

*Attamano* Here too, this meaning should not be seen as being elated due to the happiness associated with household life; rather, this is said because of the absence of a reason for not having one's own mind in those who have undertaken [the practice].

*Anavassuto* means not being affected by the influx of lust.

mula_pali:
312. ‘‘‘So vuccati yoggācariyānaṃ anuttaro purisadammasārathī’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Hatthidamakena, bhikkhave, hatthidammo sārito ekaṃyeva disaṃ dhāvati – puratthimaṃ vā pacchimaṃ vā uttaraṃ vā dakkhiṇaṃ vā. Assadamakena, bhikkhave, assadammo sārito ekaññeva disaṃ dhāvati – puratthimaṃ vā pacchimaṃ vā uttaraṃ vā dakkhiṇaṃ vā. Godamakena, bhikkhave, godammo sārito ekaṃyeva disaṃ dhāvati – puratthimaṃ vā pacchimaṃ vā uttaraṃ vā dakkhiṇaṃ vā. Tathāgatena hi, bhikkhave, arahatā sammāsambuddhena purisadammo sārito aṭṭha disā vidhāvati. Rūpī rūpāni passati – ayaṃ ekā disā; ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī bahiddhā rūpāni passati – ayaṃ dutiyā disā; subhantveva adhimutto hoti – ayaṃ tatiyā disā; sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ catutthī disā; sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ pañcamī disā; sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ chaṭṭhī disā; sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ sattamī disā; sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ aṭṭhamī disā. Tathāgatena, bhikkhave, arahatā sammāsambuddhena purisadammo sārito imā aṭṭha disā vidhāvati. ‘So vuccati yoggācariyānaṃ anuttaro purisadammasārathī’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vutta’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Saḷāyatanavibhaṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
“So it is said: ‘Among the trainers of those who are fit to be trained, he is the unsurpassed charioteer of persons to be tamed.’ It is because of this that this was said.

But in regard to what was it said? “Guided by the elephant tamer, *bhikkhus*, the elephant to be tamed goes in one direction only—east, west, north, or south. Guided by the horse tamer, *bhikkhus*, the horse to be tamed goes in one direction only—east, west, north, or south. Guided by the ox tamer, *bhikkhus*, the ox to be tamed goes in one direction only—east, west, north, or south. Bhikkhus, guided by the *Tathāgata*, the *Arhat*, the perfectly awakened one, the person to be tamed courses in eight directions.

Possessed of material form, he sees forms: this is the first direction (*disā*). Not perceiving forms internally, he sees forms externally: this is the second direction. He is resolved only upon the beautiful: this is the third direction. With the complete surmounting of perceptions of form (*rūpa-saṃjñā*), with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact (*paṭigha-saṃjñā*), with non-attention to perceptions of diversity (*nānāttasaṃjñā*), aware that ‘space is infinite’ (*ananto ākāso*), he enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*): this is the fourth direction. With the complete surmounting of the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’ (*anantaṃ viññāṇaṃ*), he enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*): this is the fifth direction. With the complete surmounting of the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing’ (*natthi kiñcī*), he enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*): this is the sixth direction. With the complete surmounting of the base of nothingness, he enters upon and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*): this is the seventh direction. With the complete surmounting of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodha*): this is the eighth direction. Bhikkhus, guided by the *Tathāgata*, the *Arhat*, the perfectly awakened one, the person to be tamed courses in these eight directions. So it was with reference to this that it was said: ‘Among the trainers of those who are fit to be trained, he is the unsurpassed charioteer of persons to be tamed.’”

This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The seventh *Saḷāyatanavibhaṅgasuttaṃ* is finished.
commentary_pali:
312.Sāritoti damito. Ekameva disaṃ dhāvatīti anivattitvā dhāvanto ekaṃyeva disaṃ dhāvati, nivattitvā pana aparaṃ dhāvituṃ sakkoti. Aṭṭhadisā vidhāvatīti ekapallaṅkena nisinno kāyena anivattitvāva vimokkhavasena ekappahāreneva aṭṭha disā vidhāvati, puratthābhimukho vā dakkhiṇādīsu aññataradisābhimukho vā nisīditvā aṭṭha samāpattiyo samāpajjatiyevāti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Saḷāyatanavibhaṅgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
312. sārito means tamed. ekameva disaṃ dhāvatī means without turning back, he runs in one direction only. Having turned back, he is able to run in another direction. aṭṭha disā vidhāvatī means seated in one posture, without turning the body, by means of liberation, with a single strike, he runs through the eight directions. Or, having sat facing east or facing any other direction, such as south, he attains the eight attainments. The rest is clear throughout.

The commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya* called *Papañcasūdanī*

The exposition of the *Saḷāyatanavibhaṅgasutta* is complete.

mula_pali:
313. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘uddesavibhaṅgaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Tathā tathā, bhikkhave, bhikkhu upaparikkheyya yathā yathā yathā yathāssa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) upaparikkhato bahiddhā cassa viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭaṃ, ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitaṃ anupādāya na paritasseyya. Bahiddhā, bhikkhave, viññāṇe avikkhitte avisaṭe sati ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhite anupādāya aparitassato āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇadukkhasamudayasambhavo na hotī’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

yathā yathāssa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Bhikkhus!”

“Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you a summary and an exposition (uddesavibhaṅgaṃ).

Listen to that, pay close attention, I will speak.”

“As you say, lord,” those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should examine things in such a way that as he examines, his consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) is neither externally scattered (avikkhittaṃ) and diffused (avisaṭaṃ), nor internally fixated (ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitaṃ), and not clinging (anupādāya) he does not become agitated (na paritasseyya).

Bhikkhus, when consciousness (viññāṇe) is not externally scattered (avikkhitte) and diffused (avisaṭe), and not internally fixated (ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhite), and not clinging (anupādāya), he is unagitated (aparitassato), then there is no coming into being of the origination of future birth (jāti), aging (jarā), death (maraṇa), suffering (dukkha), and arising (samudayasambhavo).”

This is what the Blessed One said.

Having said this, the Happy One (sugato) rose from his seat (utthāyāsanā) and went into his dwelling (vihāraṃ pāvisi).
commentary_pali: 313.Evaṃme sutanti uddesavibhaṅgasuttaṃ. Tattha uddesavibhaṅganti uddesañca vibhaṅgañca, mātikañca vibhajanañcāti attho. Upaparikkheyyāti tuleyya tīreyya pariggaṇheyya paricchindeyya. Bahiddhāti bahiddhāārammaṇesu. Avikkhittaṃ avisaṭanti nikantivasena ārammaṇe tiṭṭhamānaṃ vikkhittaṃ visaṭaṃ nāma hoti, taṃ paṭisedhento evamāha. Ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitanti gocarajjhatte nikantivasena asaṇṭhitaṃ. Anupādāya na paritasseyyāti anupādiyitvā aggahetvā taṃ viññāṇaṃ na paritasseyya. Yathā viññāṇaṃ bahiddhā avikkhittaṃ avisaṭaṃ, ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitaṃ anupādāya na paritasseyya, evaṃ bhikkhu upaparikkheyyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Jātijarāmaraṇadukkhasamudayasambhavoti jātijarāmaraṇassa ceva avasesassa ca dukkhassa nibbatti na hotīti attho.
commentary_english:
Thus, it is what I have heard (evaṃ me suta), the *uddesavibhaṅgasutta*.

There, *uddesavibhaṅga* means *uddesa* and *vibhaṅga*, *mātika* and *vibhajana*, this is the meaning (uddesaṃca vibhaṅgaṃca, mātikaṃca vibhajanaṃcāti attho).

*Upaparikkheyyā* means to weigh, to cross over, to grasp, to discriminate (tuleyya tīreyya pariggaṇheyya paricchindeyya).

*Bahiddhā* means in external objects (bahiddhāārammaṇesu).

*Avikkhittaṃ avisaṭa* means when the mind stands in an object by way of desire, it is called scattered and diffused. Preventing that, he says thus (nikantivasena ārammaṇe tiṭṭhamānaṃ vikkhittaṃ visaṭaṃ nāma hoti, taṃ paṭisedhento evamāha).

*Ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhita* means unestablished in the inner sphere of experience (gocarajjhatte nikantivasena asaṇṭhitaṃ).

*Anupādāya na paritasseyyā* means not clinging, not grasping, he is not agitated by that consciousness (anupādiyitvā aggahetvā taṃ viññāṇaṃ na paritasseyya).

Just as consciousness is neither externally scattered and diffused, nor internally positioned, not clinging he is not agitated, thus should a *bhikṣu* investigate; it is said (yathā viññāṇaṃ bahiddhā avikkhittaṃ avisaṭaṃ, ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitaṃ anupādāya na paritasseyya, evaṃ bhikkhu upaparikkheyyāti vuttaṃ hoti).

*Jātijarāmaraṇadukkhasamudayasambhavo* means the arising of birth, aging, death, suffering, does not occur, this is the meaning (jātijarāmaraṇassa ceva avasesassa ca dukkhassa nibbatti na hotīti attho).

mula_pali:
314. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, acirapakkantassa bhagavato, etadahosi – ‘‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘tathā tathā, bhikkhave , bhikkhu upaparikkheyya yathā yathā upaparikkhato bahiddhā cassa viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭaṃ, ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitaṃ anupādāya na paritasseyya. Bahiddhā , bhikkhave, viññāṇe avikkhitte avisaṭe sati ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhite anupādāya aparitassato āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇadukkhasamudayasambhavo na hotī’ti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’’ti? Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ; pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’’ti.

Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākaccānena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etadavocuṃ –

‘‘Idaṃ kho no, āvuso kaccāna, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘tathā tathā, bhikkhave, bhikkhu upaparikkheyya yathā yathā upaparikkhato bahiddhā cassa viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭaṃ, ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitaṃ anupādāya na paritasseyya. Bahiddhā, bhikkhave, viññāṇe avikkhitte avisaṭe sati ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhite anupādāya aparitassato āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇadukkhasamudayasambhavo na hotī’ti. Tesaṃ no, āvuso kaccāna, amhākaṃ, acirapakkantassa bhagavato, etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – tathā tathā, bhikkhave, bhikkhu upaparikkheyya, yathā yathā upaparikkhato bahiddhā cassa viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭaṃ ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitaṃ anupādāya na paritasseyya. Bahiddhā, bhikkhave, viññāṇe avikkhitte avisaṭe sati ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhite anupādāya aparitassato āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇadukkhasamudayasambhavo na hotī’ti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’’ti. ‘‘Tesaṃ no, āvuso kaccāna, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti – vibhajatāyasmā mahākaccāno’’ti.
mula_english:
314.
Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the monks considered: "Friends, the Blessed One gave a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, and then rose from his seat and entered his dwelling: ‘Monks, a monk should investigate in such a way that–his consciousness neither externally scattered & diffused, nor internally positioned–and by not clinging he does not become agitated.’

If his consciousness is not distracted and scattered externally nor stuck internally, and if by not clinging he does not become agitated, then for him there is no origination of suffering - of birth, ageing, and death in the future.”

Now who will expound in detail the meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One?"

Then the monks considered: "The venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One.

Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this."

Then those monks went to the venerable Mahākaccāna and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, they sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, those monks said to the venerable Mahākaccāna:

“The Blessed One gave a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, and then rose from his seat and entered his dwelling: ‘Monks, a monk should investigate in such a way that–his consciousness neither externally scattered & diffused, nor internally positioned–and by not clinging he does not become agitated.’

If his consciousness is not distracted and scattered externally nor stuck internally, and if by not clinging he does not become agitated, then for him there is no origination of suffering - of birth, ageing, and death in the future.”

Friends, we thought, soon after the Blessed One had departed: “The Blessed One gave a summary in brief without expounding the detailed meaning, and then rose from his seat and entered his dwelling: ‘Monks, a monk should investigate in such a way that–his consciousness neither externally scattered & diffused, nor internally positioned–and by not clinging he does not become agitated.’

If his consciousness is not distracted and scattered externally nor stuck internally, and if by not clinging he does not become agitated, then for him there is no origination of suffering - of birth, ageing, and death in the future.”

Now who will expound in detail the meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One?"

Friends, we thought: “The venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One.

Suppose we went to him and asked him the meaning of this.’ May the venerable Mahākaccāna explain it!”

mula_pali:
315. ‘‘‘Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṃ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva mūlaṃ atikkamma khandhaṃ sākhāpalāse sāraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ maññeyya, evaṃ sampadamidaṃ āyasmantānaṃ satthari sammukhībhūte taṃ bhagavantaṃ atisitvā amhe etamatthaṃ paṭipucchitabbaṃ maññatha. So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ passati, cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha; yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā’’’ti. ‘Addhāvuso kaccāna, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ passati, cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma; yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāma. Api cāyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Vibhajatāyasmā mahākaccāno agaruṃ karitvā’ti. ‘Tena hāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’ti. ‘Evamāvuso’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā mahākaccāno etadavoca –

‘Yaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – tathā tathā, bhikkhave, bhikkhu upaparikkheyya, yathā yathā upaparikkhato bahiddhā cassa viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭaṃ ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitaṃ anupādāya na paritasseyya, bahiddhā, bhikkhave, viññāṇe avikkhitte avisaṭe sati ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhite anupādāya aparitassato āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇadukkhasamudayasambhavo na hotī’ti. Imassa kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi.
mula_english:
315.
"'Just as, friend, a man seeking heartwood, looking for heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, might think that the heartwood should be sought in the branches and foliage of a great tree standing possessed of heartwood, having passed over the root; so also you, venerable ones, with the Teacher in your presence, slight that Blessed One and think that we should be asked about this matter.

"For knowing, the Blessed One knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision, he is knowledge, he is the Dhamma, he is the holy one; he is the sayer, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the giver of the Deathless, the lord of the Dhamma, the *Tathāgata*.

"That was the time when you should have asked the Blessed One the meaning. As he told you, so you should have remembered it."'

"'Surely, friend Kaccāna, knowing, the Blessed One knows; seeing, he sees; he is vision, he is knowledge, he is the *Dhamma*, he is the holy one; he is the sayer, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the giver of the Deathless, the lord of the *Dhamma*, the *Tathāgata*.

"That was the time when we should have asked the Blessed One the meaning. As he told us, so we should have remembered it.'

"Yet the venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life.

"The venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of expounding the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning."

"Let the venerable Mahākaccāna expound it without finding it troublesome."

"'Then listen, friends, and attend closely to what I shall say.'

"'Yes, friend,' the monks replied to the venerable Mahākaccāna.

The venerable Mahākaccāna said this:

"'That a monk should carefully examine, bhikkhus, the way the Blessed One, having in brief indicated the outline, without analysing the meaning in detail, rises from his seat and enters his dwelling—just as he examines it, so that consciousness, when it is not scattered or diffused externally and not established internally, through lack of fuel, does not become agitated. When consciousness is not scattered or diffused externally and is not established internally, through lack of fuel, there is in the future no origination of birth, aging, death, suffering and misery.'

"I understand the detailed meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One without expounding the detailed meaning to be thus."

mula_pali: 316. ‘‘Kathañcāvuso, bahiddhā viññāṇaṃ vikkhittaṃ visaṭanti vuccati? Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā rūpanimittānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti rūpanimittassādagadhitaṃ …gathitaṃ (sī. pī.) rūpanimittassādavinibandhaṃ …vinibandhaṃ (sī. pī.) rūpanimittassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ bahiddhā viññāṇaṃ vikkhittaṃ visaṭanti vuccati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya dhammanimittānusārī viññāṇaṃ hoti; dhammanimittassādagadhitaṃ dhammanimittassādavinibandhaṃ dhammanimittassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ bahiddhā viññāṇaṃ vikkhittaṃ visaṭanti vuccati. Evaṃ kho āvuso, bahiddhā viññāṇaṃ vikkhittaṃ visaṭanti vuccati.
mula_english: “How, friends, is consciousness called ‘distracted and scattered externally?’ Here, friends, when a *bhikkhu* has seen a form with the eye, if his consciousness follows after the sign of form, is tied and shackled by gratification in the sign of form, is fettered by the fetter of gratification in the sign of form, then his consciousness is called ‘distracted and scattered externally.’ When he has heard a sound with the ear…smelt an odour with the nose…tasted a flavour with the tongue…touched a tangible with the body…cognized a mind-object with the mind, if his consciousness follows after the sign of the mind-object, is tied and shackled by gratification in the sign of the mind-object, is fettered by the fetter of gratification in the sign of the mind-object, then his consciousness is called ‘distracted and scattered externally.’ Thus, friends, is consciousness called ‘distracted and scattered externally.’
commentary_pali: 316.Rūpanimittānusārīti rūpanimittaṃ anussarati anudhāvatīti rūpanimittānusārī.
commentary_english: 316. rūpanimittānusārī, meaning "one who follows the appearance or sign" (*rūpanimittaṃ anussarati anudhāvatīti rūpanimittānusārī*).

mula_pali: 317. ‘‘Kathañcāvuso, bahiddhā viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭanti vuccati ? Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na rūpanimittānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti rūpanimittassādagadhitaṃ na rūpanimittassādavinibandhaṃ na rūpanimittassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ bahiddhā viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭanti vuccati . Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya na dhammanimittānusārī viññāṇaṃ hoti na dhammanimittassādagadhitaṃ na dhammanimittassādavinibandhaṃ na dhammanimittassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ bahiddhā viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭanti vuccati. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bahiddhā viññāṇaṃ avikkhittaṃ avisaṭanti vuccati.
mula_english:
317. “And how, friends, is consciousness called ‘not distracted and scattered externally’? Here, when a *bhikkhu* has seen a form with the eye, if his consciousness does not follow after the sign of form (*rūpanimitta*), is not tied and shackled by gratification in the sign of form (*rūpanimittassāda*), is not fettered by the fetter of gratification in the sign of form, then his consciousness is called ‘not distracted and scattered externally.’

When he has heard a sound with the ear…smelt an odor with the nose…tasted a flavor with the tongue…touched a tangible with the body, cognized a mind-object with the mind, if his consciousness does not follow after the sign of the mind-object (*dhammanimitta*), is not tied and shackled by gratification in the sign of the mind-object (*dhammanimittassāda*), is not fettered by the fetter of gratification in the sign of the mind-object, then his consciousness is called ‘not distracted and scattered externally.’

Thus, friends, is consciousness called ‘not distracted and scattered externally.’”

mula_pali:
318. ‘‘Kathañcāvuso, ajjhattaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) saṇṭhitanti vuccati? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Tassa vivekajapītisukhānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti vivekajapītisukhassādagadhitaṃ vivekajapītisukhassādavinibandhaṃ vivekajapītisukhassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ saṇṭhitanti vuccati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Tassa samādhijapītisukhānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti samādhijapītisukhassādagadhitaṃ samādhijapītisukhassādavinibandhaṃ samādhijapītisukhassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ saṇṭhitanti vuccati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Tassa upekkhānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti upekkhāsukhassādagadhitaṃ upekkhāsukhassādavinibandhaṃ upekkhāsukhassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ saṇṭhitanti vuccati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Tassa adukkhamasukhānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti adukkhamasukhassādagadhitaṃ adukkhamasukhassādavinibandhaṃ adukkhamasukhassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ saṇṭhitanti vuccati. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, ajjhattaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) saṇṭhitanti vuccati.
mula_english:
318. “And how, friend, is the mind called ‘stuck internally’ (ajjhattaṃ saṇṭhitaṃ)? Here, friend, quite secluded from sensual pleasures (kāmehi), secluded from unwholesome states (akusalehi dhammehi), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought (*savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ*), with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion (*vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ*).
If his consciousness (*viññāṇaṃ*) follows after the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion (*vivekajapītisukha*), is tied and shackled by gratification in the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion, is fettered by the fetter of gratification in the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion, then his mind is called ‘stuck internally’ (ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ saṇṭhitaṃ).

“Again, friend, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought (*vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā*), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought (*avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ*), with rapture and pleasure born of concentration (*samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ*).
If his consciousness follows after the rapture and pleasure born of concentration (*samādhijapītisukha*), is tied and shackled by gratification in the rapture and pleasure born of concentration, is fettered by the fetter of gratification in the rapture and pleasure born of concentration, then his mind is called ‘stuck internally’.

“Again, friend, with the fading away of delight (*pītiyā virāgā*), remaining imperturbable (*upekkhako*), mindful (*sato*) and clearly aware (*sampajāno*), he experiences in himself the joy (*sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti*) of which the Noble Ones (*ariyā*) say: “Happy is he who dwells with equanimity (*upekkhako*), and mindfulness (*satimā*), he enters the third *jhāna* (*tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ*).
If his consciousness follows after the equanimity (*upekkhā*), is tied and shackled by gratification in the equanimity and pleasure, is fettered by the fetter of gratification in the equanimity and pleasure, then his mind is called ‘stuck internally’.

“Again, friend, with the abandoning of pleasure (*sukhassa pahānā*) and pain (*dukkhassa pahānā*), and with the previous disappearance of joy (*somanassa*) and grief (*domanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā*), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*) and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity (*upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ*).
If his consciousness follows after the neither-pain-nor-pleasure (*adukkhamasukha*), is tied and shackled by gratification in the neither-pain-nor-pleasure, is fettered by the fetter of gratification in the neither-pain-nor-pleasure, then his mind is called ‘stuck internally’.
That is how, friend, the mind is called ‘stuck internally’ (ajjhattaṃ saṇṭhitaṃ).
commentary_pali: 318.Evaṃ kho, āvuso, ajjhattaṃ asaṇṭhitanti nikantivasena asaṇṭhitaṃ. Nikantivasena hi atiṭṭhamānaṃ hānabhāgiyaṃ na hoti, visesabhāgiyameva hoti.
commentary_english: Thus indeed, friend, "unestablished internally" means unestablished in the sense of rejection. For, being unestablished in the sense of rejection, it does not partake of decline, but rather, it partakes of distinction.

mula_pali:
319. ‘‘Kathañcāvuso , ajjhattaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) asaṇṭhitanti vuccati? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Tassa na vivekajapītisukhānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti na vivekajapītisukhassādagadhitaṃ na vivekajapītisukhassādavinibandhaṃ na vivekajapītisukhassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ asaṇṭhitanti vuccati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Tassa na samādhijapītisukhānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti na samādhijapītisukhassādagadhitaṃ na samādhijapītisukhassādavinibandhaṃ na samādhijapītisukhassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ asaṇṭhitanti vuccati .

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Tassa na upekkhānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti na upekkhāsukhassādagadhitaṃ na upekkhāsukhassādavinibandhaṃ na upekkhāsukhassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ asaṇṭhitanti vuccati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Tassa na adukkhamasukhānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti na adukkhamasukhassādagadhitaṃ na adukkhamasukhassādavinibandhaṃ na adukkhamasukhassādasaṃyojanasaṃyuttaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ asaṇṭhitanti vuccati. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, ajjhattaṃ ajjhattaṃ cittaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) asaṇṭhitanti vuccati.
mula_english:
319. “And how, friends, is the mind called ‘not stuck internally’? Here, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*. If his consciousness does not follow after the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion ( *vivekajapītisukha*), is not tied and shackled by gratification in the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion, is not fettered by the fetter of gratification in the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion, then his mind is called ‘not stuck internally.’

“Again, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought (*vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā*), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*. If his consciousness does not follow after the rapture and pleasure born of concentration (*samādhijapītisukha*), is not tied and shackled by gratification in the rapture and pleasure born of concentration, is not fettered by the fetter of gratification in the rapture and pleasure born of concentration, then his mind is called ‘not stuck internally.’

“Again, with the fading away as well of rapture (*pītiyā ca virāgā*), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*. If his consciousness does not follow after the equanimity (*upekkhā*), is not tied and shackled by gratification in the pleasure of equanimity, is not fettered by the fetter of gratification in the pleasure of equanimity, then his mind is called ‘not stuck internally.’

“Again, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain (*sukkhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā*), and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief (*somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā*), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*) and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity (*upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ*). If his consciousness does not follow after the neither-pain-nor-pleasure (*adukkhamasukha*), is not tied and shackled by gratification in the neither-pain-nor-pleasure, is not fettered by the fetter of gratification in the neither-pain-nor-pleasure, then his mind is called ‘not stuck internally.’

That is how, friends, the mind is called ‘not stuck internally.’

mula_pali: 320. ‘‘Kathañcāvuso, anupādā paritassanā hoti? Idhāvuso, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā rūpaṃ rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tassa taṃ rūpaṃ vipariṇamati, aññathā hoti. Tassa rūpavipariṇāmaññathābhāvā rūpavipariṇāmānuparivatti viññāṇaṃ hoti. Tassa rūpavipariṇāmānuparivattajā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti. Cetaso pariyādānā uttāsavā ca hoti vighātavā ca apekkhavā ca anupādāya ca paritassati. Vedanaṃ …pe… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ attani vā viññāṇaṃ viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tassa taṃ viññāṇaṃ vipariṇamati, aññathā hoti. Tassa viññāṇavipariṇāmaññathābhāvā viññāṇavipariṇāmānuparivatti viññāṇaṃ hoti. Tassa viññāṇavipariṇāmānuparivattajā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti. Cetaso pariyādānā uttāsavā ca hoti vighātavā ca apekkhavā ca anupādāya ca paritassati. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, anupādā paritassanā hoti.
mula_english: 320. “But how, friend, is there agitation due to non-clinging? Here, friend, an untaught ordinary person who has no regard for noble ones and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, who has no regard for true men and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, regards material form as self, or self as possessed of material form, or material form as in self, or self as in material form. That form of his changes and alters. With the change and becoming otherwise of that material form, his consciousness is preoccupied with the change of material form. Agitation and a constellation of mental states born of preoccupation with the change of form remain obsessing his mind. Because his mind is obsessed, he is frightened, distressed, and anxious, and through non-clinging he becomes agitated. He regards feeling as self … perception as self … volitional formations as self … consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. That consciousness of his changes and alters. With the change and becoming otherwise of that consciousness, his consciousness is preoccupied with the change of consciousness. Agitation and a constellation of mental states born of preoccupation with the change of consciousness remain obsessing his mind. Because his mind is obsessed, he is frightened, distressed, and anxious, and through non-clinging he becomes agitated. That is how, friend, there is agitation due to non-clinging.
commentary_pali:
320.Anupādā paritassanāti satthārā khandhiyavagge ‘‘upādāparitassanañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anupādāaparitassanañcā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 3.7) evaṃ gahetvā paritassanā, aggahetvāva aparitassanā ca kathitā, taṃ mahāthero upādāparitassanameva anupādāparitassananti katvā dassento evamāha. Kathaṃ panesā anupādāparitassanā hotīti. Upādātabbassa abhāvato. Yadi hi koci saṅkhāro nicco vā dhuvo vā attā vā attaniyo vāti gahetabbayuttako abhavissa, ayaṃ paritassanā upādāparitassanāva assa. Yasmā pana evaṃ upādātabbo saṅkhāro nāma natthi, tasmā rūpaṃ attātiādinā nayena rūpādayo upādinnāpi anupādinnāva honti. Evamesā diṭṭhivasena upādāparitassanāpi samānā atthato anupādāparitassanāyeva nāma hotīti veditabbā.

Aññathā hotīti parivattati pakatijahanena nassati, rūpavipariṇāmānuparivattīti ‘‘mama rūpaṃ vipariṇata’’nti vā, ‘‘yaṃ ahu, taṃ vata me natthī’’ti vā ādinā (ma. ni. 1.242) nayena kammaviññāṇaṃ rūpassa bhedānuparivatti hoti. Vipariṇāmānuparivattajāti vipariṇāmassa anuparivattanato vipariṇāmārammaṇacittato jātā. Paritassanā dhammasamuppādāti taṇhāparitassanā ca akusaladhammasamuppādā ca. Cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhantīti kusalacittaṃ pariyādiyitvā gahetvā khepetvā tiṭṭhanti. Uttāsavāti bhayatāsenapi sauttāso taṇhātāsenapi sauttāso. Vighātavāti savighāto sadukkho. Apekkhavāti sālayo sasineho. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, anupādā paritassanā hotīti evaṃ maṇikaraṇḍakasaññāya tucchakaraṇḍakaṃ gahetvā tasmiṃ naṭṭhe pacchā vighātaṃ āpajjantassa viya pacchā aggahetvā paritassanā hoti.

Aññathā hotī rūpavipariṇāmānuparivattī Vipariṇāmānuparivattajā Paritassanā dhammasamuppādā Cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhantī Uttāsavā Vighātavā Apekkhavā Evaṃ kho, āvuso, anupādā paritassanā hotī
commentary_english:
320. “*Anupādā paritassanā*": The Teacher in the Khandhiya Vagga said, “I will teach you *upādāparitassanā* and *anupādāaparitassanā*” (Saṃ. Ni. 3.7). Thus, *paritassanā* is explained as seizing, and *aparitassanā* as not seizing. The great elder, showing that *upādāparitassana* is the same as *anupādāparitassana*, said thus:

How then does this *anupādāparitassanā* come to be? From the absence of what should be seized. If there were any saṃkhāra that were permanent (*nicca*) or lasting (*dhruva*) or a self (*ātmā*) or belonged to a self (*āttaniyo*) that could be rightly seized, then this *paritassanā* would be just *upādāparitassanā*. But since there is no saṃkhāra called that which should be seized, therefore, by the method beginning with “form is self” (*rūpaṃ attā*), forms (*rūpādayo*) are seized, yet they are just not seized (*anupādinnāva honti*). Thus, this *upādāparitassanā*, though the same from the viewpoint of views (*diṭṭhivasena*), is actually called just *anupādāparitassanā* in meaning (*atthato*).

"*Aññathā hotī*": it changes, it perishes by abandoning its nature. "*Rūpavipariṇāmānuparivattī*": “My form has changed (*mama rūpaṃ vipariṇata*)” or “What was, that is not mine (*yaṃ ahu, taṃ vata me natthī*)”, etc. (Ma. Ni. 1.242). By this method, consciousness of karma (*kammaviññāṇaṃ*) follows the dissolution (*bheda*) of form (*rūpassa*). "*Vipariṇāmānuparivattajā*": born from the transformation (*vipariṇāma*) following the mind that has the transformation as its object (*vipariṇāmārammaṇacittato jātā*). "*Paritassanā dhammasamuppādā*": craving- *paritassanā* (*taṇhāparitassanā*) and the arising of unwholesome things (*akusaladhammasamuppādā ca*). "*Cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhantī*": having completely taken possession of the wholesome mind (*kusalacittaṃ pariyādiyitvā*), they seize it, destroy it, and remain. "*Uttāsavā*": fearful (*bhayatāsenapi*) and very anxious (*sauttāso*), and also very anxious (*sauttāso*) with craving-fear (*taṇhātāsenapi*). "*Vighātavā*": with obstruction (*savighāto*), with suffering (*sadukkho*). "*Apekkhavā*": with attachment (*sālayo*), with affection (*sasineho*). "*Evaṃ kho, āvuso, anupādā paritassanā hotī*": Thus, having taken an empty basket (*tucchakaraṇḍakaṃ gahetvā*) with the perception of a jeweled basket (*maṇikaraṇḍakasaññāya*), when that is lost (*tasmiṃ naṭṭhe*), just as for one who experiences obstruction afterwards (*pacchā vighātaṃ āpajjantassa viya*), so afterwards, not seizing (*aggahetvā*), there is *paritassanā*.

*Aññathā hotī*, *rūpavipariṇāmānuparivattī*, *vipariṇāmānuparivattajā*, *paritassanā dhammasamuppādā*, *cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhantī*, *uttāsavā*, *vighātavā*, *apekkhavā*, *evaṃ kho, āvuso, anupādā paritassanā hotī*.

mula_pali:
321. ‘‘Kathañcāvuso, anupādānā aparitassanā hoti? Idhāvuso, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati na rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ na attani vā rūpaṃ na rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tassa taṃ rūpaṃ vipariṇamati, aññathā hoti. Tassa rūpavipariṇāmaññathābhāvā na ca rūpavipariṇāmānuparivatti viññāṇaṃ hoti. Tassa na rūpavipariṇāmānuparivattajā paritassanā dhammasamuppādā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti. Cetaso pariyādānā na cevuttāsavā na ca uttāsavā (sī.) hoti na ca vighātavā na ca apekkhavā anupādāya ca na paritassati.
