*Santimeva so sikkheyyā*

mula_pali: 344. ‘‘‘Chadhāturo ayaṃ, bhikkhu, puriso’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? (Chayimā, bhikkhu, dhātuyo) ( ) natthi sī. pī. potthakesu – pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, ākāsadhātu, viññāṇadhātu. ‘Chadhāturo ayaṃ, bhikkhu, puriso’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
344. “‘Bhikkhu, this person consists of six elements ( *ṣaṭ-dhātu* ).’ So it was said.

And with reference to what was this said? (These six elements, bhikkhu:) the earth element (*pṛthivī-dhātu*), the water element (*āpo-dhātu*), the fire element (*tejo-dhātu*), the air element (*vāyu-dhātu*), the space element (*ākāśa-dhātu*), and the consciousness element (*vijñāna-dhātu*).

So it was with reference to this that it was said: ‘Bhikkhu, this person consists of six elements.’

mula_pali: 345. ‘‘‘Chaphassāyatano ayaṃ, bhikkhu, puriso’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Cakkhusamphassāyatanaṃ, sotasamphassāyatanaṃ, ghānasamphassāyatanaṃ, jivhāsamphassāyatanaṃ, kāyasamphassāyatanaṃ, manosamphassāyatanaṃ. ‘Chaphassāyatano ayaṃ, bhikkhu, puriso’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
345.
‘“Bhikkhu, this person consists of six bases of contact ( *chaphassāyatana* ).”’ So it was said.

With reference to what was it said? It was with reference to the base of eye-contact (*cakkhusamphassāyatanaṃ*), the base of ear-contact (*sotasamphassāyatanaṃ*), the base of nose-contact (*ghānasamphassāyatanaṃ*), the base of tongue-contact (*jivhāsamphassāyatanaṃ*), the base of body-contact (*kāyasamphassāyatanaṃ*), and the base of mind-contact (*manosamphassāyatanaṃ*).

So it was with reference to this that it was said: ‘“Bhikkhu, this person consists of six bases of contact.”’
commentary_pali: 345.Phassāyatananti phassassa āyatanaṃ, ākaroti attho. Paññādhiṭṭhānantiādīni pubbe vuttānaṃ arahattaphalapaññādīnaṃ vasena veditabbāni.
commentary_english: 345. phassāyatananti: phassa’s āyatanaṃ, meaning "it produces." paññādhiṭṭhānanti, etc.: these should be understood in terms of the previously stated fruits of ship, wisdom, etc.

mula_pali: 346. ‘‘‘Aṭṭhārasamanopavicāro ayaṃ, bhikkhu, puriso’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā somanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati, domanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati, upekkhāṭṭhānīyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati; sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya somanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati, domanassaṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati , upekkhāṭṭhānīyaṃ dhammaṃ upavicarati – iti cha somanassupavicārā, cha domanassupavicārā, cha upekkhupavicārā. ‘Aṭṭhārasamanopavicāro ayaṃ, bhikkhu, puriso’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
346. “‘Bhikkhu, this person consists of eighteen kinds of mental exploration.’ So it was said.

With reference to what was this said? On seeing a *rūpa* (form) with the eye, one explores a *rūpa* productive of joy ( *saumanasya*), one explores a *rūpa* productive of grief (*daumanasya*), one explores a *rūpa* productive of equanimity (*upekṣā*); On hearing a sound (*śabda*) with the ear…On smelling an odour (*gandha*) with the nose…On tasting a flavour (*rasa*) with the tongue… On touching a tangible (*sparśa*) with the body…On cognizing a *dharma* (mind-object) with the mind, one explores a *dharma* productive of joy (*saumanasya*), one explores a *dharma* productive of grief (*daumanasya*), one explores a *dharma* productive of equanimity (*upekṣā*) - thus there are six explorations productive of joy (*saumanasya*), six explorations productive of grief (*daumanasya*), six explorations productive of equanimity (*upekṣā*).

So it was with reference to this that it was said: ‘Bhikkhu, this person consists of eighteen kinds of mental exploration.’

mula_pali: 347. ‘‘‘Caturādhiṭṭhāno ayaṃ, bhikkhu, puriso’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Paññādhiṭṭhāno, saccādhiṭṭhāno, cāgādhiṭṭhāno, upasamādhiṭṭhāno. ‘Caturādhiṭṭhāno ayaṃ, bhikkhu, puriso’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
347. “‘Bhikkhu, this person has four foundations’—so it was said.

What was said with reference to this? The foundation of wisdom (*prajñādhiṣṭhāna*), the foundation of truth (*satyādhiṣṭhāna*), the foundation of generosity (*tyāgādhiṣṭhāna*), the foundation of tranquility (*upaśamādhiṣṭhāna*).

So it was with reference to this that it was said: ‘Bhikkhu, this person has four foundations.’

mula_pali: 348. ‘‘‘Paññaṃ nappamajjeyya, saccamanurakkheyya, cāgamanubrūheyya, santimeva so sikkheyyā’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Kathañca, bhikkhu, paññaṃ nappamajjati? Chayimā, bhikkhu, dhātuyo – pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, ākāsadhātu, viññāṇadhātu.
mula_english:
"‘One should not neglect wisdom (paññā), should preserve truth (sacca), should cultivate relinquishment (cāga), and should train for peace (santi).’ So it was said.

With reference to what was this said? And how, *bhikkhu*, does one not neglect wisdom (paññā)? There are these six elements (*dhātu*), *bhikkhu*: the earth element (*pathavīdhātu*), the water element (*āpodhātu*), the fire element (*tejodhātu*), the air element (*vāyodhātu*), the space element (*ākāsadhātu*), and the consciousness element (*viññāṇadhātu*)."
commentary_pali: 348. Idāni nikkhittamātikāvasena ‘‘yattha ṭhitaṃ maññassa vā nappavattantī’’ti vattabbaṃ bhaveyya, arahatte pana patte puna ‘‘paññaṃ nappamajjeyyā’’tiādīhi kiccaṃ natthi. Iti bhagavā mātikaṃ uppaṭipāṭidhātukaṃ ṭhapetvāpi yathādhammavaseneva vibhaṅgaṃ vibhajanto paññaṃ nappamajjeyyātiādimāha. Tattha ko paññaṃ pamajjati, ko nappamajjati? Yo tāva imasmiṃ sāsane pabbajitvā vejjakammādivasena ekavīsatividhāya anesanāya jīvikaṃ kappento pabbajjānurūpena cittuppādaṃ ṭhapetuṃ na sakkoti, ayaṃ paññaṃ pamajjati nāma. Yo pana sāsane pabbajitvā sīle patiṭṭhāya buddhavacanaṃ uggaṇhitvā sappāyaṃ dhutaṅgaṃ samādāya cittarucitaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ nissāya kasiṇaparikammaṃ katvā samāpattiṃ patvā ajjeva arahattanti vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā vicarati, ayaṃ paññaṃ nappamajjati nāma. Imasmiṃ pana sutte dhātukammaṭṭhānavasena esa paññāya appamādo vutto. Dhātukammaṭṭhāne panettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā hatthipadopamasuttādīsu vuttameva.
commentary_english:
348. Now, according to the *nikkhittamātikā*, it should be stated, "Where, if he remains, thoughts do not arise," but upon attaining *arhatship*, there is no further need for things like "one should not neglect wisdom" and so forth.

Thus, the Blessed One, having set aside the *mātikā* with its reversed order of elements, spoke as follows while distinguishing the distinctions in accordance with the nature of the *dharma*: "One should not neglect wisdom" and so forth.

Therein, who neglects wisdom, and who does not neglect wisdom? He who, having gone forth in this dispensation (*sāsana*), makes a living by means of twenty-one kinds of improper livelihood like medical practice, is unable to establish a mind-moment (*cittuppāda*) in accordance with his ordination; this one is said to neglect wisdom.

But he who, having gone forth in the dispensation, being established in morality (*sīla*), having learned the Buddha's word (*buddhavacana*), having undertaken suitable ascetic practices (*dhutaṅga*), having taken up a practice (*kammaṭṭhāna*) pleasing to the mind, relying on a secluded dwelling (*senāsana*), having performed the preliminary exercises (*parikamma*) with *kasina*, having attained *samāpatti*, thinking "today itself [I will attain] *arhatship*," cultivates insight (*vipaśyanā*) and wanders about, this one is said not to neglect wisdom.

In this *sūtra*, this non-neglect of wisdom (*apramāda*) is spoken of in terms of the element-practice (*dhātukammaṭṭhāna*).

And herein, whatever should be said about the element-practice, that has already been said below in the *Hatthipadopama Sutta* and so forth.

mula_pali: 349. ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhu, pathavīdhātu? Pathavīdhātu siyā ajjhattikā siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ upādinnaṃ upādiṇṇaṃ (pī. ka.), seyyathidaṃ – kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ aṭṭhimiñjā (sī. pī.) vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu yā ca bāhirā pathavīdhātu pathavīdhāturevesā . ‘Taṃ netaṃ mama nesohamasmi na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā pathavīdhātuyā nibbindati, pathavīdhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
349.
‘‘And what, *bhikkhu*, is the earth element (*pathavīdhātu*)? The earth element (*pathavīdhātu*) can be internal (*ajjhattikā*) or external (*bāhirā*).

And what, *bhikkhu*, is the internal earth element (*ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu*)? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself, is solid (*kakkhaḷaṃ*), solidified (*kharigataṃ*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*), that is, head-hairs (*kesā*), body-hairs (*lomā*), nails (*nakhā*), teeth (*dantā*), skin (*taco*), flesh (*maṃsaṃ*), sinews (*nhāru*), bones (*aṭṭhi*), bone-marrow (*aṭṭhimiñjaṃ*), kidneys (*vakkaṃ*), heart (*hadayaṃ*), liver (*yakanaṃ*), diaphragm (*kilomakaṃ*), spleen (*pihakaṃ*), lungs (*papphāsaṃ*), intestines (*antaṃ*), mesentery (*antaguṇaṃ*), contents of the stomach (*udariyaṃ*), feces (*karīsaṃ*), or whatever else internally, belonging to oneself, is solid (*kakkhaḷaṃ*), solidified (*kharigataṃ*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*)—this is called the internal earth element (*ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu*).

Now both the internal earth element (*ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu*) and the external earth element (*bāhirā pathavīdhātu*) are simply earth element (*pathavīdhātu*).

‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not myself (*na meso attā*)’—and that should be seen as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*).

When one sees it thus as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*), one becomes disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with the earth element (*pathavīdhātuyā*) and makes the mind dispassionate (*virājeti*) towards the earth element (*pathavīdhātuyā*).

mula_pali: 350. ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhu, āpodhātu? Āpodhātu siyā ajjhattikā siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā āpodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ upādinnaṃ seyyathidaṃ – pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā āpodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā āpodhātu yā ca bāhirā āpodhātu āpodhāturevesā. ‘Taṃ netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā āpodhātuyā nibbindati, āpodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
350.
"And what, *bhikkhu* (mendicant), is the water element (*āpodhātu*)? The water element may be internal (*ajjhattikā*) or external (*bāhirā*).

And what, *bhikkhu*, is the internal water element? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself, is water, watery, and clung-to, that is, bile (*pittaṃ*), phlegm (*semhaṃ*), pus (*pubbo*), blood (*lohitaṃ*), sweat (*sedo*), fat (*medo*), tears (*assu*), grease (*vasā*), spittle (*kheḷo*), snot (*siṅghāṇikā*), oil-of-the-joints (*lasikā*), urine (*muttaṃ*), or whatever else internally, belonging to oneself, is water, watery, and clung-to: this is called the internal water element (*ajjhattikā āpodhātu*).

Now both the internal water element and the external water element are simply water element (*āpodhātu*).

‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’ (*taṃ netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti*) – and that should be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom (*yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ*).

When one sees it thus as it actually is with proper wisdom (*yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā*), one becomes disenchanted with the water element (*āpodhātuyā nibbindati*) and makes the mind dispassionate towards the water element (*āpodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti*).

mula_pali: 351. ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhu, tejodhātu? Tejodhātu siyā ajjhattikā siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā tejodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – yena ca santappati, yena ca jīrīyati, yena ca pariḍayhati, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā tejodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā tejodhātu yā ca bāhirā tejodhātu tejodhāturevesā. ‘Taṃ netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā tejodhātuyā nibbindati, tejodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
351. "And what, *bhikkhu*, is the fire element (*tejodhātu*)? The fire element may be internal (*ajjhattikā*) or may be external (*bāhirā*).

And what, *bhikkhu*, is the internal fire element (*ajjhattikā tejodhātu*)? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself (*ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ*), is fire (*tejo*), fiery (*tejogataṃ*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*), that is to say (*seyyathidaṃ*)—that by which one is warmed (*santappati*), that by which one ages (*jīrīyati*), that by which one is consumed (*pariḍayhati*), and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed and tasted (*asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ*) gets completely digested (*sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati*), or whatever else (*panaññampi kiñci*) internally, belonging to oneself (*ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ*), is fire (*tejo*), fiery (*tejogataṃ*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*)—this is called (*vuccati*), *bhikkhu*, the internal fire element (*ajjhattikā tejodhātu*).

Now both the internal fire element (*ajjhattikā tejodhātu*) and the external fire element (*bāhirā tejodhātu*) are simply fire element (*tejodhāturevesā*).

‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā*)’—and that should be seen as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*)

When one sees it thus as it actually is (*evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*), one becomes disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with the fire element (*tejodhātuyā*) and makes the mind (*cittaṃ*) dispassionate (*virājeti*) towards the fire element (*tejodhātuyā*).

mula_pali: 352. ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhu, vāyodhātu? Vāyodhātu siyā ajjhattikā siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – uddhaṅgamā vātā adhogamā vātā kucchisayā vātā koṭṭhāsayā koṭṭhasayā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vātā aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā assāso passāso iti, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā vāyodhātu yā ca bāhirā vāyodhātu vāyodhāturevesā. ‘Taṃ netaṃ mama , nesohamasmi , na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā vāyodhātuyā nibbindati, vāyodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
And what, O mendicant, is the air element (*vāyodhātu*)? The air element may be internal (*ajjhattikā*) or external (*bāhirā*).

And what, O mendicant, is the internal air element (*ajjhattikā vāyodhātu*)? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself, is air, airy, and clung-to; that is, up-going winds (*uddhhaṅgamā vātā*), down-going winds (*adhogamā vātā*), winds in the belly (*kucchisayā vātā*), winds in the bowels (*koṭṭhāsayā vātā*), winds that course through the limbs (*aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā*), in-breath (*assāso*) and out-breath (*passāso*), or whatever else internally, belonging to oneself, is air, airy, and clung-to: this is called the internal air element (*ajjhattikā vāyodhātu*).

Now both the internal air element (*ajjhattikā vāyodhātu*) and the external air element (*bāhirā vāyodhātu*) are simply air element (*vāyodhātu*).

‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā*)’—thus should this be seen as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*).

When one sees it thus as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*), one becomes disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with the air element (*vāyodhātu*) and makes the mind (*cittaṃ*) dispassionate (*virājeti*) toward the air element (*vāyodhātu*).

mula_pali: 353. ‘‘Katamā ca, bhikkhu, ākāsadhātu? Ākāsadhātu siyā ajjhattikā siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, bhikkhu, ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu ? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāsaṃ ākāsagataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṇṇacchiddaṃ nāsacchiddaṃ mukhadvāraṃ yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ ajjhoharati, yattha ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ santiṭṭhati, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ adhobhāgaṃ adhobhāgā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) devadūtasuttena sameti nikkhamati, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāsaṃ ākāsagataṃ aghaṃ aghagataṃ vivaraṃ vivaragataṃ asamphuṭṭhaṃ maṃsalohitehi upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati bhikkhu ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu yā ca bāhirā ākāsadhātu ākāsadhāturevesā. ‘Taṃ netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā ākāsadhātuyā nibbindati, ākāsadhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
353. And what, O monk, is the space element (ākāśadhātu)? The space element may be internal (ajjhattikā) or may be external (bāhirā).

And what, O monk, is the internal space element (ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu)? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself, is space (ākāśa), spatial (ākāsagata), and clung-to (upādinnaṃ), that is, the holes of the ears (kaṇṇacchiddaṃ), the nostrils (nāsacchiddaṃ), the door of the mouth (mukhadvāraṃ), and that aperture whereby what is eaten (asita), drunk (pīta), consumed (khāyita), and tasted (sāyita) gets swallowed (ajjhoharati), and where what is eaten, drunk, consumed, and tasted collects (santiṭṭhati), and whereby what is eaten, drunk, consumed, and tasted is excreted from below (adhobhāgaṃ nikkhamati), or whatever else internally, belonging to oneself, is space, spatial, and an aperture (vivara), belonging to an aperture (vivaragata), untouched (asamphuṭṭha) by flesh and blood (maṃsalohitehi), and clung-to: this is called the internal space element (ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu).

Now, both the internal space element (ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu) and the external space element (bāhirā ākāsadhātu) are simply space element (ākāsadhāturevesā).

‘This is not mine (netaṃ mama), this I am not (nesohamasmi), this is not my self (na meso attā)’ti – and that should be seen as it actually is (yathābhūtaṃ) with proper wisdom (sammappaññāya).

When one sees it thus as it actually is with proper wisdom (sammappaññāya), one becomes disenchanted (nibbindati) with the space element (ākāsadhātuyā) and makes the mind dispassionate (virājeti) towards the space element (ākāsadhātuyā).

mula_pali: 354. ‘‘Athāparaṃ viññāṇaṃyeva avasissati parisuddhaṃ pariyodātaṃ. Tena ca viññāṇena kiṃ tena viññāṇena kiñca (sī.) vijānāti? ‘Sukha’ntipi vijānāti, ‘dukkha’ntipi vijānāti, ‘adukkhamasukha’ntipi vijānāti. Sukhavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhu, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhā vedanā. So sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Tasseva sukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannā sukhā vedanā sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti.
mula_english:
354. Then there remains only consciousness (*vijñāṇa*), purified and cleansed.

What does one cognize with that consciousness (*vijñāṇa*)? One cognizes: ‘This is pleasant’ (*sukha*); one cognizes: ‘This is painful’ (*duḥkha*); one cognizes: ‘This is neither-painful-nor-pleasant’ (*adukkhamasukha*).

In dependence on a contact to be felt as pleasant (*sukhavedanīyaṃ*), there arises a pleasant (*sukhā*) feeling (*vedanā*).

When one feels a pleasant (*sukhaṃ*) feeling (*vedanaṃ*), one understands: ‘I feel a pleasant (*sukhaṃ*) feeling (*vedanaṃ*)’.

One understands: ‘With the cessation of that same contact to be felt as pleasant (*sukhavedanīyassa*), its corresponding feeling (*vedayitaṃ*) - the pleasant (*sukhā*) feeling (*vedanā*) that arose in dependence on that contact to be felt as pleasant (*sukhavedanīyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannā*) - ceases (*nirujjhati*) and subsides (*vūpasammati*)’.
commentary_pali: 354.Athāparaṃviññāṇaṃyeva avasissatīti ayampettha pāṭiyekko anusandhi. Heṭṭhato hi rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ kathitaṃ, idāni arūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ vedanāvasena nibbattetvā dassetuṃ ayaṃ desanā āraddhā. Yaṃ vā panetaṃ imassa bhikkhuno pathavīdhātuādīsu āgamaniyavipassanāvasena kammakārakaviññāṇaṃ, taṃ viññāṇadhātuvasena bhājetvā dassentopi imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha avasissatīti kimatthāya avasissati? Satthu kathanatthāya kulaputtassa ca paṭivijjhanatthāya avasissati. Parisuddhanti nirupakkilesaṃ. Pariyodātanti pabhassaraṃ. Sukhantipi vijānātīti sukhavedanaṃ vedayamāno sukhavedanaṃ vedayāmīti pajānāti. Sesapadadvayesupi eseva nayo. Sace panāyaṃ vedanākathā heṭṭhā na kathitā bhaveyya, idha ṭhatvā kathetuṃ vaṭṭeyya. Satipaṭṭhāne panesā kathitāvāti tattha kathitanayeneva veditabbā. Sukhavedaniyanti evamādi paccayavasena udayatthaṅgamanadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha sukhavedaniyanti sukhavedanāya paccayabhūtaṃ. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.
commentary_english: 354. Furthermore, "then only consciousness remains" (athāparaṃ viññāṇaṃyeva avasissatīti) is in this context a connection that pertains to a specific text. Below, the rūpakammaṭṭhāna has been discussed. Now, this teaching (desanā) is begun in order to show, by producing the arūpakammaṭṭhāna through the perspective of feeling (vedanāvasena). Or, having divided and shown as the consciousness element (viññāṇadhātuvasena) that consciousness as the agent of action (kammakārakaviññāṇaṃ) of this *bhikṣu* with regard to the earth element (pathavīdhātu) etc., in terms of the āgamaniyavipassanā, he began this teaching. There, "remains" (avasissatīti): for what purpose does it remain? It remains for the purpose of the teacher's statement (satthu kathanatthāya), and for the clansman's (kulaputtassa) penetration (paṭivijjhanatthāya). "Pure" (parisuddhaṃ) means without defilements (nirupakkilesaṃ). "Bright" (pariyodātaṃ) means radiant (pabhassaraṃ). "He understands 'pleasant' (sukhantipi vijānātīti)" means experiencing a pleasant feeling (sukhavedanaṃ), he understands, "I am experiencing a pleasant feeling" (sukhavedanaṃ vedayāmīti pajānāti). The same method (seva nayo) applies to the other two phrases as well. If this talk about feeling had not been spoken of below, it would be fitting to speak having stayed here. But it was spoken of in the *satipaṭṭhāna*; it should be understood according to the method spoken of there. "Leading to a pleasant feeling (sukhavedaniyaṃti)" etc. is said for the purpose of showing arising, cessation, and going away, in terms of conditions. There, "leading to a pleasant feeling" (sukhavedaniyaṃti) means the condition for a pleasant feeling (sukhavedanāya paccayabhūtaṃ). The same method (seva nayo) applies to the remaining phrases (sesapadesupi).

mula_pali: 355. ‘‘Dukkhavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhu, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dukkhā vedanā. So dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Tasseva dukkhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannā dukkhā vedanā sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti.
mula_english:
"O mendicant, in dependence on a contact to be felt as painful (duḥkhavedanīyaṃ), there arises a painful feeling (duḥkhā vedanā).

When one feels a painful feeling (dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ), one understands: ‘I feel a painful feeling (dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti).’

One understands: ‘With the cessation of that same contact to be felt as painful (dukkhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā), its corresponding feeling - the painful feeling (dukkhā vedanā) that arose in dependence on that contact to be felt as painful - ceases and subsides (sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti)."

mula_pali: 356. ‘‘Adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhu, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati adukkhamasukhā vedanā. So adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Tasseva adukkhamasukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannā adukkhamasukhā vedanā sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti.
mula_english:
Here, bhikkhus, in dependence on a contact (sparśaṃ pratītya) to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant (adukkhamasukhavedanīyaṃ), there arises a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (adukkhamasukhā vedanā).

When experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno), one understands: "I am experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmīti)."

One understands: ‘With the cessation (nirodhā) of that same contact (sparśasya) to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant (adukkhamasukhavedanīyassa), its corresponding feeling (yad tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ) - the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (adukkhamasukhā vedanā) that arose in dependence on that contact (sparśaṃ paṭicca uppannā) to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant (adukkhamasukhavedanīyaṃ) - ceases (sā nirujjhati) and subsides (sā vūpasammatī’ti).’

mula_pali: 357. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, dvinnaṃ kaṭṭhānaṃ saṅghaṭṭā samphassa (sī. pī.), saṅghaṭā (syā. kaṃ.) samodhānā usmā jāyati, tejo abhinibbattati, tesaṃyeva dvinnaṃ kaṭṭhānaṃ nānābhāvā vikkhepā yā tajjā usmā sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammati; evameva kho, bhikkhu, sukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhā vedanā. So sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Tasseva sukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannā sukhā vedanā sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti.
mula_english: Bhikkhu, just as from the contact and friction of two fire-sticks ( *dvinnaṃ kaṭṭhānaṃ saṅghaṭṭā* ) heat (*usmā*) is generated and fire (*tejas*) is produced, and with the separation and disjunction of these two fire-sticks the corresponding heat ceases and subsides; so too, bhikkhu, in dependence on a contact to be felt as pleasant ( *sukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca* ) there arises a pleasant feeling ( *sukhā vedanā* ). When one feels a pleasant feeling ( *sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno* ), one understands: ‘I feel a pleasant feeling ( *sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti* ).’ One understands: ‘With the cessation of that same contact to be felt as pleasant ( *tasseva sukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā* ), its corresponding feeling - the pleasant feeling that arose in dependence on that contact to be felt as pleasant - ceases and subsides ( *sā vūpasammati’ti pajānāti* ).’

mula_pali: 358. ‘‘Dukkhavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhu, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dukkhā vedanā. So dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Tasseva dukkhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannā dukkhā vedanā sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti.
mula_english: "Bhikkhu, in dependence on a contact to be felt as painful, there arises a painful feeling. When one feels a painful feeling, one understands: ‘I feel a painful feeling.’ One understands: ‘With the cessation of that same contact to be felt as painful, its corresponding feeling - the painful feeling that arose in dependence on that contact to be felt as painful - ceases and subsides.’"

mula_pali: 359. ‘‘Adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ , bhikkhu, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati adukkhamasukhā vedanā. So adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Tasseva adukkhamasukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannā adukkhamasukhā vedanā sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti.
mula_english:
359. Bhikkhu, in dependence on a contact to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant (*adukkhamasukhavedanīyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca*), there arises a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhā vedanā*).

When one feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ*), one understands: ‘I feel a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti*)’.

One understands: ‘With the cessation of that same contact to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant (*tasseva adukkhamasukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā*), its corresponding feeling - the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that arose in dependence on that contact to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant (*yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannā adukkhamasukhā vedanā*) - ceases and subsides (*sā nirujjhati, sā vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti*).

mula_pali: 360. ‘‘Athāparaṃ upekkhāyeva avasissati parisuddhā pariyodātā mudu ca kammaññā ca pabhassarā ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, dakkho suvaṇṇakāro vā suvaṇṇakārantevāsī vā ukkaṃ bandheyya, ukkaṃ bandhitvā ukkāmukhaṃ ālimpeyya, ukkāmukhaṃ ālimpetvā saṇḍāsena jātarūpaṃ gahetvā ukkāmukhe pakkhipeyya, tamenaṃ kālena kālaṃ abhidhameyya, kālena kālaṃ udakena paripphoseyya, kālena kālaṃ ajjhupekkheyya, taṃ hoti jātarūpaṃ jātarūpaṃ dhantaṃ (sī. pī.) sudhantaṃ niddhantaṃ nīhaṭaṃ nihataṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) ninnītakasāvaṃ nihatakasāvaṃ (ka.) mudu ca kammaññañca pabhassarañca, yassā yassā ca piḷandhanavikatiyā ākaṅkhati – yadi paṭṭikāya pavaṭṭikāya (sī. syā.) yadi kuṇḍalāya yadi gīveyyakāya yadi suvaṇṇamālāya tañcassa atthaṃ anubhoti; evameva kho, bhikkhu, athāparaṃ upekkhāyeva avasissati parisuddhā pariyodātā mudu ca kammaññā ca pabhassarā ca.
mula_english:
“Then there remains only equanimity ( *upekkhā*), purified and bright, malleable ( *mudu*), wieldy ( *kammaññā*), and radiant ( *pabhassarā*).

Suppose, *bhikkhu*, a skilled goldsmith or his apprentice were to prepare a furnace, heat up the crucible, take some gold (*jātarūpaṃ*) with tongs, and put it into the crucible. From time to time he would blow on it, from time to time he would sprinkle water over it, and from time to time he would just look on. That gold would become refined, well refined, completely refined, faultless, rid of dross, malleable, wieldy, and radiant. Then whatever kind of ornament he wished to make from it, whether a golden chain (*paṭṭikāya*), whether earrings (*kuṇḍalāya*), whether a necklace (*gīveyyakāya*), or whether a golden garland (*suvaṇṇamālāya*), he would accomplish his purpose. Just so, *bhikkhu*, there remains only equanimity ( *upekkhā*), purified and bright, malleable ( *mudu*), wieldy ( *kammaññā*), and radiant ( *pabhassarā*).
commentary_pali:
360.Upekkhāyeva avasissatīti ettāvatā hi yathā nāma chekena maṇikārācariyena vajirasūciyā vijjhitvā cammakhaṇḍe pātetvā pātetvā dinnamuttaṃ antevāsiko gahetvā gahetvā suttagataṃ karonto muttolambakamuttajālādīni karoti, evameva bhagavatā kathetvā kathetvā dinnaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ ayaṃ kulaputto manasikaronto manasikaronto paguṇaṃ akāsīti rūpakammaṭṭhānampissa arūpakammaṭṭhānampi paguṇaṃ jātaṃ, atha bhagavā ‘‘athāparaṃ upekkhāyeva avasissatī’’ti āha.

Kimatthaṃ pana avasissatīti? Satthu kathanatthaṃ. Kulaputtassa paṭivijjhanatthantipi vadanti , taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Kulaputtena hi sahāyassa sāsanaṃ vācetvā pāsādatale ṭhiteneva ānāpānacatutthajjhānaṃ nibbattitaṃ, yadassa ettakaṃ maggaṃ āgacchantassa yānakiccaṃ sādheti. Satthu kathanatthaṃyeva avasissati. Imasmiñhi ṭhāne satthā kulaputtassa rūpāvacarajjhāne vaṇṇaṃ kathesi. Idañhi vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘bhikkhu paguṇaṃ tava idaṃ rūpāvacaracatutthajjhāna’’nti. Parisuddhātiādi tassāyeva upekkhāya vaṇṇabhaṇanaṃ. Ukkaṃ bandheyyāti aṅgārakapallaṃ sajjeyya. Ālimpeyyāti tattha aṅgāre pakkhipitvā aggiṃ datvā nāḷikāya dhamento aggiṃ jāleyya. Ukkāmukhe pakkhipeyyāti aṅgāre viyūhitvā aṅgāramatthake vā ṭhapeyya, tattake vā pakkhipeyya. Nīhaṭanti nīhaṭadosaṃ. Ninnītakasāvanti apanītakasāvaṃ. Evameva khoti yathā taṃ suvaṇṇaṃ icchiticchitāya piḷandhanavikatiyā saṃvattati, evameva ayaṃ tāva catutthajjhānupekkhā vipassanā abhiññā nirodho bhavokkantīti imesu yaṃ icchati, tassatthāya hotīti vaṇṇaṃ kathesi.

Parisuddhā Ukkaṃ bandheyyā Ālimpeyyā Ukkāmukhe pakkhipeyyā Nīhaṭa Ninnītakasāva Evameva kho

Kasmā pana bhagavā imasmiṃ rūpāvacaracatutthajjhāne nikantipariyādānatthaṃ avaṇṇaṃ akathetvā vaṇṇaṃ kathesīti. Kulaputtassa hi catutthajjhāne nikantipariyuṭṭhānaṃ balavaṃ. Sace avaṇṇaṃ katheyya, – ‘‘mayhaṃ pabbajitvā dvānavutiyojanasataṃ āgacchantassa imaṃ catutthajjhānaṃ yānakiccaṃ sādhesi, ahaṃ ettakaṃ maggaṃ āgacchanto jhānasukhena jhānaratiyā āgato, evarūpassa nāma paṇītadhammassa avaṇṇaṃ katheti, jānaṃ nu kho katheti ajāna’’nti kulaputto saṃsayaṃ sammohaṃ āpajjeyya, tasmā bhagavā vaṇṇaṃ kathesi.
commentary_english:
"Only equanimity remains." Thus, just as a skilled jeweler pierces a piece of leather with a diamond needle, inserts and re-inserts precious gems, and a resident apprentice, taking them one by one, makes them into a string, creating pearl necklaces, pearl nets, and so on, so too, this son of a good family, considering and re-considering the meditation subject given by the Blessed One, has made it skillful. Both the form meditation and the formless meditation have become skillful. Then the Blessed One said, "Only equanimity remains."

Why does it remain? It is for the sake of the teacher's explanation. Others say it is for the sake of the son of a good family's penetration, but that should not be taken [rigidly]. Indeed, by having his companion recite the teaching, the son of a good family developed the fourth *jhāna* of mindfulness of breathing while standing on the terrace of the palace, which accomplished the task of a vehicle for him as he was coming such a distance. Only the teacher's explanation remains. In this place, the Teacher spoke of the merit of the realm-of-form *jhāna* for the son of a good family. For it was said, "Monk, this realm-of-form fourth *jhāna* is skillful for you."

"*Parisuddhā* (thoroughly pure)," etc., is a description of the merit of that equanimity.

"*Ukkam bandheyyā* (he should tie a firebrand)" means he should prepare a charcoal pan.

"*Ālimpeyyā* (he should smear)" means that there, having put embers in the fire, given fire, and blown with a tube, he should kindle a fire.

"*Ukkāmukhe pakkhipeyyā* (he should throw it into the mouth of the firebrand)" means that having scattered the embers, he should either place it on top of the embers or throw it into that heap.

"*Nīhaṭa* (removed)" means with faults removed.

"*Ninnītakasāva* (with the astringency removed)" means with the astringency taken away.

"*Evameva kho* (just so indeed)" means that just as that gold is used for whatever kind of jewelry one desires, so too, this fourth *jhāna*-equanimity, *vipaśyanā* (insight), *abhijñā* (higher knowledge), cessation, becoming, transcendence—whichever of these one desires, it is for the sake of that. Thus, he spoke of the merit.

thoroughly pure, he should tie a firebrand, he should smear, he should throw it into the mouth of the firebrand, removed, with the astringency removed, just so indeed. Why then did the Blessed One, in this realm-of-form fourth *jhāna*, speak of the merit, not speaking of the demerit, for the sake of completely abandoning attachment? For the son of a good family, attachment to the fourth *jhāna* is strong. If he were to speak of the demerit, [the son of good family] might fall into doubt and confusion, [thinking:] "Having gone forth and come a hundred and ninety *yojana*s, this fourth *jhāna* accomplished the task of a vehicle for me. I have come such a distance enjoying the bliss of *jhāna*, the delight of *jhāna*. He speaks of the demerit of such an excellent *dharma*! Does he speak knowingly or unknowingly?" Therefore, the Blessed One spoke of the merit.

mula_pali: 361. ‘‘So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘imañce ahaṃ upekkhaṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasaṃhareyyaṃ, tadanudhammañca cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ. Evaṃ me ayaṃ upekkhā taṃnissitā tadupādānā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya. Imañce ahaṃ upekkhaṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasaṃhareyyaṃ, tadanudhammañca cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ. Evaṃ me ayaṃ upekkhā taṃnissitā tadupādānā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya. Imañce ahaṃ upekkhaṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasaṃhareyyaṃ, tadanudhammañca cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ. Evaṃ me ayaṃ upekkhā taṃnissitā tadupādānā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya. Imañce ahaṃ upekkhaṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasaṃhareyyaṃ, tadanudhammañca cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ. Evaṃ me ayaṃ upekkhā taṃnissitā tadupādānā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyyā’’’ti.
mula_english:
361. “He understands thus: ‘If I were to direct this equanimity (upekkhā), so purified (parisuddhaṃ) and bright (pariyodātaṃ), to the base of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ) and to develop my mind (cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ) accordingly. Then this equanimity (upekkhā) of mine, supported by that base (taṃnissitā), clinging to it (tadupādānā), would remain for a very long time (ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya).

If I were to direct this equanimity (upekkhā), so purified (parisuddhaṃ) and bright (pariyodātaṃ), to the base of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ) and to develop my mind (cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ) accordingly. Then this equanimity (upekkhā) of mine, supported by that base (taṃnissitā), clinging to it (tadupādānā), would remain for a very long time (ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya).

If I were to direct this equanimity (upekkhā), so purified (parisuddhaṃ) and bright (pariyodātaṃ), to the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ) and to develop my mind (cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ) accordingly. Then this equanimity (upekkhā) of mine, supported by that base (taṃnissitā), clinging to it (tadupādānā), would remain for a very long time (ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya).

If I were to direct this equanimity (upekkhā), so purified (parisuddhaṃ) and bright (pariyodātaṃ), to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ) and to develop my mind (cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ) accordingly. Then this equanimity (upekkhā) of mine, supported by that base (taṃnissitā), clinging to it (tadupādānā), would remain for a very long time (ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya.’”
commentary_pali: 361.Tadanudhammanti ettha arūpāvacarajjhānaṃ dhammo nāma, taṃ anugatattā rūpāvacarajjhānaṃ anudhammoti vuttaṃ. Vipākajjhānaṃ vā dhammo, kusalajjhānaṃ anudhammo. Tadupādānāti taggahaṇā. Ciraṃ dīghamaddhānanti vīsatikappasahassāni. Vipākavasena hetaṃ vuttaṃ. Ito uttarimpi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
361. "Tadanudhamma," here, *arūpāvacarajjhāna* is called *dharma*; due to adherence to that, *rūpāvacarajjhāna* is called *anudhamma*.

Or, *vipākajjhāna* is *dharma*, *kusalajjhāna* is *anudhamma*.

"Tadupādāna" means taking that.

"Ciraṃ dīghamaddhāna" means twenty thousand *kappas*.

This is said in terms of the result (*vipāka*).

The same principle (*naya*) applies hereafter.

mula_pali:
362. ‘‘So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘imañce ahaṃ upekkhaṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasaṃhareyyaṃ, tadanudhammañca cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ; saṅkhatametaṃ. Imañce ahaṃ upekkhaṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasaṃhareyyaṃ, tadanudhammañca cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ; saṅkhatametaṃ. Imañce ahaṃ upekkhaṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasaṃhareyyaṃ, tadanudhammañca cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ; saṅkhatametaṃ. Imañce ahaṃ upekkhaṃ evaṃ parisuddhaṃ evaṃ pariyodātaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasaṃhareyyaṃ, tadanudhammañca cittaṃ bhāveyyaṃ; saṅkhatameta’’’nti.

‘‘So neva taṃ abhisaṅkharoti, na abhisañcetayati bhavāya vā vibhavāya vā. So anabhisaṅkharonto anabhisañcetayanto bhavāya vā vibhavāya vā na kiñci loke upādiyati, anupādiyaṃ na paritassati, aparitassaṃ paccattaṃyeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
mula_english:
362.
“He understands thus: ‘If I were to direct this equanimity, so purified and bright, to the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*) and to develop my mind (*citta*) accordingly, this would be conditioned (*saṅkhata*).
If I were to direct this equanimity, so purified and bright, to the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*) and to develop my mind (*citta*) accordingly, this would be conditioned (*saṅkhata*).
If I were to direct this equanimity, so purified and bright, to the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*) and to develop my mind (*citta*) accordingly, this would be conditioned (*saṅkhata*).
If I were to direct this equanimity, so purified and bright, to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) and to develop my mind (*citta*) accordingly, this would be conditioned (*saṅkhata*.’”
Since he does not generate or fashion volitional formations (*abhisaṅkharonto anabhisañcetayanto*) tending towards either being (*bhavāya*) or non-being (*vibhavāya*), he does not cling to anything in the world (*loke upādiyati*). Not clinging, he is not agitated (*na paritassati*). Not being agitated, he personally attains *Nibbana* (*parinibbāyati*).
He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) has been lived, what had to be done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*) has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being (*na aparaṃ itthattāya*)’."
commentary_pali:
362. Evaṃ catūhi vārehi arūpāvacarajjhānassa vaṇṇaṃ kathetvā idāni tasseva ādīnavaṃ dassento so evaṃ pajānātītiādimāha. Tattha saṅkhatametanti kiñcāpi ettha vīsatikappasahassāni āyu atthi, etaṃ pana saṅkhataṃ pakappitaṃ āyūhitaṃ, karontena karīyati, aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ tāvakālikaṃ, cavanaparibhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammaṃ, jātiyā anugataṃ, jarāya anusaṭaṃ, maraṇena abbhāhataṃ, dukkhe patiṭṭhitaṃ, atāṇaṃ aleṇaṃ asaraṇaṃ asaraṇībhūtanti. Viññāṇañcāyatanādīsupi eseva nayo.

Idāni arahattanikūṭena desanaṃ gaṇhanto so neva taṃ abhisaṅkharotītiādimāha. Yathā hi cheko bhisakko visavikāraṃ disvā vamanaṃ kāretvā visaṃ ṭhānato cāvetvā upari āropetvā khandhaṃ vā sīsaṃ vā gahetuṃ adatvā visaṃ otāretvā pathaviyaṃ pāteyya, evameva bhagavā kulaputtassa arūpāvacarajjhāne vaṇṇaṃ kathesi. Taṃ sutvā kulaputto rūpāvacarajjhāne nikantiṃ pariyādāya arūpāvacarajjhāne patthanaṃ ṭhapesi.

so neva taṃ abhisaṅkharotī

Bhagavā taṃ ñatvā taṃ asampattassa appaṭiladdhasseva bhikkhuno ‘‘atthesā ākāsānañcāyatanādīsu sampatti nāma. Tesañhi paṭhamabrahmaloke vīsatikappasahassāni āyu, dutiye cattālīsaṃ, tatiye saṭṭhi, catutthe caturāsīti kappasahassāni āyu. Taṃ pana aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ tāvakālikaṃ, cavanaparibhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammaṃ, jātiyā anugataṃ, jarāya anusaṭaṃ, maraṇena abbhāhataṃ, dukkhe patiṭṭhitaṃ, atāṇaṃ aleṇaṃ asaraṇaṃ asaraṇībhūtaṃ, ettakaṃ kālaṃ tattha sampattiṃ anubhavitvāpi puthujjanakālakiriyaṃ katvā puna catūsu apāyesu patitabba’’nti sabbametaṃ ādīnavaṃ ekapadeneva ‘‘saṅkhatameta’’nti kathesi. Kulaputto taṃ sutvā arūpāvacarajjhāne nikantiṃ pariyādiyi, bhagavā tassa rūpāvacarārūpāvacaresu nikantiyā pariyādinnabhāvaṃ ñatvā arahattanikūṭaṃ gaṇhanto ‘‘so neva taṃ abhisaṅkharotī’’tiādimāha.

Yathā vā paneko mahāyodho ekaṃ rājānaṃ ārādhetvā satasahassuṭṭhānakaṃ gāmavaraṃ labheyya, puna rājā tassānubhāvaṃ saritvā – ‘‘mahānubhāvo yodho, appakaṃ tena laddha’’nti – ‘‘nāyaṃ tāta gāmo tuyhaṃ anucchaviko, aññaṃ catusatasahassuṭṭhānakaṃ gaṇhāhī’’ti dadeyya so sādhu devāti taṃ vissajjetvā itaraṃ gāmaṃ gaṇheyya. Rājā asampattameva ca naṃ pakkosāpetvā – ‘‘kiṃ te tena, ahivātarogo ettha uppajjati? Asukasmiṃ pana ṭhāne mahantaṃ nagaraṃ atthi, tattha chattaṃ ussāpetvā rajjaṃ kārehī’’ti pahiṇeyya, so tathā kareyya.

Tattha rājā viya sammāsambuddho daṭṭhabbo, mahāyodho viya pukkusāti kulaputto, paṭhamaladdhagāmo viya ānāpānacatutthajjhānaṃ, taṃ vissajjetvā itaraṃ gāmaṃ gaṇhāhīti vuttakālo viya ānāpānacatutthajjhāne nikantipariyādānaṃ katvā āruppakathanaṃ, taṃ gāmaṃ asampattameva pakkosāpetvā ‘‘kiṃ te tena, ahivātarogo ettha uppajjati? Asukasmiṃ ṭhāne nagaraṃ atthi, tattha chattaṃ ussāpetvā rajjaṃ kārehī’’ti vuttakālo viya arūpe saṅkhatametanti ādīnavakathanena appattāsuyeva tāsu samāpattīsu patthanaṃ nivatthāpetvā upari arahattanikūṭena desanāgahaṇaṃ.

Tattha neva abhisaṅkharotīti nāyūhati na rāsiṃ karoti. Na abhisañcetayatīti na kappeti. Bhavāya vā vibhavāya vāti vuddhiyā vā parihāniyā vā, sassatucchedavasenapi yojetabbaṃ. Na kiñci loke upādiyatīti loke rūpādīsu kiñci ekadhammampi taṇhāya na gaṇhāti, na parāmasati. Nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātīti bhagavā attano buddhavisaye ṭhatvā desanāya arahattanikūṭaṃ gaṇhi. Kulaputto pana attano yathopanissayena tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni paṭivijjhi. Yathā nāma rājā suvaṇṇabhājanena nānārasabhojanaṃ bhuñjanto attano pamāṇena piṇḍaṃ vaṭṭetvā aṅke nisinnena rājakumārena piṇḍamhi ālaye dassite taṃ piṇḍaṃ upanāmeyya, kumāro attano mukhappamāṇeneva kabaḷaṃ kareyya, sesaṃ rājā sayaṃ vā bhuñjeyya, pātiyaṃ vā pakkhipeyya, evaṃ dhammarājā tathāgato attano pamāṇena arahattanikūṭaṃ gaṇhanto desanaṃ desesi, kulaputto attano yathopanissayena tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni paṭivijjhi.

neva abhisaṅkharotī Na abhisañcetayatī Bhavāya vā vibhavāya vā Na kiñci loke upādiyatī Nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī

Ito pubbe panassa khandhā dhātuyo āyatanānīti evarūpaṃ accantasuññataṃ tilakkhaṇāhataṃ kathaṃ kathentassa neva kaṅkhā, na vimati, nāpi – ‘‘evaṃ kira taṃ, evaṃ me ācariyena vutta’’nti iti kira na dandhāyitattaṃ na vitthāyitattaṃ atthi . Ekaccesu ca kira ṭhānesu buddhā aññātakavesena vicaranti, sammāsambuddho nu kho esoti ahudeva saṃsayo, ahu vimati. Yato anena anāgāmiphalaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, atha ayaṃ me satthāti niṭṭhaṃ gato. Yadi evaṃ kasmā accayaṃ na desesīti. Okāsābhāvato. Bhagavā hi yathānikkhittāya mātikāya acchinnadhāraṃ katvā ākāsagaṅgaṃ otārento viya desanaṃ desesiyeva.
commentary_english:
362. Thus, having described the excellence of the formless attainments (arūpāvacarajjhāna) in four ways, now, showing its fault, [he] says, "So he understands thus."

Therein, as for "conditioned is this" (saṅkhatameta), although there is a life span of twenty thousand aeons (vīsatikappasahassāni) therein, this is conditioned, constructed, accumulated, is done by one who does, is impermanent (aniccaṃ), unstable (adhuvam), not eternal (asassataṃ), temporary (tāvakālikaṃ), subject to falling away, decay, and destruction (cavanaparibhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammaṃ), is followed by birth (jātiyā anugataṃ), afflicted by old age (jarāya anusaṭaṃ), struck by death (maraṇena abbhāhataṃ), established in suffering (dukkhe patiṭṭhitaṃ), without protection (atāṇaṃ), without refuge (aleṇaṃ), without help (asaraṇaṃ), and has become without help (asaraṇībhūtanti). This is the way in the case of the sphere of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatana), and so on.

Now, taking up the teaching by way of arhatship, [he] says, "So he does not construct it" (so neva taṃ abhisaṅkharotī), and so on. Just as a skillful physician, seeing a disease caused by poison, having caused vomiting, having removed the poison from its place, and having raised it up, without giving [the poison] to take hold of the trunk or the head, having brought down the poison, and having dropped it on the earth, even so, the Blessed One described the excellence of the formless attainments to the clansman. Having heard that, the clansman, having completely rejected liking for the form attainments, established his desire in the formless attainments.

"So he does not construct it." The Blessed One, knowing that, to the monk who has not attained that, and has not regained that, [says:] "This is called attainment among the sphere of infinite space, and so on."

For, indeed, in the first Brahmā world, there is a life span of twenty thousand aeons, in the second, forty thousand, in the third, sixty thousand, in the fourth, eighty-four thousand aeons. But that is impermanent, unstable, not eternal, temporary, subject to falling away, decay, and destruction, is followed by birth, afflicted by old age, struck by death, established in suffering, without protection, without refuge, without help, and has become without help, having experienced attainment there for such a long time, having made the death of an ordinary person, again, one must fall into the four woeful states (apāyesu patitabba). The Blessed One spoke all of that fault in one word, "Conditioned is this."

Having heard that, the clansman completely rejected liking for the formless attainments, the Blessed One, knowing the state of having completely rejected liking in the form and formless attainments, taking up the arhatship peak, said, "So he does not construct it," and so on.

Just as, indeed, a great warrior, having pleased a king, might gain a choice village with an income of one hundred thousand, again, the king, recollecting his power, [might say] – "The warrior is of great power, little has been obtained by him" – "This village is not suitable for you, dear. Take another with an income of four hundred thousand," [and] might give [it]. He, [thinking,] "Good, O god," having dismissed that, might take the other village. The king, before [he] even attained [it], having summoned him, [might say] – "What is the use of that to you? A disease caused by wind and snakes arises there. But in such and such a place there is a great city. Having raised up an umbrella there, rule the kingdom," and might send [him]. So he might do thus.

Therein, the Fully Awakened One (sammāsambuddho) should be seen as like the king, the clansman Pukkusāti as like the great warrior, the fourth jhāna (catutthajjhānaṃ) of mindfulness of breathing (ānāpāna) as like the first-obtained village, the description of the formless [attainments] as like the time when it was said, "Having dismissed that, take the other village," having made the complete rejection of liking in the fourth jhāna of mindfulness of breathing, having summoned [him] before [he] even attained that village, [and the arhatship instruction itself is:] "What is the use of that to you? A disease caused by wind and snakes arises there. In such and such a place there is a city. Having raised up an umbrella there, rule the kingdom," as like the time when it was said, "Conditioned is this among the formless," having turned away desire in those very attainments by way of describing the fault, and above that, the taking up of the teaching by way of the arhatship peak.

Therein, "he does not construct it" means he does not accumulate, he does not make a heap. "He does not intend" means he does not imagine. "For becoming or for non-becoming" means it should be connected to increase or decrease, or by way of eternalism and annihilationism. "He does not cling to anything in the world" means in the world, among forms, and so on, he does not grasp even one thing with craving, he does not touch. "He does not understand there is anything further for this state" means the Blessed One, standing in his own Buddha domain, took up the arhatship peak in [his] teaching. But the clansman, according to his own support, realized the three fruits of asceticism (sāmaññaphalāni). Just as, indeed, a king, enjoying food of various flavors in a golden vessel, having made a ball of food according to his own measure, and when an abode in the ball was shown by a prince sitting on [his] lap, might offer that ball [to him], the prince might make a mouthful according to the measure of his own mouth, the king himself might eat the rest, or might throw [it] into a bowl, even so, the Dharma king, the Tathāgata, taking up the arhatship peak according to his own measure, gave a teaching, the clansman, according to his own support, realized the three fruits of asceticism (sāmaññaphalāni).

"He does not construct it, he does not intend it, for becoming or for non-becoming, he does not cling to anything in the world, he does not understand there is anything further for this state." Before this, however, for him, how is there no doubt, no uncertainty for one who speaks the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases [to be] of such a kind, extremely empty, struck by the three characteristics, nor [does he think] – "It is like this, it was said to me by the teacher," and thus, indeed, is there no slowness or expansion [of thought]?

Moreover, in some places, the Buddhas wander in unrecognizable disguise, there is just a doubt, there is uncertainty – "Is this the Fully Awakened One?" Since the fruit of non-returning was realized by him, then he has gone to the conclusion, "This is my teacher." If so, why did [he] not confess the offense? Because of lack of opportunity. The Blessed One, indeed, just as if causing the Ganges of space to descend, having made an unbroken stream for the mother who has been cast aside, [he] gave the teaching.

mula_pali: 363. ‘‘So sukhañce vedanaṃ vedeti, ‘sā aniccā’ti pajānāti, ‘anajjhositā’ti pajānāti, ‘anabhinanditā’ti pajānāti. Dukkhañce vedanaṃ vedeti , ‘sā aniccā’ti pajānāti, ‘anajjhositā’ti pajānāti, ‘anabhinanditā’ti pajānāti. Adukkhamasukhañce vedanaṃ vedeti, ‘sā aniccā’ti pajānāti, ‘anajjhositā’ti pajānāti, ‘anabhinanditā’ti pajānāti.
mula_english:
“If he feels a pleasant feeling (sukhaṃ vedanaṃ), he understands: ‘It is impermanent (aniccā)’; he understands: ‘It is not clung to (anajjhositā)’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in (anabhinanditā).’

If he feels a painful feeling (dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ), he understands: ‘It is impermanent (aniccā)’; he understands: ‘It is not clung to (anajjhositā)’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in (anabhinanditā).’

If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ), he understands: ‘It is impermanent (aniccā)’; he understands: ‘It is not clung to (anajjhositā)’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in (anabhinanditā).’
commentary_pali: 363.Soti arahā. Anajjhositāti gilitvā pariniṭṭhāpetvā gahetuṃ na yutthāti pajānāti. Anabhinanditāti taṇhādiṭṭhivasena abhinandituṃ na yuttāti pajānāti.
commentary_english: 363. So, the Worthy One (arahā). "Not dwelling on" (anajjhositā): [He/She] knows that it is not proper to swallow, complete, and take. "Not delighting in" (anabhinanditā): [He/She] knows that it is not proper to delight in craving and views.

mula_pali: 364. ‘‘So sukhañce vedanaṃ vedeti, visaṃyutto naṃ vedeti; dukkhañce vedanaṃ vedeti, visaṃyutto naṃ vedeti; adukkhamasukhañce vedanaṃ vedeti, visaṃyutto naṃ vedeti. So kāyapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘kāyapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti, jīvitapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘jīvitapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti, ‘kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā uddhaṃ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītībhavissantī’ti pajānāti.
mula_english:
“If he feels a pleasant feeling (sukhaṃ vedanaṃ), he feels it detached (visaṃyutto naṃ vedeti); if he feels a painful feeling (dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ), he feels it detached; if he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ), he feels it detached.

When he feels a feeling terminating with the body (kāyapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ), he understands: ‘I feel a feeling terminating with the body (kāyapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti).’ When he feels a feeling terminating with life (jīvitapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ), he understands: ‘I feel a feeling terminating with life (jīvitapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti).’ He understands: ‘On the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), with the ending of life (jīvitapariyādānā), all that is felt (sabbavedayitāni), not being delighted in (anabhinanditāni), will become cool (sītībhavissantī) right here (idheva).’
commentary_pali: 364.Visaṃyutto naṃ vedetīti sace hissa sukhavedanaṃ ārabbha rāgānusayo, dukkhavedanaṃ ārabbha paṭighānusayo, itaraṃ ārabbha avijjānusayo uppajjeyya, saṃyutto vediyeyya nāma. Anuppajjanato pana visaṃyutto naṃ vedeti nissaṭo vippamutto. Kāyapariyantikanti kāyakoṭikaṃ. Yāva kāyapavattā uppajjitvā tato paraṃ anuppajjanavedananti attho. Dutiyapadepi eseva nayo. Anabhinanditāni sītībhavissantīti dvādasasu āyatanesu kilesānaṃ visevanassa natthitāya anabhinanditāni hutvā idha dvādasasuyeva āyatanesu nirujjhissanti. Kilesā hi nibbānaṃ āgamma niruddhāpi yattha natthi, tattha niruddhāti vuccanti. Svāyamattho – ‘‘etthesā taṇhā nirujjhamānā nirujjhatī’’ti samudayapañhena dīpetabbo. Tasmā bhagavā nibbānaṃ āgamma sītibhūtānipi idheva sītībhavissantīti āha. Nanu ca idha vedayitāni vuttāni, na kilesāti. Vedayitānipi kilesābhāveneva sītībhavanti. Itarathā nesaṃ sītibhāvo nāma natthīti suvuttametaṃ.
commentary_english:
364. " *Visaṃyutto naṃ vedetī* ti": If, when experiencing pleasant feeling (*sukhavedanaṃ*), attachment (*rāgānusayo*) arises; when experiencing painful feeling (*dukkha vedanaṃ*), aversion (*paṭighānusayo*) arises; when experiencing neutral feeling, ignorance (*avijjānusayo*) arises, one is experiencing in a conjoined manner.

But from non-arising, one experiences in a disjoined manner, detached, and liberated (*nissaṭo vippamutto*).

"*Kāyapariyantika*nti": the limit of the body (*kāyakoṭikaṃ*).

The meaning is: having arisen as far as the continuation of the body (*yāva kāyapavattā*), thereafter, it is feeling of non-arising (*anuppajjanavedananti attho*).

The same method applies to the second phrase as well.

"*Anabhinanditāni sītībhavissantī*ti": Because of the non-existence of indulgence (*visevanassa natthitāya*) in defilements (*kilesānaṃ*) in the twelve sense bases (*dvādasasu āyatanesu*), having become un delighting (*anabhinanditāni hutvā*), here in these very twelve sense bases they will cease (*idha dvādasasuyeva āyatanesu nirujjhissanti*).

For defilements (*kilesā*) which, having come to nirvāṇa (*nibbānaṃ āgamma*), are suppressed (*niruddhāpi*), where there is no defilement, there they are said to be suppressed (*yattha natthi, tattha niruddhāti vuccanti*).

The meaning of this is: "Here, this craving (*etthesā taṇhā*), ceasing, ceases" is to be explained by the question of origin (*samudayapañhena dīpetabbo*).

Therefore, the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), having come to nirvāṇa (*nibbānaṃ āgamma*), said, "Even things that have become cool (*sītibhūtānipi*) will become cool right here (*idheva sītībhavissantīti āha*)."

But indeed, here feelings (*vedayitāni*) are said to be extinguished, not defilements (*na kilesāti*).

Even feelings (*vedayitānipi*) become cool through the absence of defilements (*kilesābhāveneva sītībhavanti*).

Otherwise, there is no such thing as their becoming cool (*itarathā nesaṃ sītibhāvo nāma natthīti suvuttametaṃ*).

mula_pali: 365. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, telañca paṭicca vaṭṭiñca paṭicca telappadīpo jhāyati; tasseva telassa ca vaṭṭiyā ca pariyādānā aññassa ca anupahārā anupāhārā (sī. pī.), anupādānā (ka.) anāhāro nibbāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhu, kāyapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘kāyapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti, jīvitapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayamāno ‘jīvitapariyantikaṃ vedanaṃ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti, ‘kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā uddhaṃ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītībhavissantī’ti pajānāti. Tasmā evaṃ samannāgato bhikkhu iminā paramena paññādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato hoti. Esā hi, bhikkhu, paramā ariyā paññā yadidaṃ – sabbadukkhakkhaye ñāṇaṃ.
mula_english: 365. Bhikkhu, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and when the oil and wick are used up, if it does not get any more fuel ( *anāhāra*), it is extinguished; so too, when a *bhikṣu* feels a feeling terminating with the body (*kāyaparīyantikam*), he understands: ‘I feel a feeling terminating with the body.’ When he feels a feeling terminating with life (*jīvitaparīyantikam*), he understands: ‘I feel a feeling terminating with life.’ He understands: ‘On the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), with the ending of life, all that is felt, not being delighted in (*anabhinanditāni*), will become cool right here.’ Therefore, a *bhikṣu* possessing this supreme foundation of wisdom (*prajñādhiṣṭhānena*) possesses the supreme foundation of wisdom. For this, *bhikṣu*, is the supreme noble wisdom (*paramā ariyā prajñā*), namely, the knowledge (*jñānam*) of the destruction of all suffering (*sabbadukkhakkhaye*).
commentary_pali:
365.Evamevakhoti ettha idaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ – yathā hi eko puriso telapadīpassa jhāyato tele khīṇe telaṃ āsiñcati, vaṭṭiyā khīṇāya vaṭṭiṃ pakkhipati, evaṃ dīpasikhāya anupacchedova hoti, evameva puthujjano ekasmiṃ bhave ṭhito kusalākusalaṃ karoti, so tena sugatiyañca apāyesu ca nibbattatiyeva, evaṃ vedanānaṃ anupacchedova hoti. Yathā paneko dīpasikhāya ukkaṇṭhito – ‘‘imaṃ purisaṃ āgamma dīpasikhā na upacchijjatī’’ti nilīno tassa purisassa sīsaṃ chindeyya, evaṃ vaṭṭiyā ca telassa ca anupahārā dīpasikhā anāhārā nibbāyati, evameva vaṭṭe ukkaṇṭhito yogāvacaro arahattamaggena kusalākusalaṃ samucchindati, tassa samucchinnattā khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno kāyassa bhedā puna vedayitāni na uppajjantīti.

Tasmāti yasmā ādimhi samādhivipassanāpaññāhi arahattaphalapaññā uttaritarā, tasmā. Evaṃ samannāgatoti iminā uttamena arahattaphalapaññādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato. Sabbadukkhakkhayeñāṇaṃ nāma arahattamagge ñāṇaṃ, imasmiṃ pana sutte arahattaphale ñāṇaṃ adhippetaṃ. Tenevāha tassa sā vimutti sacce ṭhitā akuppā hotīti.

Tasmā Evaṃ samannāgato Sabbadukkhakkhaye ñāṇaṃ tassa sā vimutti sacce ṭhitā akuppā hotī
commentary_english:
365.
Thus it is. Here, this is a comparison: Just as a man, when the oil is depleted from a lamp that is burning, pours in oil, and when the wick is depleted, puts in a wick, just so, the flame of the lamp continues. Just so, an ordinary person, standing in one existence, performs wholesome and unwholesome actions; by that, he is reborn in happy and unhappy realms. Just so, the continuity of feelings occurs.

Just as if a person, longing for the flame of a lamp, thinking, "If I come to this person, the flame of the lamp will not be extinguished," should hide and cut off the head of that person; just so, the flame of the lamp goes out due to lack of fuel and wick, without nourishment. Just so, a yogi, longing for the wick, cuts off wholesome and unwholesome actions with the path of an *arhat*. Because of his cutting off, when the body of a *bhikṣu*, whose corruptions are destroyed, is broken up, feelings do not arise again.

Therefore, because the wisdom of the fruit of *arhatship* is superior to the wisdom of concentration (*samādhi*) and insight (*vipaśyanā*) at the beginning, therefore.
"Thus endowed" means endowed with this supreme foundation of the wisdom of the fruit of *arhatship*.
"In the destruction of all suffering," namely, knowledge (*jñāna*) on the path of *arhatship*; but in this *sūtra*, knowledge (*jñāna*) in the fruit of *arhatship* is intended.
Therefore he said, "His liberation (*vimukti*) is established in truth, unshakeable."

Therefore, thus endowed, in the destruction of all suffering, knowledge (*jñāna*), his liberation (*vimukti*) is established in truth, unshakeable.

mula_pali: 366. ‘‘Tassa sā vimutti sacce ṭhitā akuppā hoti. Tañhi, bhikkhu, musā yaṃ mosadhammaṃ, taṃ saccaṃ yaṃ amosadhammaṃ nibbānaṃ. Tasmā evaṃ samannāgato bhikkhu iminā paramena saccādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato hoti. Etañhi, bhikkhu, paramaṃ ariyasaccaṃ yadidaṃ – amosadhammaṃ nibbānaṃ.
mula_english:
That is, his deliverance, being founded upon truth (satya), is unshakeable.

For that is false (mṛṣā), O monk (bhikkhu), which has a deceptive nature (moṣadharma), and that is true (satya) which has an undeceptive nature (amoṣadharma)—Nirvāṇa (nirvāṇa).

Therefore, a monk (bhikkhu) possessing this truth (satya) possesses the supreme foundation of truth (satyādhiṣṭhāna).

For this, O monk (bhikkhu), is the supreme noble truth (paramamāryasatya), namely, Nirvāṇa (nirvāṇa), which has an undeceptive nature (amoṣadharma).
commentary_pali:
366. Ettha hi vimuttīti arahattaphalavimutti, saccanti paramatthasaccaṃ nibbānaṃ. Iti akuppārammaṇakaraṇena akuppāti vuttā. Musāti vitathaṃ. Mosadhammanti nassanasabhāvaṃ. Taṃ saccanti taṃ avitathaṃ sabhāvo. Amosadhammanti anassanasabhāvaṃ.

Tasmāti yasmā ādito samathavipassanāvasena vacīsaccato dukkhasaccasamudayasaccehi ca paramatthasaccaṃ nibbānameva uttaritaraṃ, tasmā. Evaṃ samannāgatoti iminā uttamena paramatthasaccādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato.

Tasmā Evaṃ samannāgato
commentary_english:
Here, *vimutti* means the liberation that is the fruit of Arhatship, and *sacca* means the ultimate truth, nirvāṇa.

Thus, because it has unwavering (akuppa) characteristics, it is said to be *akuppā*.

*Musā* means false.

*Mosadhamma* means having the nature of destruction.

*Taṃ sacca* means that its nature is not false.

*Amosadhamma* means having the nature of non-destruction.

*Tasmā* means because, from the beginning, through tranquility and insight, and through the truth of speech, and through the truths of suffering and the origin of suffering, the ultimate truth, nirvāṇa, is superior. Therefore.

*Evaṃ samannāgato* means endowed with this supreme foundation of the ultimate truth.

*Tasmā evaṃ samannāgato*

mula_pali: 367. ‘‘Tasseva kho pana pubbe aviddasuno upadhī honti samattā samādinnā. Tyāssa pahīnā honti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Tasmā evaṃ samannāgato bhikkhu iminā paramena cāgādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato hoti. Eso hi, bhikkhu, paramo ariyo cāgo yadidaṃ – sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo.
mula_english: “Formerly, when he was ignorant, he acquired and developed attachments; now he has abandoned them, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them so that they are no more subject to future arising. Therefore a *bhikṣu* possessing this relinquishment possesses the supreme foundation of relinquishment (*cāgādhiṣṭhānena samannāgato hoti*). For this, *bhikṣu*, is the supreme noble relinquishment (*paramo ariyo cāgo*), namely, the relinquishing of all attachments (*sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo*).
commentary_pali: 367.Pubbeti puthujjanakāle. Upadhīhontīti khandhūpadhi kilesūpadhi abhisaṅkhārūpadhi pañcakāmaguṇūpadhīti ime upadhayo honti. Samattā samādinnāti paripūrā gahitā paramaṭṭhā. Tasmāti yasmā ādito samathavipassanāvasena kilesapariccāgato, sotāpattimaggādīhi ca kilesapariccāgato arahattamaggeneva kilesapariccāgo uttaritaro, tasmā. Evaṃ samannāgatoti iminā uttamena cāgādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato.
commentary_english:
Pubbe means at the time of being an ordinary person.

Upadhi hontī means these are the upadhis: the upadhi of the aggregates (skandha), the upadhi of the defilements (kilesa), the upadhi of the [karmic] formations (abhisaṅkhāra), and the upadhi of the five strands of sense pleasure (pañcakāmaguṇa).

Samattā samādinnā means completely grasped, fully taken up, ultimate.

Tasmā means since, from the beginning, through abandoning the defilements by way of serenity and insight, and through abandoning the defilements by way of the path of stream-entry, etc., the abandoning of the defilements by the path of arahantship alone is superior; therefore.

Evaṃ samannāgato means endowed with this supreme basis of generosity.

mula_pali: 368. ‘‘Tasseva kho pana pubbe aviddasuno abhijjhā hoti chando sārāgo. Svāssa pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṃkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo. Tasseva kho pana pubbe aviddasuno āghāto hoti byāpādo sampadoso. Svāssa pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṃkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo. Tasseva kho pana pubbe aviddasuno avijjā hoti sammoho. Svāssa pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṃkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo. Tasmā evaṃ samannāgato bhikkhu iminā paramena upasamādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato hoti. Eso hi, bhikkhu, paramo ariyo upasamo yadidaṃ – rāgadosamohānaṃ upasamo. ‘Paññaṃ nappamajjeyya, saccamanurakkheyya, cāgamanubrūheyya, santimeva so sikkheyyā’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english:
368. “Formerly, when he was ignorant (*aviddasuno*), he experienced covetousness (*abhijjhā*), desire (*chando*), and lust (*sārāgo*).

<pb ed="v" n="3. 0295"/> But now, these are abandoned (*pahīno hoti*), cut off at the root (*ucchinnamūlo*), made like a palm stump (*tālavatthukato*), obliterated (*anabhāvaṃkato*) so that it is no longer subject to future arising (*āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo*).

Formerly, when he was ignorant, he experienced anger (*āghāto*), ill will (*byāpādo*), and hate (*sampadoso*).

But now, these are abandoned, cut off at the root, <pb ed="p" n="3. 0246"/> made like a palm stump, obliterated so that it is no longer subject to future arising.

Formerly, when he was ignorant, he experienced ignorance (*avijjā*) and delusion (*sammoho*).

But now, these are abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated so that it is no longer subject to future arising.

Therefore, <pb ed="t" n="3. 0446"/> a *bhikkhu* possessing this possesses the supreme foundation of peace (*upasamādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato hoti*).

For this, *bhikkhu*, is the supreme noble peace (*paramo ariyo upasamo*), namely, the pacification (*upasamo*) of lust (*rāga*), hate (*dosa*), and delusion (*mohānam*).

“One should not neglect wisdom (*paññaṃ nappamajjeyya*), should preserve truth (*saccamanurakkheyya*), should cultivate relinquishment (*cāgamanubrūheyya*), and should train for peace (*santimeva so sikkheyyā’ti*)’—so it was with reference to this that it was said (*iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ*, *idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 368.Āghātotiādīsu āghātakaraṇavasena āghāto, byāpajjanavasena byāpādo, sampadussanavasena sampadosoti tīhi padehi dosākusalamūlameva vuttaṃ. Tasmāti yasmā ādito samathavipassanāvasena kilesavūpasamato, sotāpattimaggādīhi kilesavūpasamato ca arahattamaggeneva kilesavūpasamo uttaritaro, tasmā. Evaṃ samannāgatoti iminā uttamena upasamādhiṭṭhānena samannāgato.
commentary_english:
368. *Āghāto* etc.: *āghāta* due to the manner of doing harm, *byāpāda* due to the manner of malevolence, *sampadosa* due to the manner of corruption, thus, by these three terms, only the root of hatred and unwholesomeness is stated.

*Tasmā* because from the beginning, through the means of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā*, from the subsiding of the afflictions (*kleśa*), the subsiding of the afflictions by means of the path of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-mārga*) etc., and the subsiding of the afflictions through the path of *arhattva* alone is superior, therefore.

*Evaṃ samannāgato*: thus, endowed, i.e., endowed with this excellent basis of tranquility (*upaśamādhiṣṭhāna*).

mula_pali: 369. ‘‘‘Yattha ṭhitaṃ maññassavā nappavattanti, maññassave kho pana nappavattamāne muni santoti vuccatī’ti – iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? ‘Asmī’ti, bhikkhu, maññitametaṃ, ‘ayamahamasmī’ti maññitametaṃ, ‘bhavissa’nti maññitametaṃ, ‘na bhavissa’nti maññitametaṃ, ‘rūpī bhavissa’nti maññitametaṃ, ‘arūpī bhavissa’nti maññitametaṃ, ‘saññī bhavissa’nti maññitametaṃ, ‘asaññī bhavissa’nti maññitametaṃ, ‘nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissa’nti maññitametaṃ. Maññitaṃ, bhikkhu, rogo maññitaṃ gaṇḍo maññitaṃ sallaṃ. Sabbamaññitānaṃ tveva, bhikkhu, samatikkamā muni santoti vuccati. Muni kho pana, bhikkhu, santo na jāyati, na jīyati, na mīyati, na kuppati, na piheti. Tañhissa, bhikkhu, natthi yena jāyetha, ajāyamāno kiṃ jīyissati, ajīyamāno kiṃ mīyissati, amīyamāno kiṃ kuppissati, akuppamāno kissa kiṃ (ka.) pihessati? ‘Yattha ṭhitaṃ maññassavā nappavattanti, maññassave kho pana nappavattamāne muni santoti vuccatī’ti – iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ. Imaṃ kho me tvaṃ, bhikkhu, saṃkhittena chadhātuvibhaṅgaṃ dhārehī’’ti.
mula_english:
369. ‘Where the tides of conceiving (maññassavā) do not sweep over one who stands firm (ṭhitaṃ), and when the tides of conceiving (maññassave) no longer sweep over him, he is called a sage (muni) at peace (santo).’ So it was said.

With reference to what was this said? ‘I am’ (asmī’ti), bhikkhu, this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ); ‘I am this’ (ayamahamasmī’ti), this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ); ‘I will be’ (bhavissa’nti), this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ); ‘I will not be’ (na bhavissa’nti), this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ); ‘I will be with form (rūpī)’ (rūpī bhavissa’nti), this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ); ‘I will be without form (arūpī)’ (arūpī bhavissa’nti), this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ); ‘I will be with perception (saññī)’ (saññī bhavissa’nti), this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ); ‘I will be without perception (asaññī)’ (asaññī bhavissa’nti), this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ); ‘I will be neither with nor without perception (nevasaññīnāsaññī)’ (nevasaññīnāsaññī bhavissa’nti), this is conceiving (maññitametaṃ).

Conceiving (maññitaṃ), bhikkhu, is a disease (rogo), conceiving (maññitaṃ) is a tumor (gaṇḍo), conceiving (maññitaṃ) is a dart (sallaṃ).

By overcoming all conceivings (sabbamaññitānaṃ), bhikkhu, one is called a sage (muni) at peace (santo).

And the sage (muni) at peace (santo), bhikkhu, is not born (na jāyati), does not age (na jīyati), does not die (na mīyati), is not shaken (na kuppati), and is not agitated (na piheti).

For there is nothing present in him by which he might be born (jāyetha). Not being born (ajāyamāno), how could he age (jīyissati)? Not aging (ajīyamāno), how could he die (mīyissati)? Not dying (amīyamāno), how could he be shaken (kuppissati)? Not being shaken (akuppamāno), why should he be agitated (pihessati)? 'Where the tides of conceiving (maññassavā) do not sweep over one who stands firm (ṭhitaṃ), and when the tides of conceiving (maññassave) no longer sweep over him, he is called a sage (muni) at peace (santo).' So it was with reference to this that it was said (idaṃetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ).

Bhikkhu, bear in mind this brief exposition (saṃkhittena) of the six elements (chadhātuvibhaṅgaṃ).
commentary_pali: 369.Maññitametanti taṇhāmaññitaṃ mānamaññitaṃ diṭṭhimaññitanti tividhampi vaṭṭati. Ayamahamasmīti ettha pana ayamahanti ekaṃ taṇhāmaññitameva vaṭṭati. Rogotiādīsu ābādhaṭṭhena rogo, antodosaṭṭhena gaṇḍo, anupaviṭṭhaṭṭhena sallaṃ. Muni santoti vuccatīti khīṇāsavamuni santo nibbutoti vuccati. Yattha ṭhitanti yasmiṃ ṭhāne ṭhitaṃ. Saṃkhittenāti buddhānaṃ kira sabbāpi dhammadesanā saṃkhittāva, vitthāradesanā nāma natthi, samantapaṭṭhānakathāpi saṃkhittāyeva. Iti bhagavā desanaṃ yathānusandhiṃ pāpesi. Ugghāṭitaññūtiādīsu pana catūsu puggalesu pukkusāti kulaputto vipañcitaññū, iti vipañcitaññuvasena bhagavā imaṃ dhātuvibhaṅgasuttaṃ kathesi.
commentary_english:
369. "Maññitametaṃ" means that it is fitting as three kinds: craving-conceit ( *taṇhāmaññitaṃ*), pride-conceit (*mānamāññitaṃ*), and view-conceit (*diṭṭhimaññitaṃ*).

"Ayamahamasmi" Here, "ayamahaṃ" refers to only one thing: craving-conceit (*taṇhāmaññitameva vaṭṭati*).

"Rogo" etc., *rogo* [is explained] in the sense of affliction (*ābādhaṭṭhena*), *gaṇḍo* in the sense of internal defect (*antodosaṭṭhena*), and *sallaṃ* in the sense of not entering (*anupaviṭṭhaṭṭhena*).

"Muni santo'ti vuccati" means a *khīṇāsava muni* is called peaceful, extinguished (*nibbutoti vuccati*).

"Yattha ṭhitaṃ" means in whatever place (*yasmiṃ ṭhāne*) one is situated (*ṭhitaṃ*).

"Saṃkhittenā" means that all the teachings of the Buddhas are concise ( *saṃkhittāva*); there is no extensive teaching (*vitthāradesanā nāma natthi*). Even the *samantapaṭṭhānakathā* is concise (*saṃkhittāyeva*).

Thus, the Blessed One brought the teaching into accordance with what was suitable (*yathānusandhiṃ pāpesi*).

Among the four types of individuals beginning with *ugghāṭitaññū*, Pukkusāti, the son of a good family (*kulaputto*), is one who understands what is explained in detail (*vipañcitaññū*). Thus, through understanding what is explained in detail (*vipañcitaññuvasena*), the Blessed One taught this *Dhātuvibhaṅgasuttaṃ*.

mula_pali:
370. Atha kho āyasmā pukkusāti – ‘‘satthā kira me anuppatto, sugato kira me anuppatto sammāsambuddho kira me anuppatto’’ti uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yohaṃ bhagavantaṃ āvusovādena samudācaritabbaṃ amaññissaṃ. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā’’ti. ‘‘Taggha tvaṃ, bhikkhu, accayo accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ , yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ āvusovādena samudācaritabbaṃ amaññittha. Yato ca kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosi, taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuddhihesā, bhikkhu, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti, āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjatī’’ti. ‘‘Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike upasampada’’nti. ‘‘Paripuṇṇaṃ pana te, bhikkhu, pattacīvara’’nti? ‘‘Na kho me, bhante, paripuṇṇaṃ pattacīvara’’nti. ‘‘Na kho, bhikkhu, tathāgatā aparipuṇṇapattacīvaraṃ upasampādentī’’ti.

Atha kho āyasmā pukkusāti bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pattacīvarapariyesanaṃ pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmantaṃ pukkusātiṃ pattacīvarapariyesanaṃ carantaṃ vibbhantā gāvī bhantagāvī (sī. pī.), gāvī (syā. kaṃ.) jīvitā voropesi. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘yo so, bhante, pukkusāti nāma kulaputto bhagavatā saṃkhittena ovādena ovadito so kālaṅkato. Tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo’’ti? ‘‘Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, pukkusāti kulaputto paccapādi dhammassānudhammaṃ, na ca maṃ dhammādhikaraṇaṃ vihesesi viheṭhesi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) viheseti (ka.). Pukkusāti, bhikkhave, kulaputto pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’’ti.

bhantagāvī (sī. pī.), gāvī (syā. kaṃ.) viheṭhesi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) viheseti (ka.)

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Dhātuvibhaṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.
mula_english:
370.
Then, venerable Pukkusāti thought, "The Teacher has come to me! The Sublime One has come to me! The Fully Enlightened One has come to me!" Rising from his seat, he arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, prostrated himself with his head at the Blessed One's feet, and said to him, "Venerable Sir, a transgression (*accayo*) overcame me, in that, like a fool, confused and unskilled, I considered it proper to address the Blessed One as 'friend' (*āvusovādena*). May the Blessed One accept my transgression (*accayaṃ*) as a transgression (*accayato*) for the sake of my restraint (*saṃvarāya*) in the future."

"Indeed, bhikkhu, a transgression (*accayo*) overcame you, in that, like a fool, confused and unskilled, you considered it proper to address me as 'friend' (*āvusovādena*). But since you, bhikkhu, seeing your transgression (*accayaṃ*) as such (*accayato*) make amends in accordance with the Dhamma (*yathādhammaṃ*), we forgive (*paṭiggaṇhāma*) you. This, bhikkhu, is growth in the discipline (*vinaye*) of the noble (*ariyassa*) ones, when one sees one's transgression (*accayaṃ*) as such (*accayato*), makes amends in accordance with the Dhamma (*yathādhammaṃ*), and undertakes restraint (*saṃvaraṃ*) in the future."

"May I receive the going forth (*upasampada*), venerable sir, in the presence (*santike*) of the Blessed One?"

"Are your bowl (*patta*) and robes (*cīvara*) complete (*paripuṇṇaṃ*), bhikkhu?"

"No, venerable sir, my bowl (*patta*) and robes (*cīvara*) are not complete (*paripuṇṇaṃ*)."

"Tathāgatas do not confer the going forth (*upasampādentī*) on one whose bowl (*patta*) and robes (*cīvara*) are incomplete (*aparipuṇṇa*), bhikkhu."

Then, venerable Pukkusāti, delighted and rejoicing in the Blessed One's words (*bhāsitaṃ*), rose from his seat, paid homage (*abhivādetvā*) to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right (*padakkhiṇaṃ katvā*), and departed in order to search for a bowl (*patta*) and robes (*cīvara*).

Then, while venerable Pukkusāti was wandering in search of a bowl (*patta*) and robes (*cīvara*), a stray cow (*gāvī*) deprived him of life (*jīvitā voropesi*).

Then, a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One (*bhagavā*); having approached, having greeted (*abhivādetvā*) the Blessed One, they sat down at a respectful distance (*ekamantaṃ*).
