Sitting at a respectful distance (*ekamantaṃ*), those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One, "Venerable sir, that clansman (*kulaputto*) Pukkusāti, who was instructed (*ovadito*) by the Blessed One with a brief instruction (*saṃkhittena ovādena*), has passed away (*kālaṅkato*). What is his destination (*gati*)? What is his future state (*abhisamparāyo*)?"

"Bhikkhus, the clansman (*kulaputto*) Pukkusāti was wise (*paṇḍito*) and practiced the Dhamma (*dhammaṃ*) in accordance with the Dhamma (*anudhammaṃ*), and he did not trouble (*vihesesi*) me in matters of the Dhamma (*dhamma*). Pukkusāti, bhikkhus, the clansman (*kulaputto*) has, with the destruction (*parikkhayā*) of the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ*), reappeared spontaneously (*opapātiko*) and will attain final *Nibbāna* (*parinibbāyī*) there, not liable to return (*anāvattidhammo*) from that world (*lokā*)."

This the Blessed One said (*idamavoca bhagavā*). Elated (*attamanā*), those bhikkhus rejoiced in the Blessed One's words (*bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti*).

The tenth discourse, the Dhātuvibhaṅgasutta, is finished (*niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ*).
[p.]
commentary_pali:
370.Na kho me, bhante, paripuṇṇaṃ pattacīvaranti kasmā kulaputtassa iddhimayapattacīvaraṃ na nibbattanti. Pubbe aṭṭhannaṃ parikkhārānaṃ adinnattā. Kulaputto hi dinnadāno katābhinīhāro, na dinnattāti na vattabbaṃ. Iddhimayapattacīvaraṃ pana pacchimabhavikānaṃyeva nibbattati, ayañca punapaṭisandhiko, tasmā na nibbattanti. Atha bhagavā sayaṃ pariyesitvā kasmā na upasampādesīti. Okāsābhāvato. Kulaputtassa āyu parikkhīṇaṃ, suddhāvāsiko anāgāmī mahābrahmā kumbhakārasālaṃ āgantvā nisinno viya ahosi. Tasmā sayaṃ na pariyesi.

Pattacīvarapariyesanaṃ pakkāmīti kāya velāya pakkāmi? Uṭṭhite aruṇe. Bhagavato kira dhammadesanāpariniṭṭhānañca aruṇuṭṭhānañca rasmivissajjanañca ekakkhaṇe ahosi. Bhagavā kira desanaṃ niṭṭhapetvāva chabbaṇṇarasmiyo vissajji, sakalakumbhakāranivesanaṃ ekapajjotaṃ ahosi, chabbaṇṇarasmiyo jālajālā puñjapuñjā hutvā vidhāvantiyo sabbadisābhāge suvaṇṇapaṭapariyonaddhe viya ca nānāvaṇṇakusumaratanavisarasamujjale viya ca akaṃsu. Bhagavā ‘‘nagaravāsino maṃ passantū’’ti adhiṭṭhāsi. Nagaravāsino bhagavantaṃ disvāva ‘‘satthā kira āgato, kumbhakārasālāya kira nisinno’’ti aññamaññassa ārocetvā rañño ārocesuṃ.

Pattacīvarapariyesanaṃ pakkāmī

Rājā āgantvā satthāraṃ vanditvā, ‘‘bhante, kāya velāya āgatatthā’’ti pucchi. Hiyyo sūriyatthaṅgamanavelāya mahārājāti. Kena kammena bhagavāti? Tumhākaṃ sahāyo pukkusāti rājā tumhehi pahitaṃ sāsanaṃ sutvā nikkhamitvā pabbajitvā maṃ uddissa āgacchanto sāvatthiṃ atikkamma pañcacattālīsa yojanāni āgantvā imaṃ kumbhakārasālaṃ pavisitvā nisīdi, ahaṃ tassa saṅgahatthaṃ āgantvā dhammakathaṃ kathesiṃ, kulaputto tīṇi phalāni paṭivijjhi mahārājāti. Idāni kahaṃ, bhanteti? Upasampadaṃ yācitvā aparipuṇṇapattacīvaratāya pattacīvarapariyesanatthaṃ gato mahārājāti. Rājā kulaputtassa gatadisābhāgena agamāsi. Bhagavāpi ākāsenāgantvā jetavanagandhakuṭimhiyeva pāturahosi.

Kulaputtopi pattacīvaraṃ pariyesamāno neva bimbisārarañño na takkasīlakānaṃ jaṅghavāṇijānaṃ santikaṃ agamāsi. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘na kho me kukkuṭassa viya tattha tattha manāpāmanāpameva vicinitvā pattacīvaraṃ pariyesituṃ yuttaṃ, mahantaṃ nagaraṃ vajjitvā udakatitthasusānasaṅkāraṭṭhānaantaravīthīsu pariyesissāmī’’ti antaravīthiyaṃ saṅkārakūṭesu tāva pilotikaṃ pariyesituṃ āraddho.

Jīvitā voropesīti etasmiṃ saṅkārakūṭe pilotikaṃ olokentaṃ vibbhantā taruṇavacchā gāvī upadhāvitvā siṅgena vijjhitvā ghātesi. Chātakajjhatto kulaputto ākāseyeva āyukkhayaṃ patvā patito. Saṅkāraṭṭhāne adhomukhaṭṭhapitā suvaṇṇapaṭimā viya ahosi, kālaṅkato ca pana avihābrahmaloke nibbatti, nibbattamattova arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. Avihābrahmaloke kira nibbattamattāva satta janā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Vuttañhetaṃ –

Jīvitā voropesī

‘‘Avihaṃ upapannāse, vimuttā satta bhikkhavo;

Rāgadosaparikkhīṇā, tiṇṇā loke visattikaṃ.

Ke ca te ataruṃ paṅkaṃ, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ;

Ke hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upaccaguṃ.

Upako palagaṇḍo ca, pukkusāti ca te tayo;

Bhaddiyo khaṇḍadevo ca, bāhuraggi ca siṅgiyo;

Te hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upaccagu’’nti. (saṃ. ni. 1.50, 105);

Bimbisāropi ‘‘mayhaṃ sahāyo mayā pesitasāsanamattaṃ vācetvā hatthagataṃ rajjaṃ pahāya ettakaṃ addhānaṃ āgato, dukkaraṃ kataṃ kulaputtena, pabbajitasakkārena taṃ sakkarissāmī’’ti ‘‘pariyesatha me sahāyaka’’nti tattha tattha pesesi. Pesitā taṃ addasaṃsu saṅkāraṭṭhāne patitaṃ, disvā āgamma rañño ārocesuṃ. Rājā gantvā kulaputtaṃ disvā – ‘‘na vata, bho, labhimhā sahāyakassa sakkāraṃ kātuṃ, anātho me jāto sahāyako’’ti. Paridevitvā kulaputtaṃ mañcakena gaṇhāpetvā yuttokāse ṭhapetvā anupasampannassa sakkāraṃ kātuṃ jānanābhāvena nhāpakakappakādayo pakkosāpetvā kulaputtaṃ sīsaṃ nhāpetvā suddhavatthāni nivāsāpetvā rājavesena alaṅkārāpetvā sovaṇṇasivikaṃ āropetvā sabbatāḷāvacaragandhamālādīhi pūjaṃ karonto nagarā nīharitvā bahūhi gandhakaṭṭhehi mahācitakaṃ kāretvā kulaputtassa sarīrakiccaṃ katvā dhātuyo ādāya cetiyaṃ patiṭṭhapesi. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Dhātuvibhaṅgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
370. “But venerable sir, my bowl and robe (*pattacīvara*) are not complete.” Why are the bowl and robe made of spiritual power (*iddhimayapattacīvara*) not produced for a noble one (*kulaputta*)?

Because of not having given the eight requisites (*aṭṭhannaṃ parikkhārānaṃ adinnattā*) formerly.

It should not be said that the noble one (*kulaputta*) is a giver of gifts (*dinnadāna*) and has made an aspiration (*katābhinīhāra*), [but] not a giver (*dinna*).

However, the bowl and robe made of spiritual power (*iddhimayapattacīvaraṃ*) are produced only for those in their final existence (*pacchimabhavikānaṃyeva*), and this one is subject to rebirth (*punapaṭisandhiko*); therefore, they are not produced.

Then, why did the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) not ordain him after searching for them himself?

Because of the lack of opportunity (*okāsābhāvato*).

The noble one’s (*kulaputtassa*) life was exhausted (*āyu parikkhīṇaṃ*); the pure abodes (*suddhāvāsiko*), a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), the great Brahmā (*mahābrahmā*) was as if sitting after coming to the potter’s shed (*kumbhakārasālaṃ āgantvā nisinno viya ahosi*).

Therefore, he did not search for them himself.

“He departed in search of a bowl and robe (*pattacīvarapariyesanaṃ pakkāmī*),” at what time did he depart (*kāya velāya pakkāmi*)? When the dawn had risen (*uṭṭhite aruṇe*).

It is said that for the Blessed One (*bhagavato*) the completion of the teaching of the Dharma (*dhammadesanāpariniṭṭhānañca*), the rising of the dawn (*aruṇuṭṭhānañca*), and the emission of rays (*rasmivissajjanañca*) occurred at one moment (*ekakkhaṇe ahosi*).

It is said that the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) emitted the six-colored rays (*chabbaṇṇarasmiyo*) just after finishing the teaching (*desanaṃ niṭṭhapetvāva*); the entire potter’s dwelling (*sakalakumbhakāranivesanaṃ*) was a single illumination (*ekapajjotaṃ ahosi*); the six-colored rays (*chabbaṇṇarasmiyo*) having become masses of nets (*jālajālā puñjapuñjā hutvā*), running (*vidhāvantiyo*), and in every direction (*sabbadisābhāge*) were as if covered with golden cloth (*suvaṇṇapaṭapariyonaddhe viya ca*), and they made [it] as if exceedingly bright with various colored jewel lotuses (*nānāvaṇṇakusumaratanavisarasamujjale viya ca akaṃsu*).

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) resolved, “Let the city-dwellers see me (*nagaravāsino maṃ passantū*).”

The city-dwellers (*nagaravāsino*), having seen the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ*) said to each other, “It is said that the teacher (*satthā*) has come, it is said that he is sitting in the potter’s shed (*kumbhakārasālāya*),” and they announced it to the king (*rañño ārocesuṃ*).

He departed in search of a bowl and robe (*pattacīvarapariyesanaṃ pakkāmī*)

The king (*rājā*) having come, worshiped the teacher (*satthāraṃ vanditvā*), [and] asked, “Venerable sir (*bhante*), at what time did you come (*kāya velāya āgatत्था*)?”

“Yesterday, at sunset, great king (*mahārājāti*).”

“By what action, Blessed One (*bhagavāti*)?” The king [replied], “Pukkusāti, your friend (*tumhākaṃ sahāyo*), having heard the message (*sāsanaṃ*) sent by you (*tumhehi pahitaṃ*), having gone out (*nikkhamitvā*), having gone forth (*pabbajitvā*), coming (*āgacchanto*) aiming at me (*maṃ uddissa*), having passed beyond Śrāvastī (*sāvatthiṃ atikkamma*), having come forty-five *yojana*s (*pañcacattālīsa yojanāni āgantvā*), having entered this potter’s shed (*imaṃ kumbhakārasālaṃ pavisitvā nisīdi*), I, having come for the sake of helping him (*tassa saṅgahatthaṃ āgantvā*), spoke the Dharma talk (*dhammakathaṃ kathesiṃ*); the noble one (*kulaputto*) penetrated the three fruits (*tīṇi phalāni paṭivijjhi*), great king (*mahārājāti*).”

“Where [is he] now, venerable sir (*idāni kahaṃ, bhanteti*)?” “Having begged for ordination (*upasampadaṃ yācitvā*), for the sake of searching for a bowl and robe (*pattacīvarapariyesanatthaṃ*) because of the incompleteness of the bowl and robe (*aparipuṇṇapattacīvaratāya*), he has gone, great king (*gato mahārājāti*).”

The king (*rājā*) went in the direction in which the noble one (*kulaputtassa*) had gone (*gatadisābhāgena agamāsi*).

The Blessed One (*bhagavāpi*) also, having come through the sky (*ākāsenāgantvā*), appeared (*pāturahosi*) in the Jeta Grove’s Fragrant Cottage (*jetavanagandhakuṭimhiyeva*).

The noble one (*kulaputto*) also, searching for a bowl and robe (*pattacīvaraṃ pariyesamāno*), did not go to the presence (*santikaṃ agamāsi*) of either King Bimbisāra (*bimbisārarañño*) or the Taxila merchants of the leg (*takkasīlakānaṃ jaṅghavāṇijānaṃ*).

Thus, it occurred to him (*evaṃ kirassa ahosi*) – “It is not proper (*na kho me yuttaṃ*) to search for a bowl and robe (*pattacīvaraṃ pariyesituṃ*) gleaning (*vicinitvā*) only what is agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpameva*) there and there (*tattha tattha*) like a chicken (*kukkuṭassa viya*); having avoided a great city (*mahantaṃ nagaraṃ vajjitvā*), I will search in the water-crossing places, cemeteries, refuse heap places, and inner streets (*udakatitthasusānasaṅkāraṭṭhānaantaravīthīsu pariyesissāmi*),” thus, in an inner street (*antaravīthiyaṃ*), he began (*āraddho*) to search for rags (*pilotikaṃ pariyesituṃ*) in a heap of refuse (*saṅkārakūṭesu tāva*).

"He deprives [one] of life" (*jīvitā voropesī*) – in that refuse heap (*etasmiṃ saṅkārakūṭe*), while looking at a rag (*pilotikaṃ olokentaṃ*), a confused (*vibbhantā*) young calf cow (*taruṇavacchā gāvī*) having run up (*upadhāvitvā*), pierced [him] with [its] horn (*siṅgena vijjhitvā*), [and] killed [him] (*ghātesi*).

The noble one (*kulaputto*) tormented by hunger (*chātakajjhatto*), having reached the destruction of life (*āyukkhayaṃ patvā*) in the sky itself (*ākāseyeva*), fell (*patito*).

In the refuse heap (*saṅkāraṭṭhāne*) he was like a golden image (*suvaṇṇapaṭimā viya ahosi*) placed face down (*adhomukhaṭṭhapitā*), and having made time (*kālaṅkato ca*), he was born (*nibbatti*) in the Aviha Brahmā world (*avihābrahmaloke*), and just upon being born (*nibbattamattova*) he attained (*pāpuṇi*) *arhattaṃ*.

It is said that just upon being born (*nibbattamatāva*) in the Aviha Brahmā world (*avihābrahmaloke*) seven people (*satta janā*) attained *arhattaṃ*.

This was said –

"He deprives [one] of life" (*jīvitā voropesī*)

‘‘Having approached Aviha (*avihaṃ*), the seven monks (*satta bhikkhavo*) are liberated (*vimuttā*);

Having exhausted passion and hatred (*rāgadosaparikkhīṇā*), they have crossed over attachment (*visattikaṃ*) in the world (*loke*).

And which ones crossed the mud (*paṅkaṃ*), exceedingly difficult to cross, the domain of death (*maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ*)?

Who, having abandoned the human body (*mānusaṃ dehaṃ hitvā*), went beyond the divine union (*dibbayogaṃ upaccaguṃ*)?

Upaka (*upako*), Palagaṇḍa (*palagaṇḍo ca*), and Pukkusāti (*pukkusāti ca*) – those three (*te tayo*);

Bhaddiya (*bhaddiyo*), Khaṇḍadeva (*khaṇḍadevo ca*), Bāhuraggi (*bāhuraggi ca*), and Siṅgiya (*siṅgiyo*);

having abandoned the human body (*mānusaṃ dehaṃ hitvā*), they went beyond the divine union (*dibbayogaṃ upaccaguṃ*).’"

(Saṃ.
Ni.
1. 
2.  Bimbisāra also (thought): "He is my friend; having made him read the message sent by me, forsaking the kingdom that had come into his hand, he has come such a long distance. It was difficult to do for the clansman. I will honor him with the honor of a renunciate." Thus, he sent (messengers) saying, "Seek my friend" here and there.
Sent, they saw him fallen in a dust heap. Having seen (him), they went and announced it to the king.
The king, having gone and seen the clansman, (said:) "Indeed, we did not obtain the opportunity to do honor to our friend. My friend has become helpless."
Having lamented, having had the clansman taken up by a couch, having had (him) placed in a suitable place, because of the lack of knowledge to do honor to one who is not fully ordained, having had barbers and hairdressers summoned, having bathed the clansman's head, having had (him) clothed in pure garments, having had (him) adorned with royal attire, having had (him) carried up onto a golden palanquin, making an offering with all kinds of musical instruments, perfumes, garlands, and so on, leading (him) out of the city, having had a great pyre made with many fragrant pieces of wood, having performed the funeral rites for the clansman, having taken the relics, he established a *cetiya*.
The rest is clear throughout.

 The commentary to the *Dhātuvibhaṅga Sutta* is finished.

mula_pali:
371. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Tathāgatena, bhikkhave, arahatā sammāsambuddhena bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ, yadidaṃ – catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ, dukkhasamudayassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ, dukkhanirodhassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ. Tathāgatena, bhikkhave, arahatā sammāsambuddhena bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ , yadidaṃ – imesaṃ catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ.

‘‘Sevatha, bhikkhave, sāriputtamoggallāne; bhajatha, bhikkhave, sāriputtamoggallāne. Paṇḍitā bhikkhū anuggāhakā sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, janetā janetti (sī. pī.), evaṃ sāriputto; seyyathāpi jātassa āpādetā, evaṃ moggallāno. Sāriputto, bhikkhave, sotāpattiphale vineti, moggallāno uttamatthe. Sāriputto, bhikkhave, pahoti cattāri ariyasaccāni vitthārena ācikkhituṃ desetuṃ paññāpetuṃ paṭṭhapetuṃ vivarituṃ vibhajituṃ uttānīkātu’’nti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

janetti (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Baranasi in the deer park at Isipatana. There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks.” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied. The Fortunate One said this:

“At Benares, monks, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, the worthy one, the rightly self-awakened one, set in motion the unexcelled Wheel of the Dhamma that cannot be stopped by any ascetic or Brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world, that is, the proclaiming, teaching, making known, establishing, disclosing, analysing, and revealing of the Four Noble Truths ( *catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ* ). Which four? The proclaiming, teaching, making known, establishing, disclosing, analysing, and revealing of the Noble Truth of Suffering ( *dukkhassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ* ), the proclaiming… and revealing of the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering (*dukkhsamudayassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ*), the proclaiming… and revealing of the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering (*dukkhanirodhassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ*), the proclaiming… and revealing of the Noble Truth of the Path Leading to the Cessation of Suffering (*dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ*). At Benares, monks, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, the worthy one, the rightly self-awakened one, set in motion the unexcelled Wheel of the Dhamma that cannot be stopped by any ascetic or Brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world, that is, the proclaiming, teaching, making known, establishing, disclosing, analysing, and revealing of these Four Noble Truths."

“Associate with Sāriputta and Moggallāna, monks; be devoted to Sāriputta and Moggallāna, monks. They are wise monks who assist those living the spiritual life (*paṇḍitā bhikkhū anuggāhakā sabrahmacārīnaṃ*). Sāriputta is like a mother; Moggallāna is like a nurse. Sāriputta trains others for the fruit of stream-entry, Moggallāna for the supreme goal. Sāriputta, monks, is able to announce, teach, describe, establish, reveal, expound, and exhibit the Four Noble Truths in detail.”

That is what the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Happy One rose from his seat and went into his dwelling.
commentary_pali:
371.Evaṃme sutanti saccavibhaṅgasuttaṃ. Tattha ācikkhanāti idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ nāma…pe… ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ nāmāti. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Apicettha paññāpanā nāma dukkhasaccādīnaṃ ṭhapanā. Āsanaṃ ṭhapento hi āsanaṃ paññapetīti vuccati. Paṭṭhapanāti paññāpanā. Vivaraṇāti vivaṭakaraṇā. Vibhajanāti vibhāgakiriyā. Uttānīkammanti pākaṭabhāvakaraṇaṃ.

Anuggāhakāti āmisasaṅgahena dhammasaṅgahenāti dvīhipi saṅgahehi anuggāhakā. Janetāti janikā mātā. Āpādetāti posetā. Posikamātā viya moggallānoti dīpeti. Janikamātā hi nava vā dasa vā māse loṇambilādīni pariharamānā kucchiyā dārakaṃ dhāretvā kucchito nikkhantaṃ posikamātaraṃ dhātiṃ paṭicchāpeti. Sā khīranavanītādīhi dārakaṃ posetvā vaḍḍheti, so vuddhimāgamma yathāsukhaṃ vicarati. Evameva sāriputto attano vā paresaṃ vā santike pabbajite dvīhi saṅgahehi saṅgaṇhanto gilāne paṭijagganto kammaṭṭhāne yojetvā sotāpannabhāvaṃ ñatvā apāyabhayehi vuṭṭhitakālato paṭṭhāya – ‘‘idāni paccattapurisakārena uparimagge nibbattessantī’’ti tesu anapekkho hutvā aññe nave nave ovadati. Mahāmoggallānopi attano vā paresaṃ vā santike pabbajite tatheva saṅgaṇhitvā kammaṭṭhāne yojetvā heṭṭhā tīṇi phalāni pattesupi anapekkhataṃ na āpajjati. Kasmā? Evaṃ kirassa hoti – vuttaṃ bhagavatā – ‘‘seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, appamattakopi gūtho duggandho hoti…pe… appamattakampi muttaṃ… kheḷo… pubbo… lohitaṃ duggandhaṃ hoti, evameva kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, appamattakampi bhavaṃ na vaṇṇemi antamaso accharāsaṅghatamattampī’’ti (a. ni. 1.320-321). Tasmā yāva arahattaṃ na pāpuṇanti, tāva tesu anapekkhataṃ anāpajjitvā arahattaṃ pattesuyeva āpajjatīti. Tenāha bhagavā – ‘‘seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, janetā evaṃ sāriputto. Seyyathāpi jātassa āpādetā, evaṃ moggallāno. Sāriputto, bhikkhave, sotāpattiphale vineti, moggallāno uttamatthe’’ti. Pahotīti sakkoti.

Anuggāhakā Janetā Āpādetā Pahotī

Dukkheñāṇanti savanasammasanapaṭivedhañāṇaṃ, tathā dukkhasamudaye. Dukkhanirodhe savanapaṭivedhañāṇanti vaṭṭati, tathā dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya. Nekkhammasaṅkappādīsu kāmapaccanīkaṭṭhena, kāmato nissaṭabhāvena vā, kāmaṃ sammasantassa uppannoti vā, kāmapadaghātaṃ kāmavūpasamaṃ karonto uppannoti vā, kāmavivittante uppannoti vā nekkhammasaṅkappo. Sesapadadvayepi eseva nayo. Sabbepi cete pubbabhāge nānācittesu, maggakkhaṇe ekacitte labbhanti. Tatra hi micchāsaṅkappacetanāya samugghātako ekova saṅkappo labbhati, na nānā labbhati . Sammāvācādayopi pubbabhāge nānācittesu, vuttanayeneva maggakkhaṇe ekacitte labbhanti. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthārena pana saccakathā visuddhimagge ca sammādiṭṭhisutte (ma. ni. 1.89 ādayo) ca vuttāyevāti.

Dukkhe ñāṇa dukkhasamudaye. Dukkhanirodhe dukkhanirodhagāminiyā nekkhammasaṅkappo visuddhimagge

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Saccavibhaṅgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
371. Thus I have heard: the Saccavibhaṅga Sutta. There, *ācikkhanā* means: "This is called the noble truth of suffering"...pe... "This is called the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering." And so with the other three. Moreover, here, *paññāpanā* means the establishment of the truth of suffering, etc. For when one establishes a seat, it is said that one is designating a seat. *Paṭṭhapanā* means *paññāpanā*. *Vivarana* means making open. *Vibhajanā* means the act of dividing. *Uttānīkamma* means making manifest. *Anuggāhakā* means: through the two kinds of support, support of material things and support of the Dhamma, they are supporters. *Janetā* means the mother who gives birth, *janikā*. *Āpādetā* means the one who nourishes, *posetā*. It indicates that Moggallāna is like a nurse. The mother who gives birth, having carried the child in her womb for nine or ten months, avoiding salty and sour things, entrusts the child who has come forth from the womb to a wet nurse, a *posikamātaraṃ dhātiṃ*. She nourishes and raises the child with milk, fresh butter, etc., and he, having attained growth, lives comfortably. Just so, Sāriputta, gathering those who have gone forth in his own presence or in the presence of others with the two kinds of support, attending to the sick, connecting them to the meditation subject, knowing that they have [attained] the state of stream-enterer, from the time they have arisen from the fear of the lower realms, thinking, "Now, by their own effort, they will bring about the higher paths," he becomes unconcerned about them and advises other new ones. Mahāmoggallāna also, gathering those who have gone forth in his own presence or in the presence of others in the same way, connecting them to the meditation subject, does not become unconcerned even when they have attained the three lower fruits. Why? Because it occurs to him thus: it was said by the Blessed One: "Just as, monks, even a little bit of excrement is foul-smelling...pe... even a little bit of urine... phlegm... pus... blood is foul-smelling, just so, monks, I do not praise even a little bit of existence, not even as much as the joining together of syllables" (A. Ni. 1. 320-321). Therefore, until they attain arahantship, he does not become unconcerned about them, but he becomes unconcerned only when they have attained arahantship. Therefore, the Blessed One said: "Just as, monks, Sāriputta is the one who gives birth, *janetā*; just as Moggallāna is the one who nourishes the one who is born, *jātassa āpādetā*; Sāriputta, monks, trains [others] for the fruit of stream-entry, *sotāpattiphale vineti*, Moggallāna for the supreme goal." *Pahotī* means is able, *sakkoti*. *Anuggāhakā, janetā, āpādetā, pahotī.* *Ñāṇa* in suffering means the knowledge of hearing, considering, and penetrating, and so also in the origin of suffering. Knowledge of hearing and penetration applies to the cessation of suffering, and so also to the path leading to the cessation of suffering. *Nekkhamma-saṅkappo* [is] the thought of renunciation, because of being on the opposite side of sensual desire, or because of being free from sensual desire, or because it arises when one is considering sensual desire, or because it arises while destroying the place of sensual desire, [or] pacifying sensual desire, or because it arises when one is secluded from sensual desire. And the same rule applies to the other two terms also. All these are obtained in various minds in the prior part, but in one mind at the moment of the path. There, only one thought is obtained that is the destroyer of the intention of wrong thought, not various [thoughts] are obtained. 0219"/>. Right speech etc. are also available in the many different minds in the earlier part, in one mind at the moment of the path, in the manner already stated. This is a summary here; however, the detailed discussion of the truth is already stated in the *Visuddhimagga* and in the Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta (M. Ni. 1. 89 ff.).

Knowledge of suffering (*dukkhe ñāṇa*), the arising of suffering (*dukkhasamudaye*), the cessation of suffering (*dukkhanirodhe*), the path leading to the cessation of suffering (*dukkhanirodhagāminiyā*), and the thought of renunciation (*nekkhammasaṅkappo*) *Visuddhimagge* Commentary on the Saccavibhaṅga Sutta, from the Papañcasūdanī, commentary on the Majjhimanikāya, is finished.

mula_pali:
372. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto acirapakkantassa bhagavato bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘āvuso, bhikkhave’’ti. ‘‘Āvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

‘‘Tathāgatena, āvuso, arahatā sammāsambuddhena bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ, yadidaṃ – catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ, dukkhasamudayassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ, dukkhanirodhassa ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkammaṃ.
mula_english:
372. Then, soon after the Blessed One had gone, the venerable Sāriputta addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: “Friends, *bhikkhus*.”

—“Friend,” the *bhikkhus* replied to the venerable Sāriputta.

The venerable Sāriputta said this:

“At Benares, friends, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the *Tathāgata*, accomplished and fully enlightened (*arhat sammāsambuddha*), set rolling the matchless Wheel of the *Dharma*, which cannot be stopped by any recluse (*śramaṇa*) or *brāhmin* or god (*deva*) or *Māra* or *Brahmā* or anyone in the world - that is, the announcing (*ācikkhanā*), teaching (*desanā*), describing (*paññāpanā*), establishing (*paṭṭhapanā*), revealing (*vivaraṇā*), expounding (*vibhajanā*), and exhibiting (*uttānīkammaṃ*) of these Four Noble Truths (*catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ*).

Which four? The announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the noble truth of suffering (*duḥkha*). The announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the noble truth of the origin of suffering (*duḥkhasamudaya*). The announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the noble truth of the cessation of suffering (*duḥkhanirodha*). The announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering (*duḥkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadā*).

mula_pali:
373. ‘‘Katamañcāvuso, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Jātipi dukkhā, jarāpi dukkhā, maraṇampi dukkhaṃ, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsāpi dukkhā, yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ; saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā.

‘‘Katamā cāvuso, jāti? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jāti sañjāti okkanti abhinibbatti khandhānaṃ pātubhāvo āyatanānaṃ paṭilābho, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘jāti’’’.

‘‘Katamā cāvuso, jarā? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhi tamhi sattanikāye jarā jīraṇatā khaṇḍiccaṃ pāliccaṃ valittacatā āyuno saṃhāni indriyānaṃ paripāko, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘jarā’’’.

‘‘Katamañcāvuso, maraṇaṃ? Yā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ tamhā tamhā sattanikāyā cuti cavanatā bhedo antaradhānaṃ maccu maraṇaṃ kālaṃkiriyā khandhānaṃ bhedo kaḷevarassa nikkhepo jīvitindriyassupacchedo, idaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘maraṇaṃ’’’.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, soko? Yo kho, āvuso, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa soko socanā socitattaṃ antosoko antoparisoko, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘soko’’’.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, paridevo? Yo kho, āvuso, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa ādevo paridevo ādevanā paridevanā ādevitattaṃ paridevitattaṃ, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘paridevo’’’.

‘‘Katamañcāvuso, dukkhaṃ? Yaṃ kho, āvuso, kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ kāyikaṃ asātaṃ kāyasamphassajaṃ dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ, idaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘dukkhaṃ’’’.

‘‘Katamañcāvuso, domanassaṃ? Yaṃ kho, āvuso, cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetasikaṃ asātaṃ manosamphassajaṃ dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ, idaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘domanassaṃ’’’.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, upāyāso? Yo kho, āvuso, aññataraññatarena byasanena samannāgatassa aññataraññatarena dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhassa āyāso upāyāso āyāsitattaṃ upāyāsitattaṃ, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘upāyāso’’’.

‘‘Katamañcāvuso, yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ? Jātidhammānaṃ, āvuso, sattānaṃ evaṃ icchā uppajjati – ‘aho vata, mayaṃ na jātidhammā assāma; na ca, vata, no jāti āgaccheyyā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ icchāya pattabbaṃ. Idampi – ‘yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ’. Jarādhammānaṃ, āvuso, sattānaṃ…pe… byādhidhammānaṃ, āvuso, sattānaṃ… maraṇadhammānaṃ, āvuso, sattānaṃ… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammānaṃ, āvuso, sattānaṃ evaṃ icchā uppajjati – ‘aho vata, mayaṃ na sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā assāma ; na ca, vata, no sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā āgaccheyyu’nti . Na kho panetaṃ icchāya pattabbaṃ. Idampi – ‘yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ’’’.

‘‘Katame cāvuso, saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā? Seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime vuccantāvuso – ‘saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā’. Idaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ’’’.
mula_english:
373. "And what, friends, is the noble truth of suffering ( *duḥkha ariyasacca* )? Birth (*jāti*) is suffering, aging (*jarā*) is suffering, death (*maraṇa*) is suffering, sorrow (*śoka*), lamentation (*parideva*), pain (*duḥkha*), grief (*daumanassya*), and despair (*upāyāsa*) are suffering; not to obtain what one wants is suffering; in short, the five aggregates affected by clinging (*pañcupādānakkhandhā*) are suffering."

"And what, friends, is birth (*jāti*)? The birth of beings into the various orders of beings, their coming to birth, precipitation in a womb, generation, manifestation of the aggregates ( *khandha* ), obtaining the bases for contact ( *āyatana*) — this is called birth."

"And what, friends, is aging (*jarā*)? The aging of beings in the various orders of beings, their old age, brokenness of teeth, grayness of hair, wrinkling of skin, decline of life, weakness of faculties — this is called aging."

"And what, friends, is death (*maraṇa*)? The passing of beings out of the various orders of beings, their passing away, dissolution, disappearance, dying, completion of time, dissolution of the aggregates, laying down of the body, interruption of the life faculty — this is called death."

"And what, friends, is sorrow (*śoka*)? That sorrow, the state of sorrowing, the inward sorrow, the inward utter sorrow of one who is afflicted by one or another calamity, touched by one or another painful condition, this is called sorrow."

"And what, friends, is lamentation (*parideva*)? That lamenting, the state of lamenting, the inward lamenting, the inward utter lamenting of one who is afflicted by one or another calamity, touched by one or another painful condition, this is called lamentation."

"And what, friends, is pain (*duḥkha*)? Bodily pain, bodily discomfort, what is felt as uncomfortable and painful born of body contact, is called pain."

"And what, friends, is grief (*daumanassya*)? Mental pain, mental discomfort, painful, uncomfortable feeling born of mental contact - this is called grief."

"And what, friends, is despair (*upāyāsa*)? That despair, the state of despairing, the inward despair, the inward utter despair of one who is afflicted by one or another calamity, touched by one or another painful condition, this is called despair."

"And what, friends, is not to obtain what one wants is suffering? To beings subject to birth (*jātidhamma*), there comes the wish: ‘Oh, that we were not subject to birth; that birth would not come to us!’ But this is not to be obtained by wishing. This is also 'not to obtain what one wants is suffering'. To beings subject to aging… to beings subject to sickness… to beings subject to death… to beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, there comes the wish: ‘Oh, that we were not subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; and may grief, lamentation, pain, sorrow, and despair surely not come to us!’ But this is not to be obtained by wishing. This is also 'not to obtain what one wants is suffering'."

"And what, friends, are the five aggregates affected by clinging that, in short, are suffering? Namely, the aggregate of clinging to form (*rūpupādānakkhandha*), the aggregate of clinging to feeling (*vedanupādānakkhandha*), the aggregate of clinging to perception (*saññupādānakkhandha*), the aggregate of clinging to mental formations (*saṅkhārupādānakkhandha*), and the aggregate of clinging to consciousness (*viññāṇupādānakkhandha*). These, friends, are called the five aggregates affected by clinging that, in short, are suffering. This is called the noble truth of suffering."

mula_pali:
374. ‘‘Katamañcāvuso, dukkhasamudayaṃ dukkhasamudayo (syā. kaṃ.) ariyasaccaṃ? Yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā ponobhavikā (sī. pī.) nandīrāgasahagatā nandirāgasahagatā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā , idaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘dukkhasamudayaṃ dukkhasamudayo (syā. kaṃ.) ariyasaccaṃ’’’.

‘‘Katamañcāvuso, dukkhanirodhaṃ dukkhanirodho (syā. kaṃ.) ariyasaccaṃ? Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo, idaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘dukkhanirodhaṃ dukkhanirodho (syā. kaṃ.) ariyasaccaṃ’’’.

dukkhanirodho (syā. kaṃ.) dukkhanirodho (syā. kaṃ.)
mula_english:
374. “And what, friend, is the noble truth of the origin of suffering (*duḥkha-samudaya*). It is this craving (*taṇhā*) which leads to rebirth (*ponobbhavikā*), is accompanied by delight and passion (*nandīrāgasahagatā*), finding fresh delight now here, now there, namely craving for sensual pleasures (*kāmataṇhā*), craving for existence (*bhavataṇhā*), craving for non-existence (*vibhavataṇhā*). This, friend, is called the noble truth of the origin of suffering.”

“And what, friend, is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering (*duḥkha-nirodha*)? It is the complete passionless cessation, renunciation, rejection, liberation, and detachment from that very craving (*taṇhā*). This, friend, is called the noble truth of the cessation of suffering.”

mula_pali:
375. ‘‘Katamañcāvuso, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

‘‘Katamācāvuso, sammādiṭṭhi? Yaṃ kho, āvuso, dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘sammādiṭṭhi’’’.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, sammāsaṅkappo? Nekkhammasaṅkappo, abyāpādasaṅkappo , avihiṃsāsaṅkappo, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘sammāsaṅkappo’’’.

‘‘Katamā cāvuso, sammāvācā? Musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘sammāvācā’’’.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, sammākammantī? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘sammākammanto’’’.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, sammāājīvo? Idhāvuso, ariyasāvako micchāājīvaṃ pahāya sammāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘sammāājīvo’’’.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, sammāvāyāmo? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘sammāvāyāmo’’’.

‘‘Katamā cāvuso, sammāsati? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati…pe… citte cittānupassī viharati… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘sammāsati’’’.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, sammāsamādhi? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… viharati, ayaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘sammāsamādhi’. Idaṃ vuccatāvuso – ‘dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ’’’.

‘‘Tathāgatenāvuso, arahatā sammāsambuddhena bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ, yadidaṃ – imesaṃ catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ ācikkhanā desanā paññāpanā paṭṭhapanā vivaraṇā vibhajanā uttānīkamma’’nti.

Idamavoca āyasmā sāriputto. Attamanā te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Saccavibhaṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ ekādasamaṃ.
mula_english:
375. "And what, friends, is the noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering? It is just this Noble Eightfold Path; that is, right view (sammādiṭṭhi), right intention (sammāsaṅkappo), right speech (sammāvācā), right action (sammākammanto), right livelihood (sammāājīvo), right effort (sammāvāyāmo), right mindfulness (sammāsati), [and] right concentration (sammāsamādhi).

"And what, friends, is right view (sammādiṭṭhi)? It is, friends, knowledge of suffering (dukkhe ñāṇaṃ), knowledge of the origin of suffering (dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ), knowledge of the cessation of suffering (dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ), and knowledge of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering (dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ). This, friends, is called right view."

"And what, friends, is right intention (sammāsaṅkappo)? It is the intention of renunciation (nekkhamma saṅkappo), the intention of non-ill will (abyāpāda saṅkappo), and the intention of non-cruelty (avihiṃsā saṅkappo). This, friends, is called right intention."

"And what, friends, is right speech (sammāvācā)? Abstaining from false speech (musāvādā veramaṇī), abstaining from malicious speech (pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī), abstaining from harsh speech (pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī), [and] abstaining from idle chatter (samphappalāpā veramaṇī). This, friends, is called right speech."

"And what, friends, is right action (sammākammanto)? Abstaining from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā veramaṇī), abstaining from taking what is not given (adinnādānā veramaṇī), [and] abstaining from sexual misconduct (kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī). This, friends, is called right action."

"And what, friends, is right livelihood (sammāājīvo)? Here, friends, a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, makes a living by right livelihood. This, friends, is called right livelihood."

"And what, friends, is right effort (sammāvāyāmo)? Here, friends, a bhikkhu generates desire, endeavors, activates persistence, upholds & exerts his intent for the sake of the non-arising of evil, unskillful qualities that have not yet arisen; [and] generates desire, endeavors, activates persistence, upholds & exerts his intent for the sake of the abandoning of evil, unskillful qualities that have arisen; [and] generates desire, endeavors, activates persistence, upholds & exerts his intent for the sake of the arising of skillful qualities that have not yet arisen; [and] generates desire, endeavors, activates persistence, upholds & exerts his intent for the maintenance, non-confusion, increase, plenitude, development, & culmination of skillful qualities that have arisen. This, friends, is called right effort."

"And what, friends, is right mindfulness (sammāsati)? Here, friends, a bhikkhu abides contemplating the body as body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world. He abides contemplating feelings as feelings… He abides contemplating mind as mind… He abides contemplating mind-objects as mind-objects, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world. This, friends, is called right mindfulness."

"And what, friends, is right concentration (sammāsamādhi)? Here, friends, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration. With the fading away as well of rapture, he abides in equanimity… [and] abides in the third *jhāna*… This, friends, is called right concentration. This, friends, is called the noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering."

"At Benares, friends, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the unexcelled Wheel of the Dhamma, which cannot be turned back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world, namely, the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, explaining, and making known these Four Noble Truths."

This is what the Venerable Sāriputta said.

The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Venerable Sāriputta’s words.

The *Saccavibhaṅga Sutta*, the eleventh [discourse], is finished.

mula_pali: 376. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho mahāpajāpati mahāpajāpatī (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) gotamī navaṃ dussayugaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idaṃ me, bhante, navaṃ dussayugaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa sāmaṃ kantaṃ sāmaṃ vāyitaṃ. Taṃ me, bhante, bhagavā paṭiggaṇhātu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘saṅghe, gotami, dehi. Saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idaṃ me, bhante, navaṃ dussayugaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa sāmaṃ kantaṃ sāmaṃ vāyitaṃ. Taṃ me, bhante, bhagavā paṭiggaṇhātu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘saṅghe, gotami, dehi. Saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cā’’ti. Tatiyampi kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idaṃ me, bhante, navaṃ dussayugaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa sāmaṃ kantaṃ sāmaṃ vāyitaṃ. Taṃ me, bhante, bhagavā paṭiggaṇhātu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. Tatiyampi kho bhagavā mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘saṅghe, gotami, dehi . Saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cā’’ti.
mula_english:
376. Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One (bhagavā) was living in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in Nigrodha’s Park.

Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, having taken a new pair of cloths, went to where the Blessed One was; having gone and worshipped the Blessed One, she sat down on one side.

As she was sitting on one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One: “This new pair of cloths, venerable sir (bhante), has been spun by me, woven by me, especially for the Blessed One (bhagavā). Venerable sir (bhante), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) accept it from me out of compassion (anukampaṃ upādāya)."

When this was said, the Blessed One (bhagavā) said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī: “Give it to the *Saṃgha*, Gotamī. When you give it to the *Saṃgha*, the offering will be made both to me and to the *Saṃgha*.”

A second time Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One (bhagavā): “This new pair of cloths, venerable sir (bhante), has been spun by me, woven by me, especially for the Blessed One (bhagavā). Venerable sir (bhante), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) accept it from me out of compassion (anukampaṃ upādāya).”

A second time the Blessed One (bhagavā) said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī: “Give it to the *Saṃgha*, Gotamī. When you give it to the *Saṃgha*, the offering will be made both to me and to the *Saṃgha*.”

A third time Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One (bhagavā): “This new pair of cloths, venerable sir (bhante), has been spun by me, woven by me, especially for the Blessed One (bhagavā). Venerable sir (bhante), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) accept it from me out of compassion (anukampaṃ upādāya).”

A third time the Blessed One (bhagavā) said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī: “Give it to the *Saṃgha*, Gotamī.
When you give it to the *Saṃgha*, the offering will be made both to me and to the *Saṃgha*.”
commentary_pali:
376.Evaṃme sutanti dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasuttaṃ. Tattha mahāpajāpati gotamīti gotamīti gottaṃ. Nāmakaraṇadivase panassā laddhasakkārā brāhmaṇā lakkhaṇasampattiṃ disvā – ‘‘sace ayaṃ dhītaraṃ labhissati, cakkavattirañño aggamahesī bhavissati. Sace puttaṃ labhissati, cakkavattirājā bhavissatīti ubhayathāpi mahatīyevassā pajā bhavissatī’’ti byākariṃsu. Athassā mahāpajāpatīti nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Idha pana gottena saddhiṃ saṃsanditvā mahāpajāpatigotamīti vuttaṃ. Navanti ahataṃ. Sāmaṃ vāyitanti na sahattheneva vāyitaṃ, ekadivasaṃ pana dhātigaṇaparivutā sippikānaṃ vāyanaṭṭhānaṃ āgantvā vemakoṭiṃ gahetvā vāyanākāraṃ akāsi. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Kadā pana gotamiyā bhagavato dussayugaṃ dātuṃ cittaṃ uppannanti. Abhisambodhiṃ patvā paṭhamagamanena kapilapuraṃ āgatakāle. Tadā hi piṇḍāya paviṭṭhaṃ satthāraṃ gahetvā suddhodanamahārājā sakaṃ nivesanaṃ pavesesi, atha bhagavato rūpasobhaggaṃ disvā mahāpajāpatigotamī cintesi – ‘‘sobhati vata me puttassa attabhāvo’’ti. Athassā balavasomanassaṃ uppajji. Tato cintesi – ‘‘mama puttassa ekūnatiṃsa vassāni agāramajjhe vasantassa antamaso mocaphalamattampi mayā dinnakameva ahosi, idānipissa cīvarasāṭakaṃ dassāmī’’ti. ‘‘Imasmiṃ kho pana rājagehe bahūni mahagghāni vatthāni atthi, tāni maṃ na tosenti, sahatthā katameva maṃ toseti, sahatthā katvā dassāmī’’ti cittaṃ uppādesi.

Athantarāpaṇā kappāsaṃ āharāpetvā sahattheneva pisitvā pothetvā sukhumasuttaṃ kantitvā antovatthusmiṃyeva sālaṃ kārāpetvā sippike pakkosāpetvā sippikānaṃ attano paribhogakhādanīyabhojanīyameva datvā vāyāpesi, kālānukālañca dhātigaṇaparivutā gantvā vemakoṭiṃ aggahesi. Niṭṭhitakāle sippikānaṃ mahāsakkāraṃ katvā dussayugaṃ gandhasamugge pakkhipitvā vāsaṃ gāhāpetvā – ‘‘mayhaṃ puttassa cīvarasāṭakaṃ gahetvā gamissāmī’’ti rañño ārocesi . Rājā maggaṃ paṭiyādāpesi, vīthiyo sammajjitvā puṇṇaghaṭe ṭhapetvā dhajapaṭākā ussāpetvā rājagharadvārato paṭṭhāya yāva nigrodhārāmā maggaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā pupphābhikiṇṇaṃ akaṃsu. Mahāpajāpatipi sabbālaṅkāraṃ alaṅkaritvā dhātigaṇaparivutā samuggaṃ sīse ṭhapetvā bhagavato santikaṃ gantvā idaṃ me, bhante, navaṃ dussayugantiādimāha.

idaṃ me, bhante, navaṃ dussayuga

Dutiyampi khoti ‘‘saṅghe gotami dehī’’ti vutte – ‘‘pahomahaṃ, bhante, dussakoṭṭhāgārato bhikkhusatassāpi bhikkhusahassassāpi bhikkhusatasahassassāpi cīvaradussāni dātuṃ, idaṃ pana me bhagavantaṃ uddissa sāmaṃ kantaṃ sāmaṃ vāyitaṃ, taṃ me, bhante, bhagavā paṭiggaṇhātū’’ti nimantayamānā āha. Evaṃ yāvatatiyaṃ yāci, bhagavāpi paṭikkhipiyeva.

Dutiyampi kho

Kasmā pana bhagavā attano diyyamānaṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa dāpetīti? Mātari anukampāya. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘imissā maṃ ārabbha pubbacetanā muñcacetanā paracetanāti tisso cetanā uppannā, bhikkhusaṅghampissā ārabbha uppajjantu, evamassā cha cetanā ekato hutvā dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya pavattissantī’’ti. Vitaṇḍavādī panāha – ‘‘saṅghe dinnaṃ mahapphalanti tasmā evaṃ vutta’’nti. So vattabbo – ‘‘kiṃ tvaṃ satthu dinnato saṅghe dinnaṃ mahapphalataraṃ vadasī’’ti āma vadāmīti. Suttaṃ āharāti. Saṅghe gotami dehi, saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cāti. Kiṃ panassa suttassa ayameva atthoti ? Āma ayamevāti. Yadi evaṃ ‘‘tena hānanda, vighāsādānaṃ pūvaṃ dehī’’ti ca (pāci. 269) ‘‘tena hi tva, kaccāna, vighāsādānaṃ guḷaṃ dehī’’ti (mahāva. 284) ca vacanato vighāsādānaṃ dinnaṃ mahapphalatarañca bhaveyya. Evampi hi ‘‘satthā attano diyyamānaṃ dāpetī’’ti. Rājarājamahāmattādayopi attano āgataṃ paṇṇākāraṃ hatthigopakādīnaṃ dāpenti, te rājādīhi mahantatarā bhaveyyuṃ. Tasmā mā evaṃ gaṇha –

‘‘Nayimasmiṃ loke parasmiṃ vā pana,

Buddhena seṭṭho sadiso vā vijjati;

Yamāhuneyyānamaggataṃ gato,

Puññatthikānaṃ vipulaphalesina’’nti. –

Vacanato hi satthārā uttaritaro dakkhiṇeyyo nāma natthi. Evamassā cha cetanā ekato hutvā dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissantīti sandhāya yāvatatiyaṃ paṭibāhitvā saṅghassa dāpesi.

Pacchimāya janatāya saṅghe cittīkārajananatthaṃ cāpi evamāha. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘ahaṃ na ciraṭṭhitiko, mayhaṃ pana sāsanaṃ bhikkhusaṅghe patiṭṭhahissati, pacchimā janatā saṅghe cittīkāraṃ janetū’’ti yāvatatiyaṃ paṭibāhitvā saṅghassa dāpesi. Evañhi sati – ‘‘satthā attano diyyamānampi saṅghassa dāpesi, saṅgho nāma dakkhiṇeyyo’’ti pacchimā janatā saṅghe cittīkāraṃ uppādetvā cattāro paccaye dātabbe maññissati, saṅgho catūhi paccayehi akilamanto buddhavacanaṃ uggahetvā samaṇadhammaṃ karissati. Evaṃ mama sāsanaṃ pañca vassasahassāni ṭhassatīti. ‘‘Paṭiggaṇhātu, bhante, bhagavā’’ti vacanatopi cetaṃ veditabbaṃ ‘‘satthārā uttaritaro dakkhiṇeyyo nāma natthī’’ti. Na hi ānandattherassa mahāpajāpatiyā āghāto vā veraṃ vā atthi. Na thero – ‘‘tassā dakkhiṇā mā mahapphalā ahosī’’ti icchati. Paṇḍito hi thero bahussuto sekkhapaṭisambhidāpatto , so satthu dinnassa mahapphalabhāve sampassamānova paṭiggaṇhātu, bhante, bhagavāti gahaṇatthaṃ yāci.

Puna vitaṇḍavādī āha – ‘‘saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cā’’ti vacanato satthā saṅghapariyāpanno vāti. So vattabbo – ‘‘jānāsi pana tvaṃ kati saraṇāni, kati aveccappasādā’’ti jānanto tīṇīti vakkhati, tato vattabbo – tava laddhiyā satthu saṅghapariyāpannattā dveyeva honti. Evaṃ sante ca – ‘‘anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi tīhi saraṇagamanehi pabbajjaṃ upasampada’’nti (mahāva. 34) evaṃ anuññātā pabbajjāpi upasampadāpi na ruhati. Tato tvaṃ neva pabbajito asi, na gihi. Sammāsambuddhe ca gandhakuṭiyaṃ nisinne bhikkhū uposathampi pavāraṇampi saṅghakammānipi karonti, tāni satthu saṅghapariyāpannattā kuppāni bhaveyyuṃ, na ca honti. Tasmā na vattabbametaṃ ‘‘satthā saṅghapariyāpanno’’ti.
commentary_english:
376. Thus have I heard: the *Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasutta*.

There, *Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī*: *Gotamī* is the clan name.

On the naming day, Brahmins who had received honors predicted, having seen the signs of good fortune: "If she has a daughter, she will be the chief queen of a *cakkavatti* king. If she has a son, she will be a *cakkavatti* ruler." Thus, in both ways, a great progeny will be hers.

Then they gave her the name *Mahāpajāpatī*.

Here, however, having combined it with the clan name, it is said *Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī*.

*Nava* means unwashed.

*Sāmaṃ vāyita* means it was not woven by her own hands alone; however, one day, surrounded by a group of nurses, having gone to the weaving place of the weavers, taking the end of the loom, she made the gesture of weaving.

This was said with reference to that.

When did Gotamī’s thought arise to give a pair of cloths to the Blessed One?

At the time when, having attained complete awakening, he arrived at Kapilapura by the first journey.

Then, indeed, Suddhodana Mahārāja, having taken the Teacher who had entered for alms, led him into his own dwelling. Then, having seen the beauty of the Blessed One’s form, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī thought: “How beautiful, indeed, is the state of my son!”

Then a strong joy arose in her.

Then she thought: “For twenty-nine years my son, while living in the house, at least even the amount of a banana fruit had been given only by me. Now I will give him a set of monastic robes.”

“In this royal house, there are many expensive cloths, but those do not please me. Only that which is made with my own hands pleases me. Having made it with my own hands, I will give it,” she generated the thought.

Then, in between, she had cotton brought, and with her own hands she pounded, threshed, spun fine thread, had a loom set up in the inner courtyard itself, summoned weavers, and giving the weavers only her own requisites, edibles, and food, she had it woven. From time to time, surrounded by a group of nurses, she went and held the end of the loom.

At the end of the weaving, having made a great offering to the weavers, having placed the pair of cloths in a perfume box, having taken a dwelling, she announced to the king: “Having taken a set of monastic robes for my son, I will go.”

The king had the road prepared, having swept the streets, having placed full water pots, having raised flags and banners, having had the road prepared from the gate of the royal palace as far as the Banyan Tree Park, they made it strewn with flowers.

Mahāpajāpatī also, having adorned herself with all ornaments, surrounded by a group of nurses, having placed the box on her head, having gone to the presence of the Blessed One, said, beginning with, “This is my new pair of cloths, O Blessed One.”

“This is my new pair of cloths, O Blessed One.”

The second time, when he said, “Give it to the Saṅgha, Gotamī,” she said: “I am able, O Blessed One, to give monastic robes from a storehouse of cloths to even a hundred monks, even a thousand monks, even a hundred thousand monks. However, this, having intended it for the Blessed One, I spun myself, I wove myself. May the Blessed One accept that from me, O Blessed One,” she invited him.

Thus, she requested up to the third time, but the Blessed One refused.

The second time, why did the Blessed One have what was being given to himself given to the Saṅgha? Out of compassion for his mother.

Thus it occurred to him: “For her, having been begun with me, three thoughts have arisen: a prior thought, a releasing thought, and a subsequent thought. Let them also arise, having been begun with the Saṅgha. Thus, her six thoughts, having become one, will conduce to well-being and happiness for a long time.”

The debater then said: “What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit. Therefore, it was said thus.”

He should be told: “Do you say that what is given to the Teacher is of less fruit than what is given to the Saṅgha?” “Yes, I say so.”

He brings the *sutta*.

“Give to the Saṅgha, Gotamī. When it is given to the Saṅgha by you, both I will be honored, and the Saṅgha also.”

Is this itself the meaning of this *sutta*? Yes, this itself.

If so, “Then, Ānanda, give the leftover food first,” and also (Pāci.

269) “Then, Kaccāna, give the leftover food, the sugar lumps,” (Mahāva.
284) And because of the statement, giving leftovers is more greatly fruitful.

Even so, [they say,] "The Teacher makes [others] give what belongs to himself."

Even kings, chief ministers, and others cause their acquired tribute to be given to elephant drivers and others. These would be greater than the kings, etc.

Therefore, do not take it thus –

‘‘There is not in this world or in another,

a superior or equal to the Buddha;

having gone to the path of those worthy of offerings,

for those who desire merit, he is the one who gives abundant fruit.’’

–

Because of the statement, there is no one called a *dakṣiṇīya* superior to the Teacher.

Having considered that these six thoughts, being unified, will be for long-term benefit and happiness, intending this, having prevented it up to the third time, he caused it to be given to the *saṃgha*.

For the sake of generating respect in the *saṃgha* in the later generation, he also said this:

Thus it occurred to him: “I am not long-lasting, but my teaching will be established in the community of monks. May the later generation generate respect in the *saṃgha*!” Having prevented it up to the third time, he caused it to be given to the *saṃgha*.

Because it is thus, [he thought,] “The Teacher makes [others] give even what belongs to himself to the *saṃgha*. The *saṃgha* is called worthy of offerings." Having generated respect in the *saṃgha*, the later generation will think that the four requisites should be given. The *saṃgha*, not tiring with the four requisites, having mastered the Buddha's word, will do the ascetic life.

Thus, my teaching will last for five thousand years.

"May the Blessed One accept [this]," even from this statement, it should be understood that there is no *dakṣiṇīya* superior to the Teacher.

For Ānanda Thera does not have hatred or animosity towards Mahāpajāpatī.

The Thera does not desire, "May her offering not be greatly fruitful."

For the wise Thera, being very learned, having attained the *sekha-paṭisambhidā*, seeing the greatly fruitful nature of what was given by the Teacher, requested it for the purpose of acceptance, saying, "May the Blessed One accept [this], Venerable Sir."

Again, the disputatious one said, “Because of the statement, ‘When it is given to you in the *saṃgha*, I myself will be honored, and so will the *saṃgha*,’ the Teacher is included in the *saṃgha*.”

He should be told, "Do you know how many refuges there are, how many unshakable faiths there are?" Knowing, he will say, "Three." Then he should be told, "According to your doctrine, because the Teacher is included in the *saṃgha*, there are only two."

When it is thus, and – "I allow, monks, the *pravrajyā* and *upasampadā* with these three going-for-refuges" (Mahāva.

34) Thus, the permitted *pravrajyā* and *upasampadā* do not grow.

Therefore, you are neither a *pravrajita* nor a householder.

And when the monks are sitting in the *gandhakuṭī* of the Perfectly Awakened One, they perform the *uposatha*, the *pavāraṇa*, and the *saṃghakarmas*. These, because the Teacher is included in the *saṃgha*, would be ruined, but they are not.

Therefore, it should not be said that "the Teacher is included in the *saṃgha*."

mula_pali: 377. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘paṭiggaṇhātu, bhante, bhagavā mahāpajāpatiyā gotamiyā navaṃ dussayugaṃ. Bahūpakārā bahukārā (syā. kaṃ.), bhante, mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavato mātucchā āpādikā posikā khīrassa dāyikā; bhagavantaṃ janettiyā kālaṅkatāya thaññaṃ pāyesi. Bhagavāpi, bhante, bahūpakāro mahāpajāpatiyā gotamiyā. Bhagavantaṃ, bhante, āgamma mahāpajāpati gotamī buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā, saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā. Bhagavantaṃ, bhante, āgamma mahāpajāpati gotamī pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā. Bhagavantaṃ, bhante, āgamma mahāpajāpati gotamī buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā , dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgatā, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatā ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā. Bhagavantaṃ, bhante, āgamma mahāpajāpati gotamī dukkhe nikkaṅkhā, dukkhasamudaye nikkaṅkhā, dukkhanirodhe nikkaṅkhā, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya nikkaṅkhā. Bhagavāpi, bhante, bahūpakāro mahāpajāpatiyā gotamiyā’’ti.
mula_english:
When this had been said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept this new pair of cloths from Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī.

Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī has been very helpful to the Blessed One, venerable sir. As the Blessed One’s maternal aunt, she was his nurse, his foster mother, the one who gave him milk; she suckled the Blessed One when his own mother died. The Blessed One too has been very helpful to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, venerable sir.

It is owing to the Blessed One that Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī has gone for refuge to the Buddha (buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā), has gone for refuge to the Dharma (dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā), and has gone for refuge to the Saṅgha (saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā).

It is owing to the Blessed One that Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī abstains from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā), abstains from taking what is not given (adinnādānā paṭiviratā), abstains from misconduct in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā), abstains from false speech (musāvādā paṭiviratā), and abstains from wine, liquor, and intoxicants, which are the basis of negligence (surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā).

It is owing to the Blessed One that Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī possesses perfect confidence in the Buddha (buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā), possesses perfect confidence in the Dharma (dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgatā), possesses perfect confidence in the Saṅgha (saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatā), and possesses the virtues loved by noble ones (ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā).

It is owing to the Blessed One that Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī is free from doubt about suffering (dukkhe nikkaṅkhā), about the origin of suffering (dukkhasamudaye nikkaṅkhā), about the cessation of suffering ( dukkhanirodhe nikkaṅkhā), and about the way leading to the cessation of suffering ( dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya nikkaṅkhā). The Blessed One too has been very helpful to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, venerable sir.”
commentary_pali: 377.Āpādikāti saṃvaḍḍhikā, tumhākaṃ hatthapādesu hatthapādakiccaṃ asādhentesu hatthe ca pāde ca vaḍḍhetvā paṭijaggikāti attho. Posikāti divasassa dve tayo vāre nhāpetvā bhojetvā pāyetvā tumhe posesi. Thaññaṃ pāyesīti nandakumāro kira bodhisattato katipāheneva daharo, tasmiṃ jāte mahāpajāpati attano puttaṃ dhātīnaṃ datvā sayaṃ bodhisattassa dhātikiccaṃ sādhayamānā attano thaññaṃ pāyesi. Taṃ sandhāya thero evamāha. Iti mahāpajāpatiyā bahūpakārataṃ kathetvā idāni tathāgatassa bahūpakārataṃ dassento bhagavāpi, bhantetiādimāha. Tattha bhagavantaṃ, bhante, āgammāti bhagavantaṃ paṭicca nissāya sandhāya.
commentary_english:
"Āpādikā" means *saṃvaḍḍhikā*, one who fosters or brings up, [meaning] in your hands and feet, when the functions of hands and feet are not being accomplished, having increased the hands and feet, *paṭijaggikā* is the meaning.

"Posikā" means you nourish them, bathing, feeding, and giving drink two or three times a day.

"Thaññaṃ pāyesī" means Nandakumāra was young, a mere child after a few days from the Bodhisattva. When he was born, Mahāpajāpati, having given her own son to nurses, herself accomplishing the duty of a nurse for the Bodhisattva, gave her own breast milk ( *thaññaṃ* ) to drink.

Referring to that, the Elder spoke thus.

Thus, having spoken of the great helpfulness of Mahāpajāpati, now showing the great helpfulness of the *Tathāgata*, he said "Bhagavāpi, bhante" etc.

There, "Bhagavantaṃ, bhante, āgammā" means relying on, depending on, in relation to the Blessed One ( *bhagavantaṃ* ).

mula_pali:
378. ‘‘Evametaṃ , ānanda. Yaṃ hānanda, puggalo puggalaṃ āgamma buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato hoti, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato hoti, saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato hoti, imassānanda, puggalassa iminā puggalena na suppatikāraṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – abhivādana-paccuṭṭhāna-añjalikamma sāmīcikammacīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilā- nappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānuppadānena.

‘‘Yaṃ hānanda, puggalo puggalaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti, imassānanda, puggalassa iminā puggalena na suppatikāraṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – abhivādana-paccuṭṭhāna-añjalikamma-sāmīcikammacīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilā- nappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānuppadānena.

‘‘Yaṃ hānanda, puggalo puggalaṃ āgamma buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti, dhamme… saṅghe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti, imassānanda, puggalassa iminā puggalena na suppatikāraṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – abhivādana-paccuṭṭhāna-añjalikamma-sāmīcikammacīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilā- nappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānuppadānena.

‘‘Yaṃ hānanda, puggalo puggalaṃ āgamma dukkhe nikkaṅkho hoti, dukkhasamudaye nikkaṅkho hoti, dukkhanirodhe nikkaṅkho hoti, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya nikkaṅkho hoti, imassānanda, puggalassa iminā puggalena na suppatikāraṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – abhivādana-paccuṭṭhānaañjalikamma-sāmīcikamma-cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilā- nappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānuppadānena.
mula_english:
378. “So it is, Ānanda.

When one person, owing to another, has gone for refuge to the Buddha, has gone for refuge to the Dharma, and has gone for refuge to the Saṃgha, I say that it is not easy for the former to repay the latter by paying homage, rising up for him, according him reverential salutation, performing polite services, and by providing robes, almsfood, resting places, and medicinal requisites.

“When one person, owing to another, has come to abstain from killing living beings (prāṇātipātā), from taking what is not given (adinnādānā), from misconduct in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārā), from false speech (musāvādā), and from wine, liquor, and intoxicants, which are the basis of negligence (surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā), I say that it is not easy for the former to repay the latter by paying homage…and medicinal requisites.

“When one person, owing to another, has come to possess perfect confidence in the Buddha, in the Dharma, and in the Saṃgha, and to possess the virtues loved by noble ones (ariyakantehi sīlehi), I say that it is not easy for the former to repay the latter by paying homage…and medicinal requisites.

“When one person, owing to another, has become free from doubt about suffering (dukkhe), about the origin of suffering (dukkhasamudaye), about the cessation of suffering ( dukkhanirodhe), and about the way leading to the cessation of suffering ( dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya), I say that it is not easy for the former to repay the latter by paying homage…and medicinal requisites.
commentary_pali: 378. Atha bhagavā dvīsu upakāresu atirekataraṃ anumodanto evametantiādimāha. Tattha yaṃ hānanda, puggalo puggalaṃ āgammāti yaṃ ācariyapuggalaṃ antevāsikapuggalo āgamma. Imassānanda, puggalassa iminā puggalenāti imassa ācariyapuggalassa iminā antevāsikapuggalena. Na suppaṭikāraṃ vadāmīti paccūpakāraṃ na sukaraṃ vadāmi, abhivādanādīsu ācariyaṃ disvā abhivādanakaraṇaṃ abhivādanaṃ nāma. Yasmiṃ vā disābhāge ācariyo vasati, iriyāpathe vā kappento tadabhimukho vanditvā gacchati, vanditvā nisīdati, vanditvā nipajjati, ācariyaṃ pana dūratova disvā paccuṭṭhāya paccuggamanakaraṇaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ nāma. Ācariyaṃ pana disvā añjaliṃ paggayha sīse ṭhapetvā ācariyaṃ namassati, yasmiṃ vā disābhāge so vasati, tadabhimukhopi tatheva namassati, gacchantopi ṭhitopi nisinnopi añjaliṃ paggayha namassatiyevāti idaṃ añjalikammaṃ nāma. Anucchavikakammassa pana karaṇaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ nāma. Cīvarādīsu cīvaraṃ dento na yaṃ vā taṃ vā deti, mahagghaṃ satamūlikampi pañcasatamūlikampi sahassamūlikampi detiyeva . Piṇḍapātādīsupi eseva nayo. Kiṃ bahunā, catūhi paṇītapaccayehi cakkavāḷantaraṃ pūretvā sinerupabbatena kūṭaṃ gahetvā dentopi ācariyassa anucchavikaṃ kiriyaṃ kātuṃ na sakkotiyeva.
commentary_english:
378. Then the Blessed One, approving of the superior of the two kinds of help, said, "Indeed, it is so," and so forth.

There, "He approaches a person," means the student approaches the teacher.

"Of this person, by this person," means of this teacher, by this student.

"I do not say it is easy to repay," means it is not easy to return the favor. Among acts of reverence, seeing the teacher and making a respectful salutation is called *abhivādana* (respectful salutation).

In whatever direction the teacher dwells, or in whatever posture they are, facing that direction, one bows down and goes, bows down and sits, bows down and lies down. Furthermore, seeing the teacher from afar, rising and making a welcoming gesture is called *paccuṭṭhānaṃ* (rising to greet).

Furthermore, seeing the teacher, raising one's joined palms (*añjali*) and placing them on one's head, one pays homage to the teacher. In whatever direction they dwell, even facing that direction, one pays homage in the same way. Whether going, standing, or sitting, one always pays homage with raised joined palms. This is called *añjalikammaṃ* (the act of reverently joining the palms).

Moreover, performing appropriate service is called *sāmīcikammaṃ* (proper service).

When giving robes, and so forth, one does not give just any robe. One gives even a valuable robe worth one hundred, five hundred, or a thousand.

And so with alms-food, and so on; the same rule applies.

Why say more? Even if one were to fill the space between world-systems with the four excellent requisites, and taking Mount Sumeru as a container, were to give, one would still not be able to perform appropriate service for the teacher.

mula_pali:
379. ‘‘Cuddasa kho panimānanda, pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Katamā cuddasa? Tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ paṭhamā pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Paccekasambuddhe paccekabuddhe (sī. pī.) dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ dutiyā pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Tathāgatasāvake arahante dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ tatiyā pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Arahattaphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ catutthī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Anāgāmissa dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ pañcamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ chaṭṭhī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Sakadāgāmissa dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ sattamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ aṭṭhamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Sotāpanne dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ navamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ dasamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Bāhirake kāmesu vītarāge dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ ekādasamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Puthujjanasīlavante dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ dvādasamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Puthujjanadussīle dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ terasamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā. Tiracchānagate dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ cuddasamī pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇāti.

‘‘Tatrānanda, tiracchānagate dānaṃ datvā sataguṇā dakkhiṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā, puthujjanadussīle dānaṃ datvā sahassaguṇā dakkhiṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā, puthujjanasīlavante dānaṃ datvā satasahassaguṇā dakkhiṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā, bāhirake kāmesu vītarāge dānaṃ datvā koṭisatasahassaguṇā dakkhiṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne dānaṃ datvā asaṅkheyyā appameyyā dakkhiṇā pāṭikaṅkhitabbā, ko pana vādo sotāpanne, ko pana vādo sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne, ko pana vādo sakadāgāmissa, ko pana vādo anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne, ko pana vādo anāgāmissa, ko pana vādo arahattaphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne, ko pana vādo arahante, ko pana vādo paccekasambuddhe, ko pana vādo tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe!
mula_english:
379. "There are fourteen kinds of personal offerings, Ānanda. Which fourteen? One gives a gift to the *Tathāgata*, the worthy one, the perfectly enlightened one; this is the first kind of personal offering (*pāṭipuggalikā dakkhiṇā*). One gives a gift to a *Pratyekabuddha*; this is the second kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to a worthy disciple of the *Tathāgata*; this is the third kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of worthiness (*arhat*); this is the fourth kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to a non-returner (*anāgāmin*); this is the fifth kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of non-return; this is the sixth kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to a once-returner (*sakadāgāmin*); this is the seventh kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of once-return; this is the eighth kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*); this is the ninth kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry; this is the tenth kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to one outside the Dispensation who is free from lust for sensual pleasures; this is the eleventh kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to a virtuous ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*); this is the twelfth kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to an immoral ordinary person; this is the thirteenth kind of personal offering. One gives a gift to an animal; this is the fourteenth kind of personal offering."

"Herein, Ānanda, by giving a gift to an animal, the offering may be expected to repay a hundredfold. By giving a gift to an immoral ordinary person, the offering may be expected to repay a thousandfold. By giving a gift to a virtuous ordinary person, the offering may be expected to repay a hundred-thousandfold. By giving a gift to one outside the Dispensation who is free from lust for sensual pleasures, the offering may be expected to repay a hundred-thousand times a hundred-thousandfold. By giving a gift to one who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the offering may be expected to repay incalculably, immeasurably. What need to mention a stream-enterer? What need to mention one who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of once-return? What need to mention a once-returner? What need to mention one who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of non-return? What need to mention a non-returner? What need to mention one who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of *arhatship*? What need to mention an *arhat*? What need to mention a *Pratyekabuddha*? What need to mention the *Tathāgata*, the worthy one, the perfectly enlightened one!"
commentary_pali:
379.Cuddasa kho panimāti kasmā ārabhi? Idaṃ suttaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ ārabbha samuṭṭhitaṃ. Ānandattheropi ‘‘paṭiggaṇhātu, bhante, bhagavā’’ti pāṭipuggalikadakkhiṇaṃyeva samādapeti, cuddasasu ca ṭhānesu dinnadānaṃ pāṭipuggalikaṃ nāma hotīti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Ayaṃ paṭhamāti ayaṃ dakkhiṇā guṇavasenapi paṭhamā jeṭṭhakavasenapi. Ayañhi paṭhamā aggā jeṭṭhikā, imissā dakkhiṇāya pamāṇaṃ nāma natthi. Dutiyatatiyāpi paramadakkhiṇāyeva, sesā paramadakkhiṇabhāvaṃ na pāpuṇanti. Bāhirake kāmesu vītarāgeti kammavādikiriyavādimhi lokiyapañcābhiññe. Puthujjanasīlavanteti puthujjanasīlavā nāma gosīladhātuko hoti, asaṭho amāyāvī paraṃ apīḷetvā dhammena samena kasiyā vā vaṇijjāya vā jīvikaṃ kappetā. Puthujjanadussīleti puthujjanadussīlā nāma kevaṭṭamacchabandhādayo paraṃ pīḷāya jīvikaṃ kappetā.

Idāni pāṭipuggalikadakkhiṇāya vipākaṃ paricchindanto tatrānandātiādimāha. Tattha tiracchānagateti yaṃ guṇavasena upakāravasena posanatthaṃ dinnaṃ, idaṃ na gahitaṃ. Yampi ālopaaḍḍhaālopamattaṃ dinnaṃ, tampi na gahitaṃ. Yaṃ pana sunakhasūkarakukkuṭakākādīsu yassa kassaci sampattassa phalaṃ paṭikaṅkhitvā yāvadatthaṃ dinnaṃ, idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘tiracchānagate dānaṃ datvā’’ti. Sataguṇāti satānisaṃsā. Pāṭikaṅkhitabbāti icchitabbā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ayaṃ dakkhiṇā āyusataṃ vaṇṇasataṃ sukhasataṃ balasataṃ paṭibhānasatanti pañca ānisaṃsasatāni deti, attabhāvasate āyuṃ deti, vaṇṇaṃ, sukhaṃ, balaṃ, paṭibhānaṃ deti, nipparitasaṃ karoti. Bhavasatepi vutte ayameva attho. Iminā upāyena sabbattha nayo netabbo.

tatrānandā tiracchānagate Sataguṇā Pāṭikaṅkhitabbā

Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanneti ettha heṭṭhimakoṭiyā tisaraṇaṃ gato upāsakopi sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno nāma, tasmiṃ dinnadānampi asaṅkhyeyyaṃ appameyyaṃ. Pañcasīle patiṭṭhitassa tato uttari mahapphalaṃ, dasasīle patiṭṭhitassa tato uttari, tadahupabbajitassa sāmaṇerassa tato uttari, upasampannabhikkhuno tato uttari, upasampannasseva vattasampannassa tato uttari, vipassakassa tato uttari, āraddhavipassakassa tato uttari, uttamakoṭiyā pana maggasamaṅgī sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno nāma. Etassa dinnadānaṃ tato uttari mahapphalameva.

Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne

Kiṃ pana maggasamaṅgissa sakkā dānaṃ dātunti? Āma sakkā. Āraddhavipassako hi pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisati, tassa gehadvāre ṭhitassa hatthato pattaṃ gahetvā khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ pakkhipanti. Tasmiṃ khaṇe bhikkhuno maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, idaṃ dānaṃ maggasamaṅgino dinnaṃ nāma hoti. Atha vā panesa āsanasālāya nisinno hoti, manussā gantvā patte khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ ṭhapenti, tasmiṃ khaṇe tassa maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, idampi dānaṃ maggasamaṅgino dinnaṃ nāma. Atha vā panassa vihāre vā āsanasālāya vā nisinnassa upāsakā pattaṃ ādāya attano gharaṃ gantvā khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ pakkhipanti, tasmiṃ khaṇe tassa maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, idampi dānaṃ maggasamaṅgino dinnaṃ nāma. Tattha soṇḍiyaṃ udakassa viya sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne dinnadānassa asaṅkhyeyyatā veditabbā. Tāsu tāsu mahānadīsu mahāsamudde ca udakassa viya sotāpannādīsu dinnadānassa uttaritaravasena asaṅkhyeyyatā veditabbā. Pathaviyā khayamaṇḍalamatte padese paṃsuṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva mahāpathaviyā paṃsuno appameyyatāyapi ayamattho dīpetabbo.
commentary_english:
379. “*Cuddasa kho panimā*”: Why was this begun? This *sutta* arose regarding individual offerings (pāṭipuggalikaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ).

Ānanda, the Elder, too, makes clear (samādapeti): “Accept [this], venerable sir, Blessed One (bhagavā)!” It is precisely an individual offering. It was begun in order to show (dassetuṃ) that a gift (dānaṃ) given (dinnaṃ) in fourteen (cuddasasu) places (ṭhānesu) is called (nāma) an individual offering (pāṭipuggalikaṃ).

"*Ayaṃ paṭhamā*": This offering is first, even by virtue of qualities (guṇavasenapi), and first by virtue of seniority (jeṭṭhakavasenapi).

Indeed (hi), this is the first (paṭhamā), the foremost (aggā), the most senior (jeṭṭhikā). There is no measure (pamāṇaṃ nāma natthi) to this offering (dakkhiṇāya).

The second and third, too, are the highest offerings (paramadakkhiṇāyeva). The remaining ones do not attain (na pāpuṇanti) the state (bhāvaṃ) of the highest offering (paramadakkhiṇabhāvaṃ).

"*Bāhirake kāmesu vītarāge*": among those who are passionless (vītarāge) regarding external (bāhirake) pleasures (kāmesu), in worldly (lokiya) fivefold higher knowledge (pañcābhiññe).

"*Puthujjanasīlavante*": A common person who is virtuous (puthujjanasīlavā) is so-called (nāma) because he possesses the qualities of good conduct (gosīladhātuko hoti), is not deceitful (asaṭho), is without trickery (amāyāvī), and, not harming (apīḷetvā) others (paraṃ), makes a living (jīvikaṃ kappetā) righteously (dhammena samena), either by farming (kasiyā vā) or by trade (vaṇijjāya vā).

"*Puthujjanadussīle*": Common persons who are unvirtuous (puthujjanadussīlā) are so-called (nāma) because they are those such as fishermen (kevaṭṭamacchabandhādayo), who make a living (jīvikaṃ kappetā) by harming (pīḷāya) others (paraṃ).

Now (idāni), while determining (paricchindanto) the result (vipākaṃ) of individual offerings (pāṭipuggalikadakkhiṇāya), he says (āha) "*tatrānandā*" and so forth (tiādimāha).

There (tattha), "*tiracchānagate*": What is given (dinnaṃ) to animals (tiracchānagate) by virtue of qualities (guṇavasena), by virtue of assistance (upakāravasena), for the purpose of nourishment (posanatthaṃ), that is not taken (idaṃ na gahitaṃ).

Even a mouthful (ālopa) or half-mouthful (aḍḍhaālopamattaṃ) that is given is not taken.

But (pana) what is given (dinnaṃ) to dogs (sunakha), pigs (sūkara), chickens (kukkuṭa), crows (kāka), and so on (ādīsu), expecting (paṭikaṅkhitvā) a result (phalaṃ) for the attainment (sampattassa) of whomever (yassa kassaci), according to one’s means (yāvadatthaṃ), referring to this (idaṃ sandhāya) it is said (vuttaṃ), “having given (datvā) a gift (dānaṃ) to animals (tiracchānagate).”
