"*Sataguṇā*": having a hundred (sata) advantages (ānisaṃsā).

"*Pāṭikaṅkhitabbā*": should be desired (icchitabbā).

This is said (idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti): This offering (ayaṃ dakkhiṇā) gives (deti) a hundredfold life (āyusataṃ), a hundredfold beauty (vaṇṇasataṃ), a hundredfold happiness (sukhasataṃ), a hundredfold strength (balasataṃ), a hundredfold wit (paṭibhānasatanti), these five hundredfold advantages (pañca ānisaṃsasatāni), and in a hundred existences (attabhāvasate) gives (deti) life (āyuṃ), beauty (vaṇṇaṃ), happiness (sukhaṃ), strength (balaṃ), wit (paṭibhānaṃ), [and] makes (karoti) [one] without troubles (nipparitasaṃ).

Even when said (vutte) about hundreds of existences (bhavasatepi) this is the very meaning (ayameva attho).

By this method (iminā upāyena) the principle (nayo) should be applied (netabbo) everywhere (sabbattha).

*Tatranandā, tiracchānagate, sataguṇā, pāṭikaṅkhitabbā.*

"*Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne*": Here (ettha), even (api) a lay follower (upāsako) who has gone (gato) to the three refuges (tisaraṇaṃ) at the lowest level (heṭṭhimakoṭiyā) is said (nāma) to have attained (paṭipanno) the realization (sacchikiriyāya) of the fruit (phala) of stream-entry (sotāpatti). In him (tasmiṃ), too, the gift (dinnadānampi) given (dinnaṃ) [is] countless (asaṅkhyeyyaṃ) [and] immeasurable (appameyyaṃ).

For one established (patiṭṭhitassa) in the five precepts (pañcasīle), there is great fruit (mahapphalaṃ), and further (uttari) for one established (patiṭṭhitassa) in the ten precepts (dasasīle), further (uttari) for a novice (sāmaṇerassa) who has gone forth (pabbajitassa) that very day (tadahupabbajitassa), further (uttari) for a monk (bhikkhuno) who has received the higher ordination (upasampanna), further (uttari) for one who has received the higher ordination (upasampannasseva) and is accomplished in observances (vattasampannassa), further (uttari) for an insight meditator (vipassakassa), further (uttari) for one who has begun insight meditation (āraddhavipassakassa), but (pana) for one endowed with the path (maggasamaṅgī) at the highest level (uttamakoṭiyā), it is said (nāma) to have attained (paṭipanno) the realization (sacchikiriyāya) of the fruit (phala) of stream-entry (sotāpatti).

The gift (dinnadānaṃ) given (dinnaṃ) to him (etassa) [has] even greater fruit (mahapphalameva).

"*Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanne*".

Is it (kiṃ pana) possible (sakkā) to give (dātuṃ) a gift (dānaṃ) to one endowed with the path (maggasamaṅgissa)? Yes (āma), it is possible (sakkā).

For (hi) one who has begun insight meditation (āraddhavipassako), taking (ādāya) his bowl and robe (pattacīvaram), enters (pavisati) a village (gāmaṃ) for alms (piṇḍāya), they place (pakkhipanti) edible and palatable food (khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ) into the bowl (pattaṃ) taken (gahetvā) from his hand (hatthato) of him (tassa) standing (ṭhitassa) at the doorway (gehadvāre).

At that moment (tasmiṃ khaṇe) there is an arising of the path (maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti) for the monk (bhikkhuno). This gift (idaṃ dānaṃ) is said (nāma hoti) to be given (dinnaṃ) to one endowed with the path (maggasamaṅgino).

Or (atha vā) he (panesa) sits (nisinno hoti) in the alms hall (āsanasālāya), people (manussā) go (gantvā) and place (ṭhapenti) edible and palatable food (khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ) in [his] bowl (patte), at that moment (tasmiṃ khaṇe) there is an arising of the path (maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti) for him (tassa). This gift (idampi dānaṃ) is said (nāma) to be given (dinnaṃ) to one endowed with the path (maggasamaṅgino).

Or (atha vā) lay followers (upāsakā), taking (ādāya) a bowl (pattaṃ), go (gantvā) to their own (attano) home (gharaṃ) and place (pakkhipanti) edible and palatable food (khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ) to him (panassa) sitting (nisinnassa) in the monastery (vihāre vā) or in the alms hall (āsanasālāya vā), at that moment (tasmiṃ khaṇe) there is an arising of the path (maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti) for him (tassa). This gift (idampi dānaṃ) is said (nāma) to be given (dinnaṃ) to one endowed with the path (maggasamaṅgino).

There (tattha), the countlessness (asaṅkhyeyyatā veditabbā) of the gift (dinnadānassa) given (dinnaṃ) to one who has attained (paṭipanne) the realization (sacchikiriyāya) of the fruit (phala) of stream-entry (sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya) [is] like (viya) water (udakassa) in a pool (soṇḍiyaṃ).

The ever-increasing (uttaritaravasena) countlessness (asaṅkhyeyyatā veditabbā) of the gift (dinnadānassa) given (dinnaṃ) to those such as stream-enterers (sotāpannaādīsu) [is] like (viya) water (udakassa) in those various (tāsu tāsu) great rivers (mahānadīsu) and in the great ocean (mahāsamudde ca).

Beginning (ādiṃ katvā) with a grain of sand (paṃsuṃ) in an area (padese) the size of a hoofprint (khayamaṇḍalamatte) on the earth (pathaviyā), this meaning (ayamattho) should be illuminated (dīpetabbo) even up to (yāva) the immeasurability (appameyyatāyapi) of the sand (paṃsuno) on the great earth (mahāpathaviyā).

mula_pali:
380. ‘‘Satta kho panimānanda, saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā. Katamā satta? Buddhappamukhe ubhatosaṅghe dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ paṭhamā saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā. Tathāgate parinibbute ubhatosaṅghe dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ dutiyā saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā. Bhikkhusaṅghe dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ tatiyā saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā. Bhikkhunisaṅghe dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ catutthī saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā. ‘Ettakā me bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca saṅghato uddissathā’ti dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ pañcamī saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā. ‘Ettakā me bhikkhū saṅghato uddissathā’ti dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ chaṭṭhī saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā. ‘Ettakā me bhikkhuniyo saṅghato uddissathā’ti dānaṃ deti – ayaṃ sattamī saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā.

‘‘Bhavissanti kho panānanda, anāgatamaddhānaṃ gotrabhuno kāsāvakaṇṭhā dussīlā pāpadhammā. Tesu dussīlesu saṅghaṃ uddissa dānaṃ dassanti. Tadāpāhaṃ, ānanda, saṅghagataṃ dakkhiṇaṃ asaṅkheyyaṃ appameyyaṃ vadāmi. Na tvevāhaṃ, ānanda, kenaci pariyāyena saṅghagatāya dakkhiṇāya pāṭipuggalikaṃ dānaṃ mahapphalataraṃ vadāmi.
mula_english:
“There are these seven kinds of offerings made to the Saṅgha, Ānanda. Which seven? One gives a gift to a Saṅgha of both *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunīs* headed by the Buddha; this is the first kind of offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā). One gives a gift to a Saṅgha of both *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunīs* after the *Tathāgata* has attained final *Nibbāna*; this is the second kind of offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā). One gives a gift to a Saṅgha of *bhikkhus*; this is the third kind of offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā). One gives a gift to a Saṅgha of *bhikkhunīs*; this is the fourth kind of offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā). One gives a gift, saying: ‘Appoint so many *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunīs* for me from the Saṅgha’; this is the fifth kind of offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā). One gives a gift, saying: ‘Appoint so many *bhikkhus* for me from the Saṅgha’; this is the sixth kind of offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā). One gives a gift, saying: ‘Appoint so many *bhikkhunīs* for me from the Saṅgha’; this is the seventh kind of offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā).

“However, Ānanda, in the future there will be clansmen with an ochre robe around their necks who are unvirtuous (dussīlā) and bad-natured (pāpadhammā). People will give gifts to those immoral persons for the sake of the Saṅgha. Even then, Ānanda, I say, an offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagataṃ dakkhiṇaṃ) is incalculable (asaṅkheyyaṃ), immeasurable (appameyyaṃ). And I say that in no way does a gift to a person individually (pāṭipuggalikaṃ dānaṃ) ever have greater fruit than an offering made to the Saṅgha (saṅghagatāya dakkhiṇāya).
commentary_pali:
380.Satta kho panimāti kasmā ārabhi? ‘‘Saṅghe gotami dehi, saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cā’’ti hi vuttaṃ, tattha sattasu ṭhānesu dinnadānaṃ saṅghe dinnaṃ nāma hotīti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha buddhappamukhe ubhatosaṅgheti ekato bhikkhusaṅgho, ekato bhikkhunisaṅgho, satthā majjhe nisinno hotīti ayaṃ buddhappamukho ubhatosaṅgho nāma. Ayaṃ paṭhamāti imāya dakkhiṇāya samappamāṇā dakkhiṇā nāma natthi. Dutiyadakkhiṇādayo pana etaṃ paramadakkhiṇaṃ na pāpuṇanti.

Kiṃ pana tathāgate parinibbute buddhappamukhassa ubhatosaṅghassa dānaṃ dātuṃ sakkāti? Sakkā. Kathaṃ? Ubhatosaṅghassa hi pamukhe sadhātukaṃ paṭimaṃ āsane ṭhapetvā ādhārakaṃ ṭhapetvā dakkhiṇodakaṃ ādiṃ katvā sabbaṃ satthu paṭhamaṃ datvā ubhatosaṅghassa dātabbaṃ, evaṃ buddhappamukhassa ubhatosaṅghassa dānaṃ dinnaṃ nāma hoti. Tattha yaṃ satthu dinnaṃ, taṃ kiṃ kātabbanti? Yo satthāraṃ paṭijaggati vattasampanno bhikkhu, tassa dātabbaṃ. Pitusantakañhi puttassa pāpuṇāti, bhikkhusaṅghassa dātumpi vaṭṭati, sappitelāni pana gahetvā dīpā jalitabbā, sāṭakaṃ gahetvā paṭākā āropetabbāti. Bhikkhusaṅgheti aparicchinnakamahābhikkhusaṅghe. Bhikkhunisaṅghepi eseva nayo.

Bhikkhusaṅghe

Gotrabhunoti gottamattakameva anubhavamānā, nāmamattasamaṇāti attho. Kāsāvakaṇṭhāti kāsāvakaṇṭhanāmakā. Te kira ekaṃ kāsāvakhaṇḍaṃ hatthe vā gīvāya vā bandhitvā vicarissanti . Gharadvāraṃ pana tesaṃ puttabhariyā kasivaṇijjādikammāni ca pākatikāneva bhavissanti. Tesu dussīlesu saṅghaṃ uddissa dānaṃ dassantīti ettha dussīlasaṅghanti na vuttaṃ. Saṅgho hi dussīlo nāma natthi. Dussīlā pana upāsakā tesu dussīlesu bhikkhusaṅghaṃ uddissa saṅghassa demāti dānaṃ dassanti. Iti bhagavatā buddhappamukhe saṅghe dinnadakkhiṇāpi guṇasaṅkhāya asaṅkhyeyyāti vuttaṃ. Kāsāvakaṇṭhasaṅghe dinnadakkhiṇāpi guṇasaṅkhāyeva asaṅkhyeyyāti vuttā. Saṅghagatā dakkhiṇā hi saṅghe cittīkāraṃ kātuṃ sakkontassa hoti, saṅghe pana cittīkāro dukkaro hoti.

Gotrabhuno Kāsāvakaṇṭhā Tesu dussīlesu saṅghaṃ uddissa dānaṃ dassantī

Yo hi saṅghagataṃ dakkhiṇaṃ dassāmīti deyyadhammaṃ paṭiyādetvā vihāraṃ gantvā, – ‘‘bhante, saṅghaṃ uddissa ekaṃ theraṃ dethā’’ti vadati, atha saṅghato sāmaṇeraṃ labhitvā ‘‘sāmaṇero me laddho’’ti aññathattaṃ āpajjati, tassa dakkhiṇā saṅghagatā na hoti. Mahātheraṃ labhitvāpi ‘‘mahāthero me laddho’’ti somanassaṃ uppādentassāpi na hotiyeva. Yo pana sāmaṇeraṃ vā upasampannaṃ vā daharaṃ vā theraṃ vā bālaṃ vā paṇḍitaṃ vā yaṃkiñci saṅghato labhitvā nibbematiko hutvā saṅghassa demīti saṅghe cittīkāraṃ kātuṃ sakkoti, tassa dakkhiṇā saṅghagatā nāma hoti. Parasamuddavāsino kira evaṃ karonti.

Tattha hi eko vihārasāmi kuṭumbiko ‘‘saṅghagataṃ dakkhiṇaṃ dassāmī’’ti saṅghato uddisitvā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ dethāti yāci. So ekaṃ dussīlabhikkhuṃ labhitvā nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ opuñjāpetvā āsanaṃ paññāpetvā upari vitānaṃ bandhitvā gandhadhūmapupphehi pūjetvā pāde dhovitvā telena makkhetvā buddhassa nipaccakāraṃ karonto viya saṅghe cittīkārena deyyadhammaṃ adāsi. So bhikkhu pacchābhattaṃ vihārajagganatthāya kudālakaṃ dethāti gharadvāraṃ āgato, upāsako nisinnova kudālaṃ pādena khipitvā ‘‘gaṇhā’’ti adāsi. Tamenaṃ manussā āhaṃsu – ‘‘tumhehi pātova etassa katasakkāro vattuṃ na sakkā, idāni upacāramattakampi natthi, kiṃ nāmeta’’nti. Upāsako – ‘‘saṅghassa so ayyā cittīkāro, na etassā’’ti āha. Kāsāvakaṇṭhasaṅghassa dinnadakkhiṇaṃ pana ko sodhetīti? Sāriputtamoggallānādayo asīti mahātherā sodhentīti. Apica therā ciraparinibbutā, there ādiṃ katvā yāvajja dharamānā khīṇāsavā sodhentiyeva.

Na tvevāhaṃ, ānanda, kenaci pariyāyena saṅghagatāya dakkhiṇāyāti ettha atthi buddhappamukho saṅgho, atthi etarahi saṅgho, atthi anāgate kāsāvakaṇṭhasaṅgho. Buddhappamukho saṅgho etarahi saṅghena na upanetabbo, etarahi saṅgho anāgate kāsāvakaṇṭhasaṅghena saddhiṃ na upanetabbo. Tena teneva samayena kathetabbaṃ. Saṅghato uddisitvā gahitasamaṇaputhujjano hi pāṭipuggaliko sotāpanno, saṅghe cittīkāraṃ kātuṃ sakkontassa puthujjanasamaṇe dinnaṃ mahapphalataraṃ. Uddisitvā gahito sotāpanno pāṭipuggaliko sakadāgāmītiādīsupi eseva nayo. Saṅghe cittīkāraṃ kātuṃ sakkontassa hi khīṇāsave dinnadānato uddisitvā gahite dussīlepi dinnaṃ mahapphalatarameva . Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ ‘‘sīlavato kho, mahārāja, dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, no tathā dussīle’’ti, taṃ imaṃ nayaṃ pahāya ‘‘catasso kho imānanda, dakkhiṇā visuddhiyo’’ti imasmiṃ catukke daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Na tvevāhaṃ ānanda, kenaci pariyāyena saṅghagatāya dakkhiṇāyā
commentary_english:
380. Why was “*satta kho panimā*” begun? “Give to the *saṃgha*, when it is given to the *saṃgha*, both I and the *saṃgha* will be honored,” it was said. There, in those seven places, in order to show that giving a gift is called giving to the *saṃgha*, this teaching was begun.

There, “*buddhappamukhe ubhatosaṅghe*” means the *bhikkhusaṃgha* on one side, the *bhikkhunisaṃgha* on one side, and the Teacher sitting in the middle—this is called *buddhappamukho ubhatosaṅgha*.

“*ayaṃ paṭhamā*” means there is no offering equal to this offering.

But the second offering and so on do not attain this highest offering.

Moreover, is it possible to give to the *dāna* to the *buddhappamukhe ubhatosaṅghassa* when the *tathāgata* has attained *parinibbāna*? It is possible.

How? Having placed a *sadhātukaṃ paṭimaṃ* at the head of the *ubhatosaṅghassa* on a seat, having placed a support, having made *dakkhiṇodakaṃ* etc. the beginning, having given everything to the Teacher first, it should be given to the *ubhatosaṅghassa*. In this way, giving to the *buddhappamukhassa ubhatosaṅghassa* is called giving.

There, what should be done with what was given to the Teacher? It should be given to the *bhikkhu* who attends to the Teacher and is accomplished in his duties.

For a son attains his father’s property, and it is fitting to give to the *bhikkhusaṃgha*. But having taken ghee and oil, lamps should be lit, and having taken cloth, banners should be raised.

"*bhikkhusaṅghe*” means in the unlimited great *bhikkhusaṅgha*.

The same rule applies to the *bhikkhunisaṅgha* too.

"*bhikkhusaṅghe*"

"*gotrabhuno*" means only experiencing lineage, the meaning is those who are only nominally *samaṇa*.

"*kāsāvakaṇṭhā*" means those who are called *kāsāvakaṇṭha*.

They, it is said, will wander about tying a piece of *kāsāva* cloth on their hand or neck.

Moreover, the sons, wives, farming, trade, and other occupations of those people will be just as they are naturally.

"*tesu dussīlesu saṅghaṃ uddissa dānaṃ dassantī*" means it is not said here that it is a *dussīlasaṅgha*.

For there is no such thing as an immoral *saṃgha*.

But immoral lay followers give a gift to the *bhikkhusaṃgha*, intending it for those immoral ones, saying, "We give to the *saṃgha*."

Thus, it was said by the Blessed One that even the *dakkhiṇa* given to the *buddhappamukhe saṅghe* is immeasurable in terms of its qualities.

It was said that even the *dakkhiṇa* given to the *kāsāvakaṇṭhasaṅghe* is immeasurable in terms of its qualities.

For the *dakkhiṇa* that goes to the *saṃgha* belongs to one who is able to make the *saṃgha* content, but it is difficult to make the *saṃgha* content.

"*gotrabhuno kāsāvakaṇṭhā*
*tesu dussīlesu saṅghaṃ uddissa dānaṃ dassantī*"

For if someone, intending to give a *dakkhiṇa* to the *saṃgha*, prepares a gift and goes to the *vihāra*, saying, “Venerable Sirs, give me a *thera* for the sake of the *saṃgha*,” and then, having obtained a *sāmaṇera* from the *saṃgha*, becomes changed, thinking, “I have obtained a *sāmaṇera*,” his *dakkhiṇa* does not go to the *saṃgha*.

Even if he obtains a *mahāthera*, it is not so if he only generates joy, thinking, “I have obtained a *mahāthera*.”

But if someone obtains a *sāmaṇera* or an *upasampanna* or a young *thera* or an old *thera* or a fool or a wise man, whatever it may be, from the *saṃgha*, and, being without doubt, is able to make the *saṃgha* content, thinking, “I give to the *saṃgha*,” his *dakkhiṇa* is called *saṃghagatā*.

It is said that those living across the ocean do thus.

There, it is said that a certain householder who was the owner of a *vihāra*, intending to give a *dakkhiṇa* to the *saṃgha*, requested from the *saṃgha*, saying, "Give me a *bhikkhu*."

Having obtained an immoral *bhikkhu*, having had the place where he was sitting swept, having prepared a seat, having put up a canopy above, having honored him with incense, smoke, and flowers, having washed his feet, having anointed him with oil, as if making obeisance to the Buddha, he gave the gift to the *saṃgha* with contentment.

That *bhikkhu*, having come to the doorway of the house after the meal, saying, "Give me a hoe for the sake of sweeping the *vihāra*," the lay follower, while sitting, kicked the hoe with his foot, saying, "Take it!" and gave it.

Then people said to him, "You were not able to pay homage to him in the morning, and now there is not even a little respect. What is this?"

The lay follower said, "That veneration is for the *saṃgha*, not for him."

But who purifies the *dinnadakkhiṇa* of the *kāsāvakaṇṭhasaṅghassa*? Sāriputta, Moggallāna, and the other eighty *mahātheras* purify it, it is said.
Moreover, the elders, long since completely passed away, having made a beginning there, purifying those whose āsavas are destroyed while they are still living.

However, I do not say, Ānanda, that a gift given to the Saṅgha in any way... Here, there is the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head, there is the Saṅgha at the present time, there is in the future the Saṅgha with ochre robes around their necks.

The Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head should not be brought near to the present Saṅgha; the present Saṅgha should not be brought near to the future Saṅgha with ochre robes around their necks.

It should be spoken at that very time.

Indeed, the individual who is a worldling, who, having been designated from the Saṅgha, has taken (ordination), is individually a stream-enterer; a gift given to a worldling ascetic who is able to make the Saṅgha mindful is more greatly fruitful.

The stream-enterer who, having been designated, has taken (ordination) is individually a once-returner; this is the principle also in the case of these and others.

Indeed, a gift given by one who is able to make the Saṅgha mindful to one whose āsavas are destroyed is more greatly fruitful than a gift given from a donation, even a gift given to one who is immoral, having been designated and taken (ordination).

But what was said, "Indeed, O great king, a gift given to one who is virtuous is greatly fruitful, not so to one who is immoral," that, having abandoned this principle, should be regarded in this tetrad: "Indeed, Ānanda, these are the four purities of donations."

However, I do not say, Ānanda, that a gift given to the Saṅgha in any way...

mula_pali:
381. ‘‘Catasso kho imā, ānanda, dakkhiṇā visuddhiyo. Katamā catasso? Atthānanda, dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati no paṭiggāhakato. Atthānanda, dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati no dāyakato. Atthānanda, dakkhiṇā neva dāyakato visujjhati no paṭiggāhakato. Atthānanda, dakkhiṇā dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca.

‘‘Kathañcānanda, dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati no paṭiggāhakato? Idhānanda, dāyako hoti sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo, paṭiggāhakā honti dussīlā pāpadhammā – evaṃ kho, ānanda, dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati no paṭiggāhakato.

‘‘Kathañcānanda, dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati no dāyakato? Idhānanda, dāyako hoti dussīlo pāpadhammo, paṭiggāhakā honti sīlavanto sīlavantā (sī.) kalyāṇadhammā – evaṃ kho, ānanda, dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati no dāyakato.

sīlavantā (sī.)

‘‘Kathañcānanda, dakkhiṇā neva dāyakato visujjhati no paṭiggāhakato? Idhānanda, dāyako ca hoti dussīlo pāpadhammo, paṭiggāhakā ca honti dussīlā pāpadhammā – evaṃ kho, ānanda, dakkhiṇā neva dāyakato visujjhati no paṭiggāhakato.

‘‘Kathañcānanda, dakkhiṇā dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca? Idhānanda, dāyako ca hoti sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo, paṭiggāhakā ca honti sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā – evaṃ kho, ānanda, dakkhiṇā dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca. Imā kho, ānanda, catasso dakkhiṇā visuddhiyo’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

382

‘‘Yo sīlavā dussīlesu dadāti dānaṃ,

Dhammena laddhaṃ laddhā (sī. pī.) supasannacitto;

laddhā (sī. pī.)

Abhisaddahaṃ kammaphalaṃ uḷāraṃ,

Sā dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati.

‘‘Yo dussīlo sīlavantesu dadāti dānaṃ,

Adhammena laddhaṃ appasannacitto;

Anabhisaddahaṃ kammaphalaṃ uḷāraṃ,

Sā dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati.

‘‘Yo dussīlo dussīlesu dadāti dānaṃ,

Adhammena laddhaṃ appasannacitto;

Anabhisaddahaṃ kammaphalaṃ uḷāraṃ,

Na taṃ dānaṃ vipulapphalanti brūmi.

‘‘Yo sīlavā sīlavantesu dadāti dānaṃ,

Dhammena laddhaṃ supasannacitto;

Abhisaddahaṃ kammaphalaṃ uḷāraṃ,

Taṃ ve dānaṃ vipulapphalanti brūmi sā dakkhiṇā nevubhato visujjhati (sī. pī.).

sā dakkhiṇā nevubhato visujjhati (sī. pī.)

‘‘Yo vītarāgo vītarāgesu dadāti dānaṃ,

Dhammena laddhaṃ supasannacitto;

Abhisaddahaṃ kammaphalaṃ uḷāraṃ,

Taṃ ve dānaṃ āmisadānānamagga’’ taṃ ve dānaṃ vipulanti brūmi (sī.) nti.

taṃ ve dānaṃ vipulanti brūmi (sī.)

Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dvādasamaṃ.

Vibhaṅgavaggo niṭṭhito catuttho.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Bhaddekānandakaccāna, lomasakaṅgiyāsubho;

Mahākammasaḷāyatanavibhaṅgā, uddesaaraṇā dhātu saccaṃ.

Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasuttanti.
mula_english:
381. There are these four kinds of purification of offering, Ānanda.

Which four? There is the offering, Ānanda, that is purified by the giver (dāyaka), not by the receiver (paṭiggāhaka).

There is the offering, Ānanda, that is purified by the receiver, not by the giver.

There is the offering, Ānanda, that is purified neither by the giver nor by the receiver.

There is the offering, Ānanda, that is purified both by the giver and by the receiver.

How is the offering, Ānanda, purified by the giver, not by the receiver? Here, Ānanda, the giver is virtuous (sīlavā), of good qualities (kalyāṇadhammo), and the receivers are immoral (dussīlā), of evil qualities (pāpadhammā). Thus, Ānanda, the offering is purified by the giver, not by the receiver.

How is the offering, Ānanda, purified by the receiver, not by the giver? Here, Ānanda, the giver is immoral, of evil qualities, and the receivers are virtuous, of good qualities. Thus, Ānanda, the offering is purified by the receiver, not by the giver.

How is the offering, Ānanda, purified neither by the giver nor by the receiver? Here, Ānanda, the giver is immoral and of evil qualities, and the receivers are also immoral and of evil qualities. Thus, Ānanda, the offering is purified neither by the giver nor by the receiver.

How is the offering, Ānanda, purified both by the giver and by the receiver? Here, Ānanda, the giver is virtuous and of good qualities, and the receivers are also virtuous and of good qualities. Thus, Ānanda, the offering is purified both by the giver and by the receiver.

These, Ānanda, are these four purifications of offerings.

Thus spoke the Blessed One (Bhagavā).

Having said this, the Well-Gone One (Sugato), the Teacher (Satthā), then spoke further:

382. When the virtuous (sīlavā) gives a gift (dānaṃ) to the immoral (dussīlesu),

Having obtained it righteously (dhammena laddhaṃ), with a very clear mind (supasannacitto);

Believing in an excellent result of action (kammaphalaṃ uḷāraṃ),

That offering is purified by the giver (dāyakato visujjhati).

When the immoral gives a gift to the virtuous,

Having obtained it unrighteously (adhammena laddhaṃ), with an unclear mind (appasannacitto);

Not believing in an excellent result of action,

That offering is purified by the receiver (paṭiggāhakato visujjhati).

When the immoral gives a gift to the immoral,

Having obtained it unrighteously, with an unclear mind;

Not believing in an excellent result of action,

That offering, I say, is not of great fruit (vipulapphalanti).

When the virtuous gives a gift to the virtuous,

Having obtained it righteously, with a very clear mind;

Believing in an excellent result of action,

That gift, I say, is of great fruit.

When one free from passion (vītarāgo) gives a gift to those free from passion (vītarāgesu),

Having obtained it righteously, with a very clear mind;

Believing in an excellent result of action,

That gift is the best of material gifts.
I declare that gift to be abundant.

The *Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasuttaṃ*, the twelfth, is finished.

The fourth *Vibhaṅgavaggo* is finished.

Its summary:

Bhaddeka, Ānanda, Kaccāna, Lomasakaṅgiya, Subho;

Mahākamma, Saḷāyatana *Vibhaṅgā*, Uddesa, Araṇā, Dhātu, Saccaṃ.

Thus ends the Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasuttaṃ.
commentary_pali:
381.Dāyakato visujjhatīti mahapphalabhāvena visujjhati, mahapphalā hotīti attho. Kalyāṇadhammoti sucidhammo, na pāpadhammo. Dāyakato visujjhatīti cettha vessantaramahārājā kathetabbo. So hi jūjakabrāhmaṇassa dārake datvā pathaviṃ kampesi.

Paṭiggāhakatovisujjhatīti ettha kalyāṇīnadīmukhadvāravāsikevaṭṭo kathetabbo. So kira dīghasomattherassa tikkhattumpi piṇḍapātaṃ datvā maraṇamañce nipanno ‘‘ayyassa maṃ dīghasomattherassa dinnapiṇḍapāto uddharatī’’ti āha.

Paṭiggāhakato visujjhatī

Neva dāyakatoti ettha vaḍḍhamānavāsiluddako kathetabbo. So kira petadakkhiṇaṃ dento ekassa dussīlasseva tayo vāre adāsi, tatiyavāre ‘‘amanusso dussīlo maṃ vilumpatī’’ti viravi, ekassa sīlavantabhikkhuno datvā pāpitakāleyevassa pāpuṇi.

Neva dāyakato

Dāyakato ceva visujjhatīti ettha asadisadānaṃ kathetabbaṃ.

Dāyakato ceva visujjhatī

Sā dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhatīti ettha yathā nāma cheko kassako asārampi khettaṃ labhitvā samaye kasitvā paṃsuṃ apanetvā sārabījāni patiṭṭhapetvā rattindivaṃ ārakkhe pamādaṃ anāpajjanto aññassa sārakhettato adhikataraṃ dhaññaṃ labhati, evaṃ sīlavā dussīlassa datvāpi phalaṃ mahantaṃ adhigacchatīti. Iminā upāyena sabbapadesu visujjhanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Sā dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhatī

Vītarāgo vītarāgesūti ettha vītarāgo nāma anāgāmī, arahā pana ekantavītarāgova, tasmā arahatā arahato dinnadānameva aggaṃ. Kasmā? Bhavālayassa bhavapatthanāya abhāvato. Nanu khīṇāsavo dānaphalaṃ na saddahatīti? Dānaphalaṃ saddahantā khīṇāsavasadisā na honti. Khīṇāsavena katakammaṃ pana nicchandarāgattā kusalaṃ vā akusalaṃ vā na hoti, kiriyaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati, tenevassa dānaṃ aggaṃ hotīti vadanti.

Vītarāgo vītarāgesū vītarāgo

Kiṃ pana sammāsambuddhena sāriputtattherassa dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, udāhu sāriputtattherena sammāsambuddhassa dinnanti. Sammāsambuddhena sāriputtattherassa dinnaṃ mahapphalanti vadanti. Sammāsambuddhañhi ṭhapetvā añño dānassa vipākaṃ jānituṃ samattho nāma natthi. Dānañhi catūhi sampadāhi dātuṃ sakkontassa tasmiṃyeva attabhāve vipākaṃ deti. Tatrimā sampadā – deyyadhammassa dhammena samena paraṃ apīḷetvā uppannatā, pubbacetanādivasena cetanāya mahattatā, khīṇāsavabhāvena guṇātirekatā, taṃdivasaṃ nirodhato vuṭṭhitabhāvena vatthusampannatāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Catutthavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
381. "Being purified by the giver" means being purified by having great fruit, meaning it is of great fruit.

"Auspicious Dhamma" means pure Dhamma, not evil Dhamma.

Regarding "Being purified by the giver," the great king Vessantara should be mentioned. Indeed, he, having given his children to the Jūjaka Brahmin, caused the earth to tremble.

Regarding "Being purified by the receiver," the fisherman residing at the mouth of the Kalyāṇī river should be mentioned. It is said that he, having given alms food to the elder Dīghasoma even three times, lying on his deathbed said, "May the alms food given by me to the elder Dīghasoma uplift me."

Regarding "Being purified by the receiver," Vaḍḍhamānavāsiluddako should be mentioned. It is said that while giving the *petadakkhiṇa*, he gave it to an immoral person three times. The third time, he cried out, "A non-human, immoral person is robbing me!" Having given it to a virtuous *bhikkhu*, it reached him at the very moment it was given.

Regarding "Not purified by the giver," the unparalleled gift should be mentioned.

Regarding "Being purified by the giver," just as a skillful farmer, having obtained even an unproductive field, plows it at the right time, removes the dust, plants the best seeds, and without neglecting protection day and night, obtains more grain than another from a productive field, likewise, a virtuous person, even having given to an immoral person, obtains great fruit. By this method, purification should be understood in all instances.

Regarding "The one without passion [giving] to those without passion," here, "one without passion" (*vītarāga*) means a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), but an *arhat* is entirely without passion; therefore, giving to an *arhat* by an *arhat* is the highest. Why? Because of the absence of a dwelling place of becoming, of a desire for becoming. Is it not true that a *khīṇāsava* does not believe in the fruit of giving? Those who believe in the fruit of giving are not like the *khīṇāsavas*. However, action done by a *khīṇāsava*, being without desire and passion, is neither wholesome nor unwholesome; it stands in the place of mere action (*kiriyaṭṭhāne*); therefore, they say that his giving is the highest.

But is the gift given by the Perfectly Awakened One to the elder Sāriputta of great fruit, or the gift given by the elder Sāriputta to the Perfectly Awakened One? They say the gift given by the Perfectly Awakened One to the elder Sāriputta is of great fruit. For, except for the Perfectly Awakened One, there is no other who is capable of knowing the result of giving. Indeed, giving gives its result in that very existence to one who is able to give with four kinds of accomplishment. Here are these accomplishments: the given object is acquired lawfully, equally, without oppressing others; the greatness of intention by way of preliminary intention, etc.; the excellence of qualities by way of being a *khīṇāsava*; and the perfection of the object by way of having arisen from cessation that very day.

*Papañcasūdanī*, commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

The explanation of the *Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasutta* is finished.

The explanation of the fourth *vagga* is finished.

mula_pali:
383. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi vandāhi evañca vadehi (sabbattha) aññasuttesu pana natthi – ‘anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Yena cāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandāhi vandāhi evañca vadehi (sabbattha) aññasuttesu pana natthi – ‘anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho so puriso anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’’ti. Yena cāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandati; evañca vadeti – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’’ti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhībhāvena.
mula_english:
383. Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

At that time, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder was ill, suffering, and seriously sick.

Then Anāthapiṇḍika the householder addressed a certain man: "Come, good man, go to the Blessed One; having gone there, pay homage to the Blessed One’s feet with your head in my name and say — ‘Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is ill, suffering, and seriously sick.

He pays homage to the Blessed One’s feet with his head.’

Then go to the venerable Sāriputta; having gone there, pay homage to the venerable Sāriputta’s feet with your head in my name and say — ‘Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is ill, suffering, and seriously sick.

He pays homage to the venerable Sāriputta’s feet with his head.’

And speak thus: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the venerable Sāriputta would visit Anāthapiṇḍika’s house out of compassion.’"

"So be it, venerable sir," that man replied to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder. Then he went to the Blessed One; having gone there, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down on one side.

Sitting on one side, that man said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is ill, suffering, and seriously sick.

He pays homage to the Blessed One’s feet with his head."

Then he went to the venerable Sāriputta; having gone there, he paid homage to the venerable Sāriputta and sat down on one side.

Sitting on one side, that man said to the venerable Sāriputta: "Venerable sir, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder is ill, suffering, and seriously sick.

He pays homage to the venerable Sāriputta’s feet with his head; and he speaks thus: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the venerable Sāriputta would visit Anāthapiṇḍika’s house out of compassion.’"

The venerable Sāriputta consented in silence.
commentary_pali: 383.Evaṃme sutanti anāthapiṇḍikovādasuttaṃ. Tattha bāḷhagilānoti adhimattagilāno maraṇaseyyaṃ upagato. Āmantesīti gahapatissa kira yāva pādā vahiṃsu, tāva divase sakiṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā tikkhattuṃ vā buddhupaṭṭhānaṃ akhaṇḍaṃ akāsi. Yattakañcassa satthu upaṭṭhānaṃ ahosi, tattakaṃyeva mahātherānaṃ. So ajja gamanapādassa pacchinnattā anuṭṭhānaseyyaṃ upagato sāsanaṃ pesetukāmo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi. Tenupasaṅkamīti bhagavantaṃ āpucchitvā sūriyatthaṅgamanavelāya upasaṅkami.
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard: the Anāthapiṇḍikovāda-sutta.

There, *bāḷhagilāno* means extremely ill, having approached the deathbed.

*Āmantesī*: It seems that as long as the householder's feet were working, he uninterruptedly attended upon the Buddha once, twice, or three times a day. As much as he attended upon the Teacher, so much he attended upon the great elders. Today, with his ability to walk cut off, having approached a bed where he cannot get up, wishing to send a message, he addressed a certain man.

*Tenupasaṅkamī*: Having taken leave of the Blessed One, he approached at sunset.

mula_pali:
384. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āyasmatā ānandena pacchāsamaṇena yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā sāriputto anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kacci te, gahapati, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci te dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no abhikkamo’’ti?

‘‘Na me, bhante sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bhante sāriputta, balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani muddhānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) abhimattheyya abhimantheyya (sī. pī.); evameva kho me, bhante sāriputta, adhimattā vātā muddhani ohananti (syā. kaṃ.) ūhananti adhimattā vātā sīlaṃ parikantanti (sī. syā. kaṃ.). Na me, bhante sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bhante sāriputta, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakhaṇḍena sīse sīsaveṭhaṃ dadeyya; evameva kho me, bhante sāriputta, adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā. Na me, bhante sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bhante sāriputta, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṃ parikanteyya; evameva kho me, bhante sāriputta, adhimattā vātā kucchiṃ parikantanti. Na me, bhante sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bhante sāriputta, dve balavanto purisā dubbalataraṃ purisaṃ nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuyā santāpeyyuṃ, samparitāpeyyuṃ; evameva kho me, bhante sāriputta, adhimatto kāyasmiṃ ḍāho. Na me, bhante sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo’’ti.

muddhānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) abhimantheyya (sī. pī.) ohananti (syā. kaṃ.) adhimattā vātā sīlaṃ parikantanti (sī. syā. kaṃ.)
mula_english:
Then the venerable Sāriputta, having dressed, taken his bowl and robe, went to the dwelling of Anāthapindika, the householder, with the venerable Ānanda as his attendant monk; having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.

Having sat down, the venerable Sāriputta said to Anāthapindika, the householder: "I hope, householder, you are comfortable; I hope you are well. I hope your painful feelings are subsiding and not increasing; that their subsiding is apparent, and not their increasing?"

"Venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable, I am not well. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, and not their subsiding. Just as if, venerable Sāriputta, a strong man were to crush my head with a sharp weapon; just so, venerable Sāriputta, are the excessive winds cutting through my head. Venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable, I am not well. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, and not their subsiding. Just as if, venerable Sāriputta, a strong man were tightening a turban around my head with a tough leather strap; just so, venerable Sāriputta, are the excessive pains in my head. Venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable, I am not well. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, and not their subsiding. Just as if, venerable Sāriputta, a skilled butcher or his apprentice were to carve up my stomach cavity with a sharp butcher's knife; just so, venerable Sāriputta, are the excessive winds carving up my stomach cavity. Venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable, I am not well. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, and not their subsiding. Just as if, venerable Sāriputta, two strong men, seizing a weaker man by his arms, were to warm him, scorch him, over a pit of hot embers; just so, venerable Sāriputta, is the excessive burning in my body. Venerable Sāriputta, I am not comfortable, I am not well. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, and not their subsiding."

commentary_pali:
384.Paṭikkamantīti osakkanti, tanukā bhavanti. Abhikkamantīti abhivaḍḍhanti ottharanti, balavatiyo honti.

Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no paṭikkamoti yasmiñhi samaye māraṇantikā vedanā uppajjati, uparivāte jalitaggi viya hoti, yāva usmā na pariyādiyati, tāva mahatāpi upakkamena na sakkā vūpasametuṃ, usmāya pana pariyādinnāya vūpasammati.

Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no paṭikkamo
commentary_english:
*Paṭikkamantī* means recede, become thin. *Abhikkamantī* means increase, spread, become strong.

*Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no paṭikkamo* means when a deadly pain arises, it is like a fire burning in the wind; until the heat is exhausted, it cannot be calmed even with great effort, but when the heat is exhausted, it subsides.

*Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no paṭikkamo*

mula_pali:
385. ‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na cakkhuṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me cakkhunissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na sotaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me sotanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na ghānaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me ghānanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na jivhaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me jivhānissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na kāyaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me kāyanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na manaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me manonissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na rūpaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me rūpanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na saddaṃ upādiyissāmi…pe… na gandhaṃ upādiyissāmi… na rasaṃ upādiyissāmi… na phoṭṭhabbaṃ upādiyissāmi… na dhammaṃ upādiyissāmi na ca me dhammanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na cakkhuviññāṇaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me cakkhuviññāṇanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na sotaviññāṇaṃ upādiyissāmi… na ghānaviññāṇaṃ upādiyissāmi… na jivhāviññāṇaṃ upādiyissāmi… na kāyaviññāṇaṃ upādiyissāmi… na manoviññāṇaṃ upādiyissāmi na ca me manoviññāṇanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na cakkhusamphassaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me cakkhusamphassanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na sotasamphassaṃ upādiyissāmi… na ghānasamphassaṃ upādiyissāmi… na jivhāsamphassaṃ upādiyissāmi… na kāyasamphassaṃ upādiyissāmi… na manosamphassaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me manosamphassanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na cakkhusamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me cakkhusamphassajāvedanānissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te , gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na sotasamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ upādiyissāmi… na ghānasamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ upādiyissāmi… na jivhāsamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ upādiyissāmi… na kāyasamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ upādiyissāmi… na manosamphassajaṃ vedanaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me manosamphassajāvedanānissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.
mula_english:
“Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the eye; my consciousness will not be dependent on the eye.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

“Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the ear; my consciousness will not be dependent on the ear.’ That’s how you should train yourself. Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the nose; my consciousness will not be dependent on the nose.’ That’s how you should train yourself. Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the tongue; my consciousness will not be dependent on the tongue.’ That’s how you should train yourself. Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the body; my consciousness will not be dependent on the body.’ That’s how you should train yourself. Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the intellect; my consciousness will not be dependent on the intellect.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

“Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to forms; my consciousness will not be dependent on forms.’ That’s how you should train yourself. Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to sound…pe… I won’t cling to smell… I won’t cling to taste… I won’t cling to tactile sensations… I won’t cling to ideas; my consciousness will not be dependent on ideas.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

“Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to eye-consciousness; my consciousness will not be dependent on eye-consciousness.’ That’s how you should train yourself. Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to ear-consciousness… I won’t cling to nose-consciousness… I won’t cling to tongue-consciousness… I won’t cling to body-consciousness… I won’t cling to intellect-consciousness; my consciousness will not be dependent on intellect-consciousness.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

“Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to contact at the eye; my consciousness will not be dependent on contact at the eye.’ That’s how you should train yourself. Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to contact at the ear… I won’t cling to contact at the nose… I won’t cling to contact at the tongue… I won’t cling to contact at the body… I won’t cling to contact at the intellect; my consciousness will not be dependent on contact at the intellect.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

“Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to feeling born of contact at the eye; my consciousness will not be dependent on feeling born of contact at the eye.’ That’s how you should train yourself. Then, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to feeling born of contact at the ear… I won’t cling to feeling born of contact at the nose… I won’t cling to feeling born of contact at the tongue… I won’t cling to feeling born of contact at the body… I won’t cling to feeling born of contact at the intellect; my consciousness will not be dependent on feeling born of contact at the intellect.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

commentary_pali: 385. Athāyasmā sāriputto cintesi – ‘‘ayaṃ mahāseṭṭhissa vedanā māraṇantikā, na sakkā paṭibāhituṃ, avasesā kathā niratthakā, dhammakathamassa kathessāmī’’ti. Atha naṃ taṃ kathento tasmātihātiādimāha. Tattha tasmāti yasmā cakkhuṃ tīhi gāhehi gaṇhanto uppannaṃ māraṇantikaṃ vedanaṃ paṭibāhituṃ samattho nāma natthi, tasmā. Na cakkhuṃ upādiyissāmīti cakkhuṃ tīhi gāhehi na gaṇhissāmi. Na ca me cakkhunissitaṃ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāpi me cakkhunissitaṃ na bhavissati. Na rūpanti heṭṭhā āyatanarūpaṃ kathitaṃ, imasmiṃ ṭhāne sabbampi kāmabhavarūpaṃ kathento evamāha.
commentary_english:
Then venerable Śāriputta thought: "This great merchant's feeling is deadly, it is not possible to ward it off. The remaining talk is meaningless. I will speak the *dharma*-talk to him."

Then, while telling that to him, he spoke beginning with "<hi rend="bold">tasmātihā</hi>".

There, "<hi rend="bold">tasmā</hi>": Because while seizing the eye with three grasps, there is no one who is able to ward off the deadly feeling that has arisen, therefore.

"<hi rend="bold">Na cakkhuṃ upādiyissāmī</hi>": I will not take up the eye. <pb ed="v" n="4. 0240"/> I will not seize the eye with three grasps.

"<hi rend="bold">Na ca me cakkhunissitaṃ viññāṇa</hi>": And there will not be consciousness dependent on the eye for me.

"<hi rend="bold">Na rūpa</hi>": Form. Below, the sense-sphere form has been spoken of. In this place, while speaking of all form of the world of desire and existence, he said thus.

mula_pali:
386. ‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na pathavīdhātuṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me pathavīdhātunissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na āpodhātuṃ upādiyissāmi… na tejodhātuṃ upādiyissāmi… na vāyodhātuṃ upādiyissāmi… na ākāsadhātuṃ upādiyissāmi… na viññāṇadhātuṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me viññāṇadhātunissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na rūpaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me rūpanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na vedanaṃ upādiyissāmi… na saññaṃ upādiyissāmi… na saṅkhāre upādiyissāmi… na viññāṇaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me viññāṇanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upādiyissāmi , na ca me ākāsānañcāyatananissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti . Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upādiyissāmi… na ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upādiyissāmi… na nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upādiyissāmi na ca me nevasaññānāsaññāyatananissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ.

‘‘Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na idhalokaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me idhalokanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘na paralokaṃ upādiyissāmi, na ca me paralokanissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabbaṃ. Tasmātiha te, gahapati, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘yampi me diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anupariyesitaṃ anucaritaṃ manasā tampi na upādiyissāmi, na ca me taṃnissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evañhi te, gahapati, sikkhitabba’’nti.
mula_english:
386. “Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the earth property (*pathavīdhātu*), and my consciousness will not be dependent on the earth property.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the water property (*āpodhātu*)… I won’t cling to the fire property (*tejodhātu*)… I won’t cling to the air property (*vāyodhātu*)… I won’t cling to the space property (*ākāsadhātu*)… I won’t cling to the consciousness property (*viññāṇadhātu*); my consciousness will not be dependent on the consciousness property.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

“Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to forms (*rūpa*), and my consciousness will not be dependent on forms.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to feeling (*vedanā*)… perception (*sañña*)… thought-fabrications (*saṅkhāra*)… consciousness (*viññāṇa*); my consciousness will not be dependent on consciousness.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

“Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the dimension of the infinitude of space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*), and my consciousness will not be dependent on the dimension of the infinitude of space.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*)… I won’t cling to the dimension of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*)… I won’t cling to the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*); my consciousness will not be dependent on the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

“Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to this world (*idhaloka*); my consciousness will not be dependent on this world.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to the world beyond (*paraloka*); my consciousness will not be dependent on the world beyond.’ That’s how you should train yourself.

Therefore, householder, you should train yourself in this way: ‘I won’t cling to what is seen (*diṭṭhaṃ*), heard (*sutaṃ*), sensed (*mutaṃ*), cognized (*viññātaṃ*), attained (*pattaṃ*), sought after (*pariyesitaṃ*), pondered by the intellect (*anupariyesitaṃ anucaritaṃ manasā*); my consciousness will not be dependent on that.’ That’s how you should train yourself.”
commentary_pali: 386.Na idhalokanti vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vā ghāsacchādanaṃ vā na upādiyissāmīti attho. Idañhi paccayesu aparitassanatthaṃ kathitaṃ. Na paralokanti ettha pana manussalokaṃ ṭhapetvā sesā paralokā nāma. Idaṃ – ‘‘asukadevaloke nibbattitvā asukaṭṭhāne bhavissāmi, idaṃ nāma khādissāmi bhuñjissāmi nivāsessāmi pārupissāmī’’ti evarūpāya paritassanāya pahānatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tampi na upādiyissāmi, na ca me tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ bhavissatīti evaṃ tīhi gāhehi parimocetvā thero desanaṃ arahattanikūṭena niṭṭhapesi.
commentary_english:
386.
"Not in this world" means clothing and dwelling, or food and covering. The meaning is, "I will not take [these things]."

This was said to not be anxious about conditions.

"Not in the next world" here, having established the human world, the remaining ones are called next worlds.

This is said to abandon the anxiety of this form: "Having been born in such and such a heaven, I will be in such and such a place; I will eat, consume, dwell, and wear such and such a thing."

"I will not take even that, and my consciousness will not depend on that." Thus, having liberated [him] with three stanzas, the elder completed the teaching with the perfection of an *arhat* (arhattva).

mula_pali:
387. Evaṃ vutte, anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati parodi, assūni pavattesi. Atha kho āyasmā ānando anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘olīyasi kho tvaṃ, gahapati, saṃsīdasi kho tvaṃ, gahapatī’’ti? ‘‘Nāhaṃ, bhante ānanda, olīyāmi, napi saṃsīdāmi; api ca me dīgharattaṃ satthā payirupāsito manobhāvanīyā ca bhikkhū; na ca me evarūpī dhammī kathā sutapubbā’’ti. ‘‘Na kho, gahapati, gihīnaṃ odātavasanānaṃ evarūpī dhammī kathā paṭibhāti; pabbajitānaṃ kho, gahapati, evarūpī dhammī kathā paṭibhātī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, bhante sāriputta, gihīnampi odātavasanānaṃ evarūpī dhammī kathā paṭibhātu. Santi hi, bhante, kulaputtā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti; bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro’’ti.

Atha kho āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca ānando anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ iminā ovādena ovaditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati, acirapakkante āyasmante ca sāriputte āyasmante ca ānande , kālamakāsi tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapajji. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘Idañhi taṃ jetavanaṃ, isisaṅghanisevitaṃ;

Āvutthaṃ dhammarājena, pītisañjananaṃ mama.

‘‘Kammaṃ vijjā ca dhammo ca, sīlaṃ jīvitamuttamaṃ;

Etena maccā sujjhanti, na gottena dhanena vā.

‘‘Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso, sampassaṃ atthamattano;

Yoniso vicine dhammaṃ, evaṃ tattha visujjhati.

‘‘Sāriputtova paññāya, sīlena upasamena;

Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu, etāvaparamo siyā’’ti.

Idamavoca anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto. Samanuñño satthā ahosi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto – ‘‘samanuñño me satthā’’ti bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
mula_english:
When this was said, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder wept and shed tears.

Then the venerable Ānanda said to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder: “Householder, are you despondent? Householder, are you sinking down?”

“No, venerable Ānanda, I am not despondent, nor am I sinking down; but I have waited on the Teacher for a long time, and also on the bhikkhus who are delightful to the mind; and such a talk on the Dhamma as this has never been heard by me before.”

“This sort of talk on the Dhamma, householder, is not given to lay people clad in white. This sort of talk on the Dhamma is given to those gone forth.”

“In that case, Ven. Sāriputta, please let this sort of talk on the Dhamma be given to lay people clad in white. There are clansmen with little dust in their eyes who are wasting away through not hearing this Dhamma. There will be those who will understand it.”

Then Ven. Sāriputta and Ven. Ānanda, having given this instruction to Anāthapiṇḍika the householder, got up from their seats and left.

Then, not long after the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Ānanda had left, Anāthapiṇḍika the householder died and was reborn in the Tusita heaven.

Then Anāthapiṇḍika the deva’s son, in the far extreme of the night, his extreme radiance lighting up the entirety of Jeta’s Grove (Jetavana), went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, bowed down to him and stood to one side.

Standing to one side, Anāthapiṇḍika the deva’s son addressed the Blessed One in verses:

“This truly is that Jetavana, frequented by the communities of seers;

It has been dwelt in by the Dhamma-king, a generator of joy for me.

“Deed, knowledge, Dhamma, virtue, and the most excellent life:

Mortals are purified by this, not by clan nor by wealth.

“Therefore, a wise person, seeing his own good,

Should investigate the Dhamma methodically; in that way one is purified there.

“Sāriputta is foremost in wisdom, in virtue, and in peacefulness;

Any monk who has gone beyond, at best can only equal him.”

That is what Anāthapiṇḍika the deva’s son said. The Teacher approved. Then Anāthapiṇḍika the deva’s son, knowing, “The Teacher has approved of me,” bowed down to the Blessed One, circled him three times, keeping him to his right, and then disappeared right there.
commentary_pali:
387.Olīyasīti attano sampattiṃ disvā ārammaṇesu bajjhasi allīyasīti. Iti āyasmā ānando – ‘‘ayampi nāma gahapati evaṃ saddho pasanno maraṇabhayassa bhāyati, añño ko na bhāyissatī’’ti maññamāno tassa gāḷhaṃ katvā ovādaṃ dento evamāha. Na ca me evarūpī dhammīkathā sutapubbāti ayaṃ upāsako – ‘‘satthu santikāpi me evarūpī dhammakathā na sutapubbā’’ti vadati, kiṃ satthā evarūpi sukhumaṃ gambhīrakathaṃ na kathetīti? No na katheti. Evaṃ pana cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni cha bāhirāni cha viññāṇakāye cha phassakāye cha vedanākāye cha dhātuyo pañcakkhandhe cattāro arūpe idhalokañca paralokañca dassetvā diṭṭhasutamutaviññātavasena arahatte pakkhipitvā kathitakathā etena na sutapubbā, tasmā evaṃ vadati.

Apicāyaṃ upāsako dānādhimutto dānābhirato buddhānaṃ santikaṃ gacchanto tucchahattho na gatapubbo. Purebhattaṃ gacchanto yāgukhajjakādīni gāhāpetvā gacchati, pacchābhattaṃ sappimadhuphāṇitādīni. Tasmiṃ asati vālikaṃ gāhāpetvā gandhakuṭipariveṇe okirāpeti, dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ rakkhitvā gehaṃ gato. Bodhisattagatiko kiresa upāsako, tasmā bhagavā catuvīsati saṃvaccharāni upāsakassa yebhuyyena dānakathameva kathesi – ‘‘upāsaka, idaṃ dānaṃ nāma bodhisattānaṃ gatamaggo, mayhampi gatamaggo, mayā satasahassakappādhikāni cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni dānaṃ dinnaṃ, tvaṃ mayā gatamaggameva anugacchasī’’ti. Dhammasenāpatiādayo mahāsāvakāpi attano attano santikaṃ āgatakāle dānakathamevassa kathenti. Tenevāha na kho gahapati gihīnaṃ odātavasanānaṃ evarūpī dhammīkathā paṭibhātīti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – gahapati gihīnaṃ nāma khettavatthuhiraññasuvaṇṇadāsīdāsaputtabhariyādīsu tibbo ālayo tibbaṃ nikantipariyuṭṭhānaṃ , tesaṃ – ‘‘ettha ālayo na kātabbo, nikanti na kātabbā’’ti kathā na paṭibhāti na ruccatīti.

na kho gahapati gihīnaṃ odātavasanānaṃ evarūpī dhammīkathā paṭibhātī

Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamīti kasmā upasaṅkami? Tusitabhavane kirassa nibbattamattasseva tigāvutappamāṇaṃ suvaṇṇakkhandhaṃ viya vijjotamānaṃ attabhāvaṃ uyyānavimānādisampattiñca disvā – ‘‘mahatī ayaṃ mayhaṃ sampatti, kiṃ nu kho me manussapathe kammaṃ kata’’nti olokento tīsu ratanesu adhikāraṃ disvā cintesi ‘‘pamādaṭṭhānamidaṃ devattaṃ nāma, imāya hi me sampattiyā modamānassa satisammosopi siyā, handāhaṃ gantvā mama jetavanassa ceva bhikkhusaṅghassa ca tathāgatassa ca ariyamaggassa ca sāriputtattherassa ca vaṇṇaṃ kathetvā tato āgantvā sampattiṃ anubhavissāmī’’ti. So tathā akāsi. Taṃ dassetuṃ atha kho anāthapiṇḍikotiādi vuttaṃ.

Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamī atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko

Tattha isisaṅghanisevitanti bhikkhusaṅghanisevitaṃ. Evaṃ paṭhamagāthāya jetavanassa vaṇṇaṃ kathetvā idāni ariyamaggassa vaṇṇaṃ kathento kammaṃ vijjā cātiādimāha. Tattha kammanti maggacetanā. Vijjāti maggapaññā. Dhammoti samādhipakkhiko dhammo. Sīlaṃ jīvitamuttamanti sīle patiṭṭhitassa jīvitaṃ uttamanti dasseti. Atha vā vijjāti diṭṭhisaṅkappo. Dhammoti vāyāmasatisamādhayo. Sīlanti vācākammantājīvā. Jīvitamuttamanti etasmiṃ sīle patiṭṭhitassa jīvitaṃ nāma uttamaṃ. Etena maccā sujjhantīti etena aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena sattā visujjhanti.

isisaṅghanisevita kammaṃ vijjā cā kamma Vijjā Dhammo Sīlaṃ jīvitamuttama vijjā Dhammo Sīla Jīvitamuttama Etena maccā sujjhantī

Tasmāti yasmā maggena sujjhanti, na gottadhanehi, tasmā. Yoniso vicine dhammanti upāyena samādhipakkhiyaṃ dhammaṃ vicineyya. Evaṃ tattha visujjhatīti evaṃ tasmiṃ ariyamagge visujjhati . Atha vā yoniso vicine dhammanti upāyena pañcakkhandhadhammaṃ vicineyya. Evaṃ tattha visujjhatīti evaṃ tesu catūsu saccesu visujjhati.

Tasmā Yoniso vicine dhamma Evaṃ tattha visujjhatī yoniso vicine dhamma Evaṃ tattha visujjhatī

Idāni sāriputtattherassa vaṇṇaṃ kathento sāriputto vātiādimāha. Tattha sāriputto vāti avadhāraṇavacanaṃ. Etehi paññādīhi sāriputtova seyyoti vadati. Upasamenāti kilesaupasamena. Pāraṅgatoti nibbānaṃ gato. Yo koci nibbānaṃ patto bhikkhu, so etāvaparamo siyā, na therena uttaritaro nāma atthīti vadati. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

sāriputto vā sāriputto vā Upasamenā Pāraṅgato

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Anāthapiṇḍikovādasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
387. "Because of being attached," [means:] seeing one’s own prosperity, you are bound and cling to sense objects.

Thus spoke the venerable Ānanda: “This householder, though faithful and devoted, is afraid of death. Who else would not be afraid?” Thinking this, he gave him firm encouragement and spoke as follows.

"Never have I heard such a *dharma* talk!" This lay follower [says:] "Never have I heard such a *dharma* talk even from the Teacher himself!" Why doesn't the Teacher give such a subtle, profound talk?" No, he does give it.

Thus, these six internal sense bases, six external ones, six aggregates of consciousness, six aggregates of contact, six aggregates of feeling, six elements, five aggregates, four immaterial [spheres], this world and the next, having shown [all these] and having placed [them] in the state of *arhat* through insight, learning, experience and knowledge, the words spoken by this [Ānanda] have never been heard before. Therefore, he speaks thus.

Moreover, this lay follower, being intent on giving and delighting in giving, when going to the presence of the Buddhas, never went empty-handed.

When going for the forenoon meal, he would have rice gruel, cakes, and so on, brought along; and for the afternoon meal, ghee, honey, molasses, and so on.

If those were not available, he would have sand brought and spread around the monastery's perfumed chamber, and having given *dāna*, kept the precepts, and gone home.

It seems this lay follower was destined to become a *bodhisattva*. Therefore, the Blessed One for twenty-four years mainly talked to the lay follower only about *dāna*, saying, “Lay follower, this giving is called the path gone by the *bodhisattvas*, the path gone by me as well. I have given *dāna* for four incalculable *asaṃkhyeyyas*, plus hundreds of thousands of *kappas*. You are indeed following the same path gone by me.”

Dharma-senapati and other great disciples also, when they came to his presence, would talk to him only about *dāna*.

Therefore he said: "It is not that such a *dharma* talk occurs to householders wearing white clothes."

This means: Householders have intense attachment and clinging to fields, property, gold, silver, male and female servants, sons, wives, and so on. For them, talk about, "Attachment should not be made here, clinging should not be made," neither occurs nor pleases them.

Why did he approach the Blessed One, [as in the phrase,] "Where the Blessed One was, there he approached"? While in the Tuṣita heaven, as soon as he was born, seeing his own essence, shining like a mountain of gold measuring three *gāvutas*, and the abundance of gardens, celestial mansions, and so on, [he thought,] “Great is this prosperity of mine. What good *karma* did I do on the human plane?” Looking about, seeing [his] authority over the three jewels, he thought, “This state of being a god is a place of negligence. For even while I am enjoying this prosperity, there could be a loss of mindfulness. Come now, I will go, and having spoken the praises of my Jetavana and of the community of monks and of the *tathāgata* and of the noble path (*āryamārga*) and of the elder Śāriputta, I will return from there and experience prosperity."

He did so.

To show that, [the words,] "Then, Anāthapiṇḍika," and so on, were spoken.

"Haunted by the *ṛṣi* community" means haunted by the monk community.

Thus, having spoken the praises of Jetavana in the first verse, now, while speaking the praises of the noble path, he said, "Action and knowledge," and so on.

There, "*Karma*" means the intention of the path.

"*Knowledge*" means the wisdom of the path.

"*Dharma*" means the *dharma* that is on the side of *samādhi*.

"*Moral conduct is the highest life*" means it shows that life is highest for one established in moral conduct.

Or else, "*Knowledge*" means right thought.

"*Dharma*" means effort, mindfulness, and *samādhi*.

"*Moral conduct*" means speech, actions, and livelihood.

"*The highest life*" means life is indeed highest for one established in that moral conduct.

"*By this, mortals are purified*" means by this eightfold path, beings are purified.

"*Therefore,*" because they are purified by the path, not by lineage or wealth, therefore.

"*He should investigate the *dharma* wisely*" means he should investigate the *dharma* on the side of *samādhi* by means of skillful devices (*upāya*).

"*Thus he is purified there*" means thus he is purified in that noble path (*āryamārga*).

Or else, "*He should investigate the *dharma* wisely*" means he should investigate the *dharma* of the five aggregates by means of skillful devices (*upāya*).

"*Thus he is purified there*" means thus he is purified in those four noble truths (*satya*).
Therefore, carefully examine the *dhamma*; thus, one is purified there. Carefully examine the *dhamma*; thus, one is purified there.

Now, while describing the virtues of the Elder Sāriputta, he said, beginning with "*Sāriputto vā*." There, "*Sāriputto vā*" is a term of emphasis. By these [qualities] such as wisdom, he says that Sāriputta is the best. "*Upasamenā*" means by the pacification of defilements (*kilesaupasamena*). "*Pāraṅgato*" means gone to *Nibbāna* (*nibbānaṃ gato*). Whatever *bhikkhu* has attained *Nibbāna*, he would be supreme to this extent; there is no one superior to the Elder, so he says. The rest is clear throughout.

*Sāriputto vā*, *Sāriputto vā*, *upasamenā*, *pāraṅgato*.

The commentary on the *Anāthapiṇḍikovāda Sutta* is finished in the *Papañcasūdanī*, the commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

mula_pali:
388. Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘imaṃ, bhikkhave, rattiṃ aññataro devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho so devaputto maṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘Idañhi taṃ jetavanaṃ, isisaṅghanisevitaṃ;

Āvutthaṃ dhammarājena, pītisañjananaṃ mama.

‘‘Kammaṃ vijjā ca dhammo ca, sīlaṃ jīvitamuttamaṃ;

Etena maccā sujjhanti, na gottena dhanena vā.

‘‘Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso, sampassaṃ atthamattano;

Yoniso vicine dhammaṃ, evaṃ tattha visujjhati.

‘‘Sāriputtova paññāya, sīlena upasamena;

Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu, etāvaparamo siyā’’ti.

‘‘Idamavoca , bhikkhave, so devaputto. ‘Samanuñño me satthā’ti maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘so hi nūna so, bhante, anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto bhavissati. Anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati āyasmante sāriputte abhippasanno ahosī’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu, sādhu, ānanda! Yāvatakaṃ kho, ānanda, takkāya pattabbaṃ, anuppattaṃ taṃ tayā. Anāthapiṇḍiko so, ānanda, devaputto’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Anāthapiṇḍikovādasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
388. Then, as the night passed, the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks, as the night was ending, a certain *devaputta*, his radiant beauty lighting up the entirety of Jeta's Grove (Jetavana), approached me; having approached, he paid homage to me and stood to one side. Standing to one side, that *devaputta* addressed me in verses:

“This Jeta's Grove is indeed inhabited by the assembly of seers;

It is resided in by the king of the Dharma (dharma), a generator of joy for me.

"Action (karma), knowledge (*vidyā*), and the Dharma, and morality (śīla), are the supreme way of life;

By these mortals are purified, not by lineage (*gotra*) or wealth (*dhana*).

“Therefore, a wise person, seeing what is beneficial for oneself,

Should carefully investigate the Dharma; thus, one is purified there.

"Even Sāriputta, with wisdom (prajñā), morality (śīla), and tranquility (*upaśama*);

Whatever monk has gone to the beyond, may be supreme only to this extent."

“That is what the *devaputta* said, monks. Thinking, ‘The Teacher approves of me,’ he paid homage to me, circumambulated me, and then vanished right there.”

When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Surely, venerable sir, that must have been Anāthapiṇḍika the *devaputta*. Anāthapiṇḍika, venerable sir, the householder, had great faith in the venerable Sāriputta.”

“Good, good, Ānanda! Ānanda, you have attained as far as can be attained by reasoning. That *devaputta* was Anāthapiṇḍika.”

This is what the Blessed One said. The venerable Ānanda, pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

The Anāthapiṇḍikovāda Sutta is finished, the first.

mula_pali:
389. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahācundo āyasmā ca channo gijjhakūṭe pabbate viharanti. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā channo ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahācundo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahācundaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘āyāmāvuso cunda, yenāyasmā channo tenupasaṅkamissāma gilānapucchakā’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho āyasmā mahācundo āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosi.

Atha kho āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahācundo yenāyasmā channo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā channena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ channaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kacci te, āvuso channa, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci te dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no abhikkamo’’ti?

‘‘Na me, āvuso sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi , āvuso sāriputta, balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani abhimattheyya; evameva kho me, āvuso sāriputta, adhimattā vātā muddhani ūhananti. Na me, āvuso sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, āvuso sāriputta, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakkhaṇḍena sīse sīsaveṭhaṃ dadeyya; evameva kho me, āvuso sāriputta, adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā. Na me, āvuso sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, āvuso sāriputta, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṃ parikanteyya; evameva kho me, āvuso sāriputta, adhimattā vātā kucchiṃ parikantanti. Na me, āvuso sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, āvuso sāriputta, dve balavanto purisā dubbalataraṃ purisaṃ nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuyā santāpeyyuṃ samparitāpeyyuṃ; evameva kho me, āvuso sāriputta, adhimatto kāyasmiṃ ḍāho. Na me, āvuso sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Satthaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, āharissāmi, nāvakaṅkhāmi jīvita’’nti.
mula_english:
THUS HAVE I HEARD. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

Now on that occasion the venerable Sāriputta, the venerable Mahā Cunda, and the venerable Channa were living on the mountain Vulture Peak.

On that occasion the venerable Channa was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.

Then, when it was evening, the venerable Sāriputta rose from meditation, went to the venerable Mahā Cunda, and said to him: “Friend Cunda, let us go to the venerable Channa and ask about his illness.”

- “Yes, friend,” the venerable Maha Cunda replied.

Then the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Mahā Cunda went to the venerable Channa and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, they sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, the venerable Sāriputta said to the venerable Channa: “I trust, friend Channa, that things are bearable for you. I trust that things are comfortable for you. I trust that your painful feelings are subsiding, not increasing; that there are signs of their subsiding, and not of their increasing?”

“Friend Sāriputta, I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My severe pains are increasing, not lessening. There are signs of their increasing, and not of their lessening. Just as if a strong man were crushing my head with the tip of a sharp sword, so too, violent winds cut through my head. I am not getting well, friend Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My severe pains are increasing, not lessening. There are signs of their increasing, and not of their lessening. Just as if a strong man were tightening a tough leather strap around my head as a headband, so too, there are violent pains in my head. I am not getting well, friend Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My severe pains are increasing, not lessening. There are signs of their increasing, and not of their lessening. Just as if a skilled butcher or his apprentice were to carve up an ox’s belly with a sharp butcher’s knife, so too, violent winds are carving up my belly. I am not getting well, friend Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My severe pains are increasing, not lessening. There are signs of their increasing, and not of their lessening. Just as if two strong men were to seize a weaker man by the arms and roast and broil him over a charcoal pit, so too, there is an excessive fever inside my body. I am not getting well, friend Sāriputta, I am not comfortable. My severe pains are increasing, not lessening. There are signs of their increasing, and not of their lessening. I shall use the knife, friend Sāriputta; I have no desire to live.”
commentary_pali: 389.Evaṃme sutanti channovādasuttaṃ. Tattha channoti evaṃnāmako thero, na abhinikkhamanaṃ nikkhantatthero. Paṭisallānāti phalasamāpattito. Gilānapucchakāti gilānupaṭṭhānaṃ nāma buddhavaṇṇitaṃ, tasmā evamāha. Satthanti jīvitahārakasatthaṃ. Nāvakaṅkhāmīti icchāmi.
commentary_english:
389.
Thus, "me suta" is the Channovādasutta.

There, "channo" means a *thera* of such a name, not an *abhinikkhamana nikkhantatthera*.

"Paṭisallānā" means from the attainment of fruition (*phalasamāpatti*).

"Gilānapucchakā" means tending to the sick (*gilānupaṭṭhāna*), which is praised by the Buddha, therefore he spoke thus.

"Sattha" means a weapon that takes life (*jīvitahārakasatthaṃ*).

"Nāvakaṅkhāmī" means I desire (*icchāmi*).

mula_pali:
390. ‘‘Māyasmā channo satthaṃ āharesi. Yāpetāyasmā channo. Yāpentaṃ mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ channaṃ icchāma. Sace āyasmato channassa natthi sappāyāni bhojanāni, ahaṃ āyasmato channassa sappāyāni bhojanāni pariyesissāmi. Sace āyasmato channassa natthi sappāyāni bhesajjāni, ahaṃ āyasmato channassa sappāyāni bhesajjāni pariyesissāmi. Sace āyasmato channassa natthi patirūpā upaṭṭhākā, ahaṃ āyasmantaṃ channaṃ upaṭṭhahissāmi. Māyasmā channo satthaṃ āharesi. Yāpetāyasmā channo. Yāpentaṃ mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ channaṃ icchāmā’’ti.

‘‘Napi me, āvuso sāriputta, natthi sappāyāni bhojanāni; napi me natthi sappāyāni bhesajjāni; napi me natthi patirūpā upaṭṭhākā; api cāvuso sāriputta , pariciṇṇo me satthā dīgharattaṃ manāpeneva no amanāpena. Etañhi, āvuso sāriputta, sāvakassa patirūpaṃ yaṃ satthāraṃ paricareyya manāpeneva no amanāpena. ‘Anupavajjaṃ channo bhikkhu satthaṃ āharissatī’ti evametaṃ evameva kho tvaṃ (ka.), āvuso sāriputta, dhārehī’’ti. ‘‘Puccheyyāma mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ channaṃ kañcideva desaṃ, sace āyasmā channo okāsaṃ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā’’ti. ‘‘Pucchāvuso sāriputta, sutvā vedissāmī’’ti.

evameva kho tvaṃ (ka.)
mula_english:
390. Let the venerable Channa not use the knife.
Let the venerable Channa live.
We want the venerable Channa to live.
If the venerable Channa lacks suitable food, I will go in search of suitable food for him.
If the venerable Channa lacks suitable medicine, I will go in search of suitable medicine for him.
If he lacks a proper attendant, I will attend on the venerable Channa.
Let the venerable Channa not use the knife.
Let the venerable Channa live.
We want the venerable Channa to live.

Furthermore, friend Śāriputra, it is not that I have no suitable food; nor is it that I have no suitable medicine; nor is it that I have no proper attendant; but rather, friend Śāriputra, the Teacher has long been worshipped by me with love, not without love.
But rather, friend Śāriputra, it is proper for the disciple to worship the Teacher with love, not without love.
'The faultless monk Channa will use the knife', remember this, friend Śāriputra."
"We might ask the venerable Channa some question, if the venerable Channa makes an opportunity for an explanation of the question."
“Ask, friend Śāriputra, when I have heard, I shall know.”
commentary_pali: 390.Anupavajjanti anuppattikaṃ appaṭisandhikaṃ.
commentary_english: " *anupavajja* means without rebirth, without renewed existence."

mula_pali:
391. ‘‘Cakkhuṃ, āvuso channa, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasi? Sotaṃ, āvuso channa, sotaviññāṇaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ, āvuso channa, ghānaviññāṇaṃ… jivhaṃ, āvuso channa, jivhāviññāṇaṃ … kāyaṃ, āvuso channa, kāyaviññāṇaṃ… manaṃ, āvuso channa, manoviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasī’’ti?

‘‘Cakkhuṃ, āvuso sāriputta, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmi. Sotaṃ, āvuso sāriputta…pe… ghānaṃ, āvuso sāriputta… jivhaṃ, āvuso sāriputta… kāyaṃ, āvuso sāriputta… manaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, manoviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
"Friend Channa, do you regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and things cognizable by eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”
Friend Channa, the ear, ear-consciousness…the nose, nose-consciousness…the tongue, tongue-consciousness…the body, body-consciousness…the mind, mind-consciousness, and things cognizable by the mind through mind-consciousness: do you regard them thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“Friend Sariputta, I regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and things cognizable by eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’
Friend Sariputta, the ear…the nose…the tongue…the body…the mind, mind-consciousness, and things cognizable by the mind through mind-consciousness: I regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’“
commentary_pali: 391.Etaṃ mamātiādīni taṇhāmānadiṭṭhigāhavasena vuttāni. Nirodhaṃ disvāti khayavayaṃ ñatvā. Netaṃ mama nesohamasmi na meso attāti samanupassāmīti aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti samanupassāmi.
commentary_english:
This, and so forth, beginning with "<hi rend="bold">This is mine</hi>," are spoken due to craving, pride, views, and grasping.

"<hi rend="bold">Having seen cessation</hi>" means having known destruction and disappearance.

"<hi rend="bold">This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self</hi>," thus contemplating impermanence (*anitya*), suffering (*duḥkha*), and selflessness (*anātman*), I contemplate.

mula_pali:
