And when its arising & falling away are discerned, it would follow that ‘My self arises & falls away.'
That’s why it wouldn’t be tenable if anyone were to say, ‘The intellect is the self.’
So the intellect is not-self.

‘‘‘If anyone were to say, ‘Ideas are the self,’ that wouldn’t be tenable.
The arising & falling away of ideas are discerned.
And when its arising & falling away are discerned, it would follow that ‘My self arises & falls away.'
That’s why it wouldn’t be tenable if anyone were to say, ‘Ideas are the self.’
Thus the intellect is not-self and ideas are not-self.

If anyone were to say, ‘Consciousness at the intellect is the self,’ that wouldn’t be tenable…
The arising & falling away of consciousness at the intellect are discerned.
And when its arising & falling away are discerned, it would follow that ‘My self arises & falls away.
’ That’s why it wouldn’t be tenable if anyone were to say, ‘Consciousness at the intellect is the self.’
Thus the intellect is not-self, ideas are not-self, consciousness at the intellect is not-self.

If anyone were to say, ‘Contact at the intellect is the self,’ that wouldn’t be tenable…
The arising & falling away of contact at the intellect are discerned.
And when its arising & falling away are discerned, it would follow that ‘My self arises & falls away.
’ That’s why it wouldn’t be tenable if anyone were to say, ‘Contact at the intellect is the self.’
Thus the intellect is not-self, ideas are not-self, consciousness at the intellect is not-self, contact at the intellect is not-self.

If anyone were to say, ‘Feeling is the self,’ that wouldn’t be tenable…
The arising & falling away of feeling are discerned.
And when its arising & falling away are discerned, it would follow that ‘My self arises & falls away.
’ That’s why it wouldn’t be tenable if anyone were to say, ‘Feeling is the self.’
Thus the intellect is not-self, ideas are not-self, consciousness at the intellect is not-self, contact at the intellect is not-self, feeling is not self.

If anyone were to say, ‘Craving is the self,’ that wouldn’t be tenable…
The arising & falling away of craving are discerned.
And when its arising & falling away are discerned, it would follow that ‘My self arises & falls away.
’ That’s why it wouldn’t be tenable if anyone were to say, ‘Craving is the self.’
’ Thus the intellect is not-self, ideas are not-self, consciousness at the intellect is not-self, contact at the intellect is not-self, feeling is not self, craving is not-self.
[p.]

mula_pali:
424. ‘‘Ayaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkāyasamudayagāminī paṭipadā – cakkhuṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati; rūpe ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati; cakkhuviññāṇaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati; cakkhusamphassaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati; vedanaṃ ‘etaṃ mama , esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati; taṇhaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati; sotaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati…pe… ghānaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati…pe… jivhaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati…pe… kāyaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati…pe… manaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati, dhamme ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati, manoviññāṇaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati, manosamphassaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati, vedanaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati, taṇhaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati.

‘‘Ayaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā – cakkhuṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Rūpe ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Cakkhusamphassaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Vedanaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Taṇhaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Sotaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati…pe… ghānaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati… jivhaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati… kāyaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati… manaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Manoviññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Manosamphassaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Vedanaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Taṇhaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati.
mula_english:
424. Bhikkhus, this is the practice that leads to the arising of self-identification ( *sakkāyasamudayagāminī paṭipadā*): The eye (*cakkhuṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Form (*rūpe*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Eye-consciousness (*cakkhuviññāṇaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Eye-contact (*cakkhusamphassaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Feeling (*vedanaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Craving (*taṇhaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. The ear (*sotaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’…and so on… The nose (*ghānaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’…and so on… The tongue (*jivhaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’…and so on… The body (*kāyaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’…and so on… The mind (*manaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Ideas (*dhamme*) are regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Mind-consciousness (*manoviññāṇaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Mind-contact (*manosamphassaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Feeling (*vedanaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Craving (*taṇhaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is mine ( *etaṃ mama*), this I am (*esohamasmi*), this is my self (*eso me attā’ti samanupassati*)’.

Bhikkhus, this is the practice that leads to the cessation of self-identification (*sakkāyanirodhagāminī paṭipadā*): The eye (*cakkhuṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Form (*rūpe*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Eye-consciousness (*cakkhuviññāṇaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Eye-contact (*cakkhusamphassaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Feeling (*vedanaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Craving (*taṇhaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. The ear (*sotaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’…and so on… The nose (*ghānaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’…and so on… The tongue (*jivhaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’…and so on… The body (*kāyaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’…and so on… The mind (*manaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Ideas (*dhamme*) are regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Mind-consciousness (*manoviññāṇaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Mind-contact (*manosamphassaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Feeling (*vedanaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’. Craving (*taṇhaṃ*) is regarded thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti samanupassati*)’.
commentary_pali:
424.Ayaṃ kho pana, bhikkhaveti ayampi pāṭiyekko anusandhi. Ayañhi desanā tiṇṇaṃ gāhānaṃ vasena vaṭṭaṃ dassetuṃ āraddhā. Dukkhaṃ samudayoti dvinnaṃ saccānaṃ vasena vaṭṭaṃ dassetuntipi vadantiyeva. Etaṃ mamātiādīsu taṇhāmānadiṭṭhigāhāva veditabbā. Samanupassatīti gāhattayavasena passati.

Evaṃ vaṭṭaṃ dassetvā idāni tiṇṇaṃ gāhānaṃ paṭipakkhavasena, nirodho maggoti imesaṃ vā dvinnaṃ saccānaṃ vasena vivaṭṭaṃ dassetuṃ ayaṃ kho panātiādimāha. Netaṃ mamātiādīni taṇhādīnaṃ paṭisedhavacanāni. Samanupassatīti aniccaṃ dukkhamanattāti passati.

ayaṃ kho panā Netaṃ mamā
commentary_english:
424.
“*Ayaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave*” means this is a unique connection.
Indeed, this teaching (*desanā*) is begun in order to show the round of existence (*vaṭṭaṃ*) by way of the three grasps (*tiṇṇaṃ gāhānaṃ vasena*).
"*Dukkhaṃ samudayoti*" means that they speak of showing the round of existence (*vaṭṭaṃ*) by way of the two truths (*dvinnaṃ saccānaṃ vasena*), suffering (*dukkhaṃ*) and origin (*samudaya*).
"*Etaṃ mamā*"- and so on, should be understood as grasping for craving (*taṇhā*), conceit (*māna*), and views (*diṭṭhi*).
"*Samanupassatī*" means he sees by way of the three grasps (*gāhattayavasena passati*).

Having thus shown the round of existence (*vaṭṭaṃ dassetvā*), now, in order to show the unfolding (*vivaṭṭaṃ dassetuṃ*) by way of the opposition to the three grasps (*tiṇṇaṃ gāhānaṃ paṭipakkhavasena*), that is, cessation (*nirodho*) and the path (*maggo*), or by way of these two truths (*dvinnaṃ saccānaṃ vasena*), he says "*ayaṃ kho panā*," and so on.
"*Netaṃ mamā*"- and so on, [are] words of rejection of craving (*taṇhā*) and so on (*paṭisedhavacanāni*).
"*Samanupassatī*" means he sees impermanence (*aniccaṃ*), suffering (*dukkhaṃ*), and no-self (*anattā*).

"*Ayaṃ kho panā*," "*netaṃ mamā*."

mula_pali:
425. ‘‘Cakkhuñca, bhikkhave, paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso, phassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā. So sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa rāgānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno socati kilamati paridevati urattāḷiṃ kandati sammohaṃ āpajjati. Tassa paṭighānusayo anuseti. Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno tassā vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tassa avijjānusayo anuseti. So vata, bhikkhave, sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayaṃ appahāya dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayaṃ appaṭivinodetvā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayaṃ asamūhanitvā avijjaṃ appahāya vijjaṃ anuppādetvā diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro bhavissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

‘‘Sotañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇaṃ…pe… ghānañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca gandhe ca uppajjati ghānaviññāṇaṃ…pe… jivhañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca phoṭṭhabbe ca uppajjati kāyaviññāṇaṃ…pe… manañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso, phassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā. So sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa rāgānusayo anuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno socati kilamati paridevati urattāḷiṃ kandati sammohaṃ āpajjati. Tassa paṭighānusayo anuseti. Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno tassā vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tassa avijjānusayo anuseti. So vata, bhikkhave, sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayaṃ appahāya dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayaṃ appaṭivinodetvā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayaṃ asamūhanitvā avijjaṃ appahāya vijjaṃ anuppādetvā diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro bhavissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.
mula_english:
425. "Monks, dependent on the eye (*cakṣu*) and forms (*rūpa*), visual consciousness (*cakṣuviññāṇaṃ*) arises; the meeting of the three is contact (*phasso*), and dependent on contact arises feeling (*vedayitaṃ*) whether pleasant (*sukhaṃ*) or painful (*dukkhaṃ*) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*).

If, when touched by a feeling of pleasure (*sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho*), one relishes it (*abhinandati*), welcomes it (*abhivadati*), or remains fastened to it (*ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati*), then one’s passion-obsession (*rāgānusayo*) gets obsessed (*anuseti*).

If, when touched by a feeling of pain (*dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno*), one sorrows (*socati*), is weary (*kilamati*), laments (*paridevati*), beats one’s breast (*urattāḷiṃ*), cries (*kandati*), and falls into confusion (*sammohaṃ āpajjati*), then one’s resistance-obsession (*paṭighānusayo*) gets obsessed (*anuseti*).

If, when touched by a feeling of neither pleasure nor pain (*adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno*), one does not discern (*nappajānāti*), as it actually is present (*yathābhūtaṃ*), the origination (*samudayañca*), passing away (*atthaṅgamañca*), allure (*assādañca*), drawback (*ādīnavañca*), or escape (*nissaraṇañca*) from that feeling (*tassā vedanāya*), then one’s ignorance-obsession (*avijjānusayo*) gets obsessed (*anuseti*).

Monks, that a person—without abandoning passion-obsession (*rāgānusayaṃ appahāya*) with regard to a feeling of pleasure (*sukhāya vedanāya*), without abolishing resistance-obsession (*paṭighānusayaṃ appaṭivinodetvā*) with regard to a feeling of pain (*dukkhāya vedanāya*), without uprooting ignorance-obsession (*avijjānusayaṃ asamūhanitvā*) with regard to a feeling of neither pleasure nor pain (*adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya*), without abandoning ignorance (*avijjaṃ appahāya*) and giving rise to clear knowing (*vijjaṃ anuppādetvā*)—would put an end to suffering & stress (*dukkhassantakaro bhavissati*) in the here & now (*diṭṭheva dhamme*): Such a thing isn’t possible (*netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati*)."

"Monks, dependent on the ear (*sotañca*) and sounds (*sadde*), ear-consciousness (*sotaviññāṇaṃ*) arises…pe… Monks, dependent on the nose (*ghānañca*) and odors (*gandhe*), nose-consciousness (*ghānaviññāṇaṃ*) arises…pe… Monks, dependent on the tongue (*jivhañca*) and tastes (*rase*), tongue-consciousness (*jivhāviññāṇaṃ*) arises…pe… Monks, dependent on the body (*kāyañca*) and tactile objects (*phoṭṭhabbe*), body-consciousness (*kāyaviññāṇaṃ*) arises…pe… Monks, dependent on the mind (*manañca*) and ideas (*dhamme*), mind-consciousness (*manoviññāṇaṃ*) arises; the meeting of the three is contact (*phasso*), and dependent on contact arises feeling (*vedayitaṃ*) whether pleasant (*sukhaṃ*) or painful (*dukkhaṃ*) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant (*adukkhamasukhaṃ*).

If, when touched by a feeling of pleasure (*sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho*), one relishes it (*abhinandati*), welcomes it (*abhivadati*), or remains fastened to it (*ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati*), then one’s passion-obsession (*rāgānusayo*) gets obsessed (*anuseti*).

If, when touched by a feeling of pain (*dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno*), one sorrows (*socati*), is weary (*kilamati*), laments (*paridevati*), beats one’s breast (*urattāḷiṃ*), cries (*kandati*), and falls into confusion (*sammohaṃ āpajjati*), then one’s resistance-obsession (*paṭighānusayo*) gets obsessed (*anuseti*).

If, when touched by a feeling of neither pleasure nor pain (*adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno*), one does not discern (*nappajānāti*), as it actually is present (*yathābhūtaṃ*), the origination (*samudayañca*), passing away (*atthaṅgamañca*), allure (*assādañca*), drawback (*ādīnavañca*), or escape (*nissaraṇañca*) from that feeling (*tassā vedanāya*), then one’s ignorance-obsession (*avijjānusayo*) gets obsessed (*anuseti*).

Monks, that a person—without abandoning passion-obsession (*rāgānusayaṃ appahāya*) with regard to a feeling of pleasure (*sukhāya vedanāya*), without abolishing resistance-obsession (*paṭighānusayaṃ appaṭivinodetvā*) with regard to a feeling of pain (*dukkhāya vedanāya*), without uprooting ignorance-obsession (*avijjānusayaṃ asamūhanitvā*) with regard to a feeling of neither pleasure nor pain (*adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya*), without abandoning ignorance (*avijjaṃ appahāya*) and giving rise to clear knowing (*vijjaṃ anuppādetvā*)—would put an end to suffering & stress (*dukkhassantakaro bhavissati*) in the here & now (*diṭṭheva dhamme*): Such a thing isn’t possible (*netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati*).
commentary_pali: 425. Evaṃ vivaṭṭaṃ dassetvā idāni tiṇṇaṃ anusayānaṃ vasena puna vaṭṭaṃ dassetuṃ cakkhuñca, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Tattha abhinandatītiādīni taṇhādiṭṭhivaseneva vuttāni. Anusetīti appahīno hoti. Dukkhassāti vaṭṭadukkhakilesadukkhassa.
commentary_english: 425. Having shown thus the unfolding ( *vivaṭṭaṃ dassetvā*), now, in order to show again the round (of rebirth) by way of the three proclivities (*anusaya*), he says, “*Cakkhuñca, bhikkhave*” etc. There, "*abhinandatī*" etc. are stated only in terms of craving (*taṇhā*) and views (*diṭṭhi*). "*Anusetī*" means it is not abandoned (*appahīno hoti*). "*Dukkhassā*" means of the round of suffering (*vaṭṭadukkha*) and the suffering of defilements (*kilesadukkha*).

mula_pali:
426. ‘‘Cakkhuñca , bhikkhave, paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso, phassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā. So sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa rāgānusayo nānuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na socati na kilamati paridevati na urattāḷiṃ kandati na sammohaṃ āpajjati. Tassa paṭighānusayo nānuseti. Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno tassā vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa avijjānusayo nānuseti. So vata, bhikkhave, sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayaṃ pahāya dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayaṃ paṭivinodetvā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayaṃ samūhanitvā avijjaṃ pahāya vijjaṃ uppādetvā diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro bhavissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

‘‘Sotañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca sadde ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇaṃ…pe….

‘‘Ghānañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca gandhe ca uppajjati ghānaviññāṇaṃ…pe….

‘‘Jivhañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇaṃ…pe… .

‘‘Kāyañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca phoṭṭhabbe ca uppajjati kāyaviññāṇaṃ…pe….

‘‘Manañca, bhikkhave, paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso, phassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā. So sukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa rāgānusayo nānuseti. Dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na socati na kilamati na paridevati na urattāḷiṃ kandati na sammohaṃ āpajjati. Tassa paṭighānusayo nānuseti. Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno tassā vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa avijjānusayo nānuseti. So vata, bhikkhave, sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayaṃ pahāya dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayaṃ paṭivinodetvā adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayaṃ samūhanitvā avijjaṃ pahāya vijjaṃ uppādetvā diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhassantakaro bhavissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.
mula_english:
426. "Monks, dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; conditioned by contact, there arises feeling, be it pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

When touched by a pleasant feeling, one does not delight in it, welcome it, or remain attached to it. One's underlying tendency to passion does not lie within.

When touched by a painful feeling, one does not grieve, lament, or despair; one does not beat one's breast and become distraught. One's underlying tendency to aversion does not lie within.

When touched by a feeling that is neither pleasant nor painful, one understands as it really is the arising, passing away, allure, danger, and escape from that feeling. One's underlying tendency to ignorance does not lie within.

Monks, it is indeed possible that a person, having abandoned the underlying tendency to passion for pleasant feeling, having eliminated the underlying tendency to aversion for painful feeling, having uprooted the underlying tendency to ignorance for neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling, having abandoned ignorance and generated knowledge, will put an end to suffering in this very life."

"Monks, dependent on the ear and sounds, ear-consciousness arises...pe...".

"Monks, dependent on the nose and smells, nose-consciousness arises...pe...".

"Monks, dependent on the tongue and tastes, tongue-consciousness arises...pe...".

"Monks, dependent on the body and tactile objects, body-consciousness arises...pe...".

"Monks, dependent on the mind and mental objects, mind-consciousness arises; the meeting of the three is contact; conditioned by contact, there arises feeling, be it pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

When touched by a pleasant feeling, one does not delight in it, welcome it, or remain attached to it. One's underlying tendency to passion does not lie within.

When touched by a painful feeling, one does not grieve, lament, or despair; one does not beat one's breast and become distraught. One's underlying tendency to aversion does not lie within.

When touched by a feeling that is neither pleasant nor painful, one understands as it really is the arising, passing away, allure, danger, and escape from that feeling. One's underlying tendency to ignorance does not lie within.

Monks, it is indeed possible that a person, having abandoned the underlying tendency to passion for pleasant feeling, having eliminated the underlying tendency to aversion for painful feeling, having uprooted the underlying tendency to ignorance for neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling, having abandoned ignorance and generated knowledge, will put an end to suffering in this very life."
commentary_pali: 426. Evaṃ tiṇṇaṃ anusayānaṃ vasena vaṭṭaṃ kathetvā idāni tesaṃ paṭikkhepavasena vivaṭṭaṃ dassento puna cakkhuñcātiādimāha. Avijjaṃ pahāyāti vaṭṭamūlikaṃ avijjaṃ pajahitvā. Vijjanti arahattamaggavijjaṃ uppādetvā.
commentary_english:
Thus, having spoken of the cycle (vaṭṭaṃ) in terms of the three latent tendencies (tiṇṇaṃ anusayānaṃ vasena), now, showing the reversal (vivaṭṭaṃ) in terms of their rejection (paṭikkhepavasena), he says again, beginning with "the eye" (cakkhuñcātiādimāha).

"Having abandoned ignorance (avijjaṃ pahāyā)," means having abandoned ignorance (avijjaṃ pajahitvā) which is the root of the cycle (vaṭṭamūlikaṃ).

"Knowledge (vijja)," means having produced the knowledge of the path of Arhatship (arahattamaggavijjaṃ uppādetvā).

mula_pali:
427. ‘‘Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmiṃ cakkhusmimpi (syā. kaṃ.) evamitaresupi nibbindati, rūpesu nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇe nibbindati, cakkhusamphasse nibbindati, vedanāya nibbindati, taṇhāya nibbindati. Sotasmiṃ nibbindati, saddesu nibbindati…pe… ghānasmiṃ nibbindati, gandhesu nibbindati… jivhāya nibbindati, rasesu nibbindati… kāyasmiṃ nibbindati, phoṭṭhabbesu nibbindati… manasmiṃ nibbindati, dhammesu nibbindati, manoviññāṇe nibbindati, manosamphasse nibbindati, vedanāya nibbindati, taṇhāya nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati , virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti. Imasmiṃ kho pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne saṭṭhimattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsūti.

Chachakkasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
“Seeing thus, bhikkhus, a well-instructed noble disciple grows disenchanted with the eye ( *cakkhusmiṃ nibbindati*), disenchanted with forms (*rūpesu nibbindati*), disenchanted with visual consciousness (*cakkhuviññāṇe nibbindati*), disenchanted with visual contact (*cakkhusamphasse nibbindati*), disenchanted with feeling (*vedanāya nibbindati*), disenchanted with craving (*taṇhāya nibbindati*). He grows disenchanted with the ear, disenchanted with sounds…pe… He grows disenchanted with the nose, disenchanted with odors… He grows disenchanted with the tongue, disenchanted with tastes… He grows disenchanted with the body, disenchanted with tactile sensations… He grows disenchanted with the mind, disenchanted with mental phenomena, disenchanted with mental consciousness, disenchanted with mental contact, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with craving. Disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate (*nibbindaṃ virajjati*); through dispassion, he is liberated (*virāgā vimuccati*). When liberated, there is knowledge that he is liberated (*vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti*). He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti*)’”.

This the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement (*attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti*). And while this explanation was being given, the hearts of sixty monks, through non-clinging, were fully released from the taints (*imasmiṃ kho pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne saṭṭhimattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsūti*).

The Sixth Discourse on the Six Sextets is finished.
commentary_pali:
427.Ṭhānametaṃ vijjatīti ettakeneva kathāmaggena vaṭṭavivaṭṭavasena desanaṃ matthakaṃ pāpetvā puna tadeva sampiṇḍetvā dassento evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhavetiādimāha. Saṭṭhimattānaṃ bhikkhūnanti ettha anacchariyametaṃ, yaṃ sayameva tathāgate desente saṭṭhi bhikkhū arahattaṃ pattā. Imañhi suttaṃ dhammasenāpatimhi kathentepi saṭṭhi bhikkhū arahattaṃ pattā, mahāmoggallāne kathentepi, asītimahātheresu kathentesupi pattā eva. Etampi anacchariyaṃ. Mahābhiññappattā hi te sāvakā.

Aparabhāge pana tambapaṇṇidīpe māleyyadevatthero nāma heṭṭhā lohapāsāde idaṃ suttaṃ kathesi. Tadāpi saṭṭhi bhikkhū arahattaṃ pattā. Yathā ca lohapāsāde, evaṃ thero mahāmaṇḍapepi idaṃ suttaṃ kathesi. Mahāvihārā nikkhamitvā cetiyapabbataṃ gato, tatthāpi kathesi. Tato sākiyavaṃsavihāre, kūṭālivihāre, antarasobbhe, muttaṅgaṇe, vātakapabbate, pācinagharake, dīghavāpiyaṃ, lokandare, nomaṇḍalatale kathesi. Tesupi ṭhānesu saṭṭhi saṭṭhi bhikkhū arahattaṃ pattā. Tato nikkhamitvā pana thero cittalapabbataṃ gato. Tadā ca cittalapabbatavihāre atirekasaṭṭhivasso mahāthero, pokkharaṇiyaṃ kuruvakatitthaṃ nāma paṭicchannaṭṭhānaṃ atthi, tattha thero nhāyissāmīti otiṇṇo. Devatthero tassa santikaṃ gantvā nhāpemi, bhanteti āha. Thero paṭisanthāreneva – ‘‘māleyyadevo nāma atthīti vadanti, so ayaṃ bhavissatī’’ti ñatvā tvaṃ devoti āha. Āma, bhanteti. Saṭṭhivassaddhānaṃ me, āvuso, koci sarīraṃ hatthena phusituṃ nāma na labhi, tvaṃ pana nhāpehīti uttaritvā tīre nisīdi.

Thero sabbampi hatthapādādiparikammaṃ katvā mahātheraṃ nhāpesi. Taṃ divasañca dhammassavanadivaso hoti. Atha mahāthero – ‘‘deva amhākaṃ dhammadānaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti āha. Thero sādhu, bhanteti sampaṭicchi. Atthaṅgate sūriye dhammassavanaṃ ghosesuṃ. Atikkantasaṭṭhivassāva saṭṭhi mahātherā dhammassavanatthaṃ agamaṃsu. Devatthero sarabhāṇāvasāne imaṃ suttaṃ ārabhi, suttantapariyosāne ca saṭṭhi mahātherā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Tato tissamahāvihāraṃ gantvā kathesi, tasmimpi saṭṭhi therā. Tato nāgamahāvihāre kāḷakacchagāme kathesi, tasmimpi saṭṭhi therā. Tato kalyāṇiṃ gantvā tattha cātuddase heṭṭhāpāsāde kathesi, tasmimpi saṭṭhi therā. Uposathadivase uparipāsāde kathesi, tasmimpi saṭṭhi therāti evaṃ devatthereyeva idaṃ suttaṃ kathente saṭṭhiṭṭhānesu saṭṭhi saṭṭhi janā arahattaṃ pattā.

Ambilakāḷakavihāre pana tipiṭakacūḷanāgatthere imaṃ suttaṃ kathente manussaparisā gāvutaṃ ahosi, devaparisā yojanikā. Suttapariyosāne sahassabhikkhū arahattaṃ pattā, devesu pana tato tato ekekova puthujjano ahosīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Chachakkasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
427. "This is possible (ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī)"—in this way, having brought the teaching to its peak by way of revolving and reverting the discourse, and again showing it by condensing it, [the Buddha] said beginning with, "Seeing thus, *bhikkhus* (evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave)."

"Sixty monks (saṭṭhimattānaṃ bhikkhūna)"—here, this is not astonishing that sixty monks attained *arahatship* while the *Tathāgata* himself was teaching. Indeed, even when this *sutta* was being recited by the General of the *Dhamma*, sixty monks attained *arahatship*; even when recited by Mahāmoggallāna, even when recited by the eighty great elders, they attained [arahatship]. This too is not astonishing. For those disciples had attained great supernormal knowledges (mahābhiññappattā hi te sāvakā).

However, later, on the island of Tambapaṇṇi, an elder named Māleyyadeva recited this *sutta* below the Lohapāsāda. At that time too, sixty monks attained *arahatship*. Just as at the Lohapāsāda, so too the elder recited this *sutta* in the great pavilion. Having departed from the Mahāvihāra, he went to Cetiyapabbata, and there too he recited it. Then at Sākiyavaṃsavihāra, Kūṭālīvihāra, Antarasobbha, Muttaṅgaṇa, Vātakapabbata, Pācinagharaka, Dīghavāpiya, Lokandara, Nomaṇḍalatala, he recited it. In those places too, sixty monks, sixty monks attained *arahatship*. Then, having departed, the elder went to Cittalapabbata.

At that time, in the Cittalapabbata Vihāra, there was a great elder who was more than sixty years old. In the *pokkharaṇi*, there was a secluded place called Kuruvakatittha. The elder, thinking "I will bathe," descended there. Devatthera went to his presence and said, "May I bathe you, venerable sir (nhāpemi, bhante)?" The elder, just by way of cordiality, knowing, "They say there is one named Māleyyadeva, this will be him," said, "Are you a *deva* (tvaṃ deva)?" "Yes, venerable sir (āma, bhante)," [he replied]. "For sixty years, friend (*āvuso*), no one has been able to touch my body with their hand, but you, bathe me," he replied, and sat down on the bank.

The elder, having done all the services such as hand and foot massage, bathed the great elder. That day was the day for hearing the *Dhamma*. Then the great elder said, "Deva, it is fitting to give us the gift of the *Dhamma* (dhammadānaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatī)." The elder agreed, "Good, venerable sir (sādhu, bhante)." When the sun had set, they announced the hearing of the *Dhamma*. Sixty great elders, who had lived beyond sixty years, came for the purpose of hearing the *Dhamma*. Devatthera began this *sutta* at the end of the recitation, and at the conclusion of the *sutta*, sixty great elders attained *arahatship*. Then, having gone to Tissamahāvihāra, he recited it; at that place too, sixty elders [attained *arahatship*]. Then at Nāgamahāvihāra in Kāḷakacchagāma, he recited it; at that place too, sixty elders [attained *arahatship*]. Then, having gone to Kalyāṇi, there he recited it in the lower palace on the fourteenth; at that place too, sixty elders [attained *arahatship*]. On the *uposatha* day, he recited it in the upper palace; at that place too, sixty elders [attained *arahatship*]. Thus, while Devatthera was reciting this *sutta*, in sixty places, sixty people, sixty people attained *arahatship*.

However, at Ambilakāḷakavihāra, when the *Tipiṭaka* Cūḷanāgatthera was reciting this *sutta*, the assembly of humans was a *gāvuta*, the assembly of *devas* was a *yojana*. At the conclusion of the *sutta*, a thousand monks attained *arahatship*; but among the *devas*, from here and there, only one ordinary person (puthujjano) remained.

The commentary on the Chachakkasutta is finished, from the Papañcasūdanī, the commentary to the Majjhimanikāya.
[p.]

mula_pali: 428. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘mahāsaḷāyatanikaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling at Anathapindika’s monastery (anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme), in the Jeta Grove (jetavane), near Savatthi (sāvatthiyaṃ).

There the Fortunate One (bhagavā) addressed the monks (bhikkhū), saying: “Bhikkhus (bhikkhavo)!”

“Venerable sir (bhadante),” those bhikkhus (bhikkhū) replied to the Fortunate One (bhagavato).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) said this: “Bhikkhus (bhikkhave), I shall teach you a discourse on the great sixfold base (mahāsaḷāyatanikaṃ).

Listen to that (taṃ suṇātha) and attend closely, I will speak (bhāsissāmī).”

“As you say, lord (evaṃ bhante),” the monks (bhikkhū) responded to the Blessed One (bhagavato).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) said,
commentary_pali: 428.Evaṃme sutanti mahāsaḷāyatanikasuttaṃ. Tattha mahāsaḷāyatanikanti mahantānaṃ channaṃ āyatanānaṃ jotakaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ.
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard. The *Mahāsaḷāyatanikasuttaṃ*.

Therein, *mahāsaḷāyatanika* means a teaching discourse (*dhamma-pariyāyaṃ*) that illuminates the six great sense bases (*mahantānaṃ channaṃ āyatanānaṃ jotakaṃ*).

mula_pali:
429. ‘‘Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, rūpe ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, cakkhusamphassaṃ ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, yamidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, cakkhusmiṃ sārajjati, rūpesu sārajjati, cakkhuviññāṇe sārajjati, cakkhusamphasse sārajjati, yamidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi sārajjati.

‘‘Tassa sārattassa saṃyuttassa sammūḷhassa assādānupassino viharato āyatiṃ pañcupādānakkhandhā upacayaṃ gacchanti. Taṇhā cassa ponobbhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, sā cassa pavaḍḍhati. Tassa kāyikāpi darathā pavaḍḍhanti, cetasikāpi darathā pavaḍḍhanti; kāyikāpi santāpā pavaḍḍhanti , cetasikāpi santāpā pavaḍḍhanti; kāyikāpi pariḷāhā pavaḍḍhanti, cetasikāpi pariḷāhā pavaḍḍhanti. So kāyadukkhampi kāyikadukkhampi (syā. kaṃ.), kāyikaṃ dukkhampi (ka.) cetodukkhampi paṭisaṃvedeti.

kāyikadukkhampi (syā. kaṃ.), kāyikaṃ dukkhampi (ka.)

‘‘Sotaṃ , bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ, bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ…pe… jivhaṃ, bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ…pe… kāyaṃ, bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ…pe… manaṃ, bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, dhamme, bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ , manosamphassaṃ, bhikkhave, ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, yamidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ajānaṃ apassaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, manasmiṃ sārajjati, dhammesu sārajjati, manoviññāṇe sārajjati, manosamphasse sārajjati, yamidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi sārajjati.

‘‘Tassa sārattassa saṃyuttassa sammūḷhassa assādānupassino viharato āyatiṃ pañcupādānakkhandhā upacayaṃ gacchanti. Taṇhā cassa ponobbhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, sā cassa pavaḍḍhati. Tassa kāyikāpi darathā pavaḍḍhanti, cetasikāpi darathā pavaḍḍhanti; kāyikāpi santāpā pavaḍḍhanti, cetasikāpi santāpā pavaḍḍhanti; kāyikāpi pariḷāhā pavaḍḍhanti, cetasikāpi pariḷāhā pavaḍḍhanti. So kāyadukkhampi cetodukkhampi paṭisaṃvedeti.
mula_english:
429. “Bhikkhus, when one does not know and see the eye (cakkhu) as it actually is, when one does not know and see forms (rūpe) as they actually are, when one does not know and see eye-consciousness (cakkhuviññāṇaṃ) as it actually is, when one does not know and see eye-contact (cakkhusamphassaṃ) as it actually is, when one does not know and see as it actually is the feeling (vedayitaṃ) felt as pleasant (sukhaṃ) or painful (dukkhaṃ) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant (adukkhamasukhaṃ) that arises with eye-contact as condition, then one is inflamed by lust (sārajjati) for the eye, for forms, for eye-consciousness, for eye-contact, and for whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition, be it pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

“When one abides inflamed by lust (sārattassa), fettered (saṃyuttassa), infatuated (sammūḷhassa), contemplating gratification (assādānupassino), then the five aggregates affected by clinging (pañcupādānakkhandhā) are built up for oneself in the future (āyatiṃ); and one’s craving (taṇhā) - which brings renewal of being (ponobbhavikā), is accompanied by delight and lust (nandīrāgasahagatā), and delights in this and that (tatratatrābhinandinī) - increases (pavaḍḍhati).

One's bodily (kāyikāpi) troubles (darathā) increase (pavaḍḍhanti), and one's mental (cetasikāpi) troubles increase; one's bodily torments (santāpā) increase, and one's mental torments increase; one's bodily fevers (pariḷāhā) increase, and one's mental fevers increase.

One experiences bodily suffering (kāyadukkhampi) and mental suffering (cetodukkhampi) .

“Bhikkhus, when one does not know and see the ear (sotaṃ) as it actually is…pe… When one does not know and see the nose (ghānaṃ) as it actually is…pe… When one does not know and see the tongue (jivhaṃ) as it actually is…pe… When one does not know and see the body (kāyaṃ) as it actually is…pe… When one does not know and see the mind (manaṃ) as it actually is, when one does not know and see mental phenomena (dhamme) as it actually is, when one does not know and see mind-consciousness (manoviññāṇaṃ) as it actually is, when one does not know and see mind-contact (manosamphassaṃ) as it actually is, when one does not know and see as it actually is the feeling (vedayitaṃ) felt as pleasant (sukhaṃ) or painful (dukkhaṃ) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant (adukkhamasukhaṃ) that arises with mind-contact as condition, then one is inflamed by lust (sārajjati) for the mind, for mental phenomena, for mind-consciousness, for mind-contact, and for whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition, be it pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

“When one abides inflamed by lust (sārattassa), fettered (saṃyuttassa), infatuated (sammūḷhassa), contemplating gratification (assādānupassino), then the five aggregates affected by clinging (pañcupādānakkhandhā) are built up for oneself in the future (āyatiṃ); and one’s craving (taṇhā) - which brings renewal of being (ponobbhavikā), is accompanied by delight and lust (nandīrāgasahagatā), and delights in this and that (tatratatrābhinandinī) - increases (pavaḍḍhati).

One's bodily (kāyikāpi) troubles (darathā) increase (pavaḍḍhanti), and one's mental (cetasikāpi) troubles increase; one's bodily torments (santāpā) increase, and one's mental torments increase; one's bodily fevers (pariḷāhā) increase, and one's mental fevers increase.

One experiences bodily suffering (kāyadukkhampi) and mental suffering (cetodukkhampi).
commentary_pali: 429.Ajānanti sahavipassanena maggena ajānanto. Upacayaṃ gacchantīti vuḍḍhiṃ gacchanti, vasibhāvaṃ gacchantīti attho. Kāyikāti pañcadvārikadarathā. Cetasikāti manodvārikadarathā. Santāpādīsupi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
429. They do not know (*ajānanti*), because of the path of insight (*sahavipassanena maggena*), they are ignorant (*ajānanto*).

"They go to accumulation (*upacayaṃ gacchantī*)" means they go to growth (*vuḍḍhiṃ gacchanti*), they go to mastery (*vasibhāvaṃ gacchantīti*); this is the meaning (*attho*).

"Physical (*kāyikā*)" means the five-sense-door chariot (*pañcadvārikadarathā*).

"Mental (*cetasikā*)" means the mind-door chariot (*manodvārikadarathā*).

This is also the method (*eseva nayo*) in afflictions such as suffering (*santāpādīsupi*).

mula_pali:
430. ‘‘Cakkhuñca kho, bhikkhave, jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, rūpe jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, cakkhusamphassaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, yamidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, cakkhusmiṃ na sārajjati, rūpesu na sārajjati, cakkhuviññāṇe na sārajjati, cakkhusamphasse na sārajjati, yamidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi na sārajjati.

‘‘Tassa asārattassa asaṃyuttassa asammūḷhassa ādīnavānupassino viharato āyatiṃ pañcupādānakkhandhā apacayaṃ gacchanti. Taṇhā cassa ponobbhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, sā cassa pahīyati. Tassa kāyikāpi darathā pahīyanti, cetasikāpi darathā pahīyanti; kāyikāpi santāpā pahīyanti, cetasikāpi santāpā pahīyanti; kāyikāpi pariḷāhā pahīyanti , cetasikāpi pariḷāhā pahīyanti. So kāyasukhampi cetosukhampi paṭisaṃvedeti.
mula_english:
430.
“Bhikkhus, when one knows and sees the eye (cakkhu) as it actually is, when one knows and sees forms (rūpa) as they actually are, when one knows and sees eye-consciousness (cakkhuviññāṇa) as it actually is, when one knows and sees eye-contact (cakkhusamphassa) as it actually is, when one knows and sees as it actually is the feeling felt as pleasant (sukha) or painful (dukkha) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant (adukkhamasukha) that arises with eye-contact as condition, then one is not inflamed by lust for the eye, for forms, for eye-consciousness, for eye-contact, for the feeling felt as pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant that arises with eye-contact as condition.

“When one abides uninflamed by lust, unfettered, uninfatuated, contemplating danger, then the five aggregates affected by clinging (pañcupādānakkhandhā) are diminished for oneself in the future; and one's craving (taṇhā) - which brings renewal of being, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights in this or that - is abandoned.
One's bodily (kāyika) and mental (cetasika) troubles (daratha) are abandoned, one's bodily and mental torments (santāpa) are abandoned, one's bodily and mental fevers (pariḷāha) are abandoned.
And one experiences bodily (kāyasukha) and mental pleasure (cetosukha).
commentary_pali: 430.Kāyasukhanti pañcadvārikasukhaṃ. Cetosukhanti manodvārikasukhaṃ. Ettha ca pañcadvārikajavanena samāpajjanaṃ vā vuṭṭhānaṃ vā natthi, uppannamattakameva hoti. Manodvārikena sabbaṃ hoti. Ayañca maggavuṭṭhānassa paccayabhūtā balavavipassanā, sāpi manodvārikeneva hoti.
commentary_english: 430. Kāyasukha means pleasure through the five doors (pañcadvārika). Cetosukha means pleasure through the mind-door (manodvārika). Here, arising, attainment or emergence through the five-door impulsion (pañcadvārikajavana) does not exist; it only occurs momentarily. Everything happens through the mind-door (manodvārikena). Moreover, this strong insight (balavavipassanā), which is the causal condition for emergence from the path (maggavuṭṭhānassa), that also happens through the mind-door (manodvārikeneva).

mula_pali:
431. ‘‘Yā tathābhūtassa yathābhūtassa (sī. pī.) diṭṭhi sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi; yo tathābhūtassa yathābhūtassa (sī. pī.) saṅkappo svāssa hoti sammāsaṅkappo; yo tathābhūtassa yathābhūtassa (sī. pī.) vāyāmo svāssa hoti sammāvāyāmo; yā tathābhūtassa yathābhūtassa (sī. pī.) sati sāssa hoti sammāsati; yo tathābhūtassa yathābhūtassa (sī. pī.) samādhi svāssa hoti sammāsamādhi. Pubbeva kho panassa kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ ājīvo suparisuddho hoti. Evamassāyaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

‘‘Tassa evaṃ imaṃ ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayato cattāropi satipaṭṭhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi sammappadhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi iddhipādā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi indriyāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi balāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, sattapi bojjhaṅgā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

‘‘Tassime dve dhammā yuganandhā yuganaddhā (sī. syā. kaṃ.) vattanti – samatho ca vipassanā ca. So ye dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā te dhamme abhiññā parijānāti. Ye dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā te dhamme abhiññā pajahati. Ye dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā te dhamme abhiññā bhāveti. Ye dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā te dhamme abhiññā sacchikaroti.

yuganaddhā (sī. syā. kaṃ.)

‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā? ‘Pañcupādānakkhandhā’ tissa vacanīyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā.

‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā? Avijjā ca bhavataṇhā ca – ime dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā.

‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā? Samatho ca vipassanā ca – ime dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā.

‘‘Katame , bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā? Vijjā ca vimutti ca – ime dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā.
mula_english:
431. "That vision of one who is thus, that is their right vision (samyagdṛṣṭi); that thought of one who is thus, that is their right thought (samyaksaṃkalpa); that effort of one who is thus, that is their right effort (samyagvyāyāma); that mindfulness of one who is thus, that is their right mindfulness (samyaksmṛti); that absorption of one who is thus, that is their right absorption (samyaksamādhi). But his bodily action, his verbal action, and his livelihood have already been well purified earlier. Thus, this Noble Eightfold Path comes to fulfilment in him by development.

"In him who thus develops this Noble Eightfold Path, the four applications of mindfulness also come to fulfilment in him by development; the four right kinds of striving also come to fulfilment in him by development; the four bases for spiritual power also come to fulfilment in him by development; the five faculties also come to fulfilment in him by development; the five powers also come to fulfilment in him by development; the seven enlightenment factors also come to fulfilment in him by development.

"These two things - serenity (śamatha) and insight (vipaśyanā) - occur in him yoked evenly together. He fully understands by direct knowledge (abhijñā) those things that should be fully understood by direct knowledge. He abandons by direct knowledge those things that should be abandoned by direct knowledge. He develops by direct knowledge those things that should be developed by direct knowledge. He realises by direct knowledge those things that should be realised by direct knowledge.

"And what, monks, are the things that should be fully understood by direct knowledge? It should be said, 'the five aggregates of clinging' (pañcupādānakkhandhā), that is to say: the aggregate of clinging to form (rūpupādānakkhandha), the aggregate of clinging to feeling (vedanupādānakkhandha), the aggregate of clinging to perception (saṃjñupādānakkhandha), the aggregate of clinging to formations (saṃskārupādānakkhandha), the aggregate of clinging to consciousness (vijñānupādānakkhandha). These are the things that should be fully understood by direct knowledge.

"And what, monks, are the things that should be abandoned by direct knowledge? Ignorance (avidyā) and craving for existence (bhavatṛṣṇā) - these are the things that should be abandoned by direct knowledge.

"And what, monks, are the things that should be developed by direct knowledge? Serenity (śamatha) and insight (vipaśyanā) - these are the things that should be developed by direct knowledge.

"And what, monks, are the things that should be realised by direct knowledge? True knowledge (vidyā) and deliverance (vimukti) - these are the things that should be realised by direct knowledge.
commentary_pali:
431.Tathābhūtassāti kusalacittasampayuttacetosukhasamaṅgībhūtassa. Pubbeva kho panassāti assa bhikkhuno vācākammantājīvā pubbasuddhikā nāma ādito paṭṭhāya parisuddhāva honti. Diṭṭhisaṅkappavāyāmasatisamādhisaṅkhātāni pana pañcaṅgāni sabbatthakakārāpakaṅgāni nāma. Evaṃ lokuttaramaggo aṭṭhaṅgiko vā sattaṅgiko vā hoti.

Vitaṇḍavādī pana ‘‘yā yathābhūtassa diṭṭhī’’ti imameva suttapadesaṃ gahetvā ‘‘lokuttaramaggo pañcaṅgiko’’ti vadati. So – ‘‘evamassāyaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī’’ti iminā anantaravacaneneva paṭisedhitabbo. Uttari ca evaṃ saññāpetabbo – lokuttaramaggo pañcaṅgiko nāma natthi, imāni pana pañca sabbatthakakārāpakaṅgāni maggakkhaṇe virativasena pūrenti. ‘‘Yā catūhi vacīduccaritehi ārati viratī’’ti evaṃ vuttaviratīsu hi micchāvācaṃ pajahati, sammāvācaṃ bhāveti, evaṃ sammāvācaṃ bhāventassa imāni pañcaṅgikāni na vinā, saheva viratiyā pūrenti. Sammākammantājīvesupi eseva nayo. Iti vacīkammādīni ādito paṭṭhāya parisuddhāneva vaṭṭanti. Imāni pana pañca sabbatthakakārāpakaṅgāni virativasena paripūrentīti pañcaṅgiko maggo nāma natthi. Subhaddasuttepi (dī. ni. 2.214) cetaṃ vuttaṃ – ‘‘yasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo’’ti. Aññesu ca anekesu suttasatesu aṭṭhaṅgikova maggo āgatoti.
commentary_english:
431. <hi rend="bold">tathābhūtassā</hi>ti <pb ed="m" n="4. 0248"/> of one who has become endowed with the bliss of mind (cetasasukha) conjoined with wholesome thought (kusalacitta).

<hi rend="bold">pubbeva kho panassā</hi>ti <pb ed="p" n="5. 0104"/> namely, the speech, action, and livelihood of that *bhikṣu* are primarily purified from the outset.

Moreover, the five factors, namely, right view (dṛṣṭi), right thought (saṅkappa), right effort (vāyāma), right mindfulness (smṛti), and right concentration (samādhi), are called factors that accomplish everything in every respect.

Thus, the supramundane path (lokuttaramārga) is either eightfold (aṣṭāṅgika) or sevenfold (saptāṅgika).

A sophist (vitaṇḍavādī), however, taking this very passage of the *sūtra*, "whatever view is in accordance with reality (yathābhūta)," says, "the supramundane path is fivefold (pañcaṅgika)."

He should be refuted by this immediate statement: "Thus, this noble eightfold path (ārya aṣṭāṅgika mārga) goes to the complete fulfillment of cultivation (bhāvanāpāripūri)."

Moreover, it should be made known: There is no supramundane path that is fivefold (lokuttaramārga pañcaṅgika nāma natthi); rather, these five factors accomplish everything in every respect, fulfilling [the path] by way of cessation (virati) at the moment of the path (maggakkhaṇe).

"That which is abstaining and refraining from the four kinds of misconduct of speech (vacīduccarita)"—thus, in the case of those stated abstentions, one abandons wrong speech (mithyāvāc) and cultivates right speech (samyag-vāc); thus, for one cultivating right speech <pb ed="v" n="4. 0261"/>, these five factors are not separate, but together with abstinence, they fulfill [the path].

The same method (naya) applies to right action (samyak-karmānta) and right livelihood (samyag-ājīva).

Thus, speech-action and so forth are purified from the outset and continue as such.

These five factors, which accomplish everything in every respect, fulfill [the path] by way of cessation (virati), and therefore there is no fivefold path (pañcaṅgiko mārga nāma natthi).

In the Subhadda Sūtra (Dīgha Nikāya 2. 214) it was said: "In whatever Dharma and Discipline (dharma-vinaya), Subhadda, the noble eightfold path (ārya aṣṭāṅgika mārga) is [not found]."

And in many other hundreds of *sūtras*, it is the eightfold path (aṣṭāṅgika mārga) that is mentioned.

mula_pali:
432. ‘‘Sotaṃ , bhikkhave, jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ bhikkhave, jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ…pe… jivhaṃ, bhikkhave, jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ… kāyaṃ, bhikkhave, jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ… manaṃ, bhikkhave, jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, dhamme jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, manosamphassaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, yamidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi jānaṃ passaṃ yathābhūtaṃ, manasmiṃ na sārajjati, dhammesu na sārajjati, manoviññāṇe na sārajjati, manosamphasse na sārajjati, yamidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi na sārajjati.

‘‘Tassa asārattassa asaṃyuttassa asammūḷhassa ādīnavānupassino viharato āyatiṃ pañcupādānakkhandhā apacayaṃ gacchanti. Taṇhā cassa ponobbhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī , sā cassa pahīyati. Tassa kāyikāpi darathā pahīyanti, cetasikāpi darathā pahīyanti; kāyikāpi santāpā pahīyanti, cetasikāpi santāpā pahīyanti; kāyikāpi pariḷāhā pahīyanti, cetasikāpi pariḷāhā pahīyanti. So kāyasukhampi cetosukhampi paṭisaṃvedeti.
mula_english:
432. “Bhikkhus, when one knows and sees the ear (sotaṃ) as it actually is... When one knows and sees the nose (ghānaṃ) as it actually is... When one knows and sees the tongue (jivhaṃ) as it actually is... When one knows and sees the body (kāyaṃ) as it actually is... When one knows and sees the mind (manaṃ) as it actually is, when one knows and sees phenomena (dhamme) as they actually are, when one knows and sees mind-consciousness (manoviññāṇaṃ) as it actually is, when one knows and sees mind-contact (manosamphassaṃ) as it actually is, when one knows and sees as it actually is the feeling felt as pleasant (sukhaṃ) or painful (dukkhaṃ) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant (adukkhamasukhaṃ) that arises with mind-contact as condition, then one is not inflamed by lust for the mind (manasmiṃ), for phenomena (dhammesu), for mind-consciousness (manoviññāṇe), for mind-contact (manosamphasse), for the feeling felt as pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant that arises with mind-contact as condition.

“When one abides uninflamed by lust (asārattassa), unfettered (asaṃyuttassa), uninfatuated (asammūḷhassa), contemplating danger (ādīnavānupassino), then the five aggregates affected by clinging (pañcupādānakkhandhā) are diminished (apacayaṃ gacchanti) for oneself in the future; and one’s craving (taṇhā) for renewed existence (ponobbhavikā), which is accompanied by delight and attachment (nandīrāgasahagatā), finding fresh delight now here, now there (tatratatrābhinandinī), that is abandoned (pahīyati).

One’s bodily (kāyikāpi) troubles (darathā) are abandoned (pahīyanti), one’s mental (cetasikāpi) troubles (darathā) are abandoned (pahīyanti); one’s bodily (kāyikāpi) torments (santāpā) are abandoned (pahīyanti), one’s mental (cetasikāpi) torments (santāpā) are abandoned (pahīyanti); one’s bodily (kāyikāpi) fevers (pariḷāhā) are abandoned (pahīyanti), one’s mental (cetasikāpi) fevers (pariḷāhā) are abandoned (pahīyanti).

And one experiences bodily (kāyasukhampi) and mental pleasure (cetosukhampi) (paṭisaṃvedeti).

mula_pali:
433. ‘‘Yā tathābhūtassa diṭṭhi sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi; yo tathābhūtassa saṅkappo svāssa hoti sammāsaṅkappo; yo tathābhūtassa vāyāmo svāssa hoti sammāvāyāmo; yā tathābhūtassa sati sāssa hoti sammāsati; yo tathābhūtassa samādhi svāssa hoti sammāsamādhi. Pubbeva kho panassa kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ ājīvo suparisuddho hoti. Evamassāyaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

‘‘Tassa evaṃ imaṃ ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayato cattāropi satipaṭṭhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi sammappadhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi iddhipādā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi indriyāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi balāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, sattapi bojjhaṅgā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

‘‘Tassime dve dhammā yuganandhā vattanti – samatho ca vipassanā ca. So ye dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā te dhamme abhiññā parijānāti. Ye dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā te dhamme abhiññā pajahati. Ye dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā te dhamme abhiññā bhāveti. Ye dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā te dhamme abhiññā sacchikaroti.

‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā? ‘Pañcupādānakkhandhā’ tissa vacanīyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā.

‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā? Avijjā ca bhavataṇhā ca – ime dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā.

‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā? Samatho ca vipassanā ca – ime dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā.

‘‘Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā? Vijjā ca vimutti ca – ime dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Mahāsaḷāyatanikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
433. “The view of a person such as this is right view (sammādiṭṭhi); his intention is right intention (sammāsaṅkappo); his effort is right effort (sammāvāyāmo); his mindfulness is right mindfulness (sammāsati); his concentration is right concentration (sammāsamādhi). But his bodily action (kāyakammaṃ), his verbal action (vacīkammaṃ), and his livelihood (ājīvo) have already been well purified earlier. Thus, this Noble Eightfold Path (ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo) comes to fulfilment in him by development (bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati).

“When he develops this Noble Eightfold Path (ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayato), the four foundations of mindfulness (satipaṭṭhānā) also come to fulfilment in him by development (bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti); the four right kinds of striving (sammappadhānā) also come to fulfilment in him by development; the four bases for spiritual power (iddhipādā) also come to fulfilment in him by development; the five faculties (indriyāni) also come to fulfilment in him by development; the five powers (balāni) also come to fulfilment in him by development; the seven enlightenment factors (bojjhaṅgā) also come to fulfilment in him by development.

“These two things—serenity (samatho) and insight (vipassanā)—occur in him yoked evenly together. He fully understands by direct knowledge (abhiññā parijānāti) those things that should be fully understood by direct knowledge (abhiññā pariññeyyā). He abandons by direct knowledge (abhiññā pajahati) those things that should be abandoned by direct knowledge (abhiññā pahātabbā). He develops by direct knowledge (abhiññā bhāveti) those things that should be developed by direct knowledge (abhiññā bhāvetabbā). He realises by direct knowledge (abhiññā sacchikaroti) those things that should be realised by direct knowledge (abhiññā sacchikātabbā).

“And what, monks, are the things that should be fully understood by direct knowledge (dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā)? ‘The five aggregates subject to grasping (pañcupādānakkhandhā)’ should be said, that is to say: the aggregate of material form subject to grasping (rūpupādānakkhandho), the aggregate of feeling subject to grasping (vedanupādānakkhandho), the aggregate of perception subject to grasping (saññupādānakkhandho), the aggregate of mental formations subject to grasping (saṅkhārupādānakkhandho), the aggregate of consciousness subject to grasping (viññāṇupādānakkhandho). These are the things that should be fully understood by direct knowledge (dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā).

“And what, monks, are the things that should be abandoned by direct knowledge (dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā)? Ignorance (avijjā) and craving for existence (bhavataṇhā). These are the things that should be abandoned by direct knowledge (dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā).

“And what, monks, are the things that should be developed by direct knowledge (dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā)? Serenity (samatho) and insight (vipassanā). These are the things that should be developed by direct knowledge (dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā).

“And what, monks, are the things that should be realised by direct knowledge (dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā)? True knowledge (vijjā) and deliverance (vimutti). These are the things that should be realised by direct knowledge (dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā).”

The Blessed One said this. Gratified, the monks delighted in the Blessed One’s words (bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti).

The Mahāsaḷāyatanika Sutta, the seventh, is concluded.
commentary_pali:
433.Cattāropi satipaṭṭhānāti maggasampayuttāva cattāro satipaṭṭhānā. Sammappadhānādīsupi eseva nayo. Yuganandhāti ekakkhaṇikayuganandhā. Etehi aññasmiṃ khaṇe samāpatti, aññasmiṃ vipassanāti. Evaṃ nānākhaṇikāpi honti, ariyamagge pana ekakkhaṇikā.

Vijjā ca vimutti cāti arahattamaggavijjā ca phalavimutti ca. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Vijjā ca vimutti cā

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāsaḷāyatanikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
433. "The four *smṛtyupasthānas* (foundations of mindfulness)" are the four *smṛtyupasthānas* that are connected with the path (*mārga*).

And similarly in the case of the right efforts (*samyak-pradhāna*), and so on.

"*Yuganandhā* (yoked in pairs)" means yoked in pairs in a single moment (*eka-kṣaṇika*).

By these, in one moment there is attainment (*samāpatti*), in another insight (*vipaśyanā*).

Thus, they can be of different moments (*nānā-kṣaṇika*), but on the *ārya-mārga* (noble path) they are of a single moment.

"Knowledge (*vidyā*) and liberation (*vimukti*)" are the knowledge of the path of arhatship (*arhattva-mārga*) and the liberation of the fruit (*phala-vimukti*).

All the rest is clear throughout.

*Vidyā ca vimukti cā*

The Mahāsaḷāyatanikasutta commentary in the Papañcasūdanī, Majjhimanikāya commentary, is finished.

mula_pali:
434. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena nagaravindaṃ nāma kosalānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ gāmo tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho nagaravindeyyakā nagaravindeyyā (ka.) brāhmaṇagahapatikā – ‘‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ nagaravindaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī’’ti.

Atha kho nagaravindeyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu; sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho nagaravindeyyake brāhmaṇagahapatike bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
434. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the Kosalan country with a large *saṃgha* of monks, and eventually arrived at a Kosalan village named Nagaravinda, inhabited by *brāhmaṇas*.

The *brāhmaṇa* householders of Nagaravinda heard: “The *śramaṇa* Gotama, the son of the Śākyans, who went forth from the Śākya clan, while wandering in the Kosalan country with a large *saṃgha* of monks, has arrived at Nagaravinda.”

Now a good report of that Venerable Gotama has spread about: “That Blessed One is an *arhat*, a fully enlightened Buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), a Well-Farer (*sugata*), Knower of the Worlds (*lokavidū*), unsurpassed Trainer of those who can be led, Teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.”

He, having realized it by his own super-knowledge (*abhijñā*), proclaims this world with its gods (*sadevakaṃ*), its *Māras* (*samārakaṃ*) and *Brahmās* (*sabrahmakaṃ*), its ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* (*sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ*), its princes and people (*sadevamanussaṃ*).

He teaches the *Dharma* that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the (right) meaning and the (right) words; he reveals the spiritual life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) that is utterly perfect and pure.

“It is good to see such *arhats*.”

Then the *brāhmaṇa* householders of Nagaravinda went to the Blessed One. Some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some exchanged greetings with him, and when this courteous and amiable talk was finished, sat down at one side; some extended their hands in reverential salutation (*añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā*) towards the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some pronounced their name and clan in the Blessed One’s presence and sat down at one side; some kept silent and sat down at one side.

When the *brāhmaṇa* householders of Nagaravinda were seated to one side, the Blessed One said this to them:

mula_pali: 435. ‘‘Sace vo, gahapatayo, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kathaṃbhūtā, gahapatayo, samaṇabrāhmaṇā na sakkātabbā na garukātabbā na mānetabbā na pūjetabbā’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, gahapatayo, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu avītarāgā avītadosā avītamohā, ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā, samavisamaṃ caranti kāyena vācāya manasā, evarūpā samaṇabrāhmaṇā na sakkātabbā na garukātabbā na mānetabbā na pūjetabbā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Mayampi hi cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu avītarāgā avītadosā avītamohā, ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā, samavisamaṃ carāma kāyena vācāya manasā, tesaṃ no samacariyampi hetaṃ uttari apassataṃ. Tasmā te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā na sakkātabbā na garukātabbā na mānetabbā na pūjetabbā. Ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā sotaviññeyyesu saddesu… ghānaviññeyyesu gandhesu… jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu… kāyaviññeyyesu phoṭṭhabbesu… manoviññeyyesu dhammesu avītarāgā avītadosā avītamohā, ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā, samavisamaṃ caranti kāyena vācāya manasā, evarūpā samaṇabrāhmaṇā na sakkātabbā na garukātabbā na mānetabbā na pūjetabbā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Mayampi hi manoviññeyyesu dhammesu avītarāgā avītadosā avītamohā , ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā, samavisamaṃ carāma kāyena vācāya manasā, tesaṃ no samacariyampi hetaṃ uttari apassataṃ. Tasmā te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā na sakkātabbā na garukātabbā na mānetabbā na pūjetabbā’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, gahapatayo, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha.
mula_english:
435. "If, householders, wanderers of other sects should ask you thus: 'What kind of recluses and Brahmins should not be honored, respected, revered, and venerated?' Being thus asked, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: 'Those recluses and Brahmins who are not rid of lust ( *avītarāga*), hate ( *avītadosa*), and delusion ( *avītamoha*) regarding forms cognizable by the eye ( *cakṣuviññeyyesu rūpesu*), whose minds are not inwardly peaceful ( *ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā*), and who conduct themselves now righteously, now unrighteously ( *samavisamaṃ caranti*) in body ( *kāyena*), speech ( *vācāya*), and mind ( *manasā*) - such recluses and Brahmins should not be honored, respected, revered, and venerated.'

What is the reason for this? Because we ourselves are not rid of lust ( *avītarāga*), hate ( *avītadosa*), and delusion ( *avītamoha*) regarding forms cognizable by the eye ( *cakṣuviññeyyesu rūpesu*), our minds are not inwardly peaceful ( *ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā*), and we conduct ourselves now righteously, now unrighteously ( *samavisamaṃ carāma*) in body ( *kāyena*), speech ( *vācāya*), and mind ( *manasā*). Since we do not see any higher righteous conduct on the part of those, they should not be honored, respected, revered, and venerated.

Those recluses and Brahmins who are not rid of lust ( *avītarāga*), hate ( *avītadosa*), and delusion ( *avītamoha*) regarding sounds cognizable by the ear ( *sotaviññeyyesu saddesu*)...regarding odours cognizable by the nose ( *ghānaviññeyyesu gandhesu*)...regarding flavours cognizable by the tongue ( *jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu*)...regarding tangibles cognizable by the body ( *kāyaviññeyyesu phoṭṭhabbesu*)...regarding mind-objects cognizable by the mind ( *manoviññeyyesu dhammesu*), whose minds are not inwardly peaceful ( *ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā*), and who conduct themselves now righteously, now unrighteously ( *samavisamaṃ caranti*) in body ( *kāyena*), speech ( *vācāya*), and mind ( *manasā*) - such recluses and Brahmins should not be honored, respected, revered, and venerated.

What is the reason for this? Because we ourselves are not rid of lust ( *avītarāga*), hate ( *avītadosa*), and delusion ( *avītamoha*) regarding mind-objects cognizable by the mind ( *manoviññeyyesu dhammesu*), our minds are not inwardly peaceful ( *ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā*), and we conduct ourselves now righteously, now unrighteously ( *samavisamaṃ carāma*) in body ( *kāyena*), speech ( *vācāya*), and mind ( *manasā*). Since we do not see any higher righteous conduct on the part of those, they should not be honored, respected, revered, and venerated.’

Being thus asked, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects in this way.
commentary_pali: 435.Evaṃme sutanti nagaravindeyyasuttaṃ. Tattha samavisamaṃ carantīti kālena samaṃ caranti, kālena visamaṃ. Samacariyampi hetanti samacariyampi hi etaṃ.
commentary_english:
435. *evaṃ me suta*nti nagaravindeyyasuttaṃ.

There, *samavisamaṃ carantī*ti: They conduct themselves in accordance with the times, out of accordance with the times.

*samacariyampi heta*nti: This is indeed proper conduct.

mula_pali: 436. ‘‘Sace pana vo, gahapatayo, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kathaṃbhūtā, gahapatayo, samaṇabrāhmaṇā sakkātabbā garukātabbā mānetabbā pūjetabbā’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, gahapatayo, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu vītarāgā vītadosā vītamohā, ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacittā, samacariyaṃ caranti kāyena vācāya manasā, evarūpā samaṇabrāhmaṇā sakkātabbā garukātabbā mānetabbā pūjetabbā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Mayampi hi mayaṃ hi (?) cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu avītarāgā avītadosā avītamohā, ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā, samavisamaṃ carāma kāyena vācāya manasā, tesaṃ no samacariyampi hetaṃ uttari passataṃ. Tasmā te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sakkātabbā garukātabbā mānetabbā pūjetabbā. Ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā sotaviññeyyesu saddesu… ghānaviññeyyesu gandhesu… jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu… kāyaviññeyyesu phoṭṭhabbesu… manoviññeyyesu dhammesu vītarāgā vītadosā vītamohā, ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacittā, samacariyaṃ caranti kāyena vācāya manasā, evarūpā samaṇabrāhmaṇā sakkātabbā garukātabbā mānetabbā pūjetabbā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Mayampi hi manoviññeyyesu dhammesu avītarāgā avītadosā avītamohā ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā, samavisamaṃ carāma kāyena vācāya manasā, tesaṃ no samacariyampi hetaṃ uttari passataṃ. Tasmā te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā sakkātabbā garukātabbā mānetabbā pūjetabbā’ti . Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, gahapatayo, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha.
mula_english:
436. “If, householders, wanderers of other sects should ask you thus: ‘What kind of ascetics and *brāhmaṇas*, householders, should be honored, respected, revered, and venerated?’ Being thus asked, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: ‘Those ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* who are rid of lust ( *vītarāga*), hate (*vītadosa*), and delusion (*vītamoha*) regarding forms cognizable by the eye ( *cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu*), whose minds are inwardly peaceful (*ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacittā*), and who conduct themselves righteously ( *samacariyaṃ caranti*) in body ( *kāyena*), speech ( *vācāya*), and mind (*manasā*) - such ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* should be honored, respected, revered, and venerated.’

What is the reason for that? Because we ourselves are not rid of lust (*avītarāga*), hate (*avītadosa*), and delusion (*avītamoha*) regarding forms cognizable by the eye (*cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu*), our minds are not inwardly peaceful (*ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā*), and we conduct ourselves now righteously, now unrighteously (*samavisamaṃ carāma*) in body (*kāyena*), speech (*vācāya*), and mind (*manasā*). We do not see higher righteous conduct on their part.

Therefore, those good ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* should be honored, respected, revered, and venerated.

Those ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* who are rid of lust (*vītarāgā*), hate (*vītadosā*), and delusion (*vītamohā*) regarding sounds cognizable by the ear (*sotaviññeyyesu saddesu*)… regarding odours cognizable by the nose (*ghānaviññeyyesu gandhesu*)… regarding flavours cognizable by the tongue (*jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu*)… regarding tangibles cognizable by the body (*kāyaviññeyyesu phoṭṭhabbesu*)… regarding mind-objects cognizable by the mind (*manoviññeyyesu dhammesu*), whose minds are inwardly peaceful (*ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacittā*), and who conduct themselves righteously (*samacariyaṃ caranti*) in body (*kāyena*), speech (*vācāya*), and mind (*manasā*) - such ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* should be honored, respected, revered, and venerated.

What is the reason for that? Because we ourselves are not rid of lust (*avītarāgā*), hate (*avītadosā*), and delusion (*avītamohā*) regarding mind-objects cognizable by the mind (*manoviññeyyesu dhammesu*), our minds are not inwardly peaceful (*ajjhattaṃ avūpasantacittā*), and we conduct ourselves now righteously, now unrighteously (*samavisamaṃ carāma*) in body (*kāyena*), speech (*vācāya*), and mind (*manasā*). We do not see higher righteous conduct on their part.

Therefore, those good ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* should be honored, respected, revered, and venerated.’

Being thus asked, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects in this way.

mula_pali:
437. ‘‘Sace pana vo sace te (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), gahapatayo, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘ke panāyasmantānaṃ ākārā, ke anvayā, yena tumhe āyasmanto evaṃ vadetha? Addhā te āyasmanto vītarāgā vā rāgavinayāya vā paṭipannā, vītadosā vā dosavinayāya vā paṭipannā, vītamohā vā mohavinayāya vā paṭipannā’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, gahapatayo, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘tathā hi te āyasmanto araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti. Natthi kho pana tattha tathārūpā cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā ye disvā disvā abhirameyyuṃ, natthi kho pana tattha tathārūpā sotaviññeyyā saddā ye sutvā sutvā abhirameyyuṃ, natthi kho pana tattha tathārūpā ghānaviññeyyā gandhā ye ghāyitvā ghāyitvā abhirameyyuṃ , natthi kho pana tattha tathārūpā jivhāviññeyyā rasā ye sāyitvā sāyitvā abhirameyyuṃ, natthi kho pana tattha tathārūpā kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā ye phusitvā phusitvā abhirameyyuṃ. Ime kho no, āvuso, ākārā, ime anvayā, yena mayaṃ yena mayaṃ āyasmanto (sī. pī.), yena mayaṃ āyasmante (syā. kaṃ.) evaṃ vadema – addhā te āyasmanto vītarāgā vā rāgavinayāya vā paṭipannā, vītadosā vā dosavinayāya vā paṭipannā, vītamohā vā mohavinayāya vā paṭipannā’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, gahapatayo, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, nagaravindeyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṃ gate’’ti.

Nagaravindeyyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
437. "If, householders, wanderers belonging to other sects should ask you thus: 'What are the reasons, what is the evidence whereby you venerable ones speak thus? Surely these venerable ones are either rid of lust ( *vītarāga* ) or are practising for the removal of lust ( *rāgavinayāya* ), either rid of hatred ( *vītadosa* ) or are practicing for the removal of hatred ( *dosavinayāya* ), either rid of delusion ( *vītamoha* ) or are practising for the removal of delusion ( *mohavinayāya* )?' Being thus asked, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects in this way: 'The venerable ones frequent secluded lodgings in the forests and woods. For there are no forms cognizable by the eye there of a kind that they could look at and delight in ( *cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā ye disvā disvā abhirameyyuṃ* ), there are no sounds cognizable by the ear there of a kind that they could listen to and delight in ( *sotaviññeyyā saddā ye sutvā sutvā abhirameyyuṃ* ), there are no odours cognizable by the nose there of a kind that they could smell and delight in ( *ghānaviññeyyā gandhā ye ghāyitvā ghāyitvā abhirameyyuṃ* ) , there are no flavours cognizable by the tongue there of a kind that they could taste and delight in ( *jivhāviññeyyā rasā ye sāyitvā sāyitvā abhirameyyuṃ* ), there are no tangibles cognizable by the body there of a kind that they could touch and delight in ( *kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā ye phusitvā phusitvā abhirameyyuṃ* ). These, friends, are our reasons, this is our evidence ( *ime ākārā, ime anvayā* ) whereby we say: 'Surely these venerable ones are either rid of lust ( *vītarāga* ) or are practising for the removal of lust ( *rāgavinayāya* ), either rid of hatred ( *vītadosa* ) or are practicing for the removal of hatred ( *dosavinayāya* ), either rid of delusion ( *vītamoha* ) or are practising for the removal of delusion ( *mohavinayāya* ).' Being thus asked, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects in this way.'"

When this was said, the brahmin householders of Nagaravindeyya said to the Blessed One: "Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! Just as, Master Gotama, one might turn upright what had been overthrown, reveal what was hidden, show the way to one who was lost, or hold up a lamp in the dark for those with eyesight to see forms, so the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama. We go to Master Gotama for refuge ( *saraṇaṃ gacchāma* ), to the Dhamma, and to the Sangha of monks ( *bhikkhusaṅghañca* ). May Master Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone to him for refuge ( *upāsake saraṇaṃ gate* ), from this day forward, for life."

The Nagaravindeyya Sutta, the eighth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
437.Ke ākārāti kāni kāraṇāni? Ke anvayāti kā anubuddhiyo? Natthi kho pana tatthāti kasmā āha, nanu araññe haritatiṇacampakavanādivasena atimanuññā rūpādayo pañca kāmaguṇā atthīti? No natthi. Na panetaṃ vanasaṇḍena kathitaṃ, itthirūpādīni pana sandhāyetaṃ kathitaṃ. Tāni hi purisassa cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti. Yathāha – ‘‘nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekarūpampi samanupassāmi, yaṃ evaṃ purisassa cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, itthirūpaṃ. Itthirūpaṃ, bhikkhave, purisassa cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’’ti (a. ni. 1.1) vitthāretabbaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Nagaravindeyyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
