437. "What are the forms (ākārā)?" Namely, what are the causes (kāraṇāni)? "What are the connections (anvayā)?" Namely, what are the understandings (anubuddhiyo)? "But there is nothing there (natthi kho pana tatthā)": Why does he say this? Surely, in the forest (araññe), there are very attractive (atimanuññā) sights, sounds, etc. (rūpādayo), the five sense pleasures (pañca kāmaguṇā), are there not? No, there are not.

But this was not said about the forest grove (vanasaṇḍena). But this was said with reference to the forms of women, and so on (itthirūpādīni).

For they (tāni) invade (pariyādāya) and remain (tiṭṭhanti) in a man's mind (purisassa cittaṃ).

As he said: “Monks (bhikkhave), I do not see any other form (aññaṃ ekarūpampi) that so invades (pariyādāya) and remains (tiṭṭhati) in a man's mind (purisassa cittaṃ) as this, monks (bhikkhave), the form of a woman (itthirūpaṃ).

The form of a woman (itthirūpaṃ), monks (bhikkhave), invades (pariyādāya) and remains (tiṭṭhati) in a man's mind (purisassa cittaṃ),” etc. (A.
Ni.
1.
1) should be expanded (vitthāretabbaṃ).

The rest is clear (uttānam) throughout (sabbattha).

The Nagaravindeyya Sutta Commentary of the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the Middle Length Discourses (Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya), is finished (niṭṭhitā).

mula_pali:
438. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Vippasannāni kho te, sāriputta, indriyāni, parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. Katamena kho tvaṃ, sāriputta, vihārena etarahi bahulaṃ viharasī’’ti? ‘‘Suññatāvihārena kho ahaṃ, bhante, etarahi bahulaṃ viharāmī’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu, sādhu, sāriputta! Mahāpurisavihārena kira tvaṃ, sāriputta, etarahi bahulaṃ viharasi. Mahāpurisavihāro eso hesa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sāriputta, yadidaṃ – suññatā. Tasmātiha, sāriputta, bhikkhu sace ākaṅkheyya – ‘suññatāvihārena bahulaṃ etarahi bahulaṃ (sī. pī.) vihareyya’nti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘yena cāhaṃ maggena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ, yasmiñca padese piṇḍāya acariṃ, yena ca maggena gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamiṃ, atthi nu kho me tattha cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu chando vā rāgo vā doso vā moho vā paṭighaṃ vāpi cetaso’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘yena cāhaṃ maggena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ, yasmiñca padese piṇḍāya acariṃ, yena ca maggena gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamiṃ, atthi me tattha cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu chando vā rāgo vā doso vā moho vā paṭighaṃ vāpi cetaso’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘yena cāhaṃ maggena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ, yasmiñca padese piṇḍāya acariṃ, yena ca maggena gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamiṃ, natthi me tattha cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu chando vā rāgo vā doso vā moho vā paṭighaṃ vāpi cetaso’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.

hesa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) etarahi bahulaṃ (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
438. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rajagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

Then, the venerable Śāriputra rose from meditation in the evening and went to the Blessed One. After paying homage to the Blessed One, he sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Śāriputra:

“Śāriputta, your faculties are clear, the color of your skin is pure and bright.

Which abiding do you often abide in now, Śāriputta?” “I often abide in voidness-abiding, venerable sir.”

“Good, good, Śāriputta! You often abide in the abiding of a great man, Śāriputta.

This is the abiding of a great man, Śāriputta, namely, voidness ( *śūnyatā*).

Therefore, Śāriputta, if a monk should wish, ‘May I often abide in voidness-abiding,’ then that monk should consider thus: ‘On the path by which I went to the village for alms, or in the place where I wandered for alms, or on the path by which I returned from the almsround, was there any desire (*chanda*), lust (*rāga*), hate (*dosa*), delusion (*moha*), or aversion (*paṭigha*) in my mind?’ If, Śāriputta, a monk reviewing, knows thus: ‘On the path by which I went to the village for alms, or in the place where I wandered for alms, or on the path by which I returned from the almsround, there was desire, lust, hate, delusion, or aversion in my mind,’ then that monk should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states (*akusalānam dhammānam*).

But if, Śāriputta, a monk reviewing, knows thus: ‘On the path by which I went to the village for alms, or in the place where I wandered for alms, or on the path by which I returned from the almsround, there was no desire, lust, hate, delusion, or aversion in my mind regarding forms cognizable by the eye,’ then that monk can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states (*kusalesu dhammesu*).
commentary_pali:
438.Evaṃme sutanti piṇḍapātapārisuddhisuttaṃ. Tattha paṭisallānāti phalasamāpattito.

Vippasannānīti okāsavasenetaṃ vuttaṃ. Phalasamāpattito hi vuṭṭhitassa pañcahi pasādehi patiṭṭhitokāso vippasanno hoti, chavivaṇṇo parisuddho. Tasmā evamāha. Suññatavihārenāti suññataphalasamāpattivihārena. Mahāpurisavihāroti buddhapaccekabuddhatathāgatamahāsāvakānaṃ mahāpurisānaṃ vihāro. Yena cāhaṃ maggenātiādīsu vihārato paṭṭhāya yāva gāmassa indakhīlā esa paviṭṭhamaggo nāma, antogāmaṃ pavisitvā gehapaṭipāṭiyā caritvā yāva nagaradvārena nikkhamanā esa caritabbapadeso nāma, bahi indakhīlato paṭṭhāya yāva vihārā esa paṭikkantamaggo nāma. Paṭighaṃ vāpi cetasoti citte paṭihaññanakilesajātaṃ kiñci atthi natthīti. Ahorattānusikkhināti divasañca rattiñca anusikkhantena.

Vippasannānī Suññatavihārenā Mahāpurisavihāro Yena cāhaṃ maggenā Paṭighaṃ vāpi cetaso Ahorattānusikkhinā
commentary_english:
438. evaṃme sutanti piṇḍapātapārisuddhisuttaṃ. tattha paṭisallānāti phalasamāpattito.

vippasannānīti okāsavasenetaṃ vuttaṃ. phalasamāpattito hi vuṭṭhitassa pañcahi pasādehi patiṭṭhitokāso vippasanno hoti, chavivaṇṇo parisuddho. tasmā evamāha. suññatavihārenāti suññataphalasamāpattivihārena. mahāpurisavihāroti buddhapaccekabuddhatathāgatamahāsāvakānaṃ mahāpurisānaṃ vihāro. yena cāhaṃ maggenātiādīsu vihārato paṭṭhāya yāva gāmassa indakhīlā esa paviṭṭhamaggo nāma, antogāmaṃ pavisitvā gehapaṭipāṭiyā caritvā yāva nagaradvārena nikkhamanā esa caritabbapadeso nāma, bahi indakhīlato paṭṭhāya yāva vihārā esa paṭikkantamaggo nāma. paṭighaṃ vāpi cetasoti citte paṭihaññanakilesajātaṃ kiñci atthi natthīti. ahorattānusikkhināti divasañca rattiñca anusikkhantena.

vippasannānī suññatavihārenā mahāpurisavihāro yena cāhaṃ maggenā paṭighaṃ vāpi cetaso ahorattānusikkhinā

mula_pali: 439. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘yena cāhaṃ maggena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ, yasmiñca padese piṇḍāya acariṃ, yena ca maggena gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamiṃ, atthi nu kho me tattha sotaviññeyyesu saddesu…pe… ghānaviññeyyesu gandhesu… jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu … kāyaviññeyyesu phoṭṭhabbesu… manoviññeyyesu dhammesu chando vā rāgo vā doso vā moho vā paṭighaṃ vāpi cetaso’ti? Sace , sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘yena cāhaṃ maggena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ, yasmiñca padese piṇḍāya acariṃ, yena ca maggena gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamiṃ, atthi me tattha manoviññeyyesu dhammesu chando vā rāgo vā doso vā moho vā paṭighaṃ vāpi cetaso’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘yena cāhaṃ maggena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ, yasmiñca padese piṇḍāya acariṃ, yena ca maggena gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamiṃ, natthi me tattha manoviññeyyesu dhammesu chando vā rāgo vā doso vā moho vā paṭighaṃ vāpi cetaso’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
Again, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* should consider thus: 'On the path by which I went to the village for alms, or in the place where I wandered for alms, or on the path by which I returned from the almsround, was there any desire (*chando*), lust (*rāgo*), hate (*doso*), delusion (*moho*), or aversion (*paṭighaṃ*) in my mind regarding sounds cognizable by the ear? ...regarding odours cognizable by the nose? ...regarding flavours cognizable by the tongue? ...regarding tangibles cognizable by the body? ...regarding mindobjects cognizable by the mind?’

If, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu*, by reviewing, knows thus: ‘On the path by which I went to the village for alms, or in the place where I wandered for alms, or on the path by which I returned from the almsround, there was desire (*chando*), lust (*rāgo*), hate (*doso*), or delusion (*moho*), or aversion (*paṭighaṃ*) in my mind regarding mindobjects cognizable by the mind,’ then he should make an effort to abandon those evil unwholesome states (*akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ*).

But if, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu*, by reviewing, knows thus: ‘On the path by which I went to the village for alms, and in the place where I wandered for alms, and on the path by which I returned from the almsround, there was no desire (*chando*), lust (*rāgo*), hate (*doso*), delusion (*moho*), or aversion (*paṭighaṃ*) in my mind regarding mindobjects cognizable by the mind,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states (*kusalesu dhammesu*).

mula_pali: 440. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘pahīnā nu kho me pañca kāmaguṇā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘appahīnā kho me pañca kāmaguṇā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘pahīnā kho me pañca kāmaguṇā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
Furthermore, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu should reflect thus: ‘Are the five strands of sensual pleasure abandoned in me?’ If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, a bhikkhu knows thus: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure are not abandoned in me,’ then, Sāriputta, effort should be made by that bhikkhu for the abandoning of the five strands of sensual pleasure (pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ).

But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, a bhikkhu knows thus: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure are abandoned in me,’ then, Sāriputta, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome qualities.
commentary_pali:
440.Pahīnā nu kho me pañca kāmaguṇātiādīsu ekabhikkhussa paccavekkhaṇā nānā, nānābhikkhūnaṃ paccavekkhaṇā nānāti. Kathaṃ? Eko hi bhikkhu pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto pattacīvaraṃ paṭisāmetvā vivittokāse nisinno paccavekkhati ‘‘pahīnā nu kho me pañcakāmaguṇā’’ti. So ‘‘appahīnā’’ti ñatvā vīriyaṃ paggayha anāgāmimaggena pañcakāmaguṇikarāgaṃ samugghāṭetvā maggānantaraṃ phalaṃ phalānantaraṃ maggaṃ tato vuṭṭhāya paccavekkhanto ‘‘pahīnā’’ti pajānāti. Nīvaraṇādīsupi eseva nayo. Etesaṃ pana arahattamaggena pahānādīni honti, evaṃ ekabhikkhussa nānāpaccavekkhaṇā hoti. Etāsu pana paccavekkhaṇāsu añño bhikkhu ekaṃ paccavekkhaṇaṃ paccavekkhati, añño ekanti evaṃ nānābhikkhūnaṃ nānāpaccavekkhaṇā hoti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Piṇḍapātapārisuddhisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
440. "Are the five sensual qualities abandoned by me?" Thus, the reflection of one bhikkhu is different, the reflection of many bhikkhus is different.

How so? A certain bhikkhu, having returned from alms-gathering after the meal, having put away his bowl and robe, sits down in a secluded place and reflects: "Are the five sensual qualities abandoned by me?"

Knowing "They are not abandoned," he generates effort, and by the path of the non-returner, having completely eradicated the lust for the five sensual qualities, after the path, the fruit; after the fruit, the path; then, rising up and reflecting, he understands, "They are abandoned."

The same method applies in the case of the hindrances, and so on.

But for these, the abandoning, and so on, are by the path of Arhatship; thus, the reflection of one bhikkhu is different.

Moreover, among these reflections, one bhikkhu reflects on one reflection, another on another; thus, the reflection of many bhikkhus is different.

The rest is clear throughout.

The commentary on the Piṇḍapātapārisuddhisutta is finished.

mula_pali: 441. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘pahīnā nu kho me pañca nīvaraṇā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘appahīnā kho me pañca nīvaraṇā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā pañcannaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ pahānāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘pahīnā kho me pañca nīvaraṇā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
Furthermore, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* should reflect thus: ‘Are the five hindrances abandoned in me?’ If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, a *bhikkhu* knows thus: ‘The five hindrances (*pañca nīvaraṇā*) are not abandoned in me’, then, Sāriputta, that *bhikkhu* should make an effort (*vāyamitabbaṃ*) to abandon those five hindrances.

But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, a *bhikkhu* knows thus: ‘The five hindrances are abandoned in me’, then he can abide happy and glad (*pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ*), training day and night (*ahorattānusikkhinā*) in wholesome states (*kusalesu dhammesu*).

mula_pali: 442. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘pariññātā nu kho me pañcupādānakkhandhā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘apariññātā kho me pañcupādānakkhandhā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ pariññāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘pariññātā kho me pañcupādānakkhandhā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english: Furthermore, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* should consider thus: ‘Are the five aggregates affected by clinging fully understood by me?’ If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, a *bhikkhu* knows thus: ‘The five aggregates affected by clinging are not fully understood by me,’ then, Sāriputta, that *bhikkhu* should make an effort to fully understand the five aggregates affected by clinging. But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, a *bhikkhu* knows thus: ‘The five aggregates affected by clinging are fully understood by me,’ then he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

mula_pali: 443. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘bhāvitā nu kho me cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhāvitā kho me cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvanāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhāvitā kho me cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
Furthermore, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu should reflect thus: ‘Are the four foundations of mindfulness developed in me?’ If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, he knows thus: ‘The four foundations of mindfulness are not developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, that bhikkhu should make an effort to develop the four foundations of mindfulness.

But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, he knows thus: ‘The four foundations of mindfulness (catāro satipaṭṭhānā) are developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states (kusalesu dhammesu).

mula_pali: 444. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘bhāvitā nu kho me cattāro sammappadhānā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhāvitā kho me cattāro sammappadhānā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā catunnaṃ sammappadhānānaṃ bhāvanāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhāvitā kho me cattāro sammappadhānā’ti , tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
Furthermore, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* should reflect thus: ‘Are the four right exertions developed in me?’ If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, a *bhikkhu* knows thus: ‘The four right exertions are not developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, by that *bhikkhu*, effort should be made to develop the four right exertions.

But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, a *bhikkhu* knows thus: ‘The four right exertions are developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, by that *bhikkhu*, one should abide just with that joy and gladness, being continuously trained day and night in wholesome qualities (*kuśalā dharmā*).

mula_pali: 445. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘bhāvitā nu kho me cattāro iddhipādā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhāvitā kho me cattāro iddhipādā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvanāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhāvitā kho me cattāro iddhipādā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
Furthermore, Sāriputta, a monk should reflect thus: ‘Are the four bases of spiritual power developed in me?’ If, Sāriputta, a monk knows thus when reviewing: ‘The four bases of spiritual power are not developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, effort should be made by that monk for the development of the four bases of spiritual power ( *iddhipāda*).

But if, Sāriputta, a monk knows thus when reviewing: ‘The four bases of spiritual power are developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, he can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states (*kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu*).

mula_pali: 446. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘bhāvitāni nu kho me pañcindriyānī’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhāvitāni kho me pañcindriyānī’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvanāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhāvitāni kho me pañcindriyānī’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english: Again, Sāriputta, the monk should reflect thus: 'Are my five faculties developed?' If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, the monk knows thus: 'My five faculties are undeveloped,' then, Sāriputta, the monk should make an effort to develop the five faculties. But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, the monk knows thus: 'My five faculties are developed,' then, Sāriputta, the monk can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states ( *kuśalesu dharmesu*).

mula_pali: 447. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘bhāvitāni nu kho me pañca balānī’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhāvitāni kho me pañca balānī’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā pañcannaṃ balānaṃ bhāvanāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhāvitāni kho me pañca balānī’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
447. Furthermore, Sāriputta, the monk should reflect thus: ‘Are the five powers developed by me?’ If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, he knows thus: ‘The five powers are not developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, the monk should make an effort to develop the five powers.

But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, he knows thus: ‘The five powers are developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, the monk can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states ( *kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu*).

mula_pali: 448. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘bhāvitā nu kho me satta bojjhaṅgā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhāvitā kho me satta bojjhaṅgā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvanāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhāvitā kho me satta bojjhaṅgā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
Furthermore, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu should reflect thus: ‘Are the seven factors of enlightenment developed in me?’ If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, he knows thus: ‘The seven factors of enlightenment are not developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, that bhikkhu should make an effort to develop the seven factors of enlightenment ( *saptānāṃ bodhyaṅgānāṃ bhāvanāya vāyamitavyam*).

But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, he knows thus: ‘The seven factors of enlightenment are developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, that bhikkhu can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states.

mula_pali: 449. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘bhāvito nu kho me ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhāvito kho me ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa bhāvanāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhāvito kho me ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo’ti , tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
Furthermore, Sāriputta, a *bhikṣu* should reflect thus: 'Is the noble eightfold path developed by me?' If, Sāriputta, a *bhikṣu*, upon reflection, knows thus: 'The noble eightfold path is not developed by me,' then, Sāriputta, effort should be made by that *bhikṣu* for the development of the noble eightfold path.

But if, Sāriputta, a *bhikṣu*, upon reflection, knows thus: 'The noble eightfold path is developed by me,' then, Sāriputta, that *bhikṣu* should abide in that very joy and gladness, constantly training day and night in wholesome qualities (*kuśaladharmas*).

mula_pali: 450. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘bhāvitā nu kho me samatho ca vipassanā cā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhāvitā kho me samatho ca vipassanā cā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā samathavipassanānaṃ bhāvanāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘bhāvitā kho me samatho ca vipassanā cā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english: Furthermore, Sāriputta, the monk should consider thus: ‘Are serenity (*śamatha*) and insight (*vipaśyanā*) developed in me?’ If, Sāriputta, by reviewing, he knows thus: ‘Serenity and insight are not developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, the monk should make an effort to develop serenity and insight. But if, Sāriputta, by reviewing, he knows thus: ‘Serenity and insight are developed in me,’ then, Sāriputta, the monk can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states (*kuśalāḥ dharmāḥ*).

mula_pali: 451. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhunā iti paṭisañcikkhitabbaṃ – ‘sacchikatā nu kho me vijjā ca vimutti cā’ti? Sace, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘asacchikatā kho me vijjā ca vimutti cā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā vijjāya vimuttiyā sacchikiriyāya vāyamitabbaṃ. Sace pana, sāriputta, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘sacchikatā kho me vijjā ca vimutti cā’ti, tena, sāriputta, bhikkhunā teneva pītipāmojjena vihātabbaṃ ahorattānusikkhinā kusalesu dhammesu.
mula_english:
451. Furthermore, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu* should consider thus: ‘Is true knowledge (*vidjā*) and deliverance (*vimutti*) realised by me?’ If, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu*, by reviewing, knows thus: ‘True knowledge (*vidjā*) and deliverance (*vimutti*) are not realised by me,’ then, Sāriputta, that *bhikkhu* should make an effort to realise true knowledge (*vidjā*) and deliverance (*vimutti*).

But if, Sāriputta, a *bhikkhu*, by reviewing, knows thus: ‘True knowledge (*vidjā*) and deliverance (*vimutti*) are realised by me,’ then, Sāriputta, that *bhikkhu* can abide happy and glad, training day and night in wholesome states (*kusalesu dhammesu*).

mula_pali:
452. ‘‘Ye hi keci, sāriputta, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā piṇḍapātaṃ parisodhesuṃ, sabbe te evameva paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā piṇḍapātaṃ parisodhesuṃ. Yepi hi keci, sāriputta, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā piṇḍapātaṃ parisodhessanti, sabbe te evameva paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā piṇḍapātaṃ parisodhessanti. Yepi hi keci, sāriputta, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā piṇḍapātaṃ parisodhenti, sabbe te evameva paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā piṇḍapātaṃ parisodhenti. Tasmātiha, sāriputta vo sāriputta evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ (sī. pī.), ‘paccavekkhitvā paccavekkhitvā piṇḍapātaṃ parisodhessāmā’ti – evañhi vo, sāriputta, sikkhitabba’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Piṇḍapātapārisuddhisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.
mula_english:
452. “Sāriputta, whatever ascetics (*śramaṇa*) and priests (*brāhmaṇa*) in the past have purified their almsfood (*piṇḍapāta*) have all done so by repeatedly reviewing thus.

Whatever ascetics and priests in the future will purify their almsfood, all will do so by repeatedly reflecting thus.

Whatever ascetics and priests in the present are purifying their almsfood, all are doing so by repeatedly reflecting thus.

Therefore, Sāriputta, you should train thus: ‘We will purify our almsfood by repeatedly reviewing thus’."

This was said by the Blessed One (*bhagavān*). The venerable Sāriputta was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The *Piṇḍapātapārisuddhisutta* (Discourse on the Purity of Almsfood), the ninth, is finished.

mula_pali:
453. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā gajaṅgalāyaṃ kajaṅgalāyaṃ (sī. pī.), kajjaṅgalāyaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) viharati suveḷuvane veḷuvane (syā. kaṃ.), mukheluvane (sī. pī.). Atha kho uttaro māṇavo pārāsiviyantevāsī pārāsariyantevāsī (sī. pī.), pārāsiriyantevāsī (syā. kaṃ.) yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho uttaraṃ māṇavaṃ pārāsiviyantevāsiṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘deseti, uttara, pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṃ indriyabhāvana’’nti? ‘‘Deseti, bho gotama, pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṃ indriyabhāvana’’nti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana, uttara, deseti pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṃ indriyabhāvana’’nti? ‘‘Idha, bho gotama, cakkhunā rūpaṃ na passati, sotena saddaṃ na suṇāti – evaṃ kho, bho gotama, deseti pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṃ indriyabhāvana’’nti. ‘‘Evaṃ sante kho, uttara, andho bhāvitindriyo bhavissati, badhiro bhāvitindriyo bhavissati; yathā pārāsiviyassa brāhmaṇassa vacanaṃ. Andho hi, uttara, cakkhunā rūpaṃ na passati, badhiro sotena saddaṃ na suṇātī’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, uttaro māṇavo pārāsiviyantevāsī tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno nisīdi.

Atha kho bhagavā uttaraṃ māṇavaṃ pārāsiviyantevāsiṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ maṅkubhūtaṃ pattakkhandhaṃ adhomukhaṃ pajjhāyantaṃ appaṭibhānaṃ viditvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘aññathā kho, ānanda, deseti pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṃ indriyabhāvanaṃ, aññathā ca panānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā hotī’’ti. ‘‘Etassa, bhagavā, kālo; etassa, sugata, kālo yaṃ bhagavā ariyassa vinaye anuttaraṃ indriyabhāvanaṃ deseyya. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tenahānanda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
Thus have I heard:

On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the territory of the Kajangala people, at Suveluvana.

Then Uttara, a young man and a student of the Pārāsariya, went to the Blessed One; having gone, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.

Having concluded the conversation of courteous greetings, he sat down to one side. The Blessed One then said to Uttara, who was sitting to one side: “Uttara, does the Brahmin Pārāsariya teach his disciples the development of the faculties ( *indriyabhāvana*)?”

“Yes, Master Gotama, the Brahmin Pārāsariya teaches his disciples the development of the faculties.”

“But how, Uttara, does the Brahmin Pārāsariya teach his disciples the development of the faculties?”

“Here, Master Gotama, one does not see forms with the eye, one does not hear sounds with the ear – that is how, Master Gotama, the Brahmin Pārāsariya teaches his disciples the development of the faculties.”

“If that is so, Uttara, then a blind man will have developed faculties, a deaf man will have developed faculties; according to the word of the Brahmin Pārāsariya. For a blind man, Uttara, does not see forms with the eye, and a deaf man does not hear sounds with the ear.”

When this was said, Uttara, the young man and student of the Pārāsariya, sat silent, dismayed, with drooping shoulders, head down, pondering, and without a reply.

Then, knowing that Uttara, the young man and student of the Pārāsariya, was silent, dismayed, with drooping shoulders, head down, pondering, and without a reply, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda, saying: “Ānanda, the Brahmin Pārāsariya teaches the development of the faculties in one way, but in the Discipline of the Noble One, the unsurpassed development of the faculties (*anuttarā indriyabhāvana*) is another.”

“Venerable sir, this is the time! O Well-gone One, this is the time for the Blessed One to teach the unsurpassed development of the faculties in the Noble One's Discipline. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the monks will remember it.”

“Then listen, Ānanda, and pay close attention, I will speak.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:
commentary_pali:
453.Evaṃme sutanti indriyabhāvanāsuttaṃ. Tattha gajaṅgalāyanti evaṃnāmake nigame. Suveḷuvaneti suveḷu nāma ekā rukkhajāti, tehi sañchanno mahāvanasaṇḍo, tattha viharati. Cakkhunā rūpaṃ na passati, sotena saddaṃ na suṇātīti cakkhunā rūpaṃ na passitabbaṃ, sotena saddo na sotabboti evaṃ desetīti adhippāyena vadati.

Aññathā ariyassa vinayeti iminā bhagavā attano sāsane asadisāya indriyabhāvanāya kathanatthaṃ ālayaṃ akāsi. Athāyasmā ānando – ‘‘satthā ālayaṃ dasseti, handāhaṃ imissaṃ parisati bhikkhusaṅghassa indriyabhāvanākathaṃ kāremī’’ti satthāraṃ yācanto etassabhagavātiādimāha. Athassa bhagavā indriyabhāvanaṃ kathento tena hānandātiādimāha.

Aññathā ariyassa vinaye etassa bhagavā tena hānandā
commentary_english:
453. Evaṃ me suta *iti* the *indriyabhāvanāsuttaṃ*.

*Tattha gajaṅgalāya* *iti* in the settlement named Evaṃ.

*Suveḷuvane* *iti* *suveḷu* by name is a tree species. Covered by these is the great forest grove. There [he] dwells.

*Cakkhunā rūpaṃ na passati, sotena saddaṃ na suṇātī* *iti* through the eye, form is not to be seen; through the ear, sound is not to be heard; thus, with this intention, he speaks.

*Aññathā ariyassa vinaye* *iti*, by this the Blessed One (bhagavān) made a dwelling place for the purpose of speaking of the unequalled sense-faculty development in his own teaching.

Then venerable Ānanda thought: "The teacher shows a dwelling place, now what sense-faculty development talk shall I do for this assembly, the monastic community?" Thus, beseeching the teacher, he spoke, beginning with *etassa bhagavā*.

Then, as the Blessed One (bhagavān) was speaking of sense-faculty development, he spoke, beginning with *tena hānandā*.

*Aññathā ariyassa vinaye etassa bhagavā tena hānandā*.

mula_pali: 454. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā hoti? Idhānanda, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ manāpaṃ, uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ, uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ . Tañca kho saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ. Etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ – upekkhā’ti. Tassa taṃ uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati; upekkhā saṇṭhāti. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, cakkhumā puriso ummīletvā vā nimīleyya, nimīletvā vā ummīleyya; evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṃsīghaṃ evaṃtuvaṭaṃ evaṃappakasirena uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu.
mula_english:
454. And how, Ānanda, is there the unsurpassed development of the faculties (indriyabhāvanā) in the Noble One's Discipline (ariyassa vinaye)? Here, Ānanda, to a bhikkhu, on seeing a form (rūpaṃ) with the eye (cakkhunā), there arises what is agreeable (manāpaṃ), there arises what is disagreeable (amanāpaṃ), there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable (manāpāmanāpaṃ).

He understands thus: ‘There has arisen in me what is agreeable (manāpaṃ), there has arisen what is disagreeable (amanāpaṃ), there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable (manāpāmanāpaṃ).

But that is conditioned (saṅkhataṃ), gross (oḷārikaṃ), dependently arisen (paṭiccasamuppannaṃ).

This is peaceful (santaṃ), this is sublime (paṇītaṃ), that is, equanimity (upekkhā).’

The agreeable (manāpaṃ) that arose, the disagreeable (amanāpaṃ) that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable (manāpāmanāpaṃ) that arose cease in him and equanimity (upekkhā) is established (saṇṭhāti).

Just as a man with good sight, Ānanda, having opened his eyes (ummīletvā) might shut them (nimīleyya) or having shut his eyes (nimīletvā) might open them (ummīleyya); so too concerning anything at all, Ānanda, the agreeable (manāpaṃ) that arose, the disagreeable (amanāpaṃ) that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable (manāpāmanāpaṃ) that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity (upekkhā) is established (saṇṭhāti). This is called in the Noble One’s Discipline (ariyassa vinaye) the unsurpassed development of the faculties (indriyabhāvanā) regarding forms (rūpesu) cognizable by the eye (cakkhuviññeyyesu).
commentary_pali: 454. Tatha yadidaṃ upekkhāti yā esā vipassanupekkhā nāma, esā santā esā paṇītā, atappikāti attho. Iti ayaṃ bhikkhu cakkhudvāre rūpārammaṇampi iṭṭhe ārammaṇe manāpaṃ, aniṭṭhe amanāpaṃ, majjhatte manāpāmanāpañca cittaṃ, tassa rajjituṃ vā dussituṃ vā muyhituṃ vā adatvāva pariggahetvā vipassanaṃ majjhatte ṭhapeti. Cakkhumāti sampannacakkhuvisuddhanetto. Cakkhābādhikassa hi uddhaṃ ummīlananimmīlanaṃ na hoti, tasmā so na gahito.
commentary_english:
454. Furthermore, that which is equanimity (*upekkhā*), that which is called insight-equanimity (*vipassanūpekkhā*), that is serene, that is excellent, that is without torment—this is the meaning.

Thus, this *bhikkhu*, at the eye-door (*cakkhudvāre*), with regard to forms (*rūpārammaṇa*), whether an agreeable object in an agreeable sense-sphere, or a disagreeable object in a disagreeable sense-sphere, or a middling object that is both agreeable and disagreeable, without giving his mind (*citta*) over to attachment, aversion, or confusion, but rather taking hold of insight (*vipassanā*) in the middle way (*majjhatte*), he establishes it.

"One with vision" (*cakkhumā*) means one whose eye is perfected, whose vision is purified.

For one afflicted with an eye disease (*cakkhābādhikassa*), there is no upward opening and closing of the eyes (*ummīlananimmīlanaṃ*); therefore, he is not included.

mula_pali: 455. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno sotena saddaṃ sutvā uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ manāpaṃ, uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ, uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ. Tañca kho saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ. Etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ – upekkhā’ti. Tassa taṃ uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati; upekkhā saṇṭhāti. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, balavā puriso appakasireneva accharaṃ accharikaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) pahareyya; evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṃsīghaṃ evaṃtuvaṭaṃ evaṃappakasirena uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā sotaviññeyyesu saddesu.
mula_english:
455. Again, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* hears a sound with the ear, there arises in him what is agreeable (*manāpa*), there arises what is disagreeable (*amanāpa*), there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpa*).

He understands thus: “There has arisen in me what is agreeable (*manāpa*), there has arisen what is disagreeable (*amanāpa*), there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpa*).

But that is conditioned (*saṃkhataṃ*), gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannaṃ*);

this is peaceful (*santaṃ*), this is sublime (*paṇītaṃ*), that is, equanimity (*upekkhā’ti*).'

The agreeable (*manāpa*) that arose, the disagreeable (*amanāpa*) that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpa*) that arose cease in him and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established.

Just as a strong man might easily snap his fingers, so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable (*manāpa*) that arose, the disagreeable (*amanāpa*) that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpa*) that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established. This is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties regarding sounds cognizable by the ear.

mula_pali: 456. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ manāpaṃ, uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ, uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ. Tañca kho saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ. Etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ – upekkhā’ti. Tassa taṃ uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati; upekkhā saṇṭhāti. Seyyathāpi, ānanda , īsakaṃpoṇe īsakapoṇe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), īsakaphaṇe (sī. aṭṭha.), ‘‘majjhe uccaṃ hutvā’’ti ṭīkāya saṃsanditabbā padumapalāse paduminipatte (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) udakaphusitāni pavattanti, na saṇṭhanti; evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṃsīghaṃ evaṃtuvaṭaṃ evaṃappakasirena uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā ghānaviññeyyesu gandhesu.
mula_english:
“Again, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* smells an odour with the nose (*ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā*), there arises in him what is agreeable (*manāpaṃ*), there arises what is disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*), there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*).

He understands thus: “There has arisen in me what is agreeable (*manāpaṃ*), there has arisen what is disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*), there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*)."

But that is conditioned (*saṅkhataṃ*), gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannaṃ*);

this is peaceful (*santaṃ*), this is sublime (*paṇītaṃ*), that is, equanimity (*upekkhā’ti*).'

The agreeable that arose (*manāpaṃ*), the disagreeable that arose (*amanāpaṃ*), and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*) cease in him and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established (*saṇṭhāti*).

Just as, Ānanda, raindrops on a slightly sloping lotus leaf roll off and do not remain there, so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity is established. This is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme (*anuttarā*) development of the faculties (*indriyabhāvanā*) regarding odours (*gandhesu*) cognizable by the nose (*ghānaviññeyyesu*).
commentary_pali: 456.Īsakaṃpoṇeti rathīsā viya uṭṭhahitvā ṭhite.
commentary_english: "īsakaṃpoṇe" means having stood, like a chariot-pole, having risen up.

mula_pali: 457. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ manāpaṃ, uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ, uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ. Tañca kho saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ. Etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ – upekkhā’ti. Tassa taṃ uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati; upekkhā saṇṭhāti . Seyyathāpi, ānanda, balavā puriso jivhagge kheḷapiṇḍaṃ saṃyūhitvā appakasirena vameyya sandhameyya (ka.); evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṃsīghaṃ evaṃtuvaṭaṃ evaṃappakasirena uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu.
mula_english:
“Again, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* tastes a flavour with the tongue, there arises in him what is agreeable (*manāpa*), there arises what is disagreeable (*amanāpa*), there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpa*).

He understands thus: “There has arisen in me what is agreeable, there has arisen what is disagreeable, there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

But that is conditioned (*saṅkhataṃ*), gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannaṃ*);

this is peaceful (*santaṃ*), this is sublime (*paṇītaṃ*), that is, equanimity (*upekkhā*).'

The agreeable that arose (*manāpa*), the disagreeable that arose (*amanāpa*), and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose (*manāpāmanāpa*) cease in him and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established.

Just as a strong man might easily spit out a ball of spittle collected on the tip of his tongue, so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose (*manāpa*), the disagreeable that arose (*amanāpa*), and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose (*manāpāmanāpa*) cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established. This is called in the Noble One’s (*ariyassa*) Discipline the supreme development of the faculties (*indriyabhāvanā*) regarding flavours cognizable by the tongue (*jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu*).

mula_pali: 458. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ manāpaṃ, uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ, uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ. Tañca kho saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ. Etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ – upekkhā’ti. Tassa taṃ uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati; upekkhā saṇṭhāti. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṃsīghaṃ evaṃtuvaṭaṃ evaṃappakasirena uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā kāyaviññeyyesu phoṭṭhabbesu.
mula_english:
“Again, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* touches a tangible with the body (*kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā*), there arises what is agreeable (*manāpaṃ*), there arises what is disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*), there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*).

He understands thus: “There has arisen in me what is agreeable (*manāpaṃ*), there has arisen what is disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*), there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*).

But that is conditioned (*saṅkhataṃ*), gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannaṃ*);

this is peaceful (*santaṃ*), this is sublime (*paṇītaṃ*), that is, equanimity (*upekkhā’ti*).’

The agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease in him and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established (*saṇṭhāti*).

Just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable that arose, the disagreeable that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established (*saṇṭhāti*). This is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties regarding tangibles cognizable by the body.

mula_pali: 459. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno manasā dhammaṃ viññāya uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ manāpaṃ, uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ, uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ. Tañca kho saṅkhataṃ oḷārikaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ. Etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ – upekkhā’ti. Tassa taṃ uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati; upekkhā saṇṭhāti. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, balavā puriso divasaṃsantatte divasasantette (sī.) ayokaṭāhe dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni nipāteyya. Dandho, ānanda, udakaphusitānaṃ nipāto, atha kho naṃ khippameva parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya; evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṃsīghaṃ evaṃtuvaṭaṃ evaṃappakasirena uppannaṃ manāpaṃ uppannaṃ amanāpaṃ uppannaṃ manāpāmanāpaṃ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā manoviññeyyesu dhammesu. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā hoti.
mula_english:
459. Again, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* cognizes a *dhamma* (mind-object) with the mind, there arises in him what is agreeable (*manāpaṃ*), there arises what is disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*), there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*).

He understands thus: “There has arisen in me what is agreeable (*manāpaṃ*), there has arisen what is disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*), there has arisen what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*).

But that is conditioned (*saṅkhataṃ*), gross (*oḷārikaṃ*), dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannaṃ*);

this is peaceful (*santaṃ*), this is sublime (*paṇītaṃ*), that is, equanimity (*upekkhā’ti*).'

The agreeable (*manāpaṃ*) that arose, the disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*) that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*) that arose cease in him and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established.

Just as if a strong man were to let two or three drops of water fall onto an iron plate heated for a whole day,

the falling of the drops might be slow but they would quickly vaporise and vanish, so too concerning anything at all, the agreeable (*manāpaṃ*) that arose, the disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*) that arose, and the both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*) that arose cease just as quickly, just as rapidly, just as easily, and equanimity (*upekkhā*) is established. This is called in the Noble One’s Discipline the supreme development of the faculties (*indriyabhāvanā*) regarding ideas cognizable by the mind (*manoviññeyyesu dhammesu*).

“That is how there is the supreme development of the faculties (*indriyabhāvanā*) in the Noble One’s Discipline.

mula_pali: 460. ‘‘Kathañcānanda , sekho hoti pāṭipado? Idhānanda, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So tena uppannena manāpena uppannena amanāpena uppannena manāpāmanāpena aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…, jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So tena uppannena manāpena uppannena amanāpena uppannena manāpāmanāpena aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, sekho hoti pāṭipado.
mula_english: “And how, Ānanda, is one a disciple in higher training, one who has entered upon the way (sekho hoti pāṭipado)? Here, Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* sees a form (*rūpa*) with the eye, there arises in him what is agreeable (*manāpaṃ*), there arises what is disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*), there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*). He is ashamed, humiliated and disgusted by the agreeable that arose, by the disagreeable that arose, and by the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose. On hearing a sound with the ear…On smelling an odour with the nose…On tasting a flavour with the tongue…On touching a tangible with the body…On cognizing a mind-object with the mind, there arises in him what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable; he is ashamed, humiliated and disgusted by the agreeable that arose, by the disagreeable that arose, and by the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose. That is how, Ānanda, one is a disciple in higher training, one who has entered upon the way.

mula_pali: 461. ‘‘Kathañcānanda, ariyo hoti bhāvitindriyo? Idhānanda, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā uppajjati manāpaṃ, uppajjati amanāpaṃ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṃ. So sace ākaṅkhati – ‘paṭikūle paṭikkūle (sabbattha) appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘paṭikūlañca appaṭikūlañca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṃ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako tattha viharati sato sampajāno.
mula_english:
461. But how, Ānanda, is one a noble one with developed faculties? Here, Ānanda, when a *bhikṣu* sees a form with the eye, agreeable things arise, disagreeable things arise, and agreeable-disagreeable things arise.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive (*paṭikūla*)’, he abides perceiving the unrepulsive (*appaṭikūla*) in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive (*paṭikūla*) in the unrepulsive (*appaṭikūla*)’, he abides perceiving the repulsive (*paṭikūla*) in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive (*appaṭikūla*) in the repulsive (*paṭikūla*) and the unrepulsive (*appaṭikūla*)’, he abides perceiving the unrepulsive (*appaṭikūla*) in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive (*paṭikūla*) in the unrepulsive (*appaṭikūla*) and the repulsive (*paṭikūla*)’, he abides perceiving the repulsive (*paṭikūla*) in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I, avoiding both the repulsive (*paṭikūla*) and unrepulsive (*appaṭikūla*), abide in equanimity (*upekkhako*), mindful (*sato*) and fully aware (*sampajāno*)’, he abides in equanimity (*upekkhako*) towards that, mindful (*sato*) and fully aware (*sampajāno*).
commentary_pali:
461.Paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññītiādīsu paṭikūle mettāpharaṇena vā dhātuso upasaṃhārena vā appaṭikūlasaññī viharati. Appaṭikūle asubhapharaṇena vā aniccato upasaṃhārena vā paṭikūlasaññī viharati. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvāti majjhatto hutvā viharitukāmo kiṃ karotīti? Iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu āpāthagatesu neva somanassiko na domanassiko hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ –

‘‘Kathaṃ paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī viharati? Aniṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ mettāya vā pharati, dhātuto vā upasaṃharati, evaṃ paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī viharati. Kathaṃ appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī viharati? Iṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ asubhāya vā pharati, aniccato vā upasaṃharati, evaṃ appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī viharati. Kathaṃ paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī viharati? Aniṭṭhasmiñca iṭṭhasmiñca vatthusmiṃ mettāya vā pharati, dhātuto vā upasaṃharati. Evaṃ paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī viharati. Kathaṃ appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī viharati? Iṭṭhasmiñca aniṭṭhasmiñca vatthusmiṃ asubhāya vā pharati, aniccato vā upasaṃharati, evaṃ appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī viharati . Kathaṃ paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno? Idha bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno. Evaṃ paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno’’ti.

Imesu ca tīsu nayesu paṭhamanaye manāpaṃ amanāpaṃ manāpāmanāpanti saṃkilesaṃ vaṭṭati, nikkilesaṃ vaṭṭati. Dutiyanaye saṃkilesaṃ, tatiyanaye saṃkilesanikkilesaṃ vaṭṭati. Puna vuttaṃ – ‘‘paṭhamaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vaṭṭati, dutiyaṃ saṃkilesampi nikkilesampi, tatiyaṃ nikkilesameva vaṭṭatī’’ti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Indriyabhāvanāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Pañcamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Yo cāyaṃ ‘‘sabbadhammamūlapariyāyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desissāmī’’ti āraddhattā ādikalyāṇo, majjhe ‘‘suttaṃ geyyaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ gāthā udānaṃ itivuttakaṃ jātakaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ vedalla’’nti vacanato majjhekalyāṇo, sanniṭṭhāne ‘‘ariyo bhāvitindriyo’’ti vacanato pariyosānakalyāṇoti tividhakalyāṇo majjhimanikāyo ‘‘mahāvipassanā nāmāya’’nti vutto, so vaṇṇanāvasena samatto hoti.

ādikalyāṇo, majjhekalyāṇo, pariyosānakalyāṇo

Nigamanakathā

Ettāvatā ca –

Āyācito sumatinā therena bhadantabuddhamittena,

bhadantabuddhamittena,

Pubbe mayūradūtapaṭṭanamhi saddhiṃ nivasantena.

Paravādavidhaṃsanassa majjhimanikāyaseṭṭhassa,

majjhimanikāyaseṭṭhassa,

Yamahaṃ papañcasūdanimaṭṭhakathaṃ kātumārabhiṃ.

papañcasūdanimaṭṭhakathaṃ

Sā hi mahāaṭṭhakathāya sāramādāya niṭṭhitā esā,

Sattuttarasatamattāya pāḷiyā bhāṇavārehi.

Ekūnasaṭṭhimatto visuddhimaggopi bhāṇavārehi,

Atthappakāsanatthāya āgamānaṃ kato yasmā.

Tasmā tena sahā’yaṃ gāthāgaṇanānayena aṭṭhakathā,

Samadhikachasaṭṭhisatamiti viññeyyā bhāṇavārānaṃ.

Samadhikachasaṭṭhisatapamāṇamiti bhāṇavārato esā,

Samayaṃ pakāsayantī mahāvihārādhivāsīnaṃ.

Mūlaṭṭhakathāsāraṃ ādāya mayā imaṃ karontena,

Yaṃ paññamupacitaṃ tena hotu loko sadā sukhitoti.

Paramavisuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyappaṭimaṇḍitena sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇasamudayasamuditena sakasamayasamayantaragahanajjhogāhanasamatthena paññāveyyattiyasamannāgatena tipiṭakapariyattippabhede sāṭṭhakathe satthu sāsane appaṭihatañāṇappabhāvena mahāveyyākaraṇena karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacanalāvaṇṇayuttena yuttamuttavādinā vādīvarena mahākavinā pabhinnapaṭisambhidāparivāre chaḷabhiññādippabhedaguṇappaṭimaṇḍite uttarimanussadhamme suppatiṭṭhitabuddhīnaṃ theravaṃsappadīpānaṃ therānaṃ mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ vaṃsālaṅkārabhūtena vipulavisuddhabuddhinā buddhaghosoti garūhi gahitanāmadheyyena therena katā ayaṃ papañcasūdanī nāma majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathā –

buddhaghoso papañcasūdanī

Papañcasūdanī nāma

commentary_english:
461. In the phrases beginning with "perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive" ( *paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī*), one dwells perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive by suffusing it with loving-kindness (*mettāpharaṇena*) or by analyzing it into its constituent elements (*dhātuso upasaṃhārena*).

One dwells perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive by suffusing it with the perception of unattractiveness (*asubhapharaṇena*) or by analyzing it as impermanent (*aniccato upasaṃhārena*).

The same method applies to the remaining phrases (*sesapadesupi eseva nayo*).

Having completely abandoned both (*tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvāti*), desiring to dwell in equanimity (*majjhatto hutvā viharitukāmo*), what does one do? When desirable and undesirable things come into the range of perception (*iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu āpāthagatesu*), one is neither glad (*somanassiko*) nor sad (*domanassiko*).

It was said:

"How does one dwell perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive (*kathaṃ paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī viharati*)? In an undesirable object (*aniṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ*), one suffuses it with loving-kindness (*mettāya vā pharati*) or analyzes it into its elements (*dhātuto vā upasaṃharati*); thus, one dwells perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive.

How does one dwell perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive (*kathaṃ appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī viharati*)? In a desirable object (*iṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ*), one suffuses it with the perception of unattractiveness (*asubhāya vā pharati*) or analyzes it as impermanent (*aniccato vā upasaṃharati*); thus, one dwells perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive.

How does one dwell perceiving the unrepulsive in both the repulsive and the unrepulsive (*kathaṃ paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī viharati*)? In an undesirable and a desirable object (*aniṭṭhasmiñca iṭṭhasmiñca vatthusmiṃ*), one suffuses it with loving-kindness (*mettāya vā pharati*) or analyzes it into its elements (*dhātuto vā upasaṃharati*). Thus, one dwells perceiving the unrepulsive in both the repulsive and the unrepulsive.

How does one dwell perceiving the repulsive in both the unrepulsive and the repulsive (*kathaṃ appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī viharati*)? In a desirable and an undesirable object (*iṭṭhasmiñca aniṭṭhasmiñca vatthusmiṃ*), one suffuses it with the perception of unattractiveness (*asubhāya vā pharati*) or analyzes it as impermanent (*aniccato vā upasaṃharati*); thus, one dwells perceiving the repulsive in both the unrepulsive and the repulsive.

How does one, having completely abandoned both the repulsive and the unrepulsive (*kathaṃ paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā*), dwell in equanimity (*upekkhako viharati*) mindful (*sato*) and fully aware (*sampajāno*)? Here, a *bhikkhu*, seeing a form with the eye (*cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā*), is neither glad (*neva sumano hoti*) nor sad (*na dummano*); he dwells in equanimity mindful and fully aware…pe… knowing a *dhamma* with the mind (*manasā dhammaṃ viññāya*) , he is neither glad nor sad; he dwells in equanimity mindful and fully aware.

Thus, having completely abandoned both the repulsive and the unrepulsive, one dwells in equanimity mindful and fully aware."

In these three methods, in the first method (*paṭhamanaye*), the agreeable (*manāpaṃ*), the disagreeable (*amanāpaṃ*), the agreeable and disagreeable (*manāpāmanāpaṃ*) involve defilement (*saṃkilesaṃ vaṭṭati*) and non-defilement (*nikkilesaṃ vaṭṭati*). In the second method (*dutiyanaye*) there is defilement (*saṃkilesaṃ*), in the third method (*tatiyanaye*) there is defilement and non-defilement (*saṃkilesanikkilesaṃ vaṭṭati*).

Again, it was said: "In the first, there is defilement (*paṭhamaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vaṭṭati*); in the second, there is both defilement and non-defilement (*dutiyaṃ saṃkilesampi nikkilesampi*); in the third, there is only non-defilement (*tatiyaṃ nikkilesameva vaṭṭatī*)."

The rest is clear throughout (*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti*).

The commentary (*aṭṭhakathā*) on the *Indriyabhāvanāsutta* of the *Majjhimanikāya* in the *Papañcasūdanī* is finished.

The commentary on the fifth section (*pañcamavaggavaṇṇanā*) is finished.

The *Uparipaṇṇāsaṭṭhakathā* is finished.

This *Majjhimanikāya*, because it begins with the statement "I will teach you the all-Dharma root discourse" (*sabbadhammamūlapariyāyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, desissāmī*), is good in the beginning (*ādikalyāṇo*); because in the middle it contains the words "suttaṃ geyyaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ gāthā udānaṃ itivuttakaṃ jātakaṃ abbhutadhammaṃ vedallaṃ", it is good in the middle (*majjhekalyāṇo*); because in the conclusion it contains the words "noble, with cultivated senses" (*ariyo bhāvitindriyo*), it is good in the end (*pariyosānakalyāṇo*). This *Majjhimanikāya*, which is good in three ways (*tividhakalyāṇo*), is said to be "named *Mahāvipassanā*", and is thus complete in terms of its commentary (*vaṇṇanāvasena samatto hoti*).

Good in the beginning (*ādikalyāṇo*), good in the middle (*majjhekalyāṇo*), good in the end (*pariyosānakalyāṇo*). Concluding words (*nigamanakathā*).

Thus (*ettāvatā*) –

Requested by the wise elder (*āyācito sumatinā therena*) *Bhadantabuddhamitta*,

*Bhadantabuddhamitta*, who formerly lived together in *Mayūradūtapaṭṭana*,

This commentary on the destruction of rival doctrines (*paravādavidhaṃsanassa*), the best of the *Majjhimanikāya* (*majjhimanikāyaseṭṭhassa*),

I began to write (*yamahaṃ *papañcasūdanimaṭṭhakathaṃ* kātumārabhiṃ*).

This *Papañcasūdanimaṭṭhakathaṃ*, taking the essence from the great commentary (*mahāaṭṭhakathāya sāramādāya*), is finished,

with approximately one hundred and seven *bhāṇavāras* of the *Pāḷi*.

The *Visuddhimagga* is also approximately sixty minus one *bhāṇavāras*,

because it was made for the purpose of revealing the meaning (*atthappakāsanatthāya āgamānaṃ kato yasmā*).

Therefore, along with this commentary according to the method of calculating the verses (*gāthāgaṇanānayena aṭṭhakathā*),

it should be understood that there are one hundred and sixty-six plus *bhāṇavāras*.

This one reveals the *samaya* of those dwelling in the *Mahāvihāra*.

Having taken the essence of the root commentary (*mūlaṭṭhakathāsāraṃ*),

Endowed with the highest pure faith, intelligence, and energy, adorned with morality, good conduct, uprightness, gentleness, and a collection of virtues, capable of thoroughly penetrating the depths of the teachings of one's own school and other schools, possessed of discriminating wisdom, with unobstructed knowledge and radiance in the Buddha's teaching which is differentiated in the form of the Tipiṭaka (Three Baskets) along with its commentaries, by the great grammarian, whose lovely and sublime words are born of the joy produced by the perfection of his faculties, who speaks words that are fitting and liberating, the best of disputants, the great poet, surrounded by a retinue distinguished by analytical knowledge, adorned with virtues such as the six superknowledges, with intelligence well-established in the excellence of human nature, an ornament to the lineage of elders, the abode of the elders dwelling in the Mahāvihāra (Great Monastery), by the Elder whose name Buddhaghosa is respectfully taken by the teachers, this commentary on the Majjhima Nikāya (Middle Length Discourses), called Papañcasūdanī, has been made.

Buddhaghosa
Papañcasūdanī

Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘paṭikūlañca appaṭikūlañca tadubhayampi abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṃ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako tattha viharati sato sampajāno. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, ariyo hoti bhāvitindriyo.
mula_english:
Again, Ānanda, a monk, having heard a sound with the ear… smells an odor with the nose… tastes a flavor with the tongue… touches a tangible with the body… cognizes a mind-object with the mind, there arises what is agreeable, there arises what is disagreeable, there arises what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ he abides perceiving the unrepulsive in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ he abides perceiving the repulsive in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ he abides perceiving the unrepulsive in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ he abides perceiving the repulsive in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I, completely avoiding both the repulsive and the unrepulsive, abide in equanimity, mindful and fully aware,’ he abides in equanimity towards that, mindful and fully aware.

That is how, Ānanda, a noble one with developed faculties is.

mula_pali:
463. ‘‘Iti kho, ānanda, desitā mayā ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā, desito sekho pāṭipado, desito ariyo bhāvitindriyo . Yaṃ kho, ānanda, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya, kataṃ vo taṃ mayā. Etāni, ānanda, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni, jhāyathānanda, mā pamādattha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Indriyabhāvanāsuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

Saḷāyatanavaggo niṭṭhito pañcamo.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Anāthapiṇḍiko channo, puṇṇo nandakarāhulā;

Chachakkaṃ saḷāyatanikaṃ, nagaravindeyyasuddhikā;

Indriyabhāvanā cāpi, vaggo ovādapañcamoti.

Idaṃ vaggānamuddānaṃ –

Devadahonupado ca, suññato ca vibhaṅgako;

Saḷāyatanoti vaggā, uparipaṇṇāsake ṭhitāti.

Uparipaṇṇāsakaṃ samattaṃ.

Tīhi paṇṇāsakehi paṭimaṇḍito sakalo

Majjhimanikāyo samatto.
mula_english:
463.

‘‘Thus, Ānanda, the unsurpassed cultivation of the faculties ( *indriyabhāvanā* ) has been taught by me in the discipline of the noble ones ( *ariyassa vinaye* ), the training of the learner (*sekho pāṭipado*) has been taught, the noble one with cultivated faculties (*bhāvitindriyo*) has been taught.

Whatever should be done, Ānanda, by a teacher ( *satthārā* ) who seeks the welfare of his disciples (*sāvakānaṃ hitesinā*), out of compassion (*anukampakena*) and taking compassion (*anukampaṃ upādāya*), that has been done by me for you.

These are the roots of trees (*rukkhamūlāni*), these are empty dwellings (*suññāgārāni*). Meditate (*jhāyatha*), Ānanda, do not be heedless (*mā pamādattha*), lest you later fall into regret (*vippaṭisārino ahuvattha*).

This is our instruction (*anusāsanī*) to you.’’

This the Blessed One ( *bhagavā* ) said.

The venerable Ānanda ( *āyasmā ānando* ), being pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words (*bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti*).

The *Indriyabhāvanāsutta*ṃ, the tenth, is finished.

The *Saḷāyatanavagga*, the fifth, is finished.

Its summary (*tassuddānaṃ*) –

Anāthapiṇḍika, Channa, Puṇṇa, Nandaka, and Rāhula;

Six sixes, *Saḷāyatanika*, Nagaravindeyya, and Suddhika;

*Indriyabhāvanā* also, the fifth discourse ( *vaggo ovādapañcamoti* ).

This is the chapter summary (*vaggānamuddānaṃ*) –

Devadaha, Anupada, Suññata, and Vibhaṅgaka;

*Saḷāyatana* the chapter, situated in the upper fifty ( *uparipaṇṇāsake ṭhitāti* ).

The upper fifty (*uparipaṇṇāsakaṃ*) is complete.

The middle collection (*majjhimanikāyo*) is complete, adorned with three fifties ( *tīhi paṇṇāsakehi paṭimaṇḍito sakalo*).
